images.alt: By spring the court has its own version. The queen heard frogs croaking in the palace pond in midwinter, and knew the valley, and the number
images.prompt: CLOSING STILL of the episode: the final scene of this story as it ends (not the next episode). The line: “By spring the court has its own version. The queen heard frogs croaking in the palace pond in midwinter, and knew the valley, and the number. Ask the men who were there and they will tell you about a monk who was one bead short.” Context: All five hundred, Majesty. And one monk who couldn’t count. Yushin is at the door. He has been at the door since the drums. Bidam notices, and for once says nothing. Alchun will later call it the bravest thing he saw all night. By spring the court has its own version. The queen heard frogs croaking in the palace pond in midwinter, and knew the valley, and the number. Ask the men who were there and they will tell you about a monk who was one bead short. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — ALCHUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_alchun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Demeanor: Silla's senior general and Yushin's peer; steady, dry, loyal to the throne over factions. #8fb3e0 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | PLACE Jade Gate Valley (옥문곡 (여근곡)) — attached board /pl_jade_gate_valley.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). COMMONERS in every Samhan kingdom wear SIMPLE WHITE: plain undyed white or off-white hemp and ramie jackets, wide trousers and skirts, a cloth sash, straw sandals or bare feet, hair in a plain topknot or braid — no dyed silk, no dots, no gold; colour belongs to rank, so a crowd of farmers, porters, servants and townsfolk reads as a field of soft white cloth with the officials' colours standing out of it. Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: The Yard
blocks.ko: 연무장

blocks.html: Midwinter. The Hwarang yard below the Moon Palace is frozen hard. Class 77 drills on it anyway, because nobody has told them they can stop.
blocks.ko: 한겨울. 월성 아래 화랑 연무장은 꽁꽁 얼었다. 칠십칠기는 그래도 그 위에서 훈련한다. 그만해도 된다고 일러 준 사람이 없으니까.

blocks.html: On the yard rail sit three men who drilled on the same ground more than twenty years ago. The boys keep glancing over. They have heard the stories. They are not sure which ones are true.
blocks.ko: 연무장 난간에 사내 셋이 앉아 있다. 스무 해도 더 전에 같은 땅에서 훈련하던 사내들이다. 아이들이 자꾸 그쪽을 흘끔거린다. 이야기는 들었다. 어느 게 참말인지는 모른다.

blocks.html: Two of the boys have stopped drilling to stare. One wears a purple sleeve. The other’s sleeve is scarlet, and somebody has mended it twice.
blocks.ko: 아이 둘이 훈련을 멈추고 넋을 놓고 본다. 하나는 자색 소매다. 다른 하나는 비색 소매인데, 누가 두 번이나 기웠다.

blocks.speaker: A Hwarang of Class 77
en: That’s them. The Three Eternal.

blocks.speaker: The boy with the mended sleeve
en: Eternal. They’re sitting on a fence.

blocks.speaker: A Hwarang of Class 77
en: There’s a wall in the gallery. Every class paints its best man on it, and the next class paints over him.
Those three, nobody paints over. That’s what eternal means.
lines: 회랑에 벽 있다 아이가. 기수마다 제일 잘난 놈을 거기 그리고, 다음 기수가 그 위에 덧칠한다.
근데 저 셋은 아무도 못 덮는다. 그기 삼웅이다.

blocks.speaker: The boy with the mended sleeve
en: Why them?

blocks.speaker: A Hwarang of Class 77
en: The one with the beads. Bidam. He got a mat on the Council at thirty-eight. Thirty-eight!
My father’s fifty and still waiting.
lines: 염주 찬 분. 비담공. 서른여덟에 화백 자리를 받았다. 서른여덟!

blocks.speaker: The boy with the mended sleeve
en: So he’s good.

blocks.speaker: A Hwarang of Class 77
en: He’s half-sacred. Sacred Bone on one side, and nobody says which side. Bone of the bone.
They’d have given him a mat at twelve if he’d asked nicely.
lines: 반성골이다. 피 한쪽이 성골이라 카는데, 어느 쪽인지는 아무도 입 밖에 안 낸다. 뼈 중의 뼈.
곱게 청했으면 열두 살에도 자리 줬을 끼다.

blocks.speaker: The boy with the mended sleeve
en: And the big one?

blocks.speaker: A Hwarang of Class 77
en: Alchun. Choi, from old Sobuldori. But off a younger son. Good bone, wrong branch.
He had to kill a tiger to get his mat. They say he kept talking the whole time.
lines: 알천공. 최씨, 소벌도리 어른 줄. 근데 작은아들 쪽이다. 뼈는 좋은데 가지가 틀렸다.
자리 얻을라꼬 호랑이를 잡았다 카더라. 잡는 내내 말을 안 멈췄다 카고.

blocks.speaker: The boy with the mended sleeve
en: And the Marshal?

blocks.speaker: A Hwarang of Class 77
en: …Don’t.

blocks.speaker: The boy with the mended sleeve
en: What? He’s purple. He’s True Bone, isn’t he?

blocks.speaker: A Hwarang of Class 77
en: He’s True Bone. That’s all.
Nobody asks about the Marshal’s family. Not here.
lines: 대장군 집안은 아무도 안 묻는다. 여기선.

blocks.html: Nobody in Surabol finishes a sentence about the Marshal’s family. They start one, glance round, and remark on the weather.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에서 대장군 집안 이야기를 끝까지 하는 사람은 없다. 말을 꺼냈다가, 주위를 한 번 보고, 날씨 이야기를 한다.

blocks.html: Silla’s purple is older than Silla. Before there was a king, there were six villages in the valley, and each one had a Kan. An elder.
blocks.ko: 신라의 자색은 신라보다 오래됐다. 임금이 있기 전, 골짜기에 마을이 여섯 있었고, 마을마다 간이 하나 있었다. 어른.

blocks.name: Native words
blocks.ko: 우리말
blocks.note: Silla’s own words, from before anyone in Surabol could write.
blocks.noteKo: 신라 사람들 제 말이다. 서라벌에 글 아는 사람이 하나도 없던 때부터 쓰던 말.

blocks.html: The six Kans met on a hill and chose one Great Kan over all six. Where they found him is another story, and a good one.
blocks.ko: 여섯 간이 언덕에 모여, 여섯 위에 큰 간 하나를 세웠다. 그를 어디서 찾았는지는 다른 이야기다. 좋은 이야기다.

blocks.html: The six villages became the six quarters of the capital. The Kans’ grandchildren became True Bone. Every purple sleeve on this yard can count back to one of six old men on a hill, and most of them will, if you let them.
blocks.ko: 여섯 마을은 도성의 여섯 부가 되었다. 간들의 자손은 진골이 되었다. 이 연무장의 자색 소매는 하나같이 언덕 위 늙은이 여섯 중 하나까지 거슬러 셀 수 있다. 내버려 두면 대개 정말 센다.

blocks.html: Here is how Silla counts a boy. It starts with his bones.
blocks.ko: 신라가 아이 하나를 세는 법은 이렇다. 뼈부터 센다.

blocks.hanja: 骨品
blocks.html: Bone, as in the bone you were born with. Sacred Bone may wear the crown. True Bone may run the country. Everyone else may count the robes. Even among the True Bone, a boy with Sacred Bone on one side of his blood outranks every cousin he has, and at every dinner in Surabol everyone knows exactly who that is.
blocks.ko: 뼈. 타고난 그 뼈다. 성골은 왕관을 쓸 수 있다. 진골은 나라를 굴릴 수 있다. 나머지는 옷 색깔을 셀 수 있다. 진골 안에서도 피 한쪽에 성골이 흐르는 아이는 어느 사촌보다도 위에 앉고, 서라벌의 어느 잔칫상에서든 그게 누군지 모르는 사람은 없다.

Robe · 옷

blocks.html: The boy with the mended sleeve is Head Rank Six. Somewhere in the middle of a drill, he has worked out that the highest step he can ever reach is one the purple boy will walk past on his way up.
blocks.ko: 소매 기운 아이는 6두품이다. 훈련 한가운데서 셈이 끝났다. 그가 평생 오를 수 있는 가장 높은 계단은, 옆의 자색 소매가 올라가다 지나쳐 갈 계단이다.

lines: 그 불 꺼지고 네 해가 지났는데, 내 엉덩이는 아직도 감각이 없데이.
en: Four winters.
Four winters since that fire went out, and I still can’t feel my backside.
You remember Suljong’s face.
When the piece moved.
Like he’d swallowed the cup.
He said it again this morning. In the east corridor.

lines: 당연하지. 네 해 동안 아침마다. 이제 그 양반 염불이 됐어.
en: Of course he did. Every morning for four years. It has become his prayer.

blocks.html: Yushin is not looking at either of them. He is looking up the hill at the palace roofs, the way he does when he thinks nobody is counting.
blocks.ko: 유신은 둘 중 누구도 보지 않는다. 언덕 위 궁 지붕을 보고 있다. 아무도 세지 않는다고 여길 때면 늘 그러듯이.

lines: 저 궁은 시조 때부터 그 자리에 있었다. 우리도 좀 봐 주라, 잠깐.
en: Oi. Marshal. She’s not going anywhere.
That palace has been in the same spot since the Founder. You can look at us for a minute.
I face where my orders come from.

lines: 명이라. 들었나, 알천? 저 사람은 그분을 명이라 부르네.
연꽃도 해를 향하오, 대장군. 그걸 충성이라 부르는 사람은 없소.
en: Orders. Did you hear that, Alchun? He calls her orders.
A lotus faces the sun too, Marshal. Nobody calls that duty.
Her Majesty—
…The queen gives the orders. That is all I said.

lines: 스무 해째 저 말을 꺼내기만 하고, 한 번을 못 끝맺는다 아이가.
en: “Her Majesty—”
Twenty years he’s been starting that sentence. Never once finished it.

blocks.html: Down on the ice, a boy from Class 77 drops his practice sword. Nobody laughs at him. Everybody is listening to the Marshal not answer.
blocks.ko: 얼음판 위에서 칠십칠기 아이 하나가 목검을 떨어뜨린다. 아무도 웃지 않는다. 다들 대장군이 대답하지 않는 소리를 듣고 있다.

lines: 그날 밤 내가 먼저 일어섰지. 자네들 누구보다.
en: I stood first that night, you know. Before either of you.
You stood first.

lines: 나는 호랑이 땜에 일어섰고. 둘 다 시작하지 마래이.
en: And I stood for a tiger. Don’t start, the pair of you.

blocks.html: Then a drum. Not the hour drum. It comes from the palace, slow, then again. The next hill picks it up, and the next, until the whole west is answering.
blocks.ko: 그때 북이 운다. 시각을 알리는 북이 아니다. 궁에서 느리게 한 번, 또 한 번. 옆 언덕이 받고, 그다음 언덕이 받아, 서쪽 전체가 대답한다.

blocks.html: On the ice, forty boys stop at once.
blocks.ko: 얼음판 위에서 아이 마흔이 한꺼번에 멈춘다.

en: That is a muster.

lines: 한겨울에? 누가 이 날씨에 군사를 내노.
en: In midwinter? Who marches in this?

lines: 아무도 안 낼 거라고 우리가 믿기를 바라는 누군가겠지.
en: Someone who wants us to believe nobody would.

blocks.html: Yushin is already off the rail and walking up the hill toward the palace. He does not run. He walks very fast.
blocks.ko: 유신은 벌써 난간에서 내려와 궁 쪽 언덕을 오르고 있다. 뛰지는 않는다. 아주 빨리 걷는다.

en: See? Orders.

lines: 가게 둬. 누군가는 그분이 뭘 들으셨는지 보러 가야지.
너. 너. 그리고 소매 기운 너. 시는 두고 말을 끌고 와. 지금.
en: Let him go to her. Somebody should go and see what she has heard.
You. You. And you, with the mended sleeve. Horses, not poems. Now.

blocks.html: Six boys run for the stables before he finishes. They have waited their whole lives for one of those three to point at them.
blocks.ko: 말이 끝나기도 전에 아이 여섯이 마구간으로 뛴다. 평생 저 셋 중 하나가 자기를 가리켜 주기를 기다려 온 아이들이다.

blocks.html: Riding west in the last of the light, Alchun laughs at nothing. Bidam knows what the nothing is. Four winters ago, the two of them sat all night by a brazier and made a queen.
blocks.ko: 마지막 햇빛 속에서 서쪽으로 달리다가, 알천이 아무것도 아닌 일에 웃는다. 비담은 그 아무것도 아닌 게 뭔지 안다. 네 해 전, 둘은 밤새 화로 곁에 앉아 여왕을 만들었다.

blocks.label: Under the Hill
blocks.ko: 언덕 아래

blocks.html: Yushin reaches the palace before the drum has finished, and finds the queen already in council with it. The door stays shut. A Marshal can’t stand in a corridor all night being looked at, so he does the other thing he does when nobody is counting. He rides east, into hills nobody uses.
blocks.ko: 유신은 북이 그치기도 전에 궁에 닿는다. 여왕은 이미 그 북과 함께 회의 중이다. 문은 닫힌 채다. 원수가 밤새 복도에 서서 구경거리가 될 수는 없으니, 그는 아무도 세지 않을 때 하는 다른 일을 한다. 동쪽으로, 아무도 쓰지 않는 언덕으로 말을 몬다.

blocks.html: A hole in a hill east of the capital. The water is black, the steam is warm, and the hill has opinions.
blocks.ko: 도성 동쪽 언덕의 구멍 하나. 물은 검고, 김은 따뜻하고, 언덕은 할 말이 많다.

blocks.html: His father found this cave by falling into it, and told his son exactly one thing about it: go when you’re stuck. Inside, three women sit on the far rock as if they have always been there, which is roughly true. Narim, the eldest, keeps the rules. Hyullé keeps quiet. Golhwa keeps nothing.
blocks.ko: 그의 아버지는 이 동굴을 굴러떨어져서 찾았고, 아들에게는 딱 한 가지만 일러 주었다. 막히면 가라. 안에는 세 여인이 저쪽 바위에 앉아 있다. 늘 거기 있었다는 듯이. 대충 맞는 말이다. 맏이 나림은 규칙을 지킨다. 혈레는 입을 지킨다. 골화는 아무것도 안 지킨다.

blocks.html: The house rules are older than Silla: Kims only, clean-shaven, and nobody stands in the water dressed. He folds his clothes on the rock lip, lays the sword beside them, and wades in to the chest with his eyes politely on the ceiling.
blocks.ko: 집 규칙은 신라보다 오래됐다. 김씨만, 면도한 얼굴로, 그리고 옷 입고 물에 서는 사람은 없다. 그는 바위턱에 옷을 개어 두고 그 곁에 칼을 누인 뒤, 눈은 예의 바르게 천장에 둔 채 가슴께까지 걸어 들어간다.

en: Unni. Unni. Waist.
…What? I said waist. I’m being good.
lines: …왜? 허리라고만 했잖아. 나 지금 착하게 구는 거야.

en: Golhwa. Chin.
Shaved this morning. For the palace. Poor thing.
Chin passes.
lines: 오늘 아침에 깎았네. 궁 가려고. 불쌍해라.

en: Your father’s stone is cold, Marshal. I can feel it from here. So no question tonight.
lines: 아버님 돌이 차네요, 원수. 여기서도 느껴져요. 그러니 오늘 밤 질문은 없어요.

en: I didn’t come for a question.
…I came for advice.
Advice is cheaper. Go on.
Stand up a bit when you ask.
Her Majesty has been on the throne four winters. Every morning a man in the east corridor says the same word to her back.
She has a Council that votes, a war in the west, and a country that still—
lines: 폐하께서 즉위하신 지 네 해요. 아침마다 동쪽 복도에서 한 사내가 그분 등에 대고 같은 말을 하오.
표결하는 화백이 있고, 서쪽엔 전쟁이 있고, 나라는 아직도—

en: He said Her Majesty with his whole chest. Unni, did you hear—
lines: 폐하래. 가슴을 다 써서. 언니, 들었어—

en: Golhwa.
…How does a soldier help with that?
…He wants to go west. With the drums.
He keeps looking at the mouth.
Then don’t.
Bidam and the big one can carry one valley. They’d like one in public.
Every man in that palace has a sword, Marshal. Not one of them stands at her door without wanting something through it.
lines: 비담이랑 그 덩치면 골짜기 하나는 들어요. 남들 보는 데서 하나 갖고 싶어 하잖아요.
저 궁에 칼 없는 남자 없어요, 원수. 그 문 앞에 서면서 그 너머로 뭘 바라지 않는 남자도 하나 없고요.

en: I want nothing through it.
lines: 나는 그 너머로 바라는 것이 없소.

en: Liar.
…Sorry. That wasn’t the hill. That was me.
Watch her door. Not the valley. The door.
Go when she sends you. Come back to that corridor before the dust settles. That’s how a soldier helps a queen.
lines: 그분 문을 지켜요. 골짜기 말고. 문.
보내시면 가고, 먼지가 가라앉기 전에 그 복도로 돌아와요. 군인이 여왕을 돕는 건 그런 거예요.

en: …And eat something.
You never eat when she’s worried.

blocks.html: He dresses on the rock lip with his back to them, badly, the way every man does in that cave. Golhwa narrates. Narim lets her. Hyullé watches him climb back toward the city and the one lamp still lit in the palace, and says nothing at all.
blocks.ko: 그는 등을 돌린 채 바위턱에서 옷을 입는다. 그 동굴의 남자들이 다 그렇듯 서툴게. 골화가 중계한다. 나림은 내버려 둔다. 혈레는 그가 도성과, 궁에 아직 하나 켜진 등불을 향해 다시 오르는 것을 지켜보고, 아무 말도 하지 않는다.

blocks.label: Jade Gate Valley
blocks.ko: 옥문곡

blocks.html: A valley west of the capital with a polite name. Ask a scholar what a jade gate is and watch him find something interesting on the ceiling.
blocks.ko: 도성 서쪽, 이름만은 점잖은 골짜기. 학자에게 옥문이 무슨 뜻이냐고 물어보라. 그는 갑자기 천장에서 볼 게 생긴다.

blocks.html: Night is down by the time they reach the valley mouth, and a fog with it. Bidam stops the boys with one raised hand.
blocks.ko: 골짜기 어귀에 닿을 즈음엔 밤이 내렸고, 안개도 함께 내렸다. 비담이 손 하나를 들어 아이들을 세운다.

blocks.html: Smoke where there should be no smoke. Five hundred men can hide in a valley. They cannot hide their supper.
blocks.ko: 연기가 날 리 없는 데서 연기가 난다. 사내 오백은 골짜기에 숨을 수 있다. 저녁밥은 못 숨긴다.

blocks.html: Down the road out of the valley comes a monk with a bundle of firewood and a string of beads. He is walking toward the capital at an hour when monks are asleep.
blocks.ko: 골짜기에서 나오는 길로 중 하나가 장작 한 짐과 염주 한 줄을 들고 내려온다. 중들이 잠든 시각에 도성 쪽으로 걷고 있다.

blocks.speaker: The Monk
lines: 나무아미타불. 말 타기엔 추운 밤이옵니다, 도령님들.
en: Amitabha. A cold night for riders, young lords.

lines: 춥지요. 잠깐 앉으시오, 스님. 추위 쫓게 반야심경이나 같이 외웁시다.
en: It is. Sit a moment, brother. Say the Heart Sutra with me, for the cold.

blocks.html: The monk begins. He is fluent for three lines. On the fourth, his thumb moves a bead his mouth has not reached.
blocks.ko: 중이 외기 시작한다. 세 줄까진 유창하다. 넷째 줄에서, 입이 닿지도 않은 염주알을 엄지가 넘긴다.

lines: 중은 세고, 간자는 들고 다닐 뿐이지.
en: You are a bead short, brother.
Monks count. Spies only carry.

blocks.html: The firewood hits the snow. Alchun has him by the collar before he finishes turning. None of the boys saw Alchun get off his horse.
blocks.ko: 장작이 눈 위로 떨어진다. 몸을 다 돌리기도 전에 알천이 그의 멱살을 쥐고 있다. 알천이 말에서 내리는 걸 본 아이는 하나도 없다.

en: How many. Where. Who’s in charge.
Quick, I’m freezing.

blocks.speaker: The Monk
en: …Five hundred. General Uso.
The hill fort behind you. From the back, at dawn.

blocks.html: Bidam sends the boy with the mended sleeve back down the road at a gallop, to find whatever army the drums have raised. The other five lie on their bellies in the snow beside two men in their forties and look down into the valley.
blocks.ko: 비담은 소매 기운 아이를 왔던 길로 달려 보낸다. 북소리가 일으킨 군사가 어디 있든 찾아오라고. 나머지 다섯은 마흔 줄 사내 둘 곁에 눈밭에 엎드려 골짜기를 내려다본다.

blocks.html: Below, the Baekje camp. They have marched four nights in the dark. Now, at the bottom of a valley nobody watches, their captain lets them loosen their saddles.
blocks.ko: 아래에 백제 진이 있다. 나흘 밤을 어둠 속에 걸어왔다. 이제 아무도 지켜보지 않는 골짜기 바닥에서, 그들의 장수가 안장을 풀게 한다.

lines: 비담. 왼쪽 능선. 나는 마른 시내.
저짝이 안장 풀었다. 위원회 안 기다린데이.
en: Bidam. Left ridge. I take the dry creek.
They’ve loosed their saddles. We’re not waiting on a committee.

blocks.html: Alchun has opinions about committees. Every lord in Surabol does. They grew up on the one that unmade a king.
blocks.ko: 알천은 회의라면 할 말이 많다. 서라벌 귀족이라면 다 그렇다. 임금 하나를 무른 회의 얘기를 듣고 자랐으니까.

en: Finally. An enemy I am allowed to hate in public.
Alchun. On my mark.

blocks.html: The army comes up the road behind them, two thousand men breathing smoke, and does not stop to be told anything. Two men walk out in front of it. That is all the order there is.
blocks.ko: 뒤쪽 길로 군사가 올라온다. 입김을 연기처럼 뿜는 이천이다. 무엇을 들으려고 멈추지 않는다. 그 앞으로 사내 둘이 걸어 나간다. 명령은 그게 전부다.

blocks.label: Two of Class 51
blocks.ko: 오십일기 둘

blocks.html: Bidam goes down the left ridge on foot, because horses are loud. His beads are looped on his sword wrist. They click once when he draws, and that is the last sound the first sentry hears.
blocks.ko: 비담은 왼쪽 능선을 걸어서 내려간다. 말은 시끄러우니까. 염주가 칼 쥔 손목에 감겨 있다. 칼을 뽑을 때 한 번 딸깍한다. 첫 보초가 듣는 마지막 소리다.

blocks.html: He does not hurry. He moves through the camp the way he walks through a temple, courteous to the furniture. Men stand up in front of him and do not stay standing.
blocks.ko: 그는 서두르지 않는다. 절집을 걷듯 진영을 지나간다. 세간에도 예의를 갖추면서. 그의 앞에서 일어선 사내들은 서 있지 못한다.

blocks.html: Alchun comes up the dry creek like a rockslide that has learned to swear. A Baekje captain sets a spear against him. Alchun takes the spear by the shaft, and then Alchun has a spear.
blocks.ko: 알천은 욕을 배운 산사태처럼 마른 시내를 치고 올라온다. 백제 장교 하나가 창을 겨눈다. 알천이 창 자루를 잡는다. 그러자 창은 알천의 것이 된다.

blocks.html: A loose horse comes at him out of the smoke. He catches it by the bridle with one arm and turns it, the way he once turned a tiger, and rides it straight into the next fire.
blocks.ko: 연기 속에서 고삐 풀린 말 한 마리가 그에게 달려든다. 그는 한 팔로 굴레를 잡아 말머리를 돌린다. 언젠가 호랑이를 돌리던 그 솜씨로. 그러고는 그 말을 타고 다음 모닥불로 곧장 들어간다.

blocks.html: On the ridge, the five boys have forgotten to draw. Behind them the nangdo of the army, farm sons with spears, have stopped at the valley lip in a long ragged line, the way people stop at a fire.
blocks.ko: 능선 위의 아이 다섯은 칼 뽑는 것도 잊었다. 그 뒤로 군대의 낭도들이, 창을 든 농가 아들들이, 골짜기 턱에 길고 들쭉날쭉한 줄로 멈춰 서 있다. 사람들이 불구경할 때 멈추듯이.

blocks.speaker: A Hwarang of Class 77
en: Are they— is that what— are they always like that?

blocks.speaker: A Nangdo
lines: 늙어서 이 얘기 하실 낍니다. 똑바로 보이소.
en: Shut up and watch, young lord.
You’ll be telling this when you’re old. Get it right.

blocks.html: Two thousand men find they have very little to do. Some will tell it for the rest of their lives. Most will get the numbers wrong. All of them will remember that it looked easy.
blocks.ko: 이천 군사는 할 일이 별로 없다는 걸 안다. 몇몇은 남은 평생 이 얘기를 할 것이다. 대부분은 숫자를 틀리게 말할 것이다. 모두가 그게 쉬워 보였다는 것만은 기억할 것이다.

blocks.label: The Rock
blocks.ko: 큰 돌

blocks.html: Uso climbs the biggest rock in the valley with a bow and a full quiver, and holds it alone. He is good. Every arrow finds somebody. Then the quiver ends before the argument does.
blocks.ko: 우소는 활과 가득 찬 화살통을 들고 골짜기에서 제일 큰 바위에 올라가 혼자 버틴다. 솜씨가 좋다. 화살마다 누군가를 찾아간다. 그러다 화살이 먼저 바닥난다.

blocks.speaker: Uso
lines: 떼거리 말구, 사내 하나믄 내려가 줄 테니께.
en: Come up, then. One of you.
I’ll come down for a man. Not for a mob.
Go on. You’re prettier.
I am. Which is why I am staying clean.

blocks.html: Alchun climbs the rock with nothing in his hands. Uso has one arrow left and spends it. It goes through Alchun’s sleeve, which is the closest anyone comes all night. Alchun takes the bow off him like a father taking a toy, and carries the general of Baekje down the rock under one arm.
blocks.ko: 알천은 빈손으로 바위를 오른다. 우소에게 화살이 하나 남았고, 그걸 쏜다. 화살은 알천의 소매를 뚫는다. 그 밤 누구라도 그에게 가장 가까이 간 것이 그것이다. 알천은 아비가 아이 장난감을 빼앗듯 활을 빼앗고, 백제의 장수를 한 팔에 끼고 바위를 내려온다.

lines: 과녁이 성 밖에 있으면, 우린 좋은 짝이제.
en: We make a good pair when the target is outside the wall.
Inside the wall is still the sacred country.
…I do not miss, either way.

blocks.html: The boys of Class 77 ride home behind them in silence, which for boys that age is a kind of prayer. Tomorrow on the ice they will try to move like that, and fall down, and try again.
blocks.ko: 칠십칠기 아이들은 그 뒤를 따라 말없이 돌아간다. 그 나이 사내아이에게 말없음은 일종의 기도다. 내일 얼음판 위에서 아이들은 저렇게 움직여 보려다 넘어지고, 또 해 볼 것이다.

blocks.html: In Surabol the queen is waiting for a number. She will not be surprised by it. Nobody has surprised her since the flowers.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에서 여왕은 숫자 하나를 기다린다. 그 숫자에 놀라지는 않을 것이다. 그 꽃 이후로 그녀를 놀라게 한 사람은 없다.

blocks.label: The Queen’s Door
blocks.ko: 여왕의 문

blocks.html: Alchun carries something to the queen’s door again, in his fist again, because again nobody has told him there is a box. A string of a hundred and seven beads.
blocks.ko: 알천이 또 무언가를 여왕의 문 앞까지 들고 간다. 또 주먹에 쥐고. 또 아무도 함이 있다고 일러 주지 않았으니까. 백일곱 알짜리 염주 한 줄이다.

en: All of them?

lines: 오백 다요, 폐하. 셈 못 하는 중 하나까지.
en: All five hundred, Majesty. And one monk who couldn’t count.

blocks.html: Yushin is at the door. He has been at the door since he came down out of the hills, hair still damp, and somebody has made him eat. Bidam notices, and for once says nothing. Alchun will later call it the bravest thing he saw all night.
blocks.ko: 유신이 문 앞에 있다. 언덕에서 내려온 뒤로 줄곧, 머리도 덜 마른 채, 누가 억지로 뭘 먹이기까지 한 얼굴로 문 앞에 있었다. 비담은 그걸 보고도, 웬일로 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 알천은 나중에 그것이 그 밤 본 것 중 가장 용감한 일이었다고 말한다.

blocks.html: By spring the court has its own version. The queen heard frogs croaking in the palace pond in midwinter, and knew the valley, and the number. Ask the men who were there and they will tell you about a monk who was one bead short.
blocks.ko: 봄이 되자 조정엔 조정의 이야기가 생긴다. 여왕이 한겨울 궁 연못에서 개구리 우는 소리를 듣고 골짜기와 그 숫자를 알아맞혔다고. 거기 있던 사내들에게 물어보면, 염주알 하나가 모자랐던 중 이야기를 해 줄 것이다.

blocks.html: Every man who voted that night grew up in her great-grandfather’s yard. Who was the Cloud King? Ask anyone in Surabol…!
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 패를 놓은 사내들은 모두 그녀의 증조부가 만든 마당에서 컸다. 구름왕은 누구였나? 서라벌 아무에게나 물어보라…!

logline.en: Ask anyone in Surabol about the Cloud King and they’ll tell you about his stones. Ask anyone in Sabi and they’ll change the subject.
logline.ko: 서라벌 사람에게 구름왕을 물으면 그의 비석 이야기를 할 것이다. 사비 사람에게 물으면 말을 돌릴 것이다.

images.alt: Someday his great-granddaughter will put a stone in the middle of Surabol and point it at the sky. Nobody will be able to say she took that
images.prompt: CLOSING STILL of the episode: the final scene of this story as it ends (not the next episode). The line: “Someday his great-granddaughter will put a stone in the middle of Surabol and point it at the sky. Nobody will be able to say she took that from a friend.” Context: He never says. He dies that same year, still in the robe. If you want the friend’s name, ask in Sabi. They’ll change the subject. Surabol calls him the Cloud King after that, for the name he took at the end. A cloud has no border. For an afternoon, the ground under it is its ground. It never asks whose field it’s raining on. Someday his great-granddaughter will put a stone in the middle of Surabol and point it at the sky. Nobody will be able to say she took that from a friend. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.at: He was seven when they put the crown on him.
images.alt: It was too big, and nobody mentioned it.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. PARALLEL FRAME: the LAYOUT picture on the sheet is the master of a set of frames that recur across this story. Repaint ITS EXACT COMPOSITION: the same camera height, angle and lens, the same framing, the same number of figures in the same positions, sizes and poses, the same main shapes (gate, line, dais, table, waterline) in the same places, the same direction of the key light. Only the people, their faces and dress, the place and the hour change, so the two frames line up like a before-and-after. Ignore the layout picture's faces, clothes and colours. The same shot. Jinhung, seven years old, small on the huge throne, chin up, the crown far too big and sliding toward his eyebrows as the hands lower it. The spirit line behind him: King Beopheung nearest, then older Silla kings fading into the haze. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT LAYOUT picture (copy its composition, not its people), SECOND face = jinheung, THIRD face = beopheung (an ancestral spirit in the frame). Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_moon_palace (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), crown reference (shape only). KING JINHUNG — Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #2f6fd4. KING BUPHUNG — Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. PLACE Moon Palace (월궁) — attached board /pl_moon_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.

blocks.html: Ask anyone in Surabol about the Cloud King and they'll tell you about his stones. Ask anyone in Sabi and they'll change the subject. You'll find out why. Not yet.
blocks.ko: 서라벌 사람에게 구름왕을 물으면 그의 비석 이야기를 할 것이다. 사비 사람에게 물으면 말을 돌릴 것이다. 동인지는 알게 된다. 아직은 아니다.

blocks.caption: The Cloud King’s shade, and where it fell.
blocks.ko: 구름왕의 그늘, 그리고 그 그늘이 드리운 곳.

blocks.label: The Too-Big Crown
blocks.ko: 너무 큰 왕관

blocks.html: He was seven when they put the crown on him. It was too big, and nobody mentioned it. Picture the first morning. The whole court is face-down on the floor, and the crown is sliding toward his eyebrows.
blocks.ko: 왕관을 쓸 때 그는 일곱 살이었다. 왕관은 너무 컸고, 아무도 그 말을 하지 않았다. 첫날 아침을 떠올려 보라. 조정 전체가 바닥에 엎드려 있고, 왕관은 그의 눈썹 쪽으로 미끄러지는 중이다.

en: Mother. It’s slipping.
I can’t see.

blocks.speaker: The Queen Mother
lines: 고개 드세요, 전하. 다들 엎드려 있어서 아무도 못 봐요.
en: Chin up, Majesty. They’re all face-down. Nobody can see.
Then why wear it?

blocks.html: She doesn’t answer. She folds a strip of silk inside the band, and the crown stops sliding. He will remember the silk longer than any lesson she gave him.
blocks.ko: 어머니는 대답하지 않는다. 비단 한 자락을 접어 테 안쪽에 끼운다. 왕관이 더는 미끄러지지 않는다. 그는 어머니의 어떤 가르침보다 그 비단을 오래 기억할 것이다.

blocks.caption: The Cloud King. Wherever he rides, the border rides after him.
blocks.ko: 구름의 왕. 그가 말을 달리면 국경이 뒤따라 달린다.

blocks.html: By the end, Silla will have a river, a coastline and Gaya. He gets there by being the best ally in Samhan, right up until the afternoon he isn’t.
blocks.ko: 끝에 가면 신라는 강 하나, 해안 하나, 그리고 가야를 쥐게 된다. 그는 삼한에서 가장 믿을 만한 동맹이라서 거기까지 간다. 믿을 만하지 않게 되는 그 오후 전까지는.

blocks.label: The First Yard
blocks.ko: 첫 마당

blocks.html: The boy grows up. So do a great many noble sons with nothing to do. His first idea is girls. Two beauties lead the young men in song. Then one gets the other drunk and pushes her into a river. The court does not bring it up.
blocks.ko: 소년은 자란다. 할 일 없는 귀족 자제들도 잔뜩 자란다. 그의 첫 생각은 여자다. 두 미인이 젊은 사내들을 이끌고 노래한다. 그러다 하나가 다른 하나를 취하게 해서 강에 밀어 넣는다. 조정은 그 일을 입에 올리지 않는다.

blocks.html: So he tries boys. He fills a yard with the noblest sons in Surabol and watches from the porch.
blocks.ko: 그래서 이번엔 사내아이들이다. 서라벌에서 가장 귀한 집 아들들로 마당을 채우고, 그는 툇마루에서 지켜본다.

blocks.speaker: A minister
en: Powder, Majesty? On boys?

lines: 예쁘게 보이느라 바쁘면 서로 물에 빠뜨릴 틈이 없겠지.
en: If they’re busy being pretty, they won’t have time to drown each other.

blocks.speaker: A minister
en: …You said that about the girls, Majesty.

blocks.html: The king does not answer. In the yard a thirteen-year-old knocks a bigger boy flat and doesn’t offer him a hand.
blocks.ko: 왕은 대답하지 않는다. 마당에서 열세 살짜리 하나가 저보다 큰 아이를 메다꽂고는 손도 내밀지 않는다.

en: Get up. Or don’t.

blocks.speaker: A bigger boy
en: How old even are you?
Then keep up.
Who’s that one?

blocks.speaker: A minister
en: Sadaham, Majesty. Thirteen. He’s made three of them cry already.
Put him at the top of the list.

blocks.html: That is the Hwarang. Take the noblest boys and put them in one yard. Make them ride, sing and rank each other until the ranking feels like fate.
blocks.ko: 그것이 화랑이다. 가장 귀한 집 소년들을 한 마당에 모은다. 말 타고 노래하고 서로 순위를 매기게 한다. 순위가 운명처럼 느껴질 때까지.

blocks.hanja: 花郞
blocks.html: “Flower youths.” Noble sons in powder and silk, taught to ride, to sing, and to die, in about that order. The name is a joke. The enemy stopped laughing at it in the second generation.
blocks.ko: ‘꽃 같은 사내’. 분 바르고 비단 입은 귀족 자제들이 말 타기, 노래, 죽는 법을 대략 그 순서로 배운다. 이름은 농담이다. 적들은 두 번째 기수쯤에서 웃기를 그만뒀다.

blocks.html: Seventy years on, six old men around a brazier will put a woman on the throne. Every one of them learned to fall down in this yard.
blocks.ko: 칠십 년 뒤, 화로를 둘러싼 늙은이 여섯이 한 여인을 왕좌에 앉힐 것이다. 그들은 모두 이 마당에서 넘어지는 법을 배웠다.

blocks.label: The Northern Ridge
blocks.ko: 북쪽 고개

blocks.html: The boys grow up, and the border grows faster. By the time the crown fits, he is wearing it up mountains. On a bare ridge in the far north, a mason is cutting a stone taller than himself. He is also arguing.
blocks.ko: 소년들은 자라고, 국경은 그보다 빨리 자란다. 왕관이 머리에 맞을 무렵, 그는 그걸 쓰고 산을 오르고 있다. 먼 북쪽의 민둥 고개에서 석공 하나가 제 키보다 큰 돌을 쪼고 있다. 그리고 따지고 있다.

blocks.speaker: The mason
lines: 전하, 글자 하나에 쌀 한 되씩입니더.
공덕을 몇 줄 새기시믄 돌이 훨씬 번듯할 낍니더.
en: Majesty, it’s a measure of rice a character.
Put in a few virtues and it’ll look a good deal grander.

lines: 누가 왔는지, 언제 왔는지. 그리고 이 땅이 이제 안쪽이라는 것.
en: Who came, and when. And that this ground is inside now.
That’ll do.

blocks.speaker: The mason
lines: 그라믄 돌이 너무 밋밋합니더. 북쪽 놈들이 보고 웃을 낍니더.
en: Then it’s a plain stone, Majesty. The northerners will laugh.

lines: 뽐내는 건 뺏길까 걱정하는 놈들이나 하는 거야.
en: Boasting is for men who are worried about losing it.
…Also, I’m paying for the rice.

blocks.speaker: The mason
en: …Plain it is, Majesty.

blocks.html: He puts up four stones in all, on mountains, at the edges of what he takes. They are meant to be property deeds. The mason, it turns out, slipped in a few virtues anyway. Masons do.
blocks.ko: 그는 모두 넷을 세운다. 산 위에, 제가 취한 것의 가장자리에. 등기 문서가 될 참이었다. 알고 보니 석공은 공덕 몇 줄을 슬쩍 끼워 넣었다. 석공들은 원래 그런다.

blocks.html: On the twenty-first day of the eighth month, in the first year of Techang, the Great King Jinhung toured the lands in his keeping, and had this cut into stone. … And so the borders were carried out on every side, and people and land were won far and wide. Neighbouring countries swore good faith, and envoys of peace came and went.
blocks.ko: 태창 원년 무자년 8월 21일 계미일, 진흥태왕이 다스리는 땅을 순수하고 돌에 새겨 기록한다. …… 이로써 사방으로 경계를 넓혀 백성과 땅을 널리 얻었고, 이웃 나라는 신의를 맹세하였으며 화친의 사신이 오갔다.
blocks.hanja: 太昌元年歲次戊子八月卄一日癸未，眞興太王巡狩管境，刊石銘記也。……因斯四方託境，廣獲民土，隣國誓信，和使交通。
blocks.source: Jinheung Stele (眞興王巡狩碑), Maunnyeong stone (磨雲嶺碑), front face (568)

blocks.label: Dharma Cloud
blocks.ko: 법운

blocks.html: Near the end he shaves his head. The king of the four mountain stones puts on a monk’s robe and takes a new name: Dharma Cloud. His queen goes into a nunnery beside him. The court keeps calling him Majesty. He keeps answering to the other thing.
blocks.ko: 말년에 그는 머리를 깎는다. 네 산에 비석을 세운 왕이 승복을 입고 새 이름을 받는다. 법운, 법의 구름. 왕비도 그 곁 절로 들어간다. 조정은 계속 전하라 부른다. 그는 계속 다른 이름에 대답한다.

blocks.speaker: A courtier
lines: 오늘도 법운 스님 하니까 돌아보시고, 전하 하니까 못 들은 척하시더군.
en: Called him Brother Dharma Cloud today and he turned round. Called him Majesty and he didn’t hear.

blocks.speaker: Another courtier
en: He still stamps things, though.

blocks.speaker: A courtier
en: Oh, he stamps them. Chanting.

blocks.html: Some afternoons he wanders down to the Hwarang yard. Nobody has thought to stop him.
blocks.ko: 어떤 오후엔 그가 화랑의 마당으로 어슬렁어슬렁 내려간다. 말리려고 생각한 사람은 아무도 없다.

blocks.label: The Yard Fence
blocks.ko: 마당 울타리

blocks.html: A boy is losing in the yard when a bald monk leans on the fence and laughs at him. Everyone else is kneeling. The boy is too busy losing to notice.
blocks.ko: 한 소년이 연무장에서 지고 있을 때, 까까머리 중 하나가 울타리에 기대 그를 보고 웃는다. 다른 이들은 다 무릎을 꿇고 있다. 소년은 지느라 바빠서 그걸 못 본다.

en: You drop your shoulder before you swing. He knows what you’ll do before you do.
lines: 휘두르기 전에 어깨가 먼저 떨어지는구나. 니가 뭘 할지 저놈이 니보다 먼저 안다.

blocks.speaker: The Boy
en: Who asked you, monk?
Nobody. That’s the nice thing about this robe.
lines: 아무도. 이 옷의 좋은 점이 그거다.

blocks.html: Then the boy sees the kneeling yard, and the face under the shaved head, and goes down in the dust so fast he bruises a knee.
blocks.ko: 그제야 소년은 무릎 꿇은 마당을 보고, 깎은 머리 아래 얼굴을 본다. 얼마나 빨리 엎드렸는지 무릎이 멍든다.

blocks.speaker: The Boy
en: Majesty— why— the robe, Majesty, why?
lines: 전하— 어찌— 그 옷은, 전하, 어찌하여?

en: They put a crown on me at seven. It was too big. I grew into it.
Then I filled it. A river. A coast. A kingdom.
Everything I won, I won from a friend first.
…The robe is lighter. Get up. Fix your shoulder.
lines: 일곱 살에 왕관을 씌우더구나. 너무 컸지. 자라서 맞췄다.
그다음엔 채웠다. 강 하나. 바닷가 하나. 나라 하나.
얻은 건 전부, 먼저 벗한테서 얻은 것이다.
……이 옷이 더 가볍다. 일어나라. 어깨나 고쳐라.

blocks.speaker: The Boy
en: …Which friend, Majesty?
Shoulder. Again.

blocks.html: He never says. He dies that same year, still in the robe. If you want the friend’s name, ask in Sabi. They’ll change the subject.
blocks.ko: 그는 끝내 말하지 않는다. 그해, 승복을 입은 채 죽는다. 그 벗의 이름이 궁금하면 사비에 가서 물어보라. 말을 돌릴 것이다.

blocks.html: Surabol calls him the Cloud King after that, for the name he took at the end. A cloud has no border. For an afternoon, the ground under it is its ground. It never asks whose field it’s raining on.
blocks.ko: 그 뒤로 서라벌은 그를 구름왕이라 부른다. 마지막에 받은 이름을 따서. 구름에는 경계가 없다. 한나절 동안은 그 아래 땅이 다 제 땅이다. 구름은 누구 밭에 비를 뿌리는지 묻지 않는다.

blocks.html: Someday his great-granddaughter will put a stone in the middle of Surabol and point it at the sky. Nobody will be able to say she took that from a friend.
blocks.ko: 언젠가 그의 증손녀가 서라벌 한복판에 돌을 세우고 하늘을 향하게 할 것이다. 그건 벗한테서 뺏었다고 아무도 말하지 못할 것이다.

blocks.html: The rain fell on Baekje’s field, and Baekje kept the grudge. Two generations on, it names the prince who will inherit it…!
blocks.ko: 그 비는 백제의 밭에 내렸고, 백제는 원한을 간직했다. 두 대가 지나, 백제는 그 원한을 물려받을 왕자를 세운다…!

logline.en: Thirty-two is late to be named crown prince. By then the clans have had years to decide which of his sons they own.
logline.ko: 서른둘은 태자가 되기엔 늦은 나이다. 그 사이 가문들은 그의 아들 중 누구를 가질지 정할 시간이 넉넉했다.
