images.prompt: OPENING STILL of the episode: the first image the reader sees, staging its first line. The line: “Everyone in Baekje agrees that King Mu is a good king. Even the eight great houses say so. They are already discussing the next one.” Context: Everyone in Baekje agrees that King Mu is a good king. Even the eight great houses say so. They are already discussing the next one.   A wide or medium establishing frame that hooks. CANON — PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Everyone in Baekje agrees that King Mu is a good king. Even the eight great houses say so. They are already discussing the next one.
blocks.ko: 백제에서 무왕이 좋은 임금이라는 데 토를 다는 사람은 없다. 여덟 대가문조차 그렇게 말한다. 그리고 벌써 다음 임금 얘기를 하고 있다.

blocks.label: The Prince
blocks.ko: 왕자

blocks.label: The Sluice
blocks.ko: 봇둑

blocks.html: Dawn, below the walls of Sabi. Two villages share one timber sluice. This spring they have been sharing it with sticks. The king came down to look before breakfast. He is seventy-one, his sleeves are tied back, and he is up to his shins in the ditch.
blocks.ko: 새벽, 사비 성벽 아래. 두 마을이 나무 봇문 하나를 같이 쓴다. 올봄엔 몽둥이까지 같이 쓰고 있다. 임금은 아침도 들기 전에 보러 내려왔다. 일흔하나, 소매를 뒤로 동여매고, 정강이까지 도랑에 잠겨 있다.

blocks.caption: They call him the Martial King. The villages remember the ditches.
blocks.ko: 사람들은 그를 굳셀 무 자, 무왕이라 부른다. 마을들은 도랑을 기억한다.

blocks.html: 👑 King Mu (71)

en: Majesty, with respect. The upper paddies belong to the house, and the house’s fields drink first. It has always been so.
lines: 전하, 황공하오나 윗논은 댁의 논이옵니다. 댁의 논이 먼저 물을 먹는 것이 예부터의 법도이옵니다.
blocks.speaker: A Satek Steward

en: Always since last spring, he means. Before that we drank first.
Then his lads brought sticks, and I reckon his memory changed.
lines: 예부터라는 게 작년 봄부터유. 그 전엔 우리가 먼저 먹었슈.
그러다 저 댁 젊은 것들이 몽둥이를 들고 오더니, 기억이 바뀌었나 봐유.
blocks.speaker: A Farmer

en: Ha! Sticks before breakfast. Lovely.
Here’s the law, then. The house gets the water by day. The village gets it by night.
lines: 하! 아침 먹기 전부터 몽둥이라. 좋구나.
그럼 법을 정해 주마. 낮엔 댁이 물을 대고, 밤엔 마을이 댄다.

en: By night, Majesty? Who works a sluice in the dark?
lines: 밤에 말씀이옵니까, 전하? 캄캄한 데서 누가 봇문을 연단 말씀이옵니까?
blocks.speaker: A Satek Steward

en: Farmers. That’s why they get the night.

blocks.html: The farmers laugh before the steward has worked it out. By the time he has, the gate is open and the king is holding out a hand for something to eat.
blocks.ko: 집사가 알아듣기도 전에 농사꾼들이 먼저 웃는다. 그가 알아들었을 땐 봇문은 이미 열려 있고, 임금은 먹을 것을 달라고 손을 내밀고 있다.

en: It’s only barley, Majesty. In a leaf, mind, so it’s proper.
lines: 보리밥뿐이유, 전하. 그래두 잎사귀에 쌌으니께 갖출 건 갖췄슈.
blocks.speaker: A Farmer

en: Barley’s a feast. I was raised on yams. Don’t tell the palace.
lines: 보리면 잔치지. 난 마 캐 먹고 컸다. 궁에는 말하지 마라.

blocks.html: He eats it standing in the ditch. Two village children watch him chew, in case he does something royal with it.
blocks.ko: 그는 도랑에 선 채로 먹는다. 마을 아이 둘이, 혹시 임금다운 무슨 짓이라도 할까 싶어 씹는 입을 지켜본다.

en: Your boy’ll come down and do this, Majesty? When it’s his turn?
lines: 전하 아드님도 이렇게 내려와 주실까유? 그분 차례가 되믄?
blocks.speaker: A Farmer

blocks.html: The king looks up the hill, past the walls, to where the palace garden is. Something up there catches the sun. An arrowhead, probably.
blocks.ko: 임금은 언덕 위, 성벽 너머 궁의 후원 쪽을 올려다본다. 거기서 뭔가 햇빛에 번쩍인다. 아마 화살촉일 것이다.

en: …He’s a very good shot.
Majesty! Majesty— the houses are in the yard. All eight, with their boys. Early.
lines: 전하! 전하— 가문들이 마당에 와 있사옵니다. 여덟 집 다, 아이들까지 데리고요. 일찍들 왔사옵니다.

en: They’re always early. That’s how they get the good seats.
lines: 늘 일찍 오지. 그래야 좋은 자리를 차지하거든.

blocks.html: He climbs out slowly. Halfway up the bank he stops and looks back at the sluice. He has kept it working for thirty years. Somebody else will have to oil it.
blocks.ko: 그는 천천히 도랑을 빠져나온다. 둑 중간쯤에서 멈춰 봇문을 돌아본다. 삼십 년을 그가 손봐 온 문이다. 언젠가는 다른 누가 기름을 쳐야 한다.

blocks.html: He goes up the hill to see who.
blocks.ko: 그는 그게 누구일지 보러 언덕을 오른다.

blocks.html: In five days, Prince Euija becomes Crown Prince Euija. He is thirty-two, which is late for it. He has fifteen sons, which is early for everything else.
blocks.ko: 닷새 뒤, 의자왕자는 의자태자가 된다. 서른둘이니 늦은 편이다. 아들은 열다섯이니, 다른 건 다 이른 편이다.

blocks.caption: Righteous and merciful. His father chose it. The son will spend his life deciding which half to keep.
blocks.ko: 옳음과 자비. 아버지가 지어 준 이름이다. 아들은 평생 그중 어느 쪽을 남길지 고른다.

en: Fifteen, they say. Sixteen by spring.
His Majesty had fifty at that age. They say Samsin keeps a night shift just for Sabi — don’t you repeat that, now.
lines: 전하께선 그 나이에 쉰이셨다네. 삼신할미가 사비 때문에 밤일을 따로 헌다지 — 이건 못 들은 걸루 허게.

blocks.html: This is said admiringly. It is that kind of court.
blocks.ko: 감탄하며 하는 말이다. 그런 조정이다.

blocks.html: The king lives here. So do eight families who think that’s a detail.
blocks.ko: 임금이 사는 곳. 그걸 사소한 일로 여기는 여덟 가문도 산다.

blocks.label: The Rear Garden
blocks.ko: 후원

blocks.html: At mid-morning the prince is in the rear garden with a bow, a go board, a jar of wine and two court ladies, and he is winning at all four.
blocks.ko: 한낮이 되기 전, 왕자는 후원에서 활과 바둑판과 술 단지와 궁녀 둘을 끼고 있다. 넷 다 이기는 중이다.

blocks.html: The arrow goes in without his looking. He is already reaching for a stone.
blocks.ko: 화살은 보지도 않고 꽂힌다. 그의 손은 벌써 바둑돌로 가 있다.

blocks.html: Prince Euija (32)
blocks.ko: 의자태자 (32)

en: Your move.
And if you shift my stone while I drink, my lady, do it better than last time. If I’m to be cheated, I want a professional. Ha!
Pour.
lines: 내가 마시는 동안 돌 옮길 거믄 지난번보단 잘혀. 속아두 장인한테 속고 싶구먼. 하하!

en: Your Highness moved it yourself—
—twice—
—and blamed the wind.

blocks.html: The ladies stop giggling all at once, the way sparrows stop when a hawk goes over.
blocks.ko: 궁녀들의 웃음이 한꺼번에 뚝 그친다. 매가 지나갈 때 참새들이 그러듯이.

blocks.html: There is ditch mud to his knees. Nobody in the garden mentions it.
blocks.ko: 무릎까지 도랑 흙이 묻어 있다. 후원의 누구도 그 얘기를 꺼내지 않는다.

en: Up, boy.
The houses are parading their wrestlers in my yard, and the man they’re wrestling for is in a hedge with a jar.
Over the mountains, Silla crowned a woman this spring. Even she gets up before noon, I hear.
lines: 가문마다 씨름꾼을 내 마당에 끌고 와 자랑하는데, 그 씨름의 주인은 술 단지 끼구 덤불 속에 있구먼.
산 너머 신라는 올봄 여자를 왕으로 세웠다. 그 여자두 한낮 전엔 일어난댜.

en: Let Silla crown a heifer, Father. It still owes us a river. Ha!
Meanwhile I’m practising. A crown prince ought to hit what he aims at.
lines: 신라가 암소를 왕으로 세운들 어떻습니까, 아바마마. 그래두 우리한테 강 하나 빚진 건 그대루지요. 하하!
그동안 저는 연습 중입니다. 태자라면 겨눈 데는 맞혀야지요.

en: Then aim at the hall.
Analects by heart at seven. My ministers beaten at go at twelve.
And twenty years since, making very sure nobody asks you to do either again.
lines: 일곱에 논어를 외웠지. 열둘에 내 대신들을 바둑으로 이겼고.
그러구 이십 년을, 아무두 다시는 안 시키게 애쓰며 보냈지.

en: Cleverness is an ox, Father.
Let the village see it, and by morning somebody’s hitched it to his plough.
lines: 마을에 보이믄, 아침엔 누가 벌써 제 쟁기에 매어 놓지요.

en: Today it gets hitched.
Bring the jar. You’ll want it.

blocks.label: The Yard
blocks.ko: 마당

blocks.html: Five days before a crown prince is made, each of the eight houses brings a boy to the palace yard to be looked at, the way you bring a horse to market. On the day itself they wrestle. The crown prince puts up a boy too.
blocks.ko: 태자를 세우기 닷새 전, 여덟 가문은 저마다 아이 하나를 궁 마당에 데려와 선보인다. 장에 말을 끌고 가듯이. 당일에는 그 아이들이 씨름을 한다. 태자도 아이 하나를 내세운다.

blocks.html: Eight boys in white stand on the sand. The ninth place is empty, and everyone is looking at it.
blocks.ko: 흰옷 입은 아이 여덟이 모래판에 서 있다. 아홉째 자리는 비어 있고, 모두가 그 자리를 보고 있다.

en: Your man for the sand.
Pick a son. Yung’s big enough to fall on somebody.
lines: 아들 하나 골라. 융이는 누구 위에 넘어질 만큼은 크잖여.

blocks.html: His sons grow up already spoken for. Yung wears a Satek ring. Tae has a Jinmo grandmother. Little Pung has lovely handwriting and a Mokli tutor.
blocks.ko: 그의 아들들은 이미 임자가 정해진 채 자란다. 융은 사택가 반지를 낀다. 태의 할머니는 진모가다. 어린 풍은 글씨가 곱고, 스승이 목리가 사람이다.

en: Put one of mine on the sand and I’m only telling the yard which house I’ve lost him to.
lines: 제 아들을 모래판에 세우면, 어느 가문에 빼앗겼는지 마당에 알리는 것뿐입니다.

en: Then find someone who isn’t anybody’s.
Five days. After that I pick for you, and you’ll hate who I pick.
lines: 그럼 누구 것도 아닌 놈을 찾아라.
닷새여. 그 뒤엔 내가 고른다. 내가 고른 놈은 니가 싫어헐 겨.

blocks.html: Two old men reach the prince before the king has finished speaking.
blocks.ko: 임금의 말이 끝나기도 전에 노인 둘이 왕자에게 닿는다.

lines: 연비 공… 만나 뵙게 되어 영광이—
en: Lord Yunbi… an honour to—
Lord Satek… a new—
Highness. The tide is with you this week.
Up and down the river they say it. Filial to his father, kind to his brothers. The Zengzi of the East of the Sea.
lines: 저하. 이번 주 물때가 저하 편이오.
강 위아래로 다들 그러지요. 아버지께 효성스럽고 형제에게 우애롭다고. 해동증자라고.

en: We said it first. On the coast road, into a headwind.
Satek heard it from us. He usually does. Through a floorboard.
lines: 우리가 먼저 했소. 바닷길에서, 맞바람 맞아 가며.
사택은 우리한테서 들었소. 늘 그렇듯. 마룻바닥 너머로.

en: Floorboards are cheap in Yunbi.
Everything is.

blocks.hanja: 事親以孝 與兄弟以友 時號海東曾子
blocks.ko: 어버이를 섬김에 효로써 하고, 형제와 더불어 우애하니, 그때 해동증자라 일컬었다.
blocks.html: He served his parents with filial piety and treated his brothers with fraternal love; in his time he was called the Zengzi of the East of the Sea.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 28, Baekje Annals — King Uija, accession notice; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 380 · cf. Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199上, Baekje

blocks.html: The Zengzi of the East of the Sea was cheating at go an hour ago. He smiles at both of them like a man being sold his own horse.
blocks.ko: 해동증자는 한 시진 전까지 바둑에서 속임수를 쓰고 있었다. 그는 제 말을 되사라는 소리를 듣는 사람처럼 두 노인에게 웃어 준다.

blocks.html: When they have bowed themselves away, he says what he thinks. His father has been trying to cure him of that for thirty-two years.
blocks.ko: 노인들이 절을 하며 물러가자, 그는 속에 있는 말을 한다. 아버지가 서른두 해째 고치려고 애쓰는 버릇이다.

lines: 아버지... 이런 가문 싸움에 전 관심이 없습니다.
en: Father… I have no interest in these clan quarrels.
A king should be for the country—

lines: 얘야… 그래도 저들 이름은 외워 두어라.
…나도 좋아서 외운 게 아니다. 그래도 내가 먼저 부른다.
en: My child… learn their names anyway.
…I did not like mine either. I still say them first.
You reckon I like them? I’ve buried three Satek elders, and I’d dance at a fourth.
But a king rules the country he has, boy. Not the one he wants.
Fifteen sons—
lines: 내가 그놈들을 좋아허는 줄 아냐? 사택 노인을 셋이나 묻었어. 넷째 땐 춤이라두 출 겨.
허나 임금은 가진 나라를 다스리는 거다, 이놈아. 바라는 나라가 아니라.

en: Sixteen by spring.
The lady of the Hae house says it’s twins.
…Gods help the Hae.
Every son is a door, boy, and some house will try to walk through each one.
Be a father to the boys. Be a king to the doors.
lines: 아들 하나하나가 문이다, 이놈아. 어느 가문이든 그 문으로 걸어 들어오려 헐 겨.
아이들한텐 아비가 되고, 문들한텐 임금이 되거라.

blocks.label: The Boy in the River
blocks.ko: 강물 속 소년

blocks.label: The White River
blocks.ko: 백마강

blocks.html: That night Euija sneaks out of the palace in a grey hood and a grey robe. He tells himself it is to see how the common people live. Mostly it is to get away from a list with an empty ninth line.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 의자는 회색 두건에 회색 도포를 걸치고 궁을 빠져나간다. 백성이 어찌 사는지 보러 간다고 스스로에게 말한다. 실은 아홉째 줄이 빈 명단에서 도망치는 것이다.

blocks.html: Wide, slow, and fought over one berth at a time.
blocks.ko: 넓고 느리고, 선착장 한 칸씩 싸움이 붙는 강.

blocks.html: On the landing a Jinmo boy is shouting at four porters and a great gilt-bronze incense burner. The burner is wrapped in silk for the crown prince’s day. It is as tall as a child, with mountains on the lid, musicians on the mountains, and a phoenix on top who looks as if he would rather be elsewhere.
blocks.ko: 나루에서 진모가 아이 하나가 짐꾼 넷과 커다란 금동 향로에게 소리를 지르고 있다. 향로는 태자 책봉 날을 위해 비단에 싸여 있다. 아이 키만 하다. 뚜껑엔 산이, 산엔 악사들이, 꼭대기엔 어디 딴 데 가고 싶은 얼굴의 봉황이 있다.

blocks.html: A barefoot boy with a basket of eels comes round the stack at a run. The Jinmo boy steps back into him. The burner goes over the rail. It does not float.
blocks.ko: 장어 바구니를 든 맨발의 아이가 짐 더미를 돌아 뛰어온다. 진모가 아이가 뒷걸음질 치다 부딪힌다. 향로가 난간 너머로 넘어간다. 뜨지 않는다.

en: Do you know what that WAS?
My grandfather had it cast! It’s for the crown prince! It’s for the YARD—
lines: 우리 할아버지가 부어 만든 겨! 태자 거라구! 마당에 놓을 거라구—

en: Do you know who my father is, you little peasant twat?
lines: 우리 아버지가 누군지 알아, 이 천한 놈아?

en: No.
Jinmo. JINMO.
My father sits on the rock. I can have you thrown in after it, and nobody will even write it down.
lines: 우리 아버지는 바위에 앉는 분이여. 너 같은 건 저거 따라 던져 넣어도 아무도 안 적어.

blocks.html: Nobody on the landing moves. The porters find their feet very interesting.
blocks.ko: 나루의 누구도 움직이지 않는다. 짐꾼들은 제 발등이 무척 흥미로운 모양이다.

en: I will get it back.
…You?
Fine. Five days. If it isn’t on my doorstep in five days, I’ll have you killed in front of the whole street.
lines: 좋아. 닷새. 닷새 안에 우리 집 문 앞에 없으믄, 온 동네 앞에서 죽여 버릴 겨.

en: Five days.

blocks.label: The Diving Boy
blocks.ko: 물에 드는 아이

blocks.html: There is an old willow on the bank with a rock wedged in its roots. Gyebek ties one end of a rope round the rock and the other round his ankle, so the river can’t keep him. Then he goes in.
blocks.ko: 강둑에 늙은 버드나무가 있고, 그 뿌리에 바위 하나가 박혀 있다. 계백은 밧줄 한쪽을 바위에, 다른 쪽을 제 발목에 묶는다. 강이 그를 데려가지 못하게. 그리고 들어간다.

blocks.html: The boy is going back into the water. He has been at it since morning, and he is not a strong swimmer.
blocks.ko: 아이가 또 물에 들어간다. 아침부터 저러고 있다. 헤엄을 잘 치는 아이도 아니다.

en: That’s the eel boy. Been going in since dawn.
For the Jinmo pot? That’s down with the catfish by now, I reckon.
Hey, look at that idiot! Jumping into the freezing river, haha!
Give it a day. The river’s got all the time in the world.
lines: 저거 장어 파는 애잖여. 새벽부터 들어가더라구.
진모네 향로 건질라구? 그거 벌써 메기들이랑 뻘 속에 있을 겨.
야, 저 바보 좀 봐! 그 차가운 강에 뛰어드네, 하하!
하루만 기다려 봐. 강은 급할 게 읎어.

blocks.html: On the second day a man in a grey hood stops at the back of the crowd. He stays longer than he means to.
blocks.ko: 이튿날, 회색 두건의 사내 하나가 구경꾼들 뒤에 멈춰 선다. 생각보다 오래 머문다.

en: What’s he after down there?
The Jinmo pot, sir. Five days, or they kill him.
lines: 진모네 향로유. 닷새 안에 못 건지믄 죽인대요.

en: Then why hasn’t he run?
Ask him yourself. He doesn’t talk.
lines: 직접 물어보슈. 저 애는 말을 안 해유.

blocks.html: In the palace, the crown prince has been missing for two days. King Mu has the city turned over, and says several things about his son that the herald is asked not to write down.
blocks.ko: 궁에서는 태자가 이틀째 보이지 않는다. 무왕은 성안을 뒤집어엎게 하고, 아들에 대해 전령이 받아 적지 말라는 말을 여럿 한다.

en: Start with the wine houses.
Then the other houses.
The other— ah.
Yes, Majesty.

blocks.html: Gyebek does not eat. Nobody sees him sleep. Each time he comes up, the rock in the willow roots has shifted a finger’s width, and he reties the knot and goes back down.
blocks.ko: 계백은 먹지 않는다. 자는 걸 본 사람도 없다. 올라올 때마다 버드나무 뿌리의 바위가 손가락 한 마디씩 밀려나 있고, 그는 매듭을 다시 묶고 또 내려간다.

blocks.label: Night on the Bank
blocks.ko: 강가의 밤

blocks.html: On the third night the crowd has gone home. Euija comes down the bank with rice balls in a leaf and a jar he has not opened, which for him is a sacrifice.
blocks.ko: 사흘째 밤, 구경꾼들은 집에 갔다. 의자가 잎에 싼 주먹밥과 뜯지 않은 술 단지를 들고 둑을 내려온다. 그에겐 그게 희생이다.

en: How many times have you gone in?
Nineteen.
…You were counting?
At twenty I would not come back out. That is why I count.
Eat.
Then tell me. Why do you do all of this?
lines: 그리고 말해 봐. 왜 이런 짓을 하는 게냐?

en: I gave my word.
To a Jinmo brat who’ll have you killed either way? Ha!
Run. Tonight. There’s nothing for you in Sabi. There’s nothing for you in all of Baekje.
Nobody here will even notice you’ve gone.
lines: 어차피 너 죽일 진모가 꼬맹이한테? 하!
도망쳐. 오늘 밤. 사비엔 널 위한 게 없어. 백제 워디에도 없어.
니가 사라져두 여기선 아무도 모를 겨.

en: I gave my word.

blocks.html: He says it in exactly the same words, the way you set a stone back where it was.
blocks.ko: 똑같은 말이다. 돌을 제자리에 도로 놓듯이.

en: A fine young man… what is your name?
I have… no name.

lines: ...어? 백제 땅에서 이름이 없는 게 말이 된다고 생각해?
en: …What? You think it makes sense to have no name, here in Baekje?

blocks.html: Gyebek does not answer. He goes back in. Far down, in the black, something catches the moon: a curve of gold.
blocks.ko: 계백은 대답하지 않는다. 도로 들어간다. 저 아래, 캄캄한 데서 무언가가 달빛을 받는다. 금빛 곡선 하나.

blocks.html: Then the rock comes out of the willow roots. The willow, which has been leaning on that rock for a hundred years, comes after it. The rope goes taut, and the river takes the boy, the rock and the tree down together.
blocks.ko: 그때 바위가 버드나무 뿌리에서 빠져나온다. 백 년을 그 바위에 기대 온 버드나무가 뒤따라 넘어간다. 밧줄이 팽팽해지고, 강은 아이와 바위와 나무를 한꺼번에 끌어내린다.

en: Hey— HEY—!

blocks.html: The crown prince of Baekje goes in after him in a grey robe, with a knife in his teeth. He finds the rope by feel and cuts it.
blocks.ko: 백제의 태자가 회색 도포 차림으로 칼을 입에 물고 뒤따라 뛰어든다. 손끝으로 밧줄을 더듬어 찾아 끊는다.

blocks.html: They come up onto the mud together and lie there like two fish.
blocks.ko: 둘은 함께 뻘 위로 올라와, 물고기 두 마리처럼 누워 있다.

en: …Thank you.

blocks.html: Then he gets up, picks up the cut end of the rope, and starts looking for another rock.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 일어나, 끊긴 밧줄 끝을 집어 들고, 다른 바위를 찾기 시작한다.

lines: 아, 이 미친 새끼야!! 그렇게 빨리 염라대왕 앞에 끌려가고 싶은거냐?!
en: Are you insane?! In that much of a hurry to stand before Yumla?!

blocks.html: Euija hits him once, properly, in a way princes are not taught. Gyebek goes down on the mud and stays there.
blocks.ko: 의자가 한 대 친다. 제대로, 왕자들이 배우지 않는 방식으로. 계백은 뻘에 쓰러져 그대로 있다.

blocks.html: He lies with his eyes open, and the tears just come, without a sound, the way the river does.
blocks.ko: 그는 눈을 뜬 채 누워 있고, 눈물이 그냥 흐른다. 소리도 없이. 강물처럼.

blocks.html: It takes a while to get it out of him.
blocks.ko: 사연을 듣기까지는 시간이 좀 걸린다.

blocks.html: The houses go first. Silk burns faster than timber. He is still wearing the clothes they dressed him in for the morning meal.
blocks.ko: 집이 먼저 간다. 비단은 나무보다 빨리 탄다. 그는 아직 아침밥 때 입혀 준 옷을 입고 있다.

blocks.html: Men come over the wall with torches and a list. Every name on the list is his family’s.
blocks.ko: 횃불과 명단을 든 사내들이 담을 넘어온다. 명단의 이름은 모두 그의 집안 사람들이다.

en: Run away… forget me, forget all of this!
Your name too. Forget it. The name is what they are hunting.
lines: 도망쳐라… 나를 잊어라, 이 모든 걸 잊어!
이름도. 잊어버려. 저놈들이 쫓는 건 이름이다.

blocks.html: They tell him to run and not say the name. He says it once, into his sleeve, and then he does not.
blocks.ko: 뛰되 이름은 말하지 말라고 한다. 그는 소매 안에다 한 번 말하고, 그다음엔 말하지 않는다.

blocks.html: They hunt him for a season. He learns which ditches drain and which porters don’t ask questions.
blocks.ko: 그들은 한 철 내내 그를 쫓는다. 그는 어느 도랑이 물이 빠지는지, 어느 짐꾼이 묻지 않는지 배운다.

blocks.html: After that he begs. The noble collar is dirty enough that nobody bows.
blocks.ko: 그다음엔 구걸한다. 귀족의 깃이 더러우면, 아무도 절하지 않는다.

en: No name. No house.
I have my word.
If I break it, I have nothing.

blocks.html: Euija says nothing for a long time. All week he has been called the Zengzi of the East of the Sea by men who would sell him by the pound, and he had decided there were no honourable men left in Baekje. It is very annoying to be proved wrong about that on a mudbank, at night, by an eel boy.
blocks.ko: 의자는 한참 말이 없다. 한 주 내내 그를 근으로 달아 팔 사람들한테 해동증자 소리를 들었다. 그래서 백제엔 이제 의로운 사람이 없다고 정해 두었다. 그걸 한밤중 뻘밭에서, 장어 파는 아이한테 틀렸다고 증명당하니 몹시 짜증 나는 일이다.

en: All right. Your word. That one belongs to the Jinmo brat.
What’s yours? What do you want?
lines: 그려. 약조. 그건 진모가 꼬맹이 거구.
니 건 뭐여? 너는 뭘 원허냐?

en: Nothing.
Ha! Nobody wants nothing. My father wants a boy on the sand. The Jinmo want their pot. I want this jar, and I’m not opening it, which is fixing to kill me.
Do you want to die?
lines: 하! 아무것도 안 바라는 놈은 없어. 아버지는 모래판에 세울 아이를 원허고, 진모가는 향로를 원허고, 나는 이 술 단지를 원허는데 안 따고 있다. 죽을 맛이여.

en: No.
Run, then?
No.
Back to the eels?
…No.
No, no, no. That’s your whole life, isn’t it. Nobody ever asked you the other question.
I’m asking. Say it.
lines: 아니다, 아니다, 아니다. 평생 그 소리만 혔구먼. 다른 걸 물어본 놈이 아무두 없었지.

blocks.html: The boy opens his mouth, and nothing comes. A man he loved told him to forget everything, and he did as he was told. He put the words away somewhere safe when he was small. He has not looked since.
blocks.ko: 아이가 입을 연다. 아무 소리도 안 나온다. 사랑하던 사람이 다 잊으라 했고, 그는 시킨 대로 했다. 어릴 때 그 말들을 안전한 데 넣어 두었다. 그 뒤로 한 번도 꺼내 보지 않았다.

en: …I want to live.

blocks.html: It comes out as a whisper. The second time, it doesn’t.
blocks.ko: 속삭임으로 나온다. 두 번째는 아니다.

en: I want to live…!
Not in a ditch. Not without a name.
I want to be someone they have to write down…!
lines: 저도… 누가 적어 둬야 하는 사람이 되고 싶어요…!

blocks.html: Euija stands. He is soaked to the waist, the hood is gone, and for once in his life he does not laugh first.
blocks.ko: 의자가 일어선다. 허리까지 젖었고, 두건은 어디 갔는지 없다. 평생 처음으로, 그는 먼저 웃지 않는다.

en: Good. Then live.
And here’s mine. Whatever you could be, all of it, to the last inch — I’ll get you there.
I’ll stand you where no house in Baekje can pretend not to see you. They’ll write you down whether they like it or not.
You have your word. Now you have mine.
lines: 그리고 이건 내 거다. 네가 될 수 있는 것, 그 끝의 끝까지 — 내가 데려다 놓으마.
백제 어느 가문도 못 본 척 못 할 자리에 세워 주마. 싫든 좋든 너를 적게 될 게다.
너한텐 네 약조가 있지. 이제 내 약조도 있다.

en: You are a man in a grey hood.
Ha! Tonight I am.
Now leave the pot to the catfish.
No.
…Of course not.

blocks.html: Before dawn Gyebek goes in one more time, with no rope at all. He reaches the gold. He gets both arms round it. Halfway up, with the surface a body’s length away, his eyes close.
blocks.ko: 동트기 전, 계백은 밧줄도 없이 한 번 더 들어간다. 금빛에 닿는다. 두 팔로 끌어안는다. 반쯤 올라왔을 때, 수면이 한 길 남짓 남은 곳에서, 그의 눈이 감긴다.

blocks.html: Under the water, there is a flash of light.
blocks.ko: 물속에서, 빛이 번쩍한다.

blocks.label: The Crown
blocks.ko: 왕관

blocks.label: The Deer
blocks.ko: 신록

blocks.html: On the bank the crown prince-to-be is wearing a crown he has no business wearing. He took it out of his father’s chest that afternoon, the way he has been taking things out of his father’s chest since he was six.
blocks.ko: 둑 위에서, 태자 될 사람이 써서는 안 될 관을 쓰고 있다. 그날 오후 아버지의 함에서 꺼내 온 것이다. 여섯 살 때부터 아버지 함에서 이것저것 꺼내 오던 그 솜씨로.

blocks.html: Out of the river, as if the water were a door, walks a pale stag with tall antlers. Across its back lies a boy with no name, both arms still locked round a gilt-bronze incense burner.
blocks.ko: 강에서, 물이 문이라도 되는 듯, 뿔이 높은 하얀 사슴이 걸어 나온다. 그 등에 이름 없는 아이가 엎어져 있다. 두 팔은 아직도 금동 향로를 꽉 끌어안은 채다.

blocks.html: Nobody else sees it. Nobody else is up.
blocks.ko: 본 사람은 아무도 없다. 깨어 있는 사람이 없었으니까.

blocks.label: The Fifth Morning
blocks.ko: 닷새째 아침

blocks.html: On the fifth morning Gyebek knocks at the Jinmo gate with the incense burner on his back, wrapped in his own shirt.
blocks.ko: 닷새째 아침, 계백은 제 저고리로 싼 향로를 등에 지고 진모 집 대문을 두드린다.

en: That’s— how did you—
Nobody could— it’s twenty feet of river down there—
lines: 아무도 못— 거기 물 깊이가 스무 자여—

en: I said I would get it back.
…There’s mud in the mountains.
Yes.

blocks.label: The Sand
blocks.ko: 모래판

blocks.html: The investiture takes less time than the wine did. A seal, a robe, and the whole hall bowing at once, like barley under wind.
blocks.ko: 책봉은 술보다 짧게 끝난다. 인장 하나, 옷 한 벌, 그리고 온 전각이 한꺼번에 숙이는 절. 바람 맞은 보리밭처럼.

lines: 됐다. 이제 저것들이 너한테 먼저 절하고, 흉은 그다음에 볼 게다.
en: Crown Prince.
There. Now they have to bow to you first and complain about you second.

lines: 서른두 해 동안 흉부터 봤지요, 아바마마.
en: They complained first for thirty-two years, Father.
I’ll take the bow.

blocks.html: Then the yard. The houses’ boys stand at the edge of the sand in white. The herald reads the board.
blocks.ko: 그다음은 마당이다. 가문들의 아이들이 흰옷을 입고 모래판 가장자리에 선다. 전령이 판을 읽는다.

en: For the house of Satek…!
For the house of Yunbi…!
For the house of Jinmo…!
And for His Highness the Crown Prince—

blocks.html: When he woke on the bank, the man in the grey hood was still wearing the crown.
blocks.ko: 강가에서 눈을 떴을 때, 회색 두건의 사내는 아직 왕관을 쓰고 있었다.

en: First, a surname.
How about… Buyeo?
Buyeo…
Is that not the royal surname? How can you…

blocks.html: Behind him, in the reeds, the deer is standing.
blocks.ko: 그의 뒤, 갈대숲에 그 사슴이 서 있다.

en: I’ll say it again.
Do you accept my royal edict…?

blocks.html: Gyebek does not answer. He has never been given anything he did not have to pay back.
blocks.ko: 계백은 대답하지 못한다. 갚지 않아도 되는 걸 받아 본 적이 없다.

lines: 계백… 지극히 고귀한 사내에게만 어울리는 이름이지.
en: Now you’ll need a name as well.
Gye, for Utmost. Bek, for Nobility.
How about — “Gyebek”?
Gyebek… a name only for men of the utmost nobility.
Gyebek, would you like to serve a higher purpose?
lines: 계백, 더 큰 뜻을 섬겨 보겠느냐?
…그 이름이 마음에 드십니까, 제가 마음에 드십니까?
en: …Do you like the name, or do you like me?
…People don’t usually ask that.
I have to ask, or I do not know.
Yes.
— Buyeo Gyebek!

blocks.caption: A boy with no name until a prince lent him one. He means to pay it back.
blocks.ko: 왕자가 이름을 빌려주기 전까지 이름이 없던 아이. 그는 그 빚을 갚을 작정이다.

blocks.name: Gyebek
blocks.ko: 계백
blocks.note: A rung and an elder. A man with no clan, named for a ladder.
blocks.noteKo: 섬돌 하나, 맏이 하나. 가문 없는 사내가 사다리의 이름을 달았다.

blocks.html: The yard says the surname back to itself, louder each time. A royal name on an eel boy. At the edge of the sand the Jinmo boy goes the colour of his burner.
blocks.ko: 마당이 그 성을 되뇐다. 한 번 할 때마다 더 크게. 장어 소년에게 왕실의 성이라니. 모래판 가장자리에서 진모 도령의 얼굴이 제 향로 빛이 된다.

en: Run away… forget me, forget all of this!
lines: 도망쳐라… 나를 잊어라, 이 모든 걸 잊어!

en: Do you know who my father is, you little peasant twat?
lines: 우리 아버지가 누군지 알아, 이 천한 놈아?

en: Hey, look at that idiot! Jumping into the freezing river, haha!
lines: 야, 저 바보 좀 봐! 그 차가운 강에 뛰어드네, 하하!

en: Why do you do all of this?
Gyebek, would you like to serve a higher purpose?
lines: 계백, 더 큰 뜻을 섬겨 보겠느냐?

blocks.html: Gyebek looks back, and up, at the royal seats. The crown prince is already looking at him.
blocks.ko: 계백이 뒤를, 위를, 왕실 자리를 올려다본다. 태자는 벌써 그를 보고 있다.

blocks.html: Eight houses. Eight boys on the sand. And one with a borrowed name…!
blocks.ko: 여덟 가문. 모래판의 아이 여덟. 그리고 이름을 빌린 아이 하나…!

logline.en: Satek. Yunbi. Jinmo. Mokli. Hae. Bek. Guk. Ahn.
logline.ko: 사택. 연비. 진모. 목리. 해. 백. 국. 안.

images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Sabi palace at dusk, as the attached pl_sabi_palace board. Low three-quarter from the foot of the timber hall steps: Elder Satek seated on the top step, both hands on his knees, Minister Satek standing one step below at his shoulder; both wear the tall gilt-bronze noble crown, catching the low gold sun; behind them the dark hall doors; below, out of focus in the foreground, the chalked grid of the tourney yard. Device: the stair diagonal climbing to the two crowns. CANON — ELDER SATEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_satek_elder.png (face only; invent a new pose). Crown: the great-clan gilt crown (see NOBLE CROWN), no jougwan. #b8933f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | MINISTER SATEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_satek_minister.png (face only; invent a new pose). Crown: the great-clan gilt crown (see NOBLE CROWN), no jougwan. #c2a24a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. | NOBLE CROWN: Baekje great-clan lord’s gilt-bronze crown (금동관), as the attached crown (ignore its museum stand and black backdrop): a tall pointed gilt cap shaped like a peaked hood, pierced all over with openwork dragon-and-flame scrolls, a broad engraved band across the brow, a curved openwork crest arching over the top, two small cup-shaped finials on thin stems rising at the back, a pointed bud finial at the crown, and a flat openwork leaf-plume at the front. Worn high over the topknot on court and assembly days; burnished gold-bronze catching the key light. It replaces the jougwan. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. blocks.ko: 사택. 연비. 진모. 목리. 해. 백. 국. 안.

blocks.html: The Eight Great Clans run this country, and one king sits between them. Today, on the crown prince’s day, they settle nothing on the sand. They never do.
blocks.ko: 여덟 대성이 이 나라를 쥐고, 그 사이에 왕 하나가 앉아 있다. 오늘, 태자 책봉 날, 그들은 모래판에서 아무것도 결판내지 않는다. 늘 그렇다.

blocks.hanja: 大姓八族
blocks.html: The eight great surnames. Not a council and not a party. Eight families, each older than most kings, each with a seat on the rock, a berth on the river and a grudge against at least two of the others. The royal Buyeo house sits above them. Usually.
blocks.ko: 여덟 큰 성씨. 회의도 아니고 당파도 아니다. 집안 여덟, 하나하나가 웬만한 임금보다 오래됐고, 저마다 바위 위의 자리, 강가의 부두, 그리고 적어도 둘에 대한 원한을 하나씩 가졌다. 그 위에 왕실 부여씨가 앉는다. 대개는.

blocks.html: The Western wrote the eight names down too, and got half of them wrong. That tells you how often the clans let outsiders count them.
blocks.ko: 서국 사람들도 그 여덟 이름을 적어 두었는데, 절반을 틀리게 적었다. 가문들이 바깥사람에게 저희를 세게 해 주는 일이 얼마나 드문지 알 만하다.

blocks.html: The great surnames of the country are eight clans: Sa, Yeon, Hyup, Hae, Jin, Guk, Mok and Bek.
blocks.ko: 나라 안의 큰 성씨는 여덟 족이니, 사씨·연씨·협씨·해씨·진씨·국씨·목씨·백씨이다.
blocks.hanja: 國中大姓有八族，沙氏、燕氏、刕氏、解氏、貞氏、國氏、木氏、苩氏。
blocks.source: Sui Shu (隋書) bk. 81, Eastern Barbarians — Baekje

blocks.html: Ask any of the eight where they came from, and you will get a long answer that ends with their own house. Here is the short one.
blocks.ko: 여덟 가문 누구에게든 어디서 왔느냐고 물어보라. 긴 대답이 돌아오고, 그 끝은 꼭 제 집안이다. 짧은 대답은 이렇다.

blocks.html: Ten men walked south with the first king. Ten attendants. They carried his rice, led his horse and held his banner, and when he built his city each of them got a hill.
blocks.ko: 열 사내가 첫 임금을 따라 남쪽으로 걸어왔다. 열 신하. 쌀을 지고, 말을 끌고, 깃발을 들었다. 임금이 도읍을 세우자 저마다 언덕 하나씩을 받았다.

blocks.html: Eight of those hills are still in Sabi, with the same names over the gates. Nobody knows what became of the other two.
blocks.ko: 그 언덕 가운데 여덟은 아직 사비에 있다. 대문 위 이름도 그대로다. 나머지 둘이 어떻게 됐는지는 아무도 모른다.

en: Went back north, they say.
Drowned in the river.
Went over to Silla, and Silla’s too proud to say.
Married into Satek. Ever notice Satek never counts past eight?
lines: 신라루 넘어갔는디 신라가 체면 땜에 말을 안 하는 겨.
사택이랑 붙었지 뭐. 사택이 여덟 넘어 세는 거 본 적 있어?

blocks.label: The Sand
blocks.ko: 모래판

blocks.html: On the crown prince’s day, the court chalks a square grid in the palace yard. Four hard lines. No banners. The young men of each house step onto the grid in white.
blocks.ko: 태자 책봉 날, 궁은 마당에 네모난 격자를 분필로 긋는다. 단단한 선 넷. 깃발은 없다. 각 가문의 젊은이들이 흰옷을 입고 격자에 오른다.

lines: 연비네 애들이 어제 서시 다리서 사택네 짐수레를 엎었댜.
그럼 오늘 밤엔 사택네가 연비네 담을 넘겄구먼.
en: The Yunbi boys turned a Satek cart over at the west bridge yesterday.
Then I expect tonight the Satek go over a Yunbi wall.
Same as the lantern festival last year.
Last year three of them died.
White cloth. Wooden swords.
If anyone bleeds the wrong colour, the harbour talks stop for a month.
lines: 엉뚱한 색으루 피 보믄, 항구 얘기는 한 달 쉬는 겨.

blocks.caption: Head of the Yunbi. The family business is knowing things first.
blocks.ko: 연비 가문의 어른. 이 집안의 생업은 남보다 먼저 아는 것이다.

en: Then keep your boys’ wrists honest.
The chalk does not care whose sleeve they hold.
lines: 그럼 너희 애들 손목을 바르게 두게.
분필은 누구 소매를 잡았는지 안 본다.

blocks.html: Swords first. Wooden ones, which still remember steel. The Jinmo boy holds his blade high over his head, the Jinmo way, daring you. A Hae boy takes the dare. On the call they both move. Blades skim the chalk. The white sleeves clap together so close that the steps gasp.
blocks.ko: 칼부터. 목검이다. 아직 쇠를 기억하는 나무. 진모 도령이 진모식으로 칼을 머리 위로 높이 든다. 덤벼 보라는 뜻이다. 해씨 소년이 덤빈다. 구령이 떨어지자 둘이 동시에 움직인다. 칼날이 분필 위를 스친다. 흰 소매가 맞부딪는 소리에 계단이 숨을 삼킨다.

en: That Jinmo boy?
Fast wrists.
Faster feet than the Hae, too.
Point to Jinmo.

blocks.html: The Jinmo boy bows to the steps and looks straight past the Hae boy, to the edge of the sand, where the crown prince’s nobody is waiting.
blocks.ko: 진모 도령이 계단을 향해 절하고는, 해씨 소년 너머 모래판 가장자리를 똑바로 본다. 태자의 이름 없던 아이가 기다리는 곳이다.

blocks.html: When the wooden points are tallied, the sand comes out. A circle of grit inside the same square. Ssireum — satba locked before they stand, knees in the grit, equal grips on waist and thigh, then up without letting go. No circling for a hold. The bout is the hold.
blocks.ko: 목검 점수가 쌓이면 모래가 나온다. 같은 네모 안에 모래 원. 씨름 — 일어서기 전에 샅바부터 잠근다. 무릎은 모래에, 허리와 허벅지 샅바를 같은 힘으로 잡고, 놓지 않은 채로 일어선다. 잡고 돌 틈이 없다. 붙잡은 것이 곧 시합이다.

blocks.html: A Yunbi boy hooks a leg, low, the coast-road way. The Satek boy answers with his hip. He lifts, he turns, and the Yunbi boy’s feet leave the earth. The yard goes quiet the way a dock goes quiet when a rope snaps. Sand takes the shoulder. The chalk does not argue.
blocks.ko: 연비 소년이 해안 길 사람답게 낮게 다리를 건다. 사택 소년이 엉덩이로 받는다. 들어 올리고, 돌리고, 연비 소년의 발이 땅을 떠난다. 밧줄 끊긴 부두처럼 마당이 조용해진다. 모래가 어깨를 받는다. 분필은 따지지 않는다.

en: See?
Even Yunbi can fall without a cart.
Your boy’s knee touched first.
Ask the chalk.

blocks.html: The elders watch from the hall steps. They always do, and they still count wrong when it is their sleeve.
blocks.ko: 원로들은 섬돌에서 본다. 늘 본다. 그래도 제 소매 일이면 잘못 센다.

blocks.html: One step below the elders sit the crown prince’s sons. Each one sits on his mother’s side of the stair. If you know the houses, you can read the whole Assembly off that stair.
blocks.ko: 원로들 한 칸 아래엔 태자의 아들들이 앉아 있다. 저마다 어머니 집안 쪽 섬돌에 앉는다. 집안을 알면, 그 섬돌만 봐도 정사암 회의가 다 읽힌다.

blocks.caption: The eldest, at seventeen. Satek on his mother’s side, and on every other side they could arrange.
blocks.ko: 열일곱, 맏이. 어머니 쪽으로 사택이고, 사택이 손쓸 수 있는 다른 쪽으로도 다 사택이다.

en: That’s one.
…Father didn’t clap.

blocks.caption: Second son, sixteen. A Jinmo grandmother, and a score kept in his sleeve. The score is always right.
blocks.ko: 둘째, 열여섯. 할머니가 진모가고, 소매 속에 점수를 적어 둔다. 그 점수는 늘 맞다.

en: Jinmo one. Satek one. Yunbi owes my grandmother a boat.
lines: 진모 하나. 사택 하나. 연비는 우리 할머니한테 배 한 척 빚졌고.

blocks.caption: Third son, fifteen. No clan behind his chair, only his mother. The houses can’t decide whether that makes him nothing or dangerous.
blocks.ko: 셋째, 열다섯. 의자 뒤에 가문이 없다. 어머니뿐이다. 가문들은 그게 아무것도 아니라는 뜻인지, 위험하다는 뜻인지 아직 못 정했다.

en: When the eel boy comes on, are we allowed to cheer for Father’s man? Or is that— is that taking a side?
lines: 장어 파는 애 나오믄, 아버지 사람한테 환호해두 되남? 아니믄 그게— 편드는 겨?

en: Cheer quietly. It’s cheaper.

blocks.caption: Twelve. Hae on his mother’s side. Not Yung. He will tell you so.
blocks.ko: 열둘. 어머니 쪽은 해씨. 융이 아니다. 본인이 그렇게 말해 줄 것이다.

en: Prince Yung, your cushion—
Yun. Yung is over there. He’s the one with the ring.
lines: 연이여. 융 형님은 저짝. 반지 낀 쪽.

blocks.caption: Eight, the youngest who counts. Mokli on his mother’s side. Best handwriting in the palace, and nobody has found a use for it yet.
blocks.ko: 여덟 살, 셈에 드는 막내. 어머니 쪽은 목리가. 궁에서 글씨가 제일 곱다. 그 쓸모를 아직 아무도 못 찾았다.

blocks.html: Pung has a strip of wood on his knees and a brush in his fist. He is copying down every name the herald reads, because nobody told him not to.
blocks.ko: 풍은 무릎에 목간 한 조각을 올려 두고 붓을 쥐고 있다. 전령이 읽는 이름을 하나도 빠짐없이 받아 적는다. 하지 말라는 사람이 없었으니까.

blocks.label: The Last Bout
blocks.ko: 마지막 판

blocks.html: Last on the sand: the Jinmo boy, and the crown prince’s nobody. For five days the Jinmo boy has told the steps what he will do to a peasant. Now the peasant has a royal surname, and the steps want to see.
blocks.ko: 모래판의 마지막 판. 진모 도령, 그리고 태자의 이름 없던 아이. 진모 도령은 닷새 내내 천한 놈을 어떻게 해 주겠다고 계단에 떠벌렸다. 이제 그 천한 놈에게 왕실의 성이 붙었고, 계단은 구경하고 싶어 한다.

en: Buyeo. BUYEO.
You got that name off a drunk on a riverbank, eel boy. I’ll hand it back to him in pieces.
lines: 강가서 술 취한 놈한테 얻은 이름이잖여, 장어 새끼야. 조각내서 돌려줄 겨.

en: It was given.
…What?
You said I got it. It was given. That is different.

blocks.html: Satba. Equal grips, knees in the grit, then up together. The Jinmo boy is a head taller, and he knows it. He leans.
blocks.ko: 샅바. 같은 힘으로 잡고, 무릎은 모래에, 그리고 함께 일어선다. 진모 도령이 머리 하나 더 크고, 본인도 그걸 안다. 그가 밀어붙인다.

en: Jinmo’s got him—
Look at the eel boy’s feet, he’s going—
He’s not going anywhere. Look.
lines: 장어 놈 발 좀 봐, 밀린다—

blocks.html: Gyebek’s heels slide back a finger’s width, and stop. He does not try to throw. He holds, the way he held a rope in a river for five days, and he waits.
blocks.ko: 계백의 발꿈치가 손가락 한 마디만큼 밀리다가, 멈춘다. 그는 넘기려 하지 않는다. 버틴다. 닷새 동안 강물 속에서 밧줄을 버티던 것처럼. 그리고 기다린다.

en: Ha! Look at him, Father. He isn’t wrestling.
He’s waiting for the other one to get bored of breathing.
lines: 하하! 보십시오, 아바마마. 저건 씨름이 아닙니다.
저쪽이 숨 쉬는 데 질릴 때까지 기다리는 거지요.

en: Sit down. You’ll frighten the Satek.
Let— go— you—
No.

blocks.html: The Jinmo boy runs out of breath first. Gyebek turns him the way you turn over a full basket: carefully, so nothing spills.
blocks.ko: 숨이 먼저 떨어지는 쪽은 진모 도령이다. 계백은 가득 찬 바구니를 뒤집듯 그를 돌린다. 조심스럽게, 아무것도 쏟아지지 않게.

blocks.html: Sand takes a Jinmo shoulder. On the royal steps, a crown prince with no interest in clan quarrels is on his feet.
blocks.ko: 모래가 진모의 어깨를 받는다. 왕실 계단 위에서, 가문 싸움엔 관심 없다던 태자가 벌떡 일어서 있다.

blocks.html: Then someone in the crowd starts the old chant, the one every house in Sabi knows by heart, because a royal name has just won on the sand. Eraha is the old Baekje word for king.
blocks.ko: 그때 군중 속 누군가가 옛 구호를 시작한다. 사비의 집이라면 어디나 외우는 구호다. 방금 왕실의 성이 모래판에서 이겼으니까. 어라하는 백제의 옛말로 임금이다.

en: Restore the reign of the thirteenth Eraha!

blocks.html: Euija hears it and stops smiling. Nobody notices, except Gyebek, who is still on his knees in the sand and looking straight at him.
blocks.ko: 의자가 그 소리를 듣고 웃음을 거둔다. 아무도 눈치채지 못한다. 모래 위에 아직 무릎 꿇은 채 그를 똑바로 보는 계백만 빼고.

blocks.html: By dusk the white is grey with chalk and grit. Nobody has settled four generations of anything. The throne likes it that way. The boys go home with a score instead of a funeral.
blocks.ko: 해 질 녘, 흰옷은 분필과 모래로 잿빛이 된다. 사대에 걸친 무엇 하나 결판나지 않았다. 왕좌는 그게 좋다. 소년들은 장례 대신 점수를 들고 집에 간다.

blocks.html: On his way off the sand, Gyebek passes the bottom step. The littlest prince holds up his strip of wood.
blocks.ko: 모래판을 나서던 계백이 맨 아래 섬돌을 지난다. 제일 어린 왕자가 목간을 들어 보인다.

en: I cannot read.
It says you. Buyeo Gyebek. I wrote it the herald’s way, only neater.
Keep it. I’ll write another.
lines: 너라구 쓰여 있어. 부여 계백. 전령이 읽은 대로 썼는데, 더 반듯하게.

blocks.html: Gyebek looks at the marks for a long time. Then he puts the wood inside his shirt, where the burner went, and bows to a boy of eight as if he were the king.
blocks.ko: 계백은 그 획들을 오래 들여다본다. 그러고는 향로를 쌌던 저고리 안에 목간을 넣고, 여덟 살 아이에게 임금께 하듯 절한다.

en: …Thank you.

blocks.label: The Assembly
blocks.ko: 정사암 회의

blocks.html: The chalk is still on Gyebek’s sleeve when the lords climb to the rock that afternoon. Nobody invited him. Euija brings him anyway, the way you bring a new dog to dinner to see who flinches.
blocks.ko: 그날 오후 귀족들이 바위로 오를 때도 계백의 소매엔 아직 분필 가루가 묻어 있다. 아무도 그를 부르지 않았다. 의자가 그냥 데려온다. 새로 들인 개를 잔칫상에 데려가 누가 움찔하나 보는 식으로.

blocks.speaker: Servants on the stair
en: Is that him? The eel boy?
In the prince’s shadow. Look, he’s still got sand in his ears.
Satek’ll want him by the new moon.
Yunbi’ll want him by tonight.
lines: 태자 그림자 속에. 봐, 귀에 아직 모래 들었구먼.
사택은 초승달 전에 저놈을 갖고 싶어 할 겨.
연비는 오늘 밤 안에 갖고 싶어 할 거구.

blocks.html: In the Assembly they fight for power, each house holding a share of the king's sons. They fight in the street too. Same fight. The street version is older.
blocks.ko: 회의에서 그들은 권력을 두고 싸운다. 가문마다 왕의 아들 몇씩을 쥐고서. 거리에서도 싸운다. 같은 싸움이다. 거리 쪽이 더 오래됐다.

blocks.hanja: 政事巖
blocks.html: The Rock of Government. Long ago Baekje’s lords chose their prime minister by sealing three names in a box and leaving it on this rock overnight. Whichever name the rock had marked by morning got the chair. Nobody has tried it in living memory. These days the chair goes to whoever paid for it.
blocks.ko: 정사를 보는 바위. 옛날 백제의 귀족들은 이름 셋을 함에 봉해 이 바위 위에 하룻밤 두었다. 아침에 바위가 표시해 둔 이름이 재상 자리에 앉았다. 살아 있는 사람 중에 그걸 해 본 이는 없다. 요즘 그 자리는 값을 치른 쪽으로 간다.

blocks.html: Unlike Silla’s Harmony Council, the Assembly does not require every voice. A plurality of houses is enough — which is why the street fights matter. Votes can be bought in pieces. In Surabol they must be bought entire, or not at all.
blocks.ko: 신라 화백과 달리, 정사암회의는 모든 목소리를 요구하지 않는다. 가문의 다수면 족하다 — 그래서 저잣거리 싸움이 중요하다. 표는 조각으로 살 수 있다. 서라벌에서는 통째로 사거나, 아예 못 산다.

blocks.html: What the Assembly votes on, more often than war, is water. Who loads first. Whose ships winter in the river mouth. Who gets the orange levy, and who gets the silk berth. In this country, a clan without a harbour can't feed a fight.
blocks.ko: 회의가 전쟁보다 자주 표결하는 건 물이다. 누가 먼저 싣는가. 누구 배가 강어귀에서 겨울을 나는가. 귤 공물은 누가, 비단 선석은 누가 갖는가. 이 나라에서 항구 없는 가문은 싸움을 먹여 살리지 못한다.

en: The west bridge. Your boys, my cart.
I’ll take the cart out of your berth fee.
lines: 서쪽 다리 말이오. 그쪽 애들이 우리 수레를 엎었소.

en: Take it out of your wall.
Our boys are going over it tonight anyway.
lines: 오늘 밤 우리 애들이 어차피 넘을 담이니.

en: Yunbi talks of blood.
We talk of berths.
Blood cools. A winter anchorage does not.
lines: 피는 식소. 겨울 정박지는 안 식고.

en: Says the man who holds the king’s sleeve and calls it a harbour—
lines: 임금 소매 붙들고 그걸 항구라 부르는 양반이 할 소리는—

en: Three berths.
—Four.
Three, and I forget the cart.
…We don’t hold the sleeve. We hold the arm.
Three.

blocks.html: Nobody on the rock writes it down. Everybody in Sabi knows it by supper.
blocks.ko: 바위 위 누구도 그걸 적지 않는다. 사비 사람이면 저녁 전에 다 안다.

blocks.html: Satek and Yunbi have been at it for four generations. Nobody alive can say what started it. Everybody alive can list the last six things.
blocks.ko: 사택과 연비는 사대째 그러고 있다. 무엇 때문에 시작됐는지는 살아 있는 누구도 대지 못한다. 최근 여섯 건은 살아 있는 누구나 댄다.

blocks.html: Two men on the rock are not lords. They keep the Assembly honest, or try to. One keeps the tide tables. One keeps the maps.
blocks.ko: 바위 위에 귀족이 아닌 사람이 둘 있다. 회의를 정직하게 붙들어 두는 사람들이다. 아니, 그러려고 애쓰는 사람들이다. 하나는 물때표를 맡고, 하나는 지도를 맡는다.

blocks.caption: Keeps the tide tables for the berth votes. Has never once changed a number to please a lord, and sweats every time.
blocks.ko: 선석 표결에 쓰는 물때표를 맡는다. 귀족 비위 맞추려고 숫자를 고친 적이 한 번도 없다. 그리고 그때마다 진땀을 뺀다.

en: Clerk. The spring tide at the Satek berth.
lines: 서기. 봄 사리 때 사택 선석 물 깊이.

en: Four hands at the low, my lord. Which is— forgive me— not enough for a winter hull, so if the vote is about wintering, then—
lines: 썰물에 네 뼘입니다, 대감. 그건— 송구하오나— 겨울 배를 대기엔 모자라니, 표결이 겨울 정박에 관한 것이라면, 그—

en: Write five.
I— the river says four, my lord. I can write it larger. It will still be four.
lines: 저— 강이 넷이라 합니다, 대감. 크게 적을 수는 있습니다. 그래도 넷입니다.

blocks.caption: Draws the river for men who have never got their feet wet. He is already tired of explaining it.
blocks.ko: 발 한 번 안 적셔 본 사람들을 위해 강을 그린다. 설명하는 데 벌써 지쳤다.

en: He’s right. Here.
The sandbar. Vote whatever you like. Silt doesn’t come to meetings.
lines: 모래톱입니다. 표결은 마음대로 하십시오. 뻘은 회의에 안 옵니다.

blocks.html: He scratches the river mouth into the packed earth with his stick, wider than it really is, so the lords at the back can see it. Elder Yunbi laughs out loud. Elder Satek writes four.
blocks.ko: 그는 지팡이 끝으로 다져진 흙바닥에 강어귀를 긁어 그린다. 뒷줄 대감들도 보이게, 실제보다 넓게. 연비 어른이 소리 내어 웃는다. 사택 어른은 넷이라고 적는다.

blocks.html: Today, for once, they agree on something. They don’t like the boy on the sand.
blocks.ko: 오늘은 웬일로 둘이 한 가지에 뜻이 맞는다. 모래판의 그 아이가 싫다.

en: Buyeo, on an eel boy.
Every house on this rock owns one of the crown prince’s sons. Now he has a man none of us own.
lines: 이 바위 위 가문마다 태자의 아들 하나씩은 쥐고 있소. 그런데 이제 그한테 우리 누구 것도 아닌 사내가 생겼단 말이오.

en: Then we buy him. Before you do.
You’ll overpay. You always do.

blocks.html: Neither house has ever won, and nothing about that is accidental: the throne needs both of them standing. A clan with no rival starts watching the throne.
blocks.ko: 어느 집안도 이긴 적이 없고, 거기에 우연은 조금도 없다. 왕좌는 둘이 다 서 있기를 바란다 — 미워할 상대가 없는 가문은 왕좌를 보기 시작한다.

lines: 연비 짝에서 사택 회의 내용을 벌써 안댜.
그럼 둘 다 알구, 둘 다 모르는 척허는 거지.
en: They say Yunbi already knows what was said in the Satek meeting.
And Satek already knows the Yunbi one.
So both know, and both pretend not to.
That’s politics.

blocks.label: The Rock at Dusk
blocks.ko: 해 질 녘의 바위

blocks.html: When the rock is empty, the crown prince is still sitting on it, which is not allowed. His new man stands beside him, which is not allowed either.
blocks.ko: 바위가 비고 나서도 태자는 그 위에 앉아 있다. 허락되지 않는 일이다. 그 옆엔 새 사람이 서 있다. 그것도 허락되지 않는 일이다.

blocks.html: Below the rock, the two clerks are rolling up the day’s maps. The crown prince whistles them over like a man calling dogs. They come anyway.
blocks.ko: 바위 아래에서 서기 둘이 그날의 지도를 말고 있다. 태자가 개 부르듯 휘파람을 분다. 그래도 둘은 온다.

blocks.html: Euija unhooks a purse from his own belt and lobs it underhand. Sunchung catches it out of pure fright.
blocks.ko: 의자가 제 허리춤에서 돈주머니를 끌러 아래로 툭 던진다. 성충은 순전히 놀라서 받는다.

en: You. The tide.
That’s what writing five would have paid. Satek rates.
Keep it. Just tell me why you wrote four.
lines: 그게 다섯 적었으면 받았을 값이여. 사택 시세로.
가져. 대신 왜 넷이라 적었는지 말혀 봐.

en: Highness, I— if I keep it, that’s the same as if I’d written—
Because in the eleventh month a hull sits down on that bar, and somebody asks who wrote five, and—
lines: 저하, 그— 이걸 받으면, 그건 제가 다섯이라고 적은 거나 매한가지라—
동짓달에 배 한 척이 그 모래톱에 주저앉으면, 누가 다섯이라 적었느냐 묻는 사람이 꼭 있고, 그러면—

en: And it’s you.
It is always the clerk.

blocks.html: He holds the purse out. Euija doesn’t take it. Sunchung holds it at arm’s length for the rest of the evening, like a man who has picked up a snake by the wrong end.
blocks.ko: 성충이 주머니를 내민다. 의자는 받지 않는다. 성충은 그날 저녁 내내 그걸 팔을 쭉 뻗어 들고 있다. 뱀을 거꾸로 집어 든 사람처럼.

en: Ha! Not the purse, then. So what does a clerk want?
lines: 하! 돈도 싫다믄, 서기는 뭘 원햐?

en: …A king who hears a bad number and does something about it. Before the hull, Highness. Just the once would—
lines: …나쁜 숫자를 듣고 뭔가 하시는 임금입니다. 배가 주저앉기 전에요, 저하. 딱 한 번이라도—

en: And you? The stick.
Same as him.
Earlier.

blocks.html: Remember that answer. He will give it again, at the worst possible time.
blocks.ko: 그 대답을 기억해 두시라. 그는 그 말을 한 번 더 하게 된다. 가장 나쁜 때에.

en: They want to buy you, you know. All three of you. Both houses will bid all winter.
lines: 저치들이 너희를 살라구 혀. 셋 다. 두 집안이 겨울 내내 값을 부를 겨.

en: Nobody has actually offered for me, Highness. …Except you. Just now.
lines: 아직 아무도 값을 안 불렀습니다만, 저하. ……방금 저하 빼고는요.

en: They will.

blocks.html: Gyebek says nothing. His hand goes flat against his shirt, over the strip of wood with his name on it, and stays there.
blocks.ko: 계백은 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 손바닥이 저고리 앞섶 위로, 제 이름이 적힌 나뭇조각 자리에 납작하게 얹히고, 그대로 있다.

en: Ha! Three men on this rock nobody owns. That’s what frightens them.
You heard the chant on the sand?
lines: 하하! 이 바위 위에 누구 것도 아닌 사내가 셋. 그래서 저치들이 겁을 먹는 겨.

en: Yes. Everyone knows it.
Do you know what it’s about?
No.
Neither do they. That’s the trouble.
Eight houses, one river, and the only thing they’ll shout together is a king three hundred years dead.
This country needs a new story, Gyebek. The old one’s worn mighty thin.
lines: 가문 여덟, 강 하나. 근데 다 같이 외치는 거라곤 삼백 년 전에 죽은 임금 하나뿐이여.
이 나라엔 새 이야기가 있어야 혀, 계백아. 옛날 건 닳을 대루 닳았어.

en: Who will tell it?

blocks.html: Euija laughs, and does not answer, which for him is a kind of answer.
blocks.ko: 의자는 웃기만 하고 대답하지 않는다. 그에겐 그것도 대답의 한 가지다.

blocks.html: The old Prime Minister is dying, and eight houses want his chair. The king has a very old idea. It involves a rock…!
blocks.ko: 늙은 상좌평이 죽어 간다. 여덟 가문이 그 자리를 노린다. 왕에게는 아주 오래된 생각이 하나 있다. 바위가 하나 끼어 있다…!

logline.en: Three names in a sealed box, one night on the rock, and eight houses who all intend to help heaven decide.
logline.ko: 봉한 함 속의 이름 셋, 바위 위의 하룻밤. 그리고 하늘의 결정을 거들 작정인 여덟 가문.

images.alt: Every house in Sabi agrees that heaven chooses the Prime Minister. They only disagree about which house heaven owes money.
images.prompt: OPENING STILL of the episode: the first image the reader sees, staging its first line. The line: “Every house in Sabi agrees that heaven chooses the Prime Minister. They only disagree about which house heaven owes money.” Context: Every house in Sabi agrees that heaven chooses the Prime Minister. They only disagree about which house heaven owes money.  The old Prime Minister dies at the end of summer, in his own bed, which in Sabi counts as a surprise. His chair is still warm when the bidding starts. A wide or medium establishing frame that hooks. CANON — PLACE Deer Rock (정사암) — attached board /pl_deer_rock.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: Down the hill the crowd has heard. Somebody starts the old chant, because a Satek has won and the Satek like to think they wrote it. Restore

Somebody starts the old chant, because a Satek has won and the Satek like to think they wrote it. Restore the reign of the thirteenth Eraha! By noon the Yunbi are chanting it too.” Context: Yes. Somebody starts the old chant, because a Satek has won and the Satek like to think they wrote it. Restore the reign of the thirteenth Eraha! By noon the Yunbi are chanting it too. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — GYEBEK — FACE ONLY from attached /ch_gyebek_boy.png; ignore the portrait's clothing, headgear, jewelry and hair styling — dress exactly as "Now" below (invent a new pose). Rose from a nameless White River boy to 백승계백 (Hundred-Victories Gyebek); by Hwangsanbeol the taverns argue he is the stronger blade than Yushin, and one-to-one he is: twenty-five years younger, faster, never beaten in single combat. Rides low and coiled, like he fights. #d9b13a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: curved blade, katana or tsuba (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); forward textbook grip once the fight starts; yellow metal cuirass; smiling in battle. | BUYEO EUIJA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_buyeo_euija.png (face only; invent a new pose).
