Dress: Crimson robe with a dark charcoal collar and gold trim; a steel lamellar pauldron peeking at one shoulder. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Demeanor: Licensed wit: drinks, smirks, slumps on the throne, speaks in polished aphorisms. Fatalist. #e08a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: heroic battle pose; smiling innocence. | PLACE Deer Rock (정사암) — attached board /pl_deer_rock.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). COMMONERS in every Samhan kingdom wear SIMPLE WHITE: plain undyed white or off-white hemp and ramie jackets, wide trousers and skirts, a cloth sash, straw sandals or bare feet, hair in a plain topknot or braid — no dyed silk, no dots, no gold; colour belongs to rank, so a crowd of farmers, porters, servants and townsfolk reads as a field of soft white cloth with the officials' colours standing out of it. Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Every house in Sabi agrees that heaven chooses the Prime Minister. They only disagree about which house heaven owes money.
blocks.ko: 사비의 모든 가문이 동의한다. 상좌평은 하늘이 고른다고. 다만 하늘이 어느 집에 빚을 졌는지를 두고 다툴 뿐이다.

blocks.label: The Empty Chair
blocks.ko: 빈 의자

blocks.html: The old Prime Minister dies at the end of summer, in his own bed, which in Sabi counts as a surprise. His chair is still warm when the bidding starts.
blocks.ko: 늙은 상좌평이 여름 끝에 제 침상에서 죽는다. 사비에서는 그것도 놀랄 일이다. 의자가 식기도 전에 값 매기기가 시작된다.

blocks.html: By the third day, Elder Yunbi has bought four of the eight houses. On the rock, four is enough. Everyone in Sabi knows the price, down to the fishwives.
blocks.ko: 사흘째, 연비 원로는 여덟 가문 중 넷을 샀다. 바위 위에서는 넷이면 된다. 값이 얼마였는지는 사비 사람이면 생선 장수 아낙까지 안다.

blocks.html: King Mu hears the price over breakfast and laughs so hard he has to put the bowl down.
blocks.ko: 무왕은 아침상 앞에서 그 값을 듣고, 그릇을 내려놓아야 할 만큼 웃는다.

en: Four houses. For one chair.
Yunbi’s paid for a Prime Minister. Fine. Let’s see if he’s paid the rock.
lines: 연비가 상좌평 값을 치렀다. 좋지. 바위 값도 치렀나 보자.

en: The rock, Father? Nobody’s asked the rock anything since Great-grandfather’s day.
Ha! You want a stone to pick who runs Baekje?
lines: 바위 말입니까, 아바마마? 증조부 때 이후로 그 바위한테 뭘 물어본 사람이 없습니다.
하! 백제를 누가 맡을지 돌한테 고르라 하시겠다고요?

en: Stones don’t take money.
…Well. Not directly. That’s the fun of it.
lines: …뭐. 대놓고는 안 받지. 그게 재밌는 거다.

blocks.html: Here is how the rock works, according to a monk who wrote it down six hundred years later and was not there either.
blocks.ko: 바위가 어떻게 돌아가는지는 육백 년 뒤에 이걸 적어 둔 스님의 말을 빌리자. 그 스님도 거기 있지는 않았다.

blocks.html: At Hoam Temple there is a Rock of Government. When the country was to choose a chief minister, they wrote the names of the candidates, three or four of them, sealed them in a box and set it on the rock. After a little while they took it down and looked. The man whose name bore the mark of a seal became minister. That is how the rock got its name.
blocks.ko: 또 호암사에 정사암이 있다. 나라에서 재상을 뽑으려 할 때, 뽑힐 만한 사람의 이름을 서넛 써서 함에 넣어 봉하고 바위 위에 두었다. 얼마 뒤 가져다 보아, 이름 위에 도장 자국이 있는 사람을 재상으로 삼았다. 그래서 그렇게 이름 붙였다.
blocks.hanja: 又虎嵓寺有政事嵓。國家將議宰相，則書當選者名，或三四，函封置嵓上，須臾取看，名上有印跡者爲相，故名之。
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 2, Nambuyeo · Jeon-Baekje

blocks.html: “A little while,” the monk says. In Sabi a little while is exactly one night, which is long enough for every house on the rock to help heaven make up its mind.
blocks.ko: “얼마 뒤”라고 스님은 적었다. 사비에서 ‘얼마 뒤’는 딱 하룻밤이다. 바위 위의 모든 가문이 하늘의 결심을 거들기에 넉넉한 시간이다.

en: Three names. In the box, on the rock, under my seal.
Whoever heaven marks by morning gets the chair. Whoever squeals about it can take it up with heaven.
lines: 이름 셋. 함에 넣어, 바위 위에, 내 도장으로 봉한다.
아침까지 하늘이 찍어 준 놈이 의자를 갖는다. 거기 대고 꽥꽥대는 놈은 하늘한테 가서 따지라 해.

en: And when one of them helps heaven along?
Then I’ll know which one’s cleverest. That’s the one I want in the chair.
Rich I can buy, boy. Clever I have to find.
lines: 그럼 누가 제일 영리한지 알게 되겠지. 의자엔 그런 놈이 앉아야 한다.
부자는 사면 된다, 이놈아. 영리한 놈은 찾아야 하고.

blocks.label: Three Names
blocks.ko: 이름 셋

blocks.html: A long grey rock above the river, with a temple tucked under it like a servant. Eight benches face it. Nobody has sat on the rock itself in a hundred years.
blocks.ko: 강 위로 길게 누운 회색 바위. 그 아래 절 하나가 하인처럼 웅크리고 있다. 여덟 걸상이 바위를 마주한다. 바위 위에 직접 앉은 사람은 백 년 동안 없었다.

blocks.html: Three names go in at sunset. Elder Yunbi, who has paid for four houses. Lord Jinmo, who has paid for one and is praying. And a Satek nobody expected.
blocks.ko: 해 질 녘에 이름 셋이 들어간다. 가문 넷 값을 치른 연비 원로. 하나 값을 치르고 기도 중인 진모 공. 그리고 아무도 예상하지 못한 사택 하나.

blocks.html: Elder Satek has not put in his own name. He has put in his kinsman’s. Satek Jijuk is thirty-five. He has never bought anything bigger than a boat, and he talks in sentences so short that nobody has ever managed to quote him.
blocks.ko: 사택 원로는 제 이름을 넣지 않았다. 일가붙이의 이름을 넣었다. 사택지적, 서른다섯. 배보다 큰 걸 사 본 적이 없고, 말이 하도 짧아서 아무도 그의 말을 옮겨 적지 못했다.

en: You’ve sent a boy, Satek.
Short of money, or short of nerve?
Short of nothing. The tide’s coming in, Yunbi.
I sent the man who reads tides.
lines: 모자란 건 없소. 물이 들어오고 있소, 연비.

blocks.html: By custom each man writes his own name on his own slip and folds it himself. A Prime Minister should at least be able to spell his ambition.
blocks.ko: 관례상 각자 제 쪽지에 제 이름을 쓰고 제 손으로 접는다. 상좌평이 되려면 적어도 제 욕심 정도는 제 손으로 쓸 줄 알아야 하니까.

blocks.html: Jijuk writes slowly. He folds his slip three times, small and tight, the way a harbour clerk folds a bill he fully expects to be paid.
blocks.ko: 지적은 천천히 쓴다. 쪽지를 세 번, 작고 단단하게 접는다. 항구 서기가 꼭 받아 낼 어음을 접듯이.

blocks.html: Then he does the one strange thing anybody notices. He has a servant carry up a jar from the river mouth, and he pours it over the rock, slowly, end to end.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 누구나 눈치챌 만한 이상한 짓을 하나 한다. 하인을 시켜 강어귀에서 단지 하나를 지고 올라오게 하더니, 그걸 바위에 천천히, 끝에서 끝까지 붓는다.

en: What is that.
Sea water. My house blesses things with the sea.
It’s an old custom.
How old.
Since this afternoon.

blocks.html: Elder Yunbi laughs. Satek theatre. He has seen worse, and he has paid for better.
blocks.ko: 연비 원로가 웃는다. 사택네 연극이다. 더 한심한 것도 봤고, 더 비싼 것도 샀다.

blocks.html: King Mu seals the box with his own hand, and it goes up on the wet rock as the sun goes down. A monk from the temple below sits beside it to keep the night. The monk has been paid, by more than one house. Monks are generous with their time.
blocks.ko: 무왕이 제 손으로 함을 봉하고, 해가 지는 동안 젖은 바위 위에 올린다. 아래 절의 스님 하나가 그 곁에 앉아 밤을 지킨다. 스님은 돈을 받았다. 한 집에서만 받은 게 아니다. 스님들은 시간을 아끼지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Night
blocks.ko: 밤

blocks.html: Every house posts a man at the foot of the rock. Every house sends a second man to watch the first.
blocks.ko: 가문마다 바위 밑에 사람 하나를 세운다. 그리고 그 사람을 지켜볼 사람을 하나씩 더 보낸다.

blocks.html: The crown prince comes too, which is not allowed, with a jug, which is also not allowed, and his new man from the sand, who does not drink.
blocks.ko: 왕세자도 온다. 그건 안 되는 일이다. 술병을 들고 온다. 그것도 안 된다. 모래판의 새 사람도 데리고 온다. 그는 술을 마시지 않는다.

en: Watch the rock, Gyebek. Tell me everything that moves.
I’ve a bet on with my father. Loser feeds the winner’s horses for a month.
lines: 바위를 보거라, 계백. 움직이는 건 다 말해라.
아바마마와 내기를 했다. 진 쪽이 한 달 동안 이긴 쪽 말을 먹인다.

en: Yes.

blocks.html: Midnight. Somebody goes over the temple wall, badly. Roof-tiles slide. In the guesthouse a Yunbi girl of fifteen sits straight up out of sleep and names the climber before the tiles stop falling. One day she will sit in the Prime Minister’s chair herself, and she will still know that cousin by his footsteps.
blocks.ko: 자정. 누군가 절 담을 넘는다. 서툴게. 기와가 미끄러진다. 객사에서 자던 열다섯 살 연비 집 딸아이가 벌떡 일어나, 기와가 다 떨어지기도 전에 넘어온 사람 이름을 댄다. 그 아이는 언젠가 저 상좌평 의자에 직접 앉는다. 그때도 그 사촌의 발소리는 알아들을 것이다.

blocks.speaker: A Yunbi Girl
en: Sondung. It’s always Sondung.

blocks.html: Two Yunbi men drag Satek Sondung off the wall by the ankles. His sleeves are empty. He says he came to pray. Nobody believes him, and every guard at the foot of the rock runs over to not believe him in person.
blocks.ko: 연비 집 사내 둘이 사택손등의 발목을 잡아 담에서 끌어 내린다. 소매는 비었다. 기도하러 왔다고 한다. 아무도 믿지 않는다. 그래서 바위 밑의 보초들이 죄다 몰려가 직접 안 믿어 준다.

en: I came to pray! Can’t a man pray in his own city?
lines: 기도하러 왔소! 제 도성에서 기도도 못 하오?

blocks.html: On the rock, the monk’s lamp moves. Then it stops moving.
blocks.ko: 바위 위에서 스님의 등불이 움직인다. 그러다 멈춘다.

en: Highness. The monk opened the box.
Did he now. For which house?
He has a seal. He used it once. He closed the box.
lines: 도장이 있습니다. 한 번 찍었습니다. 함을 닫았습니다.

en: Ha! Once. An honest thief.
Will you tell the lords?
Nobody asked me.
…Ha. No. Nobody ever does.

blocks.html: At the far end of the rock, Satek Jijuk has not moved all night. He sits on the bottom step with his hands in his sleeves, where every guard in Sabi can see him, doing nothing as hard as he can.
blocks.ko: 바위 저쪽 끝에서 사택지적은 밤새 꼼짝도 하지 않았다. 맨 아랫단에 소매에 손을 넣고 앉아 있다. 사비의 보초란 보초가 다 볼 수 있는 자리에서, 있는 힘껏 아무것도 하지 않고 있다.

blocks.html: Toward dawn the river mist climbs the hill. The salt in the stone drinks it. By first light the whole rock is beaded and running, as if it had been working hard all night.
blocks.ko: 새벽녘 강 안개가 언덕을 오른다. 돌에 밴 소금이 그것을 빨아들인다. 첫 햇살이 들 무렵, 바위 전체가 송골송골 젖어 흘러내린다. 밤새 일이라도 한 것처럼.

blocks.label: Dawn
blocks.ko: 새벽

blocks.speaker: On the stair
en: The rock’s sweating. Look— the rock’s sweating!
It ain’t never done that.
Then heaven’s been at it all night.
lines: 바위가 땀을 흘린다. 봐— 바위가 땀을 흘려!

blocks.html: King Mu climbs the rock himself, which a king his age should not, and breaks his own seal. The box is damp right through. He takes the slips out one at a time and opens them on his knee.
blocks.ko: 무왕이 몸소 바위를 오른다. 그 나이의 왕이 할 일은 아니다. 제 봉인을 뜯는다. 함은 속까지 축축하다. 쪽지를 하나씩 꺼내 무릎 위에서 편다.

blocks.html: Lord Jinmo: a name, and nothing else. Lord Jinmo sits down.
blocks.ko: 진모 공: 이름 하나, 그뿐이다. 진모 공이 주저앉는다.

blocks.html: Elder Yunbi: a seal, fresh and red, and the damp has got into it. It has bled across the paper like a nosebleed. You cannot tell whose seal it was. You can barely tell whose name.
blocks.ko: 연비 원로: 도장 하나. 갓 찍은 붉은 도장인데 습기가 스며들었다. 코피처럼 종이 위로 번졌다. 누구 도장인지 알 수가 없다. 누구 이름인지도 겨우 알아본다.

blocks.html: Satek Jijuk: folded three times, small and tight. Inside, over the name, sits a seal mark, crisp and dry, as if it had been there for days. Nobody on the benches knows the seal. Heaven, apparently, has its own.
blocks.ko: 사택지적: 세 번, 작고 단단하게 접혀 있다. 펼치니 이름 위에 도장 자국이 하나 앉아 있다. 또렷하고 말라 있다. 며칠은 거기 있었던 것처럼. 걸상 위의 누구도 그 도장을 알아보지 못한다. 하늘에게도 제 도장이 있나 보다.

en: Well, well. Heaven’s marked two.
One of them it didn’t like much.
lines: 하나는 영 마음에 안 드셨나 보다.

en: Majesty, that slip has been tampered—
Which one?

blocks.html: Elder Yunbi opens his mouth and shuts it again. To say which slip was tampered with, he would have to say how he knows. Four houses’ worth of money is standing behind him, and not one of them wants to hear that sentence.
blocks.ko: 연비 원로가 입을 열었다 도로 닫는다. 어느 쪽지에 손을 댔는지 말하려면, 자기가 그걸 어떻게 아는지도 말해야 한다. 그의 뒤엔 가문 넷의 돈이 서 있다. 그 말을 듣고 싶어 하는 집은 하나도 없다.

en: …Neither, Majesty.
Heaven has terrible handwriting.

blocks.html: Satek Jijuk climbs to the chair in damp sleeves. Behind him the benches make the noise a room makes when it has been robbed and cannot report it.
blocks.ko: 사택지적이 젖은 소매로 의자까지 오른다. 그 뒤에서 걸상들이 소리를 낸다. 도둑을 맞고도 신고를 못 하는 방이 내는 소리다.

blocks.label: The Bottom Step
blocks.ko: 맨 아랫단

blocks.html: Afterwards Elder Yunbi finds him alone on the bottom step, wringing out a sleeve.
blocks.ko: 나중에 연비 원로는 맨 아랫단에 혼자 앉아 소매를 짜고 있는 그를 찾아낸다.

en: The sea water.
Salt drinks mist. Stone sweats. Fresh seal paste runs.
Mine was stamped three days ago, with a seal nobody owns. It’s in the river now. It had time to dry.
lines: 소금은 안개를 먹소. 돌은 땀을 흘리고. 갓 찍은 인주는 번지지.
내 건 사흘 전에 찍었소. 주인 없는 도장으로. 그 도장은 지금 강바닥에 있소. 마를 시간이 있었지.

en: You knew I’d pay the monk.
lines: 내가 중한테 돈 줄 걸 알았구려.

en: Everyone paid the monk. I paid him least.
I only asked him to do exactly what you paid for.
lines: 다들 중한테 돈을 줬소. 나는 제일 적게 줬고.
당신이 돈 낸 그대로 하라고만 했소.

en: And your cousin on the wall?
He thinks he went over it for the house. Let him.
lines: 제 딴엔 집안 위해 넘은 줄 알 거요. 그렇게 두시오.

en: We don’t hold the sleeve, Satek. We hold the arm.
Remember that, Prime Minister.
lines: 우리는 소매를 쥐지 않소, 사택. 팔을 쥐지.

en: Noted.

blocks.html: From that morning the Satek bring brine to every vote, and the rock sweats for them for twenty-five years. Nobody ever writes down why. Nobody has to.
blocks.ko: 그날 아침부터 사택 집은 표결 때마다 소금물을 들고 오고, 바위는 스물다섯 해 동안 그들을 위해 땀을 흘린다. 아무도 그 이유를 적지 않는다. 적을 필요가 없다.

blocks.label: The Bet
blocks.ko: 내기

en: Well? Who won?
You did, Father. The Satek.
…How did you know?
I didn’t. I knew Yunbi would pay. A man who’s paid stops watching the weather.
Go feed my horses. And keep an eye on the one with wet sleeves. He’ll serve you well, right up until he doesn’t.
lines: 몰랐지. 연비가 돈 쓸 건 알았다. 돈 낸 놈은 날씨를 안 봐.
가서 내 말 먹여라. 그리고 소매 젖은 저놈 잘 봐 둬라. 잘 섬길 거다. 안 섬길 때까지는.

en: Ha!
Gyebek. You saw the monk. Did you see the salt?
lines: 계백. 넌 중을 봤지. 소금도 봤느냐?

en: Yes. At sunset.
I did not know it was a weapon.
Neither did Yunbi. That’s what made it one.
lines: 연비도 몰랐지. 그래서 무기가 된 거다.

blocks.html: Down the hill the crowd has heard. Somebody starts the old chant, because a Satek has won and the Satek like to think they wrote it. Restore the reign of the thirteenth Eraha! By noon the Yunbi are chanting it too.
blocks.ko: 언덕 아래 사람들도 소식을 들었다. 누군가 그 옛 구호를 시작한다. 사택이 이겼고, 사택은 그 구호를 자기네가 지었다고 믿고 싶어 하니까. 열세 번째 어라하의 시대를 다시! 한낮이 되자 연비 사람들도 따라 외친다.

blocks.html: Eight houses had to cheat a rock to agree on one Prime Minister. They agree on that dead king for free. Why? To find out, we go back three hundred years…!
blocks.ko: 여덟 가문은 상좌평 하나에 뜻을 모으려고 바위까지 속여야 했다. 그 죽은 임금에게는 공짜로 뜻을 모은다. 왜일까? 알려면 삼백 년을 거슬러 가야 한다…!

logline.en: A Baekje king marches north, and a Goguryeo king dies on his own wall. In seven hundred years, it never happens again.
logline.ko: 백제 임금이 북으로 진군하고, 고구려 임금이 제 성벽 위에서 죽는다. 칠백 년 동안 다시는 없는 일이다.

images.prompt: CLOSING STILL of the episode: the final scene of this story as it ends (not the next episode). The line: “Goguryeo remembers it too, and differently, and for exactly as long. The boy from the wall lives to be old. He tells it to his grandsons, and they tell theirs.” Context: Restore the reign of the thirteenth Eraha. They will still be chanting that sentence three centuries later, in a courtyard, to a clever king who has already decided that a country is a story. It is the sentence that gets Daeya burned. Goguryeo remembers it too, and differently, and for exactly as long. The boy from the wall lives to be old. He tells it to his grandsons, and they tell theirs. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — PLACE Pyongyang (평양성) — attached board /pl_pyongyang_city.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Pyongyang: Goguryeo walled city on the Taedong, stone walls and red munru gate pavilions. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Baekje’s thirteenth king marches north to Pyongyang. A Goguryeo king dies on his own wall. In seven hundred years, it never happens again.
blocks.ko: 백제의 열셋째 임금이 북쪽 평양으로 진군한다. 고구려 임금이 제 성벽 위에서 죽는다. 칠백 년 동안, 그런 일은 다시 없다.

blocks.caption: The king every later Baekje king quotes when he wants to sound brave.
blocks.ko: 후대 백제 임금들이 용감해 보이고 싶을 때마다 들먹이는 임금.

blocks.html: The north’s capital, and a long walk for anyone who wants it.
blocks.ko: 북쪽의 수도. 탐내는 자에겐 먼 길이다.

blocks.caption: Baekje at its height.
blocks.ko: 백제의 전성기.

blocks.html: Baekje has the river, the coast and the sea roads east. The clans take the docks. The throne takes a cut. It is the richest kingdom in Samhan, and the strongest. Neither lasts.
blocks.ko: 백제는 강과 해안과 동쪽 뱃길을 쥐고 있다. 가문들은 부두를 갖고, 왕좌는 몫을 뗀다. 삼한에서 가장 부유하고 가장 강한 나라다. 둘 다 오래가지 않는다.

blocks.html: What its king wants is the one thing Baekje doesn’t have: the north’s capital. One winter he takes thirty thousand men up the frozen roads to get it.
blocks.ko: 임금이 원하는 건 백제에 없는 단 하나, 북쪽의 수도다. 어느 겨울 그는 군사 삼만을 이끌고 얼어붙은 길을 올라 그것을 가지러 간다.

blocks.label: The Camp
blocks.ko: 진영

blocks.html: The night before, the Baekje king sits by a fire on the south bank with his son, the crown prince. Across the water is the wall. The boy has never seen a city this big and is trying not to show it.
blocks.ko: 그 전날 밤, 백제 임금은 강 남쪽 기슭 모닥불 곁에 아들과 앉아 있다. 물 건너편에 성벽이 있다. 태자는 이렇게 큰 성을 처음 보고, 티를 내지 않으려 애쓰는 중이다.

blocks.speaker: The Crown Prince
en: They have a wall, Father. A real one. And a king on it.
lines: 성벽이 있습니다, 아바마마. 진짜 성벽이요. 그 위엔 임금두 있구요.

en: Good. I’d hate to walk this far for an empty one.
Nobody from the south has ever stood on that wall. Our grandsons will want to know who was first.
lines: 잘됐다. 빈 성 볼라구 이 먼 길 왔으믄 서운헐 뻔혔어.
남쪽 사람이 저 성벽에 서 본 적은 한 번두 없다. 손자들이 누가 처음이었는지 알고 싶어 헐 겨.

blocks.speaker: The Crown Prince
en: And if he won’t come down?
Then he’s braver than I am, and we’ll find out what that’s worth.
lines: 그럼 나보다 용감헌 거지. 그게 얼마짜리인지 알게 되겄지.

blocks.label: The Wall
blocks.ko: 성벽

blocks.html: At first light the Baekje army wades the river and comes at the wall. On the wall of Pyongyang there is a Goguryeo boy with a bow and not enough arrows. Beside him, in the same frozen mud, is his king.
blocks.ko: 동이 트자 백제군이 강을 건너 성벽으로 몰려온다. 평양 성벽 위에 활은 있고 화살은 모자란 고구려 소년 하나가 있다. 그 옆, 같은 언 진흙 위에 그의 임금이 있다.

blocks.speaker: A Goguryeo Archer
en: Majesty, get down— they’ve found the range—

blocks.speaker: The Goguryeo King
en: So have we.
A king who climbs off his wall teaches the whole wall to climb off. Shoot.
lines: 임금이 성벽에서 내려가면, 성벽 전체가 내려가는 법을 배운다. 날래 쏴라.

blocks.html: The arrow that finds him isn’t aimed at anyone. It comes over the parapet the way rain does. He sits down in the mud as if he had decided to.
blocks.ko: 그를 찾아온 화살은 누구를 겨눈 것도 아니다. 비가 오듯 성가퀴를 넘어온다. 그는 그러기로 마음먹은 사람처럼 진흙 위에 주저앉는다.

blocks.speaker: The Goguryeo King
en: …Don’t tell them.
Not till they’re away home. Keep shooting.

blocks.html: The boy tells no one. The gate stays shut. Below it, the Baekje king hears the wailing start inside the walls, and knows exactly what that sound is.
blocks.ko: 소년은 누구에게도 말하지 않는다. 성문은 닫힌 채다. 그 아래에서 백제 임금은 성 안에서 곡소리가 시작되는 걸 듣고, 그게 무슨 소리인지 정확히 안다.

en: That’s a king’s funeral.
…Turn them around. We came for a city. We’re going home with something better.
lines: ……돌려라. 성 하나 얻으러 왔는디, 그보다 나은 걸 갖구 돌아간다.

blocks.speaker: The Crown Prince
en: Father, the gate would have opened by spring. Why are we going home?
lines: 아바마마, 봄이면 성문이 열렸을 겁니다. 왜 돌아갑니까?

en: Listen.

blocks.html: Down the column, the men are already singing about it.
blocks.ko: 행렬 저 뒤에서 병사들은 벌써 그 일을 노래하고 있다.

blocks.html: Winter, tenth month. The king of Baekje came with thirty thousand men and attacked Pyongyang. The king led his troops out to meet them and was struck by a stray arrow. He died on the twenty-third day of that month.
blocks.ko: 겨울 10월, 백제 왕이 군사 3만을 이끌고 와서 평양성을 공격하였다. 왕이 군사를 내어 막다가 흐르는 화살에 맞았다. 이달 23일에 세상을 떠났다.
blocks.hanja: 冬十月，百濟王帥兵三萬，來攻平壤城。王出師拒之，為流矢所中。是月二十三日，薨。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 18, Goguryeo Annals — King Gogugwon, yr. 41 (371)

blocks.html: Back in the south they give him a chant, and the chant outlives everything else he won.
blocks.ko: 남쪽으로 돌아가자 사람들은 그에게 구호 하나를 바친다. 그 구호는 그가 얻은 다른 모든 것보다 오래 산다.

en: Restore the reign of the thirteenth Eraha.

blocks.html: They will still be chanting that sentence three centuries later, in a courtyard, to a clever king who has already decided that a country is a story. It is the sentence that gets Daeya burned.
blocks.ko: 삼백 년 뒤에도 사람들은 어느 마당에서 그 문장을 외치고 있을 것이다. 나라란 하나의 이야기라고 이미 결론 내린 영리한 임금 앞에서. 대야성을 불태우는 것이 바로 그 문장이다.

blocks.html: Goguryeo remembers it too, and differently, and for exactly as long. The boy from the wall lives to be old. He tells it to his grandsons, and they tell theirs.
blocks.ko: 고구려도 그것을 기억한다. 다르게, 그리고 꼭 그만큼 오래. 성벽 위의 그 소년은 늙도록 산다. 손자들에게 그 이야기를 하고, 손자들은 또 제 손자들에게 한다.

blocks.html: North, then, three hundred years on, to the snow and Goguryeo’s most frightening commander. First question: do you know what happens to traitors…?
blocks.ko: 이제 북으로, 삼백 년 뒤의 눈 속으로, 고구려에서 가장 무서운 장수에게로. 첫 질문이다. 반역자가 어떻게 되는지 아느냐…?

logline.en: Everyone in the north has a story about the Eternal General. None of them are bedtime stories.
logline.ko: 북쪽 사람이라면 누구나 영원의 대장군 이야기를 하나씩 안다. 자장가로 들려줄 만한 건 하나도 없다.

images.alt: A Mohe boy holds a stick against Yeon Gesomun’s chest in a burnt doorway
images.prompt: Worm’s-eye from beside a burnt doorway in a Mohe village at dusk in falling snow: a small Mohe boy with a shaved crown and two braids holds a stick against the breastplate of Yeon Gesomun, huge in red-edged armor and red cape, who has just dismounted; his red-bay horse Damul stands behind him. The stick touching his chest is the device, one short line between them. Ash and snow, a roofless charred timber frame, embers glowing under the snow at the lower right as the key light raking up across the boy’s face and the steel. No jougwan; Yeon wears no helmet. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | DAMUL (다물, gesomun's horse) — attached board /obj_damul.png: The biggest horse on any field: a red-bay Goguryeo war stallion, coat a deep BROWN-RED like oxblood lacquer (browner and darker than Hadong, redder and larger than Bisamun), a thick BLACK mane and BLACK tail, black lower legs, heavy arched neck — match the board. In battle it wears Goguryeo 개마 (gaema) barding as in the Anak Tomb No. 3 mural: steel lamellar skirts over the body and neck, a steel chamfron on the face, red cords and a red plume; the black mane falls over the steel. Named for 다물 (多勿), the old Goguryeo word for winning back the lost land; charges into water and spears without being asked, bites other horses. | GULGUL — FACE and garments from attached /ch_dae_gulgul_young.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Mohe-born, lean and weathered; dark skin, hard narrow eyes, thin moustache and a short chin beard as a man. Dress: Goguryeo border warden: grey steel lamellar under a heavy white-grey fur mantle, dark-red sash and wrapped forearms. Now: Boy (stage portrait ch_dae_gulgul_young): BEARDLESS, shaved crown with one dark centre strip, two long braids, blood-streaked defiant face, ragged fur over a white wrap. Demeanor: Grim and spare. Says little, watches the door, stands one step behind whoever he serves. #8b3a3a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: a Goguryeo court robe; a crown. | PLACE Eastern Hall (연씨 동부산성) — attached board /pl_yeon_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. CANON — PLACE Chek Fortress (책성) — attached board /pl_yeon_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.
