blocks.html: Everyone in the north has a story about the Eternal General. None of them are bedtime stories.
blocks.ko: 북쪽 사람이라면 누구나 영원의 대장군 이야기를 하나씩 안다. 자장가로 들려줄 만한 건 하나도 없다.

blocks.label: The Eastern Outpost
blocks.ko: 동부 초소

blocks.html: This one starts in the snow, two winters after Silla crowned its queen. A young man is caught on the border and dragged to Commander Yeon, who is twenty-nine and holds the east in his father’s name.
blocks.ko: 이 이야기는 눈 속에서 시작한다. 신라가 여왕을 세우고 두 번째 겨울이다. 국경에서 붙잡힌 청년 하나가 연 장군에게 끌려온다. 스물아홉, 아버지의 이름으로 동쪽을 쥔 사내다.

blocks.caption: Twenty-nine. He holds the eastern border in his father’s name, and nobody here calls him a son.
blocks.ko: 스물아홉. 아버지의 이름으로 동쪽 국경을 쥐고 있고, 여기서 그를 아들이라 부르는 이는 없다.

en: Do you know what happens to traitors, young man...?
They say you… leaked our secrets to the enemy.

blocks.speaker: Prisoner
en: I have… no name.
Good. Then nobody will miss it.

blocks.html: It is over quickly, and it is not clean. Nobody in the yard looks away, because looking away is also a report.
blocks.ko: 금방 끝났고, 깔끔하지 않았다. 마당에 선 누구도 눈을 돌리지 않는다. 눈을 돌리는 것 또한 보고가 되니까.

blocks.html: The guards talk about him the way men talk about weather. “He’s a monster, you know. He’s made the Eastern Commandery the safest in the kingdom. The barbarians run if they hear his name.”
blocks.ko: 경비병들은 날씨 얘기하듯 그를 입에 올린다. “저 사람 괴물이야, 알지? 동부 도호부를 나라에서 제일 안전한 데로 만들어 놨잖아. 오랑캐들은 이름만 들어도 도망간다니까.”

blocks.html: Gesomun*, also called Gegum. His surname was Yeon. He claimed he had been born in water, to awe the crowd. He was imposing to look at, and bold and free in spirit.
blocks.ko: 개소문*은 개금이라고도 한다. 성은 연씨이다. 스스로 물속에서 태어났다고 말하여 무리를 현혹하였다. 풍채가 웅장하고 위엄 있었으며, 기개가 호방하였다.
blocks.hanja: 蓋蘇文，或云蓋金。姓淵氏。自云生水中，以惑衆。儀表雄偉，意氣豪逸。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 49, Biographies — Yeon Gaesomun

notes.html: The Korean annals spell him Gesomun. This book says Gesomun. One man, five swords.
notes.ko: 기록의 개소문이 곧 이 책의 연개소문이다. 영어 표기만 다르다.

blocks.html: The outpost is also a building site. Three summers ago, the West flattened Goguryeo’s pile of enemy bones. It is the same emperor who sent Silla’s new queen flowers with no scent. Goguryeo got the message. Now it builds a wall. A thousand li of it. When Yeon isn’t killing anybody, he walks it with a plumb line and kicks the crooked stones.
blocks.ko: 초소는 공사장이기도 하다. 세 해 전 여름, 당이 고구려의 적군 뼈 무덤을 밀어 버렸다. 신라의 새 여왕에게 향 없는 꽃을 보낸 바로 그 황제다. 고구려는 알아들었다. 그래서 지금 성을 쌓는다. 천 리나. 연은 누굴 죽이지 않을 때면 다림줄을 들고 그 성을 걸으며 삐뚤어진 돌을 걷어찬다.

blocks.label: The Burned Village
blocks.ko: 불탄 마을

blocks.html: A month before the summons, in a Mohe village the Eastern Command has finished with, there is a boy who will not move out of the doorway of a house that no longer has a roof. Snow is settling on the ash. He has a shaved crown and two braids, and he holds a stick the way he has seen men hold spears. Yeon gets down off the red bay and walks up until the stick touches his chest.
blocks.ko: 소집령이 오기 한 달 전, 동부대가 일을 마치고 떠난 말갈 마을에, 지붕이 없어진 집 문간에서 비키지 않는 사내아이가 하나 있다. 재 위로 눈이 내려앉는다. 정수리를 밀고 머리를 두 갈래로 땋은 아이가, 어른들이 창 잡는 걸 본 대로 막대기를 쥐고 서 있다. 연은 붉은 밤색 말에서 내려, 막대기 끝이 가슴에 닿을 때까지 걸어온다.

en: Move.

blocks.caption: A Mohe boy Yeon pulled out of the snow. He has followed him ever since.
blocks.ko: 연이 눈 속에서 끌어낸 말갈 소년. 그 뒤로 줄곧 그를 따른다.

en: Don’t come any closer!
Do you understand me.
This is my house. You go.

blocks.html: The boy is speaking Mohe. A grandchild of that tongue will one day be called Manchu, and an empire will stamp it on its coins. Today nobody in the yard knows a word of it, and Commander Yeon is not a man who lets that stop him.
blocks.ko: 아이는 말갈 말을 하고 있다. 그 말의 손주뻘 되는 말이 훗날 만주어라 불리고, 한 제국의 동전에 새겨진다. 오늘 이 마당에선 아무도 그 말을 한마디도 모른다. 그리고 연 장군은 그런 걸로 멈출 사람이 아니다.

lines: 기래, 안다. 네 집이디. 좋은 집이다.
en: Aye, I ken. Your house. Fine house.
Bit short on roof.
Go!
Gene. Grand. Gene yourself.

blocks.html: Nobody in that yard understands anybody. Yeon looks at him for what his officers later agree was an unreasonable length of time. Then he laughs, the slap of a laugh they will learn to dread, and pulls off his gloves.
blocks.ko: 그 마당에선 아무도 서로 알아듣지 못한다. 연은 부하들이 뒷날 지나치게 길었다고 입을 모으는 시간 동안 아이를 본다. 그러다 웃는다. 부하들이 두려워하게 될, 뺨을 치는 듯한 웃음이다. 그러고는 장갑을 벗는다.

lines: 이놈 보라우. 다 타 버린 집을 디키구 섰구만.
en: Look at this wee one. Guarding a house that’s already burned.
Good. This is what Goguryeo looks like.
Get on. The second horse.

blocks.html: He hands the gloves down. They do not fit. The boy gets on the second horse anyway, the stick still in his fist.
blocks.ko: 장갑을 내려 준다. 맞지 않는다. 아이는 그래도 막대기를 쥔 채 두 번째 말에 오른다.

blocks.caption: An old Yeon friend. The one man at the outpost who asks the commander questions.
blocks.ko: 연의 오랜 벗. 초소에서 장군에게 질문을 하는 단 한 사람.

en: …You are taking him?

lines: 저 아이레 크면 어드메 서 있을 거 같네?
en: Where do you think that boy is standing when he is grown.
…Opposite us, I should think.
That is why I am taking him.

blocks.html: He gives him the name Gulgul, which is not a Goguryeo name and is not a Mohe one either, and raises him in Pyongyang alongside his own sons — one step behind them at every meal.
blocks.ko: 그는 아이에게 걸걸이라는 이름을 준다. 고구려 이름도 아니고 말갈 이름도 아니다. 그리고 평양에서 제 아들들과 함께 기른다. 끼니마다 아들들보다 한 걸음 뒤에서.

blocks.label: The Long Wall
blocks.ko: 긴 성벽

blocks.html: Three weeks later the boy still has no Goguryeo, but he has a job. He carries the plumb bob, in both hands, a step behind Yeon, as if it might hatch.
blocks.ko: 세 주 뒤, 아이는 아직 고구려 말을 한마디도 못 하지만 일거리는 생겼다. 다림추를 든다. 두 손으로, 연의 한 걸음 뒤에서, 무슨 알이라도 되는 것처럼 받쳐 든다.

blocks.html: The levy gangs on this stretch watch him come the way you’d watch weather.
blocks.ko: 이 구간의 일꾼 패들은 그가 오는 걸 날씨 보듯 본다.

blocks.speaker: Levy
lines: 보디 말라우. 보는 걸 다 안대.
en: That’s him. The East.
Don’t look. He kens when you look.

blocks.speaker: Another levy
lines: 데 말갈 꼬맹이는 뭘 들고 다니네?
en: What’s the wee Mohe carrying?

blocks.speaker: Levy
lines: 다림줄이다. 그걸 돌에 대 보구, 그다음에 걷어찬대.
en: His string. He hangs it off your stones, and then he kicks them.

blocks.html: Yeon stops. He holds out a hand without looking, and the boy puts the bob in it. The line drops against a stone in the third course and hangs clear of its face by a thumb. Yeon kicks the stone out of the wall. It is the fourth this morning.
blocks.ko: 연이 멈춘다. 보지도 않고 손을 내밀자, 아이가 다림추를 올려놓는다. 줄이 셋째 단의 돌 하나에 드리워지고, 돌 면에서 엄지 한 마디만큼 떨어져 흔들린다. 연이 그 돌을 걷어차 빼낸다. 오늘 아침에만 네 번째다.

en: Stone.
Aye. Very good. Whatever that was.

blocks.speaker: Another levy
en: What’s the wee one saying, sir?

lines: 모른다. 눈밭에서부터 쭉 떠든다. 기래두 대꾸는 해 준다. 우린 잘 지낸다.
en: No idea. He’s been talking since the snow. I answer him anyway. We get on fine.
Put that back. Straight.

blocks.html: The gang groans and goes after the stone. Yeon walks on along the wall, the boy a step behind him with the bob back in both hands.
blocks.ko: 일꾼 패가 끙 소리를 내며 돌을 주우러 간다. 연은 성벽을 따라 계속 걷고, 아이는 다림추를 다시 두 손에 받쳐 들고 한 걸음 뒤를 따른다.

blocks.label: The North Wall
blocks.ko: 북쪽 성벽

blocks.html: On the north wall, in a winter worse than this one, Yeon stands with the grown boy a step behind him and the river frozen white below. He says the thing he says every winter, to anyone in earshot, as if the cold might forget it otherwise.
blocks.ko: 이번보다 더 혹독한 겨울, 북쪽 성벽 위에 연이 서 있다. 다 큰 아이가 한 걸음 뒤에 있고, 아래로는 강이 하얗게 얼어 있다. 연은 겨울마다, 듣는 사람만 있으면 누구에게나 하는 말을 한다. 추위가 잊어버리기라도 할 것처럼.

en: Cold?
…No, sir.

lines: 우리 임금 한 분이 여기서 돌아가셨다. 백제 화살이었디. 기래도 성은 버텼다.
기억해라. 왕은 죽고, 조정은 지치고, 성은 무너져도—
en: Liar. I’m cold too.
A king of ours died up here once. Baekje arrow. The wall held anyway.
Remember it. Kings die, courts get tired, walls come down—
Goguryeo never dies.

blocks.html: Gulgul grows up quiet. Years from now, Yeon will send him north to guard the marches and give him a surname to take along. Dae. Big, as big as the country.
blocks.ko: 걸걸은 조용히 자란다. 훗날 연은 그를 북쪽 변경으로 보내며 성 하나를 붙여 준다. 대. 나라만큼 크라는 뜻이다.

blocks.label: The Summons
blocks.ko: 소집령

blocks.html: Back in that first winter, the summons comes. The summons isn't addressed to him. It's addressed to his father, who still holds the Eastern seal. Yeon Tejo sat in the capital's big chair for twelve years. Now he is too old to ride that far. The son has done the work for years. The seal is still the old man's.
blocks.ko: 다시 그 첫 겨울. 소집령이 온다. 소집령은 그에게 온 게 아니다. 아직 동부의 인장을 쥔 아버지에게 왔다. 연태조는 도성의 큰 자리에 열두 해를 앉아 있었다. 이제는 거기까지 말을 탈 수 없을 만큼 늙었다. 일은 몇 해째 아들이 해 왔다. 인장은 아직 노인의 것이다.

blocks.caption: The old Eastern Commander. He sat in the big chair long enough to know what it costs.
blocks.ko: 늙은 동부 대가. 큰 자리에 오래 앉아 봐서, 그 값을 안다.

lines: 인장 가져가라. 올해는 네레 내 자리에 앉는다.
en: Take the seal. You sit in my place this year.
…And say half of what you think.

lines: 제가요? 평양엔 제가 왜 가야 합니까?
어차피 쓸데없는 소리나 하려고 주둥이 벌리는 데인데...
en: Me? Why do I have to go to Pyongyang?
It’s a place where mouths open only to say useless things…

lines: 안다. 내가 열두 해를 앉아 있었다.
지금은 구세사가 그 자리에 있다. 우리 집안 먼 친척인데, 왕의 사람이다. 너를 조카라 부르구 다정하게 굴 거다. 기게 더 나쁘다.
en: I know. I sat in it for twelve years.
Gusesa chairs it now. A cousin of ours, far off, and the king’s man. He’ll call you nephew and be kind to you. That’s worse.
Half, son. Half.

blocks.html: He leaves at first light. The boy is at the stable door before him, in gloves that still don’t fit, holding the red bay’s bridle as if somebody had asked him to.
blocks.ko: 그는 첫새벽에 떠난다. 아이가 먼저 마구간 문 앞에 와 있다. 아직도 안 맞는 장갑을 끼고, 누가 시키기라도 한 것처럼 붉은 말의 고삐를 쥐고.

lines: 안 된다. 넌 남아. 도수류가 밥 멕여 줄 거다.
en: No. You stay. Dosuryu feeds you.
Don’t bite him.
I want to go.

lines: 여전히 뭔 소린지 모르갓다. 기래두 안 된다.
en: Still no idea. Still no.

blocks.html: Every morning for a month Yeon has asked him the same question, the way you’d ask a horse, and never once waited for an answer.
blocks.ko: 한 달 내내 아침마다 연은 아이에게 같은 걸 물었다. 말한테 묻듯이. 대답을 기다린 적은 한 번도 없다.

en: Cold?
…Cold.

lines: 방금 그거 말이네? 말한 거 맞디?
en: Was that a word? Did he just say a word?
He said cold.
…Aye. Me too, wee man. Me too.

blocks.html: He rides out laughing. Dosuryu has to hold the boy back by the collar for the whole length of the road.
blocks.ko: 연은 웃으면서 떠난다. 도수류는 길이 다 보이지 않을 때까지 아이의 뒷덜미를 붙잡고 있어야 한다.

blocks.html: He promised his father half. First there is a month of road, a wife seven months gone, and five roofs to explain to a boy who doesn’t speak the language…!
blocks.ko: 아버지께 반만 하겠다고 했다. 그 전에 한 달 길이 있고, 일곱 달 된 아내가 있고, 말도 안 통하는 아이에게 설명해야 할 지붕 다섯이 있다…!

logline.en: A month of road, a wife seven months gone, and five roofs that each think they hold up the house.
logline.ko: 한 달의 길, 일곱 달 된 아내, 그리고 저마다 집을 떠받친다고 믿는 지붕 다섯.

blocks.html: Goguryeo has one king and five roofs. The roofs were here first.
blocks.ko: 고구려에는 임금이 하나, 지붕이 다섯 있다. 지붕이 먼저 있었다.

blocks.title: Chek Fortress to Pyongyang
blocks.caption: A month of road. Two rivers, one old capital, and a pass that doesn’t care who you are.
blocks.ko: 한 달 길. 강 둘, 옛 도읍 하나, 그리고 누가 지나가든 상관 않는 고개 하나.

blocks.label: The Cart
blocks.ko: 수레

blocks.html: Yeon meant to ride south with six men and be in Pyongyang in twelve days. Then his wife told him she was coming.
blocks.ko: 연은 사내 여섯을 데리고 남쪽으로 달려 열이틀 만에 평양에 닿을 셈이었다. 그때 아내가 자기도 가겠다고 했다.

blocks.caption: Seven months gone. Twice the Eastern hall has made a cradle and put it away again.
blocks.ko: 일곱 달째. 동부의 집은 요람을 두 번 짰다가 두 번 치웠다.

blocks.html: This time she wants the old Yeon house in Pyongyang: the midwife who caught Yeon himself, and a painting of the birth goddess that three generations of Yeon women have rubbed pale with their hands.
blocks.ko: 이번에는 평양의 연씨 옛집에서 낳겠다고 한다. 연을 받아 낸 산파가 거기 있고, 연씨 집안 여자들이 삼 대째 손으로 쓸어 빛바랜 삼신 그림이 거기 걸려 있다.

en: A month of road. In a cart. In the thaw.
You’ll be sick at every rut.
lines: 한 달 길이다. 수레로. 얼음 풀릴 때.

en: Then drive round the ruts.
…Not in this fort. This fort has bad luck.
lines: …이 성에선 안 낳아요. 이 성은 운이 나빠요.

blocks.html: So the Eastern Commander goes to the High Summit at the pace of an ox. Six riders, one covered cart, a spare horse, and a junior soldier walking at the cart’s wheel, because somebody has to, and in the East it is always him.
blocks.ko: 그래서 동부 대가는 소걸음으로 제가회의에 간다. 기병 여섯, 덮개 수레 하나, 여벌 말 한 필, 그리고 수레바퀴 옆을 걷는 말단 군사 하나. 누군가는 걸어야 하고, 동부에서는 늘 그다.

blocks.html: He is twenty-four, a mason’s son from the hill farms under the fortress. One of his eyes looks where he looks. The other wanders off on business of its own.
blocks.ko: 스물넷, 성 아래 산골 석수장이의 아들이다. 한쪽 눈은 그가 보는 곳을 본다. 다른 쪽은 제 볼일을 보러 딴 데로 간다.

blocks.html: On the first morning Yeon loads the cart himself, grain sacks at the back. By the time he has his gloves on, the sacks are at the front.
blocks.ko: 첫날 아침, 연이 손수 수레에 짐을 싣는다. 곡식 자루는 뒤쪽에. 장갑을 다 끼고 보니 자루가 앞쪽에 가 있다.

en: Who moved my sacks.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Me, sir. Weight over the axle.
Else the back end bucks in a rut, and your lady with it.
lines: 내래 옮겼습네다. 무게는 굴대 위에 실어야 합네다.
안 기러면 바퀴 자국에서 뒤가 튑네다. 마님도 같이요.

en: Did I ask?

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: No, sir. The ruts will.
…Which one of those is looking at me?

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Both, sir. Always both.

blocks.html: Yeon has a thousand men and knows almost none of their names. He doesn’t ask this one’s either. By the second day he is calling him Eye.
blocks.ko: 연에게는 군사가 천이고, 이름을 아는 이는 거의 없다. 이 사내 이름도 묻지 않는다. 이틀째부터는 그냥 ‘눈’이라고 부른다.

blocks.html: That night a rider comes up the road behind them in the dark. It is Dosuryu, with the Mohe boy in front of him on the saddle and two neat sets of teeth marks on his wrist.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 어둠 속에서 말 한 필이 뒤따라 올라온다. 도수류다. 안장 앞에 말갈 아이를 태웠고, 손목에는 가지런한 잇자국이 두 벌 나 있다.

en: He bit me. Twice.
You told me not to let him. Nobody told him.
lines: 너는 물리지 말라 기랬디. 쟤한테는 아무도 말 안 했어.

en: So you brought him.
He was already walking. Barefoot. In that.
lines: 벌써 걷고 있었어. 맨발로. 이 눈밭을.

blocks.html: Yeon’s wife lifts the cart flap and looks at the boy for a long moment. Then she moves her feet to make room. Gulgul climbs in without a word in any language. By morning he is asleep against her belly, the baby is kicking him, and neither of them seems to mind.
blocks.ko: 연의 아내가 수레 덮개를 들추고 아이를 한참 본다. 그러고는 발을 옮겨 자리를 낸다. 걸걸은 어느 나라 말로도 아무 말 없이 기어 들어간다. 아침이 되자 아이는 그녀의 배에 기대 잠들어 있고, 배 속 아기는 그를 걷어차고 있고, 둘 다 별로 개의치 않는 눈치다.

blocks.label: The Singing Ice
blocks.ko: 우는 얼음

blocks.html: Five days south, the road meets a river frozen white from bank to bank. The headman of the nearest village swears by it. It held his ox at New Year.
blocks.ko: 남쪽으로 닷새, 길이 강과 만난다. 이 기슭부터 저 기슭까지 하얗게 얼었다. 가까운 마을 촌장이 장담한다. 설날에 자기 소가 건넜다는 것이다.

en: Then it holds a cart. Across.

blocks.html: The soldier called Eye is lying flat on the ice with one ear pressed to it.
blocks.ko: ‘눈’이라 불리는 군사가 얼음 위에 납작 엎드려 한쪽 귀를 대고 있다.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Not here, sir. Listen. It’s singing.
There’s water running under. Down by the reeds it’s quiet.
lines: 여기는 안 됩네다. 들어 보십시오. 얼음이 웁네다.
밑으로 물이 흐릅네다. 저 아래 갈대 있는 데는 조용합네다.

en: Ice doesnae sing. The man’s ox crossed here.
lines: 얼음이 무슨 울어. 데 사람 소가 여기로 건넜대.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: At New Year, sir. It’s been a warm month.
lines: 설날에요, 장군님. 그 뒤로 한 달 내내 따뜻했습네다.

en: The ice is crying.

blocks.html: Yeon looks at the headman. The headman finds something interesting in the reeds. Yeon sends the spare horse over first, at the spot he chose, to prove a point.
blocks.ko: 연이 촌장을 본다. 촌장은 갈대숲에서 갑자기 볼 것이 생긴다. 연은 제 말이 옳다는 걸 보이려고, 자기가 고른 자리로 여벌 말부터 건너보낸다.

blocks.html: Ten paces out, the ice opens like a mouth. The horse goes in to the neck. Yeon goes in after it to the chest, in his boots and his commander’s coat, and hauls it out by the bridle with his own two hands, swearing the whole time in a voice that carries to the next village.
blocks.ko: 열 걸음쯤에서 얼음이 입처럼 벌어진다. 말이 목까지 빠진다. 연이 장화에 대가의 외투를 입은 채 가슴까지 뛰어들어, 제 두 손으로 굴레를 잡아 끌어낸다. 그동안 내내 욕을 하는데, 그 소리가 옆 마을까지 간다.

blocks.html: When he climbs out, the cart is already across. The soldier walked the ox over by the reeds while everyone was watching the horse.
blocks.ko: 그가 기어 나와 보니 수레는 이미 건너가 있다. 모두가 말을 보는 사이, 그 군사가 갈대 쪽으로 소를 몰고 건너간 것이다.

en: You crossed without my order.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Aye, sir. Your lady was in it.
Next time you disobey me, I’ll have your head.
lines: 다음에 또 내 명을 어기면 네 목을 치갔다.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Aye, sir. Next time I’m wrong, have it.
lines: 예, 장군님. 다음에 제가 틀리면 치십시오.

blocks.html: Inside the cart, Yeon’s wife laughs for the first time in a month. Yeon stands dripping on the bank and decides, for reasons he will not explain, not to hear it.
blocks.ko: 수레 안에서 연의 아내가 한 달 만에 처음으로 웃는다. 연은 강가에 물을 뚝뚝 흘리며 서서, 설명할 생각도 없는 이유로 못 들은 척하기로 한다.

blocks.label: The Hill Farms
blocks.ko: 산골 마을

blocks.html: South of the river the road runs through farms the Mohe used to visit every winter. They haven’t visited in three years. The farms know exactly whose doing that is.
blocks.ko: 강 남쪽으로 길은 산골 마을들을 지난다. 말갈이 겨울마다 들르던 마을들이다. 삼 년째 오지 않는다. 그게 누구 덕인지 마을들은 똑똑히 안다.

blocks.html: They come out for him. Children run beside the red bay. Women push rice cakes into the cart until Yeon’s wife starts passing them out the other side.
blocks.ko: 사람들이 그를 보러 나온다. 아이들이 붉은 말 옆을 따라 뛴다. 아낙들이 수레 안으로 떡을 밀어 넣는데, 하도 많아서 연의 아내가 반대편으로 도로 내주기 시작한다.

blocks.speaker: Old farmer
en: Commander! Three winters and not one roof burned!
Take a hen. Take two. Take my grandson, he eats too much!
lines: 장군님! 세 겨울째 지붕 하나 안 탔습네다!
닭 가져가시라요. 두 마리 가져가시라요. 내 손주도 가져가시라요, 너무 많이 먹습네다!

en: Keep the hen. Feed the boy. I’ll want him in ten years.
lines: 닭은 두라. 아이나 먹이라우. 십 년 뒤에 데려가갔다.

blocks.html: Behind the crowd, in every village, there are also the doors that stay shut.
blocks.ko: 그리고 마을마다, 사람들 뒤쪽에는 끝내 열리지 않는 문들도 있다.

blocks.speaker: Woman at a door
en: That’s him. The one from the black-river village.
Bring the wee one in.
lines: 데 사람이야. 검은 강 마을 일 한 사람.

blocks.speaker: Her neighbour
en: He’s no going to eat him, Ok-nyeo.

blocks.speaker: Woman at a door
en: I said bring him in.

blocks.speaker: Old man on a bench
en: My grandson rode with him last winter. Came home fine.
Doesnae talk now. Not a word, since.
lines: 내 손주가 지난겨울에 데 사람 따라갔디. 멀쩡히 돌아왔어.
기런데 말을 안 해. 기 뒤로 한마디도.

blocks.html: Gulgul watches the shut doors from the cart. He has seen a village from the other side.
blocks.ko: 걸걸은 수레에서 닫힌 문들을 본다. 그는 마을이라는 걸 반대편에서 본 적이 있다.

en: And the doors?
Doors are fine. A door means the house is still standing.
lines: 문은 괜찮아. 문이 있다는 건 집이 아직 서 있다는 기야.

blocks.label: The Log
blocks.ko: 통나무

blocks.html: In a pass of fir and rock there is a log across the road, and behind it a dozen men with picks.
blocks.ko: 전나무와 바위뿐인 고개에 통나무 하나가 길을 막고 있고, 그 뒤에 곡괭이를 든 사내 열둘이 있다.

blocks.html: They are not Mohe. They are Goguryeo farm sons in the quilted jackets the wall gangs wear, and they have been living in the trees since autumn.
blocks.ko: 말갈이 아니다. 성벽 부역 패가 입는 누비저고리를 걸친 고구려 농사꾼 아들들이다. 가을부터 숲에서 살았다.

blocks.speaker: Deserter
en: Leave the cart and walk on. Nobody gets hurt.
…Is that— that’s the East’s banner.
lines: 수레 두고 걸어가라. 아무도 안 다친다.

blocks.html: It goes about as well for them as you’d expect. Eye drops the first one with a stone the size of a fist, thrown sidearm, the way a mason’s boy learns on a scree slope. Yeon’s riders do the rest without drawing.
blocks.ko: 그들에게는 짐작한 만큼 일이 풀린다. ‘눈’이 주먹만 한 돌을 옆으로 던져 첫째를 쓰러뜨린다. 석수장이 아들이 돌비탈에서 배우는 솜씨다. 나머지는 연의 기병들이 칼도 안 뽑고 끝낸다.

blocks.html: Yeon has the twelve kneeling in the snow when the county magistrate comes up the pass at a trot, waving a scroll with a royal seal on it.
blocks.ko: 연이 열둘을 눈밭에 꿇려 놓았을 때, 고을 현령이 왕의 인장이 찍힌 두루마리를 흔들며 종종걸음으로 고개를 올라온다.

blocks.speaker: Magistrate
en: Commander! Commander, they’re pardoned!
His Majesty’s New Year amnesty. Every man who ran from the wall and goes home is forgiven. Every one.
lines: 폐하의 설날 대사면입네다. 성벽에서 도망쳤어도 집에만 돌아가면 다 용서한다 하셨습네다. 하나도 빠짐없이.

en: They didn’t go home. They went into the trees with picks.
lines: 집에 안 갔어. 곡괭이 들고 숲에 들어갔디.

blocks.speaker: Magistrate
en: Then they’re going home now. His Majesty is merciful.
lines: 그럼 이제 가면 됩네다. 폐하께서는 자비로우십네다.

en: His Majesty builds a wall a thousand li long, and forgives every man who walks off it.
…Fine. Pardoned. Good. A pardoned man can carry stone.
Walk them back to the wall. All twelve. If one of them goes home on the way, he’s pardoned, and you can tell his mother where we buried him.
lines: 폐하께서는 천 리짜리 성을 쌓으시면서, 거기서 도망치는 놈은 다 용서하시는구만.
…좋다. 사면. 좋아. 사면받은 놈도 돌은 나를 수 있디.
성벽으로 도로 끌고 가라. 열둘 다. 가는 길에 하나라도 집에 가면, 그놈은 사면이다. 묻은 데는 네가 어미한테 알려 주라우.

blocks.html: The magistrate rolls his scroll back up very slowly, the way you’d put away a toy in front of a dog.
blocks.ko: 현령이 두루마리를 아주 천천히 도로 만다. 개 앞에서 장난감을 치우는 사람처럼.

blocks.html: Twelve men walk back north with two of Yeon’s riders behind them. None of them goes home on the way.
blocks.ko: 사내 열둘이 연의 기병 둘을 뒤에 달고 북쪽으로 도로 걷는다. 가는 길에 집에 간 놈은 하나도 없다.

blocks.label: Gungnae
blocks.ko: 국내성

blocks.html: The old capital, on the Amnok. Kings lived here for four hundred years. Now it keeps their tombs, and the tombs are bigger than the houses.
blocks.ko: 압록강 가의 옛 도읍. 임금들이 사백 년을 살았다. 지금은 그 무덤을 지키는데, 무덤이 집보다 크다.

blocks.html: On the twentieth day the road drops into the Amnok valley. A square stone wall stands on the near bank with the mountain fort behind it, and across the plain rise stepped stone tombs as tall as hills, as if the old kings wanted to be found.
blocks.ko: 스무날째, 길이 압록강 골짜기로 내려선다. 가까운 기슭에 네모난 돌성이 서 있고 그 뒤로 산성이 있다. 들판 건너에는 언덕만 한 계단식 돌무덤들이 솟아 있다. 옛 임금들이 꼭 찾아 주길 바랐던 것처럼.

blocks.html: Among them stands a stone taller than three men, rough as a cliff, with writing cut into all four faces. Yeon gets down and drops his plumb line against it. The string hangs flat to the stone all the way down.
blocks.ko: 그 사이에 사람 셋 키보다 높은 돌 하나가 서 있다. 벼랑처럼 거칠고, 네 면 모두에 글이 새겨져 있다. 연이 말에서 내려 다림줄을 댄다. 줄이 처음부터 끝까지 돌에 딱 붙어 내려간다.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Who set that one, sir?
A king who didnae pay anybody.

blocks.html: He does not kick it. Gulgul runs his fingers along the carved characters, as if they might turn into Mohe if he reads them fast enough.
blocks.ko: 그는 걷어차지 않는다. 걸걸이 새겨진 글자를 손가락으로 따라 훑는다. 빨리 읽으면 말갈 말이 될지도 모른다는 듯이.

blocks.label: Five Stones
blocks.ko: 돌 다섯

blocks.html: That night they camp under the tombs. Yeon, who has never explained anything to anyone, decides to explain Goguryeo to a boy who doesn’t speak the language.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그들은 무덤 아래서 야영한다. 평생 누구에게도 무엇을 설명해 본 적 없는 연이, 말도 안 통하는 아이에게 고구려를 설명하기로 한다.

blocks.html: He puts five stones on the ground by the fire.
blocks.ko: 그가 모닥불 옆 땅바닥에 돌 다섯 개를 놓는다.

en: Five roofs. Listen.
Back in Jolbon, before there was a Goguryeo, there were five tribes in one valley. Crow, horse, cow, pig, dog.
Every tribe had a ka. A chief. The crow was us.
lines: 졸본 시절, 고구려가 생기기도 전에, 한 골짜기에 부족 다섯이 있었디. 까마귀, 말, 소, 돼지, 개.
부족마다 가가 하나씩 있었어. 족장. 까마귀가 우리였디.

en: Crow.
Aye! Crow! You see? He gets it.
He’s said that at every crow since the river. It’s his word for crow, not yours.
lines: 강 건넌 뒤로 까마귀만 보면 기래. 쟤네 말로 까마귀란 거디, 네 말 알아들은 게 아니고.

en: Same thing.

blocks.hanja: 五族
blocks.html: Five roofs in one valley. Each tribe had its own ka, its own herds and its own grudges. Men in the far north named their chiefs after their herds, so four of the five were the horse, the cow, the pig and the dog. The crow was the valley’s own.
blocks.ko: 한 골짜기에 지붕 다섯. 부족마다 제 가가 있고, 제 가축이 있고, 제 원한이 있었다. 먼 북쪽 사람들은 족장을 제 가축 이름으로 불렀다. 그래서 다섯 가운데 넷이 말, 소, 돼지, 개다. 까마귀만은 그 골짜기 토박이다.

blocks.html: Then he picks up a sixth thing, a pine cone, and sets it on top of the pile.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 여섯째 것, 솔방울 하나를 집어 돌무더기 위에 얹는다.

en: And the king. The king’s house sits on top of the five.
It came over the river and married in. Then it stayed.
lines: 기리고 임금. 임금 집안은 다섯 위에 앉아 있디.

en: You’ve skipped six hundred years.
I’m getting there.
The five got bigger. They moved, swallowed their neighbours, took river names. Not animals any more.
Five tribes still. Not the same five.
lines: 다섯이 커졌디. 옮겨 다니고, 이웃을 삼키고, 강 이름을 달았어. 이젠 짐승이 아니야.
여전히 다섯 부족이디. 같은 다섯은 아니고.

head: Jolbon · 졸본
Goguryeo · 고구려
Now · 지금
rows: Crow · 까마귀
Hwanna · 환나부
East · 동부
Cow · 소
Biryuna · 비류나부
West · 서부
Pig · 돼지
Gwanna · 관나부
South · 남부
Dog · 개
Yeonna · 연나부
North · 북부
Horse · 말
Gyeru, the king’s own · 계루부, 임금의 부
Inner · 내부

en: And now they’re not tribes either.
Now they’re commanderies. Five Commanderies. East, West, South, North, and the Inner one round the palace.
The ka got bigger with them. Now he’s a Deka. A Commander. Like my father. Tomorrow, like me.
lines: 이젠 부야. 다섯 부. 동부, 서부, 남부, 북부, 기리고 대궐 둘레 내부.
가도 같이 커졌디. 이젠 대가라 부른다. 우리 아바이처럼. 내일은 나처럼.

blocks.name: Native words
blocks.ko: 우리말
blocks.note: Goguryeo’s own words, older than any character the West wrote them in.
blocks.noteKo: 고구려 사람들 제 말이다. 서쪽 사람들이 갖다 붙인 어느 글자보다도 오래됐다.

en: The Inner one sits in the middle. Whoever’s High Commander sits there.
lines: 내부는 가운데 앉디. 막리지가 누구든 거기 앉아.

en: …Deka.
Don’t teach him that one.
Tell him the rest.
What rest.
That the kings used to come from another roof, until it went soft. It still keeps its own ancestor shrine. As if it might be needed again.
lines: 임금이 원래는 다른 지붕에서 났다는 거요. 그 지붕이 물러지기 전까지는. 지금도 자기네 조상 사당을 따로 모셔요. 언제 또 쓰일지 모른다는 듯이.

en: The West. Aye. That’s why the West never starts anything. It’s waiting.
lines: 서부. 기래. 기래서 서부는 아무 일도 안 벌이는 기야. 기다리는 거디.

en: And the North gives the kings their wives.
I didnae forget the North. I was hoping.
lines: 북부 잊은 거 아니야. 잊고 싶었디.

blocks.html: She is right, and so is the record. The far west wrote the five roofs down once, under names no roof answers to. It got the kings right.
blocks.ko: 그녀 말이 맞고, 기록도 맞다. 먼 서쪽 사람들이 한번 이 지붕 다섯을 적어 둔 적이 있다. 어느 지붕도 대답하지 않는 이름으로. 임금 이야기만은 맞게 적었다.

blocks.html: From the beginning there were five clans: the Yeonno, the Jeolno, the Sunno, the Gwanno and the Gyeru. At first the Yeonno gave the king. They grew weak, and now the Gyeru have taken their place. … The Yeonno were once lords of the country. Though they no longer give the king, their rightful chief may still be called Gochu-ga, and they may keep their own ancestral shrine. … The Jeolno marry the kings, generation after generation.
blocks.ko: 본래 다섯 족이 있으니 연노부·절노부·순노부·관노부·계루부이다. 본래 연노부에서 왕이 나왔으나 점점 약해져서 지금은 계루부가 대신한다. … 연노부는 본래 나라의 주인이었으므로, 지금은 왕이 되지 못하나 그 적통 대인은 고추가라 일컬을 수 있고, 또한 종묘를 세울 수 있다. … 절노부는 대대로 왕과 혼인한다.
blocks.hanja: 本有五族，有涓奴部、絶奴部、順奴部、灌奴部、桂婁部。本涓奴部爲王，稍微弱，今桂婁部代之。…涓奴部本國主，今雖不爲王，適統大人，得稱古雛加，亦得立宗廟。…絶奴部世與王婚。
blocks.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms (三國志) bk. 30, Wei — Eastern Barbarians, Goguryeo

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Sir. Every Deka keeps his own men, aye? Our names go up to the king, but we stand behind the king’s men. Never in the same row.
lines: 장군님. 대가마다 자기 사람을 따로 둔다 했디요? 우리 이름은 임금께 올라가도, 줄은 임금 사람들 뒤에 섭네다. 한 줄에는 절대 안 서고요.

en: Aye. So?

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: So whose man am I, sir? The king’s, or yours?
lines: 기럼 저는 누구 사람입네까? 임금님 사람입네까, 장군님 사람입네까?

en: Mine.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: And whose are you?

blocks.html: Dosuryu stops chewing. Yeon looks at the soldier for an unreasonably long time.
blocks.ko: 도수류가 씹던 걸 멈춘다. 연이 그 군사를 터무니없이 오래 쳐다본다.

en: …Goguryeo’s.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Then I’m Goguryeo’s too, sir. Same as you.
lines: 기럼 저도 고구려 사람입네다, 장군님. 장군님이랑 똑같이요.

blocks.html: Yeon laughs, the slap of a laugh, and throws the pine cone at him. Years from now he will wish he had asked the man’s name that night, when it would have been easy.
blocks.ko: 연이 철썩 하는 그 웃음을 터뜨리고 솔방울을 그에게 던진다. 여러 해 뒤, 그는 그날 밤 그 사내 이름을 물어 둘 걸 그랬다고 생각하게 된다. 그날 밤이라면 쉬웠을 텐데.

blocks.label: The Ferry
blocks.ko: 나루

blocks.html: In the morning the Amnok is breaking up. Plates of grey ice the size of threshing floors turn slowly in the current and knock together like slow drums.
blocks.ko: 아침이 되자 압록강 얼음이 깨지고 있다. 타작마당만 한 잿빛 얼음판들이 물살에 천천히 돌며, 느린 북처럼 서로 부딪친다.

blocks.speaker: Ferryman
en: Can’t take a cart in that, Commander. Not on this raft.
His Majesty let the ferry tax go three years running. Kind man. Very kind.
So nobody’s mended the raft in three years.
lines: 저기로 수레는 못 건넵네다, 대가님. 이 뗏목으로는요.
폐하께서 나룻세를 삼 년째 안 받으셨습네다. 인자하신 분이디요. 아주 인자하셔.
기래서 삼 년째 뗏목 고친 사람이 없습네다.

blocks.html: Eye spends the morning lashing new crossbeams to the raft with the cart’s spare rope. Yeon spends it on the bank with the plumb line, telling him every lashing is crooked. They cross at noon with poles, between two plates of ice, and Yeon’s wife holds Gulgul’s hand the whole way and pretends it is for his sake.
blocks.ko: ‘눈’이 오전 내내 수레의 여벌 밧줄로 뗏목에 새 가로대를 묶는다. 연은 오전 내내 강가에서 다림줄을 들고 매듭마다 삐뚤어졌다고 한다. 정오에 그들은 장대를 짚어 얼음판 두 장 사이로 건넌다. 연의 아내는 내내 걸걸의 손을 잡고 있고, 그게 아이를 위해서인 척한다.

blocks.html: Halfway over, the ferryman tells them the rest of the news from the capital. He tells it the way ferrymen tell everything, to the water.
blocks.ko: 강 한복판에서 뱃사공이 도읍 소식을 마저 전한다. 뱃사공들이 늘 그러듯, 물에다 대고.

blocks.speaker: Ferryman
en: Six years back His Majesty sent the Western emperor a map. Of us. Every river, every fort.
A present, they said. The emperor had caught some khan.
lines: 육 년 전에 폐하께서 서국 황제한테 지도를 보내셨답네다. 우리 지도요. 강이란 강, 성이란 성 다.
선물이라 했답네다. 황제가 무슨 가한을 잡았다고.

en: A map.
…Of us.

blocks.speaker: Ferryman
en: And when he was new on the throne he sent ten thousand Western prisoners home. Fed them first. Very kind.
lines: 기리고 즉위하시고 얼마 안 돼서 서국 포로 만 명을 돌려보내셨디요. 배불리 먹여서. 아주 인자하셔.

blocks.html: Yeon says nothing for the rest of the crossing. Dosuryu, who has known him since he was six, moves to the far end of the raft.
blocks.ko: 연은 건너는 내내 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 그가 여섯 살 때부터 알아 온 도수류가 뗏목 반대쪽 끝으로 옮겨 간다.

blocks.label: The Pass
blocks.ko: 고개

blocks.html: Beyond the Amnok the road climbs for eight days through hills that have not heard it is spring. On the sixth, in a late snow, the cart’s axle cracks.
blocks.ko: 압록강 너머로 길은 여드레를 오른다. 봄이 온 줄도 모르는 산들이다. 엿새째, 늦눈 속에서 수레 굴대가 갈라진다.

blocks.html: Then Yeon’s wife makes a sound inside the cart that every man on the road understands.
blocks.ko: 그때 수레 안에서 연의 아내가 소리를 낸다. 길 위의 사내라면 누구나 알아듣는 소리다.

en: Not here. Not— Dosuryu, how far’s the next village?
lines: 여기서는 안 돼. 안— 도수류, 다음 마을까지 얼마네?

en: Two days. With a wheel.
…It’s not him. Not yet.
He kicks when the road is bad. Tell the road.

blocks.html: Yeon tells the road, loudly, in words the hill farms will be using for a generation. Eye, meanwhile, has walked up the slope, chosen a young pine, felled it with a borrowed axe, and is shaving it square with the axe-head turned sideways.
blocks.ko: 연이 길한테 말한다. 크게, 산골 마을들이 한 세대 동안 써먹을 말로. 그사이 ‘눈’은 비탈을 올라가 어린 소나무 하나를 골라, 빌린 도끼로 베어서는, 도낏날을 옆으로 뉘어 모나게 깎고 있다.

en: What’s that.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Axle, sir. Pine’s soft. It’ll get her to Pyongyang and not a step further.
lines: 굴대입네다, 장군님. 소나무는 무릅네다. 마님을 평양까지는 모셔다 드리고, 한 발짝도 더는 못 갑네다.

en: …Is it straight?

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: No, sir. It’s leaning. It’ll hold.

blocks.html: Yeon doesn’t get the plumb line out. That night in the cart, with the lamp low, his wife asks him the question she has been saving since the fortress.
blocks.ko: 연은 다림줄을 꺼내지 않는다. 그날 밤 수레 안, 등잔불을 낮춘 채, 아내가 성을 떠날 때부터 아껴 둔 질문을 한다.

en: Your father said half. Will you say half?
lines: 아버님이 반만 말하라 하셨죠. 반만 말할 거예요?

en: …No.
Then come home before they find a reason.
And don’t give him a poem for a name. Something he can carry.
lines: 그럼 그 사람들이 핑계를 찾기 전에 돌아와요.
그리고 아기 이름에 시 같은 거 넣지 마요. 아이가 지고 다닐 수 있는 걸로.

blocks.html: Gulgul is asleep against her, as usual. In his sleep he says the one word of Goguryeo he owns.
blocks.ko: 걸걸은 여느 때처럼 그녀에게 기대 잠들어 있다. 잠결에 자기가 가진 고구려 말 한 마디를 한다.

en: …Cold.
I know, little one. Me too.

blocks.label: The Last Ridge
blocks.ko: 마지막 고개

blocks.html: On the thirty-second day they come over the last ridge, and below them is the Taedong, wide and brown with the thaw, and on it Pyongyang: walls inside walls, smoke from ten thousand roofs, and a red two-tier gate you can see from a day away.
blocks.ko: 서른이틀째, 마지막 고개를 넘자 발아래 대동강이 보인다. 해빙에 넓고 누렇게 불었다. 그 위에 평양이 있다. 성안에 또 성, 만 개 지붕에서 오르는 연기, 하루 거리에서도 보이는 붉은 이층 문루.

blocks.html: On the road below, the capital has heard the Eastern banner is coming. Some people have come out to cheer. Some have come out to look. From up here you can’t tell which is which, and that, Yeon decides, is Pyongyang all over.
blocks.ko: 아래 길에서는 도읍 사람들이 동부 깃발이 온다는 소식을 들었다. 환호하러 나온 이도 있고, 구경하러 나온 이도 있다. 여기서는 어느 쪽이 어느 쪽인지 알 수가 없다. 연은 그게 바로 평양이라고 생각한다.

en: Eye. You walk the cart to the old house. Then come to the palace yard and hold the horses.
lines: 눈. 수레 몰고 옛집까지 가라. 기러고 궁 마당으로 와서 말 잡고 있으라우.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Aye, sir. Which yard, sir?
The one with a wall in it. You’ll find something wrong with it.
lines: 담 있는 마당. 거기서 뭐든 틀린 걸 찾아낼 기야.

blocks.html: Yeon’s wife pulls the flap back and looks at the city for a long time, one hand on her belly, the other on the Mohe boy’s head. Then she lets it fall.
blocks.ko: 연의 아내가 덮개를 젖히고 한참 도시를 본다. 한 손은 배 위에, 한 손은 말갈 아이 머리 위에. 그러고는 덮개를 내린다.

blocks.html: He promised his father half. Tomorrow, five roofs and a king find out what half sounds like…!
blocks.ko: 그는 아버지에게 반만 하겠다고 약속했다. 내일, 지붕 다섯과 임금 하나가 그 반이 어떤 소리인지 듣게 된다…!

images.at: there were five tribes in one valley
images.alt: Five chieftains in silhouette sit around one fire in a valley ring, each under a totem of his tribe: crow, horse, cow, boar, dog
images.prompt: Symbolic poster still. Five tribes in one valley, long ago at Jolbon. A packed-earth ring at the bottom of a narrow river valley between black ink mountains; around ONE fire in the centre FIVE chieftains in black silhouette sit or crouch in a wide ring, five poses (one standing and pointing, one with arms crossed, one leaning on a spear, one drinking from a horn, one half turned away); behind each a tall totem pole topped by his animal (a crow, a horse head, cow horns, a boar, a dog); the five animals loom again as smoke on the ridgeline in a crimson #c8322a sky. Ink black, crimson, bone-white haze. Every man not wearing a crown or helm wears the jougwan of the attached cap diagram: a small black peaked cap tied under the chin with TWO long barred pheasant tail feathers splayed upward in a V (shape only, ignore the labels). Women wear hair in a low bun with a long pin, no cap. Painterly Korean ink painting (sumukhwa) meets graphic film poster: splashed ink, dry-brush, hanji grain, hard flat black silhouettes against a luminous painted sky; no faces, no text, no seal, no watermark. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop: nothing important at the top or bottom edge.

Every man not wearing a crown or helm wears the jougwan of the attached cap diagram: a small black peaked cap tied under the chin with TWO long barred pheasant tail feathers splayed upward in a V (shape only, ignore the labels). Women wear hair in a low bun with a long pin, no cap. Painterly Korean ink painting (sumukhwa) meets graphic film poster: splashed ink, dry-brush, hanji grain, hard flat black silhouettes against a luminous painted sky; no faces, no text, no seal, no watermark. images.alt: Goguryeo has one king and five roofs. The roofs were here first.
images.prompt: OPENING STILL of the episode: the first image the reader sees, staging its first line. The line: “Goguryeo has one king and five roofs. The roofs were here first.” Context: Goguryeo has one king and five roofs. The roofs were here first.   A wide or medium establishing frame that hooks. CANON — PLACE Chek Fortress (책성) — attached board /pl_yeon_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

The line: “Yeon’s wife pulls the flap back and looks at the city for a long time, one hand on her belly, the other on the Mohe boy’s head. Then she lets it fall.” Context: Aye, sir. Which yard, sir? The one with a wall in it. You’ll find something wrong with it. Yeon’s wife pulls the flap back and looks at the city for a long time, one hand on her belly, the other on the Mohe boy’s head. Then she lets it fall. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | PLACE Chek Fortress (책성) — attached board /pl_yeon_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). COMMONERS in every Samhan kingdom wear SIMPLE WHITE: plain undyed white or off-white hemp and ramie jackets, wide trousers and skirts, a cloth sash, straw sandals or bare feet, hair in a plain topknot or braid — no dyed silk, no dots, no gold; colour belongs to rank, so a crowd of farmers, porters, servants and townsfolk reads as a field of soft white cloth with the officials' colours standing out of it. Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Half, his father said. Yeon manages it until the second pot of tea.
blocks.ko: 반만, 아버지는 그렇게 말했다. 연은 두 번째 차 주전자까지는 그럭저럭 해낸다.

blocks.label: Pyongyang
blocks.ko: 평양

blocks.label: Pyongyang · the High Summit
blocks.ko: 평양 · 제가회의

blocks.html: Five commands ride in at the red two-tier gate that week. Pyongyang has heard stories about every one of them, and puts on its good clothes to check.
blocks.ko: 그 주에 다섯 군단이 붉은 이중 문루로 들어온다. 평양은 그들 모두에 관한 얘기를 들어 왔고, 확인하러 좋은 옷을 꺼내 입는다.

blocks.html: Goguryeo works like this. Five commanders argue at the High Summit. The High Commander holds the first sword. The king has the last word.
blocks.ko: 고구려는 이렇게 돌아간다. 제가회의에서 대가 다섯이 다툰다. 막리지가 첫 칼을 쥔다. 마지막 말은 왕이 한다.

blocks.hanja: 諸加會議
blocks.html: The meeting of the ka. A ka was a tribal chief, back when Goguryeo was five roofs in one valley. The roofs became commands, the chiefs became generals, and the meeting kept its old name, the way old men keep their nicknames.
blocks.ko: 가(加)들의 모임. 가는 고구려가 한 골짜기의 지붕 다섯이던 시절의 부족장이다. 지붕은 군단이 되고, 족장은 장군이 됐지만, 모임은 옛 이름을 그대로 썼다. 노인들이 어릴 적 별명을 버리지 않듯이.

blocks.label: The Gate
blocks.ko: 대문

blocks.html: Before the principals sit, the gate gets its look. The commanders arrive by rank, each by his own road, and half of Pyongyang finds an errand that runs past it.
blocks.ko: 주인들이 자리에 앉기 전에, 대문이 먼저 구경을 한다. 대가들은 서열대로, 저마다 제 길로 들어오고, 평양 사람 절반은 그 길을 지나는 심부름거리를 찾아낸다.

blocks.html: The North comes first, on a Khitan horse. He took it off a Khitan, and he will tell you so.
blocks.ko: 북부가 먼저 온다. 거란 말을 타고. 거란 놈한테서 뺏은 말이고, 묻지 않아도 그렇게 말해 준다.

blocks.speaker: Gate guard
en: Is that him? The one that eats Khitans?

blocks.speaker: Old gate guard
lines: 말만 먹디. 거란 놈들은 장사할 때 쓰구.
거기서 스무 해 겨울을 나고도 귀가 둘 다 붙어 있다. 지나갈 때 세 보라우.
en: Only their horses. He keeps the Khitans for trade.
Twenty winters up there and he’s still got both ears. Count them when he passes.

blocks.caption: The Northern Commander. He holds the steppe edge against the Khitans and wants horses, not poems.
blocks.ko: 북부 대가. 초원 끝에서 거란을 막는다. 시 말고 말을 원한다.

lines: 들어갈 때 내 말 세 두라우.
나올 때 같은 숫자 볼 거다.
en: Somebody count my horses going in.
I want the same number coming out.

blocks.html: The West comes second, grey with the dust of the longest road in the kingdom.
blocks.ko: 서부가 두 번째로 온다. 나라에서 제일 긴 길의 먼지를 뒤집어써 잿빛이다.

blocks.speaker: Kitchen maid
en: Which one’s that?

blocks.speaker: Water carrier
lines: 서부 대가. 요하에 앉아서 한족을 지킨다.
데 사람들이 이번 주엔 왕조를 뭐라 부르는디 몰라두.
en: The West. He sits on the Liao and watches the Han.
Whatever they’re calling their dynasty this week.

blocks.speaker: Kitchen maid
en: They say he’s never lost a fort.

blocks.speaker: Water carrier
lines: 성 밖에 나와 본 적두 없디.
en: He’s never left one, either.

blocks.caption: The Western Commander. He has held the Liao against the Han his whole life, mostly by not starting anything.
blocks.ko: 서부 대가. 평생 요하에서 한족을 막았다. 주로 아무 일도 벌이지 않는 방식으로.

blocks.html: The South comes third, to drums. The king has sent his own chamberlain down to the gate to meet him. Nobody else got a chamberlain.
blocks.ko: 남부는 세 번째로, 북소리와 함께 온다. 왕이 시종장을 대문까지 내려보내 그를 맞는다. 다른 누구도 시종장은 못 받았다.

blocks.speaker: Gate guard
en: Look at that. A chamberlain. For the South.

blocks.speaker: Old gate guard
lines: 남부는 한 손으루 백제, 한 손으루 신라를 친다.
전하께서 둘 다 갖고 싶으시디. 기러니끼니 남부는 시종장을 받는 거다.
en: The South fights Baekje with one hand and Silla with the other.
His Majesty wants both. So the South gets a chamberlain.

blocks.speaker: Kitchen maid
lines: 김유신이랑 칼을 맞대 봤다는 거 참말이네?
en: Is it true he’s crossed swords with Kim Yushin?

blocks.speaker: Old gate guard
lines: 맞대 봤디. 끝장을 못 봤을 뿐이디.
en: Crossed. Not finished.

blocks.caption: The Southern Commander. Baekje on one side, Silla on the other, and the king’s whole heart riding in his saddlebags.
blocks.ko: 남부 대가. 한쪽엔 백제, 한쪽엔 신라. 왕의 마음은 통째로 그의 안장 주머니에 실려 온다.

en: His Majesty is well? Good.
Tell him I brought a map, not a speech.

blocks.html: Yeon comes last, in his father’s place, with Dosuryu and six riders. The cart has gone on to the old house. It is his first time through this gate with a seal in his saddlebag. Nobody here has seen his face since it grew a beard.
blocks.ko: 연은 맨 끝에, 아버지 대신, 도수류와 기병 여섯을 데리고 온다. 수레는 옛집으로 먼저 갔다. 안장 주머니에 인장을 넣고 이 문을 지나는 건 처음이다. 수염이 난 뒤로 그의 얼굴을 본 사람은 여기 아무도 없다.

blocks.speaker: Gate guard
lines: 동부 깃발이다. 늙은 연 대가 인장.
en: Eastern banner. Old Yeon’s seal.
That’s never old Yeon.

blocks.speaker: Old gate guard
en: His boy. The one that kills Mohe.
He’s smaller than the stories.

blocks.speaker: Gate guard
en: Everybody’s smaller than the stories.

blocks.speaker: Old gate guard
lines: 내래 저 집 할아버지 때부터 이 문을 지켰다. 기게 막리지였디.
말 한마디 없이 쳐다만 봐. 네가 수긍할 때까지.
en: I held this gate for his grandfather. Now there was a High Commander.
Never said a word. Just looked at you till you agreed.

blocks.speaker: Gate guard
en: This one’s looking at us.

blocks.speaker: Old gate guard
lines: 기래. 근데 이 사람은 말을 할 거다.
en: Aye. But this one’s going to talk.

blocks.speaker: Palace steward
lines: 수행원은 마당에서 기다리시오. 대가께서는 들어가셔도 되오.
en: Aides wait in the yard. Your commander may go through.

lines: 우리 대가는 집에서 무릎을 앓고 계시다.
en: My commander’s at home with his knees.
I’m what he sent.

blocks.speaker: Palace steward
lines: 동부는 상 말석이오. 칼은 대문에 두시고, 부를 때까지 기다리시오.
en: …Of course. Forgive me.
The East sits at the foot of the table. Your sword stays at the gate, and you wait to be called.
The foot of the table. Your grandfather would’ve—
Fine. I’ll sit where I’m put.
For now.

blocks.label: The Horse Wall
blocks.ko: 말 매는 담

blocks.html: So Yeon waits in the yard with the horses. A low dry-stone wall runs along it for tying reins to. A southern horse has kicked the top course loose, and somebody has already put it back.
blocks.ko: 그래서 연은 마당에서 말들과 함께 기다린다. 마당을 따라 고삐 매는 낮은 돌담이 있다. 남부 말 한 마리가 윗단을 걷어차 빠뜨렸는데, 누가 벌써 도로 앉혀 놓았다.

blocks.html: Yeon has brought a plumb line to Pyongyang. Of course he has. He drops it against the stone, and it hangs clear of the face by a thumb.
blocks.ko: 연은 평양까지 다림줄을 챙겨 왔다. 당연하다. 그 돌에 줄을 드리우자, 돌 면에서 엄지 한 마디만큼 떨어져 흔들린다.

en: Who laid this.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Me, sir.
…Of course it was.
It’s crooked. Take it out.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
lines: 삐뚠 게 아닙네다. 기대 있는 겁네다.
산 쪽으로요. 돌은 눕고 싶어 하니끼니, 눕고 싶은 쪽으로 기대 놓으면 버팁네다. 우리 아바지가 담 쌓던 사람입네다.
en: It’s no crooked, sir. It’s leaning.
Into the hill. A stone wants to lie down, so you let it lean where it wants, and it holds. My da laid walls.

lines: 너네 아바지 여기 없다. 줄이 삐뚤다는데.
en: Your da’s not here. The string says crooked.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
lines: 외람되디만, 데 줄은 평생 돌 한 번 져 본 적이 없습네다.
en: With respect, sir, the string’s never carried a stone in its life.

blocks.html: One of the southern grooms laughs. Then he notices nobody else is laughing, and turns it into a cough that fools no one.
blocks.ko: 남부 마부 하나가 웃는다. 그러다 아무도 따라 웃지 않는 걸 알아채고, 아무도 안 속는 기침으로 바꾼다.

blocks.html: Yeon looks at the soldier. The soldier looks back with one eye. The other has wandered off toward the palace on business of its own.
blocks.ko: 연이 병사를 본다. 병사는 한쪽 눈으로 마주 본다. 다른 쪽 눈은 제 볼일 보러 궁 쪽으로 가 있다.

lines: 오늘은 어느 눈으로 날 보고 있네?
en: Which one’s looking at me today?

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Both, sir. Always both.

blocks.html: Yeon kicks the stone. On the long wall at home he has kicked a good many stones out. This one stays where it is, and something in his boot makes a small sound that nobody is going to mention.
blocks.ko: 연이 돌을 걷어찬다. 집 쪽 긴 성벽에서는 걷어차 빼낸 돌이 한둘이 아니다. 이놈은 꿈쩍도 않고, 그의 장화 속에서 뭔가 작은 소리가 난다. 그 얘기를 꺼낼 사람은 아무도 없다.

en: …Leave it.
You. Name.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: It’s—

blocks.speaker: Palace steward
en: Eastern Command! The antechamber!

blocks.html: Yeon goes in limping slightly, with a face that dares anyone to ask. The soldier goes back to the horses. Yeon never forgets an insult. He has walked beside this man for a month without asking his name, and he won’t think to ask again for eleven years.
blocks.ko: 연은 아무도 묻지 못하게 하는 얼굴로, 살짝 절며 들어간다. 병사는 말들에게 돌아간다. 연은 모욕이라면 하나도 잊지 않는 사람이다. 그런데 한 달을 나란히 걸어온 이 사내의 이름은 끝내 묻지 않았고, 열한 해 동안 다시 물을 생각을 못 한다.

blocks.label: The Antechamber
blocks.ko: 대기실

blocks.html: The commanders wait in the antechamber while the king is dressed. The first pot of tea goes round by rank. It runs dry one cup before the foot of the table, so the foot of the table pours his own.
blocks.ko: 대가들은 왕이 의관을 갖추는 동안 대기실에서 기다린다. 첫 주전자가 서열대로 돈다. 말석 한 잔 앞에서 바닥이 나서, 말석은 제 차를 제가 따른다.

lines: 거란 놈들이 사백 마리를 되팔겠단다. 내 말을.
소금 받고. 소금 주마 했디. 상처에다.
en: Four hundred head the Khitans want to sell me back. My own horses.
For salt. I said I’d give them salt. In the wounds.

lines: 소금을 주시오. 장사하는 거란은 약탈하지 않소.
수레 한 대 값에 조용한 겨울이오.
en: Give them the salt. A Khitan who is trading is not raiding.
That is a quiet winter for the price of a cart.

lines: 조용한 겨울이라. 두 분은 조용한 겨울을 무 키우듯 키우시는구려.
en: Quiet winters. You two grow quiet winters like turnips.

lines: 손 대가는 뭘 키우는데? 신라 연설?
en: And what do you grow, Son? Speeches about Silla?
Silla. Once I’m given the men.
Then I’ll stop talking.

lines: 동부는 어떻소? 조용한 겨울 값으로 말갈한테 얼마를 치르오?
en: And the East? What do you pay the Mohe for a quiet winter?

lines: 말갈한테 겨울을 사디 않아. 고구려로 만들디.
en: Nothing.
I don’t buy winters off the Mohe. I make them Goguryeo.

blocks.html: There is the pause a table takes when a guest says grace in a house where nobody prays.
blocks.ko: 아무도 기도하지 않는 집에서 손님이 식전 기도를 올렸을 때, 밥상이 갖는 그런 침묵이 흐른다.

lines: 고구려로 만든다. 기거 어케 하는 건데? 노래를 가르치네?
en: Make them Goguryeo. How’s that go, then? You teach them the songs?

lines: 하나 데려왔다. 꼬맹이. 내 떠나던 날 아침에 “춥네” 하더라. 우리 말로.
en: I took one home. Wee thing. The morning I rode out, he said “cold.” In our tongue.

lines: 하늘이시여. 동부가 말갈을 데려다 노래패를 키우는구려.
en: Heaven help us. The East is raising Mohe for the choir.

lines: 웃으라우. 이 상에 앉은 놈 치고 할애비가 오랑캐 소리 안 들은 놈 있네?
성왕께서는 누구한테두 족보를 묻디 않으셨다. 고구려는 국경이 아니라—
en: Laugh. Every man at this table had a grandfather some southerner called a barbarian.
The Holy King never asked anybody for a pedigree. Goguryeo isn’t a border, it’s a—
The tea has gone cold.

blocks.html: It hasn’t. He pours anyway, for everyone, and this time the foot of the table gets a cup. The North looks at Yeon the way you’d look at a young dog that has brought you a live bird: impressed, embarrassed, and checking the floor.
blocks.ko: 식지 않았다. 그래도 그는 모두에게 따르고, 이번엔 말석에도 한 잔이 돌아간다. 북부는 산 새를 물어 온 어린 개를 보듯 연을 본다. 감탄스럽고, 민망하고, 바닥은 괜찮은지 살피면서.

en: Your grandfather talked like that.
And?

lines: 그래서 오래 막리지를 지냈지. 그러다 그만뒀고.
en: And he was High Commander a long while. Then he wasn’t.

blocks.html: The High Commander comes in by the inner door, the one the king uses. He has not come through the gate with the commands for years.
blocks.ko: 막리지는 안쪽 문으로 들어온다. 왕이 쓰는 문이다. 대가들과 함께 대문으로 들어온 지 여러 해다.

blocks.caption: The High Commander. He chairs the room like a feast and counts it like a granary.
blocks.ko: 막리지. 잔치처럼 회의를 주재하고, 곳간처럼 셈한다.

lines: 조카. 자넨 할아버님 턱을 닮았네. 그 어른은 그 턱을 공성추처럼 앞세우고 이 방에 드셨지.
en: Nephew. You have your grandfather’s chin. He used to bring it into this room like a ram against a gate.
Nephew. Is that what we are?

lines: 셈하자면 팔촌쯤 되나. 평양에선 아무도 셈하지 않네. 그래야 집안이 따뜻하거든.
en: Third cousins, if anybody counts. In Pyongyang nobody counts. It keeps the house warm.

lines: 오늘 밤 옛집에서 일가가 밥을 먹소. 오실 거디요.
en: The clan eats at the old house tonight. You’ll come.

lines: 궁도 같은 시각에 먹는다네. 일가에 안부 전해 주게.
en: The palace eats at the same hour. Give the clan my regards.
Where do you sit, then? Uncle.

lines: 자넨 말석일세, 조카. 처음엔 누구나 거기 앉지. 나도 그랬네.
en: Wherever His Majesty can see me.
And you at the foot, nephew. Everybody sits there the first time. I did.

blocks.html: They share a surname and stand an arm’s length apart, like two men who have been told they’re related and are each waiting for the other to prove it.
blocks.ko: 둘은 성이 같고, 팔 하나 거리를 두고 선다. 친척이라는 말을 듣고서, 서로 상대가 증명해 보이기를 기다리는 두 사내처럼.

blocks.html: The inner door opens again. The second pot of tea comes in with the king.
blocks.ko: 안쪽 문이 다시 열린다. 두 번째 주전자가 왕과 함께 들어온다.

blocks.label: Summit
blocks.ko: 제가회의

blocks.label: The Chamber
blocks.ko: 회의실

blocks.html: The chamber is loud before the king has sat down — not with strategy, with arithmetic. Every banner wants a larger share of the same winter grain.
blocks.ko: 왕이 앉기도 전에 전각은 시끄럽다 — 전략이 아니라 셈으로. 깃발마다 같은 겨울 군량의 더 큰 몫을 원한다.

blocks.html: Five swords sit at this table, a crow stamped in every ring. Nobody draws at the Summit. Everybody comes armed anyway. The South’s grip is worn smooth by Yushin’s passes. The North’s edge is nicked on Khitan bridles. The West oils his scabbard with Liao timber, so he smells faintly of a forest.
blocks.ko: 이 상에는 칼이 다섯 자루 놓인다. 고리마다 삼족오가 찍혀 있다. 제가회의에서 칼을 뽑는 자는 없다. 그래도 다들 차고 온다. 남부의 칼은 유신의 고개에서 손잡이가 닳아 매끈하다. 북부의 칼날엔 거란 굴레에 이 빠진 자국이 있다. 서부는 칼집에 요하 목재 기름을 먹여, 희미하게 숲 냄새가 난다.

blocks.html: The clerk who only keeps the minutes wears one too, because the rules say so. Ink on the grip, none on the edge. By the High Commander’s teacup lies the first sword, a small stone haetae carved under its crow. Yeon left his own at the gate. Junior seats do. He looks at theirs a little too long.
blocks.ko: 회의록만 적는 서기도 규칙이라 한 자루 찬다. 손잡이엔 먹이 묻었고, 날엔 아무것도 없다. 막리지의 찻잔 옆에는 첫 칼이 누워 있다. 삼족오 아래 작은 돌 해태가 새겨져 있다. 연은 제 칼을 대문에 맡겼다. 말석은 원래 그렇다. 그는 남의 칼을 조금 오래 본다.

blocks.html: The king asks the South first. He always does. The North has to clear his throat twice to get the royal eye, and the West doesn’t bother.
blocks.ko: 왕은 남부에게 먼저 묻는다. 늘 그렇다. 북부는 헛기침을 두 번 해야 왕의 눈길을 받고, 서부는 애쓰지도 않는다.

lines: 손 대가. 곳간 얘기 전에. 짐의 고개들은 어떠한가?
en: Commander Son. Before the granary. How are my passes?

lines: 징병을 내려 주시면 한쪽으로만 열리게 하겠사옵니다.
en: Open, Majesty. Both ways, for now.
Give me the levy, and they’ll only open one way.

lines: 좋구나. 좋아. 짐이 듣고 싶던 말이로다.
en: Good. Good. That is what we like to hear.
Majesty, the Khitans took four hundred head off us at the—
Yes. Horses. After.

blocks.html: Nobody asks the foot of the table anything. Yeon drinks his second cup and counts how long that takes. Then the granary comes back, the way granaries do.
blocks.ko: 말석에는 아무도 묻지 않는다. 연은 두 번째 잔을 마시며 그게 얼마나 걸리는지 센다. 그러고는 곳간 얘기가 돌아온다. 곳간 얘기는 늘 돌아온다.

en: Enough.
I did not call five commands to Pyongyang to divide a granary.
I will be the “King for All” — Samhan under one roof. Silla and Baekje first.
lines: 곳간이나 나누자고 오부를 평양에 부른 것이 아니다.
짐이 “삼한왕검”이 되리라 — 삼한을 한 지붕 아래로. 신라와 백제부터.

blocks.html: He is not the first man this year to want to be king for all. He is the first to want it on a budget.
blocks.ko: 올해 ‘모두를 위한 임금’이 되겠다는 사내가 그가 처음은 아니다. 예산 안에서 되겠다는 사내로는 처음이다.

en: Then the Southern Command takes the next levy.
Yushin’s banners have been testing the passes. If His Majesty wants Samhan, give me men — not speeches.
lines: 유신의 깃발이 고개를 두드리고 있습니다. 폐하께서 삼한을 원하시면 병력을 주십시오 — 연설이 아니라.

blocks.html: The north wants horses. The west wants timber and iron. Both want them from Central, and both say so twice.
blocks.ko: 북부는 말을 원한다. 서부는 목재와 쇠를 원한다. 둘 다 중부에서 받아 내고 싶어 하고, 둘 다 그 말을 두 번씩 한다.

en: (mild, as if chairing a feast)
Each front believes it is the only front. That is why we meet.
Eastern Command has kept the marches quiet. Let us not reward noise over results.
lines: 전선마다 자기만 전선이라 믿지. 그래서 모이는 것이오.
동부대는 변방을 조용히 지켜 왔소. 성과보다 목소리를 상 주지 맙시다.

en: Quiet?
I have been killing tribes so this room can argue about who gets the horses.
Meanwhile the Second Emperor is not a tribute account. He is a man who murders brothers for a throne and then invents a reason.
lines: 이 방이 말 배분을 놓고 다투라고 내가 오랑캐를 베어 온 줄 아시오.
그사이 서국 황제는 조공 장부가 아니오. 왕좌를 위해 형제를 죽이고 나서 이유를 발명하는 사내요.

en: Commander Yeon. Watch your tongue about foreign kings.
We have bought decades with gold. We will buy more — and spend the peace on Samhan.
lines: 연 장군. 외국 임금 혀를 조심하게.
금으로 수십 년을 샀고, 더 살 것이다 — 그 평화로 삼한을 사겠다는 뜻이야.

en: You cannot buy a man who has already decided the price of your head.
I have watched how courts die. They starve the wall that is screaming, and fatten the wall that—
lines: 제 목값을 이미 정한 사내는 살 수 없소.
조정이 죽는 꼴을 봤소. 비명 지르는 성벽은 굶기고, 아첨하는 성벽은—

en: Enough, Commander. We heard you the first time. The whole hall heard you the first time.
lines: 그만하게, 연 장군. 처음에 다 들었네. 온 전각이 처음에 다 들었어.

en: Easy for the East to lecture. You fight people without cities.
I fight Kim Yushin. Send me the next levy or stop talking about Samhan.
lines: 동부가 훈계하긴 쉽지. 당신들은 성 없는 놈들과 싸우니까.
나는 김유신과 싸운다. 다음 징발을 주든지, 삼한 이야기는 그만두시오.

blocks.html: Yeon’s hands are flat on the table. The nails have gone white. This is the face of a man who has already fought the war the room refuses to schedule.
blocks.ko: 연의 손이 상 위에 납작하다. 손톱이 하얘졌다. 방이 일정에 넣기를 거부하는 전쟁을, 이미 싸워 본 사내의 얼굴이다.

en: Listen to yourselves.
Horses. Timber. Bodies. A crown-word.
When the Second Emperor comes he will not ask which of you was most polite in committee.
lines: 당신들 말하는 꼴 좀 들어 보시오.
황제가 오면, 이 중 누가 회의에서 제일 공손했는지는 묻지 않을 거요.

blocks.html: The Southern Commander is up before the sentence is finished. The smooth grip turns once in his palm. Then the blade is out, resting a finger’s width under Yeon’s jaw.
blocks.ko: 말이 끝나기도 전에 남부 대가가 일어선다. 닳은 손잡이가 손바닥에서 한 번 돈다. 그리고 칼날이 나와, 연의 턱 밑 한 마디 거리에 멈춘다.

en: Polite?
Say it again. Say “polite” to the South.
…Nice edge. You keep it sharp.
Pity about the arm holding it.
Commander Son.
Not in my hall.

blocks.html: The blade does not move. The High Commander does not stand. He reaches over and sets two fingers on the flat of it, the way you’d steady a cup about to spill.
blocks.ko: 칼은 움직이지 않는다. 막리지는 일어서지 않는다. 손을 뻗어 칼등에 손가락 두 개를 얹는다. 넘치려는 잔을 붙잡듯이.

en: Deha. Put it away.
If this room ever cuts my nephew, it will do it properly. In writing.
lines: 이 방이 언젠가 내 조카를 벤다면, 제대로 할 걸세. 글로.

blocks.html: It goes back in on the second try. Yeon touches his throat, looks at his fingers, and finds nothing on them. He watches that scabbard for the rest of the afternoon.
blocks.ko: 칼은 두 번 만에 칼집에 들어간다. 연은 목을 한 번 만지고, 손가락을 보고, 아무것도 묻지 않은 걸 확인한다. 그날 오후 내내 그는 그 칼집을 본다.

en: If you keep defying the king, Commander Yeon…
we may have to name you a traitor.
(to Yeon, almost kindly — which is worse)
Nephew. Sit down. The Summit does not run on prophecies.
lines: 조카. 앉게. 제가회의는 예언으로 돌지 않네.

en: Then keep your Summit.
Keep your tribute. Keep your Samhan dream carved into a budget fight.
When the Second Emperor’s drums reach the Liao, remember who tried to spoil the feast.
lines: 조공도, 예산 싸움으로 깎아 낸 삼한의 꿈도.
황제의 북이 요하에 닿거든 — 잔치를 망치려 한 자가 누구였는지 기억하시오.

blocks.html: He walks out before it ends. Outside, the corridor is very long and very cold. Behind him the chamber returns to numbers — as if he had never brought an emperor into the room.
blocks.ko: 그는 회의가 끝나기 전에 나와 버린다. 밖으로 나서니 복도가 몹시 길고 몹시 차다. 등 뒤에서 전각은 다시 숫자로 돌아간다 — 그가 황제를 방에 들여온 적도 없었다는 듯이.

en: Heaven above… help this foolish country…!

blocks.html: The West keep notes on this room. Theirs are less polite.
blocks.ko: 당은 이 방에 대해 기록을 남긴다. 그쪽 기록은 덜 점잖다.

blocks.html: Their highest office is called Dedero, the High Commander. It ranks with our first grade, and its holder oversees all the business of the state. It changes hands every three years, though a man who does the job well is not held to the term. On the day of handover, if the parties will not submit to each other, they all call out their troops and fight, and the winner takes the post. Their king simply shuts the palace gates and guards himself. He cannot stop it.
blocks.ko: 그 벼슬 가운데 큰 것은 대대로라 부르니, 1품에 견주며 나랏일을 모두 맡는다. 3년마다 한 번 바뀌되, 직책을 잘 해내는 자는 햇수에 구애받지 않는다. 교대하는 날 서로 복종하지 않으면 모두 군사를 거느리고 서로 공격하여, 이긴 자가 그 자리를 차지한다. 그 왕은 다만 궁궐 문을 닫고 스스로를 지킬 뿐, 이를 막지 못한다.
blocks.hanja: 其官大者號大對盧，比一品，總知國事，三年一代，若稱職者，不拘年限。交替之日，或不相祗服，皆勒兵相攻，勝者爲之。其王但閉宮自守，不能制禦。
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199上, Eastern Barbarians — Goguryeo

blocks.label: The Palace Yard
blocks.ko: 궁 마당

blocks.html: In the yard the Eastern banners answer him anyway — a roar that has nothing to do with the Summit’s minutes.
blocks.ko: 마서국의 동부 깃발들은 그래도 그를 받아 준다 — 제가회의 회의록과는 상관없는 함성으로.

blocks.speaker: Man in the crowd
lines: 데 사람이다! 회의 박차고 나온 사람!
en: That’s him! The one that walked out on them!

blocks.speaker: Woman in the crowd
en: Is he handsome close up?

blocks.speaker: Man in the crowd
lines: 그만치 가까이 가 본 사람이 없디.
en: Nobody’s ever been close enough to say.
Look at that — see how Pyongyang loves you.
Of course. The people have never once abandoned me.
It is the politicians…!
lines: 당연하지. 백성은 날 버린 적이 없어.

en: So. That was half?
That was a quarter. You should’ve heard what I didnae say.
lines: 기게 사분의 일이다. 안 한 말을 들었어야 했어.

en: His Majesty wants Samhan under one roof.
The Summit wants the roof itemised.
…Get the horses. I’d sooner sleep in a tent the night.
lines: 폐하께서는 삼한을 한 지붕 아래 두고 싶어 하시지.
제가회의는 그 지붕을 항목별로 적고 싶어 하고.
…말 준비하라우. 오늘 밤은 천막에서 자는 게 낫갓다.

en: Gold to the West for quiet. Grain counted twice. A king who’d rather pay than ride.
There was a time Goguryeo didn’t pay anybody, Dosuryu. Other kings paid us. Silla came begging on its knees, and we rode south and saved it.
Now look at us.
lines: 조용하게 해 달라고 당에 금을 바치고. 곡식은 두 번 세고. 말 타느니 돈 내겠다는 임금이고.
고구려가 아무한테도 바치지 않던 때가 있었어, 도수류. 다른 임금들이 우리한테 바쳤디. 신라가 무릎 꿇고 빌러 왔고, 우리가 남으로 내려가 구해 줬다.

en: That was two hundred years ago.
Then we’re two hundred years late. Get the horses.
lines: 그럼 이백 년 늦은 거지. 날래 말 가져오라.

en: And Eye. The one holding our horses. Give him to the West.
lines: 기리고 ‘눈’. 우리 말 잡고 있는 놈. 서부에 줘 버리라.

en: Give him? He’s ours. He walked your wife here.
lines: 줘? 우리 사람이야. 네 마누라를 여기까지 모셔 왔어.

en: Every Deka keeps his own men. Mine are mine to give.
The West is short of men who argue with string. He can argue with the Liao.
lines: 대가마다 제 사람은 제가 둔다. 내 사람은 내가 준다.
서부엔 다림줄하고 싸울 놈이 모자라. 가서 요하하고 싸우라 하라우.

blocks.label: The West Road
blocks.ko: 서쪽 길

blocks.html: The Summit ends at dusk, without him. The commanders ride home the way they came in, by rank. The West goes last. The West always has the farthest to go.
blocks.ko: 제가회의는 해 질 녘에, 그 없이 끝난다. 대가들은 들어올 때처럼 서열대로 돌아간다. 서부가 맨 끝이다. 서부는 언제나 갈 길이 제일 멀다.

blocks.html: The junior warrior with the wandering eye rides at the Western Commander’s stirrup now. The East gave him away in the palace yard, the way you’d give away a dog that bites the right people. He held the horses by the gate all afternoon. He saw the man from the East come out early, take his sword off the rack and look at nobody.
blocks.ko: 한쪽 눈이 제멋대로 도는 그 말단 무사가 이제 서부 대가의 등자 곁에 따른다. 동부가 궁 마당에서 그를 줘 버렸다. 물어야 할 놈을 무는 개를 남에게 주듯이. 그는 오후 내내 대문 곁에서 말을 붙들고 있었다. 동쪽에서 온 사내가 일찍 나와 시렁에서 제 칼을 집어 들고, 아무도 보지 않고 가는 것도 보았다.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
lines: 한 달을 그분 수레 옆에서 걸었습네다. 오늘 아침엔 제 돌을 걷어찼고요. 꿈쩍도 안 했디요.
en: Sir. The one from the East…
I walked beside his cart a month. This morning he kicked my stone. It didn’t move.
Is he mad?

lines: 제 앞에 놓인 일은 기어이 끝내고 마는 사람이오. 값이 얼마든. 누가 치르든.
en: No.
He is a man who finishes the job in front of him. Whatever it costs. Whoever pays.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Isn’t that good? In a soldier?

lines: 태평한 때라면 그런 사람은 집을 태워 먹지. 험한 때라면…
…그리고 그 눈으로 날 보디 마시오. 어느 쪽이 듣고 있는지 통 모르갓으니.
en: Depends on the age he’s born into.
In a quiet one, a man like that burns the house down. In a bad one…
…And stop looking at me with that eye. I can never tell which half of you is listening.

blocks.speaker: Junior warrior
en: Both, sir.

blocks.html: The commander never finishes the other half of his sentence. It is a long way to the Liao. The road is quiet, and he would like it to stay that way for whatever time he has left.
blocks.ko: 대가는 끝내 그 말의 나머지 반을 하지 않는다. 요하까지는 먼 길이다. 길은 조용하고, 그는 남은 날 동안 길이 그렇게 조용하기를 바란다.

blocks.html: That night, in Yeon’s tent, a rider finds him. His wife’s time has come, and it has gone badly before.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤, 연의 천막에서 전령이 그를 찾는다. 아내의 해산이 시작됐다. 전에도 잘 안 된 적이 있다.

blocks.label: Son
blocks.ko: 아들

blocks.label: Birth of Namseng
blocks.ko: 남생의 탄생

blocks.html: He reaches the house after midnight. One lamp, one midwife, and the mother. On the wall hangs a painting of Samsin, the birth goddess, prayed at so often that the paint has gone pale where the hands touch it.
blocks.ko: 그가 집에 닿는 건 자정이 지나서다. 등불 하나, 산파 하나, 그리고 어머니. 벽에는 아이를 점지하는 여신, 삼신의 그림이 걸려 있다. 하도 빌어서 손이 닿는 자리마다 물감이 바랬다.

en: Samsin…
This child alone — please.
…This time — please.

blocks.html: The painting does not stay paint. Samsin steps from the frame the way steam steps from a kettle, and lays a hand where mortal hands have failed.
blocks.ko: 그림은 그림으로 남지 않는다. 삼신이 주전자에서 김이 오르듯 액자에서 내려와, 사람의 손이 닿지 못한 곳에 손을 얹는다.

blocks.caption: The birth goddess. She does not knock.
blocks.ko: 아이를 점지하는 여신. 문을 두드리지 않는다.

en: Do not weep.
I will open the breath.
The name — that is yours to give.

blocks.html: So the first heir arrives under Samsin's hand, the year of the Summit. They call him Namseng. Nobody wanted a poem in the name. It's the sound the room makes when the baby breathes.
blocks.ko: 그렇게 삼신의 손 아래, 제가회의가 열린 해에 맏아들이 온다. 남생. 사내가 났다는 뜻이다. 이름에 시를 넣고 싶은 사람은 없었다. 아기가 숨을 쉴 때 방이 내는 소리, 그게 이름이다.

en: Namseng.
…Heavier than it sounds.
This country. You will have to keep it.

blocks.html: He holds the boy up to the lamp and tells him the only bedtime story he knows: the one about the king who rode south and never counted grain.
blocks.ko: 그는 아이를 등불 쪽으로 들어 올리고, 제가 아는 유일한 옛날이야기를 들려준다. 남으로 말을 달렸고 곡식 따위는 세지 않았던 임금 이야기다.

blocks.html: Once, Silla begged Goguryeo for an army, and Goguryeo came. To meet the king who answered, we go back two centuries…!
blocks.ko: 한때 신라가 고구려에 군대를 빌었고, 고구려는 왔다. 그 부름에 답한 임금을 만나려면 이백 년을 거슬러 가야 한다…!

logline.en: His stele lists sixty-four fortresses. It does not list the nerve it took.
logline.ko: 그의 비석에는 성 예순네 곳이 적혀 있다. 그만한 배짱은 적혀 있지 않다.
