images.alt: The Alexander Mosaic in tesserae: Gwanggeto bareheaded on horseback charging through a forest of spears, the Eastern commander twisting in flight
images.prompt: A parody of the ALEXANDER MOSAIC from Pompeii (the Battle of Issus), made exactly like the real Roman floor mosaic: thousands of small stone tesserae, limited palette of ochre, brick red, black, white and grey, patches of missing tiles, a dark broken border. Same composition: on the left the young conqueror charges on horseback, bareheaded, eyes wide, spearing an enemy; on the right the enemy leader, in a chariot, twists back in horror and flings out an arm as his army turns to flee; a forest of long spears slanting across the sky; a bare dead tree. The conqueror is GWANGGAETO (attached portrait: face) in gray steel lamellar (attached ref) with a red #e0442e cloak; the fleeing leader is a Wa commander in lacquered plate on a boat-shaped chariot, Wa foot soldiers scattering. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.

images.alt: Two hundred and forty years later a Silla prince will stand in front of a foreign emperor and ask for an army, and every single person in Su
images.prompt: CLOSING STILL of the episode: the final scene of this story as it ends (not the next episode). The line: “Two hundred and forty years later a Silla prince will stand in front of a foreign emperor and ask for an army, and every single person in Surabol will know exactly what that costs, because it has been done to them before.” Context: His stele, naturally, remembers it more kindly. The common people were at peace in their work; the country was rich and the people abundant; the five grains ripened in plenty. Two hundred and forty years later a Silla prince will stand in front of a foreign emperor and ask for an army, and every single person in Surabol will know exactly what that costs, because it has been done to them before. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — PLACE Surabol (서라벌 (경주)) — attached board /pl_eastern_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Seorabeol palace: Silla giwa halls, packed-earth yards, timber verandas. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Silla is drowning. An army from across the sea is inside its walls, and its king has one move left.
blocks.ko: 신라가 가라앉고 있다. 바다 건너 온 군대가 도성 안에 있고, 신라 왕에게 남은 수는 하나뿐이다.

blocks.caption: Goguryeo’s widest king. The stele ran out of room before he ran out of fortresses.
blocks.ko: 고구려에서 가장 넓은 임금. 성이 바닥나기 전에 비석 자리가 먼저 바닥났다.

blocks.hanja: 生而雄偉，有倜儻之志。
blocks.html: He was born big and imposing, with a will that would not be bridled.
blocks.ko: 태어나면서부터 체격이 크고 웅장하였으며, 얽매이지 않는 뜻을 품었다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 18, Goguryeo Annals — King Gwanggaeto, accession notice

blocks.caption: Watch the red run south. One reign did that.
blocks.ko: 붉은빛이 남쪽으로 번지는 걸 보라. 한 사람의 치세가 한 일이다.

blocks.label: The Burning Capital
blocks.ko: 불타는 도성

blocks.html: The Silla king stands on his own wall and counts the sea-raiders’ fires. They sit on the north road, on the south road, and under the Western wall. There are more every night. Below, in the hall, his court is arguing about pride.
blocks.ko: 신라 왕은 제 성벽 위에 서서 바다 도적들의 불을 센다. 북쪽 길에도, 남쪽 길에도, 서쪽 성벽 밑에도 있다. 밤마다 늘어난다. 아래 전각에서는 조정이 체면을 두고 다툰다.

blocks.speaker: A Silla Elder
en: If we ask the north, they will come. And then they will stay.

blocks.speaker: The Silla King
en: And if we don’t ask, the Easterners stay. Which guest would you rather feed?
lines: 안 청하면 동국가 눌러앉지. 어느 손님을 먹이고 싶은가?

blocks.speaker: A Silla Elder
en: Majesty, the letter will have to say… they’ll want a word. A low word.
lines: 전하, 서신에는… 그쪽이 바라는 말이 있을 겁니다. 낮은 말이요.

blocks.speaker: The Silla King
en: I know the word. Bring the brush.
I’ll write it myself, so nobody else has to.
lines: 내가 직접 쓰마. 다른 누가 쓰지 않아도 되게.

blocks.label: The Plea
blocks.ko: 청원

blocks.html: His envoy rides north for nine days and kneels in the tent of a Goguryeo king who is twenty-six and has never lost.
blocks.ko: 그의 사신은 아흐레를 북으로 달려, 스물여섯에 한 번도 져 본 적 없는 고구려 임금의 막사에 무릎 꿇는다.

blocks.speaker: Silla’s Envoy
en: The East are inside our walls, Great King. My king writes in his own hand.
“Silla is your servant. Save your servant.”
lines: 동국가 우리 성 안에 들어와 있습니다, 대왕. 저희 임금께서 친필로 쓰셨습니다.

en: Servant. He wrote that word himself?
lines: 종이라. 그 글자를 제 손으로 썼단 말이냐?

blocks.speaker: Silla’s Envoy
en: …In his own hand.
Then they’ll come. Fifty thousand of them.
Tell him one thing more, so he hears it from me first. Servants don’t decide when the master’s horsemen go home.
lines: 하나 더 전해라. 나한테서 먼저 듣게. 주인의 기병이 언제 돌아갈지는 종이 정하는 게 아니다.

blocks.html: The Silla king reads the answer twice. The first half saves his kingdom. The second half he does not read aloud.
blocks.ko: 신라 왕은 답장을 두 번 읽는다. 앞의 반이 그의 나라를 구한다. 뒤의 반은 소리 내어 읽지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Horsemen
blocks.ko: 기병

blocks.html: The horsemen come down out of the north like weather.
blocks.ko: 기병들이 날씨처럼 북에서 내려온다.

blocks.speaker: A Silla Lookout
en: Majesty— the north road. That dust isn’t the East.
lines: 전하— 북쪽 길입니더. 저 먼지는 동국가 아입니더.

blocks.speaker: The Silla King
en: No. That’s my letter.

blocks.html: From his wall he watches the raiders’ fires go out one by one. Then he watches the red banners come through his own gate, and keep coming.
blocks.ko: 그는 성벽 위에서 도적들의 불이 하나씩 꺼지는 것을 본다. 그다음엔 붉은 깃발들이 제 성문으로 들어오는 것을 본다. 들어오고, 또 들어온다.

blocks.speaker: A Silla Elder
en: They’re still coming in, Majesty.

blocks.speaker: The Silla King
en: I wrote the word. Let them in.

blocks.html: A red sun. The three-legged crow rides south on his banners. The stele will list sixty-four fortresses. It will not list the nerve it took.
blocks.ko: 붉은 해. 세발까마귀가 그의 깃발에 실려 남으로 간다. 비석은 성 예순넷을 적을 것이다. 거기 든 배짱은 적지 않는다.

blocks.html: The horsemen ride at the raiders’ backs, southwest over the big river and into Gaya country. At the last fortress the gate opens before the ladders are even up.
blocks.ko: 기병들은 도적들의 등 뒤를 몰아 남서쪽으로, 큰 강을 건너 가야 땅까지 내려간다. 마지막 성은 사다리를 대기도 전에 문을 연다.

blocks.speaker: A Goguryeo Rider
en: That’s it? I didnae even get off my horse.

blocks.html: Silla had asked. That’s the part everyone forgets. Then the horsemen ride back to the Silla capital, and don’t leave for fifty years.
blocks.ko: 신라가 청했다. 다들 잊는 대목이다. 그리고 기병들은 신라 도성으로 돌아와, 오십 년 동안 떠나지 않는다.

blocks.html: Silla’s crown princes go north as hostages. The first one is twelve. Silla’s court takes Goguryeo titles. Silla’s army takes Goguryeo orders. It lasts two generations. Silla does not forget it.
blocks.ko: 신라의 태자들이 볼모로 북으로 간다. 첫 번째는 열두 살이다. 신라의 조정이 고구려의 관작을 받는다. 신라의 군대가 고구려의 명을 받는다. 두 세대가 그렇게 흐른다. 신라는 그것을 잊지 않는다.

blocks.html: He goes with a pony and a tutor. At the border he asks how long. Nobody answers him, which is how he finds out.
blocks.ko: 소년은 조랑말 한 필과 스승 하나를 데리고 간다. 국경에서 그는 얼마나 오래냐고 묻는다. 아무도 대답하지 않는다. 그렇게 그는 알게 된다.

blocks.speaker: The Silla Court
en: They did save us.
So why are they still here?

blocks.html: His stele, naturally, remembers it more kindly.
blocks.ko: 그의 비석은 물론 그 일을 더 너그럽게 기억한다.

blocks.hanja: 庶寧其業 國富民殷 五穀豊熟
blocks.ko: 서민이 그 업에 편안하고, 나라는 부유하며 백성은 은성하고, 오곡이 풍성히 익었다.
blocks.html: The common people were at peace in their work; the country was rich and the people abundant; the five grains ripened in plenty.
blocks.source: Gwanggaeto Stele (廣開土王碑), south face, ll. 3–4 (414 CE); Best, “The Kwanggaeto Stele,” p. 147

blocks.html: Two hundred and forty years later a Silla prince will stand in front of a foreign emperor and ask for an army, and every single person in Surabol will know exactly what that costs, because it has been done to them before.
blocks.ko: 이백사십 년 뒤 한 신라의 왕자가 외국 황제 앞에 서서 군대를 청한다. 그리고 서라벌의 모든 사람이 그 값을 정확히 안다. 전에 이미 당해 봤기 때문이다.

blocks.html: The prince who will beg has a son. Bupmin is fifteen now, and his uncle has one question: which rule will you break first…?
blocks.ko: 언젠가 빌러 갈 그 왕자에게는 아들이 있다. 법민이 열다섯이 되었고, 외숙에게는 질문이 하나 있다. 어느 계율을 제일 먼저 어기겠느냐…?

toneNote: A K-drama heart beats inside a season of alliances — vows, longing, and clan hands moving behind every throne.

logline.en: Fifteen is old enough for the headband, and too young to invent a country alone.

images.prompt: Minimal iconic 2:1 still composed like a symbolic old-master history painting — the STRONG, DISCIPLINED UNCLE AND THE APPRENTICE NEPHEW. INTIMATE CLOSE-UP, low angle from the dirt: seventeen-year-old Bupmin on his knees, face and shoulders large in the lower-right, sweat and dust on his cheek, head tipped back, eyes burning up at his teacher. Yushin stands over him in the upper-left holding a long plain wooden practice staff at full arm’s length; its blunt tip rests under the boy’s chin. Yushin looks down, stern, almost proud. ONE DEVICE: the long staff diagonal from the standing mentor to the kneeling student’s chin. A torch below-right lights Bupmin’s face hot gold; Yushin falls into cold shadow. Background pure black with ember bokeh. Wood only. Faces drawn, matching the attached portraits. No text. CANON — KIM YUSHIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_yushin.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Demeanor: Confucian: he STANDS — never sits in lotus. Weighs, counts, frowns at sums; tight jaw, rare dry half-smile. Grief shows as stillness, not tears. The most feared warrior in all of Samhan: a line goes quiet when the tall Silla helm and the white horse appear. Massive, deliberate, terrifying at a walk; by Hwangsan (65) heavier and slower than Gyebek but still the man armies are built around. #2A5FB8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: sitting in lotus or holding prayer beads; katana, tsuba or curved blade (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); two swords at once; blue glow aura. | BUPMIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_bupmin_hwarang.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

Medium-wide over-the-shoulder shot from behind the timber rail of the Hwarang yard fence in late afternoon sun. Midground, sharp: two grown men leaning on the rail side by side like boys: Bidam in a dark navy robe, prayer beads looped on his wrist, chin on his forearms, wry smile, eyes on the yard; Alchun beside him, broad, eating a rice cake. To the left along the rail a fifteen-year-old Bupmin in a hwarang tunic with a crescent headband edges toward them, curious, wide-eyed. Background: the dusty yard, a tiny figure of a marshal turning his head toward them, giwa roofs in haze. ONE device: the long horizontal rail cutting the frame. Low raking sun, long shadows of the posts. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = bidam, SECOND face = alchun, THIRD face = munmu. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. BIDAM — Look: Tall, handsome, clean-shaven; short slicked-back black hair; warm brown eyes, faint self-amused smile. Dress: Long white outer robe whose sleeves are embroidered with galloping horses, over a plum-magenta inner robe and white sash. Navy #141C2E lives in the room and on the beads, not on his clothes. Colour #141C2E. ALCHUN Colour #8fb3e0. BUPMIN — Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.at: His uncle keeps the yard, and the yard is where Bupmin lives now.
images.alt: His father is collecting votes. His uncle fixes the headband.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. PARALLEL FRAME: the LAYOUT picture on the sheet is the master of a set of frames that recur across this story. Repaint ITS EXACT COMPOSITION: the same camera height, angle and lens, the same framing, the same number of figures in the same positions, sizes and poses, the same main shapes (gate, line, dais, table, waterline) in the same places, the same direction of the key light. Only the people, their faces and dress, the place and the hour change, so the two frames line up like a before-and-after. Ignore the layout picture's faces, clothes and colours. The same gate, thirty years after his own. Kim Yushin, now the Marshal in his forties, stands where his father stood on the LEFT, hands raised to his nephew's crescent headband, stern and almost smiling; fifteen-year-old Bupmin on the RIGHT, eager, chin up, too big a grin, catching his uncle's wrists. Through the gate the yard and a row of new boys. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT LAYOUT picture (copy its composition, not its people), SECOND face = yushin, THIRD face = munmu. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_moon_palace (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), jougwan feather-cap board (shape only, ignore labels). KIM YUSHIN — Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Colour #2A5FB8. BUPMIN — Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Colour #C41E3A. PLACE Moon Palace (월궁) — attached board /pl_moon_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.

images.at: On the first night of every class, the Marshal walks the new boys down it with one lamp.
images.alt: He starts at the gate and walks backwards through time.

blocks.label: Flowering Youth
blocks.ko: 화랑의 꽃

blocks.html: Fifteen is old enough for the headband. It is not old enough to invent a country, though Bupmin keeps trying.
blocks.ko: 열다섯이면 머리띠를 맬 나이다. 나라를 발명할 나이는 아니다. 법민은 그래도 자꾸 해 본다.

blocks.html: The Hwarang train under the Marshal: horse, bow, verse, and above all gyuku, a horse-ball game a lazier age will call polo.
blocks.ko: 화랑은 장군 밑에서 배운다. 말, 활, 노래, 그리고 무엇보다 격구. 훗날 게으른 시대가 폴로라 부를, 말 위의 공놀이다.

blocks.html: His father is in the Council chamber, collecting votes. His uncle keeps the yard, and the yard is where Bupmin lives now.
blocks.ko: 아버지는 화백 회의실에서 표를 모으고 있다. 연무장은 외숙이 지킨다. 법민은 이제 그 연무장에서 산다.

blocks.title: Yard as state · 화랑
blocks.caption: Class 51 still sits together — Bidam, Yushin, Alchun.
blocks.ko: 51기는 아직도 같이 앉는다 — 비담, 유신, 알천.

blocks.html: Yushin does not soften the yard because the boy is royal. He softens nothing. The new boys sleep six to a hall and learn each other's snores before each other's ranks. They trade rumours about the Marshal like relics. He sleeps in his armour. He bathes in a haunted lake. He can hear a lie drop a shoulder at fifty paces.
blocks.ko: 유신은 소년이 왕손이라고 연무장을 무르게 두지 않는다. 무엇 하나 무르게 두지 않는다. 새로 온 소년들은 한 방에 여섯씩 자며, 서로의 골품보다 코 고는 소리를 먼저 익힌다. 장군 소문은 성물처럼 오간다. 갑옷을 입은 채 잔다더라. 귀신 나오는 호수에서 목욕한다더라. 오십 보 밖에서도 거짓말에 어깨 처지는 소리를 듣는다더라.

blocks.label: First Morning
blocks.ko: 첫날 아침

blocks.html: On a new boy’s first morning, the yard gives him a senior to show him round. Somebody always gets the prince. This year it is the most nervous man in the hall.
blocks.ko: 새로 들어온 아이의 첫날 아침, 연무장은 선배 하나를 붙여 준다. 왕자는 누군가 꼭 맡게 된다. 올해는 숙소에서 제일 긴장 잘하는 사람이 걸렸다.

blocks.html: Kim Pumsuk is five years older, True Bone, very handsome, and so polite he apologises to doors.
blocks.ko: 김품석은 다섯 살 위의 진골이고, 아주 잘생겼고, 문에다 대고도 사과할 만큼 예의가 바르다.

lines: 마마. 김품석입니더. 제가— 마마를 모시고— 여기가 숙소입니다.
저기서 주무십니다. 한 방에 여섯이고요. 송구합니더.
그리고 저기가 뒷간입니다. 저기도 뒷간입니다. 둘입니다. 송구합니더.
en: Your Highness. Kim Pumsuk. I’ve been— I’m to show you— this is the hall.
You sleep there. Six to a room. Forgive me.
And that’s the latrine. That’s also the latrine. There are two. Forgive me.
Why are you sorry about the latrines?

lines: ……모르겠심더. 왕자님께 뒷간을 보여 드린 적이 없어서요.
en: …I don’t know. I’ve never shown a prince a latrine before.

blocks.html: He shows him the club racks, the stables, and the long painted wall nobody may lean on. He wears a parade sword with a gilt fox in its ring, and it bumps his knee at every step.
blocks.ko: 그는 채 걸이와 마구간, 아무도 기대면 안 되는 긴 벽화를 보여 준다. 허리에는 고리에 금빛 여우가 든 의장용 칼을 찼는데, 걸음마다 무릎에 부딪힌다.

en: Is that a real sword, sunbae?
It’s for parades. It’s never cut anything.
My mother says that’s what makes it valuable.

blocks.html: At the end of the practice road, where it bends at a split pine, he stops and lowers his voice, as if the tree can hear.
blocks.ko: 연습로 끝, 길이 갈라진 소나무에서 꺾이는 곳에서 그는 멈추고 목소리를 낮춘다. 나무가 듣기라도 하는 것처럼.

lines: 첫해엔 다들 저기서 고삐를 당깁니다. 아니라는 사람 말은 믿지 마십시오.
en: That’s the pine.
Everyone pulls up there the first year. Don’t let them tell you otherwise.
Did you?
The first year.
…Shall we see the stables again?

blocks.html: Bupmin is fifteen. It does not occur to him to ask about the second year.
blocks.ko: 법민은 열다섯이다. 둘째 해는 어땠느냐고 물어볼 생각은 하지 못한다.

blocks.html: Girls crowd the fence of the yard the way other towns crowd a market — not for the ball, for the Hwarang. They pretend they came for the verse.
blocks.ko: 소녀들이 연무장 울타리에 모인다. 다른 고을이 장터에 몰리듯 — 공 때문이 아니라, 화랑 때문에. 노래 들으러 왔다고 한다.

lines: 저 채, 가야 쇠심 박은 기가?
아이다 — 월성 측백이다. 작년 시즌 끼.
en: That club — Gaya ironwood core?
No — the Moon Palace cypress. Last season’s.
…Last season? And he brought it out?

lines: 진골은 지난 시즌 채를 안 든다 카이.
en: A True Bone does not play last season’s shaft.
Is that law?
Worse.

blocks.html: Alchun is at the fence most afternoons, eating something. Today he has brought a councillor with prayer beads, and the girls find this hilarious: two grown men leaning on the rail among them like boys.
blocks.ko: 알천은 오후면 대개 울타리에 기대 뭘 먹고 있다. 오늘은 염주 든 대신 하나를 데려왔고, 아가씨들은 그게 우스워 죽는다. 다 큰 사내 둘이, 저들 틈에서 소년들처럼 난간에 기대 있으니.

lines: 저 사람, 아직도 왼쪽 어깨 떨군다.
en: He still drops his left shoulder.
Tell him.

lines: 삼십 년째 말하고 있다. 내 말 중에 저 사람이 다 듣고도 무시하는 건 그거 하나뿐이다.
en: I’ve told him for thirty years. It’s the only advice I’ve ever given him that he hears and ignores.
I heard that.
You were meant to, Marshal.

blocks.html: Bupmin, who has never heard anyone talk to his uncle like that and live, edges along the rail toward Alchun.
blocks.ko: 외숙에게 저렇게 말하고 멀쩡한 사람을 본 적 없는 법민이, 난간을 따라 알천 쪽으로 슬금슬금 다가간다.

en: Sir. Are they… friends?
Worse. Same class.

blocks.label: The Turn
blocks.ko: 굽이

blocks.html: The practice road runs east along the river and bends hard at the split pine. That bend is where boys find out who they are. Gotaso is not supposed to ride it. Gotaso rides it.
blocks.ko: 연습로는 강을 따라 동쪽으로 뻗다가 갈라진 소나무에서 확 꺾인다. 사내애들은 그 굽이에서 자기가 누군지 알게 된다. 고타소는 거기서 달리면 안 된다. 고타소는 달린다.

lines: 지는 사람이 한 달 동안 채 함 들기데이.
en: Bupmin. To the pine and back.
Loser carries the other one’s club box for a month.
You’re not allowed on the practice road.
…Fine. One month.
Gotaso. Off the road.

lines: 한 번만예, 외숙. 야가 하자 캤어요.
en: One run, Uncle. He asked me.
I did not—
…One run.

blocks.html: They go off the line together. On the straight he is ahead. At the split pine the horse leans, the ground tilts, and his hands decide for him. He pulls up. Gotaso doesn’t. She takes the bend flat out, one stirrup empty, and comes back laughing with pine needles in her hair.
blocks.ko: 둘이 함께 출발선을 박차고 나간다. 직선에서는 그가 앞선다. 갈라진 소나무에서 말이 기울고, 땅이 기울고, 그의 손이 먼저 정해 버린다. 그는 고삐를 당긴다. 고타소는 안 당긴다. 등자 하나가 빈 채로 굽이를 그대로 돌아 나오더니, 머리에 솔잎을 꽂고 깔깔 웃으며 돌아온다.

blocks.html: The girls at the fence cheer for her, which is worse than laughing. Yushin has watched from the pine the whole time. He does not cheer for anybody.
blocks.ko: 울타리의 아가씨들이 그녀에게 환호한다. 웃음보다 더 아프다. 유신은 처음부터 소나무 곁에서 보고 있었다. 그는 누구에게도 환호하지 않는다.

en: Club box. A month.
Carry it where the girls can see.
Again.
A king for all who cannot hold a saddle is a poem, not a country.
lines: 안장도 못 잡는 모두를 위한 임금은 시지, 나라가 아이다.

en: Uncle—
Father said it on the hill. I only said it louder. I was six.
lines: 아버지가 언덕에서 하신 말이라예. 저는 더 크게 말했을 뿐이고요. 여섯 살 때.

en: Then make it true at fifteen.
The Hwarang do not train for your father’s cleverness. They train for the hour the cleverness runs out.
lines: 화랑은 니 아비 꾀를 위해 닦는 기 아이다. 꾀가 바닥날 시각을 위해 닦는다.

en: West of here is Baekje.
Learn a landscape before it learns your name.
lines: 땅이 자네 이름을 익히기 전에, 자네가 먼저 그 땅을 익히게.

blocks.label: Under the Eaves
blocks.ko: 처마 밑

blocks.html: At dusk he gathers the flower youth under the eaves and speaks the Five Principles, the way other houses recite ancestors. A monk wrote them for boys who would never be monks. Loyalty to the king comes first, so nobody can say they missed it. Duty to your father is easy, until the king and your father want different things. The boys elbow each other at no retreat. They go quiet at no needless killing. Boys skip that one. Old soldiers don’t. Each of them is privately certain the Marshal is looking at him. He is looking at all of them.
blocks.ko: 해 질 녘 그는 처마 아래 꽃다운 소년들을 모으고, 다른 집이 조상을 외듯 세속오계를 왼다. 중이 될 리 없는 아이들을 위해 중 하나가 지은 계율이다. 임금에 대한 충성이 맨 앞이다. 못 들었다는 소리는 못 하게. 부모에 대한 효는 쉽다. 임금과 아버지가 서로 다른 걸 원하기 전까지는. 소년들은 임전무퇴에서 서로 팔꿈치를 찌른다. 살생유택에서는 조용해진다. 아이들은 그 계율을 건너뛴다. 늙은 군인들은 안 그런다. 저마다 장군이 바로 자기를 보고 있다고 남몰래 확신한다. 장군은 그들 모두를 보고 있다.

en: Loyalty to the sovereign.
Filial duty to parents.
Trust among friends.
No retreat in battle.
No needless killing.
Bupmin — which one will you break first?
lines: 법민아 — 니는 뭐를 제일 먼저 어길 것 같노.

en: …No retreat.
I always pull up first. At the pine, today. Every time she rides too fast.
I’d rather know it now than find out on a field.
lines: 저는 늘 먼저 고삐를 당겨요. 오늘도 소나무에서요. 고타소가 너무 빨리 달릴 때마다요.
들판에서 알게 되느니, 지금 아는 기 낫지예.

blocks.html: Nobody laughs. A few boys look down at their sandals. Every one of them has a pine of his own.
blocks.ko: 아무도 웃지 않는다. 몇몇이 제 짚신을 내려다본다. 다들 저만의 소나무가 하나씩 있다.

en: Good. Most boys lie.
Then see the country the way a Hwarang sees a field: who holds, who falters, who dies for a vow he meant.
Tomorrow you ride the pine again. Beside her.
lines: 그럼 화랑이 들판을 보듯 나라를 보게. 누가 버티고, 누가 흔들리고, 누가 진심으로 한 맹세에 죽는지.
내일 다시 소나무까지 달리게. 동생 옆에서.

blocks.html: He said the third one slower than the others, trust among friends, and nobody noticed but Bupmin. Two of the Marshal’s classmates sat in this yard with him once. One of them still sends him tea every New Year, with a note that has only the score on it.
blocks.ko: 그는 세 번째, 교우이신만 다른 것보다 천천히 말했다. 알아챈 건 법민 하나뿐이다. 장군의 동기 둘이 한때 이 마당에서 그와 함께 앉았다. 그중 하나는 지금도 설마다 차를 보낸다. 쪽지엔 점수만 적혀 있다.

blocks.html: Gotaso has been listening from the fence, where she is not supposed to be either.
blocks.ko: 고타소는 울타리에서 듣고 있었다. 거기 있으면 안 되는 건 그녀도 마찬가지다.

en: You pulled up because of me?
No. Because of me.
…Tomorrow, then. Don’t you dare let me win.

blocks.html: She means it. She always means it. That is the trouble with Gotaso, and also the best thing about her.
blocks.ko: 진심이다. 그녀는 언제나 진심이다. 고타소의 문제가 바로 그거고, 고타소의 제일 좋은 점도 그거다.

blocks.label: The Long Wall
blocks.ko: 긴 벽

blocks.html: The Hwarang hall has a wall nobody is allowed to lean on. It runs the whole length of the yard under its own little roof, and it is painted from end to end. The newest paint is by the gate. The oldest is so far down that the new boys have never walked that far.
blocks.ko: 화랑 연무장에는 아무도 기대면 안 되는 벽이 있다. 마당 길이만큼 길게, 제 지붕을 따로 이고 뻗어 있고, 끝에서 끝까지 그림이 그려져 있다. 가장 새 그림은 대문 곁에 있다. 가장 오래된 그림은 하도 멀어서, 새내기들은 거기까지 걸어가 본 적이 없다.

blocks.html: On the first night of every class, the Marshal walks the new boys down it with one lamp. He starts at the gate and walks backwards through time. He has never explained why.
blocks.ko: 기수마다 첫날 밤이면, 장군은 등불 하나를 들고 새내기들을 데리고 그 벽을 따라 걷는다. 대문에서 시작해 시간을 거꾸로 걸어간다. 왜 그런지 설명한 적은 없다.

blocks.html: The first panel is still bright. A young man in magenta sits cross-legged at a campfire among forty Baekje raiders. All of them are laughing. Every sword is on the ground.
blocks.ko: 첫 그림은 아직 선명하다. 자홍빛 옷의 젊은이가 백제 약탈꾼 마흔 틈에서 모닥불 앞에 책상다리로 앉아 있다. 다들 웃고 있다. 칼은 전부 땅바닥에 있다.

lines: 서쪽 산에 약탈꾼 진채가 있었다. 두 해 여름을 우리 곡식을 털어 갔지.
그 사람은 술 한 동이 들고 혼자 걸어 들어갔다. 새벽에 포로 마흔을 데리고 걸어 나왔다.
en: A raider camp in the western hills. Two summers they’d been taking our grain.
He walked in alone with a jar of wine. At dawn he walked out with forty prisoners.
They asked to come.

blocks.speaker: A new Hwarang
en: Who is it, Marshal?
Ask him.

blocks.html: He lifts the lamp an inch toward Bupmin. Sixty heads turn. A month as the boy who pulls up at the pine, and Bupmin is suddenly the most interesting person in Surabol.
blocks.ko: 장군이 등불을 법민 쪽으로 한 치 든다. 머리 예순 개가 돌아간다. 소나무에서 고삐 당기는 아이로 한 달을 지낸 법민이, 갑자기 서라벌에서 제일 흥미로운 사람이 된다.

blocks.speaker: The new Hwarang
en: That’s your father?!
Is it true about the wine?
Did they really ask to come?

lines: ……아버지는 술 덕이라 카시고. 어머니는 아버지 덕이라 카십니더.
en: He says it was forty.
Last New Year it was sixty.
…He says it was the wine. Mother says it was him.

blocks.html: For the rest of the walk two boys carry Bupmin’s club box without being asked. It lasts until breakfast.
blocks.ko: 남은 길 내내 두 소년이 시키지도 않았는데 법민의 채 함을 들어 준다. 그 인기는 아침밥 때까지 간다.

blocks.html: The next stretch of wall is older, and the paint has started to go. A tiger on Mount Nam, and three boys about to be eaten by it: a round one with his arms round its neck, one with a sword, one with a string of beads.
blocks.ko: 다음 벽은 더 오래됐고, 물감이 바래기 시작했다. 남산의 호랑이 한 마리, 그리고 막 잡아먹히게 생긴 소년 셋. 호랑이 목을 끌어안은 동글한 아이, 칼을 든 아이, 염주를 든 아이.

blocks.speaker: A new Hwarang
en: Marshal! That’s you!
Keep walking.

blocks.html: He doesn’t stop. He doesn’t raise the lamp. The boys have to read it at the edge of the light. The Three Eternal Hwarang, the whole country calls them, and the Marshal walks past himself like a door he has no use for.
blocks.ko: 그는 멈추지 않는다. 등불도 들지 않는다. 소년들은 불빛 가장자리에서 겨우 그림을 읽는다. 온 나라가 화랑삼웅이라 부르는 그 셋. 장군은 쓸 일 없는 문 앞을 지나가듯 제 그림을 지나간다.

en: Uncle. Who’s the one with the beads?

lines: ……아니다. 똑같다. 요새는 그걸로 녹봉을 받을 뿐이지.
그라고 호랑이는 알천이 잡았다. 적어 둬라. 그 사람 확인한다.
en: A councillor. He talks less now.
…No. He talks the same. Now they pay him for it.
And Alchun caught the tiger. Write that down. He checks.

blocks.html: Then two young men under a fallen horse, arrows standing in them like reeds, and in the corner, painted small, a monk writing.
blocks.ko: 그다음엔 쓰러진 말 밑의 두 청년. 화살이 갈대처럼 꽂혀 있다. 귀퉁이엔 작게, 뭔가 쓰고 있는 스님 하나.

lines: 둘이 스님을 찾아가 속인이 지킬 만한 계율을 청했다. 스님이 준 게 오늘 밤 너거가 외운 그 다섯이다.
이듬해 서쪽 산의 성에서, 둘 다 네 번째를 지켰다.
en: Gwisan. Chuhang.
They went to the monk and asked for rules a layman could keep. He gave them the five you said tonight.
The next year they kept the fourth one, at a fort in the western hills. Both of them.

blocks.html: Bupmin, who said tonight which rule he would break first, looks at the arrows for a long time. Nobody offers to carry his club box for this part.
blocks.ko: 오늘 밤 어느 계율을 제일 먼저 깰지 말했던 법민이, 화살들을 오래 바라본다. 이 대목에선 아무도 그의 채 함을 들어 주겠다고 나서지 않는다.

blocks.html: After that the wall gets older and the Marshal walks faster. Boys on horses. Boys on walls. A boy swimming a river with a letter in his teeth. The paint goes brown, then grey, and the lamp starts finding bare plaster between the panels, where the painters ran out of money or of heroes.
blocks.ko: 그다음부터 벽은 더 오래되고 장군의 걸음은 빨라진다. 말 탄 소년들. 성벽 위의 소년들. 편지를 입에 물고 강을 헤엄치는 소년. 물감이 갈색이 되고, 잿빛이 되고, 등불이 그림 사이사이 맨 회벽을 비추기 시작한다. 화공들이 돈이 떨어졌든 영웅이 떨어졌든 한 자리다.

blocks.html: At the very end, where the wall meets the old gate, the lamp finds two boys. No battle. No horse. Two thirteen-year-olds on a riverbank, one scratching at a flat grey stone with a knife, the other watching him do it badly.
blocks.ko: 맨 끝, 벽이 옛 대문과 만나는 자리에서 등불이 소년 둘을 찾아낸다. 싸움도 없고 말도 없다. 강가의 열세 살 둘. 하나는 납작한 잿빛 돌을 칼로 서툴게 긁고 있고, 하나는 그걸 지켜보고 있다.

blocks.speaker: A new Hwarang
en: That’s it?
What did they do?

blocks.html: Yushin sets the lamp down on the ground in front of them. He did not do that for Chunchu, or for the tiger, or for himself.
blocks.ko: 유신이 그 앞 땅바닥에 등불을 내려놓는다. 춘추 그림 앞에서도, 호랑이 앞에서도, 제 그림 앞에서도 하지 않은 일이다.

lines: 연무장이 아직도 목소리를 낮추는 이름이 둘 있다. 사다함. 무관.
en: Sit down.
The yard has two names it still whispers. Sadaham. Mugwan.
It’s a long one.

blocks.html: The yard is new. The idea is newer. Two boys share one gap in the hall, and argue about who snores…!
blocks.ko: 연무장은 새것이고, 그 생각은 더 새것이다. 숙소의 빈자리 하나를 나눠 쓰는 소년 둘이, 누가 코를 고는지 다툰다…!

logline.en: Every yard has its ghosts. This one has two, and they have never missed roll call.
logline.ko: 연무장마다 귀신이 있다. 이곳엔 둘이다. 점호에 빠진 적이 한 번도 없다.

images.alt: Tiny Sadaham on a vast empty Gaya road — ice-blue accent, monumental emptiness
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 poster. Sadaham, God of the Hwarang, fifteen, taking Great Gaya. ONE geometric device: a long empty ROAD as a pale wedge receding to a hard horizon; tiny silky Hwarang figure in the lower third, standing, not kneeling. Face matches the attached Sadaham portrait only as a tiny likeness. Ice-blue #6fa8ff as the single accent on silk. REAL empty country road, natural dusk sky. Monumental emptiness. No army catalog. No crescent halo. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental.

images.at: asks to ride against Great Gaya
images.alt: Fifteen-year-old Sadaham kneels on the stone floor of Jinhung’s hall at night, head up, asking to ride
images.prompt: Worm’s-eye from the stone floor of King Jinheung’s timber hall at night, an oil lamp set on the floor in the sharp foreground. Sadaham, fifteen, kneels mid-bow but with his head already up, chin out, refusing to look down, in his Hwarang coat; the lamp rakes up across his jaw and the ice-blue of his collar. Behind and above him, out of focus on the dais, King Jinheung leans forward on one fist, half amused, half doubtful, red robe catching the same lamp. Pillars recede at an angle; Sadaham’s shadow climbs the floor toward the dais. CANON — SADAHAM — FACE and garments from attached /ch_sadaham.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Hwarang taken Gaya at fifteen; ice-blue #6fa8ff cloth on campaign; dies young of grief. #6fa8ff as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | KING JINHEUNG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_jinheung.png (face only; invent a new pose). #2f6fd4 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first.
