This one has two, and they have never missed roll call.” Context: Every yard has its ghosts. This one has two, and they have never missed roll call.   A wide or medium establishing frame that hooks. CANON — PLACE Surabol (서라벌 (경주)) — attached board /pl_eastern_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Seorabeol palace: Silla giwa halls, packed-earth yards, timber verandas. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Repaint ITS EXACT COMPOSITION: the same camera height, angle and lens, the same framing, the same number of figures in the same positions, sizes and poses, the same main shapes (gate, line, dais, table, waterline) in the same places, the same direction of the key light. Only the people, their faces and dress, the place and the hour change, so the two frames line up like a before-and-after. Ignore the layout picture's faces, clothes and colours. The same line, the first year of the yard. The yard master has stopped on the RIGHT third in front of an EMPTY place in the line at the centre, glaring at the gap. Next to the gap stands young Mugwan, rigid, eyes sliding upward. Up on the low giwa roof of the yard hall behind the line, small in the upper middle of the frame (not at the top edge), young Sadaham sits with his knees up, grinning down. REFERENCE SHEET. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.

images.alt: Before dawn, so as not to wake anyone.

blocks.html: Every yard has its ghosts. This one has two, and they have never missed roll call.
blocks.ko: 연무장마다 귀신이 있다. 이곳엔 둘이다. 점호에 빠진 적이 한 번도 없다.

blocks.label: Hwarang
blocks.ko: 화랑

blocks.label: Surabol, the hwarang yard · 560
blocks.ko: 서라벌, 화랑 연무장 · 560

blocks.html: Mugwan has decided to be unimpressed by the hwarang. His father told him to keep his head down, his sword clean and his mouth shut, and he means to do all three.
blocks.ko: 무관은 화랑 따위에 감탄하지 않기로 마음먹었다. 아버지는 고개 숙이고, 칼 깨끗이 하고, 입 다물라고 했다. 셋 다 할 생각이다.

blocks.html: The yard is new this year, and so is the idea. A hundred noble sons stand in rows in powder and silk, trying to look like they meant to come. One of them is not in a row. He is on the roof.
blocks.ko: 올해 연무장은 새것이고, 그 생각도 새것이다. 귀한 집 아들 백 명이 분 바르고 비단 입고 줄지어 서서, 원해서 온 척을 하고 있다. 그중 하나는 줄에 없다. 지붕 위에 있다.

blocks.speaker: The yard master
en: You! Off the roof! Now!
In a moment!
From up here you can see all the way to the sea!

blocks.html: You cannot see the sea from anywhere in Surabol. Mugwan knows this. Everyone knows this. A hundred boys look up anyway, and Mugwan, who has decided to be unimpressed, looks up with them.
blocks.ko: 서라벌 어디서도 바다는 안 보인다. 무관도 안다. 다 안다. 그래도 백 명이 고개를 든다. 감탄 안 하기로 한 무관도 같이 든다.

blocks.html: The boy on the roof jumps. He lands in the dirt a step from Mugwan, rolls, and comes up grinning, as if the ground had been in on it.
blocks.ko: 지붕 위 소년이 뛰어내린다. 무관 한 걸음 앞 흙바닥에 떨어져 한 바퀴 구르더니, 땅이랑 미리 짠 것처럼 웃으며 일어선다.

blocks.caption: The first class’s brightest boy. He makes promises the way other boys throw stones.
blocks.ko: 제일기에서 가장 빛나던 소년. 다른 아이들이 돌을 던지듯 약속을 던진다.

en: You looked.
Everybody looked, but you looked longest. What’s your name?
lines: 다 봤는데, 니가 제일 오래 봤다. 이름이 뭐꼬?

en: …There’s no sea.
Not from here. Not yet.
Give me a year. I’m Sadaham. I’m going to be the best one in this yard.
lines: 일 년만 줘 봐라. 내 사다함이다. 이 연무장에서 내가 제일 잘나갈 끼다.

en: Everyone says that.
Yes, but I’m going to be right.

blocks.html: Sadaham is thirteen and talks like a dare. Mugwan is thirteen too, and says less than his horse. The hall has one gap, so they share it. They argue for a month about who snores.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 열셋이고, 말마다 내기를 건다. 무관랑도 열셋인데, 자기가 타는 말보다도 말수가 적다. 방에 빈자리가 하나뿐이라 둘은 한 방에 든다. 누가 코를 고는지 한 달을 다툰다.

en: You snore.
Don’t argue. The whole hall heard you.
lines: 우기지 마라. 방 전체가 다 들었다.

blocks.caption: Sadaham’s best friend in the First Class. The two of them made a promise boys should not make.
blocks.ko: 제일기에서 사다함의 단짝. 둘은 사내아이들이 해서는 안 되는 약속을 했다.

en: That was you.
…Then prove it. Stay up and listen.
lines: …그라믄 증명해 봐라. 안 자고 들어 보든가.

blocks.html: Mugwan stays up. It is the first of a great many nights he will stay up for Sadaham, and the only one either of them will find funny.
blocks.ko: 무관랑은 안 자고 듣는다. 앞으로 사다함 때문에 지새울 수많은 밤 가운데 첫날이고, 둘 다 웃을 수 있는 건 그날 밤뿐이다.

blocks.label: The yard · that spring
blocks.ko: 연무장 · 그해 봄

blocks.html: Mugwan is the best sword in his family. On the third morning he finds out that is not the same as the best sword in the yard. He finds out flat on his back, with Sadaham’s wooden blade resting on his collarbone.
blocks.ko: 무관은 집안에서 칼을 제일 잘 쓴다. 그게 연무장에서 제일이라는 말은 아니라는 걸, 사흘째 아침에 알게 된다. 등을 땅에 대고 누워서, 사다함의 목검을 쇄골에 얹은 채로.

en: Again.
You’ve won. Three times.
I know. I want to see what you do on the fourth.
You keep your elbow in like your father’s watching. He isn’t. Hit me like he isn’t.
lines: 안다. 네 번째에 니가 우짜는지 볼라꼬.
니 팔꿈치를 아부지가 보는 것맨치로 붙이고 있다. 안 본다. 안 보는 것맨치로 쳐 봐라.

blocks.html: On the fourth, Mugwan hits him. Sadaham sits down hard in the dust and laughs so loudly the yard master comes out to see who is dying.
blocks.ko: 네 번째에 무관이 맞힌다. 사다함은 흙바닥에 털썩 주저앉더니, 누가 죽는 줄 알고 교관이 뛰어나올 만큼 크게 웃는다.

en: THERE he is!

blocks.html: It goes on like that all spring. Sadaham rides at night because the road is empty. He sings in the bath, badly, and makes the boys at the bottom of the list sing with him until they forget they are at the bottom. He gives his rice away, is hungry by noon, and doesn’t seem to mind. Mugwan keeps waiting for him to run out. He doesn’t.
blocks.ko: 봄 내내 그렇다. 사다함은 길이 비었다고 밤에 말을 달린다. 목욕하면서 노래를 하는데, 못 부른다. 명단 맨 끝 아이들을 끌어다 같이 부르게 해서, 그 아이들이 자기가 끝인 걸 잊게 만든다. 자기 밥을 나눠 주고 점심때면 배가 고픈데, 상관도 안 하는 눈치다. 무관은 저게 언제 바닥나나 기다린다. 안 난다.

en: Ride with me.
Where?
Haven’t decided. That’s the good part.
No.

blocks.html: He says no eleven times that spring. He goes all eleven.
blocks.ko: 그해 봄 무관은 열한 번 싫다고 한다. 열한 번 다 따라간다.

blocks.html: Their first spring, the yard sends them down to the river for stones. Mugwan turns one over and goes very still. Somebody has cut writing into it.
blocks.ko: 첫봄, 연무장은 둘을 냇가로 보내 돌을 날라 오게 한다. 무관랑이 돌 하나를 뒤집더니 꼼짝도 않는다. 누군가 거기에 글을 새겨 두었다.

en: Come here.
Read this.
You read it. You’re the one who studies.

blocks.hanja: 壬申年六月十六日二人幷誓記天前誓今自三年以後忠道執持過失无誓若此事失天大罪淂誓若國不安大舐世可容行誓之又別先辛未年七月卄二日大誓詩尙書礼傳倫淂誓三年
blocks.html: Year imsin, sixth month, sixteenth day. The two of us swear together and write it down. We swear before Heaven: from today, for three years, we will hold fast to the way of loyalty and commit no fault. If we break this, we swear it is a great sin against Heaven. If the country is not at peace and the world falls into great disorder*, we swear we will go and do it. And apart from this: before, on the twenty-second day of the seventh month of the year sinmi, we swore a great oath, to master in turn the Odes, the Documents, the Rites and the Tradition† within three years.
blocks.ko: 임신년 6월 16일, 두 사람이 함께 맹세하여 적는다. 하늘 앞에 맹세한다. 지금부터 3년 동안 충도를 굳게 지니고 허물이 없기를 맹세한다. 이 일을 어기면 하늘에 큰 죄를 짓는 것이라 맹세한다. 만약 나라가 편안하지 않고 세상이 크게 어지러워지면*, 나아가 행할 것을 맹세한다. 또 따로, 앞서 신미년 7월 22일에 크게 맹세하였으니, 시경·상서·예기·전†을 차례로 3년 안에 익히기로 맹세하였다.
blocks.source: Imsin Oath Stone (壬申誓記石), Silla, year imsin (552 or 612); found 1934 at Seokjang-dong, Gyeongju; Gyeongju National Museum, Treasure No. 1411

back.html: Face down in the river mud. That is how two boys found it, and how they put it back.
back.ko: 냇가 진흙에 엎어진 채. 두 소년이 찾았을 때도, 도로 놓았을 때도.

notes.html: The stone’s character here is worn. The database prints 舐; nearly every editor reads it as 亂, “disorder”.
notes.ko: 이 자리의 글자는 닳아 있다. 판독문은 舐로 적지만, 거의 모든 연구자가 亂(어지러울 란)으로 읽는다.

notes.html: The Tradition (傳) is usually taken as the Zuo commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

blocks.html: No names. Two boys, before the yard even had a name, promised Heaven three years of books, and a war if the country wanted one. What became of them, the stone doesn’t say. Stones rarely do.
blocks.ko: 이름은 없다. 연무장에 이름이 붙기도 전의 두 소년이, 책으로 3년, 나라가 원하면 전쟁을 하늘에 약속했다. 그 둘이 어떻게 됐는지 돌은 말하지 않는다. 돌은 원래 말이 없다.

en: Three years?
That’s all they had in them? Give me your knife.
That’s not ours. Put it back.
lines: 그거 우리 꺼 아이다. 도로 놔라.

en: Not that one. We get our own.
lines: 그거 말고. 우리 꺼는 따로 만들 끼다.

blocks.html: He finds a smaller stone, flat and grey, and scratches at it until the light goes. His characters are terrible. He leaves out the books entirely. What’s left fits in a closed hand.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 더 작은 돌을 찾는다. 납작하고 잿빛이다. 해가 질 때까지 긁어 댄다. 글씨는 엉망이다. 책 얘기는 아예 뺀다. 남은 것은 주먹 하나에 다 들어간다.

en: Read it.
…“Two of us. One dies, the other follows.”
That’s it?
What else is there?

blocks.html: Mugwan takes the knife. Under the bad characters he cuts one more, small and neat: friend. Then he puts the old stone back exactly where they found it, face down, as if they had never been there.
blocks.ko: 무관랑이 칼을 받아 든다. 엉망인 글씨 아래에 한 글자를 작고 반듯하게 더 새긴다. 벗. 그러고는 옛 돌을 찾았던 자리에 그대로, 엎어서 도로 놓는다. 둘이 거기 온 적도 없다는 듯이.

blocks.html: A museum in Gyungju keeps the first stone now. Nobody has ever found the second. Good.
blocks.ko: 첫 번째 돌은 지금 경주의 박물관에 있다. 두 번째 돌은 아무도 찾지 못했다. 다행이다.

blocks.label: The Gaya border, a ford on the Hwang · autumn, 561
blocks.ko: 가야 접경, 황강 나루 · 561년 가을

blocks.html: The second autumn, the yard sends twenty boys to ride the border with a real patrol. Nobody expects anything. The border has other ideas.
blocks.ko: 두 번째 가을, 연무장은 소년 스물을 진짜 순찰대에 붙여 국경으로 보낸다. 아무도 별일 없을 줄 안다. 국경 생각은 다르다.

blocks.speaker: A patrol sergeant
en: Raiders at the ford! Gaya hill men— twenty, thirty—
Boys to the back! You hear me? To the BACK!
lines: 나루에 도적 떼다! 가야 산사람들, 스물, 서른—

blocks.html: Halfway across the ford Mugwan’s horse takes an arrow in the shoulder and goes down sideways into the river, and Mugwan goes with it. The water is cold and full of hooves. He cannot find which way is up.
blocks.ko: 강 한가운데서 무관의 말이 어깨에 화살을 맞고 옆으로 쓰러진다. 무관도 같이 처박힌다. 물은 차갑고, 말발굽 천지다. 어디가 위인지 모르겠다.

blocks.html: A hand finds his collar and drags him up into the air and the noise. It belongs to the one boy who was told to go to the back and turned round instead. Sadaham rides down the first man and cuts down the second, and he never lets go of Mugwan.
blocks.ko: 손 하나가 그의 깃을 잡아 공기와 소음 속으로 끌어올린다. 뒤로 빠지라는 말을 듣고 오히려 돌아선 단 하나의 소년의 손이다. 사다함은 첫 번째 놈은 말로 받아 넘기고 두 번째 놈은 칼로 벤다. 그동안 무관을 한 번도 놓지 않는다.

en: You— you were told to go back—
I did go back. You were back there.
That’s where I keep you. Hold on to the saddle.
lines: 니는 내가 거 둔다. 안장 꽉 잡아라.

blocks.html: The raiders break when the patrol reaches the bank. The sergeant, who has done this for twenty years, rides over to shout at the boy and finds he has nothing to say. That night Mugwan cannot stop shaking. Sadaham sits beside him and talks about horses until he stops.
blocks.ko: 순찰대가 강둑에 닿자 도적들이 흩어진다. 이십 년을 이 일 한 하사가 소년을 혼내러 말을 몰고 오는데, 막상 와서는 할 말이 없다. 그날 밤 무관은 떨림이 안 멈춘다. 사다함이 옆에 앉아 멈출 때까지 말 이야기를 한다.

blocks.label: Mount Danseok · winter, 561
blocks.ko: 단석산 · 561년 겨울

blocks.html: Winter is for mountains. The hwarang climb them, sleep on them, and sing at the top as if the mountain had asked. On the third day the snow gives way under Mugwan on a ledge, and for one long breath there is nothing beneath him at all.
blocks.ko: 겨울은 산의 계절이다. 화랑은 산을 오르고, 산에서 자고, 산이 청하기라도 한 듯 꼭대기에서 노래한다. 사흘째 되는 날 바위 턱에서 무관의 발밑 눈이 꺼진다. 숨 한 번 길게 쉬는 동안, 발밑에 아무것도 없다.

blocks.html: Then there is a fist in his belt. Sadaham is flat on the ice, one arm round a pine root and the other holding his friend over the drop. He is laughing again, the idiot, because his face is full of snow.
blocks.ko: 그다음 허리띠에 주먹이 걸린다. 사다함이 얼음 위에 납작 엎드려, 한 팔로는 솔뿌리를 감고 다른 팔로 낭떠러지 위의 친구를 붙들고 있다. 그리고 또 웃는다, 저 바보. 얼굴에 눈이 잔뜩 묻어서.

en: That’s twice!
I’m counting! Climb, I can’t feel my hand—
lines: 세고 있다! 올라온나, 손에 감각이 없다—

en: Then let go.
Don’t be stupid. Climb.
lines: 바보 같은 소리 하지 마라. 올라온나.

blocks.html: Afterward, by the fire, Mugwan watches him sleep, which is the only time Sadaham is ever still. Mugwan has met plenty of boys who are sure of things. This is the first one who makes him sure too. He doesn’t know yet what of. He thinks it might be everything.
blocks.ko: 그 뒤, 모닥불 가에서 무관은 그가 자는 걸 본다. 사다함이 가만히 있는 건 잘 때뿐이다. 무관은 뭔가를 확신하는 아이들을 많이 봤다. 자기까지 확신하게 만드는 건 이 아이가 처음이다. 뭘 확신하는지는 아직 모른다. 어쩌면 전부일지도 모른다고 생각한다.

blocks.label: Surabol, the king’s hall · 562
blocks.ko: 서라벌, 임금의 전당 · 562

blocks.html: Two summers on, the little stone has worn a hole in Sadaham’s sleeve, and Great Gaya stops paying. The king calls the war in his hall, and the hall fills up with men old enough to have opinions. Among them is the king’s younger brother, Suulbu, twenty-seven, who talks about Great Gaya the way you talk about a dog that has started to bite. Under the table the king’s second son, Saryun, seven, has fallen asleep on a cushion with a rice cake in his fist. He will be king one day. Briefly.
blocks.ko: 두 해 뒤 여름, 작은 돌은 사다함의 소매에 구멍을 냈고, 대가야는 공물을 끊는다. 왕은 전당에서 전쟁을 정하고, 전당은 할 말이 있을 만한 나이의 사내들로 가득 찬다. 그 가운데 왕의 아우 수을부가 있다. 스물일곱, 대가야 얘기를 물기 시작한 개 얘기하듯 한다. 상 밑에선 왕의 둘째 아들 사륜이 일곱 살, 떡을 쥔 채 방석 위에서 잠들었다. 언젠가 임금이 될 아이다. 잠깐.

blocks.html: A hill kingdom that has just stopped saying yes.
blocks.ko: 막 “예”라고 하기를 그만둔 산골 왕국.

blocks.html: Sadaham is fifteen when he asks to ride against Great Gaya. He asks on his knees, in front of everyone. It is the only way a boy can ask a king for anything and not be sent outside.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 열다섯에 대가야를 치겠다고 청한다. 무릎을 꿇고, 모두가 보는 앞에서. 소년이 왕에게 무언가를 청하면서 쫓겨나지 않는 방법은 그것뿐이다.

en: Go home. Grow a beard.
War is not a yard. Nobody hands the ball back.
lines: 전쟁은 연무장이 아니다. 공을 돌려주는 놈이 없어.

en: Then I’ll ask again tomorrow.

blocks.html: He does. And the day after. The old general leading the campaign once took an island by frightening it with wooden lions. He tells the king it will be quicker to bring the boy than to keep hearing him.
blocks.ko: 청한다. 그다음 날도. 원정을 맡은 늙은 장군은 예전에 나무 사자로 겁을 줘서 섬 하나를 통째로 받아 낸 사람이다. 그가 왕에게 아뢴다. 저 아이를 데려가는 편이 저 아이 말을 계속 듣는 것보다 빠르겠다고.

en: Fine. Take him.
If he dies, it was his idea. Write that down.
lines: 죽으면 제 생각이었던 거다. 적어 둬라.

en: You’re going.
We’re going.
I told them you’re my second. Don’t make me a liar.
lines: 니가 내 부장이라 캤다. 내 거짓말쟁이 만들지 마래이.

en: You didn’t ask me.
I’m asking now.
…Well?
…I’ll get the horses.

blocks.label: Great Gaya
blocks.ko: 대가야

blocks.label: The Battle of Great Gaya · 562
blocks.ko: 대가야 전투 · 562

blocks.html: The ninth month. Rain on the hill road, smoke on the hill. Great Gaya sits on its ridge behind a timber gate, and every roof inside the wall has a bow on it.
blocks.ko: 아홉째 달. 산길엔 비, 산 위엔 연기. 대가야는 능선 위 나무 성문 뒤에 앉아 있고, 성안 지붕마다 활이 하나씩 올라앉아 있다.

blocks.speaker: A Silla rider
lines: 본진은 어데 있노? 사자 그 영감은 어데 갔노?
en: Shields! Shields up, they’re on the roofs—
Where’s the main army? Where’s the old man with the lions?

blocks.speaker: A Great Gaya archer
lines: 말 타고 온다꼬? 진흙탕으로 기어 올라오라 캐라—
참아라— 아직— 성문 밑에 올 때까지 참아라—
en: Horses, is it? Let them come up the mud, then—
Hold— wait for it— wait till they’re under the gate—

blocks.html: At the head of the Silla riders Sadaham is fifteen, soaked, and grinning. Beside him a Silla general nobody in the vanguard knows well is looking up at the gate the way you look at a relative.
blocks.ko: 신라 기병의 맨 앞에서 사다함은 열다섯이고, 흠뻑 젖었고, 웃고 있다. 그 곁에서 선봉의 누구도 잘 모르는 신라 장군 하나가, 친척을 보듯 성문을 올려다본다.

blocks.html: The men on that gate wear the same helm he does: the tall Gaya cone with the iron plates.
blocks.ko: 저 성문 위의 사내들은 그와 같은 투구를 썼다. 쇠 비늘을 단 높은 가야 고깔.

en: Those are my father’s helms.
Let me walk up first. Alone.
They’ll shoot you.
Then keep the gate warm for me.

blocks.html: He takes the helm off, tucks it under his arm, and walks up the gate road alone.
blocks.ko: 그는 투구를 벗어 옆구리에 끼고, 혼자 성문 길을 걸어 올라간다.

blocks.speaker: A Silla rider
lines: 저 양반 뭐 하노— 투구를 벗었다— 돌았나?
en: What’s he— he’s taken it OFF— has he gone mad?
Is he mad, or is he winning?

lines: 둘 다. 지붕 봐라. 전부 저 사람만 보고 있다.
en: Both. Look at the roofs. They’re all looking at him.
Then nobody’s looking at me.

blocks.html: Sadaham does not wait for anyone to finish a sentence. He takes five thousand horse at the Jundan gate while the men above it are still drawing, and goes through before the gate has decided whether it is open.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 누가 말을 끝내기를 기다리지 않는다. 기병 오천을 이끌고 전단문으로 달려드는데, 성 위의 사내들은 아직 시위를 당기는 중이다. 문이 열렸는지 닫혔는지 정하기도 전에 그는 이미 안에 있다.

blocks.speaker: A Great Gaya archer
en: A child, that is. They sent a child—
He’s inside. How is he inside?

blocks.html: He is fifteen, and he fights like it: too fast, too far ahead, laughing once when a spear misses him by a hand. Mugwan stays one horse behind him all the way up the street and takes the men Sadaham doesn’t see.
blocks.ko: 열다섯이고, 열다섯처럼 싸운다. 너무 빠르고, 너무 앞서 나가고, 창이 한 뼘 차이로 비껴가자 한 번 웃기까지 한다. 무관랑은 큰길 끝까지 말 한 마리 뒤를 지키며, 사다함이 못 본 놈들을 맡는다.

blocks.html: Halfway up the street a spear takes Mugwan’s horse out from under him. He lands on his back in the mud with three men coming, and he has time to think, quite calmly, that this is how it ends: one horse behind.
blocks.ko: 거리 중턱에서 창 하나가 무관의 말을 쓰러뜨린다. 무관은 진흙탕에 등으로 떨어지고, 세 놈이 달려온다. 무관은 꽤 담담하게 생각할 틈이 있다. 이렇게 끝나는구나, 말 한 마리 뒤에서.

blocks.html: It isn’t. Sadaham comes back down the street against his own charge, the whole Silla vanguard parting round him like water, and puts his horse between Mugwan and the spears.
blocks.ko: 안 끝난다. 사다함이 자기 돌격을 거슬러 거리를 되짚어 내려온다. 신라 선봉 전체가 물처럼 그를 비켜 갈라지고, 그는 무관과 창들 사이에 말을 세운다.

en: Three!
Get up behind me. Hurry, I want that gate.
lines: 뒤에 타라. 빨리, 내 저 문 갖고 싶다.

blocks.html: They take the gate together, two boys on one horse. Sadaham plants the white banner on it, and Mugwan holds the pole straight, because Sadaham’s hands are shaking and he will not admit it.
blocks.ko: 둘은 말 한 마리에 타고 함께 문을 차지한다. 사다함이 그 위에 흰 깃발을 세우는데, 장대는 무관이 붙들어 바로 세운다. 사다함 손이 떨리는데, 본인은 절대 인정 안 하기 때문이다.

en: They said too young.
The gate didn’t.
Don’t die first.
Then keep up.

blocks.html: Ninth month. Gaya rebelled. The king ordered Isabu to punish it, with Sadaham as his second. Sadaham rode ahead with five thousand horse, went in through the Jundan Gate and planted a white banner. The people in the city were terrified and did not know what to do. When Isabu brought up his troops, they surrendered all at once.
blocks.ko: 9월, 가야가 배반하니 왕이 이사부에게 명하여 치게 하고, 사다함을 부장으로 삼았다. 사다함이 기병 5천을 거느리고 앞서 달려 전단문으로 들어가 흰 깃발을 세우니, 성안 사람들이 두려워 어찌할 바를 몰랐다. 이사부가 군사를 이끌고 다다르자 한꺼번에 모두 항복하였다.
blocks.hanja: 九月，加耶叛，王命異斯夫討之，斯多含副之。斯多含領五千騎先馳，入栴檀門，立白旗，城中恐懼，不知所爲。異斯夫引兵臨之，一時盡降。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 4, Silla Annals — King Jinheung, yr. 23 (562)

blocks.html: Across the sea, the East has been taking rent off the Gaya ports for a long time. It takes the news personally.
blocks.ko: 바다 건너 동국는 오랫동안 가야의 포구에서 세를 받아 왔다. 이 소식을 제 일처럼 받아들인다.

blocks.html: Silla is a petty villain of the western barbarians. It defies Heaven and knows no decency. It has betrayed our kindness and destroyed our miyake. It poisons our people and butchers our districts.
blocks.ko: 신라는 서쪽 오랑캐의 보잘것없는 무리로, 하늘을 거스르고 무도하다. 우리의 은혜를 저버리고 우리의 관가를 깨뜨렸으며, 우리 백성을 해치고 우리 군현을 짓밟았다.
blocks.hanja: 新羅西羌小醜，逆天無狀，違我恩義，破我官家，毒害我黎民，誅殘我郡縣。
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 19, Emperor Kinmei — yr. 23 (562), 6th month

blocks.label: Great Gaya, the square · that afternoon
blocks.ko: 대가야, 광장 · 그날 오후

blocks.html: Afterward the king pays him the way kings pay: in people. Three hundred Gaya captives, roped in a line, his to keep. Sadaham walks down the line once. Then he starts cutting rope.
blocks.ko: 싸움이 끝나자 왕은 왕들이 늘 하는 방식으로 값을 치른다. 사람으로. 줄줄이 묶인 가야 포로 삼백, 그의 몫이다. 사다함은 줄을 따라 한 번 걸어 내려간다. 그러고는 밧줄을 끊기 시작한다.

en: The court will say you’re showing off.
lines: 조정에선 니가 잘난 척한다 칼 끼다.

en: Then the court can have them back.
Help me with this knot.

blocks.speaker: A Gaya child
lines: 엄마. 엄마, 저 사람 줄에 뭐 하노?
en: Mam. Mam, what’s he doing to the rope?

blocks.speaker: Her mother
lines: 고맙다 소리도 아직 하지 마라. 그만둘지도 모른다.
en: Hush. Don’t look at him.
And don’t thank him yet. He might stop.

blocks.html: At the edge of the square, the general who walked up the gate road bareheaded has the helm back on. He watches the boy work down the line for a while. Then he gets down off his horse.
blocks.ko: 광장 가장자리에서, 맨머리로 성문 길을 걸어 올라갔던 장군이 다시 투구를 쓰고 있다. 한동안 소년이 줄을 따라 내려가는 것을 지켜본다. 그러다 말에서 내린다.

en: Those are the king’s, boy.

lines: 제 거예요. 저한테 주셨어요. 거들든지 비키든지 하세요.
en: They’re mine. He gave them to me. Help or move.

lines: 망한 나라 사람들이다. 인자 그기 전부다.
진 사람은 안 풀어 준다. 아무것도 못 된다. 내가 우째 아는지 물어봐라.
en: They’re from a beaten country. That’s all they are now.
Beaten people don’t get untied. They don’t get to be anything. Ask me how I know.

lines: 하늘 아래 사람은 다 똑같아요. 저 사람들도 다 엄마 배 속에서 나왔잖아요, 안 그래요?
en: They lost a war. So what?
Everyone under the sky’s the same. They all came out of their mothers’ wombs too, didn’t they?

blocks.html: He says it the way boys say things they have never had to test. Then he goes back to the knot.
blocks.ko: 소년은 한 번도 시험해 볼 일이 없었던 말을 하는 소년답게 그 말을 한다. 그러고는 다시 매듭으로 돌아간다.

blocks.html: The general doesn’t answer. He stays where he is, long enough to look like a man guarding prisoners, which is what everyone in the square assumes he is.
blocks.ko: 장군은 대답하지 않는다. 그 자리에 서 있다. 포로를 지키는 사람처럼 보일 만큼 오래. 광장의 모두가 그렇게 여긴다.

blocks.html: The last rope comes off near sunset.
blocks.ko: 마지막 밧줄은 해 질 녘에 풀린다.

lines: 내가 옛날에 임금한테 아들들 걸고 맹세했다. 서른 해 전에. 아직 하나도 없다.
en: I swore my sons to a king once. Thirty years back. Haven’t got any yet.
…If I ever do, I hope he’s like you.

lines: 저처럼 어떻게요? 제가 이 나라에서 말을 제일—
en: Like me how? I’m the best rider in the whole—
Not the riding.

blocks.html: The land they give him instead is a strip of stones by the Alchun that nobody wanted. The chronicle calls this virtue. Mugwan calls it typical, and holds the knot.
blocks.ko: 대신 받은 땅은 알천 가의, 아무도 원하지 않던 돌밭이다. 기록은 이를 덕이라 한다. 무관랑은 늘 그렇다고 하고, 매듭을 잡아 준다.

blocks.label: The Silla camp below Great Gaya · that night
blocks.ko: 대가야 아래 신라 진영 · 그날 밤

blocks.html: That night the freed captives sleep in the Silla camp, because they have nowhere else to sleep. Sadaham sits on a coil of the rope he cut, eating rice out of his helmet. Out of the dark comes the general from the square, on foot.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 풀려난 포로들은 신라 진영에서 잔다. 달리 잘 곳이 없어서다. 사다함은 자기가 끊은 밧줄 더미에 앉아 투구에 담은 밥을 먹는다. 어둠 속에서 광장의 그 장군이 걸어 나온다.

lines: 밧줄 찾으러 오셨으면, 제가 다 끊었어요.
en: If it’s the rope you want, I cut it. All of it.
Ask the king for more.
I came for the rice.
Smells better than ours, it does.
It’s in my helmet.
I’ve eaten out of worse.

blocks.html: He sits down on the rope beside the boy without being asked. Sadaham hands him the helmet. It is the politest thing the boy does all year.
blocks.ko: 그는 청하지도 않았는데 소년 옆 밧줄 더미에 앉는다. 사다함이 투구를 건넨다. 그해 소년이 한 일 중 가장 예의 바른 일이다.

lines: 가야 분이시죠. 말씨가 저 성문이랑 똑같네요.
en: You’re the Gaya one. You talk like the gate.
So they keep telling me.

lines: 그중에 아는 사람 있었어요? 줄에 묶였던 사람들.
en: Were any of them yours? The ones on the rope.
All of them. None of them.
Eat your rice.

lines: 아까 투구 벗고 성문으로 걸어 올라가셨잖아요.
en: You walked up to that gate with your helmet off.
I’d have been shot.

lines: 넌 돌격했겠지. 저들은 그걸 기다리고 있었다.
en: You’d have charged it. They were waiting for that.
I did charge it.

lines: 늙은이한테 화살 다 쓴 다음에. 고맙단 말은 됐다.
en: After they’d spent their arrows on an old man. You’re welcome.

blocks.html: Sadaham laughs with his mouth full, which is a mistake, and spends a while coughing rice into the fire.
blocks.ko: 사다함이 입에 밥을 문 채 웃는다. 실수다. 한동안 모닥불에 밥알을 뱉으며 기침을 한다.

lines: 도성에선 너희들 머리에 꽃 꽂고 산에서 노래나 부르더니. 오늘은 빚 받으러 온 놈처럼 성문을 뚫고 들어가더군.
en: What is it, then. This hwarang.
In the capital I see you lot up the hills with flowers in your hair, singing. Then today you go through a gate like a debt collector.
You don’t know? Everyone knows.
It’s because you’re old.
Old, I am. Tell it slow, then.

lines: 사내애들이에요. 집안 좋은. 임금님이 하나 골라 앞세우면 나머지가 산으로 따라다니고, 말 타고, 노래하고, 그리고—
en: It’s boys. Good families. The king picks one of us to lead, and the rest follow him up mountains, and we ride, and we sing, and—
Sing.
The singing’s important. Don’t laugh.
I’m not laughing.

blocks.html: He is. It never reaches his mouth, but it gets as far as his eyes, which on that face is a long way.
blocks.ko: 웃고 있다. 입까지는 안 오지만 눈까지는 온다. 그 얼굴에서는 먼 길이다.

lines: 맹세는 뭘 하나? 다들 뭔가 걸고 맹세하잖나.
en: And what do you swear? Everybody swears something.

lines: 공식으로 하는 게 있어요. 충성, 임금님, 산. 말은 아무도 기억 못 해요.
en: There’s the official one. Loyalty, the king, the mountains. Nobody remembers the words.
Then there’s the real one.
Which is?

blocks.html: Sadaham doesn’t answer. He tips his chin at the cart wheel, where Mugwan has fallen asleep sitting up, snoring loud enough to bother the horses.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 대답하지 않는다. 턱으로 수레바퀴 쪽을 가리킨다. 무관랑이 앉은 채 잠들어, 말들이 신경 쓸 만큼 크게 코를 골고 있다.

lines: 쟤는 코 고는 게 저래요. 자기면서.
en: He says that’s me. It’s him.
…That’s the swear, is it.
That’s the swear.

blocks.html: The general looks across the river, where Great Gaya’s roofs are still smoking, for longer than a man needs to look at roofs. Sadaham, for once in his short life, does not say anything at all.
blocks.ko: 장군은 강 건너, 아직 연기가 오르는 대가야의 지붕들을 본다. 지붕을 보는 데 필요한 시간보다 오래. 사다함은 그 짧은 생에 처음으로, 아무 말도 하지 않는다.

en: …There.
Now I can face front.
Live long enough to be embarrassed by tonight, Sadaham.
lines: 오늘 밤이 부끄러워질 만큼 오래 살아라, 사다함.

en: Mugwan will be embarrassed for both of us.
lines: 무관이가 둘 몫으로 부끄러워해 줄 거예요.

blocks.html: He gets up slowly, the way older men get up after a day on a horse, and walks back to the horse lines alone.
blocks.ko: 그는 하루 종일 말을 탄 나이 든 사내가 일어나듯 천천히 일어나, 혼자 말 매는 데로 걸어간다.

blocks.html: Neither of them knows how short a year can be.
blocks.ko: 한 해가 얼마나 짧을 수 있는지, 두 사람 다 아직 모른다.

blocks.html: Sadaham never asks the general’s name. You will want it. Not yet.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 끝내 장군의 이름을 묻지 않는다. 당신은 알고 싶을 것이다. 아직은 아니다.

blocks.label: Mugwan
blocks.ko: 무관

blocks.label: Surabol, the hwarang hall · winter, 563
blocks.ko: 서라벌, 화랑의 방 · 563년 겨울

blocks.html: That winter the snoring turns into a cough Mugwan cannot put down. Sadaham sits by the mat and counts his breathing, the way they used to count snores.
blocks.ko: 그 겨울, 코 고는 소리가 무관랑이 내려놓을 수 없는 기침으로 바뀐다. 사다함은 자리 옆에 앉아 숨소리를 센다. 예전에 코 고는 소리를 세던 것처럼.

blocks.html: The little grey stone sits on the sill. Neither of them looks at it. Both of them know exactly where it is.
blocks.ko: 작은 잿빛 돌이 창턱에 놓여 있다. 둘 다 그쪽을 보지 않는다. 둘 다 그게 어디 있는지 정확히 안다.

en: Go eat. You smell like a sickroom.
lines: 가가 밥 무라. 니한테 병자 냄새 난다.

en: You remember what we swore.
We were thirteen. We also swore to marry the same girl.
If you die first, I will not eat.
So don’t.
lines: 니가 먼저 죽으믄 나는 안 묵는다.

en: If I die first— you already know.
lines: 내가 먼저 죽으믄 — 니는 이미 알제.

en: Then neither of us is allowed to be late.
lines: 그라믄 우리 둘 다 늦으믄 안 된데이.

blocks.html: Mugwan pushes the stone across the mat with two fingers. It is the last thing he does on purpose.
blocks.ko: 무관랑이 두 손가락으로 돌을 자리 너머로 밀어 준다. 그가 마음먹고 한 마지막 일이다.

blocks.html: Near the end he asks to be carried outside. Sadaham carries him up the ladder onto the roof of the hall, the same roof, because Mugwan asks for it by name.
blocks.ko: 끝 무렵, 무관은 밖으로 데려가 달라고 한다. 사다함은 그를 업고 사다리를 올라 화랑 집 지붕으로 간다. 그 지붕이다. 무관이 콕 집어 거기라고 했으니까.

en: …Well?
You said a year. It’s been three.
lines: 일 년이라 캤다. 삼 년 됐다.

en: Look. Past the hills. There.
…There.

blocks.html: There is nothing past the hills but more hills and the first grey of morning. Mugwan looks for a long time anyway. He has never once been able to tell Sadaham he was wrong about anything that mattered.
blocks.ko: 산 너머엔 산하고 새벽의 첫 잿빛뿐이다. 그래도 무관은 오래 본다. 중요한 일에서 사다함이 틀렸다고, 무관은 한 번도 말해 본 적이 없다.

en: …Yeah. I see it.

blocks.html: Mugwan dies of illness not long after the campaign. He does it quietly, the way he did everything, before dawn, so as not to wake anyone.
blocks.ko: 무관랑은 전역이 끝난 지 얼마 되지 않아 병으로 죽는다. 무엇이든 그렇게 했듯 조용히, 새벽이 오기 전에, 아무도 깨우지 않으려는 듯이.

blocks.html: Sadaham doesn’t shout. He sits on the roof with him until the sun is all the way up. Then he climbs down and tells the cooks there will be one less bowl. He says it very politely. That is how they know.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 소리 지르지 않는다. 해가 다 뜰 때까지 지붕에서 그와 같이 앉아 있다. 그러고는 내려와서 부엌에 그릇 하나 덜 놓으라고 한다. 아주 공손하게 말한다. 그래서 다들 안다.

blocks.label: Surabol · seven days, 564
blocks.ko: 서라벌 · 이레, 564

blocks.html: Sadaham does not take food for seven days. The cooks leave bowls by his door. The order sends its oldest men to argue with him. He thanks them, and does not eat.
blocks.ko: 사다함은 이레 동안 음식을 들지 않는다. 부엌에선 문 앞에 그릇을 둔다. 화랑은 가장 나이 든 이들을 보내 그를 설득한다. 그는 고맙다고 하고, 먹지 않는다.

blocks.html: On the fourth day he goes down to the river where they found the stones, and the boys who follow him hear him for the first time. It is not crying, exactly. It is the sound a horse makes when it has run too far. It goes on for a long time, and nobody goes near.
blocks.ko: 나흘째 되는 날, 그는 돌을 찾았던 그 강가로 내려간다. 따라간 아이들은 그 소리를 처음 듣는다. 우는 거라고 하기는 어렵다. 너무 멀리 달린 말이 내는 소리 같은 것이다. 오래 이어지고, 아무도 다가가지 못한다.

blocks.html: On the fifth day the king comes himself.
blocks.ko: 닷새째에는 왕이 직접 온다.

en: Eat. That is an order.
You told them, Majesty. If I die, it was my idea.
Write it down.
lines: 마마께서 그러셨지예. 내 죽으면 내 생각이었다꼬.

blocks.html: The king stands in the doorway for a while. Then he goes, and does not send anyone else.
blocks.ko: 왕은 한동안 문간에 서 있다. 그러고는 돌아가, 아무도 다시 보내지 않는다.

blocks.html: He keeps the stone in his fist. At night he holds it up to the lamp, as if the bad characters might have changed.
blocks.ko: 그는 돌을 주먹에 쥐고 지낸다. 밤이면 등잔에 비춰 본다. 엉망인 글씨가 바뀌기라도 했을 것처럼.

en: …It’s quiet in here. Nobody snoring.

blocks.html: On the seventh night the bowl by the door is still full. He lies down on Mugwan’s side of the mat.
blocks.ko: 이레째 밤에도 문 앞의 그릇은 그대로다. 그는 자리의 무관랑 쪽에 눕는다.

en: …Wait up.
I’m not late.

blocks.html: He is seventeen. The order buries two headbands beside him, and one small stone with terrible handwriting. It keeps the story, because a Hwarang who outlives his vow is only a boy with a nice coat.
blocks.ko: 열일곱이다. 화랑은 그 곁에 머리띠 둘과, 글씨가 엉망인 작은 돌 하나를 묻는다. 그리고 이야기를 남긴다. 맹세보다 오래 사는 화랑은, 옷만 좋은 소년에 불과하므로.

blocks.label: The Song of Sadaham
blocks.ko: 사다함의 노래

blocks.html: One more thing came down from that year, in a manuscript that may or may not be what it says it is. It gives Sadaham a song, the Song of the Blue Bird. The book says he wrote it for a woman. The yard, which knew him, has always sung it for somebody else.
blocks.ko: 그해에서 내려온 게 하나 더 있다. 진짜인지 아닌지 모를 필사본에 실려서. 거기엔 사다함의 노래가 하나 있다. 청조가, 파랑새의 노래. 책은 그가 한 여인에게 지어 줬다고 한다. 그를 알던 연무장은, 언제나 다른 사람을 위해 불렀다.

blocks.html:
Blue bird, blue bird,
blue bird above the clouds,
why do you stay in my bean field?
Blue bird, blue bird,
blue bird of my bean field,
why fly back up into the clouds?
If you came, why not stay?
If you would go, why did you come?
Why make me weep for nothing,
ache and waste and die?
When I die, what ghost will I be?
When I die, I will be a guardian spirit.
blocks.ko:
파랑새야 파랑새야
저 구름 위의 파랑새야
어찌하여 나의 콩밭에 머무는가
파랑새야 파랑새야
너 나의 콩밭의 파랑새야
어찌하여 다시 날아들어 구름 위로 가는가
이미 왔으면 가지 말지
또 갈 것을 어찌하여 왔는가
부질없이 눈물짓게 하며
마음 아프고 여위어 죽게 하는가
나는 죽어 무슨 귀신 될꼬
나는 죽어 신병 되리
blocks.source: Hwarang Segi (花郞世紀), “Cheongjoga” (靑鳥歌), attributed to Sadaham; the manuscript’s authenticity is disputed

blocks.html: The yard still sings it at roll call. Two places in the front row stay empty.
blocks.ko: 연무장은 지금도 점호 때 이 노래를 부른다. 맨 앞줄 두 자리는 지금도 비어 있다.

blocks.html: When his little sister rides too fast, Bupmin always pulls up first. Gotaso never pulls up. Not for horses. Not for anyone…!
blocks.ko: 여동생이 너무 빨리 달리면 법민은 늘 먼저 고삐를 당긴다. 고타소는 당기지 않는다. 말 앞에서도, 누구 앞에서도…!

logline.en: A young girl is going to do what she’s going to do.
logline.ko: 어린 여자애는 하고 싶은 건 결국 하고 만다.

COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: A young girl is going to do what she’s going to do.
blocks.ko: 어린 여자애는 하고 싶은 건 결국 하고 만다.

blocks.html: Two springs ago she proved it, and her father has not slept properly since.
blocks.ko: 두 해 전 봄에 그 애가 그걸 증명했다. 그 뒤로 아버지는 잠을 제대로 자 본 적이 없다.

blocks.label: The Lantern Market
blocks.ko: 연등 장터

blocks.label: Two Springs Earlier
blocks.ko: 두 해 전 봄

blocks.html: Gotaso is twelve. She goes out to the lantern market with two maids and does not come back with any. The maids are found first, by the river, in the morning.
blocks.ko: 고타소는 열두 살이다. 시녀 둘을 데리고 등 시장에 나갔다가, 아무도 없이 돌아오지 못한다. 시녀들이 먼저 발견된다. 강가에서, 아침에.

en: Husband.
…Husband.

blocks.html: Chunchu says nothing. This is the part the household remembers afterwards and none of them can describe properly: he does not shout, he does not ask a second question, he simply stops being the man who talks.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 뒷날 집안 사람들이 모두 기억하되 아무도 제대로 옮기지 못하는 대목이 이것이다. 소리치지 않고, 두 번 묻지 않고, 그저 말하는 사람이기를 그만둔다.

en: Chunchu. Sit down.
I already have men out.
…Chunchu.
How many horses do we have.

blocks.html: It is the only sentence he speaks for two days. Yushin will try to tell it later as a joke and will stop halfway through, every time.
blocks.ko: 이틀 동안 그가 입 밖에 낸 문장은 그것 하나다. 유신은 뒷날 그 이야기를 우스개로 꺼냈다가, 매번 중간에서 그만둔다.

blocks.html: They were not bandits, in the sense that bandits want money. No word came and nothing was asked for, which is worse, and Chunchu understood what it meant before anyone in the room said it aloud.
blocks.ko: 돈을 원한다는 뜻에서의 도적은 아니었다. 기별도 없고 요구도 없었다. 그편이 더 나쁘고, 춘추는 방 안의 누가 소리 내어 말하기 전에 그 뜻을 알아들었다.

blocks.label: The Ford
blocks.ko: 여울

blocks.html: They find the road on the second night. What Chunchu does at the ford is in no record, because the two men who could have written it down were at the ford.
blocks.ko: 이틀째 밤에 길을 찾는다. 여울에서 춘추가 한 일은 어느 기록에도 없다. 그것을 적을 수 있었을 두 사람이 그 여울에 있었기 때문이다.

en: Enough.
Chunchu. Enough.
…The child is watching.

blocks.html: He stops. He wipes his hands on the grass, carefully, both sides, the way a man does before he picks up something clean.
blocks.ko: 그는 멈춘다. 풀에 손을 닦는다. 양손을, 조심스럽게 — 깨끗한 것을 들어 올리기 전에 사내가 하는 방식으로.

en: …Gotaso.
Father… there is something on your coat.
So there is.
I will change it later.

blocks.html: He carries her the whole way home. It is nineteen li. He does not let anyone take a turn and he does not put her down to eat.
blocks.ko: 그는 돌아오는 길 내내 아이를 업는다. 십구 리다. 아무에게도 넘기지 않고, 밥을 먹으려고 내려놓지도 않는다.

en: …Put her down.
Your arms will come off.
A little longer.

lines: 자네가 그렇게 조용해지는 건 처음 봤네.
en: I have never seen you go quiet like that.
…Brother.
I have two sons and one daughter.
One daughter.

blocks.label: Spring
blocks.ko: 봄

blocks.label: The Gyuku Match
blocks.ko: 격구 시합

blocks.html: Before anyone says the word wedding, there is a spring match. Gotaso attends with two new guards, and her father watches her instead of the ball.
blocks.ko: 누가 혼인이라는 말을 꺼내기도 전에, 봄 격구가 있다. 고타소는 새 호위 둘을 달고 나오고, 아버지는 공 대신 딸을 본다.

blocks.html: At a spring gyuku match the Hwarang ride for the Queen. The stands smell of horse and expensive varnish. Servants carry club-boxes the way other households carry ancestral tablets. Gotaso is fourteen now, and only meant to watch.
blocks.ko: 봄 격구에서 화랑들이 여왕 앞에서 달린다. 관중석에서는 말 냄새와 비싼 니스 냄새가 난다. 시종들은 다른 집이 신주를 모시듯 채 함을 모신다. 고타소는 이제 열넷이고, 보기만 하러 왔다.

blocks.html: In the councillors’ row two old Hwarang sit together and bet against each other out of habit: a councillor with prayer beads, and a broad man with a lunch. They have not agreed on anything since they were sixteen, except where to sit.
blocks.ko: 대신들 줄에 늙은 화랑 둘이 나란히 앉아, 버릇처럼 서로 반대편에 내기를 건다. 염주 든 대신 하나, 도시락 든 덩치 하나. 열여섯 이후로 둘이 뜻을 모은 건 앉을 자리 하나뿐이다.

en: Two cups on the Gaya boy’s side.

lines: 아는 무슨 아고, 알천아. 마흔여섯이다. 대장군 인장까지 찼다.
en: He isn’t a boy, Alchun. He’s forty-six. He carries a marshal’s seal.

lines: 니한테는 둘 중 하나 죽을 때까지 가야 아다.
en: He’s a Gaya boy to you till one of you dies.

lines: ……그라믄 저쪽에 두 잔. 누군가는 저 사람한테 져 줘야지.
en: …Two cups on his side, then. Somebody has to lose to him.

lines: 저 나이 화랑이 저런 걸 들고 나오믄… 집안이 보인데이.
en: Look at that club box.
A Hwarang that young carrying that… you can see the household.
I am not looking at the club.
Only the man.

blocks.html: Pumsuk takes the ball on the off-side — a showy, illegal-looking, completely legal cut — and for half a breath too long catches her eye instead of the goal. His premium gyuku club flashes once in the sun: presentation-silk still on the headcover, five coloured rings on the shaft, vulgar as Surabol sport gets.
blocks.ko: 품석이 오프사이드에서 공을 받는다 — 허세 같고 반칙 같아 보이지만 완전히 합법인 컷 — 그리고 반 호흡만큼 너무 길게, 골이 아니라 그의 눈을 붙잡는다. 프리미엄 격구채가 햇살에 한 번 번쩍인다. 헤드커버엔 아직 진열용 비단, 자루엔 오방색 고리 다섯. 서라벌 경기가 천박해지는 지점이다.

blocks.caption: Kim Pumsuk. Rich, handsome, and legal by about an inch.
blocks.ko: 김품석. 돈 많고, 잘생겼고, 딱 한 뼘 차이로 반칙이 아니다.

en: …Who is that.
Mother.
Mother. I asked who that is.
Hwarang Kim Pumsuk. / Don’t stare.
I already did.
And he looked back. He did, he did.

lines: 저 이제 다른 사람은 안 볼 끼라요.
en: I am never going to look at anyone else.
For the rest of my life.
…Fourteen years old, using the word “life.”
Fourteen is exactly when you are allowed to use it.
Later you get too embarrassed.

blocks.html: She looks at him the way a person looks at weather they have decided to live in — not bargaining, not counting rooms. Just the face.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 그를, 살기로 한 날씨를 보듯 본다 — 흥정하지 않고, 방을 세지 않고. 그저 그 얼굴.

lines: 자네 딸은 다른 걸 보고 있고.
en: You are watching your daughter, Chunchu.
Your daughter is watching something else.
…I see it, Majesty.
I am choosing not to.

blocks.label: The Flowering Trees
blocks.ko: 꽃나무 아래

blocks.html: They meet again under the flowering trees behind the training ground — not by accident the second time, and not the third.
blocks.ko: 수련장 뒤 꽃나무 아래에서 다시 만난다. 두 번째는 우연이 아니고, 세 번째도 아니다.

blocks.html: Under the flowering trees they forget to be a princess and a Hwarang.
blocks.ko: 꽃나무 아래에서 그들은 공주와 화랑이기를 잊는다.

en: I shouldn’t… see Your Highness here.
Then why do you come every day.
I come every day.
Yesterday I came twice.

lines: 경기 때 아버님께서 저를 보셨습니다. 쏘아야 할지도 모르는 말을 보듯이.
그래도 왔습니다. 오면 안 되는 줄 알면서.
en: …I don’t know.
Your father looked at me at the match. The way a man looks at a horse he may have to shoot.
I came anyway. Knowing I shouldn’t.

lines: 아버지는 요새 다들 그래 봐요. 그 나루 일 뒤로.
다른 사람들은 다 안 왔어요. 당신은 두 번 왔고요.
en: He looks at everyone like that now. Since the ford.
The others stopped coming. You came twice.

lines: 경기 때 그 컷 말입니다. 심판들이 다투던.
아씨 보시라고 한 겁니다. 평생 반칙을 무릅써 본 적이 없습니다.
en: That cut at the match. The one the umpires argued over.
It was for you. I have never risked a foul in my life.
…I would risk it again.

lines: 그럼 왜… 아직 제 손목을 놓지 않으세요.
en: And I’m not supposed to… touch your hand either?
Then why… won’t you let go of my wrist.
You mustn’t.
…And yet you’re holding it.
And… I cannot take it back.

blocks.label: The Club Box
blocks.ko: 채 함

blocks.html: Bupmin still owes his little sister eleven days of carrying her club box. She has found a use for them.
blocks.ko: 법민은 아직 여동생의 채 함을 열하루 더 들어 줘야 한다. 동생은 그 열하루의 쓸모를 찾아냈다.

lines: 선배들 숙소에 갖다 놔라. 세 번째 걸이.
누가 있으믄 내 끼라 캐라. 크게.
en: Take it to the seniors’ hall. Third rack.
Not the second. The third.
And if anyone’s there, say it’s mine. Loudly.
Whose is the third rack?
…Nobody’s.
Gotaso. Whose.

lines: 품석 공 끼다. 됐나. 품석 공.
en: Pumsuk’s. Fine. Pumsuk’s.
Don’t make that face.

lines: 첫날 내한테 뒷간 보여 준 사람이다. 두 군데 다.
en: Pumsuk? Pumsuk-sunbae?
He showed me the latrines. On my first day. Both of them.
He’s thorough. About everything.
Stop. Don’t say “everything” like that.
Don’t say anything like that.

lines: 그 사람이 내 손목 잡았다. 나무 밑에서. 한참.
en: He held my wrist. Under the trees. For ages.

lines: 니 채 함에 토할 것 같다.
en: I’m going to be sick on your club box.
Then it’s another month.

blocks.html: He takes it to the third rack. Pumsuk is there, polishing the five coloured rings on his own shaft, and goes red so fast that Bupmin has to look at the ceiling.
blocks.ko: 법민은 세 번째 걸이로 간다. 품석이 거기서 자기 채의 오색 고리를 닦고 있다가, 어찌나 빨리 빨개지는지 법민은 천장을 봐야 한다.

lines: 마마. 그거— 아씨께서— 무슨 전하실 말씀이라도?
en: Your Highness. Is that— did she— is there a message?
She says it’s hers. Loudly.
…Did she say anything else?

lines: 선배님. 제발예. 저 걔하고 아침 같이 먹어예.
en: Sunbae. Please. I have breakfast with her.

blocks.html: He carries the box for eleven more days. Then, for reasons he refuses to discuss, a twelfth.
blocks.ko: 그는 열하루를 더 채 함을 든다. 그러고는, 절대 말하지 않는 어떤 이유로, 열이틀째에도.

blocks.label: The Goldsmiths’ Lane
blocks.ko: 금장이 골목

blocks.html: Gotaso does not buy him a present. Buying is for people who haven’t thought about it.
blocks.ko: 고타소는 선물을 사지 않는다. 사는 건 생각을 안 해 본 사람들이나 하는 짓이다.

blocks.html: She goes down to the goldsmiths’ lane with one maid and a pouch of her own hairpin money, and asks the oldest smith there to teach her to hammer.
blocks.ko: 하녀 하나와 비녀값을 모은 주머니를 들고 금장이 골목으로 내려가서, 거기서 제일 늙은 장인에게 망치질을 가르쳐 달라고 한다.

blocks.speaker: The goldsmith
lines: 아기씨, 금은 누구 따님인지 안 따집니다. 데는 건 다 똑같아요.
en: Princess, gold doesn’t care whose daughter you are. It burns everybody the same.

lines: 나비요. 내 비녀랑 똑같이. 한 쌍이 되게.
en: Good. Then it’ll really be mine.
A butterfly. Like my pin. So we’re a pair.

blocks.html: It takes her nine days. She burns two fingers and one sleeve. One wing comes out bigger than the other, and the smith offers, very politely, to fix it.
blocks.ko: 아흐레가 걸린다. 손가락 둘과 소매 하나를 태운다. 날개 한쪽이 다른 쪽보다 크게 나오자, 장인이 아주 공손하게 고쳐 드리겠다고 한다.

lines: 그쪽이 큰 건, 그 사람 생각하면서 두드려서 그래요.
en: Don’t you dare.
That one’s bigger because I was thinking about him when I hit it.

blocks.html: She threads it on a pink cord and hides it up her sleeve. Not yet. A thing like that needs a day big enough to hold it.
blocks.ko: 분홍 끈에 꿰어 소매 속에 감춘다. 아직은 아니다. 그런 물건에는 그걸 담을 만큼 큰 날이 필요하다.

blocks.label: The Palace Steps
blocks.ko: 궁궐 계단

blocks.html: Rain finds them once on the palace steps. Neither of them moves to go inside.
blocks.ko: 비는 궁 섬돌에서 한 번 그들을 붙잡는다. 둘 다 안으로 들어갈 생각을 하지 않는다.

en: You’re soaked.
…Why are you smiling.
Ah. / Is it my hair… on your sleeve?

lines: 공주님 머리카락이… 제 소매에 붙어 있어서요.
en: Your hair is… caught on my sleeve.
I should free it.
My hand won’t move.
Neither will my feet.

lines: 저는 이 소매 옆에 평생 서 있을 수도 있어요.
en: Then leave it.
Leave it there.
The sleeve. The hair.
I could stand beside this sleeve for the rest of my life.
No — closer.
My lady.
If this goes on… I will come apart.
Here. On the steps.
So will I.
So I settled all of it last night.
Four children. I have named them.
I am telling my parents today.
…Four?
You don’t want them?
…I want to know the names.

blocks.html: Four children, already named. Now the boy has to ask her father. And her father wants a vow…!
blocks.ko: 아이 넷, 이름까지 다 지어 두었다. 이제 그 사내가 아버지께 청할 차례다. 그리고 아버지는 맹세를 원한다…!

logline.en: Pumsuk asks for the girl. Chunchu asks for something else.
logline.ko: 품석은 딸을 청한다. 춘추는 다른 것을 청한다.

THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. blocks.html: Pumsuk asks for the girl. Chunchu asks for something else.
blocks.ko: 품석은 딸을 청한다. 춘추는 다른 것을 청한다.

blocks.label: The Study
blocks.ko: 서재

blocks.html: Chunchu receives him in the study, not the hall. A go game sits half-played between them. Chunchu is wiping his hands on a cloth, slowly, both sides. He has not been doing anything to dirty them.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 그를 대청이 아니라 서재에서 맞는다. 둘 사이에 바둑판이 반쯤 두어진 채 놓여 있다. 춘추는 천으로 손을 닦는다. 천천히, 앞뒤로. 손을 더럽힐 일은 아무것도 하지 않았는데.

lines: 대감. 저— 고타소 아씨 일로 왔습니다.
허락해 주신다면, 제가— 그러니까, 청을 드리고자—
en: Sir. I— I have come about Lady Gotaso.
With your permission, I would like— that is, I would ask—

lines: 아침에 그 애가 말하더군. 아이 넷, 이름까지. 아주 꼼꼼해. 나를 닮아서.
en: Sit. You’re making the stones nervous.
She told me at breakfast. Four children, all named. She is very thorough. She gets that from me.
…Then you consent, sir?

lines: 딸은 허락하네. 그 애는 애초에 내가 붙잡아 둘 수 있는 아이가 아니었어.
화랑, 연무장에서 뭘 가르치는지 아나? 계율 다섯.
en: I consent to the girl. She was never mine to keep.
Do you know what the yard teaches, Hwarang? Five rules.
Here is a sixth.

blocks.html: Munhee is in the doorway. She has been there the whole time. Pumsuk only notices now, which tells you something about Pumsuk.
blocks.ko: 문희가 문간에 서 있다. 처음부터 거기 있었다. 품석은 이제야 알아챈다. 품석에 대해 꽤 많은 걸 말해 주는 대목이다.

en: Don’t make him swear.
…Why not.

lines: 지키면 당연한 것이고, 못 지키면 그이가 죽습니다.
en: If he keeps it, it was owed anyway. If he cannot, it kills him.

blocks.html: He makes him swear. It is the only time in this record that Chunchu misreads a room, and it is the room with his daughter in it.
blocks.ko: 그는 맹세를 시킨다. 이 기록을 통틀어 춘추가 방을 잘못 읽은 유일한 순간이고, 그 방에는 그의 딸이 있었다.

lines: 그 아이한테 무슨 일이 생기면, 내가 자네를 죽일 거라는 건 알지? 하하…
en: If anything happens to her, you know I’m going to kill you, right? Haha...

blocks.html: He laughs. He puts the cloth down. Pumsuk has heard, the way all of Surabol has heard, about a certain ford. Nobody else in the room is laughing.
blocks.ko: 그가 웃는다. 천을 내려놓는다. 품석도 들었다. 서라벌 사람이 다 들었듯, 어느 나루에서 있었던 일을. 방 안에서 웃는 사람은 그 하나뿐이다.

lines: 제 목숨을 걸고 고타소 양을 보호하겠습니다!
en: On my life, I will protect Lady Gotaso!

blocks.label: The Wedding
blocks.ko: 혼례

blocks.html: At the back of the hall, the Queen watches her great-niece marry for love.
blocks.ko: 식장 뒤편에서, 여왕은 종손녀가 사랑하는 사람과 혼인하는 것을 지켜본다.

blocks.html: Munhee does not watch the vows. She watches the doorway and remembers a different night in the same house: the girl-child arriving, pink silk already too sure of itself, Chunchu’s hand huge around a wrist that would never learn to be still. They named her Gotaso when the lantern-band was the same shape it is tonight.
blocks.ko: 문희는 서약을 보지 않는다. 문간을 본다. 같은 집의 다른 밤을 기억한다. 계집아이가 도착하던 밤. 분홍 비단이 벌써 제 일을 아는 밤. 춘추의 손이, 끝내 가만히 있는 법을 배우지 못할 손목을 크게 감싸던 밤. 등불의 띠가 오늘 밤과 같은 모양일 때, 이름을 고타소라 붙였다.

lines: 저 문간을 지나간 게 이 집안에서만 벌써 셋일세.
en: …Your son’s girl.
That doorway has taken three of this house now.

blocks.caption: The Queen’s elder sister, and Chunchu’s mother. She gave up a throne to marry for love.
blocks.ko: 여왕의 언니이자 춘추의 어머니. 사랑을 위해 왕좌를 내려놓았다.

en: Four. If Your Majesty counts honestly.
…I count honestly.
We will be happy forever!

blocks.label: The Wedding Night
blocks.ko: 첫날밤

en: …My lady. Your hands are cold.
But the back of your neck… is hot.

lines: 그리고… 품석 공 손이 너무 뜨거워서요.
en: Because I am shaking.
And… because yours are too warm.
The hand at my waist.
Don’t take it away.
Are you frightened?
If I… come closer.

lines: 빨리 아무도 없는 데로 가고 싶어서요.
저를 한 번 더 봐 주세요.
en: No.
Because I want to be somewhere with nobody in it.
Look at me once more.
Wait. Close your eyes.
…No peeking. Hold out your hand.

blocks.html: She puts it in his palm: a gold butterfly no bigger than a thumb, one wing too big, still smelling faintly of the forge. She ties the pink cord to his belt herself, with a knot nobody taught her.
blocks.ko: 그녀가 그의 손바닥에 그것을 올려놓는다. 엄지만 한 금나비. 날개 한쪽이 너무 크고, 아직 대장간 냄새가 희미하게 난다. 분홍 끈은 그녀가 직접 그의 허리띠에 묶는다. 아무도 가르쳐 준 적 없는 매듭으로.

lines: 날개 한쪽이— 송구합니다. 아름답습니다. 한쪽이 더 큽니다.
en: …You made this.
One wing is— forgive me. It’s beautiful. One wing is bigger.

lines: 내 건 비녀에, 당신 건 허리띠에. 이제 멀리서 보면 아무도 우리 구분 못 해요.
en: That’s the side where I was thinking about you.
Mine’s on my pin. Yours is on your belt. From far away nobody can tell us apart.
I will never take it off.

blocks.html: Behind the doors the feast falls away.
blocks.ko: 문 너머로 잔치가 멀어진다.

blocks.label: The Empty Hall
blocks.ko: 빈 전각

blocks.html: The hall empties. The Queen does not leave, and neither does the Marshal. Neither of them has ever been the first to leave a room.
blocks.ko: 대청이 빈다. 여왕은 일어서지 않고, 장군도 그렇다. 둘 다 한 번도 먼저 방을 나선 적이 없다.

blocks.html: She has had twenty years to learn the back of his neck: the place the armour strap has worn shiny, the two grey hairs at his temple that were not there before the last campaign. Tonight the hall is empty and nobody is writing anything down, so she looks at all of it.
blocks.ko: 그의 목덜미를 익힐 시간이 이십 년 있었다. 갑옷 끈에 쓸려 반들거리는 자리, 지난 원정 전에는 없던 관자놀이의 흰 머리 두 올. 오늘 밤은 대전이 비었고 아무도 아무것도 적지 않으므로, 여왕은 그 전부를 본다.

blocks.html: Color rises along her throat. She keeps her mouth closed so the breath will not give her away. He does not turn. That is the only mercy left in the room.
blocks.ko: 빛이 목선을 따라 오른다. 숨이 자기를 팔지 못하게 입을 다문다. 그는 돌아보지 않는다. 그 방에 남은 유일한 자비다.

en: Your Majesty.
…Not that word. Not tonight.
Then what am I to call you.
Don’t call me anything.

blocks.html: He takes one step. It is the smallest thing he does in this entire record and it costs him longer than any battle in it.
blocks.ko: 그가 한 걸음 다가선다. 이 기록을 통틀어 그가 한 가장 작은 일이고, 이 기록의 어떤 전투보다 오래 걸린다.

lines: 오늘 조카딸이 사랑하는 사내와 혼인하는 것을 보셨습니다.
저는 내내 폐하 얼굴만 보고 있었습니다.
en: Today you watched your niece marry the man she loves.
I watched your face the entire time.
Your Majesty—
Yushin.
…You said my name.
So stop.

lines: 한 마디만 하겠습니다. 딱 한 마디만.
말 두 필이면 됩니다. 오늘 밤이면 됩니다.
국경까지 사흘이고, 사흘 뒤면 우리는 아무도 아닙니다.
en: One sentence. Let me have one.
Two horses. Tonight would be enough.
Three days to the border. After three days we are nobody at all.

blocks.html: She reaches up. He is very still, the way a man is still when he has already decided not to be the one who moves. Her fingers find his mouth before the rest of the sentence can.
blocks.ko: 여왕이 손을 든다. 유신은 아주 가만히 서 있다 — 먼저 움직이지 않기로 이미 정한 사내의 방식으로. 남은 말이 나오기 전에, 손끝이 먼저 그의 입에 닿는다.

lines: 말이 되어 버리면, 내가 그걸 평생 듣고 살아야 하네.
en: Don’t say it.
If you say it, I have to hear it for the rest of my life.
Then hear it for the rest of your life.

blocks.html: For a moment she does not answer, and the moment is long enough that both of them will spend years deciding what it meant.
blocks.ko: 잠시 여왕은 대답하지 않는다. 그 잠시는, 두 사람이 뒷날 여러 해 동안 무슨 뜻이었는지 정하며 보낼 만큼 길다.

blocks.html: Her fingers are still on his mouth. He does not take the next step. The lamp between them does the looking. When she speaks again she is already Queen.
blocks.ko: 손끝은 아직 그의 입에 있다. 그는 다음 걸음을 떼지 않는다. 둘 사이의 등잔이 본다. 다시 말할 때 그녀는 이미 여왕이다.

lines: …자네가 없으면 이 나라가 반년을 못 가.
en: …Without you this country does not last half a year.
You are talking about the country.

lines: 나라 얘기밖에 할 수 있는 게 없으니까.
en: Because the country is the only thing I am permitted to talk about.

blocks.html: She is close enough now to count what it is costing him. She counts it. Then she takes her hand back and puts it where a queen’s hand goes.
blocks.ko: 이제는 그것이 그에게 얼마를 치르게 하는지 셀 수 있을 만큼 가깝다. 여왕은 정말로 센다. 그러고는 손을 거두어, 여왕의 손이 있어야 할 자리에 둔다.

lines: 한 발만 더 오면 내가 못 멈추네.
en: One more step and I do not stop.
…Then I will not take it.
Thank you.

lines: 그건 폐하께서 이기셨을 때 나는 소리입니다.
en: Don’t thank me.
That is the sound you make when you have won.
…Then neither of us has.

blocks.html: He steps back into the shape of a subject. It fits, because he has worn it twenty years. It has never once fit.
blocks.ko: 그는 신하의 모양으로 물러선다. 이십 년을 입은 옷이라 몸에 맞는다. 한 번도 몸에 맞은 적이 없다.

en: Your Majesty.
…Yes. That will do.

blocks.html: Neither of them mentions that night again. Thirty-two years later, on the last day of his life, he is asked whether he ever wanted anything for himself, and the record notes only that he took some time to answer.
blocks.ko: 두 사람은 그날 밤을 다시 입에 올리지 않는다. 삼십이 년 뒤, 생의 마지막 날에 그는 스스로를 위해 바란 것이 있었느냐는 물음을 받는다. 기록은 그가 대답하기까지 시간이 조금 걸렸다는 것만 적어 두었다.

blocks.label: The Road to Daeya
blocks.ko: 대야로 가는 길

blocks.html: Three days later the couple leave for Daeya Fortress, where Pumsuk has just been named Guardian. She waves from the cart until the capital is out of sight. He rides beside the wheel the whole way, and every time the cart jolts, the gold butterfly on his belt jumps. Daeya is a border post. Nobody at the wedding said the word border out loud.
blocks.ko: 사흘 뒤 부부는 대야성으로 떠난다. 품석이 막 성주로 임명된 곳이다. 그녀는 도성이 보이지 않을 때까지 수레에서 손을 흔든다. 그는 내내 바퀴 옆에서 말을 몬다. 수레가 덜컹일 때마다 허리띠의 금나비가 튀어 오른다. 대야성은 국경 초소다. 혼례에서 국경이라는 말을 입 밖에 낸 사람은 아무도 없었다.

blocks.html: Bupmin walks beside the other wheel as far as the city gate, carrying his sister’s club box one last time. At the gate Pumsuk leans down from the saddle, like a man who has prepared a speech.
blocks.ko: 법민은 성문까지 반대쪽 바퀴 옆을 걷는다. 마지막으로 여동생의 채 함을 들고. 성문에서 품석이 말 위에서 몸을 숙인다. 연설이라도 준비해 온 사람처럼.

en: Your Highness. I suppose now I ought to call you—
…brother.
Please don’t.
…Sunbae. The road to Daeya has a lot of bends in it.
Don’t pull up.
…I won’t.
What are you two whispering about?
Latrines.

blocks.html: A border post with a fine view of Baekje. The view works both ways.
blocks.ko: 백제가 훤히 보이는 국경 초소. 저쪽에서도 훤히 보인다.

blocks.html: Her parents stand at the gate until the dust settles. Then a little longer.
blocks.ko: 부모는 먼지가 가라앉을 때까지 대문에 서 있다. 그러고도 조금 더.

en: She waved the whole way. Like someone I know.

lines: 난 당신한테 손 흔든 적 없어요. 바느질하니라 바빴거든요.
en: I never waved at you. I was busy sewing.
…So you do remember.
Don’t you start. Not at the gate.

blocks.html: “Dear… have you already forgotten how we met?” Munhee hasn’t. It starts with a boy’s shoes in a pond, and ends with a coat torn on purpose…!
blocks.ko: “여보… 우리가 어떻게 만났는지는 벌써 까먹었나?” 문희는 잊지 않았다. 연못에 빠진 소년의 신발로 시작해서, 일부러 찢긴 저고리로 끝나는 이야기…!

logline.en: It starts with a dream, and the dream is sold.
logline.ko: 꿈에서 시작한다. 그리고 그 꿈은 팔린다.

Same composition: at the corner of a plastered wall with a tiled coping, a young man holding a paper lantern leans toward a woman whose head is hooded in a long green jangot cloak; she turns shyly aside. The man is young KIM CHUNCHU (attached portrait: face, magenta #D8258C coat); the woman is MUNHEE (attached portrait: face, pink skirt under the green jangot). The blank space top-right where the original has a poem is left as empty paper. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Now: Young hwarang (stage portrait): clean-shaven, no moustache, no goatee, a young man's face; eager. Colour #D8258C. MUNHEE Colour #E07FA8. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.

images.at: Magenta silk and pink silk share a cup.
