blocks.label: Chunchu
blocks.ko: 춘추

blocks.label: How They Met
blocks.ko: 첫 만남

lines: 여보.... 우리가 어떻게 만났는지는 벌써 까먹었나?
en: Dear… have you already forgotten how we met?
Forgotten? I was there.
You were the one without a coat.

blocks.html: To get to the coat, you have to start with the shoes.
blocks.ko: 옷 얘기를 하려면 신발부터 시작해야 한다.

blocks.html: Every yard needs somebody to laugh at. Class 59 found theirs before roll call.
blocks.ko: 연무장마다 비웃을 사람이 하나는 필요하다. 오십구기는 점호도 하기 전에 찾아냈다.

blocks.label: Surabol, the Hwarang yard gate · Class 59’s first morning
blocks.ko: 서라벌, 화랑 연무장 문 · 오십구기의 첫 아침

blocks.html: Chunchu is fifteen, and has asked his father three times not to walk him to the gate. His father walks him to the gate.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 열다섯이다. 문까지 바래다주지 마시라고 아버지께 세 번이나 말씀드렸다. 아버지는 문까지 바래다준다.

blocks.html: Other fathers stop at the gate, clap a shoulder and leave. Kim Yongsu stops at the gate, clears his throat, and turns to his son as if he had been asked to address the court.
blocks.ko: 다른 아버지들은 문 앞에서 멈추고, 어깨를 한 번 두드리고, 돌아간다. 김용수는 문 앞에서 멈추고, 헛기침을 하고, 조정에서 연설이라도 하라는 명을 받은 사람처럼 아들을 마주 선다.

lines: 화랑은 꽃이라고들 할 거다. 헛소리야. 꽃은 어디 심길지 못 고른다. 넌 골랐지. 죽이 식었을 때 그걸 기억해라.
en: Right. I’ve been practising this.
They’ll tell you a Hwarang is a flower. Nonsense. A flower doesn’t pick where it’s planted. You picked. Remember that when the porridge is cold.
Father—

lines: 둘. 뭐든 세라. 너한테 웃어 주는 놈들을 세고, 한 달 뒤에 다시 세 봐.
셋. 밥 짓는 사람한테 잘해라. 여기서 뭘 좀 아는 건 그 사람뿐이다.
en: Two. Count everything. Count the boys who smile at you, then count them again in a month.
Three. Be kind to the cook. He’s the only one here who knows anything.
Father. People are looking.

lines: 당연히 보지. 네가 잘생겼으니까. 그건 네 어미 쪽이다.
…넷. 네 신발을 못에 던질 거다. 던지게 둬라.
en: Of course they’re looking. You’re very handsome. That’s your mother’s side.
…Four. They’ll put your shoes in the pond. Let them.

blocks.html: Then he turns to the gatepost, which nobody has introduced him to, and asks it whether he has forgotten anything. He waits for the answer. He seems satisfied with it.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 아무도 소개해 준 적 없는 문기둥 쪽으로 돌아서서, 빠뜨린 게 없느냐고 묻는다. 대답을 기다린다. 대답이 마음에 드는 눈치다.

en: No? Good.
Stand up straight. They like that here.

blocks.html: Forty boys in the yard have heard every word. Chunchu doesn’t watch him go. He watches the yard watch him go.
blocks.ko: 마당의 소년 마흔이 한마디도 빠짐없이 들었다. 춘추는 아버지가 가는 걸 보지 않는다. 마당이 아버지 가는 걸 보는 걸 본다.

blocks.label: The yard · roll call
blocks.ko: 연무장 · 점호

blocks.html: The roll clerk reads each name with its bone. Kim this, True Bone. Park that, True Bone. Then he gets to Chunchu and stops, and runs his finger back along the line, as if the ink might have moved.
blocks.ko: 점호 서기가 이름마다 뼈를 붙여 읽는다. 김 아무개, 진골. 박 아무개, 진골. 그러다 춘추에서 멈추더니, 먹이 움직이기라도 했나 싶은지 손가락으로 그 줄을 다시 짚어 본다.

blocks.speaker: Roll clerk
en: Kim Chunchu. …True Bone.
It says True Bone.

blocks.speaker: Heum
en: Says who? The ghost?

blocks.html: The yard laughs. Nobody in Surabol knows for certain who Kim Yongsu’s father was. A dead king, the song says, by way of a ghost. A ghost is a poor thing to inherit a bone from.
blocks.ko: 마당이 웃는다. 서라벌의 누구도 김용수의 아비가 누구인지 확실히 모른다. 노래로는 죽은 임금이다. 혼령을 거쳐서. 뼈를 물려받기엔 혼령은 영 시원찮은 조상이다.

blocks.speaker: Heum
lines: 야. 귀신 새끼. 아까 문 앞에 그거 너희 아버지냐?
en: Oi. Ghost boy. That your dad at the gate?
Does he talk to your mum, or just the doors?

lines: 우리 집 집사야. 정신이 좀 오락가락해.
en: That? No.
That’s our steward. He gets confused.

blocks.speaker: Heum
en: Your steward’s got your nose.
It’s a very common nose.

blocks.speaker: Heum
en: Common’s the word.

blocks.html: That gets the laugh, and it isn’t his. He doesn’t mention his father again. He doesn’t have to. The yard does it for him.
blocks.ko: 웃음이 터진다. 그의 몫은 아니다. 그는 다시는 아버지 얘기를 꺼내지 않는다. 그럴 필요가 없다. 마당이 대신 꺼내 주니까.

blocks.label: The hall · the first month
blocks.ko: 숙소 · 첫 달

blocks.html: His mat is moved to the drain end of the hall. Somebody paints a goblin on his shield in lamp-black. At meals the bench fills up just before he reaches it. And on the third night his shoes go in the pond.
blocks.ko: 그의 자리는 숙소 하수구 쪽 끝으로 밀려난다. 누군가 그의 방패에 그을음으로 도깨비를 그린다. 밥때면 그가 다가가기 직전에 의자가 꽉 찬다. 그리고 사흘째 밤, 신발이 못에 빠진다.

blocks.html: His father was right about the shoes. He lets them. Every night he wades in, fishes them out and leaves them by his mat to dry, and every morning they are wet again, and nobody can work out why it isn’t working.
blocks.ko: 신발 일은 아버지 말이 맞았다. 그는 던지게 둔다. 밤마다 못에 들어가 신발을 건져 자리 옆에 말려 두고, 아침마다 신발은 또 젖어 있다. 그런데 아무도 왜 이게 먹히지 않는지 알 수가 없다.

blocks.label: The yard · the Marshal’s question
blocks.ko: 연무장 · 도감의 물음

blocks.html: The yard belongs to the Yard Marshal, a True Bone veteran with a voice like a split log and two fingers left on his sword hand, which he counts on. On the tenth morning he stands the new class in a line and walks down it, asking every boy the same question.
blocks.ko: 연무장의 주인은 도감이다. 쪼갠 장작 같은 목소리에, 칼 쥐는 손엔 손가락이 둘만 남은 진골 노장이다. 그는 그 두 손가락으로 수를 센다. 열흘째 아침, 그는 새 기를 한 줄로 세우고 그 앞을 걸으며 소년마다 같은 것을 묻는다.

blocks.speaker: The Yard Marshal
en: What are you for?

blocks.html: “For the king!” “For Silla!” “For my house, sir!” He grunts at each one and moves on. Then he gets to the goblin’s boy and stops, because the line has gone quiet to listen.
blocks.ko: “임금을 위해서입니다!” “신라를 위해서입니다!” “가문을 위해서입니다!” 그는 하나하나에 끙 소리를 내고 지나간다. 그러다 도깨비 집 아들 앞에서 멈춘다. 줄 전체가 들으려고 조용해졌으니까.

blocks.speaker: The Yard Marshal
lines: 꼴 좀 봐라. 두 팔로도 창 하나 못 들겠다. 네 아비는 물하고 말한다지. 넌 뭐하고 말하냐?
en: And you. The goblin’s boy.
Look at you. You couldn’t lift a spear with both arms. Your father talks to water. What do you talk to?

lines: 물이랑 얘기하는 게 차라리 낫겠다 싶은 사람들하고요, 도감님.
그쪽 장사가 비어 있는 것 같아서요.
en: Men who’d rather be talking to water, sir.
It seemed a gap in the market.

blocks.html: Somebody in the line snorts. Somebody else does. The Marshal’s face doesn’t move at all.
blocks.ko: 줄 어딘가에서 누가 코웃음을 친다. 또 누가 친다. 도감의 얼굴은 꿈쩍도 하지 않는다.

blocks.speaker: The Yard Marshal
en: Clever.
Clever is a coward’s sword, boy.

lines: 칼집은 연무장에서 나옵니까, 제가 가져와야 합니까?
en: Then I’ll need a scabbard, sir.
Does the yard issue those, or do I bring my own?

blocks.html: Now the whole line laughs. The Marshal waits for it to stop.
blocks.ko: 이번엔 줄 전체가 웃는다. 도감은 웃음이 그칠 때까지 기다린다.

blocks.speaker: The Yard Marshal
en: The stone. The hill. Until I say.

blocks.html: The stone is the one the yard keeps for this: an old millstone with a rope through the hole. Boys twice his size have quit on the second circuit. Chunchu does one, then two. On the fourth he falls and splits his lip. On the seventh he catches himself talking to the stone under his breath, the way his father talks to things, and he is so angry about it that he does the eighth out of spite.
blocks.ko: 돌은 연무장이 이럴 때 쓰려고 둔 것이다. 구멍에 밧줄을 꿴 낡은 맷돌. 덩치가 그의 두 배인 소년들도 두 바퀴째에 손을 들었다. 춘추는 한 바퀴, 두 바퀴를 돈다. 네 바퀴째에 넘어져 입술이 터진다. 일곱 바퀴째에, 그는 자기가 아버지처럼 돌에 대고 중얼거리고 있다는 걸 깨닫는다. 그게 너무 화가 나서 여덟 바퀴째는 오기로 돈다.

blocks.html: At the top of the hill, on the ninth, a young man in an officer’s coat is sitting on the wall eating a pear.
blocks.ko: 아홉 바퀴째, 언덕 꼭대기 담 위에 장교 옷을 입은 젊은 사내 하나가 앉아 배를 먹고 있다.

en: That’s nine.
I know. I’m counting.
The Marshal went to bed after four.

blocks.html: Chunchu stands there with the rope on his shoulder and blood on his chin and considers this. Then he sits down on the stone, because there is nowhere else.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 어깨에 밧줄을, 턱엔 피를 묻힌 채 서서 그 말을 곱씹는다. 그러고는 맷돌 위에 털썩 앉는다. 달리 앉을 데가 없으니까.

en: …Nobody told me.
No. You’d have stopped.

lines: …언덕에서 그분이시죠. 오래전에. 제 별이 행성이라고 하셨던.
en: …You’re the one from the hill. Years ago. You told me my star was a planet.
It is a planet.
Kim Yushin. Class 51.

blocks.html: Everyone in the yard knows the name. Class 51 left years ago, and the yard still runs drills under his name. The instructors already call him General, half as a joke. The joke gets thinner every year.
blocks.ko: 연무장 사람이면 다 아는 이름이다. 오십일기는 몇 해 전에 떠났는데, 연무장은 아직도 그의 이름을 붙인 훈련을 한다. 교관들은 벌써 그를 장군이라 부른다. 반은 농담이다. 해마다 농담 쪽이 줄어든다.

lines: 선배님도 이런 일 당하셨어요? 처음 들어오셨을 때요?
en: Did they do this to you too, sir? When you were new?

lines: 가야 개라고 불렀지. 두 겨울 동안.
en: They called me the Gaya dog. Two winters.
And then?
Then I stopped losing on the yard.

lines: 전 연무장에선 평생 질 거예요, 선배님. 절 보세요.
en: I’m never going to stop losing on the yard, sir. Look at me.
I’ll win at supper.

blocks.html: Yushin looks at him. Then, for the first time in Class 59’s memory, the General laughs.
blocks.ko: 유신이 그를 본다. 그러고는, 오십구기가 기억하는 한 처음으로, 장군이 웃는다.

en: Do you play gyuku?
Badly.

lines: 입술이나 씻게. 그리고 다시는 대들지 말고.
en: Good. I need somebody to beat.
Wash your lip. And don’t answer him back again.
Was it wrong?

lines: 아니. 아주 잘했네. 그러니까 하지 말라는 거야.
en: No. It was very good. That’s why.

blocks.label: The storehouse · the quartermaster’s tally
blocks.ko: 곳간 · 군량 장부

blocks.html: In the second month the class’s rice runs short. The quartermaster blames the boys. The Yard Marshal blames the one he already dislikes.
blocks.ko: 둘째 달에 오십구기의 쌀이 모자란다. 군량관은 소년들 탓을 한다. 도감은 이미 마음에 안 드는 한 놈 탓을 한다.

blocks.speaker: The Yard Marshal
en: Goblin’s boy. Turn out your bag.

lines: 기꺼이요, 도감님. 그다음에 장부 좀 봐도 되겠습니까?
en: Gladly, sir. And then may I see the tally?

blocks.html: The bag holds a spare robe and a book of Odes. The tally takes him as long as it takes to read it once.
blocks.ko: 짐 속엔 갈아입을 옷 한 벌과 시경 한 권뿐이다. 장부는 한 번 읽는 데 걸리는 시간이면 충분하다.

lines: 누가 작은 되로 담고 큰 되로 서명했어. 마흔 날이면, 아홉 자루야.
흠. 이 연무장에 쌀 대는 거, 너희 외숙이지?
en: The sacks are right. The measure isn’t.
Somebody fills them with the small scoop and signs for the large one. Forty days. That’s nine sacks.
Heum. Your uncle supplies this yard, doesn’t he?

blocks.speaker: Heum
en: …That’s a lie.

lines: 이건 셈이야. 셈은 거짓말 안 해.
en: It’s arithmetic. It doesn’t lie.
It doesn’t even like you.

blocks.speaker: The Yard Marshal
en: …Who taught you to read a tally like that?

blocks.html: Chunchu opens his mouth to say the steward. He hears himself not say it.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 집사라고 말하려고 입을 연다. 그 말이 나오지 않는 걸 자기 귀로 듣는다.

en: My father, sir.

blocks.html: Nobody laughs. Heum looks as if he would like to, and then doesn’t. The rice comes back, and so does the large scoop. Forty hungry boys learn that the goblin’s boy can count, and boys will forgive almost anything for rice.
blocks.ko: 아무도 웃지 않는다. 흠은 웃고 싶은 얼굴을 하다가 그만둔다. 쌀이 돌아온다. 큰 되도 돌아온다. 배고픈 소년 마흔은 도깨비 집 아들이 셈을 할 줄 안다는 걸 배운다. 소년들은 쌀만 주면 거의 뭐든 용서한다.

blocks.label: The yard · the autumn moon
blocks.ko: 연무장 · 가을 달

blocks.html: At the autumn moon-viewing every class must give a verse. Class 59 has nothing. One by one they look at the boy at the drain end of the hall.
blocks.ko: 가을 달맞이 때면 기마다 시를 한 수씩 내야 한다. 오십구기는 아무것도 없다. 하나둘, 그들의 눈이 숙소 하수구 쪽 끝자리 소년에게로 간다.

blocks.title: Class 59 at the Moon
lines: 나는 하수구 곁에서 잔다, 귀신들 찾아오기 쉬우라고
귀신들은 밤마다 와서 우리 쌀을 센다
소년 마흔에, 셈할 줄 아는 놈이 하나 없으니
en: My grandfather was a king, they say;
my father talks to water.
I sleep beside the drain, so the ghosts can find me.
Every night they come and count our rice:
forty boys, and not one who can add.
Even the ghosts are embarrassed for us.

blocks.html: The instructors laugh. Then the class laughs, with him for once. Even the Yard Marshal makes a noise that might, in a better light, be one. By winter the bench makes room. By spring the boys who threw his shoes in the pond are asking him to write their letters home. He writes them beautifully, charges nothing, and remembers every name.
blocks.ko: 교관들이 웃는다. 그러고는 오십구기가 웃는다. 처음으로 그와 함께. 도감조차 밝은 데서 보면 웃음일 수도 있는 소리를 낸다. 겨울이 되자 의자에 자리가 생긴다. 봄이 되자 그의 신발을 못에 던지던 소년들이 집에 보낼 편지를 써 달라고 찾아온다. 그는 편지를 아름답게 써 주고, 아무것도 받지 않고, 이름은 하나도 빠짐없이 기억한다.

blocks.html: His father told him to count the boys who smiled at him. He counts them again in a month. The number has gone up.
blocks.ko: 아버지는 웃어 주는 놈들을 세라고 했다. 그는 한 달 뒤에 다시 센다. 수가 늘었다.

blocks.label: The yard · the Council’s review
blocks.ko: 연무장 · 화백의 사열

blocks.html: In spring the Harmony Council comes to look at the new class, as it does every year, the way a man walks his own orchard. Six sleeves pass down the line of boys. They are the fathers of half of them.
blocks.ko: 봄이면 화백회의가 새 기를 보러 온다. 해마다 그렇다. 제 과수원을 둘러보는 사람처럼. 소매 여섯이 소년들의 줄을 따라 내려온다. 그 절반의 아버지들이다.

blocks.html: The High Councillor stops in front of Chunchu. He doesn’t look at the boy’s face. He looks at his shoulder, where a bone rank would be if you wore it on the outside. Behind him, half a step back, the councillor Imjong is smiling at nobody in particular.
blocks.ko: 상대등이 춘추 앞에서 멈춘다. 소년의 얼굴은 보지 않는다. 어깨를 본다. 골품을 겉에 달고 다닌다면 붙어 있을 자리를. 그 뒤로 반걸음 물러서서, 대등 임종이 누구에게랄 것 없이 웃고 있다.

blocks.speaker: The High Councillor
lines: 인기가 좋다더구나. 너희 집안에선 인기 좋은 게 위험한 일인데.
en: So this is the ghost’s grandson.
Popular, they tell me. Popular is a dangerous thing to be, in your family.

lines: 그럼 쓸모 있는 사람이 되도록 하겠습니다, 대감.
en: Then I will try to be useful instead, my lord.
Useful is safer.

blocks.html: He bows so well that two of the six look pleased. The High Councillor moves on. Chunchu stays bent until the sixth sleeve has passed, counting them.
blocks.ko: 그가 어찌나 절을 잘하는지 여섯 가운데 둘이 흐뭇한 얼굴을 한다. 상대등이 지나간다. 춘추는 여섯 번째 소매가 지나갈 때까지 허리를 굽힌 채 그들을 센다.

blocks.label: The yard wall · that night
blocks.ko: 연무장 담 · 그날 밤

en: You bowed lower than you had to.

lines: 딱 필요한 만큼 숙였어요, 선배님. 재 봤거든요.
늙은이 여섯이 이 나라에서 누가 사람인지 정해요. 누가 성골이고, 누가 진골이고, 누가 웃음거리인지.
en: I bowed exactly as low as I had to, sir. I measured.
Six old men decide who counts as a person in this country. Who’s Sacred, who’s True, who’s a joke.

lines: 그게 그 방이네. 늘 그 방이었지.
en: That’s the room. It’s always been the room.

lines: 아버지가 그 방엔 들어가지 말래요. 안 들어갈 거예요.
그래도 그 사람들 얼굴은 하나도 안 잊을 거예요.
en: My father says stay out of that room. I will.
But I’m going to remember every one of their faces.
That’s a long list.

lines: 저희 집안에 남은 것 중에 회의가 표결 안 한 건 그것뿐이에요.
en: I have a very good memory, sir.
It’s the only thing my family has left that the Council never voted on.

blocks.html: Yushin doesn’t laugh this time. He sits on the wall beside the boy until the watch changes and says nothing, which from him is a great deal. Some of the faces on that list will live long enough to bow to Chunchu. Not all of them.
blocks.ko: 이번엔 유신이 웃지 않는다. 그는 순라가 바뀔 때까지 소년 곁 담 위에 앉아 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 그에게 그건 많은 말이다. 그 명단에 오른 얼굴 몇몇은 춘추에게 절할 만큼 오래 산다. 다는 아니다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace · the archery range, after dark
blocks.ko: 월성 · 해 진 뒤의 활터

blocks.html: Every great love story in Silla has a committee behind it. This one has two members and no minutes.
blocks.ko: 신라의 위대한 연애 뒤에는 늘 위원회가 있다. 이 위원회는 둘이고, 회의록은 없다.

blocks.html: The princess has a father with no sons, and a court that can count. When the day comes she will need the best swords in Silla on her side. Swords are loyal to family.
blocks.ko: 공주에게는 아들 없는 아버지와, 셈할 줄 아는 조정이 있다. 그날이 오면 신라에서 제일 좋은 칼들이 그녀 편이어야 한다. 칼은 집안에 충성한다.

blocks.html: The best sword in Silla is walking beside her, collecting her arrows. His family has a rank. It would like a cousin.
blocks.ko: 신라에서 제일 좋은 칼은 지금 그녀 옆에서 화살을 주워 오고 있다. 그 집안에는 품계가 있다. 이제 사촌이 하나 있었으면 한다.

en: Royal blood. Unmarried. Not an idiot.
Go.
…You mean Chunchu. My gyuku partner.

lines: 자네 격구 상대. 자네 집 대문 보고 시 한 수 쓰고, 들어가지는 않을 아이라.
en: Your gyuku partner. He’d write a poem about your gate and never come through it.
…Do you have any hot sisters?

blocks.html: Yushin swallows the wrong way. The arrows in his hand rattle.
blocks.ko: 유신이 사레가 들린다. 손에 든 화살들이 달그락거린다.

lines: ……둘 있습니다. 언니는 그 사람 옷을 기워 줄 겁니다.
동생은 그 옷을 또 찢게 만들 겁니다.
en: …Two. The elder would mend his coat.
The younger would make him tear it again.
That one.
She has to want him, Princess.

lines: 원할 걸세. 얼굴 하나는 곱제. 군사적 자산은 그것뿐이지만.
en: She will. He’s very pretty. It’s his only military asset.

blocks.html: They walk on to the butts. Neither of them says the obvious thing, which is that there is a shorter way to put Gaya blood into the royal house, and it is standing on this range. A Sacred Bone princess does not marry a Gaya general. Both of them have checked the rule. Separately. More than once.
blocks.ko: 둘은 과녁 쪽으로 계속 걷는다. 누구도 뻔한 얘기는 하지 않는다. 가야 피를 왕실에 넣는 더 짧은 길이 있고, 그 길이 지금 이 활터에 서 있다는 얘기. 성골 공주는 가야 장수와 혼인하지 않는다. 둘 다 그 법도를 확인해 봤다. 따로따로. 여러 번.

lines: 물론, 더 간단한 방법도 있기는 하제.
en: Of course, there’s always a simpler arrangement.
There isn’t.
…No. There isn’t.

blocks.html: She looks at the target. He looks at the arrows. It is dark enough on the range that nobody can see either of them go red, which is lucky, because both of them do.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 과녁을 본다. 그는 화살을 본다. 활터가 충분히 어두워서 둘이 얼굴 붉히는 걸 아무도 못 본다. 다행이다. 둘 다 붉어졌으니까.

lines: 격구 끝나면 집으로 데려가게. 뭐든 밟아.
en: Bring him home from gyuku. Step on something.
On what?

lines: 옷자락. 그 아이가 아끼는 건 그것뿐이라.
en: His coat. It’s the only thing he owns that he cares about.

blocks.html: The same week, in the Gaya house, a dream is sold.
blocks.ko: 같은 주, 가야 집에서 꿈 하나가 팔린다.

lines: 어젯밤에… 남산에 올라가가 오줌을 눴는데, / 서라벌이 마카 잠겼다. / 온 도성이.
en: Last night… I climbed Namsan and I relieved myself, / and all of Surabol drowned. / The entire capital.
Sister. Sell me that dream.
…For what?
My silk skirt.

blocks.html: Bohee takes the skirt. It is the single worst trade in Silla’s thousand years, and the two of them will both live long enough to know it.
blocks.ko: 보희는 치마를 받는다. 신라 천 년을 통틀어 가장 손해 본 거래이고, 두 사람 다 그것을 알 만큼 오래 산다.

lines: 언니가 잠기게 한 도성은, / 이제 내 끼다.
en: The capital you drowned / is mine now.

blocks.label: The Torn Coat
blocks.ko: 뜯긴 옷고름

blocks.html: Five days later, on the gyuku field. Seven years on, they still play every fifth day. Yushin still wins. Chunchu still loses, and keeps a different score in his head.
blocks.ko: 닷새 뒤, 격구장. 칠 년이 지났어도 둘은 여전히 닷새마다 공을 친다. 유신은 여전히 이긴다. 춘추는 여전히 지고, 머릿속에는 다른 점수를 적어 둔다.

en: Eleven to four.
Eleven to three, if we’re honest. That last one was a foul.
lines: 열하나 대 셋이지요, 솔직히 말하면. 마지막 건 반칙이었고.

en: You fell off your horse.
I was pushed off my horse. By a large man.
On a larger horse.
Come home for supper. You can lose the argument there.
lines: 저녁 먹으러 와라. 말싸움은 거기 가서 지고.

en: I never lose at supper, sir. You know that.

blocks.html: Yushin knows. That’s the plan. He has been told to step on something.
blocks.ko: 유신은 안다. 그게 계획이다. 무언가를 밟으라는 명을 받았으니까.

blocks.html: Yushin brings him home from the field — still dusty, still arguing about the foul — and on the yard, mid-demonstration of a “proper True Bone grip,” steps on the hem of his coat on purpose. The tie comes away.
blocks.ko: 유신이 그를 집으로 데려온다 — 아직 먼지투성이로, 아직 그 반칙을 두고 다투며. 마당에서 «진골다운 손잡이»를 시범하다가, 일부러 그의 옷자락을 밟는다. 옷고름이 뜯긴다.

lines: 어이쿠. / 이거 실례를. / 누가 좀 꿰매 드리라.
en: Oh dear. / My apologies. / Somebody sew that for the gentleman.
…How could I approach a nobleman over so small a thing.
I will do it.

blocks.html: He has to take the coat off for her to mend it. Magenta silk leaves his shoulders. He sits disrobed in her brother’s hall with a True Bone’s embarrassment and nowhere to put his hands. She knits the tear standing close enough to feel the heat off his skin — and that is all, the first time. Needle. Breath. The slow fact of a man without his coat.
blocks.ko: 고쳐 주려면 겉옷을 벗어야 한다. 자홍 비단이 어깨에서 내린다. 오라비 집에서 벗은 채로 앉아, 진골의 민망함과 손 둘 곳이 없다. 그녀는 찢어진 곳을 꿰매며 그의 피부 열을 느낄 만큼 가까이 선다. 그게 전부다, 첫날은. 바늘. 숨. 겉옷 없는 남자라는 느린 사실.

blocks.html: The elder sister had some reason not to come forward, so the younger came and sewed it. Light make-up, light clothes, and a radiance that lit up the room. Chunchu saw her and was delighted…
blocks.ko: 그 언니는 일이 있어 나오지 않고, 그 아우가 앞으로 나와 꿰매었다. 옅은 화장에 가벼운 옷차림이었으나 빛나는 고움이 사람을 비추었다. 춘추가 보고 기뻐하였다……
blocks.hanja: 其姊有故不進，其季進前縫綴。淡粧輕服，光艶炤人。春秋見而悅之……
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — opening account of Bupmin's parents

lines: 나는… 이렇게 앉아 본 적이 없소.
en: …Your hands are quick.
I have… not sat like this.
Sit.
I will put the coat back on you.
Today… only that.

blocks.html: He comes back the next day, needing nothing sewn, and again the day after that. Each visit she finds a new place on the garment — and they sit closer. The needle slows. His breath learns the back of her hand. They do not leap. They accumulate.
blocks.ko: 다음 날 다시 온다. 꿰맬 것은 없다. 그다음 날도. 올 때마다 옷의 다른 곳을 찾는다. 더 가까이 앉는다. 바늘이 느려진다. 그의 숨이 손등을 배운다. 뛰어오르지 않는다. 쌓인다.

blocks.html: The second visit, she measures his shoulders with her hands. The string stays in her sleeve. He goes red to the ears and lets her.
blocks.ko: 두 번째에는 치수 끈 대신 손으로 그의 어깨를 잰다. 끈은 소매 속에 그대로 있다. 그는 귀까지 빨개져서, 그냥 재게 둔다.

blocks.html: The third, their fingers meet on the needle. Neither of them lets go first.
blocks.ko: 세 번째에는 바늘 위에서 손가락이 닿는다. 누구도 먼저 놓지 않는다.

blocks.html: The fifth, she bites off the thread. He kisses her before she can put it down.
blocks.ko: 다섯 번째에는 그녀가 이로 실을 끊는다. 그는 그녀가 실을 내려놓기도 전에 입을 맞춘다.

blocks.html: Across the city, in a house with too many servants, a young True Bone stands in his underrobe and rips the tie off his own coat with his teeth. He looks at the hem. He rips that too. Then he calls for his horse.
blocks.ko: 도성 건너편, 하인이 너무 많은 집에서 젊은 진골 하나가 속옷 바람으로 서서 제 옷고름을 이로 물어뜯는다. 밑단을 내려다본다. 그것도 뜯는다. 그러고는 말을 대령하라 이른다.

blocks.speaker: His manservant
en: My lord. That’s the third coat this month.
You didn’t play gyuku today, my lord.
…Then it’s a very violent city.

blocks.html: At the Gaya house Munhee holds the tie up to the light. There are teeth marks on it.
blocks.ko: 가야 집에서 문희가 옷고름을 빛에 비춰 든다. 이빨 자국이 나 있다.

en: You bit this.
Gyuku.

lines: …나머지도 벗어요. 꿰맬 데는 내가 찾을 테니.
en: Sit down.
…And take the rest off. I’ll find something.

blocks.html: On the fourth afternoon the house gets a visitor nobody planned for. The girls’ father is in the capital for three days, to tell the palace about a granary on the Baekje border. He comes in from the gate in his riding boots and stops in his own doorway.
blocks.ko: 나흘째 오후, 아무도 셈에 넣지 않은 손님이 든다. 아가씨들의 아버지다. 백제 접경의 곳간 일을 궁에 아뢰러 사흘 일정으로 서라벌에 와 있다. 그는 승마 신을 신은 채 대문에서 들어와, 제 집 문간에서 멈춘다.

blocks.html: A young nobleman is sitting on his floor in an underrobe. His younger daughter is standing behind him with a needle. His son is studying the rafters with great interest.
blocks.ko: 제 집 마루에 젊은 귀공자가 속적삼 바람으로 앉아 있다. 작은딸은 그 뒤에 바늘을 들고 서 있다. 아들은 서까래를 아주 열심히 올려다보고 있다.

en: My lord— forgive me— Kim Chunchu, my lord.
The coat, it— there was a foul—
Sit, sit. Please.
You’ll tear something else.
Father. You’re early.
Am I.

blocks.html: He crosses the hall and takes the coat off her arm. He holds the hem up to the window. It has not torn. Somebody has unpicked it along the seam, stitch by stitch, very neatly. He gives it back to her.
blocks.ko: 그는 대청을 건너와 딸의 팔에서 옷을 받아 든다. 밑단을 창 쪽으로 들어 본다. 뜯어진 게 아니다. 누군가 솔기를 따라 한 땀 한 땀, 아주 얌전히 풀어 놓았다. 그는 옷을 딸에게 돌려준다.

en: Torn again, is it.
It’s a poor coat, Father.
Mm.
Poor coat.
Gyuku, Father. It was a foul.
In my hall.
…It was a bad foul.

lines: 저래 갖고 나가믄— 골목이— 마저 꿰매라.
en: Finish it, then.
He can’t go out like— the lane’s— finish it.

blocks.html: Nobody in that hall has ever sewn so slowly. When the coat is back on, the old man reaches over and fixes the gentleman’s collar with both hands, the way he has fixed every collar in this house, and steps back.
blocks.ko: 그 대청에서 그토록 느린 바느질은 처음이다. 옷이 다시 어깨에 걸리자 노인은 손을 뻗어 두 손으로 귀공자의 옷깃을 바로잡는다. 이 집 옷깃이란 옷깃은 다 그렇게 바로잡아 온 손이다. 그리고 물러선다.

lines: ……내려가는 길 조심하시오. 이맘때 숯 수레가 올라오오.
en: Crooked.
…Mind the lane going down, sir. There’s a charcoal cart comes up about this hour.
…Thank you, my lord?

blocks.html: He goes out to see to his horse, which does not need seeing to. Munhee waits until his boots have crossed the yard. Through the side door, her sister has heard every word.
blocks.ko: 그는 돌볼 필요도 없는 말을 돌보러 나간다. 문희는 그의 발소리가 마당을 다 건널 때까지 기다린다. 옆문 너머에서 언니가 한 마디도 빼놓지 않고 들었다.

en: …He knows.
He doesn’t.
He held it up to the window, Munhee.

blocks.html: On a later visit the coat is off again. She stands behind him, needle forgotten, staring at the breadth of his shoulders as if the knitting were only an excuse to keep looking. Magenta silk has slipped. She does not tell him to cover it. When the needle pauses it is because her mouth has found the place above his pulse — and Yushin is careful to be looking somewhere else the entire time.
blocks.ko: 나중 방문에 또 겉옷을 벗는다. 뒤에 서서 바늘을 잊고, 어깨 너비를 본다. 뜨개질은 계속 보기 위한 핑계일 뿐인 것처럼. 자홍 비단이 흘렀다. 가리라고 하지 않는다. 바늘이 멈추는 것은 입이 맥 위를 찾아서다. 유신은 그 시간 내내 다른 곳을 보도록 조심한다.

en: …Why.
At this rate… I will tear the coat myself.
Because you have not left yet.
Before you leave…
your hand belongs at my waist.
Until the sewing is done.
And what is torn today?
Or… what shall I tear for you.
…Nothing.
No —
Here.
Where your mouth… was yesterday.
Shall I tear something for you, then?
Only the coat.
Or… your restraint as well.
…If you say it like that.
I won’t be able to leave tonight.
I am already… coming apart at the door.
Then don’t.
The sewing… can wait until morning.
Spend the night… mending me.

blocks.html: He stays. The household learns the sound of a door that is not meant to open until dawn.
blocks.ko: 그는 남는다. 집안은 새벽까지 열리지 않을 문의 소리를 배운다.

blocks.html: By midsummer the household staff have stopped announcing him.
blocks.ko: 한여름이 되자 집안 사람들은 그가 왔다고 알리는 일을 그만둔다.

blocks.html: Ask Munhee about the next part and she still blushes.
blocks.ko: 그다음 이야기를 물으면 문희는 지금도 얼굴이 붉어진다.

en: N-no, why bring up that memory again…

blocks.html: By autumn Munhee is showing. Chunchu still hasn't proposed.
blocks.ko: 가을이 되자 문희의 배가 불러 온다. 춘추는 아직 청혼을 안 했다.

lines: 누군지도 모를 사내의 아이를 배다니… 이 무슨 망신이냐!
집안을 욕보인 누이는 그 집 마당에서 태운데이.
en: Pregnant with an unknown man’s child… what a disgrace!
A sister who shames the house burns in its yard.

lines: 이름은 안 댄다. 오라버니도 이미 알제.
en: Then build it, brother.
I’m not giving you a name. You already know it.

blocks.label: Marriage
blocks.ko: 혼인

blocks.label: The Pyre
blocks.ko: 장작불

blocks.html: Yushin builds the pyre in the yard where they played gyuku, which is not lost on anyone, and sets green wood on it so that it smokes instead of burning. Munhee stands beside it with her hands folded over the child. Nobody has tied her. Nobody has needed to.
blocks.ko: 유신은 격구를 하던 그 마당에 장작을 쌓는다. 아무도 그 뜻을 놓치지 않는다. 그리고 젖은 나무를 올려 불이 붙는 대신 연기가 나게 한다. 문희는 그 곁에 서서 두 손을 배 위에 포갠다. 아무도 그녀를 묶지 않았다. 묶을 필요가 없었다.

blocks.html: The smoke goes straight up. It is visible from Namsan. It is visible from the terrace where a princess happens to be standing with the young nobleman who has gone the colour of paper.
blocks.ko: 연기가 곧게 오른다. 남산에서 보인다. 공주가 마침 서 있는 누대에서도 보인다. 그 곁에는 얼굴이 종잇장처럼 하얗게 질린 젊은 귀공자가 있다.

en: What is that smoke?

blocks.speaker: A lady-in-waiting
lines: 누이가 아이를 뱄는데 아비 이름을 대지 않는답니다. 정오에 태운다 하옵니다.
en: Kim Yushin’s yard, Highness.
His sister is with child and won’t name the father. He says she burns at noon.
Lord… Chunchu?

blocks.html: Then Chunchu is running. A True Bone does not run in front of a princess. He runs the whole way: down the terrace stairs, through two gates, into the smoke.
blocks.ko: 그러더니 춘추가 뛴다. 진골은 공주 앞에서 뛰지 않는다. 그는 끝까지 뛴다. 누대 계단을 내려가, 문 두 개를 지나, 연기 속으로.

blocks.html: The princess watches him go. Then she looks at the sun, the way a woman checks a candle clock. Noon, more or less. Higher up, on the palace’s own terrace, an old king watches the same smoke and asks who it is. He is told. He laughs, for the first time that winter, and says the boy’s grandfather would have run too.
blocks.ko: 공주는 그가 뛰어가는 걸 지켜본다. 그러고는 해를 올려다본다. 초시계를 확인하는 여자처럼. 대략 정오다. 더 높은 데, 궁의 테라스에선 늙은 왕이 같은 연기를 보고 누구 집이냐 묻는다. 대답을 듣는다. 그해 겨울 처음으로 웃고는, 그 녀석 할아버지였어도 뛰었을 거라고 한다.

en: Don’t you dare. Not because of smoke.

lines: ㄱ-그 아기의 아버지... 문희 양의.. 그..
en: Th-the father of that child… Lady Munhee’s… I mean…
It’s me!

blocks.html: He says it to the yard, to the princess on the terrace, and to half of Surabol on its rooftops. Munhee closes her eyes. She had hoped for a quieter proposal. She will take this one.
blocks.ko: 그는 마당에, 누대 위의 공주에게, 지붕에 올라앉은 서라벌 절반에게 그 말을 한다. 문희는 눈을 감는다. 좀 더 조용한 청혼을 바랐다. 이걸로 하기로 한다.

blocks.html: Yushin kicks the green wood apart. It was never going to catch.
blocks.ko: 유신이 생나무 더미를 발로 흩뜨린다. 애초에 불이 붙을 나무가 아니었다.

blocks.html: Then he looks up, across half the city, at the terrace. She is already looking somewhere else. So is he, a moment later. It is a long way between a yard and a terrace, and both of them still manage to blush across it.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 고개를 들어 도성 절반 너머의 누대를 본다. 그녀는 벌써 딴 데를 보고 있다. 잠시 뒤엔 그도 그렇다. 마당에서 누대까지는 먼 거리다. 그래도 둘 다 그 거리를 건너 얼굴을 붉힌다.

lines: 자네가 내 누이를 택한 게 아니라,
en: …Chunchu.
You did not choose my sister.
I chose you.

blocks.html: Chunchu and Munhee are married. The green-wood rumour becomes a wedding, and the wedding becomes a household that is openly fond of itself.
blocks.ko: 춘추와 문희는 혼인한다. 생나무 연기 소문은 혼례가 되고, 혼례는 제 자신을 아끼는 살림이 된다.

blocks.html: The bride’s father sits near the dais with royal Kims on every side and says almost nothing all night. Halfway through, a steward brings him a cup from a very old man across the hall. He drinks half of it. The other half goes on the step, and nobody asks him why. By the door, the groom’s father is the only guest who doesn’t look surprised.
blocks.ko: 신부의 아버지는 단 가까이, 사방이 왕족 김씨인 자리에 앉아 밤새 거의 말이 없다. 잔치가 한창일 때 청지기가 대청 건너편 아주 늙은 노인에게서 잔 하나를 들고 온다. 그는 반을 마신다. 나머지 반은 섬돌에 붓는다. 왜냐고 묻는 사람은 없다. 문간에서 신랑 아버지만이 놀라지 않은 얼굴이다.

blocks.html: At the feast the two of them end up where they always end up: outside, on the steps, sharing one cup.
blocks.ko: 잔치에서 둘은 늘 그렇듯 같은 자리에 앉는다. 바깥 계단, 잔 하나.

en: Brother.

lines: 가야의 피와 신라의 왕족을 한 침상에 눕히는 데,
en: Do you know how many years it took me
to lay Gaya blood and Silla royalty in the same bed.

lines: 형님이 왕을 하시면 될 걸 그랬습니다.
삼한에서 제일 강한 사내가 왕이 되는 게 이치 아입니꺼.
en: You should have simply become king yourself.
Surely the strongest man in Samhan ought to be the one who rules.
(laughing) Chunchu. You know exactly why not.
…I do.

blocks.html: Neither of them says the word. It sits between them anyway, the way it always has: Gaya. His grandfather bought the family a rank. Ranks are not the same as blood.
blocks.ko: 둘 다 그 말을 입에 올리지 않는다. 그래도 그 말은 늘 그랬듯 두 사람 사이에 놓여 있다. 가야. 할아버지가 집안을 위해 신분을 샀다. 신분은 피와 같지 않다.

blocks.label: The Closed Months
blocks.ko: 닫힌 달들

blocks.html: The wedding itself is quiet. Magenta silk and pink silk share a cup. What the court will later call a clever match is, in the room, simply two adults who have already learned each other’s breath.
blocks.ko: 혼례 자체는 조용하다. 자홍 비단과 분홍 비단이 잔을 나눈다. 조정이 나중에 영리한 혼사라고 부를 것은, 그 방 안에서는 서로의 숨을 이미 배운 두 어른일 뿐이다.

blocks.html: They shut the door on the yard and do not open it again for a long time. The minutes will later invent one decorous wedding night. What actually happens is weeks of it — her on him, him on her, the magenta and the pink in a heap by the door — until the meals go cold and Surabol learns to wait.
blocks.ko: 마당을 향해 문을 닫고, 한참을 다시 열지 않는다. 훗날 기록은 점잖은 첫날밤 하나를 지어낼 것이다. 실제로 있었던 일은 몇 주다 — 그녀가 위에, 그가 위에, 자홍과 분홍이 문가에 한 더미로 — 밥이 식고 서라벌이 기다리는 법을 배울 때까지.

blocks.html: The first time he is still trying to be gentle. She is not. She takes his hand and puts it where she wants it, and the sound that leaves her is not a toast. He lasts like a man who has been polite too long, which is to say not long, and says her name at the end as if he were apologising for it. She laughs, because that was the point, and does not let him go anywhere. The bedding. The chest. The floor, when the bedding is too far away. When he reaches for the water jug she pulls him back by the wrist.
blocks.ko: 처음엔 그가 아직 살살 하려 한다. 그녀는 아니다. 그의 손을 잡아 원하는 곳에 놓고, 그녀에게서 나오는 소리는 축배가 아니다. 너무 오래 예의 바르게 굴었던 사내답게 그는 오래 가지 못하고 — 말하자면 금방이다 — 끝에 그녀의 이름을 사과하듯 부른다. 그녀는 웃는다. 바로 그걸 원했으니까. 그리고 그를 아무 데도 보내지 않는다. 침상. 궤. 침상이 멀면 바닥. 그가 물주전자로 손을 뻗으면 손목을 잡아 끌어당긴다.

en: Again…?
Today… don’t even try to count.
Save counting for outside.
I… cannot count.
Munhee.
I have… already lost.
And… I will lose again.

blocks.html: The neighbors on both walls learn their names the wrong way, through plaster. At night the paper window glows, and the shadows on it are not ambiguous. Servants stop knocking. Someone on the east side moves his sleeping mat away from the shared timber and blames the draft.
blocks.ko: 양쪽 담 너머 이웃들은 두 사람의 이름을 엉뚱한 길로 배운다. 회벽 너머로. 밤이면 창호지가 환하고, 거기 비치는 그림자는 오해의 여지가 없다. 하인들은 문 두드리기를 그만둔다. 동쪽 집 누군가는 맞닿은 벽에서 잠자리를 멀찍이 옮기고 외풍 탓을 한다.

en: They say… they heard us through the wall.
And saw… the paper window.
Even our names.
Then the wall… is on our side.
And the paper window.
If Surabol hears…
let it.

blocks.html: Months pass before either of them remembers the yard. When they finally open the door she walks like someone who has been thoroughly loved and does not mind the lane knowing it, and they look at each other like people who have won a private war — still in love, still hungry, and willing, for one afternoon, to put clothes back on.
blocks.ko: 둘 중 누구든 마당을 다시 떠올리기까지 몇 달이 걸린다. 마침내 문을 열었을 때 그녀는 실컷 사랑받았고 골목이 그걸 알아도 상관없다는 사람처럼 걷고, 둘은 사사로운 전쟁에서 이긴 사람처럼 서로를 본다 — 여전히 사랑하고, 여전히 배고프고, 오후 한나절쯤은 옷을 다시 입어 줄 마음이 든 채로.

blocks.label: The Household
blocks.ko: 식구

blocks.html: Samsin comes the way she always comes when a breath starts: in white, with nobody else in the room. The first child is a boy who walks before he talks. They call him Bupmin. A year later comes a girl who talks early and never stops. They call her Gotaso. Chunchu sits where a husband sits when he has not yet learned what children will steal from him.
blocks.ko: 숨이 하나 시작될 때면 늘 그렇듯 삼신이 온다. 하얗게, 방에 아무도 들이지 않고. 첫아이는 말보다 걸음이 먼저인 아들이다. 법민이라 부른다. 한 해 뒤에는 말이 빠르고 그칠 줄 모르는 딸이 온다. 고타소라 부른다. 춘추는 아이들이 자기에게서 무엇을 훔쳐 갈지 아직 모르는 남편의 자리에 앉아 있다.

blocks.html: For a few years, Chunchu stops going to the hill.
blocks.ko: 몇 해 동안, 춘추는 언덕에 가지 않는다.

lines: 자네, 요새 회의에 통 안 나오데.
en: You have not been coming to Council lately.

lines: 형님. 저는 이제 딸 하나에 아들 하나입니다.
en: Brother. I have a daughter and a son now.
The east star… I think I will let it just be a star.
So you will.

blocks.html: Back at the gate, the dust from the Daeya road has settled. Munhee has not let go of his arm.
blocks.ko: 다시 대문 앞. 대야 길의 먼지는 가라앉았다. 문희는 아직 남편의 팔을 놓지 않았다.

en: You went back to the hill, of course.

lines: 누군가는 가야제. 별이 제 발로 내려올 리는 없으니까.
en: Somebody had to. The star wasn’t going to climb down by itself.

blocks.html: Same spring, in Pyongyang, another father walks his son to school. He means to pick a fight with the Buddha…!
blocks.ko: 같은 봄, 평양에서는 또 다른 아버지가 아들을 학당에 데려간다. 부처와 한판 붙을 작정으로…!

logline.en: Yeon has three sons. They could not be more different. There is only one seal.
logline.ko: 연에게는 아들이 셋 있다. 셋은 이보다 다를 수가 없다. 그리고 인장은 하나뿐이다.

images.alt: Three sons at a feast table — Gulgul outside with an empty bowl, watching the door
images.prompt: Cinematic historical illustration of Yeon Gesomun’s three young sons feasting at a low table while a fourth ragged boy Gulgul stands outside in the dark courtyard with an empty bowl, Goguryeo night interior, painterly digital art, warm lantern vs cold courtyard, no text, no watermark, --ar 10:3

images.at: A pot stands on three legs
images.alt: Yeon Gesomun slaps a palm on the three-legged bronze cauldron in the Academy yard while his small son looks up.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Low three-quarter WORM'S-EYE from the swept flagstones of the Taehak, the Grand Academy courtyard in Pyongyang at dusk. ONE device: a squat three-legged bronze incense cauldron (ding) in the left third of the foreground, its three legs a hard dark shape against the pale swept stone. Yeon Gesomun, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, mid-stride in muddy riding boots on the swept stone, one palm slapped down on the cauldron's rim, leaning in, mouth open mid-sentence with a crude half-grin, unarmed today. Beside him, small, his seven-year-old son in a plain child's scholar robe looks up at him, seen from behind three-quarter, face mostly turned away. Far across the courtyard, in soft bokeh, a monk with a broom has stopped sweeping and stares. Behind: the lecture hall's red pillars, giwa eaves and lit lattice doors melting into dusk haze. Key: a low red sunset shaft raking across the bronze, his face and the silk folds; the rest umber and slate. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.at: Yeon brings Namseng to the gate himself, in riding boots
images.alt: The Goguryeo version: the Grand Academy, and a father who won't take his boots off.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. PARALLEL FRAME: the LAYOUT picture on the sheet is the master of a set of frames that recur across this story. Repaint ITS EXACT COMPOSITION: the same camera height, angle and lens, the same framing, the same number of figures in the same positions, sizes and poses, the same main shapes (gate, line, dais, table, waterline) in the same places, the same direction of the key light. Only the people, their faces and dress, the place and the hour change, so the two frames line up like a before-and-after. Ignore the layout picture's faces, clothes and colours. The same layout in Goguryeo: the gate of the Grand Academy in Pyongyang, red timber and grey giwa, monks sweeping the swept stone beyond. Yeon Gesomun is the father on the LEFT, in riding boots and Goguryeo dress, hands raised to straighten his small son's collar the way you check a saddle girth; young Namseng on the RIGHT, about nine, catching his father's wrists, looking past him at a monk in the courtyard. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT LAYOUT picture (copy its composition, not its people), SECOND face = gesomun, THIRD face = namseng. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_taehak (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), jougwan feather-cap board (shape only, ignore labels). YEON GESOMUN — Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Colour #d0362f. YEON NAMSENG Colour #c25a4e. PLACE The Tehak (태학) — attached board /pl_taehak.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.

blocks.html: Yeon has three sons, and only one of them is old enough to annoy a monk.
blocks.ko: 연에게는 아들이 셋 있다. 그중 중을 성가시게 할 만큼 큰 건 하나뿐이다.

blocks.html: Namseng, seven, is the careful one: the heir, eager to be approved of.
blocks.ko: 남생은 일곱 살, 신중한 맏이다. 인정받고 싶어 하는 후계자.

blocks.caption: Yeon’s eldest. He would very much like to be told he did well.
blocks.ko: 연의 맏아들. 잘했다는 말을, 정말로 듣고 싶다.

blocks.html: Namgun, four, is the fierce one, who never backs down first.
blocks.ko: 남건은 네 살, 사나운 둘째다. 먼저 물러서는 법이 없다.

blocks.caption: The second son. Nobody ever had to teach him to push.
blocks.ko: 둘째. 밀어붙이는 법은 누구도 가르칠 필요가 없었다.

blocks.html: Namsan, two, is the quiet one, watching his brothers.
blocks.ko: 남산은 두 살, 조용한 막내다. 형들을 지켜본다.

blocks.html: There is a fourth boy at that table who is not counted, because counting him would require a word nobody in the house wants to use. Gulgul eats after the others and says nothing, and Namsan — who watches everything — is the only one who notices that he never sits with his back to a door.
blocks.ko: 그 상에는 세지 않는 네 번째 아이가 있다. 세려면 그 집 누구도 쓰고 싶어 하지 않는 낱말이 필요하기 때문이다. 걸걸은 남들이 다 먹은 뒤에 먹고 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 모든 것을 보는 남산만이, 그 아이가 한 번도 문을 등지고 앉지 않는다는 것을 알아챈다.

blocks.html: Seven years in the house, and he understands every word of Goguryeo now. He spends them like a miser: mostly nouns, with Yeon’s northern vowels on all of them.
blocks.ko: 그 집에서 일곱 해. 이제 고구려 말은 한마디도 빠짐없이 알아듣는다. 다만 구두쇠처럼 아껴 쓴다. 거의 명사뿐이고, 그 명사마다 연의 북쪽 모음이 묻어 있다.

lines: 스승님이 장군 아들은 북쪽 말도 알아야 한대.
en: Gulgul. How do you say “horse” in Mohe?
The master says a commander’s son should know the northern tongues.
…Eat.
That isn’t an answer—
Eat. Cold.

blocks.html: He says it later, in the stable, to the horse, where nobody is asking.
blocks.ko: 그 말은 나중에 한다. 마구간에서, 말한테. 아무도 묻지 않는 데서.

en: Horse. Good horse.

blocks.label: SPRING
blocks.ko: 봄

blocks.label: The Tehak
blocks.ko: 태학

blocks.html: The Grand Academy is old. It came over the river in the same season as the first Buddhas. Ever since, the school and the temple have shared Goguryeo's noble sons. Classics in the morning. Sutras after lunch. Archery whenever the masters lose their voices.
blocks.ko: 태학은 오래됐다. 첫 불상과 같은 철에 강을 건너왔다. 그 뒤로 학당과 절은 고구려 귀족 아들들을 나눠 가져 왔다. 아침엔 경전. 점심 뒤엔 불경. 선생들 목이 쉬면 활쏘기.

blocks.html: Yeon brings Namseng to the gate himself, in riding boots, and does not take them off on the swept stone. Namgun has come too, uninvited, clinging to the back of the saddle.
blocks.ko: 연은 남생을 직접 문 앞까지 데려온다. 말 탈 때 신는 장화 그대로, 쓸어 놓은 돌바닥 위에서도 벗지 않는다. 남건도 따라왔다. 아무도 부르지 않았는데, 안장 뒤에 매달려서.

blocks.speaker: Tehak Master
lines: 대가. 오부의 자제들은 논어와 법화경으로 시작합니다.
en: Commander. The sons of the five commanderies begin with the Analects and the Lotus Sutra.
As your own father did, if I remember the register.

lines: 논어는 됐어. 사내라면 절하는 법은 알구 나서 안 할디 정해야디.
en: The Analects, aye. A boy should know how to bow before he decides not to.
The sutra he can skip.
Father.
Is the Buddha not allowed?

lines: 부처는 일없다. 살찌고 조용하고, 나한테 머이 달란 적이 없디.
내가 싫은 건 그 땅 주인들이다.
en: The Buddha’s fine. Fat, quiet, never asked me for anything.
It’s his landlords I mind.

blocks.html: The landlords are not a figure of speech. Half the good valley land belongs to monasteries. The monasteries belong to the great houses whose second sons run them. None of it pays for the wall. Every spring Yeon writes to the Summit about this. Every spring the Summit thanks him for his piety.
blocks.ko: 지주는 말장난이 아니다. 좋은 골짜기 땅의 절반이 절 것이다. 절은 둘째 아들들을 주지로 앉힌 큰 집안들 것이다. 그 땅은 성 쌓는 데 한 푼도 내지 않는다. 연은 봄마다 제가회의에 그 이야기를 써 보낸다. 제가회의는 봄마다 그의 신심에 감사한다.

blocks.html: What he wants instead is the Way of Laozi, which is an odd thing for him to want, because the Western emperors claim Laozi as their ancestor. Yeon has heard this and does not care. He has a sentence for it, the only one he ever repeats word for word.
blocks.ko: 그가 대신 원하는 것은 노자의 도다. 그에게는 이상한 바람이다. 서국 황실이 노자를 제 조상이라 우기니까. 연도 그 말을 들었고, 상관하지 않는다. 그에게는 이 일에 쓰는 문장이 하나 있다. 그가 토씨 하나 안 바꾸고 되풀이하는 유일한 말이다.

lines: 공자가 하나, 부처가 둘. 셋째가 없으니끼니 솥이 불 속으로 기울디.
en: A pot stands on three legs.
Confucius is one. The Buddha’s two. We’re missing the third, and the pot’s tipping into the fire.

blocks.speaker: Tehak Master
lines: 그 셋째 다리가… 서국의 도사들이란 말씀입니까, 대가?
en: The third leg would be… The Western priests, Commander?

lines: 셋째 다리는 농장 없는 놈이면 머이든 된다.
en: The third leg is whatever doesn’t own a farm.

blocks.html: Across the courtyard a monk has stopped sweeping. His name is Boduk. His monastery, up at Banryong, owns a great deal of farm.
blocks.ko: 마당 건너편에서 승려 하나가 비질을 멈췄다. 이름은 보덕. 그가 있는 반룡사는 농토를 아주 많이 가졌다.

blocks.speaker: Boduk
lines: 손님이 있을 뿐이지요. 오래 머무는 손님도 있고요.
en: Commander. The Buddha has no landlords.
He has guests. Some of them stay a long time.

lines: 농토에 곳간에 쟁기까지 차고 앉은 손님? 기게 지주디, 중아.
쓸라우. 계속. 일하는 거 내래 막을 생각 없어. 여기서 누구 하나는 일을 해야디.
en: A guest who keeps the farm, the barn and the plough? That’s a landlord, monk.
Go on, sweep. Don’t let me stop you working. Somebody here ought to.

blocks.html: Namgun is four. He decides this is a fight and that his side is winning. He kicks the monk’s swept pile across the stone.
blocks.ko: 남건은 네 살이다. 이게 싸움이고 자기 편이 이기는 중이라고 판단한다. 그래서 중이 쓸어 모은 낙엽 더미를 돌바닥에 걷어차 흩는다.

lines: …스님. 제 아우가 네 살이라서요. 허락해 주시면 저도 불경을 읽갓습네다.
en: Namgun! Say sorry.
…Venerable sir. My brother is four. I will read the sutra too, if I am allowed.

lines: …기런 눈으로 보지 말라우. 읽고 싶으면 네 시간에 읽어. 돈만 내디 마.
en: You’re not allowed.
…Don’t look at me like that. Read it on your own time. Just don’t pay for it.

blocks.html: Boduk bows to the boy, not to the father. Then he goes back to sweeping. He sweeps the same patch of stone until dark, and he does not forget a word.
blocks.ko: 보덕은 아버지가 아니라 아이에게 절한다. 그러고는 다시 비질을 한다. 해가 질 때까지 같은 돌바닥만 쓴다. 그리고 한 마디도 잊지 않는다.

blocks.html: That is the first day. The rest of the term goes the way first terms go.
blocks.ko: 그게 첫날이다. 나머지 학기는 첫 학기가 늘 그렇듯 흘러간다.

blocks.html: Namseng is good at the Analects the way some boys are good at being tall. He recites, the masters nod, and the older boys stop calling him the Commander’s pup. Now they call him the Commander’s parrot.
blocks.ko: 남생은 논어를 잘한다. 어떤 아이들이 키가 큰 것처럼 그냥 잘한다. 외우면 스승들이 고개를 끄덕이고, 큰 아이들은 그를 대가 집 강아지라 부르던 것을 그만둔다. 이제는 대가 집 앵무새라 부른다.

blocks.html: Namgun is not enrolled. Namgun is four. He comes anyway, every day, on the back of whatever horse is leaving the house, and sits under the archery range eating dried persimmons.
blocks.ko: 남건은 입학하지 않았다. 남건은 네 살이다. 그래도 매일 온다. 집을 나서는 아무 말 뒤에 올라타고 와서, 활터 아래에 앉아 곶감을 먹는다.

blocks.speaker: An older boy
en: Your father kicks monks.
Does he kick you too, parrot?
My father keeps the east.
Yours keeps a stable.

blocks.html: Before that can turn into a fight, Namgun has already bitten someone.
blocks.ko: 그게 싸움이 되기도 전에, 남건이 벌써 누군가를 물었다.

en: Say sorry to my brother!
…Say sorry or I bite the other hand.

lines: 남건아. 대가 집 아들은 무는 거 아니야.
en: Namgun. You do not bite the sons of commanders.
…Which hand?

blocks.html: The masters punish Namseng, because he is old enough to be responsible and Namgun is not old enough to be enrolled. Namseng copies the chapter on filial piety forty times. Namgun sits beside him and fills the margins with horses.
blocks.ko: 스승들은 남생을 벌한다. 남생은 책임질 나이고, 남건은 입학할 나이도 안 됐으니까. 남생은 효에 관한 장을 마흔 번 베껴 쓴다. 남건은 그 옆에 앉아 여백마다 말을 그려 넣는다.

blocks.label: SUMMER
blocks.ko: 여름

blocks.html: Summer is when the money arrives.
blocks.ko: 여름에는 돈이 온다.

blocks.html: The Tehak owes rice. It has owed it for thirty years to the monasteries that feed its students, at a rate the monasteries call charity and the bursar calls interest. In the fourth month the debt is paid off in full, in Eastern rice, on Eastern carts. Nobody asks whose. Everybody knows.
blocks.ko: 태학은 쌀을 빚지고 있다. 학생들을 먹이는 절에 삼십 년째 빚을 졌는데, 절에서는 그 이자를 자비라 부르고 서기는 이자라 부른다. 사월에 그 빚이 한꺼번에 갚아진다. 동부의 쌀이 동부의 수레에 실려 온다. 누구 것이냐고 묻는 사람은 없다. 다들 안다.

blocks.speaker: Tehak Master
lines: 이제 태학이 대가께 무엇을 빚졌는지 여쭤도 되겠습니까?
en: Commander. The Academy is… grateful.
May I ask what the Academy owes you now?

lines: 본당에 빈 의자 하나. 거기 내가 고른 사람이 앉는다.
en: A chair.
One empty chair in the main hall, and a man of my choosing in it.

blocks.html: The man he chooses is old, and has been in Pyongyang longer than Yeon has been alive. He came with an embassy from the West seventeen winters ago to read the Way of Laozi to the late king, and was forgotten when the king stopped listening. Since then he has lived on a temple’s leftovers. Yeon finds him there, gives him a stipend and a new robe, and moves him into the Tehak.
blocks.ko: 그가 고른 사람은 늙었고, 연이 태어나기도 전부터 평양에 있었다. 열일곱 해 전 겨울 서국 사신단을 따라와 선왕에게 노자의 도를 읽어 주었고, 왕이 귀를 닫자 잊혔다. 그 뒤로 절에서 남긴 밥으로 살았다. 연은 거기서 그를 찾아내 녹봉과 새 옷을 주고 태학으로 옮긴다.

blocks.speaker: The Daoist Reader
lines: 대가, 나는 도를 가르치오. 도에 이르기를, 가장 좋은 임금은 백성이 있는 줄도 잘 모르는 임금이라 했소.
en: Commander, I teach the Way. The Way says the best ruler is one the people barely know is there.

lines: 그럼 나 좋아하겠네. 난 집에 붙어 있질 않으니까.
en: Then you’ll like me. I’m hardly ever home.

blocks.html: The sutra class is not abolished. That would be loud. It is moved: from the main hall to the east room, then from the morning to the afternoon, then to the afternoon of archery day, when no boy with a bow in his hand will sit for the Lotus Sutra. By midsummer Boduk teaches four students. By autumn, one.
blocks.ko: 불경 수업은 없애지 않는다. 없애면 시끄러우니까. 옮길 뿐이다. 본당에서 동쪽 방으로, 아침에서 오후로, 다시 활 쏘는 날 오후로. 활을 쥔 아이가 법화경을 들으러 앉을 리 없다. 한여름이 되자 보덕의 학생은 넷이다. 가을이 되자 하나다.

blocks.label: AUTUMN
blocks.ko: 가을

blocks.html: The one is Namseng.
blocks.ko: 그 하나가 남생이다.

blocks.html: He goes in secret, which for a seven-year-old means he tells exactly one person. Namgun keeps the secret for most of a day.
blocks.ko: 그는 몰래 다닌다. 일곱 살에게 몰래란 딱 한 사람에게만 말한다는 뜻이다. 남건은 그 비밀을 거의 하루 종일 지킨다.

en: Father! Brother’s going to the monk!
…I didn’t tell. I said it loud. That’s different.

blocks.html: Yeon does not shout. That is worse. He puts Namseng up on his saddle and rides him to the Tehak’s east room, where Boduk is teaching nobody.
blocks.ko: 연은 소리치지 않는다. 그게 더 무섭다. 그는 남생을 안장 앞에 태우고 태학의 동쪽 방으로 간다. 보덕이 아무도 없는 방에서 가르치고 있다.

en: Well? What’s he teach you, then?

lines: 세상에서 가장 센 것은 되받아치지 않는 것이라 하셨습니다.
en: Forbearance, Father.
He says the strongest thing in the world is the one that does not hit back.

lines: 그래? 그럼 저 중이 평양에서 제일 센 놈이구나. 내가 일 년 내내 때렸는데.
가라. 마저 배워. 그리고 집에 와서 네 동생이 떠들 수 없는 걸 말해 줘라.
en: Aye? Then he’s the strongest man in Pyongyang. I’ve been hitting him all year.
Go on. Finish the lesson. Then come home and tell your brother something he can’t shout.

blocks.html: Boduk teaches the lesson to the end, to one boy, in an empty room. He has a talent for empty rooms. One day, the storytellers say, he will pick up his whole hall and carry it south, roof and all, to a country that still wants it.
blocks.ko: 보덕은 빈 방에서 아이 하나를 앞에 두고 수업을 끝까지 한다. 그는 빈 방에 재주가 있다. 이야기꾼들 말로는, 언젠가 그가 법당을 통째로 들어 지붕째 남쪽으로 날려 보낸다고 한다. 아직 그것을 원하는 나라로.

blocks.label: WINTER
blocks.ko: 겨울

blocks.label: The Uncle’s Supper
blocks.ko: 숙부의 저녁상

blocks.html: The complaint reaches the High Commander’s table before the year is out. It is written in a monk’s neat hand. Gusesa reads it at supper, between courses.
blocks.ko: 고발장은 해가 가기 전에 막리지의 상에 오른다. 승려의 단정한 글씨다. 구세사는 저녁을 들다가, 국과 국 사이에 그것을 읽는다.

lines: (손가락을 닦으며, 부드럽게) 연가가 중들한테 뭘 가지라 마라 하는군.
내 조카는 남들이 말 모으듯 적을 모아. 말은 기나마 덜 먹는데.
en: (mild, wiping his fingers) A Yeon telling monks what to own.
My nephew collects enemies the way other men collect horses. At least horses eat less.

blocks.html: Yeon is called to the table. He does not sit, because nobody offers. He does not take his boots off, because nobody asks.
blocks.ko: 연이 상 앞으로 불려 온다. 앉으라는 말이 없으니 앉지 않는다. 신을 벗으라는 말이 없으니 벗지 않는다.

lines: 조카야. 반룡사 중들은 아침마다 임금님 잘되라고 빈다.
이제 너를 위해서도 빌 거다. 머이를 비는디는 맘에 안 들갓디만.
en: Nephew. The monks of Banryong pray for the king every morning.
They will pray for you too, now. You’ll no like what they pray.

lines: 이 나라에서 중들이 돈 안 받는 건 기거 하나뿐이니끼니.
en: Let them. Prayers are free.
Only thing in this country the monks don’t charge for.

blocks.html: Gusesa wipes his fingers and goes back to his soup. That is how the meeting ends. Only one of the two men at the table knows it is also how a list begins.
blocks.ko: 구세사는 손가락을 닦고 다시 국을 뜬다. 그렇게 자리가 끝난다. 그게 명단 하나의 시작이기도 하다는 걸, 그 상에 앉은 두 사람 중 하나만 안다.

blocks.html: By the new year three county schools in the east have the same empty chair, and the same old man’s pupils in it. That is how Yeon does everything: one room, then the room next door. In a few years every school in the country will teach what this one teaches, and the men who used to teach it will be sweeping other people’s yards.
blocks.ko: 새해가 되자 동부의 고을 학교 세 곳에 같은 빈 의자가 생기고, 그 노인의 제자들이 앉는다. 연은 무엇이든 이렇게 한다. 방 하나, 그다음은 옆방. 몇 해 지나면 이 나라의 모든 학교가 이 학교에서 가르치는 것을 가르치게 되고, 원래 가르치던 사람들은 남의 마당을 쓸게 된다.

blocks.label: The Boys’ Room
blocks.ko: 아이들 방

blocks.html: The boys share a room, because it is a commander’s house and not a palace. Namsan sleeps between his brothers like a sack of rice nobody wants to carry.
blocks.ko: 아이들은 한 방을 쓴다. 대가의 집이지 궁궐이 아니니까. 남산은 아무도 들고 싶어 하지 않는 쌀자루처럼 두 형 사이에서 잔다.

lines: 형. 아버지 돌아가시면 인장은 누가 가져?
en: Brother. When Father dies, who gets the seal?
The eldest.
That’s me.

lines: 그럼 싸움은 내가 다 이겨 줄게.
en: Then I’ll win all the fights for you.
…And if you lose it, I’ll take it back.
I won’t lose it.
…Brother.

blocks.html: Namsan, two, says the only word he has and reaches across Namseng for the other brother. Nobody notices. Gulgul, at the door with his back to the wall, notices everything.
blocks.ko: 두 살 남산이 가진 말 하나를 하고는, 남생을 넘어 다른 형 쪽으로 손을 뻗는다. 아무도 눈치채지 못한다. 등을 벽에 대고 문가에 선 걸걸만 모든 걸 본다.

blocks.html: On the days the Daoist reader is ill, Namseng reads his father’s copy of the Daodejing, which has never been opened past the first page.
blocks.ko: 도사가 앓아눕는 날이면 남생은 아버지의 도덕경을 읽는다. 첫 장 너머로는 한 번도 펼쳐진 적 없는 책이다.

blocks.html: Field trip. Yeon takes the boys to see a very big rock. The rock has a list on it, and a question…!
blocks.ko: 소풍이다. 연이 아들들을 데리고 아주 큰 바위를 보러 간다. 바위에는 목록이 하나 새겨져 있고, 질문이 하나 숨어 있다…!

logline.en: Every Goguryeo boy is raised on the Great King’s stone. Nobody tells them what it weighs.
logline.ko: 고구려 사내아이는 누구나 대왕의 비석을 듣고 자란다. 그 돌이 얼마나 무거운지는 아무도 말해 주지 않는다.

images.prompt: A Korean ink painting on aged hanji with the texture of an ink rubbing (takbon) in the stone. ICONIC MINIMAL LAYOUT: tall vertical scroll. ONE device: the Gwanggaeto Stele as one massive rough-hewn natural stone column, slightly irregular, rising from the lower third nearly to the top edge, a solid mass of dark rubbed ink texture with faint rows of carved-character pits that are NOT legible (abstract chisel marks only). Everything around it is empty paper: a flat plain as one pale ink line, faint distant Goguryeo tomb mound. At its foot, tiny, YEON GAESOMUN (face and garments from the attached portrait, face a few strokes) stands with his hand flat on the stone, a red #d0362f sash the only colour; beside him three small boys in plain robes — one boy pointing up bored, one squinting at the marks, one looking only at his father. One blank red seal square. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.

images.alt: The Great King’s stone is taller than four men. Namseng is not impressed.
images.prompt: OPENING STILL of the episode: the first image the reader sees, staging its first line. The line: “The Great King’s stone is taller than four men. Namseng is not impressed.” Context: The Great King’s stone is taller than four men. Namseng is not impressed. The old capital, where the Great King’s stone still does the bragging.  A wide or medium establishing frame that hooks. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask.
