images.prompt: CLOSING STILL of the episode: the final scene of this story as it ends (not the next episode). The line: “On the ride home Yeon is quiet, which his sons have never seen. Somewhere down the valley, a clerk’s brush is still moving.” Context: With an army, if we’re lucky. Then we find out what we’re worth. The sun goes down behind the stone. Its shadow runs all the way down the hill, past the old tombs, to the river. On the ride home Yeon is quiet, which his sons have never seen. Somewhere down the valley, a clerk’s brush is still moving. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). COMMONERS in every Samhan kingdom wear SIMPLE WHITE: plain undyed white or off-white hemp and ramie jackets, wide trousers and skirts, a cloth sash, straw sandals or bare feet, hair in a plain topknot or braid — no dyed silk, no dots, no gold; colour belongs to rank, so a crowd of farmers, porters, servants and townsfolk reads as a field of soft white cloth with the officials' colours standing out of it. Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: The Great King’s stone is taller than four men. Namseng is not impressed.
blocks.ko: 대왕의 비석은 사람 넷을 포갠 것보다 높다. 남생은 감동하지 않는다.

blocks.html: The old capital, where the Great King’s stone still does the bragging.
blocks.ko: 옛 수도. 자랑은 아직도 대왕의 비석이 대신 한다.

blocks.html: Yeon has ridden two days to the old capital to show his sons this. Namseng has heard about it since before he could sit a horse. Namgun has heard nothing and is having a wonderful time. Gulgul carries Namsan, who is asleep.
blocks.ko: 연은 이걸 보여 주려고 아들들을 데리고 옛 도읍까지 이틀을 달려왔다. 남생은 말에 앉기도 전부터 이 비석 얘기를 들었다. 남건은 아무것도 못 들었고, 그래서 신이 났다. 굴굴은 잠든 남산을 업고 있다.

lines: 에이… 이게 다야요? 기냥 큰 돌인데?
en: Aw… that’s it? A big rock?

blocks.html: Every Goguryeo boy is raised on him. He kept the west shut, and he made it look easy.
blocks.ko: 고구려 사내아이라면 누구나 그를 듣고 자란다. 서쪽을 닫아걸었고, 그걸 쉬워 보이게 했다.

en: Father! I’m going to climb it.
Go on. Fall off. Then you’ll remember it.

blocks.html: Namgun gets as high as the first crack and sits there, delighted, like a cat on a roof. Gulgul stands underneath with his arms half out. Nobody tells him to.
blocks.ko: 남건은 첫 번째 금까지 올라가서는 지붕 위 고양이처럼 신이 나서 걸터앉는다. 걸걸이 그 밑에 팔을 반쯤 벌리고 선다. 시킨 사람은 없다.

en: Don’t fall… don’t fall…

lines: 그 양반, 열여덟에 왕위에 올랐다. 제일 먼저 머이 했는지 아네?
en: He was eighteen when they put him on the throne. You ken what he did first?
Built a temple, Father?

lines: 서쪽으로 가서 할아바지가 잃은 성을 죄다 도로 찾았다. 기러고도 멈추질 않았디.
기걸로 편지 써 보낸 놈은 하나도 없었고.
en: He rode west and took back every fort his grandfather lost. Then he kept going.
Nobody wrote him a letter about it.

lines: 데 바위에 성이 예순넷 적혀 있다.
en: Sixty-four fortresses are written on that rock.
Go on. Read me one.

blocks.html: Namseng reads the Analects every morning. He gets four characters into the stone and stops. The carving is old, and the Great King’s scribes did not write for boys.
blocks.ko: 남생은 아침마다 논어를 읽는다. 비문은 네 글자를 읽고 멈춘다. 새김은 오래됐고, 대왕의 서기들은 어린애 읽으라고 쓰지 않았다.

blocks.html: In all, the fortresses he attacked and broke: sixty-four. Villages: one thousand four hundred.
blocks.ko: 무릇 쳐서 깨뜨린 성이 64곳, 마을이 1,400곳이다.
blocks.hanja: 凡所攻破城六十四，村一千四百。
blocks.source: Gwanggaeto Stele (廣開土王碑), conquest record (414)

blocks.html: They are not alone on the hill. The Western party has come up the other path: an envoy in good silk, two clerks with ink boxes, and a Goguryeo official paid to show them everything. One clerk is already copying the list.
blocks.ko: 언덕에 그들만 있는 게 아니다. 반대편 길로 서국 일행이 올라와 있다. 좋은 비단을 걸친 사신 하나, 먹통을 든 서기 둘, 그리고 전부 보여 주라고 돈을 받은 고구려 관리 하나. 서기 하나는 벌써 그 목록을 베끼고 있다.

blocks.speaker: The Western envoy
lines: 대단한 비석이오, 대가. 우리 황제께서 역사를 몹시 좋아하시지요.
전부 보고 오라 하셨소. 길이며 성이며 나루며, 하나도 빠짐없이. 귀국 관리들이 아주 친절하더이다.
en: A remarkable stone, Commander. My emperor loves history.
He asked me to see all of it. Every road, every fort, every ford. Your officials have been most generous.

blocks.html: Namseng knows exactly what a guest from afar is owed. He steps forward, bows the way his tutor taught him, and recites the first line of the Analects.
blocks.ko: 남생은 먼 데서 온 손님에게 무엇을 해야 하는지 정확히 안다. 앞으로 나서서, 스승이 가르친 대로 절하고, 논어 첫 구절을 왼다.

lines: “벗이 먼 곳에서 찾아오니 또한 즐겁지 아니한가.”
en: “Is it not a joy to have friends come from afar?”

blocks.speaker: The Western envoy
lines: 우리 황제께서 이런 아이들이라면 태학에 기꺼이 받으실 거요. 귀국 태자께서도 벌써 여럿 보내셨지.
en: Charming! The Commander’s son has been well taught.
My emperor would be glad of such boys at his academy. Your crown prince has sent him several already.

blocks.html: Namseng goes red to the ears. He had wanted to be told he did well. He was, by the wrong man.
blocks.ko: 남생의 귀까지 빨개진다. 잘했다는 말을 듣고 싶었다. 들었다. 엉뚱한 사람한테서.

lines: 그리고 저놈은 얼마 줬소? 말고삐 잡은 놈.
en: He’s not for sale.
And what did that one cost you? The one holding your horse.

blocks.html: The paid official finds something interesting in the grass. The envoy only smiles. He has been smiling for three provinces.
blocks.ko: 돈 받은 관리는 풀숲에서 뭔가 재미있는 걸 찾아낸다. 사신은 웃기만 한다. 세 고을째 웃는 중이다.

lines: 너. 말 잡은 놈. 저것들 가고 나면 나 좀 보자.
돈도 가져오라우. 나도 좀 세 보게.
en: You. With the horse. When they’re gone, come and see me.
Bring the money. I want to count it too.

blocks.html: The official goes very white, which is answer enough.
blocks.ko: 관리의 얼굴이 하얗게 질린다. 그걸로 대답은 충분하다.

en: Can I push him off now?
Later.

lines: 아바지. 제가 데 사람 밀어 버릴 수 있습네다.
en: Father. I can push that one off.
The little one. With the ink.

lines: 베끼라고 해. 하나도 빼디 말고 세라고 해.
en: Not today.
Let him copy. Let him count every one.

blocks.html: The clerk counts. The envoy bows, prettily, and takes his party down the hill before supper. His report will reach the emperor by autumn. It is very thorough.
blocks.ko: 서기는 센다. 사신은 곱게 절하고, 저녁 전에 일행을 데리고 언덕을 내려간다. 그의 보고는 가을이면 황제에게 닿는다. 아주 꼼꼼한 보고다.

lines: 예순넷. 기런데 이제는 서국 비단 걸친 놈이 우리 언덕에 올라와서 기걸 세.
자, 오늘 공부다. 봄마다 가을마다 우리는 서쪽에 조공을 보낸다. 비단, 말, 사내애들.
예순넷을 빼앗은 나라가 어쩌다 일 년에 두 번 당에 절하게 됐네?
en: Sixty-four. And now a man in the Western silk walks up our hill and counts them.
Here’s your lesson. Every spring and every autumn we send tribute west. Silk, horses, bairns.
How does a country that took sixty-four come to bow to the West twice a year?
Because… it is polite, Father?
Wrong. Again.
Because we stopped… counting?

lines: 평양에 앉은 놈들이 늙고, 살찌고, 겁을 먹고는 기걸 평화라고 불러서다.
기억해 두라우. 언젠가 네래 그 자리에 앉는다.
en: Closer.
Because the men in Pyongyang got old and fat and scared, and called it peace.
Remember it. One day you’ll sit where they sit.

blocks.html: Namseng nods as if he understands. On Gulgul’s back, Namsan has woken up. He looks at the stone, then at his father, then at the path the Western clerks took, and says nothing at all.
blocks.ko: 남생은 알아들은 척 고개를 끄덕인다. 굴굴의 등에서 남산이 깨어 있다. 비석을 보고, 아버지를 보고, 서국 서기들이 내려간 길을 본다. 그리고 아무 말도 하지 않는다.

en: Father. Will that man come back?

lines: 그놈은 안 와. 그놈 황데가 오디.
en: Not him. His emperor.
With tribute?

lines: 운이 좋으면 군대를 들고. 기래야 우리래 얼마짜린디 알디.
en: With an army, if we’re lucky. Then we find out what we’re worth.

blocks.html: The sun goes down behind the stone. Its shadow runs all the way down the hill, past the old tombs, to the river.
blocks.ko: 해가 비석 뒤로 진다. 비석 그림자가 언덕을 타고 옛 무덤들을 지나 강까지 길게 뻗는다.

blocks.html: On the ride home Yeon is quiet, which his sons have never seen. Somewhere down the valley, a clerk’s brush is still moving.
blocks.ko: 돌아오는 길에 연은 말이 없다. 아들들은 그런 아버지를 처음 본다. 골짜기 저 아래 어딘가에서, 서기의 붓은 아직 움직이고 있다.

blocks.html: Some visitors knock. Some take their boots off. One old friend is about to do neither…!
blocks.ko: 문을 두드리는 손님이 있다. 신을 벗는 손님이 있다. 그리고 둘 다 안 할 오랜 벗이 하나 있다…!

logline.en: In thirty years, old Dosuryu has never once kept his boots on in this house. Tonight he does.
logline.ko: 삼십 년 동안 도수류는 이 집에 신을 신은 채 들어온 적이 한 번도 없다. 오늘 밤은 신은 채다.

images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 movie still, 2D cel-painterly webtoon, not photoreal. DRAMATIC CHIAROSCURO: crushed black timber hall, one hard warm shaft, long shadows, not a flat seated portrait. Dutch angle. The geomungo is a long low wooden wedge across the bottom third, the one device, tassels catching the light. Dosuryu sits behind it, small against empty dark posts. FACE, long beard, orange-brown robe, black collar, and black cap with two upright wheat pins from the attached portrait. Instrument matches the attached geomungo: frets, six strings, pegs with dark tassels, struck with a thin bamboo stick in the right hand, left hand on the frets. Quiet stern face, mouth closed, eyes on the strings, restrained, not a scowl-cartoon. Thick creamy bokeh in the foreground (blurred floorboards) and giwa roofs behind. images.alt: Spring light falls across Yeon Tejo's empty bed in the Eastern Hall; his staff leans against the wall and his son kneels beside it.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. On the bed Yeon Taejo lies still under a crimson #8f3a2e cover, white beard spread on the pillow, eyes closed, hands folded, peaceful. His plain wooden staff leans against the timber wall at the edge of the shaft. Yeon Gesomun, thirty-nine, massive, black beard, charcoal robe edged red, no armor, kneels on the floor beside the bed with both fists on his knees, head bowed, back broad and rigid. A few plum petals blown in on the floorboards inside the light. Everything outside the shaft falls to umber black. Old-master tenebrist canvas, quiet, no mourners crowd, no clutter. No text. No watermark. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: one sword in a fight; gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | YEON TAEJO — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_taejo.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Gesomun's father and an old man in every still: snow-white hair in a tight topknot tied with dark red cord, long white beard and moustache, the same heavy straight Yeon brows and hard jaw as his sons, deep lines around tired, watchful eyes; shoulders once massive, now slightly stooped. Dress: Retired High Commander's court dress, not armor: long charcoal-black silk robe crossed left over right with deep crimson #8f3a2e edging at collar, cuffs and hem, crimson sash, short dark fur-trimmed overcoat over the shoulders, black boots. He no longer wears a sword. #8f3a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: armor or a helm; dark hair or a black beard; a young or vigorous body; shouting; a sword at the hip. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.prompt: CLOSING STILL of the episode: the final scene of this story as it ends (not the next episode). The line: “And when they finally hand me that seal— I’ll throw them a banquet. In Pyongyang. The biggest that city has ever seen. Every commander. My uncle. His Majesty. Nobody gets to miss it.” Context: Gulgul. Saddle the bay. Tomorrow I ride to Pyongyang and bury my father. Then I thank my uncle for supper, and I bow. To the king. To every chair at that Summit. All summer, if that’s what it takes. Yes. Saddle. The bay. And when they finally hand me that seal— I’ll throw them a banquet. In Pyongyang. The biggest that city has ever seen. Every commander. My uncle. His Majesty. Nobody gets to miss it. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | GULGUL — FACE and garments from attached /ch_dae_gulgul_young.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Mohe-born, lean and weathered; dark skin, hard narrow eyes, thin moustache and a short chin beard as a man. Dress: Goguryeo border warden: grey steel lamellar under a heavy white-grey fur mantle, dark-red sash and wrapped forearms. Now: Boy (stage portrait ch_dae_gulgul_young): BEARDLESS, shaved crown with one dark centre strip, two long braids, blood-streaked defiant face, ragged fur over a white wrap. Demeanor: Grim and spare. Says little, watches the door, stands one step behind whoever he serves. #8b3a3a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: a Goguryeo court robe; a crown. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). COMMONERS in every Samhan kingdom wear SIMPLE WHITE: plain undyed white or off-white hemp and ramie jackets, wide trousers and skirts, a cloth sash, straw sandals or bare feet, hair in a plain topknot or braid — no dyed silk, no dots, no gold; colour belongs to rank, so a crowd of farmers, porters, servants and townsfolk reads as a field of soft white cloth with the officials' colours standing out of it. Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: In thirty years Dosuryu has never knocked at this house. Tonight, for the first time, he keeps his boots on.
blocks.ko: 삼십 년 동안 도수류는 이 집 문을 두드린 적이 없다. 오늘 밤, 처음으로, 그는 신을 신은 채 들어온다.

blocks.html: Gesomun is at supper with his boots on the table, which his wife gave up on years ago. The boys are in bed. The house is warm and loud, and nobody in it is afraid of anything. Nobody in it has heard yet.
blocks.ko: 게소문은 장화 신은 발을 상에 올리고 저녁을 먹는 중이다. 아내는 오래전에 포기했다. 아이들은 잠자리에 들었다. 집은 따뜻하고 시끄럽고, 그 안에 뭘 무서워하는 사람은 하나도 없다. 아직 아무도 소식을 못 들었으니까.

blocks.html: Then the door bangs open.
blocks.ko: 그때 문이 벌컥 열린다.

en: Oi. Old man. Boots.

lines: 아니, 서 있으라우. 넌 서 있을 때 말을 더 잘 듣더라.
en: Shut up and sit down.
No — stay standing. You listen better standing.
Your father’s dead.

blocks.html: Nobody moves. The fire does all the talking for a while.
blocks.ko: 아무도 움직이지 않는다. 한동안 말은 불이 다 한다.

en: …When.

lines: 나흘 전. 궁궐 언덕 아래 그 큰 집에서.
눈 오는데 평양까지 말을 타고 내려왔더라. 네 인장 달라고 제가회의에 직접 청하러. 하루 종일 그 방에 앉아 있다가, 집에 와서 눕더니, 못 일어났다.
en: Four nights back. In the big house under the palace hill.
He rode down to Pyongyang in the snow to ask the Summit for your seal himself. Sat in that chamber all day. Came home, lay down, and didnae get up.

lines: 말을 못 타. 칠 년째 말 등에 올라 본 적이 없는 양반이야.
en: He couldn’t ride. He hasn’t been on a horse in seven years.
He rode.

lines: 너한테 남긴 말이 있다. “생각하는 거 절반만 말하라고 전해라.”
내가 기랬디, 저놈은 사분의 일도 못 할 거라고. 웃더라. 기게 마지막이었다.
en: He left you a message. “Tell him to say half of what he thinks.”
I told him you’d never manage a quarter. He laughed. That was the last of it.

blocks.html: Gesomun looks at his boots on the table as if they belong to somebody else.
blocks.ko: 게소문은 상 위에 올린 제 장화를, 남의 것이라도 되는 양 내려다본다.

en: And the seal.

lines: 북부, 서부, 남부. 셋 다. 동부의 인장은 자기들한테 소리 안 지르는 놈을 찾을 때까지 상자에 넣어 둔단다.
en: No.
The North, the West, the South. All three of them. The Eastern seal goes in a box till they find somebody who doesnae shout at them.
Who shouted?

lines: 네가. 제가회의에서. 아바지 자리에 앉을 나이가 된 뒤로 해마다.
북부 욕살한테 대놓고 말 세는 놈이라 했지. 서부한텐 서국가 젓가락으로 집어먹을 거라 했고. 기러고 임금 앞에서 박차고 나갔디.
en: You. At the Summit. Every year since you were old enough to sit in your father’s chair.
You called the Northern Commander a horse-counter to his face. You told the West the West would eat him with chopsticks. Then you walked out on the king.
He is a horse-counter.

lines: “동부를 맡기기엔 너무 뜨겁다.” 기러더라. “할 일 없으면 전쟁이라도 일으킬 놈이다.”
en: He’s a horse-counter with a vote.
“Too hot for the East,” they said. “He’ll start a war just to have something to do.”

lines: 오늘 밤 내 말이 네 대문에 서 있는 걸 누가 보면, 내 이름도 그 명단에 올라간다. 기러니 날래 들어.
en: If they see my horse at your gate tonight, my name goes on the list too. So listen fast.

lines: 폐하하고 네 숙부. 이번 달에만 세 번이다. 알현전 뒤 그 작은 방.
딴 사람은 아무도 없었어. 술 따르는 아이조차.
en: His Majesty and your uncle. Three times this month, the same little room behind the audience hall.
Nobody else in it. Not even a wee boy to pour.

lines: 이제 임금이랑 밥을 먹네? 그 양반 누구랑도 밥 안 먹는데.
en: My uncle. Gusesa.
He eats with the king now? He doesn’t eat with anybody.

lines: 올봄에 중 하나래 편지를 보냈다더라. 글씨는 단정하고, 불평은 많고.
그 뒤로 너만 보면 심사가 꼬였지.
en: A monk wrote him a letter this spring. Neat hand. Lots of complaints.
He has been in a mood about you since.
So they drink together. Good for them.

lines: 네래 제가회의에서 박차고 나간 뒤로 그 방에서 네 이름이 나와. 봄에 너를 장성 끝자락으로 보낼 작정이다. 기리고 거기서 안 돌아오게 할 작정이고.
en: They don’t drink. That’s what’s wrong with it.
Ever since you walked out of the Summit, your name comes up in that room. They mean to send you to the far end of the wall in the spring. And have you not come back from it.
When?

lines: 봄. 성벽 맨 끝, 부여성 너머. 편지가 한 달은 걸리는 데다.
기리고 거기서 어느 밤, 네가 말에서 떨어지는 거디. 참 안됐디. 장례는 크게 치러 주고.
en: Spring. The far end of the wall, past Buyeo Fortress. So far the letters take a month.
And one night out there, you fall off your horse. Very sad. Big funeral.

lines: 부여성 너머라. 하. 거기 가면 나라도 말에서 떨어지갓다. 심심해서.
en: Past Buyeo Fortress. Hah. I’d fall off my horse out there too. From boredom.
HAHAHAHAHAHA
Kill me? Yeon Gesomun?

lines: 길 우 바위엔 성이 예순넷이나 적혀 있는데, 성벽 하나로 날 묶어 두갓다고?
en: Sixty-four fortresses on a rock up the road, and they think one wall will hold me?

lines: 네 아바지는 열두 해를 제가회의 보고 웃다가 머리가 하얘져서 돌아왔다. 넌 열두 해 없어. 봄까지야.
en: Laugh. Go on.
Your father laughed at the Summit for twelve years and came home grey. You haven’t got twelve years. You’ve got till spring.
Why now?

lines: 네래 회의장을 박차고 나왔을 때 온 성안이 환호했으니끼니.
임금은 환호 소리를 셀 줄 안다. 네 삼촌은 두 번 세고.
en: Because you walked out of the Summit and the whole city cheered.
Kings can count cheering. Your uncle counts it twice.
Who told you. The cook?

lines: 요리사래 내 사촌이다. 요리사 마누라는 다른 사촌이고.
그 궁 절반이 내 사촌이야. 평양에서 사십 년 살면 기게 남는다. 친척.
en: The cook’s my cousin. The cook’s wife is my other cousin.
Half that palace is my cousin. That’s what forty years in Pyongyang buys you. Relatives.

lines: 기럼 오늘 밤 올라가디. 임금 면전에서 물어보면 되갓네.
en: Then I’ll go up there tonight. Ask His Majesty to his face.

lines: 그 얼굴로 오늘 밤 올라가면 역적으로 가는 거다. 수고 덜어 줘서 고맙다고들 하갓디.
en: You go tonight with that face, you go as a traitor. They’ll thank you for saving them the trouble.
Stand still. I said stand.

blocks.html: Yeon stops laughing. He does it all at once, the way a door shuts.
blocks.ko: 연이 웃음을 멈춘다. 문이 닫히듯, 한 번에.

blocks.html: He sits down for the first time all evening. He takes his boots off the table and sets them on the floor, side by side, the way a man lines up things he means to use.
blocks.ko: 그는 저녁 내내 처음으로 앉는다. 상 위의 장화를 내려 바닥에 나란히 놓는다. 쓸 물건을 줄 세워 두는 사람처럼.

blocks.html: In the doorway behind them, a seven-year-old in his sleeping robe has come to see why the old man is shouting. Namseng hears one word, list, and does not understand it.
blocks.ko: 둘 뒤 문간에, 잠옷 바람의 일곱 살짜리가 늙은이가 왜 소리를 지르나 보러 나와 있다. 남생은 명단이라는 말 하나를 듣고, 알아듣지 못한다.

en: Oi. Bed. Now.
Father, what list—
The rice list. Bed.

blocks.html: Gulgul picks him up and carries him back to bed without turning his back on the door.
blocks.ko: 굴굴이 그를 안아 들고 잠자리로 데려간다. 문에 등을 보이지 않은 채.

en: How many names on their list.

lines: …왜 기렇게 웃네? 그만두라우. 너 기렇게 웃는 거 질색이다.
en: One that I know of. Yours.
…Why are you smiling like that? Stop it. I cannae stand it when you do that.
Then I’ll make a list too.
Mine’ll be longer.

lines: 네 명단에 뭘 적든, 난 안 읽고 싶다.
en: Whatever you put on yours, I don’t want to read it.
I’m old. I’d like to sleep.
Old man.
…Thanks.
Don’t thank me. Put your boots back on.
You’ll need them.

blocks.html: Dosuryu goes out the way he came in, boots and all, and stands a long time in the yard before he can make himself mount. He has known the boy for thirty years. He knows exactly what kind of list it will be.
blocks.ko: 도수류는 들어올 때처럼 장화 신은 채로 나가서, 한참을 마당에 서 있다가 겨우 말에 오른다. 그 아이를 안 지 서른 해다. 그게 어떤 명단일지 그는 정확히 안다.

blocks.html: When the old man has gone, Yeon calls for a lamp and a brush. Gulgul brings both and stands where he can see the door. Yeon writes for a long time. Once he stops, counts on his fingers, and adds another name.
blocks.ko: 늙은이가 가고 나자 연은 등잔과 붓을 가져오라 한다. 굴굴이 둘 다 가져와서, 문이 보이는 자리에 선다. 연은 오래도록 쓴다. 한 번은 멈추고, 손가락을 꼽아 세고, 이름을 하나 더 적는다.

en: Don’t read it.

blocks.html: Gulgul cannot read. He looks at the door anyway, to be polite.
blocks.ko: 굴굴은 글을 모른다. 그래도 예의 삼아 문 쪽을 본다.

blocks.html: Near dawn he folds the paper twice and puts it inside his coat, against the skin, where a man keeps the things he does not mean to lose.
blocks.ko: 새벽녘 그는 종이를 두 번 접어 옷 안, 살갗에 닿는 자리에 넣는다. 잃어버릴 생각이 없는 물건을 두는 자리다.

lines: 내일 평양 가서 아바지 묻는다. 기다음엔 삼촌한테 저녁 잘 먹었다고 인사하고, 절한다. 임금한테. 제가회의 자리마다. 여름 내내라도.
en: Gulgul. Saddle the bay.
Tomorrow I ride to Pyongyang and bury my father. Then I thank my uncle for supper, and I bow. To the king. To every chair at that Summit. All summer, if that’s what it takes.
Yes. Saddle. The bay.

lines: 내래 잔치를 연다. 평양에서. 그 도성이 생긴 이래 제일 큰 잔치를.
욕살들 전부. 숙부도. 폐하도. 아무도 빠지면 안 되디.
en: And when they finally hand me that seal—
I’ll throw them a banquet. In Pyongyang. The biggest that city has ever seen.
Every commander. My uncle. His Majesty. Nobody gets to miss it.

blocks.html: Far to the south, Sabi has a new king. On his coronation morning, several hundred people see a dragon…!
blocks.ko: 저 멀리 남쪽, 사비에 새 임금이 섰다. 즉위하는 날 아침, 수백 명이 용을 본다…!

logline.en: The court will style him Righteous and Merciful. He has a sense of humour about that.
logline.ko: 조정은 그를 의롭고 자애롭다 부를 것이다. 그는 그 말에 웃을 줄 안다.

Half a step behind his shoulder Gyebek (high messy ponytail, steel lamellar over ochre, red scarf) stands with arms crossed, deadpan, eyes sliding sideways at the king, half his face in shadow. Look: Broad, bearded king; black hair in a topknot with a yellow-gold headband whose tails trail; heavy brows, cynical eyes. Dress: Crimson robe with a dark charcoal collar and gold trim; a steel lamellar pauldron peeking at one shoulder. Demeanor: Licensed wit: drinks, smirks, slumps on the throne, speaks in polished aphorisms. Fatalist. #e08a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: heroic battle pose; smiling innocence. | GYEBEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gyebek.png (face only; invent a new pose). Dress: Ochre-gold jeogori and trousers, a crimson scarf knotted at the chest, crimson sash at the waist, forearms wrapped in dark cloth. Demeanor: Says little. Counts under his breath. Grim, tired, absolutely decided; never smiles in a fight. Rose from a nameless White River boy to 백승계백 (Hundred-Victories Gyebek); by Hwangsanbeol the taverns argue he is the stronger blade than Yushin, and one-to-one he is: twenty-five years younger, faster, never beaten in single combat. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows.
