LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.at: Euija takes the throne at forty-one.
images.alt: Righteous and Merciful. He has a sense of humour about that.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. The same shot in the Baekje palace at Sabi. King Euija, forty-one, broad and grinning, takes the black silk crown with its gold flame ornaments. The spirit line behind him: King Mu nearest, his father, then older Baekje kings fading into river haze. Far beyond the open doors, over the Sabi river, a dragon shape in the clouds. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = euija, SECOND face = kingmu (an ancestral spirit in the frame). Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_sabi_palace (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), crown reference (shape only). KING EUIJA — Look: Broad, bearded king; black hair in a topknot with a yellow-gold headband whose tails trail; heavy brows, cynical eyes. Dress: Crimson robe with a dark charcoal collar and gold trim; a steel lamellar pauldron peeking at one shoulder. Crown: Baekje king: a tall rounded black silk cap (오라관) with a plain black band at the brow, and a pair of tall openwork gold flame-and-leaf ornaments (금제관식) pinned to either side of the cap, rising above it like twin flames — thin gold blades fanning upward with leaf buds and curls. On Euija the two side ornaments are King Muryeong's gold diadem ornaments exactly as the attached museum photo (ignore its backdrop): a pair of thin sheet-gold flame-and-honeysuckle sprays, each a central stem with curling leaf-flames fanning up and out, pierced openwork and hung with small round gold spangles, one pinned on each side of the black silk cap and rising well above it. Colour #e08a2e. KING MU — Crown: Baekje king: a tall rounded black silk cap (오라관) with a plain black band at the brow, and a pair of tall openwork gold flame-and-leaf ornaments (금제관식) pinned to either side of the cap, rising above it like twin flames — thin gold blades fanning upward with leaf buds and curls. Colour #b8862c. PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.

blocks.html: Several hundred people see the dragon. Only one of them can see the string.
blocks.ko: 수백 명이 용을 본다. 줄이 보이는 사람은 그중 하나뿐이다.

blocks.html: On the morning of his coronation, a dragon is seen over the Sabi River. The court diarist writes it down, because it happened.
blocks.ko: 즉위하는 날 아침, 사비강 위로 용이 나타난다. 사관은 그것을 적는다. 실제로 일어난 일이므로.

blocks.html: It was four lacquered paper kites, a low mist, six boatmen paid in advance, and one hour of the year when the light comes up the river at exactly the right angle. Euija had been planning it since the previous autumn.
blocks.ko: 옻칠한 종이 연 넷, 낮게 깔린 안개, 미리 삯을 받은 뱃사공 여섯, 그리고 빛이 강을 거슬러 꼭 알맞은 각도로 올라오는 한 해 중 한 시각. 의자는 지난가을부터 그것을 준비해 왔다.

blocks.html: King Mu is dead at eighty, still cursing Silla, and nobody at the river is thinking about him.
blocks.ko: 무왕은 여든에 죽었다. 죽는 날까지 신라를 욕했다. 그런데 강가의 누구도 지금 그를 생각하지 않는다.

blocks.html: Euija takes the throne at forty-one. The court will style him Righteous and Merciful. He has a sense of humour about that.
blocks.ko: 의자가 마흔하나에 왕위에 오른다. 조정은 그를 인자군왕이라 부를 것이다. 본인은 그 이름에 웃을 줄 안다.

blocks.hanja: 於羅瑕
blocks.html: What Baekje’s lords call their king. The farmers have their own word for him. The king has heard it, and prefers this one.
blocks.ko: 백제의 귀족들이 임금을 부르는 말. 농사꾼들은 따로 부르는 말이 있다. 임금도 그 말을 들어 봤고, 이쪽을 더 좋아한다.

blocks.caption: The boy with the borrowed name, grown. He still cannot say a thing he does not believe.
blocks.ko: 이름을 빌린 아이가 자랐다. 아직도 믿지 않는 말은 입에 올리지 못한다.

en: …Your Majesty. That is not a dragon.

lines: 아녀. / 근데 저기 서 있는 사람들한테 가서 그렇게 말해 봐라. / 누가 이기나.
en: No, sir, it is not. / Now go and say so to those people standing there. / See who wins.
Wins what.
It is paper and sticks. I can see the string.
I will go and tell them. You said to.

lines: 가라는 말이 아니여. 누가 이기나 보라는 거지.
en: They cannot see the string.
I did not say go. I said see who wins.
That is the same order.
I will not call it a dragon anywhere.

lines: 한 시각만 여기 서 있어라. 입은 다물구.
너는 그걸 못 하지. 그래서 내가 너를 옆에 두는 겨.
en: Stand here for one hour. Mouth shut.
You cannot do the other thing. That is why I keep you beside me.

lines: 폐하. 그 용, 저희두 봤슈. / …폐하 곁에서두유.
en: Your Majesty. We saw the dragon too. / …From beside you.
…You two know better.

lines: 알지유. / 그래두 폐하께서 만드신 것 중에… 젤 오래 남는 건 용이 아니구유.
en: We surely do. / But of all Your Majesty has made… the thing that lasts longest isn’t a dragon.
…What did you say.

lines: 기적이유, 폐하. / 밤에만 가까이 두는 기적.
en: Miracles, Your Majesty. / The kind you keep close only at night.

blocks.html: His father had done it first, and better. Before he was king, King Mu paid the children of Sabi to sing a song he had written himself. By the third month the song was older than anyone could remember, and what it said about him had become a thing everybody had always known.
blocks.ko: 아버지가 먼저 했고, 더 잘했다. 왕이 되기 전 무왕은 제가 지은 노래를 사비의 아이들에게 삯을 주고 부르게 했다. 석 달이 지나자 그 노래는 아무도 기억하지 못할 만큼 오래된 것이 되었고, 그 노래가 그에 대해 말하는 바는 모두가 처음부터 알고 있던 사실이 되었다.

blocks.html: Nobody had to pay the children again. Euija filed that away.
blocks.ko: 아이들에게 다시 삯을 준 사람은 없다. 줄 필요가 없었다. 의자는 그것을 마음에 새겨 두었다.

lines: 서른째 어라하는 노래로 나라를 사셨지. 군대두 없이, 돈두 거의 없이.
그때 내가 열둘이었지. 그 뒤로 그만큼 감탄헌 적이 없어.
en: The thirtieth Eraha bought a country with a song. No army, almost no money.
I was twelve. Nothing since has impressed me near that much.

blocks.html: So the reign begins with small wonders. All of them arranged. None of them expensive.
blocks.ko: 그리하여 치세는 작은 기적으로 시작된다. 전부 꾸민 것이고, 어느 것도 비싸지 않다.

blocks.html: The white deer is the cheapest one. You take a young doe, you keep it out of the sun for a season, and you let it out on the hunting ground on a day the ministers are watching.
blocks.ko: 흰 사슴이 가장 싸다. 어린 암사슴 한 마리를 한 철 동안 볕에 내놓지 않다가, 재상들이 보고 있는 날에 사냥터에 풀면 된다.

blocks.html: The stone at the Rock of Politics sweats before a good decision. It sweats because somebody rubs it with brine the night before, and the somebody is always the same man.
blocks.ko: 정사암의 바위는 좋은 결정이 나기 전에 땀을 흘린다. 전날 밤 누군가 소금물로 문질러 두기 때문이고, 그 누군가는 늘 같은 사람이다.

blocks.html: Rice comes up on ground where nothing was planted. Something was planted. It was planted at night.
blocks.ko: 아무것도 심지 않은 땅에서 벼가 올라온다. 무언가 심겼다. 밤에 심겼다.

blocks.caption: Nine years on, the tide clerk sits on the rock. He still asks the question the king hoped nobody would.
blocks.ko: 아홉 해가 지나, 물때 서기는 바위 위에 앉아 있다. 아직도 임금이 아무도 묻지 않기를 바란 질문을 묻는다.

en: Your Majesty. What happens when the people work it out?

lines: 알아채지 못혀. / 사람은 자기가 믿구 싶은 것의 증거는 절대 검사 안 혀.
en: They won’t. / Nobody inspects the evidence for a thing they already want to believe.

blocks.label: The Morning After
blocks.ko: 이튿날 아침

blocks.html: He walks the riverbank the morning after the dragon as if the mist itself had appointed him. Children point. A grandmother weeps. A clerk from the Board of Rites drops his brush and does not pick it up, because picking it up would mean deciding whether to write what he saw or what he was told.
blocks.ko: 용을 만든 다음 날 아침, 그는 안개 자체가 임명한 사람처럼 강둑을 걷는다. 아이들이 가리킨다. 할멈이 운다. 예조의 서리가 붓을 떨어뜨리고도 집지 않는다. 집는 순간 — 본 것을 쓸지, 들은 것을 쓸지 — 결정해야 하니까.

lines: 군대는 국경을 옮기는 데 한 달이 걸리지.
이야기는 하룻밤에 옮기고, 그 특권을 고맙다 하지.
en: Look at them.
An army takes a month to move a border.
A story moves it overnight, and thanks you for the privilege.
Your Majesty is… enjoying this.

lines: 잘하는 일은 즐겨야지. 안 그러믄 심통이 나서 못허게 되거든.
en: I am good at it.
A man should enjoy what he is good at. Otherwise he does it badly, out of spite.

blocks.label: The Rock
blocks.ko: 정사암

blocks.html: At the Rock of Politics he arrives last, lets the ministers wait, rests two fingers on the sweating stone as if taking a pulse, and smiles the small smile of a physician who already wrote the prescription.
blocks.ko: 정사암에는 가장 늦게 도착해 대신들을 기다리게 한 뒤, 땀 흘리는 바위에 손가락 둘을 올려 맥박을 짚듯 하고, 처방을 이미 써 둔 의원처럼 작게 웃는다.

lines: 바위의 취향이 이리 좋다니, 우리 모두 행운이오.
en: The rock agrees.
How fortunate for all of us that the rock has such good taste.
The rock did not agree.
It is brine. I can smell it.
I am not going to nod at a wet rock.

lines: 대신들은 바위를 듣고 있소. 그대를 듣는 게 아니야.
고개는 끄덕이지 마시오. 침묵은 저들이 마음대로 읽거든. 그대 입은 못 읽고.
en: The ministers are listening to the rock. Not to you.
Do not nod. Silence they can misread. Your mouth they cannot.

lines: 그걸 진짜라고 믿는 자는, 이미 내 배역이고.
en: Gods are props. Spirits are lighting.
And any man who believes it is already in my cast.

blocks.html: This is entirely correct, and it is the sentence that kills him, nineteen years later, word for word.
blocks.ko: 완전히 옳은 말이고, 십구 년 뒤 그를 죽이는 문장이며, 한 글자도 다르지 않다.

en: …Your Majesty.

lines: 다만 통하지 않는다는 소리는 하지 마시오.
en: Sunchung. Hate the method. You have my permission.
Only do not stand there telling me it does not work.
Tonight?
One miracle, or two?

lines: 나라는 용을 보구. 너희는 임금을 보구.
en: Two.
I am in a mighty generous mood.
The country can watch the dragon. You can watch the king.

blocks.html: This is the Righteous and Merciful at full height: before the wine years. He wrote the sky this morning. He walks under it and does not look up.
blocks.ko: 전성기의 인자군왕이 이렇다. 술의 시절 이전이다. 오늘 아침 하늘을 써 넣었다. 올려다보지 않고 그 아래를 걷는다.

blocks.label: The King’s Chamber
blocks.ko: 침전

blocks.html: Two court maids attend him — close enough that the air between them feels arranged. He is proud of the number the way a man is proud of a hunger he has not yet failed to satisfy.
blocks.ko: 궁녀 둘이 그를 모신다 — 그 사이 공기가 이미 정해진 것처럼 가깝게. 그는 그 수효를 자랑스러워한다. 아직 실패해 보지 않은 허기를 자랑하는 사내의 방식으로.

en: …Don’t both be greedy.
I am… looking at a map.

lines: 지도보다… 저희 목이 더 가까이 있잖유.
en: The greed is Your Majesty’s.
You look at us… as if you already know.
Our throats… are closer than the map.

lines: …나는 시방 신라 국경 얘기를 허구 있었다.
en: …I was talking about the Silla border.

lines: 국경 얘기 허실 때 목소리가 젤 좋으셔유.
en: Yes, Your Majesty.
Your voice is at its best when you talk about borders.
So we keep asking.
…Leave.
Shall we?
Your Majesty has not let go.

lines: 천록의 나라, 부처님의 나라 — 두 이름을 따뜻이 두어라. 하나는 장사치의 것, 하나는 스님의 것.
en: Righteous and merciful — so he was named.
Land of the Heavenly Deer, Land of the Lord Buddha — keep both names warm. One is for merchants. One is for monks.

blocks.label: The Princes
blocks.ko: 왕자들

blocks.html: Gyebek is twenty-one, and seated far down the table. No market calls him Hundred-Victories. Not yet. He is passed over every season, because nobody knows what clan he comes from, and he won’t make one up.
blocks.ko: 계백은 스물하나, 상 끝자락에 앉아 있다. 아직 어느 장터도 그를 백승이라 부르지 않는다. 아직은. 철마다 승진에서 밀린다. 어느 가문 출신인지 아무도 모르고, 그는 지어낼 생각이 없다.

blocks.html: At the coronation feast the princes sit by age, and the table has to be lengthened twice. Yung sits nearest the king, with a Satek cup-bearer at his elbow. Behind every brother's chair stands a clan tutor, like a second shadow. At the far end, servants pour for boys who don't have names worth carving yet.
blocks.ko: 즉위 잔치에서 왕자들은 나이순으로 앉고, 상을 두 번이나 늘려야 한다. 왕 바로 옆엔 융, 그 곁엔 사택의 술 시중. 형제들 의자 뒤마다 가문의 스승이 두 번째 그림자처럼 서 있다. 저 끝에선 아직 새길 만한 이름도 없는 아이들에게 시종들이 술을 따른다.

lines: 저 상 좀 봐라! 서른 번째 어라하께선 나라를 하나 남기셨지. 나는 아들로 나라를 하나 더 만들었다.
세어 봐라, 성충. 어서. 나는 서른 넘어가면 헷갈려.
en: Look at that table! The thirtieth Eraha left me a country. I made a second one out of sons.
Count them, Sunchung. Go on. I lose track after thirty.

lines: 마흔하나입니다, 전하. 올봄에 난 둘까지 치면.
…그리고 언젠가는 저마다 자리가 하나씩 필요할 겁니다. 자리는 정해져 있는데, 그…
en: Forty-one, Majesty. If the two born this spring are counted.
…And each of them will need a chair, one day. There are only so many chairs, and—
Thirty-four.
I counted the chairs.

lines: 그럼 자리를 더 만들지. 아니면 몇 개 비우든가.
en: Then we’ll build more chairs. Or empty some.
Pung! Where’s Pung?

blocks.html: Prince Pung stands. He is seventeen. He is the quiet one, the one with the good handwriting, and he already knows what is coming because his mother told him the night before, crying into his collar.
blocks.ko: 풍 왕자가 일어선다. 열일곱 살이다. 말수 적고 글씨 잘 쓰는 아들. 무슨 말이 나올지 그는 이미 안다. 어젯밤 어머니가 그의 옷깃에 얼굴을 묻고 울면서 말해 주었으니까.

blocks.caption: The quiet prince with the good handwriting. He is about to learn what a hostage is for.
blocks.ko: 글씨 잘 쓰는 조용한 왕자. 볼모가 무엇에 쓰이는지 곧 배운다.

lines: 바다 건너 섬나라 임금이 백제 왕자를 제 조정에 두고 싶어 한다. 우리 둘이 얼마나 가까운지 세상에 보이고 싶은 게지. 네가 가거라.
그쪽 시를 배우고, 그쪽 술을 마셔라. 내가 전쟁까지 치러야 할 여자랑은 혼인하지 말고.
en: The island king across the sea wants a prince of Baekje at his court, to show the world how close we are. You’re going.
Learn their poems. Drink their wine. Don’t marry anyone I’ll have to go to war over.
As Your Majesty commands.
…For how long?

lines: 하! 그런 얼굴 하지 마라. 칭찬이다. 다시 찾을 생각 없는 왕자를 보내는 놈은 없어.
en: Until I need you.
Ha! Don’t look like that. It’s a compliment. Nobody sends a prince he doesn’t mean to want back.

blocks.html: Pung bows and walks the length of the table to the door. It is a long table. At the far end, a man nobody has promoted gets up from his cushion.
blocks.ko: 풍이 절하고 상을 따라 문까지 걸어간다. 긴 상이다. 저 끝에서, 아무도 승진시켜 주지 않은 사내 하나가 방석에서 일어난다.

en: Prince. I still have the wood.
lines: 왕자님. 그 목간, 아직 가지고 있습니다.

en: …You still can’t read it.
No. I know what it says.

blocks.html: One day Baekje will send for him after all. Nobody at the feast would have believed it, Pung least of all.
blocks.ko: 언젠가 백제는 결국 그를 부르러 사람을 보낸다. 잔치에 있던 누구도 믿지 않았을 것이다. 풍 자신이 가장.

blocks.label: The royal stables · that night
blocks.ko: 왕실 마구간 · 그날 밤

blocks.html: That night the promotions go up on the palace gate. Gyebek cannot read them. He holds Pung’s old strip of wood up beside the list and checks every name, shape by shape. None of them match.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 궁문에 승진 명단이 붙는다. 계백은 읽지 못한다. 그는 풍이 써 준 낡은 목간을 명단 옆에 대고, 이름을 하나하나 획의 모양으로 맞춰 본다. 맞는 것이 없다.

blocks.html: A groom finds him there. The king wants him at the stables. Now. It is the king’s favourite word.
blocks.ko: 마부 하나가 그를 찾아온다. 임금께서 마구간으로 부르신다. 지금 당장. 임금이 제일 좋아하는 말이다.

blocks.html: The king is standing in the straw in his coronation silk, holding the halter of a black horse that will not keep still. It is tall and long in the back, black from nose to tail, and it looks at Gyebek the way Gyebek looks at everyone: straight, and without manners.
blocks.ko: 임금은 즉위식 비단옷 차림으로 짚더미 위에 서서, 가만있지 않는 검은 말의 고삐를 쥐고 있다. 키가 크고 등이 길며, 코부터 꼬리까지 까맣다. 말은 계백이 누구에게나 그러듯 계백을 본다. 똑바로, 예의 없이.

en: There you are! They passed you over again. The houses wrote the list and I signed it. Don’t look at me like that.
lines: 왔구먼! 또 밀렸더구먼. 가문들이 쓰구 과인이 서명혔다. 그런 눈으로 보지 마라.

en: I am not looking at you like anything.
Ha! No. You never do.
So. Here. The fastest horse in Samhan. Bred at the bear ferry, at Gomanaru. My grooms swear nothing on four legs can catch him.
They also swear the rock sweats.
lines: 그래서. 옜다. 삼한에서 제일 빠른 말이여. 곰나루에서 난 놈이구. 네 발 달린 것 중엔 저놈을 따라잡을 게 없다고 마부들이 맹세허더라.

en: Then I will time him.
What do I owe for him.
Nothing. It’s a gift.
I do not know what to do with a gift.
You ride it. That’s the whole trick.
On the mud I said the last inch. You can’t get there on foot. Not on an army nag either, the way you sit one, like a sack of rice somebody’s angry at.
lines: 그 뻘밭에서 끝의 끝까지라 혔지. 걸어서는 못 가. 군마루두 못 가. 네가 그거 타는 꼴이, 누가 화나서 던져 놓은 쌀가마니 같더라.

blocks.html: Gyebek says nothing. In his whole life he has been given exactly two things he did not have to pay back. Both came from this man.
blocks.ko: 계백은 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 평생 갚지 않아도 되는 것을 받아 본 게 꼭 두 번이다. 둘 다 이 사람에게서였다.

blocks.html: He puts out his hand. The horse considers biting it, and doesn’t. Gyebek leans in and rests his forehead against the black neck. His lips move. He is counting to ten.
blocks.ko: 그가 손을 내민다. 말은 물까 말까 하다가 물지 않는다. 계백은 몸을 기울여 검은 목덜미에 이마를 댄다. 입술이 움직인다. 열까지 세는 중이다.

en: What are you counting?
Until I can talk.

blocks.html: Euija looks very hard at a saddle on the wall until he can, too.
blocks.ko: 의자는 벽에 걸린 안장을 뚫어지게 본다. 저도 말할 수 있을 때까지.

en: Well? Name him. He came up from the ferry with no name, same as somebody I know.
lines: 그래서? 이름을 지어 줘. 나루서 이름두 없이 올라왔어. 내가 아는 누구처럼.

en: Gomanari. For the ferry.
That’s not a name, that’s a signpost.
It is where he is from. A name should say where you are from.
Mine does not.
lines: 거기서 왔으니까요. 이름은 어디서 왔는지 말해 줘야 합니다.

en: …Yours says where you’re going.
Ride him to the ferry and back tomorrow. Learn on him. And then time him, you lunatic.
lines: 내일 저놈 타구 나루까지 갔다 와. 저놈한테 배워. 그리구 재 봐라, 이 미친놈아.

blocks.html: Euija can fake a dragon. He can’t fake a fortress. For that he needs a general who does exactly what he says…!
blocks.ko: 의자는 용을 지어낼 수 있다. 성은 지어낼 수 없다. 그러려면 말한 대로만 하는 장수가 하나 필요하다…!

logline.en: There was only one man Euija knew he could trust to deliver.
logline.ko: 의자가 믿고 맡길 수 있는 사람은 단 한 명뿐이었다.

images.alt: Worm’s-eye: crowned Euija mid-cut on his own forearm — hard red blood-line, empty Sabi hall
images.at: Your Majesty. Does that mean you will not use me, or tha
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 still. WORM’S-EYE dutch: crowned King Euija mid-cut on his own forearm before an empty REAL Sabi court hall — timber from attached palace. FACE from attached portrait — fierce will, NEW kinetic body. ONE device: a hard red #C30000 blood-line on pale silk forearm as the only accent plane. Crushed blacks, empty hall. No army. No court crowd dump. No text. No watermark. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock: anamorphic movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain. A CAMERA in a real Korean place — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D archviz, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow, rim-aura, or god-ray envelope around people — light is a plane or a hard key. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portrait — NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: dutch, crane, worm’s-eye, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key + long shadows — not even daylight wash. ICONIC MINIMAL: ONE architectural device a lens can see; empty negative space; tiny figures or lower-third; the world stays in the shot. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex is lighting / a plane / one accent — NEVER recolor portrait garments gold. Real Korean architecture: grey giwa, timber, packed earth. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: movie frame in a real place, not a graphic poster; iconic one-device layout, empty frame, lower-third; high contrast chiaroscuro, not even wash; 2D animated cel-painterly, no photoreal; cinematography: dutch, wide, bokeh, mise-en-scène. Never: halo / bloom / glow around figures; graphic split-screen or black-triangle overlay; photoreal live-action or 3D archviz; busy extras crowding an iconic frame; copy-pasted reference as a fashion plate; flat even-daylight postcard wide.

images.alt: King Euija shoves the good cushion across the floor to General Yunchung, who has not yet decided to sit
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, interior at night = old-master tenebrist canvas. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. The king’s winter chamber in the Sabi palace: dark timber pillars, plank floor, a low lacquered table, one bronze brazier. Low two-shot across the floor, worm’s-eye from beside the brazier set on the planks: King Euija leaning forward on one knee with a grin, shoving a thick embroidered silk cushion across the boards with one hand; General Yunchung standing stiff in his lamellar on the other side of the frame, helm tucked under one arm, looking down at the cushion as if it were a trap. The brazier between them is the one warm key, raking up across the king’s crimson silk and the grey plates; their shadows climb the pillars at an angle. Device: the cushion sliding across the empty floor between them. CANON — KING EUIJA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_king_euija.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Broad, bearded king; black hair in a topknot with a yellow-gold headband whose tails trail; heavy brows, cynical eyes. Dress: Crimson robe with a dark charcoal collar and gold trim; a steel lamellar pauldron peeking at one shoulder. Crown: Baekje king, as the attached crown (ignore its studio backdrop and logo): a tall rounded black silk cap (오라관) with a plain black band at the brow, and a pair of tall openwork gold flame-and-leaf ornaments (금제관식) pinned to either side of the cap, rising above it like twin flames — thin gold blades fanning upward with leaf buds and curls; the king’s red robe and wide-sleeved layers as the Baekje king on the costume chart. Demeanor: Licensed wit: drinks, smirks, slumps on the throne, speaks in polished aphorisms. Fatalist. #e08a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: heroic battle pose; smiling innocence. | YUNCHUNG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yunchung.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Hard-bitten Baekje frontier general in his forties: full black beard, heavy scowling brows, a band of red war-paint smeared across both eyes, long black hair falling from under a dented round steel helm with a cracked crown and a short red-black plume knob. Dress: Grey steel lamellar with red-edged shoulder guards over an ochre-yellow robe, a broad red sash with a round bronze boss, red-and-black striped bracers; a ring-pommel sword in a red-lacquered scabbard. Demeanor: Plain speech is also a weapon: says the ugly thing without a cushion under it, and does exactly what he says he will. #c9932a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: There was only one man Euija knew he could trust to deliver.
blocks.ko: 의자가 믿고 맡길 수 있는 사람은 단 한 명뿐이었다.

blocks.html: That winter Euija sends for Yunchung, and nobody from the eight houses is told. Yunchung is a general from a family too small to keep a clan tutor. He has held the Silla frontier for eleven years by doing exactly what he says he will do, which the Assembly finds tiring.
blocks.ko: 그해 겨울 의자는 윤충을 부르고, 여덟 가문 누구에게도 알리지 않는다. 윤충은 가문 스승을 둘 만큼 크지 않은 집안의 장수다. 그는 열한 해 동안 신라 국경을 지켰다. 하겠다고 한 일을 꼭 그대로 해서인데, 대신회의는 그게 피곤하다.

blocks.caption: A frontier general from a family too small to count. That is the point.
blocks.ko: 셈에도 안 들 만큼 작은 집안의 변방 장수. 바로 그게 요점이다.

lines: 앉게, 장군. 아니, 그 좋은 방석 말여. 내 맘 바뀌기 전에 깔고 앉으라니께.
en: Sit, General. No, the good cushion. Take it before I change my mind.
Tell me. Who rules Baekje?
Your Majesty does.
On paper.
Ha! And off paper?

lines: 문서 밖에서는 바위가 다스립니다. 그리고 그 바위에 소금물 바르는 자들이요.
여덟 가문이 좌평을 고르고, 좌평이 대신들을 고르고, 대신들이 제게 군량을 늦게 보냅니다. 제 군사들 녹은 그쪽이 주니, 군사들도 압니다.
en: Off paper, the Rock does. And whoever rubs the brine on it.
The eight houses pick the Prime Minister, the Prime Minister picks the ministers, and the ministers send me the grain late. They pay my men. My men know it.

lines: 그려. 왕이 안에서 피 안 보구 바위한테서 나라를 도로 찾으려면 워찌해야 허나?
en: So. How does a king get his country back off the Rock without a war at home?

lines: 성을 하나 빼앗은 왕은 그 성을 빼앗은 군사들을 갖습니다. 가문들은 승리를 두고 표결할 수 없습니다. 잔치에 얼굴이나 내밀 수 있지요.
en: With a war abroad, Majesty.
A king who wins a fortress owns the men who took it. The clans can’t vote on a victory. They can only show up to the feast.

lines: 거 참 말 한번 시원허게 허네.
나는 험한 말을 방석두 안 깔고 허는 사람이 좋아. 제가 내 방석에 앉아 있어두 말여.
en: Plainly put.
I do like a man who says the ugly thing without a cushion under it. Even when he’s sitting on mine.

blocks.html: It is the first time in the reign that Euija says what he has decided before the Assembly hears it. By spring the Assembly will hear it anyway, in the form of a question he has already answered.
blocks.ko: 의자가 대신회의보다 먼저 제 결정을 입 밖에 낸 것은 이 치세에서 처음이다. 봄이면 대신회의도 결국 듣게 된다. 그가 이미 답을 정해 둔 질문의 모양으로.

blocks.label: The Assembly
blocks.ko: 정사암 회의

blocks.html: By spring the Assembly is fighting about harbours, as it always is. Gyebek sits through three sessions. He understands every number and none of the smiles.
blocks.ko: 봄이 되자 정사암 회의는 늘 그렇듯 항구 문제로 싸운다. 계백은 세 번의 회의를 끝까지 앉아 있는다. 숫자는 다 알아듣고, 웃음은 하나도 못 알아듣는다.

en: Enough.
You can count berths when the frontier is settled.
Until then, the Eraha counts fortresses.

blocks.html: Euija has already decided. Now the clans have to believe it was their idea.
blocks.ko: 의자는 이미 정했다. 이제 가문들이 그게 제 생각이었다고 믿게만 하면 된다.

blocks.caption: A young Satek with good manners and a quick eye for an opening.
blocks.ko: 예의 바르고, 빈틈을 빨리 보는 젊은 사택.

en: As Your Majesty well knows,
the will of the Rock is the will of Heaven.
The eight houses decide it together.

lines: 하늘…? 아, 그 안 보이는 위원회.
en: Heaven…? Ah — the invisible committee.
Restore the reign of the thirteenth Eraha…!
The thirteenth Eraha…! Ten thousand years!

lines: 우리가 왜 백제 사람이고 고구려나 신라 사람이 아니냐? 생긴 건 똑같은데.
백제 땅 어디를 가도 시조는 다 안다.
en: Do you know what a country is?
A country is a territory governed by a single story.
Why are we Baekje people, and not Goguryeo or Silla people? We look exactly the same.
Anywhere in Baekje, everyone knows the founders.
Speak of King Onjo — that is Baekje.
So the king makes the story.
Let us make an interesting one…!
Goguryeo is too large to move.
Silla is too old to surprise anybody.

lines: 지금 신라왕은 군대를 통솔하지 못하는 여인이며,
그 나라 안에서도 민심이 확실치 않은 것으로 압니다.
이 틈을 타 신라 변방의 성을 치신다면, 대업을 이루시기 어렵지 않을 것입니다.
en: The present king of Silla is a woman who cannot command an army,
and even within her country, the people’s hearts are unsettled.
Seize this opening, take a border fortress, and the great work will be within reach.

lines: 폐하. 왕자님들께 이런 나라를 물려주실 셈입니까?
en: Your Majesty — is this the country you mean to hand the princes?

blocks.html: The man who asked is Sunchung, Yunchung’s elder brother. At home the two of them argue about everything. In the hall they have never once disagreed in public. Until today.
blocks.ko: 물은 사람은 성충, 윤충의 형이다. 집에서 둘은 모든 걸 두고 다툰다. 전각에서는 한 번도 남들 앞에서 맞선 적이 없다. 오늘까지는.

blocks.html: Gyebek steps forward. Nobody asked him to.
blocks.ko: 계백이 앞으로 나선다. 아무도 시키지 않았다.

lines: 닭 잡는 데 소 잡는 칼을 쓰겠느냐?
en: No, Gyebek… not you.
Why use an ox-cleaver to kill a chicken?

lines: 폐하. 그건 저를 쓰지 않겠다는 뜻입니까, 아끼겠다는 뜻입니까?
en: Your Majesty. Does that mean you will not use me, or that you are saving me?
…It means I am saving you.

lines: 그러면 그렇게 말씀해 주십시오. 저는 비유를 못 알아듣습니다.
en: Then say that. I do not follow figures of speech.

blocks.html: The Assembly finds him rude, which misses the point by a courtyard’s width. All he wants — every single time — is the sentence handed over with nothing folded inside it, and nobody at that court has spoken that way in their lives.
blocks.ko: 회의는 그를 무례하다 여기지만, 그것은 마당 하나쯤 빗나간 판단이다. 그가 바라는 것은 매번 하나뿐이다 — 안에 아무것도 접혀 있지 않은 문장을 그대로 건네받는 것. 그런데 그 조정의 누구도 평생 그렇게 말해 본 적이 없다.

en: A border fortress…
That too is good.
I have one in mind.

lines: 사실… 이 나라 사람들에게는 새 이야기가 필요하다.
en: In truth… the people of this country need a new story.
They have lived in the old one long enough.

lines: 삼한에서 우리가 제일 컸던 때가 있다.
열셋째. 군대를 이끌고 평양 한복판까지 들어갔지.
그 뒤로 백제는 한 조각이 되었다. 이름은 남고, 몸집은 빠지고.
그런데 하늘이, 늘 그렇듯 친절하게, 표식을 보내더군. 우리를 구할 새 임금이라고.
en: There was a time we were the greatest power in Samhan.
The thirteenth. He led armies into the heart of Pyongyang.
Then came the Severing.
After that, Baekje was a fraction. The name stayed. The size did not.
And then heaven, helpful as always, sent signs. A new king, meant to save us.
The thirty-first. Great King Euija.

blocks.caption: The thirteenth’s Baekje, and what is left of it.
blocks.ko: 열세 번째 어라하의 백제, 그리고 남은 것.

en: What is the Severing.
You said you do not follow figures of speech.
This is not one. It is the Severing.
Today we only have to tell it.
Baekje… is in crisis!
Then we make the crisis.
We take back the Silla frontier.

blocks.caption: Daeya. The last wall between Baekje and the Silla capital.
blocks.ko: 대야성. 백제와 신라 도성 사이의 마지막 성벽.

blocks.html: You’ve been to Daeya. You waved a cart into it.
blocks.ko: 대야에는 당신도 가 봤다. 수레 한 대를 손 흔들어 들여보냈다.

en: Then Silla’s finished at Daeya. Plain and simple.

lines: 하! 그럼 가서 끝장을 보게, 장군. 군사 만이야.
en: Ha! Then go and finish it, General. Ten thousand men.
Bring me back the fortress. And a story to go with it.
Daeya by autumn, Majesty.

blocks.html: The hall empties. Gyebek does not.
blocks.ko: 회의장이 빈다. 계백은 남는다.

en: Majesty. You are saving me. For what.
lines: 전하. 저를 아끼신다 하셨습니다. 무엇에 쓰시려고입니까.

en: Ha! For the day I need a man I can’t buy, and the houses have bought everybody else.
lines: 하! 내가 살 수 없는 사내가 필요헌 날을 위해서여. 가문들이 딴 놈은 죄다 사 버린 날.

en: How will I know the day.
I’ll send for you.
Then I will wait.

lines: 비유가 아니라 하셨습니다. 그럼 사실입니다. 저는 그 사실을 모릅니다.
왜 진군하느냐고 병사들이 물을 것입니다. 사실로 답하고 싶습니다.
en: And the Severing.
You said it is not a figure of speech. Then it is a fact. I do not know it.
Men will ask me why we march. I want to answer with a fact.

lines: 하! 전쟁을 허면서 장부까지 달라는 놈은 첨 보는구먼.
사비 아무 할미한테나 물어봐. 나보다 잘 얘기혀. 나는 용을 보태서 탈이지.
en: Ha! A man who wants his war with the ledger attached.
Ask any grandmother in Sabi. They tell it better than I do. I add dragons.

blocks.html: “What is the Severing?” Gyebek asked. Any grandmother in Sabi could tell him. We’ll go back a hundred years and see for ourselves…!
blocks.ko: “斷이 뭡니까.” 계백이 물었다. 사비의 할머니라면 누구나 말해 줄 수 있다. 우리는 백 년을 거슬러 가서 직접 보자…!

logline.en: The sad thing about betrayal… is that it never comes from your enemies.
logline.ko: 배신이 슬픈 건… 그게 절대 적에게서 오지 않는다는 거다.

ICONIC MINIMAL LAYOUT: the only light areas are a thin pale strip of road running across the lower third and a faint grey ridge line near the top. On the road, left of centre, a tiny tight cluster of about fifty ink riders reined in, horses rearing, a single small royal parasol among them; nobody’s face readable. Heavy empty darkness everywhere else, dread, stillness. One blank red seal square. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. blocks.html: The sad thing about betrayal… is that it never comes from your enemies.
blocks.ko: 배신이 슬픈 건… 그게 절대 적에게서 오지 않는다는 거다.

blocks.html: Gyebek finds the chestnut seller at the west gate of Sabi. She is not his grandmother. She is everybody’s, and she has waited her whole life for a soldier to ask.
blocks.ko: 계백은 사비 서문에서 군밤 파는 할미를 찾아낸다. 그의 할미는 아니다. 사비 모두의 할미다. 그리고 군인 하나가 이걸 물어 주기를 평생 기다려 왔다.

lines: 전하께서 아무 할머니나 이야기해 줄 수 있다 하셨습니다.
en: What is the Severing.
His Majesty said any grandmother could tell it.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 아무 할미나? 흥. 앉어 봐. 밤 하나 먹구. 진군허기엔 너무 말랐어.
강에서 시작혀. 그리구 친구. 이런 얘긴 늘 친구루 시작허지.
en: Any grandmother? Hmph. Sit, then. Eat a chestnut. You’re mighty thin for marching.
It starts with a river, and a friend. They always start with a friend.
How long ago.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 백 년. 소식이 왔을 때 우리 할미의 할미가 이 문에서 밤을 팔았지.
온 성안이 눈 온 것처럼 조용해졌댜. 그날 하루 종일 아무두 아무것두 안 샀댜.
en: A hundred years. My grandmother’s grandmother sold chestnuts at this gate when the news came.
She said the whole city went quiet, like snow. Nobody bought a thing all day.

blocks.hanja: 斷
blocks.html: For a hundred and twenty years Baekje and Silla kept one rule: when Goguryeo comes south, we stand together. Baekje calls the day that rule broke the Severing. Silla doesn’t call it anything. Winners rarely name things.
blocks.ko: 백이십 년 동안 백제와 신라에게는 규칙이 하나 있었다. 고구려가 내려오면 함께 막는다. 백제는 그 규칙이 깨진 날을 단(斷)이라 부른다. 신라는 아무 이름도 붙이지 않는다. 이긴 쪽은 좀처럼 이름을 붙이지 않는다.

blocks.caption: Two kings took the river together. One of them kept it.
blocks.ko: 두 임금이 강을 함께 되찾았다. 한 사람이 그것을 가졌다.

blocks.html: Two kings take a river back together: Sung of Baekje and the Cloud King of Silla. For a while their banners fly side by side. Then the Cloud King turns his army on Baekje’s half. He takes the river mouth and fills it with men who won’t ask what the alliance meant.
blocks.ko: 두 임금이 함께 강을 되찾는다. 백제의 성왕과 신라의 구름왕. 한동안 두 나라 깃발은 나란히 나부낀다. 그러다 구름왕이 백제 몫으로 군대를 돌린다. 하류를 빼앗고, 동맹이 무엇이었는지 묻지 않을 사람들로 그곳을 채운다.

blocks.html: King Sung feels the cut in the marrow. He calls in everyone who still owes him: the last Gaya houses, a boatload of soldiers from the islands. Then he marches east, on the fortress that opens Silla’s throat.
blocks.ko: 성왕은 그 칼날을 골수로 느낀다. 아직 그에게 빚진 이들을 모두 불러 모은다. 가야의 남은 집안들, 섬나라에서 건너온 군사들. 그리고 동쪽으로, 신라의 목을 여는 성으로 진군한다.

blocks.caption: Baekje’s king. He has lost a river, and he means to get it back.
blocks.ko: 백제의 임금. 강 하나를 잃었고, 되찾을 작정이다.

blocks.html: Every road into Silla’s valley squeezes through here.
blocks.ko: 신라 골짜기로 드는 길은 모두 여기서 좁아진다.

en: How many.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 다. 빚진 집은 다 아들을 보냈어. 그 행렬이 이 문 지나가는 데 아침나절이 다 걸렸댜.
en: All of them. Every house that owed him sent its sons. The column took a whole morning to pass this gate.

blocks.html: For months the fight goes Baekje’s way. The garrison keeps trying its gate and keeps getting shoved back inside. The crown prince holds the forward camp below the wall, half-starved; his men are boiling their saddle leather.
blocks.ko: 몇 달 동안 싸움은 백제 쪽으로 기운다. 수비군은 자꾸 성문을 나서고, 자꾸 도로 밀려 들어간다. 태자는 성벽 아래 앞 진영에서 굶주리며 버틴다. 군사들은 안장 가죽을 삶아 먹는다.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 이기구 있었다니께. 그해 내내 사비는 이기고 있었어.
우리 할미의 할미가 밤을 두 배루 팔았댜. 수레 지나갈 때 다들 뭐 따뜻한 거 하나씩 쥐고 흔들고 싶어 했거든.
en: Winning, see. All that year Sabi was winning.
My grandmother’s grandmother sold twice the chestnuts. Everybody wanted something warm in their hand to wave at the carts.

blocks.html: Nobody in the forward camp is watching the north road. Down it comes a second Silla army, out of the new lands on the river. Part of it leaves the road, goes into the hills, and swings south and then west, around behind the prince.
blocks.ko: 앞 진영에서 북쪽 길을 보는 사람은 아무도 없다. 그 길로 신라군이 하나 더 내려온다. 강가에 새로 얻은 땅에서. 그중 일부가 길을 벗어나 산으로 들어가더니, 남쪽으로, 다시 서쪽으로 돌아 태자의 등 뒤로 간다.

en: Behind him.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 등 뒤로. 태자는 내내 성벽만 보구 있었지. 시방 네가 나 보듯이.
en: Behind him. And the prince was looking at the wall the whole time. The way you’re looking at me.

blocks.label: The Night Road
blocks.ko: 밤길

blocks.html: One night King Sung rides out from the west with fifty horse to steady his son. Silla’s ambush is waiting. The road to the prince is a ditch that was not there at dusk. Fifty horse stop, because the torches coming up the bank are the wrong color.
blocks.ko: 어느 밤, 성왕이 아들을 다독이러 기병 쉰을 이끌고 서쪽에서 달려온다. 신라의 복병이 기다린다. 태자에게 가는 길은, 해 질 녘에는 없던 도랑이다. 보기 오십이 멈춘다. 둑으로 올라오는 횃불이 틀린 색이어서.

blocks.html: On the ridge, the Cloud King’s hand drops. That is the signal. He has already said the rest, low, to the only man the rank will allow to finish it.
blocks.ko: 능선 위에서 구름왕의 손이 떨어진다. 그것이 신호다. 나머지는 이미 낮게, 골품이 끝을 허락할 단 한 사람에게 말해 두었다.

blocks.html: Beside the king stands his younger brother, Suulbu, nineteen, who has never watched a king die and would like a better view. He looks down at the general in the ditch and decides, for reasons he will spend forty years polishing, that he does not like him.
blocks.ko: 왕 곁에는 아우 수을부가 서 있다. 열아홉, 임금이 죽는 걸 본 적이 없어서 더 잘 보이는 자리를 원한다. 그는 도랑 속 장수를 내려다보고, 앞으로 사십 년 동안 다듬게 될 이유로, 그 사내가 싫다고 정한다.

lines: 종이 베는 기다. 뒷사람이 입에서 못 잊게.
en: You. A slave.
He is a lord with a name.
A slave does the cutting. So later mouths cannot forget it.

blocks.html: A Silla general is already down in the cut. His tall helm cuts the night ridge. He does not draw. He watches.
blocks.ko: 신라 장수 하나가 이미 패인 길 아래에 있다. 그의 높은 투구가 밤 능선을 가른다. 그는 칼을 뽑지 않는다. 지켜본다.

lines: 신라 장수가— 이 길에, 오늘 밤. 어찌 그대가.
en: Silla…?
A general of Silla— on this road, tonight. Why you.
Military governor of Sinju.
Sit.

blocks.html: They sit him on a camp stool. Out of the helm’s shadow a man kneels twice, the way you kneel to a king, and asks.
blocks.ko: 그를 호상 위에 앉힌다. 투구의 그림자에서 한 사내가 두 번 무릎을 꿇는다. 임금에게 꿇듯. 그리고 청한다.

blocks.caption: A slave in the Silla camp. Remember the name; the annals almost didn’t.
blocks.ko: 신라 진영의 노비. 이름을 기억해 두라. 사서는 하마터면 잊을 뻔했다.

en: …I’m asking.
Let me take the head.

lines: 종의 손이— 안 돼. 왕의 머리는 종의 손을 안 받아.
en: What.
A slave’s hand— no. A king’s head does not take a slave’s hand.

lines: 왕이라도… 받는다 카데요. 지는, 그래 들었심더.
en: If you broke the oath.
Even a king… takes it. I was told.

blocks.html: Which oath, and whose, nobody on the ridge asks.
blocks.ko: 어느 맹세를, 누가 깼는지. 능선 위에서 그걸 묻는 사람은 없다.

en: Dodo.
Every time I think of it…
It went into the marrow.
I cannot live on in disgrace.

blocks.html: He looks up. The breath that leaves him is not another sentence. He unfastens his own knife, gives it to the kneeling man, and puts his neck out.
blocks.ko: 그가 올려다본다. 빠져나가는 숨은 다음 문장이 아니다. 제 칼을 풀어 꿇은 사내의 손에 주고, 목을 내민다.

blocks.html: The ditch takes the head. Dodo does the work the rank will not put on a general’s hands. The record almost forgets the slave.
blocks.ko: 도랑이 목을 가져간다. 도도가, 골품이 장수의 손에 올리지 않을 일을 한다. 기록은 노비를 거의 잊는다.

blocks.html: By dawn the news is at the fortress. Thirty thousand men hear it at once. Silla comes down the north road and up out of the ditch together, and the ring around the wall comes apart. The prince gets out west, behind the island archers.
blocks.ko: 새벽이 되자 소식이 성에 닿는다. 삼만이 한꺼번에 듣는다. 신라가 북쪽 길로 내려오고 도랑에서 올라와 한꺼번에 덮치자, 성을 두른 고리가 풀린다. 태자는 섬나라 궁수들 뒤에 숨어 서쪽으로 빠져나간다.

blocks.html: The chestnuts have gone cold. Gyebek has not eaten his.
blocks.ko: 군밤이 식었다. 계백은 제 몫을 먹지 않았다.

en: How many came home.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 태자. 섬사람 몇. 말은 묻지두 말어.
en: The prince. A few islanders. Don’t ask me about the horses.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 그게 斷이여. 신라는 그 해골을 계단 밑에 두구 아침마다 밟고 다녀.
en: That’s the Severing. Silla keeps his skull under a staircase and walks on it every morning.
So. Now I reckon you know why you march.

lines: 맹세를 깬 건 신라입니다. 종은 성왕이 깼다고 했습니다.
en: That is a fact. Thank you.
Silla broke the oath. The slave said Sung did.
I will remember which.

blocks.speaker: A Sabi grandmother
lines: 어느 쪽인지 기억혀. 다들 그 걸상만 기억허더라.
en: Remember which. Most people only remember the stool.

blocks.html: A hundred years on, Baekje has not forgiven the cloud that emptied itself over its side of the river. The grandmothers tell it with chestnuts. Euija tells it with dragons. Either way, ten thousand men are about to march on it.
blocks.ko: 백 년이 지나도 백제는 강 건너 제 쪽에 비를 다 쏟아 버린 그 구름을 용서하지 않았다. 할미들은 군밤을 까며 이야기하고, 의자는 용을 띄워 이야기한다. 어느 쪽이든, 이제 만 명이 그 이야기를 들고 진군한다.

blocks.html: Ten thousand Baekje men march on Daeya. Its grain clerk is called Gumil. Remember that name…!
blocks.ko: 백제군 만 명이 대야성으로 향한다. 그 성의 곳간지기 이름은 검일. 기억해 두라…!

toneNote: The year everything hardens: coup-thriller nights, a tragedy played sincerely, and steam-cavern respites between them.
title: Iron Will

logline.en: In Silla, bone decides how high a man can climb. Gumil has climbed exactly that high.
logline.ko: 신라에서는 뼈가 사내가 오를 수 있는 높이를 정한다. 검일은 딱 그만큼 올랐다.

Intimate emotional comfort - one head resting on bare shoulder, protective arms wrapped around exposed back and waist, robes loosened revealing shoulders and collarbones, bodies pressed together, gentle caress on bare shoulder and neck - physical closeness during vulnerability, comfort and connection
Daeya Fortress on its hill in daylight, the river wrapping three sides of it, white haze over the valley.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Wide establishing shot from a low riverbank, bright clear morning. Daeya Fortress on its hill: weathered stone walls with crenellations following the ridge, a curved giwa munru pavilion over the arched north gate, timber storehouse roofs inside the ring, blue Silla banners with a white crescent stirring on the towers. The Hwang river curls around three sides of the hill. Sharp foreground: reeds and a moored flat boat. Tiny figures of porters on the road. Pale white sky and river mist dissolving into bare paper at the edges; one hard low sun from the left carving the wall's stones; the frame is calm and quiet before anything happens. PLACE Daeya (대야성 (합천)) — attached board /pl_daeya_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Daeya seongmun: weathered stone wall with crenellations, curved giwa pavilion over a hongye arch, heavy iron-bossed timber doors. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.

images.alt: Gumil counts rice for a living. None of it has ever been his.
images.prompt: OPENING STILL of the episode: the first image the reader sees, staging its first line. The line: “Gumil counts rice for a living. None of it has ever been his.” Context: Gumil counts rice for a living. None of it has ever been his.   A wide or medium establishing frame that hooks. CANON — GUMIL — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gumil.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Thirties, lean border officer, stubble and a thin moustache, orange-red head-wrap with trailing tails, tired angry eyes. Dress: Rust-red border-officer coat over dark trousers, navy sash, leather bracers, a plain sword at the hip (portrait-true). Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Demeanor: Grumbling, humiliated, counting: a yellow-sleeve clerk who knows every sack in the granary. #6b7f9e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | PLACE Daeya (대야성 (합천)) — attached board /pl_daeya_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Daeya seongmun: weathered stone wall with crenellations, curved giwa pavilion over a hongye arch, heavy iron-bossed timber doors. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). COMMONERS in every Samhan kingdom wear SIMPLE WHITE: plain undyed white or off-white hemp and ramie jackets, wide trousers and skirts, a cloth sash, straw sandals or bare feet, hair in a plain topknot or braid — no dyed silk, no dots, no gold; colour belongs to rank, so a crowd of farmers, porters, servants and townsfolk reads as a field of soft white cloth with the officials' colours standing out of it. Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. images.prompt: CLOSING STILL of the episode: the final scene of this story as it ends (not the next episode). The line: “She knows his body the way a person knows a door they have opened every winter. He says her name at the end, not a rank. They sleep facing the same wall. In the morning the silk goes back on as if the night had been ordinary. It never is.” Context: They stop talking. The lamp is too small for manners. The red sash comes off the way it always does in this room, one impatient pull, and the old silk follows it onto the boards. Thirty-one, and she still puts him where she wants him. Tomorrow can wait. Tonight you stay under me. Don’t use a name. / Just… stay. She knows his body the way a person knows a door they have opened every winter. He says her name at the end, not a rank. They sleep facing the same wall. In the morning the silk goes back on as if the night had been ordinary. It never is. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — PLACE Daeya (대야성 (합천)) — attached board /pl_daeya_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Daeya seongmun: weathered stone wall with crenellations, curved giwa pavilion over a hongye arch, heavy iron-bossed timber doors.
