FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. blocks.html: Gumil counts rice for a living. None of it has ever been his.
blocks.ko: 검일은 쌀을 세어 먹고산다. 그중 제 것이었던 쌀은 한 톨도 없다.

blocks.label: The Tally
blocks.ko: 장부

blocks.label: DAEYA FORTRESS
blocks.ko: 대야성

blocks.html: The last wall between Baekje and the capital, and the granary behind it.
blocks.ko: 백제와 서라벌 사이의 마지막 성벽, 그리고 그 뒤의 곳간.

blocks.html: The granary at Daeya can feed the garrison through a winter siege. Gumil knows the exact number of sacks. He counted them. Every tally he writes goes up the stair to a young man in a purple sleeve, who seals it without reading it.
blocks.ko: 대야성 곳간은 겨울 농성 한 철을 버틸 만큼의 쌀을 품고 있다. 검일은 그 가마니 수를 정확히 안다. 그가 셌으니까. 그가 쓰는 장부는 전부 계단 위, 자줏빛 소매의 젊은이에게 올라간다. 그 젊은이는 읽지도 않고 도장을 찍는다.

blocks.caption: A yellow-sleeve officer. He does the work, and the purple sleeve signs it.
blocks.ko: 누런 소매의 관리. 일은 그가 하고, 서명은 자줏빛 소매가 한다.

blocks.html: In Silla the sleeve tells you everything. Purple is True Bone, the old royal blood. Yellow is a man who will die at the rank he was born to. Nobody has to explain it twice. You can see it from across a yard.
blocks.ko: 신라에서는 소매가 모든 걸 말해 준다. 자주는 진골, 오래된 왕의 피다. 누런 소매는 태어난 그 자리에서 죽을 사람이다. 두 번 설명할 필요도 없다. 마당 건너편에서도 보인다.

blocks.label: The Stair
blocks.ko: 계단

blocks.html: This morning Gumil climbs the stair with the harvest tally and one more sheet under it. The second sheet is his. Four years of border pay, owed and never paid, added up to the last measure.
blocks.ko: 오늘 아침 검일은 추수 장부와, 그 밑에 한 장을 더 끼워 계단을 오른다. 그 한 장은 제 것이다. 사 년 치 변방 녹봉, 받을 것인데 한 번도 못 받은 것을 마지막 한 되까지 더한 것.

blocks.html: Pumsuk is twenty-one. He came in with the first frost, riding beside his wife’s cart, and he holds the fortress because his blood is right and his wife’s father is Chunchu. He is not a bad man. He is just a man who has never had to read the second sheet.
blocks.ko: 품석은 스물하나다. 첫서리와 함께, 아내의 수레 옆에서 말을 타고 들어왔다. 그가 성을 맡은 건 피가 맞고 장인이 춘추이기 때문이다. 나쁜 사람은 아니다. 두 번째 장을 읽어 볼 필요가 한 번도 없었던 사람일 뿐이다.

en: The harvest count. Good.
And this?

lines: 제 녹봉입니더, 성주님. 사 년 치.
서라벌에선 쌀을 보낸다 캅니더. 서라벌하고 지 사이 어데선가 누가 다 묵어 치우고요.
en: My pay, Commander. Four years of it.
The capital sends the rice. Somewhere between the capital and me, it gets eaten.

lines: 그런— 그런 일이 있어선 안 되오. 서라벌에 서신을 쓰겠소.
잔치가 끝나면. 이번 주에 폐하의 인장이 오니, 모든 게 잔치 다음이오.
en: Four years…
I— that should not happen. I will write to Surabol.
After the banquet. The Queen’s seal comes this week, and everything is after the banquet.

blocks.html: He seals the harvest count. He hands the second sheet back, unsealed, with a kind smile. He does not ask Gumil’s name. In five months he has never needed it.
blocks.ko: 그는 추수 장부에 인장을 찍는다. 두 번째 장은 인장 없이, 다정한 미소와 함께 돌려준다. 검일의 이름은 묻지 않는다. 다섯 달 동안 한 번도 필요 없었다.

blocks.label: The Granary
blocks.ko: 곳간

blocks.html: Down in the granary Mochuk is waiting. He is yellow too: same rank, same pay, same four years. He reads Gumil’s face before Gumil sits.
blocks.ko: 곳간 아래에서 모척이 기다리고 있다. 그도 누런 소매다. 같은 품계, 같은 녹봉, 같은 사 년. 검일이 앉기도 전에 얼굴부터 읽는다.

en: After the feast?

lines: 아니, 이런 귀에 피도 안 마른 놈을 국경에 앉히는 기 말이 되나?
en: After the feast.
Putting a boy this green in charge of the border — does that make any sense?

lines: 저쪽은 말이 된다 카지. 그기 문제다.
en: Keep your voice down.
It makes sense to them. That’s the whole trouble.

lines: 아, 여기가 무슨 나란지 까뭇나? 우린 결국 흙만도 못한 것들이라~
진골이라 카믄 하늘이 알아서 쫙 열리는 그런 나라 아이가~~
en: Ah, forgotten what country this is? To them we’re not even dirt~
Say “True Bone” and the heavens part on their own~~

lines: 아니~~ 내는 또 와 이런 망할 나라에 태어나가 이 고생을 하고 있노!!
en: Why was I even born in this wretched country, to suffer like this!!

blocks.html: Silla uses men by bone rank. If you are not of the right lineage, then however great your talent and however outstanding your deeds, you cannot rise past it.
blocks.ko: 신라는 사람을 쓸 때 골품을 따지니, 그 족속이 아니면 비록 큰 재주와 뛰어난 공이 있어도 넘어설 수 없다.
blocks.hanja: 新羅用人論骨品，苟非其族，雖有鴻才傑功，不能踰越。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 47, Biographies — Seol Gyedu (621)

lines: 자네 마누라도 똑같은 소리 하더만. 더 예쁘게.
en: Your wife says the same thing. Prettier.

lines: 잔치에 입을 새 저고리가 갖고 싶다 카대. 비단으로. 초록으로. 그라마 했다.
en: My wife says a lot of things.
She wants a new jeogori for the feast. Silk. Green. I said yes.
…With what, I didn’t say.

blocks.label: Maehwa
blocks.ko: 매화

blocks.label: Home
blocks.ko: 집

blocks.html: Maehwa is the poorest woman in Daeya and the one every eye in it finds first. She is thirty-one. She stopped pretending not to know what happens to a room when she walks into it a long time ago, and the fortress has never forgiven her for it.
blocks.ko: 매화는 대야에서 가장 가난한 여자이고, 성 안의 모든 눈이 가장 먼저 찾는 여자다. 서른하나. 자기가 들어서면 방이 어떻게 되는지 모르는 척하기를 그만둔 지 오래고, 이 성은 그것을 한 번도 용서한 적이 없다.

blocks.caption: Maehwa. Plum blossom: the flower that does not wait for spring.
blocks.ko: 매화. 봄을 기다리지 않는 꽃.

lines: 이 성에 있는 사내들 말이다. 다 똑같은 냄새가 난다. / 흙이랑 술이랑… 그라고 자꾸만 곁눈질하는 냄새.
en: The men in this fortress. They all smell the same. / Dirt, drink… and looking when they think I won’t notice.
Cover yourself when you go out.

lines: 옷을 사 주시든가요. / 있는 기라곤 몸에 안 맞는 것뿐인데예.
en: Buy me clothes, then. / Everything I own refuses to fit.
…You know what I am paid.

lines: 알지예. / 그래서 사람들이 다 보는 기라요.
en: I do. / Which is why everyone looks.

lines: 오늘 달라 캤다. 사 년 치.
en: I asked today. For the four years.
And?
He smiled at me.
Did he.
What colour was the smile?
…Purple.

lines: 그라믄 헌 초록 입고 가지 뭐.
당신 녹봉이 얼만지 다들 보라 카지.
en: Then I’ll wear the old green.
Let them all see what you’re paid.

blocks.label: The Well-Post
blocks.ko: 우물 기둥

blocks.html: By noon the yard splits. Porters, smiths and the grain boys find work at the well-post. Maehwa crosses alone, in the green jeogori washed too many times and one red sash. They do not come closer. She does not invite them.
blocks.ko: 한낮이 되면 마당이 갈라진다. 짐꾼, 대장장이, 곳간 아이들이 우물 기둥 곁에서 일거리를 찾는다. 매화가 혼자 마당을 건넌다. 너무 여러 번 빤 초록 저고리에 붉은 띠 하나. 사내들은 가까이 오지 않는다. 그녀도 부르지 않는다.

en: Look at that hem…
No — the waist. The waist.
That's Gumil's wife.
I know. That's why it's worse—

blocks.html: She hears every unfinished sentence. Bored chin, and the men keep looking anyway. Dirt under the nails, the same sour drink on every breath. She is tired of being their festival. She walks as if the yard were built around her anyway.
blocks.ko: 끝나지 않은 문장을 하나도 빠짐없이 듣는다. 지루한 턱. 사내들은 그래도 본다. 손톱 밑의 흙, 숨마다 같은 시큼한 술. 그들의 구경거리 노릇도 지겹다. 그래도 마당이 자기를 둘러 지어진 것처럼 걷는다.

en: That is a road.
Do not stand in it.

blocks.html: One of them forgets to close his mouth. She turns just enough. The hem stays a breath too long, and she lets him have that second like a coin she can afford to drop. Then the silk falls back.
blocks.ko: 한 놈이 입 다무는 걸 잊는다. 그녀는 딱 그만큼만 돈다. 치맛자락이 한 숨쯤 오래 머문다. 떨어뜨려도 아깝지 않은 동전처럼 그 한순간을 그에게 준다. 그리고 비단이 다시 내려온다.

en: Just now—
I saw. I saw.
…She didn't even say anything.

blocks.html: She leaves them wrecked on the packed earth and almost smiles. Up on the stair, a purple sleeve has stopped in the middle of a sentence. The yard is about the curve she takes with her.
blocks.ko: 흙마당에 그들을 무너뜨려 놓고, 그녀는 거의 웃는다. 계단 위에서 자줏빛 소매 하나가 말을 하다 멈춘다. 마당은 그녀가 데리고 가는 곡선의 것이다.

blocks.html: Over the western hills, King Euija reads Silla’s border the way he reads everything: patiently, and only once. Daeya is young at the top and hollow underneath. He sends Yunchung east with ten thousand men.
blocks.ko: 서쪽 산 너머에서 의자왕은 신라의 국경을, 모든 것을 읽듯이 읽는다. 참을성 있게, 그리고 단 한 번만. 대야성은 윗자리가 어리고 그 밑이 비어 있다. 그는 윤충에게 군사 만 명을 주어 동쪽으로 보낸다.

lines: 뒤의 이천은 하루 늦게 따라오슈. 누가 묻거든 짐이라구 허슈.
en: Three weeks to the river, I reckon, if the roads behave.
The last two thousand keep a day behind us. If anyone asks, they are the baggage.

blocks.html: Surabol’s dreams don’t change. Its famous sword is far from here this week, on some other errand of the queen’s. Nobody tells Daeya anything.
blocks.ko: 서라벌의 꿈자리는 그대로다. 그 유명한 칼은 이번 주 여기서 멀리, 여왕의 다른 심부름 길에 있다. 대야에는 아무도 아무 말도 해 주지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Night Before
blocks.ko: 전날 밤

blocks.html: The night before the feast, the room is only a lamp and the two of them. The old green jeogori hangs on its peg, mended at the seam for tomorrow. They still know how to find each other. They will not know how tomorrow.
blocks.ko: 잔치 전날 밤, 방에는 등잔 하나와 두 사람뿐이다. 헌 초록 저고리가 내일을 위해 솔기를 기운 채 못에 걸려 있다. 그들은 아직 서로를 찾을 줄 안다. 내일은 모를 것이다.

en: Tomorrow they all look.
Today… only today.
Keep your hand on my waist.
It does not have to be a True Bone hand.
I know.
I know.
…Leave tomorrow for tomorrow.

lines: 사 년 치 받아 낼 끼다. 진짜로.
en: I’ll get the four years. I will.
You’ll have silk by the first frost.
Liar.
…Say it again anyway.

blocks.html: They stop talking. The lamp is too small for manners. The red sash comes off the way it always does in this room, one impatient pull, and the old silk follows it onto the boards. Thirty-one, and she still puts him where she wants him.
blocks.ko: 말이 멎는다. 예의를 차리기엔 등잔이 너무 작다. 붉은 띠는 이 방에서 늘 그렇듯 성급하게 한 번에 풀리고, 헌 비단이 그 뒤를 따라 마루에 떨어진다. 서른하나. 그녀는 아직도 그를 원하는 자리에 둔다.

en: Tomorrow can wait.
Tonight you stay under me.
Don’t use a name. / Just… stay.

blocks.html: She knows his body the way a person knows a door they have opened every winter. He says her name at the end, not a rank. They sleep facing the same wall. In the morning the silk goes back on as if the night had been ordinary. It never is.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 그의 몸을 겨울마다 열어 온 문처럼 안다. 끝에 그는 품계가 아니라 그녀 이름을 부른다. 둘은 같은 벽을 보고 잠든다. 아침이면 비단은 아무 일 없던 밤처럼 다시 입혀진다. 그런 밤은 없다.

blocks.html: Tomorrow the Queen’s seal arrives, and Daeya throws its new Guardian a banquet. Every eye in the hall will find her first…!
blocks.ko: 내일 폐하의 인장이 도착하고, 대야성은 새 성주를 위해 잔치를 연다. 그 잔칫자리의 모든 눈이 제일 먼저 그녀를 찾을 것이다…!

logline.en: A man is measured by his self-control.
logline.ko: 사내의 그릇은 자제력으로 잰다.

So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: A man is measured by his self-control.
blocks.ko: 사내의 그릇은 자제력으로 잰다.

blocks.label: Feast
blocks.ko: 잔치

blocks.label: The Banquet
blocks.ko: 연회

blocks.html: The Queen’s seal arrives in a lacquer box, and Daeya, which has eaten millet all winter, gets a banquet out of it.
blocks.ko: 폐하의 인장이 옻칠 상자에 담겨 도착하고, 겨우내 조밥만 먹던 대야성은 그 덕에 잔치를 얻는다.

blocks.html: The long hall is lit end to end. Purple at the top table, yellow at the back, families on the floor between. Every toast is to the new Guardian of Daeya. He is twenty-one, and he has never been toasted by people who weren’t related to him.
blocks.ko: 긴 전각에 끝에서 끝까지 불이 켜진다. 윗상엔 자색, 뒷줄엔 황색, 그 사이 바닥엔 가족들. 건배는 전부 대야성의 새 성주에게 간다. 그는 스물하나이고, 친척 아닌 사람들에게 건배를 받아 본 건 처음이다.

blocks.html: Lady Gotaso sits beside him for the first cup and goes up at the first drum. She is fifteen, and wine makes her sleepy. She squeezes his hand under the table on her way, and the gold butterfly on his belt rocks on its cord.
blocks.ko: 고타소 부인은 첫 잔까지 그의 곁에 앉아 있다가 첫 북소리에 올라간다. 열다섯이고, 술을 마시면 졸리다. 가면서 상 밑으로 그의 손을 꼭 쥐고, 허리띠의 금나비가 끈에 매달려 흔들린다.

en: Don’t stay up all night being important.
…Come up soon. I’ll pretend I’m awake.
Soon. I promise.

blocks.html: Then the lamp-line is hers. Maehwa walks under the cheap hanging lamps like she built them, in the old green and the red sash tied by habit, carrying a jug nobody asked her to carry. Every head at the top table turns. His turns last, and stays.
blocks.ko: 그다음, 등불 줄은 그녀의 것이 된다. 매화는 싸구려 매단 등 아래를 제가 지은 집처럼 걷는다. 낡은 초록 저고리, 버릇처럼 맨 붉은 띠, 아무도 들라고 하지 않은 술병. 윗상의 고개가 전부 돌아간다. 그의 고개가 제일 늦게 돌아가고, 돌아가서는 멈춘다.

blocks.html: The old green has been washed so thin it holds her like a hand: the narrowest waist in Daeya, cinched hard by the red sash, and above and below it everything the top table pretends not to see. Maehwa has never once needed a man to look twice. She has never once let one stop at the first look.
blocks.ko: 낡은 초록은 하도 빨아서 얇아진 나머지 손처럼 그녀를 감싼다. 붉은 띠로 바짝 조인 대야에서 제일 가는 허리, 그 위와 아래로는 윗상이 못 본 척하는 모든 것. 매화는 사내에게 두 번 보라고 할 필요가 없었다. 첫 번째에서 멈추게 둔 적도 없다.

blocks.html: She pours for the yellow tables first. She takes her time getting to the purple one.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 황색 상부터 따른다. 자색 상까지는 천천히 온다.

lines: …오늘 밤엔 다들 그렇게 부르던데요. 올라오는 길에 열한 번 들었어요.
en: Wine, Guardian?
…That’s what they’re calling you tonight, isn’t it. I heard it eleven times on the way up the hall.
Twelve, now.
I— thank you. Yes. Half a cup.

lines: 자기 잔치에서 반 잔 받는 남자는, 아주 조심스럽거나 아주 겁먹었거나 둘 중 하나죠.
en: Half.
A man who takes half a cup at his own banquet is either very careful or very scared.
Which am I?
Ask me when the jug’s empty.

blocks.html: She moves on. She doesn’t look back, which is how he knows she meant him to watch her go.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 다음 상으로 간다. 돌아보지 않는다. 그래서 그는 그녀가 일부러 보라고 했다는 걸 안다.

blocks.html: She takes a peach from a tray and does not bite it. She sucks at it, slowly, eyes on nothing, because a peach is cheaper than silk and does more work. The juice runs down to her wrist and she lets it. At the back of the hall, among the yellow sleeves, Gumil watches the purple sleeve watch his wife. He has seen her eat a peach like that before. He knows what comes after it.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 쟁반에서 복숭아 하나를 집는다. 베어 물지 않는다. 아무것도 보지 않는 눈으로 천천히 빤다. 복숭아는 비단보다 싸고, 일은 더 한다. 즙이 손목까지 흘러내려도 그냥 둔다. 전각 뒤쪽 황색 소매들 사이에서, 검일은 자색 소매가 제 아내를 보는 걸 본다. 그녀가 복숭아를 저렇게 먹는 걸 전에도 봤다. 그다음에 뭐가 오는지도 안다.

blocks.html: Pumsuk talks to his cup. It doesn’t help. Nine years of Hwarang drill, and nobody taught him what to do with his eyes.
blocks.ko: 품석은 잔에 대고 말한다. 소용없다. 구 년 화랑 수련에, 눈을 어디 둬야 하는지는 아무도 가르쳐 주지 않았다.

blocks.html: Then he does something he has not done in a year. He sends for the grain clerk.
blocks.ko: 그러다 그는 한 해 동안 한 번도 안 하던 일을 한다. 곳간지기를 부른다.

en: You. The— grain tallies. You are…
I am sorry. Your name.
Gumil, Commander.
Four years.
Gumil. Yes.
That woman. In the green. Who is she?

blocks.html: Gumil has waited four years for the purple sleeve to learn his name. It has taken a peach.
blocks.ko: 자줏빛 소매가 제 이름을 알게 되기까지 검일은 사 년을 기다렸다. 복숭아 하나면 되는 일이었다.

en: My wife, Commander.

blocks.html: Pumsuk goes very red. He looks into his cup. Then he does the worst kind thing a man in his chair can do.
blocks.ko: 품석의 얼굴이 아주 붉어진다. 잔 속을 내려다본다. 그리고 그 자리에 앉은 사내가 베풀 수 있는 가장 고약한 친절을 베푼다.

lines: 자네 녹봉 말이오. 사 년 치.
내일 그 장을 가져오시오. 내가 직접 도장을 찍겠소.
그리고— 오늘 밤. 백제가 길에 올랐소. 날이 밝기 전에 곳간 가마니를 전부 세어 놓으시오. 제대로 셀 사람은 자네뿐이오.
en: Your pay. The four years.
Bring the sheet to me tomorrow. I will seal it myself.
And— tonight. Baekje is on the road. Every sack in the stores counted by dawn. You are the only one who can do it properly.

blocks.html: It may be an honest order. Baekje really is on the road. Gumil will spend the rest of his life deciding which it was.
blocks.ko: 정직한 명령일 수도 있다. 백제는 정말 길에 올랐다. 검일은 그게 어느 쪽이었는지 남은 평생 따지게 될 것이다.

en: …By dawn, Commander.

blocks.html: On his way out he passes Maehwa. He does not tell her to cover herself. She does not ask where he is going. She saw him on the stair, and she can count too.
blocks.ko: 나가는 길에 매화를 지난다. 가리라는 말은 하지 않는다. 그녀도 어디 가느냐고 묻지 않는다. 계단 앞의 그를 봤고, 그녀도 셀 줄은 안다.

blocks.html: Later, when the hall is half asleep, the jug is empty and she is at his table again, refilling nothing.
blocks.ko: 나중에, 전각이 반쯤 잠들었을 때, 술병은 비었고 그녀는 다시 그의 상 앞에 있다. 아무것도 채우지 않으면서.

en: …Jug’s empty, Guardian.
Then which am I.

lines: 조심스러운 쪽보다 나아요. 조심스러운 남자는 재미없거든요.
en: Scared.
It’s nicer than careful. Careful men are boring.

blocks.html: He does the correct thing. He stands. He bows to a banquet that hasn’t asked him to leave, and goes up past Gotaso’s pink door to the little room at the top of the stair, where the Guardian sleeps when he works late. Tonight he tells himself he is working late.
blocks.ko: 그는 옳은 일을 한다. 일어선다. 아무도 가라고 하지 않은 잔치에 절을 하고, 고타소의 분홍 문을 지나 계단 꼭대기의 작은 방으로 올라간다. 성주가 늦게까지 일할 때 자는 방이다. 오늘 밤 그는 늦게까지 일하는 거라고 스스로에게 말한다.

blocks.label: He Tries to Sleep
blocks.ko: 자려고 한다

blocks.html: One dying lamp on dark timber. He lies in ice-blue with his eyes open. The hall has come up the stair with him: the jug, the plum, ask me when the jug’s empty. A True Bone should be able to close his eyes. He is twenty-one. He knows exactly why he can’t.
blocks.ko: 어두운 나무 위에 꺼져 가는 등잔 하나. 그는 얼음빛 푸른 옷을 입은 채 눈을 뜨고 누워 있다. 잔칫자리가 계단을 따라 같이 올라왔다. 술병, 매실, 술병 비면 물어보세요. 진골이라면 눈쯤은 감을 수 있어야 한다. 그는 스물하나다. 왜 못 감는지 정확히 안다.

blocks.html: He gets up for air. That’s what he tells the lamp.
blocks.ko: 바람 좀 쐬러 일어난다. 등잔한테는 그렇게 말한다.

blocks.html: On his way down he passes Gotaso’s door. A pink ribbon hangs on the post where her maid tied it. He turns his shoulder so his sleeve won’t brush it. That is the whole of his self-control tonight, and he is proud of it for four steps.
blocks.ko: 내려가는 길에 고타소의 방문을 지난다. 하녀가 묶어 둔 분홍 리본이 기둥에 걸려 있다. 그는 소매가 스치지 않게 어깨를 돌린다. 오늘 밤 그의 절제는 그게 전부고, 그는 네 걸음 동안 그게 자랑스럽다.

blocks.label: The Night
blocks.ko: 그날 밤

blocks.label: The Wall-Walk
blocks.ko: 성벽길

blocks.html: The wall-walk above the river is the only place in Daeya where nobody is counting anything. The moon is on the water. The sentries are at the far towers. She is sitting on the parapet steps in the old green, a shawl around her knees and the banquet peach in her hand, as if she has been there a while.
blocks.ko: 강 위의 성벽길은 대야성에서 아무도 뭘 세지 않는 유일한 곳이다. 달이 물 위에 떠 있다. 보초들은 먼 망루에 있다. 그녀는 낡은 초록 저고리 차림으로 무릎에 숄을 두르고 연회의 복숭아를 손에 든 채 성가퀴 계단에 앉아 있다. 한참 그러고 있었던 것처럼.

blocks.html: She has. She knew which stair he would take. It’s the only one that doesn’t go past the barracks.
blocks.ko: 한참 그러고 있었다. 그가 어느 계단으로 올지 알았다. 병영 앞을 안 지나는 계단은 그것 하나뿐이다.

lines: 아니— 좋은 밤이오. 여기 누가 있을 줄은 몰랐소.
en: …You.
I mean— good evening. I didn’t think anyone would be up here.

lines: 아무도 없어요. 난 아무것도 아니잖아요, 기억나요?
앉아요. 이쪽 돌은 따뜻해. 한 시간째 내가 깔고 앉아 있었거든.
en: Nobody is. I’m nobody, remember?
Sit. The stone’s warm on this side. I’ve been sitting on it for an hour.

blocks.html: He sits. Not close. A True Bone’s arm’s length, which is longer than other people’s.
blocks.ko: 그는 앉는다. 가깝지는 않게. 진골의 팔 길이만큼. 남들 팔보다 길다.

en: …Is that from the banquet?
I don’t finish things in front of people.
Sit. You’ll see.
Your husband is in the stores.

lines: 성주님 쌀가마 세고 있죠. 알아요. 당신이 보냈잖아요.
그런 얼굴 하지 마요. 그 사람 어디 보낸 남자, 당신이 처음 아니니까.
en: Counting your sacks. I know. You sent him.
Don’t make that face. You’re not the first man to send him somewhere.

lines: 그래서. 대야성 성주님이 왜 공주님 옆에 안 누워 있고 한밤중에 성벽에 계실까.
en: So. Why’s the Guardian of Daeya on a wall at midnight, instead of in bed with his princess?
She’s asleep. She sleeps like a child. She is—
…I couldn’t sleep. That’s all.

lines: 거짓말. 말해 봐요. 여기선 아무도 안 받아 적어요.
en: Liar. Go on. Nobody up here writes anything down.

lines: 내가 이 성을 어떻게 얻었는지 아시오?
태어났소. 그게 다요. 할아버지가 누구였고, 내가 누구의 딸과 혼인했고, 폐하께서 거기 인장을 찍으셨소.
오늘 잔치에 온 사내들은 하나같이 내가 칼을 잡은 세월보다 오래 성벽을 지켰소. 열두 번 건배를 했는데, 믿는 자는 하나도 없었소.
en: Do you know how I got this fortress?
I was born. That’s the whole of it. My grandfather was somebody, I married somebody’s daughter, and the Queen put a seal on it.
Every man at that banquet has held a wall longer than I’ve held a sword. They toasted me twelve times. Not one of them believed it.
Eleven. The twelfth was me.
…And did you believe it?

lines: 겁먹었다는 건 믿었죠. 저 사람들이 준 것보단 많잖아요.
en: I believed you were scared. That’s more than they gave you.

lines: 이제 당신 차례요. 당신은 왜 여기 있소?
en: Your turn. Why are you up here?

lines: 저 밑에선 검일이 마누라고, 여기선 그냥 추운 사람이니까.
열다섯에 시집왔어요. 그 사람 옷이 좋았고, 인장 찍히는 일자리가 있었죠. 언젠가 그 인장이 집까지 따라올 줄 알았어요.
십육 년. 옷은 그때 그 옷이에요.
en: Because down there I’m Gumil’s wife. Up here I’m just cold.
I was fifteen when I married him. He had a good coat and a job with a seal on it. I thought the seal would follow him home one day.
Sixteen years. It’s the same coat.

lines: 내가 뭘 원했는지 알아요? 바다. 한 번만. 끝까지 평평하다던데. 난 저 강 너머로 가 본 적이 없어요.
en: You know what I wanted? To see the sea. Once. They say it’s flat all the way to the edge. I’ve never been past that river.

lines: 평평하오. 그게— 끝이 없소. 자꾸 건너편을 기다리게 되오.
en: I’ve seen it. From the east hills at Surabol.
It is flat. It— doesn’t stop. You keep waiting for the other side.

lines: 그러지 마요. 좋게 말하지 마. 난 평생 못 볼 거니까.
en: Don’t. Don’t make it nice. I’m never going to see it.

blocks.html: She says it lightly. It doesn’t come out light. For a while neither of them says anything, and the river does the talking.
blocks.ko: 가볍게 말한다. 가볍게 나오지 않는다. 한동안 둘 다 아무 말도 하지 않고, 말은 강이 한다.

en: I have a wife.
I know. Gotaso. The pink ribbon.
Did you walk past it on the way out?
…I turned my shoulder.

lines: 그래도 우리 집 양반이 평생 될 수 있는 것보단 많아.
en: Half of a True Bone.
Still more than mine will ever be.

blocks.html: Her eyes go to his belt. The gold butterfly is catching the moon.
blocks.ko: 그녀의 눈이 그의 허리띠로 간다. 금나비가 달빛을 받고 있다.

en: Is that real?
…Gold. Yes. My wife made it.

lines: 난 금을 쥐어 본 적이 없어요. 웃기죠? 금 천지인 성에서 십육 년을 살았는데, 한 번도.
en: Made it. Of course she did.
I’ve never held gold. Isn’t that stupid? Sixteen years in a fortress full of it, and I’ve never once held any.

blocks.html: He should say something kind and go to bed. Instead his hands are already at the knot. It is a knot nobody taught Gotaso, and it comes apart for him on the first pull, the way it was never meant to.
blocks.ko: 다정한 말 한마디 하고 자러 가야 한다. 그런데 그의 손은 벌써 매듭에 가 있다. 아무도 고타소에게 가르쳐 준 적 없는 매듭인데, 첫 번에 그에게 풀려 버린다. 그러라고 맨 매듭이 아니었는데.

en: Here. Hold it.
…Keep it.
You don’t mean that.

lines: 내가 무슨 뜻인지 모르겠소. 한 번도— 오늘 밤은 내가 무슨 뜻인지 모르겠소.
en: I don’t know what I mean. I’ve never— I don’t know what I mean tonight.

blocks.html: She closes her hand over it. Then over his.
blocks.ko: 그녀가 그것 위로 손을 오므린다. 그다음 그의 손 위로.

blocks.html: She doesn’t let go. She turns his hand over in hers like a coin she is checking, and finds it shaking.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 놓지 않는다. 동전을 확인하듯 그의 손을 뒤집어 보고, 그 손이 떨리는 걸 알아낸다.

lines: 바람 때문이에요? 아니면 그 잘난 절제 때문이에요?
en: Your hand’s shaking, Guardian.
Is that the wind? Or is that your famous self-control?
It is— the wind. The wind is cold.
The stone’s warm. I told you.

blocks.html: She moves his hand to the inside of her wrist, where he can feel what her pulse is doing, and leaves it there for exactly one breath. Then she takes it back.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 그의 손을 제 손목 안쪽으로 옮긴다. 맥이 뭘 하고 있는지 느껴지는 자리다. 딱 한 숨 동안 거기 둔다. 그러고는 도로 가져간다.

en: …That is not fair.

lines: 여기 위엔 공정한 게 하나도 없어요. 그래서 올라오는 거고.
en: Nothing up here is fair. That’s why I come up.

blocks.html: She lifts the peach she has been holding all this time and sucks the last of the juice off it, slowly, looking at him the whole while. Then she sets it down on the parapet, half-eaten, still dripping. The juice runs down the warm stone in one slow line. He watches it all the way down.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 내내 들고 있던 복숭아를 들어 올려, 그를 빤히 보면서 남은 즙을 천천히 빨아 먹는다. 그러고는 반쯤 먹은 복숭아를, 아직 즙이 떨어지는 채로 성가퀴 위에 내려놓는다. 즙이 따뜻한 돌을 타고 한 줄로 천천히 흘러내린다. 그는 그 줄이 끝까지 내려가는 걸 지켜본다.

blocks.html: She stands, shakes the shawl off her knees and stretches, slowly, like a woman with nowhere to be. The old green rides up at the waist. He looks. She lets him, and watches him do it.
blocks.ko: 그녀가 일어나 무릎의 숄을 털고, 갈 데 없는 여자처럼 천천히 기지개를 켠다. 낡은 초록이 허리께로 말려 올라간다. 그는 본다. 그녀는 보게 두고, 그가 보는 걸 지켜본다.

lines: 성주님 방, 계단 꼭대기 그 작은 방이죠. 등잔 차가운 방.
en: Your room’s the little one at the top of the stair. The one with the cold lamp.
…I’ve watched the light in it for five months.

lines: 절제 잘 챙기시고요. 사내는 그걸로 잰다던데.
en: Goodnight, Guardian.
Mind your self-control. I hear it’s what a man is measured by.

blocks.html: She goes down the wall stair without hurrying, the butterfly in her fist, and does not look back. The True Bone stays on the parapet. He decides to count to ten. He gets to four.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 서두르지 않고 성벽 계단을 내려간다. 주먹엔 금나비. 돌아보지 않는다. 진골은 성가퀴에 남는다. 열까지 세기로 한다. 넷에서 멈춘다.

blocks.html: He catches her on the landing under his own door: her wrist, then her waist, then the rest of her against the timber. He has never taken anything that wasn’t handed to him on a tray, and he doesn’t know how to do it gently. He doesn’t try. He pulls her up the last three steps and through the door with the cold lamp.
blocks.ko: 그는 제 방 문 아래 층계참에서 그녀를 붙잡는다. 손목, 그다음 허리, 그다음 나머지 전부를 나무 벽에 대고. 쟁반에 받쳐 건네받지 않은 걸 가져 본 적이 없는 사내라, 살살 가져가는 법을 모른다. 해 보지도 않는다. 마지막 세 계단을 끌어 올려, 차가운 등잔이 있는 방 문 안으로 들인다.

blocks.html: She laughs into his collar. She was counting too. She got to three.
blocks.ko: 그녀가 그의 옷깃에 대고 웃는다. 그녀도 세고 있었다. 셋까지 셌다.

en: There you are.

blocks.label: The Little Room
blocks.ko: 작은 방

blocks.html: He doesn’t remember the stair. He remembers the door, and her hand finding the bar behind them before his does.
blocks.ko: 계단은 기억나지 않는다. 문이 기억나고, 등 뒤의 빗장을 그의 손보다 먼저 찾는 그녀의 손이 기억난다.

blocks.html: A bowl of banquet peaches sits on the sill, sent up for the Guardian working late. She takes one on her way past him, as if she has all night, and sucks it once, slowly, holding his eyes. Then she sets it down on the sill by the lamp, bitten open. It goes on leaking onto the timber all night.
blocks.ko: 창턱에 연회에서 올려 보낸 복숭아 한 그릇이 있다. 늦게까지 일하는 성주 몫이다. 그녀는 밤새 시간이 있는 것처럼 그의 곁을 지나며 하나를 집어, 그의 눈을 붙든 채 천천히 한 번 빤다. 그러고는 베어 문 자리가 벌어진 채로 등잔 옆 창턱에 내려놓는다. 복숭아는 밤새 나무 위로 즙을 흘린다.

blocks.html: The lamp is too small for manners. The red sash comes off in one impatient pull, and the old green follows it. She is thirty-one, and she knows exactly where she wants him. He is twenty-one, and for once in his life nobody has told him what comes next.
blocks.ko: 등잔이 너무 작아서 예의 차릴 데가 없다. 붉은 띠가 성급한 손짓 한 번에 풀리고, 낡은 초록이 그 뒤를 따른다. 그녀는 서른하나고, 그를 어디에 두고 싶은지 정확히 안다. 그는 스물하나이고, 평생 처음으로 다음에 뭘 해야 하는지 아무도 말해 주지 않았다.

blocks.html: He is not gentle, and she doesn’t ask him to be. He has her against the door before the bar has settled, then on the narrow mat, which was laid for one Guardian working late and complains about two. She puts his hands where she wants them, and every rule of the Hwarang yard leaves him at once. The first time he lasts about as long as a True Bone has ever waited for anything, which is to say not long. He hides his face in her neck. She laughs and pulls him back down by the hair.
blocks.ko: 그는 살살 하지 않고, 그녀도 그러라고 하지 않는다. 빗장이 다 걸리기도 전에 그녀를 문에 붙이고, 그다음엔 좁은 요 위다. 늦게까지 일하는 성주 하나 눕자고 깐 요라, 둘이 되자 삐걱대며 투덜댄다. 그녀가 그의 손을 원하는 데 놓는다. 화랑 연무장에서 배운 법도가 한꺼번에 그를 떠난다. 처음엔 진골이 뭘 기다려 본 만큼밖에 못 버틴다. 말하자면 금방이다. 그는 그녀 목덜미에 얼굴을 묻는다. 그녀는 웃으며 그의 머리채를 잡아 도로 끌어내린다.

lines: …아무도 안 와요. 여긴 아무도 안 올라와요. 내가 봤어요.
en: Slow. Slow down.
…Nobody’s coming. Nobody ever comes up here. I checked.

blocks.html: The second time she is on top and in no hurry at all, and she makes him watch her. He does. He has stopped being able to do anything else.
blocks.ko: 두 번째엔 그녀가 위에 있고, 조금도 서두르지 않는다. 그리고 그에게 자기를 보게 한다. 그는 본다. 이제 다른 건 아무것도 못 한다.

lines: 내 이름을 불러 주시오. 그거 말고. 성주 말고.
en: Say my name. Not the other thing. Not Guardian.
…Pumsuk.

lines: …한 번 더. 부탁이오. 나는— 한 번 더.
en: …Again. Please. I— again.
Greedy.
…Good.

blocks.html: The lamp burns down. Neither of them gets up to fix it. On the sill the peach has split along its seam and run down the wood in a dark, sweet line. Somewhere below, a clerk is counting sacks by torchlight, in the order he will one day burn them.
blocks.ko: 등잔이 다 탄다. 둘 다 고치러 일어나지 않는다. 창턱의 복숭아는 골을 따라 갈라져, 나무를 타고 검고 단 줄을 그으며 흘러내렸다. 저 아래 어딘가에서, 서기 하나가 횃불 아래 쌀가마를 센다. 언젠가 그것들을 태울 순서대로.

blocks.label: Dawn
blocks.ko: 새벽

blocks.html: Grey in the door-slit. She wakes alone. His side of the mat is cold, the ice-blue robe is gone from its peg, and the lamp has been out for hours. On the pillow where his head was, he has left the gold butterfly, as if it were a note. Beside the cold lamp, the peach is only a stone in a dark, sticky ring.
blocks.ko: 문틈에 잿빛. 그녀는 혼자 깬다. 요의 그쪽은 식었고, 얼음빛 푸른 겉옷은 횃대에서 사라졌고, 등잔은 꺼진 지 오래다. 그가 머리를 뉘었던 베개 위에 금나비가 놓여 있다. 쪽지라도 되는 것처럼. 식은 등잔 옆에서 복숭아는 끈적하고 검은 자국 속의 씨 하나로 남았다.

blocks.html: Gumil is standing in the doorway. He has the tally in his hand: every sack in the stores, counted by dawn, as ordered. He climbed the stair to give it to the Guardian.
blocks.ko: 문간에 검일이 서 있다. 손에 장부를 들고 있다. 곳간의 쌀가마 전부, 분부대로 새벽까지 센 것. 성주에게 건네려고 계단을 올라왔다.

en: Every sack. By dawn.
…Commander.

blocks.html: He says it to the empty half of the mat. Then he looks at the other half.
blocks.ko: 그는 요의 빈 쪽에 대고 말한다. 그러고는 나머지 반쪽을 본다.

en: Where is he.
Gone. Before I woke.
…They always are.

blocks.html: Down the stair, the Guardian of Daeya is sitting outside a door with a pink ribbon on it, waiting for his wife to wake up, so that he can lie to her first.
blocks.ko: 계단 아래, 대야성 성주는 분홍 리본이 걸린 문 앞에 앉아 있다. 아내가 깨기를 기다리고 있다. 먼저 거짓말을 하려고.

en: From the start.
All of it.
Don’t leave any out.
The banquet. The jug.
The wall. The river.
After that… his room.
After that.
The name.
How many times.

blocks.html: She tells it. The jug. The wall. The knot on his belt that came apart on the first pull. He makes her say the gold last.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 말한다. 술병. 성벽. 첫 번에 풀린 허리띠의 매듭. 그는 금 이야기를 맨 마지막에 하게 한다.

lines: 자기 아내가 만든 거래요. 그 말부터 하더라고. 그러고도 줬어요.
en: He gave it to me.
His wife made it. He told me that first. Then he gave it to me anyway.
Half a True Bone.
More than mine.
You said that too. Did you.

lines: 당신 부하들도. 이 성벽도. 이 나라도.
en: I did.
Because everyone in this fortress is trash.
Your men. These walls. This country.
…Right.
But you are here too.
You are trash as well.

blocks.html: They stand in the door-slit of morning and do not touch. What is left is the count of what she said, and a marriage that has finished speaking.
blocks.ko: 둘은 아침 문틈에 서서 서로 닿지 않는다. 남은 것은 그녀가 한 말의 셈, 그리고 할 말을 다 해 버린 혼인이다.

blocks.html: She leaves his room at grey dawn by the back stair, past her husband, the butterfly in her fist. The well-post sees her anyway. The well-post sees everything.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 잿빛 새벽에 뒷계단으로 그의 방을 나선다. 남편 곁을 지나, 주먹엔 금나비를 쥐고. 그래도 우물가는 본다. 우물가는 다 본다.

lines: 뺏은 기다. 진골 아이가. 적을 땐 그래 적는 기다.
en: The commander took Gumil’s wife.
Took? I heard she—
Took. He’s True Bone. That’s how it gets written.
Took.
…Is that what happened.

blocks.html: Before this, the commander Pumsuk had seen that the wife of his staff officer, the saji Gumil, was beautiful, and took her. Gumil resented it.
blocks.ko: 이에 앞서 도독 품석이 막객인 사지 검일의 아내가 아름다운 것을 보고 빼앗으니, 검일이 이를 원망하였다.
blocks.hanja: 先是，都督品釋，見幕客舍知黔日之妻有色，奪之，黔日恨之。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 47, Biographies — Jukjuk

blocks.label: The Drums
blocks.ko: 북소리

blocks.label: NOON
blocks.ko: 정오

blocks.html: She has a bundle, the old green on her back and a gold butterfly in her fist. She leaves by the south gate on her own feet. Nobody else in Daeya will.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 보따리 하나에 낡은 초록 저고리를 걸치고, 주먹엔 금나비를 쥐고 있다. 남문으로, 제 발로 나간다. 대야성의 다른 누구도 그러지 못할 것이다.

en: Where.
Somewhere nobody knows my husband.

blocks.html: That is the last thing they ever say to each other.
blocks.ko: 두 사람이 서로에게 한 마지막 말이다.

blocks.label: The North Wall
blocks.ko: 북벽

blocks.html: The drums start before the quarrel is over. Low, from the north wall. The signal-drum, not the parade one. Gumil knows the difference the way a man knows his own wife’s step. Everybody in the fortress stops talking at once.
blocks.ko: 다툼이 끝나기도 전에 북소리가 시작된다. 낮게, 북벽에서. 의식용이 아니라 신호용 북이다. 구밀은 제 아내 발소리 알듯 그 차이를 안다. 성 안의 모든 말이 한꺼번에 멎는다.

blocks.speaker: A runner
en: Commander— dust on the north road. Columns.
Whose?
Baekje. Yunchung’s banners.

blocks.html: The drums have started, and Daeya has three weeks. The siege is next…!
blocks.ko: 북이 울렸다. 대야에는 세 주가 남았다. 다음은 공성이다…!

logline.en: Gumil doesn’t ask his wife if she’s hurt. He asks for the story.
logline.ko: 검일은 아내에게 다쳤느냐고 묻지 않는다. 이야기를 하라고 한다.

images.prompt: A parody of Yi Jeong’s PUNGJUKDO (풍죽도, Bamboo in the Wind), painted exactly like the real Joseon ink scroll: pure black ink on dark-toned silk, sharp calligraphic leaf strokes, pale ink for distant stalks, deep ink for the near one. ICONIC MINIMAL LAYOUT: tall vertical scroll, mostly empty. ONE device: a single bamboo stalk rising DEAD STRAIGHT from bottom to top like a black vertical line while every leaf around it is whipped hard sideways by the gale; faint pale-ink stalks behind it bent low. At its root, tiny, a fragment of a stone fortress parapet with a few broken giwa tiles, and on it one small Silla officer in dark steel lamellar with a cloth sash in deep bamboo green #2f4a3a, standing just as straight as the stalk, spear grounded, facing into the wind; his face is a few strokes. Behind the parapet a faint ink smear of smoke. No other figures. One blank red seal square. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.
