Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). As a hwarang he keeps the crescent-moon headband across the brow, its tails trailing; the jougwan sits on the crown of the head above it. Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. | PLACE Daeya (대야성 (합천)) — attached board /pl_daeya_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Daeya seongmun: weathered stone wall with crenellations, curved giwa pavilion over a hongye arch, heavy iron-bossed timber doors. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). COMMONERS in every Samhan kingdom wear SIMPLE WHITE: plain undyed white or off-white hemp and ramie jackets, wide trousers and skirts, a cloth sash, straw sandals or bare feet, hair in a plain topknot or braid — no dyed silk, no dots, no gold; colour belongs to rank, so a crowd of farmers, porters, servants and townsfolk reads as a field of soft white cloth with the officials' colours standing out of it. Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Nobody in Daeya has ever seen ten thousand of anything. Tonight they get to count.
blocks.ko: 대야성에서 만 개짜리 무언가를 본 사람은 아무도 없다. 오늘 밤 세어 볼 기회가 생긴다.

blocks.label: The Siege
blocks.ko: 포위

blocks.label: Daeya · the officers’ row, the night of the drums
blocks.ko: 대야성 · 관리들 사는 골목, 북소리가 시작된 밤

blocks.html: Three weeks before the torches, Jukjuk is in his own yard, cutting bamboo. His father planted the grove by the door the year he was born. Then he named the boy after it, and expected the two of them to behave the same.
blocks.ko: 횃불이 오기 세 주 전, 죽죽은 제 집 마당에서 대나무를 베고 있다. 그가 태어난 해에 아버지가 대문 옆에 심은 대숲이다. 아버지는 아들 이름도 거기서 따 왔고, 둘이 똑같이 굴기를 바랐다.

blocks.html: His wife comes out with a letter. Their eldest is twenty-two, in the Hwarang yard at Surabol, and writes the way he does everything: small, exact, and far too much.
blocks.ko: 아내가 편지를 들고 나온다. 맏아들은 스물둘, 서라벌 화랑 연무장에 있다. 무슨 일이든 하는 식대로 편지를 쓴다. 잘게, 정확하게, 그리고 너무 길게.

blocks.speaker: Jukjuk’s wife
en: Jukji’s written. Three sheets.
He says the new Commander was the worst archer in their class.
lines: 새로 오신 도독 나리가 저거 기수에서 활을 제일 못 쐈다 카네예.

en: He was. He’s better now.
Now he’s only the worst archer on my wall.
lines: 이제는 내 성벽에서만 제일 못 쏘지.

blocks.speaker: Jukjuk’s wife
en: Be kind to him. He’s our boy’s age.
lines: 잘해 주소. 우리 아 또래 아입니꺼.

en: I’m always kind to him. That’s the trouble.
He thinks I’ll give him the answers.

blocks.html: Then the drums start in the west, faint, the way weather starts. He listens for a while. He puts the knife down.
blocks.ko: 그때 서쪽에서 북소리가 시작된다. 날씨가 바뀔 때처럼 희미하게. 그는 한참 듣는다. 그리고 낫을 내려놓는다.

en: Pack. Take the little ones to your mother’s, up the river.
Tonight.
lines: 짐 싸시오. 작은 것들 데리고 강 위 처가로 가오.

blocks.speaker: Jukjuk’s wife
en: And the Commander’s lady? Is she packing?
lines: 도독 나리 마님은예? 그 댁도 짐 쌉니꺼?

en: That’s his to decide. This is mine.
lines: 그건 그 사람이 정할 일이오. 이건 내가 정하는 일이고.

blocks.speaker: Jukjuk’s wife
en: And you?
I’m the wall.
You ever see a wall go to its mother-in-law’s?

blocks.html: She cuts a joint from the grove and pushes it into his hands, because she has to give him something and that is what is there. He gives it back.
blocks.ko: 아내는 대숲에서 한 마디를 잘라 그의 손에 쥐여 준다. 뭐라도 줘야 했고, 거기 있는 게 그것뿐이었다. 그는 도로 돌려준다.

en: Keep it. Plant it wherever you end up.
It grows anywhere. It’s only stubborn about bending.
lines: 가지고 가오. 어디 가서 살든 심어 두고.
아무 데서나 잘 자라오. 굽히는 것만 고집이 세지.

blocks.html: The cart goes up the river road at midnight: his wife, the two youngest, and a joint of bamboo wrapped in a skirt. He doesn’t watch it go. He has a wall to look at.
blocks.ko: 한밤중에 수레가 강 위 길로 올라간다. 아내와 막내 둘, 그리고 치마에 싼 대나무 한 마디. 그는 떠나는 걸 지켜보지 않는다. 지켜볼 성벽이 있다.

blocks.label: The North Road
blocks.ko: 북쪽 길

blocks.html: They come at night, three weeks after the drums, the way the drums promised. The river covers three sides of the hill, so they all come up the fourth. A line of torches, then another behind it, then so many that the north road looks like a river of its own, running the wrong way.
blocks.ko: 북이 울린 지 삼 주 뒤, 북이 약속한 대로 그들이 밤에 온다. 강이 언덕 세 면을 감싸고 있으니, 전부 나머지 한 면으로 올라온다. 횃불 한 줄, 그 뒤에 또 한 줄, 그러다 북쪽 길 전체가 거꾸로 흐르는 또 하나의 강처럼 보일 만큼.

blocks.html: The villages under the wall get in first. Carts, goats, grandmothers, a pig nobody owns. The north gate jams with them. A woman loses a child in the press and screams a name over and over, and the whole gate takes it up, until it isn’t anybody’s name any more.
blocks.ko: 성벽 아래 마을들이 먼저 밀려 들어온다. 수레, 염소, 할머니들, 주인 없는 돼지 한 마리. 북문이 그들로 막힌다. 한 여자가 인파 속에서 아이를 놓치고 이름 하나를 자꾸 부르고, 문 전체가 그 이름을 따라 부르다가, 결국 그건 누구의 이름도 아니게 된다.

blocks.speaker: The gate
en: Open it— open the other leaf!
My mother’s still out there—
Push! PUSH!

blocks.html: Up on the gatehouse the Guardian of Daeya is in his armour for the first time outside a parade yard. It fits. That’s the trouble. Everything about him fits except the face.
blocks.ko: 문루 위에서 대야성 성주는 열병장 밖에서 처음으로 갑옷을 입고 있다. 잘 맞는다. 그게 문제다. 얼굴만 빼고 다 잘 맞는다.

lines: 아니— 잠깐. 아직 밖에 사람들이— 열어 두어라. 반만. 반만 열 수 있소?
en: Close the gate.
No— wait. There are still people out— leave it open. Half. Can we open it half?

blocks.html: Beside him stands Jukjuk, yellow sleeve, who has been holding this wall since Pumsuk was learning to ride. He does not raise his voice. He has never needed to.
blocks.ko: 그의 곁에는 황색 소매의 죽죽이 서 있다. 품석이 말 타기를 배울 때부터 이 성벽을 지켜 온 사람이다. 목소리를 높이지 않는다. 높일 필요가 한 번도 없었다.

lines: 반만 연 문도 저놈들한테는 다 연 문입니다, 성주님.
지금 닫으면 저 사람들이 밖에서 죽고, 열어 두면 우리가 다 죽습니다. 명을 내리십시오.
en: Half a gate is a whole gate, Commander. To them.
Close it now and those people die outside. Leave it and we all do. Your order.

blocks.html: Pumsuk looks at him the way he used to look at his tutors: for the answer. Jukjuk doesn’t give it to him. It is the cruelest kindness of the night.
blocks.ko: 품석은 스승들을 보던 눈으로 그를 본다. 답을 달라는 눈으로. 죽죽은 주지 않는다. 그날 밤 가장 잔인한 친절이다.

en: …Close it.

blocks.html: The bar comes down on the woman’s screaming. Pumsuk does not look over the parapet. He hasn’t learned that part yet either.
blocks.ko: 여자의 비명 위로 빗장이 내려온다. 품석은 성가퀴 너머를 보지 않는다. 그것도 아직 못 배웠다.

blocks.label: The Baekje Camp
blocks.ko: 백제 진영

blocks.html: Below the wall, Yunchung eats standing up. He heard the gate close. He knows the sound.
blocks.ko: 성벽 아래에서 윤충은 선 채로 밥을 먹는다. 성문 닫히는 소리를 들었다. 아는 소리다.

blocks.html: The villagers who didn’t get in are brought to him. He doesn’t look up from his bowl.
blocks.ko: 못 들어간 마을 사람들이 그 앞에 끌려온다. 그는 밥그릇에서 눈을 들지 않는다.

en: Farmers?

blocks.speaker: A Baekje captain
en: Farmers, General. Some of them old.
What do we—

lines: 그리고 저녁 마저 먹어. 긴 밤이 될 거다.
en: Put them where the wall can see.
Then finish your supper. It’s going to be a long night.

blocks.html: That is the whole order. Up on the gatehouse, Pumsuk watches it carried out by torchlight, and learns, one at a time, what the word siege means.
blocks.ko: 명령은 그게 전부다. 문루 위에서 품석은 횃불 아래 그 명령이 집행되는 걸 지켜보며, 포위라는 말이 무슨 뜻인지 한 명씩 배운다.

blocks.label: The Gatehouse
blocks.ko: 문루

blocks.html: By the second night Pumsuk has given eleven orders and taken back four. He is counting. So is everyone else.
blocks.ko: 둘째 날 밤까지 품석은 명령 열한 개를 내리고 넷을 거둬들였다. 본인도 세고 있다. 다른 사람들도 다 세고 있다.

en: How long can we hold?

lines: 곳간만 있으면 겨울 내내 버팁니다. 우리가 굶기 전에 저놈들이 얼어 죽습니다.
en: With the granary? All winter. They’ll freeze before we starve.

lines: 좋소. 좋소. 그럼— 성벽 병사들이 어제부터 못 먹었소. 곳간에 사람을 보내라. 두 배로 내주어라. 넉넉하다는 걸 보여 주어야 하오.
en: Good. Good. Then— the wall men haven’t eaten since yesterday. Send someone to the stores. Double rations. Let them see we have plenty.

blocks.html: It is the first good order he gives. A boy from the levy runs down the stair with an empty sack over his shoulder.
blocks.ko: 그가 내린 첫 번째 좋은 명령이다. 징집된 소년 하나가 빈 자루를 어깨에 메고 계단을 뛰어 내려간다.

blocks.html: He comes back without the sack.
blocks.ko: 소년은 자루 없이 돌아온다.

blocks.speaker: The levy boy
lines: 없어요. 다요. 다— 다 탔어요, 성주님. 안에 불밖에 없어요.
en: Commander—
The stores. The granary.
It’s gone. All of it. It’s— it’s burnt, sir. There’s nothing in there but fire.

blocks.html: Everyone on the gatehouse turns south. Above the granary roof the sky is orange, and has been for a while, and nobody looked.
blocks.ko: 문루 위의 모두가 남쪽으로 돌아선다. 곳간 지붕 위 하늘이 주황색이다. 한참 전부터 그랬는데, 아무도 보지 않았다.

en: Who keeps the granary?
…Gumil, Commander.

blocks.html: Pumsuk knows the name now. He learned it at a banquet.
blocks.ko: 품석은 이제 그 이름을 안다. 잔칫자리에서 배웠다.

blocks.html: An hour earlier. The granary is dark and smells of rice and rats. Gumil walks the rows with a torch, the way he has every night for four years, counting.
blocks.ko: 한 시간 전. 곳간은 어둡고 쌀과 쥐 냄새가 난다. 검일은 횃불을 들고 줄 사이를 걷는다. 사 년 동안 매일 밤 그랬듯이, 세면서.

blocks.html: Every sack is in his ledger, written in a hand nobody upstairs ever read. Tonight he reads them back to himself, out loud.
blocks.ko: 모든 가마는 그의 장부에 있다. 위층의 누구도 읽어 본 적 없는 글씨로. 오늘 밤 그는 그걸 소리 내어 자기한테 읽어 준다.

lines: 사 년 치 녹봉. 인장 안 찍힘.
en: Forty from the east fields. Sealed.
Sixty from the river farms. Sealed.
Four years’ pay. Not sealed.

blocks.html: Close on his face in the torchlight. He isn’t crying. He isn’t even angry. He looks like a man finishing a sum.
blocks.ko: 횃불 아래 그의 얼굴. 울지 않는다. 화가 난 얼굴도 아니다. 셈을 끝내는 사람의 얼굴이다.

en: And one gold butterfly.
…Not sealed either.

blocks.html: He puts the torch to the first sack. Then the next, in the order he wrote them down.
blocks.ko: 그가 첫 가마에 횃불을 댄다. 그다음 가마, 그가 적어 둔 순서대로.

blocks.html: Mochuk is at the river postern with the bar already lifted. He is yellow too: same rank, same pay, same four years. He reads Gumil’s face before Gumil reaches him.
blocks.ko: 모척은 이미 빗장을 들어 올린 채 강 쪽 쪽문에 있다. 그도 황색이다. 같은 등급, 같은 녹봉, 같은 사 년. 검일이 닿기도 전에 그의 얼굴을 읽는다.

lines: 동쪽 곳간 줄이 통째로 타고 있다, 이 사람아—
en: The whole east row is going up, man—
Why are you doing this. Truly.
Because everyone in this fortress is trash.

blocks.html: He is quoting her. He will keep quoting her for the eighteen years he has left, until a king he wronged finds him.
blocks.ko: 아내의 말을 옮기는 것이다. 남은 십팔 년 동안 그는 계속 그 말을 옮길 것이다. 그가 저버린 왕이 그를 찾아낼 때까지.

blocks.html: They go out along the river in the dark. At the Baekje lines a torch comes up into Gumil’s face, and Yunchung looks at him for exactly as long as it takes to decide he is useful.
blocks.ko: 둘은 어둠 속에서 강을 따라 나간다. 백제 진영에서 횃불 하나가 검일의 얼굴 앞으로 올라오고, 윤충은 그가 쓸모 있다고 판단하는 데 필요한 만큼만 그를 본다.

en: You’re the grain clerk.
I was.
Kneel, then. You’re mine now.

blocks.html: Gumil kneels in the mud. Behind him, over the wall, the sky is starting to turn orange.
blocks.ko: 검일이 진흙에 무릎을 꿇는다. 그의 등 뒤, 성벽 너머 하늘이 주황빛으로 물들기 시작한다.

blocks.label: The Fire
blocks.ko: 불

blocks.html: Without the granary, Daeya is a stone ring around a bonfire. The fire jumps from the stores to the barracks roof, from the barracks to the stables. The horses scream in a way the levy boys will hear for the rest of their lives, which is about a day.
blocks.ko: 곳간이 없는 대야성은 모닥불을 둘러싼 돌 고리다. 불은 곳간에서 병영 지붕으로, 병영에서 마구간으로 옮겨붙는다. 말들이 비명을 지른다. 징집된 소년들은 남은 평생 그 소리를 듣게 될 것이다. 하루쯤 되는 평생을.

blocks.html: Outside, Yunchung sits his horse on the rise and watches it burn. He doesn’t cheer. He doesn’t hurry. When a few men drop from the wall to run for the river, he points with two fingers, his riders ride them down, and he goes back to watching.
blocks.ko: 밖에서 윤충은 둔덕 위 말 등에 앉아 불타는 걸 지켜본다. 환호하지 않는다. 서두르지도 않는다. 몇 사람이 성벽에서 뛰어내려 강으로 달아나자, 손가락 두 개로 가리킨다. 기병들이 그들을 짓밟고, 그는 다시 지켜본다.

en: Don’t waste arrows on the ones who jump.
Wait at the bottom.

blocks.label: The Wall
blocks.ko: 성벽

blocks.html: Just before dawn, a Baekje herald rides to the foot of the wall under a white cloth. He has a good voice, and the smoke carries it.
blocks.ko: 동트기 직전, 백제 전령 하나가 흰 천을 달고 성벽 아래로 말을 몰아온다. 목청이 좋고, 연기가 그 소리를 실어 올린다.

blocks.speaker: A Baekje herald
en: The General says: enough.
Open the gate, and every soul inside walks out alive. Soldiers, women, children, the grain clerk’s cat. He swears it.
He would rather have a fortress than a graveyard. Graveyards pay no tax.
lines: 성문을 열면 안에 있는 목숨은 하나도 빠짐없이 걸어 나간다. 군사도, 아녀자도, 아이도, 곳간지기 고양이까지. 장군께서 맹세하신다.
무덤보다는 성을 갖고 싶으시단다. 무덤은 세금을 안 내니까.

blocks.html: Pumsuk turns from the parapet with his whole face open. He looks twenty-one, which he is.
blocks.ko: 품석이 성가퀴에서 돌아선다. 얼굴이 활짝 열려 있다. 스물한 살로 보인다. 스물한 살이다.

en: Everyone. Did you hear? He said everyone.
He said it loudly, Commander. That isn’t the same thing.
lines: 크게 말했지요, 성주님. 그건 같은 게 아닙니다.

en: We have no grain. The barracks are gone. The men are drinking out of their helmets—
lines: 곡식이 없소. 막사도 다 탔소. 병사들이 투구로 물을 떠 마시고 있—

en: We have water and a wall. That’s all a siege ever is.
Two nights ago he put farmers in front of this gate and let us watch. It’s the same man asking you to trust him.
lines: 물 있고 성벽 있습니다. 농성이란 게 원래 그게 다입니다.
이틀 전 저자가 농사꾼들을 이 문 앞에 세워 놓고 우리더러 보라 했습니다. 지금 믿어 달라는 것도 같은 자입니다.

en: Then what do I— if I say no they burn us. If I say yes—
lines: 그럼 나더러 어쩌— 싫다 하면 태워 죽일 테고, 좋다 하면—

en: If you say yes, he doesn’t have to climb.
That’s the whole gift.
lines: 좋다 하시면, 저자는 성벽을 안 기어올라도 됩니다.

blocks.html: Pumsuk looks at him for the answer, the way he did on the first night. This time Jukjuk gives it. It is the only time he ever does.
blocks.ko: 품석은 첫날 밤처럼 답을 구하는 얼굴로 그를 본다. 이번에는 죽죽이 답을 준다. 처음이자 마지막이다.

en: Don’t open it.

blocks.html: So a purple sleeve stands on the wall in the smoke and asks the dark for the terms again, in his own voice.
blocks.ko: 그래서 자색 소매 하나가 연기 속 성벽 위에 서서, 제 목소리로 어둠에 대고 다시 조건을 묻는다.

en: If you swear to spare us all, I will surrender.

lines: 만일 그렇게 한다면 공과 나에게 모두 좋은 일이 될 것이요. 저 밝은 해를 두고 맹세하리다.
en: If you do, it will go well for both you and me. I swear it on that bright sun.

blocks.html: He points east. The sun isn’t up yet. Nobody on the wall notices what he has sworn on.
blocks.ko: 그가 동쪽을 가리킨다. 해는 아직 뜨지 않았다. 그가 무엇에 걸고 맹세했는지, 성벽 위의 누구도 눈치채지 못한다.

lines: 성주님. 백제는 손바닥 뒤집듯 말을 바꾸는 나라입니다.
저 달콤한 말은 미끼입니다. 걸어 나가는 순간 다 사로잡힙니다.
쥐처럼 엎드려 사느니, 범처럼 싸우다 죽는 게 낫습니다.
en: Commander. Baekje turns its word over like a hand.
That sweet talk is bait. Walk out there and we’re prisoners.
Better to fight like a tiger and die than crouch like a rat and live.
…My wife is inside.

lines: 북소리 나던 밤에 강 위로 보냈습니다.
en: Mine isn’t, Commander.
I sent her up the river the night of the drums.

blocks.html: Pumsuk doesn’t answer that. He goes down to open the gate himself.
blocks.ko: 품석은 대답하지 않는다. 직접 성문을 열러 내려간다.

blocks.html: There is a split pine on a practice road in Surabol. Everyone pulls up there the first year. Pumsuk never told anyone about the other years.
blocks.ko: 서라벌 연습로에 갈라진 소나무가 하나 있다. 첫해엔 다들 거기서 고삐를 당긴다. 품석은 그다음 해들 이야기를 누구에게도 하지 않았다.

blocks.html: The north gate opens. The garrison files out first, shields down, onto the road toward the Baekje camp. Out of the west come the men Yunchung kept a day behind. The oath lasts until the last Silla shield is down.
blocks.ko: 북문이 열린다. 수비군이 먼저, 방패를 내린 채 백제 진영 쪽 길로 줄지어 나간다. 서쪽에서, 윤충이 하루 뒤에 두었던 군사들이 몰려온다. 맹세는 마지막 신라 방패가 내려질 때까지만 간다.

blocks.html: Then the killing starts. Yunchung doesn’t turn his horse. He watches it the way he watched the fire. When a captain asks about the wounded, he says one word.
blocks.ko: 그리고 살육이 시작된다. 윤충은 말머리를 돌리지 않는다. 불을 볼 때처럼 본다. 한 군관이 부상자는 어떻게 하느냐고 묻자, 한 마디만 한다.

en: All.

blocks.html: On the rise behind him, Gumil is not glad. He had thought he would be.
blocks.ko: 그 뒤 둔덕 위에서, 검일은 기쁘지 않다. 기쁠 줄 알았다.

blocks.html: A Silla shield-boy from the levy, fourteen, holds the gate road for the length of a song and dies with somebody else’s spear in his hands. Nobody learns his village. The rope in the morning will not have his name on it either, because the rope only counts the living.
blocks.ko: 징집된 신라 방패 소년, 열넷. 노래 한 곡 길이만큼 길목을 지키고, 남의 창을 쥔 채 죽는다. 고향 마을을 아는 사람이 없다. 아침의 밧줄에도 그의 이름은 없다. 밧줄은 산 사람만 세니까.

blocks.label: The Fall
blocks.ko: 함락

blocks.label: The Inner Room
blocks.ko: 안채

blocks.html: Pumsuk is at the inner gate with his wife’s hand in his, about to walk her out, when he hears it. Not a battle. A battle has two sides. This is one sound, going on and on, from the road where his men laid their shields down.
blocks.ko: 품석은 아내의 손을 잡고 안문 앞에서 막 그녀를 데리고 나가려던 참에 그 소리를 듣는다. 전투가 아니다. 전투에는 양쪽이 있다. 이건 한 가지 소리다. 그의 병사들이 방패를 내려놓은 길에서, 끝없이 이어지는.

blocks.html: He turns around and takes her back up the stair. She lets him. She has been reading his face since the gyuku match.
blocks.ko: 그는 돌아서서 그녀를 데리고 계단을 다시 올라간다. 그녀는 따라간다. 격구 시합 때부터 그의 얼굴을 읽어 온 사람이다.

blocks.html: In the inner room Gotaso understands before anyone says the word. Her pink ribbon is crooked on the post. She tied it again herself at dawn, badly, and knew why. She is fifteen, and the forever she promised at the wedding has run out of road.
blocks.ko: 안채에서 고타소는 누가 말하기도 전에 안다. 기둥의 분홍 리본이 비뚤어져 있다. 새벽에 자기가 다시 묶었다. 서툴게. 그리고 동인지 알았다. 그녀는 열다섯이고, 혼례 날 약속한 영원은 갈 길이 다 떨어졌다.

blocks.html: She looks at his belt. The pink cord is there. The butterfly isn’t.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 그의 허리띠를 본다. 분홍 끈은 있다. 나비는 없다.

en: …Where’s the butterfly?
I— lost it.

blocks.html: She looks at him for a long moment, and decides something. You can watch her decide it, the way you can watch a girl decide to jump into cold water.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 한참 그를 본다. 그리고 뭔가를 정한다. 차가운 물에 뛰어들기로 정하는 여자아이를 보듯, 그녀가 정하는 게 보인다.

en: Then I’ll make you another one.
I’ll make the other wing bigger this time.
Husband…
If you are going to do it — look at me.

blocks.html: He draws the parade sword with the fox in its ring. It has never been blooded. He looks at her the whole time, the way she asked.
blocks.ko: 그는 고리에 여우가 든 의장용 칼을 뽑는다. 한 번도 피를 묻혀 본 적 없는 칼이다. 그녀가 부탁한 대로, 그는 내내 그녀를 본다.

blocks.html: It is fast. It is the one thing he does well all night.
blocks.ko: 빠르다. 그날 밤 그가 제대로 해낸 유일한 일이다.

blocks.html: It doesn’t hurt the way she thought. It is more like missing a step in the dark. Then the room is very quiet, the smoke has stopped moving, and she is standing by the lattice, and there is a man in the room who was not in the room.
blocks.ko: 생각했던 것처럼 아프지 않다. 어둠 속에서 계단 하나를 헛디딘 느낌에 가깝다. 그러고 나니 방이 아주 조용하고, 연기가 멈춰 있고, 그녀는 창살 옆에 서 있고, 방에 없던 남자가 방에 있다.

blocks.html: Ledger under one arm, crow-dark robe, standing the polite distance of a messenger. The underworld’s. Whose king is Yumla.
blocks.ko: 명부를 한 팔에 끼고, 까마귀빛 도포를 입고, 전령다운 예의 바른 거리에 서 있다. 저승의 사람이다. 그곳의 왕은 염라다.

blocks.html: It keeps a ledger, and it is never late.
blocks.ko: 명부를 쥐고 있고, 늦는 법이 없다.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads her name aloud three times before he asks anything. Gotaso. Gotaso. Gotaso. It is the underworld’s way of making sure the ledger has opened the right door.
blocks.ko: 강림은 무엇을 묻기 전에 그녀의 이름을 세 번 크게 부른다. 고타소. 고타소. 고타소. 명부가 올바른 문을 열었는지 확인하는 저승의 방식이다.

blocks.caption: The underworld’s fetch. He asks one question at the door, and he waits for the answer.
blocks.ko: 저승차사. 문 앞에서 질문 하나를 묻고, 대답을 기다린다.

en: Lady Gotaso.
One question, then we walk.
When you chose forever — did you choose the man, or the vow?
lines: 영원을 고르실 때 — 그 사람을 고르신 겁니까, 맹세를 고르신 겁니까?

en: Who… are you?
I don’t know your face. I don’t know your house.
Are you Baekje? Are you—
Neither. I collect.
You do not need to know me. Almost nobody does, until they do.
The question stands.
lines: 둘 다 아닙니다. 저는 거둬 갑니다.
저를 아실 필요 없습니다. 알기 전까지는 거의 아무도 모릅니다.

en: …Both.
Is that allowed?
…When he came for me there was something on his coat. He said he would change it later.
lines: …저를 데리러 왔을 때, 그이 옷에 뭐가 묻어 있었어요. 이따 갈아입겠다고 했고.

en: Honest. Rare.
Come. Nobody where we are going will ask you to swear anything.
lines: 갑시다. 우리가 갈 곳에서는 아무도 낭자께 맹세를 시키지 않습니다.
새를 잃었니? 하나 더 접어 줄게
en: Kim Gotaso, little bird,
married a sleeve without a word.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Lost the bird? She’ll fold one more,
bigger wings than the one before.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Fire at the gate and smoke in the hall —
“Look at me,” and that was all.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
blocks.title: Gotaso the Paper Bird

blocks.caption: Lady Gotaso, daughter of Kim Chunchu, wife of Pumsuk. She asked him to look at her.
blocks.ko: 김춘추의 딸, 품석의 아내 고타소. 자기를 보라고 했다.

blocks.html: Behind her, Pumsuk kneels beside what she left on the floor. He doesn’t see the man in the gat. Not yet.
blocks.ko: 그녀 뒤에서 품석은 그녀가 바닥에 남기고 간 것 옆에 무릎을 꿇는다. 갓 쓴 남자는 보이지 않는다. 아직은.

blocks.html: He turns the fox-ring blade around in his hands. He is a True Bone, and there is no road left, and he does what a True Bone does.
blocks.ko: 그는 여우 고리 칼을 손안에서 돌려 쥔다. 진골이고, 남은 길이 없고, 진골이 하는 일을 한다.

blocks.html: For him it isn’t like missing a step. It is like being very cold, very quickly. Then he is on his knees on the same boards, there is no blood on his coat, and a second man in a black gat is standing over him with a red book open.
blocks.ko: 그에게는 계단을 헛디딘 느낌이 아니다. 아주 빠르게, 아주 추워지는 느낌이다. 그러고 나니 그는 같은 마룻바닥에 무릎을 꿇고 있고, 옷에 피가 없고, 검은 갓을 쓴 두 번째 남자가 붉은 책을 펼친 채 그를 내려다보고 있다.

blocks.html: He reads the name three times. Pumsuk. Pumsuk. Pumsuk. A second door in the same fortress.
blocks.ko: 남자가 이름을 세 번 읽는다. 품석. 품석. 품석. 같은 성의 두 번째 문.

blocks.caption: Kangrim’s partner on the reaper roads. He doesn’t ask a question. He asks for last words.
blocks.ko: 저승길에서 강림과 짝을 이루는 차사. 질문은 하지 않는다. 유언을 묻는다.

en: The red book is open.
Any last words?
Is she—
Where is she?
Ahead. With the other one.
Last words.

lines: 첫날밤에. 그 사람 손이 차가워서 내가 그리 말했더니, 떨려서 그렇다 했소.
en: …Her hands were cold.
On our wedding night. Her hands were cold, and I said so, and she said it was because she was shaking.
That’s not last words. That’s a report.
It’s all I have.

lines: 가진 게 그뿐이라 그 말만 했네
en: Kim Pumsuk, in purple dressed,
smiled so kind and never guessed.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Rode by her wheel and not ahead;
walks behind her now instead.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Her hands were cold the night they wed —
that’s all he had, so that’s what he said.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
blocks.title: Pumsuk Who Walked Behind

blocks.caption: Kim Pumsuk, True Bone, Guardian of Daeya. He walked behind her.
blocks.ko: 진골, 대야성 도독 김품석. 그녀 뒤를 따라 걸었다.

blocks.label: The Last Gate
blocks.ko: 마지막 문

blocks.html: Jukjuk gathers the men who are left and shuts the inner gate behind them.
blocks.ko: 죽죽이 남은 군사를 모아 안쪽 성문을 닫아건다.

blocks.speaker: Yongsuk
lines: 나리— 다 끝났십니더. 받아 줄 때 항복하입시더.
en: Sir— it’s lost. Surrender while they’re still offering.
Live. Do something about it later.

lines: 아버지께서 대나무를 따라 내 이름을 지으셨소.
추운 철에도 시들지 말라고. 부러질지언정 굽히지는 말라고.
죽음이 두려워 항복해서 살 수야 있겠소?
en: You’re right, Yongsuk.
My father named me for the bamboo.
So I would not wither in the cold season. So I might be broken but never bent.
How should I fear death, and live by surrendering?

blocks.html: Yongsuk is right, and knows it, and stays anyway. The annals keep both their names, which is more than they do for most men who are right.
blocks.ko: 용석은 옳았고, 그걸 알았고, 그래도 남는다. 사서는 두 사람 이름을 다 남긴다. 옳았던 사람 대부분에게는 해 주지 않는 대접이다.

blocks.html: Down the hill the officers’ row has caught. The bamboo by his door goes up one joint at a time, each one cracking like a slap. He can hear it from the gate. It sounds like somebody arguing.
blocks.ko: 언덕 아래 관리들 사는 골목에도 불이 붙었다. 그의 집 대문 옆 대숲이 한 마디씩 타오른다. 마디마다 따귀 소리처럼 터진다. 안문에서도 들린다. 누가 말다툼을 하는 소리 같다.

blocks.html: They come up the hill from the north gate, the way the garrison went down. He holds the inner gate until the sun is up, the bright one Yunchung swore on. Then he is broken, exactly as promised, and not bent.
blocks.ko: 수비대가 내려간 그 길로, 그들이 북문에서 언덕을 올라온다. 그는 해가 뜰 때까지 안문을 지킨다. 윤충이 걸고 맹세한 그 밝은 해가. 그리고 약속대로 꺾인다. 굽지는 않는다.

blocks.html: When it is over, Yunchung walks up to the inner room himself. He looks at the two of them on the boards for about as long as he looked at Gumil. Then he has their heads taken and packed in salt for Sabi. The king will want to see what True Bone looks like up close.
blocks.ko: 다 끝나자 윤충은 직접 안채로 올라간다. 마룻바닥의 두 사람을, 검일을 볼 때만큼만 본다. 그리고 두 사람의 목을 베어 소금에 절여 사비로 보내게 한다. 임금께서 진골이 가까이서 어떻게 생겼는지 보고 싶어 하실 테니.

blocks.html: In the morning a thousand of Daeya’s people walk west on one long rope. Gumil walks beside the rope, not on it.
blocks.ko: 아침이 되자 대야 사람 천 명이 긴 밧줄 하나에 묶여 서쪽으로 걷는다. 검일은 그 밧줄 곁에서 걷는다. 묶이지 않은 채.

blocks.speaker: A Daeya captive
lines: 검일이? …검일아! 말 좀 해 도. 내 안다꼬 말 좀—
en: Gumil? …Gumil! Tell them. Tell them you know me—

blocks.html: Gumil does not turn his head.
blocks.ko: 검일은 고개를 돌리지 않는다.

blocks.label: Chunchu
blocks.ko: 춘추

blocks.label: The Moon Palace
blocks.ko: 월성

lines: 대야성이 함락되고... 품석 화랑, 고타소 양은 염라대왕 앞으로 가셨다 합니다...!
en: Daeya has fallen… They say Hwarang Pumsuk and Lady Gotaso have gone before Yumla…!
…What was it that girl said at her wedding.
“We will be happy forever.”

blocks.html: Chunchu does not shout. He asks, very calmly, for the names of everyone who was inside the fortress. Then, more calmly still, for the name of the man who opened the gate.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 소리치지 않는다. 아주 차분하게, 그 성 안에 있던 사람들의 이름을 모두 적어 오라 이른다. 그리고 더 차분하게, 성문을 연 자의 이름을.

blocks.caption: One summer. Daeya was the door, and the capital sits right behind it.
blocks.ko: 한 여름. 대야성은 문이었고, 도성은 바로 그 뒤에 있다.

lines: 자네 딸을 지키겠다꼬 맹세한 건 품석이었네.
en: Chunchu.
It was Pumsuk who swore to protect your daughter.
Not you.
Brother.
I am the one who made him swear it.

blocks.label: The Empty Hall
blocks.ko: 빈 대전

blocks.html: That night his mother finds him in the empty audience hall, sitting on the floor below the dais the way he used to sit there when he was small enough to be overlooked. Princess Chunmyung is fifty-seven. She gave up a throne to marry his father and has never once brought it up. She lowers herself down beside him slowly, one hand on his shoulder for the knees, and does not ask how he is.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 어머니는 텅 빈 정전에서 그를 찾아낸다. 어좌 단 아래 바닥에 앉아 있다. 눈에 띄지 않을 만큼 작았을 때 거기 앉곤 하던 그대로. 천명 공주는 쉰일곱이다. 그의 아버지와 혼인하려고 왕위를 내려놓았고, 그 얘기를 꺼낸 적은 한 번도 없다. 그녀는 무릎 때문에 아들 어깨에 한 손을 짚고 천천히 그 옆에 앉는다. 괜찮으냐고 묻지 않는다.

lines: 바둑에선 돌 하나 잃으면, 그게 얼마짜리 집이었는지 세요.
en: Mother.
In go, when you lose a stone, you count the territory it cost.
This one… I can’t find the edge of it.

lines: 아홉 살 때부터 세고 있다 아이가. 네 아버지가 가르쳤고, 난 내버려 뒀제.
……머리 대. 오늘 밤만. 이 방에선 아직 내가 너보다 크다.
en: Then stop counting.
You’ve been counting since you were nine. Your father taught you, and I let him.
…Put your head down. Just tonight. In this hall I’m still bigger than you.

blocks.html: He does. The most cunning man in Samhan sleeps an hour with his head on his mother’s knee, and in the morning he asks the Queen for a road north.
blocks.ko: 그는 그렇게 한다. 삼한에서 가장 교활한 사내가 어머니 무릎을 베고 한 시진을 잔다. 그리고 아침에 여왕께 북으로 가는 길을 청한다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace Gate
blocks.ko: 월성 문

blocks.html: In Surabol Bupmin waits at the gate the way a boy waits for a sister who promised forever. Munhee does not send him inside. She lets him see the empty road. Some educations are cruel on purpose.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에서 법민은 영원히를 약속한 여동생을 기다리듯 문 앞에서 기다린다. 문희는 그를 들여보내지 않는다. 빈 길을 보게 둔다. 어떤 교육은 일부러 잔인하다.

en: Look at the road. Don’t look away.
You said you would be king for everyone.
Everyone includes the ones who do not come back.
…I will make a country where sisters come home.
Good. Start by surviving your father.
lines: 좋다. 일단 아버지 옆에서 살아남는 거부터.

blocks.html: Bupmin isn’t alone at the gate. Jukji, his friend from the yard, has stood at the other post since dawn, saying nothing, which is normal, and writing nothing down, which isn’t.
blocks.ko: 문 앞의 법민은 혼자가 아니다. 연무장 친구 죽지가 새벽부터 맞은편 기둥 곁에 서 있다. 아무 말도 하지 않는 건 늘 그렇고, 아무것도 적지 않는 건 처음이다.

blocks.html: In the afternoon a cart comes up the west road under the Queen’s pennant. She has raised the dead of the inner gate in rank and sent for their families. It is what a court does when it has nothing else to give.
blocks.ko: 오후에 여왕의 깃발을 단 수레 하나가 서쪽 길로 올라온다. 여왕은 안문에서 죽은 이들의 관등을 올리고, 그 식구들을 서울로 불러들였다. 줄 것이 그것밖에 없을 때 조정이 하는 일이다.

blocks.html: The cart is for Jukji. His mother climbs down with his two little brothers and a joint of bamboo wrapped in a skirt.
blocks.ko: 수레는 죽지 몫이다. 어머니가 어린 동생 둘을 데리고 내린다. 치마에 싼 대나무 한 마디도 함께.

blocks.speaker: Jukjuk’s wife
en: They made your father a geupchan.
Four ranks up.
…He’d have called that bending.

blocks.speaker: Jukjuk’s wife
en: He’d have said it louder.
He said to plant this wherever we end up.
lines: 어디 가서 살든 이거 심으라 카더라.

blocks.html: Jukji takes the bamboo in both hands, the way he takes a ledger. Bupmin watches him, then looks back at his own road, which stays empty all day.
blocks.ko: 죽지는 장부를 받듯 두 손으로 대나무를 받는다. 법민은 그를 지켜보다가, 다시 제 길로 눈을 돌린다. 그 길은 해가 지도록 비어 있다.

blocks.html: They plant it that week behind a small house in Surabol, and it takes. Jukji will spend his life learning the other half of what bamboo does, which is bend. His father would have hated it. It will hold up a kingdom.
blocks.ko: 그 주에 서라벌의 작은 집 뒤에 그것을 심는다. 뿌리를 내린다. 죽지는 평생 대나무가 하는 나머지 반쪽을 배우며 살게 된다. 휘는 법이다. 아버지라면 질색했을 것이다. 그 휘는 법이 나라 하나를 떠받친다.

blocks.html: In Pyongyang, Yeon has spent all summer bowing. Now he is throwing a party, and everyone important is invited…!
blocks.ko: 평양에서 연은 여름 내내 고개를 숙였다. 이제 그가 잔치를 연다. 중요한 사람은 빠짐없이 초대받았다…!

logline.en: All summer he has bowed. Now he’s hosting a banquet, and the king is coming.
logline.ko: 여름 내내 그는 고개를 숙였다. 이제 그가 잔치를 연다. 왕도 온다.

DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.at: Yeon enthrones the king’s nephew as King Bojang
images.alt: The new king is crowned by the man who killed the last one.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. The same shot, at night in the Goguryeo palace at Pyongyang, torchlight. King Bojang, pale and frightened, takes the Goguryeo crown; the hands lowering it are armoured and bloody at the cuff. The spirit line behind him: King Yeongnyu nearest, murdered tonight, still in his feast robe, looking down at his nephew; then older Goguryeo kings fading into smoke. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = bojang, SECOND face = yeongnyu (an ancestral spirit in the frame). Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_pyongyang_fortress (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), crown reference (shape only). KING BOJANG — Crown: Goguryeo gold crown: a gold band crowded with upright flame and branch sprays hung with small round gold spangles; at court the king may instead wear the tall silk cap of the king on the costume chart. Colour #8f4a44. KING YOUNGRYU — Crown: Goguryeo gold crown: a gold band crowded with upright flame and branch sprays hung with small round gold spangles; at court the king may instead wear the tall silk cap of the king on the costume chart. Colour #a83b34. PLACE pyongyang_fortress — attached board /pl_pyongyang_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Pyongyang fortress: the same red two-tier munru on the stone ridge in every still. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.

blocks.html: Everyone in Pyongyang agrees that a man who bows all summer has learned his place.
blocks.ko: 여름 내내 고개를 숙인 사내라면 제 분수를 배운 것이다. 평양에서는 다들 그렇게 생각한다.

blocks.html: The Summit takes the whole summer to hand the son his father’s seal. When it finally does, Yeon decides to host a banquet, the one he promised the night Dosuryu came. The king is in attendance.
blocks.ko: 제가회의는 아버지의 인장을 아들에게 넘기는 데 여름 한 철을 다 쓴다. 마침내 넘기자, 연은 연회를 열기로 한다. 도수류가 찾아왔던 그 밤에 약속한 잔치다. 왕도 자리한다.

blocks.html: All summer he has bowed. He went to every seat at the Summit one at a time and asked for his father’s seal like a younger son asking for an inheritance. Among themselves they have already agreed that he will have it for one winter, out on the border forts, and not come back.
blocks.ko: 여름 내내 그는 고개를 숙였다. 제가회의의 자리를 하나하나 찾아가, 막내아들이 유산을 청하듯 아버지의 인장을 청했다. 그들끼리는 이미 정해 두었다. 인장은 주되, 한 겨울만. 변경의 성 쌓는 데로 보내고, 돌아오지 못하게.

blocks.label: The Banquet
blocks.ko: 연회

blocks.html: October cold sits under the eaves. The lamps are already lit when the Five Commanderies take their seats — wine first, then meat, then the old joke that Pyongyang never runs out of either. Each commander wears a ring-pommel sword at his hip, the three-legged crow stamped in the ring. The hall smells of sesame oil and autumn horse-sweat brought in on Eastern boots.
blocks.ko: 시월의 냉기가 처마 아래 앉아 있다. 오부가 자리에 들 때 등불은 이미 켜져 있다 — 술 먼저, 고기 다음, 그리고 평양엔 둘 다 마르지 않는다는 낡은 농담. 욕살마다 허리에 환두대도를 찼고, 고리에는 삼족오가 찍혀 있다. 전각에서는 참기름 냄새와, 동부의 군화가 들여온 가을 말땀 냄새가 난다.

blocks.html: Yeon stands first, before the king can. He has a cup in one hand and his father’s seal on his belt, and he smiles at the room like a good host.
blocks.ko: 왕보다 먼저 연이 일어선다. 한 손엔 잔, 허리엔 아버지의 인장. 그는 좋은 주인답게 방 안을 향해 웃는다.

lines: 저 자리에 열두 해 앉았다가 백발로 돌아온 우리 아바지를 위하여.
기 양반 말에 수긍하는 데 여름 한 철밖에 안 걸린 제가회의를 위하여.
얼굴 한 번 보면 안 잊는 우리 숙부를 위하여. 기리고 폐하를 위하여.
쭉 드시라우. 목마른 채로 이 전각을 나가는 사람은 없을 거우다.
en: A cup! Everyone, a cup!
To my father, who sat in that chair twelve years and came home grey.
To the Summit, which took only one summer to agree with him.
To my uncle, who never forgets a face. And to His Majesty.
Drink up. Nobody leaves this hall thirsty.

blocks.html: They drink. Every one of them.
blocks.ko: 그들은 마신다. 하나도 빠짐없이.

lines: 아, 그 명망 높은 개소문도 이제 고개 숙일 줄을 아는구나…
en: Ah — so even the renowned Gesomun has learned to bow…
Your father would have liked to see it.
Good — everyone is here.
We settle the succession today.
Gesomun! So you kneel at last!
Ah—

lines: 제가... 이제 신의 운명은 신이 책임지려 합니다...!
en: I… will take responsibility for my own fate from now on…!
May Your Majesty live ten thousand years….!

blocks.html: Every door in the hall closes at once, from the outside.
blocks.ko: 전각의 문이 바깥에서 한꺼번에 닫힌다.

blocks.html: The side doors were never for servants. When they open again, Yeon’s soldiers come through every one of them. Tables overturn. Wine becomes a darker color before anyone names it. Yeon does not shout orders. He walks the length of the room the way a man walks a border he has already decided to keep, and he takes each commander’s blade himself.
blocks.ko: 옆문은 원래 하인을 위한 것이 아니었다. 다시 열릴 때, 그 문마다 연의 군사들이 들이닥친다. 상이 뒤집힌다. 술이, 누가 이름 붙이기 전에, 더 어두운 색이 된다. 연은 명령을 외치지 않는다. 이미 지키기로 한 국경을 걷듯 전각을 가로지르며, 장수들의 칼은 제 손으로 거둔다.

blocks.html: First the Southern Commander. He wanted the next levy for Yushin’s passes, and called Eastern fighting easy work.
blocks.ko: 먼저 남부 욕살. 유신의 고개를 막겠다며 다음 징발을 달라 했고, 동부의 싸움은 쉬운 일이라 하던 자.

en: Yeon…!
Samhan… the Samhan His Majesty named—

lines: 지난번엔 이게 내 턱 밑에 있었지.
연설 말고 병력을 달라 했지. 병력은 내가 가져가오.
en: Son Deha.
Last time, this was under my chin.
You asked for men, not speeches. I am taking the men.

blocks.html: He draws the Southern ring-pommel from a belt that no longer needs it. The grip is still smooth. One crow. One weight on the spine to come.
blocks.ko: 더 이상 필요하지 않은 허리띠에서 남부의 환두를 뽑는다. 손잡이는 여전히 매끈하다. 삼족오 하나. 앞으로 등에 올릴 무게 하나.

blocks.html: Then the Northern Commander. He would not freeze another winter while the capital counted his remounts twice.
blocks.ko: 다음은 북부 욕살. 중앙이 보충 말을 두 번 세는 동안 또 한 겨울을 얼고 싶지는 않다던 자.

en: The horses… still in… the warehouses…
blocks.art: In his own blood, still counting.

en: Go Ul.
…The three villages. I remember them.

blocks.html: The Northern crow joins the first, frost-nicks and all. Outside, a horse screams in the yard and then does not.
blocks.ko: 서리에 이 빠진 북부의 삼족오가 첫 번째에 더해진다. 바깥 마당에서 말이 울다 만다.

blocks.html: The Western Commander had warned that this would gift the West a road. He dies looking west, as if the road might still be argued shut.
blocks.ko: 서부 욕살은 이러다 당에게 길을 선물하게 된다고 경고했었다. 그는 서쪽을 보며 죽는다. 그 길을 아직 말로 닫을 수 있다는 듯이.

blocks.html: A palace boy with his first spear stands it between himself and the door. It does not help. Yeon steps over him the way a man steps over a threshold, and somebody’s son stays on the floor of the room he was told to guard.
blocks.ko: 첫 창을 든 궁궐 소년이 창을 세워 자신과 문 사이를 막는다. 소용없다. 연은 문지방 넘듯 그를 넘어간다. 누군가의 아들이 지키라던 방 바닥에 남는다.

en: The Liao…
The Emperor’s drums…
You were right about the road.

blocks.html: Three crows. The third still smells of Liao timber. The hall’s lamps lean as if listening.
blocks.ko: 삼족오 셋. 세 번째에선 아직 요하 목재 냄새가 난다. 전각의 등불이 듣는 것처럼 기운다.

blocks.html: Lee Gesa carries no banner. He is the Summit’s clerk, and he wrote its verdict on Yeon: one winter on the border, and do not come back. Tonight he has wine in his mouth, and then nothing.
blocks.ko: 이가사는 깃발을 든 적이 없다. 대대로 회의의 서기이고, 연에게 내린 판결을 제 손으로 적었다. 국경에서 겨울 한 철, 그리고 돌아오지 말 것. 오늘 밤 그의 입에는 술이 있고, 그다음엔 아무것도 없다.

en: Traitor…!
That day… I…

lines: 그대는 내게 겨울 한 철을 적어 주었소.
en: Lee Gesa.
You wrote me one winter.
I am giving you one night.

blocks.html: Four. Ink on the grip, and now something on the edge. The verdict becomes metal he can wear.
blocks.ko: 넷. 손잡이엔 먹, 이제 날에도 무언가. 그에게 내린 판결이, 멜 수 있는 쇠가 된다.

blocks.html: Last of the banners: his uncle. The soft voice that told a nephew to sit down, because the Summit does not run on prophecies.
blocks.ko: 깃발의 마지막은 숙부다. 제가회의는 예언으로 돌아가지 않는다며 조카에게 앉으라 하던, 그 부드러운 목소리.

en: Nephew…
Traitor… a feast… like this…
blocks.art: Almost kindly, which hurts more.

en: Uncle.
You told me to sit down.
You called me traitor for standing.
A Yeon takes this one from a Yeon.

blocks.html: Five ring-pommels. Five crows. The first sword comes off the High Commander’s belt last, stone haetae and all. Yeon wipes none of them clean.
blocks.ko: 환두 다섯. 삼족오 다섯. 첫 칼이 막리지의 허리에서 마지막으로 풀린다. 돌 해태째. 연은 하나도 닦지 않는다.

blocks.html: He finally approaches King Youngryu for the final blow. The crown has slid. The Samhan dream is still in the king’s mouth, too late to be a budget.
blocks.ko: 마침내 영류왕 앞에 선다 — 마지막 일격. 면류관이 비뚤어져 있다. 삼한의 꿈은 아직 왕의 입에 남아, 예산이 되기엔 너무 늦다.

en: Gesomun…
With gold… decades…
The King for All…

lines: 금으로 될 일이 아니었습니다. 서국 황제는 이미 폐하의 목값을 매겨 두었으니.
en: Your Majesty.
The gold was never going to be enough. The Western emperor had already priced your head.
May You live ten thousand years.

blocks.html: The blade goes in under the ribs, the way the drill teaches, and the king folds over the Samhan dream like a man finishing a letter. His last breath moves the crown where it lies. It does not roll. Nothing in the room rolls. A hundred commanders are already down, and the boy at the door makes it a hundred and one.
blocks.ko: 칼은 교본대로 갈빗대 아래로 들어간다. 임금은 편지를 끝내는 사람처럼 삼한의 꿈 위로 접힌다. 마지막 숨이 떨어진 왕관을 흔든다. 구르지는 않는다. 방 안의 아무것도 구르지 않는다. 지휘관 백이 이미 쓰러졌고, 문가의 소년이 백하나째가 된다.

blocks.html: Yeon places each of the Five Blades onto his own back.
blocks.ko: 연은 다섯 자루의 칼을 모두 제 등에 짊어진다.

blocks.html: He wore five swords on his body, and no one around him dared look up at him. Every time he mounted or dismounted, he made nobles and generals lie on the ground and stepped on them.
blocks.ko: 몸에 칼 다섯 자루를 차니, 좌우가 감히 우러러보지 못하였다. 말에 오르내릴 때마다 늘 귀인과 무장을 땅에 엎드리게 하고 그를 밟았다.
blocks.hanja: 身佩五刀，左右莫敢仰視。每上下馬，常令貴人、武將伏地而履之。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 49, Biographies — Yeon Gaesomun
blocks.claim: He wore five swords, and stood on men to mount.
blocks.claimKo: 그는 칼 다섯 자루를 찼고, 사람을 밟고 말에 올랐다.

blocks.html: He was imposing and handsome, with a fine beard, and his cap and robes were all trimmed in gold. He wore five swords, and no one around him dared look up. He made nobles lie on the ground and stepped on them to mount his horse.
blocks.ko: 생김새가 우람하고 빼어났으며 수염이 아름다웠고, 관과 옷을 모두 금으로 꾸몄다. 칼 다섯 자루를 차니 좌우가 감히 우러러보지 못하였다. 귀인을 땅에 엎드리게 하고 그를 밟고 말에 올랐다.
blocks.hanja: 貌魁秀，美須髯，冠服皆飾以金，佩五刀，左右莫敢仰視。使貴人伏諸地，踐以升馬。
blocks.source: Xin Tangshu (新唐書) bk. 220, Eastern Barbarians — Goguryeo

blocks.html: He steps into the doorway with the blades on his back. Red-wing chalgap fills the door.
blocks.ko: 그가 칼들을 등에 진 채 문간에 선다. 붉은 날개 찰갑이 문을 가득 채운다.
blocks.art: Worm’s-eye from the hall floor: Yeon in the doorway, steel lamellar and red-wing shoulder cloth filling the frame.

lines: 고구려의 충신들은 이 연개소문의 말을 들으시오!
서쪽에서는 황제가 나라를 하나씩 도륙하며 이리로 오고 있소!
그동안 무능한 임금과 썩은 신하들은 눈을 감고, 이 나라를 망국의 길로 끌고 갔소!!
오늘은 신라와 동쪽, 내일은 백제, 그다음은 당이오!
en: Loyal men of Goguryeo — hear the words of Yeon Gesomun!
In the south, Baekje and Silla covet us,
and in the west the Second Emperor comes this way, butchering nation after nation!
And all the while an incompetent king and rotten ministers shut their eyes to the world and lead this country down the road to ruin!!
Silla and the East, then Baekje the next day, then the West!

lines: 그러면 백성은 어찌 되오? 우리는 갈 데가 없소!
이 땅에서 살고 이 땅에서 죽고, 저들이 올 때마다 피 흘리는 건 우리요!
세상은 우릴 미쳤다 할 거우다! 기렇갓디 — 제 운명 제 손으로 쥐는 건 언제나 세상 눈엔 미친 짓이었으니끼니!
en: But what of the people? We have nowhere else to go!
We live on this land, we die on it, and we are the ones who bleed every time they come!
The world will call us mad! Of course — to take your own fate in your own hands has always looked like madness to the world!

lines: 우리를 구하러 오는 자는 없소!! 오직 우리래, 우리 손으로 해야 하우다!!
en: No one is coming to save us!! Only we can do it — with our own hands!!

blocks.html: In the aftermath, Yeon enthrones the king’s nephew as King Bojang and creates a new position for himself, as the Supreme Commander.
blocks.ko: 연은 왕의 조카를 보장왕으로 세우고, 스스로를 위한 새 자리를 만든다 — 대막리지.

en: You there… what is your name?
M-my name? My surname is Go—
You there… what is your name?

blocks.caption: The old king’s nephew. He has been given a crown and very little to do with it.
blocks.ko: 옛 임금의 조카. 왕관은 받았는데, 그걸로 할 일은 별로 받지 못했다.

blocks.caption: A chair he built himself, above every other chair in the room.
blocks.ko: 스스로 짠 자리. 방 안의 모든 자리 위에 있다.

blocks.html: He makes one more appointment before the blood is dry. Dosuryu — an old friend of the Yeon house, one of the few men who has ever told him no and lived — is named Grand Herald, a post that did not exist until the banquet needed a voice that was not the throne’s.
blocks.ko: 피가 마르기 전에 임명 하나를 더 한다. 도수류 — 연씨 집안의 오랜 벗, 그에게 아니라고 말하고도 살아남은 몇 안 되는 사람 — 을 대대로에 앉힌다. 연회가 왕좌가 아닌 목소리를 필요로 하기 전까지는 없던 자리이다.

lines: 내래 네 아바지 살아 계실 때부터 네 뒷덜미를 잡던 사람인데.
en: Grand Herald…
I have had you by the scruff since your father was alive.
And now you want that mouth to read the country aloud?
If you will not, who will.
That Bojang… I only need the name.
The one who speaks to the people is you.

lines: 다만 — 네래 내 말을 들을 때만이야.
안 들으면 나는 전령이디, 친구가 아니야.
en: Very well.
Only — for as long as you still listen to me.
If you stop, I am a herald, not a friend.

blocks.html: Yeon listens. Not always. Often enough that the court learns which door to fear besides his.
blocks.ko: 연은 듣는다. 늘은 아니다. 그래도 조정이, 그를 빼고도 두려워할 문이 하나 더 있다는 걸 배울 만큼은.

blocks.label: The Temples
blocks.ko: 절집

blocks.html: After the blood dries, Yeon looks at the temples. They are rich, and they pray for whoever is winning. He has an idea about that, which can wait. One young monk named Shinsung learns how to wait too.
blocks.ko: 피가 마른 뒤 연은 절들을 본다. 부자이고, 누가 이기든 이기는 쪽을 위해 비는 절들이다. 거기에 대해 그는 생각이 하나 있다. 그건 기다려도 된다. 신성이라는 젊은 스님도 기다리는 법을 배운다.

en: Pray quieter.
Or pray to something that does not own half the capital.
lines: 아니면 수도 절반을 소유하지 않은 것한테 기도하라우.

blocks.caption: A monk of Pyongyang. Very quiet, and very well connected.
blocks.ko: 평양의 승려. 아주 조용하고, 아는 사람이 아주 많다.

en: Amitabha.
blocks.art: Bows.

blocks.html: What has the most strength? Forbearance is the strongest. One who forbears bears no grudge, and is sure to be honoured among men.
blocks.ko: 무엇이 가장 힘이 센가? 참는 것이 가장 굳세다. 참는 이는 원한을 품지 않으니, 반드시 사람들의 존경을 받는다.
blocks.hanja: 何者多力？忍辱最健，忍者無怨，必為人尊。
blocks.source: Sutra of Forty-two Sections (四十二章經), attr. Kāśyapa Mātaṅga & Zhu Falan · T17n0784, p. 722c

blocks.label: AFTER THE KNIVES
blocks.ko: 칼이 마른 뒤

blocks.html: In the markets the news arrives the way all bad news arrives — ahead of the official word, behind the smell of smoke. Grain sellers count on their fingers. Children stop racing. Someone says banquet and means blood.
blocks.ko: 저잣거리에 소식이 닿는 법은, 나쁜 소식이 늘 닿는 법과 같다 — 공식 말보다 먼저, 연기 냄새보다 늦게. 곡식 장수가 손가락을 접는다. 아이들이 달리기를 멈춘다. 누군가 연회라 말하고 피를 뜻한다.

blocks.speaker: Vendor
en: The king… they say he’s dead.
The commanders too. More than a hundred.

blocks.speaker: Wall sentry
lines: 어떤 이들은 영원의 대장군이 우릴 살렸다 하디.
조정에서 먼저 칼을 갈았대. 담은 우리였갓디. 평민들은… 연보다 기 이름을 먼저 불러.
en: Some say the Eternal General saved us.
The court was sharpening first. We were next. Commoners… we say that name before we say Yeon.

lines: 기 칼… 다섯 자루를 등에 맸다더라.
en: Those blades… they say he strapped five of them to his back.
The commanders’ swords. On his own spine.
By Haemosu’s light… incredible…
No — terrifying. Incredible, and terrifying.

blocks.speaker: Quiet man
lines: 기래도… 연회장에서 베는 게 나라를 구하는 거네.
en: Still… is butchering a banquet the same as saving a country.
blocks.art: Low.

blocks.speaker: Wall sentry
en: Dinnae say that on the wall.

blocks.html: On the barracks steps the same argument runs until the drum tells them to stop arguing and start marching.
blocks.ko: 병영 층계에서도 같은 논쟁이 돌다가, 북이 다투지 말고 행진하라 이른다.

blocks.html: The capital learns a new etiquette. Officials swear loyalty to the Supreme Commander’s door, not the nephew-king’s smile. Envoys who ask for an audience are told the kingdom is closed for inventory: of grain, of blades, of who belongs inside the walls.
blocks.ko: 도읍이 새 예법을 배운다. 관리들은 조카왕의 미소가 아니라 대막리지의 문에 충성을 맹세한다. 알현을 청하는 사신은 나라가 재고 조사 중이라는 말을 듣고 돌아간다. 곡식과, 칼과, 성 안에 남을 자격의.

blocks.label: The Yeon House
blocks.ko: 연씨 집

blocks.html: At night the house is quieter than the city. Yeon’s wife has kept three boys from the sound of cheering that is not quite cheer. She waits until the lamps are few enough that even a Supreme Commander looks like a husband.
blocks.ko: 밤이 되면 집은 도읍보다 고요하다. 연씨부인은 환호가 아닌 환호 소리로부터 아들 셋을 막아 두었다. 등불이 적어져 대막리지조차 남편처럼 보일 때까지 기다린다.

lines: 바깥에서 우리 겨레를 어떻게 부를디… 생각만 해도—
en: What will the West say…
Silla too. Baekje.
Massacre. Traitor.
How those outside will name our people… even thinking of it—

lines: 들어… 데것들이 우리에 대해 뭐라 하든, 일없어.
들리네? 전혀. 제로. 한 톨도 아니야.
en: Listen… it doesn’t matter what they’ll say about us.
Do you hear me? It doesn’t matter at all — zero. Not even one bit.

lines: 데것들 조상이 이 흙을 위해 죽어 줬네?
우리래 피 흘릴 차례가 오면, 데것들이 여기 서 있어 주갓네?
en: Did their ancestors die for this dirt?
Will they be standing here when it is our turn to bleed?

lines: 기러니 바깥에서 우리 겨레를, 우리 사는 법을 뭐라 하든 —
네 인생 단 일 초도 거기 쓰디 마. 제발.
en: So whatever they say out there about our people, our way of living —
not one second of your life. Please.
Look at me. Promise me.

lines: 다만 — 아이들이 자라면, 당신은 그 말도 해 주시라요.
en: …I promise.
Only — when the boys are grown, tell them that too.

blocks.html: He nods. Outside, the drums keep time for a kingdom learning to live with its doors shut.
blocks.ko: 그는 끄덕인다. 바깥에서는, 문을 닫고 사는 법을 배우는 나라의 북이 박자를 맞춘다.

blocks.html: A kingdom with its doors shut, and a man with five swords on his back. Naturally, Chunchu wants to go and knock…!
blocks.ko: 문을 걸어 잠근 나라, 그리고 칼 다섯 자루를 등에 멘 사내. 그러니 당연히, 춘추는 그 문을 두드리러 가겠다고 한다…!

logline.en: To save Silla, Chunchu has to walk into Pyongyang and ask the most dangerous man in Samhan for a favour.
logline.ko: 신라를 살리려면, 춘추는 평양으로 걸어 들어가 삼한에서 가장 위험한 사내에게 부탁을 해야 한다.
