images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 movie still. 2D cel-painterly webtoon. A dark corridor, crushed black, ONE hard shaft grazing Kim Chunchu's face and a single daegeum. The rest of his magenta robe falls into black. Dutch angle, he is in the lower third. Only ONE flute, horizontal at his mouth, bamboo with a blue wrap, matching the instrument ref. No second flute in the foreground. Foreground is a blurred timber post and creamy bokeh, not another instrument. FACE and magenta robe from the portrait, shoulder-length hair, small goatee. Lips at the embouchure, eyes lowered, quiet, not shouting. Background giwa in bokeh. No glow. No text. No watermark.

images.alt: One huge black brush mass fills the left, flying white at its edge, and thins to a point.
images.prompt: Original sumi on white paper. No pasted face. Story: Chunchu's revenge is a long shadow. One huge black brush mass fills the left, flying white at its edge, and thins to a point. A tiny mark stands at the dark end. A small magenta bleed only in that mark. No text, no seal.

images.at: His left hand is a red glove.
images.alt: Caravaggio’s Ecce Homo: Chunchu presented between two attendants, bleeding hand lifted, face perfectly composed
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Caravaggio’s Ecce Homo. Tight three-figure frame in a dark Pyongyang palace corridor at night: Chunchu stands between two attendants who grip his arms, his left hand lifted a little before him, red and dripping, his face calm and almost amused. Dosuryu leans in from the right edge in profile, hand on his sword hilt, the ring-pommel catching the light. One torch off frame left rakes hard across Chunchu’s face, the blood and Dosuryu’s blade; a guard’s spear tip glints in the black behind. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — KIM CHUNCHU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_chunchu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Demeanor: Diplomat and strategist: talks with his hands, smiles while calculating, never shouts; half-lidded watchful eyes. #D8258C as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: front-line armored warrior pose; shouting battle face; katana. | DOSURYU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_dosuryu.png (face only; invent a new pose). #c98578 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). Pyongyang: Goguryeo walled city on the Taedong, stone walls and red munru gate pavilions. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). COMMONERS in every Samhan kingdom wear SIMPLE WHITE: plain undyed white or off-white hemp and ramie jackets, wide trousers and skirts, a cloth sash, straw sandals or bare feet, hair in a plain topknot or braid — no dyed silk, no dots, no gold; colour belongs to rank, so a crowd of farmers, porters, servants and townsfolk reads as a field of soft white cloth with the officials' colours standing out of it. Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Every morning since Daeya, Chunchu asks the Queen for the same thing. Every morning she says no.
blocks.ko: 대야성이 떨어진 뒤로 아침마다 춘추는 여왕께 같은 것을 청한다. 아침마다 여왕은 안 된다고 한다.

blocks.html: He wants to go north to Pyongyang and borrow an army against Baekje. Then news comes down from the north, a month late, the way it always does.
blocks.ko: 북쪽 평양에 가서 백제를 칠 군사를 빌려 오겠다는 것이다. 그러다 북쪽 소식이 내려온다. 늘 그렇듯 한 달 늦게.

en: What…! The King of Goryeo, murdered by his own subject?

lines: 허 참… 난 우리나라가 먼저 망하는 줄 알았더니, 고려가 먼저 가는구먼. 그래, 그 신하는 또 누군가?
en: Well I never… I thought our country would fall first, and Goryeo goes ahead of us. So who is this subject?

lines: 영원의 대장군이라 부릅니다 — 연, 혹은 개소문. 평민들은 조정이 못 들을 때 평양의 붉은 해라고 하지요.
en: They call him the Eternal General — Yeon, or Gesomun. Commoners say Red Sun of Pyongyang when they think courts cannot hear.
“Yeon Gesomun”…

lines: 그런 자에게 자네가 부탁을 하러 가겠다고?
en: A man who kills his own king at a banquet.
And you want to go and ask him for a favour.

lines: 그런 자라야 아직 "예"라고 할 수 있습니다, 폐하.
다른 이들은 다 회의에 물어야 하니까요.
en: A man like that is the only kind who can still say yes, Majesty.
Everyone else has to ask a council.
And what will it cost?
Only me. I’m cheap.

lines: 자네가 하는 일 중에 싼 건 없네, 춘추.
…가게. 내가 더 좋은 질문을 떠올리기 전에.
en: Nothing you do is cheap, Chunchu.
…Go. Before I think of a better question.

blocks.html: The Queen lets him go. Nobody offers to go instead.
blocks.ko: 여왕이 그를 보낸다. 대신 가겠다는 사람은 없다.

lines: 공이 가서 돌아오지 않는다면, 내 흰 말의 말발굽이 반드시 고려 왕정을 짓밟을 것이오.
en: If you go and do not return, my white horse will trample Goryeo underfoot without fail.

lines: 60일 이내면 돌아올 것인데 이때에도 돌아오지 않는다면 다시 볼 기약이 없을 것입니다.
en: I will return within sixty days. If I have not returned by then, there will be no promise of meeting again.

blocks.label: The Envoy
blocks.ko: 사신

blocks.label: The West Gate
blocks.ko: 서문

blocks.html: He leaves by the west gate of the Moon Palace on Hadong, a lean red bay he named for summer and winter, because a diplomat’s horse, he says, has to stand in both. Yushin walks beside the bridle as far as the gate and no farther, which for Yushin is a speech.
blocks.ko: 그는 하동을 타고 월성 서문으로 떠난다. 여름과 겨울에서 이름을 딴 마른 적갈색 말. 사신의 말은 둘 다 견뎌야 한다고, 그는 말한다. 유신은 굴레 옆을 걸어 문까지만 따라오고 그 이상은 오지 않는다. 유신에게 그건 연설이다.

blocks.caption: Sixty days there and back, through a country that has just killed its own king. He packs light.
blocks.ko: 가고 오는 데 육십 일. 방금 제 왕을 죽인 나라를 지나는 길이다. 짐은 가볍게 꾸린다.

en: Sixty days.
He knows the way back. Even if you forget.
You’re saying he’s smarter than me.
…Hear that, Hadong? Yushin trusts you.
It’s you I don’t trust.

blocks.label: Pyongyang
blocks.ko: 평양

blocks.html: Pyongyang lets him in through the red gate and keeps him waiting on the stair. When someone finally comes down, it is Dosuryu, the Grand Herald.
blocks.ko: 평양은 붉은 문루로 그를 들이고, 층계에서 기다리게 한다. 마침내 누가 내려오는데, 대대로 도수류다.

en: Your Excellency…

blocks.html: Chunchu requests to see the king.
blocks.ko: 춘추가 왕의 알현을 청한다.

blocks.html: King Bojang makes his request — though the word his is doing generous work, and everyone in the room knows for whom.
blocks.ko: 보장왕이 요구를 내놓는다 — 그의라는 말이 꽤 후하게 쓰인 셈이고, 방 안의 모두가 그것이 실은 누구의 요구인지 안다.

blocks.html: The price is simple. Give back the passes Silla took.
blocks.ko: 값은 간단하다. 신라가 가져간 고개들을 돌려 달라는 것이다.

en: Oi, Silla — why the long face?
And call it Goguryeo.
Not Goryeo. I am not tired enough to shorten my own country.
lines: 고려가 아니라. 내 나라를 줄일 만큼 지치지 않았다.

en: Goguryeo, then — if the chronicles insist.
Most men I meet have already shortened it.
lines: 제가 만난 대부분은 이미 줄여 부릅니다.
이 땅의 위기를 기회 삼아 영토를 내놓으라 하실 수 있습니까?
저는 신하이니 어쩔 수 없지요. 처분만 기다리겠습니다. 그럼, 이만…
en: You would take this land’s crisis as your chance, and demand territory?
As a subject I have no say, so I await your judgement. And now — I take my leave…

lines: 남의 집에 들어와 값을 거절하고도 눈을 피하지 않는구나.
신라엔 자존심이 없나? 아니면 자네만 없나?
en: You come into another man’s house, refuse his price, and still look me in the eye.
Has Silla no pride left? Or is it only you?

lines: 저한테 자존심 같은 건 없습니다. 오직 목표만 있을 뿐이지요…!
그리고 그 길을 막는 자는 누구든, 갈가리 찢겨 곧장 지옥으로 갈 겁니다…!
en: I have no such thing as pride. I only have my goal…!
And whoever gets in my way will be ripped apart, straight into hell…!

blocks.html: Outside the door, two Goguryeo soldiers have been listening the way soldiers listen — professionally, and for sport.
blocks.ko: 문 밖에서는 고구려 병사 둘이, 병사들이 듣는 방식으로 — 직업적으로, 그리고 심심풀이로 — 듣고 있다.

lines: …대막리지 면전에 대고 기러고도, 눈 한 번을 안 깜빡여.
en: Did you hear him?
…Said it to the Supreme Commander’s face. Didn’t blink once.

lines: 신라 놈들은 염라대왕 앞에 폼 나게 끌려가고 싶을 때 데런 소리를 하디.
en: Silla men talk like that when they want to walk into Yumla’s court stylishly.

lines: 말린 생선 하나 걸디. 무릎으로 기어 나오갓디.
en: Bet you a dried fish he crawls out on his knees.
Bet you two he cries.

blocks.html: The door opens. Chunchu is escorted out between two attendants. His left hand is a red glove. Blood runs off the wrist and dots the stone like a trail someone meant to follow.
blocks.ko: 문이 열린다. 춘추가 시종 둘 사이에 호송되어 나온다. 왼손이 붉은 장갑이다. 피가 손목에서 흘러 돌바닥에 점점이 찍힌다. 누가 따라오라고 남긴 자국처럼.

en: …Ah?

lines: 왜 피가 나네. 성왕의 활에 맹세코, 왜 이리 피가 많네.
en: Why is there blood. By the Holy King’s bow, why is there so much blood.
Did—— did the Supreme Commander cut him?
Move. Prison.

lines: 옥? 저승사자 코앞까지 갔다 온 놈이 얼굴은 기대론데.
en: Prison? The man brushed past the death escort and he still has that face on.

blocks.label: The Cell
blocks.ko: 옥

blocks.html: They put him in a cell with a window. That is meant to be a courtesy. The courtesy does not include a physician.
blocks.ko: 그들은 창이 있는 방에 그를 가둔다. 나름의 예우라고 한다. 그 예우에는 의원은 포함되지 않는다.

en: (…Good. He looked. He will remember looking.)
blocks.art: Thought balloon.

blocks.html: What the guards do not know — what nobody in the corridor knows — is whose blade opened the hand. That answer waits in another man’s memory, for another meeting.
blocks.ko: 병사들이 모르는 것 — 복도의 그 누구도 모르는 것 — 은 누구의 칼이 그 손을 열었느냐다. 그 답은 다른 사람의 기억 속에, 다른 만남을 위해 기다려 둔다.

blocks.html: Chunchu has no physician, but he has a sleeve, and sewn into it is what a Silla envoy carries when he expects to be robbed. Somehow it reaches Sun Dohae, the king’s favourite, without passing through any door the Supreme Commander is watching.
blocks.ko: 춘추에게 의원은 없지만 소매는 있다. 그 안에는 털릴 각오를 한 신라 사신이 챙기는 것이 꿰매져 있다. 그것은 어찌어찌 대막리지가 지키는 어느 문도 지나지 않고 왕의 총신 선도해에게 닿는다.

blocks.html: Chunchu secretly gave three hundred measures of blue cloth to the king’s favourite, Sun Dohae.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 푸른 베 삼백 보를 왕의 총신 선도해에게 몰래 주었다.
blocks.hanja: 春秋以靑布三百步 密贈王之寵臣先道解
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Chunchu in Goguryeo, 642)

blocks.html: Sun Dohae arrives with a jar of wine and no guards, which is either courage or an arrangement. He pours two cups, drinks both when Chunchu does not reach for his, and starts talking about the sea.
blocks.ko: 선도해는 술 한 단지를 들고 호위도 없이 온다. 배짱이거나, 이미 말이 된 일이거나. 그는 두 잔을 따르고, 춘추가 손을 뻗지 않자 두 잔을 다 마신 뒤, 바다 이야기를 꺼낸다.

lines: 손이 그래서야 잔을 들겠소. 내가 마셔 드리지.
……그런데 공, 거북이와 토끼 이야기 들어 보셨소?
en: Can’t hold a cup with a hand like that. I’ll drink it for you.
…Tell me, my lord. Ever heard the one about the turtle and the rabbit?

lines: ……들어 봤어도, 공의 입으로 다시 듣고 싶군요.
en: …Even if I had, I’d like to hear it from you.

lines: 동해 용왕의 딸이 가슴앓이를 했다지. 의원이 그러는 거요, 토끼 간이면 낫는다고.
바다에 토끼가 있나. 그래서 거북이가 뭍에 올라가 토끼한테 말을 걸어.
“저 바다 한가운데 섬이 있는데, 물 맑고 열매 많고, 매도 수리도 못 오는 데다. 가자, 내 등에 타라.”
en: The Dragon King of the Eastern Sea had a daughter with a sick heart. The physician said a rabbit’s liver would cure her.
No rabbits in the sea. So the turtle climbs up on land and strikes up a conversation with a rabbit.
“Out in the middle of the sea there’s an island. Clear water, fruit everywhere, no hawks, no eagles. Come on. Get on my back.”
And the rabbit got on.

lines: 탔지. 성왕께서 강 건너실 때도 거북이 등을 밟으셨으니, 거북이는 대개 믿을 만하거든. 대개는.
두어 리쯤 가서 거북이가 고개를 돌리고 실토를 해. 사실은 네 간이 필요하다고.
en: Got right on. The Holy King ran across a river on turtles’ backs, so turtles are generally trustworthy. Generally.
Two or three li out, the turtle turns his head and confesses. Actually, we need your liver.
And do you know what the rabbit said?

lines: “아이고, 나는 신령의 자손이라 오장을 꺼내 씻어 둘 수 있거든. 마침 요새 속이 답답해서 간을 꺼내 바위 밑에 말려 두고 왔지 뭐냐. 돌아가서 가져오자.”
거북이가 믿고 돌아갔지. 뭍에 닿자마자 토끼는 풀숲으로 쏙.
“멍청하긴. 간 없이 사는 놈이 어디 있냐.”
en: “Oh dear. I’m descended from spirits, I can take out my insides and wash them. My chest’s been tight lately, so I left my liver drying under a rock. Let’s go back and fetch it.”
The turtle believed him and turned around. The moment they touched the shore, the rabbit was into the grass.
“Idiot. Who lives without a liver?”

blocks.html: Sun Dohae refills his own cup and looks at nothing in particular. Chunchu looks at his ruined hand for a long time, then laughs once, quietly, the way a man laughs when a lock he has been picking turns over.
blocks.ko: 선도해는 제 잔을 다시 채우고 아무 데도 아닌 곳을 본다. 춘추는 망가진 손을 오래 내려다보다가, 한 번 조용히 웃는다. 붙들고 있던 자물쇠가 돌아갈 때 사람이 웃는 식으로.

en: …Could I trouble you for paper?
The left one’s in no state, so I’ll use the right.

blocks.html: The letter goes to the king, not the Supreme Commander. The passes were Goguryeo's to begin with, it says, and once Chunchu is home he will ask his sovereign to give them back. He signs with a flourish. He has no intention of doing any such thing. His drinking partner, finishing the jar, has no intention of mentioning it.
blocks.ko: 편지는 대막리지가 아니라 왕에게 간다. 그 고개들은 본래 고구려 땅이니, 돌아가면 제 임금께 돌려드리라 청하겠다고 적혀 있다. 춘추는 멋들어지게 서명한다. 그럴 생각은 털끝만큼도 없다. 술단지를 비우던 술친구도 그 말을 꺼낼 생각이 털끝만큼도 없다.

blocks.label: Sixty Days
blocks.ko: 예순 날

blocks.label: Surabol
blocks.ko: 서라벌

blocks.html: On the sixtieth day Yushin starts counting out men. He does not ask the Queen first.
blocks.ko: 예순째 되는 날, 유신은 병사를 헤아리기 시작한다. 여왕께 먼저 여쭙지 않는다.

blocks.html: She finds out anyway, from the stables, and comes down to the muster yard in a plain cloak as if nobody would recognise the only woman in Silla who walks like that.
blocks.ko: 그래도 그녀는 마구간에서 그 소식을 듣는다. 그리고 수수한 망토를 걸치고 소집 마당으로 내려온다. 신라에서 그렇게 걷는 여자가 자기 하나뿐이라는 걸 아무도 못 알아볼 것처럼.

en: You didn’t ask me.
You’d have said no, Majesty.

lines: 천천히 안 된다 했겠지. 내 말 끝나기 전에 자네는 떠났을 거고.
en: I’d have said no slowly. You’d have been gone by the end of it.
…Yes, Majesty.

lines: 그 아이 데려오게. 자네도 돌아오고. 둘 중 하나 골라야 하면—
en: Bring him back. Bring yourself back. If you have to choose which—
……Don’t choose.

blocks.html: He bows lower than the yard requires. When he straightens she is studying a saddle girth with great interest, and he finds he has to check his own sword is still there.
blocks.ko: 그는 마당이 요구하는 것보다 깊이 절한다. 허리를 펴 보니 그녀는 안장 뱃대끈을 몹시 흥미롭게 들여다보고 있다. 그는 자기 칼이 아직 허리에 있는지 확인해야 한다.

blocks.label: The Supreme Commander’s Desk
blocks.ko: 대막리지의 책상

blocks.html: In Pyongyang, Dosuryu brings Yeon two pieces of paper on the same morning. One is the envoy’s letter to the king. The other is a scout’s report from the border.
blocks.ko: 평양에서 도수류가 같은 날 아침 연에게 종이 두 장을 가져온다. 하나는 사신이 왕에게 쓴 편지다. 다른 하나는 국경에서 온 척후의 보고다.

lines: 편지엔 데놈이 제 여왕한테 고개를 돌려 달라 청하갓다고 써 있어.
이건 신라 군사 만이 국경에 진을 쳤다는 거고. 맨 앞에 흰 말이 있대.
en: The letter says he’ll ask his queen to give back the passes.
He won’t, of course.
This one says ten thousand Silla men are camped at the border. With a white horse at the front.
…What? The Sword of the Divine Country is coming?
…Let him go.
Sir?

lines: 기런데 진짜… 삼한에서 가장 교활한 자라는 이 춘추가 머이길래, 신라의 도검이 직접 온다는 거네?
en: Did you not hear me? Release Chunchu.
But truly… who is this Chunchu — the most cunning man in Samhan — that the Sword of Silla comes for him himself?

lines: 신라의 검이 누군데 영원의 대장군이 이렇게 펄쩍 뛰네?
en: Who is this Sword of Silla, that the Eternal General jumps like this?
Don’t tell me… you’re afraid?

lines: 형님, 아무리 죽을 각오를 한 자라도, 호랑이는 함부로 건드리는 게 아니우다.
우리도 언젠가 유신을 대적할 날이 오갓디…
하지만 춘추 따위로 기럴 건 아니우다.
en: Old man— even a man ready to die does not poke a tiger for no reason.
The day will come when we face Yushin…
but not over something like Chunchu.

lines: 저놈이 서명했소. 언젠가 내 앞에서 소리 내 읽게 할 거요.
en: Keep the letter.
He signed it. One day I’ll make him read it back to me.
That’s the win.

blocks.label: The Border Camp
blocks.ko: 국경 진영

blocks.html: On the Silla side of the border, in a camp that should not exist, Yushin has brought the horse. Hadong is tied at the front of the lines with an empty saddle, the way some armies carry an empty chair. When Chunchu comes down the last hill on foot, thinner, the left hand bound against his chest, the horse sees him before the men do.
blocks.ko: 국경 이쪽, 있어서는 안 될 진영에 유신은 그 말을 데려와 있다. 하동은 빈 안장을 얹은 채 대열 맨 앞에 매여 있다. 어떤 군대가 빈 의자를 메고 다니듯이. 춘추가 마지막 언덕을 걸어 내려올 때, 더 마르고, 왼손을 가슴에 동여맨 채, 사람들보다 말이 먼저 그를 알아본다.

lines: 니 살쪘데이. 유신이가 나보다 잘 먹였네.
en: …Hadong.
You got fat. Yushin fed you better than they fed me.
Hand.
…Give it here. The right one.

blocks.html: Chunchu cannot close the left hand on a rein, so Yushin ties both reins around his right wrist himself, in a knot he learned in the drill yard for men who have been shot. He says nothing about the hand, and Chunchu says nothing about the camp.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 왼손으로 고삐를 쥘 수 없다. 그래서 유신이 두 고삐를 그의 오른 손목에 직접 묶는다. 화살 맞은 사람을 위해 연병장에서 배운 매듭으로. 그는 손에 대해 아무 말도 하지 않고, 춘추도 진영에 대해 아무 말도 하지 않는다.

lines: 자네 진이 선 그날 아침에 내 방 문이 열렸네. 까닭도 없이.
en: They opened my door the morning your camp appeared. No reason given.
Perhaps he heard I was coming.
(…A more fearsome man than I expected. Both of them.)

blocks.caption: One envoy coming south, ten thousand Silla men coming north, and a border between them that has gone very polite.
blocks.ko: 남쪽으로 오는 사신 하나, 북쪽으로 가는 신라군 만 명. 그 사이의 국경은 갑자기 몹시 예의 바르다.

blocks.html: One envoy left Pyongyang bleeding. Whose blade was it? Now the King of Baekje walks in on purpose, laughing…!
blocks.ko: 사신 하나가 피를 흘리며 평양을 떠났다. 누구의 칼이었을까? 이번엔 백제의 왕이 제 발로 걸어 들어온다. 웃으면서…!

logline.en: Two new strongmen, one table. Yeon is surprised the King of Baekje came himself.
logline.ko: 새로 힘을 쥔 두 사내, 탁자 하나. 연은 백제 왕이 몸소 왔다는 게 놀랍다.

images.alt: Caravaggio’s Supper at Emmaus: Euija flings both arms wide laughing, Gesomun leans in over the sword on the table
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Caravaggio’s Supper at Emmaus. Low across a dark table in a closed Pyongyang room at night: a ring-pommel sword lies flat on the table between them, pointed at nothing. Right, Euija throws himself back in his chair with both arms flung wide, head tipped back, roaring with laughter. Left, Gesomun half-risen, leaning over the table on one fist beside the sword, glaring. One clay oil dish on the table edge is the only light, rakes across both faces from below and runs a bright streak down the blade; a wine jar and two cups catch it at the near edge; the walls are black. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — KING EUIJA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_buyeo_euija.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Broad, bearded king; black hair in a topknot with a yellow-gold headband whose tails trail; heavy brows, cynical eyes. Dress: Crimson robe with a dark charcoal collar and gold trim; a steel lamellar pauldron peeking at one shoulder. Demeanor: Licensed wit: drinks, smirks, slumps on the throne, speaks in polished aphorisms. Fatalist. Fighting: Tiger-ring sword is ceremonial; he barely draws it. #e08a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: heroic battle pose; smiling innocence. | YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. Sword: High Commander Blade — Ring-pommel High Commander Blade — haetae carved beneath the crow stamp; the 막리지검 of the Summit’s first chair. Pommel motif crow inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: FIVE crow-ring swords (身佩五刀): four crossed in a fan on his back with the hilts rising above his shoulders, plus one at the hip. Fighting: DUAL-WIELDS: a crow-ring sword in EACH hand, both forward one-hand grips, ring pommels at the heel of each fist. Wide aggressive stance, arms flung apart, scissoring cross-cuts and windmill slashes; lose one blade and he pulls another off his back. Each blade straight sw_bidam anatomy, 1:3. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: one sword in a fight; gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: King Euija hears how Goguryeo’s king died, and feels the one thing a king should never admit to. Envy.
blocks.ko: 의자왕은 고구려 왕이 어떻게 죽었는지 듣고, 왕이라면 절대 인정해선 안 될 감정을 느낀다. 부러움.

blocks.label: Sabi
blocks.ko: 사비

en: What…! The King of Goryeo, murdered by his own subject?
This is an opportunity…

lines: 회의 하나를 통째로, 저녁 한 끼에.
내가 그랬다간 사택 놈들이 나를 국에 넣어 끓일 겨.
en: A whole Summit, in one dinner.
If I tried that, the Satek would serve me in the soup.
Gyebek. We’re going north.
How many days.
As long as it takes. Forever, if he’s charming.
Forever is not a number, Majesty.
I will pack for twenty.

blocks.html: Other kings would write for troops. Euija rides north himself, with three men, one of them Gyebek counting the days. The man at the door does not give his name.
blocks.ko: 다른 왕이라면 군사를 청하는 편지를 쓸 것이다. 의자는 직접 북으로 간다. 데려가는 것은 셋, 그중 하나는 날짜를 세는 계백이다. 문 앞의 사내는 이름을 대지 않는다.

blocks.label: Pyongyang
blocks.ko: 평양

en: Have you come to see the king?
No… I have come to see the one with real power.
He does not grant an audience to just anyone.
Tell him who I am, and he will come at once.

blocks.html: Yeon is surprised that the new King of Baekje has come personally.
blocks.ko: 백제의 새 임금이 몸소 왔다는 사실에 연도 놀란다.

lines: 벽은 왕과 귀족세력을 싹 다 갈아엎어버렸다지요? 그거 하나만은 조금 부럽네...
en: I hear you ploughed under the king and the whole noble faction? That one thing, I rather envy…
Could you not do the same on your side?

lines: 나는 폭군 소리 듣고 그다음 날 죽을 거요, 참.
en: Look here — I am the king myself.
General Gesomun—
I would be called a tyrant and killed the next day, ah.

lines: 그대들이 저 바깥 성벽에서 우리 임금을 죽였소. 이 방에서도 보이는 저기서.
en: Your people killed a king of ours on that wall out there. You can see it from this room.

lines: 그럼 한성은? 우리 임금 목을 그쪽 성벽에 걸어 놓고 한 철 농사라 하지 않았소.
en: And Hansung? You put our king’s head on your own wall and called it a season’s work.

blocks.html: Once, a Goguryeo king came south and took Baekje’s old capital. The Baekje king tried to run. They caught him and killed him at the foot of a mountain. Baekje has not forgotten. Goguryeo has not apologised.
blocks.ko: 한때 고구려 왕이 남으로 내려와 백제의 옛 도읍을 빼앗았다. 백제 왕은 달아나려 했다. 그들은 그를 붙잡아 산 아래에서 죽였다. 백제는 잊지 않았다. 고구려는 사과하지 않았다.

lines: 게다가… 이 방에 있는 둘 중, 실제로 고려왕을 시해해 본 자는 하나뿐이고. 나는 아니외다.
en: Besides… of the two men in this room, only one has actually murdered a king of Goryeo. It was not me.

blocks.html: Yeon puts the blade on the table between them. Not pointed at anything. Just there.
blocks.ko: 연이 칼을 둘 사이의 상 위에 올려놓는다. 겨눈 것도 아니다. 그냥 거기에 놓아둔다.

blocks.html: Behind the king, Gyebek’s hand is already on his own hilt. Nobody saw it get there.
blocks.ko: 왕의 등 뒤에서 계백의 손은 이미 제 칼자루에 가 있다. 언제 갔는지 본 사람이 없다.

lines: 내가 지금 이 칼로 그대를 베지 말아야 할 이유를, 하나만 대 보시오…!
en: Give me one reason I should not cut you down with this blade where you stand…!
Four steps.
Three.

lines: 네 걸음이오. 몸을 뒤로 빼고 있소.
en: Four. You are leaning back.
Pfft—hahahahahaha!!

lines: 개소문 자네… 군사는 통솔할 줄 알아도, 정치는 딱 봐도 초보구려. 정치가 뭔지 아나?
정치는 연금술이야. 내가 이미 하고 싶은 일에다, 명분을 만들어 붙이는 연금술.
지금 이웃 나라 백성들 사이에 자네를 우러르는 자가 얼마나 되는지 아나?
연개소문 — 탐관오리를 싹 갈아엎고 새 시대를 열 사내.
그런데… 여기서 백제왕을 죽이면, 그 나라들에 죄다 소문이 나겠지.
자네는 임금 죽이기를 즐기는 미친놈이 되는 거야. 그것뿐이고.
en: Gesomun… you may know how to command an army, but in politics you are plainly a novice. Do you know what politics is?
Politics is alchemy. The alchemy of manufacturing a justification for what I already want to do.
Do you know how many people in the surrounding countries admire you right now?
Yeon Gesomun — the man who ploughed under the corrupt officials and will bring a new age.
But… kill the King of Baekje now, and word reaches every one of those countries.
You become a madman who enjoys killing kings. Nothing else.

lines: 고구려는 태양신의 피를 이은 성스러운 임금이 세운 나라요.
성왕. 해모수의 아들. 하늘에서 내려온 줄기요.
en: This land is not just dirt.
Goguryeo is the land of the holy king, descended from the sun god.
The Holy King. Son of Haemosu. A line that came down from heaven.

lines: 잠깐… 잠깐만. 지금 한 나라의 대막리지가 —
다 큰 사내가, 나라를 이끄는 사내가 —
en: Pfft—!!
Hahahahaha!!
Wait… wait. The Supreme Commander of a country —
a grown man, a man who leads a kingdom —
still believes in spirits and sun chariots?

lines: 그는 하늘에서 내려왔다. 활로 나라를 열었다.
en: Do not laugh.
He came down from heaven. He opened a kingdom with a bow.
That blood is the bone of these people.

lines: 아, 물론. 활 잘 쏘는 사내는 하나 있었겠지.
나머지는 백성 줄 세우려고 지은 이야기고.
농부를 무릎 꿇리는 데는, 칼보다 태양신이 싸게 먹히거든.
en: Oh, certainly. There was probably a man who shot well.
The rest is a story for keeping people in line.
To make a farmer kneel, a sun god is cheaper than a sword.

lines: 나는 들에서 자랐소. 들에서 들은 건 — 거짓이 아니오.
en: …So that is what your palace teaches.
I grew up in the marches. What the marches tell — is not a lie.

blocks.html: Yeon asks for the same thing he asked Chunchu for. He has only ever had one price.
blocks.ko: 연은 춘추에게 요구했던 것과 똑같은 것을 요구한다. 그의 값은 언제나 하나뿐이었다.

lines: 죽령 이북 땅은 본래 고구려의 것이었다. 돌려주면 구원병을 보내 주겠다.
en: The land north of the pass was Goguryeo’s. Return it, and I will send relief troops.

lines: 도대체 무슨 배짱으로 저 앞에 나선 건지…!
en: What nerve, to come before him like that…!

lines: 이보게, 나는 한 나라의 왕일세. 왕은 사람이 아니야.
죽을 자리까지 다 정해 두고 왔고, 바깥에도 미리 일러 두었네.
나를 죽여 봐야, 더 젊고 더 성난 백제왕이 하나 앉을 뿐이지.
en: Listen — I am the king of a country. A king is not a man.
I made my arrangements even for death, and gave warning abroad beforehand.
Kill me and all you get is a newer, angrier King of Baekje on the throne.
Not a man, you say…

lines: 신라에는 «노비는 사람 수에 넣지 않는다»는 말이 있다더군.
우습지 않소? 맨 아래도 사람이 아니고, 맨 위도 사람이 아니야.
사람인 것들은 전부 그 사이에 끼어 있고.
en: They have a saying in Silla — that slaves are not counted as people.
Funny, is it not? The bottom is not a person, and the top is not a person either.
Everyone who gets to be a person is wedged in between.

lines: 신라에는 바닷길이 없어. 당이든 천축이든 서역이든, 나가려면 이 항구 하나뿐이야.
en: Look at this map.
Silla has no trade route at all — for the West, for Tianzhu, for the western regions, there is only this one harbour.
Danghang Fortress would be the right target.

blocks.caption: One harbour. Silla’s only door to the West.
blocks.ko: 항구 하나. 신라가 당으로 나가는 단 하나의 문.

en: We have our own mouth — the White River under Sabi.
Clan berths stacked like teeth. Cut Danghang Fortress and Silla starves for partners; keep our river and we eat either way.
lines: 우리에겐 우리 하구가 있다 — 사비 아래 백강.
가문 선석이 이빨처럼 겹쳐 있지. 당항성을 끊으면 신라는 짝이 굶고, 우리 강만 지키면 우리는 어느 쪽이든 먹는다.

en: You sound like a harbour clerk.
Good. Kings who forget docks start wars they cannot feed.
lines: 좋다. 부두를 잊는 임금은, 먹일 수 없는 전쟁을 시작한다.

en: Do you know a “Kim Chunchu” of Silla?
Kim Chunchu? First I have heard of him… royalty? Why?

lines: 그냥… 궁금해서. 자네를 그리 좋아하는 것 같지가 않더군.
자네를 없애 달라고, 두 손 모아 빌더구먼.
en: Just… curious. He does not seem to care for you much.
He spoke of being rid of you, hands folded in prayer.

lines: 춘추라… 누군지는 몰라도, 그렇게 쌓아 두는 자는 만만치 않지.
허나 남에게 무릎 꿇는 자는 두렵지 않소이다.
en: Chunchu… whoever he is, a man who stores things up like that is no easy sort.
But I do not fear a man who kneels to others.

blocks.html: For a moment Yeon’s eyes go somewhere else — to a door, to a hand, to a stare that did not ask to be liked.
blocks.ko: 잠깐, 연의 눈이 다른 곳으로 간다 — 문과, 손과, 호감을 바라지 않던 눈빛으로.

blocks.html: After the territory talk the room had gone quiet in the wrong way. Yeon had asked if the man had no pride. The answer had been worse than no.
blocks.ko: 영토 이야기가 끝난 뒤 방은 잘못된 방식으로 조용해졌다. 연이 자존심이 없느냐고 물었다. 대답은 없다는 것보다 나빴다.

en: I have no such thing as pride.
I only have my goal.

blocks.html: Then Chunchu had reached to his own belt, drawn a short blade, and driven it through his own left hand — clean, deliberate, eyes never leaving Yeon’s face — and held the wound up like a seal.
blocks.ko: 그때 춘추는 제 허리에서 짧은 칼을 빼어, 제 왼손을 스스로 찔렀다 — 말쑥하고 고의적으로, 눈은 한 번도 연의 얼굴에서 떼지 않은 채 — 그리고 그 상처를 도장처럼 들어 올렸다.

lines: 제가 저를 얼마까지 쓸 수 있는지, 이것입니다.
자존심을 묻지 마십시오. 무엇을 망가뜨릴 각오인지 물으십시오.
en: This is how much of myself I will spend.
Do not ask me for pride. Ask me what I am willing to ruin.

blocks.html: Yeon remembers the stare more than the blood. Hot, dry, almost joyful. The stare of a man who had decided the room would believe him, and had paid in advance.
blocks.ko: 연은 피보다 그 눈빛을 더 오래 기억한다. 뜨겁고, 건조하고, 거의 기쁘기까지 한. 방이 자기를 믿게 되리라 결정한 사람의 눈빛. 값을 먼저 치른 사람의 눈빛.

lines: 제 손을 제 칼로 뚫어서 내 귀를 열더군.
그런 눈을 한 사람을 하나 더 만났소.
en: That Chunchu…
He put steel through his own hand to make me listen.
I have met one other man with eyes like that.
Oh?

lines: 둘 중 누가 더 무서운지는 아직 모르겠소.
en: You.
I do not yet know which of you frightens me more.
Flattery. Keep going.
It was not flattery.

lines: 그럼 다른 하나는? 저쪽 칼 말이오. 김유신.
en: And the other one? Their sword. Kim Yushin.

blocks.html: Yeon’s cup stops an inch from his mouth. Just for a breath. Then he drinks.
blocks.ko: 연의 잔이 입 앞 한 치에서 멈춘다. 딱 한 숨. 그리고 마신다.

en: Ha! Did you see that, Gyebek? His cup stopped.
I don’t flinch.
It stopped, Majesty.

lines: 올 때는 셋이더니, 갈 때는 다섯이구려.
en: You came with three. You’re leaving with five.
…Did Your Majesty come as an envoy, or to do some shopping?
blocks.art: Dusk in the guest-house yard: Gesomun looks over Euija’s retinue, two more faces than came with him.

lines: 나는 사람을 모으는 재주가 있소. 공은 사람을 줄이는 재주가 있고.
en: I have a gift for gathering people. You have a gift for reducing them.

lines: 평양에 남아라. 탈 만한 말 한 필 주지.
en: You. The one who counts steps.
Stay in Pyongyang. I’ll give you a horse worth riding.
I gave my word.

lines: 관두시오. 저놈은 그 말을 딱 한 번만 하오.
en: Don’t bother. He only ever says it once.

blocks.html: In the morning he rides south with all five. Nobody raises the subject of the extra two. He carries a map of Danghang Fortress in his head, and Yeon’s warning about Chunchu folded away like a knife he intends to use later.
blocks.ko: 아침에 그는 다섯을 모두 거느리고 남으로 떠난다. 늘어난 둘에 대해서는 아무도 입을 열지 않는다. 머릿속에는 당항성 지도가 있고, 춘추를 조심하라던 개소문의 말은 나중에 쓸 칼처럼 접어 품에 넣어 두었다.

blocks.html: On the road home, Euija is still laughing.
blocks.ko: 돌아오는 길에도 의자는 계속 웃는다.

en: His cup stopped! Find out why.
Yes, Majesty.

blocks.html: He does not wait for the answer. By the first frost, forty-odd Silla fortresses are flying Baekje yellow. He takes them in one autumn, and he laughs the whole way.
blocks.ko: 그는 답을 기다리지 않는다. 첫서리가 내릴 무렵, 신라 성 마흔 남짓에 백제의 누런 깃발이 걸린다. 한 가을에 다 거두고, 내내 웃는다.

blocks.html: In the sixteenth year Euija raised troops, attacked more than forty Silla cities and sent men to hold them. He made peace and friendship with Goguryeo, and plotted to take Danghang Fortress and cut off Silla's road to court.
blocks.ko: 16년, 의자가 군사를 일으켜 신라의 40여 성을 치고 또 군사를 보내 지키게 하였다. 고구려와 화친하여 우호를 맺고, 당항성을 빼앗아 신라가 조정에 들어오는 길을 끊으려 꾀하였다.
blocks.hanja: 十六年，義慈興兵伐新羅四十餘城，又發兵以守之，與高麗和親通好，謀欲取党項城以絕新羅入朝之路。
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199上, Eastern Barbarians — Baekje, Zhenguan 16 (642)

blocks.html: Why does the Eternal General flinch at one Silla name? Go back to a ditch, a white horse, and an unknown captain…!
blocks.ko: 영원의 대장군은 왜 신라의 이름 하나에 움찔하는가? 참호 하나, 흰 말 한 마리, 이름 없는 대장 하나에게로 거슬러 가 보자…!

logline.en: Kim Yushin — a name that strikes fear in all of Samhan. Maybe this is why.
logline.ko: 김유신. 삼한 어디서든 두려움을 부르는 이름. 아마 이래서일 것이다.
