Gesomun’s cup stops an inch from his mouth. Now you know why.” Context: …Kim Yushin. That’s where the name comes from. Not from his own capital, which likes its titles stamped and filed. From the people he beat. Goguryeo calls him the Sword of Silla first, and means it as a warning. On the border, mothers use it to get children indoors before dark. Thirteen years later, Gesomun hears that sword is riding for the Silla envoy in his prison, and opens the cell. A few months after that, a laughing king says the name across a table. Gesomun’s cup stops an inch from his mouth. Now you know why. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). COMMONERS in every Samhan kingdom wear SIMPLE WHITE: plain undyed white or off-white hemp and ramie jackets, wide trousers and skirts, a cloth sash, straw sandals or bare feet, hair in a plain topknot or braid — no dyed silk, no dots, no gold; colour belongs to rank, so a crowd of farmers, porters, servants and townsfolk reads as a field of soft white cloth with the officials' colours standing out of it. Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Kim Yushin — a name that strikes fear in all of Samhan. Maybe this is why.
blocks.ko: 김유신. 삼한 어디서든 두려움을 부르는 이름. 아마 이래서일 것이다.

blocks.html: Autumn. Silla’s army is breaking against a Goguryeo line that didn’t bother to stay behind its wall. It came down the hill and formed up behind a row of pits, and now the men who should be charging are sitting in the trenches. Yushin is thirty-four, a banner captain. His white horse doesn’t even have a name.
blocks.ko: 가을. 신라군이 부서지고 있다. 고구려군은 성벽 뒤에 머물 생각도 하지 않았다. 언덕을 내려와 구덩이 줄 뒤에 진을 쳤고, 돌격해야 할 병사들은 지금 참호에 주저앉아 있다. 유신은 서른넷, 깃발 하나를 맡은 대장이다. 그의 흰 말에는 아직 이름도 없다.

blocks.html: A Goguryeo wall that is about to make somebody famous.
blocks.ko: 곧 누군가를 유명하게 만들 고구려의 성벽.

blocks.speaker: A spearman in the trench
lines: 성에서 나왔심더, 나리. 아예 나와삤어요. 나와도 되는 줄 아는 기지예.
en: They came out of the fort, sir. Right out. They knew they could.

blocks.html: On the rise behind the trenches, the general’s staff have been arguing for an hour about how to retreat without calling it one. The general has said nothing. He is holding a cup of barley tea he has forgotten to drink.
blocks.ko: 참호 뒤 언덕에서 장군의 참모들은 한 시진째, 후퇴를 후퇴라 부르지 않고 하는 법을 두고 다투고 있다. 장군은 말이 없다. 마시는 걸 잊은 보리차 잔을 들고 있다.

blocks.speaker: A staff officer
lines: 좌군을 개울까지 물리시이소, 장군. 진을 고쳐 친다 카면 됩니더.
en: Pull the left back to the stream, sir. Call it reforming.

blocks.speaker: Another officer
lines: 뭐라 카든 고구려 놈들은 도망이라 캅니더.
en: Call it what you like. Goguryeo will call it running.

lines: 저 누고. 흰 말 탄 거.
en: Who’s that. On the white horse.

blocks.speaker: A staff officer
en: …Your son, sir.
I know.
I was hoping you’d say someone— I know.

blocks.html: He rides back to his father’s command post, gets down, and takes off his helmet, which is how a son asks permission in front of an army.
blocks.ko: 그는 아버지의 지휘소로 말을 몰아 돌아와 내리고, 투구를 벗는다. 군대 앞에서 아들이 허락을 구하는 방식이다.

lines: 옷깃을 쥐고 떨쳐야 갖옷이 바로 서고, 벼리를 들어야 그물이 펴진다고 했습니다.
en: Father. We’re losing.
They say you shake a coat by the collar to make it hang straight, and lift the head-rope to open a net.
…Let me be the collar.
…Put your helmet on.
Then go.

blocks.speaker: A staff officer
lines: 장군— 당주 하나가 혼자서 저기를— 아드님이—
en: My lord— a banner captain, alone, into that— he’s your—

lines: 옷깃이 되겠다 안 카나. 되라 캐라.
en: I know whose he is.
He said collar. Let him be the collar.

blocks.html: The white horse takes the trench in one jump that the men in it will describe for the rest of their lives, usually with their hands. Mud to the girth. A horn somewhere, too late. The Goguryeo line bends where he hits it, like a wall that has just remembered it is made of men. In, out. In again. The third time Yushin comes back there is something heavy hanging from his saddle, and the men in the trench are already climbing out after him.
blocks.ko: 흰 말은 단번에 참호를 뛰어넘는다. 그 안에 있던 병사들이 평생, 대개는 손짓까지 해 가며 이야기하게 될 도약이다. 뱃대끈까지 차오르는 진흙. 어딘가에서 뒤늦은 뿔피리. 그가 부딪친 자리에서 고구려의 줄이 휜다. 제가 사람으로 쌓였다는 걸 막 떠올린 성벽처럼. 들어갔다, 나왔다. 다시 들어간다. 세 번째로 유신이 돌아올 때 안장에는 묵직한 것이 매달려 있고, 참호의 병사들은 벌써 그를 따라 기어 나오고 있다.

blocks.html: On the rise, his father has not moved. The officer nearest him hears him counting under his breath, the way you count a breath you are afraid will be the last. One. A long while. Two. At three he sets the cold cup down on the ground, very carefully, as if it might spill.
blocks.ko: 언덕 위, 아버지는 꼼짝도 않는다. 제일 가까이 선 장교가 그가 숨죽여 세는 소리를 듣는다. 마지막일까 겁나는 숨을 세듯. 하나. 한참. 둘. 셋에서 그는 식은 잔을 땅에 내려놓는다. 쏟아질까 봐 아주 조심스럽게.

blocks.html: He brings the weight on his saddle back to the command post and sets it down in the mud in front of his father, wrapped in a torn banner, because he does not know what else a son is supposed to do with a general’s head. The staff officers wait for the speech. Seohyun looks at the bundle, then at the boy, for long enough that someone coughs.
blocks.ko: 그는 안장에 매달린 것을 지휘소로 가져와 아버지 앞 진흙 위에 내려놓는다. 찢긴 깃발에 싸여 있다. 장군의 머리를 아들이 어떻게 해야 하는지, 그는 모른다. 참모들이 연설을 기다린다. 서현은 보따리를 보고, 아들을 본다. 누군가 헛기침을 할 만큼 오래.

en: …Your helmet’s crooked.

blocks.html: He reaches up and straightens it himself, both hands, the way you fix a boy’s collar before a feast, and then turns away and shouts for his officers before anyone can see his face. By Kim Seohyun’s standards it is a speech, and Yushin will carry it longer than the helmet.
blocks.ko: 그는 손을 뻗어 직접 바로잡는다. 두 손으로, 잔치 전에 아이 옷깃을 매만지듯. 그리고 누가 얼굴을 보기 전에 돌아서서 장교들을 부른다. 김서현 기준으로는 연설이다. 유신은 그것을 투구보다 오래 지니고 다닌다.

blocks.html: Nobody waits for the officers. The trench climbs out after the white horse, uphill, and by dusk the Goguryeo line is lying in the field. The fort on the hill opens its gate before anyone knocks.
blocks.ko: 장교들을 기다리는 사람은 없다. 참호가 흰 말을 따라 언덕 위로 기어 나오고, 해 질 녘이면 고구려의 줄은 들판에 누워 있다. 언덕 위 성은 누가 두드리기도 전에 문을 연다.

blocks.speaker: A Silla spearman
lines: 저 흰 말 누고? 누 집 아들이고?
en: Who was that? The white horse— whose son is that?

blocks.html: That night he asks the groom what the white horse is called. The groom says it has no name; it came from the royal stable as a spare. Yushin looks at it for a long time, at the mud on its chest and the way it still will not quite stand still.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 마부에게 흰 말의 이름을 묻는다. 이름은 없다고, 왕실 마구간에서 여벌로 온 말이라고 마부가 답한다. 유신은 오래도록 말을 바라본다. 가슴팍의 진흙을, 아직도 가만히 서 있지 못하는 모양을.

en: Hangyul.
…It means steady. It came back steady. All three times.

blocks.html: The few who get out of Nangbi walk north for nine days with the story, and it grows a little at every well. By Pyongyang the white horse has cleared the trench at a gallop with a general’s head in one hand and a banner in the other, and the man on it has a name the Goguryeo clerks must write down for the first time.
blocks.ko: 낭비성을 빠져나간 몇 안 되는 자들이 이야기를 들고 아흐레를 북으로 걷는다. 이야기는 우물을 지날 때마다 조금씩 자란다. 평양에 닿을 무렵 흰 말은 한 손에 장군의 머리, 한 손에 깃발을 들고 전속력으로 참호를 넘었고, 그 위의 사내에게는 고구려 서기들이 처음으로 받아 적어야 하는 이름이 생겨 있다.

blocks.label: The Pyongyang Court
blocks.ko: 평양 조정

blocks.html: In Pyongyang the report is read to the king twice, the second time because he asks for it. At the back of the hall the Yeon heir, twenty-four, stands with his arms folded, the way he stands everywhere.
blocks.ko: 평양에서 보고는 왕 앞에서 두 번 읽힌다. 두 번째는 왕이 다시 읽으라 해서다. 전각 뒤편에서 연씨 가문의 후계자, 스물넷이 팔짱을 끼고 서 있다. 그는 어디서나 그렇게 선다.

en: Kim Yushin… a banner captain.
We have never heard the name.

lines: 놈 하나가 도랑 하나 넘었는데 우리 오천이 드러누웠소. 그게 당주요? 칼이지.
en: You’ll hear it again.
One man jumps one ditch and five thousand of ours lie down. That’s a captain? That’s a sword.
Silla’s sword.

blocks.label: The High Commander’s House
blocks.ko: 막리지의 집

blocks.html: Gesomun’s family lives in the big house below the palace hill. His father, Yeon Tejo, has run the Summit for ten years. Long enough to outlive most of the men who voted for him. None of the ones who voted against. Most nights he comes home in a silence the servants have learned to walk around.
blocks.ko: 개소문의 집안은 왕궁 언덕 아래 큰 집에 산다. 아버지 연태조는 십 년째 회의의 윗자리를 지키고 있다. 그를 밀어준 사람들이 대부분 먼저 죽을 만큼 긴 세월이다. 반대한 사람들은 하나도 안 죽었다. 거의 매일 밤 그는 말없이 돌아오고, 하인들은 그 침묵을 비켜 다니는 법을 익혔다.

blocks.html: Tonight he does not take off his boots. He sits at the low table with a copy of the Nangbi report, the one the king asked to hear twice, and reads it a third time with his finger under the lines.
blocks.ko: 오늘 밤 그는 신도 벗지 않는다. 낮은 상 앞에 앉아, 왕이 두 번 읽으라 한 낭비성 보고의 사본을 펼쳐 놓고, 손가락으로 줄을 짚어 가며 세 번째로 읽는다.

en: Father. You’re still on that?
It’s one fortress. We take it back by spring.

lines: …오천 수급이다. 한 번 뛰어들어서. 기런 놈을 몇이나 봤네?
en: Sit.
…Five thousand heads. Off one charge. How many men have you seen do that?
One.
You. At the Colossal River.

lines: 내한텐 삼만 군사가 있었고, 강도 우리 편이었고, 을지 공이 명을 내렸다.
이놈은 도랑 하나에 말 한 필이다.
en: I had thirty thousand men, a river on my side, and Ulchi giving the orders.
He had a ditch and a horse.

blocks.html: Gesomun has seen his father angry, drunk and bleeding, and once, when he was seven, riding home from the Colossal River with the Western banner rolled under his arm like a bolt of cloth. He has never seen him frightened of a piece of paper. He finds he does not know where to put his hands.
blocks.ko: 개소문은 아버지가 화내는 것도, 취한 것도, 피 흘리는 것도 보았다. 일곱 살 때는 서국 깃발을 비단 한 필처럼 옆구리에 말아 끼고 살수에서 돌아오는 것도 보았다. 종이 한 장을 두려워하는 아버지는 처음 본다. 손을 어디 둬야 할지 모르겠다.

lines: 서른넷에 아직 당주다. 신라 놈들이 가야 손자를 더 빨리 올려 줄 리가 없디.
썩히고 있는 거다. 언제까지나 썩히진 않갓디.
en: Thirty-four, and still a banner captain. Silla won’t let a Gaya grandson climb any faster.
They’re wasting him. They won’t waste him forever.

lines: 기럼 기 전에 제가 죽이면 됩네다.
en: Then I’ll kill him before they stop.

lines: 잘 들어라. 그놈이 고른 땅에선 절대 싸우디 마라. 화났을 때도 마라. 기리고 이 도성이 그놈을 고작 당주라고 하거든, 믿지 마라.
en: Aye, you’ll try.
Listen to me. Never on a field he picked. Never when you’re angry. And when this city tells you he’s only a captain, don’t believe it.
His Majesty already did.

lines: 전하는 두 번 들으시고 회의에 물으셨디.
회의가 뭘 했는지 아네? 성 다시 쌓는 값을 누가 낼디 반나절을 싸웠다. 아무도 그놈 이름을 입에 안 올렸어. 한 번도.
십 년을 그 방에 앉아 있었다. 데것들은 곳간 하나씩 이 나라를 잃어버릴 거다. 기러고는 신중했다고 하갓디.
en: His Majesty heard it twice and asked the Summit what to do.
Do you know what the Summit did? Argued half a day over who pays to rebuild the fort. Nobody said his name. Not once.
Ten years I’ve sat in that room. They’ll lose this country one granary at a time and call it caution.

blocks.html: Each of them learns his country at home. Euija learns the great clans at his father’s table. Chunchu learns the council from the day it walked his grandfather off the throne. And Gesomun learns this city here, from an old man reading one report three times by lamplight. Nobody else in the city would read it once.
blocks.ko: 셋 다 나라를 집에서 배운다. 의자는 아버지의 밥상머리에서 큰 가문들을 배운다. 춘추는 회의가 할아버지를 왕좌에서 걸어 내려보낸 그날에서 회의를 배운다. 그리고 개소문은 여기서 이 도시를 배운다. 등불 아래 같은 보고서를 세 번 읽는 늙은이에게서. 이 도시의 누구도 한 번 읽지 않을 보고서를.

en: …Kim Yushin.

blocks.html: That’s where the name comes from. Not from his own capital, which likes its titles stamped and filed. From the people he beat. Goguryeo calls him the Sword of Silla first, and means it as a warning. On the border, mothers use it to get children indoors before dark.
blocks.ko: 그 이름은 거기서 나왔다. 칭호에 도장 찍어 철해 두기 좋아하는 제 나라 도읍에서가 아니다. 그에게 진 사람들에게서다. 고구려가 먼저 그를 신라의 검이라 부른다. 경고의 뜻으로. 국경의 어머니들은 해 지기 전 아이들을 불러들일 때 그 이름을 쓴다.

blocks.html: Thirteen years later, Gesomun hears that sword is riding for the Silla envoy in his prison, and opens the cell. A few months after that, a laughing king says the name across a table. Gesomun’s cup stops an inch from his mouth. Now you know why.
blocks.ko: 십삼 년 뒤, 개소문은 그 검이 자기 감옥의 신라 사신을 구하러 온다는 소식을 듣고 옥문을 연다. 몇 달 뒤, 잘 웃는 왕 하나가 술상 너머로 그 이름을 입에 올린다. 개소문의 잔이 입 앞 한 치에서 멈춘다. 이제 동인지 아실 것이다.

blocks.html: Thirteen years on, the banner captain has a queen, a title, and forty fortresses Baekje just took from her. He wants them back…!
blocks.ko: 십삼 년이 지나, 그 깃발 대장에게는 여왕과 칭호가 있다. 그리고 백제가 방금 그 여왕에게서 빼앗은 성 마흔 개. 그는 그걸 되찾고 싶다…!

logline.en: In Baekje’s markets they spit when they say his title. They add, quietly, that Gyebek hasn’t met him yet.
logline.ko: 백제 저잣거리에서는 그의 이름을 말할 때 침을 뱉는다. 그리고 조용히 덧붙인다. 계백은 아직 그를 만나지 않았다고.

images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Donatello’s St George. Low worm’s-eye from the stone floor of a dark fortress gatehouse at night: Kim Yushin stands square in contrapposto, weight on one leg, head turned a little aside with a level stare, his ring-pommel sword point-down on the flagstone between his boots, both gauntleted hands stacked on the small ring. One narrow shaft from a high arrow-slit falls on him from the side and runs straight down the blade to the floor. Steel lamellar plates catch the key; blue cloth at the collar; the gatehouse arch dissolves into black. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — KIM YUSHIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_yushin.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Demeanor: Confucian: he STANDS — never sits in lotus. Weighs, counts, frowns at sums; tight jaw, rare dry half-smile. Grief shows as stillness, not tears. The most feared warrior in all of Samhan: a line goes quiet when the tall Silla helm and the white horse appear. Massive, deliberate, terrifying at a walk; by Hwangsan (65) heavier and slower than Gyebek but still the man armies are built around. Armor: Silla kit: steel lamellar cuirass and skirt, tall pointed jonghyeongju helm with a short plume. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Sword: Fish sword — Ring-pommel fish sword — Gaya fish on the pommel, Silla blue in the fuller. Pommel motif fish inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: One fish-ring sword at the left hip. Never two blades. Fighting: Orthodox FORWARD one-hand grip, ring at the heel of the fist; square upright stance, short economical straight cuts and thrusts — the drill-yard form he teaches. Mounted, he cuts down from the saddle on the off side. #2A5FB8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: sitting in lotus or holding prayer beads; katana, tsuba or curved blade (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); two swords at once; blue glow aura. | HANGYUL (한결, yushin's horse) — attached board /obj_hangyul.png: Pure white war horse, long flowing white mane, powerful galloping build — match the board. Eighteen years under Yushin since Nangbi; puts his nose into Yushin's chest and waits. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Silla banners: blue silk with a white crescent moon. Attached flag /flag_silla.png. | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Baekje took forty Silla fortresses in one autumn. Silla’s answer reaches Sabi at breakfast.
blocks.ko: 백제는 한 가을에 신라 성 마흔 개를 빼앗았다. 신라의 대답은 아침상에 맞춰 사비에 닿는다.

en: I-i-it’s Kim Yushin!!
You’ve never heard of Kim Yushin…?

lines: 이 바보야 — 김유신이 삼한 최강의 칼이야…!
연개소문, 계백 장군 — 다 비키라고 해. 아니면 계백에게 그 칭호가 아직 다툼 중이라고 해. 웃지 않을 거다.
en: You fool — Kim Yushin is the Greatest Blade of Samhan…!
Yeon Gesomun, General Gyebek — tell them all to stand aside. Or tell Gyebek the title is still disputed. He will not laugh.

blocks.html: In Baekje’s markets they spit when they say his title. At home they toast it. Both sides add, quietly, that Gyebek hasn’t met him yet. Until he does, “greatest blade” is a tavern argument with two right answers.
blocks.ko: 백제 장터에선 그의 칭호를 말할 때 침을 뱉는다. 고향에선 축배를 든다. 양쪽 다 누군가 조용히 덧붙인다. 계백과는 아직 붙어 보지 않았다고. 붙기 전까지 ‘최강의 칼’은 정답이 둘인 주점 논쟁이다.

blocks.caption: Forty fortresses, along a border nobody could draw the same way twice.
blocks.ko: 두 번 같게 그릴 수 없는 국경을 따라, 마흔 개의 성.

blocks.html: What reached Sabi had started a week earlier, in Surabol.
blocks.ko: 사비에 닿은 그것은 한 주 전 서라벌에서 시작되었다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace
blocks.ko: 월성

en: Forty, Yushin.
I’ll start with one, Majesty.
Which one?

lines: 저쪽 것으로요. 저들이 제일 안전하다고 여기는 것.
en: One of theirs. The one they think is safest.
And the forty?

lines: 백제는 이제 성 마흔을 지켜야 합니다, 폐하. 곳간 마흔. 겨울 마흔.
en: Baekje has forty forts to hold now, Majesty. Forty granaries. Forty winters.
Let them feed it.

lines: 조정에 우리가 그걸 내버려 둔다고 말하란 말인가?
en: You want me to tell the court we’re letting them keep it?
Tell the court I’m busy.
…That, they’ll believe.

blocks.html: He bows to go. She says his name before he reaches the door, and then has nothing to put after it.
blocks.ko: 그는 절하고 물러난다. 문에 닿기 전에 그녀가 그의 이름을 부른다. 그러고는 그 뒤에 붙일 말이 없다.

en: Yushin.
Majesty?
……Your collar’s crooked.
…So it is.

blocks.html: Neither of them fixes it. He looks at the door. She looks at the map. They are both nearly fifty, and the lamp is the only one in the room with the nerve to look at either of them.
blocks.ko: 아무도 그 깃을 고쳐 주지 않는다. 그는 문을 본다. 그녀는 지도를 본다. 둘 다 쉰을 바라보는 나이다. 방 안에서 두 사람을 똑바로 볼 배짱이 있는 건 등잔뿐이다.

blocks.label: The Gate
blocks.ko: 대문

blocks.html: He rides out that afternoon. The road runs past his own gate, and his household is lined up outside it, hoping. He does not turn his head. Fifty paces on he stops and sends a spearman back to the house for a cup of water.
blocks.ko: 그는 그날 오후 떠난다. 길은 제 집 대문 앞을 지나고, 집안 사람들이 혹시나 하고 대문 밖에 줄지어 서 있다. 그는 고개를 돌리지 않는다. 오십 걸음쯤 가서 말을 세우고, 창병 하나를 집으로 보내 물 한 잔을 떠 오게 한다.

lines: 우리 집 물은 아직도 옛 맛이 나는구나.
en: The water at home still tastes the way it used to.
He didn’t even look at the house.
…He drank the water, though.

blocks.html: Chunchu is waiting at the city gate, as if by accident.
blocks.ko: 춘추가 성문에서 기다리고 있다. 우연인 척.

lines: 자네 부인이 대문 앞에 서 있더군. 내가 봤네.
잠깐 들를 수도 있었다 아이가. 안에서 한 잔.
en: Your wife was at the gate. I saw her.
You could have stopped. One cup, inside.

lines: …멈추면, 멈춘 이유를 저들이 알아서 지어낼 테니.
en: …If I stopped, they would invent a reason for my stopping.

lines: 이유는 내가 지어 주지. 그건 내가 더 잘하네.
en: Then don’t stop.
I’ll invent the reasons for you. I’m rather better at it.

blocks.label: The Hill
blocks.ko: 언덕

blocks.html: He doesn’t stop at his own gate. He stops at the hill. Thirty riders wait on the road below with the horses and are told it’s a shrine, which in a way it is.
blocks.ko: 제 집 대문에선 서지 않는다. 언덕에선 선다. 기병 서른이 아래 길에서 말과 함께 기다리며 사당이라는 말을 듣는다. 어떻게 보면 틀린 말도 아니다.

blocks.html: He undresses fast, like a man with forty forts to not take back.
blocks.ko: 그는 되찾지 않을 성 마흔이 걸린 사람처럼 빠르게 옷을 벗는다.

en: Slow down. We only get you between wars.
…Which is never. Fine. Go fast.
lines: 천천히 해. 우린 전쟁 사이에만 너 보잖아.

en: Forty.
The hill heard. Even the moss is talking about it.
I’ll start with one.
…Which one?
One of theirs. The one they think is safest.
lines: 저쪽 것 하나. 제일 안전하다고 믿는 곳.

en: Then the hill has one thing for you, and it isn’t an answer.
Every fort on a river trusts its cliff. Nobody climbs the side the water guards.
lines: 그럼 언덕이 줄 게 하나 있어요. 답은 아니고요.
강가의 성은 다 제 벼랑을 믿어요. 물이 지키는 쪽으론 아무도 안 올라요.

en: Go up in your socks. Boots ring.
…That one actually was the hill. I’m as surprised as you.
…Your wife was at the gate.
You didn’t look. …We did.

blocks.html: He doesn’t answer that. He dresses with his back to them and goes down to the road, where thirty men are pretending they didn’t just hear a shrine laugh at their general.
blocks.ko: 그 말엔 답하지 않는다. 등을 돌려 옷을 입고 길로 내려간다. 서른 명이 방금 사당이 자기네 장군을 비웃는 소리를 못 들은 척하고 있다.

blocks.label: The River Fort
blocks.ko: 강가의 성

blocks.html: The fort sits on a bluff over a crossing, the kind of post a Baekje sentry gets sent to for a rest. Two of them are dicing by the brazier.
blocks.ko: 성은 나루 위 벼랑에 앉아 있다. 백제 보초가 쉬러 보내지는 그런 자리다. 둘이 화로 곁에서 주사위를 던지고 있다.

lines: 신라가 여기까진 안 와. 성 마흔 개 잃구 우느라 바쁠 겨.
en: Silla won’t come this far. They’re busy crying over forty forts.
Throw.

blocks.html: The other one does not throw. He is looking at the ridge. There is a pale horse on it, standing very still, and then there isn’t.
blocks.ko: 다른 하나는 던지지 않는다. 능선을 보고 있다. 거기 흰 말 한 마리가 아주 가만히 서 있다. 그리고 없다.

blocks.html: An hour earlier, at the foot of the bluff, an officer had looked up at the rock and then at his general.
blocks.ko: 한 시진 전, 벼랑 밑에서 장교 하나가 바위를 올려다보다가 제 장군을 보았다.

en: Sir. Nobody climbs that side.
Then nobody is watching it.

blocks.html: They go up in their socks, swords tied flat to their backs so nothing rings on the stone. Yushin goes third. Not first, which would be vanity. Not last, which would be worse.
blocks.ko: 그들은 버선발로 오른다. 칼은 등에 납작하게 묶어 바위에 쇳소리가 나지 않게 한다. 유신은 세 번째로 오른다. 맨 앞은 허세다. 맨 뒤는 더 나쁘다.

blocks.html: Yushin’s men come up the bluff in the dark, where nobody climbs because nobody can. By the time the brazier is kicked over they are on the wall.
blocks.ko: 유신의 군사들은 어둠 속에서 벼랑을 오른다. 아무도 못 오르니 아무도 안 지키는 자리다. 화로가 걷어차일 무렵 그들은 이미 성벽 위에 있다.

en: K-… IT’S KIM YUSHIN!!

blocks.html: The defence breaks before it starts. In the storehouse a young Baekje officer is trying to fire the rice before Silla can eat it. His hands shake too much for the flint.
blocks.ko: 방어는 시작되기도 전에 무너진다. 곳간에서는 백제의 젊은 장교 하나가 신라가 먹기 전에 쌀에 불을 지르려 애쓰고 있다. 손이 너무 떨려 부싯돌이 안 맞는다.

lines: 내려놓게. 오늘 밤엔 아무도 아무것도 태우지 않네.
en: Put it down. Nobody burns anything tonight.
…You’re not going to kill me?
Go home. Tell them who sent you.
Who— who do I say it was?
They’ll know.

blocks.html: It is not one of the forty. It is one of Baekje’s own, and that is the message. He has never been in a hurry about anything except a charge.
blocks.ko: 마흔 중 하나가 아니다. 백제 제 성이다. 그게 전하는 말이다. 그는 돌격 말고는 무엇에도 서두른 적이 없다.

blocks.html: Autumn, ninth month. The queen made him Supreme General and sent him with troops against seven Baekje fortresses, Gahye, Sungyul, Donghwa and the rest. He won a great victory and opened the Gahye crossing.
blocks.ko: 가을 9월, 왕이 그를 상장군으로 삼아 군사를 이끌고 백제의 가혜성·성열성·동화성 등 일곱 성을 치게 하니, 크게 이기고 이어 가혜 나루를 열었다.
blocks.hanja: 秋九月，王命為上將軍，使領兵伐百濟加兮城、省熱城、同火城等七城，大克之，因開加兮之津。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin I, Queen Seondeok yr. 13 (644)

blocks.caption: Seven ridges, one abacus.
blocks.ko: 일곱 능선, 주판 하나.

blocks.label: The Beacons
blocks.ko: 봉화

blocks.html: He does not take a second fort. He takes Baekje’s sleep instead. For seven nights his riders light fires on seven ridges, a different ridge every night, and the forty forts light their own beacons in answer, turn out their garrisons, and stand in the cold until dawn.
blocks.ko: 두 번째 성은 취하지 않는다. 백제의 잠을 취한다. 이레 동안 밤마다 그의 기병이 일곱 능선에 불을 밝힌다. 밤마다 다른 능선. 마흔 성은 답으로 저희 봉화에 불을 붙이고, 수비병을 깨워, 새벽까지 추위에 세워 둔다.

blocks.html: Beacon oil is not free. Neither is a garrison’s breakfast after a false alarm. On the eighth night the ridges stay dark, and the forty forts sleep through the one rider who actually comes.
blocks.ko: 봉화 기름은 공짜가 아니다. 오경보 뒤 수비병의 아침밥도 그렇다. 여드레째 밤 능선은 깜깜하다. 마흔 성은 그 사이로 정말로 오는 한 기병을 자면서 맞이한다.

blocks.speaker: The grain clerk
lines: 한 성에 기름 세 북. 마흔 성. 이레 밤.
대장이 산수 가르쳐 줘서 고맙다고 하오.
en: Three drums of oil a fort. Times forty. Times seven nights.
The marshal thanks you for the arithmetic.

blocks.label: Sabi
blocks.ko: 사비

blocks.html: The young officer comes home. He tells it the way he was told to.
blocks.ko: 젊은 장교가 돌아온다. 시킨 그대로 전한다.

en: He sent you home? With your sword on?

lines: 무장한 장교를 그냥 보냈답니다, 폐하. 신라가 물러졌습니다.
en: He let an officer walk out armed, Majesty. Silla’s gone soft.
Soft? He sent me a messenger with a sword on.
That’s a man saying, next time bring more.

lines: 자네 이름만 들어두 우리 애들이 밥을 안 먹어.
en: Yushin, my friend~~
My men stop eating at the sound of your name.
Gyebek. How many did he take?

lines: 하나입니다, 폐하. 우리 성 하나. 마흔 중엔 하나도 없습니다.
en: One, Majesty. One of ours. None of the forty.
…He isn’t taking them back.
He’s sending me the bill.
Reckon you could beat him?
I have not met him.
Then go and meet him.
Not yet, Majesty.
He picked this field.

blocks.html: Euija laughs, because it is the most honest answer anyone has given him all morning.
blocks.ko: 의자가 웃는다. 오늘 아침 누구한테 들은 대답보다 정직했으니까.

blocks.html: One star over Samhan tonight. Three men are looking up at it, and every one of them wants to be the King for All…!
blocks.ko: 오늘 밤 삼한 위에 별 하나. 세 사내가 그 별을 올려다본다. 셋 다 “삼한왕검”이 되고 싶다…!

logline.en: Same star. Same minute. Three places.
logline.ko: 같은 별. 같은 시각. 세 곳.

images.alt: Five heroes charge — manhwa warriors in cold blue night

images.at: The queen has had the pond lit
images.alt: The palace pond at night, covered in small floating lamps, a giwa pavilion on its bank with two tiny men sitting on its steps and two women at the water's edge.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Wide establishing shot, high three-quarter angle over the royal pond of the old palace in Surabol at night: a long dark pond with an irregular stone-edged shore, a two-storey giwa-roofed timber pavilion on a stone terrace at its edge with a short flight of granite steps down to the water. Hundreds of small paper lotus lamps float on the black water, each a warm dot, their reflections doubling them. Two tiny seated men on the pavilion steps, backs to the water; two tiny women in court hanbok crouched at the water's edge setting lamps afloat. Old pines and dark garden shrubs along a low wall. One bright star low in the eastern sky above the pavilion roof. ONE device: the curve of the shoreline sweeping from the lamps to the steps. Sharp foreground: a pine bough and one lamp drifting close to the lens. Few hues: ink black, warm lamp gold, pale stone. PLACE Moon Palace (월궁) — attached board /pl_moon_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.
