blocks.html: Every kingdom keeps one neighbour it hates more than any empire. Goguryeo’s has a family name.
blocks.ko: 나라마다 어느 제국보다 더 미운 이웃이 하나씩 있다. 고구려의 그 이웃에겐 성씨가 붙어 있다.

blocks.html: Gongsun. Three Lords Gongsun in a row have sat in Liaodong, between Goguryeo and the West, like a fat man in a doorway. One of them burned a Goguryeo capital. Another took in a Goguryeo prince who wanted his brother’s throne, and fed him soldiers. The one sitting there now sends silk in spring and spies in autumn. Lately he calls himself a king.
blocks.ko: 공손. 공손씨 영주가 삼대째 요동에 앉아 있다. 고구려와 서쪽 사이, 문간을 막고 앉은 뚱뚱한 사내처럼. 하나는 고구려의 도읍을 불태웠다. 또 하나는 형의 왕좌를 탐내던 고구려 왕자를 받아 주고 군사까지 먹였다. 지금 앉아 있는 자는 봄엔 비단을, 가을엔 첩자를 보낸다. 요즘은 스스로를 왕이라 부른다.

blocks.label: The Young King
blocks.ko: 젊은 왕

blocks.label: Hwando · spring
blocks.ko: 환도 · 봄

blocks.caption: The West, the hills, and in the doorway between them, Lord Gongsun.
blocks.ko: 서쪽, 산골, 그리고 그 사이 문간에 앉은 공손씨.

blocks.html: In a mountain capital that smells of pine smoke, a young king is listening to a horse trader lie, and enjoying it.
blocks.ko: 솔 연기 냄새가 나는 산속 도읍에서, 젊은 왕이 말장수의 허풍을 듣고 있다. 아주 즐겁게.

blocks.caption: Young, proud, and fond of any war he can win from the saddle. So far, that has been all of them.
blocks.ko: 젊고, 콧대 높고, 말 위에서 이길 수 있는 전쟁이라면 다 좋아한다. 지금까지는 전부 그랬다.

blocks.speaker: The horse trader
lines: 그래 그 남쪽 천재 말이우, 부채 든 양반. 그 양반이 늙은이 성 앞에 백 날을 앉아 있었다 이거요.
그러구는 늙은이한테 여편네 치마를 보냈디요. 함에 넣어서. 끈까지 매서.
en: So the southern genius, the one with the fan, he sits outside this old man’s fort a hundred days.
Sends him a lady’s dress. In a box. With a ribbon on.
Says, come out and fight, or wear this.
And?

blocks.speaker: The horse trader
lines: 선물 고맙다 하구. 꼭 맞는다 하구.
그러구 안 나왔디요. 그날도, 그다음 날도. 천재가 백 날을 기다리다가, 천재가 먼저 죽었시요.
en: He puts it on, Majesty.
Thanks the man for the gift. Says it fits.
And he doesnae come out. Not that day, not the next. A hundred days the genius waits, and then the genius dies.

blocks.html: The hall laughs. The king laughs loudest, then stops halfway, and asks the only question a king cares about.
blocks.ko: 대전이 웃음바다가 된다. 왕이 제일 크게 웃다가, 중간에 멈추고, 임금이 궁금해할 만한 단 하나를 묻는다.

en: What’s his name?

blocks.speaker: The horse trader
lines: 서쪽에선 아무도 그 이름을 입에 안 올려요, 전하. 재수 없다구.
그냥 서쪽 승상이라구 부르디요. 무슨 날씨 부르듯이.
en: Out west nobody says it, Majesty. Bad luck.
They call him the Western Chancellor. Like he’s weather.

blocks.html: The trader has never been within five hundred li of the man. Nobody in this hall has. That is how legends travel: on horseback, with the price going up at every stop.
blocks.ko: 말장수는 그 사내 근처 오백 리 안에도 가 본 적이 없다. 이 대전의 누구도 마찬가지다. 전설은 원래 그렇게 다닌다. 말을 타고, 들르는 데마다 값이 오르면서.

blocks.html: Then a letter comes from the West. It has a seal and no name, and it turns out the legend wants something.
blocks.ko: 그러다 서쪽에서 편지 한 통이 온다. 인장은 찍혔는데 이름은 없다. 그리고 그 전설이 뭔가를 원한다는 게 드러난다.

lines: 벗이 있으면 반갑겠다는군. 벗. 봐라, 두 번이나 썼다.
en: Wei is marching on Lord Gongsun.
Wei would welcome friends. Friends. Look, he wrote it twice.

blocks.speaker: The old minister
lines: 전하, 위는 천 리 밖이옵고 공손씨는 바로 옆집이옵니다.
위가 지면, 공손씨는 누가 누구 편을 들었는지—
en: Majesty, Wei is a thousand li away. Lord Gongsun is next door.
If Wei loses, he will remember who—

lines: —누가 아버님 도성을 태웠는지? 그건 나도 기억한다.
먼 놈 도와서 가까운 놈 치는 거다. 병법이랄 것도 없어. 집안 청소지.
en: —who burned my father’s city? I remember that too.
Help the far one kill the near one. That’s not strategy. That’s housekeeping.

lines: 천 기 안장 얹어라. 내가 간다.
치마 입은 그 사내, 내 눈으로 좀 봐야겠다.
en: Saddle a thousand. I’m going.
I want to see this man in a dress.

blocks.speaker: The old minister
en: Majesty, a king does not ride out himself to—

lines: 이 임금은 나간다. 누가 셈할 줄 아는 대장 하나 데려와.
en: This one does. Somebody find me a captain who can count.

blocks.html: They find him one. A young captain who can count, ride, and keep his mouth shut, which is two more skills than the king asked for. Nobody tells the king his name. The king doesn’t ask.
blocks.ko: 하나 찾아온다. 셈도 하고 말도 타고 입도 무거운 젊은 대장. 왕이 바란 것보다 재주가 둘이나 더 많다. 아무도 왕에게 그의 이름을 일러 주지 않는다. 왕도 묻지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Old Man
blocks.ko: 노인

blocks.label: The Liao · summer
blocks.ko: 요하 · 여름

blocks.html: The Wei camp is the first thing the king has seen that is bigger than a mountain and flatter than a lake. Forty thousand men, and every one of them is digging.
blocks.ko: 위나라 진영은 왕이 난생처음 보는, 산보다 크고 호수보다 납작한 물건이다. 사만 명이 있고, 그 하나하나가 땅을 파고 있다.

blocks.html: Everywhere the Goguryeo thousand ride, the Western Chancellor has just left. He was at the ford this morning. He was at the ditch by noon. He has looked at this hill. He did not like it.
blocks.ko: 고구려의 천 기가 가는 곳마다, 서쪽 승상은 방금 떠나고 없다. 아침엔 나루에 있었다. 한낮엔 도랑에 있었다. 이 언덕도 보고 갔다. 마음에 안 들었다고 한다.

blocks.speaker: Wei soldier
lines: 영감님이 또 도랑을 걸으셨어. 발로 재 보시더라.
en: The old man walked the ditch again. Measured it with his feet.
Says it’s two fingers too shallow.
zh: 老頭子又來走了一遍溝，用腳量的。
zhLatn: Lǎotóuzi yòu lái zǒu le yí biàn gōu, yòng jiǎo liáng de.
Shuō qiǎn le liǎng zhǐ.

blocks.speaker: Another digger
lines: 두 손가락? 말 위에서 그게 보인대?
en: Two fingers. He can see two fingers from a horse?
zh: 兩指？他騎在馬上看得見兩指？
zhLatn: Liǎng zhǐ? Tā qí zài mǎ shàng kàn de jiàn liǎng zhǐ?

blocks.speaker: Wei soldier
lines: 부채 든 그 양반 오는 걸 다섯 해 전에 내다보신 분이야. 두 손가락쯤이야.
en: He saw the man with the fan coming five years off. He can see two fingers.
Dig.
zh: 拿扇子的那位要來，他五年前就看見了。兩指算什麼。
zhLatn: Ná shànzi de nà wèi yào lái, tā wǔ nián qián jiù kànjiàn le. Liǎng zhǐ suàn shénme.
Wā.

blocks.speaker: The captain
lines: 전하, 방금 떠났다는 진이 이걸로 세 번째입니다.
귀신이든지, 우릴 안 만나구 싶든지 둘 중 하나디요.
en: Majesty, that’s the third camp he’s “just left”.
Either he’s a ghost or he doesnae want to meet us.

lines: 아니면 우리더러 찾아오라는 거지. 그게 더 고약하다.
en: Or he wants us to come and find him. Which is worse.
Where’s his tent?

blocks.html: His tent is the plain one. No banner on it, no guard worth the name, and an argument going on inside.
blocks.ko: 그의 막사는 제일 수수한 것이다. 깃발도 없고, 이렇다 할 호위도 없고, 안에서는 말다툼이 한창이다.

blocks.label: The plain tent
blocks.ko: 수수한 막사

blocks.html: The king stops outside the canvas. He has more Han than he lets on, and tonight, for once, it is useful.
blocks.ko: 왕은 천막 밖에서 걸음을 멈춘다. 그는 남들이 아는 것보다 한어를 잘한다. 오늘 밤엔 모처럼 그게 쓸모가 있다.

blocks.speaker: The secretary
lines: 태위 각하, 외람되오나. 우리가 칠 상대는 유비 쪽 무리가 아닙니까?
en: Grand Commandant, with respect. Shouldn’t we be fighting Liu Bei’s people?
Zhuge Liang—
zh: 太尉，恕下官直言。我們該打的，不是劉備那邊的人嗎？
zhLatn: Tàiwèi, shù xiàguān zhíyán. Wǒmen gāi dǎ de, bú shì Liú Bèi nà biān de rén ma?
Zhūgě Liàng——

lines: 그 사람은 나를 치러 북으로 오기 전에 먼저 남으로 갔네. 남쪽 오랑캐를 일곱 번 꺾었지. 다시는 안 일어날 때까지.
그러고 나서야 등 뒤를 비워 두고 북으로 왔네.
en: —is dead. He’d laugh at you.
Before he came north at me, he went south. Beat the southern barbarians seven times, until they stayed beaten.
Then he came north with nothing at his back.
zh: 他北上打我之前，先南征。南蠻七擒七縱，打到服為止。
然後才北上，背後空無一物。
zhLatn: ——Sǐ le. Tā ruò zài, huì xiào nǐ.
Tā běishàng dǎ wǒ zhīqián, xiān nánzhēng. Nánmán qī qín qī zòng, dǎ dào fú wéizhǐ.
Ránhòu cái běishàng, bèihòu kōng wú yí wù.

blocks.speaker: The secretary
en: So…
zhLatn: Nàme……

lines: 그러니까. 그 사람이 남쪽을 치웠으니, 나는 동쪽을 치우겠네.
먼저 문간. 그다음엔 문간 뒤에 있는 것.
en: So. He took the south. I’ll take the east.
The doorway first. Then whatever is behind the doorway.
zhLatn: Suǒyǐ. Tā qǔ nán, wǒ qǔ dōng.
Xiān qǔ ménkǒu. Zài qǔ mén hòu de.

blocks.speaker: The secretary
lines: 문간 뒤는 고구려입니다, 각하. 우리 동맹이고요.
en: Behind the doorway is Goguryeo, Grand Commandant. Our ally.
Their king is meant to arrive today, in fact—
zh: 門後是高句麗，太尉。是我們的盟友。
其實他們的王今天就該到——
zhLatn: Mén hòu shì Gāogōulí, tàiwèi. Shì wǒmen de méngyǒu.
Qíshí tāmen de wáng jīntiān jiù gāi dào——

lines: 그렇지. 말 타는 걸 좀 보고 싶네.
en: Yes. I’d like to see how he rides.
zh: 是啊。我想看看他騎得怎樣。
zhLatn: Shì a. Wǒ xiǎng kànkan tā qí de zěnyàng.

blocks.html: The flap opens. The eastern barbarian walks in, dusty to the knees, and does not wait to be translated.
blocks.ko: 천막 자락이 걷힌다. 동쪽 오랑캐가 무릎까지 먼지를 뒤집어쓰고 들어온다. 통역을 기다리지도 않는다.

en: I ride well.
I’m told I’m next.
zhLatn: Wǒ qí de hǎo.
Tīngshuō xià yí ge shì wǒ.

blocks.html: The man on the camp stool does not stand. He is old and thin, in a plain robe with ink on one cuff. He looks the king over the way a farmer looks at a field after rain. So this is the Western Chancellor. You may have guessed already. Goguryeo hasn’t. His name, which nobody out west says for luck, is Sima Yi.
blocks.ko: 걸상에 앉은 사내는 일어서지 않는다. 늙고 마른 몸에, 소매 한쪽에 먹이 묻은 수수한 옷. 그는 농부가 비 갠 밭을 보듯 왕을 훑어본다. 이 사람이 서쪽 승상이다. 당신은 벌써 눈치챘을지도 모른다. 고구려는 아직이다. 서쪽에서 재수 없다고 아무도 입에 올리지 않는 그 이름은, 사마의다.

blocks.caption: Fifty-nine years old, and he has never once been in a hurry. Everyone who fought him has learned to find that frightening.
blocks.ko: 쉰아홉. 평생 한 번도 서두른 적이 없다. 그와 싸운 자들은 모두 그게 무섭다는 걸 배웠다.

lines: 앉게. 무례하려고 천 리를 왔으니, 편히 앉아서 하게.
en: “Next” is a long word.
Sit. You rode a thousand li to be rude to me. Be comfortable doing it.
zh: 坐。你騎了千里來對我無禮，坐著無禮吧。
zhLatn: “Xià yí ge”, shì hěn cháng de huà.
Zuò. Nǐ qí le qiān lǐ lái duì wǒ wúlǐ, zuòzhe wúlǐ ba.

en: Did you just talk to me like one of your captains?

lines: 자네도 내 막사에 내 부하처럼 들어오지 않았나.
en: You walked into my tent like one of my captains.
We’ll call it even. Wine?
zh: 你也像我的部將一樣闖進我的帳。
zhLatn: Nǐ yě xiàng wǒ de bùjiàng yíyàng chuǎng jìn wǒ de zhàng.
Chěpíng le. Hē jiǔ?

blocks.html: The secretary, who has served the old man eleven years and never once been offered wine, goes to fetch it.
blocks.ko: 열한 해를 노인을 모시면서 술 한 잔 권받아 본 적 없는 서기가, 술을 가지러 나간다.

blocks.label: Liaodong · the rains
blocks.ko: 요동 · 장마

blocks.html: Lord Gongsun has built twenty li of earthworks along the river and is sitting behind them. The old man looks at them for one afternoon. That night he leaves his banners standing in the south, crosses in the north, and walks past the earthworks toward the city behind them. The men guarding the earthworks find they are guarding nothing. They run home.
blocks.ko: 공손씨는 강을 따라 이십 리 토루를 쌓고 그 뒤에 앉아 있다. 노인은 그걸 한나절 들여다본다. 그날 밤 그는 남쪽에 깃발을 세워 둔 채 북쪽으로 강을 건너, 토루를 지나쳐 그 뒤의 성으로 곧장 걸어간다. 토루를 지키던 자들은 자기들이 아무것도 안 지키고 있다는 걸 깨닫는다. 그리고 집으로 달아난다.

lines: 안으로 도망치는군. 길에서 잡을 수 있소.
en: They’re running back inside. We could catch them on the road.

lines: 왜? 내가 원하는 데로 꼭 가고 있는데.
달아나는 자는 잡기 어렵네. 성에 들어앉은 자는 이미 잡힌 걸세.
아직 그 말을 못 들었을 뿐이지.
en: Why? He is going exactly where I want him.
A man who runs is hard to catch. A man who sits in a city has already been caught.
He simply hasn’t been told.
zh: 何必？他正往我要他去的地方去。
逃的人難抓。坐在城裡的人，已經抓住了。
zhLatn: Hébì? Tā zhèng wǎng wǒ yào tā qù de dìfang qù.
Táo de rén nán zhuā. Zuò zài chéng lǐ de rén, yǐjīng zhuāzhù le.
Zhǐshì hái méi rén gàosu tā.

blocks.html: Then it rains. It rains for a month. The river comes over its banks, and forty thousand men stand in a lake a few feet deep.
blocks.ko: 그리고 비가 온다. 한 달 내내 온다. 강이 둑을 넘고, 사만 명이 발목 넘는 호수 한가운데 서 있게 된다.

blocks.html: Inside the walls, Lord Gongsun is delighted.
blocks.ko: 성안에서, 공손씨는 신이 났다.

blocks.caption: Lord of Liaodong, third of his line, and a friend to anyone who might help him. He is running out of anyone.
blocks.ko: 요동의 영주, 그 집안의 세 번째. 자기를 도울 만한 자라면 누구의 벗이든 되었다. 이제 그 누구가 바닥나고 있다.

lines: 저것들 좀 봐라. 호수에 서 있는 꼴이 꼭 백로 떼로구나.
하늘은 늘 나를 아꼈다. 소를 내보내 풀을 먹여라. 우리가 먹는 걸 구경이나 하라지.
en: Look at them. Standing in the lake like herons.
Heaven has always liked me. Send the cattle out to graze. Let them watch us eat.
zh: 看看他們。站在湖裡，跟白鷺似的。
天一向眷顧我。把牛放出去吃草。讓他們看著我們吃。
zhLatn: Kànkan tāmen. Zhàn zài hú lǐ, gēn báilù shìde.
Tiān yíxiàng juàngù wǒ. Bǎ niú fàng chūqù chī cǎo. Ràng tāmen kànzhe wǒmen chī.

blocks.html: So the cattle graze in full view, and the city’s woodcutters work under the walls. The Goguryeo riders sit their horses in the water and watch dinner walk past.
blocks.ko: 그래서 소 떼가 보란 듯이 풀을 뜯고, 성안 나무꾼들이 성벽 아래서 장작을 팬다. 고구려 기병들은 물속에서 말 위에 앉아 저녁거리가 지나가는 걸 구경한다.

lines: 소 이백 마리가 훤히 나와 있소. 기병 쉰만 주시오. 오늘 밤 쇠고기 드시게 해 드리리다.
en: Two hundred head, in the open. Give me fifty riders and you eat beef tonight.

lines: 자네 산에서 비 오는 날 사슴을 잡을 때, 쫓아가나?
en: I know.
In your hills, when you hunt deer in the rain, do you chase them?
zh: 你們山裡，雨天獵鹿，會追嗎？
zhLatn: Wǒ zhīdào.
Nǐmen shān lǐ, yǔtiān liè lù, huì zhuī ma?

en: …No. They’re faster in the mud than we are.
So is a frightened city.
zhLatn: Shòujīng de chéng yě shì.

lines: 겁먹은 꼴이 아니오. 꽃놀이 나온 꼴이지.
en: They don’t look frightened. They look like they’re having a picnic.

lines: 좋네. 꽃놀이 나온 사람은 안 달아나거든.
en: Good. A man at a picnic doesn’t run.
zh: 好。出來野宴的人，不會跑。
zhLatn: Hǎo. Chūlái yěyàn de rén, bú huì pǎo.

blocks.html: That afternoon a Wei officer asks to move the camp to higher ground. The old man has his head taken off and put on a pole above the water. Nobody asks again.
blocks.ko: 그날 오후 위나라 장교 하나가 진을 높은 데로 옮기자고 청한다. 노인은 그의 목을 베어 물 위 장대에 걸게 한다. 다시 묻는 사람은 없다.

lines: 발 좀 말리고 싶다고 사람을 죽였소.
en: You killed a man for wanting dry feet.

lines: 다들 발 마르기를 아주 조용히 바라고 있네. 자네도.
en: For saying so out loud.
Everyone else wants dry feet very quietly. You included.
zh: 其他人都很安靜地想要乾腳。你也是。
zhLatn: Shì yīnwèi tā shuō chūkǒu le.
Qítā rén dōu hěn ānjìng de xiǎng yào gān jiǎo. Nǐ yě shì.

lines: 나는 임금이오. 뭘 바라도 크게 바라지.
en: I’m a king. I want things loudly.

lines: 그럼 이걸 바라게. 물이 빠지면, 이 들판 어디가 제일 먼저 마르겠나?
en: Then want this. When the water goes down, which part of this plain dries first?
zh: 那就要這個。水退了，這片平地哪裡先乾？
zhLatn: Nà jiù yào zhège. Shuǐ tuì le, zhè piàn píngdì nǎlǐ xiān gān?

en: …How would I know?

lines: 말은 잘 타더군. 땅도 그만큼 잘 보나?
가서 알아 오게. 땅부터 보게. 언제나.
en: You ride well. Do you look at the ground as well as you ride?
Go and find out. Look at the ground first. Always.
zh: 你騎得好。看地也看得那麼好嗎？
去查清楚。先看地。永遠先看地。
zhLatn: Nǐ qí de hǎo. Kàn dì yě kàn de nàme hǎo ma?
Qù chá qīngchu. Xiān kàn dì. Yǒngyuǎn xiān kàn dì.

blocks.html: So for the rest of the rain, the King of Goguryeo rides around a besieged city in water to his horse’s knees. He pokes the mud with a spear butt, like a farmer deciding when to plant. His captain rides behind him with a charcoal map on a board. The south-east dries first. Under the water, a spine of gravel runs down to a little river behind the city.
blocks.ko: 그래서 비가 그칠 때까지, 고구려 왕은 말 무릎까지 차는 물속에서 포위된 성을 빙빙 돈다. 씨 뿌릴 날을 가늠하는 농부처럼 창 자루로 진흙을 쿡쿡 찔러 본다. 대장이 판때기에 숯으로 지도를 그리며 뒤를 따른다. 동남쪽이 제일 먼저 마른다. 물 밑으로 자갈 등줄기가 성 뒤 작은 강까지 뻗어 있다.

blocks.speaker: The captain
lines: 전하, 세상에 이러는 임금은 전하뿐인 거 아시디요.
en: Majesty, you ken you’re the only king in the world doing this.
Shut up and write. South-east. Firm.

blocks.label: The plain tent · nights
blocks.ko: 수수한 막사 · 밤

blocks.html: In the evenings the king comes back to the plain tent wet to the thigh, and the old man has the stone board out.
blocks.ko: 저녁이면 왕은 허벅지까지 젖어서 수수한 막사로 돌아오고, 노인은 바둑판을 꺼내 놓고 기다린다.

en: Again.
That’s the fourth “again”.
zhLatn: Zhè shì dì sì ge “zài lái” le.

en: You keep winning. It’s rude to a guest.

lines: 자네는 자꾸 덤비지 않나. 판한테 무례하게.
en: You keep attacking. It’s rude to the board.
zh: 你一直進攻。對棋盤無禮。
zhLatn: Nǐ yìzhí jìngōng. Duì qípán wúlǐ.

blocks.html: The king plays the way he rides, straight at a thing until it dies. The old man plays the way it rains.
blocks.ko: 왕은 말 타듯 둔다. 죽을 때까지 곧장 들이받는다. 노인은 비 오듯 둔다.

lines: 자네 대장, 지도를 잘 그리더군. 이름이 뭔가?
en: Your captain draws a good map. What’s his name?
zh: 你那個隊長，地圖畫得好。叫什麼名字？
zhLatn: Nǐ nàge duìzhǎng, dìtú huà de hǎo. Jiào shénme míngzi?

en: He has one.
Your move.

lines: 한 판만 더. 내가 이기면, 빚이오.
en: One more. If I win, you owe me.
Owe you what?
zhLatn: Qiàn nǐ shénme?

en: Something big. I’ll think of it.
Kings always do.
zhLatn: Jūnwáng zǒngshì zhèyàng.

blocks.html: On the twentieth night of rain the king plays slowly. He takes nothing. He waits. The old man looks at the board for a long time, then at the king, and puts his stones back in the box.
blocks.ko: 장마 스무째 날 밤, 왕은 느리게 둔다. 아무것도 따 먹지 않는다. 기다린다. 노인은 오래도록 판을 들여다보다가, 왕을 보고, 제 돌을 통에 도로 담는다.

en: Where did you learn that?
zhLatn: Nǎlǐ xué de?

en: From a man in a dress.

blocks.html: Across the tent, the secretary drops a cup.
blocks.ko: 막사 저쪽에서 서기가 잔을 떨어뜨린다.

en: …Who told you that story?
zhLatn: ……Shéi gēn nǐ shuō de?

en: Everybody. It’s the only story anyone tells about you.
…It fit, you know.
zhLatn: ……Qíshí tǐng héshēn de.

blocks.html: Two clever men, thirty years apart, who like each other rather more than their courts would want. History will try this pairing again in four hundred years, with different hats.
blocks.ko: 서른 살 차이 나는 영리한 사내 둘이, 각자의 조정이 바랄 만한 것보다 서로를 훨씬 더 좋아한다. 역사는 사백 년 뒤에 이 짝을 한 번 더 시험해 본다. 모자만 바꿔 쓰고.

blocks.label: The Siege
blocks.ko: 공성

blocks.label: Liaodong · the rain stops
blocks.ko: 요동 · 비가 그치다

blocks.html: The rain stops. Within a week Wei has ramps against the walls, ladders, rams, and engines throwing stones over the parapet. Inside, the grain runs out. Then the cattle. Then people start to go missing, and nobody asks where.
blocks.ko: 비가 그친다. 한 주 만에 위나라는 성벽에 흙 비탈을 대고, 사다리와 충차를 붙이고, 성가퀴 너머로 돌을 날리는 포차를 세운다. 성안에선 곡식이 떨어진다. 그다음엔 소가. 그다음엔 사람들이 하나둘 사라지는데, 어디로 갔는지 묻는 사람이 없다.

blocks.html: One night the king and his captain are on watch on the south-east gravel when the sky does something.
blocks.ko: 어느 밤 왕과 대장이 동남쪽 자갈밭에서 망을 보고 있는데, 하늘이 무언가를 한다.

blocks.speaker: The captain
en: Majesty— look up—

blocks.html: A long white star with a tail like a horse’s mane crosses over the city and drops into the little river behind it. Right where the gravel runs down to the water.
blocks.ko: 말갈기 같은 꼬리를 단 긴 흰 별 하나가 성 위를 가로질러 성 뒤 작은 강으로 떨어진다. 꼭 자갈밭이 물로 내려가는 그 자리에.

en: …That’s our gravel.

blocks.speaker: The captain
lines: 저게 그놈 무덤이디요, 전하. 우리 할매라면 그랬을 거요.
en: That’s his grave, Majesty. My grannie’d say so.
She’d also say dinnae point at it.

blocks.html: Inside the walls, everyone saw it. Nobody sleeps.
blocks.ko: 성안에서도 모두 그걸 봤다. 아무도 잠들지 못한다.

blocks.html: In the morning old men come out under a white flag with terms, then a younger one offering a hostage. The old man sends them all back with a list.
blocks.ko: 아침이 되자 늙은 신하들이 흰 깃발을 들고 나와 조건을 내민다. 다음엔 젊은 자가 나와 볼모를 내민다. 노인은 그들 모두를 목록 하나 들려서 돌려보낸다.

lines: 장수가 할 수 있는 일은 다섯이네.
싸우거나, 지키거나, 달아나거나, 무릎 꿇거나, 죽거나.
en: There are five things a general can do.
Fight. Hold. Run. Kneel. Die.
zhLatn: Wéi jiàng zhě néng zuò de, yǒu wǔ jiàn.
Zhàn, shǒu, zǒu, xiáng, sǐ.

lines: 싸우진 못하고, 지키는 건 끝났고. 무릎 꿇을 생각이었으면 늙은이들 대신 제가 나왔겠지.
en: He can’t fight. He’s done holding. And he won’t kneel, or he’d have come out himself instead of sending old men.
So.
Which way does he run?
zhLatn: Suǒyǐ.
Tā wǎng nǎ biān pǎo?

en: …South-east. It’s the only ground that will hold a horse.
Then go and sit on it.
zhLatn: Nà jiù qù nàlǐ zuòzhe.

lines: 말에 안장을 얹어라. 아직 말인 놈들한테만.
en: A list. He sends me a list, like a grain merchant.
Saddle the horses. Whichever ones are still horses.
zh: 一張單子。他給我送來一張單子，跟糧商似的。
zhLatn: Yì zhāng dānzi. Tā gěi wǒ sòng lái yì zhāng dānzi, gēn liángshāng shìde.
Bèi mǎ. Hái suàn shì mǎ de nàxiē.

blocks.label: The little river
blocks.ko: 작은 강

blocks.html: He breaks out at night through the southern lines, with his son and a few hundred riders, and turns south-east. Of course he does.
blocks.ko: 그는 밤에 아들과 기병 수백을 데리고 남쪽 포위를 뚫고 나와 동남쪽으로 꺾는다. 당연히 그렇다.

blocks.html: The Goguryeo thousand are already sitting on it.
blocks.ko: 고구려의 천 기는 이미 거기 앉아 있다.

en: Told you. Firm.

blocks.speaker: The captain
lines: 판때기한테 말씀하셨디요, 전하. 적은 건 저고요.
en: You told a board, Majesty. I wrote it.

blocks.html: It isn’t much of a fight. The lord’s riders are starved, and their horses are worse. The king’s arrow takes Lord Gongsun’s horse at the water’s edge, about where the star went in. Lord Gongsun goes into the shallows on his hands and knees and comes up muddy to the eyes, still in silk.
blocks.ko: 싸움이랄 것도 없다. 영주의 기병들은 굶주렸고, 말들은 더하다. 왕의 화살이 물가에서 공손씨의 말을 꿰뚫는다. 별이 떨어진 바로 그 언저리다. 공손씨는 손과 무릎으로 여울에 처박혔다가, 눈까지 진흙을 뒤집어쓰고 일어난다. 여전히 비단 차림이다.

lines: 고구려! 너 고구려지? 그 모자 좀 봐.
들어 봐. 내 말 좀 들어. 나 너희 이웃이야.
en: Goguryeo! You’re Goguryeo, aren’t you? Look at your hat.
Listen. Listen to me. I’m your neighbour.
zh: 高句麗！你是高句麗的，對吧？看你那帽子。
聽著。聽我說。我是你們的鄰居。
zhLatn: Gāogōulí! Nǐ shì Gāogōulí de, duì ba? Kàn nǐ nà màozi.
Tīngzhe. Tīng wǒ shuō. Wǒ shì nǐmen de línjū.

en: Your family burned my father’s city.

lines: 그건 우리 아버지가 한 거야! 나는 비단을 보냈잖아! 봄마다!
생각 좀 해, 이놈아. 오늘 밤 나를 죽이면, 내일 너희 이웃은 누구냐?
en: That was my father! I send you silk! Every spring!
Think, boy. Kill me tonight, and tomorrow who’s your neighbour?
Them.
zh: 那是我爹！我給你們送綢緞！每年春天！
想想，小子。今晚殺了我，明天誰是你的鄰居？
zhLatn: Nà shì wǒ diē! Wǒ gěi nǐmen sòng chóuduàn! Měi nián chūntiān!
Xiǎngxiang, xiǎozi. Jīnwǎn shā le wǒ, míngtiān shéi shì nǐ de línjū?
Tāmen.

blocks.html: The king’s bow stays half drawn. He looks up the gravel at the Wei banners coming down it, and the old man riding slowly under them. For one breath he does the arithmetic.
blocks.ko: 왕의 활은 반쯤 당겨진 채 멈춘다. 그는 자갈밭 위로, 내려오는 위나라 깃발들과 그 아래 느릿느릿 말을 모는 노인을 올려다본다. 한 숨 동안, 그는 셈을 한다.

en: Grand Commandant! Look, I’m kneeling! I’m kneeling!
zh: 太尉！你看，我跪了！我跪了！
zhLatn: Tàiwèi! Nǐ kàn, wǒ guì le! Wǒ guì le!

en: In a river.
It doesn’t count.
zhLatn: Zài hé lǐ.
Bú suàn.

blocks.html: The king lets the arrow go. Three generations of Gongsun end in a little river behind a city, in silk. The Wei riders find the son a little further up the bank.
blocks.ko: 왕이 시위를 놓는다. 공손씨 삼대가 성 뒤 작은 강에서, 비단 차림으로 끝난다. 위나라 기병들은 조금 더 위 둑에서 아들을 찾아낸다.

lines: 저자가 그러던데, 이제 당신이 내 이웃이라고.
en: He said you’d be my neighbour now.

lines: 맞는 말이네. 내가 더 나은 이웃이지.
나는 첩자를 안 보내네. 직접 오지.
en: He was right. I’m a better one.
I don’t send spies. I come myself.
zh: 他說得對。我是更好的鄰居。
zhLatn: Tā shuō de duì. Wǒ shì gèng hǎo de línjū.
Wǒ bú pài tànzi. Wǒ qīnzì lái.

blocks.label: Liaodong · after
blocks.ko: 요동 · 그 뒤

blocks.html: The old man enters the city the next day and sorts it like a clerk sorting grain. Every man over fifteen is walked out onto the plain. The heads go into a mound by the gate, so that anyone coming down the western road will understand.
blocks.ko: 노인은 다음 날 성에 들어가 아전이 곡식 고르듯 성을 고른다. 열다섯 넘은 사내는 모두 들판으로 끌려 나간다. 머리들은 성문 옆에 무덤처럼 쌓인다. 서쪽 길로 오는 자라면 누구든 알아듣게.

blocks.html: It turns cold early that year. Some Wei soldiers come to the old man’s tent about coats.
blocks.ko: 그해는 추위가 일찍 온다. 위나라 병사 몇이 솜옷 일로 노인의 막사를 찾아온다.

blocks.speaker: Wei soldier
en: Grand Commandant. The stores are full of padded coats.
We’re freezing out there.
zhLatn: Tàiwèi, kù lǐ duī mǎn le xùyī.
Wǒmen zài wàitou dòng huài le.

lines: 올해는 추위도 나라의 것이다. 나라를 위해 견뎌라.
en: The stores belong to the state.
So does the cold, this year. Bear it for the state.
zh: 今年，冷也是國家的。為國家忍著。
zhLatn: Kù shì guójiā de.
Jīnnián, lěng yě shì guójiā de. Wèi guójiā rěnzhe.

blocks.html: The king stands at the mound for a long time. He has killed men. He has never seen them stacked.
blocks.ko: 왕은 그 무더기 앞에 오래 서 있다. 사람을 죽여 본 적은 있다. 쌓아 놓은 건 처음 본다.

lines: 고구려 같았으면 성문이나 태우고 집에 갔을 거요.
en: In Goguryeo we’d have burned the gate and gone home.

lines: 고구려 같았으면 자네는 아직 호수에 서 있을 걸세.
en: In Goguryeo you’d still be standing in the lake.
zh: 在高句麗，你還站在湖裡呢。
zhLatn: Zài Gāogōulí, nǐ hái zhàn zài hú lǐ ne.

en: You’re a cold old man. You know that?
Yes. It’s how I got old.
zhLatn: Zhīdào. Suǒyǐ cái huó dào lǎo.

blocks.label: The Liao ford · autumn
blocks.ko: 요하 나루 · 가을

blocks.html: The thousand go home before the first snow. The old man rides with them as far as the ford, which a Grand Commandant has no business doing. His secretary mentions this twice.
blocks.ko: 천 기는 첫눈 전에 집으로 간다. 노인은 나루까지 그들과 함께 말을 탄다. 태위라는 자리가 할 일은 아니다. 서기가 그 말을 두 번 한다.

blocks.speaker: The secretary
en: Grand Commandant, the court will—
zhLatn: Tàiwèi, cháotíng nà biān——

lines: 조정은 내가 돌아가도 거기 있을 걸세. 조정이란 늘 그렇지.
en: The court will be there when I get back. Courts always are.
zh: 我回去，朝廷還在。朝廷總是在的。
zhLatn: Wǒ huíqù, cháotíng hái zài. Cháotíng zǒngshì zài de.

blocks.html: At the water the king pulls off his riding coat, Goguryeo cut with the fur turned in, and throws it at the old man.
blocks.ko: 물가에서 왕은 털을 안으로 댄 고구려식 승마 외투를 벗어 노인에게 던진다.

en: I can’t take that.
zhLatn: Zhè wǒ bù néng shōu.

en: In Goguryeo a coat belongs to whoever’s cold.
Bear it for the state.

blocks.html: The old man puts it on. It is too big in the shoulders.
blocks.ko: 노인이 그걸 걸친다. 어깨가 너무 크다.

en: …It fits.
zhLatn: ……Héshēn.

lines: 빚 있소. 바둑판 빚. 큰 걸로 생각해 뒀지.
en: You owe me. From the board. I’ve thought of something big.
Go on.
zhLatn: Shuō ba.

lines: 당신이랑 나 말고. 우린 쉽지. 저쪽 다들 말이오.
en: Samhan and the West stay friends.
Not you and me. We’re easy. Them.
That’s big.
zhLatn: Zhēn dà.

en: I said it would be.

lines: 내가 살아 있는 동안, 위는 자네 강을 건너지 않네. 그만큼은 내가 도장을 찍을 수 있지.
en: While I live, Wei does not cross your river. That much I can sign.
The rest I can only wish.
zh: 我在世一日，魏不渡你的河。這個我能落印。
zhLatn: Wǒ zàishì yí rì, Wèi bú dù nǐ de hé. Zhège wǒ néng luò yìn.
Qíyú de, zhǐ néng pànzhe.

lines: 그럼 크게 바라시오. 나도 그럴 테니.
en: Then wish it loudly. I will.

blocks.html: They drink to it at the ford, and pour the rest into the Liao, which has heard this sort of thing before.
blocks.ko: 둘은 나루에서 그 약속에 잔을 들고, 남은 술을 요하에 붓는다. 요하는 이런 말을 전에도 들어 본 강이다.

en: Look at the ground first. Always.
zhLatn: Xiān kàn dì. Yǒngyuǎn.

en: You said that already.

lines: 늙어서 그렇네. 두 번 말해야 하나는 남거든.
en: I’m old. I say things twice, so one of them stays.
zh: 老了。話說兩遍，總有一遍留得住。
zhLatn: Lǎo le. Huà shuō liǎng biàn, zǒng yǒu yí biàn liú de zhù.

blocks.html: A word about vows between kingdoms. Two men make them on a riverbank. Courts that were not there keep them. The old man means every word. He will spend his last years very busy at court, which is a long way from any river.
blocks.ko: 나라 사이의 맹세에 대해 한마디만 하자. 맹세는 강가에서 두 사내가 한다. 지키는 건 그 자리에 없던 조정들이다. 노인은 한 마디 한 마디 진심이다. 그는 남은 해들을 조정에서 몹시 바쁘게 보낼 것이다. 조정은 어느 강에서든 멀다.

blocks.html: The king rides home and tells everyone the Western Chancellor is his friend. For a while, it is even true.
blocks.ko: 왕은 집으로 돌아가 만나는 사람마다 서쪽 승상이 자기 벗이라고 말한다. 한동안은, 그게 사실이기까지 하다.

blocks.html: Four hundred years later, another western army reaches the same walls. This one did not bring a friend…!
blocks.ko: 사백 년 뒤, 또 다른 서쪽 군대가 같은 성벽 앞에 선다. 이번엔 벗을 데려오지 않았다…!

logline.en: Goguryeo spent fourteen years building a wall. The Blue Dragon simply walks around it.
logline.ko: 고구려는 열네 해 동안 성벽을 쌓았다. 청룡은 그냥 돌아서 간다.

HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Every wall assumes the enemy will knock. Goguryeo has spent fourteen years building a wall of forts along the river. The Blue Dragon simply walks around it. He shows his banners on the middle road, then turns north in the night. By morning his horse are across an unwatched ford. The first fortress shuts its gates. It holds exactly as long as the gates do.
blocks.ko: 모든 성벽은 적이 문을 두드릴 거라고 믿는다. 고구려는 십사 년 동안 강을 따라 성의 벽을 쌓았다. 청룡은 그 벽을 그냥 돌아간다. 가운데 길에 깃발을 보여 주고, 밤에 북으로 꺾는다. 아침이 되자 그의 기병은 아무도 지키지 않던 여울을 건너 있다. 첫 성이 문을 닫는다. 딱 그 문이 버티는 만큼만 버틴다.

blocks.html: Envoys went to the Great Tang and said: “Goguryeo and Baekje trample on your servant’s country. We are attacked again and again, and have lost dozens of forts. The two countries have joined their armies and swear to take us, and they will march in force this ninth month. Our altars will not survive. We send this envoy to submit to the great country, and beg for a detachment to save us.”
blocks.ko: 사신을 대당에 보내 아뢰었다. “고구려와 백제가 신의 나라를 침범하여 여러 차례 공격을 받아 수십 성을 잃었습니다. 두 나라가 군사를 합쳐 기어이 빼앗으려 하며, 이번 9월에 크게 일어나려 합니다. 저희 나라의 사직은 반드시 온전하지 못할 것이니, 삼가 배신을 보내 대국에 목숨을 맡기오며, 군사 얼마를 빌려 구원해 주시기를 청합니다.”
blocks.hanja: 遣使大唐上言：「高句麗、百濟侵凌臣國，累遭攻襲數十城。兩國連兵，期之必取，將以今玆九月大擧。下國社稷必不獲全，謹遣陪臣歸命大國，願乞偏師，以存救援。」
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Seondeok, yr. 12 (643), 9th month

blocks.html: The emperor said: “Gai Suwen murdered his lord, butchered his ministers and tortures his people. Now he defies Our edict and preys on his neighbours. He cannot go unpunished.”
blocks.ko: 황제가 말하였다. “개소문은 그 임금을 시해하고 대신들을 해쳤으며 백성을 잔혹하게 학대하였다. 이제 또 짐의 조명을 어기고 이웃 나라를 침략하니, 치지 않을 수 없다.”
blocks.hanja: 上曰：「蓋蘇文弒其君，賊其大臣，殘虐其民，今又違我詔命，侵暴鄰國，不可以不討。」
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 197, Tang Taizong, Zhenguan 18 (644)

blocks.html: Gai Suwen said to the envoy Xuanjiang: “Silla and I have hated each other a long time. When the Sui invaded us, Silla took its chance and seized five hundred li of our land, every walled town on it. Unless they give back what they took, I doubt the fighting can stop.”
blocks.ko: 개소문이 현장에게 말하였다. “우리와 신라는 원한이 쌓인 지 오래다. 지난날 수나라가 쳐들어왔을 때 신라가 그 틈을 타 우리 땅 오백 리를 빼앗아 성읍을 모두 차지하였다. 빼앗은 땅을 돌려주지 않는 한, 싸움은 그치지 않을 것이다.”
blocks.hanja: 蓋蘇文謂玄獎曰：「我與新羅怨隙已久。往者隋人入寇，新羅乘釁奪我地五百里，城邑皆據有之。自非歸我侵地，兵恐未能已。」
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 197, Tang Taizong, Zhenguan 18 (644)

blocks.caption: Banners on the middle road, horses at the northern ford. Goguryeo watched the banners.
blocks.ko: 깃발은 가운데 길에, 말은 북쪽 여울에. 고구려는 깃발을 보고 있었다.

blocks.html: The New Fortress doesn’t fall. The emperor’s cousin spends ten days under its walls and leaves with nothing. So the Blue Dragon posts a guard on it and turns south. The next fort lasts a little over ten days. Seven hundred men Yeon sent to hold it are taken in the gate. They ask to serve the emperor instead.
blocks.ko: 신성은 무너지지 않는다. 황제의 사촌이 열흘을 성 아래 머물다 빈손으로 물러난다. 그래서 청룡은 신성에 감시병을 남기고 남으로 돈다. 다음 성은 열흘 남짓 버틴다. 연이 지키라고 보낸 칠백 명이 성문에서 붙잡힌다. 그들은 대신 황제를 섬기겠다고 청한다.

lines: 짐을 위해 싸우면, 대막리지가 처자식을 다 죽일 게다.
한 사람의 힘을 얻자고 한 집안을 없애는 짓은 짐이 차마 못 하겠다. 돌려보내거라.
en: Their homes are all in Gasi, I am told.
If they fight for Us, the Supreme Commander will kill every wife and child they have.
To gain one man’s arm by wiping out his house — that We cannot bring Ourselves to do. Send them home.
zh: 若為朕而戰，莫離支必盡殺其妻子。
得一人之力而滅一家，朕不忍也。遣之歸。
zhLatn: Tīngshuō tāmen jiā dōu zài Jiāshī.
Ruò wèi zhèn ér zhàn, Mòlízhī bì jìn shā qí qīzǐ.
Dé yī rén zhī lì ér miè yī jiā, zhèn bùrěn yě. Qiǎn zhī guī.

blocks.html: They go home with grain for the road. It is a kindness, and it is also arithmetic: seven hundred men who have seen the size of this army will describe it to Gasi better than any envoy could.
blocks.ko: 그들은 길양식까지 받아 집으로 돌아간다. 자비이기도 하고 셈이기도 하다. 이 군대의 크기를 제 눈으로 본 칠백 명은 어떤 사신보다도 그것을 가시성에 잘 전할 것이다.

blocks.html: Between the army and the walls lies the Liao marsh. Two hundred li of mud. The Western host once went in up to the knee and came out as a song. The emperor’s engineer lays a road of earth across it as the column walks, wide enough for carts. The Blue Dragon is already under Yodong’s walls, waiting for him.
blocks.ko: 군대와 성벽 사이에 요하의 늪이 있다. 이백 리의 진흙. 서국 대군이 무릎까지 빠져 들어갔다가 노래가 되어 나온 곳이다. 황제의 장인이 대열이 걷는 대로 그 위에 수레가 다닐 만한 흙길을 깐다. 청룡은 벌써 요동성 아래서 그를 기다린다.

blocks.speaker: The West lookout
lines: 아니, 길이 둘이야. 북쪽하고 동쪽. 저건 순찰이 아니라 군대다.
en: Dust! North road—
No. Two roads. North and east. That’s not a patrol, that’s an army.

blocks.html: Goguryeo has sent forty thousand to break the siege. The emperor’s cousin has four thousand, and orders to dig in and wait. He charges instead. His line breaks. He climbs a rise, sees their ranks in a muddle, and goes back in.
blocks.ko: 고구려가 포위를 풀러 사만을 보냈다. 황제의 사촌에게는 사천과, 참호를 파고 기다리라는 명이 있다. 그는 대신 돌격한다. 줄이 무너진다. 그는 언덕에 올라 저쪽 대열이 엉망인 걸 보고, 다시 들어간다.

lines: …머리가 천이요, 명은 어겼다. 길게 꾸짖어야겠구나. 저녁을 든 뒤에.
en: He was told to wait for Us.
…A thousand heads, and he disobeyed. We shall have to scold him at length. After dinner.

blocks.html: When the last wagon is over the marsh, the emperor has the road torn up. Nobody goes home the way they came. He wants every man in the column to know it.
blocks.ko: 마지막 수레가 늪을 건너자 황제는 길을 걷어 내게 한다. 아무도 왔던 길로 돌아가지 못한다. 그는 대열의 모든 병사가 그걸 알기를 바란다.

blocks.html: Then Yodong itself, the Eastern Fortress. It held off the last dynasty for three summers and never opened. The Blue Dragon has already driven one sortie back through the gate when the emperor arrives. He rides to the moat with a sack of earth across his saddle and throws it in. His officers can’t be seen carrying less than him. They carry two. The army rings the walls a hundred deep and beats the drums until the ground answers.
blocks.ko: 그리고 요동, 동쪽의 성 그 자체. 지난 왕조를 세 번의 여름 동안 막아 내고 끝내 열리지 않은 성이다. 황제가 도착했을 때 청룡은 이미 한 번의 출격을 성문 안으로 밀어 넣은 뒤다. 황제는 안장에 흙 자루 하나를 얹고 해자 끝까지 달려가 그것을 던져 넣는다. 장수들은 황제보다 적게 나르는 모습을 보일 수 없다. 그래서 두 자루씩 나른다. 군대는 성을 백 겹으로 둘러싸고 땅이 대답할 때까지 북을 친다.

blocks.html: The gate the West keeps knocking on.
blocks.ko: 서쪽이 자꾸 두드리는 문.

blocks.label: The Shrine
blocks.ko: 사당

blocks.html: Inside the walls there is a shrine to the Holy King. Ask the town who he was and they say Jumong, as if that settles it. A coat of chain mail hangs in it, and a long sharp spear, and the town will tell you both came down from heaven. By the eighth day stones are coming over the parapet. The elders choose a girl from the town, wash her, paint her, dress her in red silk and a bride’s crown, and walk her up to the shrine to be given to the god.
blocks.ko: 성안에는 성왕의 사당이 있다. 성 사람들에게 그가 누구냐고 물으면 주몽이라고 한다. 그거면 다 설명된다는 듯이. 사당에는 쇠사슬 갑옷 한 벌과 날 선 긴 창이 걸려 있는데, 성 사람들은 둘 다 하늘에서 내려온 것이라고 말한다. 여드레째가 되자 성가퀴 너머로 돌이 날아든다. 어른들은 성안에서 처녀 하나를 골라 씻기고, 단장시키고, 붉은 비단과 신부의 관을 입혀, 신에게 바치러 사당으로 데려간다.

en: It’s… heavy. The dress.
…Tell my mam. Tell her I didn’t cry.
The Holy King… is smiling.
He has taken his bride! This city will stand whole!

blocks.html: They close the shrine door on her. The town sleeps better that night. She doesn’t.
blocks.ko: 그들은 아이를 들여보내고 사당 문을 닫는다. 그날 밤 성은 조금 편히 잔다. 아이는 못 잔다.

blocks.html: The Holy King isn’t consulted again. Towers roll up to the parapet. On the twelfth day a south wind rises. They fire the south-west tower, and the wind carries it into town.
blocks.ko: 성왕께 다시 묻는 사람은 없다. 공성탑이 성가퀴에 붙는다. 열이틀째 남풍이 인다. 그들이 서남쪽 망루에 불을 지르자 바람이 불길을 성안으로 실어 간다.

blocks.speaker: Yodong soldier
lines: 망루는 놔두라우! 집, 집이야— 애들 날래 끌어내!
en: Wind’s turned— it’s coming in!
Leave the tower! The houses— get the bairns out of the houses!

blocks.html: The fire takes the town street by street. The shrine is stone, so it is the last roof standing when the gate gives. The Western squad kicks its door in, looking for gold.
blocks.ko: 불은 거리를 하나씩 삼킨다. 사당은 돌집이라, 성문이 무너질 때 서 있는 마지막 지붕이 된다. 서군 한 무리가 금붙이를 찾아 사당 문을 걷어찬다.

blocks.html: They find a girl in red silk sitting under the chain mail, holding the god’s spear the wrong way round.
blocks.ko: 그들이 찾은 건 쇠사슬 갑옷 아래 앉은 붉은 비단의 처녀 하나다. 신의 창을 거꾸로 쥐고 있다.

en: Don’t.
I’m married.

blocks.html: The soldiers laugh. Then the emperor’s horse is in the doorway, and nobody laughs.
blocks.ko: 병사들이 웃는다. 그러다 문간에 황제의 말이 들어서고, 아무도 웃지 않는다.

en: Whose bride is this?

lines: 저들 신의 신부랍니다, 폐하. 저 갑옷 주인이요.
en: Their god’s, Majesty. The one who owns the armour.

lines: 그렇다면 남의 아내는 취하지 않는다. 죽은 자의 아내라도.
그에게 두어라. 저들의 신이 그녀에게 무엇을 해 줄 수 있는지, 이 성이 보게 하라.
en: Then We do not take another man’s wife. Not even a dead man’s.
Leave her to him. Let the city see what its god can do for her.

blocks.html: When the fighting stops, the clerks count ten thousand dead, then lose interest and count the grain. The fortress a million men couldn’t open has lasted twelve days.
blocks.ko: 싸움이 그치자 서기들은 죽은 자를 만까지 세다가, 흥미를 잃고 곡식을 센다. 백만 대군이 열지 못한 성이 열이틀을 버텼다.

blocks.html: Veterans spit and say the real argument is still ahead, at Ansi.
blocks.ko: 늙은 병사들은 침을 뱉으며 말한다. 진짜 싸움은 아직이라고. 안시에서.

blocks.label: Below Ansi
blocks.ko: 안시성 아래

blocks.html: Then the Second Emperor rides on to look at Ansi, and the man who holds it comes out onto the wall to look back. Nobody on the Western side ever writes down his name.
blocks.ko: 그러고 나서 황제는 안시를 보러 말을 몬다. 안시를 지키는 사내가 성벽 위로 나와 그를 마주 본다. 서국 쪽의 누구도 끝내 그의 이름을 적지 않는다.

lines: 짐은 용서할 자의 이름은 알아 두는 편이다.
en: You. On the wall. Your name.
We like to know whom We are about to forgive.

lines: 듣자 하니 그쪽은 이름 불리는 거 질색이라며.
en: You will simply… have to call me the man on the wall.
I hear you don’t care for names anyway.

lines: 역사는 너를 기억하는 수고를 하지 않으리라. 역사는 짐이 쓰는 것이니.
en: A nameless man, then.
History will not trouble itself to remember you. We are the one writing it.

lines: 그쪽 뒤엔 이백 리 진흙에, 돌아갈 길도 없잖아. 난 성벽 하나랑 가을 한 철이 통째로 있고.
en: Write fast, then.
You’ve got two hundred li of mud behind you and no road home. I’ve got a wall and all autumn.

blocks.html: The emperor does not ask twice. Nobody has ever made him ask twice. He turns his horse and starts looking at the ground around Ansi the way a cook looks at a goose.
blocks.ko: 황제는 두 번 묻지 않는다. 누구도 그에게 두 번 묻게 만든 적이 없다. 그는 말머리를 돌리고, 요리사가 거위를 보듯 안시 주변의 땅을 살피기 시작한다.

blocks.label: The Rest of the Line
blocks.ko: 남은 성들

blocks.html: The rest of the line comes down like roof tiles. At White Cliff, Yeon’s riders break out and put a spear into the White Dragon’s waist. He has it bound and is back in the saddle by evening, laughing.
blocks.ko: 나머지 방어선은 기왓장처럼 무너져 내린다. 백암성에서는 연의 기병이 뛰쳐나와 백룡의 허리에 창을 꽂는다. 백룡은 상처를 동여매고 저녁이 되기 전에 다시 안장에 오른다. 웃으면서.

blocks.speaker: Lord of White Cliff
lines: 데놈 다시 말에 올랐어. 구멍 난 채로.
…성문 열라우. 창 맞고 웃는 놈하고는 못 싸운다.
en: He’s back on his horse. With a hole in him.
…Open the gate. I’ll no fight a man who laughs at spears.

blocks.label: The Cape
blocks.ko: 곶

blocks.html: Meanwhile, the sea. Five hundred hulls leave the West’s coast and cross in four days. Nobody aboard has fought on water. Nobody thinks they’ll need to. Theirs are the bigger ships.
blocks.ko: 그사이, 바다. 배 오백 척이 서쪽 해안을 떠나 나흘 만에 건넌다. 배에 탄 누구도 물 위에서 싸워 본 적이 없다. 그럴 일이 있으리라 생각하는 사람도 없다. 배는 저쪽이 더 크니까.

blocks.html: Where the land runs out, Bisa sits on a ridge with cliffs on every side. Below it, in the inlet, Goguryeo keeps a few warships. The records don’t mention them. The records were written on the other side’s decks.
blocks.ko: 땅이 끝나는 곳, 비사성은 사방이 벼랑인 능선 위에 앉아 있다. 그 아래 포구에 고구려는 전함 몇 척을 둔다. 기록에는 그 배들이 없다. 기록은 저쪽 갑판 위에서 쓰였다.

blocks.speaker: A Goguryeo lookout
lines: 선장님— 돛입니다. 남쪽. 백까지 세다 그만뒀습니다.
en: Captain— sails. South. I stopped counting at a hundred.
They keep coming out of the haze.

blocks.speaker: A Goguryeo captain
lines: 그럼 지금 간다. 저놈들이 아직 줄지어 올 때.
노 잡아! 오래 살고 싶은 놈은 헤엄쳐서 집에 가라.
en: Then we go now, while they’re still in a line.
Oars! Anyone who wants to live forever can swim home.

blocks.html: A Goguryeo warship is a big ship. It stays a big ship right up to the moment it comes alongside a tower-ship. Then the enemy deck is two men above its own, and the arrows come down.
blocks.ko: 고구려 전함은 큰 배다. 누선 옆에 붙는 그 순간까지는. 붙고 나면 적의 갑판이 제 갑판보다 사람 둘 키만큼 높고, 화살이 위에서 쏟아진다.

blocks.speaker: A Tang crossbowman
lines: 우리 쪽으로 저어 온다. 우리 쪽으로!
en: They’re rowing at us. At us!
…They look so small from up here.

blocks.html: The coast ships burn or run. The fleet beaches under the ridge, and the army walks up out of the surf.
blocks.ko: 연안 함선들은 불타거나 달아난다. 함대는 능선 아래에 배를 대고, 군대가 파도 속에서 걸어 올라온다.

blocks.html: From the beach every side of Bisa is a cliff. Every side but one. A column goes round to the west gate in the dark, and a junior officer named Wang Wendu is the first over the wall. Nobody remembers him for anything else.
blocks.ko: 해변에서 보면 비사성은 어느 쪽이나 벼랑이다. 한 쪽만 빼고. 한 부대가 어둠 속에 서문으로 돌아가고, 왕문도라는 하급 장교가 맨 먼저 성벽을 넘는다. 그 밖의 일로 그를 기억하는 사람은 없다.

blocks.html: In the fifth month the clerks count eight thousand people taken, men and women. The fleet sails on round the cape.
blocks.ko: 오월, 서기들은 사로잡은 사람을 남녀 합쳐 팔천으로 센다. 함대는 곶을 돌아 계속 간다.

blocks.html: Of all the forts Yeon spent fourteen years hauling stone for, two still fly Goguryeo’s banners. One of them is Ansi.
blocks.ko: 연이 십사 년 동안 돌을 날라 쌓은 성들 가운데, 아직 고구려 깃발을 단 곳은 둘뿐이다. 그중 하나가 안시다.

blocks.title: The rest of the line
blocks.caption: A spear in the White Dragon, a fleet on the cape. The tiles keep falling anyway.
blocks.ko: 흰 용의 허리에 창 하나, 곶에는 함대 하나. 기왓장은 그래도 계속 떨어진다.

blocks.label: Pyongyang
blocks.ko: 평양

blocks.html: In Pyongyang, Gesomun reads the Yodong report twice and feeds it to the brazier.
blocks.ko: 평양에서 개소문은 요동의 보고를 두 번 읽고 화로에 던져 넣는다.

lines: 서국 놈들은 그 성 앞에서 여름을 세 번 났어. 이놈은 열이틀이야!
en: Twelve days.
The West sat outside that wall for three summers. This one does it in twelve days!
Go Yunsu. How many can you march by the new moon?
A hundred and fifty thousand, Supreme Commander. With the Mohe horse.

lines: 좋아. 안시로 가라우. 들판에서 맞붙어서 박살 내.
내 아새끼들도 치중대에 딸려 보내. 황데가 도망치는 꼴 좀 보게.
en: Good. Go to Ansi. Meet him in the open and break him on the plain.
And take my bairns with the baggage. Let them watch an emperor run.

blocks.html: An old officer at the end of the table clears his throat. He has been clearing it for forty years. This time he finishes.
blocks.ko: 탁자 끝의 늙은 장교가 헛기침을 한다. 사십 년째 하는 헛기침이다. 이번에는 끝까지 한다.

blocks.speaker: The old officer
lines: 마지막으로 들판에서 제국의 군대를 맞은 임금은… 땅을 안 보셨디요.
en: The open field, sir? With respect.
The last king who met an empire in the open… didn’t look at the ground.

lines: 그럼 가는 길에 고연수한테 해 주라우. 나흘이다. 짧게.
en: Then tell Go Yunsu on the road. You’ve got four days. Make it short.

blocks.html: On the road to Ansi, the old man tells it anyway. Once, a king won twice and went back for a third…!
blocks.ko: 안시로 가는 길에서 노인은 끝내 이야기를 꺼낸다. 옛날, 두 번 이긴 왕이 세 번째를 하러 나갔다…!

logline.en: A king picks a fight over a diplomatic spat. Then he picks a battlefield he hasn’t looked at.
logline.ko: 임금이 외교 말다툼 하나로 싸움을 건다. 그러고는 한 번도 살펴보지 않은 땅을 싸움터로 고른다.

images.alt: The old officer starts with the part kings like to hear. Goguryeo won. Twice.
images.prompt: OPENING STILL of the episode: the first image the reader sees, staging its first line. The line: “The old officer starts with the part kings like to hear. Goguryeo won. Twice.” Context: The old officer starts with the part kings like to hear. Goguryeo won. Twice.   A wide or medium establishing frame that hooks. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: The old officer starts with the part kings like to hear. Goguryeo won. Twice.
blocks.ko: 늙은 장교는 왕들이 듣기 좋아하는 대목부터 꺼낸다. 고구려가 이겼다. 두 번.

blocks.caption: A king who starts a war over a letter. This time, someone writes back.
blocks.ko: 편지 한 장으로 싸움을 거는 임금. 이번엔 답장이 온다.

blocks.html: Four hundred years back, a few summers after a vow at a ford, King Dongchun picked a fight with Wei anyway. Wei did not send its old Chancellor. It sent a general who had stood behind him at Liaodong and taken notes. Goguryeo met him at the Boiling River and won. Then it chased him west up a valley and won again.
blocks.ko: 사백 년 전, 나루에서 맹세를 하고 몇 해 지나지 않아, 동천왕은 기어이 위나라에 싸움을 걸었다. 위는 늙은 승상을 보내지 않았다. 요동에서 그 뒤에 서서 받아 적던 장수를 보냈다. 고구려는 비류수에서 그를 맞아 이겼다. 그리고 서쪽 골짜기로 그를 쫓아가 또 이겼다.

lines: 그 이름난 장수란 놈? 그놈 목숨은 내 손바닥 안에 있다.
en: Wei’s great army is worse than our small one.
Their famous general? His life is in the palm of my hand.
Five thousand horse. We ride now.

blocks.speaker: The captain
lines: 전하, 강 건너 땅은— 아무도 달려 보지 않았습니다.
척후를 보내게 해 주십시오. 반나절이면 됩니다.
en: Majesty, the ground past the river— nobody’s ridden it.
Let me send scouts. One afternoon.
One afternoon is all I need to win.

blocks.html: So the king took five thousand horse out to win a third time, on ground he had not looked at. The Wei general formed a square on a slope that ran his way, and waited.
blocks.ko: 그렇게 왕은 세 번째 승리를 거두러 철기 오천을 끌고 나갔다. 들여다본 적도 없는 땅으로. 위의 장수는 제 쪽으로 기운 비탈에 방진을 치고 기다렸다.

blocks.speaker: The captain
en: Majesty, they’re not running.
Why aren’t they running?

blocks.html: The square held. The horses didn’t. Eighteen thousand men died in an afternoon.
blocks.ko: 방진은 버텼다. 말들은 버티지 못했다. 한나절 만에 만 팔천이 죽었다.

en: …I did not look at the ground.

blocks.html: Hwando is burned. The king runs east with a handful of men, and the Wei riders are one valley behind and closing.
blocks.ko: 환도성이 불탄다. 왕은 한 줌의 사람을 데리고 동쪽으로 달아나고, 위의 기병은 골짜기 하나 뒤에서 좁혀 온다.

blocks.html: At a ford in the rain, the captain who asked for scouts holds out his hand.
blocks.ko: 빗속의 여울목에서, 척후를 청했던 그 장교가 손을 내민다.

blocks.speaker: The captain
lines: 놈들은 임금의 옷을 쫓고 있습니다. 하나 잡게 해 주지요.
en: Your robe, Majesty.
They’re chasing a king’s robe. Let them catch one.

lines: …네 이름. 내가 네 이름도 묻지 않았구나.
en: …Your name. I never even asked your name.

blocks.speaker: The captain
en: You didn’t look at the ground either, Majesty.
Go.

blocks.html: He rides back up the valley in the king’s robe, slowly, so they can see it. They see it. Nobody on either side writes down his name.
blocks.ko: 그는 임금의 옷을 입고 골짜기를 거슬러 천천히 올라간다. 저들이 볼 수 있게. 저들은 본다. 어느 쪽에서도 그의 이름을 적어 두지 않는다.

blocks.html: A mountain capital, built for the day the plain is lost.
blocks.ko: 들판을 잃는 날을 위해 지은 산 위의 수도.

blocks.html: Goguryeo takes forty years to be a kingdom again. It is the first time in this story that a Samhan capital burns because of one bad afternoon, and it is not the last, and every king in this record has heard about it.
blocks.ko: 고구려가 다시 나라 꼴을 갖추는 데 사십 년이 걸린다. 이 이야기에서 하루 오후의 잘못으로 삼한의 도성이 불탄 첫 번째 일이고, 마지막은 아니며, 이 기록의 모든 임금이 그 이야기를 들어 알고 있다.

blocks.html: On the road to Ansi, the young general hears him out politely, the way you let a grandfather finish.
blocks.ko: 안시로 가는 길에서, 젊은 장수는 끝까지 공손히 듣는다. 할아버지 얘기를 끊지 않고 들어 드리듯이.

lines: 그런데 그 임금은 기병 오천이었디요. 저는 십오만입니다.
en: Good story, grandfather.
But he had five thousand horse. I have a hundred and fifty thousand men.

blocks.speaker: The old officer
en: …So did Wei.

blocks.html: A hundred and fifty thousand men march toward an open plain. On a hill above it, the emperor is waiting…!
blocks.ko: 십오만 대군이 탁 트인 들판으로 나아간다. 그 위 언덕에서 황제가 기다리고 있다…!

logline.en: A farmer in a white coat walks onto the field as a name on a muster roll. The Emperor is watching.
logline.ko: 흰 옷을 입은 농부 하나가 군적부의 이름 한 줄로 싸움터에 들어선다. 황제가 지켜보고 있다.
