images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Caravaggio’s Calling of Saint Matthew. Inside the Emperor’s dark campaign pavilion at dusk: from the right, in shadow, the Second Emperor stretches out his arm and points across the frame; Li Shiji at his shoulder. Left, Xue Rengui kneels on one knee in dirt-streaked white armour, looking up, the fangtian ji upright in his fist, its crescent blade wet and glistening. A single hard shaft of low sun slants in through the open tent flap above the Emperor’s pointing hand and lands on Xue’s face and the ji; the rest of the pavilion is black. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — XUE RENGUI — FACE and garments from attached /ch_xue_rengui.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Tang's white-robed champion; showman of the charge. Carry: Fangtian ji halberd — no ring sword at all. #e8e3d5 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: ring-pommel sword. | THE SECOND EMPEROR — FACE and garments from attached /ch_taizong.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Bearded Tang emperor: black futou cap with an upright pin, thick black beard and moustache, fierce scowl. Dress: Imperial yellow robe-cape over black brocade. Demeanor: Commands; never asks. Conqueror's contempt that curdles at Ansi. Presence: THE SON OF HEAVEN — every frame he is in bends around him. He is SHROUDED IN DARKNESS: the black of the hall gathers around him like a mantle. One close practical light (a lamp, a brazier, a lamp-tree) rakes across him from below or from the side and SCULPTS him — the heavy yellow silk breaks into deep protruding folds brushed in loaded oil strokes that follow each fold, gold thread flicked in with impasto, the beard and cheekbones carved — and then falls off into black across his body and half his face; that falloff is the darkness, never a flat backlit silhouette. The camera sits BELOW his eyeline (low angle or worm’s-eye) and he is always placed HIGHER than anyone near him — on the dais, on a step, standing while others kneel or sit. He reads larger than life through lens and staging, not as a giant: broad shoulders, the robe spreading wide and heavy into the dark like a mountain, his shadow enormous on walls and floor. Unhurried, heavy stillness — never fidgeting, never casual, never a colleague at someone’s shoulder; when he smiles or laughs it is a predator’s ease, and the room goes quiet around it. Everyone else in frame is smaller, lower, less lit, turned toward him. The aura is darkness, scale and the hush around him — never a glow, never a halo, never rays behind his head. #c97a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: Korean ring-pommel sword; Korean lamellar. | BLUE DRAGON — FACE and garments from attached /ch_blue_dragon.png (face only; invent a new pose). #4b78c9 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Establishing extreme wide shot, raging battle at noon on the plain below a steep pine-dark mountain in Liaodong. Tens of thousands of Goguryeo infantry and cavalry as massed painted shapes press against a long Tang line, red Goguryeo banners against Tang vermilion-and-white, dust standing up off the field like a second army in sculpted gouache columns. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Go Yunsu liked the old man’s story. He just didn’t think it was about him.
blocks.ko: 고연수는 노인의 이야기가 마음에 들었다. 다만 그게 자기 얘기라고는 생각하지 않았다.

blocks.html: Named for where an emperor stopped. Emperors name a lot of things.
blocks.ko: 황제가 멈춰 선 자리라 붙은 이름. 황제들은 이름 붙이길 좋아한다.

blocks.caption: Goguryeo sends a hundred and fifty thousand down the crow road. The emperor sends himself.
blocks.ko: 고구려는 까마귀 길로 십오만을 내려보낸다. 황제는 자기 자신을 보낸다.

blocks.html: At Stallion Mountain the Second Emperor does not wait behind the line.
blocks.ko: 주필산에서 황제는 진 뒤에서 기다리지 않는다.

en: I myself am the vanguard…!
zhLatn: Zhèn jí shì xiānfēng…!

blocks.html: The relief army comes down the crow road under banners that think numbers are an argument. Go Yunsu and Go Hyejin ride at the front. The emperor sends a thousand Turkish horse to meet them and tells them to lose. They lose beautifully, all the way west to the foot of a mountain. Across the plain, under a ridge, the West look like a single army of fifteen thousand.
blocks.ko: 구원군은 숫자가 곧 논리라고 믿는 깃발을 앞세우고 까마귀 길을 내려온다. 고연수와 고혜진이 맨 앞에서 달린다. 황제는 돌궐 기병 천을 내보내 맞서게 하고, 지라고 이른다. 그들은 아주 보기 좋게 진다. 서쪽으로, 산기슭까지 내내. 들판 건너 고개 아래, 서군은 만오천짜리 군대 하나로 보인다.

blocks.speaker: The old officer
lines: 황제가 고작 만오천 데리고 여기까지 오진 않습니다. 진을 치십시오. 군량을 끊고 싸움은 겨울한테 맡기십시오.
en: Since when do Turks run?
That’s no all of them.
An emperor doesn’t come this far with fifteen thousand. Dig in. Cut his grain. Let winter do the fighting.

lines: 겨울은 아직 안 왔소, 어르신. 저자는 왔디. 몸소.
황데 목을 칠 기회가 이보다 좋을 순 없소.
en: Winter’s no here yet, grandfather. He is. In person.
We will never get a better chance at an emperor’s head.

blocks.html: Nobody tells Go Yunsu about the valley behind him. In the night the Black Dragon takes a second army round the north of the mountain and into it. The emperor climbs the mountain with his drums, banners furled.
blocks.ko: 고연수 뒤편 골짜기 얘기는 아무도 해 주지 않는다. 밤사이 흑룡이 또 한 무리를 이끌고 산 북쪽을 돌아 그 골짜기로 든다. 황제는 북을 데리고, 깃발을 눕힌 채 산에 오른다.

blocks.speaker: Goguryeo picket
lines: 장군. 산 우에 뭐이 움직입네다. 많이요.
en: Sir. Something’s moving on the mountain. A lot of something.
No banners, mind.

lines: 가서 자. 아침엔 황데를 먹을 거니까.
en: No banners, no army. Deer.
Away to your bed. We’re having an emperor for breakfast.

blocks.html: At dawn, drums start on the mountain above the field. The emperor is up there with his horns and his flags, playing the battle like a court orchestra.
blocks.ko: 새벽, 들판 위 산에서 북이 울리기 시작한다. 황제가 그 위에서 뿔나팔과 깃발로, 궁중 악단 부리듯 싸움을 연주한다.

blocks.label: The Mountain
blocks.ko: 주필산

blocks.label: The West Line
blocks.ko: 서군 진영

blocks.html: In the Western line stands a guard captain whose accent still has the sea in it. Sul Gedu left Silla twenty-four winters ago, in the hold of a merchant ship. When the emperor called for volunteers, he put his own name down. It’s the only way a foreigner gets a captain’s sash. Across the field, the enemy’s banners are close enough to read.
blocks.ko: 서국 진영의 근위 대장들 사이에, 말투에 아직 바다가 묻어 있는 사내가 하나 있다. 설계두는 스물네 해 전 상선 짐칸에 숨어 신라를 떠났다. 황제가 지원자를 부르자 그는 제 이름을 써넣었다. 이방인이 대장의 띠를 받는 길은 그것뿐이다. 들판 건너편, 적의 깃발이 글자가 읽힐 만큼 가깝다.

lines: 어이, 설 과의. 저쪽 놈들 말이오… 삼한 사람들이라던데.
en: Hey, Captain Xue. That lot over there… they say they’re Samhan men.
Aren’t you from Samhan as well?
zh: 喂，薛果毅。對面那些人……聽說是三韓人。
zhLatn: Wèi, Xuē guǒyì. Duìmiàn nàxiē rén… tīngshuō shì Sānhán rén.
Nǐ bù yě shì Sānhán lái de ma?

lines: 신라선 사람 쓸 때 뼈부터 따진데이. 재주가 아무리 크고 공이 아무리 커도, 뼈가 아이면 몬 넘는다. 그냥 몬 넘는다.
그래가 바다 건너왔제. 천자 곁에서 관 쓰고 띠 두르고 칼 차고 드나들어 볼라꼬.
en: Samhan. Silla.
In Silla they count your bones before they hire you. Doesn’t matter how big your talent is or how big your deeds — wrong bones, and you don’t get over the wall. Simply don’t.
So I crossed the sea. To walk in and out at the Son of Heaven’s side with a cap and a sash and a sword.
…That’ll do me.
zh: 新羅用人，先論骨頭。才再大、功再高，骨頭不對，就是過不去。就是過不去。
所以我渡海來了。想在天子身邊，戴冠束帶、佩劍出入。
zhLatn: Sānhán. Xīnluó.
Xīnluó yòng rén, xiān lùn gǔtou. Cái zài dà, gōng zài gāo, gǔtou bú duì, jiùshì guò bú qù. Jiùshì guò bú qù.
Suǒyǐ wǒ dù hǎi lái le. Xiǎng zài tiānzǐ shēnbiān, dài guān shù dài, pèi jiàn chūrù.
……Zhè jiù gòu le.

blocks.html: The soldier laughs, not sure he was meant to. Sul Gedu ties off his helmet cord and does not look at the banners again.
blocks.ko: 병사는 웃어도 되는 건지 모른 채 웃는다. 설계두는 투구 끈을 묶고, 다시는 그 깃발 쪽을 보지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Field Below the Mountain
blocks.ko: 산 아래 벌판

blocks.html: Noon. The plain under the mountain is one long noise: drums above, horns, a hundred and fifty thousand men leaning on a line that will not give. Dust stands up off the field like a second army. Somewhere inside it the Goguryeo centre is winning, knows it, and is shouting about it.
blocks.ko: 한낮. 산 아래 벌판은 하나의 긴 소음이다. 위에선 북과 뿔나팔, 아래에선 꿈쩍 않는 대열을 미는 십오만. 먼지가 두 번째 군대처럼 벌판에서 일어선다. 그 속 어딘가에서 고구려 중군이 이기고 있고, 그걸 알고, 그걸 소리치고 있다.

blocks.speaker: Goguryeo ranks
en: Push! PUSH, they’re giving—
Where’s the Turks gone? Where’s the bloody Turks—
Never mind the Turks, mind your feet!
Who’s yon in white?
lines: 돌궐 놈들 어드메 갔네? 그 돌궐 놈들—

blocks.html: The one in white is a low officer of the Western line who decided an hour ago that this field needed a mark it could not look away from. He put on white armour — not for mourning, for visibility — hung two bows at his waist, and took up his grandfather’s old ji, the one his wife bought back with eggs. Now he rides into the front so hard the relief army has to notice him or die without knowing why.
blocks.ko: 흰 것은 당진의 낮은 장교 하나다. 한 시진 전에, 이 벌판엔 눈을 뗄 수 없는 표식이 필요하다고 판단한 사람. 그는 흰 갑옷을 입었다 — 상중이라서가 아니라, 보이려고 — 허리에 활 둘을 차고, 아내가 달걀로 되사 온 할아버지의 낡은 극을 들었다. 그리고 지금, 구원군이 그를 알아채거나 모른 채 죽게 되도록 선두로 파고든다.

en: Make a path.
If you will not — the ji will.
zhLatn: Ràng lù.
Ruò bù ràng——jǐ zì huì ràng.

blocks.speaker: Goguryeo ranks
en: Shoot him! Shoot the white one!
I did! Twice!
Then shoot him a third—
Drums. Listen— the drums have changed—
BEHIND! They’re behind us!

blocks.html: No one in the Goguryeo line stops him for long. Then the drums on the mountain change, and the Black Dragon’s banners come out of the valley behind them. The relief army turns to face the wrong way twice. The formation breaks. The mountain learns a new colour.
blocks.ko: 고구려 진에서 그를 오래 막아서는 자는 없다. 그때 산 위의 북소리가 바뀌고, 뒤편 골짜기에서 흑룡의 깃발이 쏟아져 나온다. 구원군은 엉뚱한 쪽으로 두 번 돌아선다. 진이 무너진다. 산이 새로운 색 하나를 배운다.

blocks.html: Just then came thunder and lightning. Xue Rengui, a man of Longmen, in strange clothing, broke into the enemy line with a great shout, and nothing could stand before him. The Goguryeo troops gave way; the main army followed through, and the Goguryeo troops broke completely…
blocks.ko: 마침 천둥과 번개가 쳤는데, 용문 사람 설인귀가 기이한 옷을 입고 크게 소리치며 적진을 무너뜨리니 향하는 곳마다 대적할 자가 없었다. 고구려 군사가 쓰러지듯 흩어지자 대군이 그 틈을 타니, 고구려 군사가 크게 무너졌다…
blocks.hanja: 會有雷電，龍門人薛仁貴著奇服，大呼陷陳，所向無敵；高麗兵披靡，大軍乘之，高麗兵大潰…
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 198, Tang Zhenguan 19 (645), 6th month

en: Who is that man in white armour.
The one at the tip of the spear.
zhLatn: Nà báijiǎ shì hérén.
Máojiān nà hànzi.

en: Xue Rengui, Your Majesty.
A soldier… who was a farmer.
zhLatn: Xuē Rénguì, Bìxià.
Yī jiè… céng wéi nóngfū zhī bīng.

blocks.html: They bring him up. Dirt on the white. Blood on the crescent of the ji. He kneels like a man who has never been in a palace and does not intend to apologise for it.
blocks.ko: 그를 앞으로 불러낸다. 흰옷에 흙. 극의 초승달에 피. 그는 궁에 들어와 본 적 없는 사람처럼 무릎을 꿇고, 그걸 사과할 생각은 없어 보인다.

lines: 변경의 일을 맡길 날랜 장수를 고르려 하거늘 — 경만 한 자가 없도다.
짐은 요동을 얻은 것보다, 경을 얻은 것이 더 기쁘다.
en: My old generals are all aged.
I have been looking for a fierce one to entrust the frontier to — and I find none better than you.
I am less happy about gaining Liaodong than about gaining you.
zh: 欲擇猛將托邊事——無有過於卿者。
朕得遼東之喜，不及得卿。
zhLatn: Zhèn jiùjiàng jiē lǎo yǐ.
Yù zé měngjiàng tuō biānshì——wú yǒu guòyú qīng zhě.
Zhèn dé Liáodōng zhī xǐ, bùjí dé qīng.

lines: 다만 이 극이, 폐하의 길을 조금 넓혀 드렸을 뿐입니다.
en: A farmer… how could he dare.
This ji only widened Your Majesty’s road a little.
zh: 此戟不過略開陛下之路罷了。
zhLatn: Nóngfū… ān gǎn.
Cǐ jǐ bùguò lüè kāi Bìxià zhī lù bàle.

blocks.html: The emperor looks at the ji longer than at the man. New cord over old wood. A blade sharpened so many times it has gone thin as a leaf.
blocks.ko: 황제는 사내보다 극을 더 오래 본다. 묵은 나무에 감은 새 끈. 하도 갈아서 잎사귀처럼 얇아진 날.

lines: 제 할 일은 다 했다. 무고에 있는 것을 가져오너라.
en: That ji is older than Our dynasty.
It has done its work. Bring him the one from the armoury.
zh: 它的事做完了。把武庫那一把拿來給他。
zhLatn: Zhè jǐ, bǐ zhèn de guó hái lǎo.
Tā de shì zuò wán le. Bǎ wǔkù nà yì bǎ ná lái gěi tā.

blocks.html: The one from the armoury is a fangtian huaji: a painted shaft taller than a man, a spear point, and two crescent blades set back to back like a pair of moons. The tag on it says it belonged to Lu Bu, the best fighter of the Han’s last days and its worst son. Armoury tags say a lot of things. Nobody has swung it properly in four hundred years.
blocks.ko: 무고에서 나온 것은 방천화극이다. 사람 키보다 긴 칠한 자루, 창끝 하나, 그리고 등을 맞댄 달 두 개처럼 붙은 초승달 날 한 쌍. 달린 꼬리표에는 여포의 것이라고 적혀 있다. 한나라 끝물에 가장 잘 싸운 사내이자, 가장 못난 아들. 무고의 꼬리표는 별말을 다 한다. 사백 년 동안 이걸 제대로 휘두른 사람은 없었다.

lines: 이것을 들던 자는 아비를 둘이나 죽이고도 졌다.
제 조상을 묻을 줄 아는 집에서 예의를 좀 배우게 하거라.
en: The man who carried this killed two fathers, and lost anyway.
Let it learn some manners in a house that buries its own.
zh: 持此戟者，弒了兩個父親，還是敗了。
讓它到一個肯葬祖先的人家，學學規矩。
zhLatn: Chí cǐ jǐ zhě, shì le liǎng ge fùqīn, háishì bài le.
Ràng tā dào yí ge kěn zàng zǔxiān de rénjiā, xuéxue guīju.

en: A farmer’s house is strict, Majesty.
It will learn.
zhLatn: Nóngjiā guīju yán, bìxià.
Tā huì xué de.

blocks.html: He swings it once to learn the weight. The horses on the picket line step back. So do two of the guards.
blocks.ko: 무게를 익히려고 한 번 휘두른다. 말뚝에 맨 말들이 뒷걸음친다. 호위병 둘도 그런다.

en: Did you see that?
That’s Lu Bu. Lu Bu come back from the dead, I swear it.
zh: 呂布。呂布還魂了，我發誓。
zhLatn: Kànjiàn méi?
Lǚ Bù. Lǚ Bù huánhún le, wǒ fāshì.

blocks.html: They give him gold, silk, a general’s title, and a place among the men who stand at the northern gate. The white coat stays. The old ji rides behind his saddle in its oiled hemp. He made it a promise.
blocks.ko: 금과 비단과 장군의 호와, 북문을 지키는 자리까지 내린다. 흰옷은 남는다. 낡은 극은 기름 먹인 삼베에 싸여 안장 뒤에 실린다. 그 극에게 한 약속이 있다.

blocks.html: That night he has a clerk write home for him. Two lines. The mounds can be finished properly now. Liu should buy the good stone. He does not mention the halberd. She would only say she told him so.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 서기를 시켜 집에 편지를 쓴다. 두 줄이다. 이제 무덤을 제대로 마무리할 수 있다. 유씨는 좋은 돌을 사라. 화극 얘기는 쓰지 않는다. 그러면 그녀는 내가 뭐랬냐고만 할 것이다.

blocks.html: Go Yunsu pulls what is left onto a hill to regroup. Behind the hill, the West have already burned the bridges. Nobody goes home the way they came. The emperor likes that trick.
blocks.ko: 고연수는 남은 군을 수습하려고 언덕 위로 물린다. 언덕 뒤의 다리는 서군이 이미 불태웠다. 왔던 길로 돌아가는 자는 없다. 황제가 아끼는 수법이다.

blocks.html: When the dust settles, the two relief commanders walk into the Western camp on their knees. Their army walks in behind them.
blocks.ko: 먼지가 가라앉자 구원군의 두 장수가 무릎걸음으로 서국 진영에 들어간다. 그들의 군대가 뒤를 따라 들어온다.

lines: …그 양반 살아 있네? 누가 좀 알아보라우. 사과할 게 있어.
en: The old man said dig in.
…Is he alive? Somebody find out. I owe him an apology.

blocks.html: The officers are sent inland, to be subjects far from any border. The common soldiers are sent home. The Mohe riders who came south with them are marched into a valley and buried alive.
blocks.ko: 장교들은 국경에서 먼 내지로 보내져 서국의 백성이 된다. 병졸들은 집으로 돌려보내진다. 그들과 함께 남하한 말갈 기병은 골짜기로 끌려가 산 채로 묻힌다.

blocks.html: Go Yunsu does not live out the year. The records say he died of grief, which is the only cause of death the West ever let a surrendered general keep.
blocks.ko: 고연수는 그해를 넘기지 못한다. 기록은 그가 울화로 죽었다고 적는다. 항복한 장수에게 당이 남겨 준 사인은 그것 하나뿐이다.

blocks.label: The Field at Night
blocks.ko: 밤의 들판

blocks.html: There is another foreigner in the reckoning that night. Riding over the ground where the Goguryeo centre stood, the emperor finds Sul Gedu farther in than any of his own men got, face down among the dead he made.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 공을 헤아리는 자리에는 이방인이 하나 더 있다. 고구려 중군이 서 있던 땅을 말을 타고 지나던 황제는, 자기 군사 누구보다 깊이 들어간 자리에서, 제가 쓰러뜨린 시신들 사이에 엎어져 있는 설계두를 찾는다.

en: Who is this?
He is further in than any of Ours.

lines: 동료들 말이, 폐하 곁에서 관과 띠와 칼을 받는 게 평생 소원이었답니다.
en: A Silla man, Majesty. Sul Gedu.
His friends say he wanted a cap, a sash and a sword. At your side.

lines: 짐의 군사들은 죽음이 두려워 두리번거리며 나아가지 않는데, 이방 사람이 짐을 위해 죽었구나.
벼슬을 내려라. 예를 갖추어 장사 지내라.
en: Our own men look about them and will not advance. A foreigner dies for Us.
Give him the rank. Bury him with full rites.

blocks.html: Then he takes off the imperial robe and lays it over the dead man himself.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 손수 어포를 벗어 죽은 이 위에 덮는다.

blocks.html: The cap, the sash and the sword, more or less. He gets them lying down.
blocks.ko: 관과 띠와 칼, 대강 그것이다. 그는 그것을 누워서 받는다.

blocks.html: Fame is a short leash. Before the army even settles into the Ansi siege, Goguryeo stops trying to kill the man in white in the open and starts trying to keep him.
blocks.ko: 명성은 짧은 밧줄이다. 군이 안시 포위에 자리를 잡기도 전에, 고구려는 흰옷의 사내를 벌판에서 죽이려 하기보다 가두려 한다.

blocks.label: Prisoners
blocks.ko: 포로

blocks.label: The Cell Under the Wall
blocks.ko: 성벽 밑 옥

blocks.html: They take him in a night fight east of the Liao — nets, numbers, the halberd knocked from his hands — and drag him inland to a lesser fortress that is not Ansi and does not want to be famous. Iron on the wrists. A cell under the wall. The white coat cut off him like a trophy.
blocks.ko: 요하 동쪽의 밤싸움에서 그를 잡는다 — 그물, 머릿수, 손에서 떨어진 화극 — 그리고 안시가 아닌, 유명해지고 싶지 않은 작은 성으로 끌고 간다. 손목의 쇠. 성벽 아래 감방. 하얀 옷은 전리품처럼 벗겨진다.

lines: 오늘 밤. 흰옷 입은 놈을 은으로 사 가갓다고. 성왕이시여, 굽어살피소서.
en: The Second Emperor… is coming this way.
Tonight. With silver, to buy back the man in white. Holy King, look down.
…Before His Majesty arrives.
I will have to be out.
zhLatn: …Bìxià jiàdào zhī qián.
Wǒ děi chūqù.

blocks.html: He breaks the irons. He breaks the door. The white coat only made him easy to see.
blocks.ko: 쇠사슬을 부순다. 문을 부순다. 하얀 옷은 그를 보이게만 했을 뿐이다.

blocks.html: He finds the ji on a rack in the yard, still sticky from someone else’s hands, and takes the wall the way water takes a crack. By the time the Second Emperor’s banners show on the ridge, the cell is empty and the fortress is explaining itself to no one.
blocks.ko: 마당 시렁에서 남의 손이 묻은 화극을 찾아 들고, 물이 틈을 찾듯 성벽을 넘는다. 황제의 깃발이 능선에 보일 즈음, 감방은 비어 있고 성은 아무에게도 설명을 하지 못한다.

lines: 달 두 개 달린 그걸 한 손에 들고 성벽을 넘었어.
서국 포로들이 데놈을 여포라고 부르더라. 기땐 웃었는데. 이젠 안 웃기다.
en: He went over the wall with that two-moon thing in one hand.
The Western prisoners call him Lu Bu. I laughed at them. I’m no laughing now.
…That white coat again.
Arriving before Us, I see.
zhLatn: …Yòu shì nà shēn báiyī.
Jìng bǐ zhèn xiān dào.

lines: 폐하를 오래 기다리게 할 수 없었습니다.
en: I could not keep Your Majesty waiting.
The chains… were impolite.
zhLatn: Bù gǎn ràng Bìxià jiǔ hòu.
Nàxiē suǒliàn… tài wúlǐ le.

blocks.html: The Second Emperor laughs once — short, relieved — and does not ask how. A sovereign who has to ask how has already lost the man.
blocks.ko: 황제는 짧게, 안도하며 한 번 웃고, 어떻게 했는지는 묻지 않는다. 어떻게를 물어야 하는 군주는 이미 그 사내를 잃은 것이다.

blocks.label: Two Boys
blocks.ko: 두 소년

blocks.html: Among the prisoners taken at the mountain are two boys, eleven and eight: Gesomun’s sons, the careful one and the one who never backs down first. Their father sent them with the baggage to watch an emperor run.
blocks.ko: 주필산에서 잡힌 포로 가운데 열한 살, 여덟 살 난 사내아이 둘이 있다. 개소문의 아들들이다. 조심성 많은 맏이와, 먼저 물러서는 법이 없는 둘째. 황제가 도망치는 꼴을 보라며 아버지가 치중대에 딸려 보낸 아이들이다.

lines: 너희 아비는 임금을 죽였다. 짐은 형제를 죽였고.
en: So. Gai Suwen’s sons.
Your father killed his king. I killed my brothers.
So you see, he and I understand one another.
zh: 如此，朕與他倒有相通之處。
zhLatn: Yuánlái shì Gàisūwén zhī zǐ.
Ěr fù shā jūn. Zhèn shā xiōngdì.
Rúcǐ, zhèn yǔ tā dào yǒu xiāngtōng zhī chù.

lines: 무릎을 꿇고 대서국의 신하가 되겠다 하면, 둘 다 관작을 주마.
장안의 집, 비단, 이름. 고려에서는 평생 못 가질 것들이다.
en: Here is my offer.
Kneel, call yourselves servants of the great West, and I will give you both titles.
A house in Chang’an, silk, a name. Things Goryeo will never give you.
zh: 跪稱大唐臣子，朕賜爾二人官爵。
長安宅第、絲綢、名號。高麗永不能予者。
zhLatn: Zhèn yǒu yī yì.
Guì chēng Dà Táng chénzǐ, zhèn cì ěr èr rén guānjué.
Cháng'ān zháidì、sīchóu、mínghào. Gāolí yǒng bùnéng yǔ zhě.

en: …Is it true all your horses have names? All six?
lines: ……폐하 말들이 다 이름이 있다는 거, 참말입니까? 여섯 마리 다요?

en: Kneel, and you may ask the groom yourself.
lines: 꿇거라. 그러면 마부에게 직접 물어보게 해 주마.
zhLatn: Guìxià, biàn xǔ nǐ qīn wèn mǎfū.

blocks.html: Namgun’s knee starts to bend. His brother’s hand closes on the back of his collar and holds him straight.
blocks.ko: 남건의 무릎이 굽기 시작한다. 형의 손이 뒷덜미 옷깃을 움켜쥐고 그를 똑바로 세운다.

en: Brother.

blocks.html: Namseng is eleven. He works out, quite quickly, that the Second Emperor wants two and will settle for one, and that only one of them has to be the one who refuses.
blocks.ko: 남생은 열한 살이다. 그는 꽤 빠르게 계산해 낸다. 황제는 둘을 원하지만 하나로도 만족할 것이고, 거절하는 역할은 둘 중 하나만 맡으면 된다는 것을.

lines: 폐하. 제 아우는 어립니다. 아무것도 모릅니다.
거절하는 건 접니다. 벌은 저에게 주십시오.
en: Your Majesty. My brother is small. He understands nothing.
It is I who refuse. Give the punishment to me.
…You are the elder?
zhLatn: …Nǐ shì xiōngzhǎng?

en: I am.

blocks.html: They flog him in front of his brother and send them both back across the Liao in the spring, as a gesture. Namgun does not speak for the whole journey.
blocks.ko: 그들은 아우가 보는 앞에서 그를 매질했고, 봄이 되자 아량이라며 둘 다 요하 너머로 돌려보냈다. 남건은 돌아오는 내내 한마디도 하지 않았다.

en: You took it for me.
I am the elder.

blocks.label: Pyongyang
blocks.ko: 평양

blocks.html: The news reaches Pyongyang in two pieces. The field army is gone. The boys are in the emperor’s tent.
blocks.ko: 소식은 두 토막으로 평양에 닿는다. 들판의 군대는 사라졌다. 아이들은 황제의 막사에 있다.

en: Both of them?

blocks.speaker: Rider
lines: 둘 다입니다, 대막리지. 황데가 아이들에게 너그럽게 하갓다고 전해 왔습니다.
en: Both, Supreme Commander. The emperor sends word he will be kind to them.

lines: 제 형제 죽인 놈이 내 아새끼들한테 너그럽갓다고.
en: Kind.
A man that killed his own brothers, being kind to my bairns.

blocks.html: The hall waits for him to break something. He doesn’t. He calls for a map and puts his thumb on the one fort still flying the old king’s colours. The fort that refused him.
blocks.ko: 대청은 그가 뭔가 부수기를 기다린다. 그는 부수지 않는다. 지도를 가져오게 하고, 아직 옛 왕의 깃발을 단 성 하나에 엄지를 얹는다. 그를 거부한 성이다.

lines: 내가 일곱 살 때, 아버지가 살수에서 서국 깃발을 옆구리에 끼고 돌아왔어. 난 깃발이 황데한테서 열리는 열맨 줄 알았디.
깊이 들어오라 기래. 저번 놈도 기랬어.
en: Ansi. That madman.
When I was seven, my father came home from the Colossal River with the West flag under his arm. I thought flags grew on emperors.
Let him come deep, aye. The last one did.

blocks.html: Why isn’t Gesomun afraid? Go back thirty-three years, to a general who surrendered seven times and won…!
blocks.ko: 개소문은 왜 두려워하지 않는가? 서른세 해 전으로 가 보자. 일곱 번 항복하고 이긴 장수가 있었다…!

logline.en: Ulchi Munduk surrenders seven times on the way south. Every time, the river gets closer.
logline.ko: 을지문덕은 남쪽으로 내려가며 일곱 번 항복한다. 그때마다 강이 가까워진다.

images.alt: Emperor Yang of the West's vast host marches on Goguryeo in 612
images.prompt: Cinematic historical illustration of salsu flashback, Three Kingdoms of Samhan / Tang era (612), scene: Great River, painterly digital art, dramatic natural light, rich period costume, no modern elements, no text, no watermark, --ar 3:2 --stylize 250

images.at: Ulchi Munduk surrenders seven times on the way south.
images.alt: The endless the Western host crosses the Liao on pontoon bridges while Ulchi Munduk watches from a ridge
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE battle frame. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. The Battle of the Colossal River (Salsu), summer 612: a broad shallow river over pale gravel bars between low pine hills in northern Goguryeo. Sui banners are dull gold and black, Goguryeo banners red, their marks illegible brush strokes. The Sui host crossing the Liao River on three long pontoon bridges: a sea of spears and gold-and-black banners under towering dust clouds lit orange by the low sun, columns stretching to the horizon. In the dark foreground on a pine ridge, Ulchi Munduk on horseback, small, watching. Device: the three bridges as long diagonals across the water. HEEWON BATTLE STYLE — this is a battle frame, and every still of this battle shares ONE look so the set plays as one film. Copy the BRUSHWORK AND STYLIZATION of the two attached style_battle boards ONLY — never their ships, flags, figures or composition (the painted board shows 19th-century steam and sailing ships; this battle is 7th-century East Asia). The look is the background art of a hand-painted 2D animated epic crossed with an East Asian woodblock battle scroll. SMOKE AND CLOUD are the big shapes: towering sculpted columns and rolling banks painted as broad soft gouache masses, lit warm orange from the fires underneath and cooling to slate and charcoal at the top; where they curl they break into stylised scroll-cloud spirals outlined in thin ink, like a painted screen. WATER is Hokusai: heavy slate-teal swells with claw-like cream-white foam crests drawn in ink line, spray as stippled dots. FIRE is flat curling ribbons of vermilion and orange with darker red edges licking up hulls, sails and banners — never photographic flame. BANNERS are long silk ribbons whipping in the wind, kingdom colour only, their marks illegible brush strokes. FIGURES are many small drawn silhouettes — soldiers packed in boats, oars, spears, shields — read as massed shapes, the nearest ones dark against the bright smoke; named heroes are drawn larger with clean webtoon faces. DEPTH is layered like stage flats: dark foreground waves, boats and figures; midground ships or ranks in clear silhouette; background smoke, haze and a pale sky that fades like cream paper; a few seabirds or embers. PALETTE is fixed for the whole battle: cream-paper sky, slate blue-grey and teal water, charcoal smoke, vermilion-and-orange fire, ink black, plus each kingdom's banner colour — no purple sunset, no neon, no other hues. Painted texture everywhere (gouache grain, dry-brush, ink line on waves and clouds); not photoreal, not 3D, not a map or satellite view, not a manga speed-line panel. SHIPS are 7th-century only: Tang multi-storey louchuan tower-ships with stacked timber cabins, rows of oars and battened junk sails; Yamato and Baekje open oared war-boats with a single mast — never European hulls, cannon, funnels or square-rigged masts. OVERRIDES of the house rules below for battle frames: massed hosts and fleets are allowed as silhouetted masses; daylight through smoke is allowed (the dark masses are the smoke, the bright break is the pale sky or the fire); still ONE device (a waterline, a smoke column, a ring of hulls, a ford) and big quiet areas of smoke or sky. CANON — ULCHI MUNDUK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_ulchi_munduk.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean, weathered Goguryeo general: narrow watchful eyes, thin moustache and small chin beard, calm unreadable face of a man counting the enemy. Dress: Steel lamellar with a round bronze boss on the chest, a red scarf wound at the throat, red cloth sleeves and skirt; red-winged steel helm with a red plume. Demeanor: The Defender: patient, sly, unhurried — retreats on purpose, writes the enemy a poem, then springs the river. Armor: Goguryeo kit: steel lamellar with red-edged plates and RED WING shoulder-flaps, peaked helm with plume — red cloth, never gold plate. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Fighting: Commands from the saddle with a long spear; a ring sword at the hip, rarely drawn. #e0503f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: Chinese general armor; katana. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Goguryeo banners: red silk with the black three-legged crow inside a studded black sun-ring. Attached flag /flag_goguryeo.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Ulchi Munduk surrenders seven times on the way south. Every time, the river gets closer.
blocks.ko: 을지문덕은 남쪽으로 내려가는 길에 일곱 번 항복한다. 그때마다 강이 가까워진다.

blocks.caption: Nine armies over the Liao, a fleet up the Tedong. The West planned everything except the walk home.
blocks.ko: 요하를 건너는 아홉 군단, 대동강을 오르는 함대. 서국는 돌아가는 길만 빼고 다 계획했다.

blocks.html: Gesomun is seven that summer. The last dynasty’s emperor has sent three hundred thousand men at Pyongyang. Goguryeo sends one man to look at them.
blocks.ko: 그해 여름 개소문은 일곱 살이다. 지난 왕조의 황제가 삼십만 대군을 평양으로 보냈다. 고구려는 그들을 구경하라고 사람 하나를 보낸다.

blocks.html: Ask a Goguryeo grandfather. He will raise a cup first.
blocks.ko: 고구려 할아버지에게 물어보라. 잔부터 들 것이다.

blocks.label: The West Camp
blocks.ko: 서국 진영

blocks.html: Munduk walks into the enemy camp himself first, to look at them. He brings a white flag, a polite face and no guards. He has come, he says, to surrender.
blocks.ko: 을지문덕은 먼저 몸소 적진으로 걸어 들어가 그들을 살핀다. 흰 깃발 하나, 공손한 얼굴 하나, 호위는 없다. 항복하러 왔다고 한다.

blocks.speaker: Western general
en: Goguryeo surrenders? Just like that?

lines: 저희는 작은 나라고, 장군께선 아주 큰 군대시니까요.
…병사들이 제 군량을 지고 다닌 지 얼마나 됐습니까? 다들 지쳐 보이는군요.
en: Just like that, General.
We are a small country. You are a very large army.
…How long have your men carried their own rice? They look tired.

blocks.html: A hundred days of rice each, on their own backs. At night most of them bury half of it under the tent to lighten the load. Munduk notices the fresh dirt.
blocks.ko: 한 사람당 백 일 치 쌀을 제 등에 졌다. 밤이면 대부분 짐을 덜려고 막사 밑에 절반을 묻는다. 을지문덕은 갓 뒤집힌 흙을 본다.

blocks.speaker: Western general
lines: 황상의 명은, 네가 오면 붙잡으라는 것이다.
en: The emperor’s orders are to seize you if you come.

blocks.speaker: The Western officer
lines: 장군— 항복하러 온 사신을 잡으면 앞으로 아무도 우리한테 항복하지 않을 겁니다.
en: General— if we seize an envoy who came to surrender, nobody will ever surrender to us again.

blocks.html: So they let him walk out. He has seen everything he came for. By evening the general regrets it and sends a rider after him: come back, there is more to discuss.
blocks.ko: 그래서 그들은 그를 걸어 나가게 둔다. 그는 보러 온 것을 다 보았다. 저녁이 되자 장군은 후회하고 기병 하나를 뒤쫓아 보낸다. 돌아오라, 더 의논할 것이 있다.

en: Tell the general I’m flattered.
Tell him we can discuss it further south.

blocks.label: Seven
blocks.ko: 일곱 번

blocks.html: He surrenders seven times on the way south and runs seven times. Each time the West win a small fight, plant a flag and feel wonderful. Each running pulls them further from their buried rice and closer to Pyongyang.
blocks.ko: 그는 남쪽으로 가는 길에 일곱 번 항복하고 일곱 번 달아난다. 그때마다 서국는 작은 싸움에서 이기고, 깃발을 꽂고, 기분이 아주 좋다. 달아날 때마다 그들은 묻어 둔 쌀에서 멀어지고 평양에 가까워진다.

blocks.speaker: Western general
lines: 하루에 일곱 번 이겼다! 받아 적어라.
en: Seven victories in a day! Write that down.

blocks.speaker: The Western officer
lines: 장군… 일곱 번 이겼는데 얻은 게 없습니다. 곳간 하나도요.
en: General… we have won seven times and taken nothing. Not one granary.

blocks.title: The walk home
blocks.caption: They marched to within thirty li of Pyongyang. Munduk had been counting on exactly that.
blocks.ko: 평양 삼십 리 앞까지 왔다. 을지문덕이 바란 게 바로 그거였다.

blocks.html: The Colossal River is low that summer. They wade it without losing a man and nobody thinks about it twice. Thirty li from Pyongyang, the army stops and looks at the walls. The walls look back.
blocks.ko: 그해 여름 살수는 얕다. 그들은 한 명도 잃지 않고 걸어서 건넌다. 아무도 그걸 두 번 생각하지 않는다. 평양 삼십 리 앞에서 군대는 멈춰 성벽을 바라본다. 성벽도 마주 본다.

blocks.speaker: The Western officer
en: General, we have no ladders up here, and no rice to wait with.
lines: 장군, 여기엔 사다리도 없고, 버틸 쌀도 없습니다.

blocks.html: Then a letter arrives from Munduk. It is a poem.
blocks.ko: 그때 을지문덕의 편지가 온다. 시다.

blocks.title: Poem sent to the Western general
blocks.hanja:
神策究天文
妙算窮地理
戰勝功旣高
知足願云止
blocks.html:
Your godlike strategy has searched out the patterns of heaven;
your wondrous reckoning has mastered the lie of the land.
Your victories have already won you high merit —
know it is enough, and I pray you stop.
blocks.ko:
그대의 귀신 같은 계책은 하늘의 이치를 다 헤아렸고
신묘한 계산은 땅의 이치를 통달했다
전쟁에 이겨 쌓은 공이 이미 높으니
만족함을 알고 그치기를 바라노라
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 44, Biographies — Eulji Mundeok

blocks.speaker: Western general
en: Is he… praising me?

blocks.speaker: The Western officer
en: He’s telling you to go home, General.

blocks.html: A second note follows, plainer. If the West turn around, the king of Goguryeo will come and bow to their emperor in person. It is the eighth surrender. The general takes it, because it is the only one he can carry home.
blocks.ko: 두 번째 편지가 뒤따른다. 이번엔 쉬운 말이다. 서국가 군을 돌리면 고구려 왕이 몸소 황제께 나아가 절하겠다. 여덟 번째 항복이다. 장군은 받아들인다. 집에 들고 갈 수 있는 건 그것뿐이니까.

blocks.label: The River
blocks.ko: 살수

blocks.html: They turn for home starving, in squares, with Goguryeo riders on every side. At the Colossal River the water is still low and wide, and the army starts back across.
blocks.ko: 그들은 굶주린 채 방진을 짜고 돌아선다. 사방에 고구려 기병이 붙는다. 살수의 물은 여전히 얕고 넓다. 군대가 다시 건너기 시작한다.

en: Wait.
…Wait.
Now. While their feet are wet.

blocks.html: When the army is halfway over, Goguryeo comes down on the rearguard. Men on the far bank can’t come back. Men on the near bank can’t get over. The ones in the middle find out how deep a shallow river is.
blocks.ko: 군대가 절반쯤 건넜을 때 고구려가 후군을 덮친다. 건너편에 닿은 자들은 돌아올 수 없다. 이쪽에 남은 자들은 건너갈 수 없다. 한가운데 있던 자들은 얕은 강이 얼마나 깊은지 알게 된다.

blocks.speaker: A Western soldier
en: It was knee-deep! It was knee-deep on the way down—

blocks.html: When the nine armies crossed the Liao there were three hundred and five thousand of them. When they got back to the Liaodong fortress there were two thousand seven hundred. Stores and weapons by the tens of thousands were lost, every one.
blocks.ko: 처음 아홉 군대가 요수를 건넌 것이 모두 30만 5천이었는데, 요동성으로 돌아온 것은 겨우 2천 7백 명이었다. 수만을 헤아리던 군량과 기계도 모두 잃어버렸다.
blocks.hanja: 初，九軍渡遼，凡三十萬五千，及還至遼東城，唯二千七百人，資儲器械巨萬計，失亡蕩盡。
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 181, Sui Daye 8 (612), 7th month

blocks.html: Munduk is honored with the title “The Defender” after the battle.
blocks.ko: 문덕은 전투 후 «수호신»이라는 칭호를 받는다.

blocks.html: Gesomun’s father rides home through the Pyongyang gate with the Western banner rolled under his arm like a bolt of cloth. The boy at the gate decides, then and there, what emperors are for.
blocks.ko: 개소문의 아버지는 서국 깃발을 비단 필처럼 옆구리에 말아 끼고 평양 성문으로 돌아온다. 성문에 선 아이는 그 자리에서 정한다. 황제란 무엇에 쓰는 것인지.

blocks.speaker: The boy
en: Is that the emperor’s?

blocks.speaker: His father
lines: 도망칠 때 흘리고 가거든. 자. 비단 말고 장대를 잡으라우.
en: Aye, one of them. Emperors have plenty.
They drop them when they run. Here. Hold it by the pole, not the silk.

blocks.html: Yodong fell. The forts fell. One wall is left, held by a madman whose name nobody wrote down…!
blocks.ko: 요동이 무너졌다. 성들이 무너졌다. 남은 성벽은 하나. 그 성을 지키는 미치광이의 이름은 아무도 적어 두지 않았다…!

logline.en: Ansi dances all night, follows a man with a lazy eye, and answers to no one. Now the emperor is at the gate.
logline.ko: 안시는 밤새 춤추고, 짝눈이 사내를 따르고, 누구의 명도 받지 않는다. 이제 황제가 성문 앞에 있다.
