LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Every town has one man it would follow off a wall. Ansi’s can’t look at you straight.
blocks.ko: 어느 고을에나 성벽 아래로라도 따라 뛰어내릴 사내가 하나쯤 있다. 안시의 그 사내는 사람을 똑바로 못 본다.

blocks.label: The Town
blocks.ko: 고을

blocks.label: Ansi · autumn 642
blocks.ko: 안시 · 642년 가을

blocks.html: One small fortress, and one stubborn man on top of it.
blocks.ko: 작은 성 하나, 그 위에 고집 센 사내 하나.

blocks.html: Ansi is a hill town inside a ring of stone, a day’s ride from the Liao. It grows millet, breeds horses, and goes to bed far too late.
blocks.ko: 안시는 돌 성벽 안에 들어앉은 산 고을이다. 요하에서 말 타고 하루 거리. 조를 기르고, 말을 치고, 밤에는 너무 늦게 잔다.

blocks.html: Travellers from the West noticed this a long time ago. They wrote it down, a little scandalised.
blocks.ko: 서쪽에서 온 길손들은 오래전에 이걸 보았다. 그리고 얼굴을 조금 붉히며 적어 두었다.

blocks.hanja: 其民喜歌舞，國中邑落，暮夜男女群聚，相就歌戲。
blocks.html: Its people love to sing and dance. In the towns and villages all over the country, when night falls, men and women gather in crowds and pair off to sing and play.
blocks.ko: 그 백성은 노래와 춤을 즐긴다. 나라 안 고을과 마을마다 밤이 되면 남녀가 무리 지어 모여 서로 짝을 지어 노래하며 논다.
blocks.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms (三國志), Wei 30, Eastern Barbarians: Goguryeo

blocks.html: Tonight the fire is in the yard under the east gate. Somebody has brought out a drum. The chief is dancing, which is the worst thing that happens to that drum all year.
blocks.ko: 오늘 밤 불은 동문 아래 마당에 피었다. 누가 북을 들고 나왔다. 성주가 춤을 추고 있다. 그 북한테는 일 년 중 제일 험한 밤이다.

blocks.html: He is thirty-two. One of his eyes looks where he looks. The other wanders off on business of its own, and the town has never once let him forget it.
blocks.ko: 그는 서른둘이다. 한쪽 눈은 그가 보는 데를 본다. 다른 쪽 눈은 제 볼일을 보러 딴 데로 간다. 고을 사람들은 그걸 한 번도 잊게 놔둔 적이 없다.

blocks.caption: His town calls him Lazy-eye, and he answers to it. The rest of the world never gets his name.
blocks.ko: 제 고을에선 짝눈이라 불리고, 그렇게 불러도 대답한다. 바깥세상은 끝내 그의 이름을 얻지 못한다.

blocks.speaker: Kkachi
lines: 짝눈이 아저씨! 지금 우리 중에 누구 보네?
en: Lazy-eye! Which one of us are you looking at?
Both. Aye, always both.

blocks.speaker: Granny
lines: 내 발을 세 번이나 밟았다, 너.
en: That’s three times you’ve stepped on my foot.
Your foot keeps getting in the way, Granny.

blocks.speaker: Granny
lines: 네 앞엔 머이든 길을 막디. 문짝 지고 가는 놈처럼 추는구나.
en: Everything gets in your way. You dance like a man carrying a door.

blocks.html: In Ansi the girls do the asking. A weaver crosses the circle and takes a young archer by the sleeve. He goes the colour of the fire, and goes.
blocks.ko: 안시에서는 처녀가 먼저 청한다. 베 짜는 처녀 하나가 춤판을 가로질러 젊은 궁수의 소매를 잡는다. 궁수는 불빛처럼 빨개져서, 따라간다.

blocks.html: At the edge of the light the mason sits on a block with a cup, squinting at the chief’s face like it owes him money.
blocks.ko: 불빛 가장자리에 석수가 돌덩이에 걸터앉아 잔을 들고, 빚쟁이 보듯 성주의 얼굴을 노려본다.

blocks.speaker: The mason
en: Hold still a wee minute.
I’m dancing.

blocks.speaker: The mason
lines: 그럼 천천히 춰. 얼굴 익히는 중이야. 언젠가 이 고을이 그 얼굴을 돌에 새기자고 하갓디.
en: Then dance slower. I’m learning your face. One day this town’ll want it in stone.
Stone’s for kings and dead men.

blocks.speaker: The mason
lines: 그럼 둘 중 하나라도 날래 돼 보라우.
en: Then hurry up and be one or the other.

blocks.html: The drum stops before the rider is through the gate. He has come from Pyongyang without changing horses, and it shows on both of them.
blocks.ko: 기수가 성문을 다 지나기도 전에 북이 멎는다. 평양에서 말을 갈아타지도 않고 달려왔다. 사람도 말도 그 꼴이다.

blocks.speaker: Rider from Pyongyang
lines: 성주님— 연회가요. 평양에서. 연이 문을 닫았답니다.
en: Chief— the banquet. In Pyongyang. Yeon shut the doors.
The king. The commanders. Every one.
…The West too?

blocks.speaker: Rider from Pyongyang
lines: 칼을 거둬 갔답니다. 이제 그걸 등에 메고 다닌대요.
en: He took their swords. He wears them on his back now.

blocks.html: Nobody picks the drum back up. The chief turns his back to the fire so the town can’t see his face. It doesn’t help. They can see his shoulders.
blocks.ko: 아무도 북을 다시 들지 않는다. 성주는 고을 사람들이 얼굴을 못 보게 불을 등지고 선다. 소용없다. 어깨가 다 보인다.

blocks.html: Eight years ago, outside the Summit in Pyongyang, he held the horses and watched a young man from the East walk out early and look at nobody.
blocks.ko: 여덟 해 전, 평양 제가회의 바깥에서 그는 말고삐를 잡고 있었다. 동쪽에서 온 젊은 사내 하나가 일찍 나와, 아무도 보지 않고 지나가는 것을 보았다.

en: Depends on the age he’s born into.
…Aye.
Now we ken what age it is.

blocks.speaker: Kkachi
en: Lazy-eye? Is there going to be a war?

blocks.speaker: Granny
lines: 누가 북 좀 들라우. 세상이 망해도 장단은 맞춰서 망해야디.
en: Somebody pick up the drum. If the world’s ending, it can end on the beat.

blocks.label: The Red Seal
blocks.ko: 붉은 인장

blocks.label: Ansi · that winter
blocks.ko: 안시 · 그해 겨울

blocks.html: A few months later, Yeon’s messenger rides the line of the western forts with a red seal and the same short speech for each. Every gate opens. Every lord kneels to the seal.
blocks.ko: 몇 달 뒤, 연의 사자가 붉은 인장을 들고 서쪽 성들을 차례로 돈다. 성마다 같은 짧은 말을 한다. 성문마다 열린다. 성주마다 인장에 무릎을 꿇는다.

blocks.html: Then Ansi. The messenger is young, and he has had a very good month.
blocks.ko: 그리고 안시. 사자는 젊고, 이번 달 내내 일이 아주 잘 풀렸다.

blocks.speaker: Yeon’s messenger
lines: 대막리지께서 안시의 맹세를 받아 오라 하셨소. 요하의 성이란 성은 다 바쳤소. 하나도 빠짐없이.
인장에 무릎 꿇으시오, 성주. 그럼 다들 집에 갈 수 있소.
en: The Supreme Commander requires the oath of Ansi. Every fortress on the Liao has given it. Every one.
Kneel to the seal, Chief, and we can all go home.
I have heard that a true man needs only
one person to cherish,
and one person to serve,
and that is enough.

blocks.speaker: Yeon’s messenger
en: …And whom do you serve?

lines: 네 주인한테 물어보라우. 그 잔치에 같이 있었으니끼니.
en: Ask your master. He was at the same dinner.
Do you know what happens to traitors, young man...?

blocks.speaker: Yeon’s messenger
en: I carry the Supreme Commander’s seal—

lines: 그럼 돌려받고 싶갓디. 머리랑 같이 보내.
en: Then he’ll want it back. Send it with the head.

blocks.html: It is done in the yard, quickly, the way a certain young commander once did it in the snow. Nobody looks away. In Ansi that isn’t fear. They want to see if he flinches. He doesn’t, until he is alone on the wall.
blocks.ko: 마당에서, 빨리 끝난다. 어느 젊은 장군이 예전에 눈밭에서 하던 식으로. 아무도 눈을 돌리지 않는다. 안시에서 그건 두려움이 아니다. 성주가 움찔하는지 보고 싶은 거다. 그는 움찔하지 않는다. 성벽 위에 혼자 남을 때까지는.

blocks.label: Ansi · the thaw
blocks.ko: 안시 · 얼음 풀릴 무렵

blocks.html: Yeon does not come himself. He sends three thousand men. That is an army for a town, not a wall. They come up the valley in the thaw, under red banners. The wall flies the same red.
blocks.ko: 연은 직접 오지 않는다. 삼천을 보낸다. 고을 하나 치는 군대지, 성벽 치는 군대가 아니다. 그들은 얼음 풀린 골짜기를 붉은 깃발 아래 올라온다. 성벽에도 같은 붉은 깃발이 걸려 있다.

blocks.speaker: Young archer
lines: 성주님, 데거 우리 깃발인데요. 누굴 쏴요?
en: Chief, those are our colours. Who do I shoot?
The ones walking uphill.

blocks.html: The whole town is on the wall. The weaver hauls stone. Kkachi runs arrows along the parapet in a basket bigger than she is. The mason heaves over a millstone he spent a year cutting, and watches it go with real grief.
blocks.ko: 온 고을이 성벽 위에 있다. 베 짜는 처녀는 돌을 나른다. 까치는 제 몸보다 큰 바구니에 화살을 담아 성가퀴를 따라 뛴다. 석수는 일 년 걸려 깎은 맷돌을 밀어 떨어뜨리고, 진심으로 서운한 얼굴로 그게 굴러가는 걸 본다.

blocks.speaker: Granny
en: Who’s paying for that millstone?

blocks.speaker: The mason
lines: 평양이 내야디. 값 받으러 사람 보내갓다.
en: Pyongyang. I’ll send somebody to collect.

blocks.html: At dusk the chief opens the gate, which nobody expects, least of all the men outside it. Half the garrison comes out behind him, and most of the town’s butchers. By dark the valley is quiet. The red banners lie in the mud with their poles snapped.
blocks.ko: 해 질 녘, 성주가 성문을 연다. 아무도 예상 못 한 일이다. 성 밖의 사내들은 더더욱. 수비병 절반이 그 뒤를 따라 나가고, 고을 백정들도 거의 다 따라 나간다. 어두워질 무렵 골짜기는 조용하다. 붉은 깃발들이 깃대가 부러진 채 진흙에 누워 있다.

blocks.speaker: Kkachi
lines: 짝눈이 아저씨! 눈이 내내 딴 데 보고 있었잖아!
en: Lazy-eye! Your eye was looking the wrong way the whole time!
That’s how I saw them coming.

blocks.label: Pyongyang
blocks.ko: 평양

blocks.html: The news reaches Pyongyang with the survivors, who are fewer than the men who left, and much quieter.
blocks.ko: 소식은 살아 돌아온 자들과 함께 평양에 닿는다. 떠난 자들보다 수가 적고, 훨씬 조용하다.

en: Ansi… so that man is still alive.
He dares refuse the Supreme Commander’s order?
You know him?
Never got his name.
Want me to send ten thousand this time?

blocks.html: Yeon laughs, once, like a slap.
blocks.ko: 연이 한 번, 따귀 같은 웃음을 터뜨린다.

lines: 농사꾼들 데리고. 농사꾼이랑 북 하나로 내 군사를 깼다고.
…일없어. 당이 요하에서 말을 세고 있어. 창이란 창은 전부 서쪽을 봐야디, 산꼭대기 볼 때가 아니야.
성 하나다. 가지라고 해. 기렇게 잘 지키면, 황데한테서도 지켜 보라디.
en: With farmers. He beat my men with farmers and a drum.
…Naw. The West is counting horses at the Liao. I need every spear facing west, not up some hill.
One wall. Let him keep it. If he’s that good at keeping it, he can keep it from the emperor.

blocks.html: So Ansi answers to no one. It keeps the old king’s colours on the wall, and nobody in Pyongyang mentions it at dinner.
blocks.ko: 그렇게 안시는 누구의 명도 받지 않는다. 성벽에는 옛 왕의 깃발을 그대로 걸어 두고, 평양에서는 아무도 밥상머리에서 그 얘기를 꺼내지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Emperor
blocks.ko: 황제

blocks.label: Ansi · summer 645
blocks.ko: 안시 · 645년 여름

blocks.caption: The emperor wants Pyongyang. One small fortress is in the way.
blocks.ko: 황제는 평양을 원한다. 작은 성 하나가 길을 막고 있다.

blocks.html: Two summers later the emperor comes. Yodong burns. The forts that knelt to Yeon’s seal fall one after another, and the road to Pyongyang runs right under Ansi’s wall.
blocks.ko: 두 해 여름이 지나 황제가 온다. 요동이 불탄다. 연의 인장에 무릎 꿇었던 성들이 하나씩 떨어지고, 평양 가는 길은 안시 성벽 바로 아래로 지나간다.

blocks.html: Nobody writes his name down. To the people inside the walls he is just Lazy-eye, and that turns out to be enough.
blocks.ko: 누구도 그의 이름을 적어 두지 않았다. 성 안 사람들에게 그는 그저 짝눈이였고, 결국 그것으로 충분했다.

blocks.label: The Earthen Mountain
blocks.ko: 토산

blocks.html: The Second Emperor tries the wall first. The Blue Dragon’s rams go at the Western wall six or seven times a day. Every tower they knock down is a timber fence by dark.
blocks.ko: 황제는 먼저 성벽을 쳐 본다. 청룡의 충차가 하루 예닐곱 번 서쪽 성벽에 붙는다. 무너진 망루는 해 질 녘이면 나무 울타리가 되어 있다.

blocks.speaker: Ansi soldier
lines: 누런 깃발이다! 데놈이다— 북 쳐, 북!
어이, 천자 양반! 우리 울타리레 너네 망루보다 높다!
en: Yellow banners! That’s him— drums, drums!
Oi, Son of Heaven! Our fence is taller than your wee tower!

blocks.html: When the wall does not work he tries the ground, which is the sort of thing only an empire can afford to try. His cousin starts piling earth against the south-east corner, and the emperor moves his camp south to watch it grow. The archers on the parapet watch every basket.
blocks.ko: 성벽이 안 되자 그는 땅을 쳐 본다. 제국이나 되어야 해 볼 수 있는 짓이다. 사촌이 동남쪽 모서리에 흙을 쌓기 시작하고, 황제는 그게 자라는 걸 보려고 진영을 남쪽으로 옮긴다. 성가퀴의 궁수들은 흙짐 하나하나를 지켜본다.

en: How many baskets is that now?
blocks.speaker: The West hauler
blocks.art: The West haulers on the mound’s slope at dusk, baskets of earth on their backs.

en: Don’t count. It gets heavier when you count.
blocks.speaker: Another hauler

lines: 성주님, 데놈들 벌써 예순 날째 저럽니다.
en: Chief, that’s sixty days they’ve been at it.
blocks.speaker: Ansi soldier
blocks.art: Night. Torches on the inner wall; the garrison passing stones hand to hand, raising the wall course by course while the mound’s black shoulder looms outside.

lines: 그럼 우리는 예순 밤째다. 돌 넘기라우.
en: Then it’s sixty nights for us. Pass the stone.

blocks.html: Somebody passes it. He sets it himself, on the inside face, with a tilt you could see from the emperor’s tent.
blocks.ko: 누군가 건넨다. 그는 안쪽 면에 손수 그 돌을 앉힌다. 황제 천막에서도 보일 만큼 비스듬하게.

blocks.speaker: Young archer
en: Chief. That one’s crooked.

lines: 돌은 눕고 싶어 해. 눕고 싶은 쪽으로 기대 놓으면 버틴다.
en: It’s leaning. Into the hill.
A stone wants to lie down. Let it lean where it wants and it holds.

blocks.speaker: Young archer
en: Says who?

lines: 우리 아바지가. 너만 할 때 평양 말 매는 담에서 어느 장군한테 그 말을 했디.
걷어차더라. 꿈쩍도 안 했어. 내 이름 듣기도 전에 절룩거리며 가 버렸디.
en: My da. I told a commander that once, at a horse wall in Pyongyang, the year I was your age.
He kicked it. It didnae move. He limped off before he ever got my name.

blocks.speaker: Young archer
en: Which commander?

blocks.html: The chief doesn’t answer. He looks south-east, toward Pyongyang, with the eye that can be bothered. Then he holds out his hand for the next stone.
blocks.ko: 성주는 대답하지 않는다. 남동쪽, 평양 쪽을 본다. 그럴 마음이 있는 쪽 눈으로. 그러고는 다음 돌을 달라고 손을 내민다.

blocks.html: Inside the walls the stone runs out first. Then the doors. Then the roof beams of the houses nearest that corner. Families sleep in the open and pass their own lintels up the ladder.
blocks.ko: 성안에서는 돌이 먼저 떨어진다. 다음은 문짝이다. 그다음은 그 모서리 가까운 집들의 서까래다. 사람들은 한데서 자고, 제 집 문지방을 사다리 위로 올려 보낸다.

blocks.speaker: Granny
lines: 보라우. 문짝을 지워 놓으니끼니 춤이 되네.
en: See? Give him a door to carry and he dances fine.

blocks.speaker: Weaver
lines: 그거 내 베틀 들보야. 쓸모 있는 데 박으라우.
en: That’s my loom beam. Put it somewhere it’ll do some good.

lines: 맨 윗단에. 성벽에서 제일 좋은 자리다.
en: Top course. Best seat on the wall.

blocks.html: Five hundred thousand man-days, sixty days of hauling, and the mountain’s crown stands higher than the wall. From up there you can count the cook fires.
blocks.ko: 연인원 오십만, 예순 날의 흙짐. 마침내 흙산 꼭대기가 성벽보다 높아진다. 거기 서면 성안의 밥 짓는 불까지 셀 수 있다.

blocks.speaker: Ansi soldier
lines: 성주님. 데 우에서 우리 밥솥꺼정 보이갓시요.
en: Chief. They can see our rice pots from up there.

lines: 그럼 냄새 좋은 거 해. 데놈들도 한번 배고파 보라디.
en: Then cook something that smells good. Let them be hungry for a change.

blocks.title: Ansi Fortress, sixth to ninth month, 645
blocks.note: Every night the defenders built their wall higher than the mound had grown that day. The siege became a race between shovels.

blocks.html: Then it rains, and the mountain slumps — sideways, into the wall it was built to overlook, taking a stretch of Ansi down with it. Both sides stare at the gap.
blocks.ko: 그러다 비가 온다. 산이 무너진다. 내려다보려 쌓은 그 성벽 쪽으로 옆으로 무너지며, 안시성 한 자락을 함께 무너뜨린다. 양쪽 모두 그 틈을 바라본다.

en: Chief, the wall—
blocks.speaker: Ansi soldier

lines: 벽은 일없고. 데 우에 지금 누가 있네?
en: Never mind the wall. Who’s up on yon thing right now?

blocks.html: The officer who was supposed to be holding the mound has stepped away.
blocks.ko: 흙산을 지켜야 할 장수는 자리를 비운 참이었다.
blocks.art: Cut to the mound’s crown: an empty command stool in the rain.

en: …There’s nobody up there.
blocks.speaker: Ansi soldier

en: Then it’s ours.

blocks.html: A few hundred men are standing on sixty days of the Western work. They pile timber on its slopes and set it alight. By noon there is a Goguryeo banner on top.
blocks.ko: 수백 명이 서군의 예순 날 위에 서 있다. 그들은 비탈에 나무를 쌓아 불을 지른다. 한낮이 되자 꼭대기에 고구려 깃발이 선다.

lines: …짐의 산 위에 걸린 저 깃발은 누구의 것이냐?
en: Sixty days.
…Whose banner is that, on Our mountain?

blocks.speaker: Western officer
lines: 저들 것이옵니다, 폐하. 부복애가… 잠시 자리를 비웠다 하옵니다.
en: Theirs, Majesty. Fu Fuai had… stepped down from it.

blocks.html: The emperor has Fu Fuai beheaded, very courteously, and orders three days of assault on the mound.
blocks.ko: 황제는 아주 정중하게 부복애의 목을 베고, 흙산에 사흘간의 총공격을 명한다.

blocks.html: The emperor rides up to watch. Too close.
blocks.ko: 황제가 지켜보러 다가온다. 너무 가까이.

blocks.html: On the second day the Guardian sees him: a yellow parasol on the near slope, closer than any emperor should be. He takes the bow out of the young archer’s hands.
blocks.ko: 이틀째, 성주의 눈에 그가 들어온다. 가까운 비탈 위의 누런 일산. 어느 황제도 그렇게 가까이 와선 안 된다. 성주는 옆에 선 젊은 궁수의 손에서 활을 빼앗아 든다.

en: Hold still, you.

blocks.html: The arrow takes the helmet clean off. The lacquered bowl leaves his head and rings once on packed earth, then keeps rolling. For the first time in the siege, the two men look straight at each other.
blocks.ko: 화살이 투구를 깨끗이 벗겨 낸다. 옻칠한 투구가 머리를 떠나 다진 흙 위에서 한 번 울리고는 계속 굴러간다. 포위가 시작된 뒤 처음으로, 두 사내가 서로를 똑바로 바라본다.

en: …That man.
Find out his name.

blocks.html: Nobody can. A cut over the emperor’s eye bleeds into his beard. The surgeons say it is nothing, and he lets them.
blocks.ko: 아무도 알아 오지 못한다. 황제의 눈썹 위 상처에서 피가 수염으로 흘러든다. 의원들은 별것 아니라 하고, 그는 그렇게 믿어 준다.

blocks.speaker: Young archer
en: You were aiming for his head.

lines: 일산 노렸어. 나머진 눈이 알아서 했디.
en: I was aiming for the parasol. The eye did the rest.

blocks.label: The Retreat
blocks.ko: 회군

blocks.html: Then the cold comes early. Sixty days of hauling earth were sixty days of horses eating the plain, and the plain is bare. There is nothing left to feed them.
blocks.ko: 그러다 추위가 일찍 온다. 흙을 나른 예순 날은 말들이 들판을 뜯어 먹은 예순 날이기도 했다. 들판은 맨땅이다. 말을 먹일 것이 남지 않았다.

blocks.html: On the morning he turns for home, the emperor parades his army under the wall one last time, so the wall can see what it beat. Inside, nobody shows a face. Then one man climbs the parapet and bows.
blocks.ko: 회군하는 날 아침, 황제는 마지막으로 성 아래에서 군을 사열한다. 성이 무엇을 이겼는지 보라는 듯이. 성안에서는 아무도 얼굴을 내밀지 않는다. 그러다 한 사내가 성가퀴에 올라 절을 한다.

blocks.html: A proper bow, from the waist. The kind you give a guest who stayed too long.
blocks.ko: 허리를 굽힌 제대로 된 절이다. 너무 오래 머문 손님에게 하는 그런 절.

lines: 제 주군을 잘 섬긴 자에게 주는 것이다. 짐의 천하 모든 성이 듣게 하라.
그리고 이름을 물어라. 한 번 더.
en: Bring up the silk. A hundred bolts.
For a man who serves his lord well. Let every wall in Our empire hear of it.
And ask him his name. Once more.

lines: 그리고 이것도. 수가 많은 것도 알고, 머리가 좋은 것도 알겠소.
그런데 당신들은 절대로 우리보다 미치지는 못할 거요…!
en: Tell him thanks for the silk.
And tell him this. You may outnumber us. You may outthink us.
But you will never be crazier than we are…!
blocks.art: On the wall the day the West turn for home, the bolts of silk at his feet.

blocks.html: The silk goes up the wall on a rope. The name does not come down.
blocks.ko: 비단은 밧줄에 매달려 성벽을 올라간다. 이름은 내려오지 않는다.

blocks.html: Then the marsh. Two hundred li of mud, and the road across it is the road he tore up himself. Nobody goes home the way they came. He said that.
blocks.ko: 그리고 늪이다. 이백 리 진흙. 그 위를 건너던 길은 그가 손수 걷어 낸 길이다. 왔던 길로 돌아가는 자는 없다. 그가 한 말이다.

blocks.html: Snow comes down on the column in the mud. The emperor gets off his horse and cuts brush with his own hands to fill the ruts. His officers can’t be seen carrying less.
blocks.ko: 진흙 속 행렬 위로 눈이 내린다. 황제는 말에서 내려 손수 덤불을 베어 바퀴 자국을 메운다. 장수들은 황제보다 적게 나르는 모습을 보일 수 없다.

lines: 내가 천하의 군사를 가지고도 작은 오랑캐에게 곤욕을 당한 것은 무엇 때문인가?
…그 노신이 살아 있었다면, 짐을 결코 오게 두지 않았을 것을.
en: With all the armies under heaven, how was I humiliated by so small a barbarian land?
…If the old minister were alive, he would never have let me come.
Somebody tell me no. Anybody.

blocks.html: Nobody does. That was the whole trouble.
blocks.ko: 아무도 말하지 않는다. 처음부터 그게 문제였다.

blocks.title: The Seventh Invasion, start to finish
blocks.caption: All those arrows in, and two dotted lines out. One small wall did that.
blocks.ko: 들어간 화살은 저렇게 많은데, 나온 건 점선 두 줄. 작은 성벽 하나가 한 일이다.

blocks.label: Ansi · that winter
blocks.ko: 안시 · 그해 겨울

blocks.html: That winter the mason gets his way. The chief sits for his statue on an upturned basket in the yard, under protest, and the whole town comes to supervise.
blocks.ko: 그해 겨울, 석수는 결국 뜻을 이룬다. 성주는 마당에 엎어 놓은 광주리에 앉아, 투덜대며, 석상의 본이 된다. 온 고을이 감독하러 나온다.

blocks.speaker: The mason
en: Hold still.
I am holding still.

blocks.speaker: The mason
en: Your eye isn’t.

blocks.speaker: Kkachi
en: Do the eye! Carve the lazy eye!
Don’t you dare do the eye.

blocks.speaker: The mason
en: I’m doing the eye.

blocks.speaker: Kkachi
lines: 맨 처음 석상은 누구 거였어? 제일 처음.
en: Who got the very first statue? Ever?

blocks.speaker: The mason
lines: 성왕님. 요동 사당에 있디. 이 성벽보다 오래됐어.
en: The Holy King. In the shrine at Yodong. Older than this wall.

blocks.speaker: Kkachi
en: Who was he?

blocks.speaker: The mason
en: Everybody knows who he was.

blocks.speaker: Kkachi
en: So who?

blocks.html: The chisel stops. The mason looks at Granny. Granny looks at the fire. It turns out everybody knows, and nobody can tell it.
blocks.ko: 끌이 멈춘다. 석수가 할매를 본다. 할매는 불을 본다. 알고 보니 다들 알고는 있는데, 아무도 얘기할 줄은 모른다.

lines: 나 보디 마. 난 활 나오는 대목밖에 몰라.
en: Don’t look at me. I only ken the part with the bow.

blocks.html: Nobody writes down what became of him after that winter. The statue kept the eye.
blocks.ko: 그 겨울 뒤로 그가 어떻게 되었는지는 아무도 적어 두지 않았다. 석상은 그 눈을 간직했다.

blocks.label: Yodong
blocks.ko: 요동

blocks.html: A day’s ride from Ansi, a rider in red comes up the empty road from Pyongyang, alone, and stops at Yodong. He goes no farther. Nobody on that wall has asked him to.
blocks.ko: 안시에서 말로 하루 거리. 붉은 옷의 기수 하나가 평양에서 텅 빈 길을 홀로 올라와 요동에서 멈춘다. 더는 가지 않는다. 그 성벽 위의 누구도 오라고 한 적이 없다.

en: Madman…
Still — you did what had to be done.

blocks.html: The West marched Yodong’s people west when they left, seventy thousand of them, roped in lines. What is left is ash, and a stone shrine on the hill with its door open. Inside stands the oldest statue in Goguryeo, black with smoke.
blocks.ko: 서군은 물러가며 요동 사람들을 서쪽으로 끌고 갔다. 칠만 명을 줄줄이 엮어서. 남은 건 재와, 언덕 위 문 열린 돌 사당 하나다. 그 안에 고구려에서 제일 오래된 석상이 그을린 채 서 있다.

blocks.html: Under the chain mail sits a girl in red silk gone the colour of rust. A lamp beside her. She has kept it lit for three months on what the soldiers left behind.
blocks.ko: 쇠사슬 갑옷 아래, 녹슨 빛이 된 붉은 비단의 처녀 하나가 앉아 있다. 곁에 등잔이 있다. 병사들이 버리고 간 것으로 석 달째 불을 지켜 왔다.

en: You’re not him either.
Who?

lines: 내 신랑이요. 다른 사람들은 다 서쪽으로 갔어요. 황제가 나는 그분 거라고 해서 나만 두고 갔어요.
…그분이 누군지 아무도 안 알려 줬어요. 그냥 나를 줬어요.
en: My husband. Everybody else went west. The emperor said I belonged to him, so they left me here.
…Nobody ever told me who he is. They just gave me to him.

lines: …하. 좀 비켜 앉아. 얘기가 길어. 신 하나가 강물 속 에미나이를 내려다본 데서 시작하디.
en: Nobody told you.
…Ha. Move over. It’s a long one. It starts with a god looking down at a girl in a river.

blocks.html: Who was the Holy King, and why does Goguryeo give him brides? Seven hundred years back, the sun looked down…!
blocks.ko: 성왕은 누구였고, 고구려는 왜 그에게 신부를 바치는가? 칠백 년 전, 해가 내려다보았다…!

logline.en: Every day the sun crosses the sky on the same road. Today he looks down.
logline.ko: 해는 날마다 같은 길로 하늘을 건넌다. 오늘, 그가 내려다본다.

images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; no title, no lettering. Dusk at the reed-ringed pond of Gonyeon on the Buyeo plain: still black water, mist, one great grey boulder at the water's edge. Poster composition: the king and the horse fill the frame together as one bold silhouette on the right two-thirds, seen from a low angle at the water line. INTERACTION: King Geumwa, gold crown and red-burgundy court robe, stands pressed against the old chocolate-brown steppe horse Gonyeon, his forehead resting on the horse's broad forehead, eyes closed, one ringed hand cupping its cheek under the shaggy forelock; the horse leans into him with its eyes half shut, breath steaming between them — an old man and the animal that found him under a stone. The boulder looms behind them on the left, reflected in the pond. Above, half the frame is a splashed-ink storm sky with one break of low gold sunset; that gold light (#a89a72) rakes in from the left and catches the crown, the king's cheek, the horse's mane and the gold frog charm on its halter; the rest falls into ink-black and indigo. Reeds as dark dry-brush strokes in the near foreground. Tiny far off, the timber palisade of Buyeo dissolving in mist. CANON — KING GEUMWA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_geumwa.png (face only; invent a new pose). #a89a72 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | GONYEON (곤연, geumwa's brown horse, guardian of Buyeo) — attached board /obj_gonyeon.png: Stocky, powerful northern steppe horse — deep-bodied and shorter-legged than a war horse, thick crested neck, round barrel, heavy quarters, broad forehead, large kind dark eyes; coat an even deep CHOCOLATE BROWN (not red bay, not black) with a lighter mealy tan muzzle; THICK SHAGGY dark-brown mane falling both sides, long full tail nearly to the ground; plain old leather halter with one small gold frog charm at the brow band — match the board. Old, patient and wise. Stopped at the pond of Gonyeon and wept at a boulder until King Haeburu had it turned over, and the gold-frog child Geumwa was underneath; it has walked beside him ever since. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

Today he looks down.” Context: Every day the sun crosses the sky on the same road. Today he looks down. The sky is empty first. Then come five dragons in the yoke, gold, crimson, azure, jade and white, and behind them a small gold chariot cutting the noon on the run they make every day. From the ground it is a fleck and a wheel, nothing a bather could call a face. The driver stands in it the way a man stands in a doorway he owns, one palm on the rail, laughing at nothing in particular.  A wide or medium establishing frame that hooks. CANON — PLACE Buyeo (부여) — attached board /pl_buyeo_yard.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.at: She kisses him with river still on her mouth.
images.alt: The kiss tastes like the shallows.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. PARALLEL FRAME: the LAYOUT picture on the sheet is the master of a set of frames that recur across this story. Repaint ITS EXACT COMPOSITION: the same camera height, angle and lens, the same framing, the same number of figures in the same positions, sizes and poses, the same main shapes (gate, line, dais, table, waterline) in the same places, the same direction of the key light. Only the people, their faces and dress, the place and the hour change, so the two frames line up like a before-and-after. Ignore the layout picture's faces, clothes and colours. The same profile kiss in the shallows of the Amnok. Haemosu on the LEFT, bare-chested sky god, head bowed to her; Yuhwa on the RIGHT, up out of the water, wet silk clinging, both hands in his hair; river light flickering on their faces, the far bank and reeds in bokeh. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT LAYOUT picture (copy its composition, not its people), SECOND face = haemosu, THIRD face = yuhwa. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), binyeo board yuhwa (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing). HAEMOSU Colour #f0b429. LADY YUHWA Colour #8fc4e0. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.

blocks.html: Every day the sun crosses the sky on the same road. Today he looks down.
blocks.ko: 해는 날마다 같은 길로 하늘을 건넌다. 오늘, 그가 내려다본다.

blocks.html: The sky is empty first. Then come five dragons in the yoke, gold, crimson, azure, jade and white, and behind them a small gold chariot cutting the noon on the run they make every day. From the ground it is a fleck and a wheel, nothing a bather could call a face. The driver stands in it the way a man stands in a doorway he owns, one palm on the rail, laughing at nothing in particular.
blocks.ko: 하늘이 먼저 비어 있다. 그러고 멍에를 멘 용 다섯이 온다. 금빛, 진홍, 푸른빛, 비취, 흰빛. 그 뒤로 작은 금 수레가 매일 하는 그 운행으로 한낮을 가른다. 땅에서 보면 금빛 점 하나와 바퀴 하나, 목욕하는 사람이 얼굴이라 부를 만한 것은 없다. 몰이꾼은 제 문간에 선 사내처럼 수레에 서서, 난간에 손바닥을 얹고, 딱히 누구한테랄 것 없이 웃는다.

blocks.html: Dawn, noon, dusk, night, always the same route. Below, the Amnok is a line he is not supposed to break: wet stone, morning shallows with no boat in them, rocks that are only rocks.
blocks.ko: 새벽, 한낮, 해질녘, 밤, 늘 같은 길이다. 아래로 압록은 그가 넘으면 안 되는 선이다. 젖은 돌, 배 한 척 없는 아침 여울, 그냥 바위일 뿐인 바위.

blocks.html: Every god’s road crosses it. Most of them keep going.
blocks.ko: 신들의 길은 모두 이 강을 건넌다. 대개는 그냥 지나간다.

blocks.html: Haemosu, god of the sun, has kept this hour since before the river had daughters. Today the Amnok flashes under the wheel. He looks down, and the hour breaks.
blocks.ko: 태양신 해모수는 강에 딸이 생기기 전부터 이 시각을 지켜 왔다. 오늘은 바퀴 아래로 압록이 번뜩인다. 그가 내려다보고, 시각이 깨진다.

blocks.caption: The sun god. Punctual since before the rivers, until this afternoon.
blocks.ko: 태양신. 강이 생기기 전부터 시간을 지켰다. 오늘 오후까지는.

blocks.html: In the shallows, three river-daughters are bathing: Yuhwa and her two sisters. Wet hair down their backs, the river at their hips. Nobody dressed for heaven. He falls in love and in lust in the same glance.
blocks.ko: 얕은 물에서 강의 딸 셋이 멱을 감는다. 유화와 두 언니다. 젖은 머리칼은 등을 타고 흐르고, 강물은 허리까지 찼다. 아무도 하늘을 위해 옷을 차려입지 않았다. 그는 한눈에 사랑과 욕정에 동시에 빠진다.

blocks.caption: The river’s youngest daughter, a nymph of the Amnok. Heaven is about to ruin her afternoon, or make it.
blocks.ko: 강의 막내딸, 압록의 물의 요정. 하늘이 그녀의 오후를 망치려 한다. 아니면 만들어 주거나.

blocks.caption: The eldest river-daughter. First into the water, every time.
blocks.ko: 강의 맏딸. 물에 들어가는 건 언제나 그녀가 먼저다.

blocks.caption: The middle sister. She laughs first and dives second.
blocks.ko: 둘째. 먼저 웃고, 그다음에 뛰어든다.

blocks.html: Hwahye and Wihye have left their silk on the rocks. The eldest folded hers once; the middle did not bother. Yuhwa’s ice-blue is still on her shoulder, wet.
blocks.ko: 화혜와 위혜의 비단은 바위 위에 있다. 언니는 한 번 접어 두었고, 둘째는 귀찮아했다. 유화의 얼음빛은 아직 어깨에, 젖은 채로 있다.

blocks.html: Yuhwa kneels in the shallows with her hair in one fist like a dark rope and rinses the river out of it without hurrying. Heaven can wait on a rinse; she has decided that without saying it. With her back to the sky she looks over her shoulder, as if someone up there had said her name.
blocks.ko: 유화가 여울에 무릎을 꿇고, 검은 밧줄 같은 머리채를 한 손에 쥔 채 서두르지 않고 강물을 헹궈 낸다. 하늘은 헹굼쯤 기다려도 된다. 말은 안 했지만 그렇게 정했다. 하늘을 등진 채, 위에서 누가 이름이라도 부른 것처럼 어깨 너머로 돌아본다.

en: …Stop. Stop the chariot.
Those thighs…
The water…
Unni.
Go. I’m here.
…I was going to say don’t look up.
Hey. In.
Now. You hear me?

blocks.html: Hwahye dives first and does not look back. The eldest treats the sky like a timetable she will not miss.
blocks.ko: 화혜가 먼저 잠수하고 뒤를 안 본다. 언니는 하늘을 놓치면 안 되는 시간표처럼 다룬다.

en: Pfft— wait up.
You, seriously—
Whatever, I’m going—

blocks.html: Wihye laughs and follows, a splash that is mostly amusement.
blocks.ko: 위혜가 웃으며 따라간다. 물보라의 대부분이 재미다.

blocks.html: Two wakes cut the shallows and close. Yuhwa stays. She gets up off her knees, looks straight up as if she had been waiting for heaven to notice, and draws her wet hair over one shoulder.
blocks.ko: 물살 두 줄이 여울을 가르고 닫힌다. 유화는 남는다. 무릎을 펴고 일어나, 하늘이 알아채기를 기다리던 사람처럼 위를 똑바로 올려다보고, 젖은 머리를 한쪽 어깨로 넘긴다.

blocks.html: She draws the wet silk higher, one hip and then the other, and lets the sun finish looking.
blocks.ko: 젖은 비단을 더 끌어올린다. 한쪽 엉덩이, 그리고 다른 쪽. 해가 보기를 끝내게 둔다.

lines: 왜 안 숨어? 그렇게 쳐다보면… 나 내려간다.
en: Hey—
Wait. Hey. You.
Why aren’t you hiding? Look at me like that and I’m coming down.
Heaven looks down every day.
So today I’m supposed to blush?
…Come closer, if you want to see.
Into the water.
And decide… where your hands are going.
…Your name.
I need it… before I come down.
Or… I kiss you without one.
Come down first.
From the sky it’s an order.
At the water… I’ll hear it as a request.
Ask with your mouth… and I’ll answer with my name.

blocks.html: He forgets how to swallow, a god doing a mortal’s small panic. Then he grins, and the grin arrives before the plan. He leaves the rail and the hour in the same motion, the dragons keep the joke going without him, and the water takes him at the knee.
blocks.ko: 삼키는 법을 잊는다. 신이 인간의 작은 공황을 겪는다. 그러고 웃는데, 계획보다 웃음이 먼저 온다. 난간과 시각을 한 동작으로 떠나고, 용들은 그 없이 농담을 잇고, 물이 무릎에서 그를 받는다.

blocks.html: He wades close. She does not run. He stops where a stranger should stop. Then he doesn’t.
blocks.ko: 가까이 걸어 들어온다. 그녀는 도망가지 않는다. 낯선 사람이 설 자리에서 선다. 그러고 안 선다.

en: Why didn’t you run away?
Your sisters did.
…Didn’t see any reason.
The water’s cold. You’re warm. That’s all there is to it.
lines: 물은 차갑고, 당신은 따뜻하고. 그게 다예요.

en: Look straight at the sun
and you burn.
Oh, is that so?
Then I should blink.
It’ll burn your eyes out.
I’m not a lamp.
I like what I see.
I’m looking anyway. You came down.
Don’t make me say it twice.

blocks.html: He swallows. The grin survives it. Barely.
blocks.ko: 그가 삼킨다. 웃음은 산다. 간신히.

blocks.html: She tips her mouth and asks whether the sun likes what it sees, silk already losing the argument with the water.
blocks.ko: 입을 기울여 묻는다. 해는 보이는 게 좋으냐고. 비단은 이미 물과의 말다툼에서 지고 있다.

en: This way. The bank.
The sky has too many sisters.

blocks.html: He follows like the hour had been her idea.
blocks.ko: 시각이 그녀의 생각이었다는 듯이 따라간다.

blocks.html: The copper room rises on the bank like a kiln. He builds it the same afternoon, because the open sky has become too many witnesses.
blocks.ko: 구리 방이 강턱에 가마처럼 올라온다. 같은 날 오후 짓는다. 열린 하늘이 너무 많은 증인이 되어서.

lines: 구리에 기대면… 어디에 데었는지 구분 못 하실 거예요.
en: Copper gets hot in summer.
…You’ll know if you touch it.
My back, too.
If you press me to it… you won’t tell which burned you.
I know.
That’s why I can’t take my hands off you.
Or my mouth.
Then don’t.
Not while heaven is watching.
And while it watches… deeper.

blocks.html: She kisses him with river still on her mouth. The kiss tastes like the shallows. He makes a sound he will deny.
blocks.ko: 입에 강이 남은 채로 그를 입 맞춘다. 키스는 여울 맛이다. 그는 나중에 부인할 소리를 낸다.

blocks.html: Inside, the copper has kept the afternoon’s heat. She leans into it and does not look away from him. Gold lies across wet skin in a hard bar, and the ice-blue silk slips from one shoulder, then gives up the other.
blocks.ko: 안에서 구리는 오후의 열을 간직하고 있다. 그녀는 거기 기대어 그에게서 눈을 떼지 않는다. 젖은 살 위로 금빛이 단단한 띠처럼 눕고, 얼음빛 비단이 한쪽 어깨에서 흘러내리더니, 이윽고 다른 쪽도 내준다.

en: If you want it, say so.
I’m not asking twice.
Give me— all of it.
Don’t save any.

blocks.html: He puts her back to it anyway. The river-silk is gathered at her hip and her thighs close around a sun-god who has never learned to be gentle with an hour. She takes him in with the same wet hand that washed her hair for heaven, and when he is all the way inside her she laughs, as if this were what she had meant by looking.
blocks.ko: 그래도 그는 그녀의 등을 거기 댄다. 강의 비단이 허리께에 모이고, 시각을 살살 다룰 줄 모르는 태양신을 그녀의 허벅지가 감싼다. 하늘을 위해 머리를 감던 그 젖은 손으로 그를 이끌어 들이고, 그가 끝까지 들어오자, 올려다본 게 이거였다는 듯이 웃는다.

en: Haa— is heaven always this heavy?
More— against the copper— don’t stop—
I broke the hour.
I don’t care.
Your name— now—
Yuhwa— ah— it’s Yuhwa—
Stay— stay inside me—
All of it— the whole sun—

blocks.html: He takes her through the heat of the wall, gold on wet skin, and every stroke knocks a sound out of her that the river throws back. She comes first and loudly, looking up as if heaven were still watching. Then he spills into her, a god’s whole careless heat, and does not draw back, because she told him not to, and because the hour is already ruined.
blocks.ko: 벽의 열 속에서 그가 그녀를 안는다. 젖은 살 위에 금빛이 앉고, 한 번 움직일 때마다 그녀에게서 터져 나오는 소리를 강이 되던진다. 그녀가 먼저, 크게 끝에 닿는다. 하늘이 아직 보고 있는 것처럼 위를 올려다보며. 그러고 그가 그녀 안에 쏟는다. 신의 무심한 열 전부를. 그리고 물러나지 않는다. 그러지 말라고 했으니까. 시각은 이미 깨졌으니까.

blocks.html: The copper keeps the afternoon. Outside, the river goes on being a river.
blocks.ko: 구리가 오후를 간직한다. 밖에서는 강이 계속 강이다.

blocks.html: Up on the road, the dragons have hauled an empty chariot to dusk on their own. Half the world got its evening late. Heaven noticed.
blocks.ko: 하늘 길 위에선 용들이 빈 수레를 저희끼리 끌고 해 질 녘까지 갔다. 세상 절반이 저녁을 늦게 맞았다. 하늘이 알아챘다.

en: They’re calling.
I’m late. I’m never late.

lines: …내일 또 와요. 같은 시각에. 이번엔 내가 깨 줄게요.
en: Go, then.
…Come back tomorrow. Same hour. I’ll break it for you this time.

lines: 두 번은 안 내려 보내 줘. 해 떠 있는 동안은.
야. 그런 눈으로 보지 마. 방법 찾을게.
en: They won’t let me come down twice. Not while I’m up there.
Hey. Don’t look at me like that. I’ll find a way.

blocks.html: He goes up in a flash of copper. Heaven fines the sun the only way it can: while he is in the sky, he may not set foot on the earth. He may look. He may talk. That is all.
blocks.ko: 그는 구릿빛 섬광 속에 올라간다. 하늘이 해에게 내릴 수 있는 벌은 그것뿐이다. 하늘에 떠 있는 동안에는 땅을 밟지 못한다. 볼 수는 있다. 말할 수도 있다. 거기까지다.

blocks.label: Habek's Court
blocks.ko: 하백의 조정

blocks.html: The copper is still warm when the river notices. The Amnok keeps its own court: Habek, god of the river and father of three daughters, stands on the wet stones as if the current were a hall. Mist is the dais. He does not need a chair.
blocks.ko: 구리가 아직 따뜻할 때 강이 알아챈다. 압록에는 제 조정이 있다. 강의 신이자 세 딸의 아버지인 하백이 여울이 대청이라도 되는 듯 젖은 돌 위에 선다. 안개가 대좌다. 의자는 필요 없다.

blocks.caption: The Amnok’s river god. He keeps his borders the way kings do, and his daughters the same way.
blocks.ko: 압록의 강신. 국경을 지키듯 딸들도 지킨다.

en: Who stopped the chariot. Say a name.
lines: 수레를 멈춘 게 누구냐. 이름을 대라.

en: I… looked up.
I just— looked. That’s all it was.
You don’t sleep in my mist after that.
You smell like copper.
lines: 그 다음엔 내 안개에서 자지 못한다.

en: Go. The bank is closed.

blocks.html: Hwahye and Wihye do not argue the sentence. The eldest watches the current. The middle one watches the copper glow die. Neither looks at their father’s face.
blocks.ko: 화혜와 위혜는 판결을 논하지 않는다. 언니는 여울을 본다. 둘째는 죽어 가는 구리 빛을 본다. 둘 다 아버지 얼굴은 안 본다.

blocks.html: Habek kicks Yuhwa out with a look, not a foot. The bank understands.
blocks.ko: 하백이 유화를 내쫓는다. 발이 아니라 눈으로. 강턱이 알아듣는다.

blocks.html: The pavilion walkway does not catch her. Habek’s sleeve is already the closed door. She hits packed earth with ice-blue still wet from the copper.
blocks.ko: 누각 복도가 받아주지 않는다. 하백의 소매가 이미 닫힌 문이다. 구리가 덜 마른 얼음빛으로 다진 흙에 엎어진다.

blocks.html: For a while nobody comes. The mist that used to be a bed is just weather. She sits where the river can see her and does not look up.
blocks.ko: 한동안 아무도 안 온다. 침대였던 안개가 그냥 날씨다. 강이 보이는 자리에 앉아서, 올려다보지 않는다.
blocks.art: Episode break: side story S1 ends here.

blocks.html: The sky talks first. She hears him before she sees anything with paws.
blocks.ko: 하늘이 먼저 말한다. 발 달린 걸 보기 전에 그 목소리를 듣는다.

en: Hey.
Wait. Don’t sit in the dust.
Follow the fox.

blocks.html: The fox is already on the packed earth, pale gold-white, looking back once as if she might miss the joke. Yuhwa follows it south, barefoot, the ice-blue gone dull with dust: pine shade, a river-bend that is not the Amnok, a pass of bare stone where she is smaller than the ridge. The fox does not explain the map.
blocks.ko: 여우가 이미 다진 흙 위에 있다. 창백한 금빛 흰 털, 농담을 놓칠까 봐 한 번 돌아본다. 유화는 맨발로, 먼지에 탁해진 얼음빛으로 그 뒤를 따라 남쪽으로 간다. 소나무 그늘, 압록이 아닌 강굽이, 능선보다 그녀가 작아지는 벗은 돌 고개. 여우는 지도를 설명하지 않는다.

blocks.label: Buyeo
blocks.ko: 부여

blocks.html: From the river, Buyeo’s capital is a palisade of timber teeth and a hill of grey roofs. The studded doors open. King Gumwa, the gold-frog king, comes out to the yard himself.
blocks.ko: 강에서 보면 부여의 도읍은 나무 이빨 같은 목책과 잿빛 기와 언덕이다. 징 박힌 문이 열린다. 금개구리 왕 금와가 몸소 마당으로 나온다.

blocks.caption: The gold-frog king. Found under a rock, raised in a palace, kind to strays.
blocks.ko: 금개구리 임금. 바위 밑에서 발견되어 궁에서 자랐고, 떠돌이에게 너그럽다.

blocks.html: An old kingdom that takes in strays and keeps count.
blocks.ko: 떠돌이를 받아 주고, 셈은 해 두는 오래된 나라.

en: Come in. I’ve got a room free.
The yard can learn thy name later.

blocks.html: A sun-shaft finds her where she kneels to wring the river out of her sleeve. When she crosses the yard at night it moves with her, a bar of gold keeping her sleeve.
blocks.ko: 해 한 줄기가, 소매에서 강을 짜내려 무릎 꿇은 그녀를 찾아낸다. 밤에 마당을 건너면 그 빛이 따라 움직인다. 소매를 지키는 금빛 막대.

blocks.html: Yuhwa’s ice-blue sleeve is the first roof the boy will remember, though he is not a boy yet.
blocks.ko: 유화의 얼음빛 소매가 첫 지붕이다. 아이는 그걸 기억할 것이다. 아직 아이가 아닌데.

blocks.html: In time Yuhwa lays a great egg. Gumwa has the egg taken from her before the court has agreed what a river-daughter is allowed to bear.
blocks.ko: 때가 되어 유화가 커다란 알을 낳는다. 금와가 알을 빼앗아 간다. 조정은 강의 딸이 무엇을 낳아도 되는지 아직 합의하지 못했다.

blocks.html: Dogs won't eat it. An axe won't split it. What on earth is inside Yuhwa's egg…?
blocks.ko: 개도 먹지 않는다. 도끼로도 쪼개지지 않는다. 유화의 알 속에는 대체 무엇이 들어 있는가…?

logline.en: Dogs won’t eat it. Hooves step around it. An axe won’t split it. Nobody in the hall wants to say what it is.
logline.ko: 개도 먹지 않는다. 말굽도 비켜 간다. 도끼로도 쪼개지지 않는다. 그게 무엇인지 궁 안의 누구도 말하고 싶어 하지 않는다.

Night stable in Buyeo: Yuhwa holds out a needle between two fingers while Jumong, mid-brushstroke on the best horse, turns to stare at her
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 still. Over-shoulder two-shot inside a Buyeo royal stable at night: timber posts, straw, one hanging oil lamp. Sharp foreground: the dark flank and mane of a lean fine horse, soft in bokeh. Midground: YUHWA (face, white jeogori and garments from the attached portrait; hair ornament matches the attached binyeo ref) leaning on a stall post, holding out a single thin iron needle between two fingers, sly mother’s half-smile. Young JUMONG (face and red silk from the attached portrait, CLEAN-SHAVEN, no mustache, no facial hair) caught mid-brushstroke on the horse’s neck, turning to stare at her, laughing in disbelief. ONE device: the long dark stall partition cutting the frame diagonally, the lamp the only key. Jumong red #e8563f as the lamp’s warm bounce on his sleeve and the horse’s eye, NOT a glow aura. Crushed blacks, straw motes in the lamp shaft. EVERY FRAME A PAINTING: compose as a master canvas — one geometry or one body owns the frame; light is the plot; negative space is ink; not coverage, not a tourist postcard, not a game-map. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock: anamorphic movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain. A CAMERA in a real Korean place — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D archviz, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portrait — NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: dutch, crane, worm’s-eye, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key + long shadows — not even daylight wash. ICONIC MINIMAL: ONE architectural device a lens can see; empty negative space; tiny figures or lower-third; the world stays in the shot. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor portrait garments gold. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point.
