blocks.html: Buyeo tries very hard to get rid of the egg. The egg declines.
blocks.ko: 부여는 그 알을 치우려고 무진 애를 쓴다. 알은 사양한다.

blocks.html: Dogs and pigs will not eat it; the sty refuses the guest, and the ministers pretend that is a kind of answer. In the road, cattle and horses step around it, hooves knowing better than the hall. In the open field, birds cover it with their wings instead of pecking, and the yard goes quiet at that.
blocks.ko: 개와 돼지가 먹지 않는다. 돼지우리가 손님을 거절하고, 신하들은 그걸 대답인 척한다. 길에 버리면 소와 말이 피해서 간다. 발굽이 대청보다 낫다. 들에 두면 새들이 쪼지 않고 날개로 덮는다. 마당이 그걸 보고 조용해진다.

blocks.html: An axe is brought. The axe will not split the egg. The edge sings and the shell does not bother to crack.
blocks.ko: 도끼를 가져온다. 도끼로도 알이 안 깨진다. 날이 울고, 껍질은 갈라질 생각도 안 한다.

blocks.html: Someone winds up with both arms and hurls it off the palisade. It meets the stones and stays whole.
blocks.ko: 누군가 두 팔로 자세를 잡더니 목책 밖으로 내던진다. 알은 돌에 부딪히고도 멀쩡하다.

blocks.html: Yuhwa wraps it warm in her own sleeve and takes it back upstairs, and nobody reaches for the axe again.
blocks.ko: 유화가 제 소매로 따뜻하게 싼다. 다시 위층으로 가져간다. 다시 도끼에 손대는 사람이 없다.

blocks.html: Then the shell gives, and out comes a baby boy, wet and furious, already trying to focus. He looks up as if the room had owed him an explanation.
blocks.ko: 그러고 껍질이 열리고 사내아이가 나온다. 젖고, 화가 나 있고, 벌써 초점을 맞추려 한다. 방이 해명이라도 빚진 것처럼 올려다본다.

blocks.html: They name him Jumong, the good shot, because in those days people were named for what heaven had plainly already decided. He grows up with Gumwa’s sons, Deso and Galsa.
blocks.ko: 그들은 아이를 주몽, 활 잘 쏘는 이라 부른다. 그 시절엔 하늘이 이미 정해 둔 것을 이름으로 붙였다. 아이는 금와의 아들 대소, 갈사와 함께 자란다.

blocks.html: They are boys first, three princes at one stake in one square, before anybody is an heir on purpose. They shoot with borrowed bows, too long in the arm.
blocks.ko: 처음에는 그냥 아이들이다. 마당 하나, 말뚝 하나에 왕자 셋. 누가 일부러 태자가 되기 전이다. 빌린 활로 쏜다. 팔보다 긴 활이다.

blocks.html: Jumong can find a fly’s wing with an arrow before the bow fits his arm.
blocks.ko: 팔에 활이 맞기도 전에, 주몽은 화살로 파리의 날개를 찾아낸다.

blocks.html: Odd things happen around the sun’s son, and the yard learns not to mention them. Lamps lean toward him in a still room. Deso’s hounds leave their master for his feet. Once, at noon, his shadow points the wrong way, and the whole square looks elsewhere.
blocks.ko: 태양의 아들 둘레에서는 이상한 일이 일어난다. 마당은 말하지 않기로 배운다. 바람 없는 방에서 등잔불이 그쪽으로 눕는다. 대소의 사냥개들이 주인을 버리고 그의 발치에 눕는다. 한번은 정오에 그의 그림자가 엉뚱한 쪽을 가리켰고, 마당 전체가 딴 데를 봤다.

blocks.caption: The best archer in Buyeo. The princes have noticed.
blocks.ko: 부여에서 활을 제일 잘 쏘는 아이. 왕자들도 눈치챘다.

blocks.hanja: 骨表英奇。年甫七歲，嶷然異常，自作弓矢射之，百發百中。扶餘俗語，善射爲朱蒙，故以名云。
blocks.html: His frame and face were striking and strange. At seven he was already unlike other children; he made his own bow and arrows, and of a hundred shots, a hundred hit. In the Buyeo tongue a good archer is called jumong, and so they named him.
blocks.ko: 골격과 생김새가 빼어나고 기이하였다. 나이 겨우 일곱에 의젓함이 남달랐는데, 스스로 활과 화살을 만들어 쏘면 백 번 쏘아 백 번 맞혔다. 부여 말에 활 잘 쏘는 이를 주몽이라 하므로, 그렇게 이름 지었다고 한다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 13, Goguryeo Annals — King Dongmyeong

en: I’ll take the fly.

blocks.html: Deso teaches the grip, then resents the hit. The lesson ends the moment the arrow is better than the teacher.
blocks.ko: 대소가 쥐는 법을 가르치고, 맞히면 분을 낸다. 화살이 스승보다 나아지는 순간 수업이 끝난다.

blocks.html: The yard hears the wood take it, a clean tick, and the praise does not arrive. Deso keeps his hands on his own bow as if applause were a confession. Galsa looks at the dirt instead of the hit.
blocks.ko: 마당이 나무가 화살을 받는 소리를 듣는다. 깨끗한 딱 소리. 칭찬은 오지 않는다. 대소는 박수가 자백이라도 되는 듯 손을 제 활에 둔다. 갈사는 맞은 자리 대신 흙을 본다.

blocks.html: They sleep in a pile like dogs under one quilt, and in the morning the quilt has taken sides. Jumong steals the last millet and grins through it, which is worse than the theft.
blocks.ko: 개들처럼 이불 하나에 뭉쳐 자고, 아침이면 이불이 편을 든다. 주몽은 마지막 기장을 훔치고, 훔치면서 웃는다. 도둑질보다 그게 더 나쁘다.

blocks.html: Yuhwa watches from the hall door, ice-blue sleeve on the post, not stepping into the boys’ weather.
blocks.ko: 유화가 대청 문에서 본다. 기둥에 얼음빛 소매. 아이들 날씨 안으로 들어가지 않는다.

blocks.html: Only two come back talking from the stake. The third has already started a country in his head.
blocks.ko: 말하면서 돌아오는 건 둘뿐이다. 셋째는 이미 머릿속에서 나라를 시작했다.

blocks.html: The ministers start keeping two counts: the heir’s arrows and the foundling’s. Deso notices, and stops inviting Jumong on the hunts that matter. The excuse is different every time. The reason never is.
blocks.ko: 신하들이 두 가지 셈을 시작한다. 태자의 화살과 주워 온 아이의 화살. 대소가 알아차리고, 중요한 사냥에는 주몽을 부르지 않기 시작한다. 핑계는 매번 다르다. 속내는 한결같다.

blocks.label: The Mark-Stake
blocks.ko: 과녁 말뚝

blocks.html: Grown, they still shoot at the princes’ mark-stake. Deso stands too close when Jumong’s arrow lands.
blocks.ko: 다 자라서도 왕자들은 과녁 말뚝에 쏜다. 주몽의 화살이 꽂힐 때 대소는 너무 가까이 서 있다.

blocks.caption: Buyeo’s crown prince. Good with a bow, until someone is better.
blocks.ko: 부여의 태자. 활을 잘 쏜다. 누가 더 잘 쏘기 전까지는.

lines: 먹여 주는 집보다 멀리 쏘지 마라.
en: Do not outshoot the house that feeds thee.
Then put the mark farther.

blocks.caption: Gumwa’s younger son. He smiles at everything, for now.
blocks.ko: 금와의 둘째 아들. 아직은 무엇에든 웃는다.

en: If it lands, I meant to applaud.

blocks.html: Jumong keeps the grin because grinning is cheaper than asking why, and Deso hates the price.
blocks.ko: 주몽은 웃음을 유지한다. 왜냐고 묻는 것보다 웃음이 싸서. 대소는 그 값을 싫어한다.

blocks.html: Deso starts counting things: how many of his own men laugh at Jumong’s jokes, how many ask the foundling to judge their shots. The count goes the wrong way. That is when the side room starts filling after lamps-out.
blocks.ko: 대소는 세기 시작한다. 제 사람들 중 몇이 주몽의 농담에 웃는지, 몇이 주워 온 아이에게 제 활솜씨를 봐 달라는지. 셈은 엉뚱한 쪽으로 간다. 그때부터 등잔이 꺼진 뒤 곁방에 사람이 모이기 시작한다.

blocks.html: Jumong’s arranged marriage to Lady Ye is a hall’s solution: a wife, a lamp, a door that still opens onto Buyeo.
blocks.ko: 주몽의 정략혼은 대청의 해법이다. 아내, 등잔, 아직 부여로 열리는 문.

blocks.html: Lady Ye gets pregnant with their son Yuri while the yard is still pretending the foundling is a guest.
blocks.ko: 예씨부인이 아들 유리를 밴다. 마당은 아직 그 주워 온 아이를 손님인 척한다.

blocks.label: The Plot
blocks.ko: 음모

blocks.label: The Side Room
blocks.ko: 곁방

blocks.html: Gumwa will not take the heir’s counsel, so Deso takes the ministers into a side room. Lamp low. If they write it down, the scandal arrives before the knife.
blocks.ko: 금와가 태자의 말을 받지 않아서, 대소가 신하들을 곁방으로 부른다. 등잔은 낮고. 적으면 칼보다 소문이 먼저 온다.

en: Do it afore the next hunt.
Quiet will do.

blocks.html: Gumwa answers his heir the way tired kings answer. He refuses the knife and gives the foundling a chore instead: Jumong is sent to the royal stables, which in Buyeo is where a hall keeps a prince it would rather not see at dinner.
blocks.ko: 금와는 지친 왕들이 답하는 식으로 맏아들에게 답한다. 칼은 거절하고, 주워 온 아이에게는 일거리를 준다. 주몽은 왕의 마구간으로 보내진다. 부여에서 마구간은, 저녁상에서 마주치고 싶지 않은 왕자를 두는 곳이다.

blocks.html: The stables come with three boys who smell worse than he does. Oi, who is always already packing. Mari, who asks why. Hyupbo, who carries the extra. By the end of the month they are his.
blocks.ko: 마구간에는 그보다 냄새 고약한 사내아이 셋이 딸려 있다. 늘 짐부터 싸 두는 오이. 왜냐고 묻는 마리. 남는 짐을 드는 협보. 달이 다 가기 전에 셋은 그의 사람이 된다.

blocks.html: The month teaches them each other’s shapes. Oi eats half his millet and puts the other half in Jumong’s bowl without a word. Mari asks why about everything until Jumong runs out of answers and starts inventing. Hyupbo cries the first night and lies about it for a year.
blocks.ko: 한 달이면 서로의 결이 보인다. 오이는 제 기장 절반을 먹고 나머지를 말없이 주몽의 그릇에 담는다. 마리는 모든 것에 왜냐고 묻다가, 주몽의 답이 떨어지면 주몽이 지어내기 시작한다. 협보는 첫날 밤 울고, 일 년 내내 잡아뗀다.

en: They’ll kill thee, lad.
Tha knows that.

lines: 그럼 짐 빨리 싸고, 왜냐고 묻고, 남는 짐 드는 사람이 필요하지.
en: Then I need men who pack fast, ask why, and carry extra.
Stay. All three of you.

blocks.label: The Stable
blocks.ko: 마구간

blocks.html: Yuhwa comes to the stable after the lamps are out, a river-daughter in a frog-king’s straw, and finds her son brushing the best horse in Buyeo as if he could apologise to it in advance.
blocks.ko: 등잔이 꺼진 뒤 유화가 마구간에 온다. 개구리 왕의 짚더미에 선 강의 딸. 아들은 부여에서 제일 좋은 말을 빗질하고 있다. 미리 사과라도 해 두려는 듯이.

en: This one, isn’t it?
The fast one.
…How’d you know?
I didn’t tell anyone.

lines: 너 이 녀석만 빗질을 오래 하잖아.
나중에 미안하다 하고, 배 터지게 먹이고.
en: You brush this one longer than the others.
I’ll give you a needle. Put it in his tongue.
Say sorry later, and feed him till he bursts.
Mother, you’re terrifying.
…For how many days?
Until Deso’s done sharpening.

blocks.html: By the next moon the fastest horse in the yard looks like a rack of kindling with a mane, and the slow ones shine like lacquer. Gumwa walks the stalls, picks the fattest for himself, and tosses the thin one to the foundling with a joke about how well they match. Deso laughs loudest, which is a pity, because he is the one man in Buyeo who should have looked twice.
blocks.ko: 다음 달이 되자 마구간에서 제일 빠른 말은 갈기 달린 장작더미가 되어 있고, 느린 말들은 옻칠한 듯 번들거린다. 금와는 마구간을 돌며 제일 살찐 말을 자기 몫으로 고르고, 여윈 말은 주워 온 아이에게 던져 준다. 둘이 참 닮았다는 농담과 함께. 대소가 제일 크게 웃는다. 안됐다. 부여에서 두 번 쳐다봤어야 할 사람은 그 하나뿐이었는데.

lines: 둘 다 내 밥으 먹고도 마르는구나.
en: Suits thee.
The pair of you eat my rice and still stay thin.
Thank you, Majesty.
I’ll take good care of him.

blocks.html: He pulls the needle out that night. The horse eats until dawn.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 바늘을 뽑는다. 말은 새벽까지 먹는다.

blocks.label: The Knife
blocks.ko: 칼

blocks.html: Before the next hunt, a knife comes through the dark of his room. Lady Ye’s lamp is still lit, so the shadow moves on the wall before the man does. Jumong rolls. The blade goes into the quilt up to the hilt.
blocks.ko: 다음 사냥이 오기 전, 어둠 속에서 칼 하나가 그의 방으로 들어온다. 예씨 부인의 등잔이 아직 켜져 있어, 사내보다 그림자가 먼저 벽 위에서 움직인다. 주몽이 구른다. 칼날이 손잡이까지 이불에 박힌다.

blocks.html: The man runs. He wears a palace sleeve, and he runs toward Deso’s end of the hall.
blocks.ko: 사내는 달아난다. 궁의 소매를 입었고, 대소의 처소 쪽으로 달린다.

blocks.caption: A Buyeo girl with a steady hand and a long memory.
blocks.ko: 손이 야무지고 기억이 긴 부여의 처녀.

en: Leave Buyeo. Tonight.
I’ll keep the lamp.

blocks.html: He takes his sword down from the wall and breaks it across the seven-sided stone under the pine pillar. It takes two tries. He is not a swordsman.
blocks.ko: 그는 벽에서 칼을 내려, 소나무 기둥 밑 일곱 모 주춧돌에 대고 꺾는다. 두 번 만에 부러진다. 그는 칼잡이가 아니다.

lines: 반은 여기 둬. 기둥 밑 틈에.
아들이면 말해 줘. 소나무 아래, 일곱 모 돌 위. 알아서 찾을 거야.
en: Half stays. In the crack, under the pillar.
If it’s a boy, tell him: under the pine, on the seven-sided stone. He’ll work it out.
And if it’s a girl?
Then she’ll work it out faster.
Leave the door half open.
So I know which way is still yours.
lines: 어느 쪽이 아직 네 건지 알게.

blocks.html: Night at the palisade. Iron studs, a red sleeve, and a wife who does not come out to wave.
blocks.ko: 목책의 밤. 쇠 못, 붉은 소매, 손 흔들러 나오지 않는 아내.

blocks.html: His friends Oi, Mari and Hyupbo take the hills with him. Behind them come the riders Deso sent, less a hunt than a net, and under the pines it closes from above.
blocks.ko: 벗 오이, 마리, 협보가 그와 함께 산으로 든다. 뒤로 대소가 보낸 기병이 따라붙는다. 사냥이라기보다 그물이고, 소나무 아래에서 그물은 위에서부터 조여 온다.

blocks.caption: Buyeo behind him, Deso’s riders behind that, and a river ahead with no bridge on it. Yet.
blocks.ko: 등 뒤엔 부여, 그 뒤엔 대소의 기병, 앞엔 다리 하나 없는 강. 아직은.

blocks.label: The River
blocks.ko: 강

blocks.label: The Flight
blocks.ko: 달아남

blocks.html: They split in the pines before the river, four men and one horse between them, the one Gumwa thought was thin.
blocks.ko: 강 앞 소나무 숲에서 넷이 갈라진다. 사람은 넷, 말은 한 마리. 금와가 여위었다고 여긴 그 말이다.

en: We’ll take the ridge, lad.
Find us while tha still has a bow.

lines: 능선 길은 너희가 더 멀어. 강은 내가 혼자 건널게.
en: Take him.
Your road over the ridge is longer. I’ll do the river alone.
Has tha gone daft? He’s thy horse.
Exactly. Fatten him up for me.
…I’ll come find you.

blocks.html: He runs until the pines smear. Behind him the net is spears in the dark, points only, no faces he is allowed to know.
blocks.ko: 소나무가 번질 때까지 뛴다. 뒤에서 그물은 어둠 속의 창이다. 날만 있고, 알아도 되는 얼굴은 없다.

blocks.html: Something keeps pace with him above the trees, black on black, going from branch to branch without seeming to hurry. A crow. He is too frightened to count its legs.
blocks.ko: 나무 위로 무언가가 그와 나란히 간다. 검은 위의 검은 것, 서두르는 기색도 없이 가지에서 가지로. 까마귀다. 다리를 셀 정신이 그에게는 없다.

blocks.html: Jumong reaches the water alone, his death already written down for that day. No ford. No boat. The friends are a ridge away, on purpose.
blocks.ko: 주몽이 홀로 물에 닿는다. 그날 죽기로 이미 적혀 있는 목숨이다. 여울도 배도 없다. 벗들은 일부러 능선 하나 떨어져 있다.

blocks.html: Haewonmek, the reaper who collects each day’s dead, is already in the air. He skims the river toward him. Black hat, black silk, mouth bound shut. Jumong doesn’t see him. He’s looking at the water and the rain.
blocks.ko: 그날의 죽은 자를 거두는 저승사자 해원맥이 벌써 공중에 떠 있다. 그는 강물 위를 스치듯 날아 그에게 다가온다. 검은 갓, 검은 비단, 꽁꽁 묶인 입. 주몽은 그를 보지 못한다. 그는 물과 빗줄기만 보고 있다.

blocks.caption: A fetch of the underworld. Black hat, black silk, and a mouth bound shut so he can’t haggle.
blocks.ko: 저승의 차사. 검은 갓, 검은 비단, 흥정 못 하게 묶인 입.

blocks.html: A root takes his foot. He goes down on the wet stones, pine needles in his mouth, the bow a pace off as if it had been the first thing taken. Haewonmek crouches over him to collect what is owed, and the blow is already coming down.
blocks.ko: 뿌리가 발을 잡는다. 젖은 돌 위로 넘어지고, 입에는 솔잎, 활은 먼저 빼앗긴 것처럼 한 걸음 떨어져 있다. 해원맥이 거둘 것을 거두러 그 위에 엎드리고, 일격은 이미 내려오고 있다.

blocks.html: The cloak arrives before the face. Rain fills it. A hand closes on Haewonmek’s wrist from behind, and the strike simply stops — the way an elder stops a sleeve that has gone too far.
blocks.ko: 망토가 얼굴보다 먼저 온다. 비가 그것을 채운다. 뒤에서 손이 해원맥의 손목을 잡고, 일격은 그냥 멈춘다 — 너무 멀리 간 소매를 맏이가 멈추듯.
blocks.art: Episode break: side story S2 ends here.

blocks.html: Jumong’s cheek is in the mud. Haewonmek looks back. Behind him, in a dark hood, the sun god is holding his wrist and laughing, as if the night had grabbed the wrong man. The night is Haewonmek’s road. The joke is Haemosu’s.
blocks.ko: 주몽의 뺨은 진흙에 있다. 해원맥이 돌아본다. 그 뒤에서 검은 두건을 쓴 태양신이 그의 손목을 잡은 채 웃고 있다. 밤이 사람을 잘못 집었다는 듯이. 밤은 해원맥의 길이다. 농담은 해모수의 것이다.

en: Haemosu…
The night is not your domain…!

lines: 바다를 건너다 네가 오는 소리가 들리더군.
en: Heh…
Do you really think the sun disappears at night?
I was just crossing the ocean when I heard you coming over.
This man is fated to die today…
You are not to interfere with Yumla’s domain…!

lines: 넌 내 아우고, 이 일 맡은 지 이레도 안 됐지. 살살 해 줄게.
염라가 할 말 있으면, 직접 와서 보라 해라.
en: Hey, Haewonmek.
You’re my little brother and it’s your first week. I’ll go easy on you.
But this is my son.
And he still hasn’t completed his purpose in this world.
And besides… I outrank you.
If Yumla has any complaints, tell him to come see me himself.

blocks.html: He puts Haewonmek aside and leans to Jumong’s ear. Jumong cannot see him, only the night, the river, a warmth that should not be there. The idea arrives as breath.
blocks.ko: 해원맥을 옆으로 밀어 두고 주몽의 귀에 입을 댄다. 주몽은 그를 보지 못한다. 밤과 강과, 거기 있어서는 안 될 온기뿐. 생각은 숨결로 온다.

blocks.label: The Crossing
blocks.ko: 건넌 강

lines: 나는 태양의 주인, 위대한 해모수의 아들이다!
en: I am the son of the great Haemosu, the lord of the sun!
Make way for me!

blocks.html: The river answers. Tortoises rise and lock shell to shell in the dark. Jumong runs the wet backs as if they had always been a road.
blocks.ko: 강이 응답한다. 자라들이 떠올라 어둠 속에서 등딱지를 잇는다. 주몽이 젖은 등 위를 달린다 — 원래부터 길이었던 것처럼.

blocks.html: Of old, the founder King Chumo laid the foundations. He came out of North Buyeo, son of the Heavenly Emperor; his mother was Habek’s daughter; he broke the egg and came down into the world… The king came to the ford and said: “I am King Chumo, son of August Heaven, whose mother is Habek’s daughter. Link the reeds and float the turtles for me.” At his voice the reeds linked and the turtles floated, and so he crossed.
blocks.ko: 옛날 시조 추모왕이 나라의 터를 열었다. 북부여에서 나왔으니 천제의 아들이요, 어머니는 하백의 딸로, 알을 깨고 세상에 내려왔다… 왕이 나루에 이르러 말하였다. “나는 황천의 아들이요, 어머니는 하백의 딸인 추모왕이다. 나를 위하여 갈대를 잇고 거북을 띄워라.” 그 소리에 응하여 곧 갈대가 이어지고 거북이 떠오르니, 그제야 건넜다.
blocks.hanja: 惟昔始祖，鄒牟王之創基也。出自北夫餘，天帝之子，母河伯女郎，剖卵降世…王臨津言曰：「我是皇天之子，母河伯女郎，鄒牟王，為我連葭浮龜。」應聲，即為連葭浮龜，然後造渡。
blocks.source: Gwanggaeto Stele (廣開土王碑) face I, opening lines (414)

blocks.html: The two brothers stay on the near stones. Jumong is already a red speck on the far dark. Haemosu throws an arm across Haewonmek’s shoulder and laughs like the job is done. Haewonmek’s gat is still askew — the look of a clerk whose ledger just walked off.
blocks.ko: 두 형제는 가까운 쪽 돌에 남는다. 주몽은 이미 먼 어둠의 붉은 점이다. 해모수가 해원맥의 어깨에 팔을 걸치고, 일이 끝난 듯이 웃는다. 해원맥의 갓은 아직 비뚤다 — 명부가 제 발로 걸어 나간 서기의 얼굴.

en: He is still mortal…

lines: 허나 말이야… 사람은 누구나 이승에 온 까닭이 있다.
때가 되면, 그때는 네가 데려가게 두지.
en: Yes, of course.
But you know… every man comes into this world for a purpose.
He’s going to do great things.
When his time comes, I’ll let you take him.
Look at him go.
That's my boy.
You just robbed a ledger.
I borrowed a day.
I'll give it back.
Yumla isn’t going to like this…
blocks.art: Grumbling.

blocks.html: The bird that watches him is not an ordinary crow. On Goguryeo’s banners it will stand on three legs under a red sun, the samjoko, the bird that can look at the day without blinking.
blocks.ko: 그를 지켜보는 새는 여느 까마귀가 아니다. 훗날 고구려의 기에서 그 새는 붉은 해 아래 세 다리로 설 것이다. 삼족오, 해를 깜빡이지 않고 바라보는 새.

blocks.html: It is sitting on a rock on the far bank when he comes off the last shell, soaked, laughing like an idiot because he is alive. This time he counts.
blocks.ko: 마지막 등껍질에서 내려섰을 때 그것은 건너편 강가 바위에 앉아 있다. 그는 흠뻑 젖어서, 살아 있다는 게 우스워 바보처럼 웃고 있다. 이번에는 센다.

en: …One, two.
Three?
Hey. Why’ve you got three legs?

blocks.html: The crow looks at him without blinking, which is either rude or holy, then drops off the rock, flies ten paces into the pines, lands again, and looks back.
blocks.ko: 까마귀는 눈도 깜박이지 않고 그를 본다. 무례하거나 신령하거나 둘 중 하나다. 그러고는 바위에서 내려앉아 소나무 숲으로 열 걸음 날아가 다시 앉고, 돌아본다.

lines: ……너 나 곰한테 데려가면 진짜 구워 먹는다.
en: Follow you?
…If you’re leading me to a bear, I swear I’m roasting you.
Three legs. There’d be one to spare.

blocks.html: He follows it all afternoon, uphill, through pines that stop being Buyeo’s and start being nobody’s. It keeps ten paces ahead and never once lets him catch up. At dusk it lands on a stone lip above a dark opening in the hill and stays there, folded, like a doorman whose shift is over.
blocks.ko: 그는 오후 내내 그것을 따라 오르막을, 부여의 것이기를 그만두고 누구의 것도 아니게 된 소나무 숲을 간다. 까마귀는 늘 열 걸음 앞에 있고 한 번도 따라잡히지 않는다. 해 질 녘 그것은 산허리에 난 어두운 입구 위 돌턱에 내려앉아, 날개를 접고 그대로 있다. 교대를 마친 문지기처럼.

en: …Here?
Thanks. Really.
Can’t roast you now, can I.

blocks.html: Before the valley has a name for him he goes in, into stone and leaf-light and a country-shaped dark. In what will be called the Jumong cavern, he prays for a roof of his own.
blocks.ko: 골짜기가 그를 부를 이름을 갖기도 전에, 그는 그 안으로 들어간다. 돌과 잎빛과 나라 모양의 어둠. 훗날 국동대혈이라 불릴 그곳에서, 제 지붕 하나를 빈다.

blocks.html: A soaked exile, a hall full of spears, and a chieftain's daughter who won't look at him. Jumong's luck is about to get complicated…!
blocks.ko: 흠뻑 젖은 망명자, 창이 가득한 전각, 그리고 끝까지 그를 쳐다보지 않는 족장의 딸. 주몽의 운이 복잡해지기 시작한다…!

logline.en: He’s still wet from the river when the spears find him. The chieftain’s daughter is sharper than the spears.
logline.ko: 강물이 채 마르기도 전에 창끝이 그를 찾아낸다. 족장의 딸은 그 창보다 날카롭다.

images.alt: High crane: the five Jolbon chieftains sit on five animal hides around one fire in Tabal's hall — crow feathers, horse, cow, pig, dog
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE watercolor painting, minimal iconic 2:1 still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop with nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Night inside Tabal's timber hall at Jolbon: packed-earth floor, rough timber posts, a smoke hole in the dark roof, ONE low fire pit at the exact centre as the only light. High crane angle looking steeply down. ONE device: FIVE ANIMAL HIDES laid flat on the earth floor in a ring around the fire like five petals, each a different skin: a spread mat of glossy BLACK CROW FEATHERS; a chestnut HORSE hide with a strip of black mane; a brown-and-white COW hide; a bristly dark grey-black PIG hide; a shaggy pale grey-white DOG pelt. EXACTLY FIVE men, one sitting cross-legged on each hide, facing the fire, nobody else in the hall: Yeon Tabal on the crow feathers (red headband, black beard); the Horse Ka, heavy and bearded, dark robe with a red sash, on the horse hide; the Cow Ka, youngest, red headband and white feathers in his long hair, on the cow hide; the Pig Ka, thick and heavy, on the pig hide; the Dog Ka, the eldest, white beard and grey headband, on the dog pelt. FACES ONLY from the attached chieftain portraits: IGNORE the tiger pelts and bear heads drawn on the portraits — nobody wears a tiger or bear skin; they wear plain hemp and leather tunics, wrapped forearms and their headbands, and the only animal skins in the frame are the five hides on the floor. Unstrung bows lie flat beside them. They lean in and argue — one stabbing a finger at the dirt, one with arms folded, one laughing, one weighing with his palms — not posing. Ember-orange firelight as the one hard key from below, faces carved out of total darkness, the five men's long shadows thrown outward across the floor like spokes, smoke rising into black. Background and foreground are a Renaissance tenebrist oil painting: umber-to-black timber posts and earth floor modelled in glazed oil, sfumato into black at the frame edges, a dark out-of-focus post in one foreground corner; the webtoon figures are painted into that oil space in watercolor washes under the same fire key. CANON — YEON TABAL — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_tabal.png (face only; invent a new pose). #a97c4a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | HORSE KA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_horse_chief.png (face only; invent a new pose). #2c2c30 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | COW KA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_cow_chief.png (face only; invent a new pose). #c45a2a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | PIG KA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_pig_chief.png (face only; invent a new pose). #6b4a32 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | DOG KA — FACE and garments from attached /ch_dog_chief.png (face only; invent a new pose). #c8d0d4 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER canvas, composed like a Romanticist master painting. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is painted with European old-master technique — Renaissance and Baroque oil (Titian, Rembrandt, Tiepolo, Turner): visible broken-colour brushwork, skies scumbled from short loaded dabs, layered glazes in the darks, sfumato edges, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlights — over watercolor wet-in-wet blooms, pigment granulation and faint paper grain; edges of the frame dissolve into paint. BACKGROUND AND FOREGROUND are a high-contrast Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST OIL PAINTING in their own right (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt, late Titian): a warm umber-to-black ground; walls, timber, stone, drapery, tables and the dark foreground shapes modelled in glazed oil and pulled out of the darkness by the one candle, lamp or window, with soft sfumato falloff into black — the webtoon figures are set INTO that old-master oil space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is Romanticism (Delacroix, Géricault, Friedrich, Goya, Turner): heroic diagonal or pyramid composition, small figures against a sublime storm sky or vast field, extreme foreshortening (worm’s-eye from the dirt or straight down from above), one break in the clouds or one shaft as the key. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, night-interior cinema): an extreme value range — inky blacks right beside small near-white highlights, almost no middle grey; 70–80% of the frame in deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo and black); ONE hard directional key (a lamp, a single cloud-break, a low sun shaft, firelight) carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.prompt: A parody of the Goguryeo MUYONGCHONG TOMB HUNTING MURAL (무용총 수렵도), painted exactly like the real 5th-century tomb wall: mineral pigments on cracked, stained plaster, flat outlined figures, ochre, red-brown, black and pale cream, water-damage blooms, no shading. Same composition: horsemen galloping across the wall between stylised stacked wavy ridge-bands of white, red and yellow, a tiger and spotted deer fleeing, one rider twisted fully BACKWARD in the saddle drawing his bow at full draw behind him (the Parthian shot). That rider is KING JUMONG (attached king portrait: face, beard, feathered cap), in a red jacket #e8563f with black dots, on a galloping horse with flying legs. Tiny tree strokes, a few falling flowers painted as dots. PARODY RULES: always a hand-made PAINTING, never photoreal. Reproduce the original work’s composition, poses and signature look so it reads instantly as that exact work, with our characters swapped in. If the original is a painting, mural, print or scroll, match its medium, surface and brushwork. If the original is a photograph, film poster, album cover, anime frame or statue, PAINT it: a painterly illustration of that image with visible brushstrokes, simplified forms and anime-adjacent faces, NOT a photo, NOT photoreal skin or pores, NOT a 3D render, NOT a CGI statue. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portraits, recognizable but restyled into the medium; never the portrait’s standing clasped-hands stance. Character hex lives only as real color inside the work (pigment, cloth, light), never a glow aura, halo, emissive skin or neon outline. If a sword is visible it is the ring-pommel 환두대도 (small ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, long straight blade, handle:blade 1:3), never a katana, never a tsuba. No readable text, no title, no credits, no legible inscriptions or signatures (red seal stamps only as blank red squares), no logos, no watermark.

images.alt: By the hearth Sosuno, blushing furiously, hauls Jumong up by the front of his robe while he grins up at her from the grain sacks
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 2:1 still composed like a symbolic old-master history painting — the LAID-BACK, CHARMING KING AND THE DOTING, HOT-BLOODED, CLINGY TSUNDERE QUEEN. INTIMATE CLOSE-UP, faces fill the frame: Sosuno (high topknot with gold binyeo, thin red jewelled headband, dusty-rose hanbok, red wrist wraps) leans down over Jumong gripping the front of his red silk robe in both fists, blushing to the ears, glaring, teeth clenched. Jumong (red headband, clean-shaven, no crown) lies back on grain sacks with a lazy, delighted grin, hands open and relaxed. ONE DEVICE: her two fists on his chest and the hand-width gap between the faces. Hearth fire below rakes up across both; background black with ember bokeh and, deep in blur, the empty carved chair. Not kissing. Faces drawn, matching the attached portraits. No text. CANON — JUMONG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_dongmyung.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean archer; black hair half-bound under a knotted red headband with long tails; dark warm eyes, easy grin. CLEAN-SHAVEN before he is king — ignore the moustache and chin hair on his portrait. Dress: Red silk jeogori and po over a charcoal underlayer, rope-tied sash, wrapped forearms; bow across his back. Demeanor: Fun: grins, laughs, winks, easy eyes when Sosuno is mean; scared and a little stupid when it matters. Carry: Bow always (his object board); crow bow-knife at the belt. #e8563f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: facial hair before he is king; grim founder-statue face; sword-duel hero pose. | SOSUNO — FACE and garments from attached /ch_sosuno.png (face only; invent a new pose). Hair ornament matches attached /bn_sosuno.png when the head is visible. Look: Long straight black hair with a high topknot pinned by her gold binyeo, a thin red headband with a center jewel; sharp brows, cool appraising eyes. Dress: Dusty-rose hanbok over white sleeves, black wrap sash with red cords, red-wrapped wrists; bow and quiver on her back. Her hex is lamplight or a ground stamp — never gold robes. Demeanor: Sharp, quick, too much, then covering; a merchant's appraising glance. #e8a04a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: gold robes; meek downcast pose. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.
