CANON — KIM YUSHIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_yushin.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Demeanor: Confucian: he STANDS — never sits in lotus. Weighs, counts, frowns at sums; tight jaw, rare dry half-smile. Grief shows as stillness, not tears. The most feared warrior in all of Samhan: a line goes quiet when the tall Silla helm and the white horse appear. Massive, deliberate, terrifying at a walk; by Hwangsan (65) heavier and slower than Gyebek but still the man armies are built around. #2A5FB8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: sitting in lotus or holding prayer beads; katana, tsuba or curved blade (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); two swords at once; blue glow aura. | BIDAM — FACE and garments from attached /ch_bidam_old.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, handsome, clean-shaven; short slicked-back black hair; warm brown eyes, faint self-amused smile. Dress: His signature hybrid coat: a long white outer robe whose wide sleeves are embroidered with galloping black horses, with deep navy #141C2E bands down the lapels and a navy yoke across the shoulders, over a plum-magenta inner robe and dark sash; the bead string looped on the right wrist. Navy lives only in those lapel and shoulder bands and on the beads — never a glow. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Now: Older Sangdaedeung (stage portrait): grey at the temples, same smile. Demeanor: Buddhist: 108 beads wrapped on the wrist or rolling through his fingers, lotus seat, incense, a sutra under his breath; calm, ironic, never hurried. In anger the smile stays and the eyes go flat. #141C2E as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: headband; Confucian rank tablet; navy glow aura; dual swords. | PLACE Surabol (서라벌 (경주)) — attached board /pl_eastern_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Seorabeol palace: Silla giwa halls, packed-earth yards, timber verandas. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). COMMONERS in every Samhan kingdom wear SIMPLE WHITE: plain undyed white or off-white hemp and ramie jackets, wide trousers and skirts, a cloth sash, straw sandals or bare feet, hair in a plain topknot or braid — no dyed silk, no dots, no gold; colour belongs to rank, so a crowd of farmers, porters, servants and townsfolk reads as a field of soft white cloth with the officials' colours standing out of it. Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: The Pavilion
blocks.ko: 정자

blocks.label: DAY 2
blocks.ko: 둘째 날

blocks.html: Of course he comes. Yushin has never once refused Bidam a rematch. Between the camps a small pavilion goes up, open on every side, so nobody can say the other side hid archers. A low table. Tea already poured. A half moon in an empty sky. They meet the way they used to after sparring: gloves off, courtesy on.
blocks.ko: 물론 그는 온다. 유신은 비담의 재대결 청을 한 번도 거절한 적이 없다. 두 진영 사이에 사방이 트인 작은 정자가 선다. 어느 쪽도 상대가 궁수를 숨겼다고 말하지 못하게. 낮은 탁자 하나. 차는 이미 따라져 있다. 빈 하늘에 반달. 그들은 예전 대련이 끝난 뒤처럼 만난다. 장갑은 벗고, 예의는 갖추고.

lines: …육촌이 서라벌을 세울 때 — 이, 최, 정, 손, 배, 설.
en: Yushin.
Tea first.
…When the Six Elders raised Surabol — Lee, Choi, Jung, Son, Bae, Sul.
Park came from an egg.
There was no Kim.
…And?

lines: 그리고 지금 이 성 안의 두 김 가문은 —
en: And now the two Kim houses inside this wall —
Surabol Kim, Alji Kim —
both imports.
I alone… am Six-Elder blood.

blocks.html: The tea cools between them. Neither man drinks enough to call it peace. Bidam smiles as if nothing ugly had been said — the same smile he wore when he crowned a woman king. Yushin sets his cup down unfinished.
blocks.ko: 차가 그 사이 식는다. 둘 다 평화라 부를 만큼은 마시지 않는다. 비담은 못된 말을 한 적 없는 것처럼 웃는다 — 여왕을 세울 때 쓰던 그 미소다. 유신은 잔을 비우지 않은 채 내려놓는다.

en: Alchun sends his regards. From the middle of the field.
He’s eating alone again.

lines: 그분은 늘 우리 둘 사이에서 먹었소.
en: He always did eat between us.

blocks.html: Three Hwarang. One princess. The yard remembers what the Council never wrote down.
blocks.ko: 화랑 셋. 공주 하나. 연무장은 화백이 끝내 적지 않은 것을 기억한다.

blocks.html: Bidam, Alchun, and Yushin — same Hwarang line, same bruised knuckles, same impossible orbit around Princess Dukman. They do not say the word love. The gyuku field says it for them, badly.
blocks.ko: 비담, 알천, 유신 — 같은 화랑 계보, 같은 멍든 손등, 덕만공주를 도는 같은 불가능한 궤도. 사랑이라는 말은 하지 않는다. 격구장이 대신 서툴게 말한다.

lines: 성골에 남자가 바닥나면, 가장 총명한 여자를 고르시오.
나는 어린 시절부터 덕만을 안다. 총명함에는 성별이 없다.
en: If the Sacred Bone runs out of men, pick the cleverest woman.
I have known Dukman since we were children. Cleverness is not a gender.
Well stood.
Tomorrow on the yard — the hundred-and-ninth is mine.

lines: 너거 둘은 점수 때문에 서로 쥑일 끼다.
나는 가운데 있는 아 때문에 내를 쥑일 끼고.
en: You two will kill each other over a score.
I shall kill myself over the girl in the middle.
…That was a joke. File it as a joke.
If you three are finished deciding my life—
the ball is still on the field.

blocks.html: Even their names take sides. Bidam’s sounds like this soil and its sutras. Chunchu’s is a foreign classic. Any clerk across the sea could file it without asking. Nobody notices yet. Names are patient.
blocks.ko: 이름들조차 편을 든다. 비담의 이름은 이 땅과 그 경전의 소리가 난다. 춘추의 이름은 남의 나라 고전이다. 바다 건너 어느 서기라도 묻지 않고 철해 둘 수 있다. 아직은 아무도 눈치채지 못한다. 이름은 참을성이 많다.

lines: 너희 중 누가 사소한 이유로 저 아이를 울리면 — 얼굴로 점수를 맞추겠다.
en: Yushin.
Alchun.
If either of you ever makes her cry for a small reason — I will even the score on your face.

blocks.label: DAY 3
blocks.ko: 셋째 날

blocks.html: Arrows trade across the open ground between the camps. Each morning the palace blue comes up the road, the black headbands come down to meet it, and by dusk both are home again. Messengers lie; the Harmony Council discovers it can convene without deciding anything, which is its highest form. Chunchu’s clerks call the unanimity rule quaint. Bidam calls it ours. Inside the palace, the stewards count eight days of grain.
blocks.ko: 두 진영 사이 빈 땅으로 화살이 오간다. 아침마다 궁의 푸른 띠가 길을 올라오고, 검은 머리띠가 내려와 맞서고, 해 질 녘이면 둘 다 제자리로 돌아간다. 전령은 거짓말하고, 화백회의는 아무것도 결정하지 않고도 모일 수 있음을 발견한다. 그것이 회의의 최고 형태다. 춘추의 서기들은 만장일치 규칙을 예스럽다고 부른다. 비담은 우리 것이라고 부른다. 궁 안에서 집사들은 여드레 치 곡식을 센다.

lines: 어이. 어제 그 도랑이다. 내일도 그 도랑일 끼고.
둘 중 하나라도 진심이면 그때 깨워라.
en: Oi. Same ditch as yesterday. Same ditch tomorrow.
Wake me when one of you means it.

blocks.html: Third night. Same pavilion. Same half moon. Bidam has brought a map — not of the siege, of the roads west.
blocks.ko: 셋째 밤. 같은 정자. 같은 반달. 비담은 포위도가 아니라 — 서쪽 길 지도를 가져왔다.

lines: 삼한은 피로도, 마음으로도 식민지가 되고 있어.
유신 — 네 눈 색은 예쁘다. 서쪽에서 온 색이다.
…내가 먼저 일어섰을 때는, 그들이 나를 개화파라 불렀지.
en: Samhan is being colonized — in blood, and in the mind.
The West sends institutions. India sends…
…through Queen Hu’s blood, sutras.
Yushin — your eyes are handsome. They are a western colour.
…When I stood first, they called me the liberal.

lines: 열다섯 해 전, 네가 그렇게 말했을 때 — 일어나라고 했소.
en: Gaya blood came from the west too.
I… stood up.
Fifteen winters past, when you spoke — you told me to stand.
That was when you were weak.
…A joke. Drink your tea.

blocks.html: On the wall Bidam looks west and remembers a cleaner war: Jade Gate Valley, when the enemy still had the courtesy to be foreign, and Alchun climbed a rock for him without being asked.
blocks.ko: 성벽 위에서 비담은 서쪽을 보며 더 깨끗했던 전쟁을 떠올린다. 옥문곡. 적이 아직 외국인이라는 예의를 지키던 때, 알천이 부탁받지 않고도 그를 위해 바위를 오르던 때.

blocks.html: Before the fourth night’s tea, the Moon Palace tries a quieter weapon. Chunchu sends his son Bupmin, twenty-one, to the steam — the water that shows a man’s inner conscience, the past that is driving his hand. Yushin is told only to keep him talking.
blocks.ko: 넷째 밤의 차 전에, 월성은 더 조용한 무기를 쓴다. 춘추가 스물한 살 아들 법민을 김으로 보낸다 — 사람의 속마음과, 그 손을 움직이는 과거를 보여주는 물. 유신에게는 말만 붙들어 두라고만 한다.

blocks.html: Chunchu is home from the islands. They kept him just long enough to be rude about it, then sent him back with compliments and no ships.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 섬에서 돌아왔다. 섬나라는 무례하다 싶을 만큼만 그를 붙잡아 두었다가, 칭찬만 들려 배 한 척 없이 돌려보냈다.

lines: 샘은 니 외숙이 아는 데다. 니가 김씨니까 문이 열릴 끼다.
en: Bupmin.
Take a jar.
The spring is a place your uncle knows. You’re a Kim — the door will open.
Splash him.
Father…
What does the water do to a man…
I understand. I’ll go.

blocks.label: The Steam Cavern
blocks.ko: 온천 동굴

blocks.html: This is the first time the cavern goddesses meet Bupmin. He is twenty-one. He does not yet have a king’s name. He has a jar and Chunchu’s weather.
blocks.ko: 동굴 여신들이 법민을 만나는 첫날이다. 스물하나. 아직 왕의 이름은 없다. 항아리와, 춘추의 날씨만 있다.

lines: 너… 너는 양쪽의 최선이야. 어깨는 가야. 입은 서라벌. 서 있으면 골화가 타고 오를 거야. 앉아.
en: A Kim.
Sit. No — the jar first.
You… He is the best of both. Gaya in the shoulders. Surabol in the mouth. Golhwa is going to climb you if you stay standing. Sit.

lines: 물 받아. 양심이 달라붙어. 트라우마. 원한. 그 손을 움직이는 거.
en: Oh.
A Kim we haven’t had. He’s both.
Take the water. Conscience sticks to it. Trauma. Grudge. Whatever’s driving the hand.
…And stop standing like that.

lines: 나 언덕이려 하는데, 너는 무릎 위에 두고 싶은 문제처럼 생겼어.
en: I’m trying to be a hill and you are shaped like a problem I want in my lap.
…Be careful.
If you splash it, you see why he’s doing it.
If you don’t see anything… that’s its own answer.
…He’s pretty. I’ll be quiet. I won’t be calm.
Goddesses…
Thank you. I was only—
I’ll just take the water.

blocks.html: He fills the jar. He does not stay for the lake’s other lessons. He is the best of both, and he leaves because his father told him to.
blocks.ko: 항아리를 채운다. 호수의 다른 수업은 받지 않는다. 그는 양쪽의 최선이고, 아버지가 시키니까 돌아간다.

blocks.label: Hunger
blocks.ko: 굶주림

blocks.label: DAY 4
blocks.ko: 넷째 날

blocks.html: Seven days of grain. The Moon Palace’s wells drop. Rumour rises to replace them. Chunchu files contingency letters the way other men file prayers.
blocks.ko: 이레 치 곡식. 월성의 우물이 준다. 소문이 그 자리를 채운다. 춘추는 다른 사람이 기도를 정리하듯 비상 서한을 정리한다.

blocks.html: Fourth night. Same low table under the half moon. Bidam reads a rumoured draft — never enough secretariat, never enough emperor. His voice stays pleasant. The sentences do not.
blocks.ko: 넷째 밤. 반달 아래 같은 낮은 상. 비담은 소문난 초안을 읽는다 — 집사부는 늘 부족하고, 황제는 늘 부족하다. 목소리는 여전히 부드럽다. 문장만 그렇지 않다.

lines: 화백의 만장일치 — 우리가 남긴 유일한 것 — 을 태울 셈이지.
en: What Chunchu wants…
is a country that fits inside the Western envelope.
Central rule. Emperor. Clerks.
He would burn the Harmony Council’s unanimity — the one thing we kept.
Baekje comes with swords, not sentences.

lines: …그 여인이 즉위하던 해엔 나도, 여주를 위해 일어선 개화파였는데.
지금은 삼한 피를 지키는 자라 부르는구나. 아이러니하지, 유신?
en: Yes — and that is why you always win.
On the yard, and here.
Effort… speaks louder than my blood.
…The year they crowned her, I was the liberal who stood for the woman king.
Now they call me the blood-and-soil man. Ironic, Yushin?
…That young Hwarang is still here.
Where?

blocks.html: He folds the rumoured draft. The next sentences have been waiting in the sleeve all night.
blocks.ko: 그는 소문난 초안을 접는다. 다음에 올 문장은 밤 내내 소매 안에 있었다.

lines: 승만공주와, 김춘추의 횡포 — 둘 다 반대다.
저 파가 이기면 삼한은 그 천 해를 서국의 번국으로 살게 된다.
제 앞날을 제 손으로 정하지 못하는 나라로.
en: Princess Sungman, and the tyranny of Kim Chunchu — I stand against both.
He speaks of a thousand-year kingdom.
If his faction wins, Samhan will spend those thousand years as a Western vassal.
A country that never again turns its own wheel.

lines: 승만공주 아래 이 개혁이 서면, 몇 해 안에 신라가 삼한에서 제일 강한 나라가 될 수 있소.
en: Under Sungman, with these reforms, Silla could be the strongest country in Samhan in a few harvests.

lines: 이웃이 서로의 이름을 아는 나라를 원하지.
한 담장을 나누는 남이 아니라 — 진짜 겨레.
en: I do not need the strongest nation.
I want neighbours who still know one another’s names.
The young lifting the old.
A true people — not strangers who happen to share a wall.

lines: 신라가 백제와 고려에 뒤처지면, 고개로 들어오는 것은 칼과 기근이오.
en: The people’s livelihood hangs on the nation’s fullness.
Fullness hangs on institutions — on a government that can still stand.
If Silla falls behind Baekje and Goryeo, what comes through the pass is spear and famine.
Then tell me how the neighbours keep their names.

lines: 왕실이 도성 밖에서 한 해라도 살아 봤느냐. 춘추가?
저 밖에선 아무도 남의 황제 멍에를 원하지 않는다.
en: Yushin.
Has the royal house spent one year outside the capital? Has Chunchu?
I have.
Out there, nobody wants a foreign emperor’s yoke.

lines: 바깥사람 이야기로 치자면, 비담 공, 바깥사람은 평생 공이 아니라 나일 것이오.
육촌의 피를 이은 공은 이 땅을 일군 집들을 그리 얕보는데,
정복당한 나라의 막내아들인 나는 이 땅을 위해 죽을 각오가 돼 있소.
en: As for outsiders, Lord Bidam, I will always be more outsider than you.
You, of Six-Elder blood, speak poorly of the halls that raised this land,
while I, last son of a conquered kingdom, would die for it.

blocks.html: Yushin does not close the argument. He asks again about the pass, about names, about harvests — anything that keeps Bidam’s back to the dark. Behind the pavilion, Bupmin’s jar ticks once against a post.
blocks.ko: 유신은 논쟁을 닫지 않는다. 고개, 이름, 수확 — 비담의 등이 어둠을 향하게 붙들어 두는 것이면 된다. 정자 뒤에서 법민의 항아리가 기둥에 한 번 닿는다.

lines: 백성이 황제를 원치 않는다. 그 말은 어디서 들었소?
en: Bidam.
Say it once more.
The people have no wish for an emperor. Where did you hear that?

blocks.html: Bupmin comes from behind to splash the water. It is ugly and precise — cavern water as a hard sheet across Bidam’s shoulders, beads and all.
blocks.ko: 법민이 뒤에서 와 물을 끼얹는다. 흉하고 정확하다 — 동굴 물이 비담의 어깨와 염주 위로 딱딱한 면처럼 떨어진다.

en: Ha…
What is this…

lines: 유신 공… 왜 아무 일도 없는데…?
en: Your trauma….
Yushin… why isn’t it doing anything…?

blocks.html: Nothing rises. No childhood. No princess. No grudge-film in the steam. The water runs off the black robe as if it had mistaken a man for a wound. Chunchu, at the pavilion’s edge, does not move. The stoic act holds; the eyes do not.
blocks.ko: 아무것도 안 뜬다. 어린 시절도, 공주도, 김 속의 한 필름도. 물은 흑의를 타고 내린다. 사람을 상처로 착각한 것처럼. 정자 가장자리의 춘추는 움직이지 않는다. 담담한 연기는 유지된다. 눈만 아니다.

lines: 들어 본 적 있어… 이 물이지…?
en: Oh… haha…
I’ve heard of this… this is that water, isn’t it…?
HAHAHAHAHA!

lines: 정녕 내가 무슨 개인적 트라우마가 있어야 한다고 생각했느냐??
한순간이라도… 단 일 초라도… 너희 생각이 그냥 형편없을 가능성…
제정신인 사내라면 누구나 반대할 가능성… 생각해 본 적 있느냐?
아니면 너희가 하는 일은 전부 옳고…
누구든 반대하는 이유는 정신의 병 뿐이라고…
하… 친구들, 오늘 밤 너희가 한 일이라곤 제 논리를 증명한 것뿐이다.
어느 나라도 이끌 자격이 없다는 걸 스스로 증명했어.
en: Behold, the arrogance of the sacred bone class!!
You really thought I had to have some sort of personal trauma??
That that was the reason I was doing all of this?
That I hated the princess? The queen?
That I hated you, Chunchu, or Yushin?
Have you ever… even for a SECOND… considered the POSSIBILITY…
that your ideas are simply terrible?
That they’ll lead this nation to ruin?
That ANY reasonable man would oppose them?
Or are you so ARROGANT to assume… that EVERYTHING you lot do is correct…
and that the ONLY reason for ANYONE to disagree… is because they were suffering some sort of mental disease? Because they were angry and bitter?
Ha… well, my friends, I’m afraid all you’ve done tonight is prove your point.
You’ve proven yourself to be unworthy of leading any country.
So please… my friends… step aside…!

blocks.html: Alchun, arriving late with a lamp, goes pale. An officer asks whether to seize the jar. Nobody answers. Bidam is still laughing, and still alive, and the beads are still counting.
blocks.ko: 늦게 등을 들고 온 알천의 얼굴이 하얘진다. 장교 하나가 항아리를 빼앗을지 묻는다. 대답하는 사람이 없다. 비담은 아직 웃고, 아직 살아 있고, 염주는 아직 세고 있다.

blocks.label: Chunchu’s Rooms
blocks.ko: 춘추의 방

lines: 비담이 이기면 집사부는 고상한 취미가 된다.
비담이 져도, 우리에게는 죽어 가는 여왕과 서쪽의 서국 모양 구멍이 남는다.
그 사람은 좋은 생각도 서국 봉투에 담겨 오믄 태울 사람이다. 강령의 전부가 그기고 — 인기는 좋데이.
en: If Bidam wins, the Secretariat becomes a quaint hobby.
If Bidam loses, we still have a dying queen and a West-shaped hole in the west.
The man would burn a good idea for arriving in the Western envelope. That is the whole platform — and it polls rather well.
Munhee — pack for either weather.

lines: 여왕께서 즉위하시던 해에 쌌어예. 당신은 포위 때만 눈치채시지예.
en: I’ve already packed.
I packed the year the Queen was crowned. You only notice in sieges.

blocks.html: Alchun eats alone between the camps. Both sides send him wine. He drinks neither. Surabol will later call it treason with better stationery.
blocks.ko: 알천은 진영 사이에서 혼자 먹는다. 양쪽이 술을 보낸다. 그는 어느 쪽도 마시지 않는다. 서라벌은 나중에 더 좋은 편지지의 반역이라 부를 것이다.

blocks.label: DAY 5
blocks.ko: 다섯째 날

blocks.html: Fifth night — the pavilion again. They sit on the floor, alone, the way they used to meet on the training ground. The tea is cold before anyone raises a blade. Six days of grain.
blocks.ko: 다섯째 밤 — 다시 그 정자. 두 사람은 바닥에서 단둘이 앉는다. 옛날 연무장에서 만나던 것과 같은 방식으로. 차가 식고 나서야 누군가 칼을 든다. 엿새 치 곡식.

lines: 삼한의 둘째 칼 — 비담이여!! 무기를 내려놓고 푸른 달께 충성을 돌려드려라!!
en: Second Blade of Samhan — Bidam!! Lay down your arms and give your loyalty back to the Blue Moon!!

blocks.html: For a breath they are only the old score again — one hundred and eight to one hundred and eight — two boys who never let the other keep a lead. Then Bidam speaks, and the yard is gone.
blocks.ko: 한순간 둘은 다시 옛 점수판일 뿐이다 — 백팔 대 백팔 — 상대를 앞서 두지 않던 소년 둘. 그러다 비담이 입을 열고, 연무장은 사라진다.

blocks.html: The yard after rain. Two Hwarang, neither willing to leave the mud with the score uneven.
blocks.ko: 비 온 뒤 연무장. 화랑 둘. 점수가 기우는 채로 진흙을 떠나려 하지 않는다.

en: One hundred and eight…!
Today I take the lead, Gaya!

lines: 일어나시오, 형님. 기우는 숫자는 밤에 못 자오.
en: One hundred and eight.
Get up, hyung. An uneven number does not sleep.

lines: 가야 피가 신라 피한테 졌다고 적히면 창피해서 그러시오?
en: Ha!
Afraid it will be written that Gaya blood lost to Silla blood?
Written or not.
Again.

lines: ……그라고 이길 때는 형님 소리 하지 마라.
en: …And don’t call me hyung when you’re winning.

blocks.html: They end the evening even. They always do.
blocks.ko: 그날 저녁도 비긴다. 언제나 그랬다.

lines: 이 나라에서 제일 똑똑한 자들은 이 나라를 미워하고,
en: Yushin.
In this country the smartest people hate this country,
and the most patriotic people… are all stupid.
That’s Silla.
The country you’re trying to sell.
Yushin….
And besides — you…
you were never even of Silla…!
Blood is inevitable.

blocks.html: The tea has not been touched. He says it like a compliment that curdled — still the gentleman, still the black robe, still the voice that once shielded this same man from the yard.
blocks.ko: 차는 손대지 않았다. 상처 주는 칭찬처럼 말한다 — 여전히 군자, 여전히 흑의, 여전히 연무장에서 이 같은 사람을 막아 세던 그 목소리.

lines: 비담 공... 우리는 함께 인생에 맹세로 한 걸로 기억하는데...
en: Lord Bidam… I remember we swore our lives to this together…

lines: 너한테는 원래 나라가 없으니, 이 나라를 팔아먹는 것도 거슬리지 않겠지...
하지만 우리는 다르다. 우리는 이 땅에서 뗄 수 없는 관계야…
내 조상이 세운 나라를 황제한테 넘겨줄 셈이냐...!
en: You never had a country of your own — selling this one must cost you nothing…
But we are different. We cannot be cut from this land…
Would you hand the country my ancestors built to an emperor…!
I am a son of the sacred country.

lines: 춘추 공은 서국의 제도를 배우자는 것뿐이오. 백제는 문장이 아니라 칼로 오니까.
en: Selling — I have sold nothing.
Lord Chunchu only asks that we learn the West’s institutions. Baekje comes with swords, not sentences.

lines: 춘추 — 春秋. 이름부터가 서국 책이다.
그런 자에게 신국의 내일을 쓰게 하겠단 말이냐.
남의 제도를 오래 배우다 보면 — 어느 아침엔, 배운 것만 남아 있을 것이다.
en: Chunchu — 春秋. The man is named after a Western book.
And you would let him write the sacred country’s tomorrow.
Learn another country’s institutions long enough — and one morning, the learning is all that is left.
I will raise the sacred country’s glory again,
I will return the sacred country’s future to its own people!

blocks.html: Yushin does not answer the speech. He looks at the cold tea as if the answer were at the bottom of the cup.
blocks.ko: 유신은 그 연설에 대답하지 않는다. 답이 잔 바닥에 있기라도 한 듯 식은 차를 내려다본다.

lines: 염종 말로는 네 증조부가 금관을 수레에 싣고 서라벌에 왔다더군.
할아버지 이야기는 아무도 안 해. 그분은 뭘 넘겼나, 유신?
en: Yumjong says your great-grandfather drove Golden Gaya to Surabol in a cart.
Fine. Everyone knows the cart.
Nobody talks about the grandfather. What did he hand over, Yushin?

lines: 죽은 사람은 제 방에 두시오, 비담.
en: Leave the dead in their rooms, Bidam.

lines: 닷새 밤을 내 차를 마시면서, 네 것은 하나도 말하지 않았다.
en: No.
Five nights you’ve drunk my tea and told me nothing that was yours.
Give me one thing. Then call me a traitor.

blocks.html: For a long time the only sound is the wind through the open pavilion. Yushin has not said this aloud in Surabol since he was fifteen.
blocks.ko: 한참 동안, 트인 정자를 지나는 바람 소리뿐이다. 유신은 열다섯 이후로 서라벌에서 이 이야기를 입 밖에 낸 적이 없다.

lines: ……백제에는 관산성 길의 어느 밤을 부르는 이름이 있소.
서쪽 고개 너머 아무 군사에게나 물어보시오. 단이라 부르지.
en: …Baekje has a name for one night on the Gwansan road.
Ask any soldier over the western hills. They call it the Severing.

lines: 그쪽 임금이 목을 잃은 밤. 다 아는 얘기다. 칼은 노비가 들었지.
en: The night their king lost his head. Everyone knows it. A slave held the knife.

lines: 가야 고깔 투구를 쓴 사내가 그쪽 임금을 호상에 앉히고, 앉으라 했소.
en: A slave held the knife.
A man in a Gaya cone helm sat their king on a camp stool and told him to sit.
…That was my grandfather.

blocks.html: Bidam’s beads stop for the second time this winter.
blocks.ko: 비담의 염주가 올겨울 들어 두 번째로 멈춘다.

lines: ……가야 왕자가 삼한에서 가장 오래된 화친을 끊었다.
en: …A Gaya prince broke the oldest peace in Samhan.
For us.

lines: 그리고 그 손자가 공의 상에 앉아, 애초에 신라 사람이 아니었다는 말을 듣고 있소.
en: For Silla.

blocks.html: A cone helm, a king on a camp stool, and a name Yushin won’t say. Who was his grandfather…?

When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. blocks.html: King Guhae promised his youngest son a kingdom. It seemed a safe promise. He had one.
blocks.ko: 구해왕은 막내아들에게 나라를 약속했다. 안전한 약속 같았다. 나라가 있었으니까.

blocks.label: Prince of Golden Gaya
blocks.ko: 금관가야의 왕자

blocks.label: The Golden Gaya palace
blocks.ko: 금관, 금관가야 왕궁

blocks.html: Six eggs, one harbour, and the best iron in Samhan. Everybody wants the iron.
blocks.ko: 알 여섯, 포구 하나, 그리고 삼한에서 제일 좋은 쇠. 다들 쇠를 원한다.

blocks.html: Before dawn the king gets his three sons out of bed and walks them down the long hall in their sleeping clothes. The youngest he carries. The walls are painted from floor to rafters. In the dark they are only shapes. The king has timed this. He opens the east doors, and the sun does the rest.
blocks.ko: 동트기 전, 임금은 세 아들을 깨워 잠옷 바람으로 긴 전각을 걸어 내려간다. 막내는 안고 간다. 벽은 바닥부터 서까래까지 그림이다. 어둠 속에서는 형체뿐이다. 임금은 시간을 맞춰 두었다. 동쪽 문을 열면, 나머지는 해가 한다.

blocks.caption: King of Golden Gaya. A generous man with a small country.
blocks.ko: 금관가야의 임금. 작은 나라를 가진 후한 사내.

en: Father, it’s the middle of the night.

lines: 와 무력이만 안아 주는데예? 내도 안아 주이소.
en: Why does Muryuk get carried? I want carrying.

lines: 가가 젤 작으니까 그렇다, 무덕아. 덜 커라.
en: Because he’s the smallest, Muduk-a. Grow less.
Hush, both of you. Watch the wall.
Muryuk-a. Up you get. Look.
No, up. Higher. There.
…There’s a man in the clouds, there is.
Upside down, why is he?

lines: 산 우에 아씨를 한분 보시고는 집에 가는 거를 까묵으셨다 아이가.
en: Coming down, he is. That’s Ibiga. The sky.
Saw a lady on a mountain once and forgot to go home, didn’t he.
Why?
You’ll understand when you’re older.
Or never, if you’re lucky. Next one.

blocks.html: The light crawls along the wall. Nine chiefs on a hilltop, singing. A purple rope coming down out of a cloud, and on the end of it a gold box.
blocks.ko: 빛이 벽을 따라 기어간다. 산꼭대기에서 노래하는 추장 아홉. 구름에서 내려오는 보랏빛 줄, 그 끝에 매달린 금빛 상자.

lines: 혼자서 바닷가꺼정 걸어 내려가가, 붉은 돛 단 배를 기다렸어예.
en: Six eggs! And the first one’s Suro.
Walked down to the beach all by himself, he did, and waited for a ship with red sails.
This one you know.
Every New Year. Tell it anyway, go on.

lines: 허왕후. 얼마나 먼 데서 오셨는지, 여서는 아무도 그 나라 이름을 제대로 말을 몬 했다.
당신 성을 지키셨지. 아들 둘이 그 성을 받았고, 수로왕은 그러라 하셨다.
그리고 그 아들들. 또 그 아들들. 이 벽을 따라 쭉—
en: Fine. The ship.
Queen Hu. So far off she came that nobody here could say the name of her country.
She kept her own name. Two of her sons took it, and Suro let them.
Then their sons. And theirs. All the way down this wall—
—to you.
To me. And then?
…Then me, is it?

blocks.html: The sun reaches the end of the wall, where the plaster is still bare. The king sets the boy down on the threshold and turns him to face the harbour. Ships. Smoke from the iron sheds. The hills behind.
blocks.ko: 해가 벽 끝에 닿는다. 거기는 아직 회벽이 비어 있다. 임금은 아이를 문턱에 내려놓고 포구 쪽으로 돌려세운다. 배들. 쇠 굽는 막의 연기. 그 뒤의 언덕들.

lines: 포구도, 쇠도, 언덕도. 언젠가 저걸 다 니가 돌보게 될 끼다.
en: Everything the sun touches from here.
The harbour, the iron, the hills. Yours to look after one day, all of it.
All of it?
What about Noribu-hyung and Muduk-hyung, then?

lines: 내한테도 작년에 똑같이 말씀하셨다. 같은 문에서.
en: He told me the same thing last year. Same door.
Me too. Same sun, even.

lines: 너거 둘은 가서 자라. 무력이 니는 말고. 니는 있어라.
en: …Then it’s a very big harbour, isn’t it.
Back to bed, you two. Not you, Muryuk. You stay.

blocks.html: He has made the same promise to all three sons. Gaya is a small country, and its kings are generous with it.
blocks.ko: 그는 세 아들 모두에게 같은 약속을 했다. 가야는 작은 나라고, 그 임금들은 나라 인심이 후하다.

blocks.html: Then he lifts his own helm off its stand, the tall Gaya cone with the iron plates, and sets it on the boy’s head. It comes down over his eyes.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 받침대에서 제 투구를 내린다. 쇠 비늘을 단 높은 가야 고깔. 아이 머리에 씌우자 눈까지 푹 내려온다.

en: I can’t see anything.

lines: 그라고 못 보는 임금은 들어야 안 되나. 나쁜 버릇은 아이다.
en: You’ll grow into it.
And a king who can’t see has to listen. Not the worst habit, that.

blocks.html: His name was Muryuk.
blocks.ko: 그의 이름은 무력이었다.

blocks.caption: The youngest prince. He believed every word on that wall.
blocks.ko: 막내 왕자. 그 벽의 말을 한 마디도 빼지 않고 믿었다.

blocks.label: Golden Gaya · eight years later
blocks.ko: 금관 · 여덟 해 뒤

blocks.html: He grows into the helm. He learns the six eggs in order, the price of iron at the harbour, and which Silla lord takes his bribes in bolts of silk. Mostly he learns the sword, because somebody has to look after all of it. Noribu prefers the ledgers. Muduk prefers whatever Noribu prefers.
blocks.ko: 그는 투구에 맞게 자란다. 여섯 알을 순서대로 외우고, 포구의 쇠 값을 익히고, 어느 신라 귀족이 비단 필로 뇌물을 받는지 배운다. 무엇보다 칼을 배운다. 누군가는 이걸 다 지켜야 하니까. 노리부는 장부를 좋아한다. 무덕은 노리부가 좋아하는 걸 좋아한다.

blocks.html: Every dawn the old arms-master knocks him down in the yard. Every dawn he is up again before the man has finished turning away.
blocks.ko: 새벽마다 늙은 무술 사범이 마당에서 그를 쓰러뜨린다. 새벽마다 그는 사범이 등을 다 돌리기도 전에 다시 일어나 있다.

blocks.speaker: The arms-master
en: Again, is it? Highness, the sun isn’t even up.
Your brothers are still asleep.

lines: 그라믄 주무시라 카게. 내가 깨어 있으믄 되지.
en: Then let them sleep. I’ll be up, won’t I.
Again.

blocks.html: On the gate tower the king watches with his hands behind his back and does not come down. Kings are not supposed to have favourites. He has one.
blocks.ko: 성문 누각에서 임금이 뒷짐을 지고 지켜본다. 내려오지는 않는다. 임금은 편애하면 안 된다. 그에게는 하나 있다.

blocks.html: For five hundred years the people of Gaya lived by iron and by six eggs, and they enjoyed great peace. Then Silla came shopping.
blocks.ko: 오백 년 동안 가야 사람들은 쇠와 여섯 알로 살며 태평을 누렸다. 그러다 신라가 장을 보러 왔다.

blocks.caption: Baekje to the west. Silla to the north. A harbour of iron in between.
blocks.ko: 서쪽엔 백제. 북쪽엔 신라. 그 사이에 쇠의 포구.

blocks.label: The Battle of Golden Gaya
blocks.ko: 금관가야 전투

blocks.html: The river is full of men, and none of them are swimming. Smoke stands up off the iron sheds in black columns. The harbour bell has been ringing since dawn, and nobody has had a spare moment to tell the ringer to stop.
blocks.ko: 강에 사람이 가득한데, 헤엄치는 사람은 하나도 없다. 쇠 굽는 막에서 검은 연기 기둥이 선다. 포구의 종은 새벽부터 울리고 있고, 종지기에게 그만 치라고 일러 줄 짬이 난 사람은 아무도 없다.

blocks.speaker: A Gaya shieldman
lines: 둑 넘어왔다! 서쪽 둑 다 넘어왔다, 저놈들—
en: Bank’s gone! West bank’s gone, they’re over the—
Where’s the cone, then? Where’s the prince?

blocks.speaker: A Silla officer
lines: 방패 올리라! 저놈들 쇠가 좋다, 그대로 뚫고 들어온다—
en: Shields UP! They’ve got the good iron, the bastards, it goes straight through—
The ford! Take the ford and it’s finished—

blocks.speaker: A Gaya archer
lines: 화살! 화살 있는 사람— 니 거 내놔라, 퍼뜩 이리 내놔라—
en: Arrows! Who’s got arrows— give us yours, bach, give it HERE—

blocks.html: Silla came down the river at first light, with more spears than Golden Gaya has people. The king did the arithmetic first. His youngest son refused to.
blocks.ko: 신라는 새벽에 금관의 백성보다 많은 창을 이끌고 강을 따라 내려왔다. 임금이 먼저 셈을 했다. 막내아들은 셈하기를 거부했다.

blocks.html: By noon the Gaya line has broken on the riverbank. The tall Gaya cone still fights. Muryuk holds the ford with his father’s guard at his back, and the Silla men who come up the bank do not come up it twice.
blocks.ko: 한낮이 되자 가야의 줄이 강둑에서 무너진다. 높은 가야 고깔은 아직 싸운다. 무력은 아버지의 호위들을 등에 두고 여울을 지키고, 둑을 오른 신라 군사들은 두 번 오르지 못한다.

blocks.speaker: A Silla spearman
lines: 고깔— 고깔한테 붙지 마라! 돌아가, 돌아서 가라 안 카나—
몇 명째고— 저거 겸이 아이가, 방금 겸이—
en: The cone— stay off the cone! Go round him, go ROUND—
How many’s that— that was Gyum, he’s just done Gyum—

blocks.html: He stops counting somewhere past thirty. Then, up the slope behind him, his father’s standard goes down.
blocks.ko: 서른을 넘긴 어디쯤에서 그는 세기를 그만둔다. 그때 등 뒤 비탈 위에서 아버지의 깃발이 쓰러진다.

lines: 여울 지키라. 지키라 카이. 내 올라간데이.
en: Father—
Hold the ford. HOLD it, I said. Up I go.

blocks.html: Silla men lead the king of Golden Gaya up the hill, to a stand of pines under a canopy. Muryuk cuts his way up after him. At the trees he is red to the elbow, and alone.
blocks.ko: 신라 군사들이 금관의 임금을 언덕 위 소나무 숲, 차일 아래로 끌고 간다. 무력은 칼로 길을 내며 뒤쫓는다. 숲에 닿았을 때 그는 팔꿈치까지 피투성이고, 혼자다.

blocks.label: The pines above the ford
blocks.ko: 여울 위 소나무 숲

blocks.html: He comes in behind a pine, close enough to hear, and stops. His father is not in chains. His father is on his knees, and talking.
blocks.ko: 그는 소나무 뒤로 들어간다. 들릴 만큼 가깝다. 그리고 멈춘다. 아버지는 묶여 있지 않다. 아버지는 무릎을 꿇고, 말을 하고 있다.

blocks.html: Under the canopy sits the king of Silla. He has bought harbours before.
blocks.ko: 차일 아래에 신라 임금이 앉아 있다. 그는 포구를 사 본 적이 있다.

blocks.caption: King of Silla. He could take Gaya. He would rather buy it.
blocks.ko: 신라의 임금. 가야를 빼앗을 수도 있었다. 사는 쪽을 더 좋아한다.

lines: 제 아들들이 신라에서 부끄럽지 않게 살게 해 주십시오…
en: If we are to surrender, I have one condition…
Let my sons live in Silla without shame…
And what do you mean by that?

lines: 신라에서는... 사람의 성분이 모든 걸 좌지우지한다고 알고 있습니다...
성골, 진골... 이미 다 알고 있습니다...
제 막내가 지금 저 아래 여울에 있습니다. 아침부터 폐하의 군사를 베고 있지요.
en: In Silla… I know a man’s blood decides everything…
Sacred Bone, True Bone… I know it all…
My youngest is down at the ford. He has been killing your men since morning.
I promised that boy a kingdom, Majesty.
Then you should have kept one.

lines: ……이제 그 아이에게 나라를 줄 수는 없습니다. 그래서 남은 것을 청하는 겁니다.
en: Yes.
…I can’t give him a kingdom now. So I am asking you for what is left.
Which is?

lines: 포로로 만들지 마십시오. 그 머리를 폐하의 성문에 걸지 마십시오.
아무것도 없는 왕자로, 폐하의 잔치에서 뼈다귀나 바라며 절하게 하지도 마십시오.
그 아이에게 진골을 주십시오. 폐하의 도성에서 고개를 들고 걷게 해 주십시오.
en: Don’t make him a prisoner. Don’t put his head on your gate.
And don’t make him a prince of nothing, bowing at your banquets for the bones.
Give him True Bone. Let him walk in your city with his head up.

lines: 제 자손... 수로왕과 허왕후의 아들과 딸들이 좋은 자리에 자리잡을 수만 있다면...
저 또한 가진 모든 것을 신라에 바칠 준비가 되어 있습니다...
en: If my descendants — the sons and daughters of Suro and Hu — can take a worthy place…
then I too am ready to give Silla everything I have…

lines: 아들 하나 앉을 자리에 나라를 내놓겠다는 건가.
en: You would trade a kingdom for one boy’s seat at dinner.
I would trade it for less.
Please don’t tell him that.

blocks.html: Behind the pine, the boy who held the ford all morning cannot make a sound.
blocks.ko: 소나무 뒤, 아침 내내 여울을 지킨 소년은 아무 소리도 내지 못한다.

lines: 알겠다. 너희 후손들은 신라의 진골로 추대해주마.
en: Very well. Your descendants shall be raised as True Bones of Silla.

lines: 전쟁 끝에 임금이 한 말은 사람들이 잊습니다. 적어 둔 것은 기억하지요.
en: Write it down, Majesty. Please.
Men forget what a king says at the end of a war. They remember what he writes.

lines: 신라의 어느 집도 핏줄을 이유로 수로의 후손에게 문을 닫지 못한다. 됐는가?
en: …An edict, then.
No house in Silla shall shut its door on the line of Suro for its blood. Will that do?

lines: 오늘부터 자네 집안은 김가다. 과인의 성을 쓰게.
en: …I nearly forgot one thing.
From this day your house is Kim. You will carry my own surname.

lines: 그렇다면 제 아들들은 임금과 같은 성을 쓰고 다니게 되는 것입니까.
en: Kim…
Then my sons will walk under the same name as the king.
Your grace is boundless… Your Majesty…!

blocks.html: He stands behind the pine with his sword in his hand and the helm strap wet under his chin. He makes no sound at all. A king who can’t see has to listen. He has listened.
blocks.ko: 그는 칼을 쥔 채 소나무 뒤에 서 있다. 턱 밑 투구 끈이 젖어 있다. 아무 소리도 내지 않는다. 못 보는 임금은 들어야 한다. 그는 들었다.

blocks.html: Then he wipes the blade on the grass, goes round the long way, and walks into the clearing from the other side, as if he had only just arrived.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 풀에 칼날을 닦고, 먼 길로 돌아, 방금 막 도착한 사람처럼 반대편에서 빈터로 걸어 들어간다.

en: …Muryuk.
Father.
…I’ve come to surrender.

blocks.html: He lays his sword on the ground before the king of Silla and kneels beside his father. He never tells his father what he heard behind the pine. His father never asks.
blocks.ko: 그는 신라 임금 앞 땅바닥에 칼을 내려놓고 아버지 곁에 무릎을 꿇는다. 소나무 뒤에서 무엇을 들었는지 그는 끝내 아버지에게 말하지 않는다. 아버지도 끝내 묻지 않는다.

blocks.html: They will call it the Royal Edict. It will be read aloud in the Surabol market, and a good many True Bone houses will spend the next sixty years complaining about it at dinner.
blocks.ko: 사람들은 그것을 어명이라 부를 것이다. 서라벌 저잣거리에서 소리 내어 읽힐 것이고, 꽤 많은 진골 집안이 그 뒤 육십 년 동안 저녁상에서 그걸 두고 투덜댈 것이다.

blocks.label: The road to Surabol
blocks.ko: 서라벌 가는 길

blocks.html: He is the youngest of three sons in the cart, and the only one who looks back.
blocks.ko: 수레에 탄 세 아들 중 막내이고, 뒤를 돌아보는 건 그 하나뿐이다.

blocks.html: The cart is slow. The road to Surabol is long enough for a boy to change his mind several times.
blocks.ko: 수레는 느리다. 서라벌 가는 길은 아이가 마음을 여러 번 바꿀 만큼 길다.

en: Face front, Muryuk.
Your brothers are facing front, aren’t they.
Somebody should remember what it looked like, shouldn’t they.
…The harbour. Before.

lines: 그라믄 조용히 기억해라. 임금들은 지가 산 거 들추는 걸 싫어한데이.
en: Then remember it quietly. Don’t like being reminded what they bought, kings don’t.

blocks.html: He keeps looking back until the river bends out of sight.
blocks.ko: 그는 강이 굽어 보이지 않을 때까지 뒤를 돌아본다.

blocks.label: Surabol, the Moon Palace
blocks.ko: 서라벌, 월성

blocks.html: In Surabol the treasury is counted, the crown is set on a cushion, and the three princes are lined up before the dais.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에서 곳간이 셈해지고, 왕관은 방석 위에 놓이고, 세 왕자는 단 앞에 나란히 선다.

blocks.html: The king on the dais has bought harbours before. He has never bought one that talks back.
blocks.ko: 단 위의 임금은 포구를 사 본 적이 있다. 말대꾸하는 포구를 사 본 적은 없다.

en: So. You’re the ford.
How many of mine?

lines: ……그다음부터는 세지 못했습니다. 원하시면 폐하를 위해 다시 세겠습니다.
en: Thirty-one, Majesty.
…I lost count after that. I can start again for you, if you like.

blocks.html: The court goes very quiet. The king laughs, once, like a man who has just been undercharged.
blocks.ko: 조정이 쥐 죽은 듯 조용해진다. 임금이 한 번 웃는다. 값을 덜 치른 사람처럼.

lines: 자네 아비는 자네에게 품계를 샀네. 나는 장수를 사겠네.
en: Your father bought you a rank. I am buying a general.
Bought things stay bought.

lines: 대신 자네는 나를 위해 말을 타야 하네. 북으로, 서로. 국경이 가려운 곳이면 어디든.
en: In return you ride for me. North, west. Wherever the border itches.
…Even south.
…Even south.
Swear it on something.
On my sons, Majesty.
You have sons?
…Not yet.

blocks.html: Three generations later, his grandson will still be told he is not really one of them.
blocks.ko: 세 대가 지난 뒤에도, 그의 손자는 여전히 «진짜 우리 편은 아니다»라는 말을 듣게 된다.

blocks.label: Surabol, the Gaya house · the first winter
blocks.ko: 서라벌, 가야 집 · 첫 겨울

blocks.html: The house Silla gives them is a good one, two lanes below the Moon Palace. The roof doesn’t leak. The wall is a hand lower than the neighbours’. The neighbours have checked.
blocks.ko: 신라가 내준 집은 좋은 집이다. 월성에서 두 골목 아래. 지붕은 새지 않는다. 담은 이웃집보다 한 뼘 낮다. 이웃들이 재 봤다.

blocks.html: Noribu learns the Silla bow in a week and practises it on the servants. Muduk learns the accent. Muryuk learns nothing, on purpose.
blocks.ko: 노리부는 일주일 만에 신라식 절을 익혀 하인들한테 연습한다. 무덕은 말씨를 익힌다. 무력은 아무것도 안 익힌다. 일부러.

lines: 그래 말고. 여 사람들은 노래하듯 안 한다. 심드렁하게, 납작하게.
en: Not like that. They don’t sing it here. Flat, like you’re bored.
“Yes, my lord.” Go on.

lines: …됐나. 인자 사 온 물건 소리 난다.
en: Yes, my lord.
…There. Now I sound like something they bought.

lines: 사 온 물건 맞다. 아부지가 값은 잘 받으셨다.
더 숙이고, 그 낯 좀 치아라.
en: We are something they bought. Father got a good price.
Bow lower, and stop making that face.

lines: 더 숙이면 바닥에 박힙니더, 형님. 거 박혀 있으라 카는 깁니꺼?
en: Any lower and I’ll be in the floor, hyung. Is that where they want us?

blocks.html: That winter he decides Gaya lost because Gaya deserved to. A harbour that sells itself is a shop, and the prince of a shop is a clerk. He keeps the helm on in the street. Better they look at that than at his face.
blocks.ko: 그 겨울 그는 결론을 내린다. 가야는 질 만해서 졌다고. 제 몸을 파는 포구는 가게고, 가게의 왕자는 점원이다. 그는 길에서도 투구를 벗지 않는다. 얼굴보다는 그걸 보는 게 낫다.

blocks.label: The Gaya house gate · that spring
blocks.ko: 가야 집 대문 · 그해 봄

blocks.html: By spring the Gaya people in the city have found the house. A few came in the treasury carts. Most walked. They come to the gate in twos and threes with dried fish and bad news, and they kneel in the lane.
blocks.ko: 봄이 되자 도성의 가야 사람들이 이 집을 찾아낸다. 몇은 보물 수레를 따라왔고, 대부분은 걸어왔다. 둘씩 셋씩 마른 생선과 나쁜 소식을 들고 대문에 와서, 골목에 무릎을 꿇는다.

blocks.speaker: A Gaya smith
lines: 마마. 저희라예, 마마. 포구 대장간 사람들.
인자 신라 쇠를 두드리고 있심더. 품삯이 개판이라예. 마마께서 한 말씀만 하시면—
en: Majesty. It’s us, Majesty, from the harbour sheds.
They’ve got us forging for Silla now, and the pay’s rotten. You only have to say the word—

lines: 이 집엔 마마 없다. 임금은 저 언덕 위에 계신다. 인자 그분한테 절해라.
en: Get up, all of you. The lane’s wet.
There’s no Majesty in this house. The king lives up the hill. You bow to him now.

blocks.speaker: A Gaya smith
en: He doesn’t know our names.

lines: 그라믄 가서 알려 드려라. 되거든 이 동네 말씨로.
이 도성에서는 그래야 이름이 생긴다. 내도 지금 배우는 중이다.
en: Then go and tell him. In his accent, if you can manage it.
That’s how a man gets a name in this city. I’m learning it myself.

blocks.html: The smith bows anyway. To Kim Guhae.
blocks.ko: 대장장이는 그래도 절한다. 김구해에게.

blocks.html: Not everyone from Gaya kneels. A handful from the river villages never forgave the canopy under the pines, and they have found the house too.
blocks.ko: 가야 사람이 다 무릎을 꿇는 건 아니다. 강마을 몇몇은 소나무 아래 차일을 끝내 용서하지 않았고, 그들도 이 집을 찾아냈다.

blocks.speaker: A man in the lane
lines: 수로왕 뼈다구는 얼마에 넘겼노? 수레로 달아서 팔았나?
en: Oi! Iron-seller! What did you get for the harbour?
What did Suro’s bones go for, eh? By the cartload?

blocks.speaker: Another voice
en: Go on, bow! You’re good at it! Traitor king!

blocks.html: Kim Guhae walks past them every morning on his way up the hill and never turns his head. Muryuk turns his every time. He doesn’t shout back. The trouble is, he agrees with the men shouting and with the men kneeling, and he can’t work out which is worse.
blocks.ko: 김구해는 아침마다 언덕을 오르며 그들 곁을 지나고, 한 번도 고개를 돌리지 않는다. 무력은 매번 돌린다. 맞받아 소리치지는 않는다. 문제는 그가 소리치는 쪽에도, 무릎 꿇는 쪽에도 다 수긍한다는 것이다. 어느 쪽이 더 나쁜지 모르겠다.

en: Why don’t you answer them?

lines: 틀린 말은 아이다, 무력아. 시끄러울 뿐이지.
너무 크게 옳은 사람하고는 싸우는 기 아이다. 지치게 놔둬라.
en: They’re not wrong, Muryuk. Only loud.
You don’t fight a man for being right too loudly. You let him get tired.

blocks.label: The Harmony Council · some years on
blocks.ko: 화백회의 · 몇 해 뒤

blocks.html: Silla is run by a council of great lords who all have to say yes before anything happens. They call it the Harmony Council, because nobody has ever come out of one in a good mood.
blocks.ko: 신라는 큰 귀족들의 회의가 다스린다. 무슨 일이든 모두가 “예” 해야 굴러간다. 사람들은 이걸 화백이라 부른다. 기분 좋게 나온 사람이 아무도 없어서다.

blocks.html: They give the old king of Golden Gaya a seat on it, the way you give a guest the chair by the draught. Within a few years he has the middle chair. Then he is High Councillor, and every lord on the bench has to wait for the man they bought to call the vote.
blocks.ko: 그들은 금관의 늙은 임금에게 자리를 하나 내준다. 손님한테 바람 드는 의자를 내주듯이. 몇 해 안 돼 그는 가운데 자리에 앉는다. 그러더니 상대등이 된다. 이제 의자에 앉은 귀족들은 다, 자기들이 사 온 사내가 표결을 부를 때까지 기다려야 한다.

blocks.speaker: A Silla lord
lines: 오 년 전에 저 자는 소나무 밑에서 무릎 꿇고 있었소.
en: Five years ago that man was on his knees under a pine tree.

blocks.speaker: Another lord
lines: 그리고 지금은 여기서 셈할 줄 아는 유일한 사람이오. 앉으시오.
en: And now he’s the only one in here who can count. Sit down.

lines: 표결할까요, 여러분? 아니면 내가 오 년 전에 어디서 무릎을 꿇었는지 얘기할까요?
둘 다 할 시간은 있습니다. 내가 전에 임금이었거든요. 아주 한가한 일이더군요.
en: Shall we vote, my lords? Or shall we talk about where I was kneeling five years ago?
I’ve time for both. I used to be a king. It’s very restful.

blocks.html: At home Muryuk hears about it and says nothing. He polishes the helm. A bought king in a good chair is still bought, he thinks. He is wrong about a great many things that year.
blocks.ko: 집에서 무력은 그 얘기를 듣고 아무 말도 안 한다. 투구를 닦는다. 좋은 의자에 앉아도 사 온 임금은 사 온 임금이라고, 그는 생각한다. 그해 그가 틀린 건 한두 가지가 아니다.

blocks.label: General of Silla
blocks.ko: 신라의 장군

blocks.label: Surabol · the years after
blocks.ko: 서라벌 · 그 뒤

blocks.html: He keeps the oath. For the rest of his life he rides north and west for Silla, and wherever the border itches, it stops. He does it well, and he does it without hope. He doesn’t marry. Why give Silla one more Gaya boy to look down on? He never takes off the helm. One night, twenty-two years on, a king of Baekje will ride into his ditch. You have seen that night already. You just didn’t know whose ditch it was.
blocks.ko: 그는 맹세를 지킨다. 평생 신라를 위해 북으로 서로 달리고, 국경이 근질거리는 곳마다 그게 멎는다. 잘 해낸다. 그리고 아무 희망 없이 해낸다. 장가는 들지 않는다. 신라에게 깔볼 가야 사내아이를 하나 더 줄 까닭이 있나? 투구는 끝내 벗지 않는다. 스물두 해 뒤 어느 밤, 백제의 임금이 그의 도랑으로 말을 몰아 들어올 것이다. 그 밤은 이미 보았다. 누구의 도랑인지 몰랐을 뿐.

blocks.label: The Night Road
blocks.ko: 밤길

blocks.html: Muryuk rides the cut with Silla’s commission folded inside his helm. Military governor of Sinju. The title fits the way the cone never will, which is to say it pinches. Below him, on the west road, fifty Baekje horse ride into Jinhung’s arithmetic.
blocks.ko: 무력은 신라의 임명장을 투구 속에 접어 넣고 패인 길로 탄다. 신주 군주. 관직은 투구처럼 맞지 않는다. 꽉 낀다는 뜻이다. 아래 서쪽 길로 백제 기병 쉰이 진흥의 셈 속으로 들어간다.

blocks.html: He is first down into the cut, because the cone is the tallest thing on the ridge and hiding it is a habit he has not learned. The fallen king looks up and sees Gaya before he sees Silla. That is the whole of Muryuk’s orders, arriving before he does.
blocks.ko: 그는 맨 먼저 패인 길로 내려간다. 뿔투구가 능선에서 제일 크기 때문이다. 숨기는 버릇은 아직 못 배웠다. 쓰러진 임금이 올려다보고, 신라보다 먼저 가야를 본다. 그것이 무력의 명령 전부다. 그보다 먼저 도착한다.

en: Military governor of Sinju.
Sit.

blocks.html: They sit the king on a camp stool. A Silla slave asks for the head, and the king refuses the slave’s hand, and Muryuk says the slave’s name once, the way a door closes. Dodo. He will remember the name longer than the annals do.
blocks.ko: 임금을 야전의자에 앉힌다. 신라 노비가 목을 달라 하고, 임금은 노비의 손을 거부하고, 무력은 노비의 이름을 한 번 부른다. 문 닫히듯. 도도. 연대기보다 오래 기억할 것이다.

blocks.html: The king unfastens his own knife. Muryuk does not look away, because looking away is a Silla habit and he is not Silla tonight. He is Gaya, watching a king die well, and taking notes for the day his own turn comes.
blocks.ko: 임금이 제 칼을 푼다. 무력은 눈을 돌리지 않는다. 눈 돌리기는 신라 버릇이고, 오늘 밤 그는 신라가 아니다. 그는 가야다. 임금이 잘 죽는 것을 보고, 제 차례가 올 날을 위해 적어 둔다.

blocks.title: The Gwansan road · twenty-two years on

blocks.html: A man in a Gaya cone helm is already down in the cut. He wears Silla's commission over it. His cone cuts the night ridge. He does not draw. He watches.
blocks.ko: 가야의 고깔 투구를 쓴 사내가 이미 패인 길 아래에 있다. 그 위에 신라의 임명을 걸쳤다. 그의 고깔이 밤 능선을 가른다. 그는 칼을 뽑지 않는다. 본다.

en: Gaya…?
A prince of Golden Gaya — on this road, tonight, why.
Military governor of Sinju.
Sit.

blocks.hanja: 十九年 金官國主金仇亥 與妃及三子 長曰奴宗 仲曰武德 季曰武力 以國帑寶物來降 王禮待之 授位上等 以本國爲食邑 子武力仕至角干
blocks.ko: <19년>에 금관국(金官國)의 왕인 김구해(金仇亥)가 왕비와 세 명의 아들 즉 큰 아들인 노종(奴宗), 둘째 아들인 무덕(武德), 막내 아들인 무력(武力)을 데리고 나라의 창고에 있던 보물을 가지고 와서 항복하였다. 왕이 예(禮)로써 대접하고 상등(上等)의 벼슬을 주었으며, 본국을 식읍(食邑)으로 삼게 하였다. 아들인 무력은 벼슬이 각간(角干)에 이르렀다.
blocks.html: In the nineteenth year, Kim Guhae, king of Gumgwan, came with his queen and his three sons (the eldest Nojong, the second Muduk, the youngest Muryuk), bringing the treasures from the kingdom’s storehouses, and surrendered. The king received him with courtesy, gave him the highest rank, and granted him his own country as his tax-estate. His son Muryuk rose in office to gakgan.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi 4, Annals of Silla, Beopheung year 19

blocks.label: Great Gaya · 562
blocks.ko: 대가야 · 562

blocks.html: Thirty years on, the cone is still on his head and Silla is still shopping. This time the shop is Great Gaya, the last of the six eggs still calling itself a kingdom. Muryuk rides south with the army. Nobody rides behind him to hold the horses. He swore a king his sons once, and he still hasn’t got any.
blocks.ko: 서른 해가 지나도 고깔은 여전히 그의 머리에 있고, 신라는 여전히 장을 보러 다닌다. 이번 가게는 대가야. 여섯 알 가운데 아직 나라라고 자처하는 마지막 하나다. 무력은 군대와 함께 남으로 간다. 뒤에서 말을 잡아 줄 사람은 없다. 한때 임금 앞에서 아들들을 걸고 맹세했는데, 아직 하나도 없다.

blocks.html: From the road, the gate of Great Gaya looks like every gate he grew up behind. The men on it wear his father’s helm.
blocks.ko: 길에서 보면 대가야의 성문은 그가 자라며 뒤에 숨었던 모든 성문과 닮았다. 그 위의 사내들은 아버지의 투구를 썼다.

en: Those are my father’s helms.
Let me walk up first. Alone.
They’ll shoot you.
Then keep the gate warm for me.

blocks.html: He walks up the gate road bareheaded, the helm in his hand. Every bow on the wall finds him.
blocks.ko: 그는 투구를 손에 든 맨머리로 성문 길을 걸어 올라간다. 성벽의 활이란 활은 모두 그를 찾는다.

blocks.html: The wall answers first. Gaya arrows, from Gaya bows, with Gaya iron on the points. Great Gaya has been forging Silla’s blades for a generation and is about to find out how good they were.
blocks.ko: 성벽이 먼저 답한다. 가야의 활로 쏜 가야의 화살, 촉에는 가야의 쇠. 대가야는 한 세대 동안 신라의 칼을 벼려 왔고, 이제 그 칼이 얼마나 좋았는지 알게 될 참이다.

blocks.html: Somewhere behind him a fifteen-year-old notices where every bow is pointing, and five thousand horse go through the Jundan Gate while the archers are still busy with the old man.
blocks.ko: 등 뒤 어딘가에서 열다섯 살짜리가 활이 모두 어디를 겨누는지 알아채고, 궁수들이 아직 그 늙은이에게 매달려 있는 사이 기병 오천이 전단문을 뚫는다.

blocks.hanja: 九月 加耶叛 王命異斯夫討之 斯多含副之 異斯夫引兵臨之 一時盡降
blocks.ko: 구월에 가야가 배반하니, 왕이 이사부에게 토벌하라 명하고 사다함으로 보좌하게 하였다. 이사부가 군사를 이끌고 이르니, 일시에 모두 항복하였다.
blocks.html: In the ninth month Gaya rebelled. The king ordered Isabu to punish them, with Sadaham as deputy. Isabu brought up the army, and they all surrendered at once.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 4, Silla Annals — King Jinheung, yr. 23 (562), 9th month; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 98

blocks.html: Inside the walls the fighting is short and mean, street by street, the way it is when everyone knows the end and nobody wants to be the one who says it. Muryuk walks up the main street with his helm in his hand. Nobody on the rooftops knows what to do with a Gaya face under a Silla banner.
blocks.ko: 성안의 싸움은 짧고 독하다. 골목마다, 다들 끝을 알면서 그 말을 먼저 꺼내고 싶지 않을 때의 싸움이다. 무력은 투구를 손에 든 채 큰길을 걸어 올라간다. 지붕 위 누구도 신라 깃발 아래의 가야 얼굴을 어찌해야 할지 모른다.

blocks.html: He finds the old lords of Great Gaya in the hall, sitting very straight, the way men sit when they have decided to die well and have not yet been told the price of living.
blocks.ko: 그는 대가야의 늙은 귀족들을 전각에서 찾는다. 다들 꼿꼿이 앉아 있다. 잘 죽기로 마음먹었는데, 살아남는 값은 아직 듣지 못한 사람들의 앉음새다.

blocks.speaker: An old lord of Great Gaya
en: Golden Gaya’s youngest, is it.
So they sent you to say it.
Nobody sent me. Asked to come, I did.
lines: 보낸 사람 없심더. 지가 오겠다 캤심더.

blocks.speaker: An old lord of Great Gaya
en: What’s it like, then? Over there.
Cold, for the first ten years.
Then you have grandchildren, and they don’t remember the cold.
lines: 그라다 손주가 생기는데, 그 아아들은 추웠던 거 기억 몬 합니더.

blocks.speaker: An old lord of Great Gaya
lines: 백성은? 저놈들이 줄줄이 묶어 갈 사람들은?
en: And the people? The ones they’ll rope?

lines: ……그건 내가 팔 수 있는 기 아이요. 거짓말은 안 하겠소.
en: …Not mine to sell. I’ll not lie to you about it.

blocks.html: The old man looks at him for a long time. Gaya has always listened to a good price.
blocks.ko: 노인은 오래도록 그를 바라본다. 가야는 언제나 좋은 값에는 귀를 기울였다.

blocks.html: An hour later the king’s prize is roped in a line across the square below the hall: three hundred Gaya, the boy-general’s to keep. From the hall steps Muryuk watches the boy walk down the line once, and start cutting.
blocks.ko: 한 시진 뒤, 임금이 내린 상이 전각 아래 광장에 줄줄이 묶여 있다. 가야 사람 삼백, 소년 장수의 몫이다. 무력은 전각 계단에서, 소년이 줄을 따라 한 번 걸어 내려가더니 밧줄을 끊기 시작하는 것을 본다.

blocks.speaker: An old lord of Great Gaya
en: ……Silla, that is?
One of them.

blocks.html: Then he comes down the steps. He doesn’t know why until he hears his own voice.
blocks.ko: 그러다 그는 계단을 내려간다. 동인지는 제 목소리를 듣고서야 안다.

en: Those are the king’s, boy.

lines: 제 거예요. 저한테 주셨어요. 거들든지 비키든지 하세요.
en: They’re mine. He gave them to me. Help or move.

lines: 망한 나라 사람들이다. 인자 그기 전부다.
진 사람은 안 풀어 준다. 아무것도 못 된다. 내가 우째 아는지 물어봐라.
en: They’re from a beaten country. That’s all they are now.
Beaten people don’t get untied. They don’t get to be anything. Ask me how I know.

lines: 하늘 아래 사람은 다 똑같아요. 저 사람들도 다 엄마 배 속에서 나왔잖아요, 안 그래요?
en: They lost a war. So what?
Everyone under the sky’s the same. They all came out of their mothers’ wombs too, didn’t they?

blocks.html: He says it the way boys say things they have never had to test. Then he goes back to the knot.
blocks.ko: 소년은 한 번도 시험해 볼 일이 없었던 말을 하는 소년답게 그 말을 한다. 그러고는 다시 매듭으로 돌아간다.

blocks.html: Muryuk stays where he is, long enough to look like a man guarding prisoners. He isn’t guarding anything. He is thinking about a cart, and a wall a hand lower than the neighbours’, and a word he has spent thirty years saying like the name of a dog that bit him.
blocks.ko: 무력은 그 자리에 서 있다. 포로를 지키는 사람처럼 보일 만큼 오래. 아무것도 지키고 있지 않다. 수레를 생각하고 있다. 이웃집보다 한 뼘 낮은 담을, 그리고 서른 해 동안 자기를 문 개 이름처럼 불러 온 한 낱말을.

blocks.html: The last rope comes off near sunset.
blocks.ko: 마지막 밧줄은 해 질 녘에 풀린다.

lines: 내가 옛날에 임금한테 아들들 걸고 맹세했다. 서른 해 전에. 아직 하나도 없다.
en: I swore my sons to a king once. Thirty years back. Haven’t got any yet.
…If I ever do, I hope he’s like you.

lines: 저처럼 어떻게요? 제가 이 나라에서 말을 제일—
en: Like me how? I’m the best rider in the whole—
Not the riding.

blocks.label: The Cut Rope
blocks.ko: 끊긴 밧줄

blocks.html: That night he goes looking for the boy. He tells himself it is for the rice. He finds him on a coil of the rope he cut, eating out of his helmet, with a friend snoring against a cart wheel.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 소년을 찾아 나선다. 밥 때문이라고 스스로에게 말한다. 소년은 자기가 끊은 밧줄 더미 위에서 투구에 밥을 담아 먹고 있고, 벗 하나가 수레바퀴에 기대어 코를 골고 있다.

lines: 밧줄 찾으러 오셨으면, 제가 다 끊었어요.
en: If it’s the rope you want, I cut it. All of it.
Ask the king for more.
I came for the rice.
Smells better than ours, it does.
It’s in my helmet.
I’ve eaten out of worse.

blocks.html: Muryuk sits down on the rope beside the boy without being asked. Sadaham hands him the helmet. It is the politest thing the boy does all year.
blocks.ko: 무력은 청하지도 않았는데 소년 옆 밧줄 더미에 앉는다. 사다함이 투구를 건넨다. 그해 소년이 한 일 중 가장 예의 바른 일이다.

lines: 가야 분이시죠. 말씨가 저 성문이랑 똑같네요.
en: You’re the Gaya one. You talk like the gate.
So they keep telling me.

lines: 그중에 아는 사람 있었어요? 줄에 묶였던 사람들.
en: Were any of them yours? The ones on the rope.
All of them. None of them.
Eat your rice.

blocks.html: All of them, because they talk like his mother. None of them, because he said so himself this afternoon, to an old man in a hall.
blocks.ko: 전부다. 다들 어머니 말씨로 말하니까. 아무도 아니다. 오늘 오후 전각에서 한 노인에게 제 입으로 그렇게 말했으니까.

lines: 도성에선 너희들 머리에 꽃 꽂고 산에서 노래나 부르더니. 오늘은 빚 받으러 온 놈처럼 성문을 뚫고 들어가더군.
en: What is it, then. This hwarang.
In the capital I see you lot up the hills with flowers in your hair, singing. Then today you go through a gate like a debt collector.
You don’t know? Everyone knows.
It’s because you’re old.
Old, I am. Tell it slow, then.

lines: 사내애들이에요. 집안 좋은. 임금님이 하나 골라 앞세우면 나머지가 산으로 따라다니고, 말 타고, 노래하고, 그리고—
en: It’s boys. Good families. The king picks one of us to lead, and the rest follow him up mountains, and we ride, and we sing, and—
Sing.
The singing’s important. Don’t laugh.

blocks.html: He asks who gets in, and what they swear. The boy answers the first question and points his chin at his snoring friend for the second. Muryuk doesn’t need it explained.
blocks.ko: 누가 들어가는지, 무엇을 맹세하는지 묻는다. 소년은 앞의 것에 대답하고, 뒤의 것에는 턱으로 코 고는 벗을 가리킨다. 무력에게는 설명이 필요 없다.

blocks.html: Muryuk looks across the river at Great Gaya’s smoking roofs. Thirty years ago he looked back from a cart until the river bent, because somebody should remember what it looked like. He looks now until he has it. It takes less time than he thought. The boy beside him, for once in his short life, does not say anything at all.
blocks.ko: 무력은 강 건너, 연기 오르는 대가야의 지붕들을 본다. 서른 해 전 그는 수레에서 강이 굽을 때까지 뒤를 돌아보았다. 누군가는 어떤 모습이었는지 기억해야 했으니까. 지금은 그 모습을 다 담을 때까지 본다. 생각보다 오래 걸리지 않는다. 곁의 소년은 그 짧은 생에 처음으로, 아무 말도 하지 않는다.

en: …There.
Now I can face front.
Live long enough to be embarrassed by tonight, Sadaham.
lines: 오늘 밤이 부끄러워질 만큼 오래 살아라, 사다함.

en: Mugwan will be embarrassed for both of us.
lines: 무관이가 둘 몫으로 부끄러워해 줄 거예요.

blocks.html: He goes back to the horse lines alone. Nobody is waiting there to hold his horse wrong. He finds, to his surprise, that he minds.
blocks.ko: 그는 혼자 말 매어 둔 곳으로 돌아간다. 거기서 그의 말을 잘못 쥐고 기다리는 사람은 없다. 그게 서운하다는 걸 알고, 그는 스스로 놀란다.

blocks.html: Somewhere between the fire and the horse lines he decides two things. He will marry. And if a boy comes, the boy goes to that yard, flowers and singing and all.
blocks.ko: 모닥불에서 말 매는 데까지 걸어가는 사이 그는 두 가지를 정한다. 장가를 들 것이다. 그리고 아들이 생기면, 그 아이는 그 마당에 보낼 것이다. 꽃이며 노래며 다.

blocks.html: They ride north in the morning. Muryuk rides at the back of the column, where nobody can see his face. He doesn’t look back at Gaya once. Halfway to Surabol he notices he hasn’t been trying not to.
blocks.ko: 아침에 군대는 북으로 떠난다. 무력은 아무도 얼굴을 볼 수 없는 행렬 맨 뒤에서 말을 몬다. 그는 가야를 한 번도 돌아보지 않는다. 서라벌까지 반쯤 왔을 때, 안 돌아보려고 애쓰지도 않았다는 걸 깨닫는다.

blocks.label: Surabol, the Gaya house · the next spring
blocks.ko: 서라벌, 가야 집 · 이듬해 봄

blocks.html: He marries the next spring, a Silla woman who laughs at his accent exactly once. Noribu makes the speech. Muduk corrects his vowels during it. The old king sits at the head of the table in a Silla robe and cries, which nobody mentions.
blocks.ko: 이듬해 봄 그는 장가를 든다. 신부는 신라 여자인데, 그의 말씨를 딱 한 번 웃는다. 노리부가 축사를 한다. 무덕은 축사 도중에 형의 모음을 고쳐 준다. 늙은 임금은 신라 옷을 입고 상석에 앉아 운다. 아무도 그 얘기는 하지 않는다.

blocks.label: Surabol, the Gaya house · eight years after Great Gaya
blocks.ko: 서라벌, 가야 집 · 대가야 여덟 해 뒤

blocks.html: The birth takes all night. Muryuk spends it in the yard in full armour, because nobody told him what else a man wears to this.
blocks.ko: 해산은 밤새 걸린다. 무력은 그 밤을 마당에서 보낸다. 갑옷을 다 갖춰 입은 채. 이럴 때 사내가 뭘 입는지 아무도 말해 주지 않아서.

blocks.html: At dawn the midwife brings out a boy, red and furious, and puts him in hands that have only ever held reins and swords.
blocks.ko: 새벽에 산파가 시뻘겋게 성난 사내아이를 안고 나와, 고삐와 칼밖에 쥐어 본 적 없는 손에 건넨다.

blocks.speaker: Muryuk’s wife
lines: 뭐 하능교? 뭐라꼬 말 좀 해 주소.
en: Well? Do say something to him.
He’s been waiting all night to hear you.

lines: 신라 말을 먼저 들어야 안 되겠나.
en: …You first.
Silla he should hear first.

blocks.html: They name him Seohyun. The first voice he hears is his mother’s, in a Surabol accent. His father says nothing until the boy is asleep. Then he leans over the cradle and says something very quietly, in the accent of a harbour that isn’t there any more.
blocks.ko: 아이 이름은 서현이라 짓는다. 아이가 처음 듣는 목소리는 서라벌 말씨의 어머니 목소리다. 아버지는 아이가 잠들 때까지 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 그러고는 요람 위로 몸을 숙여 아주 작게 무언가를 말한다. 이제는 없는 포구의 말씨로.

lines: 마당에 보낼 끼다. 화랑 시킬 끼다.
en: He’ll go to the yard. Hwarang, he’ll be.

blocks.speaker: Muryuk’s wife
en: He’s an hour old.
Then there’s time.

blocks.html: He is fifty-five. He will hold this boy’s son once, for one breath, in a county house at the top of the Goguryeo road. That is for later.
blocks.ko: 그는 쉰다섯이다. 이 아이의 아들을 그는 딱 한 번, 한 숨 동안 안게 된다. 고구려 길 꼭대기의 어느 고을 관아에서. 그건 나중 이야기다.

blocks.label: DAY 6
blocks.ko: 여섯째 날

blocks.html: On the sixth night there are two cups on the pavilion table. Bidam poured them himself. Last night he found out whose grandson he has been calling a Gaya ox.
blocks.ko: 여섯째 밤, 정자 탁자에 찻잔 둘이 놓여 있다. 비담이 손수 따랐다. 어젯밤 그는 자기가 가야 소라 부르던 사내가 누구의 손자인지 알았다.

blocks.html: Five days of grain. Two cups poured. Will the grandson of the cone helm come to tea…?
blocks.ko: 닷새 치 곡식. 채워 둔 찻잔 둘. 고깔 투구의 손자는 차를 마시러 올 것인가…?

logline.en: The sixth night’s tea turns to insult, the cavern throws Bidam out, a white horse burns for a falling star, and Yushin leaves the gate for one night to sit by his father.
logline.ko: 여섯째 밤의 차는 욕설로 끝나고, 동굴은 비담을 내쫓고, 떨어진 별을 위해 흰 말이 바쳐지고, 유신은 하룻밤 성문을 떠나 아버지 곁에 앉는다.

NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.

Neither will ever mention it to the other.” Context: He asked which horse. I said a grey. …That was true, at least. You’re grey.
