Two men grieve on the same road tonight, a li apart. Neither will ever mention it to the other. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — KIM YUSHIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_yushin.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Demeanor: Confucian: he STANDS — never sits in lotus. Weighs, counts, frowns at sums; tight jaw, rare dry half-smile. Grief shows as stillness, not tears. The most feared warrior in all of Samhan: a line goes quiet when the tall Silla helm and the white horse appear. Massive, deliberate, terrifying at a walk; by Hwangsan (65) heavier and slower than Gyebek but still the man armies are built around. #2A5FB8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: sitting in lotus or holding prayer beads; katana, tsuba or curved blade (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); two swords at once; blue glow aura. | PLACE Surabol (서라벌 (경주)) — attached board /pl_eastern_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Seorabeol palace: Silla giwa halls, packed-earth yards, timber verandas. | HEADWEAR: JOUGWAN (조우관, feather cap) — copy the SHAPE from the attached hat boards and ignore their Korean labels, museum photos, paper-craft gems and dragon medallion: a small black lacquered gauze cap (변형모, a peaked or square-topped crown no bigger than the topknot it covers) set high on the crown of the head over a small knot of gathered hair (any loose hair the portrait shows still falls beneath it); a thin black band round the head with a small square opening at the front; black cords tied under the chin; two long barred pheasant tail feathers (tan with umber bars), or a spray of bird plumes, rising straight up or sweeping back from either side of the cap, much taller than the cap itself. It replaces any other hat or cap on the portrait; headbands and ribbons stay. Real lacquer and feathers lit by the scene key, never a glow. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). COMMONERS in every Samhan kingdom wear SIMPLE WHITE: plain undyed white or off-white hemp and ramie jackets, wide trousers and skirts, a cloth sash, straw sandals or bare feet, hair in a plain topknot or braid — no dyed silk, no dots, no gold; colour belongs to rank, so a crowd of farmers, porters, servants and townsfolk reads as a field of soft white cloth with the officials' colours standing out of it. Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: The Wait
blocks.ko: 대치

blocks.label: DAY 6
blocks.ko: 여섯째 날

blocks.html: Night rain. Five days of grain behind the palace gate. Bidam’s officers want a dawn assault. Bidam wants the score finished properly. He wants Yushin to come out again.
blocks.ko: 밤비. 궁문 안에는 닷새 치 곡식. 비담의 장교들은 새벽 돌격을 원한다. 비담은 점수를 제대로 끝내고 싶다. 유신이 다시 나오기를 원한다.

blocks.html: Sixth night. Yushin does not come to the pavilion. Bidam sends tea anyway — two cups poured, one left steaming.
blocks.ko: 여섯째 밤. 유신은 정자에 오지 않는다. 비담은 그래도 차를 보낸다 — 잔 둘, 하나는 김이 오른 채.

lines: 됐다. 여섯 번째 밤까지는 예의를 지켰다 아이가.
en: …He is not coming today.
Very well. Courtesy held until the sixth night.

blocks.html: The Hwarang hall, the new boy’s first day. Two seniors lean across his desk.
blocks.ko: 화랑 강당, 새로 온 아이의 첫날. 선배 둘이 그 아이 책상 너머로 몸을 기울인다.

en: So he isn’t even a real True Bone!
blocks.speaker: Senior Hwarang

lines: 너희는 뭐, 잘한 거 있어서 진골이 됐냐?
en: Hey, enough!
What did any of you do to earn True Bone?
You were merely born into it.

blocks.html: He punches the nearer one before the other can answer, then the second for good measure. Then he wipes his knuckles on his own black headband.
blocks.ko: 그는 대답이 나오기도 전에 가까운 놈을 치고, 덤으로 다른 놈도 친다. 그러고는 제 검은 머리띠에 주먹을 닦는다.

en: Thank you.

lines: 이거 가지라. 내 머리띠인데, 이걸 가지고 있으면 아무도 안 괴롭힐 거야.
en: What is there to thank?
Take this headband. Keep it, and no one will trouble you.

blocks.html: Near midnight Yushin comes to the pavilion after all. He does not touch the cup.
blocks.ko: 자정 무렵, 유신이 끝내 정자로 온다. 잔에는 손대지 않는다.

en: You Gaya wretch…!
You dare call yourself the sacred country’s saviour….

lines: 열다섯 해 전, 화백회의에서 — 덕만공주를 위해 일어선 자가 누구였소?
en: Lord Bidam.
Fifteen years past, in the Harmony Council — who was it that stood up for Princess Dukman?

lines: 그 젊은 화랑은 셋 중 가장 총명한 이를 고르겠다고 했소.
그 사람은 어디로 갔소, 비담 공?
en: That young Hwarang said he would choose the cleverest of the three.
Where did that man go, Lord Bidam?

lines: …그 사람은 신국이 아직 나라였을 때 살았지.
en: …That man lived back when the sacred country was still a country.

lines: 그러나 신국에 깃발을 든 것은 내가 아니오…!
en: But it is not I who raised a banner against the sacred country…!

blocks.label: DAY 7
blocks.ko: 일곱째 날

blocks.html: Seven days in, nobody pours. Four days of grain. Last night’s two cups are still on the pavilion table, and one of them was never touched.
blocks.ko: 이레째, 아무도 차를 따르지 않는다. 곡식은 나흘 치. 어젯밤의 찻잔 둘이 정자 탁자에 그대로 있고, 하나는 끝내 아무도 손대지 않았다.

blocks.label: Not a Kim
blocks.ko: 김씨가 아니다

blocks.html: Bidam isn’t looking for it. He is riding the eastern hills alone at night to count the queen’s fires from behind, and his horse goes lame on a path nobody uses. He walks. The path gets warm under his boots. Then the rock breathes, and there is a cave mouth with steam coming out of it like a temple at New Year. Sword on the lip. Beads in the fist. Six nights in armour; a hot spring is a hot spring, and no sutra forbids a wash.
blocks.ko: 비담은 그걸 찾던 게 아니다. 여왕의 불을 뒤에서 세려고 홀로 밤의 동쪽 언덕을 타다가, 아무도 안 쓰는 길에서 말이 다리를 전다. 걸어간다. 장화 밑의 길이 따뜻해진다. 그러다 바위가 숨을 쉬고, 설날 절간처럼 김을 뿜는 동굴 입구가 나온다. 칼은 턱에. 염주는 주먹에. 엿새 밤을 갑옷 속에서 지냈다. 온천은 온천이고, 씻지 말라는 경은 없다.

blocks.html: He walks into the steam with nothing on but water and one hundred and eight beads.
blocks.ko: 물과 백팔 염주만 걸치고 김 속으로 들어간다.

blocks.html: The three sisters are already on the far rock. Narim looks at him the way an eldest looks at a door that opened wrong.
blocks.ko: 세 자매는 이미 저쪽 바위에 있다. 나림은 잘못 열린 문을 보는 언니처럼 그를 본다.
blocks.art: Golhwa on the rock, legs spread wide, chima hiked; Hyullé, knees pressed, eyes down, soaked.

blocks.html: The spring does not hide much. Heat hits him low. He recites. The beads do not help.
blocks.ko: 샘이 감춰 주는 게 없다. 열이 아래서 온다. 염불을 한다. 염주가 도움이 안 된다.

blocks.html: I came to wash. The sutra does not cover this. I am standing in a door I cannot close.
blocks.ko: 씻으러 왔다. 경이 이걸 가리지 못한다. 닫을 수 없는 문에 서 있다.

blocks.html: The beads stop mid-count. He stares. The waterline drops.
blocks.ko: 염주가 세다 만다. 본다. 수선이 내려간다.

en: Wrong door. He brought iron. And that.
lines: 문 잘못 들었어. 쇠를 들고 왔네. 그리고 그것도.

en: He is not a Kim. The steam already knows.
…The mouth. Before the water takes the blade.

blocks.html: They do not stay women.
blocks.ko: 여자로 남지 않는다.

blocks.html: Golhwa goes first — fire unfolding into a tiger the size of the rock, ember pelt, steam off the fangs. Hyullé’s silk becomes a water-serpent, long as the bowl, cyan scales. Narim’s elder-shape thickens into a moss-bear, leaves in the fur, the hill’s weight on four feet.
blocks.ko: 골화가 먼저다 — 불이 바위만 한 호랑이로 펼쳐지고, 불씨 털, 송곳니에서 김. 혈레의 비단이 사발만큼 긴 물뱀이 되고, 청록 비늘. 나림의 언니 형상이 이끼 곰으로 두꺼워진다. 털에 잎, 네 발에 언덕의 무게.

blocks.html: He recoils. The beads jump. The sword is a hard black line he cannot lift in time.
blocks.ko: 뒷걸음친다. 염주가 튄다. 칼은 제때 들지 못하는 단단한 검은 선이다.

blocks.html: They kick him toward the light — tiger-shoulder, serpent-coil, bear-shove. Three beasts, one refusal. The night has him again. The lake keeps Kims. It does not keep slogans.
blocks.ko: 셋이 그를 빛 쪽으로 밀어낸다 — 호랑이 어깨, 뱀의 몸, 곰의 밀침. 짐승 셋, 거절 하나. 밤이 다시 그를 갖는다. 호수는 김씨를 지킨다. 구호는 지키지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Falling Star
blocks.ko: 떨어진 별

blocks.label: DAY 8
blocks.ko: 여덟째 날

blocks.html: On the eighth night the eastern star falls.
blocks.ko: 여덟째 밤, 동쪽 별이 떨어진다.

blocks.html: Not a shooting star. Those come and go, and nobody writes them down. This is the big one, low in the east, the one two boys used to argue about on a hill. It comes loose, slides down the sky with a tail like a torn sleeve, and goes out somewhere past the west wall of the Moon Palace. Both camps see it. Both camps stop talking.
blocks.ko: 별똥별이 아니다. 그런 건 왔다 가고, 아무도 적어 두지 않는다. 이건 동쪽 낮은 하늘의 그 큰 별이다. 두 소년이 언덕 위에서 두고 다투던 그 별. 그것이 떨어져 나와, 찢어진 소매 같은 꼬리를 달고 하늘을 미끄러져 내려가, 월성 서쪽 담 너머 어딘가에서 꺼진다. 양쪽 진영이 다 본다. 양쪽 진영이 다 말을 멈춘다.

blocks.html: On the palace wall, Chunchu has stopped halfway through a sentence about rice.
blocks.ko: 월성 성벽 위에서, 춘추는 쌀 이야기를 하다 말고 멈춰 있다.

en: Brother.
That was ours.
…It was a planet.

lines: 그라믄 방금 행성이 이모님 궁에 떨어진 기네예. 그 차이는 형님이 군사들한테 설명하이소.
en: Then a planet has just fallen on my aunt’s palace. You can explain the difference to the soldiers.

blocks.html: Across the field the Radiance wall begins to roar. Bidam does not invent the omen. He only names it in a useful direction.
blocks.ko: 들판 건너 명활성 성벽이 함성을 지르기 시작한다. 비담이 징조를 지어낸 건 아니다. 쓸모 있는 쪽으로 이름을 붙였을 뿐이다.

blocks.hanja: 吾聞落星之下必有流血 此殆女主敗績之兆也
blocks.ko: 내가 듣건대 별이 떨어지는 곳에는 반드시 피가 나리라. 이는 거의 여주가 패할 징조다.
blocks.html: I have heard that where a star falls, blood will surely be shed. This is likely an omen that the woman sovereign will be defeated.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Bidam’s rebellion, 647)

lines: 하늘은 이미 여왕의 자리에 반대표를 던졌다.
女主不能善理 — 이제 하늘이 불로 쓴다.
en: You heard it.
Heaven has already voted against a woman on the throne.
女主不能善理 — and now the sky writes it in fire.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace
blocks.ko: 월성

blocks.html: The rebel shout shakes the ground. Inside the Moon Palace Queen Sunduk goes pale. Yushin asks for leave to speak — and for a kite, a torch, and enough lies to edit heaven.
blocks.ko: 반군의 함성이 땅을 흔든다. 월성 안에서 선덕여왕의 얼굴이 창백해진다. 유신은 아뢰기를 청한다 — 연과 횃불, 그리고 하늘을 고칠 만큼의 거짓을.

blocks.speaker: Palace guards
en: Did you see where it came down?
Inside. Inside the wall, I’m telling you.
It never. West wall. Outside.
Same thing, if you’re Bidam.
lines: 안에. 성 안에 떨어졌다 캤다 아이가.
별을 읽을 수 있다면, 읽지 못하게 할 수도 있습니다.
en: Your Majesty — do not fear a falling light.
If they can read a star, they can also unread one.
Who here can build a kite?
lines: 이 궁에 연 만들 줄 아는 자 있나.

blocks.speaker: A Hwarang
en: A kite, Marshal? …Now?
A big one.

blocks.speaker: A Hwarang
en: How big?
Big enough to carry a scarecrow. Soaked in oil.
lines: 허수아비 하나 태울 만큼. 기름 먹여서.

blocks.speaker: A Hwarang
en: …Is it for Her Majesty?
For heaven.

blocks.html: They build it in the queen’s own yard by torchlight, out of what a palace has: bamboo from the garden, and the oiled paper off the lattice doors of the hall where the queen lies listening. A steward objects. A maid comes out with the answer.
blocks.ko: 연은 여왕의 뜰에서, 횃불 아래, 궁궐에 있는 것으로 만든다. 정원의 대나무, 그리고 여왕이 누워서 듣고 있는 전각의 살창에서 뜯어낸 기름 먹인 창호지. 한 내관이 막아선다. 시녀 하나가 대답을 들고 나온다.

blocks.speaker: A maid
en: Her Majesty says take the doors.
She says she can do a little draught.

blocks.html: The scarecrow is a guard’s spare coat stuffed with straw and soaked in lamp oil. Somebody paints a face on it. Yushin makes them wipe it off.
blocks.ko: 허수아비는 경비병의 여벌 웃옷에 짚을 채우고 등잔 기름에 적신 것이다. 누가 거기에 얼굴을 그린다. 유신이 지우게 한다.

en: No face.
It’s a star.

blocks.html: There is a west wind off the hills, the first useful thing heaven has done all week. Yushin takes the line himself. Four Hwarang hold the reel. He lights the scarecrow with his own torch and lets it go.
blocks.ko: 서쪽 산에서 바람이 분다. 이번 주 들어 하늘이 처음으로 쓸모 있는 일을 한다. 유신이 손수 줄을 잡는다. 화랑 넷이 얼레를 붙든다. 그는 제 횃불로 허수아비에 불을 붙이고, 놓는다.

blocks.html: It climbs. One spool of line runs out, then a second knotted to the first, then the fishing line off every hook in the palace kitchens. The kite goes out of sight. The paper goes, the bamboo goes, the burning coat goes, and what is left is one small hard point of fire, higher than anyone has ever put anything in the sky.
blocks.ko: 연이 오른다. 얼레 하나가 다 풀리고, 거기 이어 묶은 두 번째도 풀리고, 궁궐 부엌의 낚싯바늘마다 매달려 있던 낚싯줄까지 다 풀린다. 연이 보이지 않게 된다. 종이가 사라지고, 대나무가 사라지고, 불타는 웃옷이 사라지고, 남는 건 작고 단단한 불빛 하나. 사람이 하늘에 무언가를 올려 본 중에 가장 높은 데다.

blocks.html: Then it stops. Low in the east. Exactly where the old star used to hang.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 멈춘다. 동쪽 낮은 하늘. 옛 별이 걸려 있던 바로 그 자리.

en: …Brother.
You’ve put it back.
It’s a star tonight.

lines: 하늘이 마음을 바꿨다 — 아니면 우리가 하늘의 필체를 고쳤다.
en: Look up.
Heaven changed its mind — or we changed heaven’s handwriting.
Hwarang, with me.

blocks.speaker: On the palace wall
lines: 도로 올라갔다. 저거 봐라. 저거 좀 봐라!
en: It’s back.
It’s back up. Look at it. Look at it!
Told you it never came down inside.
You told me it came down on the kitchens.

blocks.speaker: On the Radiance wall
en: It’s going back up.
Stars don’t go back up.
That one is.
…Councillor? Councillor, the star’s going back up.

blocks.speaker: A boy on the Radiance wall
lines: 저거 사람이 할 수 있는 기가?
사람이 별을 도로 걸 수 있나?
en: Can people do that?
Can people put a star back?

blocks.html: Nobody on either wall can say what it is. Both walls decide what it means. For one night the sky is on the queen’s side, and in a siege one night is a long time.
blocks.ko: 어느 성벽에서도 그게 뭔지 말할 수 있는 사람은 없다. 두 성벽 다 그게 무슨 뜻인지는 정해 버린다. 하룻밤 동안 하늘은 여왕 편이다. 그리고 포위전에서 하룻밤은 긴 시간이다.

en: Then someone over there has read the same books I have.
…Bring another cup.
lines: 그럼 저쪽에도 나와 같은 책을 읽은 자가 있다는 게지.

blocks.label: The Stables
blocks.ko: 마구간

blocks.html: The kite buys one night. A sky can only be argued with for so long, and by midnight both camps are already arguing about what they saw. While the drums are still asleep, Yushin goes down to the palace stables alone and leads out the white horse.
blocks.ko: 연은 하룻밤을 번다. 하늘과는 그리 오래 다툴 수 없고, 자정이 되자 두 진영은 벌써 자기들이 무엇을 보았는지를 두고 다툰다. 북이 아직 잠든 사이, 유신은 홀로 궁의 마구간으로 내려가 흰 말을 끌어낸다.

blocks.html: Hangyul has carried him for eighteen years, since the charge at Nangbi Fortress, to every border the queen sent him to and a few he went to without asking. The groom, a boy of fourteen, works out what the rope in the marshal’s other hand is for before anyone says it, and starts to cry with his mouth shut.
blocks.ko: 한결은 낭비성 돌격 때부터 열여덟 해 동안 그를 태웠다. 여왕이 보낸 모든 국경으로, 묻지 않고 간 몇몇 국경으로. 열네 살 마부 아이는 대장군의 다른 손에 들린 밧줄이 무엇에 쓰일지 누가 말하기도 전에 알아차리고, 입을 꾹 다문 채 운다.

blocks.html: Seventeen, drunk, and asleep in the saddle. His first horse, Hanbyul, does what any good horse does with a sleeping rider and takes him where he always goes. He wakes at the courtesan Chungwan’s gate with her lantern already lifted and her face already glad.
blocks.ko: 열일곱, 취해서, 안장 위에서 잠든 채. 첫 말 한별은 잠든 주인을 태운 좋은 말이라면 누구나 하는 일을 한다. 늘 가던 곳으로 데려간다. 그가 눈을 뜬 곳은 기생 천관의 문 앞이고, 그녀의 등불은 이미 들려 있고, 얼굴은 이미 반갑다.

en: You came?
…They said you swore to your mother you’d never come again.

blocks.html: He had sworn it. The horse had not. He gets down, draws, and takes Hanbyul’s head off at the gate in one stroke, then walks home past the lantern without looking at it. The song Chungwan made about that night outlives both of them.
blocks.ko: 맹세는 그가 했다. 말은 하지 않았다. 그는 내려서 칼을 뽑아, 문 앞에서 단칼에 한별의 목을 벤다. 그리고 등불은 쳐다보지도 않고 걸어서 집으로 간다. 그날 밤을 두고 천관이 지은 노래는 두 사람보다 오래 산다.

blocks.label: The Scorched Ground
blocks.ko: 별 떨어진 자리

blocks.html: The star came down past the Western wall of the Moon Palace, where the ground is still scorched in a long smear. Yushin walks Hangyul there himself. Chunchu is already waiting with two priests, a bronze basin, and a face that has decided not to argue.
blocks.ko: 별은 월성 서쪽 담 너머에 떨어졌고, 그곳 땅은 아직 길게 그을려 있다. 유신은 한결을 직접 끌고 간다. 춘추는 이미 제관 둘과 청동 대야, 그리고 따지지 않기로 마음먹은 얼굴을 하고 기다리고 있다.

en: …There are other white horses. Three in the stable.
Must it be this one?

lines: 저쪽도 다 안다. 내가 무슨 말 타는지.
남의 말 바치믄 하늘이 웃는 기 아이라 비담이가 웃는다.
en: They know over there. Everyone knows which horse I ride.
Offer someone else’s horse and it isn’t heaven that laughs. It’s Bidam.

blocks.html: He takes the halter off with his own hands. Hangyul, who has been led to a great many strange places at night, puts his nose into Yushin’s chest and waits for the reason, as he always has.
blocks.ko: 그는 제 손으로 굴레를 벗긴다. 밤마다 낯선 곳으로 수없이 끌려가 본 한결은, 늘 그래 왔듯 유신의 가슴에 코를 묻고 이유를 기다린다.

lines: 낭비성에서 니 아이었으믄 난 거서 끝났다.
en: Eighteen years.
If it weren’t for you at Nangbi, I’d have ended there.
…I’m sorry. This time I’m the one who brought you.
Yushin.
…Shall I do it?
No.
He’s mine.

blocks.html: He does it the way the rite asks and faster than the rite asks, so the horse never quite finishes turning his head. White goes down into the scorched black. The priests begin the prayer, and Yushin, who has never once let another man finish a sentence for him, lets them.
blocks.ko: 그는 의례가 시키는 대로, 그러나 의례보다 빠르게 한다. 말이 고개를 미처 다 돌리기도 전에. 흰 것이 그을린 검은 땅 위로 무너진다. 제관들이 축문을 시작하고, 평생 남이 제 말을 대신 끝맺게 둔 적 없는 유신이 이번에는 그렇게 둔다.

blocks.html: He slaughtered a white horse and offered it at the place where the star had fallen, and prayed: “In the way of Heaven, yang is firm and yin is yielding; in the way of men, the sovereign is honoured and the subject humble. Should this ever be reversed, there is great disorder.”
blocks.ko: 흰 말을 잡아 별이 떨어진 곳에 제사 지내고 빌었다. “하늘의 도는 양이 굳세고 음이 부드러우며, 사람의 도는 임금이 높고 신하가 낮습니다. 만일 이를 바꾸면 곧 큰 난리가 됩니다.”
blocks.hanja: 刑白馬 祭於星落之地 祝曰 天道則陽剛而陰柔 人道則君尊而臣卑 苟或易之 卽爲大亂
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Bidam’s rebellion, 647)

blocks.html: Across the field, on the Radiance wall, Bidam watches the smoke of the offering go up and asks an officer what was burned. When he is told, he puts his beads away for the first time in eight days and goes down to the lines to stand beside his own horse, Bisamun, for a while, saying nothing to anybody.
blocks.ko: 들판 건너 명활성 성벽에서 비담은 제물 연기가 오르는 것을 보고, 무엇을 태웠느냐고 장교에게 묻는다. 대답을 듣자 그는 여드레 만에 처음으로 염주를 거두고, 진영으로 내려가 제 말 비사문 곁에 한동안 서 있다. 아무에게도 아무 말 없이.

blocks.html: Afterwards the groom leads out a young grey, too green for a marshal, the only horse left in the royal stable that nobody has been afraid of all week.
blocks.ko: 그 뒤 마부 아이가 어린 회색 말을 끌고 나온다. 대장군이 타기엔 아직 풋내기, 이번 주 내내 아무도 무서워하지 않은 왕궁 마구간의 마지막 말.

en: Name?

blocks.html: The boy shakes his head. He is still crying.
blocks.ko: 아이는 고개를 젓는다. 아직 울고 있다.

lines: ……부르기 쉽게 지었다. 고마 울고 불러 봐라.
en: Hansul.
…It’s easy to say. Stop crying and try it.

blocks.html: It is the last horse he names. He rides Hansul out on the tenth day, and across the Yellow Mountain fields thirteen years later, and never once lets a groom catch him brushing it longer than the others.
blocks.ko: 그가 이름을 지어 준 마지막 말이다. 열째 날 그는 한슬을 타고 나가고, 열세 해 뒤 황산벌도 한슬을 타고 건넌다. 그리고 다른 말보다 그 녀석을 오래 빗질하는 모습을, 마부에게 단 한 번도 들키지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace · near midnight
blocks.ko: 월성 · 자정 무렵

blocks.html: Near midnight Chunchu comes to Yushin’s desk to say there are three days of rice left and not to tell the kitchen. A runner from the Kim house has beaten him there by a breath.
blocks.ko: 자정 무렵, 쌀이 사흘 치 남았으니 부엌엔 말하지 말라고 전하러 춘추가 유신의 책상으로 온다. 김씨 집 심부름꾼이 한 숨 먼저 와 있다.

blocks.speaker: A runner
en: Marshal— it’s your father.
The physicians say tonight. He keeps asking for you.
…And for his horse. We don’t know which one he means.
lines: 의원들이 오늘 밤이라 캅니더. 자꾸 대장군을 찾으십니더.
…말도 찾으십니더. 어느 말을 말씀하시는지 저희는 모르겠고예.

blocks.html: Yushin stands up. Then he looks at the grain tally, and at the window where the Radiance fires are, and doesn’t move.
blocks.ko: 유신이 일어선다. 그러고는 곡식 장부를 보고, 명활성 불빛이 보이는 창을 보고는, 움직이지 않는다.

en: Go.
A rebel on the wall. Three days of rice. And the marshal goes home.
lines: 성벽엔 역적이 있고 쌀은 사흘 치일세. 그런데 대장군이 집엘 간다고.

en: For one night. I’ll sit in your chair and frown at the gate.
If Bidam sends a poem, I’ll answer it. If he sends men, I’ll wake your captain.
…He won’t, though. He’s a gentleman. Rather the worst thing about him.
lines: 하룻밤이야. 네 자리에 앉아서 성문을 노려보고 있을게.
비담이 시를 보내면 내가 답하고, 군사를 보내면 네 부장을 깨우지.
…안 보낼 끼다. 점잖은 양반 아이가. 그기 제일 고약한 기라.

blocks.html: Yushin gives the gate to his captain in one sentence: shut, and shut it stays. Then he takes the young grey out by the back way. It is Hansul’s first errand, and it is this one.
blocks.ko: 유신은 한 문장으로 성문을 부장에게 맡긴다. 닫아 두고, 닫힌 채로 둘 것. 그리고 어린 회색 말을 뒷길로 끌고 나간다. 한슬의 첫 심부름이 하필 이것이다.

blocks.html: On the Radiance wall an officer counts the torches leaving the palace. One. Riding south, fast.
blocks.ko: 명활성 성벽 위에서 한 장교가 궁을 빠져나가는 횃불을 센다. 하나. 남쪽으로, 빠르게.

lines: 이백만 주이소. 아침이믄 저 성문은 우리 낍니더.
en: Councillor. The marshal’s ridden out. Alone.
Give me two hundred men and the gate is ours by morning.
Where to?

lines: 김씨 집입니더. 어르신이 오늘을 못 넘긴답니더.
en: The Kim house. They say the old man’s dying.

blocks.html: Bidam doesn’t answer for a while. He has already put his beads away tonight, so his hands have nothing to do.
blocks.ko: 비담은 한동안 대답하지 않는다. 염주는 오늘 밤 이미 거둬 두었으니, 손이 할 일이 없다.

en: I ate at that man’s table when I was sixteen. He apologised for the soup all night.
…Let him go home.
lines: 열여섯에 그 어른 밥상에서 밥을 묵었다. 밤새 국이 싱겁다꼬 사과하시더라.

en: Councillor, the gate—
Will still be there tomorrow. So will I.

blocks.html: Yumjong bows. He goes down off the wall, and he does not take two hundred men. He takes twenty, and the word they like shouting. A road that takes a man home also brings him back.
blocks.ko: 염종은 고개를 숙인다. 성벽을 내려가는데, 이백은 데려가지 않는다. 스물을 데려간다. 그리고 다들 외치기 좋아하는 그 말도. 사람을 집으로 데려가는 길은, 그 사람을 다시 데려오기도 한다.

blocks.label: Father
blocks.ko: 아버지

blocks.label: The Kim house, Surabol · the small hours
blocks.ko: 서라벌, 김씨 집 · 새벽녘

blocks.html: The house is full of physicians who have stopped pretending. Kim Seohyun lies under two quilts with his riding boots beside the bed. He asked for them, and nobody has had the heart to ask where he thinks he’s going.
blocks.ko: 집 안엔 시늉을 그만둔 의원들이 가득하다. 김서현은 이불 두 채 아래 누워 있고, 침상 옆엔 그의 승마 신이 놓여 있다. 본인이 달라고 했고, 어딜 가시려느냐고 물을 만큼 모진 사람은 아무도 없었다.

en: Captain? Are the horses— somebody see to the—
…Ah. It’s you.
It’s me, Father.
Which horse did you— not the white. You’ll lame him on these stones.
lines: 무슨 말을 타고— 흰 말은 안 된다. 이 돌길에 다리 절게 해.

blocks.html: Tonight Yushin edited heaven with a kite and a lie and never blinked. He finds he can’t tell this man about the white horse.
blocks.ko: 오늘 밤 유신은 연 하나와 거짓말 하나로 하늘을 고치면서 눈 한 번 깜빡이지 않았다. 그런데 이 사람에게는 흰 말 얘기를 못 하겠다.

en: A grey, Father. A new one.
Grey. Good. Greys are— sensible.
They said there was fire in the sky tonight. Over the palace. I thought, that’ll be him.
lines: 오늘 밤 하늘에 불이 났다더구나. 궁 위에. 그 녀석이구나 했다.

en: It was me.
Hm. Always said it, your mother did, that you’d set the sky on fire one day. Told her not to encourage you, I did.
lines: 흠. 니 어매가 늘 그캤다 아이가. 언젠가 니가 하늘에 불을 놓을 끼라꼬. 부추기지 마라 캤는데.

blocks.html: Somewhere in that sentence his vowels go south. When Yushin was seven, this man sat him down and made him say the capital’s vowels until he cried. He never once let his own slip in front of anyone. Tonight they have gone home without asking.
blocks.ko: 그 문장 어딘가에서 그의 모음이 남쪽으로 내려간다. 유신이 일곱 살 때, 이 사람은 아들을 앉혀 놓고 울 때까지 도읍 말씨를 따라 하게 했다. 제 말씨는 누구 앞에서도 단 한 번 흘린 적이 없다. 오늘 밤 그 말씨가 허락도 없이 고향으로 돌아갔다.

en: Father. Your voice.
Hm? …Ah.
Don’t you tell anyone, now.

blocks.html: He smiles about that for a while. Then he stops smiling and takes hold of his son’s sleeve, the one with the stone in it, hard enough to hurt.
blocks.ko: 그는 한동안 그 일로 웃는다. 그러다 웃음을 멈추고 아들의 소매를, 돌이 든 그 소매를, 아플 만큼 세게 움켜쥔다.

en: Yushin. Closer, bach. There’s a thing I— forty years I’ve meant to say it, and always a horse to see to, or—
lines: 유신아. 가까이 온나. 할 말이— 마흔 해를 할라 캤는데, 늘 말을 봐야 했거나, 아이믄—

en: I’m here.
No matter what you do…

blocks.html: The rest of it doesn’t come. Yushin waits for it with his ear at his father’s mouth for a long time after there is nothing there to wait for.
blocks.ko: 나머지는 오지 않는다. 기다릴 것이 없어진 뒤로도 한참을, 유신은 아버지의 입가에 귀를 댄 채 그 나머지를 기다린다.

blocks.html: Kangrim is already in the doorway with the red ledger open. He reads the name three times — Seohyun. Seohyun. Seohyun. — and makes the small cut.
blocks.ko: 강림은 이미 문간에 서 있다. 붉은 명부를 펼친 채. 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 서현. 서현. 서현. — 그리고 짧게 끊는다.

en: Ah— excuse me. Not finished, I wasn’t.
I was in the middle of telling my son something, and he didn’t—
lines: 아들한테 하던 말이 있는데, 저 아가 끝을—

en: Most people are in the middle of something, sir. The ledger has never once waited for a full stop.
lines: 대개들 무슨 말인가 하시던 중이오. 명부는 마침표를 기다려 준 적이 한 번도 없소.

en: One question, then we walk.
Kim Seohyun. The life you just finished — was it a Gaya life, or a Silla one?
lines: 김서현. 방금 마치신 그 삶 — 가야의 삶이었소, 신라의 삶이었소?

blocks.html: Seohyun looks at his son, still bent over the bed with his ear at a mouth that has stopped.
blocks.ko: 서현은 아들을 본다. 이미 멈춘 입에 아직도 귀를 대고 침상에 엎드려 있는 아들을.

en: …Long one, that’s going to be.
It’s a long road, sir.
Kim Seohyun, giddy-up, go!
Riding in the dark where nobody knows.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Father looked back; he looked at the sky,
ran with a princess and didn’t ask why.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
He never could tell the short way through,
so we sing it long, the whole road too.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
blocks.title: Seohyun Who Rode in the Dark

blocks.caption: Kim Seohyun, a Gaya boy on a Silla horse. Never any good at the short version.
blocks.ko: 신라 말을 탄 가야 소년, 김서현. 짧게 말하는 법은 끝내 몰랐다.

blocks.label: The Outer Ditch · before light
blocks.ko: 바깥 도랑 · 동트기 전

blocks.html: Yushin rides back before light, because the gate is still a gate. He hasn’t said a word since the house. Hansul doesn’t know the road yet, and Yushin lets him find it. Low in the east his star is still burning, a little smaller now.
blocks.ko: 유신은 동트기 전에 돌아간다. 성문은 여전히 성문이니까. 그 집을 나선 뒤로 한마디도 하지 않았다. 한슬은 아직 이 길을 모른다. 유신은 녀석이 알아서 찾게 둔다. 동쪽 낮은 하늘에서 그의 별이 아직 타고 있다. 조금 작아졌다.

blocks.html: Where the south road crosses the outer ditch, there are torches across it. Twenty black headbands, and in the middle a mild man on foot, leaning on a spear like a walking stick.
blocks.ko: 남쪽 길이 바깥 도랑을 건너는 자리에, 횃불이 길을 막고 있다. 검은 머리띠 스물. 그 한가운데, 순해 보이는 사내 하나가 창을 지팡이처럼 짚고 서 있다.

lines: 삼가 조의를 표합니더. 진심입니더. 저녁 먹다 들었지예.
en: Marshal.
My condolences. I mean it. We heard at supper.
Move your men.

lines: 상대등께서 집에는 보내 드리라 카셨지예. 신사시거든요, 우리 상대등은.
돌아오는 길 얘기는 한마디도 안 하셨습니더.
en: The Councillor said let you go home. He’s a gentleman, the Councillor.
He never said a word about letting you come back.
Yumjong. Not tonight.
Tonight’s the only night you’ve come out alone.

blocks.speaker: Twenty black headbands
en: Gaya!
Gaya dog! Back to your cart!

lines: 하나만 먼저 정하입시더, 대장군. 점잖은 사람끼리. 누가 쓰러지든, 남은 쪽이 집에 보내 주기로.
en: Shh. Manners.
One thing first, Marshal. Between gentlemen. Whoever falls, the other sends him home.
Not to the dogs. Home.
No bargains tonight.

lines: 어르신은 어떻게 가셨습니꺼, 대장군? 사람이 마지막엔 지 어매 말투로 돌아간다 카던데.
en: …Pity.
How did the old man go, then, Marshal? They say at the end a man talks the way his mother did.

blocks.html: Yushin gets down. He leaves the rein on the saddle, and the grey stands where it is left, as if it already knows this is not a night for wandering.
blocks.ko: 유신이 말에서 내린다. 고삐는 안장에 걸쳐 둔다. 회색 말은 둔 자리에 그대로 선다. 오늘 밤은 돌아다닐 밤이 아니라는 걸 벌써 아는 것처럼.

blocks.html: Nobody has ever noticed Yumjong. It turns out he has spent thirty years of mornings with a spear where nobody was looking. The first thrust is faster than it has any right to be. It opens Yushin’s sleeve from wrist to elbow, and something small and grey drops out of it into the ditch.
blocks.ko: 염종을 눈여겨본 사람은 아무도 없었다. 알고 보니 그는 아무도 안 보는 데서 삼십 년 아침을 창과 보냈다. 첫 찌르기가 터무니없이 빠르다. 유신의 소매가 손목부터 팔꿈치까지 갈라지고, 작고 잿빛인 무언가가 도랑으로 떨어진다.

blocks.html: Yushin doesn’t look down. Something in his face does, and the twenty see it. He comes through them the way the river comes through a weir. Torches go into the ditch and hiss. Black headbands go up the slope. In the time it takes to say it, there are no twenty. There is a mild man with a spear, and the marshal.
blocks.ko: 유신은 내려다보지 않는다. 대신 그의 얼굴 속 무언가가 내려앉는다. 스물이 그걸 본다. 그는 보를 넘는 강물처럼 그들 사이를 뚫고 지나간다. 횃불들이 도랑에 떨어져 치익 소리를 낸다. 검은 머리띠들이 비탈 위로 달아난다. 말 한마디 할 동안에 스물은 없다. 창을 든 순한 사내 하나와, 대장군이 있을 뿐이다.

blocks.html: Yumjong is brave for exactly as long as he has twenty men. Then he runs. Along the ditch, in the dark, under the Radiance wall, with the marshal behind him not running but walking, the way you walk after a horse you know will tire. The length of the ditch. Back. Once more. Up on the wall the sentries find their torches and start shouting for the Councillor.
blocks.ko: 염종의 용기는 딱 스물이 곁에 있는 동안만 간다. 그러고는 달린다. 어둠 속에서, 도랑을 따라, 명활성 성벽 밑으로. 대장군은 그 뒤를 뛰지 않고 걸어서 따라간다. 지칠 줄 아는 말을 쫓아갈 때처럼. 도랑 끝까지. 되돌아서. 한 번 더. 성벽 위의 보초들이 횃불을 찾아 들고 상대등을 부르기 시작한다.

blocks.html: Somewhere in the far west, a blind poet once sang this lap of a wall, with a city and a chariot in it. Yushin has never heard of him. He is about to sing it differently.
blocks.ko: 저 먼 서쪽 어딘가에서, 눈먼 시인 하나가 성벽을 도는 이 장면을 노래한 적이 있다. 거기엔 도시가 하나 있었고 전차가 하나 있었다. 유신은 그런 시인을 들어 본 적이 없다. 그는 이 노래를 다르게 부르려는 참이다.

blocks.html: At the third turn Yumjong stops. He is a True Bone. He has just remembered.
blocks.ko: 세 번째로 돌아설 때 염종이 멈춘다. 그는 진골이다. 방금 그게 생각났다.

lines: 도랑 빙빙 돌다가는 아니지. 성벽 앞에서는.
en: No.
Not round a ditch. Not in front of the wall.

blocks.html: He levels the spear, and this time he is good. He takes Yushin across the cheek. He takes him again along the ribs. Spear against ring-pommel sword, in the mud, in the dark, with the whole Radiance wall leaning over to watch.
blocks.ko: 그가 창을 겨누고, 이번에는 제대로다. 유신의 뺨을 긋는다. 다시 갈비뼈를 따라 긋는다. 창과 환두대도가 진흙 속에서, 어둠 속에서 맞붙고, 명활성 성벽 전체가 몸을 내밀고 내려다본다.

lines: 상대등께서 대장군은 왼쪽 어깨를 떨군다 카시던데예.
en: The Councillor says you drop your left shoulder.
He’s said so for thirty years.

blocks.html: Yushin drops it. On purpose, for the first time in thirty years. The gap opens on his left like a door. Yumjong goes for the door with everything he has, and Yushin steps inside the spear with the old yard step, the one two boys of Class 51 learned together in the mud, and puts the blade into his chest.
blocks.ko: 유신이 어깨를 떨군다. 삼십 년 만에 처음으로, 일부러. 그의 왼쪽에 빈틈이 문처럼 열린다. 염종이 온 힘을 다해 그 문으로 뛰어든다. 유신은 옛 연무장의 그 걸음으로 창 안쪽에 들어서서, 칼날을 그의 가슴에 박는다. 오십일기의 두 소년이 진흙탕에서 함께 익힌 걸음이다.

blocks.html: Yumjong sits down in the ditch as if somebody had offered him a seat.
blocks.ko: 염종은 누가 자리라도 권한 것처럼 도랑에 주저앉는다.

en: …Huh.
He said you would.
…You said no bargains. Send me back anyway.
I’ll send you.
…It was a good word, though. Gaya.
They liked shouting it.

blocks.html: Yushin kneels in the mud beside him. First for the stone. He finds it by feel, wipes it on the torn sleeve, and closes his fist on it. Then, with the same hand, he closes Yumjong’s eyes.
blocks.ko: 유신이 그 옆 진흙에 무릎을 꿇는다. 먼저 돌을 위해서. 손으로 더듬어 찾아, 찢어진 소매에 닦고, 주먹 안에 쥔다. 그러고는 같은 손으로 염종의 눈을 감긴다.

blocks.html: One of the twenty has left a horse at the ditch. Yushin lifts the body across its saddle, ties it there with the dead man’s own sash, leaves the black headband where it is, and turns the horse’s head toward the Radiance gate. Then he slaps its rump once.
blocks.ko: 스물 중 누군가 도랑가에 말 한 마리를 두고 갔다. 유신은 시신을 그 안장 위에 가로로 얹고, 죽은 이의 허리띠로 묶고, 검은 머리띠는 그대로 둔 채, 말머리를 명활성 성문 쪽으로 돌린다. 그리고 엉덩이를 한 번 친다.

blocks.html: The horse walks up the slope alone, its rider folded over the saddle. On the wall the shouting stops. Yushin mounts the grey and is gone up the road before the gate opens.
blocks.ko: 말이 혼자 비탈을 걸어 오른다. 탄 이는 안장 위에 접혀 있다. 성벽 위의 고함이 멎는다. 유신은 회색 말에 올라, 성문이 열리기 전에 길 위로 사라진다.

blocks.label: The Radiance Gate
blocks.ko: 명활성 성문

blocks.html: The gate opens for a horse. Bidam comes down through it with no sword, only the beads he put away at dusk, snatched up again on the way down. He lifts Yumjong’s face from the saddle with both hands.
blocks.ko: 성문이 말 한 마리를 위해 열린다. 비담이 칼도 없이 그 문을 지나 내려온다. 해 질 녘 치워 두었던 염주를, 내려오는 길에 도로 움켜쥐었을 뿐이다. 그는 두 손으로 안장에서 염종의 얼굴을 들어 올린다.

lines: 내일이라 안 캤나. 성문은 내일도 있다꼬 안 캤나.
en: Yumjong.
…Yumjong.
I said tomorrow. I said the gate would still be there.

blocks.html: Somebody has closed his eyes. Bidam knows whose hand it was, and that is worse. He unties the sash and takes his friend down into his arms, and kneels in the mud with him. The wound is under the left arm, where a man goes in when a door opens on his left. Bidam knows that step. He taught half of it.
blocks.ko: 누군가 그의 눈을 감겨 주었다. 비담은 그게 누구 손인지 안다. 그래서 더 아프다. 그는 허리띠를 풀어 벗을 안아 내리고, 그를 안은 채 진흙에 무릎을 꿇는다. 상처는 왼팔 아래다. 왼쪽에 문이 열릴 때 사람이 파고드는 자리. 비담은 그 걸음을 안다. 그 절반은 그가 가르쳤다.

blocks.html: The quieter name on the banner goes first. Bidam unties the black headband from Yumjong’s brow and winds it round his own wrist, under the beads, and does not let anyone see his hand.
blocks.ko: 깃발의 조용한 이름이 먼저 간다. 비담은 염종의 이마에서 검은 머리띠를 풀어 제 손목에, 염주 밑에 감는다. 그리고 그 손을 아무에게도 보이지 않는다.

blocks.html: He recites for the dead, the whole sutra, slowly, while the men on the wall hold their torches and don’t know where to look. When he reaches the end he lays Yumjong down, and stands, and walks out onto the open slope, and looks up.
blocks.ko: 그는 망자를 위한 경을 왼다. 처음부터 끝까지, 천천히. 성벽 위의 군사들은 횃불을 든 채 어디를 봐야 할지 모른다. 끝까지 다 외고 나서, 그는 염종을 내려놓고, 일어나, 트인 비탈로 걸어 나가, 하늘을 올려다본다.

blocks.html: In the east the marshal’s star has burned out. The place where it hung is empty.
blocks.ko: 동쪽에서 대장군의 별은 다 타 버렸다. 그것이 걸려 있던 자리가 비어 있다.

lines: 여자 하나 겨냥해 별을 내던지더니, 저놈은 종이로 그걸 도로 걸어 놨다!
저 사람한테는 어디 있었노?! 니한테 뭘 달라 칸 적도 없는 사람이다! 한 번도!
en: Is that your omen?!
You threw a star down at her, and he hung it back up with paper!
Where were you for him?! He never asked you for anything! Not once!

blocks.html: Then there are no more words, only the noise a man makes at the sky when the sky has nothing to say back. The whole Radiance wall hears it. So does the palace. Nobody on either side will describe it afterwards, and nobody on either side forgets it.
blocks.ko: 그다음엔 말이 없다. 하늘이 아무 대답도 하지 않을 때 사람이 하늘에 대고 내는 소리만 있다. 명활성 성벽 전체가 그걸 듣는다. 궁궐도 듣는다. 어느 쪽도 나중에 그 소리를 입에 올리지 않고, 어느 쪽도 잊지 않는다.

lines: 그 걸음, 우리 같이 배운 기다. 오늘 밤 니는 그걸 저 사람한테 썼다.
en: Yushin! Brother of the yard!
We learned that step together. Tonight you used it on him.

blocks.label: The South Road
blocks.ko: 남쪽 길

blocks.html: A li up the road, out of sight of both walls, Yushin gets down again. He sits in the road like a boy who has been sent out of a room.
blocks.ko: 길을 따라 한 리쯤, 양쪽 성벽 어디서도 보이지 않는 데서 유신은 다시 말에서 내린다. 방에서 쫓겨난 아이처럼 길바닥에 앉는다.

blocks.html: Hansul puts his nose into his chest and waits for the reason, the way the white horse used to. That is what does it.
blocks.ko: 한슬이 그의 가슴에 코를 묻고 까닭을 기다린다. 흰 말이 늘 그랬던 것처럼. 그게 그를 무너뜨린다.

en: He asked which horse.
I said a grey.
…That was true, at least. You’re grey.

blocks.html: Then the Marshal of Silla cries in the road, the way men cry who have held it the whole way on horseback, with the stone in his fist and the grey standing over him.
blocks.ko: 그러고 나서 신라의 대장군은 길바닥에서 운다. 말 등에서 내내 참아 온 사내들이 우는 식으로. 주먹엔 돌을 쥐고, 회색 말이 그 위에 서 있다.

blocks.html: Two men grieve on the same road tonight, a li apart. Neither will ever mention it to the other.
blocks.ko: 오늘 밤 두 사내가 같은 길 위에서, 한 리를 사이에 두고 운다. 어느 쪽도 상대에게 그 얘기를 꺼내지 않을 것이다.

blocks.html: To answer Kangrim, Seohyun has to go back to a road, a gate, and a young man who got lost on purpose…!
blocks.ko: 강림에게 대답하려면 서현은 돌아가야 한다. 길 하나, 대문 하나, 그리고 일부러 길을 잃었던 젊은이에게로…!

logline.en: Before there is a Yushin there is a road, and a man on it who should be looking where he is going.
logline.ko: 유신이 있기 전에 길이 있다. 그리고 그 길 위에, 앞을 보고 다녀야 할 사내가 하나 있다.

Faces stay clean webtoon ink line with fierce narrowed eyes. Full-bleed single frame: NO panel borders, NO speech bubbles, NO onomatopoeia or sound-effect lettering, NO text of any kind. Look: Young Sacred-Bone noblewoman, oval face, strong dark brows, amused knowing eyes, a stubborn chin; long black hair in a low coiled chignon with a plain gold pin. Dress: Rich plum-violet silk chima with a pale ivory jeogori and a deep plum ribbon; good silk she will ruin in the rain. Demeanor: Teasing, decisive, braver than the men around her; she makes the decisions and lets Seohyun think he did. #c98bb9 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. Dawn at the timber gate of a small wooden-walled county house on Silla's northern road. Medium two-shot, low three-quarter. ONE device: the gate's dark post-and-lintel framing them. Kim Seohyun, FACE ONLY from his attached portrait, standing close behind his son, both hands at the back of the boy's head retying the hwarang headband too tight, brows knotted, lips pressed. Young Kim Yushin, fifteen, FACE ONLY from the attached hwarang portrait, beardless, crescent-moon headband across his brow, standing stiff, eyes rolled up and sideways, enduring it. A saddled horse waits beyond the gate in pale road mist. In the doorway behind, in soft focus, his mother watches with her arms folded, face in shadow. Key: a low cold dawn break raking across both faces and the silk; Silla blue #2A5FB8 in the headband tails. CANON — KIM SEOHYEON — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_seohyun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). As a hwarang he keeps the crescent-moon headband across the brow, its tails trailing; the jougwan sits on the crown of the head above it. Now: Hwarang years (stage portrait): BEARDLESS, Silla-blue headband with a gold crescent moon, its tails trailing. Demeanor: Confucian: he STANDS — never sits in lotus. Weighs, counts, frowns at sums; tight jaw, rare dry half-smile. Grief shows as stillness, not tears. The most feared warrior in all of Samhan: a line goes quiet when the tall Silla helm and the white horse appear. Massive, deliberate, terrifying at a walk; by Hwangsan (65) heavier and slower than Gyebek but still the man armies are built around. #2A5FB8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. Now: Young official in his twenties, CLEAN-SHAVEN, no beard or moustache: steel-blue silk po, white collar, dark sash, jougwan cap over a loose topknot with long loose strands. Colour #3E8EF0. MANMYUNG — Look: Young royal Kim noblewoman whose face runs in the family: mostly her granddaughter Gotaso's (oval face, bright almond eyes, small nose, cheerful sly mouth) with a touch of her daughter Munhee's long jaw and arched brows; one eyebrow up, a closed-mouth smirk. Black hair in a high round bun with loose strands at the temples, one gold binyeo with a red bead, small gold hoop earrings. Dress: Short white silk jeogori with deep crimson collar ribbon and cuffs, long deep-crimson chima with a gold-embroidered waistband, a pale celadon-green shawl; good silk she will ruin in the rain. Colour #c98bb9. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.

images.at: The hut has a roof, mostly, and a cold hearth
images.alt: No wedding anyone was invited to.
