blocks.html: Yushin has carried his father’s stone in his sleeve for thirty years, and it has never once been warm. Before light on the ninth day, on the road back from his father’s house, it is.
blocks.ko: 유신이 아버지의 돌을 소매에 넣고 다닌 지 서른 해, 한 번도 따뜻했던 적이 없다. 아홉째 날 동트기 전, 아버지 집에서 돌아오는 길에, 돌이 따뜻하다.

blocks.label: The cavern under the hill · before light
blocks.ko: 언덕 아래 동굴 · 동트기 전

blocks.html: The one room in Silla where nobody asks him for a victory. This morning it has guests.
blocks.ko: 신라에서 아무도 그에게 승리를 요구하지 않는 단 하나의 방. 오늘 새벽엔 손님이 있다.

blocks.html: So Yushin goes to the cavern lake, as if habit could hold a country together. He leaves the young grey shivering at the mouth, his sword and his clothes on the rock lip, and wades in to the chest.
blocks.ko: 그래서 유신은 습관이 나라를 붙잡아 주기라도 할 것처럼 동굴 호수로 간다. 어린 회색 말은 어귀에 떨게 두고, 칼과 옷은 바위턱에 두고, 가슴까지 물에 들어간다.

blocks.html: The three sisters are on the far rock. For once nobody says anything. Golhwa doesn’t even look at his waist, which has never happened, and he is too tired to notice that it hasn’t.
blocks.ko: 세 자매는 저쪽 바위에 있다. 웬일로 아무도 입을 열지 않는다. 골화가 그의 허리를 쳐다보지도 않는다. 처음 있는 일인데, 그는 너무 지쳐서 그걸 알아채지도 못한다.

blocks.html: He washes his hands. Then he washes them again.
blocks.ko: 그는 손을 씻는다. 그리고 또 씻는다.

en: Turtle, turtle, show your head…
Mm. How does the rest go, now?

blocks.html: Yushin turns so fast the water slaps the rock. A man is sitting on the lip beside his sword, where nobody was a moment ago: purple silk, a little gold crown worn like a joke he is in on, feet in the water, humming. You have met him. Yushin hasn’t.
blocks.ko: 유신이 어찌나 빨리 돌아서는지 물이 바위를 친다. 방금까지 아무도 없던 그의 칼 옆 바위턱에 사내 하나가 앉아 있다. 보랏빛 비단, 혼자만 아는 농담처럼 걸친 작은 금관, 물에 담근 발. 흥얼거리고 있다. 당신은 이 사내를 만난 적이 있다. 유신은 없다.

en: Who’s there?
Hm? No, no. Wrong way round, you’ve got it.
Who are you?
…I am Kim Yushin. General of—

blocks.html: He stops on the last word as if it were a step that isn’t there.
blocks.ko: 마지막 말 앞에서 그는 멈춘다. 있어야 할 계단이 없는 것처럼.

en: …of Silla.
Hm…
Why the hesitation, then?
…Some people still don’t think I belong to this country.
lines: …아직도 내가 이 나라 사람이 아니라는 이들이 있소.

en: Do you?
Bidam says I was never—
No, no, not asking what Bidam thinks, am I.
Do you?
lines: 아이다, 아이다, 비담 생각 묻는 기 아이요.

en: …How did you know about our conversation?
Are you a spirit as well?
…Something like that.

blocks.html: He says it with the old southern music on every vowel, unashamed. Yushin hasn’t heard it said out loud since he was seven, and he heard it last night.
blocks.ko: 그는 모음마다 옛 남쪽 가락을 실어, 부끄럼 없이 말한다. 유신은 일곱 살 이후로 그 말씨를 소리 내어 들은 적이 없다. 어젯밤만 빼고.

en: You talk like Gaya.
My father told me never to talk like that.
lines: 아버지가 나더러 절대 그렇게 말하지 말라 하셨소.

en: Did he! Good for him.
And did it work, then?
…Mostly.
Mostly, is it!

blocks.html: The stranger laughs until he has to hold on to the rock. Four hundred years dead, and still the best audience in the cave.
blocks.ko: 사내는 바위를 붙잡아야 할 만큼 웃는다. 죽은 지 사백 년인데, 아직도 이 동굴에서 제일 잘 웃어 주는 관객이다.

en: So. Came down here with a question, you did.
Ask it, then.
Not of a stranger.
A stranger, is it! In this water?

blocks.html: He nudges the sword beside him with one wet toe. The little fish in its pommel ring turns over in the lamplight.
blocks.ko: 그는 젖은 발가락으로 옆에 놓인 칼을 쿡 찌른다. 자루 머리 고리 속의 작은 물고기가 불빛에 뒤집힌다.

en: Made of what, this is?
Iron.
Whose iron?
…Gaya’s. Everyone’s is. Gaya had the mines.
lines: …가야 쇠요. 다들 그렇소. 광산이 가야에 있었으니.

en: Hm! And cuts for Silla, it does.
Mind, does it, the iron?
Iron doesn’t mind anything.
Then why do you, cariad?

blocks.html: Yushin opens his mouth. Nothing he owns fits in it.
blocks.ko: 유신이 입을 연다. 가진 말 중에 맞는 게 없다.

en: Look down, now.

blocks.html: Yushin looks down. The water has gone still as lacquer. There is only his own face in it, older than he thinks of it, with grey at the temple.
blocks.ko: 유신이 내려다본다. 물이 옻칠처럼 잔잔해졌다. 거기엔 제 얼굴뿐이다. 그가 생각하는 것보다 늙었고, 관자놀이가 희끗하다.

en: It’s only me.
Only! Small, you make it sound.
Look harder, bach.

blocks.html: He looks harder. Steam crosses the water, and the face in it isn’t quite his any more. The beard is wrong. The eyes are older than any he has met in a mirror. When he looks up to say so, the rock is empty. There is only the sword, and wet prints where nobody was sitting.
blocks.ko: 더 자세히 본다. 김이 물 위를 지나가고, 물속의 얼굴이 더는 온전히 제 것이 아니다. 수염이 다르다. 눈은 그가 거울에서 본 어떤 눈보다 늙었다. 그 말을 하려고 고개를 드니 바위가 비어 있다. 칼 한 자루, 그리고 아무도 앉지 않았던 자리의 젖은 발자국뿐.

en: Stand in the water the way I did, you do.
Weight on the back foot. Ready to leave.
lines: 물에 서 있는 꼴이 내캉 똑같네.
뒷발에 무게 싣고. 언제든 떠날 사람맨치로.

blocks.html: The voice is behind him. Yushin turns. An old soldier stands where the rock shelves into black, a cone helm under his arm, and it is the face from the water.
blocks.ko: 목소리는 등 뒤에서 온다. 유신이 돌아선다. 바위가 검은 물로 꺾이는 곳에 늙은 군인 하나가 고깔 투구를 옆구리에 끼고 서 있다. 물속의 그 얼굴이다.

en: …Have we met?
You look—
Yushin, my beloved grandson.

blocks.html: The pause after it is long. Muryuk was always a man of long pauses. The histories never had the room.
blocks.ko: 그 뒤의 침묵이 길다. 무력은 늘 침묵이 긴 사람이었다. 사서에 그걸 적을 자리가 없었을 뿐.

en: …Grandfather.
A prince I was, once. The youngest of three, in a cart going north.
My brothers watched the road ahead. I looked back.
lines: 나도 한때는 왕자였다 아이가. 셋 중 막내로, 북쪽으로 가는 수레에 타고.
형들은 앞길을 봤제. 나는 뒤를 돌아봤고.

en: …The surrender.
A general, then, for the people who owned the road.
I sat a king on a camp stool for them. I talked the last gate of Gaya open for them.
lines: 그 담엔 장수였제. 그 길 주인들을 위한.
그들을 위해 임금 하나를 군막 걸상에 앉혔고, 가야의 마지막 성문을 말로 열었다.

blocks.html: Somebody called him a traitor for each of those. He doesn’t say who. His grandson has just had six nights of it.
blocks.ko: 그 하나하나마다 누군가는 그를 역적이라 불렀다. 누가 그랬는지는 말하지 않는다. 손자가 방금 엿새 밤을 그 소리를 들었으니.

en: Why?
When I swore allegiance to the Silla crown, it was not for my own sake, but for yours.
lines: 내가 신라 왕실에 충성을 맹세했을 때, 그것은 나 자신을 위해서가 아니라 — 너를 위해서였다.

en: You never met me. I wasn’t even born.
lines: 저를 보신 적도 없잖습니까. 태어나지도 않았는데.

en: I loved you before I knew you.
lines: 나는 너를 알기 전에 너를 사랑했다.

blocks.html: Yushin looks at the water, because it is easier.
blocks.ko: 유신은 물을 본다. 그게 쉬우니까.

en: Yushin, look at me.
I am so, so proud of you…!

blocks.html: Behind the old man the steam stirs again. A third man comes out of it barefoot, in the night-robe he died in a few hours ago, peering about like a guest who has walked into the wrong banquet.
blocks.ko: 노인 뒤에서 김이 다시 일렁인다. 세 번째 사내가 맨발로 걸어 나온다. 몇 시간 전 숨을 거둘 때 입었던 잠옷 차림으로, 잔치를 잘못 찾아온 손님처럼 두리번거리며.

en: Father, you said wait by the— I wasn’t sure which rock you—
…Ah.
lines: 아버지, 기다리라 하신 데가— 어느 바위인지 몰라서—

en: Father.

blocks.html: Yushin goes through the water at him. He throws his arms around his father, and they close on steam. He tries again. Steam. The Marshal of Silla is crying in front of three goddesses and two dead men, and he doesn’t stop to mind.
blocks.ko: 유신이 물을 헤치고 그에게 간다. 아버지를 끌어안는데, 두 팔이 김을 안는다. 다시 해 본다. 김. 신라의 대장군이 여신 셋과 죽은 사내 둘 앞에서 울고 있고, 그는 그걸 개의치도 않는다.

en: No— no, don’t, son. It doesn’t work.
I tried it on your grandfather an hour ago. Nearly drowned. And I’m already dead.
lines: 아니— 아니다, 그러지 마라. 안 된다.
나도 아까 네 할아버지한테 해 봤다. 물에 빠져 죽을 뻔했어. 이미 죽었는데도.

en: Look at him — he’s crying.

blocks.html: She says it to the rock wall, so nobody can see her face.
blocks.ko: 골화는 그 말을 바위벽에 대고 한다. 아무도 제 얼굴을 못 보게.

en: You didn’t finish.
Last night. You were saying something and you didn’t—
I know. I never was much good at the end of things.
Yushin, my beloved son.
You were the light of my life, and now the nation needs you to be its savior.
lines: 너는 내 인생의 빛이었고, 이제 나라는 네가 구원자가 되기를 필요로 한다.

en: I am sorry that I was not of Silla blood… I tried my hardest to forget my Gaya roots, and tried to pretend that I was something I was not.
lines: 미안하다… 내가 신라의 피가 아니어서. 가야의 뿌리를 잊으려 애썼고, 내가 아닌 무언가인 척하려 했다.

en: The vowels.
You made me say them till I cried.
I know. I know.
But you don’t need to do that anymore.
lines: 하지만 너는 더 이상 그렇게 할 필요가 없다.

en: Son, you are the mighty Sword of Silla, and the Last Prince of Gaya.
But you are infinitely more than that…!
You are my son. You are Kim Yushin.
lines: 아들아, 너는 강력한 신라의 도검이며, 가야의 마지막 왕자이기도 하다.
그러나 너는 그보다 무한히 더 크다…!

blocks.html: He leans in, close enough that his breath ought to stir the steam, and it doesn’t. It is the same lean as last night, by the bed.
blocks.ko: 그가 몸을 기울인다. 숨결이 김을 흔들어야 할 만큼 가까이. 김은 흔들리지 않는다. 어젯밤 침상 곁에서와 똑같은 기울기다.

en: Yushin. What I was saying.
No matter what you do…

blocks.label: The cavern mouth · first light
blocks.ko: 동굴 어귀 · 첫새벽

blocks.html: Yushin comes up out of the cavern into first light with his hair still wet and the stone gone cold again in his fist. Whatever his father said after that, he tells nobody. You’ll hear it. Not yet.
blocks.ko: 유신이 젖은 머리로, 다시 식어 버린 돌을 주먹에 쥐고 첫새벽 속으로 동굴을 나온다. 아버지가 그 뒤에 무슨 말을 했는지는 아무에게도 말하지 않는다. 당신은 듣게 될 것이다. 아직은 아니다.

blocks.html: Hansul is waiting at the mouth, shivering. Across the valley the Radiance wall is grey with morning and already black with banners. Yushin mounts and rides at it. One more day of this. Then one more morning, and Bidam.
blocks.ko: 한슬이 어귀에서 떨며 기다린다. 골짜기 건너 명활성 성벽은 아침빛에 잿빛이고, 벌써 깃발로 검다. 유신은 말에 올라 그쪽으로 달린다. 하루만 더. 그리고 아침 한 번 더, 그리고 비담.

blocks.label: The Outer Works
blocks.ko: 외성

blocks.html: Yushin is back at the palace gate by mid-morning. Chunchu is out of his chair before the guards have finished saluting.
blocks.ko: 유신은 오전 중에 궁문으로 돌아온다. 위병들이 경례를 다 마치기도 전에 춘추가 의자에서 일어나 있다.

en: Your hair’s wet.
Bring the drums up.
Where’ve you been?
With my father.
…How is he?
Bring the drums up.

blocks.html: Chunchu looks at him one breath longer than a friend should. Then he sends for the drums.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 친구로서 봐도 될 만큼보다 한 숨 더 오래 그를 본다. 그러고는 북을 가져오라 이른다.

blocks.html: By midday the ninth day has turned into the battle both sides spent eight days pretending they could avoid. The palace blue goes up the road to the outer works under the Radiance wall, and the black comes down off the rampart to throw it back. From the Moon Palace it looks like two rivers trying to go through one gate.
blocks.ko: 한낮이 되자 아홉째 날은, 양쪽이 여드레 동안 피할 수 있는 척했던 싸움이 된다. 궁의 푸른 띠가 길을 따라 명활성 아래 외성까지 밀고 올라가고, 검은 띠가 성벽에서 쏟아져 내려와 그것을 밀어낸다. 월성에서 보면 강 두 줄기가 문 하나를 한꺼번에 지나려는 것 같다.

blocks.speaker: In the outer ditch
en: Ladders! Ladders left—
Whose left?!
GAYA! GAYA DOG!
Don’t stop on them, don’t stop on the bodies, keep—
Blue’s over the second ditch! BLUE’S OVER—
lines: 밟고 서지 마라, 시체 위에 서지 마라, 계속—

blocks.html: Bidam still walks the rampart past the outer ditch every night, and every night he stops where Yumjong fell. Yumjong’s black headband hangs from his wrist now. He has stopped explaining it to anyone.
blocks.ko: 비담은 여전히 밤마다 바깥 도랑 앞 성가퀴를 걷고, 밤마다 염종이 쓰러진 자리에서 멈춘다. 염종의 검은 두건은 이제 그의 손목에 걸려 있다. 누구에게도 설명하지 않는다.

blocks.html: By dusk the granary inside the Moon Palace is down to its last sacks, and men who have never prayed are learning the postures. Chunchu finds Alchun on the inner stair, where he has spent nine days standing exactly halfway between two walls.
blocks.ko: 해 질 무렵 월성 안 곳간은 마지막 섬만 남고, 기도해 본 적 없는 사내들이 무릎 꿇는 자세를 배운다. 춘추는 안쪽 계단에서 알천을 찾는다. 아흐레 동안 두 성벽 사이 딱 한가운데에 서 있던 자리다.

en: Alchun. The granary’s on its last sacks.
I need to know which wall you’re on before supper.
Supper. There’s a word.

blocks.html: Nobody laughs. On the yard it would have got one. The stair is not the yard.
blocks.ko: 아무도 웃지 않는다. 연무장이었으면 웃음이 터졌을 말이다. 계단은 연무장이 아니다.

en: Alchun.

lines: 나는 이 주를 살아남는 나라에 속한다.
그 답이 공허하다면 — 너희가 나중에 내게 줄 자리도 공허할 것이다.
en: I belong to the country that survives the week.
If that answer is empty — then so is the chair you will offer me afterward.

blocks.html: He still does not draw. Surabol will remember that sentence for years: the man who caught tigers, filed under Neither.
blocks.ko: 그는 끝내 칼을 뽑지 않는다. 서라벌은 그 문장을 오래 기억할 것이다. 호랑이를 잡던 남자, ‘어느 쪽도 아님’으로 분류되어.

blocks.label: The Rampart
blocks.ko: 성벽 위

blocks.html: That night, on Radiance’s rampart, Bidam speaks — to his officers, to the wall, to whichever chronicler is still awake. They expect a battle plan. They get a confession.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤, 명활성 성벽 위에서 비담이 말한다 — 장교들에게, 성벽에게, 아직 깨어 있는 사관에게. 그들은 작전을 기대한다. 돌아오는 것은 고백이다.

lines: 알겠느냐… 우리는 이 나라를 “신국”이라 부른다. 하지만 우리나라는 세상에서 가장 위대한 나라가 아니다.
그 왕들이 가장 지혜로운 것도 아니다. 그 군대가 가장 강한 것도 아니다.
그 남자들이 가장 고결한 것도, 그 여자들이 가장 정숙한 것도 아니다.
우리 산천은 아름답지만, 더 아름다운 경치는 다른 곳에 있다.
우리나라가 가진 좋은 것 하나마다, 더 큰 것을 가진 나라들이 있다.
en: You know… we call this country the “sacred country.” But our country isn’t the greatest in the world.
Its kings are not the most wise. Its armies are not the strongest.
Its men are not the most noble. Its women are not the most chaste.
Our natural scenery is beautiful, but there are more beautiful sights elsewhere.
For every good thing our nation has, there are other nations with greater things.

lines: 하지만 — 그래서 신국이라 부르는 것이 아니다.
en: However — that is not why we call it the sacred country.

lines: 우리가 신국이라 부르는 것은, 이 나라가 우리의 것이기 때문이다.
우리의 왕이 우리의 백성을 다스리기 때문이다. 우리의 군대가 우리의 아들들로 이루어져 있기 때문이다.
우리의 남자들이 매일 일어나, 내일을 오늘보다 낫게 만들려 하기 때문이다.
우리의 여자들이 매일 밤, 우리의 피와 씨로 다음 세대를 길러 냈음을 알고 잠들기 때문이다.
우리의 산과 강이, 우리가 어려서 함께 자란 곳이기 때문이다 — 아버지와 놀던 곳, 그리고 우리의 아들과 놀 곳.
en: We call it the sacred country, because it is ours.
Because our kings rule over our people. Because our armies are composed of our sons.
Because our men get up every day, and try to make the next day better.
Because our women go to sleep every night, knowing that they have raised our next generation with our blood and our seed.
Because our hills and rivers are the ones that we have grown up with as children — where we used to play with our fathers, and where we will play with our sons.
That is what I am defending.

lines: 왕실은 나를 반역자라, 이단자라, 시대에 맞춰야 할 늙은이라 부르겠지…
…그 모든 것에 나는 그저 아니라고 말한다.
en: The crown may call me a traitor, a heretic, an old man who needs to adapt to the times…
…and to all of that, I simply say no.
I don’t need to say any more than that.

lines: 그리고 언젠가, 우리의 후손들이 내가 옳았음을 증명할 것이다.
그러니 오라, 운명이여! 비담은 우리의 것을 지킬 준비가 되었다.
en: And one day, our descendants will prove me right.
So come at me, fate! Bidam is ready to defend what is ours.

blocks.label: The Gate
blocks.ko: 성문

blocks.label: DAY 10
blocks.ko: 열째 날

blocks.html: Before the gate opens Bidam goes down to the lines and saddles Bisamun himself, which a High Councillor does not do. He slips nine beads off the end of his string and knots them to the bridle, under the horse’s jaw.
blocks.ko: 성문이 열리기 전 비담은 진영으로 내려가 비사문에 손수 안장을 얹는다. 상대등이 할 일은 아니다. 염주 끝에서 아홉 알을 빼내, 말 턱 아래 굴레에 매듭지어 묶는다.

en: Sangdedung, those are…

lines: 부리는 짐승은 죽이지 마라. 말, 소, 닭, 개.
……저짝은 그저께 흰 말을 태웠제. 내가 지더라도 이놈은 누가 붙잡고 있어야 된다.
en: Master Wongwang’s fifth precept. Be choosy about killing.
Never the animals that work for you. Horse, ox, chicken, dog.
…They burned a white horse over there two nights ago. Even if I lose, somebody should still be holding on to this one.

blocks.html: Bisamun is named for the guardian king who stands at the north of every temple with a pagoda in his hand. Bidam rubs the horse’s nose once and speaks to it in the voice he keeps for sutras.
blocks.ko: 비사문은 탑을 손에 들고 모든 절의 북쪽에 서 있는 천왕에게서 따온 이름이다. 비담은 말의 코를 한 번 쓰다듬고, 경을 욀 때의 목소리로 말한다.

en: You’re named for the one who guards the north.
Today just watch the west.

blocks.html: All conditioned things are like a dream, an illusion, a bubble, a shadow; like dew, and like lightning. So should you see them.
blocks.ko: 모든 유위법은 꿈과 같고 환상과 같고 물거품과 같고 그림자와 같으며, 이슬과 같고 번개와 같으니, 마땅히 이와 같이 볼지니라.
blocks.hanja: 一切有為法，如夢、幻、泡、影，如露亦如電，應作如是觀。
blocks.source: Diamond Sutra (金剛般若波羅蜜經) §32, tr. Kumārajīva · T08n0235, p. 752b · Sanskrit: Vajracchedikā §32 (Conze ed.)
blocks.native: तारका तिमिरं दीपो मायावश्याय बुद्बुदम् । सुपिनं विद्युदभ्रं च एवं द्रष्टव्यं संस्कृतम् ॥
blocks.nativeLatn: tārakā timiraṃ dīpo māyāvaśyāya budbudam | supinaṃ vidyud abhraṃ ca evaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ saṃskṛtam ||

blocks.label: Between the Camps
blocks.ko: 두 진영 사이

blocks.html: On the tenth morning the grain is gone, and the palace gate opens from the inside, exactly as Bidam said it would. Out of it comes the Marshal of Silla at a gallop, on a grey horse that had no name the day before yesterday.
blocks.ko: 열째 날 아침, 곳간은 비었고, 궁문이 안에서 열린다. 비담이 말한 그대로다. 그 문에서 나오는 것은 신라의 대장군이다. 그저께까지 이름도 없던 회색 말을 타고, 질풍처럼.

blocks.html: Bidam rides out to meet him and stops halfway. He gets down, slaps Bisamun on the rump and sends him back to the lines. A spear’s length off, Yushin gets down too. They learned this on foot.
blocks.ko: 비담이 마주 나가다 중간에서 멈춘다. 말에서 내려 비사문의 엉덩이를 쳐 진영으로 돌려보낸다. 창 한 자루 거리에서 유신도 내린다. 둘은 이것을 땅에서 배웠다.

blocks.html: They meet again between the camps — not as High Councillor and marshal, but as the yard’s two best. Fish pommel against heavenly horse. The first exchanges are almost gentle. That is how Hwarang kill each other.
blocks.ko: 다시 진영 사이에서 만난다 — 상대등과 대장군이 아니라, 연무장의 두 최고로. 물고기 자루 머리와 천마. 처음 몇 수는 거의 다정하다. 화랑은 그렇게 서로를 죽인다.

blocks.html: The yard drill first. High guard, cut, step, return. Bidam is fifty-three and moves like it, until he doesn’t.
blocks.ko: 먼저 연무장 연습 그대로다. 높은 자세, 베기, 한 걸음, 제자리. 비담은 쉰셋이고 쉰셋처럼 움직인다. 그러지 않을 때까지는.

en: You still drop your left shoulder.
You still talk.

blocks.html: Bidam’s third cut is a feint and the fourth isn’t. It opens a line above Yushin’s brow, right where a Hwarang headband sits. Yushin’s hand goes to his forehead, the way a new boy’s does in the hall when the seniors start in on him.
blocks.ko: 비담의 셋째 칼은 허초이고, 넷째는 아니다. 그 칼이 유신의 이마 위, 화랑 머리띠가 앉는 바로 그 자리에 금을 긋는다. 유신의 손이 이마로 간다. 강당에서 선배들이 시비를 걸 때 새로 온 아이의 손이 그러듯.

blocks.html: Yushin steps inside the next cut, too close for either blade. Bidam’s bead string catches on the fish ring of his hilt. For one breath they are tied together at the wrist.
blocks.ko: 유신이 다음 칼 안쪽으로, 어느 칼도 쓸 수 없을 만큼 가까이 파고든다. 비담의 염주 줄이 유신 칼자루의 물고기 고리에 걸린다. 한 숨 동안 둘은 손목으로 묶여 있다.

en: …Let go, Gaya.
You let go.

blocks.html: Neither does. The string does instead, and ninety-nine beads go into the mud between their feet. Yushin’s back heel comes down on a handful of them, and the Marshal of Silla, who has not been knocked off his feet since he was a boy, goes over backwards.
blocks.ko: 둘 다 놓지 않는다. 대신 줄이 놓고, 아흔아홉 알이 두 사람 발 사이 진흙으로 쏟아진다. 유신의 뒤꿈치가 그중 한 줌을 밟고, 어려서 이후 한 번도 넘어진 적 없는 신라의 대장군이 뒤로 나자빠진다.

blocks.html: Bidam is on him before he finishes landing. A knee on the sword arm. The heavenly-horse blade up, point down, over the throat. Fifty-three, and for once he doesn’t move like it.
blocks.ko: 유신이 다 떨어지기도 전에 비담이 그 위에 있다. 칼 든 팔에 무릎. 천마 칼은 위로, 칼끝은 아래로, 목 위에. 쉰셋인데, 이번만은 쉰셋처럼 움직이지 않는다.

en: Say it.
Once in your life. Say “yield.”

blocks.html: Yushin never learned the word. The point starts down.
blocks.ko: 유신은 그 말을 배운 적이 없다. 칼끝이 내려오기 시작한다.

blocks.html: Steam. His father’s face an arm’s length away, no use to anybody’s arms, getting to the end of a sentence at last.
blocks.ko: 김. 한 팔 거리의 아버지 얼굴. 누구의 팔로도 안을 수 없는 그 얼굴이, 마침내 문장의 끝에 닿는다.

en: No matter what you do…
Look at me.
I am so, so proud of you…!

blocks.html: The point goes into the mud where his throat was. Yushin has rolled out from under the knee with the fish hilt still in his fist and the cut on his brow running into one eye. He comes up. He does not step back. He steps in.
blocks.ko: 칼끝이 방금까지 그의 목이 있던 진흙에 박힌다. 유신은 물고기 자루를 쥔 채 무릎 밑에서 굴러 나왔고, 이마의 상처에서 흐른 피가 한쪽 눈으로 들어간다. 그가 일어선다. 물러서지 않는다. 파고든다.

blocks.html: Yushin wins the way a man wins when he would rather lose — late, ugly, through a guard he taught Bidam twenty years ago. The heavenly-horse blade drops. Blood finds the mud that used to be a scoreboard.
blocks.ko: 유신은 차라리 지고 싶은 사람이 이기듯 이긴다 — 늦게, 흉하게, 이십 년 전 비담에게 가르친 가드를 뚫고. 천마 칼이 떨어진다. 피가, 한때 점수판이던 진흙을 찾는다.

blocks.html: The beads are still rolling when it’s over. They stop one at a time, in the blood, like somebody counting.
blocks.ko: 끝났을 때도 염주알들은 아직 구르고 있다. 핏속에서 하나씩 멈춘다. 누가 세기라도 하듯.

en: …One hundred and nine.
Finally.

blocks.html: Bidam smiles with blood in his teeth — the same boy who once offered a headband across a desk.
blocks.ko: 비담은 피에 젖은 이로 웃는다 — 한때 책상 너머로 머리띠를 건네던 그 아이.

en: Hwarang Kim Yushin…

blocks.html: Yushin does not move to finish it, and there is nothing left to finish. For as long as the breath lasts the two of them look at each other the way they used to across the yard, back when the score was even and neither one wanted to go home.
blocks.ko: 유신은 끝을 내려 움직이지 않고, 끝낼 것도 남아 있지 않다. 숨이 붙어 있는 동안 둘은 서로를 본다 — 점수가 비겼고 둘 다 집에 가기 싫던 시절, 연무장 건너로 보던 그 눈으로.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads his name three times where the body has not yet finished falling — Bidam. Bidam. Bidam. — the ledger catching up to the last word.
blocks.ko: 강림은 몸이 아직 완전히 쓰러지기 전 그의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 비담. 비담. 비담. — 마지막 말에 명부가 따라잡도록.

lines: 명부가 여기까지요. 함께 가십시다 — 폐하의 나라는 서라벌보다 회의록을 잘 남깁니다.
en: High Councillor.
Your list ends here. Walk with me — His Majesty’s kingdom keeps better minutes than Surabol.
One question, then we walk.
Were you a righteous traitor, or an unrighteous king?
…My father asked me that at a gate.
Write that I was his son.
Tell the sacred country I loved it badly.

lines: 검은 띠 매고 너무 오래 섰네
en: Son Bidam, beads go round;
a star fell down and he stood his ground.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Loved his country, loved it wrong,
tied the black band and stayed too long.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Traitor or king? Nobody knows;
his horse went north, and so he goes.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
blocks.title: Bidam of the Hundred and Eight Beads

blocks.caption: Bidam of the Son house, High Councillor of Silla. He loved the sacred country badly.
blocks.ko: 손씨 가문, 신라의 상대등 비담. 거룩한 나라를 서툴게 사랑했다.

blocks.html: Bisamun comes through the lines without a rider, at a walk, and stops over him. Nine beads swing under its jaw. When a Silla groom reaches for the bridle it lays its ears flat and shows him its teeth, and the groom, who has had a long ten days, steps back.
blocks.ko: 비사문이 주인 없이, 걸어서 대열을 지나와 그의 곁에 멈춰 선다. 턱 아래 아홉 알이 흔들린다. 신라 마부가 굴레에 손을 뻗자 말은 귀를 납작 젖히고 이를 드러내고, 열흘이 길었던 마부는 물러선다.

en: Leave it.
…Let it go. North.

blocks.html: Nobody asks him why north. The horse stands there until the body is taken, then turns and goes, past the Radiance wall and up the valley road, and afterwards the officers on the rampart cannot agree whether anyone opened the gate for it.
blocks.ko: 왜 북쪽이냐고 묻는 사람은 없다. 말은 시신이 옮겨질 때까지 서 있다가, 돌아서서 명활성 성벽을 지나 골짜기 길로 올라간다. 나중에 성벽 위의 장교들은 누가 그 말에게 문을 열어 주었는지를 두고 끝내 의견이 갈린다.

blocks.html: By then the Radiance wall is emptying. Black headbands go over the back of it and up the same valley road, and the palace blue goes up the slope after them.
blocks.ko: 그때쯤 명활성 성벽은 비어 가고 있다. 검은 머리띠들이 성 뒤로 넘어가 같은 골짜기 길로 달아나고, 궁의 푸른 띠가 비탈을 올라 그 뒤를 쫓는다.

blocks.speaker: A Hwarang
en: Marshal— the wall’s empty. They’re running up the valley.
Do we go after them?

blocks.html: Yushin kneels once, only to untie the black headband from the body. Then he stands, mud still wet, turns to the Hwarang behind him and names a house. Bidam’s own line. The one he carried in his jaw and never once claimed aloud.
blocks.ko: 유신은 한 번 무릎을 꿇는다. 시신에서 검은 머리띠를 풀기 위해서만. 그러고는 일어나, 진흙이 마르기도 전에 뒤따른 화랑들을 돌아보고 한 집안의 이름을 댄다. 비담의 핏줄. 비담이 턱 안에 물고 다니면서도 한 번도 입 밖에 내지 않은 그 핏줄.

en: Erase Bidam’s house.
The Son line, every one of them.
Treason’s blood must be cut.

lines: 비담은 죽었다. 열흘 동안 차를 따르고, 칼을 맞았다.
그의 대청까지 태우면 — 우리가 지키려던 육촌 중 하나를 스스로 지운다.
en: Yushin…
Bidam is dead. He poured tea for ten days, then took the blade.
If you burn his hall — we erase one of the Six Elders with our own hands.

blocks.html: Yushin leans close — close enough that the officers hear only breath, and Alchun hears the sentence.
blocks.ko: 유신이 몸을 기울인다 — 장교들에게는 숨소리만 들릴 만큼, 알천에게는 문장이 들릴 만큼.

en: Blood is inevitable…

blocks.html: Alchun goes pale. Down the line an officer asks for the order to be repeated. Nobody repeats it. Yushin mounts, and the order stands.
blocks.ko: 알천의 얼굴이 창백해진다. 대열 저쪽에서 한 장교가 명령을 다시 내려 달라 청한다. 아무도 되풀이하지 않는다. 유신이 말에 오르고, 명령은 선다.

blocks.html: Somewhere behind the palace wall, the queen is already slipping away.
blocks.ko: 궁 담장 너머 어딘가에서, 여왕은 이미 떠나가고 있다.

blocks.label: The Queen
blocks.ko: 여왕

blocks.label: The Queen’s Bedside
blocks.ko: 여왕의 머리맡

blocks.html: Rain finds the lattice before the physicians do. It is a small rain. It beads on the marshal’s sleeve and on the queen’s mouth, and neither of them has a hand free for it.
blocks.ko: 의원보다 비가 먼저 창살에 닿는다. 작은 비다. 원수의 소매에, 여왕의 입술에 맺힌다. 둘 다 그 비를 닦을 손이 없다.

en: Your Majesty.
General.
The physicians are in the corridor.
I told them the rain can wait.

lines: 작은 비야. 나를 데려갈 비는 아니네.
en: Leave them.
It is a small rain. It will not be what takes me.
Your Majesty—
The year I took the crown. You remember.
You said you would serve me to the end.
“I will serve you to the end.”
Yes.
And here we are.
Did I not promise to stay to the last moment.
You did. General.

lines: 네가 연무장에서 셈을 놓치던 때, 나는 공주였어.
en: …Princess.
Say it the old way.
When you lost the count on the yard, I was a princess.
Hwarang. That is what I was.
A hwarang who lost one count.
You do not lose counts.
I lost one.
Which one, I will not say.
Then stop being a general about it.
Dukman.
…Don’t.
Since the vote I have been Majesty.
Say the name I had before the room.
Dukman.
Yushin.
I am here.
I know.
Stay.
I can do a little rain.

blocks.html: The rain keeps on, small, on the lattice and on his sleeve. Her hand stays in his until it does not. The escort waits until the marshal’s hands have finished their work.
blocks.ko: 비는 그대로다. 창살에, 그의 소매에, 작게. 그녀의 손은 그의 손 안에 있다가, 어느 순간 아니게 된다. 호위는 원수의 손이 일을 마칠 때까지 기다린다.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads her name three times — Dukman. Dukman. Dukman. — the ledger’s habit before a Sacred Bone line closes.
blocks.ko: 강림은 그녀의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 덕만. 덕만. 덕만. — 성골의 혈통이 닫히기 전 명부의 버릇대로.
blocks.art: One panel: the ledger closing in Kangrim’s hands, rain on the lattice behind.

blocks.html: The ministers did not know where that was, and asked, “Where?” The queen said, “South of Mount Nang.” On that very month and day the queen did die, and the ministers buried her on the sunny slope of Mount Nang.
blocks.ko: 신하들이 그곳이 어디인지 몰라 “어디입니까?” 하고 아뢰니, 왕이 “낭산 남쪽이다.” 하였다. 그 달 그 날에 이르러 왕이 과연 세상을 떠나니, 신하들이 낭산 남쪽 기슭에 장사 지냈다.
blocks.hanja: 群臣罔知其處，奏云：「何所？」王曰：「狼山南也。」至其月日王果崩，群臣葬於狼山之陽。
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonders 1 — Queen Seondeok knows three things in advance (善德王知幾三事)

en: Kim Dukman, queen in gold,
“Ridiculous!” the old men scold.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Built a tower to talk to the stars,
heard winter frogs and found where they are.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Picked her grave on Mount Nang’s side,
and on the day she said, she died.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
blocks.title: Dukman, the Queen Who Read the Sky

blocks.caption: Queen Sunduk, the first queen of Silla. A queen? Ridiculous.
blocks.ko: 신라의 첫 여왕, 선덕. 여왕이라니, 웃기지.

blocks.html: That night Yushin remembers the first morning on the yard, and it is not the way he has been telling it.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 유신은 연무장의 첫 아침을 기억한다. 그것은 그가 말해 온 방식이 아니다.

blocks.html: The same desk. The same headband held out across it, still wet at the knuckle end.
blocks.ko: 같은 책상. 그 너머로 내밀어진 같은 머리띠. 주먹 닿은 끝은 아직 젖어 있다.

lines: 내 이름은 김유신! 신라의 대장군이 될 거요!!
en: It’s all right. I will overcome it myself.
My name is Kim Yushin! I will be the great general of Silla!!
Oh — and your name, hyung?
My name? Bidam.
That kid…. he’ll be someone great.

blocks.label: The Empty Pavilion
blocks.ko: 빈 정자

blocks.html: That night Yushin walks out alone to the pavilion between the old camp lines. The low table is still there, and on it the cup he never touched. He lays the black headband beside it and sits down across from no one.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 유신은 혼자 옛 진영 사이의 정자로 걸어 나간다. 낮은 상은 그대로 있고, 그 위에 그가 끝내 손대지 않은 잔이 있다. 그는 그 옆에 검은 머리띠를 내려놓고, 아무도 없는 맞은편을 두고 앉는다.
blocks.art: Wide: the empty pavilion at night, Yushin small at the low table, the untouched cup in front of him.

en: You Gaya wretch…!
blocks.art: Echo balloon over Yushin at the table; Bidam is not in the panel.

blocks.html: The one hand that said no is gone. Now the crown has to fit Sungman, and it was made for someone else…!
blocks.ko: 반대하던 단 한 손은 사라졌다. 이제 승만이 그 왕관을 써야 한다. 다른 사람에게 맞춰 만든 왕관을…!

logline.en: The crown was made for her cousin and has to be padded at the temples.
logline.ko: 왕관은 사촌에게 맞춰 만든 것이라, 관자놀이에 솜을 대야 한다.

images.alt: Queen Jinduk in crimson silk, gold unfinished-frame in the upper-right, wine void
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 poster. Queen Jinduk, last Sacred Bone queen of Silla, crowned before the blood dries. ONE geometric device: two thin gold lines meeting at a RIGHT ANGLE in the upper-right corner only — an unfinished frame, the rest of the picture open. Face matches the attached portrait: youthful East Asian woman, almond dark-brown eyes, long thick black hair falling over the shoulders (center part), tall Silla gold tree-antler crown with jade gogok, long gold tassel earrings. Isolated poster-scale body in the lower-left third. Deep wine void #7f1d1d as the plane. Striking silky crimson hanbok, one royal-blue shoulder plane, white inner collar, few hues, premium sheen, wide sleeves. Gold is the single accent. Flat wine-black void. No attendants. No banners. No palace clutter. No clouds. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental. NOT photoreal. NOT busy.

images.alt: Poster key art: newly crowned Queen Jinduk steps barefoot onto the washed yard and the white heavenly horse kneels before her through the censer smoke
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Grey dawn in the palace yard of Seorabeol, flagstones still wet where the blood was scrubbed, bronze censers trailing smoke. Low angle along the wet stones. INTERACTION: the wingless white heavenly horse Chunma kneels on its forelegs on the wet flagstones; Queen Jinduk, in her new gold Silla crown and violet-and-white royal silk, steps forward and rests both hands on its bowed head, her face grave and tired, accepting it. Their reflections lie together in the wet stone. CHUNMA HAS NO WINGS: a wingless white heavenly horse, bare white back and shoulders, nothing feathered anywhere; it rides the air on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs. One pale violet dawn break (#9d7bd0) through the smoke catches her crown, her hands and the horse’s mane; the yard and the halls behind sink into slate and ink. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.at: Sungman is crowned Queen Jinduk before the blood on the yard dries.
images.alt: The crown was made for her cousin and had to be padded at the temples.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. The same shot. Queen Jinduk, a mild woman in her forties, sits very still and does not fidget as the crown, padded at the temples, comes down. The spirit line behind her: Queen Sunduk nearest, newly dead, then King Jinpyung, then older kings. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = jinduk, SECOND face = sunduk (an ancestral spirit in the frame), THIRD face = jinpyung (an ancestral spirit in the frame). Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_moon_palace (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), jougwan feather-cap board (shape only, ignore labels), binyeo board jinduk (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing), binyeo board sunduk (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing), crown reference (shape only). QUEEN JINDUK — Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #9d7bd0. QUEEN SUNDUK — Look: Pale oval face, dark calm eyes; black hair in a full coiled updo; when crowned, the gold Silla tree-and-antler crown hung with jade gogok. Dress: Crimson court robe with gold phoenix brocade, blue embroidered cape-collar, a red ribbon bow at the chest. Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #E8552B. KING JINPYUNG Colour #5a86d6. PLACE Moon Palace (월궁) — attached board /pl_moon_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.

blocks.html: The crown was made for her cousin and has to be padded at the temples. Sungman sits very still while the goldsmith does it, because somebody told her once that Dukman never fidgeted, and she has believed it for forty years.
blocks.ko: 왕관은 사촌 언니에게 맞춰 만든 것이라 관자놀이에 솜을 대야 한다. 금장이 그 일을 하는 동안 승만은 꼼짝 않고 앉아 있다. 덕만은 한 번도 몸을 비튼 적이 없다고 누가 말해 준 적이 있고, 그녀는 마흔 해 동안 그 말을 믿어 왔다.

blocks.html: Sungman is crowned Queen Jinduk before the blood on the yard dries. The bloodline’s last polite miracle, stamped and filed while the censers are still warm. The succession Bidam died objecting to passes at last. Unanimously.
blocks.ko: 마서국의 피가 마르기도 전에 승만이 진덕여왕으로 즉위한다. 그 핏줄의 마지막 점잖은 기적, 향로가 식기도 전에 도장 찍혀 철해진다. 비담이 반대하다 죽은 계승이 마침내 통과된다. 만장일치로.

blocks.html: Taizong* of Tang sent an envoy bearing his tally to confer on the late queen the posthumous rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and to invest the new queen as Pillar of State and King of Lelang Commandery.
blocks.ko: 당 태종*이 사신에게 부절을 주어 보내, 앞 임금에게 광록대부를 추증하고, 이어 왕을 책봉하여 주국으로 삼고 낙랑군왕에 봉하였다.
blocks.hanja: 唐太宗遣使持節，追贈前王爲光祿大夫。仍冊命王爲柱國封樂浪郡王。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Jindeok, yr. 1 (647), 2nd month

notes.html: Taizong is the temple name Tang gave him after death. In this book he is the Second Emperor.
notes.ko: 태종은 죽은 뒤 받은 묘호다. 이 책에서는 ‘두 번째 황제’다.

blocks.hanja: 勝曼姿質豐麗，長七尺，垂手過膝。
blocks.html: Sungman was full-figured and beautiful, seven feet tall, and her hands hung down past her knees.
blocks.ko: 승만은 자태가 풍만하고 아름다웠으며, 키가 일곱 자에, 손을 내리면 무릎 아래까지 닿았다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — Queen Jindeok, accession notice

blocks.html: Alchun is not at the coronation. The court writes his absence down as illness. Everyone knows the illness’s name. It lasted ten days.
blocks.ko: 알천은 즉위식에 없다. 궁은 그의 부재를 병으로 적는다. 모두가 그 병의 이름을 안다. 그 병은 열흘을 갔다.

blocks.html: The court does not mean to compare. It simply cannot stop. The old Queen read the peony seeds before they were planted. She heard frogs at Jade Gate Pond in midwinter and sent two thousand men to the exact valley where five hundred Baekje soldiers were hiding. She named the day of her own death and was right about it. The new Queen is gentle, and good at a loom, and has never once predicted anything.
blocks.ko: 조정은 견주려는 게 아니다. 그냥 멈출 수가 없다. 선왕은 모란씨를 심기도 전에 읽어 냈다. 한겨울 옥문지에서 개구리 우는 소리를 듣고 이천 군사를 꼭 그 골짜기로 보내 숨어 있던 백제군 오백을 잡았다. 제가 죽을 날을 짚었고, 그 날이 맞았다. 새 여왕은 온화하고, 베틀을 잘 다루고, 무엇 하나 예언한 적이 없다.

lines: 선왕마마 같았으믄 비 올 줄 아셨을 낀데.
en: The old Queen would have known it was going to rain.
Shh.
…She would have, though.

blocks.html: After the rites, the new queen keeps two men behind. One of them has not had time to wash the mud off his boots.
blocks.ko: 의식이 끝나자 새 여왕은 두 사람을 남긴다. 그중 하나는 아직 신발의 진흙을 씻을 틈도 없었다.

en: Yushin… preserve the sacred country…
Bidam…

blocks.html: She does not finish the name. Everyone in Surabol has heard what Bidam called him by the end. Gaya. Never of Silla.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 이름을 끝까지 부르지 못한다. 비담이 끝에 그를 뭐라 불렀는지 서라벌에서 모르는 사람이 없다. 가야 놈. 신라 사람이었던 적도 없는 놈.

lines: 유신… 설마 비담의 말이 마음에 걸리느냐…?
en: Yushin… surely Bidam’s words are not weighing on you…?
No — what could there be to weigh on me.
I am a loyal servant of the sacred country.

blocks.html: He says it the way he says the oath on the yard, every word where it belongs. His right hand has closed on his sword belt and does not open. She grew up beside Dukman. She notices hands.
blocks.ko: 그는 연무장에서 맹세를 외듯 말한다. 단어 하나하나가 제자리에 있다. 오른손은 칼띠를 쥔 채 펴지지 않는다. 그녀는 덕만 곁에서 자랐다. 손을 볼 줄 안다.

en: Then let go of the belt, General.
Nobody here is going to draw on you.
lines: 여기서 자네한테 칼 뽑을 사람은 없네.

blocks.html: He lets go. It takes him a moment to remember how.
blocks.ko: 그가 손을 놓는다. 어떻게 놓는지 떠올리는 데 잠깐이 걸린다.

lines: 언니는 개구리보다 먼저 개구리를 알았네. 나는 비 올 날도 모르는데.
en: Chunchu.
Unni knew about the frogs before the frogs did. I can’t even tell when it’s going to rain.

lines: 전하, 누구도 달더러 해가 되라 하지 않습니다.
사람들이 달을 사랑하는 건 똑바로 쳐다보게 해 주기 때문이지요.
en: Majesty, nobody asks the moon to be the sun.
They love it because it lets them look straight at it.
…You had that ready.
Since the funeral, Majesty.

blocks.html: Then the border spoils the moment, the way borders do. A runner comes in still wearing the road. Baekje is over the western line again, three forts at once. The court turns to the new queen the way it used to turn to the old one, waiting for her to already know.
blocks.ko: 그때 국경이 이 순간을 망친다. 국경은 늘 그렇다. 길을 그대로 뒤집어쓴 전령이 들어온다. 백제가 또 서쪽 경계를 넘었다. 성 셋을 한꺼번에. 조정은 예전에 선왕을 보던 눈으로 새 여왕을 본다. 그녀가 이미 알고 있기를 기다리며.

en: I don’t know.
Unni would have dreamed it last week. I didn’t dream anything. I slept badly, that’s all.
lines: 언니였으면 지난주에 꿈으로 봤겠지. 나는 아무 꿈도 안 꿨어. 잠을 설쳤을 뿐이야.

en: Give me the men, Majesty. I’ll go.
I won’t need a dream to find three forts.
lines: 성 셋 찾는 데 꿈은 필요 없습니다.

en: He’ll win them back. He always does.
And next spring they’ll come for three more. And the spring after that.
Majesty, we can hold the door forever. We can’t make it stop knocking.
lines: 그리고 내년 봄이면 또 셋을 노리겠지요. 그다음 봄에도.
전하, 문은 영원히 막을 수 있습니다. 두드리는 걸 멈추게 할 수는 없지만요.

en: Then what stops it?
A bigger door.
One man alive has an army that size. He lost a summer at Ansi, and he hates losing.
Let me go west and ask him.
lines: 그만한 군대를 가진 사람은 세상에 하나뿐입니다. 안시에서 여름 한 철을 잃었고, 지는 걸 싫어하지요.
서쪽으로 가서 청해 보게 해 주십시오.

blocks.html: The old queen would have decided this with a smile, as if she had read it in the stars the night before. The new one has read nothing. She looks at Yushin’s hand, which is back on the belt. She looks at Chunchu, who has clearly had this ready since the funeral too.
blocks.ko: 선왕이었다면 전날 밤 별에서 읽기라도 한 듯 웃으며 정했을 일이다. 새 여왕은 아무것도 읽지 않았다. 그녀는 다시 칼띠로 돌아간 유신의 손을 본다. 춘추를 본다. 이 말도 장례 때부터 준비해 둔 게 분명한 얼굴이다.

en: Yushin, take the men.
Chunchu, go west.
…If you’re both wrong, I want to hear it from you. Not from a runner.
lines: ……둘 다 틀리거든, 전령 말고 자네들한테서 듣고 싶네.

blocks.html: Outside, it starts to rain. Nobody predicted it.
blocks.ko: 밖에 비가 내리기 시작한다. 아무도 예언하지 않은 비다.

en: …It’s raining.
Did anybody know?
Shh.

blocks.html: Nobody says a word about the old queen. For the maids, that is the coronation.
blocks.ko: 선왕 이야기는 아무도 꺼내지 않는다. 시녀들에게는 그게 즉위식이다.

blocks.html: At night she sits at a loom, because her hands want work that nobody will compare. Three years from now she will weave an ode to the Western emperor into a length of silk, and it will do more for Silla than any prophecy her cousin made. Nobody at court thinks to compare that.
blocks.ko: 밤이면 그녀는 베틀 앞에 앉는다. 누구도 견주지 않을 일을 손이 원해서다. 세 해 뒤 그녀는 서국 황제에게 바치는 송시를 비단 한 필에 짜 넣을 것이고, 그것이 사촌 언니의 어떤 예언보다 신라에 더 큰 일을 해낼 것이다. 조정의 누구도 그것은 견주어 볼 생각을 하지 않는다.

blocks.html: Silla needs an army. Only one man alive can lend it, and he has never lent anything for free. Chunchu goes west…!
blocks.ko: 신라에는 군대가 필요하다. 그것을 빌려줄 사람은 세상에 단 하나, 공짜로는 아무것도 빌려준 적 없는 사람이다. 춘추가 서쪽으로 간다…!

logline.en: Everyone on earth wants something from the Son of Heaven. Most of them bring tribute. Chunchu brings an offer.
logline.ko: 땅 위의 모든 이가 천자에게 바라는 것이 있다. 대개는 공물을 들고 온다. 춘추는 제안을 들고 온다.

images.alt: Wide two-hall plane: Silla blue bar and the Western gold bar across one wet floor
images.prompt: Wide cinematic EXPOSITION still, 16:9. Camera far back. REAL recognizable place. Wide two-hall plane: Silla blue bar and Tang gold bar across one wet floor Tiny silky hanbok figures, few hues, one accent. Flat sky, no clouds. Painterly cinema, not photoreal, not cartoon. No readable text, no watermark.

images.alt: Silla and the West hands clasped in alliance - blue and gold sleeves
Two small figures walking toward each other on a vast pale-gold empty hall — smiling, no kowtow
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 16:9 poster. Taizong and Kim Chunchu, two men alone. The Goguryeo warship's prow, from its board, has rammed it amidships. Tiny sailors leap. Fire on the black water is the only light. Huge smoke. Not a flat side diagram, not daylight. Boards are design only: ignore their bright daylight sky and calm sea, repaint the ship in the scene light. 7th-century timber ships only, never European hulls, cannon or funnels. Silla ship: plain broad timber hull with a low deck cabin, two masts with cream battened square sails, small blue Silla pennant. Smaller and lighter than the Goguryeo and Tang warships. Goguryeo warship: long high-sided timber hull with an oar-port gallery along the side, raised stern castle, three masts with cream battened sails, red Goguryeo banners at the stern. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject.
