images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Myth twin on the IDENTICAL layout of km-gildal-kneel: the man in the patched red coat in the right foreground is a huge red-furred fox seen from behind, red headband still tied, forelegs bent into the mud in a bow, white-tipped tail curling round the corner; the two goblins glow-eyed dokkaebi with blue smoke; Bihyung crouched mid-frame, human. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Reality twin on the IDENTICAL layout of bh-myth-ride-weeping: Bihyung weeping on horseback, and across his saddle not a fox but Gildal’s body, face-down in a torn orange robe, the fox mask slipping off his head, an arrow in his leg; no spirit swirls, plain moonlight and one lantern in a doorway. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #2f6fd4. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. blocks.html: Nobody kills the strange boy.
blocks.ko: 이상한 애는 아무도 안 죽인다.

blocks.html: His mother told him that when he was eight. She was right for seventy years, which is longer than most mothers get to be right about anything.
blocks.ko: 여덟 살 때 어머니가 해 준 말이다. 그 말은 일흔 해 동안 맞았다. 어머니들이 뭐가 됐든 맞는 기간으로는 꽤 긴 편이다.

blocks.html: You’ve heard the song. Now here is the same story with the lamps turned up. Same people. Same bridge. Same fox. It just has fewer ghosts in it, and more men.
blocks.ko: 노래는 들었을 것이다. 이제 같은 이야기를 등잔 심지 올리고 다시 해 보자. 같은 사람들. 같은 다리. 같은 여우. 귀신이 좀 줄고, 사람이 좀 늘었을 뿐이다.

blocks.label: The bluff over the river · the night of the lotuses
blocks.ko: 강 위 벼랑 · 연등 띄우던 밤

blocks.html: The palace ends at the bluff. Below it the river is black, and the paper lotuses go by one at a time, very small, on their way to the sea.
blocks.ko: 궁은 벼랑에서 끝난다. 그 아래 강은 검고, 종이 연꽃들이 하나씩, 아주 작게, 바다로 흘러간다.

lines: …저건 네 어미가 접은 거다. 모서리를 두 번 접거든.
en: There goes another one.
…Your mother folded that one. She does the corners twice.

lines: 아버지, 슬픔 얘기라면 전 괜찮아요. 전— 어머니가 시키셨죠. 그렇죠.
en: Father, if this is about grief, I’m fine. I’m— Mother asked you to. Didn’t she.

lines: 난 딴 얘기를 할 거다. 같은 얘기야. 좀 오래 걸렸을 뿐이지.
en: She did.
I’m going to talk about something else. It’s the same thing. It just took longer.

blocks.html: He looks down at the water for a long time, and his lips move. Chunchu has watched him talk to rivers all his life and has never once been close enough to hear. He is close enough now. His father is counting.
blocks.ko: 그는 오래도록 물을 내려다본다. 입술이 달싹인다. 춘추는 평생 아버지가 강에 말을 거는 걸 봐 왔지만, 들릴 만큼 가까이 있어 본 적은 한 번도 없다. 지금은 들린다. 아버지는 수를 세고 있다.

en: …Forty.
Right.
Chunchu, there are no goblins.
…What?

lines: 처음부터 없었다. 도깨비도, 혼령도, 말하는 개울도.
나 안 미쳤다. 미친 적 없어. 단 하루도.
en: There never were. No goblins, no ghost, no stream that talks.
I’m not mad. I’ve never been mad. Not for one day.

blocks.html: Chunchu laughs, because what else do you do. His father doesn’t.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 웃는다. 달리 어쩌겠는가. 아버지는 웃지 않는다.

blocks.label: The house by the stream · a night when Chunchu was seven
blocks.ko: 개울가 집 · 춘추가 일곱 살이던 어느 밤

blocks.html: He was seven. He woke in the dark and needed the privy, and stopped at his parents’ door because there was a voice behind it he didn’t know.
blocks.ko: 일곱 살이었다. 어둠 속에서 깨어 뒷간에 가다가, 부모 방 문 앞에서 멈췄다. 문 너머에서 모르는 목소리가 들렸다.

blocks.html: It was quick and plain and a little dry. It was adding grain against riders against roads, faster than his tutor could. His mother said something, and the voice laughed exactly on the beat.
blocks.ko: 빠르고, 꾸밈없고, 조금 메마른 목소리. 곡식과 사병과 길을 맞대어 셈하고 있었다. 그의 선생보다 빨랐다. 어머니가 뭐라 하자 그 목소리가 정확히 박자에 맞춰 웃었다.

blocks.html: In the morning his father was talking to the rafters again. Chunchu decided he had dreamed it. You can decide that at seven. It holds for about thirty years.
blocks.ko: 아침이 되자 아버지는 또 서까래와 얘기하고 있었다. 춘추는 꿈을 꾼 거라고 정했다. 일곱 살이면 그렇게 정할 수 있다. 그건 한 서른 해쯤 간다.

blocks.label: The bluff
blocks.ko: 벼랑

lines: …한 번 들었어요. 문 너머로. 어머니랑 셈을 하시다가, 박자에 맞춰 웃으셨어요.
en: …I heard you once. Through the door. You were doing sums with Mother, and you laughed on the beat.

lines: 넌 일곱 살이었다. 자는 줄 알았지.
en: You were seven. I thought you were asleep.
So did I.
Father, the whole city—

lines: 온 도성이 그렇게 믿으라고 한 거다.
en: The whole city was meant to.
Sit down. I won’t be able to say this twice.

blocks.html: Then he tells it, for the first time in his life, and badly, the way people tell the true things. I’ll tell it properly. I was there for most of it.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 이야기한다. 평생 처음으로, 서툴게. 사람들이 참말을 할 때 늘 그렇듯이. 제대로는 내가 들려주겠다. 나는 거의 다 거기 있었으니까.

blocks.label: Jinji
blocks.ko: 진지

blocks.label: The palace · the Cloud King’s last night
blocks.ko: 궁 · 구름왕의 마지막 밤

blocks.html: The Cloud King dies in a monk’s robe. His second son Saryun kneels by the bed smelling of plum wine, with his dead brother’s boy Baekjung asleep across his knees.
blocks.ko: 구름왕이 승복을 입고 죽는다. 둘째 아들 사륜이 매실주 냄새를 풍기며 침상 곁에 무릎을 꿇고, 그 무릎엔 죽은 형의 아들 백정이 잠들어 있다.

blocks.label: The eastern hills · the Cloud King’s tomb
blocks.ko: 동쪽 언덕 · 구름왕의 무덤

blocks.html: They bury him under a hill a thousand men build in a month. At the top the new king turns, looks at all of it, and asks for a cup.
blocks.ko: 천 명이 한 달 걸려 쌓은 언덕 아래 그를 묻는다. 꼭대기에서 새 임금은 돌아서서 그 모든 걸 내려다보고, 잔을 달라고 한다.

blocks.label: The Harmony Council · three days later
blocks.ko: 화백회의 · 사흘 뒤

blocks.html: Three days later six old men vote, and a boy named Eulje writes the new king’s name in the minutes. Saryun is crowned Jinji. Remember the boy’s face.
blocks.ko: 사흘 뒤 늙은이 여섯이 표결하고, 을제라는 소년이 새 임금의 이름을 회의록에 적는다. 사륜은 진지왕이 된다. 그 소년의 얼굴을 기억해 두라.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace · the wine years
blocks.ko: 월성 · 술의 해들

blocks.html: He tries, for one winter. Then the forts start falling, the Moon Palace fills with lantern boats and dancers, and the Council’s reports wait outside a shut door.
blocks.ko: 그는 한 해 겨울은 애쓴다. 그러다 성들이 떨어지기 시작하고, 월성은 등불 띄운 배와 춤꾼들로 가득 차고, 화백의 보고는 닫힌 문 밖에서 기다린다.

blocks.html: The parties don’t stay inside the palace. Twice a month he opens the Moon Palace gate and feeds the city: rice, wine, a pig on a spit, Saryang ward eating off silver it will never see again.
blocks.ko: 잔치는 궁 안에만 머물지 않는다. 한 달에 두 번 그는 월성 문을 열고 도성을 먹인다. 쌀, 술, 꼬챙이에 꿴 돼지 한 마리. 사량부 사람들이 다시는 구경도 못 할 은그릇에 밥을 먹는다.

blocks.html: The rice is the Council’s, more or less. One feast night he climbs onto a table and announces a new levy on the True Bone estates, one sack in ten, for the city. He hasn’t asked anyone. The applause is enormous.
blocks.ko: 쌀은 대충 화백의 것이다. 어느 잔칫날 밤 그는 상 위에 올라서서 진골 장원에 새 세를 매긴다고 외친다. 열 섬에 한 섬, 도성 몫으로. 아무에게도 묻지 않았다. 박수 소리가 어마어마하다.

en: Eat! It’s the Council’s rice.
Don’t worry about them. Look at them. They’ve never missed a meal in their lives.
lines: 그 양반들 걱정은 마. 봐라. 평생 끼니 한 번 거른 적 없는 얼굴들이다.

blocks.html: He is a bad king and a generous drunk, and a city can love both. Saryang ward loves him. Saryang ward also writes the songs.
blocks.ko: 그는 형편없는 임금이고 인심 좋은 술꾼이다. 도성은 둘 다 사랑할 수 있다. 사량부는 그를 사랑한다. 노래를 짓는 것도 사량부다.

blocks.label: The throne hall · after midnight
blocks.ko: 정전 · 자정 넘어

blocks.html: One night after midnight the drunk king lifts his ten-year-old nephew onto the throne, and the musicians stop. Then he carries the boy back to bed and ties back his sleeves so he won’t trip. Remember the sleeves.
blocks.ko: 어느 날 자정 넘어 술 취한 임금이 열 살 조카를 왕좌에 올려 앉히고, 악사들이 멈춘다. 그러고는 아이를 안아다 재우며, 밤에 걸려 넘어지지 않게 소매를 묶어 준다. 그 소매를 기억해 두라.

blocks.label: Saryang ward · the king’s summons
blocks.ko: 사량부 · 임금의 부름

blocks.html: In Saryang ward there is a woman so lovely the neighbours call her the peach blossom. Her name is Dohwa. She is married to a man who sells charcoal, and she likes him.
blocks.ko: 사량부에 이웃들이 복숭아꽃이라고 부를 만큼 고운 여인이 산다. 이름은 도화. 숯 파는 사내의 아내이고, 그 사내를 좋아한다.

blocks.html: The king hears about her the way kings hear about everything. By evening she is standing in his hall, still in her apron.
blocks.ko: 임금은 다른 모든 일을 듣는 식으로 그녀 이야기를 듣는다. 저녁이 되자 그녀는 앞치마도 못 벗은 채 그의 전각에 서 있다.

lines: 오늘 밤 있어라. 있고 싶은 만큼.
en: So you’re the peach blossom.
Stay tonight. Stay as long as you like.

lines: 여자는 남편이 하나예요. 둘은 안 돼요. 임금님이라도요.
en: I have a husband, Majesty.
A woman has one. Not two. Not even for a king.

lines: 그 말로 너를 죽일 수도 있다.
en: I could have you killed for that.
I know.
…Then kill me. I’d rather that than the other thing.

blocks.html: The hall goes very quiet. The musicians look at the floor. Somebody’s cup tips and nobody rights it.
blocks.ko: 전각이 아주 조용해진다. 악공들은 바닥만 본다. 누군가의 잔이 기울어지는데 아무도 세우지 않는다.

en: …And if you had no husband?
Would you come then?
Then, yes.

blocks.html: He laughs, really laughs, for the first time in a year. The song keeps that part, and so far the song is right.
blocks.ko: 그가 웃는다. 한 해 만에 처음으로, 진짜로. 노래는 거기까지 기억하고, 거기까지는 노래가 맞다.

en: Then go home, peach blossom.
It’s dark, and the gates are shut. Somebody give her a room. She leaves at first light.
lines: 날은 저물었고 문도 닫혔다. 누가 방 하나 내줘라. 날 밝으면 보내고.

blocks.html: A steward gives her a room off the back corridor, with one lamp and a lock that only works from outside. She doesn’t notice the lock. She is too busy being alive.
blocks.ko: 시종 하나가 뒤쪽 복도 옆 방을 내준다. 등잔 하나, 그리고 밖에서만 잠기는 자물쇠. 그녀는 자물쇠를 눈여겨보지 않는다. 살아 있다는 게 너무 바빠서.

blocks.html: She folds her apron and wraps her shoes in it, because the road home is mud. She is laughing a little, the way you do after a fall you didn’t take. By breakfast she’ll be home, telling her husband, and he won’t believe a word.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 앞치마를 개어 신발을 싼다. 집에 가는 길은 진창이니까. 조금 웃고 있다. 넘어질 뻔하고 안 넘어졌을 때처럼. 아침밥 때면 집에 가 있을 것이다. 남편한테 얘기할 것이고, 남편은 한마디도 안 믿을 것이다.

blocks.html: Some time after midnight, the lamp in the corridor moves.
blocks.ko: 자정이 지나고, 복도의 등불이 움직인다.

blocks.html: From the yard you can see the paper door. Two shadows on it. One of them is trying to get to the door. The other one is bigger.
blocks.ko: 마당에서는 종이 문이 보인다. 그림자 둘. 하나는 문 쪽으로 가려 한다. 다른 하나가 더 크다.

blocks.html: Nobody in the yard goes in. He is still the king.
blocks.ko: 마당의 누구도 들어가지 않는다. 그는 아직 임금이니까.

blocks.html: At first light they let her go home, as promised. Not by the gate she came in. A steward walks her out through the market gate, on foot, the long way, while the stalls are opening. She carries her shoes in her hand the whole way, her apron tied on wrong, and all of Saryang ward watches the peach blossom come home from the palace and decides what it means.
blocks.ko: 날이 밝자 약속대로 그녀를 집에 보낸다. 들어온 문이 아니다. 시종 하나가 그녀를 장터 문으로 데리고 나간다. 걸어서, 먼 길로, 가게들이 문을 여는 시각에. 그녀는 내내 신발을 손에 들고 간다. 앞치마는 거꾸로 매여 있다. 사량부 사람들 모두가 궁에서 돌아오는 복숭아꽃을 지켜보고, 그게 무슨 뜻인지 저마다 정해 버린다.

blocks.html: The song says he let her go home. He did. The song was written by people who liked him.
blocks.ko: 노래는 그가 그녀를 집에 보내 줬다고 한다. 보내 주긴 했다. 노래를 지은 건 그를 좋아하던 사람들이다.

blocks.label: The bluff
blocks.ko: 벼랑

lines: 왕관을 빼앗긴 그 임금. 내 아버지다.
혼령 말고. 그 사람. 살아 있고, 취해 있었고— 장터에서 어머니를 봤지.
en: The king they took the crown off. My father.
Not his ghost. Him. Alive, and drunk, and— he saw my mother at the market.
The peach blossom. She said no.

lines: 노래에선 그 사람이 웃고 집에 보내 줬다고 하지.
en: She said no.
The song says he laughed and let her go home.

blocks.html: He stops. The river goes by.
blocks.ko: 그가 멈춘다. 강물이 흘러간다.

en: He let her go home.
In the morning.

blocks.html: That is all he says about it, and all he will ever say. Chunchu is thirty-nine and has lived in palaces all his life. He doesn’t ask.
blocks.ko: 그 일에 대해 그가 하는 말은 그게 전부다. 앞으로도 그게 전부일 것이다. 춘추는 서른아홉이고, 평생 궁에서 살았다. 그는 묻지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Harmony Council · the night drum
blocks.ko: 화백회의 · 밤의 북

blocks.html: The drum on the palace wall is for fires and invasions. At midnight it beats for neither.
blocks.ko: 궁 담장 위의 북은 불이 났을 때와 적이 쳐들어왔을 때 친다. 그날 자정에 울린 북은 둘 다 아니다.

blocks.html: The councillors come through the dark in whatever they were sleeping in. One of them is carried. Geochilbu has been dying since spring. He insists on a litter, and coughs into a cloth all the way, because he was in the room that crowned this king and means to be in the one that uncrowns him.
blocks.ko: 대등들이 자다 입은 차림 그대로 어둠을 뚫고 온다. 하나는 실려 온다. 거칠부는 봄부터 죽어 가고 있다. 그는 기어이 가마에 실려 오며 내내 천에 대고 기침을 한다. 이 임금을 세운 방에 있었으니, 끌어내리는 방에도 있겠다는 것이다.

blocks.html: The summons came from the queen mother. Nobody says that out loud either.
blocks.ko: 부름은 대비에게서 왔다. 그 말도 아무도 입 밖에 내지 않는다.

lines: 왜 불렀는지는 다들 알 걸세. 내가 말하지. 나중에 아무도 모른 척할 수 없게.
내 아들은 세 해째 성치 않네. 나라는 그 애가 나을 때까지 기다려 줄 수가 없어.
en: You all know why I sent for you. I’ll say it, so nobody has to pretend later.
My son has not been well for three years. The country cannot wait for him to get better.

blocks.speaker: A councillor
lines: 마마— 화로가. 아직 푸르게 안 탔습니다.
en: Majesty— the brazier. It hasn’t turned blue.

lines: 난 숨이 없소. 젊은 사람 하나가 불어.
en: Then blow on it.
I haven’t the breath. One of you young ones.

blocks.html: Eulje is twenty-four. He kneels and blows on the coals until the flame turns, and when he picks up his brush his hand is already shaking. You have seen this room count. At midnight it counts faster.
blocks.ko: 을제는 스물넷이다. 그가 무릎을 꿇고 숯에 바람을 불어 불꽃을 푸르게 바꾼다. 붓을 집어 들 때 그의 손은 이미 떨리고 있다. 이 방이 셈하는 건 이미 보았다. 자정의 셈은 더 빠르다.

blocks.html: The song will say they deposed him for wine and women. Both are in the charge. Neither is what the room argues about.
blocks.ko: 노래는 술과 여자 때문에 그를 끌어내렸다고 할 것이다. 둘 다 죄목에 들어간다. 이 방이 다투는 건 둘 다 아니다.

en: Item. A levy on the True Bone estates. One sack in ten.
Announced at a banquet. From a table. It never came to this room.
lines: 하나. 진골 장원에 매긴 세. 열 섬에 한 섬.
잔치에서 정했소. 상 위에 올라서서. 이 방엔 한 번도 오지 않았고.

blocks.speaker: A councillor
en: Item. The same rice, given away at the palace gate.
To charcoal-sellers.
lines: 하나. 그 쌀을 궁문에서 나눠 줬소.

blocks.speaker: An old councillor
en: It was a bad year. He fed the city.
Is that the charge? That the city ate?
The charge is that he did it without us.
A king who can tax us at dinner can do anything he likes at breakfast.
lines: 저녁상에서 우리한테 세를 매길 수 있는 임금이면, 아침상에선 무슨 짓이든 할 수 있소.

en: Put the wives in the charge.
The city won’t understand a levy. It’ll understand the wives.
lines: 도성은 세금은 모르오. 아내들은 알 거요.

blocks.speaker: An old councillor
en: And then? Baekjung is eleven.
Eleven is a good age.
He listens.

blocks.html: The queen mother says nothing to that. She raised a son who never listened, and she has already done the sum.
blocks.ko: 대비는 그 말에 아무 대꾸도 하지 않는다. 말 안 듣는 아들을 키운 사람이다. 셈은 이미 끝냈다.

blocks.html: The old councillor holds his piece a long time. In this room one holdout is enough to save a king. He puts it with the others.
blocks.ko: 늙은 대등은 나무 조각을 오래 쥐고 있다. 이 방에서는 한 사람만 버텨도 임금을 살릴 수 있다. 그는 그것을 다른 조각들 곁에 놓는다.

blocks.html: Before the first count is cold, the door bangs open. The king has come from his party. He still has a cup in his hand and a dancer’s hairpin caught in his collar.
blocks.ko: 첫 셈의 온기가 가시기도 전에 문이 벌컥 열린다. 임금이 잔치에서 곧장 왔다. 손엔 아직 잔이 들려 있고, 옷깃엔 무희의 비녀가 걸려 있다.

en: You would unseat a Sacred Bone for a night’s rumour?

lines: 하룻밤이 아니다, 사륜아. 세 해 동안의 밤들이다.
en: Not for one night, Saryun. For three years of them.
Mother.
…You sent for them. You did.
A son can be forgiven, Saryun.
A king has to be useful.
Useful.
…It’s the rice, isn’t it. You can say it. It’s the rice.
Majesty. It is the wives.

blocks.html: Eulje writes down the wives. Of everything said that night, it is the only word that makes it into the record.
blocks.ko: 을제는 아내들이라고 적는다. 그날 밤 나온 말 가운데 기록에 남는 건 그 한마디뿐이다.

blocks.html: He stays for the rest of it, swaying, because leaving would be agreeing. Six pieces go to the no side. Geochilbu reads the count aloud, the last thing he ever does in that room. He will be dead before the leaves turn.
blocks.ko: 그는 끝까지 남는다. 휘청이면서. 나가면 동의하는 셈이 되니까. 나무 조각 여섯이 아니오 쪽으로 간다. 거칠부가 셈을 소리 내어 읽는다. 그가 그 방에서 한 마지막 일이다. 잎이 물들기 전에 그는 죽는다.

lines: 그럼 난 내 전각으로 가서 잔이나 비우련다.
데려가고 싶으면 와서 데려가. 누가 나를 메고 나가기 전까진 내가 임금이다.
en: Then I’m going back to my hall to finish my cup.
Come and get me, if you want me. I’m the king until somebody carries me out.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace · before dawn
blocks.ko: 월성 · 동트기 전

blocks.html: Before dawn forty guards knock three times on a barred door. The party is still going when they come in.
blocks.ko: 동트기 전, 군사 마흔이 빗장 걸린 문을 세 번 두드린다. 그들이 들어설 때도 잔치는 아직 계속되고 있다.

blocks.label: The throne hall · three days later
blocks.ko: 정전 · 사흘 뒤

blocks.html: Three days later they bring him back to watch his nephew crowned in a robe hemmed in a hurry. For a moment, across the hall, it is only a boy and his uncle.
blocks.ko: 사흘 뒤 그를 다시 데려와, 급히 단을 꿰맨 옷을 입고 왕관을 쓰는 조카를 보게 한다. 잠깐 동안, 전각을 사이에 두고, 그저 소년과 그의 숙부일 뿐이다.

blocks.label: The walled house · autumn
blocks.ko: 담 높은 집 · 가을

blocks.html: His mother comes once. He dies before the first frost in the walled house with a cup in his hand, and his house drops a bone, from Sacred to True.
blocks.ko: 어머니는 한 번 찾아온다. 그는 첫서리 전에 담 높은 집에서 잔을 든 채 죽고, 그의 집은 뼈 하나가 내려앉는다. 성골에서 진골로.

blocks.title: The royal house · 신라 왕실
blocks.caption: Jinhung’s grandsons part here. Jinpyung’s line keeps the Sacred Bone. The deposed Jinji’s son drops to True Bone, and so does everyone after him.
blocks.ko: 진흥왕의 손자들이 여기서 갈린다. 진평왕의 줄은 성골을 지키고, 폐위된 진지왕의 아들은 진골로 내려앉는다. 그 뒤로 이어지는 사람들도 모두.

blocks.title: The Sacred Bone, up close · 성골 안의 서열
blocks.caption: The king at the top, his daughters on the primary line, his brothers’ houses on the secondary. The deposed Jinji’s son stands with them, a bone lower than everyone around him.
blocks.ko: 맨 위엔 임금, 직계엔 그의 딸들, 방계엔 아우들의 집. 폐위된 진지왕의 아들도 그 단에 선다. 둘레의 누구보다 뼈 하나 낮은 자리에.

blocks.label: Saryang ward · the tenth night
blocks.ko: 사량부 · 열흘째 밤

blocks.html: That same autumn the charcoal seller does not die of a fever. He takes one look at his wife, counts backwards on his fingers, and is gone by the next market day.
blocks.ko: 그해 가을 숯장수는 열병으로 죽지 않는다. 아내를 한 번 보고, 손가락으로 거꾸로 날을 세어 보고, 다음 장날이 오기 전에 사라진다.

blocks.html: On the tenth night nobody knocks. Dohwa sits up anyway, in her mourning white, with a hand on her belly, and watches the door until dawn. She isn’t waiting for anyone. She just wants to see it stay shut.
blocks.ko: 열흘째 밤엔 아무도 문을 두드리지 않는다. 도화는 그래도 상복 차림으로 배에 손을 얹고 앉아 새벽까지 문을 지켜본다. 누굴 기다리는 게 아니다. 그냥 그 문이 닫혀 있는 걸 보고 싶다.

blocks.html: The lane counts too. At the well the women stop talking when she comes, and start again behind her. Somebody spits. It lands near her feet, which in that lane counts as manners.
blocks.ko: 골목도 날을 센다. 우물가 여자들은 그녀가 오면 말을 멈추고, 지나가면 다시 시작한다. 누가 침을 뱉는다. 발치 근처에 떨어진다. 그 골목에선 그게 예의다.

blocks.speaker: Dohwa’s mother
en: Tell them it was the king.
The dead one. Tell them he came back for you, the way he promised. A ghost they’ll forgive.
lines: 죽은 그 임금. 약속대로 널 찾아왔다고 해. 귀신이면 용서해 줄 거다.

en: He never promised anything, Mother.
lines: 그 사람은 아무것도 약속 안 했어요, 어머니.

blocks.speaker: Dohwa’s mother
en: Then he can start now. He’s got nothing else to do.
lines: 그럼 이제부터 하라지. 달리 할 일도 없을 텐데.

blocks.html: So the lane gets its story: a dead king at the door on the tenth night, seven days of coloured cloud, a ghost who kept his word. It’s a lovely story. People still spit. Just less.
blocks.ko: 그렇게 골목은 이야기를 얻는다. 열흘째 밤 문 앞의 죽은 임금, 이레 동안의 오색구름, 약속을 지킨 귀신. 고운 이야기다. 사람들은 그래도 침을 뱉는다. 덜 뱉을 뿐이다.

blocks.label: Saryang ward · the birth
blocks.ko: 사량부 · 해산

blocks.html: The boy comes in spring, small and loud, in a hut with no cloud over it. One midwife. She takes her fee before she takes her coat off.
blocks.ko: 아이는 봄에 온다. 작고, 시끄럽게. 구름 한 점 없는 오두막에서. 산파는 하나. 외투보다 삯을 먼저 받는다.

blocks.html: Three days after the birth, an old woman comes down to the hut from the palace. She swept the back rooms of the Moon Palace for twenty years, and nobody there ever learned her name. She has brought rice, and she has brought something else.
blocks.ko: 해산 사흘 뒤, 궁에서 노파 하나가 오두막으로 내려온다. 월성 뒷방을 이십 년 쓸었는데, 궁에서 그 이름을 아는 사람은 하나도 없었다. 쌀을 가져왔다. 다른 것도 가져왔다.

blocks.speaker: An old palace maid
lines: 돌아가신 전하께서 술잔 바닥이 보일 때면 늘 그러셨어요, 마님. 첫 아들 이름은 뭐라 짓겠다고.
용수. 불경에서 따온 이름이에요. 왕실은 아들 이름을 불경에서 짓거든요.
en: His late Majesty used to say it, mistress, at the bottom of a cup. What he’d call his first boy.
Yongsu. Out of the sutras. The royal house names its sons out of the sutras.

lines: 그 사람은 제 것엔 아무 이름도 못 붙여요.
en: He doesn’t get to name anything of mine.

blocks.speaker: An old palace maid
lines: 그분 것이 아니었어요, 마님. 잠깐 빌려 쓰셨을 뿐이지.
신라 거예요. 사내아이 하나를 기다리던 이름이에요. 이 아이가 그 아이고요.
en: It was never his, mistress. He was only borrowing it.
It belongs to Silla. It was waiting for a boy. This is the boy.

blocks.html: Dohwa looks at the baby for a long time. He sneezes, which settles nothing.
blocks.ko: 도화는 오래 아기를 들여다본다. 아기가 재채기를 한다. 그래서 정해지는 건 없다.

lines: 이 집에선 비형이에요. 코 좀 봐요. 가시 같잖아요.
en: …Yongsu, then. For the country.
In this house he’s Bihyung. Look at that nose. Like a thorn.

blocks.html: So the boy gets two names: one for Silla and one for the hut. The record keeps the hut’s. Saryang ward gives him a third, the ghost’s bastard, which at least was short.
blocks.ko: 그래서 아이는 이름을 둘 얻는다. 하나는 신라 몫, 하나는 오두막 몫. 기록은 오두막 쪽을 남긴다. 사량부는 세 번째 이름을 붙인다. 귀신의 사생아. 짧기는 했다.

blocks.label: Yongsu
blocks.ko: 용수

blocks.label: The edge of Surabol · the charcoal road
blocks.ko: 서라벌 끝 · 숯 길

blocks.html: Surabol has an edge, where the tiled roofs give up and the fields start. The boy lives there. He carries charcoal into the city in a basket bigger than he is, and carries the money home, and the other boys carry stones.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에도 끝이 있다. 기와지붕이 손을 놓고 밭이 시작되는 곳. 아이는 거기 산다. 자기보다 큰 바구니에 숯을 담아 성안으로 지고 가서, 돈을 지고 돌아온다. 다른 아이들은 돌을 지고 다닌다.

blocks.speaker: A boy with a stone
en: Ghost’s bastard! Where’s your daddy? Under the floor?
lines: 귀신 새끼! 니 아빠 어딨냐? 마루 밑에?

en: Don’t fight them.
Be strange. Talk to something they can’t see. Nobody kills the strange boy.
lines: 이상하게 굴어. 쟤들 눈에 안 보이는 거한테 말을 걸어. 이상한 애는 아무도 안 죽여.

en: What do I say to it?
Anything. Tell it about your day. It’s had a worse one.
lines: 아무거나. 오늘 있었던 일. 그쪽은 더 험한 하루였을 테니.

blocks.html: The next morning he stops in the lane and has a long, polite conversation with the empty air beside the well. The stones stop. Within a month the other boys cross the road when they see him. He is eight, and it is the first thing that has ever worked.
blocks.ko: 이튿날 아침 아이는 골목에 멈춰 서서 우물 옆 빈 허공과 길고 공손한 대화를 나눈다. 돌이 멈춘다. 한 달이 안 돼 다른 아이들은 그를 보면 길을 건넌다. 여덟 살, 처음으로 뭔가가 통했다.

blocks.label: Saryang ward · the charcoal hut
blocks.ko: 사량부 · 숯 오두막

blocks.html: The record says a king met a boy on a river bank. There is no river bank. There is an old woman from the back rooms who goes to the king, and a king who goes to a hut.
blocks.ko: 기록은 임금이 강둑에서 소년을 만났다고 한다. 강둑은 없다. 뒷방 노파가 임금에게 갔고, 임금이 오두막으로 왔을 뿐이다.

blocks.html: He comes at dusk in a groom’s borrowed coat, ducks under the lintel, and stops. A woman on a mat, very thin. A boy of fifteen holding a bowl for her. The boy looks up and does not bow, because nobody has ever taught him who to bow to.
blocks.ko: 그는 해 질 녘에 마부 외투를 빌려 입고 와서, 문인방 밑으로 고개를 숙이고 들어오다 멈춘다. 거적 위에 아주 마른 여자. 그녀에게 사발을 들어 주는 열다섯 살 소년. 소년이 올려다보고도 절하지 않는다. 누구한테 절하는지 가르쳐 준 사람이 없었으니까.

en: …Who are your parents, boy?

lines: 어머니는 숯 팔아요. 팔았어요. 지금은 아파요.
en: My mother sells charcoal. Sold. She’s sick now.
And your father?

lines: 이 동네 사람은 다 알아요. 물어보세요.
en: Haven’t got one. I was born without.
Everybody round here knows. You can ask.
Name?

lines: …집에선 비형이고요. 엄마가 그건 좋은 날에만 쓰는 이름이래요.
en: Yongsu.
…Bihyung, at home. Mother says the other one’s for best.

blocks.html: Yongsu. A sutra name, the kind the royal house gives its sons. Jinpyung goes very still. Everybody in Surabol knows the song about the peach-blossom woman and the king’s ghost. He looks at the boy a long time: the jaw, the eyes. It is the way you look at a house you used to live in.
blocks.ko: 용수. 불경 이름이다. 왕실이 아들에게 붙이는 그런 이름. 진평왕이 그대로 굳는다. 서라벌에서 복사꽃 여인과 임금 귀신 노래를 모르는 사람은 없다. 왕은 오래 아이를 본다. 턱을, 눈을. 예전에 살던 집을 바라보는 눈이다.

en: How old are you?
Fifteen.

lines: 짐 나를 줄 아느냐? 입은 다물 줄 알고?
en: Can you carry things? Can you keep your mouth shut?
…The first one.
That’ll do. You’re coming to the palace.
Sir.
Whoever you are. Keep him.
I know who his father was.
…I’ll keep him. I promise.
And you. Be strange.
Promise me.

blocks.html: She dies that summer. On the ride back from the burial the king and the boy make up the river bank between them, the slumping earth, the voices, the bridle. The king is very good at it. If he hadn’t been a king he would have been a wonderful liar.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 그해 여름에 죽는다. 장례에서 돌아오는 길에 임금과 소년은 둘이서 강둑을 지어낸다. 무너지는 흙, 목소리들, 말고삐. 임금은 아주 잘한다. 임금만 아니었으면 대단한 거짓말쟁이가 됐을 것이다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace · the king’s small room
blocks.ko: 월성 · 임금의 작은 방

blocks.html: The first night, once the servants are asleep, the king sends for the new boy. One lamp. Nobody else in the room. Kings are almost never alone, so when one is, it’s on purpose.
blocks.ko: 첫날 밤, 하인들이 잠들자 왕이 새 아이를 부른다. 등잔 하나. 방엔 둘뿐이다. 임금은 혼자 있는 법이 거의 없다. 그러니 혼자라면 일부러다.

en: Sit. No, on the cushion.
You’re not in trouble.
Then why am I here, sir?

lines: 네 어미가 너한테 아비가 없다고 했지.
en: Your mother told you you haven’t got a father.
You’ve got one. He was my uncle.

blocks.html: The boy waits for the joke. It doesn’t come.
blocks.ko: 아이는 농담이 나오길 기다린다. 나오지 않는다.

en: …The king. The one in the song.

lines: 노래에 나오는 그분. 늙은이 여섯이 그분 관을 벗기고, 집을 빼앗고, 호위를 하나씩 없앴다. 아직 안 끝났어.
그분 피가 섞인 건 다 없애고 싶어 해. 조용히. 조용히 하는 데는 아주 선수들이지.
en: The one in the song. Six old men took his crown, then his house, then his guards, one at a time. They haven’t finished.
Anything with his blood in it, they’d like gone. Quietly. They’re very good at quietly.
…So I’m—

lines: 내 사촌이지. 이 궁에서 사내아이가 될 수 있는 것 중에 제일 위험한 거.
en: My cousin. Which in this palace is the most dangerous thing a boy can be.
Then why’d you bring me in?

lines: 궁에 하인은 가득한데 말 섞을 친척은 하나도 없어서.
…그리고 넌 그분 얼굴을 하고 있다. 그 얼굴을 이 궁에서 다시 보고 싶었어.
en: Because I have a palace full of servants and not one relation I can talk to.
…And you’ve got his face. I’d like to see it in this palace again.

lines: 하나만. 이 담 안에선 절대 용수라고 하지 마라.
네 아버지가 쓰러지던 밤, 수을부가 명단을 들고 이 도성을 돌았다. 그 사람 아직 살아 있고, 아직도 그 명단을 읽는다. 하인 아이한테 붙은 불경 이름은, 그 사람이 마저 채우고 싶어 할 한 줄이야.
en: One thing. Never say Yongsu inside these walls.
The night your father fell, Suulbu walked this city with a list. He is still alive, and he still reads it. A sutra name on a servant boy is a line he will want to finish.
What does your mother call you?
Bihyung. …It’s because of my nose.

lines: 그럼 넌 비형이다. 아침에 집사한테 일러두마.
en: Then you’re Bihyung. I’ll tell the steward in the morning.
Nobody ever counted a nose.

blocks.html: So the king tells the palace the ghost’s boy is called Bihyung, and the palace, which loves a joke at a servant’s expense, takes it up gladly. Yongsu answers to both names. He knows which one is the disguise. Some nights he isn’t sure. Not for the joke. For the list.
blocks.ko: 그래서 왕은 귀신 아이 이름이 비형이라고 궁에 알린다. 하인 놀리는 농담이라면 사족을 못 쓰는 궁은 기꺼이 받아 부른다. 용수는 두 이름 다 대답한다. 어느 쪽이 변장인지 안다. 어떤 밤엔 잘 모르겠다. 농담 때문이 아니다. 그 명단 때문이다.

blocks.html: He likes his cousin at once. Nobody in that palace has ever done that on purpose.
blocks.ko: 그는 사촌이 단번에 좋아진다. 그 궁에서 일부러 그런 사람은 처음이다.

blocks.html: The Council ought to have counted him that spring. It was busy. The High Councillor’s own daughter had just run north with a Gaya officer, and every banquet in Surabol was counting her months instead.
blocks.ko: 화백은 그해 봄 그를 셌어야 했다. 바빴다. 상대등의 친딸이 가야 출신 무관과 북으로 달아난 참이라, 서라벌의 잔치마다 그 딸의 달수를 세느라 정신이 없었다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace · the servants’ yard
blocks.ko: 월성 · 하인 마당

blocks.html: A palace servant who talks to the air is the lowest thing in the palace. They salt his shoes and leave his bowl by the kitchen door like a dog’s, and the maids who won’t sleep near him still walk past his door.
blocks.ko: 허공에 대고 말하는 궁 하인은 궁에서 제일 낮은 존재다. 사람들은 그의 신발에 소금을 치고, 개밥처럼 부엌문 밖에 그릇을 내놓는다. 그래도 그 곁에선 안 자겠다는 시녀들이 그의 방 앞을 지나간다.

blocks.label: The king’s small room · baduk
blocks.ko: 임금의 작은 방 · 바둑

blocks.html: Some nights the king sends for the madman to play baduk. One lamp. The door shut. Inside that room there is no madman, and nobody has ever told the steward.
blocks.ko: 어떤 밤이면 임금은 미치광이를 불러 바둑을 둔다. 등잔 하나. 닫힌 문. 그 방 안에는 미치광이가 없다. 집사한테 그걸 말해 준 사람은 아무도 없다.

en: You’re letting me win.
You’re letting me let you.
…Do you know how many people in this palace call me by my name?
None. Call me Baekjung.
lines: …이 궁에서 내 이름 부르는 사람이 몇인지 아나?

en: …Baekjung?
It sounded like a question.
Your father put me on that chair when I was ten. He tied my sleeves back so I wouldn’t trip on them.
lines: 네 아버지가 열 살 난 날 저 의자에 앉혔다. 넘어지지 말라고 소매를 묶어 줬지.

en: Was he kind?

blocks.html: The king puts down a stone in the wrong place, on purpose or not.
blocks.ko: 임금이 엉뚱한 자리에 돌을 놓는다. 일부러인지 아닌지.

en: He was kind to me.
…I’ve heard he wasn’t kind to everyone.

blocks.html: Neither of them says anything for a while. The boy wins the game. It is the only time he ever does.
blocks.ko: 한동안 둘 다 아무 말이 없다. 소년이 그 판을 이긴다. 평생 그 한 번뿐이다.

blocks.label: The palace roof · the night of the plum wine
blocks.ko: 궁 지붕 · 매실주 마시던 밤

blocks.html: The other place they talk is the roof of the east hall, which the king is not allowed on, so he goes there often. Plum wine. Legs over the edge. Below them the city, and the lamps in the Council’s windows.
blocks.ko: 둘이 이야기하는 다른 자리는 동궁 지붕이다. 임금은 올라가면 안 되는 곳이라, 자주 올라간다. 매실주. 처마 끝에 걸친 다리. 발아래 도성, 그리고 화백들 창에 켜진 등불.

en: Six old men.
They took your father. Every morning I count them, to see if any of them died in the night.
lines: 네 아버지를 끌어내린 자들이지. 아침마다 세어 본다. 밤새 누가 죽었나 하고.

en: So do I.
…Then we’ll count together. It’ll go faster.
You laugh too soon, cousin. When they say something clever. Laugh a beat late. Then they think you didn’t get it.
lines: 형님은 너무 빨리 웃어요. 저쪽이 영리한 말 하면요. 한 박자 늦게 웃으세요. 그럼 못 알아들은 줄 알아요.

en: Is that what you do?
I’m doing it now.

blocks.html: The king laughs, a beat late. It is the first lesson. He will be laughing late at the Council for thirty-eight more years, and none of them will ever work out why.
blocks.ko: 임금이 한 박자 늦게 웃는다. 첫 수업이다. 그는 앞으로 서른여덟 해 동안 화백 앞에서 늦게 웃을 것이고, 화백 누구도 끝내 그 까닭을 알아내지 못할 것이다.

blocks.label: The Hwangchun reeds · a walk at night
blocks.ko: 황천 갈대밭 · 밤 산책

blocks.html: Seventeen, then, and barefoot, walking the bank because the palace is too loud with sleeping men. The moon is behind cloud. Something in the reeds says Majesty.
blocks.ko: 그러니까 열일곱, 맨발로 둑을 걷는다. 잠든 사내들 숨소리로 궁이 너무 시끄러워서. 달은 구름 뒤에 있다. 갈대 속에서 무언가가 말한다. 전하.

blocks.html: Not Bihyung. Not ghost boy. Majesty.
blocks.ko: 비형이 아니다. 귀신 아이도 아니다. 전하다.

blocks.html: He nearly runs. Instead a man steps out of the reeds: thin, half a dozen years older than him, clean the way people are who wash in rivers, with a grinning dokkaebi mask of carved wood pushed up on his forehead. He goes down on both knees in the mud.
blocks.ko: 그는 하마터면 달아난다. 대신 갈대 속에서 사내 하나가 걸어 나온다. 마르고, 그보다 대여섯 살 위, 강물에 씻는 사람 특유의 깨끗함. 나무로 깎은 히죽 웃는 도깨비탈을 이마 위로 올려 쓰고 있다. 사내가 진흙에 두 무릎을 꿇는다.

lines: 맞는 얼굴에 그 말을 하려고 오래 기다렸소.
en: Majesty. Forgive me.
I have waited a long time to say it to the right face.

lines: 일어나— 일어나요, 미쳤어요? 그렇게 부르지 마요. 누구예요? 누가 보냈어요?
이 둑에서 누가 그 말 들으면 우리 둘 다 같은 나무에 매달려요.
en: Get up— get up, are you mad? Don’t call me that. Who are you? Who sent you?
If anybody hears that word on this bank, they’ll hang us off the same tree.

lines: 이 둑에선 아무도 아무것도 못 듣소. 우리가 그리 해 두었소.
그대는 김용수… 김사륜, 돌아가신 진지대왕의 아드님이시오…!
en: Nobody hears anything on this bank. We have made sure of it.
You are Kim Yongsu… son of Kim Saryun, the late King Jinji…!

blocks.html: The name lands like a stone in the water. Only one person has ever said his father’s name to him out loud, and that was a king, in a small room, with the lamp turned down.
blocks.ko: 그 이름이 물에 돌처럼 떨어진다. 그에게 아버지 이름을 소리 내 말해 준 사람은 지금껏 하나뿐이었다. 임금이, 작은 방에서, 등잔 심지를 낮추고.

en: Why me?
Everyone walks right past you lot. Why do I hear you?
lines: 다들 그쪽 사람들 그냥 지나치잖아요. 근데 왜 나한텐 들려요?

en: Because you are one of us, sir. They took your father’s crown and struck out your name.
They did the same to ours. Deposed children hear each other in the dark.
lines: 그대도 우리와 같기 때문이오. 아버님 관을 벗기고 그대 이름을 지웠지.
우리 아비들한테도 똑같이 했소. 쫓겨난 집 자식들은 어둠 속에서 서로 알아듣소.
아주 나쁜 사람. 다시는 그 이름 꺼내지 마요.
en: …My father was a bad man.
A very bad man. Do not speak his name again.

lines: 소문 들었소. 신에 소금을 넣었더니 고맙다 했다지. 연못에 던졌는데 그 아이를 도로 빠뜨리지 않았다지. 그대는 좋은 사람이오…!
아비 죄를 아들이 갚아서는 아니 되오…!
en: But you are not, sir…!
I have heard of you. They put salt in your shoes and you thanked them. They threw you in the pond and you didn’t drown the boy back. You are a good man…!
Sons should not have to pay for the sins of their fathers…!
…Of course they should.
A man is nothing if not his blood.

blocks.html: He says it the way you say a thing you’ve heard every day of your life, until it’s the one thing you’re sure of.
blocks.ko: 평생 날마다 들어서, 끝내 그것 하나만 확실해진 말을 하듯 말한다.

en: Please. We beg you to reconsider!
Yes, sir. There are more of us.
Please. Follow me…!

blocks.label: Under the west wall · the Ghost Children
blocks.ko: 서쪽 성벽 밑 · 귀자

blocks.html: Gildal doesn’t take him round the palace. He takes him under it. Where the stream goes in below the west wall there is an old culvert, choked with reeds. Fifty men watching the top of a wall never once look at the bottom. Remember the fifty men.
blocks.ko: 길달은 그를 궁 둘레로 데려가지 않는다. 밑으로 데려간다. 서쪽 성벽 아래 개울이 들어가는 곳에 갈대로 막힌 옛 수로가 있다. 성벽 꼭대기를 지키는 오십 명은 밑은 한 번도 안 본다. 그 오십 명을 기억해 두라.

blocks.html: At the far end is a dry storehouse nobody has used since the old king’s time, and a fire, and faces. Then masks: dokkaebi from the village plays, horned, red, white-eyed, one on every face that turns toward him. They come off one at a time.
blocks.ko: 끝에는 옛 임금 때부터 아무도 안 쓴 마른 창고가 있다. 불이 있고, 얼굴들이 있다. 아니, 탈들이다. 마을 놀이판의 도깨비탈, 뿔 달린 것, 붉은 것, 흰자위만 있는 것. 그를 향해 돌아보는 얼굴마다 하나씩. 탈이 하나씩 벗겨진다.

blocks.html: Under them: an old man with one eye, the other a puckered scar. A woman with a baby on her back and nobody else beside her. Three boys who look like brothers and aren’t; the smallest wears a red mask and won’t take it off for anybody. And a girl of about six with a sharp chin, in a fox mask of her own.
blocks.ko: 그 밑엔 눈 하나가 없는 노인. 남은 자리는 오그라든 흉터다. 아기를 업은 여자. 곁엔 아무도 없다. 형제처럼 생겼는데 형제가 아닌 사내아이 셋. 제일 작은 놈은 빨간 탈을 쓰고 누가 뭐래도 안 벗는다. 그리고 턱이 뾰족한 여섯 살쯤 된 계집아이 하나. 그 애도 여우탈이 있다.

en: These are the Ghost Children, Majesty.

blocks.html: Here is what the song leaves out. When the Council took the crown off Jinji, Suulbu, the old king’s brother and the next High Councillor, went through the city with a list and forty riders. The guards who had stood at the king’s door went first. He had their eyes put out, so they would never again stand at a door and see who came through it.
blocks.ko: 노래가 빼먹는 대목은 이렇다. 화백이 진지의 관을 벗기자, 선왕의 아우이자 다음 상대등이 될 수을부가 명단과 기병 마흔을 데리고 성안을 돌았다. 맨 먼저 임금 문 앞을 지키던 호위들. 그는 그들의 눈을 뽑게 했다. 다시는 어느 문 앞에 서서 누가 드나드는지 보지 못하게.

blocks.html: Then the men who had argued against the vote: hanged in their own yards, or sent to the northern forts in chains, which came to the same thing a winter later. Their wives went after them. Then the children. The small ones were tied in rice sacks and put in the Hwangchun at night, where the current runs fast, so that nobody would have to dig. The older ones were simply left: no parents, no house, no name.
blocks.ko: 다음은 표결에 반대한 자들. 제 집 마당에서 목이 매달리거나, 쇠사슬에 묶여 북쪽 성으로 보내졌다. 한 해 겨울이 지나면 결국 같은 일이었다. 아내들도 뒤따랐다. 그다음은 아이들. 어린것들은 쌀자루에 묶여 밤에 물살 빠른 황천에 던져졌다. 아무도 땅을 팔 필요가 없게. 큰 아이들은 그냥 남겨졌다. 부모도, 집도, 이름도 없이.

blocks.html: And once nobody had stopped him, anybody Suulbu simply didn’t like got “Jinji’s man” written beside his name too. You’d be surprised how many Jinji’s men there turned out to be.
blocks.ko: 그리고 아무도 말리지 않자, 그냥 수을부 눈에 거슬리는 자 누구든 이름 옆에 “진지의 사람”이 적혔다. 진지의 사람이 그렇게 많았는지 알면 놀랄 거다.

blocks.html: Their sons and daughters live here. Their houses are gone and their names are struck from the rolls, and in Silla a person with no name can’t marry, can’t hold a field, can’t stand in the market without someone asking whose they are. So they live like ghosts. At some point they started calling themselves that. It was funnier than the alternative.
blocks.ko: 그 아들딸들이 여기 산다. 집은 없어졌고 이름은 명부에서 지워졌다. 신라에서 이름 없는 사람은 혼인도 못 하고, 밭도 못 갖고, 장터에 서 있기만 해도 누구네 사람이냐는 소리를 듣는다. 그래서 귀신처럼 산다. 언제부턴가 스스로를 그렇게 불렀다. 다른 이름보단 그게 웃겼다.

blocks.speaker: An old man with one eye
lines: 우린 당신 아버지 안 좋아했소, 전하. 불 앞이니 솔직히 합시다. 술주정뱅이에 바보였고, 당신 어머니한테 한 짓은 우리 절반이 알았소.
허나 내 눈은 그 죄로 뽑힌 거요. 숙청하던 밤에. 내가 그 문 앞에 서 있었거든. 죄목은 그게 다였소.
en: We didn’t love your father, Majesty. Let’s be honest in front of the fire. He was a drunk and a fool, and what he did to your mother, half of us knew.
But they took my eye for his sins all the same. The night of the purge. I’d stood at his door. That was the whole charge.

lines: 얘가 마지막이에요. 우리 막내. 위로 셋이 더 있었어요.
수을부가 걔들 아버지 이름 옆에 “진지의 사람”이라고 썼고, 그다음엔 걔들 이름 옆에도 썼어요. 열네 살, 열두 살, 아홉 살.
쌀자루에 묶어서 강으로 지고 갔어요. 둑에서 다 들었어요. 세 번.
얘는 이름도 없어요. 죽어도 제대로 묻히지도 못해요. 이름만 돌려줘요. 그게 다예요.
en: She’s the last. My littlest. There were three before her.
Suulbu wrote “Jinji’s man” next to their father’s name, and then next to theirs. Fourteen, twelve and nine.
They tied them in rice sacks and carried them down to the river. I heard it from the bank. Three times.
She’s got no name. She can’t even be buried properly. Give her back a name. That’s all.
blocks.speaker: A woman with a baby

blocks.html: The three boys don’t say anything. They don’t have to. One father sent to the islands and never written to. One hanged at the west gate. One mother who went to the Council to ask after her husband and didn’t come home. The smallest has worn the red mask ever since.
blocks.ko: 사내아이 셋은 아무 말도 안 한다. 할 필요가 없다. 섬으로 귀양 가서 편지 한 장 없는 아버지 하나. 서문에 목 매달린 아버지 하나. 남편 소식 물으러 화백에 갔다가 안 돌아온 어머니 하나. 제일 작은 놈은 그 뒤로 빨간 탈을 안 벗었다.

lines: 그대 핏줄이 복권되면, 이들 핏줄도 함께 복권되오. 그 명단의 집 전부.
화백엔 화백의 무리가 있소. 우리도 우리 무리를 갖고 싶소.
en: If your blood is restored, sir, theirs is restored with it. Every house on that list.
The Council has its faction. We would like one of our own.

blocks.html: So there it is. On one side the Council Faction, which has the palace, the riders and the minutes. On the other, a storehouse under a wall full of people in masks who want a dead king’s son on the throne. Not because they loved the father. Because their children would get to have surnames again. Call them the Restoration Faction. They never did. They called it waiting.
blocks.ko: 그러니 이렇다. 한쪽엔 화백파. 궁도, 사병도, 회의록도 다 가졌다. 다른 쪽엔 성벽 밑 창고 하나, 죽은 임금의 아들을 왕좌에 앉히고 싶은 탈 쓴 사람들. 아버지를 사랑해서가 아니다. 제 아이들이 다시 성을 갖게 되니까. 복권파라 부르자. 그들 스스론 그렇게 부른 적 없다. 기다림이라 불렀다.

en: …You want me to overthrow my cousin.
We want you to be what you are.

lines: 그 궁에서 날 사람으로 보는 건 그분뿐이에요. 나랑 바둑을 둬요. 일부러 져요. 엉망으로.
en: He took me off a river bank—
He’s the only one in that palace who looks at me like a person. He plays baduk with me. He loses on purpose. Badly.
And you want me to take his chair.

blocks.html: Nobody answers. The baby on the woman’s back starts to cry, and she rocks it, and doesn’t stop looking at him.
blocks.ko: 아무도 대답하지 않는다. 여자 등에서 아기가 운다. 여자는 아기를 흔들면서 그에게서 눈을 떼지 않는다.

blocks.speaker: Little Fox
lines: 길달 아저씨가 클 거라 했어. 아저씨는 맨날 맞아.
en: You’re taller than I thought.
Gildal said you’d be tall. He’s always right.

blocks.html: Everybody tells her to shush. She doesn’t.
blocks.ko: 다들 쉿 한다. 아이는 안 쉿한다.

en: …Not yet.
But I’ll tell you how we wait.

lines: 벌써 탈을 쓰고 있네요. 잘됐다. 오늘 밤부터 여러분은 사람이 아니에요. 도깨비예요. 도깨비 잡으러 다니는 사람은 없어요. 떡이나 놔두지.
그리고 난 여러분이랑 얘기하는 미친놈이고요. 미친놈은 그 궁 어디든 다닐 수 있어요. 미친놈은 아무도 안 세요.
en: You already wear masks. Good. From tonight you’re not people. You’re goblins. Nobody hunts goblins. They leave them rice cakes.
And I’m the madman who talks to you. A madman can go anywhere in that palace. Nobody counts a madman.

lines: …전하, 그건 아주 어리석거나 아주 영리하거나 둘 중 하나요.
en: …Majesty, that is either very stupid or very clever.
Both. That’s how you know it’ll work.
Who taught you to think like that?

lines: 주로 사촌이요. 바둑을 일부러 져요. 난 그분이 어디서 지는지 봐요.
en: My cousin, mostly. He loses at baduk on purpose. I watch where he loses.
We have lived on less, Majesty.

blocks.html: He goes back through the culvert before the temple bell. By morning the guards swear he went over the wall like a bird. That was his idea too. A boy who can fly is much less interesting than a boy who knows where the drain is.
blocks.ko: 그는 절 종이 울리기 전에 수로로 돌아간다. 아침이 되자 파수들은 그가 새처럼 담을 넘었다고 맹세한다. 그것도 그의 생각이었다. 날아다니는 아이는 하수구 자리를 아는 아이보다 훨씬 덜 궁금하니까.

blocks.html: He is seventeen, and his cousin King Jinpyung has two small daughters and no son, and the court is doing arithmetic. Even a ghost’s son, if the ghost was a king, is a very interesting number. Men start visiting Yongsu with gifts. Men who visit with gifts are counting.
blocks.ko: 그는 열일곱이다. 사촌 형 진평왕에게는 어린 딸 둘뿐이고 아들이 없다. 조정은 셈을 시작한다. 귀신의 아들이라도, 그 귀신이 임금이었다면, 아주 흥미로운 숫자다. 사내들이 선물을 들고 용수를 찾아오기 시작한다. 선물을 들고 오는 사내들은 세고 있는 것이다.

lines: 도련님 같은 핏줄이 과연… 만족하고 계신지 궁금해들 하시지요.
en: Young lord. The Council asks after your health.
They wonder whether a man of your blood is… content.
blocks.speaker: A man with gifts

lines: 쉿. 지금 말고. 개울이 말하는 중이야.
en: Content?
Shh. Not now. The stream is talking.

blocks.html: That night he goes down to the reeds in his sleeping robe and talks to them until dawn, loudly, where the night watch can hear. He laughs. By the market hour, so has everybody else.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 잠옷 바람으로 갈대숲에 내려가 새벽까지 그것들과 이야기한다. 순라꾼들이 들을 수 있게, 큰 소리로. 그가 웃는다. 장이 설 무렵엔 온 도성이 다 웃었다.

blocks.html: Surabol takes the king’s nickname and turns it into an insult. Bihyung: the ghost’s bastard, the clerk who runs with things that have no feet. Mothers use it to frighten children. Courtiers use it to end a conversation. He lets them.
blocks.ko: 서라벌은 임금이 붙인 별명을 욕으로 바꾼다. 비형. 귀신의 사생아, 발 없는 것들과 뛰노는 서기. 어미들은 아이 겁줄 때 쓰고, 벼슬아치들은 말을 끊을 때 쓴다. 그는 내버려 둔다.

blocks.html: The men with gifts stop coming. Nobody counts a madman.
blocks.ko: 선물 든 사내들은 발길을 끊는다. 미치광이는 아무도 세지 않는다.

blocks.label: The king’s rooms · supper
blocks.ko: 왕의 처소 · 저녁상

blocks.html: The king eats with his family when he can, which is not often, and with the door shut, which is the point. A queen, two daughters, and a servant with the soup.
blocks.ko: 왕은 틈이 나면 가족과 밥을 먹는다. 자주는 아니다. 문은 닫는다. 그게 핵심이다. 왕비, 두 딸, 그리고 국을 든 하인 하나.

blocks.speaker: Queen Maya
en: Dukman. One more spoon.
No.

lines: 세 살이잖아요. 뭐든 싫대요. 어젯밤엔 달한테도 싫대요.
en: She’s three. She says no to everything. She said no to the moon last night.

lines: 넌 열세 살인데 생선에 손도 안 대고.
먹어라. 안 그러면 개울가 미친놈한테 시집보낸다.
en: And you’re thirteen and won’t touch your fish.
Eat it, or I’ll marry you off to the madman by the stream.
You wouldn’t.

lines: 바로 저기 있는데. 비형아. 내 딸한테 장가들겠느냐?
en: He’s right there. Bihyung. Would you marry my daughter?

lines: 개울이 공주님은 말이 너무 많대요, 전하.
…덕만 공주님. 이 숟가락은 용이에요. 엄청 배가 고픈데, 무는 한 번도 못 먹어 봤대요.
en: The stream says she talks too much, Majesty.
…Princess Dukman. This spoon is a dragon. It is very hungry and it has never once eaten a radish.

blocks.html: Dukman eats the radish. Then the next one. The queen looks at the servant for a long moment, and then at her husband, who is pretending to read a tax roll at his own supper table.
blocks.ko: 덕만이 무를 먹는다. 그다음 것도. 왕비는 하인을 한참 보다가 남편을 본다. 남편은 제 밥상에서 세금 명부를 읽는 척하고 있다.

en: I hate him.

blocks.speaker: Queen Maya
en: Eat your fish.

blocks.html: Chunmyung decides that night that the madman is the most annoying man in Silla. She is thirteen. That is how it starts.
blocks.ko: 천명은 그날 밤 그 미친놈이 신라에서 제일 짜증 나는 사내라고 정한다. 열세 살이다. 다 그렇게 시작한다.

blocks.speaker: Queen Maya
en: You’re thinking something.

lines: 난 늘 무슨 생각을 하지. 그게 일이야.
en: I’m always thinking something. It’s the job.

blocks.label: Chunmyung
blocks.ko: 천명

blocks.label: The king’s rooms · supper
blocks.ko: 왕의 처소 · 저녁상

blocks.html: Four years later, the same table. The fish is still there. So is the servant with the soup.
blocks.ko: 네 해 뒤, 같은 밥상. 생선도 그대로다. 국 든 하인도 그대로다.

en: Chunmyung. I’ve found you a husband.
…Who?
My cousin.
You haven’t got a cousin.
I’ve got one. He’s holding the soup.

blocks.html: The soup does not spill. That is the first thing she will hold against him.
blocks.ko: 국은 한 방울도 안 흘린다. 그게 그녀가 그를 두고 처음 품는 앙심이다.

en: You said that was a joke!
It was. Then I thought about it.
Unni— the one who talks to the stream?!
Is the stream coming to the wedding?
Eat your porridge, Dukman.

blocks.label: The king’s rooms · after supper
blocks.ko: 왕의 처소 · 저녁상 물린 뒤

blocks.speaker: Queen Maya
en: Why him?

lines: 숙부의 핏줄이 신에 소금 든 채 하인 마당에 앉아 있소. 화백이 거기 앉혔고.
관을 돌려줄 순 없소. 공주는 줄 수 있지. 조용히. 방이 그 생각에 익숙해지게.
en: Because my uncle’s line is sitting in a servants’ yard with salt in its shoes, and the Council put it there.
I can’t give it back a crown. I can give it a princess. Quietly. Let the room get used to the idea.

blocks.speaker: Queen Maya
en: And our daughter?

lines: 그 녀석을 사람으로 만들든가, 이미 사람이라는 걸 알아내든가 할 거요.
en: Is cleverer than both of us.
She’ll either make a man of him, or find out he already is one.

blocks.label: The palace · the High Councillor’s visit
blocks.ko: 궁 · 상대등의 방문

blocks.html: The High Councillor comes to see the king that afternoon. He does not sit down. He compliments the garden.
blocks.ko: 그날 오후 상대등이 왕을 찾아온다. 앉지 않는다. 정원을 칭찬한다.

lines: 직계 공주를, 전하. 진지가 남긴 찌꺼기에게.
그 피에 시집가는 공주는 잔의 어느 쪽에 설지 고른 겁니다. 방이 받아들이지 않을 겁니다.
en: A princess of the primary line, Majesty. To Jinji’s leftover.
A princess who marries that blood has chosen her side of the cup. The room will not have it.

lines: 방은 듣는 게 많지요, 숙부. 나도 좀 들었소.
숙부 따님 이야기. 그리고 숙부 대문 앞을 지나다니던 그 가야 녀석.
손자가 이제 몇 살이오? 일곱? 묘하지. 그 잔치판에서 누구도 달수를 맞추지 못했다던데.
en: The room hears a great many things, my lord. I’ve heard a few myself.
About your own daughter. And that Gaya boy who used to ride past your gate.
How old is the grandson now? Seven? Funny. Nobody at those banquets could ever make the months add up.

blocks.html: Suulbu opens his mouth. Nothing comes out. It is the only time anybody in that palace ever sees him lose a sentence. He compliments the garden again on his way out, which is how a High Councillor retreats.
blocks.ko: 수을부가 입을 연다. 아무 말도 나오지 않는다. 그 궁에서 그가 말을 잃는 걸 본 건 그때가 유일하다. 나가는 길에 그는 정원을 한 번 더 칭찬한다. 상대등은 그렇게 물러난다.

blocks.html: Thirty years later, when the room has to choose between the king’s daughters, it passes over the elder without once saying her name. Nobody has to explain why. Chunmyung never asks.
blocks.ko: 서른 해 뒤, 그 방이 임금의 딸들 가운데 하나를 골라야 할 때, 방은 맏딸을 이름 한 번 부르지 않고 건너뛴다. 아무도 까닭을 설명할 필요가 없다. 천명은 끝내 묻지 않는다.

blocks.label: The palace garden · the introduction
blocks.ko: 궁 정원 · 첫 대면

blocks.html: The king introduces them in the garden, the madman in a borrowed coat and the princess in a temper, and leaves them alone, which is a terrible idea.
blocks.ko: 임금은 정원에서 둘을 인사시킨다. 빌린 옷을 입은 미치광이와, 잔뜩 성난 공주. 그리고 둘만 두고 간다. 아주 나쁜 생각이다.

blocks.label: The princesses’ room · that night
blocks.ko: 공주들 방 · 그날 밤

blocks.html: That night Chunmyung cries into her pillow with great efficiency, the way she does everything.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 천명은 베개에 대고 운다. 무슨 일이든 그렇듯, 아주 효율적으로.

en: I’d rather marry the stream.
The stream’s probably nicer.
…Unni. Does he really talk to ghosts?
He talks to everything except people.
Go to sleep, Dukman.

blocks.html: Dukman doesn’t go to sleep. She lies awake deciding that her sister’s madman is the most interesting thing that has ever happened to the family.
blocks.ko: 덕만은 안 잔다. 깨어 누워서, 언니의 미치광이야말로 이 집안에 일어난 일 중 제일 재미있는 일이라고 결론 내린다.

blocks.label: The Sinwon temple ditch · night
blocks.ko: 신원사 도랑 · 밤

blocks.html: King Jinpyung tests his ghost in public: a bridge over the Sinwon ditch in one night. In the morning there is a bridge, a little crooked, and the court walks the long way round.
blocks.ko: 진평왕은 사람들 앞에서 제 귀신을 시험한다. 하룻밤 만에 신원사 도랑에 다리를 놓으라고. 아침이 되자 조금 삐뚤어진 다리가 놓여 있고, 조정은 먼 길로 돌아간다.

blocks.label: The Sinwon ditch · the night of the bridge
blocks.ko: 신원사 도랑 · 다리 놓던 밤

blocks.html: Here is how a miracle is done. He designs it on a roof tile, and Gildal fixes his arithmetic. Forty people in masks come out of the reeds at the first watch with stone they have been cutting for a month in a storehouse under a wall. The madman sits on the bank and talks to the stream at the top of his voice, so that nobody in the temple hears the hammers. By dawn the masks are back in the reeds, and the stones are wet with dew.
blocks.ko: 기적은 이렇게 한다. 그가 기왓장에 설계를 하고, 길달이 셈을 바로잡는다. 초경에 탈 쓴 사람 마흔이 갈대밭에서 나온다. 성벽 밑 창고에서 한 달 동안 다듬은 돌을 지고. 미친놈은 둑에 앉아 목청껏 개울한테 떠든다. 절에서 망치 소리를 못 듣게. 새벽이면 탈들은 갈대밭으로 돌아가 있고, 돌에는 이슬이 맺혀 있다.

blocks.html: Gildal won’t take a coin. A king’s bridge, he says, should not be paid for. Yongsu pays the other thirty-nine anyway, with every coin he has, which is how a princess found forty men’s wages on a wax tablet.
blocks.ko: 길달은 한 푼도 안 받는다. 임금의 다리는 돈 받고 놓는 게 아니라고. 용수는 나머지 서른아홉한테 어쨌든 준다. 가진 돈 전부. 공주가 밀랍판에서 사내 마흔 명 품삯을 찾아낸 게 그래서다.

blocks.html: After the bridge, a miracle a season, all his. The steward who beat the ghost boy finds his lost seal under his own pillow, because a girl in a fox mask put it there. The steward stops beating servants. That was the whole point of that one.
blocks.ko: 다리 뒤로는 철마다 기적 하나. 전부 그의 작품이다. 귀신 아이를 때리던 집사는 잃어버린 도장을 제 베개 밑에서 찾는다. 여우탈 쓴 계집애가 넣어 뒀다. 집사는 그 뒤로 하인을 안 때린다. 그 기적은 그게 목적이었다.

blocks.label: The Ghost Bridge · the next night
blocks.ko: 귀교 · 이튿날 밤

blocks.html: Princess Chunmyung is seventeen, and engaged to a madman, and she has walked out alone to see the goblin bridge. She finds her intended sitting on it, doing sums on a wax tablet.
blocks.ko: 천명공주는 열일곱, 미친놈과 정혼한 몸이다. 혼자 도깨비 다리를 보러 나왔다. 다리 위에 정혼자가 앉아 밀랍판에 셈을 하고 있다.

en: Forty men. Two nights’ wages, and the stone.
That’s very cheap, for goblins.
…The goblins drove a hard bargain.
You can’t tell anyone.

lines: 정신 멀쩡한 그 핏줄은 후보가 되니까. 후보는 송장이 되고.
en: Why not?
Oh.
Because a sane man of your blood is a candidate. And a candidate is a corpse.
Princess. Please go home.
The stream is very talkative tonight.

blocks.html: She doesn’t go home. Four years ago her father threatened to marry her to the madman to make her eat her fish. Now he has done it to make a point. She has not decided which of the two men she is angrier with.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 집에 가지 않는다. 네 해 전 아버지는 생선을 먹이려고 미친놈한테 시집보낸다고 을렀다. 이제는 무언가를 보여 주려고 정말로 보냈다. 둘 중 누구한테 더 화가 나는지 아직 못 정했다.

blocks.html: She sits down on the bridge beside him, takes the stylus out of his hand without asking, and corrects one of his sums.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 다리 위 그의 곁에 앉더니, 묻지도 않고 그의 손에서 철필을 빼앗아 셈 하나를 고친다.

en: You’ve charged them for the stone twice.
…I have not.
…I have.

blocks.html: He laughs, a beat late. She doesn’t. She is looking at his hands, which are a clerk’s hands, ink in the creases, nothing mad about them at all.
blocks.ko: 그가 한 박자 늦게 웃는다. 그녀는 웃지 않는다. 그녀는 그의 손을 보고 있다. 주름마다 먹이 낀 서기의 손. 미친 구석이라곤 하나도 없는 손.

lines: 아버지가 그쪽이 누구 아들인지 말해 줬어요.
en: Father told me whose son you are.
Everybody knows, Princess. A ghost’s.

lines: …그분이 그쪽 어머니한테 한 짓도요. 그쪽한테 시집간다고 말한 그날 밤에 그것도 말해 줬어요.
en: Not the ghost. The other one.
…And what he did to your mother. He told me that too, the night he told me I was marrying you.

blocks.html: The madman stops being mad for exactly as long as it takes to look at her.
blocks.ko: 미치광이는 그녀를 바라보는 딱 그만큼의 시간 동안 미치광이이기를 멈춘다.

lines: 그럼 여기 앉아 계시면 안 된다는 것도 아시겠네요.
en: Then you know you shouldn’t be sitting here.

lines: 알면 안 되는 건 많이 알아.
내일. 같은 종 칠 때. 장부는 좀 제대로 된 걸로 가져와. 이건 엉망이야.
en: I know a great many things I shouldn’t.
Tomorrow. Same bell. Bring a better tally. This one’s a disgrace.

blocks.html: He comes back the next night. So does she.
blocks.ko: 그는 다음 날 밤 다시 온다. 그녀도 온다.

blocks.html: Behind the plum tree at the end of the bridge, a seven-year-old in a sleeping robe is watching all of it and memorising. Nobody in the family ever works out where Dukman learned to keep a secret. It was here.
blocks.ko: 다리 끝 매화나무 뒤에서 잠옷 바람의 일곱 살 아이가 전부 지켜보며 외우고 있다. 덕만이 어디서 비밀 지키는 법을 배웠는지 집안 누구도 끝내 알아내지 못한다. 여기서였다.

blocks.label: Under the west wall · the night the princess followed
blocks.ko: 서쪽 성벽 밑 · 공주가 뒤따라온 밤

blocks.html: Back up to the bridge month. One night, somebody follows him. Not the Council. Worse.
blocks.ko: 다리를 오가던 그달로 잠깐 돌아가자. 어느 밤, 누군가 그를 따라온다. 화백이 아니다. 더 나쁘다.

blocks.html: Chunmyung comes down the culvert in a maid’s coat, wet to the knees, and stands in the storehouse door while forty masks turn to look at her. Gildal has a plan of the palace spread on the floor. The old man with one eye is saying “when he’s king.”
blocks.ko: 천명이 시녀 옷을 입고 무릎까지 젖은 채 수로를 따라 내려와 창고 문간에 선다. 탈 마흔 개가 그녀를 돌아본다. 바닥엔 길달이 궁궐 도면을 펼쳐 놓았다. 귀 없는 노인이 “그분이 임금 되시면” 하고 말하는 중이다.

blocks.html: The smell reaches her first. Smoke, wet straw, too many people in one room. A one-eyed man smiles at her, and she steps back into the water without meaning to.
blocks.ko: 냄새가 먼저 닿는다. 연기, 젖은 짚, 한 방에 너무 많은 사람. 외눈 사내가 그녀에게 웃어 보이고, 그녀는 저도 모르게 물속으로 한 걸음 물러선다.

en: These are traitors’ children.
They were six when their fathers became traitors.
Somebody wrote it next to their names. It took one brush.
lines: 아비들이 역적이 됐을 때 이 애들은 여섯 살이었어요.
누가 이름 옆에 적었죠. 붓질 한 번이었어요.

en: …You’re raising an army. Under my father’s wall.
It isn’t an army. Look at them. It’s a—

lines: 우리 아버지랑 바둑 두잖아요. 아버지가 일부러 져 주잖아요. 그러고 여기 내려와서 아버지 자리를 재요?
en: I heard him. “When he’s king.”
You play baduk with my father. He loses to you on purpose. And you come down here and measure his chair.
Yes.

blocks.html: It is the worst thing he could have said, and the only true one.
blocks.ko: 그가 할 수 있는 가장 나쁜 말이다. 그리고 유일한 참말이다.

lines: 가도 돼요. 오늘 밤. 미친놈이 무서웠다고 하세요. 믿으실 거예요. 다들 믿을 거고. 공주님 탓은 한마디도 안 할게요.
대신 부탁이에요. 이 사람들 얘긴 하지 마요. 이걸 끄지 마요. 이 사람들한텐 이게 유일한 불빛이에요.
en: You can go. Tonight. Tell him the madman frightened you. He’ll believe it. Everyone will. I’ll never say a word against you.
But please. Don’t tell him about them. Don’t put this out. It’s the only light they’ve got.
You’re asking me to lie to my father.

lines: 말을 안 하시라는 거예요. 달라요. 조금.
en: I’m asking you not to say something. It’s different. Slightly.

blocks.html: She runs. Back up the culvert, through the water, toward the palace and her father’s door, with her mind already making the sentence she will say to him.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 달린다. 수로를 거슬러, 물을 헤치고, 궁으로, 아버지 방문으로. 머릿속에선 벌써 아버지에게 할 말을 짓고 있다.

blocks.html: At the mouth of the culvert a girl in a fox mask is sitting on the step, waiting for her.
blocks.ko: 수로 어귀 계단에 여우탈 쓴 계집아이가 앉아 그녀를 기다리고 있다.

blocks.speaker: Little Fox
en: Are you going to tell?
…Yes.

blocks.speaker: Little Fox
lines: …그럼 우리 엄마 이름도 말해 줄래? 그 사람들 올 때. 누가 한 번은 소리 내서 말해 줘야 하잖아. 소리였어.
en: Okay.
…Then can you tell him my mum’s name? When they come? Somebody should say it once, out loud. It was Sori.

blocks.html: Chunmyung has been a princess all her life, and nobody has ever once asked her to carry a name. She stands in the culvert with the water going past her ankles for a long time.
blocks.ko: 천명은 평생 공주로 살았지만, 누가 이름 하나를 맡아 달라고 한 건 처음이다. 그녀는 발목으로 물이 지나가는 수로에 한참을 서 있다.

blocks.html: Then she goes back down.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 다시 내려간다.

lines: 돕지도 않을 거예요. 절대. 창 하나라도 보이면 내가 직접 이를 거예요.
그리고 약속해요. 무슨 일이 있어도, 그쪽이 뭐가 되든, 우리 아버지는 살아요. 아버지 집에서. 아버지 이름으로. 늙어서 죽어요.
en: I won’t tell him.
I won’t help you, either. Not ever. If I see one spear, I’ll tell him myself.
And you’ll promise me. Whatever happens, whatever you turn into, my father lives. In his own house. With his name. And he dies old.
I promise.

blocks.html: The song will say he showed her a world of ghosts under the bridge that month. He did. It just wasn’t the one in the song.
blocks.ko: 노래는 그달 그가 다리 밑 귀신들의 세상을 그녀에게 보여 줬다고 할 것이다. 보여 줬다. 다만 노래 속의 그 세상은 아니었다.

blocks.html: Every night he takes her down the culvert. The old man shows her where his eye was. The woman shows her three small mounds with no stones on them. The red-mask boy shows her the west gate, where the rope is still there. Up in the Moon Palace, the same men who did it are called her uncles.
blocks.ko: 밤마다 그는 그녀를 데리고 수로를 내려간다. 노인은 눈이 있던 자리를 보여 준다. 여자는 비석 하나 없는 작은 무덤 셋을 보여 준다. 빨간 탈은 서문을 보여 준다. 밧줄이 아직 그대로 걸려 있다. 월성 위에서는 그 짓을 한 사람들을 그녀가 아저씨라고 부른다.

blocks.html: The first night she can’t look at the eye. The fifth night she brings salve for it. The three boys steal her shoes and bring them back the next night, mended. By the end of the month she is holding the baby so its mother can sleep, and doing the rice-cake sums in her head, and losing her temper at the price of lamp oil like a woman who lives here.
blocks.ko: 첫날 밤 그녀는 그 눈을 쳐다보지 못한다. 닷새째 밤엔 연고를 들고 온다. 세 녀석은 그녀의 신을 훔쳐 가더니, 다음 날 밤 기워서 돌려준다. 그달 끝 무렵엔 애 엄마가 잘 수 있게 아기를 안고 있고, 떡값 셈을 머릿속으로 하고, 등잔 기름값에 성을 낸다. 여기 사는 여자처럼.

blocks.html: She comes back up each dawn with mud to the knee and a new list in her head: whose field, whose son, whose name under whose brush.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 새벽마다 무릎까지 진흙투성이로 올라온다. 머릿속엔 새 명단이 하나씩 늘어 있다. 누구네 밭, 누구네 아들, 누구의 붓 밑에 누구의 이름.

en: I’ve lived on top of this my whole life.
Everybody up there has.
That’s what the wall is for.
…Show me the rest.
Say it properly. Like a sane man.

lines: …약속해, 천명. 아버님은 당신 집에서, 당신 이름으로 사시다가, 늙어서 돌아가신다.
en: …I promise, Chunmyung. Your father lives in his own house, with his name, and dies old.

blocks.html: It is the first time he has said her name without a title in front of it. She notices. So does he.
blocks.ko: 그가 칭호 없이 그녀 이름을 부른 건 처음이다. 그녀가 알아챈다. 그도 안다.

lines: 이분은 약속을 지키오, 공주. 늦는 걸 한 번도 본 적이 없소.
en: He keeps his word, Highness. I have never once known him late.

blocks.html: That is the night it stops being an arrangement. Neither of them says so. At the top of the culvert she takes his hand because the steps are wet, and at the bottom of the lane she still hasn’t given it back.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그건 정해 준 혼사이기를 멈춘다. 둘 다 그렇게 말하진 않는다. 수로 꼭대기에서 그녀는 계단이 미끄러워 그의 손을 잡고, 골목 끝에 이르도록 돌려주지 않는다.

blocks.html: They are very proper about it. On the bridge she sits a hand’s width from him. Every night the hand’s width gets smaller, and both of them pretend to be measuring something else.
blocks.ko: 둘은 아주 점잖다. 다리 위에서 그녀는 그에게서 한 뼘 떨어져 앉는다. 밤마다 한 뼘이 줄어들고, 둘 다 다른 걸 재는 척한다.

blocks.html: At the top of the culvert, wet to the knees, she takes his collar in her fist to pull him up the last step, and then doesn’t let go of it.
blocks.ko: 수로 꼭대기에서, 무릎까지 젖은 채로, 그녀가 마지막 계단에서 끌어올리려고 그의 옷깃을 움켜쥔다. 그러고는 놓지 않는다.

en: You’re very quiet for a madman.
The stream told me to be careful with princesses.
The stream’s a coward.
Don’t come tomorrow.
Why.

lines: 그러다 어느 밤 누가 공주님 뒤를 밟겠지요. 그럼 다리도, 미치광이도, 셈하는 공주님도 없어지는 겁니다.
en: Because I’ll be here.
And one night somebody will follow you. Then there won’t be a bridge, or a madman, or a princess who does sums.

lines: 그쪽한테 시집갈게요. 아버지가 시켜서가 아니라. 내가 정해서.
en: Then I’ll make it simple for them.
I’ll marry you. Not because Father says. Because I’ve decided.
…Princess, he already decided.
Then it’s unanimous. Say yes.
My feet are cold.

blocks.html: He says yes. It is the first thing he has said in eight years that nobody was meant to overhear.
blocks.ko: 그는 좋다고 한다. 여덟 해 만에 처음으로, 아무도 엿듣지 않기를 바라며 한 말이다.

blocks.html: The court is scandalised for a season. A Sacred Bone princess, marrying down a bone, to a servant who argues with water. Then it decides this is good news. A princess who marries a madman has taken herself out of the count. A madman married into the king’s house is a madman nobody has to watch. Two birds, one wedding.
blocks.ko: 조정은 한 철 내내 발칵 뒤집힌다. 성골 공주가 뼈 하나를 내려가 시집을 간다. 그것도 물하고 말다툼하는 하인한테. 그러다 조정은 이게 좋은 소식이라고 결론 내린다. 미치광이에게 시집가는 공주는 스스로 셈에서 빠진 것이다. 왕실에 장가든 미치광이는 아무도 지켜볼 필요가 없는 미치광이다. 혼례 한 번에 새 두 마리.

blocks.html: The wedding is small, at the house by the stream. Only one other royal child comes. Dukman is seven. She has brought a rice cake for the stream, and she sets it on the water very seriously, and spends the whole night watching her sister as if she were learning a trade.
blocks.ko: 혼례는 개울가 집에서 조촐하게 치러진다. 다른 왕실 아이는 딱 하나 온다. 덕만은 일곱 살이다. 개울 몫으로 떡을 하나 가져와서 아주 진지하게 물 위에 띄우고는, 밤새 언니를 지켜본다. 무슨 기술이라도 배우는 사람처럼.

blocks.html: At the gate, uninvited, a woman in a plain coat stands with a boy of seven by the hand. She is the High Councillor’s daughter, the one who ran north with a Gaya boy, and the boy has a wooden sword through his belt and is standing like a guard. Suulbu’s chair is carried past them twice. He does not look. The boy looks at everything. His name is Yushin.
