blocks.ko: 대문 밖에, 초대받지 않은 여자가 수수한 옷차림으로 일곱 살 사내아이 손을 잡고 서 있다. 가야 사내와 북쪽으로 달아났던 그 상대등의 딸이다. 아이는 허리에 나무칼을 차고 파수처럼 서 있다. 수을부의 가마가 그 앞을 두 번 지나간다. 그는 쳐다보지 않는다. 아이는 전부 쳐다본다. 이름은 유신이다.

blocks.html: The first night in the house by the stream, out of habit, he starts telling the rafters about his day. She puts her hand over his mouth.
blocks.ko: 개울가 집에서의 첫날 밤, 그는 버릇처럼 서까래에 대고 하루 이야기를 늘어놓기 시작한다. 그녀가 손으로 그의 입을 막는다.

lines: 여기선 내 거야. 밖에서나 그 사람들 거 해.
en: Not in here.
In here you’re mine. Out there you can be theirs.

blocks.html: It is the only room in Surabol where he never once performs. The neighbours, listening at the wall for goblins, are bitterly disappointed.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에서 그가 단 한 번도 연기하지 않은 방은 그 방뿐이다. 담에 귀를 대고 도깨비 소리를 기다리던 이웃들은 몹시 실망한다.

blocks.label: The storehouse · the night before the clerk
blocks.ko: 창고 · 서기가 되기 전날 밤

lines: 임금이 사람 꼴 하고 나랏일 도울 도깨비를 원해요.
en: The king wants a goblin who can wear a man’s shape and help him govern.
Take the mask off. Come to the palace.
As what, young lord?

lines: 당신 자신으로요. 깨끗하고, 시간 지키고. 서기들보다 글도 잘 읽잖아요. 한 달이면 거기 다 꿰찰 거예요.
화백을 바꾸고 싶어요? 그 방에 있어요.
en: As yourself. Clean. Punctual. You read better than the clerks. You’d run the place inside a month.
You want the Council to change? Be in the room.
And when they ask where I came from?

lines: 귀신한테 가족이 있다는 것보단 훨씬 빨리 믿을걸요.
en: I’ll tell them I turned you into a man.
They’ll believe that long before they believe a ghost has a family.

blocks.html: Here is how a goblin is turned into a man. A basket with a real fox in it, bought from a trapper for a week of wages. A red cloth with a slit sewn down the middle. A floorboard under the dais that Gildal loosened himself, because he is good with floors. The madman sets the fox down and throws the cloth. Under it, the fox goes into a sack in his sleeve, and Gildal comes up through the floor. It takes the time of three words.
blocks.ko: 도깨비를 사람으로 바꾸는 법은 이렇다. 사냥꾼한테 일주일 품삯을 주고 산 진짜 여우가 든 바구니 하나. 가운데를 터서 꿰맨 붉은 천 하나. 길달이 손수 헐겁게 해 둔 옥좌 앞 마루청 하나. 마루는 그의 장기다. 미치광이가 여우를 내려놓고 천을 던진다. 천 밑에서 여우는 그의 소매 속 자루로 들어가고, 길달은 마루 밑에서 올라온다. 말 세 마디면 끝나는 시간이다.

en: And if the fox bites?
Then I’ll be a madman with a bandage. Nobody will notice.
lines: 그럼 붕대 감은 미치광이가 되는 거지. 아무도 눈치 못 채.

blocks.html: So he does. The court is very impressed by the transformation. Gildal says nothing, which they take for goblin modesty. Imjong adopts him because the king asks nicely. Gildal builds his new father a gate and sleeps on top of it, and from the roof of that gate you can see the Council’s whole street.
blocks.ko: 그래서 그렇게 된다. 조정은 그 둔갑에 크게 감탄한다. 길달은 아무 말도 안 하고, 사람들은 그걸 도깨비의 겸손으로 친다. 임종은 임금이 정중히 청하니 그를 양자로 들인다. 길달은 새 아버지에게 문을 지어 주고 그 위에서 잔다. 그 문루 지붕에선 화백 거리가 한눈에 보인다.

blocks.html: One man is not impressed. Suulbu has been counting the madman for years: who sells him rice cakes, why the stream talks loudest on nights the Council sits, how a servant with no office pays forty men. He doesn’t know the answer yet. He knows it adds up to something.
blocks.ko: 감탄하지 않는 사람이 하나 있다. 수을부는 몇 해째 미치광이를 세고 있었다. 누가 떡을 대 주는지, 왜 화백이 열리는 밤에만 냇물이 제일 시끄러운지, 벼슬도 없는 하인이 어떻게 마흔 사람 품삯을 대는지. 답은 아직 모른다. 다만 셈이 뭔가로 맞아떨어진다는 건 안다.

blocks.html: A month later Suulbu puts a servant behind the screen in the east corridor, where the madman talks to the rafters every evening. The servant comes back white.
blocks.ko: 한 달 뒤 수을부는 동쪽 회랑 병풍 뒤에 하인 하나를 숨긴다. 미치광이가 저녁마다 서까래와 떠드는 곳이다. 하인은 하얗게 질려 돌아온다.

blocks.speaker: A servant
en: He was talking to something, my lord. It answered. I couldn’t hear it, but he kept waiting for it to finish.
…And it was about wages, my lord. Who’s owed for what.
lines: 뭔가랑 말을 하고 있었습니다, 나리. 대답도 했고요. 저한텐 안 들렸는데, 그분이 자꾸 그게 말 끝나길 기다렸어요.
…그런데 품삯 얘기였습니다, 나리. 누구한테 얼마 줘야 하는지.

en: Ghosts don’t get paid.

blocks.html: The next morning he asks the king, very politely, whether a palace is the right place for a man who argues with walls.
blocks.ko: 이튿날 아침 그는 아주 공손하게 왕에게 묻는다. 벽과 말다툼하는 자가 궁에 있어도 되겠느냐고.

en: The provinces are quieter, Majesty. Fewer walls. He might get well.
lines: 지방은 조용하옵니다, 폐하. 벽도 적고요. 나을지도 모르지요.

en: He talks to walls, uncle. You talk to the Council.
I know which one of you I’d rather send away.
lines: 저 아이는 벽이랑 말하지요, 숙부. 숙부는 화백이랑 하시고.
둘 중 누굴 보내고 싶은지는 과인이 압니다.

blocks.label: The Harmony Council · the cellar
blocks.ko: 화백회의 · 지하 옥

blocks.html: Then a child gets caught. That is how it always goes. Never the clever man. The child.
blocks.ko: 그러다 아이 하나가 잡힌다. 늘 그렇게 된다. 똑똑한 사내는 절대 안 잡힌다. 아이가 잡힌다.

blocks.html: The smallest of the three boys is twelve now, and quick, and he has been running messages through the culvert for years in his red mask. One night the watch is somewhere it usually isn’t. They bring him to the Council’s cellar with the mask still on. Somebody takes it off. He is furious about that.
blocks.ko: 사내아이 셋 중 제일 작은 놈이 이제 열둘, 날쌔다. 몇 해째 빨간 탈을 쓰고 수로로 전갈을 날라 왔다. 어느 밤 순라가 평소엔 없던 자리에 있다. 탈을 쓴 채로 화백 지하 옥에 끌려온다. 누가 탈을 벗긴다. 아이는 그게 제일 분하다.

blocks.speaker: Little Red
lines: 후회할걸. 다 후회할 거야. 그분이 임금 되면—
en: Give it back. That’s mine.
You’ll be sorry. You’ll all be sorry. When he’s king—
When who is king, child?

blocks.speaker: Little Red
lines: …복권이 되면 다 돌려받는 거야, 그럼 너희가 절해야 돼, 그리고 길달 아저씨가—
en: I’m not telling.
…The Restoration’s going to restore everybody, and you’ll have to bow, and Gildal says—
I’m not TELLING!

blocks.html: He doesn’t tell. She doesn’t need to. Suulbu has heard “Gildal.” He has heard “when he’s king.” In this city there is exactly one man who could be he, and he talks to streams.
blocks.ko: 아이는 말하지 않는다. 그럴 필요도 없다. 수을부는 “길달”을 들었다. “그분이 임금 되면”도 들었다. 이 도성에서 그분일 수 있는 사내는 딱 하나, 개울하고 얘기하는 놈이다.

lines: 그리고 임종을 불러라. 여우를 양자로 들였더구나.
en: Put him somewhere.
And send for Imjong. He’s adopted a fox.

blocks.label: The gate south of Heungnyun temple · that night
blocks.ko: 흥륜사 남쪽 문 · 그날 밤

blocks.html: Gildal hears by the second watch. He has never once been late. He leaves his gate, which a fox will do, goes into the Council’s cellar by a drain only he knows, and comes out with a twelve-year-old on his back. By dawn the boy is somewhere safe. He isn’t.
blocks.ko: 길달은 이경에 소식을 듣는다. 그는 한 번도 늦은 적이 없다. 그는 문을 비운다. 여우라면 그런다. 자기만 아는 수채로 화백 지하 옥에 들어가서 열두 살짜리를 업고 나온다. 새벽이면 아이는 안전한 데 있다. 그는 아니다.

blocks.html: The gate is empty in the morning. Imjong writes to the Council within the hour. That is the fox running down the south road with its tail very low.
blocks.ko: 아침에 문이 비어 있다. 임종은 한 시진도 안 돼 화백에 글을 올린다. 그게 꼬리를 축 늘어뜨리고 남쪽 길로 달아나는 여우다.

blocks.label: The throne hall · the next morning
blocks.ko: 정전 · 이튿날 아침

blocks.html: The Council doesn’t ask the king for a hanging. It asks for something cleverer.
blocks.ko: 화백은 임금에게 교수형을 청하지 않는다. 더 영리한 걸 청한다.

lines: 전하, 전하의 서기는 역도이옵니다. 전하의 미치광이가 들여온 자지요.
그 미치광이를 보내 데려오게 하십시오. 사병을 붙여서. 죽여서.
en: Majesty, your clerk is a rebel. Your madman brought him to us.
Send the madman to fetch him back. With riders. Dead.
Bihyung doesn’t know anything about—
Then it will cost him nothing.

blocks.html: Jinpyung doesn’t know. That matters. Nobody ever told him. He looks down the hall at his cousin, who is at the back in a sleeping robe, telling a pillar about the weather.
blocks.ko: 진평왕은 모른다. 그게 중요하다. 아무도 말해 준 적이 없다. 그는 전각 끝의 사촌을 내려다본다. 잠옷 차림으로 맨 뒤에 서서 기둥한테 날씨 얘기를 하고 있다.

en: Bihyung. The fox ran.
Go and get him.

lines: 전하, 여우는 엄청 빠르고 저는 엄청—
여우는 제 말 안 들어요, 전하. 개울이 오늘은 여우한테 안 좋은 날이래요, 그리고—
en: Majesty, the fox is very fast and I’m very—
Foxes don’t listen to me, Majesty. The stream says it’s a bad day for foxes, and—

lines: 전하, 저자가 안 간다면 답은 나온 겁니다. 역도를 못 쫓겠다는 자가 바로 그 역도를 부려 온 자지요.
en: The stream can come too.
Majesty, if he won’t go, then we have our answer. A man who won’t hunt a rebel is the man who’s been running him.

blocks.html: It’s true, which is the worst kind of threat. Yongsu looks at his cousin. His cousin looks back with nothing in his face but trust, and that is worse.
blocks.ko: 맞는 말이다. 그게 가장 나쁜 협박이다. 용수는 사촌을 본다. 사촌은 믿음 말고는 아무것도 없는 얼굴로 그를 마주 본다. 그게 더 나쁘다.

en: …Bihyung. Please.
…Yes, Majesty.
I’ll bring him back. The goblins will help.

blocks.label: The south road · the reeds at dawn
blocks.ko: 남쪽 길 · 새벽 갈대밭

blocks.html: Forty of Imjong’s riders, and Imjong himself at the back, very upright, because a man whose adopted son has run had better be seen riding after him. At the front, the madman on a borrowed horse, singing to it.
blocks.ko: 임종의 사병 마흔. 맨 뒤엔 임종 자신이 꼿꼿이 앉아 있다. 양아들이 달아난 사내라면 뒤쫓는 모습을 보여야 하니까. 맨 앞엔 빌린 말 위의 미친놈. 말한테 노래를 불러 준다.

blocks.html: They find Gildal at dawn where the south road meets the river, sitting in the reeds with an arrow in his leg from the night before. He has been waiting. He has folded his hands.
blocks.ko: 새벽, 남쪽 길이 강과 만나는 갈대밭에서 길달을 찾는다. 간밤에 맞은 화살을 다리에 꽂은 채 앉아 있다. 기다리고 있었다. 손을 모으고 있다.

blocks.html: Yongsu gets down. He walks out into the reeds alone with the knife the riders gave him, scolding all the way: bad fox, late fox. The riders laugh. When he reaches Gildal, he stops talking.
blocks.ko: 용수가 말에서 내린다. 사병들이 쥐여 준 칼을 들고 혼자 갈대밭으로 걸어 들어간다. 가는 내내 꾸짖는다. 나쁜 여우, 늦은 여우. 사병들이 웃는다. 길달 앞에 이르자 그는 말을 멈춘다.

blocks.html: The knife doesn’t move. Gildal looks up at him, then at the riders, then at Imjong on his horse, and understands the whole thing before Yongsu can say a word of it.
blocks.ko: 칼이 움직이지 않는다. 길달은 그를 올려다보고, 사병들을 보고, 말 위의 임종을 보고, 용수가 한마디 꺼내기도 전에 전부 알아챈다.

en: …Ah. They sent you.
Of course they did. It’s clever. I would have done the same.
Young lord. The knife.
…What knife?

lines: 손에 든 그 칼이오. 손목을 주시오.
저들 말 위에서 보면, 이걸 하는 사람은 충신이오. 다시는 도련님을 세지 않을 거요.
en: The one in your hand. Give me your wrist.
From their horses, a man who does this is loyal. They will stop counting you.
It’s heavy.
Then I will hold it with you.
No, Gildal! You cannot…
You must not…

lines: 그대는 큰 운명을 지닌 분이오……! 나는 그저 도깨비일 뿐이오.
도련님의 도깨비로 내 이름이 이야기에 실린다면, 그것으로 족하오.
en: Young lord…
You are a man with a great fate…! I am just a goblin.
If my name goes into the stories as your goblin, that will be enough for me.

blocks.html: Yongsu has talked his way past fifty guards, a Council and a princess. He has nothing to say to this. His eyes go first.
blocks.ko: 용수는 말 한마디로 파수 오십과 화백과 공주를 지나왔다. 그런 그가 이 말 앞에서는 할 말이 없다. 눈이 먼저 무너진다.

en: Very well…
I’ll make sure your name is remembered for all time.

lines: 저 위에서 다시 만납시다. 늦지 않으리다.
en: We’ll meet again, up there. I won’t be late.

blocks.html: He takes Yongsu’s wrist, very gently, the way you steady a boy’s hand on a brush, and sets the knife where it needs to go. Neither of them can hold it steady the first time. Then he looks past Yongsu at the forty riders, and fills his chest with the last of his air.
blocks.ko: 그는 용수의 손목을 아주 살며시 잡는다. 붓 잡은 아이 손을 잡아 주듯이. 그리고 칼을 가야 할 자리에 갖다 댄다. 둘 다 첫 번엔 손이 떨려 못 한다. 그러고는 용수 너머 사병 마흔을 보며, 남은 숨을 가슴 가득 들이쉰다.

en: THE BLOODLINE OF KIM YONGSU WILL BE RESTORED…!

blocks.html: The riders look at each other. Yongsu? Who’s Yongsu? One of them laughs. Somebody says it must be a goblin word.
blocks.ko: 사병들이 서로 쳐다본다. 용수? 용수가 누구야? 하나가 웃는다. 누가 도깨비 말인가 보다 한다.

blocks.html: At the back, Imjong sits very still. He has seen Suulbu’s list. There is one name near the top that was never crossed off, because nobody could ever find a boy called that. The hair stands up along his arms. He says nothing. He will say nothing for fifty years. That is how he lives so long.
blocks.ko: 맨 뒤의 임종은 꼼짝 않는다. 그는 수을부의 명단을 본 적이 있다. 맨 위 가까이에 끝내 지워지지 않은 이름이 하나 있었다. 그런 이름의 아이를 아무도 찾지 못했으니까. 팔에 소름이 돋는다. 그는 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 오십 년 동안 아무 말도 하지 않을 것이다. 그렇게 오래 산다.

blocks.html: Yongsu weeps without a sound, so that nobody behind him can see his shoulders move, and cuts his friend’s throat.
blocks.ko: 용수는 소리 없이 운다. 뒤에서 어깨가 들썩이는 게 안 보이게. 그리고 친구의 목을 벤다.

blocks.label: Surabol · the ride
blocks.ko: 서라벌 · 말 달리기

blocks.html: Then he does the strangest thing anyone in Surabol has ever seen him do, which is saying something.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 서라벌 누구도 본 적 없는 가장 이상한 짓을 한다. 그에게서 그 정도면 대단한 거다.

blocks.html: He lifts the body over his saddle himself. He won’t let the riders touch it. He climbs up behind it and turns the horse not toward the palace but into the city, and rides. Every ward. Every market. Past the temples and the wells and the Council’s street, at a gallop, all day, screaming at the top of his lungs.
blocks.ko: 그는 시신을 제 손으로 안장에 걸친다. 사병들은 손도 못 대게 한다. 그 뒤에 올라타 말머리를 궁이 아니라 도성 안으로 돌리고, 달린다. 모든 부. 모든 장터. 절과 우물과 화백 거리를 지나, 전속력으로, 하루 종일, 목이 터져라 외치면서.

lines: 대왕 만세! 여우가 죽었다! 대왕 만세…!
en: LONG LIVE KING JINPYUNG…!
LONG LIVE THE KING! THE FOX IS DEAD! LONG LIVE THE KING…!

blocks.html: From the palace wall he is very small: one horse, one rider, something orange across the saddle, going ward by ward. Nobody up there can see his face. They can see what the ride does to the streets. Doors close. A child is pulled indoors by the collar. On the Council’s balcony Suulbu stands up so fast his chair goes over, and for once in his life he looks old.
blocks.ko: 궁성 담 위에서 보면 그는 아주 작다. 말 한 필, 사람 하나, 안장에 걸친 주황빛 무언가. 동네에서 동네로. 위에서는 아무도 그의 얼굴을 못 본다. 보이는 건 그 행렬이 거리에 하는 짓이다. 문이 닫힌다. 아이 하나가 멱살 잡혀 집 안으로 끌려 들어간다. 화백 누각에서 수을부가 너무 급히 일어나 의자가 넘어가고, 그는 평생 처음으로 늙어 보인다.

blocks.html: Surabol comes out to watch. Most of it decides he has finally gone all the way mad, and says so. Children throw things. An old woman spits. Behind the palace screens, Jinpyung hears it come round the wall for the third time and lets out a breath he has been holding since morning. His cousin was never against him. He told them so.
blocks.ko: 서라벌이 구경하러 나온다. 대부분은 이제 완전히 미쳤구나 하고, 대놓고 그렇게 말한다. 아이들이 뭘 던진다. 노파 하나가 침을 뱉는다. 궁 병풍 뒤의 진평왕은 그 소리가 세 번째로 담을 돌아오는 걸 듣고, 아침부터 참고 있던 숨을 내쉰다. 사촌은 한 번도 그를 등진 적이 없다. 그가 그렇게 말하지 않았던가.

blocks.html: The Council hears it too, and enjoys it less. Their little fox told them the madman and the clerk were in it together. Well, there goes the madman, screaming the king’s name with the clerk’s blood down his leg. At the next sitting three councillors find reasons not to look at Suulbu. A council keeps two ledgers. This goes in the other one.
blocks.ko: 화백도 듣는다. 덜 즐겁다. 그들의 작은 여우는 미친놈과 서기가 한패라 했다. 그런데 저기 미친놈이 서기 피를 다리에 묻힌 채 임금 이름을 외치며 지나간다. 다음 회의에서 화백 셋이 수을부와 눈을 안 맞출 핑계를 찾는다. 화백은 장부를 둘 둔다. 이건 다른 쪽에 적힌다.

blocks.html: And under the bridges, in the culvert, in the reeds, people in masks hear a madman scream a king’s name across the whole city, and understand exactly what he is telling them. It’s over. Stay down. Don’t come for me. Don’t come.
blocks.ko: 그리고 다리 밑에서, 수로 속에서, 갈대밭에서, 탈 쓴 사람들은 온 도성을 가로질러 임금 이름을 외치는 미친놈의 목소리를 듣고, 그가 하는 말을 정확히 알아듣는다. 끝났다. 엎드려 있어라. 나한테 오지 마라. 오지 마.

blocks.html: They don’t come. They never come again. That is why, the song says, the ghosts of Surabol are afraid of the name Bihyung.
blocks.ko: 그들은 오지 않는다. 다시는 오지 않는다. 그래서, 노래에 따르면, 서라벌 귀신들은 비형이라는 이름만 들어도 겁을 낸다.

blocks.html: He rides until the horse won’t. Nobody notices he is crying. A madman’s face is always doing something.
blocks.ko: 그는 말이 더 못 갈 때까지 달린다. 그가 울고 있다는 건 아무도 모른다. 미친놈 얼굴은 늘 뭔가를 하고 있으니까.

blocks.html: When he gets home Chunmyung puts him in the bath and sits on the floor beside it until morning. She doesn’t say a word. She is very good at that.
blocks.ko: 집에 오자 천명은 그를 목욕통에 넣고 아침까지 그 옆 바닥에 앉아 있다. 한마디도 안 한다. 그런 걸 아주 잘한다.

blocks.html: The next morning the king hugs him in front of the whole hall. “I told them,” he says. Yongsu lets him. He never tells him either. That one is his to carry.
blocks.ko: 이튿날 아침 임금은 온 조정 앞에서 그를 안는다. “내가 그렇게 말했잖나.” 용수는 가만히 있는다. 그에게도 끝내 말하지 않는다. 그건 그가 질 짐이다.

blocks.label: Chunchu
blocks.ko: 춘추

blocks.label: The House by the Stream · spring
blocks.ko: 개울가 집 · 봄

blocks.html: Spring comes early. Chunmyung labours all night in the house by the water while her husband talks to the stream for nine hours, loudly, and in the morning there is a boy.
blocks.ko: 봄이 일찍 온다. 천명이 물가 집에서 밤새 산고를 겪는 동안 남편은 아홉 시간 내내 큰 소리로 개울에 말을 건다. 아침이 되자 사내아이가 하나 있다.

blocks.label: The palace stream · night
blocks.ko: 궁 개울 · 밤

blocks.html: Chunchu is nine and mortified. The boys in the yard call him the goblin’s whelp, and he has started to believe them.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 아홉 살이고, 창피해 죽을 지경이다. 마당 아이들은 그를 도깨비 새끼라고 부르고, 그도 슬슬 그 말을 믿기 시작했다.

blocks.html: Tonight his father is kneeling in the stream with his sleeves tied back, laying flat stones in a line and muttering to each one before he sets it down.
blocks.ko: 오늘 밤 아버지는 소매를 걷어 묶고 개울에 무릎을 꿇은 채, 납작한 돌을 한 줄로 놓고 있다. 돌 하나 놓을 때마다 뭐라고 중얼거리면서.

en: Father. Everyone can see you.
The watchmen are laughing.

lines: 잘됐다. 웃게 둬라. 웃는 사람은 셈을 안 해.
이리 와. 이거 하나 들어 봐.
en: Good. Let them laugh. Laughing men aren’t counting.
Come here. Hold this one.
Who are you talking to?

lines: 궁에 의자 여섯 개 놓인 방이 있다. 그 방은 저를 즐겁게 해 주는 사내들을 잡아먹어. 그 방엔 들어가지 마라.
en: The stones.
…You, mostly. You just don’t know it yet.
There’s a room in the palace with six chairs in it. That room eats the men who amuse it. Stay out of that room.

blocks.html: Chunchu decides his father is the strangest man in Silla. He will go on thinking so for thirty years. He will be wrong for all thirty.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 아버지가 신라에서 제일 이상한 사람이라고 결론 내린다. 그 생각은 서른 해 동안 이어진다. 서른 해 내내 틀린 생각이다.

blocks.label: The palace yard · the winter Chunchu was eleven
blocks.ko: 궁 마당 · 춘추가 열한 살이던 겨울

blocks.html: He was eleven, and there were five of them, and they had him down in the slush behind the stables. His father was on the stream bank thirty paces away, singing to a stone. He didn’t come. He kept singing.
blocks.ko: 열한 살이었고, 그들은 다섯이었고, 마구간 뒤 진창에 그를 눕혀 놓았다. 아버지는 서른 걸음 떨어진 개울가에서 돌한테 노래를 불러 주고 있었다. 오지 않았다. 계속 노래했다.

blocks.html: That night, in the one room where his father never performed, he cleaned the cut over Chunchu’s eye without a word. Then he asked the only question.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤, 아버지가 한 번도 연기하지 않던 그 방에서, 아버지는 말없이 춘추 눈 위 상처를 닦았다. 그러고는 단 하나를 물었다.

en: Did you count them?
…Five.
Names.

blocks.html: Chunchu gave him the names. His father nodded at each one, like a clerk.
blocks.ko: 춘추가 이름을 댔다. 아버지는 하나하나 서기처럼 고개를 끄덕였다.

en: Good. Keep them. Don’t use them yet.

blocks.html: He hated his father that winter more than he hated the five.
blocks.ko: 그해 겨울 그는 그 다섯보다 아버지가 더 미웠다.

blocks.label: Surabol · Chunchu’s wedding
blocks.ko: 서라벌 · 춘추의 혼례

blocks.html: Thirteen years later the goblin’s whelp marries the sister of the strongest boy in Silla. Across the hall, ninety-year-old Suulbu sends a cup, and only the groom’s father understands it.
blocks.ko: 열세 해 뒤 도깨비 새끼가 신라에서 제일 센 소년의 누이와 혼인한다. 전각 건너편에서 아흔 살 수을부가 잔을 보내고, 그 뜻을 아는 건 신랑의 아버지뿐이다.

blocks.label: The palace · the year of the crown
blocks.ko: 궁 · 즉위하던 해

blocks.html: The little girl who asked whether the stream was invited to the wedding grows up and becomes the first queen of Silla. On his last night, her father sends everyone out of the room but her, and tells her a story that is not in any book.
blocks.ko: 혼례에 개울도 초대받았냐고 묻던 꼬마는 자라서 신라의 첫 여왕이 된다. 아버지는 마지막 밤, 그녀만 남기고 모두 방에서 내보낸 뒤, 어느 책에도 없는 이야기를 들려준다.

blocks.html: A week after the funeral she sends for her sister’s husband. Not to the hall. To the small room behind it, with one lamp, where kings keep the things they would rather the Council didn’t see.
blocks.ko: 장례가 끝나고 한 주 뒤, 그녀는 언니의 남편을 부른다. 정전이 아니라, 그 뒤의 등불 하나 켜진 작은 방으로. 임금들이 회의에 보이고 싶지 않은 것들을 두는 방이다.

lines: 전하! 동쪽 채 서까래가 엄청 수다스럽다는 거 아셨습니까? 누구한테 말해야지 하던 참이었는데—
en: Majesty! Did you know the rafters in the east wing are terribly talkative? I’ve been meaning to tell someone—

lines: 아버지가 말씀해 주셨네. 마지막 밤에. 전부.
en: Sit down, brother-in-law.
Father told me. The last night. All of it.

blocks.html: He stops. For a while he looks at the lamp instead of her, the way a man looks at a road he had decided never to walk down again.
blocks.ko: 그가 멈춘다. 한동안 그는 그녀 대신 등불을 본다. 다시는 걷지 않기로 한 길을 바라보는 사람처럼.

en: …All of it is a great deal for one night.

lines: 형부 어머니. 아버지의 숙부. 있지도 않았던 강둑.
언니는 혼례 전에 알았어. 난 서른일곱에, 죽어 가는 사람한테 들었고. 순서가 좀 서운해.
en: He’d been saving it up.
Your mother. His uncle. A river bank that never happened.
Unni knew before her wedding. I was told at thirty-seven by a dying man. I’m a little cross about the order.

lines: 언니는 혼자 알아냈어요. 마마는 일곱 살이었고.
en: Your sister found out on her own. You were seven.
It isn’t a race.
Everything in this family is a race.

blocks.html: Then she leans across the table and says the thing she sent for him to say.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 상 너머로 몸을 기울여, 그를 불러 놓고 하려던 말을 한다.

lines: 형부는 내 곳간의 누구보다 셈이 빠른데, 사십 년을 열까지도 못 세는 척하며 살았지.
이 나라엔 지어야 할 게 산더미야. 그중 하나쯤은 정직한 사람이 지었으면 하네.
en: I want you out of the reeds.
You add faster than anyone in my treasury, and you’ve spent forty years pretending you can’t count to ten.
I have a kingdom full of things that need building. I’d like one of them built by somebody honest.

lines: 전하, 서라벌 절반이 귀신 쫓는다고 제 이름을 대문에 붙입니다.
en: Honest.
Majesty, half of Surabol pastes my name on its doors to keep the ghosts out.

lines: 그럼 형부가 귀신들 장부를 들여다보기 시작하면, 귀신들이 무척 헷갈려 하겠군.
en: Then the ghosts will be very confused when you start checking their accounts.
The Council won’t like it.
The Council doesn’t like me either.
We can keep each other company.

lines: …그럼 이야기는 그대로 둡시다. 도깨비, 여우, 약속을 지킨 혼령.
en: …Then the story stays. The goblins, the fox, the ghost who kept his word.
Let the book keep that one.
Why?

lines: 진짜 이야기엔 아직 산 사람들이 나오니까요.
그중 몇은 전하의 회의에 앉아 있고요.
en: Because the true one still has living men in it.
Some of them sit on your Council.

blocks.html: She thinks about that for as long as it takes the lamp to gutter. Then she nods. That winter the two of them write the ghost story down properly, so that nobody will ever need to go looking for the other one.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 등불이 한 번 일렁일 동안 생각한다. 그리고 고개를 끄덕인다. 그해 겨울 두 사람은 귀신 이야기를 제대로 받아 적는다. 아무도 다른 이야기를 찾으러 나설 필요가 없도록.

en: Does Chunchu know?
No.
Only the stories.

lines: 그 애가 스물아홉이야. 우리 둘보다 영리하고.
en: He’s twenty-nine. He’s cleverer than both of us.
That’s why.
…Unni knew. And she married you anyway.
She says it was the sums.

lines: 어렸을 땐 언니처럼 되고 싶었어. 대신 여왕이 됐지.
en: When I was small I wanted to be her. I got to be queen instead.
…It isn’t the same.

blocks.html: She pours the tea herself. Everyone who comes into this room wants something, and she would rather hear it now.
blocks.ko: 차는 그녀가 손수 따른다. 이 방에 드는 사람은 누구나 뭔가를 원한다. 그녀는 그걸 지금 듣는 편이 낫다.

lines: 자. 품계. 땅. 어머님 이름을 새긴 위패.
en: So. A rank. Land. Your mother’s name on a tablet.
Name it.

lines: 이 도성 밑에 마흔 해째 죽어 지내는 사람들이 있어요. 그 사람들을 살려 주세요.
en: One thing.
There are people under this city who’ve been dead for forty years. Bring them back.
…How many?

lines: 마흔하나요. 이제는 서른여덟. 나무 할배가 봄에 갔어요.
그때 애였던 놈들도 있어요. 지금은 장가까지 든 어른인데, 누구 하나 대낮에 부를 이름이 없어요.
en: Forty-one. Thirty-eight, now. Old Man Tree went in the spring.
Some of them were children when it happened. They’re grown men with wives, and none of them has a name you can say in daylight.
The Council will hate this more than they hate you.
Then you’ll have even more company.
Write me the list.

blocks.html: He takes it out of his sleeve. It is very old, the paper soft as cloth, written in a boy’s hand in a culvert and added to for forty years.
blocks.ko: 그는 소매에서 그걸 꺼낸다. 아주 오래된 종이다. 천처럼 보드랍다. 수로 속에서 소년의 손으로 쓰기 시작해 마흔 해 동안 보태 온 명단이다.

blocks.html: She reads it twice. Half the names she has seen before, on the Council’s own list, crossed out. She takes up her brush and uncrosses them.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 두 번 읽는다. 절반은 본 적 있는 이름이다. 화백의 명단에서, 줄이 그어진 채로. 그녀는 붓을 들어 그 줄을 걷어 낸다.

blocks.html: The next morning the east wing gets a new resident and a title nobody can object to, because it doesn’t mean anything. The servants still cross the courtyard rather than pass his door after dark. He still talks to the rafters when anyone is listening. When nobody is, he reads the treasury’s books, and for the first time in years the treasury starts to add up.
blocks.ko: 이튿날 아침 동쪽 채에 새 식구가 들고, 아무도 토를 달 수 없는 직함이 붙는다. 아무 뜻도 없는 직함이니까. 하인들은 여전히 해가 지면 그의 방문 앞을 지나가느니 마당을 가로질러 돌아간다. 누가 듣고 있으면 그는 여전히 서까래와 이야기한다. 아무도 없을 땐 곳간 장부를 읽는다. 그리고 몇 해 만에 처음으로, 곳간의 셈이 맞아떨어지기 시작한다.

blocks.label: The hill above the reeds · the first spring of the restoration
blocks.ko: 갈대밭 위 언덕 · 복권 첫 봄

blocks.html: The first thing the restored do with their names is bury somebody properly.
blocks.ko: 복권된 사람들이 제 이름을 되찾고 맨 먼저 한 일은, 누군가를 제대로 묻어 주는 것이다.

blocks.html: Gildal has been in the reeds for thirty years under a stone with nothing on it. They lift him in daylight and carry him up the hill, where you can hear the Heungnyun bells. No Council men. No song.
blocks.ko: 길달은 서른 해 동안 아무것도 새기지 않은 돌 밑, 갈대밭에 누워 있었다. 그들은 대낮에 그를 들어 올려 흥륜사 종소리가 들리는 언덕으로 메고 간다. 화백 사람은 없다. 노래도 없다.

blocks.html: The Rock Lady walks in front. The three brothers who aren’t brothers carry the bier, grey at the temples now. The one who never took off his red mask has taken it off.
blocks.ko: 바위 할매가 맨 앞에서 걷는다. 형제 아닌 세 형제가 상여를 멘다. 이제 관자놀이가 희끗하다. 빨간 탈을 한 번도 벗지 않던 녀석은 오늘 탈을 벗었다.

blocks.html: At the top, the girl from the culvert step, forty now, unties the fox mask she has worn since she was six and puts it in Yongsu’s hands. She doesn’t need it any more. She has a name.
blocks.ko: 꼭대기에서, 수로 계단의 그 계집아이가, 이제 마흔인 그녀가, 여섯 살부터 쓰던 여우탈을 풀어 용수 손에 쥐여 준다. 이제 그녀에겐 필요 없다. 이름이 있으니까.

blocks.html: He ties it to a pole himself and drives the pole into the top of the mound, so the fox looks down the south road.
blocks.ko: 그는 손수 그것을 장대에 매달아 봉분 꼭대기에 꽂는다. 여우가 남쪽 길을 내려다보도록.

lines: 됐다. 이제 오는 게 다 보이지.
en: There. Now you’ll see them coming.
…I’m the late one this time. Thirty years.

lines: 그 사람이면 딱 맞춰 왔다고 할 거야.
en: He’d say you were exactly on time.
He’d say it to be polite.
Then he’d shim the pole.

blocks.html: Down in the valley the Heungnyun bell rings the hour. Exactly on it.
blocks.ko: 골짜기 아래에서 흥륜사 종이 시를 친다. 딱 맞춰서.

blocks.label: The bluff
blocks.ko: 벼랑

lines: 보고 계셨죠. 그해 겨울. 다섯이었는데, 노래를 부르셨어요.
en: You watched. That winter. Five of them, and you sang.

lines: 내가 내려갔으면 그 사람들이 너를 세기 시작했을 거다.
en: If I’d come down, they’d have started counting you.
…Do you still have the names?

lines: 둘은 죽었어요. 하나는 화백에 앉아 있고요.
en: Two are dead. One sits on the Council.

lines: 그럼 한동안은 그 사람한테 깍듯하게 하렴.
en: Then you’ll want to be polite to him for a while.

lines: 그럼 전부 다요. 못에 던져진 거. 신발에 든 소금.
누가 아버지랑 같이 있는 걸 볼까 봐 제가 먼 길로 돌아다닌 것까지—
en: So all of it. The pond. The salt in your shoes.
Every time I walked the long way round so nobody would see me with you—

lines: 네가 나한테 해 준 일 중에 제일 고마운 일이었다. 아비를 부끄러워하는 아들은 아비랑 작당을 안 하거든. 아무도 너를 세지 않았다. 넌 안전했지.
en: I saw you.
It was the best thing you ever did for me. A boy who’s ashamed of his father isn’t plotting with him. Nobody counted you. You were safe.

blocks.html: Chunchu is crying. He doesn’t notice when it starts. His father doesn’t mention it.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 울고 있다. 언제부터인지도 모른다. 아버지는 아무 말도 하지 않는다.

lines: 다리 위의 도깨비들. 아버지한테 절하던 여우. 전 그 애한테 할아버지 얘기 그만 들으라고 했어요.
en: Bupmin’s dreams.
The goblins on the bridge. The fox who bowed to you. I told him to stop listening to you.

lines: 나 죽고 나면 누군가는 그 애들 이름을 기억해야지. 여섯 살짜리 말은 아무도 안 믿거든.
en: Every one of them true.
Somebody has to remember their names when I’m gone. Nobody believes a six-year-old.
Does Mother—

lines: 네 어미는 혼례 한 달 전에 알아냈다. 시녀 옷을 입고 날 따라 하수구로 내려왔지.
그러고는 남았다. 자기 아버지가 당신 집에서, 당신 이름으로, 늙어서 죽게 해 달라고 약속을 받아 냈어. 그대로 되셨지. 그 자리에서 쉰세 해.
덕만은 앞 절반만 안다. 돌아가시던 밤 아버지한테 들었지. 그해 겨울 둘이서 귀신 이야기를 적었다. 아무도 다른 쪽을 찾으러 오지 않게.
en: Your mother found out a month before the wedding. She followed me down a drain in a maid’s coat.
She stayed. She made me promise her father would die old, in his own house, with his name. He did. Fifty-three years on that chair.
Dukman knows the first half. Her father told her the night he died. She and I wrote the ghost story down that winter, so nobody would go looking for the other one.
Why now?

lines: 오늘 밤 네 얼굴이 네 할아버지 얼굴이다. 안 좋은 쪽. 고타소 일로 뭔가 할 거고, 그러자면 무릎을 꿇어야 할 거다. 그 사람들 전각에서. 그 사람들 웃음 앞에서. 어쩌면 빌기도 하고.
그러니 그 궁이 나한테 가르쳐 준 유일하게 쓸모 있는 걸 들어라.
en: Because of your face.
You’ve got your grandfather’s face on tonight. The bad one. You’re going to do something about Gotaso, and it’s going to mean kneeling. Their halls. Their laughing. Begging, maybe.
So here’s the only useful thing that palace ever taught me.

lines: 내겐 자존심 같은 건 없다. 오직 목표만 있을 뿐이다…!
그리고 그 길을 막는 놈은 누구든, 갈가리 찢겨 곧장 지옥으로 간다…!
en: I have no such thing as pride. I only have my goal…!
And whoever gets in my way will be ripped apart, straight into hell…!

blocks.html: He says it the way other men say grace. Quietly. The gentlest man in Surabol, on a bluff, with his sleeve over his son’s shoulders.
blocks.ko: 그는 그 말을 남들이 식전 기도 하듯 한다. 조용히. 서라벌에서 제일 순한 사내가, 벼랑 위에서, 아들 어깨에 소매를 걸친 채로.

en: …You’ve been saying that your whole life.

lines: 순라꾼들은 내가 도깨비랑 얘기하는 줄 알았지.
en: Every night. In the reeds. Loudly.
The watch thought I was talking to goblins.

blocks.html: Then he takes his arm off his son’s shoulders and is, all at once, a mad old man again, peering over the edge at the water as if it had said something rude.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 아들 어깨에서 팔을 거두더니, 단숨에 다시 미친 노인이 된다. 물이 뭔가 무례한 말이라도 한 것처럼 벼랑 끝에서 아래를 들여다보며.

lines: 가 봐라. 네 친구 기다린다. 그 친구한텐 말하지 말고.
…그리고 네 어미 앞에서 날 용서하기만 해 봐라. 네 어미가 울면, 나도 울어야 하잖냐.
en: Go on. Your friend’s waiting. Don’t tell him.
…And don’t you dare forgive me in front of your mother. She’ll cry, and then I’ll have to.

blocks.label: Hwangnyong Temple · the tower yard
blocks.ko: 황룡사 · 탑 마당

blocks.html: The queen wants a tower. Nine storeys of timber in the yard of Hwangnyong Temple, one for each neighbour that troubles Silla, tall enough that all nine can see it.
blocks.ko: , 여왕은 탑을 원한다. 황룡사 마당에 나무로 아홉 층. 신라를 괴롭히는 이웃 하나에 한 층씩, 아홉 나라가 다 볼 수 있을 만큼 높게.

blocks.html: Nobody in Silla can build it. So she pays silk and treasure to Baekje, the enemy, for a master carpenter named Abiji. Somebody has to stand between one Baekje craftsman and two hundred Silla workmen who would rather not take his orders.
blocks.ko: 신라에는 그걸 지을 사람이 없다. 그래서 여왕은 비단과 보물을 주고 적국 백제에서 아비지라는 장인을 데려온다. 백제 장인 하나와, 그의 말을 듣기 싫은 신라 일꾼 이백 사이에 누군가 서 있어야 한다.

lines: 언니가 그러던데요. 형부가 품삯 계산을 잘하신다고.
en: My sister tells me you’re good with wages.
…She promised she’d never tell anyone.

lines: 이백 명이에요. 이번엔 다리가 아니라 탑이고.
en: I’m not anyone. I’m the queen.
Two hundred men. A tower this time, not a bridge.

blocks.hanja: 匠名阿非知 受命而來 經營木石 伊干龍春[一云龍樹]幹蠱 率小匠二百人
blocks.html: The craftsman, named Abiji, came at the command and worked the timber and stone. The igan Yongchun (some say Yongsu) oversaw the work, leading two hundred lesser craftsmen.
blocks.ko: 장인의 이름은 아비지였다. 명을 받고 와서 나무와 돌을 다스렸고, 이간 용춘(용수라고도 한다)이 일을 주관하여 소장 이백 명을 거느렸다.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事), The Nine-Storey Pagoda of Hwangnyong Temple

blocks.html: On the day they raise the heart pillar, the Baekje man dreams of his own country burning and puts down his tools. The yard waits. Then, says the record, an old monk and a giant walk out of the Golden Hall, set the pillar up between them, and vanish. Yongsu, who has been accused of keeping that kind of company, says nothing at all. Two of the workmen that morning wore masks against the sawdust. Nobody remembers their faces.
blocks.ko: 심주를 세우는 날, 백제 장인은 제 나라가 불타는 꿈을 꾸고 연장을 내려놓는다. 마당이 기다린다. 그러자, 기록에 따르면, 늙은 스님 하나와 장사 하나가 금당에서 걸어 나와 둘이서 기둥을 세우고 사라진다. 그런 무리와 어울린다는 소리를 평생 들어 온 용수는 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 그날 아침 일꾼 둘이 톱밥 막는다고 탈을 쓰고 있었다. 그 얼굴을 기억하는 사람은 없다.

blocks.html: The tower goes up within the year. From the top you can see the whole city: the palace, the river, and, if you know where to look, a small crooked bridge.
blocks.ko: 탑은 그해 안에 올라간다. 꼭대기에 서면 도성이 다 보인다. 궁궐, 강, 그리고 어디를 봐야 하는지 안다면, 작고 삐뚤어진 다리 하나.

blocks.label: The hill west of the stream · the burial
blocks.ko: 개울 서쪽 언덕 · 장례

blocks.html: They are buried on the same day, on the hill west of the stream, in one mound, because nobody in the family could imagine digging two. The Council sends six men in good sleeves. Chunchu thanks each of them by name. He has known all their names for a long time.
blocks.ko: 두 사람은 같은 날, 개울 서쪽 언덕, 한 봉분에 묻힌다. 두 개를 판다는 건 집안 누구도 상상하지 못했다. 회의는 좋은 소매를 입은 사람 여섯을 보낸다. 춘추는 하나하나 이름을 불러 고맙다고 한다. 그는 그 이름들을 오래전부터 다 알고 있었다.

blocks.html: Afterwards he walks down to the stream alone. The Ghost Bridge is still there, a little crooked. He stands on it for a long time.
blocks.ko: 장례가 끝나고 그는 혼자 개울로 내려간다. 귀교는 아직 거기 있다. 조금 삐뚤게. 그는 그 위에 한참을 서 있다.

blocks.html: Then he says something to the water. Nobody hears what.
blocks.ko: 그러다 물에 대고 뭐라고 말한다. 무슨 말인지는 아무도 듣지 못한다.

blocks.html: If you’ve been keeping both books, here they are side by side.
blocks.ko: 두 장부를 다 챙겨 왔다면, 여기 나란히 펼쳐 둔다.

head: The song · 노래
The truth · 진실
What it means · 뜻
rows: Bihyung talks to ghosts because a ghost fathered him · 귀신의 아들이라 귀신과 말한다
The Ghost Children follow Yongsu because he is Jinji’s son, the first child of the purge · 귀자들이 용수를 따르는 건 그가 진지의 아들, 숙청의 첫 아이라서다
The ghosts are the purged. He is the one they were waiting for. · 귀신은 숙청당한 사람들이다. 그는 그들이 기다리던 사람이다.
Old Man Tree has one empty eye hole · 나무 할배는 눈구멍이 하나뿐이다
His eye was put out the night of the purge, for having stood at Jinji’s door · 진지의 문을 지켰다는 죄로 숙청하던 밤 눈을 뽑혔다
The wound becomes the mask. · 상처가 탈이 된다.
The Rock Lady will not move off the bridge stone · 바위 할매는 다리 돌에서 꿈쩍도 안 한다
A mother whose three elder children were listed as Jinji’s men and killed · 위로 셋을 “진지의 사람”으로 올려 잃은 어미
Grief that stays put. · 자리를 뜨지 않는 슬픔.
Three rascal goblins steal the pages’ shoes · 꼬마 도깨비 셋이 시동들 신을 훔친다
Three orphans whose parents were exiled or hanged; the smallest never takes off his red mask · 부모가 귀양 가거나 목 매달린 고아 셋. 제일 작은 놈은 빨간 탈을 안 벗는다
Children with nothing left but mischief. · 장난 말고는 남은 게 없는 아이들.
The goblins build a bridge in one night · 도깨비들이 하룻밤에 다리를 놓는다
Forty masked people cut stone for a month; the madman shouts at the stream to cover the hammers · 탈 쓴 마흔이 한 달 동안 돌을 깎는다. 미치광이는 망치 소리를 덮으려 냇물에 고함친다
A miracle is work nobody is allowed to name. · 기적이란 이름을 댈 수 없는 사람들의 일이다.
The reeds bow to him · 갈대가 그에게 절한다
The masked children kneel in the reeds · 탈 쓴 아이들이 갈대밭에 엎드린다
Loyalty mistaken for magic. · 도술로 오해받은 충성.
A lost seal reappears under the cruel steward’s pillow · 잃어버린 인장이 못된 집사의 베개 밑에서 나온다
A girl in a fox mask puts it there · 여우탈 쓴 계집아이가 넣어 둔다
The weak can reach the bedroom of the strong. · 약한 자도 강한 자의 침실에 닿을 수 있다.
Chunmyung is won over by the wonder of the spirit world · 천명은 귀신 세상의 신비에 마음을 뺏긴다
Chunmyung is won over by the plight of the Ghost Children and the cruelty above them · 천명은 귀자들의 처지와 그 위의 잔인함에 마음을 뺏긴다
Love starts when she sees past the palace wall. · 사랑은 그녀가 담 너머를 볼 때 시작된다.
The goblin Gildal takes human shape and serves the court · 도깨비 길달이 사람이 되어 조정을 섬긴다
A purge orphan comes out of hiding as Imjong’s clerk · 숙청의 고아가 임종의 서기로 세상에 나온다
The hidden coming up into the light. · 숨은 자가 빛으로 올라온다.
Gildal turns into a fox and runs · 길달이 여우로 변해 달아난다
Gildal leaves his gate to carry the red-mask boy out of the Council’s cellar · 길달이 빨간 탈을 화백의 지하 옥에서 꺼내려 문을 비운다
The Council’s word for loyalty is betrayal. · 화백의 말로 충성은 배신이다.
Bihyung has the goblins kill the fox · 비형이 도깨비들을 시켜 여우를 죽인다
Yongsu cuts his friend’s throat on the south road, with Gildal guiding the knife · 남쪽 길에서 용수가 벗의 목을 벤다. 칼은 길달이 잡아 준다
The loyal man pays; the clever master weeps and accepts. · 충신은 값을 치르고, 영리한 주인은 울며 받아들인다.
The ghosts are afraid of Bihyung, and his name on a door keeps them out · 귀신은 비형을 무서워하고, 문에 붙인 그 이름에 못 들어온다
He rode Gildal’s body through every ward to tell the masks the plot was over · 길달의 시신을 싣고 온 도성을 돌며 탈들에게 거사가 끝났다고 알렸다
The charm is a warning. · 부적은 경고다.

blocks.html: Up in the Moon Palace, the last Sacred Bone queen is counting her breaths. And the story his father told him on a cliff is finally ours to hear…!
blocks.ko: 월성 위에서는 마지막 성골 여왕이 숨을 세고 있다. 그리고 아버지가 벼랑 위에서 들려준 이야기를, 이제야 우리가 듣는다…!

logline.en: For seven years the crown has sat on the Queen. The work has sat on her nephew’s table.
logline.ko: 일곱 해 동안 왕관은 여왕의 머리에 있었다. 일은 조카의 탁자 위에 있었다.

images.alt: King Muyeol — full frontal, eyes in hard shadow, magenta court silk
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 3:4 poster. Kim Chunchu as King Muyeol. ONE geometric device: FULL FRONTAL STAMP, eyes lost in HARD SHADOW under the Silla crown — not a film-noir half-face. Extreme chiaroscuro. Face matches the attached portrait. Magenta #D8258C as the plane. Flat charcoal-black void. No throne. No second figure. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental.

images.prompt: Wide cinematic EXPOSITION still, 16:9. Camera far back. REAL recognizable place. Wide Seorabeol coronation court: one magenta plane, tiny crown-speck Tiny silky hanbok figures, few hues, one accent. Flat sky, no clouds. Painterly cinema, not photoreal, not cartoon. No readable text, no watermark.

images.at: For seven years the crown has sat on
images.alt: Poster key art: Queen Jinduk weaves her ode of peace into silk at a lamp-lit loom while the white heavenly horse watches over her shoulder through the open door
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Night in a tenebrist Silla palace chamber: one oil lamp, a big wooden loom, a long length of silk with woven lines of verse, the timber door slid open onto a moonlit courtyard. Over-shoulder two-shot. INTERACTION: Queen Jinduk sits at the loom in violet-and-white silk and gold crown, shuttle in hand, mid-throw; the wingless white heavenly horse Chunma has pushed its head and long neck in through the open door and rests its chin on her shoulder, watching the shuttle; without looking she reaches back and scratches its jaw. The woven silk glows only where the lamp touches it. CHUNMA HAS NO WINGS: a wingless white heavenly horse, bare white back and shoulders, nothing feathered anywhere; it rides the air on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs. The lamp is the only key (#9d7bd0 bounce off the silk): it catches her profile, the shuttle, the horse’s eye and muzzle; the room falls into umber-black. Loom frame as a dark foreground shape. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — QUEEN JINDUK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_jinduk.png (face only; invent a new pose). Hair ornament matches attached /bn_jinduk.png when the head is visible. #9d7bd0 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | CHUNMA (천마, hyukgose's heavenly horse, guardian of Silla) — attached board /obj_chunma.png: WINGLESS white heavenly horse in the Cheonmachong saddle-flap style: long arched neck, streaming white mane and tail, legs flung out in a flying gallop. It has NO WINGS — no feathers, no bird wings, nothing growing from the shoulders. It rides the sky on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs and chest, as on the painted birch-bark flap. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, never a glow outline. Kneels and cries beside the purple egg at Najeong, sees men approach, neighs and rises into the sky. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. blocks.html: Every king is dressed by somebody who knew him before.
blocks.ko: 어느 임금이든 옷은 그를 그 전부터 알던 사람이 입힌다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace · the last of the Sacred Bone
blocks.ko: 월성 · 마지막 성골

jump.en: The Last Night of the Sacred Bone…

blocks.html: For seven years the crown has sat on Queen Jinduk. The work has sat on her nephew’s table. Nobody has ever called her foolish. She’s simply outnumbered by seals.
blocks.ko: 칠 년 동안 왕관은 진덕여왕의 머리에 있었다. 일은 그녀 조카의 탁자 위에 있었다. 아무도 그녀를 어리석다 한 적 없다. 그저 도장 수에서 밀렸을 뿐이다.

en: Nephew.
When I die, do not pretend I ruled.
Say I kept the chair warm until the country was ready to admit who was already sitting in it.
lines: 내가 죽거든 내가 다스렸다고 하지 마라.
나라가, 이미 앉아 있던 사람을 인정할 준비가 될 때까지 자리를 따뜻하게 지켜 줬다고 해라.

en: Aunt.
You ruled the only way left to Sacred Bone — by lasting.
lines: 성골에게 남은 유일한 방식으로 다스리셨습니다 — 버팀으로.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads her name three times — Jinduk. Jinduk. Jinduk. — the ledger's habit before a Sacred Bone line closes.
blocks.ko: 강림은 그녀의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 진덕. 진덕. 진덕. — 성골의 혈통이 닫히기 전 명부의 버릇대로.

en: Majesty.
Sacred Bone ends on your breath. One question.
Did you keep the crown warm for the next hand — or keep it from cooling into a man’s?
lines: 성골이 당신 숨에서 끝납니다. 질문 하나.
다음 손을 위해 왕관을 따뜻이 두셨습니까 — 아니면 사내의 것으로 식지 않게 지키신 겁니까?

en: …I kept a seat from becoming a joke.
That is all the Sacred Bone had left to do.
Then the minutes are clean.
Walk.

lines: 그 숨 꺼지자 거룩한 뼈도 꺼져
en: Kim Seungman, last of the Bone,
kept the gold chair warm on her own.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Stitched a song in silk for the West,
sent it away and did her best.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
When she went, the old bone went too —
the last bright lamp, and then it was through.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
blocks.title: Seungman, the Last of the Bone

blocks.caption: Queen Jinduk, the last of the Sacred Bone. She kept a seat from becoming a joke.
blocks.ko: 마지막 성골, 진덕여왕. 자리 하나가 웃음거리가 되지 않게 지켰다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace · the morning of the crown
blocks.ko: 월성 · 즉위하는 아침

blocks.html: The robes are brought to him at dawn. Purple-crimson silk, the gold belt, and the crown wrapped in a cloth like something that might catch cold.
blocks.ko: 새벽에 옷이 들어온다. 자줏빛 비단, 금허리띠, 그리고 감기라도 들까 봐 보자기에 싼 듯한 왕관.

blocks.html: There are two stands in the room this morning. On the second hang a queen’s robes, which nobody in Silla has sewn for a True Bone woman before. The seamstresses argued about the hem for a month.
blocks.ko: 오늘 아침 방에는 옷걸이가 둘이다. 두 번째에는 왕비의 옷이 걸려 있다. 신라에서 진골 여인을 위해 그런 옷을 지은 건 처음이다. 침방 사람들이 밑단 하나로 한 달을 다퉜다.

blocks.html: Munhee dresses him herself and sends the servants out. She does the ties at his wrists last, and tight, the way she once sewed a coat.
blocks.ko: 문희가 손수 그에게 옷을 입힌다. 하인들은 내보낸다. 손목의 고름은 맨 마지막에, 단단히 맨다. 언젠가 옷을 꿰매 주던 그 솜씨로.

en: Hold still.
…You’re shaking.
It’s cold.
It’s spring.
My father would have talked to the crown.
Your father would have told it a joke and made it laugh.
…He’d have hated this.

lines: 아뇨. 못 말리게 들뜨셨을 거예요. 팔 들어요.
en: No. He’d have been unbearable. Arms up.

blocks.html: Then it is her turn. He sends the maids out too, and does her cords himself, under the chin, the way you tie something that belongs to a temple. He can’t do the knot the first time. His hands remember another knot, in the hold of a ship, under one lamp.
blocks.ko: 이번엔 그녀 차례다. 그도 시녀들을 내보내고, 턱 밑 끈을 손수 맨다. 절에 바치는 물건을 매듯이. 첫 번엔 매듭이 안 지어진다. 손이 다른 매듭을 기억한다. 배 짐칸, 등잔 하나 아래.

lines: 다시요. 천천히. 이번엔 쫓아오는 사람 없어요.
en: Again. Slowly. Nobody’s chasing us this time.

blocks.html: He walks to the throne hall on foot, the long way, past the stream. The bridge is still crooked. Somewhere around the third gate he stops being in the street at all. It is twelve years ago, the night of the paper lotuses, and he is on the bluff over the river with his father’s hand on his elbow.
blocks.ko: 그는 걸어서, 먼 길로, 개울을 지나 정전으로 간다. 다리는 여전히 비뚤다. 세 번째 문 어디쯤에서 그는 더 이상 길 위에 있지 않다. 열두 해 전, 종이 연꽃의 밤, 그는 강 위 벼랑에서 아버지 손에 팔꿈치를 잡혀 있다.

blocks.html: You know what his father told him there. The lotuses went out to sea, and for one night the madman of Surabol was not mad.
blocks.ko: 거기서 아버지가 무슨 말을 했는지 당신은 안다. 연등은 바다로 흘러갔고, 하룻밤 동안 서라벌의 미치광이는 미치지 않았다.

blocks.html: That is what Yushin saw come back up the pavilion steps that night. Not grief. A man with a goal.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 정자 계단을 다시 올라오는 그를 보고 유신이 본 건 그것이었다. 슬픔이 아니라, 목표를 가진 사내.

blocks.html: Seven years after the bluff, in the hold of a ship under one lamp, a man his own height asked him for his cap. Chunchu had heard every word of it before, on a cliff, in his father’s voice. He just hadn’t known it was a family thing: the clever ones live, and somebody kinder ties the knot.
blocks.ko: 벼랑에서 일곱 해 뒤, 배 짐칸 등잔 하나 아래에서, 그와 키가 같은 사내가 그의 관을 달라고 했다. 춘추는 그 말을 한 마디 한 마디 다 들어 본 적이 있었다. 벼랑에서, 아버지 목소리로. 다만 그게 집안 내력인 줄은 몰랐다. 영리한 쪽은 살아남고, 더 다정한 쪽이 매듭을 짓는다.

blocks.html: Chunchu comes to the throne hall. Munhee’s ties are still tight at his wrists. The six councillors of the Harmony Council are waiting in a row to bow to him. He looks at each of them in turn, the way you look at men who will not be in your way for long. The third from the left was one of five boys behind a stable, one winter. Chunchu smiles at him. The man has no idea why that frightens him.
blocks.ko: 춘추가 정전에 닿는다. 문희가 맨 손목 고름은 아직 단단하다. 화백회의 대등 여섯이 그에게 절하려고 한 줄로 서 있다. 그는 한 사람 한 사람을 차례로 본다. 오래 앞을 막지는 못할 사람들을 보는 눈으로. 왼쪽에서 세 번째는 어느 겨울 마구간 뒤에 있던 다섯 중 하나다. 춘추가 그에게 미소 짓는다. 사내는 그게 왜 무서운지 모른다.

blocks.label: The Ghost Bridge · the same hour
blocks.ko: 귀교 · 같은 시각

blocks.html: While the drums go in the palace, four figures stand on a crooked bridge over a stream. Two of them have been dead for a year. Kangrim does not as a rule let the dead wait a year. He is not sure why he has. He suspects it was the sums.
blocks.ko: 궁에서 북이 울리는 동안, 개울 위 삐뚤어진 다리에 넷이 서 있다. 그중 둘은 죽은 지 한 해가 됐다. 강림은 원래 죽은 이를 한 해씩 기다리게 두지 않는다. 왜 그랬는지 자기도 잘 모른다. 아마 그 셈 때문이었을 거라고 짐작한다.

blocks.html: Haewonmek stands a little way off, being silent at the water.
blocks.ko: 해원맥은 조금 떨어져 서서, 물을 향해 말이 없다.

en: The drums. That’s him, then.
That’s him.

lines: 아직 내 물음에 답을 안 하셨소.
en: You never answered my question, sir.
Who is Bihyung.

blocks.html: He has had a year. He still thinks about it.
blocks.ko: 한 해가 있었다. 그래도 그는 생각에 잠긴다.

lines: 어머니가 코 때문에 붙였죠. 임금이 다른 이름을 아무도 못 듣게 궁에 퍼뜨렸고요. 귀자들은 그걸 기다릴 무언가로 만들었고, 덕만이랑 저는 아무도 찾으러 오지 않게 적어 뒀어요.
en: A story.

My mother called me it because of my nose. A king gave it to his palace so nobody would hear the other name. The Ghost Children made it something to wait for. Dukman and I wrote it down so nobody would come looking.
He was a good story. Better than me.
He’s showing off.
He’s had a year to work on that.
…Write down Yongsu.
I’ll write both.

lines: 그리고 길달. 그 사람도 적어 줘요.
en: And Gildal. Write him in.

lines: 이미 들어 있습니다, 어르신. 누가 여우로 책에 넣었더군요.
en: He’s already in, sir. Somebody put him in a book as a fox.
…He’d have liked that. He hated being left out of things.
…Walk.

blocks.html: Then the four of them walk off the far end of the bridge, slowly, in no particular hurry, and the stream goes on talking to nobody.
blocks.ko: 그리고 넷은 다리 저편 끝으로 걸어 나간다. 천천히, 딱히 서두를 것 없이. 개울은 아무도 없는 데에 대고 계속 말을 건다.

blocks.label: The throne hall · the crown
blocks.ko: 정전 · 관

blocks.html: Within the hour the crown will sit on his head, and the tree will quietly redraw itself around him. The side branch his grandfather fell onto becomes the trunk. Everyone who looked down on it now has to look up.
blocks.ko: 한 시진 안에 왕관이 그의 머리에 얹히면, 나무는 그를 중심으로 조용히 다시 그려진다. 할아버지가 떨어진 곁가지가 줄기가 된다. 그 가지를 내려다보던 사람들은 이제 올려다봐야 한다.

blocks.title: The royal house, redrawn · 새 직계
blocks.caption: Chunchu on the king’s rung, his house on the primary line beneath him. The Sacred Bone is gone; the royal house now stands inside the True Bone.
blocks.ko: 임금의 단엔 춘추, 그 아래 직계엔 그의 집. 성골은 사라졌고, 이제 왕실 전체가 진골 안에 선다.

blocks.html: Munhee becomes queen. Years ago her sister sold her a dream on a hill. She married in disgrace, to a man with no claim to anything. Now she stands beside his throne.
blocks.ko: 문희가 왕비가 된다. 오래전 언니가 언덕 위에서 그녀에게 꿈을 팔았다. 그녀는 아무것도 물려받을 것 없는 사내에게 망신스럽게 시집갔다. 이제 그 사내의 왕좌 곁에 선다.

lines: 언니가 그 꿈을 비단 치마 한 벌에 팔았습니다. / 지금 생각하면 헐값이었지요.
en: My sister sold me that dream for one silk skirt. / In hindsight she undercharged.

blocks.html: So it is done. A True Bone king, the first since there was a throne, and a queen who bought a dream for one silk skirt. The six councillors bow, some of them late. Down by the stream, a crooked bridge goes on being a bridge, and nobody stands on it talking to the water anymore.
blocks.ko: 그렇게 끝난다. 왕좌가 생긴 이래 첫 진골 임금, 그리고 비단 치마 한 벌로 꿈을 산 왕비. 화백 여섯이 절한다. 몇은 늦게. 개울가에선 비뚤어진 다리가 여전히 다리로 서 있고, 그 위에서 물에게 말을 거는 사람은 이제 없다.

blocks.html: He has been king for one morning. Baekje is already on the table…!
blocks.ko: 임금이 된 지 하루아침. 백제가 벌써 상 위에 올라와 있다…!

logline.en: The quay doesn’t care that he’s a prince. She has already decided his arithmetic is sloppy.
logline.ko: 항구는 그가 왕자든 말든 상관없다. 그녀는 이미 그의 셈이 헐겁다고 결론을 내렸다.

images.prompt: OPENING STILL of the episode: the first image the reader sees, staging its first line. The line: “Ten years earlier, at Silla’s only western harbour, the prince is eighteen and losing an argument with a tide book.” Context: Ten years earlier, at Silla’s only western harbour, the prince is eighteen and losing an argument with a tide book. Yushin sent him here for the season, to work under Kim Sunpum, who runs the quay. No yard. No horses. Grain ships, tide marks, and sums that will not close. Silla’s only door to the western sea. Everyone knows which door. A wide or medium establishing frame that hooks. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.at: until there is a stolen brush between their mouths, and then they do
images.alt: A prince learning the harbour by kissing the girl who can count.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. PARALLEL FRAME: the LAYOUT picture on the sheet is the master of a set of frames that recur across this story. Repaint ITS EXACT COMPOSITION: the same camera height, angle and lens, the same framing, the same number of figures in the same positions, sizes and poses, the same main shapes (gate, line, dais, table, waterline) in the same places, the same direction of the key light. Only the people, their faces and dress, the place and the hour change, so the two frames line up like a before-and-after. Ignore the layout picture's faces, clothes and colours. The same profile kiss under a warehouse eave in hard night rain at the harbour. Bupmin on the LEFT, young prince, bowed to her; Jahee on the RIGHT, a sharp quay girl, both hands in his hair, a wet ledger crushed between them and a writing brush fallen at their feet; a hard curtain of rain off the eave in the foreground, warehouse lamp the key. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT LAYOUT picture (copy its composition, not its people), SECOND face = munmu, THIRD face = jayi. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), binyeo board jayi (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing). BUPMIN — Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Colour #C41E3A. JAHEE Colour #e8a0bf. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.

images.at: He has had wedding silk folded in a chest since the night of the forty sacks.
images.alt: In the Marshal's family this is practically a proposal.
