blocks.label: The Moon Palace · the new king’s first council
blocks.ko: 월성 · 새 임금의 첫 회의

blocks.html: The new king’s first council is about Baekje. It is short.
blocks.ko: 새 임금의 첫 회의 안건은 백제다. 회의는 짧다.

lines: 사적인 원한으로 나라를 망국의 길로 인도하시는 것은 어진 일이 아니라 봅니다...!
en: Your Majesty… even so….
To lead the country down a road of ruin for a private grudge — that is not the act of a wise king…!

lines: 자네들, 나를 진정 그렇게 보고 있었나?
내 딸의 죽음에 미쳐 복수를 가르는 노인으로?
en: ….What? A private grudge?
Is that truly how you have all seen me?
An old man maddened by his daughter’s death, sharpening revenge?
How… disappointing.
I am a man looking at the thousand-year flourishing of the sacred country.
I was raised on the study of kingship from childhood…

lines: 무서워 해야 할지, 동경해야 할 지 모르겠다....
en: I do not know whether to fear him or admire him….
And yet—
Kim Chunchu…

blocks.html: That night a letter leaves Surabol for Chang’an, written in a hand that still remembers the Wei River. It begins without titles: Zhi — I kept the appointment. Do not let the coat eat you.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 서라벌에서 장안으로 편지가 떠난다. 위수를 아직 기억하는 손씨. 존호 없이 시작한다. 治 — 약속 지켰네. 겉옷에게 먹히지는 말게.

blocks.label: Chang’an
blocks.ko: 장안

lines: 말을 보내게. 그리고 여기 먼지엔 불편한 사람 하나 더 들어갈 자리가 있다고 전하게.
en: He became king.
Of course he did.
Send him horses. And tell him the dust here still has room for one more inconvenient man.
zh: 送他馬。並告訴他——這兒的塵土還容得下一個不便之人。
zhLatn: Tā chéng le wáng.
Guǒrán.
Sòng tā mǎ. Bìng gàosu tā——zhèr de chéntǔ hái róng de xià yīgè bùbiàn zhī rén.

blocks.html: Far west, the Third Emperor’s court learns a new gravity. The young woman who once waited in an anteroom now finishes sentences the emperor starts. Clerks say her influence is growing by the day. They say it softly.
blocks.ko: 서쪽 멀리, 고종의 조정은 새 중력을 배운다. 곁방에서 기다리던 젊은 여인이 이제 황제가 시작한 문장을 끝낸다. 서기들은 영향력이 날로 커진다고 한다. 작게 말한다.

blocks.label: The Crown Prince’s Rooms
blocks.ko: 태자의 처소

blocks.html: Late that night the new crown prince is still at his table, with the levy rolls for his father’s war. His wife reads them over his shoulder. She has been doing it for ten years.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 늦게, 새 태자는 아버지의 전쟁에 쓸 징발 장부를 붙들고 아직 탁자 앞에 있다. 아내가 어깨 너머로 그것을 읽는다. 십 년째 해 온 일이다.

en: Your sums are wrong.
The rice for the western forts. You carried a one.
lines: 서쪽 성들 쌀. 하나 잘못 올렸다 아이가.

en: …Ten years, and you still say it the same way.
Ten years, and you still carry the one.
lines: 십 년인데, 아직도 하나 잘못 올린다 아이가.

blocks.html: The first time she said it, he was eighteen, the quay was wet, and the brush in her hand was stolen…!
blocks.ko: 그녀가 처음 그 말을 했을 때, 그는 열여덟이었고, 부두는 젖어 있었고, 그녀 손의 붓은 훔친 것이었다…!

blocks.html: Ten years earlier, at Silla’s only western harbour, the prince is eighteen and losing an argument with a tide book.
blocks.ko: 십 년 전, 신라의 하나뿐인 서쪽 항구. 왕자는 열여덟이고, 조수 장부와의 싸움에서 지는 중이다.

blocks.html: Yushin sent him here for the season, to work under Kim Sunpum, who runs the quay. No yard. No horses. Grain ships, tide marks, and sums that will not close.
blocks.ko: 유신이 그를 이 한 철 동안 이곳에 보냈다. 부두를 맡은 김선품 밑에서 일하라고. 연무장도 없다. 말도 없다. 곡식 배와 물때 표시와, 맞아떨어지지 않는 셈뿐이다.

blocks.html: Silla’s only door to the western sea. Everyone knows which door.
blocks.ko: 서쪽 바다로 난 신라의 단 하나뿐인 문. 다들 그 문이 어딘지 안다.

blocks.html: Sunpum has a daughter who keeps his inkstones. Her name is Jahee. She has watched the prince for three days, and she has already decided his arithmetic is sloppy.
blocks.ko: 선품에게는 그의 벼루를 지키는 딸이 있다. 이름은 자희. 사흘 동안 왕자를 지켜보았고, 그의 셈이 헐겁다고 이미 결론을 내렸다.

blocks.caption: A harbour girl who counts faster than the customs men.
blocks.ko: 세관 관리보다 셈이 빠른 항구의 처녀.

lines: 조수는 왕자든 말든 상관 안 해예.
en: Your sums are wrong.
The tide does not care that you are a prince.
Count again.
While I am watching.
…Where.
No — / Please show me.

blocks.html: She corrects the sum with her father’s good brush. She is not supposed to touch it. She took it off his desk an hour ago, because it is the only one that writes small enough. He watches her mouth instead of the numbers, and she lets him, once.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 아버지의 좋은 붓으로 셈을 고친다. 손대면 안 되는 붓이다. 한 시진 전에 아버지 책상에서 슬쩍 가져왔다. 글씨를 그만큼 작게 쓰는 붓은 그것뿐이라서. 그는 숫자 대신 그녀의 입을 보고, 그녀는 한 번 허락한다.

blocks.html: Then a rider comes down the coast road with a letter from Yushin. The army is marching west, against seven Baekje forts. The grain sails on the morning tide. Bupmin is to sail with it.
blocks.ko: 그때 해안 길로 말 탄 전령이 유신의 글월을 들고 내려온다. 군대가 서쪽으로, 백제의 일곱 성을 향해 나선다. 곡식은 아침 물때에 배에 실려 떠난다. 법민도 그 배로 오라는 것이다.

en: The morning tide.
…Then the book has to close tonight.
It won’t. You’re forty sacks short, somewhere between the third ship and the fifth.
Forty sacks is a company that doesn’t eat for a week.
lines: 안 닫혀예. 마흔 섬이 빕니더. 셋째 배캉 다섯째 배 사이 어데서.
마흔 섬이믄 한 부대가 이레를 굶어예.

en: Then show me where.

blocks.html: They count until the lamp needs oil, and then by the light from the warehouse door. Somewhere around the fourth ship she stops correcting him, because he has stopped making mistakes. Neither of them knows what to do with their hands.
blocks.ko: 등잔에 기름이 떨어질 때까지 센다. 그다음엔 창고 문간의 불빛으로 센다. 넷째 배쯤에서 그녀는 그를 고쳐 주기를 멈춘다. 그가 더는 틀리지 않기 때문이다. 둘 다 손을 어디 둬야 할지 모른다.

blocks.html: Rain finds the eave. They stand inside a hard rain-curtain with a wet ledger between them, and almost do the stupid thing, and do not — until there is a stolen brush between their mouths, and then they do.
blocks.ko: 비가 처마를 찾는다. 그들은 젖은 장부를 사이에 두고 단단한 빗줄기 커튼 안에 서서, 바보 같은 일을 거의 하고, 하지 않는다 — 훔친 붓이 입 사이에 놓일 때까지. 그리고 그때는 한다.

en: …That’s my father coughing.
He only coughs like that when he’s pretending not to be there.
…Which is why it has to be now.
Before the tide comes in.
Do not close the book.
If you close it I…
will not know where to go.

blocks.html: Sunpum coughs once from the dark and pretends he did not see a prince learning the harbour by kissing the girl who can count.
blocks.ko: 선품이 어둠에서 한 번 기침하고, 셈할 줄 아는 소녀에게 입 맞추며 항구를 배우는 왕자를 보지 못한 척한다.

blocks.html: They find it at the fifth ship, an hour before dawn. Forty sacks written down by somebody who never loaded them. The grain can sail on time and short, or a day late and whole.
blocks.ko: 새벽 한 시진 전, 다섯째 배에서 찾아낸다. 싣지도 않은 마흔 섬을 누군가 실었다고 적어 두었다. 곡식은 제때 모자란 채로 떠날 수도 있고, 하루 늦게 온전히 떠날 수도 있다.

en: Load them. All forty.
I’ll take the next tide.
Yushin said the morning tide.
lines: 유신 장군은 아침 물때라 캤다 아입니꺼.

en: Then he can hit me for it.
At least the company that eats will be his.
lines: 그래도 밥을 먹는 부대는 그분 부대일 테니까요.

en: …And you’ll come back and fix your sums?
Only if you’re watching.

blocks.html: Years later the court will call her Jayi. The quay already had the true name.
blocks.ko: 여러 해 뒤 조정은 그녀를 자의라 부를 것이다. 항구는 이미 진짜 이름을 가지고 있었다.

blocks.label: The Western Forts
blocks.ko: 서쪽 성들

blocks.html: He reaches the army a day late, with forty sacks of rice nobody else knew were missing. Yushin is waiting at the edge of the camp.
blocks.ko: 그는 하루 늦게 군에 닿는다. 아무도 비는 줄 몰랐던 쌀 마흔 섬과 함께. 유신이 진영 끝에서 기다리고 있다.

en: You missed the tide.
Yes, Marshal. The fifth ship was forty sacks short. I stayed and loaded them.
lines: 예, 대장군. 다섯째 배가 마흔 섬이 비었습니다. 남아서 실었습니다.

blocks.html: Yushin hits him once, open-handed, because the order was the morning tide. Then he sends the forty sacks to the company that was going to go without.
blocks.ko: 유신은 손바닥으로 그를 한 대 친다. 명은 아침 물때였으니까. 그러고는 마흔 섬을 굶을 뻔한 부대로 보낸다.

en: Marshal.
When I said king for all — did I mean every kingdom, or every person who bleeds for one?
lines: 모두를 위한 임금이라 했을 때 — 모든 나라를 말한 겁니까, 아니면 하나를 위해 피 흘리는 모든 사람을 말한 겁니까.

en: Ask the yard again tomorrow.
If the answer is only a speech, you are still six.
If it costs you a bruise — you are becoming Hwarang.
lines: 멍이 값이믄 — 화랑이 되어 가는 기다.

blocks.label: The Quay, Again
blocks.ko: 다시, 포구

blocks.html: He comes back in the spring to fix his sums. The sums are fine. He brings them anyway, every morning, and she finds mistakes in them that are not there.
blocks.ko: 봄에 그는 셈을 고치러 돌아온다. 셈은 멀쩡하다. 그래도 매일 아침 들고 오고, 그녀는 거기서 있지도 않은 틀린 곳을 찾아낸다.

en: This one’s wrong.
It isn’t.
I know. Sit down.

blocks.html: She decides his brush hand is the real problem. He holds a brush like a spear. She stands behind his stool, puts her hand over his, and shows him how much ink a small brush can take.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 진짜 문제가 붓 잡는 손이라고 정한다. 그는 붓을 창처럼 쥔다. 그녀는 그의 의자 뒤에 서서 그의 손 위에 제 손을 얹고, 작은 붓이 먹을 얼마나 머금을 수 있는지 보여 준다.

lines: 먹을 제대로 묻히이소. 끝까지 푹, 그라고 천천히. 벼루 찌르지 말고예.
en: Lighter. You press like a soldier.
Wet it properly. All the way down, then slow. Don’t stab the stone.
…Is this still about the brush?
You’re a prince. You should be able to tell.

blocks.html: He can tell. He writes the next column so badly that she has to stand there for an hour.
blocks.ko: 그는 알아듣는다. 다음 줄을 어찌나 엉망으로 쓰는지, 그녀는 한 시진을 그 자리에 서 있어야 한다.

blocks.html: In the second week she teaches him the spring tides. At new moon the sea comes in higher and harder than any other day, and it does not ask the quay first. She explains this with her mouth very close to his ear.
blocks.ko: 둘째 주에는 사리를 가르친다. 그믐에는 바다가 어느 날보다 높고 세게 들어오고, 부두한테 먼저 묻지 않는다. 그녀는 그의 귀에 입을 바짝 대고 이것을 설명한다.

lines: 하루에 두 번 들어와예. 매일. 막을 수는 없고, 받을 준비만 하는 기라예.
en: Twice a day it comes in. Every day. You can’t stop it, you can only be ready for it.

lines: 우리… 지금 바다 얘기 하는 겁니까.
en: Are we… talking about the sea.

lines: 세 보이소, 왕자님. 그믐이 엿새 남았어예.
en: Count it, prince. The new moon is in six days.

blocks.html: He counts it. He counts it every night for six nights, on his back in the guesthouse, and gets the same number every time, which has never happened to him before.
blocks.ko: 그는 센다. 엿새 밤을 객사에 누워 세고, 매번 같은 숫자가 나온다. 그에게는 처음 있는 일이다.

blocks.label: The Grain Loft
blocks.ko: 곡간 다락

blocks.html: The new moon. The fifth ship’s warehouse, the one that was forty sacks short. Her father has gone up the coast to argue about salt. The tide climbs the pilings under the floor, and the whole loft creaks with it.
blocks.ko: 그믐. 마흔 섬이 모자랐던 다섯째 배의 창고. 아버지는 소금 일로 다투러 해안을 따라 올라갔다. 바닥 밑에서 물이 기둥을 타고 오르고, 다락 전체가 그 소리로 삐걱인다.

blocks.html: She brought the lamp. He brought nothing, and has been standing at the top of the ladder for some time.
blocks.ko: 등잔은 그녀가 들고 왔다. 그는 아무것도 안 들고 왔고, 한참째 사다리 꼭대기에 서 있다.

lines: 올라올 기가, 아니믄 거 서서 사다리 칸이나 셀 기가?
en: Are you coming up, or are you going to stand there and count the rungs?
I was— I already counted them. Nine.
Ten. You’re standing on one.

blocks.html: He comes up. He tries to undo her jacket tie and gets it wrong, and she laughs at him, and takes his hands, and does it with him slowly, the way she did the brush.
blocks.ko: 그가 올라온다. 그녀의 옷고름을 풀려다 엉뚱하게 당기고, 그녀는 웃고, 그의 손을 잡아, 붓을 가르칠 때처럼 천천히 같이 푼다.

en: Not like that. You’re one knot short.
…There. Now you’re not.

blocks.html: His red coat comes off and goes somewhere in the dark. She pulls him down onto the sacks by the collar of what’s left. Below them the sea keeps coming in, twice as high as it has any right to, and nobody on the quay is counting anything.
blocks.ko: 그의 붉은 겉옷이 벗겨져 어둠 어딘가로 간다. 그녀는 남은 옷의 깃을 잡고 그를 가마니 위로 끌어내린다. 그 밑에서 바다는 자격도 없이 두 배 높이로 자꾸 들어오고, 부두의 누구도 아무것도 세지 않는다.

blocks.html: Around midnight a sack splits under them. Rice pours out over red silk and down between the boards, and the lamp gutters, and for a while neither of them can breathe well enough to care.
blocks.ko: 자정쯤 가마니 하나가 그들 밑에서 터진다. 쌀이 붉은 비단 위로 쏟아져 널빤지 틈으로 흘러내리고, 등잔불이 흔들리고, 한동안 둘 다 숨이 차서 신경 쓸 겨를이 없다.

en: …Forty-one.
What?

lines: 가마니. 저거 터졌다 아이가. 누가 적어야 되는데, 니는 아이다. 니 손은 하나도 쓸모가 없다.
en: Sacks. That one’s split. Somebody has to write it down, and it won’t be you, your hands are useless.
You said that about my hands in the autumn too.
…You were wrong then as well.

blocks.html: In the morning Sunpum comes back, finds a split sack in the fifth warehouse, and writes it in the book in his own small hand: one sack, damaged by the tide. Then he coughs, though there is nobody there to hear it.
blocks.ko: 아침에 선품이 돌아와 다섯째 창고에서 터진 가마니를 찾아내고, 제 작은 글씨로 장부에 적는다. 한 섬, 물에 상함. 그러고는 기침을 한다. 들을 사람이 아무도 없는데도.

blocks.html: The tide comes in twice a day, all spring. He is ready for it every time.
blocks.ko: 그 봄 내내 물은 하루에 두 번 들어온다. 그는 매번 받을 준비가 되어 있다.

blocks.html: By midsummer Jahee is not fine, in the way that shows, and her father picks the busiest hour on the quay to notice.
blocks.ko: 한여름이 되자 자희는 괜찮지 않다. 티가 나는 쪽으로. 그리고 아버지는 부두가 가장 붐비는 시각을 골라 그것을 알아챈다.

en: Pregnant with an unknown man’s child… what a disgrace!
In front of the whole harbour!
lines: 누군지도 모를 사내의 아이를 배다니… 이 무슨 망신이냐!

en: Father. Everyone on this quay can count.
You taught them.
lines: 아부지. 이 포구 사람들 다 셈할 줄 압니더.

en: Not a word from you. Whose is it? Name him!
lines: 니는 입 다물어라. 누고? 이름 대라!

en: …Mine. Sir. I’m the— it’s mine.
I’m the unknown man.
The prince. Well.
What a frightful shock.

blocks.html: He has had wedding silk folded in a chest since the night of the forty sacks. In the Marshal’s family this is practically a proposal. The prince’s mother managed hers with a bonfire. His grandmother did it through a drain.
blocks.ko: 그는 마흔 섬이 빈 그 밤부터 혼례 비단을 궤짝에 접어 넣어 두었다. 대장군 집안에서는 이게 거의 청혼이다. 왕자의 어머니는 모닥불로 해냈고, 할머니는 하수구로 해냈다.

blocks.label: The Coronation Year
blocks.ko: 즉위하던 해

blocks.html: The bruise is long gone. The girl from the quay is the crown prince’s wife. The whole court stands in the palace yard in the Western silk to watch his father crowned.
blocks.ko: 멍은 진작 사라졌다. 부두의 그 아가씨는 태자비가 되었다. 온 조정이 서국의 비단을 입고 궁 마당에 서서 그의 아버지가 왕관 쓰는 것을 지켜본다.

blocks.html: This king has a Secretariat, an emperor for a friend, and an army that answers to one brush. He means to make three kingdoms one. Everybody in the yard can feel a new age starting.
blocks.ko: 이 임금에게는 집사부가 있고, 벗이라 부르는 황제가 있고, 붓 한 자루에 움직이는 군대가 있다. 그는 세 나라를 하나로 만들 작정이다. 마서국의 누구나 새 시대가 시작되는 것을 느낀다.

blocks.html: Along the back row stand the oldest houses in Surabol, the six families who were here before there was a king. They wear the new robes because the Secretariat says so. They wear them like borrowed skin.
blocks.ko: 뒷줄에는 서라벌에서 가장 오래된 집안들이 서 있다. 임금이 있기 전부터 여기 있던 여섯 가문이다. 집사부가 입으라니 새 관복을 입었다. 빌린 살가죽처럼 입었다.

en: In my grandfather’s day a king wore what his grandfather wore.
In the first king’s day he came out of an egg.
Now he comes out of a Secretariat.
lines: 우리 할아버지 때는 임금이 제 할아버지 옷을 입었소.
blocks.speaker: The old houses

en: Uncle. Why do they mind so much?
It’s only a robe.
Nothing in this country is only a robe, lad.
Their grandfathers chose the first king. So did mine.
Ask how the first one got here. Then you’ll know what they’re muttering about.
lines: 이 나라에 옷일 뿐인 기 없다, 얘야.
저 양반들 할아버지가 첫 임금을 골랐다. 내 할아버지도.
첫 임금이 어데서 왔는지 물어봐라. 그라믄 저 양반들이 뭘 투덜대는지 알 끼다.

blocks.html: Silla’s newest king wears the Western silk. To see why the old houses mind, go back to a white horse kneeling in the grass…!
blocks.ko: 신라의 새 임금은 서국의 비단을 입는다. 늙은 가문들이 왜 그걸 못마땅해하는지 알려면, 풀밭에 무릎 꿇은 흰 말에게로 거슬러 올라가야 한다…!

logline.en: A white horse kneels by a well and cries. Six chiefs start digging.
logline.ko: 흰 말 한 마리가 우물가에 무릎 꿇고 운다. 여섯 촌장이 땅을 파기 시작한다.

images.alt: Six chiefs in a circle around a glowing blue egg and white horse — cool blue versus warm gold
images.prompt: Anime-painterly egg-and-horse gathering, hard blue/gold split, flat color fields, not photoreal mountains.

images.alt: A white winged horse kneels crying beside Najung well under a hanging shaft of light
images.at: a white horse folded onto its knees
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. Bird’s-eye from the pine crowns over Najeong well: a white winged horse kneels beside a round stone well-mouth in a small clearing, neck bent, crying up at the sky; the horse is left as blinding bare paper inside a ring of splashed black pine forest; one thin column of lightning-mist hangs straight down from the sky onto the well. Six tiny chiefs in wide-sleeved robes crouch at the forest edge. ONE device: the vertical shaft of light dropping into the circular well. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

images.alt: A chicken-dragon coils at Alyungjung well; a baby girl comes from its rib
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. At the stone mouth of Alyeongjeong well, a gyeryong (chicken-dragon: rooster head and comb, long serpent-dragon body in dry-brush scales) coils around the well-mouth; from its left side a newborn girl emerges into a burst of bare paper light, wrapped in nothing but mist. Worm’s-eye from the well stones. ONE device: the dragon’s coil around the round well. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

images.alt: Adult King Hyukgosé and Queen Alyoung in a close moonlit kiss — blue silk, porcelain-gold hairpin, her hand on his chest
images.prompt: Intimate cinematic CLOSE-UP still, 16:9. Adult founding king Hyukgosé (dark side-parted hair, light-blue hanbok) and adult Queen Alyoung (black bun, porcelain-gold floral binyeo, blue silk) in a close moonlit kiss, her hand on his chest, collarbones catching moonlight. Personal, not tiny figures under a huge moon, not silhouettes. No text, no watermark.

images.alt: Photoreal Hyukgosé mostly in shadow, a broken eggshell-arc and cerulean rim-light the only accent
images.prompt: Minimal iconic 3:4 poster. Hyukgosé, photoreal demigod founder. ONE geometric device: a BROKEN EGGSHELL as an incomplete white arc. Photoreal face matches the attached portrait, mostly in shadow; pale-blue #6f9fe8 rim. No horse. No egg-circle. No army. No text. No watermark. Graphic color-blocking, photoreal demigod face, monumental.

images.at: crown him king while he is still a boy
images.alt: The six chiefs crown the thirteen-year-old Hyukgosé on a riverbank mound at dusk
images.prompt: History, not myth: the six village chiefs of Saro crown the boy king. Low three-quarter worm’s-eye on a packed-earth ritual mound above the Alcheon river at dusk, 57 BC: no palace yet, only thatch, timber and earth. The six chiefs in plain wide-sleeved robes and black jougwan stand in a half-ring; the eldest, white-bearded, raises the gold crown in both hands over a THIRTEEN-YEAR-OLD boy, Hyukgose, kneeling on a straw mat with his head up and unafraid (his face is a boy’s version of the attached portrait). A brazier just outside the frame at lower right rakes firelight up across the boy’s face, the chiefs’ sleeves and the raised gold; behind them the river and the six villages’ thatched roofs dissolve into blue dusk haze, small lamps as bokeh. ONE device: the half-ring of chiefs converging on the raised crown. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.at: The boy king does not laugh. He looks at his bride
images.alt: As if somebody had finally said something interesting.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. PARALLEL FRAME: the LAYOUT picture on the sheet is the master of a set of frames that recur across this story. Repaint ITS EXACT COMPOSITION: the same camera height, angle and lens, the same framing, the same number of figures in the same positions, sizes and poses, the same main shapes (gate, line, dais, table, waterline) in the same places, the same direction of the key light. Only the people, their faces and dress, the place and the hour change, so the two frames line up like a before-and-after. Ignore the layout picture's faces, clothes and colours. The same wedding table at the first wedding Silla ever had, a feast hall of timber and thatch, torchlit, the six chiefs standing up in the blur behind. Hyukgose, thirteen, the boy king, on the LEFT; Alyoung on the RIGHT; both holding up their halves of the gourd, the boy king staring at his bride, not laughing. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT LAYOUT picture (copy its composition, not its people), SECOND face = hyukgose, THIRD face = alyoung. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), binyeo board alyoung (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing), crown reference (shape only). HYUKGOSÉ — Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #6f9fe8. LADY ALYOUNG — Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #a8c8f0. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.

blocks.html: Seven hundred years before anyone in Surabol wore the Western silk, six old men creep up on a horse.
blocks.ko: 서라벌의 누구도 서국의 비단을 입기 칠백 년 전, 늙은이 여섯이 말 한 마리에게 살금살금 다가간다.

blocks.title: The road south
blocks.caption: Out of the fallen north, down the east side of the mountains, to six valleys by the sea.
blocks.ko: 무너진 북쪽에서, 산줄기 동쪽을 타고, 바다 가까운 여섯 골짜기로.

blocks.label: The Road South
blocks.ko: 남쪽 길

blocks.html: Start further back. Fifty years before the horse, an emperor from the west takes the old kingdom in the north. Its people do what people do. They pick up the pot, the seed bag and the grandmother, and they walk.
blocks.ko: 조금 더 앞에서 시작하자. 그 말이 나타나기 쉰 해 전, 서쪽의 황제가 북쪽의 옛 나라를 삼킨다. 그 나라 사람들은 사람들이 늘 하는 일을 한다. 솥을 지고, 씨앗 자루를 들고, 할머니를 업고, 걷는다.

blocks.speaker: A woman on the road
en: Where are we going?

blocks.speaker: Her husband
en: South.

blocks.speaker: A woman on the road
en: What’s south?

blocks.speaker: Her husband
en: Not them.

blocks.speaker: An old man
en: There’s no Joseon to go back to. Stop looking over your shoulder.

blocks.html: They do not go as one people. They go as families, then as whoever shares a fire, then as whoever is still walking. By the time the mountains run out, the road has sorted them into six groups.
blocks.ko: 그들은 한 무리로 가지 않는다. 처음엔 집안끼리, 그다음엔 불을 나눠 쓰는 사람끼리, 나중엔 아직 걷고 있는 사람끼리 간다. 산이 끝날 무렵, 길은 그들을 여섯 무리로 갈라 놓았다.

blocks.html: Each group finds a valley and stays. Six valleys, six villages. Each village has a Kan, an elder, who settles the fights about water and gets blamed for the weather.
blocks.ko: 무리마다 골짜기 하나를 찾아 눌러앉는다. 골짜기 여섯, 마을 여섯. 마을마다 간이 하나 있다. 물싸움을 말리고, 날씨 탓을 뒤집어쓰는 어른.

blocks.html: Remember the surnames. Their grandchildren will still be using them in seven hundred years. Lee Alpyung talks first. Choi Sobuldori asks what everyone else was avoiding. Jung Jibekho brings the wine, or complains that nobody did. Son Gurema says almost nothing and is listened to anyway. Bae Jita counts. Sul Hojin came the farthest and has never let anyone forget it.
blocks.ko: 성을 기억해 두라. 그 손자의 손자들이 칠백 년 뒤에도 그 성을 쓴다. 이알평은 먼저 말한다. 최소벌도리는 다들 피하던 질문을 한다. 정지백호는 술을 가져오거나, 아무도 안 가져왔다고 투덜댄다. 손구례마는 거의 말이 없는데도 다들 귀를 기울인다. 배지타는 센다. 설호진은 제일 멀리서 왔고, 그걸 아무에게도 잊게 두지 않는다.

blocks.html: Strictly, the surnames came later, from a grateful king. The six families will tell you they had them all along.
blocks.ko: 엄밀히 말하면 성은 나중에, 고마워한 어느 임금이 내려 준 것이다. 여섯 집안은 원래부터 있었다고 할 것이다.

blocks.label: The Ridge of Mount Yang
blocks.ko: 양산 능선

blocks.html: Every spring the six Kans meet on the ridge of Mount Yang to choose a king. Every spring they vote. Six stones, one bowl, and it has to be all six, or the losers go home and sharpen something.
blocks.ko: 해마다 봄이면 여섯 간이 양산 능선에 모여 임금을 뽑는다. 해마다 패를 넣는다. 돌 여섯, 그릇 하나. 여섯이 다 같아야 한다. 아니면 진 쪽이 집에 가서 뭔가를 간다.

blocks.html: This spring they count the bowl. Six stones, five names. Every Kan has voted for himself, except Son Gurema, who voted for Lee Alpyung. Lee Alpyung voted for himself.
blocks.ko: 올봄에도 그릇을 센다. 돌 여섯에 이름 다섯. 간마다 저 자신을 찍었다. 손구례마만 이알평을 찍었다. 이알평은 저 자신을 찍었다.

lines: 올해 모임은 우리 골짜기서 하자 캤제. 술은 누가 가왔노?
en: We said this year’s meeting was at my valley. Who brought the wine?

lines: 술 얘기 하러 왔나. 임금 얘기 하러 왔지.
en: Did we come about wine? We came about a king.

lines: 임금 얘기는 작년에도 했다. 재작년에도 했고. 술은 그때도 없었다.
en: We talked about a king last year. And the year before. There wasn’t any wine then either.

lines: 북쪽 살 적에 우리 아배들은 임금이 있었다 카더라.
en: Our fathers had a king up north, they say.
Some say that’s why it fell.

lines: 그라믄 임금 없이 계속 이래 싸우자고?
en: So we just keep arguing like this, with no king?

lines: 싸우는 게 아이고 모이는 기다. 술만 있으믄.
en: It’s not arguing, it’s meeting. Given wine.

blocks.html: Alpyung stops in the middle of a word. Five heads turn.
blocks.ko: 알평이 말하다 말고 멈춘다. 다섯 고개가 돌아간다.

blocks.html: The chroniclers disagree about the colour of the egg and agree about the horse. Before anyone dug, the six chiefs saw it from the ridge of Mount Yang: a light hanging down beside Najung like lightning that had forgotten to leave, and under it a white horse folded onto its knees, as if someone important were waiting in the grass.
blocks.ko: 알의 빛깔을 두고는 사서들이 다투지만, 말에 대해서는 다투지 않는다. 땅을 파기도 전에 여섯 촌장은 양산 능선에서 그것을 보았다. 나정 곁으로 떠나기를 잊은 번개처럼 빛이 드리워 있고, 그 아래 흰 말 한 마리가, 풀숲에 귀한 이라도 기다리는 듯 무릎을 꿇고 있었다.

en: That’s… a horse, right?
Why’s a horse kneeling? Who to?

lines: 날개 달린 말 본 적 있어? 난 없어.
en: You ever seen a horse with wings? I haven’t.
…That one’s got wings, though.
Slow. Go slow. If it spooks—

blocks.html: It does not spook. It lets them come close enough to see that its wings are folded the way a bird folds them and that its eyes are on the grass, not on them. Then it looks up and sees six grown men creeping at it through the pines with their sleeves held out like nets.
blocks.ko: 말은 놀라지 않는다. 새가 날개를 접듯 날개를 접고 있다는 것, 눈이 그들이 아니라 풀숲에 가 있다는 것이 보일 만큼 가까이 오게 둔다. 그러다 고개를 들고, 다 큰 사내 여섯이 그물처럼 소매를 벌린 채 소나무 사이로 기어 오는 것을 본다.

blocks.html: Six chiefs stand in a wet field with their arms still out, holding nothing. Much later, when the country has a name and a calendar and a clerk for everything, the horse will be painted on a saddle-flap and buried with a king and called Chunma, the heavenly horse. That morning nobody calls it anything. Alpyung is the first to look down at what it was kneeling over.
blocks.ko: 여섯 촌장이 젖은 들판에 팔을 벌린 채, 아무것도 쥐지 못하고 서 있다. 한참 뒤, 나라에 이름과 달력과 무엇에나 서기가 생긴 뒤, 그 말은 말다래에 그려져 어느 왕과 함께 묻히고 천마라 불릴 것이다. 그날 아침엔 아무도 그것을 무어라 부르지 않는다. 발밑, 말이 꿇어앉아 있던 자리를 처음 내려다본 것은 알평이다.

lines: 파 봐. 다들 뭐 해, 파 보라니까.
en: …It left something.
Dig. What are you all doing? Dig.

blocks.html: They dig with their hands, then with somebody’s hoe. Under the grass is an egg the size of a gourd, and the same shape. When it cracks there is a boy inside, already looking at them as if they were late.
blocks.ko: 처음엔 손으로, 다음엔 누군가의 괭이로 판다. 풀 밑에 박만 한 알이 있다. 생김새도 박이다. 알이 갈라지자 사내아이가 있다. 벌써, 늦게 온 사람들을 보듯 그들을 쳐다본다.

en: It’s a gourd. We dug up a gourd with a baby in it.
Then that’s his name. Park. Gourd.

blocks.html: They call him Park, for the gourd, and Hyukgosé, to rule with brightness. Then six practical men look at each other and crown him king while he is still a boy. A boy, they reason, cannot have taken sides yet.
blocks.ko: 박에서 나왔으니 박, 세상을 밝게 다스리라고 혁거세. 그러고는 실속 있는 사내 여섯이 서로를 보고, 아직 어린아이인 그를 임금으로 세운다. 아이라면 아직 어느 편도 들지 않았을 테니까.

blocks.caption: Hyukgosé. Born from an egg, crowned before his voice broke.
blocks.ko: 혁거세. 알에서 태어나, 목소리가 굵어지기도 전에 왕관을 썼다.

blocks.hanja: 浴於東泉，身生光彩，鳥獸率舞，天地振動，日月淸明。
blocks.html: They bathed him in the eastern spring. His body gave off light, the birds and beasts danced together, heaven and earth shook, and the sun and moon turned clear and bright.
blocks.ko: 동천에서 목욕시키니 몸에서 광채가 나고, 새와 짐승이 함께 춤추며, 하늘과 땅이 진동하고, 해와 달이 맑고 밝아졌다.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonders — Silla’s Founder Hyeokgeose

blocks.label: Alyung Well
blocks.ko: 알영정

blocks.html: At Alyungjung well, a dragon with a chicken’s head leaves a girl behind. She has a beak where her lips should be, until they wash her in the north stream and it falls off. They name her Alyoung, after the well.
blocks.ko: 알영정 우물가에서 닭 머리를 한 용이 여자아이 하나를 두고 간다. 입술 자리에 부리가 달려 있었는데, 북쪽 시내에 씻기자 떨어져 나간다. 우물 이름을 따 알영이라 부른다.

blocks.caption: Lady Alyoung. Born from a dragon’s rib, and the one person in Surabol who can tell the king no.
blocks.ko: 알영부인. 계룡의 갈비뼈에서 났고, 서라벌에서 임금에게 안 된다고 말할 수 있는 단 한 사람.

en: One from an egg, one from a chicken.
…Did this country start in a kitchen?

blocks.html: At the wedding feast the six chiefs stand up. They have a plan.
blocks.ko: 혼인 잔치에서 여섯 촌장이 일어선다. 그들에겐 계획이 있다.

en: We’re going to make a brand new country.
Every family cares for the others like one great house. Nobody left outside the gate.
The royals watch over the people like their own children. The nobles are wise and righteous, and decide for the good of the nation.
And everyone else we divide into six ranks, according to their virtues.
A new unity…! Silla!
lines: 우리는 아주 새로운 나라를 만들 것이오.
가문들이 한집안처럼 서로 돌보고, 누구도 문밖에 버려지지 않는 나라.
왕족은 백성을 제 자식처럼 보살피고, 귀족은 지혜롭고 의롭게 나라를 위해 판단하오.
그리고 백성은 그 덕에 따라 여섯 등급으로 나누겠소.

en: According to their virtues.
Who measures the virtue?
Well— we do. The six of us.
Then say “by whoever is sitting at this table.”
It’s shorter. And in three generations you’ll mean it.
lines: 그럼 “이 상에 앉은 사람 마음대로”라고 하시오.
더 짧소. 그리고 세 대만 지나면 정말 그 뜻이 될 테니.

blocks.html: The chiefs laugh, because it is a wedding. The boy king does not laugh. He looks at his bride as if somebody had finally said something interesting.
blocks.ko: 촌장들은 웃는다. 혼인 잔치니까. 소년 임금은 웃지 않는다. 마침내 누군가 재미있는 말을 했다는 듯 신부를 바라본다.

blocks.html: Six families end up running everything. In every new country, six families always do.
blocks.ko: 여섯 가문이 정치를 쥔다. 새 나라는 어디든, 결국 여섯 가문이 쥔다.

en: I have heard that a true man needs only
one person to cherish,
and one person to serve,
and that is enough.

blocks.html: They write the ranks down their way anyway. Alyoung is right, the way queens usually are, a few generations early. Ranks by virtue become ranks by birth. Ranks by birth become ranks by bone.
blocks.ko: 그래도 그들은 등급을 자기들 식대로 적는다. 알영이 옳다. 왕비들이 대개 그렇듯, 몇 세대 일찍. 덕에 따른 등급은 태생에 따른 등급이 된다. 태생에 따른 등급은 뼈에 따른 등급이 된다.

blocks.html: Here is how bones work in Surabol. The egg’s line marries the rib’s line, and marries it again, until a child is royal on every side. That child is Sacred Bone. Royal on one side only is True Bone. Below that, the ranks go down like steps, and every step knows exactly who is above it.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에서 뼈가 어떻게 돌아가는지 말해 주지. 알의 핏줄이 갈비뼈의 핏줄과 혼인하고, 또 혼인한다. 그러다 사방 어디로 보나 왕족인 아이가 난다. 그 아이가 성골이다. 한쪽만 왕족이면 진골이다. 그 아래로 등급이 계단처럼 내려가고, 계단마다 제 위에 누가 있는지 정확히 안다.

blocks.html: And the six who dug up the egg? Their grandchildren keep the oldest names in the country and, a few kings later, not the highest chairs. Kings arrive in eggs, chests and boxes. The six just came up out of the ground, like rice.
blocks.ko: 그럼 알을 파낸 여섯은? 그 손자들은 이 나라에서 가장 오래된 성씨를 지킨다. 그리고 몇 임금 뒤에는, 가장 높은 자리는 지키지 못한다. 임금들은 알에서, 궤짝에서, 상자에서 온다. 여섯은 그냥 땅에서 올라왔다. 벼처럼.

blocks.html: Six hundred years on, one of their grandsons will pour tea for a room full of Kims and remind them of it. Nobody will thank him.
blocks.ko: 육백 년 뒤, 그 손자 하나가 김씨들로 가득한 방에 차를 따르며 그 일을 일깨울 것이다. 고맙다는 사람은 없을 것이다.

blocks.label: The Six Villages
blocks.ko: 여섯 마을

blocks.html: The boy from the egg and the girl from the well grow up, and they turn out to be good at the job. Every spring the king and queen walk the six villages together. He takes his shoes off in the paddies. She checks the mulberry leaves for worms, and the village heads for lies.
blocks.ko: 알에서 난 소년과 우물에서 난 소녀는 자라서, 일을 꽤 잘한다. 봄마다 왕과 왕비는 함께 여섯 마을을 걷는다. 그는 논에 들어가 신을 벗는다. 그녀는 뽕잎에 벌레가 없는지, 촌장들 얼굴에 거짓말이 없는지 살핀다.

blocks.speaker: A farmer
lines: 전하, 발 빠집니더! 거기 거머리 천지입니더—
en: Majesty, you’ll sink! That end’s all leeches—
I know. That’s why I’m in it.
Your seedlings are all leaning.

lines: 이 집 뽕잎은 반이 벌레요. 작년에 누에 몇 섶 올렸소?
en: Half the leaves on this tree have worms. How many trays of silkworms did you raise last year?

blocks.speaker: A village head
en: Oh… plenty, Your Highness.
Plenty isn’t a number.
Alyoung, this man’s rows are straight!

lines: 그 집 말고. 이 집 말이오.
en: Not his. This one’s.

blocks.html: The villages start calling them the Two Saints, which is the kind of thing villages say when the tax is light. One night raiders come over the hills from the Han commandery in the north. They find the doors unbarred and the grain stacked loose in the fields. They go home. A land with no locks, they decide, must have something worse than locks.
blocks.ko: 마을들은 두 사람을 두 성인이라 부르기 시작한다. 세금이 가벼울 때 마을들이 흔히 하는 소리다. 어느 밤 북쪽 한나라 군현에서 약탈꾼들이 고개를 넘어온다. 문은 빗장이 없고, 곡식은 들판에 그냥 쌓여 있다. 그들은 돌아간다. 자물쇠가 없는 땅이라면 자물쇠보다 더 무서운 게 있겠지, 하고.

blocks.label: The Hall of Mahan
blocks.ko: 마한의 궁

blocks.html: Not every neighbour is so easily embarrassed. To the west sits Mahan, a big old country that thinks of the southern valleys as its porch. When Surabol stops sending tribute, its king wants an explanation. Surabol sends a man from the East with a gourd still tied at his belt. It is the kind of errand where you want someone who floats.
blocks.ko: 모든 이웃이 그렇게 쉽게 머쓱해지지는 않는다. 서쪽에는 마한이 있다. 남쪽 골짜기들을 제 집 툇마루쯤으로 여기는, 크고 오래된 나라다. 서라벌이 공물을 끊자 마한 왕은 해명을 요구한다. 서라벌은 허리에 아직 박을 매단 왜 사람 하나를 보낸다. 물에 뜨는 사람이 필요한 심부름이다.

blocks.speaker: The King of Mahan
lines: 진한도 변한도 내 울타리 안이다. 몇 해째 공물이 없어.
큰 나라 섬기는 예법이 그 모양이냐?
en: Jinhan and Byunhan are inside my fence. Years now, and no tribute.
Is that how you serve a greater country?

blocks.speaker: The envoy
lines: 저희 나라는 두 성인께서 일어나신 뒤로 하늘이 고르고 창고가 찼습니다.
북에서 내려온 유민부터 변한, 낙랑, 왜 사람까지 저희를 어려워합니다.
en: Since our Two Saints rose, the weather’s been fair and the granaries full.
Refugees from the north, Byunhan, Lelang, my own people from the East. They all mind their manners with us.

blocks.speaker: The King of Mahan
en: So?

blocks.speaker: The envoy
lines: 그런데도 저희 임금께서 굳이 저를 보내 인사를 여쭙게 하셨지요. 예법이 넘친 겁니다, 대왕.
en: So my king sent me to pay his respects anyway. That’s more courtesy than he owes, Great King.
And the Great King reaches for a sword—

blocks.html: He does reach for one. Two ministers grab his sleeves.
blocks.ko: 왕은 정말로 칼에 손을 뻗는다. 신하 둘이 소매를 붙든다.

blocks.speaker: A Mahan minister
en: Great King! He’s an envoy!

blocks.speaker: The King of Mahan
en: …Get the man with the gourd out of my hall.

blocks.speaker: The envoy
lines: 나가는 길은 압니다. 물에 뜨는 법도 알고요.
en: I know the way out. I also know how to float.

blocks.html: The next year the king of Mahan dies. In Surabol somebody suggests the obvious.
blocks.ko: 이듬해 마한 왕이 죽는다. 서라벌에서 누군가 뻔한 소리를 한다.

blocks.speaker: A minister
lines: 그 왕이 우리 사신을 욕보였습니다. 지금 상중이니 치면 하루거리입니다.
en: That king insulted our envoy. They’re in mourning. We’d be done in a day.

lines: 남의 초상을 틈타는 건 어진 일이 아니오.
en: Using another man’s funeral isn’t kind.

blocks.speaker: A minister
lines: 어진 거 말고, 이기는 거 말씀드린 겁니다.
en: I wasn’t talking about kind, Majesty. I was talking about winning.

blocks.html: The king does not repeat himself. Alyoung pours the minister more wine, which in that house means the meeting is over.
blocks.ko: 왕은 같은 말을 두 번 하지 않는다. 알영이 신하의 잔에 술을 더 따른다. 그 집에서 그건 회의가 끝났다는 뜻이다.

blocks.label: The Five Tombs
blocks.ko: 오릉

blocks.html: Sixty-one years later, the chronicle says, the king went up into the sky, and seven days after that his body came down again in five pieces, scattered over the ground. Nobody records a horse. Everybody in Surabol says there was one.
blocks.ko: 예순한 해 뒤, 편년은 말한다. 왕이 하늘로 올라갔고, 이레 뒤 그 몸이 다섯 조각으로 땅에 흩어져 내려왔다고. 말이 있었다고 적은 사람은 없다. 서라벌 사람들은 모두 있었다고 말한다.

blocks.html: A chest rides the tide in, a magpie screaming over it. Whatever is inside needs a house. Preferably someone else’s…!
blocks.ko: 밀물을 타고 궤짝 하나가 들어온다. 까치 한 마리가 그 위에서 울어 댄다. 안에 든 놈은 집이 필요하다. 되도록이면 남의 집이…!

logline.en: A chest washes in on the tide with a magpie crying over it. What climbs out is a con man.
logline.ko: 밀물에 궤짝 하나가 밀려오고, 그 위로 까치가 운다. 거기서 나온 건 사기꾼이다.

images.at: a chest comes in on the tide at
images.alt: A chest rides the tide into Ajinpo under a crying magpie
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. A heavy timber chest rides a towering ink swell into the cove at Ajinpo, the sea splashed black with claw-shaped crests of bare paper; a black magpie wheels and cries above it; the shore is a dry-brush strip with one tiny old woman holding a rope. ONE device: the long diagonal of the wave carrying the chest. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

images.at: standing in the middle of the hall with feathers on his shoulders
images.alt: In King Suro’s hall: Talhae, a man again, bows with feathers drifting off his shoulders; Suro on the throne, feathers settling, pale with relief
images.prompt: Inside King Suro’s torchlit Gaya hall at night, worm’s-eye from the floor, hard dutch tilt: a burst of brown sparrow feathers explodes outward around Talhae as he lands back in his own body, already dropping into a lopsided bow, grinning; behind and above him on the dais King Suro, falcon feathers still swirling off his shoulders, grips the throne arms, pale with relief. Feathers fly at the lens. MANGA ACTION FRAME: a single seinen historical-manga action panel painted in ink and oil — bold dry-brush sumi-ink SPEED LINES streaking along the direction of motion, radial FOCUS LINES converging on the face or the blade, motion smears on legs, mane, cloth and steel, flung ink-splatter dirt and dust, extreme foreshortening and a hard dutch tilt so the frame itself feels like it is moving; heavy black ink masses against a few hard highlights, one gold accent. Faces stay clean webtoon ink line with fierce narrowed eyes. Full-bleed single frame: NO panel borders, NO speech bubbles, NO onomatopoeia or sound-effect lettering, NO text of any kind. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — SEOK TALHAE. Look: Very tall (nine cheok), long-limbed and sea-weathered, tanned, broad easy grin, sly narrow eyes; black hair in a loose topknot with salt-stiff strands; clean-shaven as a young man, a short grey beard when he is old and king. Dress: Young: plain undyed hemp jeogori and trousers, sleeves rolled, a fisherman’s cord belt. King: deep sea-green silk robe with a gold-ringed belt and a low gold diadem. Demeanor: A con man who became a king and never stopped enjoying the joke. Deadpan when caught, delighted when he wins. #5a7fa8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | KING SURO — FACE and garments from attached /ch_suro.png (face only; invent a new pose). #e0a33c as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.at: His first night as king, Talhae lies awake
images.alt: On his first night as king, Talhae lies awake on his mat in the stolen house, listening toward the gate, while Hogong grumbles from the doorway with a lamp.

Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. In the doorway, Hogong, an elderly lean man in a nightrobe, a dried gourd hanging on a peg beside him, holds a second lamp and scowls. Moonlight through the lattice paints a cold pale grid across the floor. Long shadows climb the wall.
