blocks.html: Late in the first king’s reign, a chest comes in on the tide at a fishing beach. A magpie flies over it, crying.
blocks.ko: 첫 임금의 치세도 저물 무렵, 밀물을 타고 궤짝 하나가 갯마을 바닷가로 들어온다. 그 위로 까치 한 마리가 울며 난다.

blocks.label: The Chest
blocks.ko: 궤짝

blocks.label: Dapana, a thousand li beyond the East
blocks.ko: 다파나, 왜 너머 천 리

blocks.html: It has come a long way. A thousand li north-east of the East, the islands across the sea, the queen of a country called Dapana carried a child for seven years and was delivered of an egg. The king said a person who lays an egg is an ill omen and should get rid of it. She could not. She wrapped it in silk, packed it in a chest with treasure, and gave it to the sea.
blocks.ko: 먼 길을 왔다. 바다 건너 섬나라 동국에서 동북쪽으로 천 리, 다파나라는 나라의 왕비가 아이를 일곱 해 품고는 알을 낳았다. 왕은 사람이 알을 낳는 것은 상서롭지 못하니 버리라 했다. 왕비는 그러지 못했다. 알을 비단에 싸서 보물과 함께 궤짝에 넣고, 바다에 맡겼다.

blocks.html: The night she lets it go, she talks to the egg the whole way down to the water, the way mothers talk to things that can’t answer yet.
blocks.ko: 알을 놓아 보내던 밤, 왕비는 물가로 내려가는 내내 알에게 말을 건다. 아직 대답 못 하는 것에게 어미들이 늘 그러듯.

blocks.speaker: The Queen of Dapana
lines: 너를 반기는 데로 가. 누군가는 반길 거야.
집부터 이루고, 나라는 그다음에. 될 수 있으면 그 순서로.
en: Hush. …No, that’s me. I’m the one making the noise.
Go wherever you’re wanted. Somebody will want you.
Make a house first. Then a country. In that order, if you can manage it.

blocks.html: The books say a red dragon swims out behind the chest as far as the open sea, so that nobody can bring it back. Nobody wrote down what the king did that night. The queen stood on the beach until there was nothing left to look at.
blocks.ko: 사서는 붉은 용 한 마리가 궤짝 뒤를 따라 먼바다까지 헤엄쳐 나갔다고 한다. 아무도 도로 끌고 오지 못하게. 그날 밤 왕이 무엇을 했는지는 아무도 적지 않았다. 왕비는 더 바라볼 것이 남지 않을 때까지 바닷가에 서 있었다.

blocks.label: Golden Gaya
blocks.ko: 금관가야

blocks.caption: Two beaches, one chest, and two kingdoms that each tell it to their own credit.
blocks.ko: 바닷가 둘, 궤짝 하나, 그리고 그 이야기를 저마다 제 자랑으로 하는 나라 둘.

blocks.html: It reaches Gaya first. Silla’s chronicle says King Suro came down to the beach with drums, and the whole town shouted at the chest to make it stay. It didn’t. Silla tells that part with a perfectly straight face.
blocks.ko: 궤짝은 먼저 가야에 닿는다. 신라의 기록에 따르면 수로왕이 북을 치며 바닷가로 내려왔고, 온 고을이 궤짝더러 머물라고 소리쳤다. 궤짝은 머물지 않았다. 신라는 이 대목을 아주 진지한 얼굴로 전한다.

blocks.html: The dates don’t work, by the way. Gaya puts him on its beach a lifetime later, as a grown man. Nobody in either kingdom has ever let that spoil a good story.
blocks.ko: 덧붙이자면 연대가 맞지 않는다. 가야는 한 사람 평생쯤 뒤에, 다 큰 사내로 그를 제 바닷가에 올려놓는다. 두 나라 누구도 그런 일로 좋은 이야기를 망친 적은 없다.

blocks.html: Gaya tells it differently, and with more nerve. In the Gaya chronicle Talhae comes ashore a grown man, walks into King Suro’s hall, and asks for the throne.
blocks.ko: 가야는 이 이야기를 다르게, 더 배짱 좋게 한다. 가야의 기록에서 탈해는 다 큰 사내로 뭍에 올라 수로왕의 전각으로 걸어 들어가서는, 왕좌를 내놓으라고 한다.

blocks.caption: Suk Talhae. He arrived in a chest and talks like he owns the beach.
blocks.ko: 석탈해. 궤짝에 실려 왔는데, 말투는 해변 주인이다.

blocks.hanja: 身長九尺，風神秀朗，智識過人。
blocks.html: He stood nine feet tall, fine and bright in bearing, and cleverer than other men.
blocks.ko: 키가 아홉 자요, 풍채가 빼어나고 환하였으며, 지혜와 식견이 남보다 뛰어났다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum

blocks.html: That is Silla’s book. Gaya’s makes him three feet tall, with a head a foot around. You can guess whose hall he lost in.
blocks.ko: 그건 신라의 책이다. 가야의 책에서 그는 키가 석 자에 머리 둘레가 한 자다. 누구네 전각에서 졌는지 짐작이 갈 것이다.

en: I’ve come for your throne.
You can fight me for it, or you can save us both the afternoon.
lines: 겨루어도 좋고, 서로 오후를 아껴도 좋소.

en: …Heaven gave it to me.
I— it isn’t mine to give. Or to… lose.
lines: 과인이— 내줄 수 있는 것이 아니오. 잃을 수 있는 것도…
그리고 백성은. 백성을… 그대에게 줄 수는 없소.
en: And the people. I can’t… give you the people.
They aren’t a chair.

lines: 그럼 농사꾼처럼 싸우지는 맙시다. 술법으로 하지요, 폐하.
누가 딴것이 되는 데 더 능한지.
en: Then let’s not fight like farmers. Arts, Majesty.
Whoever is better at being something else.
…Something else?

blocks.html: So they fight the way kings fight in that country. Talhae becomes a hawk, and Suro becomes an eagle.
blocks.ko: 그래서 둘은 그 나라에서 왕들이 겨루는 방식으로 겨룬다. 탈해가 매가 되자 수로는 독수리가 된다.

blocks.html: The hawk goes for the rafters. The eagle is already there. For one beat its talons close around the hawk’s back, hard enough to feel the bones, and then they open.
blocks.ko: 매가 서까래로 내닫는다. 독수리가 이미 거기 있다. 한순간 발톱이 매의 등을 움켜쥔다. 뼈가 느껴질 만큼 세게. 그리고 펴진다.

blocks.html: Talhae becomes a sparrow, small enough to hide in a lattice. Suro becomes a falcon, which is the bird that eats sparrows. It drops on him once and misses by the width of a feather, on purpose.
blocks.ko: 탈해가 참새가 된다. 창살 틈에 숨을 만큼 작다. 수로는 새매가 된다. 참새를 잡아먹는 새다. 새매가 한 번 내리꽂히고, 깃털 하나 너비로 빗나간다. 일부러.

blocks.html: When Talhae is a man again he is standing in the middle of the hall with feathers on his shoulders. He is breathing hard, and he bows.
blocks.ko: 탈해가 다시 사람이 되었을 때 그는 어깨에 깃털을 얹은 채 전각 한가운데 서 있다. 숨이 거칠다. 그리고 절을 한다.

en: …That was a falcon.
You had me twice. Why didn’t you—

lines: 그라고 그대, 배고파 보였소. 혹시— 묵을 기 있소만.
en: I don’t… like it. The killing.
And hungry, you looked. Are you— there’s food.
Ha. No. No, thank you.
I’ll find a country with a smaller king.

blocks.html: He walks straight out of the hall and down to the ferry, toward the lane the Han ships use. Suro, who has just spared him twice, sends five hundred ships after him. Mercy is one thing. A man who can turn into a sparrow, loose on your own coast, is another.
blocks.ko: 그는 곧장 전각을 나와 나루로 내려간다. 한나라 배들이 다니는 뱃길 쪽이다. 방금 그를 두 번 살려 준 수로가 그 뒤로 배 오백 척을 보낸다. 자비는 자비고, 참새로 변하는 사내를 제 바닷가에 풀어 두는 건 또 다른 일이다.

blocks.html: The ships chase him to the edge of another king’s water and turn back. Gaya’s chronicle lets him go there, small and dripping and grinning. Silla picks up the story with a baby.
blocks.ko: 배들은 다른 임금의 바다 끝까지 그를 쫓다가 돌아선다. 가야의 기록은 거기서 그를 놓아준다. 작고, 흠뻑 젖고, 씩 웃는 채로. 신라는 아기 하나로 이야기를 이어받는다.

blocks.label: Ajinpo
blocks.ko: 아진포

blocks.html: Either way, the chest goes on. At Ajinpo an old woman sees magpies wheeling over a rock that was never in that sea. She rows out, hauls the chest in with a rope and opens it, and there is a little boy inside, sitting among the treasure as if it were his luggage.
blocks.ko: 어느 쪽이든 궤짝은 계속 간다. 아진포의 한 노파가, 그 바다에 있은 적 없는 바위 위로 까치들이 맴도는 것을 본다. 노를 저어 나가 밧줄로 궤짝을 끌어올려 열어 보니, 안에 사내아이 하나가 보물 사이에 짐 보따리라도 되는 듯 앉아 있다.

blocks.caption: Ejin. Her son fishes for the king. Today she has caught something better.
blocks.ko: 아진의선. 아들은 임금의 고기를 잡는다. 오늘 그녀는 그보다 나은 것을 낚았다.

en: Well.
You’re not a fish.
No.
Is this the country?
What country?

lines: 제가 세우기로 한 나라요. 어머니가 그랬어요.
en: The one I’m supposed to make. Mother said.
…Make it after supper.

blocks.html: She names him herself, since there is nobody else to ask. A magpie followed the chest in, so she takes the bird out of the character for magpie, and what is left, Suk, is his surname. He got loose from the chest and came out of it, so he is Talhae, the one who got loose.
blocks.ko: 달리 물어볼 사람도 없으니 이름은 그녀가 짓는다. 까치가 궤짝을 따라왔으니 까치 작(鵲) 자에서 새 조(鳥)를 떼어 낸다. 남은 석(昔)이 그의 성이다. 궤짝을 풀고 나왔으니 탈해(脫解), 풀려난 아이다.

lines: 그 뼈대는 그물 당기라고 생긴 게 아니다. 가서 뭐라도 배워.
en: Those bones aren’t for nets. Go and learn something.
I’ve learned where the fish are.

lines: 그럼 땅 있는 데를 배워. 고기는 집을 남겨 주지 않아.
en: Then learn where the land is. Fish don’t leave you a house.

blocks.html: He grows nine cheok tall and fishes to feed her, and never once complains about it. He keeps the chest by his bed long after he has outgrown it. And he studies, the way she told him to. Geography, mostly the part about where the good ground is.
blocks.ko: 그는 아홉 자로 자라고, 고기를 낚아 노파를 먹이며 한 번도 싫은 내색을 하지 않는다. 궤짝은 몸이 훌쩍 커 버린 뒤에도 머리맡에 둔다. 그리고 노파 말대로 공부를 한다. 지리를. 주로 좋은 땅이 어디 있는지에 관한 부분을.

blocks.label: The Whetstone
blocks.ko: 숫돌

blocks.label: Mount Toham
blocks.ko: 토함산

blocks.html: When he is grown he climbs Mount Toham, the high ridge east of the city, with two servants and a walking stick. On top he piles up a little stone hut and sits in it for seven days, looking down at Surabol like a man reading a menu.
blocks.ko: 다 자라자 그는 지팡이 하나와 종 둘을 데리고 도성 동쪽 높은 등성이, 토함산에 오른다. 꼭대기에 돌을 쌓아 작은 움막을 짓고, 이레 동안 그 안에 앉아 서라벌을 내려다본다. 차림표 읽는 사람처럼.

blocks.html: On the way down he sends a servant called Begui for water. Begui is thirsty too, and the spring is a long way from his master, so he drinks first.
blocks.ko: 내려오는 길에 그는 백의라는 종을 물 뜨러 보낸다. 백의도 목이 마르고, 샘은 주인에게서 멀다. 그래서 먼저 마신다.

blocks.html: When he comes back, the horn cup is stuck to his mouth. He tugs. It doesn’t move.
blocks.ko: 돌아온 백의의 입에 뿔잔이 붙어 있다. 잡아당긴다. 꿈쩍도 않는다.

en: Something wrong with the water?

blocks.speaker: Begui
en: Mmf— mm— mmmf.

lines: 다시는 안 그러겠다고 해. 가까운 데서든 먼 데서든. 진심으로.
en: Drank first, did you.
Say you won’t again. Near or far. Say it and mean it.

blocks.speaker: Begui
lines: 다시는— 읍— 다시는 안 그럽니다, 나리, 가깝든 멀든—
en: Nnever— mmf— never again, master, near or far—

blocks.html: The cup drops off into his hand. Begui never cheats his master again, the chronicle says, and Talhae keeps the cup. A man who means to live among liars can use one.
blocks.ko: 잔이 툭 떨어져 손에 들린다. 사서는 백의가 다시는 주인을 속이지 않았다고 한다. 그리고 탈해는 그 잔을 간직한다. 거짓말쟁이들 사이에서 살 작정인 사내에게는 쓸모가 있다.

blocks.html: Looking over the city, he picks the best ground in it, a crescent-shaped rise above the river, and finds that someone already lives there. The house belongs to Hogong, a minister who came over the sea from the East long ago with a gourd tied at his waist to float on, and has the name to prove it.
blocks.ko: 도성을 내려다보며 그는 그 안에서 가장 좋은 땅을 고른다. 강 위로 반달 모양으로 솟은 언덕. 그런데 이미 누가 살고 있다. 집주인은 호공이다. 오래전 허리에 박을 매달고 동국에서 바다를 건너온 대신으로, 그 이름이 증거다.

blocks.hanja: 瓠公者，未詳其族姓，本倭人，初以瓠繫腰渡海而來，故稱瓠公。
blocks.html: As for Hogong, his clan and surname are not known. He was a man of Wa, and at first he crossed the sea with a gourd tied at his waist; hence he was called Hogong, Lord Gourd.
blocks.ko: 호공은 그 족성을 자세히 알 수 없다. 본래 왜인으로, 처음에 박을 허리에 매고 바다를 건너왔으므로 호공이라 불렀다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Hyeokgeose, yr. 38

blocks.label: The Crescent House
blocks.ko: 반월의 집

blocks.html: Talhae does not have a house. He has a plan. One night he buries a whetstone and a sack of charcoal beside Hogong’s gate, and in the morning he goes to the magistrate and says the house was his family’s, taken while they were away.
blocks.ko: 탈해에게는 집이 없다. 계획이 있다. 어느 밤 그는 호공의 대문 옆에 숫돌과 숯 한 자루를 묻고, 아침이 되자 관아에 가서 그 집이 원래 자기 집안 것이었는데 집을 비운 사이 빼앗겼다고 아뢴다.

en: I have lived in that house thirty years!
lines: 내가 저 집에서 삼십 년을 살았소!

en: And my family lived there before you. We were smiths.
Dig by the gate, if you don’t believe me.
lines: 그 전에는 우리 집안이 살았소. 대장장이였지.
못 믿겠거든 대문 옆을 파 보시오.

blocks.html: They dig. The whetstone and the charcoal come up out of the ground, black and convincing, and the magistrate gives Talhae the house.
blocks.ko: 파 본다. 숫돌과 숯이 땅속에서 나온다. 시커멓고, 그럴듯하게. 관아는 집을 탈해에게 준다.

en: …You buried those last night.
Prove it.

blocks.html: The ground becomes the Moon Palace, where every king of Silla after him will live, which means every king of Silla lives in a stolen house, including the one who has just moved in. Nobody in the palace likes it when you mention this.
blocks.ko: 그 땅이 월성, 반월성이 된다. 그 뒤 신라의 모든 왕이 그곳에 산다. 다시 말해 신라의 모든 왕은 훔친 집에 산다. 방금 이사 들어온 임금까지. 궁에서는 누가 이 말을 꺼내면 다들 싫어한다.

blocks.html: His mother told him to make a house first. She never said whose.
blocks.ko: 어머니는 집부터 이루라고 했다. 누구 집인지는 말하지 않았다.

blocks.label: King Namhae’s hall
blocks.ko: 남해왕의 궁

blocks.html: The egg-king’s son is on the throne now, and he hears about the young man who won a house with a sack of charcoal.
blocks.ko: 이제 왕좌에는 알에서 난 임금의 아들이 앉아 있다. 그는 숯 한 자루로 집을 따낸 젊은이 이야기를 듣는다.

blocks.caption: King Namhae. The egg-king’s son, and a shaman. He reads an omen in every bird, and this one came with a magpie.
blocks.ko: 남해왕. 알에서 난 임금의 아들이자 무당. 새마다 징조를 읽는데, 이번 건 까치를 달고 왔다.

lines: 궤짝에서 나온 놈이, 숯으로 송사를 이겨.
저런 놈은 문밖보다 집 안에 두는 게 낫다.
en: A boy from a chest. Who wins lawsuits with charcoal.
…Marry him to my eldest.
I’d rather have that one inside the family than outside the gate.

blocks.html: So the con man marries a princess. For twenty years the shaman-king keeps him close, listens to him, and watches him the way you watch weather.
blocks.ko: 그래서 사기꾼은 공주와 혼인한다. 그 뒤 스무 해 동안 무당 임금은 그를 곁에 두고, 그의 말을 듣고, 날씨 보듯 그를 지켜본다.

blocks.html: When Namhae is dying he calls in his son Yuri and his son-in-law Talhae, and says the thing a careful man says when he can’t decide.
blocks.ko: 남해는 죽어 가며 아들 유리와 사위 탈해를 불러들인다. 그리고 신중한 사람이 결정을 못 할 때 하는 말을 한다.

lines: 둘 중 나이 많은 쪽. 나이 많은 쪽이 맡아라.
en: Park or Suk. I don’t mind which.
The elder of you. Let the elder have it.

blocks.html: Then he dies, which leaves two men at a bedside working out who is older. Neither of them knows his own birthday. One of them came out of an egg in a box.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 숨을 거둔다. 침상 곁에는 누가 더 나이가 많은지 따져야 하는 두 사내가 남는다. 둘 다 제 생일을 모른다. 하나는 궤짝 속 알에서 나왔다.

blocks.caption: Yuri. The egg-king’s grandson. Kind, shy, and much harder to fool than he looks.
blocks.ko: 유리. 알에서 난 임금의 손자. 다정하고, 수줍고, 보기보다 훨씬 속이기 어렵다.

lines: 형님이 더 많으시오. 아마도. 그리고 더 영리하시고. 그건 확실하고.
en: You’re older. Probably. And you’re cleverer. Definitely.
Take it, brother. I mean it.

lines: 허나 왕좌는 범인이 앉을 자리가 아니오. 듣자니 슬기로운 사람은 이가 많다더군.
en: Kind. Very kind.
But the throne isn’t for ordinary men, and I hear a wise man has more teeth.
Somebody bring a rice cake.

blocks.html: They each bite the same rice cake. The six villages send their headmen to count, because somebody has to and nobody trusts the family. The old headman whose village keeps the lineages holds the cake up to the lamp.
blocks.ko: 둘이 같은 떡을 한 입씩 문다. 여섯 마을에서 촌장들이 와서 센다. 누군가는 세야 하고, 집안사람은 아무도 못 믿으니까. 족보를 맡은 마을의 늙은 촌장이 떡을 등불에 비춰 든다.

blocks.speaker: The Lineage Keeper
lines: 탈해 왕자… 열하나. 흠. 몇 개는 같은 이를 두 번 센 것 같기도 하고.
en: Prince Talhae… eleven. Hm. Some of these might be the same tooth twice.
Prince Yuri. Fourteen.
…Prince Yuri has more teeth.

blocks.html: Talhae, who has been a hawk and a sparrow, turns out to have a surprising amount of trouble biting a rice cake. Nobody remarks on it. Yuri looks at him for a long moment, and doesn’t either.
blocks.ko: 매도 되고 참새도 되었던 탈해가, 떡 한 입 무는 데에는 뜻밖에 애를 먹는다. 아무도 그 말을 꺼내지 않는다. 유리는 한참 그를 바라보다가, 역시 아무 말도 하지 않는다.

blocks.html: So the kings of Silla are called Isagum from then on: tooth-marks. As far as anyone knows, it is the only royal title in the world named after a bite of rice cake.
blocks.ko: 그래서 그 뒤로 신라의 임금은 이사금이라 불린다. 잇금, 이 자국이다. 아는 한, 떡 한 입에서 이름을 딴 임금 칭호는 세상에 이것 하나뿐이다.

blocks.html: Yuri turns out to be a good king, and does one thing nobody remembers and everybody uses. He gives the six old valleys surnames. The grandsons of the men who dug up the egg become the Lees and the Chois and four more. A village with a surname has decided to stay.
blocks.ko: 유리는 좋은 임금이 된다. 그리고 아무도 기억하지 않지만 모두가 쓰는 일을 하나 한다. 여섯 옛 골짜기에 성을 내린다. 알을 파낸 사내들의 손자들이 이씨가 되고, 최씨가 되고, 넷이 더 된다. 성을 얻은 마을은 눌러살기로 작정한 마을이다.

blocks.html: In his fifth year Yuri does something no king before him has done. He writes a song. The court sings the Dosolga at every feast after that. The shy boy who counted teeth has the whole hall singing his words back at him.
blocks.ko: 5년째에 유리는 그전 임금들이 아무도 한 적 없는 일을 한다. 노래를 짓는다. 그 뒤로 궁에서는 잔치 때마다 도솔가를 부른다. 이빨 세던 수줍은 소년이 온 전각에 제 노랫말을 되받아 부르게 만든 것이다.

blocks.html: Then he invents a holiday. On the full moon of the eighth month he splits the women of the six houses into two weaving teams, and the side with more cloth by moonrise wins. The losers feast the winners, and everyone sings the Hoesogok. The wager is called Gabae. They still play it. You call it Chuseok.
blocks.ko: 그리고 명절을 하나 만든다. 8월 보름달이 뜨면 여섯 집안의 여인들을 두 편으로 갈라 베를 짜게 한다. 달이 뜨기까지 더 많이 짠 편이 이긴다. 진 편이 이긴 편에 잔치를 차리고, 다 함께 회소곡을 부른다. 그 내기의 이름은 가배다. 지금도 한다. 사람들은 추석이라 부른다.

blocks.html: He counts the offices too. Seventeen ranks, from Ibeolchan at the top to Jowi at the bottom. Every man in Surabol now knows exactly how tall he stands.
blocks.ko: 관직도 다 센다. 이벌찬부터 조위까지 열일곱 등급. 서라벌의 모든 사내는 이제 제 키가 얼마인지 정확히 안다.

blocks.html: Lelang marches on his border. Yuri makes peace with the Maek instead of fighting two enemies at once, and takes the hill fort of Iseoguk.
blocks.ko: 낙랑이 국경을 치고 들어온다. 유리는 두 적과 한꺼번에 싸우는 대신 맥과 화친하고, 산골의 이서국 성을 취한다.

blocks.html: Years later Goguryeo smashes Lelang’s city, and five thousand Lelang people walk south. Yuri divides them among the six houses. Uninvited new cousins.
blocks.ko: 몇 해 뒤 고구려가 낙랑 성을 깨뜨리자 낙랑 사람 오천이 남쪽으로 걸어 내려온다. 유리는 그들을 여섯 집안에 나누어 준다. 초대받지 못한 새 사촌들이다.

blocks.label: King
blocks.ko: 왕

blocks.label: Surabol · 57
blocks.ko: 서라벌 · 57년

blocks.html: Thirty-three years later Yuri is dying, and his brother-in-law sits with him. Talhae is past sixty now, still tall, still cheerful, still in the stolen house.
blocks.ko: 서른세 해 뒤, 유리가 죽어 간다. 매형이 그 곁을 지킨다. 탈해는 이제 예순이 넘었다. 여전히 키가 크고, 여전히 쾌활하고, 여전히 훔친 집에 산다.

en: My boys are good boys.
That isn’t the same thing, is it.
They’re young.
Thirty years ago. The rice cake.
You bit soft. Didn’t you.
Prove it.

blocks.html: Yuri laughs, and it hurts him. Before morning he has named Talhae king and passed over both his sons. Then he is dead, and nobody in Surabol knows whether a dead king’s word is enough. They lay him at Sareung, the Snake Mound.
blocks.ko: 유리가 웃는다. 웃으니 아프다. 아침이 오기 전에 그는 두 아들을 제쳐 두고 탈해를 임금으로 지목한다. 그리고 숨을 거둔다. 서라벌의 누구도 죽은 임금의 말 한마디로 충분한지 모른다. 사릉, 뱀무덤에 눕힌다.

blocks.html: There is no rule for this. The first king came out of the ground, and the next two were sons. This one came in a chest, married in, and is not Park on any side. So the six houses do the only thing they can think of. They send for their old men and shut the door.
blocks.ko: 이럴 때 쓰는 법이 없다. 첫 임금은 땅에서 나왔고, 다음 둘은 아들이었다. 이번 사람은 궤짝에 실려 와 장가로 들어왔고, 어느 쪽으로 봐도 박씨가 아니다. 그래서 여섯 집안은 생각나는 유일한 일을 한다. 집안 어른들을 불러 모으고, 문을 닫는다.

blocks.speaker: Elder Lee
lines: 우리 할아버지들은 들판에서 임금을 파냈소. 말이 무릎을 꿇었고, 빛이 있었소.
우리한테 뭐가 있소? 까치 한 마리하고, 남의 집 훔친 사내 하나.
en: Our grandfathers dug a king out of a field. A horse knelt. There was light.
What have we got? A magpie and a man who stole a house.

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
lines: 그리고 스무 해 동안 하는 말마다 맞았던 사내지. 그건 빼먹지 마쇼.
en: And twenty years of him being right about everything. Don’t leave that part out.

blocks.speaker: Elder Lee
en: Yuri had sons.

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
lines: 아들 있지. 그리고 유리 임금이 아니라 했지. 당신도 거기 있었잖소.
en: Yuri had sons, and Yuri said no. You were there.

blocks.html: The old man who counted the teeth is here too, thirty years older and a Jung now. He has been to the Han commandery in the north, which makes him the only man in the room who has seen how a real empire does this.
blocks.ko: 이를 세던 그 노인도 와 있다. 서른 해 더 늙었고, 이제는 정씨다. 북쪽 한나라 군현에 다녀온 적이 있어서, 진짜 제국이 이런 일을 어떻게 하는지 본 사람은 방 안에 그 하나뿐이다.

blocks.speaker: Elder Jung
lines: 올봄에 한나라 황제가 죽은 거 아시오.
몸이 식기도 전에 아들이 옥새를 쥐었소. 아무도 마루에 둘러앉지 않았소. 아무도 아무것도 세지 않았고.
en: You know the Han emperor died this spring.
His son had the seal before the body was cold. Nobody sat on a floor. Nobody counted anything.

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
lines: 우리 할아버지들이 박 파낼 때도 한나라한테 묻진 않았소.
en: Good for the Han.
Nobody asked the Han when our grandfathers dug up a gourd, either.

blocks.speaker: Elder Jung
lines: 그건 징조였소. 이건— 이건 뭐요? 여섯이서 정한다고?
en: That was an omen. This would be— what would this be? Six men deciding?
If that’s allowed, anything’s allowed.

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
lines: 그럼 해 봅시다. 저 사람 받을 거면 소매 드쇼.
en: Then let’s find out. Sleeves up if you’ll have him.

blocks.html: Nobody has ever done this before, so nobody knows how high to hold a sleeve. Four go up, at four different heights. Two stay in laps.
blocks.ko: 아무도 해 본 적이 없으니, 소매를 얼마나 높이 드는지도 아무도 모른다. 넷이 올라간다. 높이가 다 다르다. 둘은 무릎 위에 그대로 있다.

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
en: Four. So he’s king.

blocks.speaker: Elder Lee
en: Of four valleys.

blocks.html: Nobody says anything for a while. Everyone in the room can count to six, and everyone knows what happens when two old men go home angry to their own hills.
blocks.ko: 한동안 아무도 말이 없다. 방 안의 누구나 여섯까지는 셀 줄 안다. 늙은이 둘이 화난 채 제 언덕으로 돌아가면 무슨 일이 생기는지도 누구나 안다.

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
en: …Right. Then nobody goes home.

blocks.html: Outside in the yard, Talhae sits on the step. Hogong stands next to him, because he is old and from the East and nobody offered him a seat on the floor either.
blocks.ko: 밖, 마당. 탈해는 섬돌에 앉아 있고 호공은 그 곁에 서 있다. 늙었고 동국에서 왔으니, 그에게도 마루에 앉으라는 사람이 없었다.

en: How long do they usually take?

lines: 첫 임금은 파낸 거고, 나머지는 아들이었소. 이건— 이게 뭔지 나도 모르겠소, 나리.
en: Usually? They’ve never done it.
The first one was dug up. The rest were sons. This is— I don’t know what this is, my lord.
Then they’ll take all night.

blocks.html: They take all night. Somewhere before dawn the Lee elder stops arguing about the horse and starts arguing about terms.
blocks.ko: 밤을 꼬박 새운다. 동트기 전 어느 무렵, 이씨 어른이 말 이야기를 그만두고 조건 이야기를 시작한다.

blocks.speaker: Elder Lee
lines: 저 사람이 쓰시오. 죽으면 아들한테 가는 게 아니라 여기로 돌아오오. 이 마루로.
en: Then it’s a loan.
He wears it. When he dies it doesn’t go to his sons. It comes back here. To this floor.

blocks.speaker: Elder Jung
lines: 그럼 또 이걸 하자는 거요? 매번?
en: And then we do this again? Every time?

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
lines: 매번. 저 양반들 오는 꼴을 보쇼.
알, 궤짝. 다음 놈은 나무에서 내려올 거요.
en: Every time. Look at how they keep arriving.
Egg, chest. Next one’ll come down out of a tree.

blocks.speaker: Elder Jung
lines: 우리가 소매 들어 임금을 고른다는 소리를 한나라가 들으면?
en: And if the Han hear we pick our kings by a show of sleeves?

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
en: Then they’ll laugh.
Let them laugh in Han.

blocks.html: When the sun comes up there are six sleeves in the air, all at roughly the same height. It is the first time the six houses have agreed on anything since the egg.
blocks.ko: 해가 뜰 때 소매 여섯이 올라가 있다. 높이도 대충 비슷하다. 알 이후로 여섯 집안이 무엇에든 뜻을 모은 건 이것이 처음이다.

blocks.html: They open the door. Talhae is still on the step. He stands, walks in, and before he goes anywhere near the throne he bows to the six old men on the floor. Every king of Silla after him will make the same bow, and most of them will mind.
blocks.ko: 문을 연다. 탈해는 아직 섬돌에 있다. 그는 일어나 안으로 들어서고, 왕좌 근처에 가기도 전에 마루에 앉은 여섯 노인에게 먼저 절한다. 그 뒤 신라의 모든 임금이 같은 절을 하게 되고, 대개는 그게 못마땅할 것이다.

lines: 어르신들. 나는 매도 되어 봤고, 참새도, 어부도, 도둑도 되어 봤소.
en: Gentlemen. I’ve been a hawk, a sparrow, a fisherman and a thief.
Chosen is new.

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
en: Don’t get used to it. It’s on loan.

blocks.html: So Talhae is king at sixty-two, and one of the first things he does is make Hogong his chief minister, which is either an apology or the best joke in the annals.
blocks.ko: 그렇게 탈해는 예순둘에 임금이 된다. 그가 맨 먼저 한 일 가운데 하나는 호공을 대보로 삼은 것이다. 사과이거나, 아니면 사서 전체에서 가장 좋은 농담이거나.

blocks.hanja: 二年春正月，拜瓠公爲大輔。
blocks.html: Second year, spring, first month: he appointed Hogong Grand Minister.
blocks.ko: 이년 봄 정월, 호공을 대보로 삼았다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum

en: …Grand Minister.
You know the best ground in the city. I could use a man like that.
lines: 도성에서 제일 좋은 땅을 아는 사람 아니오. 그런 사람이 필요하오.

en: I knew it. You did bury them.
Prove it.

blocks.label: The First Night
blocks.ko: 첫날 밤

blocks.html: His first night as king, Talhae lies awake in the house he stole. He keeps listening for someone digging by the gate.
blocks.ko: 왕이 된 첫날 밤, 탈해는 훔친 집에서 뜬눈으로 누워 있다. 누가 대문 옆을 파는 소리가 나지 않나 자꾸 귀를 기울인다.

lines: 밖에 누가 땅 파는 소리 안 들리오?
en: Grand Minister. Asleep?
You don’t hear anyone digging out there?

lines: 판다 해도 제가 파겠지요. 밤에. 누구한테 배웠는지는 아실 테고.
en: Nobody’s digging, Majesty. Go to sleep.
And if anyone does, it’ll be me. At night. You know who taught me.
Ha.
…Good night, Grand Minister.

blocks.html: He sleeps, eventually. Kings do. Eight springs later, something in the woods will wake him.
blocks.ko: 결국 그는 잠든다. 왕들도 잠은 잔다. 여덟 해 뒤 봄, 숲에서 무언가가 그를 깨울 것이다.

blocks.html: “Hogong. There’s a rooster in the woods.” It is the middle of the night. Roosters don’t crow at night…!
blocks.ko: “호공. 숲에서 닭이 운다.” 한밤중이다. 닭은 밤에 울지 않는다…!

logline.en: Roosters don’t crow at night. In the woods west of the city, one does.
logline.ko: 닭은 밤에 울지 않는다. 도성 서쪽 숲에서, 한 마리가 운다.

images.at: a small box of gold hanging from a branch
images.alt: A small gold box hangs from a pine branch in Sirim; a white rooster crows beneath
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. Sirim wood at first light: one bent black pine branch crosses the frame; from it hangs a small box on a cord, the only colour a translucent gold wash; beneath it a white rooster on the roots crows upward, left as bare paper; far off at the wood’s edge a tiny Hogong with a lantern. Mist as untouched paper. ONE device: the hanging cord from branch to box. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

images.at: I came in a box too
images.alt: The old king Talhae crouches over the opened golden box, grinning; the small boy inside looks back at him as if the king were the strange one
images.prompt: Point of view from inside the opened golden box looking up: old King Talhae, short grey beard, leans down over the rim grinning, his face foreshortened and huge; at the bottom edge of the frame the small boy’s tiny hand and white silk sleeve reach up. Courtiers lean in blurred behind the king; a lattice shaft of morning light falls past him into the box. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — SEOK TALHAE. Look: Very tall (nine cheok), long-limbed and sea-weathered, tanned, broad easy grin, sly narrow eyes; black hair in a loose topknot with salt-stiff strands; clean-shaven as a young man, a short grey beard when he is old and king. Dress: Young: plain undyed hemp jeogori and trousers, sleeves rolled, a fisherman’s cord belt. King: deep sea-green silk robe with a gold-ringed belt and a low gold diadem. Demeanor: A con man who became a king and never stopped enjoying the joke. Deadpan when caught, delighted when he wins. #5a7fa8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | KIM ALJI. Look: A small boy of about four, round solemn face, bright wide-awake black eyes, short black hair tied in a tiny tuft. Dress: Wrapped in a little white silk cloth with a thin gold thread edge. Demeanor: Unafraid; looks at kings as if they were the strange ones. #d4b86a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. images.at: wakes to a rooster crowing in the woods west of the city
images.alt: At night a band of cloud hangs into Sirim wood and a rooster crows
images.prompt: Ink painting of the myth. Night over Sirim: a long band of cloud hangs straight down out of a black ink sky into the wood like a lowered scroll; at its foot, among black trunks, the small silhouette of a rooster crowing; the city’s roofs tiny and black in the far distance with one lit window. ONE device: the vertical cloud band. MYTH INK — this beat is myth, not history, so it is painted as a STRIKING Korean ink painting (sumukhwa), not the house colour style. Joseon sumi ink on raw hanji paper with EXTREME LIGHT AGAINST DARK: huge saturated masses of black ink set against blinding bare paper; light is always the unpainted paper itself, never painted white; almost no mid-grey; hard edges where light meets dark, wet bleeding edges everywhere else. Splashed ink (pomuk), dry-brush flying white, ink spatter, mist left as untouched paper. Monumental emptiness and ONE graphic device carrying the frame; a dramatic angle (worm’s-eye, bird’s-eye, dutch). Gods, giants, beasts and wonders may fill the frame; mortals stay small inside the wonder. Figures in confident calligraphic brush line; named faces match the attached portraits, translated into a few ink strokes. Black ink and paper only, except at most ONE small translucent wash of a single colour on the one symbolic object the scene names. Not photoreal, not webtoon shading, not watercolor landscape, not oil, no glow, no halo. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. No text, no calligraphy, no seal stamp, no watermark.

images.alt: Talhae’s huge bones laid out in an opened grave
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE: Korean webtoon figures with bold tapered ink contours and drawn faces, painted into a watercolor-and-oil world; old-master tenebrist canvas for night and interiors. JOSEON SUMI INK myth frame: a giant old king’s skeleton laid out in an opened earth grave, far taller than the two tiny diggers measuring it with a rope; huge black ink masses against bare paper, a single magpie on the grave’s rim, one translucent gold wash on the measuring rope. FULL-BLEED, no paper margin.

images.at: Suk Talhae, who came in a box
images.alt: a huge broad-faced old king in a fisherman’s plain robe laid on his back alone on black, the reapers’ robes closing in from the edges
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE: Korean webtoon figures with bold tapered ink contours and drawn faces, painted into a watercolor-and-oil world; old-master tenebrist canvas for night and interiors. Movie tenebrism: 75% of the frame in deep painted shadow, one hard practical key raking the subject, crushed blacks, long shadows, three depth planes with bokeh. FULL-BLEED 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop, nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Not photoreal, not a 3D render. No text, no lettering, no watermark. FINAL FRAME. A pure ALL-BLACK void, no floor, no room, no sky. Straight down from above, centred: a huge broad-faced old king in a fisherman’s plain robe laid on his back, a magpie feather on his chest — eyes closed, still. The body is lit by one cold soft key from directly above, falling off into black. Around the four edges of the frame, and only there, the grim reapers’ cloth: black reaper robes over blue and vermilion silk layers, white gat strings and the wide black gat brims, rendered in ink-brush strokes that dissolve into smoke slowly curl inward in a loose ring, circling the body like a slow whirlpool, never touching it; the centre and most of the frame stay pure black. Silent, monumental, funereal.

blocks.html: Bidam said there was no Kim. He was right for about a hundred and twenty years. Then, one spring night, King Talhae wakes to a rooster crowing in the woods west of the city.
blocks.ko: 비담은 김씨가 없었다고 했다. 백이십 년쯤은 그 말이 맞았다. 그러다 어느 봄밤, 탈해왕이 도성 서쪽 숲에서 닭이 우는 소리에 잠을 깬다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace · Talhae’s ninth spring
blocks.ko: 월성 · 탈해 아홉 해 봄

en: Hogong. There’s a rooster in Sirim.
Go and see what it wants.
Majesty, it’s a rooster. It wants—
…Yes, Majesty. Going.

blocks.html: At first light Hogong walks into Sirim with a lantern he no longer needs, and finds a small box of gold hanging from a branch, and a white rooster underneath it, crowing at nothing.
blocks.ko: 날이 밝을 무렵 호공은 이제 필요도 없는 등불을 들고 시림으로 들어간다. 나뭇가지에 작은 금빛 궤짝이 걸려 있고, 그 아래에서 흰 닭 한 마리가 아무것도 없는 데를 향해 울고 있다.

blocks.html: They bring the box to the king and open it, and inside is a little boy, handsome and wide awake, who looks at the king as if the king were the one who had turned up in a box.
blocks.ko: 궤짝을 왕 앞에 가져와 여니, 안에 잘생기고 눈이 말똥말똥한 사내아이가 있다. 아이는 궤짝에서 나타난 쪽이 왕이기라도 한 것처럼 왕을 쳐다본다.

en: Well.
I came in a box too, you know. Mine’s in the next room. It’s bigger.
lines: 나도 궤짝 타고 왔다. 내 건 옆방에 있어. 더 크지.

blocks.hanja: 瓠公還告，王使人取櫝開之，有小男兒在其中，姿容奇偉。上喜，謂左右曰：「此豈非天遺我以令胤乎！」乃收養之。
blocks.html: Hogong came back and reported it. The king had the chest brought and opened, and inside was a little boy of remarkable looks. The king was glad and said to those around him: “Is this not Heaven sending me a fine heir?” And he took him in and raised him.
blocks.ko: 호공이 돌아와 아뢰자, 왕이 사람을 시켜 궤짝을 가져와 열게 하니, 그 안에 작은 사내아이가 있었는데 생김새가 뛰어났다. 왕이 기뻐하여 좌우에 말하였다. “이 어찌 하늘이 내게 훌륭한 아들을 보내 준 것이 아니겠는가!” 그리고 거두어 길렀다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 1, Silla Annals — Talhae Isageum

blocks.html: Because he came out of a golden box, he is given the surname Kim, gold. Because he is a child, he is called Alji. The wood where the rooster crowed is renamed Gyerim, Rooster Wood, and for a while the whole country goes by that name.
blocks.ko: 금빛 궤짝에서 나왔으니 성은 김, 금이다. 아이이니 이름은 알지다. 닭이 울던 숲은 계림, 닭의 숲으로 이름이 바뀌고, 한동안은 나라 전체가 그 이름으로 불린다.

blocks.html: The boy grows up in the palace, quick and easy to like. The court notices. Talhae has sons of his own. He also has ministers who can count.
blocks.ko: 아이는 궁에서 자란다. 영리하고, 미워하기 어렵다. 조정이 눈여겨본다. 탈해에게는 제 아들들이 있다. 셈할 줄 아는 대신들도 있다.

blocks.label: Gyerim · ten springs later
blocks.ko: 계림 · 열 해 뒤 봄

blocks.html: The old king and the boy get on suspiciously well. Talhae teaches him to fish, and to lose a bet without the other man noticing. One evening he shows him the horn cup.
blocks.ko: 늙은 임금과 아이는 수상할 만큼 죽이 잘 맞는다. 탈해는 아이에게 낚시를 가르친다. 상대가 눈치 못 채게 내기에서 지는 법도. 그리고 어느 저녁, 뿔잔을 보여 준다.

lines: 거짓말하는 놈 입술에 붙는 잔이다. 해 봐라. 거짓말 하나 해 봐.
en: It sticks to a liar’s lips. Go on. Tell me a lie.
…I don’t like fishing.

blocks.html: He drinks. The cup comes away clean. He turns it over and sniffs the rim.
blocks.ko: 아이가 마신다. 잔이 말끔히 떨어진다. 아이는 잔을 뒤집어 보고, 전에 코를 대 본다.

en: It smells of pine.

lines: 토함산에 있는 건 다 송진 냄새가 나.
en: Everything on Toham smells of pine.
…You do like fishing, don’t you.
Very much, Majesty.

blocks.html: Neither of them mentions it again.
blocks.ko: 둘 다 다시는 그 이야기를 꺼내지 않는다.

en: Alji. The ministers say Heaven sent you to me as an heir.
Heaven sends a great many things. It sent me a magpie.
So. Do you want the chair?
lines: 알지. 대신들이 하늘이 그대를 내 후사로 보냈다 하오.
하늘은 이것저것 많이도 보내지. 나한텐 까치를 보냈어.
폐하께서 주실 수 있는 게 아니잖습니까. 마루로 돌아가는 것이지요.
en: …No, Majesty.
It isn’t yours to give. It goes back to the floor.
Ha! Who told you that?
You did, Majesty. Whenever there’s wine.
…So you’ll pass.
I’ll wait.
How long?

lines: 걸리는 만큼요. 금은 녹슬지 않으니까요, 폐하.
en: As long as it takes. Gold doesn’t rust, Majesty.

blocks.html: Talhae writes his name down as heir anyway. He has never once taken no for an answer from someone he likes.
blocks.ko: 탈해는 그래도 아이의 이름을 후사로 적어 둔다. 좋아하는 사람이 싫다고 해서 물러선 적이 평생 한 번도 없는 사내다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace · Talhae’s last winter
blocks.ko: 월성 · 탈해의 마지막 겨울

blocks.html: Talhae lives to be very old, in the house he stole, with the chest in the next room. One winter night a man in black is standing at the foot of the bed with a red book open, and Talhae, who has never been surprised by anything in his life, is.
blocks.ko: 탈해는 아주 오래 산다. 훔친 집에서, 옆방에 궤짝을 둔 채. 어느 겨울밤, 검은 옷의 사내가 붉은 책을 펼쳐 들고 침상 발치에 서 있다. 평생 무엇에도 놀란 적 없는 탈해가, 놀란다.

lines: 다파나의 왕자였소, 아진포 어부 집 아이였소?
en: Suk Talhae. Suk Talhae. Suk Talhae.
One question, then we walk.
Were you a prince of Dapana, or a fisherman’s boy from Ajinpo?
…What does your book say?

lines: 석이라고 적혀 있소. 까치의 이름. 나머지는 그대에게 맡기고.
en: It says Suk. The magpie’s name. The rest it leaves to you.
Then put me down as hers.
The old woman’s. She made me study.

lines: 깨끗한 답이오. 갑시다. 짧은 길이고, 그 길엔 집 가진 사람이 아무도 없소.
en: Clean answer. Come. It’s a short walk, and nobody on it owns a house.

lines: 아주 먼 훗날 무덤 파 보니
en: Suk Talhae, out of a box;
a magpie cried on the seaside rocks.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Buried some charcoal — “That one’s mine!” —
and won a house with a smith’s design.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Dig him up in a long, long while:
just as tall as he said, with a smile.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
blocks.title: Talhae Out of the Box

blocks.caption: Suk Talhae, who came in a box on the sea and took a house with a whetstone.
blocks.ko: 상자를 타고 바다를 건너와 숫돌 하나로 집을 얻은 석탈해.

blocks.html: His bones have a longer road. Six hundred years on, a king of Silla will dream of an angry old man, dig him up, and measure him. He is exactly as tall as he said.
blocks.ko: 그의 뼈는 더 먼 길을 간다. 육백 년 뒤, 신라의 어느 임금이 화난 노인 꿈을 꾸고 그를 파내어 재 본다. 그가 말한 키 그대로다.

blocks.label: The elders’ floor · that same winter
blocks.ko: 어른들의 마루 · 그해 겨울

blocks.html: The six houses meet in the same room. The faces are new and the arguments are not. Somebody has set the dead king’s horn cup in the middle of the floor, and each man has a small wooden piece in front of him, because sleeves turned out to be hard to count by lamplight.
blocks.ko: 여섯 집안이 같은 방에 모인다. 얼굴은 새것이고 다툼은 옛것이다. 누군가 죽은 임금의 뿔잔을 마루 한가운데 놓았고, 저마다 앞에 작은 나무패가 하나씩 있다. 등불 아래서는 소매를 세기가 어렵다는 걸 알았기 때문이다.

blocks.speaker: Elder Jung
lines: 거짓말하는 입술에 붙는다니 다들 거짓말은 마시오.
en: Left of the cup is no. Right is yes.
They say it sticks to a liar’s lips, so nobody lie.

blocks.html: Alji, fifteen now, sits by the wall where heirs sit. He looks at the cup and says nothing about pine.
blocks.ko: 이제 열다섯인 알지는 후사가 앉는 벽 쪽 자리에 있다. 그는 잔을 바라보며 송진 이야기는 하지 않는다.

blocks.speaker: Elder Lee
en: It comes back to the Park. That was the bargain.

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
en: The bargain was it comes back to the floor.
…Fine. Which Park?

blocks.speaker: Elder Jung
en: The eldest is Ilsung.

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
lines: 맏이는 일성이지. 똑똑한 건 파사고. 그리고 마루에 앉은 건 우리요.
en: The eldest is Ilsung. The cleverest is Pasa. And we’re the ones on the floor.

blocks.speaker: Elder Jung
en: In the Han, the eldest—

blocks.speaker: Elder Lee
en: We know.

blocks.speaker: Elder Jung
lines: 그리고 상자 아이. 선왕께서 이 아이 이름을 적으셨소.
en: And the box boy. The late king wrote his name.
Boy. Do you claim it?

lines: 선왕께도 빌린 것이었습니다. 물려주실 수 있는 게 아니었지요.
en: No, sir.
It was on loan to him. It wasn’t his to leave.

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
en: …Huh. The boy listens.

blocks.html: They raise Pasa over his elder brother, which no one in the Han would dream of doing. By morning all six pieces sit to the right of the cup. Nobody’s lips stick to anything.
blocks.ko: 그들은 형을 제치고 파사를 세운다. 한나라에서라면 꿈도 못 꿀 일이다. 아침이 되자 나무패 여섯이 모두 잔 오른쪽에 놓여 있다. 누구 입술에도 아무것도 붙지 않는다.

blocks.html: So Alji never wears it, and by every account he never asks again. The crown goes on passing between the Parks and the Suks, and every time it passes, the six houses pull up their mats. Nobody ever asks the Han.
blocks.ko: 그래서 알지는 끝내 왕관을 쓰지 않고, 어느 기록을 보아도 다시는 청하지 않는다. 왕관은 박씨와 석씨 사이를 오가고, 오갈 때마다 여섯 집안이 자리를 당겨 앉는다. 한나라에 묻는 사람은 아무도 없다.

blocks.label: Surabol · 262
blocks.ko: 서라벌 · 262년

blocks.html: Nearly two hundred years on, a Suk king dies without a son. The men on the floor are great-great-grandsons of the ones who raised Talhae, and they make the same three arguments in the same order. Their ledgers have run thin. The Parks have married into everything and have nobody left standing. The Suks have one boy, and he really is a boy.
blocks.ko: 이백 년 가까이 지나, 석씨 임금 하나가 아들 없이 죽는다. 마루에 앉은 사내들은 탈해를 세운 이들의 고손자들이고, 같은 세 가지 다툼을 같은 순서로 벌인다. 장부에 남은 이름이 얇다. 박씨는 온 데로 혼인해 들어가 서 있는 사람이 없다. 석씨에게는 아이 하나가 있는데, 정말로 아이다.

blocks.speaker: Elder Jung
lines: 상자에서 일곱째. 석씨 공주에게 장가들었고. 듬직하오. 그를 미워하는 사람이 없소.
en: There’s a Kim.
Seventh from the box. Married to a Suk princess. Steady. Nobody hates him.

blocks.speaker: Elder Lee
lines: 상자 아이네 핏줄? 그 집은 왕관을 써 본 적이 없소.
en: The box boy’s line? They’ve never worn it.

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
en: Neither had the chest, once.

blocks.html: It takes them all night, the way it always does now. In the morning they send for a careful man named Michu, who has been told nothing and has assumed the worst.
blocks.ko: 늘 그렇듯 밤을 새운다. 아침에 그들은 미추라는 신중한 사내를 부른다. 아무 말도 듣지 못했고, 그래서 최악을 짐작하고 온 사람이다.

blocks.caption: Michu. Seventh from the golden box, and nobody’s enemy. That turns out to be the qualification.
blocks.ko: 미추. 금빛 상자에서 일곱째, 누구의 적도 아닌 사내. 알고 보니 그게 자격이다.

en: …Why me?

blocks.speaker: Elder Choi
lines: 우리 여섯이 다 참아 줄 수 있는 사람이 당신뿐이라서.
en: Because you’re the one all six of us could stand.
Don’t let it go to your head.
And my sons?

blocks.speaker: Elder Jung
lines: 아드님들도 남들처럼 이 마루에 와야 하오.
en: Your sons come to the floor like everyone else’s.

blocks.html: So the first Kim wears the crown, seven generations after a rooster crowed at midnight. The Suks take it back after him. The Kims get it back again, and that time they keep it.
blocks.ko: 그렇게 첫 김씨가 왕관을 쓴다. 한밤중에 닭이 운 지 일곱 대 만이다. 그가 죽자 석씨가 도로 가져간다. 김씨가 다시 찾아오고, 이번에는 놓지 않는다.

blocks.html: Here is the trouble with a country that counts bones. Every house that ever wore this crown arrived in something: an egg, a chest, a box. The people who were here first need something to count. And the more carefully you count, the fewer you have. Every few generations a royal house runs short of sons who count, and the crown has to come from the floor instead. So no king of Silla can lean on the egg. He leans on the room.
blocks.ko: 뼈를 세는 나라의 골치는 이렇다. 이 왕관을 쓴 집안은 모두 무언가를 타고 왔다. 알, 궤짝, 상자. 먼저 와 있던 사람들에게는 셀 것이 있어야 한다. 그런데 꼼꼼히 셀수록 남는 게 적다. 몇 대에 한 번씩 왕가는 셈에 드는 아들이 모자라고, 그러면 왕관은 마루에서 나와야 한다. 그래서 신라의 어느 임금도 알에 기댈 수 없다. 그는 방에 기댄다.

blocks.html: By the time the Western historian hears about it, the floor has a name. He writes it down the way you would write down a calf with two heads.
blocks.ko: 서국 사관이 이 이야기를 들을 무렵, 그 마루에는 이름이 붙어 있다. 사관은 머리 둘 달린 송아지 이야기를 받아 적듯 그것을 적는다.

blocks.hanja: 事必與衆議，號和白，一人異則罷。
blocks.html: Every matter must be put to the many. They call it Hwabek. If one man differs, it is dropped.
blocks.ko: 일은 반드시 여럿과 의논한다. 이를 화백이라 부른다. 한 사람이라도 뜻이 다르면 그만둔다.
blocks.source: New Book of Tang (新唐書) bk. 220, Eastern Barbarians — Silla

blocks.html: The Kims of Surabol keep the crown a long time after that, and look down on a family from Gaya who have the same name for a different reason. Many generations on, one of them is a man named Chunchu.
blocks.ko: 서라벌 김씨는 그 뒤로 오래 왕관을 지킨다. 그리고 다른 이유로 같은 성을 가진 가야 출신 집안을 내려다본다. 그로부터 여러 대 뒤, 그 가운데 하나가 춘추라는 사내다.

blocks.html: Under a certain hill beyond the city lies a black pond in a steam-filled cave — Golhwacheon. The steam says the same word every time it leaves the water. Kim. It will be a long time before anybody answers it.
blocks.ko: 도성 너머 어느 언덕 아래에 검은 못이 있다 — 골화천. 김이 물을 떠날 때마다 같은 말을 한다. 김. 누군가 그 말에 대답하기까지는 아직 오래 걸릴 것이다.

blocks.html: Across the border in Sabi, a funeral bell. For three years the king can’t sign a thing. The clans already have a list…!
blocks.ko: 국경 너머 사비에 상종이 울린다. 삼 년 동안 임금은 도장 하나 찍지 못한다. 가문들 손에는 이미 명단이 있다…!

toneNote: A grandmother's fireside cycle on Tamla, braided against a court rotting from the inside.
title: The Fall of Euija

logline.en: Three years of mourning, by the rite. Everyone in Sabi knows exactly what can be done inside them.
logline.ko: 예법대로라면 삼년상이다. 사비 사람이라면 그 삼 년 안에 무엇을 할 수 있는지 정확히 안다.

Far wide at storm dusk: a Silla general and his escort on a low rise look the wrong way while a tiny black rider streaks toward them across the empty field, a single line of dust behind him
images.prompt: Far wide from low in dry autumn stubble at storm dusk. On a low rise on the right third, a Silla general in steel lamellar with a tall pointed jonghyeongju helm, blue cloth peeking at the collar, on a chestnut horse, with four mounted escorts and limp blue banners on poles, all looking the wrong way toward smoke on the horizon. Across the vast empty field from the left, a tiny black horse and rider streak toward them flat out, one long thin plume of dust trailing behind like a drawn line. ONE device: that dust-line diagonal across the empty field. Half the frame granulated storm sky; one low cloud-break rakes gold across the stubble and catches the dust line. Dark out-of-focus grass heads in the foreground. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — GYEBEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gyebek.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean and hard, sun-dark skin; black hair in a high topknot with loose strands over the brow; heavy scowl, narrow dark eyes, clean-shaven. Dress: Ochre-gold jeogori and trousers, a crimson scarf knotted at the chest, crimson sash at the waist, forearms wrapped in dark cloth. Demeanor: Says little. Counts under his breath. Grim, tired, absolutely decided; never smiles in a fight. Rose from a nameless White River boy to 백승계백 (Hundred-Victories Gyebek); by Hwangsanbeol the taverns argue he is the stronger blade than Yushin, and one-to-one he is: twenty-five years younger, faster, never beaten in single combat. Rides low and coiled, like he fights. Armor: Baekje kit: steel lamellar, rounded Baekje helm with neck guard; yellow cloth peeking, red sash/skirt accent — never a yellow metal cuirass. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Sword: Phoenix blade — Single-edged phoenix blade — straight, held backwards along the forearm, phoenix on the ring pommel; one side only, as he is. Pommel motif phoenix inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: One phoenix-ring sword, scabbard worn edge-up on the left hip. Fighting: REVERSE GRIP (역수), like a Japanese warrior's backhand hold: the small RING pommel pokes out ABOVE his thumb, the blade exits BELOW his little finger and lies flat back along the outside of his forearm toward the elbow, edge facing out. Low coiled crouch, blade-arm held across his body like a shield; he draws and cuts in one rising backhand slash, then stabs downward. Mounted, the blade trails back along the horse's flank. The blade is still the STRAIGHT ring-pommel sword of sw_bidam (handle:blade 1:3) — reverse grip is the hold, not a different sword. This hold overrides the hanging-blade 'ring at the little-finger side' note in SWORD ANATOMY; the ring→band→grip→collar→blade order is unchanged. SIGNATURE MOVE (the general-killer): alone on Gomanari at a flat-out gallop, he comes out of nowhere across an empty field straight at the enemy general, body folded flat and aerodynamic along the horse’s neck, cheek almost on the mane, the reverse-gripped blade laid back along his forearm and the horse’s flank; on the pass he snaps one backhand draw-cut, swift and clean like a samurai iai cut, and is already past, the blade flicked out to the side, before the escort moves. Show speed through the long low line of horse and rider, streaming mane, flung mud, motion-blurred ground — never gore; the cut reads as a bright arc, a flying helm plume or a riderless horse. #d9b13a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: curved blade, katana or tsuba (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); forward textbook grip once the fight starts; yellow metal cuirass; smiling in battle. | GOMANARI (고마나리, gyebek's horse) — attached board /obj_gomanari.png: Jet-black war horse with a long flowing black mane and tail — match the board. Plain dark tack, a yellow cord at the bridle. The fastest horse in Samhan: at full gallop his body stretches long and low, neck level, ears pinned, mane and tail streaming flat behind, hooves barely touching. Named for Gomanaru (Ungjin); stands by its master's planted sword after the field. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Baekje banners: warm yellow silk with a darker gold door-lintel and three gold stars. Attached flag /flag_baekje.png. Silla banners: blue silk with a white crescent moon. Attached flag /flag_silla.png. | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame.
