blocks.html: The tribute boat comes home light. The oranges stayed in Sabi. The news did not.
blocks.ko: 조공선이 가볍게 돌아온다. 귤은 사비에 두고 왔다. 소식은 두고 오지 않았다.

blocks.html: Gyebek has been waiting for this boat for nine hundred and sixty-one days. He knows, because he has cut a notch for every one of them in the beam by Yuri Dora’s door. They are the days left on the king’s mourning, counted down from the morning he washed up. When they run out, the king can sign again.
blocks.ko: 계백은 이 배를 구백육십하루 동안 기다렸다. 그걸 아는 건, 유리도라의 집 문 옆 들보에 하루에 하나씩 금을 그어 왔기 때문이다. 왕의 상이 끝날 때까지 남은 날들이다. 바닷가에서 깨어난 아침부터 거꾸로 세어 왔다. 그게 다 떨어지면 왕은 다시 어보를 찍을 수 있다.

blocks.html: Every one of those nights, Yuri Dora poured two cups and told him one of the island’s stories. Gyebek heard all of them standing by the door. The second cup always went cold there.
blocks.ko: 그 밤마다 유리도라는 잔 둘을 채우고 섬의 이야기를 하나씩 들려주었다. 계백은 그 이야기를 전부 문간에 선 채로 들었다. 두 번째 잔은 늘 거기서 식었다.

blocks.html: Gyebek is on the sand before the sail has a shape. The captain holds a Yunbi contract and has been told not to talk to him. He talks anyway. It is a long way to sail with a thing like that in your mouth.
blocks.ko: 돛이 모양을 갖추기도 전에 계백은 모래밭에 나와 있다. 선장은 윤비의 계약을 쥐고 있고, 그와 말을 섞지 말라는 당부를 들었다. 그래도 말한다. 그런 걸 입에 물고 오기엔 먼 뱃길이다.

blocks.speaker: The Captain
lines: 폐하께서 초하루에 정사암을 부르십니다. 여덟 가문 전부.
en: The rite is over, General. Done at the new year, sir.
His Majesty calls the Assembly on the first of the month. All eight houses.
Did he send for me.

blocks.speaker: The Captain
en: Nobody said your name, General.
Did anyone say it.

blocks.speaker: The Captain
lines: …배 댈 때 부인께서 부두에 나오셨습니다. 전해 달라구—
en: No, sir.
…Your wife came to the berth when we docked. She said to tell you—
the boy counts too.

blocks.html: Gyebek thanks him exactly once. He walks up the beach to the beam by the door, where the notches have run out. Nothing. He has never had a number end on him before.
blocks.ko: 계백은 꼭 한 번 고맙다고 한다. 그러고는 해변을 걸어 올라가 문 옆 들보 앞에 선다. 금이 다 그어져 있다. 영. 숫자가 그보다 먼저 끝나 버린 건 처음이다.

blocks.label: Two Cups
blocks.ko: 잔 둘

blocks.html: That night Yuri Dora pours two cups, as usual. Gyebek stands by the door, as usual. Nobody mentions the beam.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤에도 유리도라는 잔 둘을 채운다. 계백은 여느 때처럼 문간에 선다. 들보 얘기는 아무도 꺼내지 않는다.

lines: 거북아, 이젠 다 했저. 이 섬에 이녁이 안 들은 이야기는 하나도 엇다.
en: That’s the lot, Turtle. There’s not a story left on this island you haven’t had off me.

lines: 그것을 한 번 더 해 주십시오.
en: The fetch.
Tell that one again.

lines: 원님이 산 사람을 저승에 보내 염라를 잡아 오렌 했주. 경헌디 염라가 그 사람을 붙잡아 둬 불었저.
en: Kangrim, is it?
A magistrate sent a living man down to arrest the judge of the dead. And the judge kept him.
The magistrate let him go.

lines: 아니. 둘이 갈라 가졌주. 둘 다 그 사람을 원했으난.
en: He did not. They split him between them. Sure it’s the both of them wanted him.
…Someone sent for him.

blocks.html: Yuri Dora looks at him over the cup for a long time. Gyebek changes the subject, which he has never done before. It comes out as a question about debts.
blocks.ko: 유리도라는 잔 너머로 오래 그를 바라본다. 계백이 말을 돌린다. 처음 있는 일이다. 빚에 관한 물음으로 나온다.

lines: 왜 이 섬은 백제의 사람들을 맡아 줍니까.
en: Why does your island keep Baekje’s men.
You owe Baekje nothing.

lines: 빚이 엇어? 하. 옛날에 우리가 귤을 깜빡헌 적이 있주.
en: Owe nothing, is it? Ha. Once, long ago, we forgot the oranges.

blocks.html: One year, long ago, Tamla stops sending tribute. Rebellion would at least have been legible. This is closer to forgetting, which a large kingdom finds harder to forgive.
blocks.ko: 옛날 어느 해, 탐라가 조공을 끊는다. 반란이었다면 차라리 읽어 낼 수는 있었을 것이다. 이것은 잊어버림에 가깝고, 큰 나라에게는 그쪽이 더 용서하기 어렵다.

blocks.html: Baekje’s king marches an army to the southern harbour and stops. He lets the news cross the water on its own. It gets there faster than he would have.
blocks.ko: 백제 임금이 군사를 이끌고 남쪽 포구까지 가서 멈춘다. 소문이 제 발로 바다를 건너게 둔다. 소문이 그보다 빨리 닿는다.

blocks.html: Eighth month. Because Tamla had not sent its tribute, the king went out to punish it himself and got as far as Mujin Province. Tamla heard, sent envoys to beg pardon, and he stopped.
blocks.ko: 8월, 왕이 탐라가 공물과 부세를 바치지 않는다 하여 몸소 치러 나서 무진주에 이르렀다. 탐라가 이를 듣고 사신을 보내 죄를 비니, 그만두었다.
blocks.hanja: 八月，王以耽羅不修貢賦，親征，至武珍州。耽羅聞之，遣使乞罪，乃止。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 26, Baekje Annals — King Dongseong, yr. 20 (498), eighth month

blocks.html: Tamla apologises. Baekje accepts. Nobody is killed, everybody is satisfied, and the oranges resume. For a hundred and fifty years, that is the whole relationship.
blocks.ko: 탐라가 사죄한다. 백제가 받아들인다. 죽은 이는 없고 모두가 만족하며, 귤이 다시 온다. 이후 백오십 년 동안 두 나라 사이는 그것이다.

blocks.html: So when Baekje needs somewhere to put a man it cannot kill, there is an island, and the island owes it a favour.
blocks.ko: 그러니 백제가 죽일 수 없는 사람을 어딘가에 두어야 할 때, 섬이 하나 있고, 그 섬은 신세를 지고 있다.

lines: 건너고 싶었던 게 아니여. 건널 수 있덴 걸 알리고 싶었던 거주.
en: See what he did? He marched to the harbour, and stopped.
It wasn’t crossing he wanted. He wanted us to know he could.
His Majesty will cross.
After the Assembly.

lines: 거북아. 항구까지 왕 멈추는 임금은 뭔가를 말하는 거라.
en: Turtle. A king who marches to the harbour and stops is telling you something.
His Majesty has not marched to the harbour.
So he has not stopped.

blocks.html: Yuri Dora opens his mouth, and shuts it. There is no answer to that. There is only the next morning.
blocks.ko: 유리도라가 입을 열었다가 다문다. 거기엔 대답이 없다. 다음 날 아침이 있을 뿐이다.

blocks.html: He has run out of days to count. So at dawn he goes down to the black rock and starts counting something else.
blocks.ko: 셀 날이 다 떨어졌다. 그래서 새벽에 그는 검은 바위로 내려가 다른 것을 세기 시작한다.

blocks.label: Black Rock
blocks.ko: 검은 돌

blocks.html: He trains at the same hour on the same slab of lava on the eastern shore, and when the tide takes that slab he waits for the tide rather than use another one.
blocks.ko: 동쪽 갯가의 같은 현무암 너럭바위에서, 같은 시각에 훈련한다. 물이 그 바위를 덮으면 다른 바위를 쓰지 않고 물이 빠지기를 기다린다.

en: Sure the next rock is the same.
It is not the same.

blocks.html: The rock is porous and cruel and nothing like a drill ground. You cannot plant a foot on it twice in the same place. Two seasons of it and he no longer needs to know where his feet are.
blocks.ko: 그 바위는 구멍이 많고 모질며, 훈련장과는 조금도 같지 않다. 같은 자리에 두 번 발을 디딜 수 없다. 두 철을 그러고 나자, 그는 제 발이 어디 있는지 알 필요가 없어진다.

lines: 숨은 참는 게 아니여, 노래로 미는 거라.
en: It’s not holding the breath you do. You push it out with singing.
…I cannot sing.

lines: 못 허는 사람이 어디 이시니. 안 허는 사람만 있주.
en: Sure nobody cannot. There’s only them that don’t.

blocks.html: The village children learn the count of his drills before they learn his name, and stand on the rocks doing it badly behind him, and he does not once turn round to stop them, because stopping would be an interruption and he does not interrupt.
blocks.ko: 마을 아이들은 그의 이름보다 그의 훈련 횟수를 먼저 익힌다. 바위에 서서 뒤에서 서툴게 따라 하는데, 그는 한 번도 돌아서서 말리지 않는다. 멈추는 것은 중단이고, 그는 중단하지 않는다.

blocks.label: the warning
blocks.html: A man who cannot vary anything will be unbeatable on the ground he chose, and helpless on any other. Give him the choosing.
blocks.ko: 아무것도 바꾸지 못하는 사람은 제가 고른 땅에서는 무적이고 다른 땅에서는 속수무책이다. 그에게 고르게 하라.

blocks.label: Five Thousand
blocks.ko: 오천

blocks.html: He is asked, once, why he counts everything, and he answers honestly, which is the only way he has ever answered anything.
blocks.ko: 어째서 모든 것을 세느냐는 물음을 한 번 받는다. 그는 정직하게 답한다. 그가 무엇에든 답해 온 유일한 방식으로.

en: Numbers do not lie to me.
And people do?

lines: 사람은 속이려는 게 아니라, / 제가 못 알아듣습니다. / 얼굴을 읽는 법을 모릅니다.
en: People are not trying to. / I simply do not follow them. / I have never learned to read a face.

lines: 게민 이십 년을 조정에서 어떵 살안?
en: Then how is it you survived twenty years at a court?
I trusted one man.

blocks.html: The island considers this the saddest sentence anybody has said on it, and nobody explains to him why they have all gone quiet, and he does not ask, because he has not noticed.
blocks.ko: 섬은 그것을 여태 이 섬에서 나온 가장 슬픈 문장으로 여긴다. 아무도 그에게 왜들 조용해졌는지 설명해 주지 않고, 그는 묻지 않는다. 알아차리지 못했기 때문이다.

en: (Tamla fisher, laughing)
Hundred-Victories, they call him on the mainland — and he here counting oranges like they might desert.
lines: 육지선 백승이렌 부르주 — 이디선 귤이 도망갈까 봐 세엄서.

blocks.html: He drills in units of five hundred. One day he will take ten of those units to a field and leave the rest behind. The count is already in his mouth.
blocks.ko: 그는 오백을 한 단위로 훈련한다. 언젠가 그는 그것 열 개를 벌판으로 데려가고 나머지는 남겨 둘 것이다. 숫자는 이미 입에 있다.

blocks.html: That night he cuts a new notch at the other end of the beam. One. If the king sends, he will be ready. If the king does not send, he will be ready.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 들보 반대쪽 끝에 새 금을 하나 긋는다. 하나. 왕이 부르면, 준비가 되어 있을 것이다. 왕이 부르지 않아도, 준비가 되어 있을 것이다.

blocks.html: Meanwhile, in Sabi, Euija calls the Assembly. He has a smile, a speech, and a proclamation printed before anyone sat down…!
blocks.ko: 그 무렵 사비. 의자가 회의를 소집한다. 미소 하나, 연설 하나, 그리고 다들 앉기도 전에 찍어 둔 포고문 한 장…!

entries.tone: coup satire — martial law as theatre
entries.subtitle: 혁명

logline.en: He calls the assembly the way a gambler calls a final hand.
logline.ko: 그는 마지막 패를 부르는 노름꾼처럼 회의를 소집한다.

entries.toneNote: Deer Rock packed with sons; the speech is safety, the scroll is a padlock.

images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Night in the Satek clan hall at Sabi: a low lacquered table, ONE oil lamp on it. Minister Satek at the head, scarred face lit from below, leaning forward on his fists; three older Satek lords leaning in along the sides. Every man wears the tall gilt-bronze noble crown, gold catching the lamp; their shadows climb the plaster wall behind. Low angle from the end of the table. Device: the table as a dark wedge toward the lamp. CANON — MINISTER SATEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_satek_minister.png (face only; invent a new pose). Crown: the great-clan gilt crown (see NOBLE CROWN), no jougwan. #c2a24a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | NOBLE CROWN: Baekje great-clan lord’s gilt-bronze crown (금동관), as the attached crown (ignore its museum stand and black backdrop): a tall pointed gilt cap shaped like a peaked hood, pierced all over with openwork dragon-and-flame scrolls, a broad engraved band across the brow, a curved openwork crest arching over the top, two small cup-shaped finials on thin stems rising at the back, a pointed bud finial at the crown, and a flat openwork leaf-plume at the front. Worn high over the topknot on court and assembly days; burnished gold-bronze catching the key light. It replaces the jougwan. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: He calls the assembly the way a gambler calls a final hand — smiling, sleeves perfect, already knowing which tiles he slipped into the set.
blocks.ko: 그는 마지막 패를 부르는 노름꾼처럼 어전회의를 소집한다 — 웃고, 소매는 반듯하고, 패 속에 자기가 섞어 둔 패가 무엇인지 이미 아는 얼굴로.

blocks.html: Mourning ends at dawn. By breakfast Euija has called the Ministers’ Assembly to the Rock of Politics. The rock is dry. Someone forgot the brine, or remembered it and chose not to.
blocks.ko: 상은 새벽에 끝난다. 아침상이 들어오기도 전에 의자는 정사암으로 회의를 소집한다. 바위는 말라 있다. 소금물을 잊었거나, 기억하고도 바르지 않았다.

blocks.html: Look at the room while it still looks like this. Eight senior benches, one to a great house. Four generations, the same eight houses. Satek and Yunbi sit highest. The Prime Minister’s chair belongs to Satek, the way the brine does.
blocks.ko: 이 방이 아직 이 모양일 때 잘 봐 두라. 좌평 자리 여덟, 대성 한 집에 한 자리. 네 대째 같은 여덟 가문이다. 사택과 연비가 가장 높이 앉는다. 상좌평 자리는 사택의 것이다. 소금물이 그렇듯이.

blocks.title: The Rock of Politics, before · 정사암, 그 전
blocks.caption: Eight senior benches, eight houses, and a Satek in the Prime Minister’s chair.
blocks.ko: 좌평 여덟 자리에 여덟 가문, 상좌평 자리에는 사택.

lines: 우리 백성의 자유와 행복을 약탈하는 파렴치한 친서 반국가세력을 일거에 척결하기 위해 —
en: Beloved people.
As Eraha, I appeal to you with a heart that spits blood.
To eradicate in one stroke the shameless pro-West anti-state forces that plunder our people’s freedom and happiness —
I hereby declare emergency martial law.

blocks.html: Somebody coughs. Nobody looks at the rock. On the Satek bench a young man leans to his elder and whispers, loud enough to carry two benches over.
blocks.ko: 누군가 기침을 한다. 아무도 바위를 보지 않는다. 사택 쪽 자리에서 젊은 사내 하나가 어른 쪽으로 몸을 기울여 속삭인다. 두 자리 건너까지 들릴 만큼.

lines: 회의 전에 포고문을 찍어 두셨네. 먹 냄새 나유.
en: King Onjo preserve us — he’s lost his mind…
Also he printed the proclamation before the session. I can smell the ink.
The characters for “in one stroke” are still wet.

lines: 이 나라의 법도를 믿고 따라 온 선량한 백성들께 다소 불편이 있을 수 있소.
en: There may be some inconveniences for the good people who have followed the lawful order of this country.
We will strive to minimize such inconveniences.
I place my trust solely in you.
Please trust me.
Majesty. For how long?

lines: 임시란 — 영구라고 말하기 두려울 때 영구가 시작되는 방식이지.
en: This is temporary.
Temporary is how permanent things begin when you are afraid to say permanent.

blocks.html: Then he unrolls a second scroll — shorter, denser, the kind of law that fits on one sheet because the power is in what it erases. The clerks name it before he does: the Law to Remedy the Distress of the People and the Country.
blocks.ko: 이어 두 번째 두루마리를 펼친다 — 더 짧고, 더 빽빽하고, 지우는 것에 힘이 있어서 한 장으로 충분한 법. 서리들이 그보다 먼저 이름을 붙인다. 백성과 나라의 곤경을 덜기 위한 법.

lines: 백제의 법은 회의가 정한 절차 외에, 어라하의 명으로도 제정할 수 있다.
그 법은 옛 관례에서 벗어날 수 있다 — 회의 그 자체를 폐하지 않는 한.
회의의 존립은 위태롭지 않다. 상좌평의 자리도 그대로 둔다.
en: Laws of Baekje may also be enacted by the Eraha’s command.
Such laws may deviate from old custom — insofar as the Assembly as such is not abolished.
The existence of the Assembly is not endangered. The Prime Minister’s chair remains undisturbed.
Your Majesty. That is… a law for emptying the Assembly.
It keeps the name. It changes the people.

lines: 이제 여러분 스스로 고르시오. 평화인가, 전쟁인가.
en: If the name remains, the country remains.
If the people remain, the people eat the country.
May you now choose for yourselves — peace, or war.

blocks.html: Nobody chooses war out loud. Choosing peace means raising a sleeve for the scroll, and for a long moment nobody does that either. Then a sleeve goes up on the Satek bench. It belongs to Satek Chunbok, the young man who was whispering about wet ink.
blocks.ko: 아무도 큰 소리로 전쟁을 고르지 않는다. 평화를 고르려면 두루마리에 소매를 들어야 하는데, 한참 동안 그것도 아무도 하지 않는다. 그때 사택 쪽 자리에서 소매 하나가 올라간다. 젖은 먹 냄새를 속삭이던 그 젊은이, 사택춘복이다.

en: Chunbok. Put your arm down.

lines: 어르신께서도 잘 아시다시피, 폐하께서는 평화냐 전쟁이냐를 물으셨습니다.
en: As my lord well knows, His Majesty asked for peace or war.
I am choosing peace.

blocks.html: The old men try to rally, Satek calling in four generations of favors. Too late. The other houses, the ones Satek kept out of the light for a century, raise their sleeves one after another, delighted. Some are already paid. Some are already afraid. Some are the king’s own sons, waiting in the corridor.
blocks.ko: 늙은 대신들이 판을 되돌리려 한다. 사택은 사 대에 걸친 빚을 한꺼번에 불러들인다. 너무 늦었다. 백 년 동안 사택에 가려 그늘에 있던 다른 가문들이 신이 나서 하나씩 소매를 든다. 이미 삯을 받은 자, 이미 겁난 자, 그리고 복도에서 기다리던 왕의 아들들.

blocks.html: A face-off only works if you know your opponent’s style, and Euija has spent twenty years teaching them his. They lined up for a duel. He had already changed who was sitting.
blocks.ko: 맞대결은 상대의 수를 알 때나 통한다. 의자는 이십 년 동안 그들에게 자기 수를 가르쳐 왔다. 그들은 결투하려고 줄을 섰다. 그는 이미 앉는 사람을 바꿔 놓았다.

blocks.html: Euija names forty-one of his own sons to the Assembly, firing every single existing member. Eight houses spent four generations sharpening tricks on each other. Marriages. Roads. Clerks planted in rival counting-rooms. In one morning the king clears the board. He simply changes the pieces. By noon nobody has an answer.
blocks.ko: 의자는 제 아들 마흔하나를 좌평에 앉히고, 기존 인사를 모조리 내친다. 여덟 가문은 네 대에 걸쳐 서로를 겨눈 수를 갈아 왔다. 혼인. 길. 상대 계산방에 심어 둔 서기. 왕은 하루아침에 판을 쓸어 버린다. 그냥 말을 바꿔 버린 것이다. 정오가 되어도 받아칠 말이 없다.

blocks.html: Satek Chunbok is named Prime Minister. His own clan watches him walk to the chair. The Enabling Law did not abolish the chair. It only changed who sits in it.
blocks.ko: 사택춘복이 상좌평에 오른다. 제 가문이 그가 그 자리로 걸어가는 것을 지켜본다. 수권법은 그 자리를 없애지 않았다. 앉는 사람만 바꿨을 뿐이다.

blocks.title: The Rock of Politics, after · 정사암, 그 후
blocks.caption: The same benches. Every one of them a son.
blocks.ko: 같은 자리. 전부 아들이다.

blocks.caption: A Satek in the Satek chair, sitting for the king.
blocks.ko: 사택의 자리에 앉은 사택. 왕을 위해 앉았다.

blocks.html: Forty-one sons need forty-one seats. None goes to the Ye family. They have held Bear Fortress for four generations and never once been asked to court. Ye Sikjin reads the list at home, twice. Then he puts it in a drawer.
blocks.ko: 아들 마흔하나에게는 자리 마흔하나가 필요하다. 예씨 몫은 하나도 없다. 네 대째 웅진성을 지켜 왔건만 조정에 한 번도 불려 간 적 없는 집안이다. 예식진은 집에서 명단을 두 번 읽는다. 그리고 서랍에 넣는다.

blocks.html: Four generations of the Ye family, and not one invitation.
blocks.ko: 예씨 가문 사 대, 초대장은 한 장도 없었다.

blocks.html: Then he hands out the quiet money that really runs Baekje. Harbour warehouses. River pilot fees. The stamp a ship needs before it sails east. The martial law was the noise. The stamps are what change.
blocks.ko: 그다음 그는 백제를 실제로 굴리는 조용한 돈을 다시 나눈다. 바닷가 창고. 강의 도선료. 동쪽으로 떠나는 배에 찍는 도장. 계엄은 소음이었다. 바뀌는 건 도장이다.

blocks.html: He cannot do what Yeon did. Baekje would not forgive it, and more to the point, he would not. He does not need a banquet. He needs a majority that looks like kinship.
blocks.ko: 연개소문이 한 짓은 하지 못한다. 백제가 용서하지 않을 것이고, 더 중요한 건 — 그 자신도 하지 않을 것이다. 잔치는 필요 없다. 혈연처럼 보이는 다수가 필요할 뿐이다.

blocks.label: The Mark Moves
blocks.ko: 표가 옮겨간다

blocks.html: There is one more chair that is not a chair. The crown-prince mark has sat on Yung’s forehead since the boy could walk — Satek tutors, Satek berths, Satek inevitability. Euija has been counting the cost of it the way other men count harvests.
blocks.ko: 의자가 아닌 의자가 하나 더 있다. 태자의 표는 융이 걸음마를 시작할 때부터 그 이마에 앉아 있었다 — 사택 스승, 사택 자리, 사택의 필연. 의자는 그것을 다른 사내들이 추수를 세듯 세어 왔다.

en: Yung. Twenty years you carried my mark, and never once dropped it where the people could see.
lines: 융. 스무 해 넘게 내 표를 짊어졌고, 백성들 보는 앞에선 한 번도 떨어뜨린 적 없지.

en: Eleven, Father. Eleven years since the appointment. I keep the number for both of us.
lines: 열한 해입니다, 아버님. 책봉받은 지 열한 해. 두 분 몫으로 제가 세고 있습니다.

en: Eleven. And in those eleven, whose tutors taught you? Whose berths berthed you? Whose inevitability did you sleep in?
lines: 열한 해. 그 열한 해 동안, 누구 스승이 너를 가르쳤고, 누구 자리가 너를 재웠느냐? 누구의 필연 속에서 잤느냐?

en: My mother’s house. Which you chose for me.
A crown prince is not an eldest son. He is a choice. Mine.
lines: 태자는 맏아들이 아니다. 선택이다. 내 선택.

blocks.html: Hyo comes forward before he is called, which is the most Hyo thing he has ever done. Behind the screen, Ungo says one word — the way she ends all bargains.
blocks.ko: 효는 불리기 전에 앞으로 나온다. 효답지 않게 가장 효다운 짓이다. 병풍 뒤에서 은고가 한 마디 한다 — 그녀가 모든 흥정을 끝내는 방식으로.

en: Done.
Father. Brother. I did not ask for—
No. You never ask. Things arrive for you.
lines: 아니. 넌 청한 적이 없지. 것들은 제 발로 오니까.

en: Then give me the asking, brother. Tell me what to refuse and I will refuse it.
lines: 그럼 청하는 걸 다오, 형. 뭐를 사양해야 하는지만 말해라. 사양할게.

en: You cannot refuse it. It is already on. I counted the years. You count the rest.
lines: 사양 못 해. 이미 얹혔어. 지나간 해는 내가 셌으니, 남은 해는 네가 세어라.

blocks.html: Yung bows to his father, to his brother, to the screen — three bows, three depths, the Satek tutors watching their eleven years walk out. That night the tutors are dismissed. The resentment stays, and it starts learning to count in a new currency.
blocks.ko: 융은 아버님께, 아우에게, 병풍에게 절한다 — 세 번, 깊이를 달리해. 사택 스승들은 열한 해가 걸어 나가는 것을 본다. 그날 밤 스승들은 물러난다. 원망은 남고, 새 돈으로 셈을 배우기 시작한다.

blocks.label: That Night
blocks.ko: 그날 밤

blocks.html: That night he writes one letter himself, with no clerk in the room. It is short, because the man it is for cannot read. A boatman will have to say it to him aloud.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 서기도 물리고 손수 편지 한 장을 쓴다. 짧다. 받을 사람이 글을 못 읽기 때문이다. 뱃사공이 소리 내어 일러 줘야 할 것이다.

lines: 오늘 밤이다, 춘복. 늙은이들이 잃은 걸 다 세기 전에.
en: Tamla. The fastest boat in the harbour.
Tonight, Chunbok. Before the old men finish counting what they lost.

lines: 폐하… 폐하께서도 잘 아시다시피, 오늘 밤 가문들은 셈을 하고 있습니다.
자리가 식기도 전에 탐라로 배가 떠나면, 저들은 그것을 전쟁으로 읽을 것입니다.
먼저 지는 데 익숙해지게 두십시오. 한 달입니다. 그다음에 부르십시오.
en: Your Majesty… as Your Majesty well knows, the houses are counting tonight.
If a boat leaves for Tamla before the benches are cold, they will read it as war.
Let them get used to losing first. A month. Then send for him.

lines: 그려. 한 달. 그놈은 기다리는 건 잘혀. 세거든.
en: …A month.
Fine. A month. He’s mighty good at waiting. He counts.

blocks.html: He folds the letter into his sleeve. It will stay there a good deal longer than a month.
blocks.ko: 그는 편지를 접어 소매에 넣는다. 그 편지는 한 달보다 훨씬 오래 거기 머물 것이다.

lines: 폐하. 오늘은 몇 분이나 자르셨습니까? / …저희는 몇이나 남기시려구유.
en: Your Majesty. How many did you dismiss today? / …And how many of us are you fixing to keep.
All of them. / You… I keep.

lines: …무서워라. / 그런디 워쩌유. 그런 폐하가… 더 가깝게 느껴져유.
en: …Mercy, how frightening. / And yet — that kind of Majesty… feels nearer.
…What was your name again.

lines: 아직 없습니다. / 오늘 밤에 하나 지어 주셔유. / 계백 장군한테 하셨듯이 — 오래.
en: I don’t have one yet. / Make me one tonight. / As you did for General Gyebek — take your time.

blocks.html: Eleven of them by morning.
blocks.ko: 아침이 오기 전에 열하나가 된다.

blocks.html: Months later, the new Prime Minister is in Chang’an, talking too much. A spy who learns his trade that well rarely works for only one house.
blocks.ko: 몇 달 뒤, 새 상좌평은 장안에서 말이 많다. 일을 그만큼 잘 배운 첩자는 한 집만 섬기는 법이 드물다.

blocks.label: Chang’an
blocks.ko: 장안

en: So… Baekje? What of Baekje—
zhLatn: Nàme… Bǎijì? Bǎijì yòu rúhé——

en: Do not trouble yourself over Baekje.

lines: 백제 족속들은 가문 싸움을 좋아해서, 서로 시기하다가 망할 것입니다.
en: Baekje will fall on its own.
Where blood ties are strong, the state grows weak.
The Baekje clans love a family feud — they will envy each other into ruin.
Then why am I needed at all?
zhLatn: Nà zhèn yòu hébì cúnzài?

lines: 아무리 약해도, 한 번의 충격은 줘야죠.
서군이 쳐들어온다고 하면, 그 소문만으로도 나라의 기세가 기울어질 것입니다.
en: However weak it is, it still needs one shock.
Say the Western army is coming — the rumour alone will tip the country’s spirit.

blocks.html: He beat eight houses in one morning. Now he can’t sleep. In his dreams, somebody keeps counting…?

blocks.html: When a kingdom falls, somebody always finds a woman to blame. Baekje had one picked out years early.
blocks.ko: 나라가 무너지면 누군가는 꼭 탓할 여자를 찾아낸다. 백제는 몇 해나 앞서 하나를 골라 두었다.

blocks.label: The Dream
blocks.ko: 꿈

blocks.label: Nightmares
blocks.ko: 악몽

blocks.html: He starts dreaming about the Rock of Politics. In the dream it is dry, and he is rubbing it with brine, and the brine will not stay. Every time he lifts the cloth the stone is dry again, and the eight elders are standing round it waiting for it to sweat.
blocks.ko: 그는 정사암 꿈을 꾸기 시작한다. 꿈속에서 바위는 말라 있고, 그는 소금물을 문지르는데 소금물이 배지 않는다. 천을 들 때마다 돌은 다시 말라 있고, 여덟 원로가 그 둘레에 서서 바위가 땀 흘리기를 기다린다.

blocks.html: Some nights it is the white deer, come back out of the dark it was kept in, and too big for the hunting ground. Some nights it is a boat on the water with a man sitting very straight in the stern, not rowing, counting.
blocks.ko: 어떤 밤은 흰 사슴이다. 가둬 두었던 어둠에서 다시 나왔는데, 사냥터에 들기엔 너무 크다. 어떤 밤은 물 위의 배 한 척이고, 고물에 한 사내가 아주 꼿꼿이 앉아 있다. 노는 젓지 않고, 센다.

lines: (잠에서 깨어, 어둠에 대고) 누가 세고 있느냐?
…거기 누구냐. 불. 누가 불 좀 가져와라!
en: (waking, to the dark) Who’s counting?
…Who’s there. Light. Somebody bring a light!
Majesty. It’s only us.
…You were saying numbers again.

lines: 아니. 물 타지 말어. 물 타믄 다 알어.
en: Wine.
No. Don’t you go watering it. I can tell when you water it.

blocks.html: The light comes before the wine does. Queen Ungo carries it herself, across three courtyards, in her sleeping robe. The maids find somewhere else to be.
blocks.ko: 술보다 불이 먼저 온다. 왕후 은고가 손수 들고 왔다. 마당 셋을 건너, 잠옷 차림으로. 궁녀들은 각자 있을 곳을 찾아 흩어진다.

blocks.caption: The queen. The court has its own word for her, and it isn’t queen.
blocks.ko: 왕후. 조정은 그녀를 부르는 말이 따로 있다. 왕후는 아니다.

en: They don’t water it. I do.
Half and half. You stop tasting it after the second cup.
lines: 물은 쟤들이 안 타요. 내가 타지.

en: I taste it at the first.
…What are you doing up?
Somebody shouted for a light. I was nearest.
lines: 누가 불 가져오라고 소리치길래. 내가 제일 가까웠어요.

en: You were three courtyards off.
Then I was quick.

blocks.html: She sets the lamp where he can see her face, and sits on the edge of the bed like a woman who has done this before. She has. Most nights this year.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 얼굴이 보이는 자리에 등잔을 내려놓고, 한두 번 해 본 솜씨가 아닌 듯 침상 끝에 앉는다. 한두 번이 아니다. 올해 들어 거의 매일 밤이다.

en: I was counting again.
Nine hundred and seventy-two. Then you lose your place and start over.
lines: 구백칠십이. 그러다 어디까지 셌는지 잊고 처음부터 다시.

blocks.html: She does not ask what the number is. She was in Sabi the year a minister counted it at his door every morning.
blocks.ko: 그 숫자가 뭔지 그녀는 묻지 않는다. 대신 하나가 아침마다 그의 문 앞에서 그 수를 세던 해에, 그녀도 사비에 있었다.

en: Where’s the boy?
Asleep. Like a crown prince.
He sits the Rock in the morning. Top bench. Yung’s had his robe pressed since yesterday.
lines: 아침에 정사암에 앉아요. 맨 윗자리. 융은 어제부터 옷을 다려 놨대요.

en: Yung presses his robe for funerals.
…Whose?
Ha! Nobody’s. Yet. Go to sleep, woman.
lines: 하! 아무도 아녀. 아직은. 가서 자.

en: Come to the Rock tomorrow.
You go.
Queens don’t sit on the Rock.
Then sit behind it. You hear better from behind things.
lines: 그럼 뒤에 앉어. 뭐든 뒤에서 들어야 잘 들리는 겨.

blocks.html: He means it as a compliment. It is the most important order he gives all year, and he is asleep again before the lamp gutters.
blocks.ko: 그는 칭찬으로 한 말이다. 그해 그가 내린 명령 중 가장 중요한 명령인데, 등잔불이 사그라지기도 전에 그는 다시 잠든다.

blocks.label: The Hall
blocks.ko: 전각

blocks.html: The first man to say the obvious thing out loud is Hungsu. He says it smiling, the way he says everything.
blocks.ko: 뻔한 말을 맨 먼저 소리 내어 한 사람은 흥수다. 늘 그렇듯 웃으면서 한다.

lines: 금강경에 이르기를, 지어진 모든 것은 꿈과 같다 하였습니다, 폐하. 이슬 같고 번개 같다고.
en: The Diamond Sutra says every made thing is like a dream, Majesty. A dewdrop. A flash of lightning.
Your new Assembly is a made thing.
Hungsu. Is this a sermon or a memorial?

lines: 겨울이 오기 전에 사택과 윤비 사람들을 자리로 돌려놓으십시오. 신라가 온다면 탄현으로 옵니다. 당이 온다면—
en: Both, Majesty. The sermon is free.
Bring the Satek and Yunbi men back to the benches before winter. If Silla comes, it comes over Tanhyun. If the West comes—

lines: —강으로 온다. 그래. 과인도 지도는 읽을 줄 안다.
목소리 좋구나, 흥수. 고마미지에는 그걸 들어 줄 사람이 없지. 가서 그들에게 경이나 읽어 주거라.
en: —it comes up the river. Yes. I can read a map.
You have a lovely voice, Hungsu. Gomamiji has nobody to hear it. Go and read them sutras.

blocks.html: Euija calls it a temporary posting. The court knows better. The paper names a county far to the south: packed earth, a magistrate’s hut, and a long way from anyone who matters.
blocks.ko: 의자는 잠시 내려보내는 것이라 한다. 조정은 다 안다. 종이에 적힌 곳은 먼 남쪽 고을이다. 다져진 흙, 원님 오두막 하나, 그리고 중요한 사람들에게서 아주 먼 곳.

blocks.label: Gomamiji
blocks.ko: 고마미지

blocks.html: Gomamiji is a posting, not a retirement. He sits on the threshold until the dust on the hem looks like the hem. His office sword hangs on the doorpost. Nobody from Sabi writes.
blocks.ko: 고마미지는 부임지다. 은퇴가 아니다. 그는 문지방에 앉아 있다. 옷자락의 먼지가 옷자락처럼 보일 때까지. 관직 칼은 문설주에 걸려 있다. 사비에서는 아무도 편지하지 않는다.

blocks.html: Somebody does write, from the other direction. The letter comes from a hill fort east of Charcoal Pass. It is short, because the fort is gone.
blocks.ko: 편지는 오긴 온다. 반대쪽에서. 탄현 동쪽 산성 하나에서 온 편지다. 짧다. 그 성이 이제 없으니까.

blocks.title: The eastern forts
blocks.caption: While Sabi drinks, Silla takes the hill forts one at a time.
blocks.ko: 사비가 마시는 동안, 신라는 산성을 하나씩 가져간다.

blocks.label: The Rock of Politics
blocks.ko: 정사암

blocks.html: The letter reaches the Rock on a morning when the Prime Minister is in Chang’an and the king is in bed. That leaves forty-one sons and one screen.
blocks.ko: 편지가 정사암에 닿은 아침, 상좌평은 장안에 가 있고 임금은 침상에 있다. 남은 건 아들 마흔하나와 병풍 하나다.

blocks.html: Behind the screen sits the queen. The king told her to, half asleep. Nobody else heard him say it.
blocks.ko: 병풍 뒤에는 왕후가 앉아 있다. 반쯤 잠든 임금이 그러라고 했다. 그 말을 들은 사람은 그녀뿐이다.

blocks.html: The clerk reads standing. Nobody tells him to sit, because two princes at the far end are using the only spare cushion to settle something.
blocks.ko: 서기는 선 채로 읽는다. 앉으라는 사람이 없다. 맨 끝자리 왕자 둘이 하나 남은 방석을 두고 뭔가를 결판내는 중이라서다.

en: “…the fort at—” The name’s smudged, my lords. Something-seong.
lines: “……의 성이—” 이름이 번졌사옵니다, 나리들. 무슨무슨 성이옵니다.
blocks.speaker: The Clerk

en: —it was mine on the second day—
—you weren’t even here on the second day—
blocks.speaker: Two Princes

en: “…is lost. The garrison is—” That part’s smudged too.
blocks.speaker: The Clerk

en: Smudged. Then it was small.
Small, and Silla’s now. Write that. It’s shorter.
lines: 작고, 이젠 신라 거지. 그렇게 적어. 그게 더 짧다.

blocks.html: Tae laughs at his own joke. He is the only one.
blocks.ko: 태가 제 농담에 웃는다. 혼자다.

en: We send men. Today. From Bear Fortress—
Ye Sikjin’s men? He’s still sulking over his invitation.
lines: 예식진 군사를? 그 양반 아직도 초대장 못 받은 걸로 삐쳐 있소.

en: The capital guard, then.
Father’s guard. Ask Father.
…Oh. He’s asleep. Ask your mother.

blocks.html: Forty heads turn to the screen, then away from it, as if it were hot.
blocks.ko: 마흔 개의 머리가 병풍 쪽으로 돌아갔다가, 데기라도 한 듯 도로 돌아간다.

en: The capital guard stays in the capital.
Prince Yung. Your mother’s house keeps two thousand men on the eastern road. Lend them.
lines: 융 왕자. 그대 외가가 동쪽 길에 군사 이천을 두고 있지요. 빌려주시오.

en: My mother’s house has no bench on this Rock, Majesty. Father saw to that.
lines: 제 외가는 이 바위에 자리가 없습니다, 마마. 아버님이 그리 만드셨지요.

en: Then they’ll be glad of the work.
…Two thousand men. And the river pilot fees go back to Satek.
lines: ……군사 이천. 대신 강 뱃길 삯은 사택에 돌려주시지요.

en: Those are Father’s—
Done.
Mother—
Done, I said. Clerk, write it.

blocks.html: The clerk writes it. Yung bows to the screen as though he had paid something. The screen paid more, and everyone on the Rock knows exactly how much.
blocks.ko: 서기가 받아 적는다. 융은 뭔가 치른 사람처럼 병풍에 절한다. 더 많이 치른 건 병풍 쪽이고, 정사암의 모두가 그게 얼마인지 정확히 안다.

blocks.html: The Satek men march nine days later. They arrive in time to count the smoke.
blocks.ko: 사택의 군사는 아흐레 뒤에 떠난다. 도착해 보니 셀 수 있는 건 연기뿐이다.

blocks.html: At the foot of the Rock, where the benches end, an old man with an office sword and no office has listened to all of it.
blocks.ko: 정사암 아래, 자리가 끝나는 곳에서, 관직 없이 관검만 찬 노인 하나가 그 모든 걸 듣고 있었다.

en: My lords. If the eastern forts go, the next thing is the pass, and after the pass—
lines: 나리들. 동쪽 성들이 떨어지면 다음은 고개고, 고개 다음은—

en: You don’t have a bench, Sunchung.
…No, my lord. I’ll take it to someone who does.

blocks.label: The Fox
blocks.ko: 여우

blocks.label: The Corridor
blocks.ko: 회랑

en: She gave away the pilot fees. From behind a screen.
blocks.speaker: A Clerk

en: She did? Or the screen did?
blocks.speaker: Another Clerk

en: My aunt says a fox sits behind screens. A white one. Nine tails.
lines: 우리 이모가 그러는디, 병풍 뒤엔 여우가 앉는댜. 흰 놈. 꼬리 아홉 달린.
blocks.speaker: A Clerk

en: Your aunt cooks for the Satek.
blocks.speaker: Another Clerk

en: Still.
blocks.speaker: A Clerk

blocks.html: By the end of the month the whole palace has heard about the white fox. The queen hears it last, and laughs, which does not help.
blocks.ko: 그달이 다 가기 전에 온 궁이 흰 여우 얘기를 듣는다. 왕후는 맨 나중에 듣고 웃는다. 그게 도움이 되진 않는다.

en: My aunt says the queen’s calendar comes from the shaman’s hut. Which basket moves, which waits — the mudang marks the days.
lines: 우리 이모가 그러는디, 왕후마마의 달력은 무당집에서 온댜. 어느 광주리가 가고 어느 게 기다리는지 — 무당이 날을 찍어 준댜.
blocks.speaker: A Clerk

en: So the shaman rules now? Shall we bow toward the hut?
lines: 그럼 이제 무당이 다스리냐? 오두막 쪽으로 절할까?
blocks.speaker: Another Clerk

en: Bow toward whoever decides who kneels, and when.
lines: 누가 언제 꿇는지를 정하는 쪽으로 절해라.
blocks.speaker: A Clerk

blocks.html: Nobody laughs at that one.
blocks.ko: 그 말엔 아무도 안 웃는다.

blocks.label: The Stair
blocks.ko: 계단

blocks.html: On the stair between the Rock and the wine, the two princes meet coming opposite ways. Hyo carries a basket of his father’s unopened memorials. Yung carries nothing, which these days is a statement.
blocks.ko: 바위와 술잔 사이 계단에서 두 왕자가 엇갈린다. 효는 아버님의 뜯지 않은 상소 한 광주리를 들고 있다. 융은 아무것도 들고 있지 않다. 요즘은 그것도 뜻이다.

en: Brother. Mother reads them all. She only sleeps when—
lines: 형. 어머님이 다 읽으세요. 주무시는 건—

en: When what. When the mark sits straight on your forehead?
lines: 언제. 표가 네 이마에 바로 앉을 때?

en: It itches. If you want it back, take it. Tell Father I dropped it.
lines: 가렵다. 도로 가져가려면 가져가. 아버님께 떨어뜨렸다고 해라.

en: I take nothing from behind screens. Enjoy the basket.
lines: 병풍 뒤에서 받는 건 없어. 광주리나 즐겨라.

blocks.html: He goes up. Hyo goes down. On the stair between them, eleven years — one going, one coming — and neither looks back, because brothers who look back on stairs fall.
blocks.ko: 그는 올라가고 효는 내려간다. 사이 계단에 열한 해 — 하나는 가고 하나는 오고 — 둘 다 뒤돌아보지 않는다. 계단에서 뒤돌아보는 형제는 떨어지니까.

blocks.label: The Banquet Hall
blocks.ko: 연회장

blocks.html: He stops holding court. The wine comes earlier each day, and then it stops being tied to the day at all.
blocks.ko: 그는 조회를 열지 않는다. 술은 날마다 조금씩 더 이른 시각에 올라오다가, 이윽고 시각과 상관없어진다.

blocks.html: Hundreds, by now. Nobody keeps the roll. They no longer have separate duties — only who pours, who steadies his wrist, who is still there when the wine runs out, and who is bold enough to speak while his mouth is busy elsewhere.
blocks.ko: 이제는 수백이다. 명부를 적는 사람이 없다. 소임은 없다 — 누가 따르는지, 누가 손목을 붙드는지, 술이 떨어지면 누가 남아 있는지, 그리고 폐하의 입이 다른 데에 있는 동안에도 감히 말하는 자가 누구인지뿐.

blocks.html: The hems keep time better than the roll. A pour, a step, a kneel — the long court silk opens, and he watches that before he watches the wine.
blocks.ko: 명부보다 자락이 시각을 지킨다. 따르고, 오르고, 무릎을 굽히면 — 긴 조정 비단이 열리고, 그는 술보다 그것을 먼저 본다.

blocks.html: The feast is no longer a feast. The stories say three thousand. The room is not that. It is still too many, a harem so packed the lamp never finds a wall. Robes open early. The maids show him their bodies the way other courts show tribute, and he studies them the way he once studied a map.
blocks.ko: 연회는 더 이상 연회가 아니다. 이야기로는 삼천이라 한다. 방이 그만큼은 아니다. 그래도 너무 많다. 등불이 벽에 닿지 못할 만큼 빽빽한 후궁이다. 옷고름은 일찍 풀린다. 궁녀들은 다른 조정이 조공을 바치듯 그에게 몸을 내보이고, 그는 예전에 지도를 들여다보던 눈으로 그것을 들여다본다.

blocks.html: He is half-undressed by the second jar and does not bother to hide what the wine has done to him. They climb into his lap two at a time. They hike the silk and laugh when he looks. They toast until the lamps blur. On rainy nights the party spills out onto the night veranda, and he follows a hip down the night corridor as if it were the last order anyone will ever give him.
blocks.ko: 두 번째 단지쯤이면 그는 반쯤 벗었고, 술이 제 몸에 한 일을 굳이 감추지도 않는다. 궁녀들은 둘씩 그의 무릎에 오른다. 비단 자락을 걷어 올리고, 그가 보면 웃는다. 등불이 번질 때까지 잔을 든다. 비 오는 밤이면 잔치는 밤 툇마루로 넘쳐 나가고, 그는 누군가의 허리를 따라 밤 복도를 걷는다. 그것이 세상에 남은 마지막 명령이라도 되는 듯이.

blocks.html: Here is what the lamps do not show. The headband is gone, and nobody tells him to put it back on. The prince who could read a room in one glance cannot read past the next fold of silk. Every one of them flatters him. He knows it, and he likes knowing it. It is the only sum left in Sabi that always comes out in his favour.
blocks.ko: 등불이 보여 주지 않는 것이 있다. 머리띠는 사라졌고, 다시 매라고 말하는 사람은 없다. 한 번 훑어보면 방 하나를 다 읽던 왕자가, 이제는 다음 비단 주름 너머를 읽지 못한다. 모두가 그에게 아첨한다. 그도 안다. 알아서 좋다. 사비에 남은 셈 가운데 언제나 그에게 유리하게 떨어지는 셈은 그것 하나뿐이다.

lines: 폐하. 어제 하신 말씀을 오늘 또 하셨습니다.
en: Your Majesty. You said that yesterday, and again today.
…With the same breath on us.
The same teeth… at our collarbones.
Was it good?
Or… was it a good night.

lines: 폐하가 멈추라구 하셔두… 허리가 먼저 대답해유.
en: …It was, yesterday.
The body still remembers.
Even if Your Majesty says stop… the hips answer first.

lines: 폐하. 젊으실 때 얘기 좀 해 주십시오.
en: Your Majesty. Tell us about when you were young.
Before you… undo anything.
No —
While you undo it.
One word per knot.
…What is it you want to know.

lines: 삼신께서 폐하 몫 장부를 따로 두시나 봐요. 부엌에선 그게 워찌 되는 건가 내기꺼정 붙었어요.
en: They say you have more than fifty sons.
Samsin must keep a whole ledger just for Your Majesty. The kitchens have a wager going on how.
Nightly.
…That was the thirtieth Eraha. My father.

lines: 아, 그럼 폐하는 아직 여유가 있으시네유.
en: Ah. Then Your Majesty still has room to work with, I reckon.
We can testify to it.
We knew already, in fairness.
Asking was only manners.

blocks.html: He laughs for the first time in four months. It is the last recorded instance.
blocks.ko: 넉 달 만에 처음으로 그가 웃는다. 기록에 남은 마지막 웃음이다.

blocks.label: The Queen’s Rooms
blocks.ko: 왕후전

blocks.html: Three courtyards away it is very quiet. The queen’s rooms smell of ink, not wine. The memorials the king will not open come here instead.
blocks.ko: 마당 셋 건너는 아주 조용하다. 왕후전에선 술 냄새 대신 먹 냄새가 난다. 임금이 펴 보지 않는 상소들이 대신 이리로 온다.

blocks.html: She reads every one and sorts them into two baskets. The left is for things he would laugh at. The right is for things he would hate. The right basket is always fuller.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 한 장도 빼지 않고 읽고, 바구니 두 개에 나눈다. 왼쪽은 그가 웃어넘길 것들, 오른쪽은 그가 질색할 것들이다. 늘 오른쪽이 더 차 있다.

en: You’re reading Father’s mail again.
Somebody has to. Sit. You look like your father did at forty.
lines: 누군가는 읽어야지. 앉아. 네 아버지 마흔 때 얼굴이구나.

en: I am forty.
Then it suits you less than it suited him.
Yung is telling every bench you sold the river.
And the kitchens are saying something worse.
lines: 융 형님이 자리마다 다니며 어머님이 강을 팔았다고 해요.

en: The fox.
…You’ve heard.
I’m told I have nine tails. I’d settle for nine generals.
Here. Read this one. It came from Daeya.
lines: 꼬리가 아홉이라더라. 꼬리 말고 장수 아홉이면 좋겠다만.
자. 이거 읽어 봐. 대야성에서 온 거다.

en: Grandmother, do you have tails?
blocks.speaker: Hyo’s Little Girl

en: Eat your pear.
“The road to Sabi is cut in two places. We have grain until the first frost. Send—”
It stops there.
lines: “사비 가는 길이 두 군데서 끊겼사옵니다. 첫서리까지 먹을 곡식은 있사오니, 보내 주—”

en: They always stop there.
Does Father know?

blocks.html: She puts the letter in the right-hand basket.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 편지를 오른쪽 바구니에 넣는다.

blocks.html: Nine days one memorial has waited in the left basket. It asks for grain for the eastern forts.
blocks.ko: 아흐레째 한 상소가 왼쪽 광주리에서 기다리고 있다. 동부 성들에 군량을 달라는 것이다.

en: That one has waited nine days.
The gate day is bad. She says wait.
lines: 문 여는 날이 나쁘다. 그분이 기다리래.

en: Mother. Father says she is theatre.
Your father says a great many things from inside a wine jar. The basket stays where she put it.
lines: 네 아버님은 술독 안에서 큰 말씀을 많이 하시지. 광주리는 그분이 둔 자리에 둔다.

blocks.html: He hears about the baskets, and laughs the way he laughs at his own jokes — first, and loudest. Theatre with a calendar. A mudang with a filing system. It does not occur to him to ask whose days the court is keeping, until the court starts keeping them without asking him.
blocks.ko: 그는 광주리 얘기를 듣고 제가 짠 농담을 들을 때처럼 웃는다 — 먼저, 그리고 제일 크게. 달력 딸린 구경거리. 정리벽 있는 무당. 조정이 누구의 날을 지키는지 물을 생각은 못 한다. 조정이 그에게 묻지 않고 지키기 시작할 때까지는.

en: Mother. Do you do all this for Father, or for me?
lines: 어머님. 이 모든 걸 아버님 위해 하세요, 저 위해 하세요?

blocks.html: Somebody asked the king a question shaped like that once, on a mudbank. He is still answering it.
blocks.ko: 예전에 강가 갯벌에서 누군가 임금에게 꼭 그렇게 생긴 질문을 한 적이 있다. 임금은 아직도 거기에 답하는 중이다.

en: Eat something. You’ve gone grey at the mouth.

blocks.label: The Last Memorial
blocks.ko: 마지막 상소

blocks.label: The Monastery
blocks.ko: 산사

blocks.html: Across the city, at the monastery that belongs to neither of them, two old men have nothing to do but talk. They used to sit on the Rock. Now they hear about it.
blocks.ko: 도성 건너편, 어느 쪽 것도 아닌 그 산사에서, 할 일 없는 노인 둘이 이야기를 나눈다. 둘 다 정사암에 앉던 사람들이다. 이제는 전해 듣는다.

en: A queen behind a screen. In my grandfather’s day—
lines: 병풍 뒤에 왕후라니. 우리 조부 때 같았으면—

en: Your grandfather’s day had a king in the room.
lines: 그대 조부 때는 방 안에 임금이 있었소.

en: …It did.
Our two thousand came home at half strength. She paid for them with my own fees.
Next time a fort writes, the roads will be wet.
lines: 우리 군사 이천이 반토막으로 돌아왔소. 그 값을 내 뱃삯으로 치렀고.
다음번에 성에서 편지가 오면, 길이 질 거요.

en: And the fort?
A small one. Let the woman lose one, and the Rock will remember who sat behind the screen when it went.
lines: 작은 거 하나. 그 여자가 하나 잃게 두면, 그때 병풍 뒤에 누가 앉아 있었는지 정사암이 기억할 거요.

en: Which fort?
Does it matter? You couldn’t find it on a map.
lines: 그게 중요하오? 지도에서 찾지도 못할 텐데.

en: I could. I’ve just never had to walk there.
lines: 찾을 수야 있지. 걸어가 볼 일이 없었을 뿐이오.

blocks.title: Daeya’s road
blocks.caption: Two forts on Daeya’s road fall. Nobody in Sabi sends the men.
blocks.ko: 대야로 가는 길목의 성 둘이 떨어진다. 사비에선 아무도 군사를 보내지 않는다.

blocks.html: Nobody sends them. The Satek reply that the roads are wet. On the Rock, the princes argue about whose turn it is to be blamed. In the end the queen moves the capital guard without asking anyone. They are four days late, and now the court has two things to whisper.
blocks.ko: 아무도 보내지 않는다. 사택 쪽은 길이 질다고 답한다. 정사암에선 왕자들이 이번엔 누가 욕먹을 차례인지 다툰다. 결국 왕후가 누구에게도 묻지 않고 도성 수비군을 움직인다. 나흘 늦는다. 이제 조정이 수군거릴 거리가 둘이다.

blocks.html: Somewhere in the third year he stops going out to the hall, and some time after that they stop sending for him. The distance between those two things is the rest of the reign.
blocks.ko: 삼 년째 어느 무렵 그는 대전에 나가지 않게 되고, 그 얼마 뒤에는 부르러 오지도 않게 된다. 그 둘 사이의 거리가 남은 치세의 전부다.

blocks.html: Every season Chunbok asks the same question, in front of witnesses, the way a careful man pays a small tax. It buys him a name for loyalty. He already knows the answer.
blocks.ko: 철마다 춘복은 사람들 앞에서 같은 질문을 한다. 조심성 많은 사람이 작은 세금을 내듯이. 그걸로 충신이라는 이름을 산다. 답은 이미 알고 있다.

en: Your Majesty…

lines: 계백 장군을 데려오는 게 최선 아니겠습니까?
en: Would it not be best to bring back General Gyebek?

blocks.html: The letter is still in the king’s sleeve. It has gone soft at the folds.
blocks.ko: 편지는 아직 왕의 소매 속에 있다. 접힌 자리가 보드라워졌다.

en: That… who?
You there! Bring more wine!
Ahh~~ over here, Your Majesty~~
Your Majesty. The ministers are waiting outside.
…Let them wait.
Till when, Majesty?

blocks.html: He does not answer. After a while the question stops being asked, and after a while longer the ministers stop coming to the door. He notices none of it, and it is the first thing in his life he has not arranged on purpose.
blocks.ko: 그는 대답하지 않는다. 얼마 뒤 그 물음이 사라지고, 다시 얼마 뒤 재상들이 문 앞에 오지 않게 된다. 그는 그중 아무것도 알아채지 못한다. 평생 처음으로, 그가 일부러 꾸미지 않은 일이다.

blocks.html: Sunchung comes while the wine is still being poured. He does not wait for a gap. He is Yunchung’s elder brother, the councillor who used to read the tides for the king, and he still wears his office sword as if there were an office.
blocks.ko: 성충은 술이 아직 따라지는 중에 온다. 틈을 기다리지 않는다. 윤충의 형, 왕을 위해 물때를 읽던 좌평이다. 아직 관직이 있다는 듯 허리에 관직 칼을 차고 있다.

en: Your Majesty. Open court. Today.
We opened it.
With the cup.
There is a tide.
If you miss it—

blocks.html: He does not finish. The king is already on his feet.
blocks.ko: 끝내지 못한다. 왕은 이미 일어서 있다.

lines: 조회를 열라고? 하루 종일 떠들 수 있는 방을 하나 내줘라.
en: Take his belt.
He wants open court? Give him a room where he can talk all day.

blocks.html: The belt comes off in the aisle, and his rank goes with it. The guards walk him to a cell. After that, nobody else tries to speak.
blocks.ko: 허리띠가 복도에서 벗겨지고, 품계도 함께 벗겨진다. 군졸들이 그를 옥으로 끌고 간다. 그 뒤로는 아무도 입을 열려 하지 않는다.

blocks.html: Somebody does, that night. The queen walks into the banquet hall for the first time in a year. The music stops by itself.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤, 누군가 입을 연다. 왕후가 일 년 만에 처음 연회장에 들어선다. 풍악이 저절로 멎는다.

en: Let him out.
He told me I’d miss the tide. In front of the maids.
Then send him where the tide is. Gomamiji, next to Hungsu. Far, and alive.
lines: 그럼 조수 있는 데로 보내요. 고마미지, 흥수 옆으로. 멀리, 살려서.

en: You want him gone too.
lines: 당신도 그 사람 치우고 싶은 거구먼.

en: I want him alive and far. Those are two different things. You used to know that.
lines: 살려서 멀리 두자는 거예요. 그건 다른 얘기예요. 전엔 당신도 알았잖아요.

en: …Tomorrow. Remind me tomorrow.

blocks.html: She reminds him the next day, and the day after. By then he is asking which minister she means.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 이튿날도, 그다음 날도 말한다. 그때쯤 그는 어느 대신 얘기냐고 묻는다.

blocks.html: The kitchens tell it differently. In their version the queen walked in and asked for the belt.
blocks.ko: 부엌에선 다르게 전한다. 거기선 왕후가 걸어 들어와 허리띠를 벗기라고 했다.

blocks.label: The Cell
blocks.ko: 옥

blocks.html: Sunchung starves in a cell within earshot of the feast. His office sword hangs on the post outside. With the last of his ink he writes the king one page.
blocks.ko: 성충은 연회 소리가 들리는 옥에서 굶어 간다. 관직 칼은 바깥 기둥에 걸려 있다. 마지막 남은 먹으로, 왕에게 종이 한 장을 쓴다.

blocks.html: In the cell where he starved, Kangrim reads his name three times — Sunchung. Sunchung. Sunchung. — loud enough for the feast next door to hear, or not hear.
blocks.ko: 굶어 죽어 가던 칸 안에서, 강림은 그의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 성충. 성충. 성충. — 옆 연회가 들을지, 못 들을지 모를 만큼 크게.

en: Councillor Sunchung.
You chose the cell over silence. Was that loyalty to the king — or loyalty to being right?
lines: 침묵 대신 옥을 고르셨군요. 임금에 대한 충성이었습니까 — 아니면 옳음에 대한 충성이었습니까?

en: …Being right is the only loyalty left when a king stops listening.
The paper is for him. Not for you.
lines: 종이는 그이를 위한 것이오. 공이 아니오.

en: I will keep the minutes. Walk.

lines: 쌀 한 톨 없는 깜깜한 옥에서
임금님은 한 줄 읽고 술독 올려놓고
en: Sunchung, Sunchung, honest and plain,
told the king the truth again.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Locked in the dark with a brush and no rice,
he wrote, “Hold the pass,” and he wrote it twice.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
The king read one line and set the wine jar on,
and honest old Sunchung was gone.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
blocks.title: Sunchung the Honest

blocks.caption: Sunchung, councillor of Baekje. He chose the cell over silence.
blocks.ko: 백제의 좌평 성충. 침묵 대신 옥을 택했다.

blocks.hanja: 忠臣死不忘君，願一言而死。臣常觀時察變，必有兵革之事。凡用兵，必審擇其地，處上流以延敵，然後可以保全。若異國兵來，陸路不使過沈峴，水軍不使入伎伐浦之岸，擧其險隘以禦之，然後可也。
blocks.ko: 충신은 죽어도 임금을 잊지 않으니, 한마디 아뢰고 죽고자 합니다. 신이 늘 때를 보고 변화를 살폈는데, 반드시 전쟁이 있을 것입니다. 무릇 군사를 쓸 때는 반드시 그 땅을 잘 가려야 하니, 상류에 자리 잡고 적을 끌어들여야 보전할 수 있습니다. 만일 다른 나라 군사가 오거든, 육로로는 침현을 넘지 못하게 하고 수군은 기벌포 기슭에 들어오지 못하게 하여, 험하고 좁은 곳에 의지해 막아야 합니다.
blocks.html: A loyal servant does not forget his king even in death, so let me say one thing and die. I have always watched the times and studied their changes, and there will surely be war. Whoever uses soldiers must choose his ground with care: take the upper stream and draw the enemy to you, and you can keep the country whole. If foreign soldiers come, do not let them cross Chimhyun by land, and do not let their ships into the banks of Final Ford. Hold the narrow, difficult places, and stop them there.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 28, Baekje Annals — King Uija, yr. 16, dying memorial of Seongchung; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 384

blocks.html: The page reaches the banquet hall folded inside a guard’s glove. The king reads the first line. Then he sets it under a wine jar, and does not take it in.
blocks.ko: 그 종이는 군졸의 장갑 속에 접힌 채 연회장에 닿는다. 왕은 첫 줄을 읽는다. 그러고는 술 단지 밑에 깔아 두고, 마음에 들이지 않는다.

blocks.html: The page names two places. One of them is a pass. That same autumn, Silla sends men to look at it.
blocks.ko: 그 글엔 두 곳이 적혀 있다. 하나는 고개다. 바로 그해 가을, 신라가 그 고개를 보러 사람을 보낸다.

blocks.title: Charcoal Pass
blocks.caption: The pass in the page. Silla walks up to it, and nobody stops them.
blocks.ko: 그 글에 적힌 고개. 신라가 걸어 올라와도 막는 사람이 없다.

blocks.label: Charcoal Pass
blocks.ko: 탄현

en: Oi. Anybody up here?
blocks.speaker: A Silla Scout

en: Nobody. Not a fire. Not a dog.
lines: 아무도 없다. 불도 없고, 개 한 마리 없다.
blocks.speaker: Another Scout

en: Mark it, then. How wide?
blocks.speaker: A Silla Scout

en: Two carts. Three if they’re friendly.
Who builds a door this size and doesn’t lock it?
lines: 이만한 문을 내 놓고 안 잠그는 놈이 어딨노?
blocks.speaker: Another Scout

en: Baekje, apparently. Write it small. The general likes small writing.
lines: 백제지 뭐. 작게 적어라. 장군님은 글씨 작은 거 좋아하신다.
blocks.speaker: A Silla Scout

blocks.label: The Empty Rock
blocks.ko: 빈 바위

blocks.html: That night the queen goes to the Rock alone, with the same lamp. The Prime Minister’s chair is empty. It has been empty since spring.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 왕후는 같은 등잔을 들고 혼자 정사암에 간다. 상좌평 자리가 비어 있다. 봄부터 비어 있다.

en: Sit in it, Mother. They think you do anyway.
lines: 앉으세요, 어머님. 어차피 다들 어머님이 앉아 계신 줄 알아요.

en: That’s why I don’t.
Then who does?

blocks.html: She doesn’t answer. She holds the lamp over the chair for a while, the way you hold a light over a well to see if anything is down there. Then she blows it out.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 대답하지 않는다. 우물 속에 뭐가 있나 비춰 보듯, 한동안 등잔을 의자 위로 들고 있다. 그러고는 불을 끈다.

blocks.label: The Night Visit
blocks.ko: 밤 방문

blocks.html: The foxes came that week — into the hall, onto the Prime Minister’s desk. Ungo says tonight. Not tomorrow. The shaman keeps your hour, she says, the way she says Done. And for the first time in years Euija goes somewhere with no wine in him and no audience around him.
blocks.ko: 여우가 그주에 왔다 — 전각 안으로, 상좌평 책상 위로. 은고가 오늘 밤이란다. 내일이 아니다. 그분이 폐하의 시간을 비워 두었단다, 됐다고 말하듯 말한다. 그리고 의자는 여러 해 만에 처음으로 술기운 없이, 구경꾼 없이 어딘가를 간다.

en: …You.
…No audience. Don’t make one.
Sit. She said you would come after the foxes. The lamp has been waiting longer than you have.
lines: 앉으십시오. 여우 뒤에 오시리라 그분이 말씀하셨습니다. 등잔이 폐하보다 오래 기다렸습니다.

en: …I count. Nine hundred and seventy-two. Then I lose the place.
…Tell me what the number is.
lines: …나는 셈을 한다. 아홉백일흔둘. 그러고는 자리를 잃는다.

en: The number is a door you will not open. Send for the general whose name you will not say.
lines: 그 수는 폐하께서 열지 않으실 문입니다. 이름 부르지 않으시는 장군을 불러들이십시오.

en: …Amusement.
This was amusement.

blocks.html: He never sends for him. Chunbok will have to ask, months later, in front of witnesses, the way a careful man pays a small tax. The queen’s lamp is still burning when Euija gets back to his rooms. It was her hour. It was always her hour.
blocks.ko: 그는 끝내 부르지 않는다. 춘복이 달들 뒤에 증인들 앞에서 묻게 될 것이다, 조심스러운 사내가 적은 세금을 내듯. 의자가 처소에 돌아오니 왕후의 등잔이 아직 타고 있다. 그녀의 시간이었다. 언제나 그녀의 시간이었다.

blocks.hanja: 或曰 百濟自亡 由君大夫人妖女之無道 擅奪國柄 誅殺賢良 故召斯禍矣 可不愼歟 可不愼歟
blocks.ko: 혹자는 말한다. 백제는 스스로 망했다. 임금의 대부인, 요사한 여자가 무도하여 나라의 권세를 제멋대로 빼앗고 어질고 착한 이들을 죽였으니, 그래서 이 화를 불렀다. 삼가지 않을 수 있겠는가, 삼가지 않을 수 있겠는가.
blocks.html: Some say Baekje destroyed itself. The king’s great lady, a bewitching woman, was lawless: she seized the handle of the state and put the wise and good to death, and so called down this disaster. Can one fail to take care? Can one fail to take care?
blocks.source: Nihon Shoki (日本書紀) bk. 26, Saimei 6, 7th month, citing the Goguryeo monk Dohyeon’s Nihon Seki (日本世記)

blocks.html: A monk wrote that later, in another country. He never met her. Neither did most of the people who agreed with him.
blocks.ko: 훗날 다른 나라에서 한 승려가 쓴 글이다. 그는 그녀를 만난 적이 없다. 그 글에 고개를 끄덕인 사람들 대부분도 그랬다.

blocks.html: Foxes in the Assembly. Toads in the treetops. A river running red. Nine signs, and a king who swears he doesn’t believe in signs…!
blocks.ko: 정사암에 여우 떼. 나무 꼭대기에 두꺼비. 핏빛으로 흐르는 강. 징조가 아홉, 그리고 징조 따윈 믿지 않는다는 임금…!

logline.en: Every omen is real, in the sense that people saw it. That was always the only sense that mattered.
logline.ko: 징조는 모두 진짜다. 사람들이 보았다는 의미에서. 중요한 건 언제나 그 의미뿐이었다.

images.alt: A blood-marked hand — first of the nine omens over Sabi
images.prompt: Historical manhwa: bloody omen hand / Nine Plagues. Match Euija era. Refs: Euija. No text, --ar 3:2

images.alt: Lightning breaks over Sabi palace as the people cry that Baekje falls
images.prompt: Historical manhwa: lightning over Sabi palace — Baekje falls omen. Refs: Euija, Sabi. No text, --ar 3:2

images.alt: In a torchlit pit in the Sabi palace yard, diggers lift out a living turtle with faint carved marks on its shell where a ghost sank into the earth.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Ninth of the nine omens, 659. TOP-DOWN BIRD'S-EYE into a freshly dug square pit in the inner yard of Sabi palace at night (attached pl_sabi_palace board: stone paving and giwa eaves at the frame edges). ONE DEVICE: the square black pit as a hard frame-within-the-frame in the centre. At its bottom, two Baekje palace laborers in hemp hanbok with topknots, no brimmed hats, crouch with iron spades, recoiling, as one lifts a living turtle out of the dark soil; on its shell faint carved marks, illegible, not readable text. A thin trail of pale grey mist sinks into the earth at the pit's edge where the ghost went down. A pine torch jammed into the spoil heap is the practical key raking across the shell and the men's faces. Foreground: the blurred edge of a minister's dark sleeve at the rim. Crushed blacks, long torch shadows on the pit walls, gold #facc15 as the specular on the wet shell, NOT a glow aura. No text. No watermark. CANON — PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows.
