blocks.html: Foxes walk into the Assembly hall in a pack, and a white one sits down on the Prime Minister’s desk. A hen mates with a sparrow. A dead fish as long as a boat washes up on the river. Then a dead woman, longer than the fish.
blocks.ko: 여우 떼가 회의장에 들어오고, 흰 여우 한 마리가 상좌평의 책상에 올라앉는다. 암탉이 참새와 교미한다. 배만 한 죽은 물고기가 강가에 떠오른다. 그다음엔 죽은 여인이, 물고기보다 더 길게.

blocks.html: The palace trees weep at night. The White River turns red with blood. Toads gather in the tops of the trees by the ten thousand. Storm winds, rain, lightning, and black clouds fighting like dragons over the temples. Last, a ghost runs into the palace shouting, and burrows into the ground. They dig, and find a turtle.
blocks.ko: 밤이면 궁궐의 나무가 운다. 백강이 피처럼 붉게 물든다. 두꺼비 수만 마리가 나무 꼭대기에 모인다. 폭풍과 비와 번개, 그리고 절 위에서 용처럼 싸우는 검은 구름. 마지막으로, 귀신 하나가 소리치며 궁으로 뛰어들어 땅속으로 파고든다. 파 보니 거북 한 마리가 나온다.

blocks.html: They bring the turtle to the king in a lacquer box. He turns it over in his hands like a forgery he is pricing.
blocks.ko: 사람들이 거북을 옻칠한 상자에 담아 왕에게 가져온다. 그는 값을 매기는 위조품처럼 그것을 손안에서 뒤집어 본다.

lines: 내 궁 밑, 석 자 아래라.
en: Three feet down, under my own palace.
Who buried you, little one?
…Hm. Somebody with mighty good taste in shells.

blocks.title: A room in Surabol, some months earlier

lines: 의자는 스무 해 동안 백성한테 기적을 팔았소. / 용이니 흰 사슴이니 카는 것들.
en: For twenty years Euija has been selling his people miracles. / Dragons. White deer. That sort of thing.
Knowing they were false?

lines: 만든 사람이 본인 아이가. / 그러니 이제 그자는 세상에서 징조를 제일 못 읽는 사람이오. / 한평생 징조가 사람 손으로 만들어진다는 걸 알면서 살았으니까.
en: He made them himself, didn’t he. / Which makes him, I dare say, the worst reader of signs alive. / He has spent his whole life knowing that signs are made by hands.
…Right. Then why would it work on him?

lines: 그자한테 통할 필요가 없소. / 그자의 백성한테만 통하믄 되제.
en: It needn’t work on him. / It only has to work on his people.

blocks.html: He does not order any of it, exactly. He asks for men who can travel, he asks what the markets of Sabi are frightened of, and he asks how deep one has to bury a turtle shell for the finding of it to look like an accident.
blocks.ko: 그는 딱히 무엇을 명하지는 않는다. 다닐 만한 사람을 구하고, 사비의 저잣거리가 무엇을 무서워하는지 묻고, 거북 등껍질을 얼마나 깊이 묻어야 찾아낸 것이 우연처럼 보이는지를 묻는다.

lines: 나라를 무너뜨리는 데 군대는 마지막에나 필요하오. / 먼저 필요한 건 소문이고. / 소문은 백성이 이미 두려워하는 걸로 만들믄 되는 기라.
en: An army is the last thing you need to bring down a country. / First you need a rumour. / And you build a rumour out of what the people are already afraid of.
Baekje falls! Baekje falls!

blocks.label: The Shaman
blocks.ko: 무당

blocks.html: He keeps a shaman on retainer the way other kings keep song-girls. He likes watching someone else believe the sky talks; he has told Gyebek the gods are cheap civil servants, and told Gesomun the same with wine on his breath. The shaman thinks he is frightened. He lets her.
blocks.ko: 그는 다른 임금들이 가창꾼을 두듯 무당을 둔다. 하늘이 말한다고 믿는 사람을 보는 재미가 있다. 계백에게는 신을 값싼 관리라 했고, 개소문에게도 술 취해 같은 말을 했다. 무당은 그가 겁먹었다고 생각한다. 그는 그냥 둔다.

en: I came for amusement today.
There are nine. / Read them.

lines: 큰 여인의 주검 — 백성이 그 탓에 신음합니다.
en: The foxes — the politicians are corrupt.
The hen and the sparrow — public morals have declined.
The great fish — the economy is in decline.
The great woman’s corpse — the people suffer for it.

lines: 나무 위의 두꺼비 — 거짓 장사치들만 목청이 큽니다.
용의 구름 — 나라가 저희끼리 싸우기 시작합니다.
en: The ghost-screams — the forgotten common man cries out.
The blood-red river — the public sphere is polluted.
The toads in the trees — only lying peddlers have loud voices.
The dragon-clouds — the nation begins fighting itself.
…The turtle. / From the shell.

blocks.hanja: 得一龜 背有文曰 百濟同月輪 新羅如月新
blocks.ko: 거북 하나를 얻으니, 등에 글이 있어 이르되, 백제는 보름달과 같고, 신라는 초승달과 같다.
blocks.html: They obtained a tortoise; on its back was writing that said: Baekje is like the full moon; Silla is like the new moon.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 28, Baekje Annals — King Uija, yr. 20 (660); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 1, p. 386

lines: 보름달 같다는 것은 가득 찬 것이니, 가득 차면 기울며 —
초승달 같다는 것은 가득 차지 못한 것이니, 가득 차지 못하면 점점 차게 됩니다.
en: To be like a full moon is to be full — and what is full must wane —
to be like a crescent is to be not yet full — and what is not yet full grows fuller.
Baekje wanes. Silla fills.
You wretch!!!

blocks.html: The blade is out before the last word cools. He cuts her down where she sits. The turtle’s sentence stays in the room.
blocks.ko: 마지막 말이 식기 전에 칼이 나온다. 그는 그가 앉은 자리에서 벤다. 거북의 말은 방에 남는다.

blocks.html: People start saying it out loud in the markets, which is how you know it is already over.
blocks.ko: 저잣거리에서 사람들이 그 말을 소리 내어 하기 시작한다. 그쯤 되면 이미 끝난 것이다.

lines: 폐하. 지금 필요하신 건 술이 아닙니다.
en: Your Majesty. What you need right now is not wine.
Your Majesty…
Say one name.
I will go and bring him.
…That name was one I made up.
When I was a prince on a mudbank.
…Your Majesty.
What are they saying in the markets these days.
…That Baekje is the full moon.
…Yes.
Mighty well made.

blocks.html: He never says that the signs were made. He could name the price of every piece of it. To say a man made this one is to say it about the dragon over the Sabi, and the white deer, and the twenty years in between.
blocks.ko: 그는 그 징조들이 만들어졌다는 말을 하지 않는다. 한 조각 한 조각의 값까지 댈 수 있으면서도. 이것은 사람이 만든 것이다라고 말하는 순간, 사비강의 용에 대해서도, 흰 사슴에 대해서도, 그 사이 스무 해에 대해서도 그렇게 말하는 것이 되기 때문이다.

blocks.html: The best lie a man ever tells is the one he cannot afford to expose.
blocks.ko: 사람이 하는 가장 훌륭한 거짓말은, 스스로 들출 수 없게 된 거짓말이다.

blocks.label: The White River
blocks.ko: 백마강

blocks.html: That night he leaves the palace the way he left it as a boy — without asking, without banners. The White River is waiting where it always waited. The omen said it ran red. Under the moon it is only black water and the smell of wet stone.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 소년 때처럼 궁을 나선다 — 묻지 않고, 깃발 없이. 백강은 늘 기다리던 자리에 있다. 징조는 붉다 했고, 달 아래에서는 검은 물과 젖은 돌 냄새뿐이다.

blocks.html: He has spent years drowning on dry land: wine, women, and a letter he never sent to the man he never sent for. The river does not care. It knew him before the crown.
blocks.ko: 그는 여러 해를 마른 땅에서 익사하며 보냈다. 술, 여자, 그리고 끝내 부르지 않은 사람에게 끝내 보내지 않은 편지. 강은 상관하지 않는다. 강은 왕관 이전의 그를 알았다.

en: I named you here.
I will not die drunk on the bank of my own invention.
lines: 내 발명품 강둑에서 취해 죽지는 않겠다.

blocks.html: He jumps. The cold takes the wine off him. When he surfaces he is coughing, furious, awake — the promising prince the eight clans once feared, scraped clean by the same river that taught him friendship.
blocks.ko: 뛰어든다. 추위가 술을 벗겨 낸다. 물 밖으로 나올 때 그는 기침하고, 분노하고, 깨어 있다 — 대성팔족이 한때 두려워하던 촉망받는 왕자, 우정을 가르친 바로 그 강에 긁혀 깨끗해진.

en: Summon Gyebek…!

blocks.html: Chunbok has followed him down with a lamp, the way a careful man follows a king who might be about to do something historic. He holds out a dry robe. The king does not take it.
blocks.ko: 춘복이 등불을 들고 뒤따라 내려와 있다. 역사에 남을 짓을 할지도 모르는 임금을 조심성 많은 사람이 따라다니듯이. 그가 마른 옷을 내민다. 왕은 받지 않는다.

lines: 폐하께서도 잘 아시다시피, 탐라까지 배는 시간이 걸립니다.
그리고 저잣거리에서는… 송구합니다. 저잣거리에서는 그가 돌아올 백제가 남아 있겠느냐고들 합니다.
en: Majesty, you’ll catch your death—
As Your Majesty well knows, a boat to Tamla takes time.
And the markets… forgive me. The markets are asking whether there will be a Baekje for him to come home to.

lines: 우린 처음부터 작은아들네 집이었어, 춘복. 고구려가 대청을 가졌구, 우리는 남쪽 길을 가졌지.
빌린 길 위에서 칠백 년이여. 그래두 아직 여기 있잖여.
en: Let them ask.
We were a younger son’s house from the very start, Chunbok. Goguryeo got the hall. We got the road south.
Seven hundred years on a borrowed road, and we’re still here.
…For now, Majesty.

lines: 맨 처음 그분헌테두 딱 그렇게들 말혔지.
en: ‘For now.’ Ha.
That’s exactly what they told the first one, too.

blocks.html: Will Baekje survive? To answer that, go back to how it began: a mother, two sons, and a father who already had one…!
blocks.ko: 백제는 살아남을까? 그 답을 알려면 처음으로 돌아가야 한다. 어머니 하나, 아들 둘, 그리고 이미 아들이 있던 아버지…!

logline.en: Nobody in their father’s hall ever mentions Buyeo. Then a boy with a sling turns up.
logline.ko: 아버지의 궁에서는 누구도 부여 이야기를 꺼내지 않는다. 그러다 새총을 든 소년 하나가 나타난다.

images.prompt: 16:9 over-the-shoulder still from behind Biryu's drawn bow: sharp foreground of his shoulder, the bent bow and taut string, an arrow nocked. Midground on a narrow mountain ridge path, the pale white-gold stag Sinrok stands broadside, calm, looking straight back, antlers branching against a pale break in the clouds. Onjo's hand enters from the right, pressing down on Biryu's bow arm, his face urgent. Far peaks in blue wash bokeh. Low contre-jour sun catching the antlers as the key. CANON — BIRYU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_biryu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Elder brother, sea-hungry and proud; wants the coast at Michuhol and will not listen. #d8b276 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | ONJO — FACE and garments from attached /ch_onjo.png (face only; invent a new pose). Demeanor: Younger brother, steadier; listens to the ten ministers and stays inland at Wirye. The Sinrok deer stays with him. #f0c04a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | SINROK (신록, guardian deer of Baekje, guide of onjo and biryu) — attached board /obj_sinrok.png: Pale white-gold stag with tall branching antlers — match the board's animal, but ignore its glow outline: light catches the antlers and coat as real light. Owned by no one; leads the brothers south and stays with Onjo. HEEWON STYLE: a hand-painted ANIME film frame composed like a Romanticist master painting. FIGURES are anime: clean ink linework, simplified anime faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is watercolor and oil: skies, dust, ground and light are visibly hand-painted — wet-in-wet blooms, pigment granulation, soft bleeding edges, dry-brush dust, rich oil glazes in the darks, faint paper grain; edges of the frame dissolve into wash. LAYOUT is Romanticism (Delacroix, Géricault, Friedrich, Goya, Turner): heroic diagonal or pyramid composition, small figures against a sublime storm sky or vast field, extreme foreshortening (worm’s-eye from the dirt or straight down from above), one break in the clouds or one shaft as the key. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, night-interior cinema): an extreme value range — inky blacks right beside small near-white highlights, almost no middle grey; 70–80% of the frame in deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo and black); ONE hard directional key (a lamp, a single cloud-break, a low sun shaft, firelight) carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock: anamorphic movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain. A CAMERA in a real Korean place — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D archviz, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portrait — NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: dutch, crane, worm’s-eye, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key + long shadows — not even daylight wash. ICONIC MINIMAL: ONE architectural device a lens can see; empty negative space; tiny figures or lower-third; the world stays in the shot. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor portrait garments gold. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Not a katana, not a tsuba, not a short jian, not a ball pommel. Real Korean architecture: grey giwa, timber, packed earth. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: movie frame in a real place, not a graphic poster; iconic one-device layout, empty frame, lower-third; high contrast chiaroscuro, not even wash; 2D animated cel-painterly, no photoreal; cinematography: dutch, wide, bokeh, mise-en-scène. Never: halo / bloom / glow aura / emissive skin around figures; graphic split-screen or black-triangle overlay; photoreal live-action or 3D archviz; busy extras crowding an iconic frame; copy-pasted reference as a fashion plate; flat even-daylight postcard wide; katana / tsuba / random sabre length instead of sw_bidam 환두대도.

Neither has forgiven the other since. Seven hundred years later, the road ends at a riverbank in Sabi. Onjo’s heir is wringing the White River out of his sleeves. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Every child in Baekje can tell you this story. Most of them get the beginning wrong.
blocks.ko: 백제 아이라면 누구나 이 이야기를 할 줄 안다. 대부분은 첫머리를 틀리게 한다.

blocks.html: Onjo and Biryu grow up princes in their father’s hall. Nobody there ever mentions Buyeo.
blocks.ko: 온조와 비류는 아버지의 궁에서 왕자로 자란다. 거기서는 아무도 부여 얘기를 꺼내지 않는다.

blocks.label: The First Son
blocks.ko: 맏아들

blocks.label: Buyeo
blocks.ko: 부여

blocks.html: In Buyeo, Lady Ye has raised Jumong’s first son alone.
blocks.ko: 부여에서는 예씨부인이 주몽의 첫아들을 홀로 키워 왔다.

blocks.html: Yuri is a boy with a sling and bad aim, or good aim and bad luck. The pebble cracks a woman’s water jar on her way back from the well.
blocks.ko: 유리는 새총을 든 아이다. 겨냥이 나쁜 건지, 겨냥은 좋은데 운이 나쁜 건지. 돌멩이가 우물에서 돌아오던 여자의 물동이를 깬다.

blocks.caption: Yuri. Bad aim or bad luck, and a mother who will not answer one question.
blocks.ko: 유리. 조준이 나쁘거나 운이 나쁘거나. 그리고 질문 하나에 대답하지 않는 어머니.

lines: 어느 집 아새끼야, 대체? 애비 없이 커서 버릇두 없지비.
en: Whose lad are tha, any road? No father, no manners.
blocks.speaker: Water-carrier

lines: 우리 아버지는 어떤 사람입니까? 지금 어디 계심둥?
en: What manner of man was my father? Where is he now?

lines: 네 아버지는 보통 사람이 아니었다. 이 나라가 그를 담지 못했지비.
일곱 모 난 돌 위 소나무 밑에 뭔가를 두고 갔다.
en: Thy father was no ordinary man. The country couldn’t hold him.
He went south and made himself a king.
He left something under the pine on the seven-sided stone.
Find it, and he’ll know thee.

blocks.html: There is no pine on any hill he climbs. He finds it at home: the house’s pine pillar stands on a seven-sided foundation stone, and in the crack beneath it lies half a sword.
blocks.ko: 오르는 산마다 소나무는 없다. 그는 집에서 찾는다. 집의 소나무 기둥이 일곱 모 주춧돌 위에 서 있고, 그 밑 틈에 부러진 칼 반쪽이 있다.

en: Yuri….!

blocks.html: With his friends, three boys as stubborn as he is, he walks his father’s road backwards, south.
blocks.ko: 그만큼 고집 센 친구 셋과 함께, 그는 아버지의 길을 거꾸로, 남쪽으로 걷는다.

blocks.label: The Half Sword
blocks.ko: 부러진 칼

blocks.html: In the hall at Jolbon he lays the half-sword on the boards. Jumong goes to a chest nobody has opened since the river, takes out the other half, and kneels. The two halves click.
blocks.ko: 졸본 대청에서 유리가 칼 반쪽을 마루에 놓는다. 주몽이 강을 건넌 뒤로 아무도 열지 않은 궤짝에서 나머지 반쪽을 꺼내 무릎을 꿇는다. 두 쪽이 딸깍 맞물린다.

en: Father…!

blocks.html: Onjo and Biryu watch from the porch rail. The rail already knows what the hall will decide.
blocks.ko: 온조와 비류가 누대 난간에서 본다. 대청이 무엇을 정할지, 난간은 이미 안다.

blocks.label: The Last Night
blocks.ko: 마지막 밤

blocks.html: When Yuri is named crown prince, Sosuno does not fight the hall. She packs her dusty-rose silk. She packs the boys. She leaves the well.
blocks.ko: 유리가 태자로 책봉되자, 소서노는 대청과 싸우지 않는다. 빛바랜 장밋빛 비단을 싼다. 아이들을 챙긴다. 우물은 두고 간다.

blocks.html: Jumong finds her at the old well, two buckets that have outlived the argument. Twenty winters in the same yard. He is still grinning. She is still pretending she came for water.
blocks.ko: 주몽이 옛 우물에서 그녀를 찾는다. 싸움보다 오래 버틴 두레박 둘. 같은 마당에서 스무 겨울. 그는 아직 웃고 있다. 그녀는 아직 물 뜨러 온 척한다.

en: Hey.
You’re packed.
That’s… a lot of buckets for one road.
Not buckets.
Grain. Boys. Me.

lines: 소나무 밑에 쇠붙이 하나 두고 왔을 뿐인데. 그게 자라서 걸어 들어올 줄은—
en: I left iron under a pine. I didn’t think it would grow up and walk in—
Don’t— don’t make a speech. I’ll hit you.
Wasn’t going to.
Well’s still here.
I kept it. For you. Stupid, I know.
lines: 남겨 뒀어. 너 때문에. 바보인 거 알아.

en: Don’t be nice.
I’ll get stupid.
Yuri can have the chair. I’m not sitting in a footnote.
You know that. You always knew.
lines: 의자는 유리가 가져. 난 각주로 안 앉아.

en: Yeah.
South, then.
Take the glow. Leave me the well.
…Come here. Please. One night. I’m still thirsty.
Big idiot.
The boys are asleep.
If you compliment me I will scream.
…That’s not a no.

blocks.html: They do not make it to a feast. They make it to the grain room that has been theirs since the first night, and she kisses him before the door is shut.
blocks.ko: 잔치까지는 못 간다. 첫날 밤부터 둘의 것이던 곡식방까지 가서, 문이 닫히기도 전에 그녀가 입을 맞춘다.

blocks.html: Older. Hungrier. The hide has been off for years and she is worse now, not better.
blocks.ko: 나이가 들었고, 더 고프다. 껍질은 몇 해 전에 벗었고, 지금은 나아지기는커녕 더 심하다.

en: Still you.
Still that mouth.
Look at you. Older. Better. Sorry. Not sorry.
lines: 봐라. 나이 먹고. 더 좋아졌어. 미안. 안 미안해.

en: Don’t— ha— don’t you dare be sweet now.
Twenty winters, and you still breathe like you ran here.
…Slower. No. Not slower.
I want to remember this one. I’m not getting another.
lines: 하지 마— 하— 지금 다정하게 굴기만 해 봐.
스무 해 겨울을 지나고도 꼭 뛰어온 사람처럼 숨을 쉬네.
이번 건 기억할 거야. 다음은 없으니까.

en: Then don’t count.
I’ll count.
You know I’m bad at it.
lines: 나 세는 거 못하는 거 알잖아.

en: I hate you. I hate you, don’t stop—
…Say it. The thing you never say.
Say it now, while I can’t hit you.
lines: …말해. 너 한 번도 안 한 그 말.
지금 해. 내가 못 때릴 때.

blocks.html: He says it into her hair. Even the sky looks away for this part. She laughs, and then she doesn’t, and the lamp burns down to a coal.
blocks.ko: 그는 그녀의 머리칼에 대고 말한다. 이 대목에서는 하늘도 고개를 돌린다. 그녀는 웃다가, 이내 웃지 않고, 등잔은 숯불이 될 때까지 타들어 간다.

en: There.
Now you have to come back someday and hit me for it.
lines: 이제 언젠가 돌아와서 그걸로 날 때려야 해.

blocks.html: Before dawn the lamp is out, and neither of them has slept.
blocks.ko: 새벽이 오기 전에 등잔은 꺼져 있고, 둘 다 한숨도 자지 않았다.

en: Don’t be nice.
I’ll get stupid.
…I’m already stupid.
Keep the well. I’m taking the glow.
Take it.
You’re beautiful.
Go found the other one. I’ll be here. Grinning. Like an idiot.
lines: 가서 다른 거 세워. 난 여기 있을게. 웃으면서. 바보처럼.

blocks.label: The Yard at Dawn
blocks.ko: 새벽 마당

blocks.html: By sunrise the whole yard knows, because a yard always does. The five roofs come out in their good clothes to watch a family leave politely.
blocks.ko: 해가 뜰 무렵엔 마당이 다 안다. 마당이란 원래 그렇다. 다섯 지붕의 사람들이 좋은 옷을 차려입고 나와, 한 집안이 점잖게 떠나는 걸 구경한다.

blocks.html: Jumong sits in the hall door. Yuri stands beside him, new to standing beside anything. Onjo steps out in front of them with a speech he has practised all night.
blocks.ko: 주몽은 전각 문간에 앉아 있다. 유리가 그 곁에 선다. 누구 곁에 서 보는 게 처음이다. 온조가 밤새 연습한 연설을 들고 그 앞에 나선다.

lines: 어머니랑 형이랑 저요. 그리고 따라오고 싶은 사람은 누구든—
en: Father. Majesty. We’re going south.
Mam, Hyung and me. And whoever wants to—
…That’s it. That was the announcement. It was longer in my head.
I cut the bit about the sunrise.
No need to thank me.
…How long was the bit about the sunrise?

lines: 아바지 곡식, 아바지 수레만 가져간다. 네 건 하나도 안 가져가.
내 사람들 중에 걷고 싶은 사람은 걸으라우.
en: Long.
We take my father’s grain and my father’s carts. Nothing of yours.
Anyone of mine who wants to walk, walks.
Take something of mine.
…Anything. Not the well.

blocks.html: Then the yard finds out whose people are whose. Ogan stands first, because he has already counted the carts twice and hates to waste a count. Maryeo stands second and says something that makes the guards laugh, which is how he volunteers for everything.
blocks.ko: 그제야 마당은 누가 누구 사람인지 알게 된다. 오간이 먼저 일어선다. 수레를 이미 두 번 세어 놨는데 그 셈을 버리기 싫어서다. 마려가 두 번째로 일어서며 뭐라고 하자 경비병들이 웃는다. 그는 늘 그렇게 자원한다.

blocks.speaker: Ogan
en: Ten carts. Counted twice.
…Kicked the wheels too, Majesty. They’ll hold.

blocks.speaker: Maryeo
lines: 저 아래 가면 누군가는 말을 해야지요. 왕자님은 중간에 끊으시니까.
en: Somebody has to do the talking down there. The prince stops halfway.

blocks.html: Eight more stand. The records lose them, so here they are, once. Sa Dol carries a hoe like a spear. Yeon Ga can’t swim, and says so. Jin Hoe writes everything down; Mok Hyeop writes nothing. Hae Ru is the oldest and was born in Buyeo. Baek Sun sings. The youngest two, Guk Ji and Ahn Mo, stand up together because neither will go first. Don’t bother with the men. Remember the surnames.
blocks.ko: 여덟이 더 일어선다. 기록은 이들을 잃어버렸으니, 여기서 한 번만 부른다. 사돌은 괭이를 창처럼 든다. 연가는 헤엄을 못 치고, 그렇다고 말한다. 진회는 뭐든 적고, 목협은 아무것도 안 적는다. 해루는 제일 늙었고 부여 태생이다. 백순은 노래를 한다. 막내 둘, 국지와 안모는 서로 먼저 안 나서려다 같이 일어선다. 사람은 굳이 기억할 것 없다. 성을 기억하라.

blocks.html: Behind the ten come the old Jolbon people, the ones who remember when this yard was her father’s. Granny Boksil, who nursed her. Old Dalgu, her father’s storekeeper, with his tally-sticks in a bundle. A dozen households from the five roofs. They have put on their court clothes for it: jackets banded at the collar and cuffs in a second colour, wide trousers, and on the men who once held office, the little peaked cap with two feathers. They are dressed for a court that does not exist yet.
blocks.ko: 열 명 뒤로 옛 졸본 사람들이 따라온다. 이 마당이 그녀 아버지의 것이던 시절을 기억하는 이들이다. 그녀를 젖 먹여 키운 복실 할미. 셈 막대를 한 묶음 든, 아버지의 곳간지기 달구 영감. 다섯 지붕에서 나온 열두어 집. 다들 관복을 차려입었다. 깃과 소맷부리에 다른 색 단을 댄 저고리, 통 넓은 바지, 그리고 한때 벼슬을 했던 사내들 머리엔 새 깃 두 개 꽂은 작은 절풍. 아직 있지도 않은 조정에 나갈 차림이다.

blocks.speaker: Granny Boksil
lines: 아기씨. 아바지가 밥을 어드렇게 드셨는지 기억하는 사람 하나는 있어야디.
en: Agassi. You’ll want somebody who remembers how your father liked his rice.
Granny, it’s three months of road.

blocks.speaker: Granny Boksil
en: Then I’ll remember it slowly.

blocks.html: At the gate she does not look back. That lasts eleven steps.
blocks.ko: 문에서 그녀는 돌아보지 않는다. 열한 걸음 동안은.

en: …Don’t follow me.
Wasn’t going to.

blocks.html: He has followed her to the gate anyway. She turns, takes him by the collar of the red silk, and kisses him in front of the whole yard: the ten, the carts, the old people in their feathers, the new crown prince. It is not a goodbye kiss. It is the kind that makes a yard look at its feet. Her fist stays in his collar. His hand goes into her hair and finds the gold pin. Yuri studies the roof. Biryu coughs. Onjo does not know where to put his face.
blocks.ko: 그래 놓고 그는 문까지 따라와 있다. 그녀가 돌아서서 붉은 비단 깃을 움켜잡고, 마당 전체가 보는 앞에서 입을 맞춘다. 열 사람, 수레들, 깃털 꽂은 노인들, 새 태자까지. 작별 입맞춤이 아니다. 마당이 제 발끝을 내려다보게 만드는 그런 입맞춤이다. 그녀의 주먹은 그의 깃을 놓지 않는다. 그의 손은 그녀 머리칼 속으로 들어가 금비녀를 찾는다. 유리는 지붕을 살핀다. 비류는 헛기침을 한다. 온조는 얼굴을 어디 둬야 할지 모른다.

en: …Ha.
That’s the last one.
You said that last night.
I meant it last night too.
…Grin all you like. I’m not looking.

blocks.label: Four Rivers
blocks.ko: 네 강

blocks.label: The Road South
blocks.ko: 남쪽 길

blocks.html: At dawn ten carts roll out through the gate, and she looks back once, at the gate, where a man is still grinning like an idiot because she told him to. Onjo and Biryu take their mother south. She walks like a woman who has been thoroughly answered and will not explain it to a deer, a son, or a chronicle.
blocks.ko: 새벽, 수레 열 대가 문을 나선다. 그녀는 딱 한 번 돌아본다. 문 앞에 한 사내가, 시킨 대로 바보같이 웃고 서 있다. 온조와 비류가 어머니를 모시고 남쪽으로 간다. 그녀는 제대로 대답을 들은 여자처럼 걷고, 그 대답을 사슴에게도, 아들에게도, 연대기에게도 설명하지 않는다.

blocks.title: The Road South
blocks.caption: Three months, five rivers, and somebody else’s commandery in the way.
blocks.ko: 석 달, 강 다섯, 그리고 길을 막은 남의 군현.

blocks.label: The Amnok
blocks.ko: 압록강

blocks.html: The first river is the one Jumong crossed coming the other way. It is late spring, and the Amnok is high and green with snowmelt. There are no turtles.
blocks.ko: 첫 강은 주몽이 반대 방향으로 건넜던 그 강이다. 늦봄, 압록강은 눈 녹은 물로 높고 푸르다. 거북이는 없다.

lines: 어머니. 아버지가 그러는데 거북이들이 올라와서 다리를 놔 줬대.
en: Mam. Father said turtles came up and made him a bridge.
…Where are the turtles?

lines: 너희 아바지는 잔치 자리에서 별소리를 다 해.
en: Your father says a lot of things at feasts.
Build a raft.

blocks.html: They build rafts. Yeon Ga, who can’t swim, crosses flat on the grain sacks with his eyes shut. Halfway over, a cormorant lands on his chest. He doesn’t open them.
blocks.ko: 뗏목을 엮는다. 헤엄을 못 치는 연가는 곡식 자루 위에 납작 엎드려 눈을 꼭 감고 건넌다. 강 한가운데서 가마우지 한 마리가 그의 가슴에 내려앉는다. 그래도 눈을 안 뜬다.

blocks.label: Myohyang
blocks.ko: 묘향산

blocks.html: South of the river the land stands up. The Myohyang hills are fir and granite and fog. The cart paths are deer paths, and the deer paths are worse. On the ninth night something big walks past the fires and does not hurry.
blocks.ko: 강 남쪽에서 땅이 일어선다. 묘향의 산들은 전나무와 화강암과 안개다. 수레 길은 짐승 길이고, 짐승 길은 더 나쁘다. 아흐레째 밤, 커다란 무언가가 모닥불 곁을 지나간다. 서두르지도 않는다.

blocks.speaker: Ogan
en: Tiger.
…One. I counted.

blocks.speaker: Maryeo
en: Should I talk to it?

lines: 마려, 저 범한테 말 걸믄 안 묻어 준다.
en: Maryeo, you talk to that tiger, I’m not burying you.

blocks.html: Nobody talks to the tiger. In the morning its prints are in the frost round Granny Boksil’s bedroll, neat as a seal on a letter. She says it was only looking at her rice.
blocks.ko: 아무도 범에게 말을 걸지 않는다. 아침이 되자 복실 할미의 잠자리 둘레 서리 위에 발자국이 찍혀 있다. 편지에 찍은 도장처럼 반듯하다. 할미는 범이 자기 쌀을 구경했을 뿐이라고 한다.

blocks.label: The Taedong
blocks.ko: 대동강

blocks.html: The next river has a city on it, and the city has a Han flag. The commandery has sat on the Taedong for a hundred years, collecting grain and names. A column of northerners with ten carts and two princes is exactly the kind of thing it writes down.
blocks.ko: 다음 강에는 성이 있고, 성에는 한나라 깃발이 있다. 군현이 대동강에 앉은 지 백 년, 곡식과 이름을 거둬 왔다. 수레 열 대에 왕자 둘을 거느린 북쪽 행렬은 딱 그 성이 적어 두는 종류의 물건이다.

lines: 치믄 되디. 수레 열에 창 몇 자루믄—
en: We could take it. Ten carts, a few spears—
We could die in it, is what we could do.
Upstream. At night.

blocks.html: They cross upstream in the dark, wheels wrapped in rice straw, the oxen led by the nose. On the far bank Onjo looks back at the watchfires on the city wall and counts them, the way Ogan would. It is the first time he has looked at a wall and wondered how to build one.
blocks.ko: 그들은 어둠 속에 상류로 건넌다. 바퀴는 볏짚으로 싸고, 소는 코뚜레를 잡고 끈다. 건너편 기슭에서 온조는 성벽 위 횃불을 돌아보며 하나하나 센다. 오간이 그러듯이. 성벽을 보며 저걸 어떻게 쌓나 생각한 건 그게 처음이다.

blocks.label: The Imjin
blocks.ko: 임진강

blocks.html: Past the Myeorak hills the ground goes soft and red, and then the Imjin cuts across it in a trench of black stone: cliffs of basalt columns standing in rows like a palace nobody ordered. Cranes stand in the shallows below, red-capped and white, and watch the carts with the faces of officials.
blocks.ko: 멸악의 산들을 지나면 땅이 붉고 물러지다가, 임진강이 검은 돌 골짜기로 그 땅을 가른다. 아무도 짓지 않은 궁궐처럼 줄지어 선 현무암 기둥 절벽. 그 아래 여울에 머리 붉은 흰 학들이 서서, 벼슬아치 같은 얼굴로 수레를 구경한다.

lines: 형. 저기 봐. 저 절벽. 누가 깎았어?
en: Hyung. Look. Those cliffs. Who cut them?

lines: 깎긴 누가 깎아. 절벽이다. 자라는 거디.
en: Nobody cut them. Them’s cliffs. They grow.
…Cliffs don’t grow.
These did. Ask the cranes.

blocks.label: A Mahan Hall
blocks.ko: 마한의 집

blocks.html: South of the Imjin the villages change. Houses sit half in the ground under grass roofs, with the door in the roof. The men wear tattoos on their arms and beads instead of gold. On the third evening one village takes the column at spear-point and walks the princes into its headman’s hall, which is warm, and smoky, and has no mat for guests.
blocks.ko: 임진강 남쪽에서 마을이 달라진다. 집은 풀 지붕을 이고 땅에 반쯤 묻혀 있고, 문은 지붕에 나 있다. 사내들은 팔에 문신을 하고, 금 대신 구슬을 건다. 사흘째 저녁, 한 마을이 창끝으로 행렬을 붙잡아 왕자들을 우두머리의 집으로 데려간다. 따뜻하고, 연기 자욱하고, 손님에게 내줄 자리는 없는 집이다.

blocks.speaker: A Mahan headman
en: So who sent you.

lines: 당신네 사람들이 잡았잖아요. 우린 그냥… 길에 있었어요.
en: Nobody sent us.
Your men grabbed us. We were just— on the road.

blocks.speaker: A Mahan headman
en: I asked for a name.

blocks.html: Behind her sons, Sosuno makes a noise into her sleeve. It might be a cough. It is not a cough.
blocks.ko: 아들들 뒤에서 소서노가 소매에 대고 무슨 소리를 낸다. 기침일 수도 있다. 기침이 아니다.

en: …Onjo. Mam, what?

lines: 너희 아바지도 딱 이런 집에서 무릎 꿇고 똑같이 그랬어.
en: Nothing.
Your father knelt in a hall just like this and said it exactly like that.
Then he married the chief’s daughter.

blocks.html: The headman’s daughter, who has been standing at his shoulder with a lamp, looks at Onjo very hard and then at nothing at all. Onjo goes red to the ears. The headman, who has daughters and has seen this before, sighs and sends for a mat.
blocks.ko: 우두머리 어깨 뒤에서 등잔을 들고 서 있던 딸이 온조를 한참 뚫어지게 보다가, 아무것도 안 보는 척한다. 온조는 귀까지 빨개진다. 딸이 있고 이런 걸 전에도 본 우두머리는 한숨을 쉬고 자리를 깔라 이른다.

blocks.speaker: A Mahan headman
lines: 앉으시오, 그럼. 북쪽 사람들은 늘 이 길로 내려오지.
늘 아무도 안 보냈다 하고. 그리고 늘 눌러앉고.
en: Sit, then. Northerners always come down this road.
They always say nobody sent them. And they always stay.

blocks.label: The Han
blocks.ko: 한강

blocks.title: Halfway
blocks.caption: Where the Han comes down out of the mountains, something is waiting.
blocks.ko: 한강이 산에서 내려오는 곳, 무언가 기다리고 있다.

blocks.html: Halfway, where the Han comes down wide and brown out of the eastern mountains, on a ridge path too narrow for the cart, a stag is standing in the way. Pale as mulberry paper, gold wherever the light touches it, antlers branching like a winter tree somebody decided to keep. It does not run. It looks at the three of them as if it had been told to expect three.
blocks.ko: 길의 절반, 한강이 동쪽 산에서 넓고 누렇게 흘러 내려오는 곳, 수레가 지나기엔 너무 좁은 능선 길에 수사슴 한 마리가 길을 막고 서 있다. 닥종이처럼 희고, 빛이 닿는 곳마다 금빛이며, 뿔은 누군가 남겨 두기로 한 겨울나무처럼 갈라져 있다. 달아나지 않는다. 셋을 기다리라는 말을 들은 듯 세 사람을 바라본다.

lines: 열 신하 저녁거리다. 저 뿔만 해도 한 달은—
en: Don’t move.
That’s dinner for ten ministers, that. The antlers alone, a month of—
Hyung. Hyung, wait.
…That look like dinner to you? Really?
Looks like antlers to me. Meat with antlers.
Biryu. Lower it.
…Listen to your mam. Bow down.

blocks.html: Biryu lowers the bow the way an elder son does, slowly enough that everyone understands it was his own idea. The stag turns, walks ten paces up the ridge, and stops to look back. When they do not follow, it waits. When they do, it walks on. It keeps that up for three days.
blocks.ko: 비류는 맏아들답게 활을 내린다. 제 생각이었다는 걸 모두가 알아볼 만큼 천천히. 사슴은 돌아서서 능선을 열 걸음 오르더니 멈춰 서서 돌아본다. 따라가지 않으면 기다린다. 따라가면 다시 걷는다. 그렇게 사흘를 간다.

en: It wants us to follow, right?
…A deer knows the way, Mam?

lines: 너희 아바지는 거북이 등 밟고 강 건넜어.
en: Thy father crossed a river on turtles’ backs.
A deer’s practically civilised.

blocks.label: Two Brothers
blocks.ko: 두 형제

blocks.label: Mount Buak
blocks.ko: 부아악

blocks.html: On the third day it takes them up Mount Buak, and from the top the brothers see all of it: a river looped across the plain like a belt somebody has unbuckled, high peaks at their backs, wet green flats to the south and, somewhere past the haze, the sea. Biryu smells the salt before he sees it.
blocks.ko: 사흘째 사슴은 그들을 부아악 위로 데려가고, 꼭대기에서 형제는 그 모두를 본다. 누가 풀어 놓은 허리띠처럼 들판을 감아 도는 강, 등 뒤의 높은 봉우리들, 남쪽의 젖은 푸른 벌, 그리고 안개 너머 어딘가의 바다. 비류는 바다를 보기도 전에 소금 냄새부터 맡는다.

blocks.speaker: Ogan
lines: 동쪽은 성벽 삼을 높은 산. 남쪽은 기름진 들. 서쪽은 해자 삼을 바다.
하늘이 여기를 요새로 만들었는데, 아무도 못 알아봤다. 여기에 세우시오.
en: North, the river for a belt.
East, high mountains for a wall. South, fat fields. West, the sea for a moat.
Heaven made this place a fortress, and nobody else noticed. Build here.

lines: 바다 냄새 나디. 내레 저기로 간다.
강 끼고 산 등지고, 다 좋아. 기런데 배를 못 띄우잖아.
en: Smell that? Sea. I’m off there.
River in front, mountains behind, aye, lovely. Tha can’t float a ship on it.

lines: ……열 사람이 다 틀릴 수도 있긴 한데, 열 사람이 다—
en: Hyung, all ten of them say here.
…I mean, ten people can all be wrong, but all ten—

lines: 기럼 열 사람은 여기 살라 기래.
en: Then the ten can live here.
And Mam? Who’s Mam coming with?
…Don’t ask me that.

blocks.html: Nobody answers him. The stag, which has stood a little apart all morning, turns and walks off the summit to the west, toward the salt. Biryu laughs out loud and says even the deer agrees. So they follow it, all of them, down off Buak and across the wet flats, and it walks them all the way to Michuhol. At the edge of the sea it stops, because there is nowhere left to walk. It looks at the water a long time. Then it looks back at the river.
blocks.ko: 아무도 대답하지 않는다. 아침 내내 조금 떨어져 서 있던 사슴이 돌아서서 서쪽으로, 소금 냄새 쪽으로 꼭대기를 내려간다. 비류가 소리 내어 웃으며 사슴도 내 편이라 한다. 그래서 모두 따라간다. 부아악을 내려와 질척한 벌판을 건너, 사슴은 그들을 미추홀까지 데려간다. 바다 끝에서 멈춘다. 더 걸을 데가 없으니까. 한참 물을 바라본다. 그러고는 강 쪽을 돌아본다.

blocks.html: Biryu stays. The youngest two of the ten stay with him, because somebody has to make sure the elder prince eats. They promise to write. They don’t. Onjo turns the other eight back east, and in the morning the stag is already ahead of them on the riverbank. It lies down in the grass at Onjo’s feet, facing the river. Baekje will call it Sinrok, the guardian deer, for as long as Baekje has anything to call.
blocks.ko: 비류는 남는다. 열 중 막내 둘이 그와 함께 남는다. 큰 왕자가 밥은 챙겨 먹는지 누군가는 봐야 하니까. 편지 쓰겠다고 약속한다. 안 쓴다. 온조는 나머지 여덟을 데리고 동쪽으로 돌아선다. 아침이 되자 사슴은 벌써 강둑에서 그들을 앞서 있다. 강을 바라보며 온조의 발치 풀밭에 엎드린다. 백제는 그것을 신록, 나라를 지키는 사슴이라 부를 것이다. 백제가 무언가를 부를 수 있는 동안은.

blocks.html: Salt flats and sea wind. Biryu calls it a view.
blocks.ko: 갯벌과 바닷바람. 비류는 그걸 경치라 부른다.

lines: 열 부족의 땅이라… 십제라! 이봐, 더 크게 가자고. 백 부족의 땅… 백제! 그래, 그게 낫지….
en: The land of ten tribes… Sipje! Hey, c’mon… we can think bigger than that. The land of a HUNDRED tribes… Baekje! Now that’s more like it….
“Baekje” — how does that sound?

blocks.html: Biryu takes the sea. Onjo takes the river. Up north, their half-brother Yuri keeps the chair, and his line keeps it after him.
blocks.ko: 비류는 바다를 갖는다. 온조는 강을 갖는다. 북쪽에서는 이복형 유리가 자리를 지키고, 그 뒤로도 그의 핏줄이 지킨다.

blocks.html: The land south of the river already has an owner. Mahan holds it, fifty-four small countries under one high king the Han histories call Jin. Onjo sends Maryeo with iron and salt, and instructions to bow lower than feels necessary.
blocks.ko: 강 남쪽 땅에는 이미 주인이 있다. 마한이 쥐고 있다. 쉰네 개의 작은 나라들, 그 위에는 한나라 역사책이 진왕이라 부르는 높은 임금. 온조는 쇠와 소금을 들려 마려를 보낸다. 자존심 상할 만큼 절하고 오라는 당부와 함께.

blocks.speaker: A Mahan headman
lines: 또 북쪽 사람이로구만. 저번에는 네 아비가 왔지.
낮은 땅에 살아. 곡식은 바치고. 위로는 짓지 마.
en: More northerners. Last time it was thy father.
Take the low ground. Pay the grain. Nothing upward.

blocks.speaker: Maryeo
lines: 우리 왕자는 원래 낮게 사오. 겸손해서.
en: Low ground. Grain. Nothing upward.
My prince builds low anyway. He is modest.

blocks.html: On the way out of the high king’s hall, Maryeo is passed on the steps by a small bald foreigner being shown out much faster. He has a dried gourd tied at his waist, and the face of a man who has just been threatened with death and considers it a scheduling problem.
blocks.ko: 높은 임금의 전각을 나오는 계단에서, 마려는 자기보다 훨씬 빨리 쫓겨나는 작은 대머리 이방인과 엇갈린다. 허리에 마른 박을 매달았고, 방금 죽이겠다는 소리를 듣고도 그걸 일정 문제쯤으로 여기는 얼굴이다.

lines: 더 낮게 절하시오, 북쪽 양반. 나는 딱 알맞게 절했는데, 저 양반이 그걸로 내 목을 달라 하더이다.
en: Bow lower, northerner. I bowed to exactly the right height, and he wanted my head for it.

blocks.speaker: Maryeo
en: Who do you serve, uncle?

lines: 당신네 임금보다 예의가 바르오. 당신네 전부보다.
en: A boy on the east coast who came out of an egg.
He has better manners than yours. Than all of yours.

blocks.html: Maryeo laughs all the way back to the river. It will be a long time before Baekje meets that boy’s people properly.
blocks.ko: 마려는 강에 닿을 때까지 웃는다. 백제가 그 소년의 사람들을 제대로 만나려면 한참 걸릴 것이다.

blocks.html: The Mahan villages watch Wirye’s wall rise and decide these northerners know how to dig a ditch. They bring grain. They bring daughters. The glad following starts here, a hundred crossings before anyone counts them.
blocks.ko: 마한 마을들은 위례의 담이 오르는 걸 보고, 이 북쪽 사람들이 도랑 팔 줄은 안다고 판단한다. 곡식을 가져온다. 딸들을 데려온다. 기꺼운 따름이 여기서 시작된다. 아무도 세기 전, 백 번의 건너옴보다 먼저.

blocks.label: Michuhol
blocks.ko: 미추홀

blocks.html: Michuhol is damp earth and salt water. The wells come up brackish. The stored grain sweats. Biryu’s people cough through their first winter, and the youngest two of the ten write north letters they don’t send.
blocks.ko: 미추홀은 젖은 흙과 짠물이다. 우물은 짠물이 올라온다. 쌓아 둔 곡식은 땀을 흘린다. 비류의 백성은 첫겨울을 기침하며 난다. 열 중 막내 둘은 북으로 보낼 편지를 쓰고, 보내지 않는다.

blocks.html: In the second year Biryu walks back over the ridge to look at his brother’s town. The wall is finished. The market is loud. Nobody is coughing. He stands outside the gate for a long time, and does not go in.
blocks.ko: 이듬해 비류는 능선을 넘어 동생의 고을을 보러 온다. 담은 완성됐다. 장은 시끌벅적하다. 기침하는 사람이 없다. 그는 문밖에서 한참 서 있다. 들어가지 않는다.

en: The sea lied, little brother.
Don’t let them carve that on anything.
Hyung. The gate is open.
It has always been open.

blocks.html: They bury him facing the sea he wanted. His people walk north to Wirye with their carts, and the youngest two of the ten walk in front, crying and pretending it is the dust. Sipje grows by a hundred crossings at once.
blocks.ko: 그가 원하던 바다를 보게 묻는다. 그의 백성은 수레를 끌고 북쪽 위례로 간다. 열 중 막내 둘이 앞에서 걷는다. 울면서 먼지 탓을 한다. 십제는 단숨에 백 번의 건너옴만큼 는다.

blocks.html: People keep coming — Mahan villages, river folk, Biryu’s people — gladly, unforced. Ten crossings become a hundred. The joke Onjo made on the mountain finally fits, and Sipje, the land of ten, becomes Baekje, the land of a hundred crossings.
blocks.ko: 사람들은 계속 온다. 마한 마을, 강마을, 비류의 백성. 기꺼이, 억지 없이. 열 번의 건너옴이 백 번이 된다. 온조가 산에서 하던 농담이 마침내 들어맞는다. 열의 땅 십제는 백 번 건너옴의 땅, 백제가 된다.

blocks.html: So that is the family joke Euija and Gesomun used to throw at each other over wine. Goguryeo and Baekje are one father’s sons. One got the hall. One got the road. Neither has forgiven the other since.
blocks.ko: 의자와 개소문이 술자리에서 서로에게 던지던 집안 농담이 바로 이것이다. 고구려와 백제는 한 아버지의 아들들이다. 하나는 대청을 가졌고, 하나는 길을 가졌다. 그 뒤로 어느 쪽도 상대를 용서하지 않았다.

blocks.html: Seven hundred years later, the road ends at a riverbank in Sabi. Onjo’s heir is wringing the White River out of his sleeves. He once said a country is a territory governed by a single story. This was the story. He is about to learn who else can tell it.
blocks.ko: 칠백 년 뒤, 그 길은 사비의 강둑에서 끝난다. 온조의 후손이 소매에서 백강 물을 짜내고 있다. 그는 언젠가 나라란 하나의 이야기가 다스리는 땅이라고 말했다. 이것이 그 이야기였다. 이제 그는 그 이야기를 누가 또 할 줄 아는지 알게 될 참이다.

blocks.html: Back to Sabi. Two armies are on the road, the boat for Gyebek still hasn’t sailed, and the king wants to know why…!
blocks.ko: 다시 사비. 두 군대가 이미 길 위에 있고, 계백을 데리러 갈 배는 아직 떠나지 않았다. 왕은 그 까닭을 알고 싶다…!

logline.en: Two armies are coming for the capital, one by sea and one over the hills. The markets already have a name for it.
logline.ko: 두 군대가 도성으로 오고 있다. 하나는 바다로, 하나는 산을 넘어. 저잣거리는 벌써 이름을 붙였다.

images.alt: Sunchung, Hungsu, and Gyebek — the three loyalists of Baekje
images.at: Who is the Eraha of this country?!
images.prompt: Historical manhwa: Seongchung, Heungsu, Gyebek — three loyalists. No text, --ar 3:2

images.alt: The war reaches Sabi the way bad news always does: through the fish market first.
images.prompt: OPENING STILL of the episode: the first image the reader sees, staging its first line. The line: “The war reaches Sabi the way bad news always does: through the fish market first.” Context: The war reaches Sabi the way bad news always does: through the fish market first. Two armies are coming for the capital, one by sea and one over the hills. The fishwives already have a name for it: the Chunchu Army. The king hears it from a maid, who heard it from a fishwife.  A wide or medium establishing frame that hooks. CANON — PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: The war reaches Sabi the way bad news always does: through the fish market first.
blocks.ko: 전쟁은 나쁜 소식이 늘 그렇듯 사비에 닿는다. 어시장부터.

blocks.html: Two armies are coming for the capital, one by sea and one over the hills. The fishwives already have a name for it: the Chunchu Army. The king hears it from a maid, who heard it from a fishwife.
blocks.ko: 두 군대가 도성으로 오고 있다. 하나는 바다로, 하나는 산을 넘어. 생선 장수 아낙들은 벌써 이름을 붙였다. 춘추군. 왕은 그 말을 궁녀에게서 듣고, 궁녀는 생선 장수에게서 들었다.

blocks.title: The Sabi wharf · the autumn Daeya fell

blocks.html: Eighteen autumns back, two brothers stood on the Sabi wharf and watched a boat unload heads. The younger had taken Daeya. The elder had told the king not to try.
blocks.ko: 열여덟 해 전 가을, 두 형제가 사비 나루에 서서 배에서 머리들이 내려지는 것을 보았다. 아우는 대야를 떨어뜨렸다. 형은 임금에게 하지 말라고 했었다.

lines: 잘했다 한마디는 해 주시오, 형님. 다들 하는데.
en: You could say well done, hyung. Everybody else has.

lines: 저건 누구 거냐. 저 옻칠 상자.
en: Whose is that? The lacquer box.

lines: 성주 아내요. 춘추의 딸. 임금께서 이야기를 원하셨소.
en: The governor’s wife. Chunchu’s daughter. The king wanted a story.

lines: 그럼 잘했다, 아우야. 신라한테도 이야기를 하나 줬구나.
en: Then well done, little brother. You’ve given Silla one too.

blocks.html: Yunchung laughed. He thought a grudge was a thing you could settle with ten thousand men. His brother spent the rest of his life reading tides, waiting for this one to come in.
blocks.ko: 윤충은 웃었다. 원한은 만 명이면 정리되는 거라고 여겼다. 형은 남은 평생 물때를 읽으며 이 물이 들어오기를 기다렸다.

blocks.label: The Hall
blocks.ko: 전각

blocks.html: Euija holds court for the first time in three years. Half the benches are his sons. They watch him the way sons watch a father who has come home sober: politely, and counting the exits.
blocks.ko: 의자가 세 해 만에 처음으로 조회를 연다. 자리 절반이 그의 아들들이다. 아들들은 술 깨고 돌아온 아버지를 보듯 그를 본다. 공손하게, 그리고 문이 몇 개인지 세면서.

lines: 과인이 강둑에서, 흠뻑 젖은 채로, 보는 눈들 앞에서 내린 명이다.
en: The boat for Gyebek.
I gave that order on a riverbank, soaking wet, in front of witnesses.
Where is he?

lines: 폐하… 폐하께서도 잘 아시다시피, 겨울 뱃길은—
en: Your Majesty… as Your Majesty well knows, the winter crossings are—
And then the spring winds were—

lines: 춘복. 과인을 바보로 아느냐, 술주정뱅이로 아느냐?
en: The winds. A whole year of winds.
Chunbok. Do you take me for a fool, or for a drunk?

lines: 폐하, 온조묘에 걸고 아뢰오니, 계백 장군에게 딸려 보낼 군사가 너무 적습니다!
사택가가 잃은 것은 자리이지 사병이 아닙니다. 사택 공의 군사를 기다리시는 것이…
en: Majesty, by Onjo’s shrine, we have too few troops to send General Gyebek!
The Satek house lost its benches, not its levies. Better to wait for Lord Satek’s men…
Who is the Eraha of this country?!
Buyeo Euija?
Or Minister Satek?
Send him NOW!

blocks.html: Chunbok bows very low, which is what he does instead of answering. A boat leaves for Tamla that afternoon. It is the fastest in the harbour. It is a year late.
blocks.ko: 춘복은 아주 깊이 절한다. 대답 대신 하는 일이다. 그날 오후 탐라로 배 한 척이 떠난다. 포구에서 가장 빠른 배다. 한 해 늦었다.

blocks.label: The Letter
blocks.ko: 편지

blocks.html: That night the king does something he has not done in three years. He goes looking for a piece of paper.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 왕은 세 해 동안 하지 않던 일을 한다. 종이 한 장을 찾으러 간다.

blocks.html: It is where he left it in the banquet hall, under a wine jar, with a red ring where the jar stood. The maids watch him lift the jar. Nobody giggles.
blocks.ko: 종이는 그가 둔 자리, 연회장의 술 단지 밑에 있다. 단지가 놓였던 자리에 붉은 테가 져 있다. 궁녀들이 그가 단지를 드는 것을 지켜본다. 아무도 킥킥대지 않는다.

lines: 폐하… 그건 그 좌평 나리 거예유.
en: Majesty… that’s the councillor’s.
We didn’t throw it away.
We didn’t know if we were allowed to.
Read it to me.
My eyes are— just read it.

lines: ‘충신은 죽어도 임금을 잊지 않으니, 한 말씀 올리고 죽겠나이다. 때를 살피니 반드시 전쟁이 있을 것이옵니다—’
폐하, 그다음은 땅 고르는 얘기여유. 강 위쪽 높은 데서 맞으라구유.
‘육로로는 침현을 넘지 못하게 하고, 수군은 기벌포에 들이지 마소서. 험한 데를 지키소서.’
en: ‘A loyal servant does not forget his king even in death. Let me say one word, and die. I have watched the times. There will be war—’
Majesty, then it’s about picking ground. Take the high ground upriver, he says, and meet them there.
‘Do not let them cross Chimhyun by land. Do not let their ships into Final Ford. Hold the narrows.’
…Then just his name.

lines: 세 해 전에 고개와 강을 일러 주었다. 굶어 가면서. 저 벽 너머에서.
그런데 과인은 그 위에 술 단지를 올려놓았다.
en: Chimhyun. The soldiers call it Tanhyun.
He told me the pass and the river three years ago. Starving. Through that wall.
And I put a jar on him.

lines: 그 사람 실어 낸 뒤로, 세 해 동안 이 전각에서 아무도 과인에게 아무 말도 안 했다.
과인은 과인이 옳아서 그런 줄 알았지.
en: After they carried him out, nobody in this hall told me anything for three years.
I thought it was because I was right.
Majesty—

lines: 누가 또 이 말을 했어. 저 사람보다 먼저. 날 보고 웃으면서, 경을 읊으면서—
en: Somebody else said this. Before him. Smiling at me, quoting sutras—
…Hungsu.

blocks.label: The Back of the Hall
blocks.ko: 전각 뒤편

blocks.html: Next morning the provincial lords are summoned too, even the ones nobody has ever summoned.
blocks.ko: 이튿날 아침에는 지방의 성주들도 불려 온다. 한 번도 불린 적 없는 이들까지.

blocks.html: At the back of the hall, the lord of Bear Fortress says nothing. Ye Sikjin is doing the sum every provincial lord is doing. How many days from the river mouth to the capital? And how many from the capital to his own gate?
blocks.ko: 대전 뒤편에서 웅진성 성주는 한마디도 없다. 예식진은 방 안의 지방 성주들이 다 하는 셈을 하고 있다. 강어귀에서 도성까지 며칠인가. 그리고 도성에서 제 성문까지는 며칠인가.

lines: 예 공! 웅진성! 사 대 동안 한 번도 조정에 부르지 않았구나. 과인의 실수다.
en: Lord Ye! Bear Fortress! Four generations and I never once asked you to court. My mistake.
How many men can you give me?

lines: 웅진성은 꼭 필요한 만큼 하겠습니다, 폐하. 숫자는 길에 달렸습니다.
en: Your Majesty is generous to say so.
Bear Fortress will do exactly what is needed, Majesty. The number depends on the road.

lines: 숫자야 다 길에 달렸지. 하나만 대 봐라.
en: Every number depends on the road. Give me one.
…As many as the road allows, Majesty.

blocks.html: Euija laughs, because a king has to laugh at something before noon. Ye Sikjin bows exactly as low as the man beside him. That afternoon he rides home to Bear Fortress and opens a drawer.
blocks.ko: 의자는 웃는다. 임금은 낮이 되기 전에 뭐라도 웃어야 하니까. 예식진은 옆 사람과 꼭 같은 깊이로 절한다. 그날 오후 그는 웅진성으로 돌아가 서랍 하나를 연다.

blocks.html: One man might still know what to do. Euija sent him away too. Somebody ride. Now…!
blocks.ko: 어찌해야 할지 아는 사람이 하나 남았을지 모른다. 그도 의자가 내쫓았다. 누가 말을 달려라. 지금…!

logline.en: The king sends for the one man he sent away for being right.
logline.ko: 왕은 옳은 말을 했다는 죄로 내보낸 단 한 사람을 부른다.
