Sword hangs at the hip like sw_bidam.png: small RING at the heel of the fist, short grip, thin gold band, blade DOWN toward his feet along the rock — not at the camera. Handle:blade 1:3. ONE small circle — the pommel. No tsuba. Ignore the portrait katana. #2A5FB8 bounce. No text. No watermark.

images.alt: Hungsu has drawn the same map in the dirt every morning for three years. Today the king has finally sent someone to look at it.
images.prompt: OPENING STILL of the episode: the first image the reader sees, staging its first line. The line: “Hungsu has drawn the same map in the dirt every morning for three years. Today the king has finally sent someone to look at it.” Context: Hungsu has drawn the same map in the dirt every morning for three years. Today the king has finally sent someone to look at it.   A wide or medium establishing frame that hooks. CANON — PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. The line: “The histories do not mention him again.” Context: No second courier comes to Gomamiji. On the twelfth it rains, and he stands under the eave and watches the White River and Tanhyun run together into one brown puddle. He does not draw them again. He lifts the sword off the doorpost and starts north on foot, toward a pass that has already been crossed. The histories do not mention him again. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. blocks.html: Hungsu has drawn the same map in the dirt every morning for three years. Today the king has finally sent someone to look at it.
blocks.ko: 흥수는 세 해 동안 아침마다 흙바닥에 같은 지도를 그렸다. 오늘에야 왕이 그것을 보러 사람을 보냈다.

blocks.html: The county is a day’s ride from the sea and a month from anyone who matters. Hungsu arrives with one chest and his office sword, hangs the sword on the doorpost, and on the first morning, before the clerk has finished his bow, scratches a map into the packed earth of the yard with the end of a broom handle.
blocks.ko: 고을은 바다에서 하루 길이고, 중요한 사람들에게서는 한 달 길이다. 흥수는 궤짝 하나와 관직 칼 하나를 들고 와서, 칼을 문설주에 걸고, 첫날 아침 향리가 절을 다 마치기도 전에 빗자루 끝으로 마서국의 다져진 흙에 지도를 긋는다.

blocks.html: A coastline. One river mouth, the White River’s, drawn twice as wide as it is. One notch in the eastern hills for Tanhyun. Sabi as a thumbprint. Every morning the chickens and the children walk it out of shape, and every morning he sweeps it flat and draws it again, the same lines in the same order, like a monk at his morning sutra.
blocks.ko: 해안선 하나. 강어귀 하나, 백강의 것을 실제보다 두 배 넓게. 동쪽 산줄기에 홈 하나, 탄현. 사비는 엄지 지문 하나. 아침마다 닭과 아이들이 밟아 모양을 흐트러뜨리고, 아침마다 그는 바닥을 쓸어 평평하게 한 뒤 같은 선을 같은 순서로 다시 긋는다. 아침 독경을 하는 중처럼.

en: Mister, is that a snake?
A river.
What river?
One I hope you never see.
lines: 니가 평생 안 봤으믄 허는 강이여.

blocks.html: Nobody from Sabi writes. The news about Sunchung comes a season after the cell, on a salt boat, folded in between the price of salt and the price of rice, and the clerk reads it out because he reads everything out.
blocks.ko: 사비에서는 아무도 편지하지 않는다. 성충의 소식은 옥에서 한 철이 지나 소금배에 실려 온다. 소금값과 쌀값 사이에 접혀서. 향리는 무엇이든 소리 내어 읽는 사람이라 그것도 소리 내어 읽는다.

en: The councillor in Sabi. The one who— in the cell.
…Was he someone you knew, sir?
lines: 사비의 그 좌평 나리요. 옥에서 그—

en: …Better handwriting than mine, I reckon.

blocks.html: That morning he does not draw the map. The next morning he does, and adds nothing to it, which the clerk takes as grief and the children take as permission to walk on Tanhyun.
blocks.ko: 그날 아침 그는 지도를 긋지 않는다. 이튿날 아침에는 긋는다. 아무것도 보태지 않고. 향리는 그것을 슬픔으로 읽고, 아이들은 탄현을 밟아도 된다는 허락으로 읽는다.

blocks.html: In the last year the rumours come down the coast faster than the salt: foxes in the Ministers’ Assembly, a river gone red. Hungsu hears each one out and goes back to his broom.
blocks.ko: 마지막 해에는 소문이 소금보다 빨리 해안을 타고 내려온다. 대신 회의장에 여우 떼, 핏빛이 된 강. 흥수는 하나하나 끝까지 듣고는 다시 빗자루로 돌아간다.

blocks.label: The Courier
blocks.ko: 파발

blocks.html: The courier does not sit. Dust is still on him. The sword on the doorpost is the only bright thing in the yard.
blocks.ko: 파발은 앉지 않는다. 먼지를 그대로 뒤집어쓰고 있다. 문설주의 칼만이 마당에서 유일하게 반짝인다.

blocks.html: He has stopped in the middle of the yard, which is to say in the middle of the map.
blocks.ko: 그는 마당 한가운데 멈춰 서 있다. 말하자면 지도 한가운데.

en: His Majesty asks.
The matter is urgent. What then.
blocks.speaker: The Courier

en: …Sunchung already wrote it.
Same paper. I don’t have a second one.
…That is all?
His Majesty asked for a plan, sir. Not a—
lines: 폐하께서는 계책을 물으셨습니다. 그런 게 아니라—
blocks.speaker: The Courier

en: You’re standing on Tanhyun, friend.

blocks.html: The courier looks down and steps off a notch in the dirt, as if it might give way under him.
blocks.ko: 사자는 발밑을 내려다보고, 흙바닥의 홈에서 발을 뗀다. 꺼지기라도 할 것처럼.

lines: 성충이 안 쓴 거 하나만 더 전하슈. 서군은 많구 군율이 엄해유. 신라까지 붙었구. 들판에서 맞서믄 안 돼유.
날랜 놈들을 강어귀하구 고개에 두슈. 창 하나 든 사내 하나가 거기선 만 명을 막아유. 그러구 도성 문 닫구 기다리슈. 저것들 바다 건너 쌀 지고 왔슈. 그거 다 먹을 때까지.
en: Tell him one thing Sunchung didn’t write. The West are many and they keep good order, and Silla’s with them. Don’t meet them in the open.
Put your best men in the river mouth and the pass. One man with a spear can hold either against ten thousand. Then shut the gates and wait. They carried their rice across a sea. Let them eat it.
And Gyebek?
Has anybody sent for Gyebek?

blocks.speaker: The Courier
lines: 이번 주에 배가 갔습니다, 나리. 탐라로.
en: A boat went for him this week, sir. To Tamla.
This week.
Five years, and this week.

blocks.html: He looks down at the river mouth he has drawn too wide, and remembers the last time he saw the man they have finally sent for.
blocks.ko: 그는 너무 넓게 그린 강어귀를 내려다보며, 그들이 이제야 부른 사람을 마지막으로 본 날을 떠올린다.

blocks.html: It was a berth on Satek water, the afternoon the clans put Gyebek on a boat. Hungsu still had his office then. He came down to the water because nobody else from court did.
blocks.ko: 사택의 물가 나루였다. 가문들이 계백을 배에 태우던 날 오후. 흥수는 그때만 해도 아직 관직이 있었다. 조정에서 아무도 나오지 않았기에 그가 물가로 나왔다.

blocks.caption: A Baekje minister sent far from court for saying what the king didn’t want to hear.
blocks.ko: 왕이 듣기 싫어하는 말을 해서 조정에서 멀리 보내진 백제의 대신.

blocks.html: Gyebek’s wife came too, with their boy at her side and a small girl on her hip. She had packed his bag. He had unpacked it on the dock and packed it again, in order.
blocks.ko: 계백의 아내도 나왔다. 사내아이를 곁에 세우고, 어린 딸을 허리에 안고. 짐은 아내가 쌌다. 그는 나루에서 짐을 풀어 순서대로 다시 쌌다.

en: You… you truly mean to go?
Without a word to the king—

lines: 폐하께서는 상중이십니다. 서명을 하실 수 없습니다.
명에는 폐하의 인장이 있습니다. 저는 백제의 충신입니다.
en: The king is in mourning. He cannot sign.
The order has his seal. I am a loyal servant of Baekje.
His Majesty gave me a name.
A name — to a child who had none.
If he wants it back, he will send for it.

blocks.speaker: Gyebek’s Son
en: Father. How many days is Tamla, sir?
Four, with a good wind.

blocks.speaker: Gyebek’s Son
en: Then I’ll count to four.

lines: 다섯까지 세라. 바람이 늘 좋은 건 아니여.
en: Count to five, son. The wind is not always good.
…Do you know the story of the Guardian of Ansi?

lines: 아끼는 사람 하나, 섬기는 사람 하나.
en: I do.
One person to cherish. One person to serve.

lines: 저는 그 둘이 같은 사람이라 문제입니다.
en: My trouble is that for me they are the same person.

blocks.html: His wife was standing close enough to hear it. She shifted the girl to her other hip and looked at the water. Hungsu has never forgotten that she did not look surprised.
blocks.ko: 아내는 그 말이 들릴 만큼 가까이 서 있었다. 딸을 다른 쪽 허리로 옮겨 안고 물을 바라보았다. 흥수는 그녀가 놀라는 기색이 없었던 것을 지금껏 잊지 못한다.

en: Then hear one thing that is not a story.
If they ever send for you, hold the White River mouth and the Tanhyun pass — or there will be no Sabi left to be loyal to.
The West do not need our clans’ permission to land. They need our absence.
lines: 그러면 이야기가 아닌 것 하나만 들으시게.
언젠가 자네를 부르거든, 백강 하구와 탄현을 지키게 — 그렇지 않으면 충성할 사비가 남지 않네.
당은 상륙에 우리 가문의 허가가 필요 없네. 우리의 빈자리가 필요할 뿐이지.

en: I know the roads, sir.
Yellow Mountain first — if that door holds, the river still has a kingdom behind it.
If it does not… then the berths you all fought over will belong to whoever can spell our names.
lines: 황산이 먼저요 — 그 문이 버티면, 강 뒤에 아직 나라가 있소.
못 버티면… 당신들이 싸우던 선석은, 우리 이름을 받아 적을 줄 아는 자의 것이 되오.

blocks.html: Then the captain with the Yunbi contract called the tide. Gyebek stepped aboard and did not look back, because looking back was not on the list. The boy counted out loud until the sail was gone. He got to four hundred and something before his mother made him stop.
blocks.ko: 그때 윤비 가문 계약서를 품은 선장이 물때를 불렀다. 계백은 배에 올랐고 돌아보지 않았다. 돌아보는 일은 목록에 없었기 때문이다. 아이는 돛이 사라질 때까지 소리 내어 셌다. 사백 몇까지 갔을 때 어머니가 그만 세라고 했다.

en: Tell His Majesty—
…No. He has the paper.

blocks.label: Sabi
blocks.ko: 사비

blocks.html: The answer comes back to Sabi. The ministers do not like the source.
blocks.ko: 대답이 사비로 돌아온다. 대신들은 출처가 마음에 들지 않는다.

lines: 폐하, 흥수는 유배 중인 사람입니다. 임금을 원망하고 있습니다.
임금을 원망하는 자는 나라를 사랑하지 않습니다. 폐하께서도 잘 아시다시피, 그의 말은 쓸 수 없습니다.
en: Majesty, Hungsu is a man in exile. He resents his lord.
A man who resents his lord has no love of country. As Your Majesty well knows, his words must not be used.

blocks.speaker: A Minister
lines: 서군은 강을 거슬러 한 줄로 오게 하여 배를 벌리지 못하게 하고, 신라군은 탄현을 오르게 하여 말 두 필이 나란히 서지 못하게 하십시오.
그때 치면 됩니다. 삼태기 속의 닭이요, 그물 속의 고기입니다.
en: Let them in, Majesty.
Let the West come up the river single file, with no room to spread their boats. Let Silla climb Tanhyun, a path too narrow for two horses abreast.
Then strike. Chickens in a basket. Fish in a net.

lines: …하. 좋구나. 과인이 예전에 생각해 내던 그런 수야.
en: Chickens in a basket.
…Ha. That’s good. That’s the kind of thing I used to think of.
Hungsu would say—

lines: 흥수는 성충이 한 말을 하는 것입니다, 폐하.
그리고 폐하께서는 성충의 말도 쓰지 않으셨습니다.
en: Hungsu says what Sunchung said, Majesty.
And Your Majesty did not take Sunchung’s advice either.

blocks.html: It is very quiet. To take the advice now, the king would have to admit what it cost the last man who gave it. Kings will pay almost anything not to admit that.
blocks.ko: 아주 조용하다. 이제 와서 그 말을 쓰려면, 왕은 앞서 그 말을 한 사람이 무엇을 치렀는지 인정해야 한다. 임금들은 그것만은 인정하지 않으려고 거의 무엇이든 치른다.

en: So it is.

blocks.html: The next courier is shorter. The Western keels are already in the mud of Final Ford. Yushin is already on the switchback. The White River and the Tanhyun pass are already theirs.
blocks.ko: 다음 파발은 더 짧다. 서국의 배가 이미 기벌포 진흙에 박혀 있다. 유신은 이미 고갯길을 오르고 있다. 백강도 탄현도 벌써 저들 손에 있다.

blocks.html: No second courier comes to Gomamiji. Hungsu sweeps the yard and draws the map for eleven more mornings, the river mouth still twice as wide as it is, because nobody has told him it is already full of the Western keels.
blocks.ko: 고마미지로는 두 번째 사자가 오지 않는다. 흥수는 열하루 아침을 더 마당을 쓸고 지도를 긋는다. 강어귀는 여전히 실제보다 두 배 넓다. 그 강어귀가 이미 서국의 용골로 가득하다고 말해 주는 사람이 없으니까.

blocks.html: On the twelfth it rains, and he stands under the eave and watches the White River and Tanhyun run together into one brown puddle. He does not draw them again. He lifts the sword off the doorpost and starts north on foot, toward a pass that has already been crossed.
blocks.ko: 열이틀째 아침에는 비가 온다. 그는 처마 밑에 서서 백강과 탄현이 한데 흘러 갈색 웅덩이 하나가 되는 것을 지켜본다. 다시 긋지 않는다. 문설주에서 칼을 내려 들고, 걸어서 북쪽으로 나선다. 이미 넘어간 고개를 향해.

blocks.html: The histories do not mention him again.
blocks.ko: 사서는 그를 다시 적지 않는다.

blocks.html: Across the sea, a boat is coming for the Turtle. He is on the shore before they finish tying it up…!
blocks.ko: 바다 건너, 거북이를 데리러 배가 온다. 밧줄을 다 매기도 전에 그는 이미 물가에 서 있다…!

logline.en: Somewhere in the fourth year he notices he has stopped counting the days. Then a boat comes.
logline.ko: 넷째 해 어디쯤에서 그는 날수 세기를 그만두었음을 알아차린다. 그리고 배가 온다.

images.alt: On Tamla's black rocks Gyebek kneels to Yuri Dora, who grips his shoulder, laughing and wet-eyed.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Dawn on a black basalt shore of Tamla, the orange island. Low wide two-shot. ONE device: the waterline, a hard horizontal of white surf against black volcanic rock; a small open boat waits at the right edge, oars shipped. Gyebek, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, in plain travel clothes, unarmed, on one knee on the wet black rock, bowing low with his fists pressed together, head down. Yuri Dora, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, orange robe and white sash, standing over him, one big hand gripping Gyebek's shoulder, laughing and wet-eyed at once. On the hill behind, tangerine trees and low black-stone thatched houses dissolve into sea mist. Key: a low dawn sun break over the sea, orange #ff9a3d specular on wet rock and silk; slate storm sky. Foreground: an out-of-focus mooring rope. CANON — GYEBEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gyebek.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean and hard, sun-dark skin; black hair in a high topknot with loose strands over the brow; heavy scowl, narrow dark eyes, clean-shaven. Dress: Ochre-gold jeogori and trousers, a crimson scarf knotted at the chest, crimson sash at the waist, forearms wrapped in dark cloth. Headwear: the jougwan (see HEADWEAR). Demeanor: Says little. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Somewhere in the fourth year he notices he has stopped counting the days. It frightens him for a week. Then it does not.
blocks.ko: 넷째 해 어디쯤에서, 그는 날수 세기를 그만두었음을 알아차린다. 한 주 동안 그것이 그를 겁먹게 한다. 그 뒤로는 아니다.

blocks.html: He stops correcting the people who call him Turtle, and carries water for the women who dive. He cannot write home. He never learned. Some evenings he counts to five on the beach, out loud, for a boy the island cannot see. For the first and last time in his life, he is in a place where being exactly what he is costs him nothing.
blocks.ko: 거북이라 부르는 사람들을 더는 바로잡지 않고, 물질하는 여자들의 물을 날라 준다. 집에 편지를 쓸 수 없다. 배운 적이 없다. 어떤 저녁이면 바닷가에서 소리 내어 다섯까지 센다. 섬사람들 눈에는 보이지 않는 아이를 위해. 평생 처음이자 마지막으로, 그는 있는 그대로의 자신이 아무 값도 치르지 않는 곳에 있다.

blocks.html: A boat comes for him in the fifth year. He is on the shore before they finish tying it up.
blocks.ko: 다섯째 해에 배가 온다. 배를 다 매기도 전에 그는 이미 물가에 서 있다.

blocks.speaker: The Boatman
lines: 폐하의 말씀입니다. 두 번이나 따라 외우게 하셨습니다.
en: General Gyebek?
His Majesty’s words. He made me say them back to him twice.
‘The river was cold. I went in. Come home.’
…That is three things.

blocks.speaker: The Boatman
en: Sir?

lines: 세 가지를 말씀하셨소. 셋 다 들었소.
en: He said three things. I heard all three.

lines: 거북아. 무사 경 급허냐. / 이디서 죽으민 펜안헐 건디.
en: Turtle. What’s the hurry on you? / Sure you could die comfortable here.
Nothing here is mine to keep.
Then what is yours.
…A promise.

blocks.html: He takes nothing off the island except the stories, which is the only export it has ever had.
blocks.ko: 그는 섬에서 아무것도 가져가지 않는다. 이야기만 빼고. 이 섬이 여태 내놓은 유일한 수출품이다.

lines: 거북아. 하나만 배왕 가라. / 이야기는 끝을 정해 두엉 시작허는 게 아니여.
en: Turtle. Learn one thing before you go. / A story is not begun with its ending already fixed.
…Mine is fixed.

blocks.html: Five years of listening, and that is the one lesson that does not take.
blocks.ko: 다섯 해를 들었고, 끝내 배지 않은 가르침은 그 하나다.

blocks.html: He says goodbye at the water. It takes longer than he planned.
blocks.ko: 그는 물가에서 작별한다. 생각보다 오래 걸린다.

lines: 계백! 이녁 같은 사내를 만나난 나 하영 지꺼졌저.
육지로 돌아가민, 우리 다시 볼 수 있을지 모르주.
en: Gyebek! It’s glad I was to know a man like yourself.
Once you’re back on the mainland, who knows will we meet again.
Promise me the one thing.
Do not forget people.

lines: 한 나라의 태자께서 제게 이름을 주시고, 마음에 드느냐고 물으셨습니다.
저는 글도 못 읽는 무식한 사람입니다.
en: …My lord. I was a child with no family and no name.
The crown prince of a kingdom gave me a name, and asked if I liked it.
I am an ignorant man who cannot even read.
But as a man, I will keep faith.

blocks.label: Sabi
blocks.ko: 사비

blocks.html: He lands at the White River mouth and rides to the palace without changing his clothes. The guards do not know his face any more. The king does.
blocks.ko: 그는 백강 어귀에 내려 옷도 갈아입지 않고 궁으로 달린다. 문지기들은 이제 그의 얼굴을 모른다. 왕은 안다.

blocks.html: Euija meets him in the yard, not the hall. He is thinner, and sober, and sobriety does not suit him yet. For a moment neither of them says anything, which for Euija is some kind of record.
blocks.ko: 의자는 대청이 아니라 마당에서 그를 맞는다. 더 말랐고, 술이 깨어 있으며, 맨정신은 아직 그에게 어울리지 않는다. 잠시 둘 다 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 의자에게는 일종의 기록이다.

lines: 거기서 너를 그렇게 부른다며? 뱃사공이 그러더라구.
하— 어울린다. 바위 밑에서 살다 온 꼴이구먼.
en: Turtle!
That’s what they call you down there, isn’t it? The boatman told me.
Ha— suits you mighty fine. You look like you’ve been living under a rock.
Five years.
Your Majesty sent for me after four.

lines: 보내지 않았다. 가문들이 셈을 하고 있었고, 조심성 많은 놈 하나가 한 달만 기다리라 했고, 과인은—
과인은 임금이여. 같은 말 두 번 안 혀.
en: …I wrote it the night of the Assembly.
I didn’t send it. The houses were counting, and a careful man said wait a month, and I—
I’m a king. I don’t explain myself twice.
You explained it once.

lines: 그럼 내 몫은 다 쓴 거구먼!
en: Then that’s my allowance spent!

blocks.html: He laughs first, the way he always does. Then he tells him the rest the way a king gives orders. The Western ships for the river mouth. Silla on the eastern road. Fifty thousand between them. He does not pretend that five thousand is enough.
blocks.ko: 그가 먼저 웃는다. 늘 그랬듯이. 그러고는 임금이 명을 내리듯 나머지를 말한다. 강어귀로 오는 서국의 배. 동쪽 길로 오는 신라. 둘을 합쳐 오만. 오천으로 충분하다는 시늉은 하지 않는다.

lines: 사택네 사병은 ‘오는 중’이랴. 한 해째 오는 중이지.
en: Five thousand. That’s the whole purse.
The Satek levies are ‘on the way’. They’ve been on the way for a year.
Where.
Wherever you judge.
You remember what I told you. The last time.

lines: ‘내가 언젠가 어리석은 명을 내릴 게다. 그때는 네가 판단해라.’
en: ‘One day I will give you a stupid order. Judge it yourself.’
‘You are still the king of your own life.’

lines: 이건 어리석은 명이 아니여. 그냥 나쁜 명이지.
너는 이걸 빚진 게 아니다. 이름은 선물이었어.
en: Word for word. Of course.
This isn’t a stupid order. It’s just a bad one.
You don’t owe me this. The name was a gift.
I gave my word.
…So did I. On the mud, with a knife in my belt. All of it, to the last inch.
And then I let them put you on an island.
lines: …과인도 했다. 그 뻘밭에서, 칼을 허리에 찬 채로. 끝의 끝까지라고.
그러고는 저놈들이 너를 섬에 보내게 뒀지.

en: Five thousand against fifty. Has anyone done it?
…No.
Then you kept it.

lines: …네가 언젠가 물었지. 이름이 좋으냐, 네가 좋으냐.
en: …You asked me once whether I liked the name, or you.
I never answered.
No.

lines: 이제 가라. 과인이 임금 같은 소리 하기 전에.
en: Both.
Now go, before I say something royal.

blocks.html: Gyebek bows and turns. He is at the gate when the king calls after him.
blocks.ko: 계백이 절하고 돌아선다. 문에 이르렀을 때 왕이 뒤에서 부른다.

lines: 웅진성으로 보내라. 예 공의 성벽이 두껍다.
en: Gyebek— your house. Your wife, the children.
Send them to Bear Fortress. Lord Ye’s walls are thick.

lines: 사비가 무너지면, 백제에 두꺼운 성벽은 없습니다.
en: If Sabi falls, no wall in Baekje is thick.
…Then judge it yourself. You always do.

blocks.html: It is the kindest thing he can think of to say. Gyebek, who takes every word exactly as it is given, takes it home.
blocks.ko: 그가 생각해 낼 수 있는 가장 다정한 말이다. 모든 말을 받은 그대로 받는 계백은, 그 말을 집으로 가져간다.

blocks.label: Home
blocks.ko: 집

blocks.html: Before he marches he goes home. His wife is in the yard. She has heard; the whole street has heard. She does not ask how many. She has been married to him long enough to know he will tell her the exact number.
blocks.ko: 출정하기 전에 그는 집에 들른다. 아내가 마당에 있다. 이미 들었다. 온 거리가 들었다. 몇이냐고 묻지 않는다. 그가 정확한 숫자를 말해 주리라는 걸 알 만큼 오래 그의 아내였다.

en: Five thousand. Against fifty.

blocks.speaker: Gyebek’s Wife
lines: 당신이 그만허라 할 때까지 안 멈출 거유.
en: …The boy has been counting since the boat was sighted.
He won’t stop till you tell him to.

blocks.speaker: Gyebek’s Son
en: Father! Nine thousand, four hundred and— and twelve!
You can stop.

blocks.speaker: Gyebek’s Son
en: Was it right, sir?
Yes.

blocks.html: His wife looks at him for a long time. Then she takes the children inside and leaves the door open, and he goes in after them.
blocks.ko: 아내는 오래 그를 바라본다. 그러고는 아이들을 데리고 안으로 들어가, 문을 열어 둔다. 그가 뒤따라 들어간다.

blocks.html: What he does there he does so that nothing of his can be used against him. The histories record it in one line.
blocks.ko: 그가 거기서 하는 일은, 그의 것 그 무엇도 적에게 쓰이지 않게 하려는 것이다. 사서는 그것을 한 줄로 적는다.

blocks.hanja: 恐吾妻孥 沒爲奴婢 與其生辱 不如死快 遂盡殺之
blocks.html: I fear my wife and children will be taken and made slaves. Better a quick death than a life of shame. And so he killed them all.
blocks.ko: 내 처자가 붙잡혀 노비가 될까 두렵다. 살아서 욕을 보느니 차라리 죽는 것이 낫다. 마침내 모두 죽였다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 47, Biographies, Gyebaek

blocks.html: He comes out before the light is properly up. The yard is swept. Nothing in it is his any more except a black horse at the post. Gomanari was a king’s gift, the night they passed him over. It is the one thing he owns that the West cannot sell in a slave market.
blocks.ko: 날이 채 밝기도 전에 그가 집에서 나온다. 마당은 쓸려 있다. 그 안에 이제 그의 것은 말뚝에 매인 검은 말 한 마리뿐이다. 고마나리. 승진에서 밀린 그날 밤, 임금이 준 선물이다. 당이 노예 시장에 내다 팔 수 없는, 그가 가진 단 하나다.

blocks.html: The groom, a boy from the next village who did not sleep in the house and is therefore alive, holds the bridle out at arm’s length and will not look at him.
blocks.ko: 마부는 옆 마을 아이다. 그 집에서 자지 않았고, 그래서 살아 있다. 아이는 팔을 한껏 뻗어 굴레를 내밀 뿐 그를 쳐다보지 못한다.

en: H-here, General.
…Gomanari too?
A horse can’t be made a slave.
A horse is just a horse.

blocks.html: He saddles it himself, counting the buckles under his breath, and when he is done he stands with his forehead against the black neck for exactly as long as it takes to count to ten. Then he mounts and does not look at the house.
blocks.ko: 그는 손수 안장을 얹는다. 버클을 입속으로 세면서. 다 얹고 나서는 검은 목덜미에 이마를 대고, 꼭 열을 셀 만큼만 서 있는다. 그러고는 말에 오르고, 집 쪽은 돌아보지 않는다.

blocks.label: The March
blocks.ko: 출정

blocks.html: Gyebek and his five thousand set out for the Yellow Mountain. It is the last latch on the road to Sabi. Merchants have cursed its summer dust for years.
blocks.ko: 계백과 그의 오천이 황산으로 떠난다. 사비로 가는 길의 마지막 빗장이다. 장사꾼들이 여름 먼지 때문에 몇 해째 욕하던 곳이다.

blocks.html: They are waiting at the crossroads outside the city: farmers’ sons, old border men, a few who stood on the mudbank the day a prince named a boy. Nobody cheers. Somebody holds out a spare spear. Gyebek takes it, and counts them row by row before he says a word.
blocks.ko: 그들은 성 밖 갈림길에서 기다리고 있다. 농부의 아들들, 늙은 국경 병사들, 그리고 왕자가 한 소년에게 이름을 지어 주던 날 갯벌에 서 있던 몇 사람. 아무도 환호하지 않는다. 누군가 여분의 창을 내민다. 계백은 그것을 받아 들고, 한마디 하기 전에 줄줄이 그들을 센다.

en: Long live Baekje….!

blocks.html: Somewhere, Kangrim closes his ledger on a swept yard. Then he goes up to a meeting with one question he shouldn’t ask…!
blocks.ko: 어딘가에서 강림이 쓸어 놓은 마당 위로 장부를 덮는다. 그러고는 물어선 안 될 질문 하나를 품고 회의에 올라간다…!

toneNote: The Three Realms gossip like any court — mythic-cosmic warmth.

logline.en: Once a year the gods meet in a pavilion on the clouds. This year the reaper comes late from a swept yard in Baekje, with a question about the dead.

blocks.html: Once a year the gods hold a meeting. Kangrim is late to this one, because of a yard in Baekje.
blocks.ko: 해마다 한 번 신들이 회의를 연다. 올해 강림은 늦는다. 백제의 어느 마당 때문이다.

blocks.html: The annual meeting is a small pavilion: four posts, a raised floor, clouds for a yard. Living, dead and western rows all fit if nobody stretches.
blocks.ko: 해마다 여는 그 회의 자리는 작은 정자다. 기둥 넷, 높인 마루, 마당 삼은 구름. 이승과 저승과 서천 자리가 모두 들어간다. 아무도 다리를 뻗지 않는다면.

blocks.html: Four posts, clouds for a yard, and very strict seating.
blocks.ko: 기둥 넷, 구름 마당, 그리고 아주 엄격한 자리 배치.

blocks.title: The Three Realms · 삼계
blocks.caption: Hannim above; Living, Dead, and Western Flower Field below. Heaven is not a fourth peer realm.
blocks.ko: 한님이 위에 있고, 이승·저승·서천꽃밭이 아래에 있다. 하늘나라는 네 번째 계가 아니다.

blocks.html: Before the principals sit — servants first. The Three Realms under the Big Man Upstairs still gossip like any court.
blocks.ko: 본존들이 앉기 전 — 시종들 먼저. 위에 계신 어른 아래 삼계도, 여느 조정처럼 수다를 떤다.

lines: 아, 강림이…. 늘 그렇게 젊어 보이는군, 응?
en: Ah, Kangrim…. Looking as young as ever, eh?
Shut it, sun. I’ve had a long morning.
H-hey, Samsin.

lines: 어머, 염라! 오랜만이네. 저승은 요즘 어때?
en: Oh, long time no see, Yumla! How's the Underworld these days?
Y-you know… full of dead people.

blocks.html: Then the midwife and the sun find the same rail. The rest of the pavilion develops a sudden, devout interest in clouds.
blocks.ko: 그러고 산파와 태양이 같은 난간을 찾는다. 정자의 나머지는 갑자기, 경건하게, 구름에 관심이 생긴다.

en: Hey, Haemosu.
Did you see Yumla’s face? Went straight purple.
And I barely hiked the skirt.

lines: 이 정자에서 우리보다 배고픈 애 있어? 하나라도.
en: Barely? I felt that from the chariot.
Anyone in this pavilion hungrier than us? Name one.

lines: 강림이는 공책만 보고. 염라는 내가 숨만 쉬어도 보라색.
남자든 뭐든 — 너랑은 이런 수다 가능해서 좋아.
en: Ibiga? He flirts with weather.
Kangrim stares at his notebook. Yumla goes purple if I breathe.
We’re the only ones actually hot in here.
Man or not — I like that I can gossip like this with you.
…Nothing for the ledger.
And that’s correct.

blocks.html: Then the principals duck the lintel — Hallakgungi alone, Big Star with his dark court, Little Star with sky and sun and birth.
blocks.ko: 그러고 본존들이 처마를 숙여 들어온다 — 할락궁이는 혼자, 대별왕은 어두운 조정과 함께, 소별왕은 하늘과 태양과 출산과 함께.

blocks.html: The pavilion was not built for three sovereignties. They sit anyway.
blocks.ko: 그 정자는 세 주권을 위해 지어진 것이 아니다. 그래도 앉는다.

lines: 야, 소별왕… 위에 계신 어른이 아들 하나 이승으로 내려보냈다며?
en: Hey Little Star… didn’t the Big Man Upstairs send his son down to the mortal domain a while back?
Whatever happened to him?

lines: 단군이 세운 나라를 다시 하나로 모으겠다는 소리가, 사람들 입에서 나오기 시작했어.
en: Speaking of which…
Big things are happening in the mortal realm.
The mortals are starting to speak of reunifying Dangun's kingdom.

lines: 꽃밭에선 부활이랑 멸망이 같은 이랑에 자라. 통일도 아마 비슷할걸.
en: Elder brother of the dead goes quiet again.
In my field, resurrection and ruin grow in the same rows. Reunification probably does too.

blocks.html: Kangrim has not sat down. This morning he collected a woman and two children from a swept yard in Baekje. The girl asked if her father was coming too. Kangrim does not lie, so he said, “Later.” He has been thinking about the flower field ever since.
blocks.ko: 강림은 아직 앉지 않았다. 오늘 아침 그는 백제의 쓸어 놓은 마당에서 여인 하나와 아이 둘을 거두었다. 계집아이가 아버지도 오느냐고 물었다. 강림은 거짓말을 하지 않는다. 그래서 “나중에.”라고 했다. 그 뒤로 내내 꽃밭 생각을 하고 있다.

en: Sir.
Yes?

lines: 늘 궁금했습니다… 나리 밭에는 어떤 꽃들이 핍니까?
en: I've always been curious… what sorts of flowers grow in your fields?

lines: 하하… 뭐, 새 피를 돋우는 꽃, 새 살을 키우는 꽃, 새 뼈를 기르는 꽃…
솔직히 이젠 다 기억도 안 나.
en: Haha… well, there are those that regenerate new blood, grow new skin, grow new bones…
To be honest, I can't even keep track of all of them anymore.
Why do you ask?

blocks.html: “Seeing the Western Flower Field — what flower is this?” “The flower that gives back speech. This one, the flower that brings blood back. The flower that brings flesh back, the one for the organs and bowels, the flower that brings bones back.”
blocks.ko: “서천꽃밭 구경 가서 보니, 이 꽃은 무슨 꽃입니까?” “말하게 할 꽃, 이 꽃은 피 오를 꽃, 살 오를 꽃, 오장육부 오를 꽃, 뼈 오를 꽃이로다.”
blocks.source: Segyeong Bonpuri (세경본풀이) recited by Lee Seung-sun (이승순), recorded by Gang Jeong-sik, Gang So-jeon and Song Jeong-hui, 2011 — Sanggari, Aewol-eup (Hanguk Gubimunhak Daegye, rev. ed.)
blocks.native: “서천꼿밧 구경간 요 꼿은 미신 꼿입네까?” “말 ᄀᆞᆯ을 꼿, 이 꼿은 피 오를 꼿, ᄉᆞᆯ 오를 꼿 오장육부 오를 꼿 뻬 오를 꼿이로다.”

lines: 그냥 궁금해서요… 그 꽃들을 한꺼번에 쓰면…
en: I was just curious… using all of these flowers at once…
Is it… is it possible to resurrect a dead person?

blocks.html: Hallakgungi’s face hardens.
blocks.ko: 할락궁이의 얼굴이 굳는다.

en: Grim Reaper Kangrim. What is this line of questioning?
Do you have something you need to tell me?
No, sir. I was—

lines: 내가 해 봤다… 단 한 사람뿐.
그러나 나는 인간 일에 끼어들지 않는다.
en: Well, to answer your question. It is possible.
I've done it… only for one person.
But I do not get involved in mortal affairs.
Only one.
…And who decides which one?

lines: 꽃밭 규칙이야, 저승차사. 사람 하나 위해 꽃을 꺾으면 그 줄이 통째로 시들어. 앉아.
en: I do. Cheerfully. And I already have.
Rule of the field, reaper: pick a flower for one mortal and the whole row wilts. Sit down.

blocks.html: Kangrim sits down at the end of the dead’s row. He opens his ledger to a page headed Yellow Mountain, and does not like how long it is.
blocks.ko: 강림은 저승 줄 맨 끝에 앉는다. 장부를 펼치니 황산벌이라 적힌 쪽이 나온다. 그 길이가 마음에 들지 않는다.

lines: 사람들이 서로 베는 것도… 내 작은 법이지.
그래도 — 단군을 다시 부르면, 위에 계신 어른이 웃을까, 한숨을 쉴까.
en: I cheated for the living world.
Them cutting each other… that is my small law too.
Still — when they call Dangun’s name again, does the Big Man Upstairs laugh, or sigh?

lines: 산 자들의 이야기는… 안건 맨 마지막이다.
en: Let the meeting begin.
Business of the living… last item on the agenda.

blocks.html: The minutes of that meeting never leave Heaven’s table. Down below, five thousand men are counting fifty thousand…!
blocks.ko: 그 회의록은 하늘의 탁자를 떠나지 않는다. 저 아래에서는 오천이 오만을 세고 있다…!

toneNote: A kingdom's last days told at full gravity — last stands, falling palaces, and the escort of the dead.
title: The Fall of Baekje
