Romanticist layout: the tomb on the thirds, half the frame sky, one cloud-break or lamp as the only key, long raking shadow across the grass.

images.alt: Gyebek can count to fifty thousand. He has done it twice since dawn. The answer has not improved.
images.prompt: OPENING STILL of the episode: the first image the reader sees, staging its first line. The line: “Gyebek can count to fifty thousand. He has done it twice since dawn. The answer has not improved.” Context: Gyebek can count to fifty thousand. He has done it twice since dawn. The answer has not improved.   A wide or medium establishing frame that hooks. CANON — PLACE Yellow Mountain (황산벌 (논산)) — attached board /pl_yellow_mountain.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Low rolling yellow-dust plain under a vast sky, Baekje stockade on a rise; few trees; dust is the weather. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Gyebek can count to fifty thousand. He has done it twice since dawn. The answer has not improved.
blocks.ko: 계백은 오만까지 셀 줄 안다. 동틀 녘부터 벌써 두 번 셌다. 답은 나아지지 않았다.

blocks.label: The Field
blocks.ko: 벌판

blocks.label: Yellow Mountain Fields
blocks.ko: 황산벌

blocks.html: Hundred-Victories gets to the Yellow Mountain Fields first and picks his ground. Then he waits, for the Sword of Silla or for arithmetic, whichever arrives with a banner.
blocks.ko: 백승이 황산벌에 먼저 닿아 자리를 고른다. 그리고 기다린다. 신라의 칼이든 셈이든, 깃발을 달고 먼저 오는 쪽을.

blocks.html: Good ground for whoever gets there first.
blocks.ko: 먼저 온 자에게 좋은 땅.

blocks.html: He sets three camps across the three ways in. There is no fourth way in; that is why he chose the place.
blocks.ko: 그는 들어오는 세 길목에 세 진영을 세운다. 네 번째 길은 없다. 그래서 그곳을 골랐다.

blocks.html: He walked the ground for two days before choosing it, in the same direction each time, and he can still tell you the number of paces between the centre camp and the stream.
blocks.ko: 그는 자리를 고르기 전 이틀 동안 그 땅을 걸었다. 매번 같은 방향으로 걸었다. 가운데 진영에서 개울까지 몇 걸음인지 그는 지금도 말할 수 있다.

en: Four hundred and twelve.
…Nobody asked. I know.

blocks.html: His adjutant is Sukdal, a ferryman’s son from the bear ferry. He has kept Gyebek’s tallies since the border and has never once been thanked for it. He does not expect to start today.
blocks.ko: 부관은 석달이다. 곰나루 뱃사공의 아들이다. 국경 시절부터 계백의 셈을 받아 적었고, 고맙다는 말은 한 번도 듣지 못했다. 오늘부터 들을 거라 기대하지도 않는다.

blocks.speaker: Sukdal
lines: 척후가 돌아왔슈, 장군. 탄현을 넘어오는디, 맨 앞에 유신의 깃발이구먼요.
en: Scouts are back, General. Over the Tanhyun pass. Yushin’s banner in front.
How many.

blocks.speaker: Sukdal
en: Fifty thousand, my lord.
And ours.

blocks.speaker: Sukdal
en: …You know ours, General.

lines: 말허슈. 한 번은 소리루 듣구 싶소.
en: Say it. I want it said once.

blocks.speaker: Sukdal
en: Five thousand.
Five thousand against fifty thousand….

blocks.hanja: 以一國之人 當唐羅之大兵 國之存亡 未可知也…
blocks.ko: 한 나라의 사람으로 당과 신라의 대병을 당하니, 나라의 존망을 알 수 없다…
blocks.html: With the men of one country I face the great armies of Tang and Silla, and whether the country lives or dies cannot be known…
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 47, Biographies — Gyebek; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2, p. 452

blocks.speaker: Sukdal
lines: 그리구 바다입니다, 장군. 강어귀에 돛이 그득허구, 뱃사람들이 세다가 그만뒀대유.
en: And the sea, General. A mighty lot of sails at the river mouth. The boatmen gave up counting them.
Then I will count them later.

blocks.html: Here is the man the boatmen gave up on. His name is Su Dingfang, and he is sixty-five. Three winters ago he took a qaghan’s camp in a blizzard, before anyone in it had found his boots. His regiment painted a red bird on his tent afterwards, and Chang’an calls him the Red Fowl.
blocks.ko: 뱃사람들이 세다 만 그 사내다. 이름은 소정방, 나이는 예순다섯. 세 해 전 겨울, 그는 눈보라 속에서 가한의 진영을 통째로 먹었다. 그 진영 안의 누구도 장화를 찾기 전이었다. 그 뒤로 부하들이 그의 군막에 붉은 새를 그려 넣었고, 장안은 그를 주작이라 부른다.

blocks.caption: The Red Fowl. Sixty-five, and he still prefers to march at night.
blocks.ko: 주작. 예순다섯, 아직도 밤에 진군하는 걸 좋아한다.

lines: 그 속에선 아무도 너를 기다리지 않는다. 눈이 좋은 건 그거 하나다.
en: Snow is just cold sand.
Nobody expects you in it. That’s the only good thing about it.
zh: 沒人料到你會在雪裡來。雪就這點好。
zhLatn: Xuě búguò shì lěng shā.
Méi rén liàodào nǐ huì zài xuě lǐ lái. Xuě jiù zhè diǎn hǎo.

blocks.label: Dukmul Island
blocks.ko: 덕물도

blocks.html: That summer he sails east with a hundred and thirty thousand men and anchors off a small island. A hundred Silla ships come out to meet him. At their head is the crown prince, Bupmin. He is thirty-four, and trying not to stare at the size of the Western flagship.
blocks.ko: 그해 여름, 그는 십삼만 군사를 싣고 동쪽으로 건너와 작은 섬 앞에 닻을 내린다. 신라 배 백 척이 그를 맞으러 나온다. 맨 앞에 태자 법민이 있다. 서른넷이고, 서국 기함이 얼마나 큰지 빤히 쳐다보지 않으려 애쓰는 중이다.

blocks.caption: An empire crosses the sea. A prince rows out to meet it and tries not to stare.
blocks.ko: 제국이 바다를 건넌다. 왕자는 노를 저어 마중 나가며 빤히 쳐다보지 않으려 애쓴다.

en: You’re the son?
zhLatn: Nǐ shì érzi?

en: Kim Bupmin, General. My father the king sends his—

lines: 칠월 열흘. 사비 남쪽. 너희 군대와 내 군대가 같은 들판에, 같은 아침에.
en: Tenth day of the seventh month. South of Sabi. Your army and mine, on the same field, on the same morning.
Tell your father. Tell him twice.
zh: 七月十日，泗沘之南。你軍我軍，同一片地，同一個早晨。
zhLatn: Qīyuè shí rì, Sìbì zhī nán. Nǐ jūn wǒ jūn, tóng yí piàn dì, tóng yí ge zǎochén.
Gàosu nǐ fùqīn. Shuō liǎng biàn.

en: We will be there, General.

blocks.html: Bupmin is rowed back to his own ship. Behind him the Red Fowl says something to his staff that makes them laugh.
blocks.ko: 법민은 노를 저어 제 배로 돌아간다. 그 뒤에서 주작이 참모들에게 뭐라 하자 그들이 웃는다.

lines: 늦을 거다. 작은 나라는 늘 늦어. 물어볼 삼촌이 너무 많거든.
en: They’ll be late. Small countries always are. They have to ask too many uncles.
zh: 他們會遲到。小國總是遲。要問的叔伯太多。
zhLatn: Tāmen huì chídào. Xiǎo guó zǒngshì chí. Yào wèn de shūbó tài duō.

blocks.label: Gumdol Fortress
blocks.ko: 금돌성

blocks.html: The king rides as far as a hill fort and no farther. The field belongs to his son and to Yushin. Under Yushin ride two more generals. Humsun is his younger brother, with a boy of fifteen in the ranks. Pumil has one of sixteen. Fifty thousand men march west with a date in their heads, and between them and the date sits a man called Gyebek.
blocks.ko: 임금은 산성 하나까지만 오고 더는 오지 않는다. 들판은 아들과 유신의 몫이다. 유신 밑으로 장수가 둘 더 있다. 흠순은 유신의 아우이고, 대열 속에 열다섯 살 아들이 있다. 품일에게는 열여섯 살이 하나 있다. 오만 군사가 머릿속에 날짜 하나를 넣고 서쪽으로 간다. 그들과 그 날짜 사이에 계백이라는 사내가 앉아 있다.

lines: …유신. 당이 먼저 도착하게 하지 마래이. 저들은 천 년 동안 그래 적을 끼다.
en: The tenth day, then.
…Yushin. Don’t let the West get there first. They’ll write it down that way for a thousand years.

blocks.label: Final Ford
blocks.ko: 기벌포

blocks.html: On the ninth day, the Western fleet sails into the river mouth at Final Ford. The shore there is a mile of grey mud. Baekje’s soldiers wait on the high ground. They watch the first the Western companies wade in up to the thigh.
blocks.ko: 아흐렛날, 서국의 함대가 기벌포 강어귀로 들어온다. 그곳 물가는 십 리에 걸친 잿빛 진흙이다. 백제 군사들은 높은 땅에서 기다린다. 서국의 첫 부대가 허벅지까지 빠지며 걸어 들어오는 것을 지켜본다.

blocks.html: A river mouth made of mud, and Sabi’s front door.
blocks.ko: 진흙으로 된 강어귀, 사비의 앞문.

en: Mud is just wet road.
Give it something to hold.
zhLatn: Ní búguò shì shī lù.
Gěi tā diàn diǎn dōngxi.

blocks.html: His men lay willow mats on the mud, one after another, a road made of baskets, and the army walks across it dry-shod. By evening the Baekje line is broken and the river is open to Sabi.
blocks.ko: 그의 병사들이 진흙 위에 버들 거적을 한 장 한 장 깐다. 광주리로 만든 길이다. 군대는 발을 적시지 않고 그 위를 건넌다. 저녁이 되자 백제의 진은 무너지고, 사비로 가는 강이 열린다.

blocks.html: The same morning, forty miles east, the Silla army comes down out of the hills onto the Yellow Mountain Fields, and finds five thousand men already standing in its way.
blocks.ko: 같은 날 아침, 동쪽으로 백 리 떨어진 곳에서 신라군이 산을 내려와 황산벌로 들어선다. 오천 명이 이미 길을 막고 서 있다.

blocks.caption: One army from the sea, one from the hills, and one road to the capital between them.
blocks.ko: 바다에서 한 군대, 산에서 한 군대. 그 사이로 도성 가는 길이 하나뿐이다.

blocks.html: From the pass, Gyebek watches the dust come off the eastern hills. It splits three ways, one cloud to each road, as if it had seen his map.
blocks.ko: 고개 위에서 계백은 동쪽 산에서 내려오는 먼지를 지켜본다. 먼지가 셋으로 갈라진다. 길마다 한 줄기씩. 그의 지도를 보기라도 한 것처럼.

blocks.speaker: Sukdal
lines: 개울 건너서 진을 치는디, 팔천 걸음은 되겄어유.
en: Three columns, General. One on each road.
They’re making camp past the stream. Eight thousand paces, I reckon.
Eight thousand three hundred.

blocks.html: Then the air above the Yellow Mountain does what air should not. Kangrim hangs there in plain day — visible not to one dying man but to all five thousand at once. They have already finished negotiating with life.
blocks.ko: 그때 황산 위 공기가 하면 안 되는 일을 한다. 강림이 대낮에 떠 있다 — 죽어 가는 한 사람이 아니라 오천이 한꺼번에 본다. 그들은 이미 삶과의 협상을 끝냈다.

blocks.html: They cheer. They wave. Someone shouts a greeting as if King Yumla’s escort were a popular general arriving late to his own war. Kangrim, who has collected kings with less fuss for His Majesty, actually blinks.
blocks.ko: 그들은 환호한다. 손을 흔든다. 누군가는 염라대왕의 사신을 — 자기 전쟁에 늦게 도착한 인기 장군처럼 — 소리쳐 맞는다. 폐하를 위해 왕을 더 조용히 데려가 본 강림이 정말로 눈을 깜빡인다.

en: …You can all see me.
That is — new.
Ah. You have already decided. Of course.
Men of Baekje —
If even death showed up early, we must be on time.
Spears.
lines: 죽음이 일찍 왔다면, 우리는 제시각인 겨.

blocks.html: Gyebek kneels. He plants his sword in the yellow dust, point down. Inside its ring pommel sits a phoenix, the same bird that rode the incense burner he once dove for. He keeps his hand on it. Gyebek stands when the dust has learned the shape.
blocks.ko: 계백은 무릎을 꿇는다. 칼끝을 아래로 하여 노란 먼지에 칼을 꽂는다. 고리 자루 안에 봉황이 앉아 있다. 언젠가 그가 강에 뛰어들어 건져 낸 향로 꼭대기의 그 새다. 그는 손을 그 위에 얹고 있다. 먼지가 그 모양을 기억하면, 계백은 일어선다.

blocks.html: Seventh-month heat sits on the Yellow Mountain like a second army. Dust rises white off the three roads. Downstream, the Western sails already crowd the river mouth. They are waiting for the inland door to open. This field is that door.
blocks.ko: 칠월의 더위가 황산 위에 두 번째 군대처럼 앉아 있다. 세 길목에서 먼지가 희게 오른다. 하류에서는 서국의 돛이 벌써 강어귀를 메운다. 내륙의 문이 열리기를 기다리는 중이다. 이 들판이 그 문이다.

blocks.html: Dust on the ridge. The Silla marshal rides out ahead of his army.
blocks.ko: 고갯마루에 먼지가 인다. 신라 장수가 군대보다 앞서 나온다.

lines: 주점들은 아직도 삼한 최강의 칼을 우리 둘로 나눈다. 그 논쟁, 여기서 끝낼까?
en: So — you are this Hundred-Victories Gyebek I have heard of?
The taverns still split the Greatest Blade of Samhan between us. Shall we settle their argument?

lines: 나는 주점에서 마시지 않소. 나는 셉니다. 오늘은 오 대 오십 — 칭호는 그 다음이오.
en: Then you must be the Sword of the Divine Country.
I do not drink in taverns. I count. Today the count is five against fifty — and titles after.
Fifty thousand is a number.
Five thousand that already waved at death is another kind of number.
Hold your ground, then. We will come and measure it.
lines: 이미 죽음에 손 흔든 오천은 다른 종류의 숫자요.
그럼 자리를 지키시오. 우리가 가서 재어 보겠소.

blocks.label: Four Clashes
blocks.ko: 네 번의 격돌

blocks.label: The First Clash
blocks.ko: 첫 번째 접전

blocks.html: Silla comes on the first time in three columns. Humsun takes the northern road to the left camp. Yushin takes the middle, straight at the pass. Pumil takes the southern road to the right camp. All three at once, exactly as the arithmetic says. They wade the stream, and then it is uphill. In the heat. Into yellow shields set edge to edge. The archers wait to see which column is thickest, and loose at that one. All three camps throw them back across the water into their own dust.
blocks.ko: 신라는 첫 공격을 세 갈래로 해 온다. 흠순은 북쪽 길로 왼쪽 진영을 친다. 유신은 가운데로, 곧장 고개를 향한다. 품일은 남쪽 길로 오른쪽 진영을 친다. 산수가 시키는 그대로, 셋이 한꺼번에. 개울을 건너면 그다음은 오르막이다. 땡볕에. 가장자리를 맞댄 노란 방패를 향해. 궁수들은 어느 줄이 가장 두꺼운지 보고 나서야 그 줄에 쏜다. 세 진영이 그들을 개울 건너 제 먼지 속으로 도로 밀어낸다.

blocks.html: On the ridge Sukdal makes three marks in the dust with his thumb — left, middle, right — and wipes them out again. The tally is the same as morning. Five thousand. The arithmetic has not moved. That is the whole Baekje war plan, and it is working.
blocks.ko: 능선에서 숙달이 엄지로 먼지에 세 금을 긋는다 — 왼쪽, 가운데, 오른쪽 — 도로 지운다. 셈은 아침과 같다. 오천. 산수가 움직이지 않았다. 그것이 백제 전쟁 계획의 전부이며, 먹히고 있다.

en: Arrows?
Half what we loosed, General. The left camp shot wide on purpose.
lines: 쏜 것의 절반이 남았습니다, 장군. 왼쪽 진영은 일부러 헛쐈습니다.

blocks.speaker: Sukdal
lines: 셋 다 개울 너머루 물러가유, 장군.
en: All three back over the stream, General.
One.

blocks.label: The Second Clash
blocks.ko: 두 번째 접전

blocks.html: The second time Silla does not spread itself across three roads. Humsun brings it down the northern road in one fist at the left camp, hwarang in front, on the theory that the camp which shot the most is the camp with the fewest arrows left. It is a good theory. The left camp has counted its arrows too, and has been shooting half of what it could. Behind the fist, Yushin’s centre edges north, waiting for a hole. The fist opens on the stakes and goes back down the road, over the stream, carrying its own.
blocks.ko: 두 번째에 신라는 세 길로 흩어지지 않는다. 흠순이 북쪽 길로 한 주먹이 되어 왼쪽 진영을 친다. 화랑을 맨 앞에 세우고. 가장 많이 쏜 진영이 화살이 가장 적게 남은 진영이라는 이론에서다. 좋은 이론이다. 왼쪽 진영도 제 화살을 세어 두었고, 쏠 수 있는 것의 절반만 쏘아 왔다. 주먹 뒤로 유신의 가운데가 북쪽으로 슬며시 붙는다. 구멍이 나기를 기다리며. 주먹은 말뚝 앞에서 펴지고, 제 사람들을 메고 길을 되짚어 개울 너머로 내려간다.

blocks.html: The hwarang wedge reaches the stakes. That is the farthest any Silla man gets that day. A hwarang captain — seventeen, first campaign, helmet too big — takes a spear where the stakes break and holds it standing long enough for the men behind him to see his face. Yushin will ask his name at supper. Nobody will know it.
blocks.ko: 화랑 쐐기가 말뚝에 닿는다. 그날 신라 군사 중에선 가장 먼 곳이다. 화랑 대장 하나 — 열일곱, 첫 출전, 투구가 크다 — 말뚝이 부서지는 자리에서 창을 받고도 뒤따르는 군사들이 제 얼굴을 볼 때까지 서서 버틴다. 유신은 저녁에 그 이름을 물을 것이다. 아는 사람이 없을 것이다.

en: The wedge broke on the stakes, Marshal. The boy held.
lines: 쐐기는 말뚝에서 부서졌습니다, 원수. 아이는 버텼습니다.

en: Two.
Report.

blocks.speaker: Sukdal
lines: 오른쪽은 둘 다 있는디, 한 시진 전보다 둘 다 줄었슈.
en: …Left camp still has arrows.
Centre has men.
Right has both, and less of each than an hour ago.

blocks.label: The Third Clash
blocks.ko: 세 번째 접전

blocks.html: The third time Pumil takes the southern road, where the ground is softest and the right camp sits lowest. For the length of a held breath the road almost opens. Then it closes again on spears counted in the night. The right camp is not quite where Pumil’s scouts drew it at dawn. It is further back and higher. Every pace of the difference is uphill, and the Silla line arrives at the stakes with nothing left in its legs.
blocks.ko: 세 번째에 품일이 남쪽 길을 탄다. 땅이 가장 무르고 오른쪽 진영이 가장 낮게 앉은 곳이다. 숨 한 번 참는 동안 길이 거의 열린다. 그러고는 밤에 세어 둔 창에 다시 닫힌다. 오른쪽 진영은 새벽에 품일의 척후가 그려 온 자리에 꼭 있지 않다. 더 뒤에, 더 높은 곳에 있다. 그 차이의 걸음은 전부 오르막이라, 신라의 대열은 다리에 남은 것 없이 말뚝에 닿는다.

en: Forty paces. Pace it again.
Forty-one, General. Uphill.

blocks.html: Pumil looks at the higher stakes for a long time. Somewhere up there Gyebek is counting too. That is the worst part of this morning. The counting.
blocks.ko: 품일은 높아진 말뚝을 오래 본다. 저 위 어딘가에서 계백도 세고 있다. 오늘 아침 최악은 그거다. 셈하고 있다는 것.

en: Three.

blocks.label: The Fourth Clash
blocks.ko: 네 번째 접전

blocks.html: The fourth time Yushin rides at the head of the centre himself, on the white horse, straight up the middle road toward the pass, and meets Hundred-Victories in the gap between the camps. Both armies stop to watch two men, which armies are not supposed to do.
blocks.ko: 네 번째에는 유신이 몸소 흰 말을 타고 가운데 맨 앞에 서서, 가운데 길을 곧장 올라 고개로 향한다. 그리고 진영과 진영 사이의 틈에서 백승을 만난다. 양쪽 군대가 두 사내를 구경하느라 멈춘다. 군대가 해서는 안 되는 일이다.

blocks.speaker: Sukdal
en: General— the white horse. That’s him.
Yushin himself, on the middle road.
Hold the camps.

blocks.html: Gyebek comes the way the border remembers him. Gomanari at full stretch, Gyebek flat along the black neck like a thrown knife. His blade lies reversed along his forearm, edge out. There is no sword in his hand to watch. That is the point.
blocks.ko: 계백은 국경이 기억하는 그대로 온다. 고마나리가 몸을 끝까지 뻗고, 계백은 던진 칼처럼 검은 목덜미에 바짝 엎드린다. 칼날은 거꾸로 쥐어 팔뚝을 따라 눕혔고, 날은 바깥을 향한다. 손에 지켜볼 칼이 없다. 그게 요점이다.

blocks.html: The tall Silla helm comes in at a gallop. Yushin has heard the tavern stories. He watches the hand, the way the stories say to, and reads the reversed blade half a beat late.
blocks.ko: 신라의 높은 투구가 달려 들어온다. 유신도 주막의 이야기를 들었다. 이야기가 시키는 대로 손을 본다. 그리고 거꾸로 쥔 칼날을 반 박자 늦게 읽는다.

blocks.html: They meet in the dust. Nobody hears steel. They hear the white horse scream.
blocks.ko: 먼지 속에서 만난다. 쇳소리는 아무도 듣지 못한다. 흰 말이 비명 지르는 소리만 듣는다.

blocks.html: Then the white horse is going back the way it came with a red line along its shoulder, and the Sword of Silla is holding his left arm against his ribs. Gyebek turns Gomanari in his own length and walks him home. He came for one cut. He got half of one.
blocks.ko: 그러고 나면 흰 말은 왔던 길로 돌아가고 있고, 그 어깨에 붉은 줄이 하나 그어져 있으며, 신라의 칼은 왼팔을 갈비뼈에 붙여 안고 있다. 계백은 고마나리를 제자리에서 돌려 천천히 걸려 돌아간다. 한 번 베러 왔다. 반 번을 벴다.

blocks.html: On the ridge Humsun puts his hand on his son’s shoulder and leaves it there. Bangul is fifteen and has been watching his father lose all morning the way sons watch. The hand says what Humsun will say with his mouth an hour from now, at his stirrup.
blocks.ko: 능선에서 흠순이 아들 어깨에 손을 얹고 떼지 않는다. 방울은 열다섯이고, 아침 내내 아버지가 지는 것을 아들들이 보는 방식으로 봐 왔다. 그 손은 흠순이 한 시간 뒤 등자 앞에서 입으로 할 말을 미리 한다.

en: The white horse is bleeding, General.
Half a cut. Note it.

blocks.html: Behind him the fifty thousand sit down where they stand. Four times up the same slope in the same heat — the clerks will write that the soldiers’ strength was spent, which is the polite way to say that grown men are lying in the dust of their own road and cannot be made to get up.
blocks.ko: 그의 뒤에서 오만이 선 자리에 주저앉는다. 같은 더위에 같은 비탈을 네 번 — 서기들은 군사의 힘이 다했다고 적을 것이다. 다 큰 사내들이 제 길의 먼지에 누워 일으켜 세울 수 없게 되었다는 말을 예의 바르게 하는 방법이다.

en: Four.

blocks.html: After the fourth time there is a lull, the kind both sides pretend is for water. Yushin rides out alone into the gap on the white horse, his sleeve tied off with his own sash, and stops at a distance where a bow would be bad manners. After a while the black horse comes out of the centre camp to meet him. Nobody is near enough to hear. The chronicle has it anyway, the way it has most things, from men who swore afterwards they had not been listening.
blocks.ko: 네 번째가 끝나고 소강이 온다. 양쪽 다 물 마시는 시간인 척하는 그런 소강이다. 유신이 제 띠로 소매를 동여맨 채 흰 말을 타고 혼자 틈으로 나와, 활을 쏘면 무례가 될 거리에서 멈춘다. 한참 뒤 가운데 진영에서 검은 말이 마중을 나온다. 들을 만큼 가까이 있는 사람은 없다. 그래도 기록에는 남아 있다. 대부분이 그렇듯, 나중에 자기는 안 듣고 있었다고 맹세한 사내들에게서.

blocks.html: Black horse, white horse, nose to nose in the yellow dust. From either line they look like a pair of go stones someone has forgotten to play.
blocks.ko: 검은 말, 흰 말, 누런 먼지 속에서 코와 코를 맞댄다. 어느 쪽 대열에서 보아도, 누가 두다 만 바둑돌 한 쌍 같다.

en: Your right camp. You moved it in the night.
Forty paces.
…You noticed.
On the third time. Not before.
…How old are you.

lines: 마흔. 그쯤이오. 아무도 적어 두지 않았소.
en: Forty. Near enough. Nobody wrote it down.

lines: 내가 마흔일 때 만났으면 내가 이겼을 거요.
en: Sixty-five.
If we had met when I was forty, I would have had you.
…No. I would not have.

blocks.html: Gyebek looks at the tied sleeve and does not say anything polite about it.
blocks.ko: 계백은 동여맨 소매를 본다. 그것에 대해 예의 바른 말은 하지 않는다.

lines: 네 번째엔 직접 나왔소. 안 그래도 됐을 텐데.
en: You came yourself, the fourth time. You did not have to.

lines: 애들이 봐야 했소. 할 수 있다는 걸.
en: The boys needed to see it could be done.
Could it?

lines: 오만을 데리고 왔소. 아직 사만 몇은 남았고. 그대는 오천을 데리고 왔지.
en: Not by me. Not today.
I came with fifty thousand. I still have forty-some. You came with five.
Four. Now.

lines: 알고 있소. 나도 셀 줄 아오.
en: I know. I can count too.
Then go home.
You first.

blocks.html: Neither of them laughs, but it is close.
blocks.ko: 둘 다 웃지는 않는다. 웃을 뻔했을 뿐이다.

en: Your taverns.
What about them.
Nothing. They will have a long winter.

blocks.html: They turn the horses at the same moment, black and white, as if somebody had rehearsed it, and ride back to their counts.
blocks.ko: 둘은 같은 순간에 말머리를 돌린다. 검은 말과 흰 말, 누가 미리 맞춰 둔 것처럼. 그리고 각자의 셈으로 돌아간다.

blocks.speaker: Kim Humsun
en: Brother. The West are at the river mouth.
Tomorrow is the tenth.
I know quite well what day it is.

blocks.html: Humsun looks at the slope. Then, for longer, at his son.
blocks.ko: 흠순은 비탈을 본다. 그리고 그보다 오래, 제 아들을 본다.

blocks.label: Gwanchang
blocks.ko: 관창

blocks.label: Bangul & Gwanchang
blocks.ko: 반굴과 관창

blocks.html: Humsun calls his son to his stirrup. Bangul is fifteen, near enough, and Yushin’s nephew; he comes at a run, because he has been watching his father look at him since the white horse came back.
blocks.ko: 흠순이 아들을 등자 곁으로 부른다. 반굴은 얼추 열다섯, 유신의 조카다. 흰 말이 돌아온 뒤로 아비가 자기를 보고 있는 것을 줄곧 지켜보았기에, 그는 달려온다.

blocks.speaker: Kim Humsun
lines: 신하로서는 충만 한 것이 없고, 자식으로서는 효만 한 것이 없다.
위태로움을 보고 목숨을 바치면 — 충과 효를 함께 온전히 하는 것이다.
en: For a subject, nothing is greater than loyalty. For a son, nothing is greater than filial piety.
To see the danger and give your life to it — that keeps both, whole, at once.

blocks.caption: Yushin’s nephew. Young, brave, and in a hurry.
blocks.ko: 유신의 조카. 젊고, 용감하고, 급하다.

en: I have heard you, Father.

blocks.html: Bangul rides out alone up the middle road and does not come back. He goes into the Baekje line at the pass, where it is thickest, and fights there until it closes over him, and the place where it closed is the place Silla aims at next.
blocks.ko: 반굴이 홀로 가운데 길을 달려 올라가 돌아오지 않는다. 그는 고개 앞, 백제의 대열이 가장 두터운 곳으로 들어가, 대열이 그를 덮을 때까지 싸운다. 대열이 닫힌 그 자리가, 신라가 다음에 겨누는 자리다.

blocks.html: Pumil does not call his son. He has him brought to stand in front of his horse, before all the generals, and points at him the way a man points at a map.
blocks.ko: 품일은 아들을 부르지 않는다. 장수들이 다 보는 앞에서 아들을 제 말 앞에 세우게 하고, 지도를 가리키듯 그를 가리킨다.

blocks.caption: Gwanchang. A hwarang so young they had to pad the helmet.
blocks.ko: 관창. 투구 안에 솜을 덧대야 할 만큼 어린 화랑.

blocks.caption: A Silla general with a son in the ranks. He knows exactly where the boy is standing.
blocks.ko: 아들을 군중에 둔 신라 장군. 아이가 어디 서 있는지 정확히 안다.

en: My son is only sixteen, but his spirit is brave enough.
In today’s battle — can he be the mark the three armies aim by?
lines: 내 아이는 겨우 열여섯이나, 뜻과 기개가 자못 용감하오.
오늘 싸움에서 — 삼군이 겨눌 표적이 될 수 있겠느냐?

en: Yes.

blocks.html: He takes an armoured horse and one spear and goes straight at the Baekje centre. He gets further than Bangul did. Then they pull him off the horse alive and bring him to Gyebek.
blocks.ko: 그는 갑옷 입힌 말 한 필과 창 한 자루로 곧장 백제의 가운데로 달려든다. 반굴보다 더 깊이 들어간다. 그리고 산 채로 말에서 끌어내려져 계백 앞에 끌려온다.

blocks.html: Gyebek has the helmet taken off. Inside it is a boy’s face, sweat-striped, furious at being alive.
blocks.ko: 계백이 투구를 벗기게 한다. 그 안에 소년의 얼굴이 있다. 땀으로 줄이 지고, 살아 있다는 데 분해 하는 얼굴.

en: Silla cannot be withstood.
If a boy is like this — what are its grown men?
Go home.

blocks.html: They put him back on his horse and point it at the Silla line. At his father’s stirrup Gwanchang does not get down.
blocks.ko: 그들은 그를 다시 말에 태워 신라 쪽으로 머리를 돌려 보낸다. 아비의 등자 곁에서 관창은 말에서 내리지 않는다.

en: I went into their midst and could not cut down their general or take their banner.
It was not because I was afraid to die.
lines: 제가 적진에 들어가 장수를 베지도, 깃발을 뽑지도 못한 것은

blocks.html: Behind the Silla line there is a well, dug that morning for the horses. He scoops the water out with both hands, drinks, and rides back the way he came. Gyebek sends him home once. He comes back.
blocks.ko: 신라 대열 뒤에 그날 아침 말들을 위해 판 우물이 있다. 그는 두 손으로 물을 떠 마시고, 왔던 길로 다시 달려간다. 계백은 그를 한 번 돌려보냈다. 그는 다시 온다.

blocks.html: The second time, Gyebek has his helmet unstrapped again, and looks at the face inside it for a while. He has looked at faces like this once already this week, in his own house, before the light was up. Then he does what he has to. He ties the head to the saddle and sends the horse back down the middle road.
blocks.ko: 두 번째로 계백은 다시 그 투구를 벗기게 하고, 안에 든 얼굴을 한참 바라본다. 이런 얼굴들은 이번 주에 이미 한 번 보았다. 제 집에서, 날이 밝기 전에. 그리고 해야 할 일을 한다. 그 머리를 안장에 매어 말을 가운데 길로 돌려보낸다.

blocks.html: Pumil holds the head up in front of the army and wipes the blood from its face with his own sleeve, so that the three armies can see whose son it is.
blocks.ko: 품일은 그 머리를 군사들 앞에 들어 올리고, 제 소매로 얼굴의 피를 닦는다. 삼군이 그것이 누구의 아들인지 볼 수 있도록.

lines: 보아라. 얼굴이 살아 있는 것 같지 않으냐.
en: Look at him. His face is as if he were alive.
He died in the king’s service. …I have nothing to regret.

blocks.label: The Fifth Clash · The Final Stand
blocks.ko: 다섯 번째 접전 · 최후의 항전

blocks.html: Nobody gives an order. The drums start on their own, one column and then the next, and fifty thousand men who could not be made to get up an hour ago are on their feet and shouting.
blocks.ko: 아무도 명령하지 않는다. 북이 저절로 울기 시작한다. 한 대열, 그다음 대열. 한 시진 전만 해도 일으켜 세울 수 없던 오만이 일어서서 함성을 지른다.

blocks.html: The Silla line, which has failed four times that morning, comes up all three roads at once and does not stop. A father’s wet sleeve is worth more than a fourth failure. The left camp on the northern road goes under first — not broken so much as used up. The right camp holds the southern road one more breath, then folds north toward the centre like a hinge that has decided to finish.
blocks.ko: 그날 아침 네 번을 실패한 신라의 대열이 세 길로 한꺼번에 올라오고, 이번엔 멈추지 않는다. 아비의 젖은 소매가 네 번째 실패보다 값이 크다. 북쪽 길의 왼쪽 진영이 먼저 가라앉는다 — 부서졌다기보다 다 쓰인 것에 가깝다. 오른쪽 진영이 남쪽 길을 한 숨 더 버티다가, 끝내기로 한 경첩처럼 북쪽 가운데로 접힌다.

blocks.html: On the Baekje side, nobody says five.
blocks.ko: 백제 쪽에서는, 아무도 다섯이라고 말하지 않는다.

blocks.html: By the fifth charge the left camp is a rumour of men. Spears shorten. Names stop answering. Sukdal stops somewhere between one tally and the next. Gyebek calls the name twice, then says the next number himself.
blocks.ko: 다섯 번째 돌격쯤이면 왼쪽 진영은 사람의 소문에 가깝다. 창이 짧아진다. 이름이 대답을 멈춘다. 석달은 셈과 셈 사이 어디쯤에서 멈춘다. 계백은 그 이름을 두 번 부르고, 다음 숫자는 제 입으로 센다.

blocks.html: Kangrim, who has been hanging in the day like unfinished weather, comes down to speaking distance.
blocks.ko: 미완의 날씨처럼 대낮에 걸려 있던 강림이, 말 닿는 거리까지 내려온다.

blocks.html: He reads the general's name three times across the field — Gyebek. Gyebek. Gyebek. — though five thousand throats have already answered.
blocks.ko: 그는 벌판을 가로질러 장군의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 계백. 계백. 계백. — 오천의 목구멍이 이미 대답했어도.

en: General.
Your five thousand already waved. So I ask you alone.
When you killed your family to keep your oath: was that loyalty, or terror of becoming soft?
lines: 오천은 이미 손을 흔들었소. 그러니 당신에게만 묻겠소.
약조를 지키려 집안을 베었을 때: 그것이 충성이었습니까, 아니면 무르게 될까 두려운 것이었습니까?
두려움이었다면 그들에게 말하지 마시오. 더 예쁜 말을 갖게 두시오.
고을 원님이 염라대왕을 잡아 오라고 당신을 내려보냈지. 염라가 당신을 붙잡아 두었고.
en: …Loyalty.
If it was terror, do not tell them. Let them keep the prettier word.
A magistrate sent you down to arrest King Yumla. Yumla kept you.

lines: 산 사람은 그 문장을 끝까지 말하면 안 되는데.
en: …The island told you.
Living men are not supposed to finish that sentence.

lines: 위에서, 정원지기에게 물었소. 죽은 사람을 되돌릴 수 있느냐고.
en: Upstairs, I asked a gardener whether the dead can be put back.
He said it can be done.
Don’t.
…No. I didn’t think you would want it.
I asked anyway.

blocks.html: Gyebek turns his head toward the river road, toward Sabi, where nobody is coming.
blocks.ko: 계백은 고개를 강 쪽 길로 돌린다. 사비 쪽으로. 아무도 오지 않는 쪽으로.

blocks.html: A mudbank on the White River at night. A boy who has gone into the water nineteen times, and a prince in a grey hood with a jar he has not opened.
blocks.ko: 밤의 백강 진흙둑. 열아홉 번 물에 들어간 아이와, 뜯지 않은 술 단지를 든 회색 두건의 왕자.

en: Why on earth do you do all of this?
I gave my word.
…I want to live.
You have your word. Now you have mine.
lines: 너한텐 네 약조가 있지. 이제 내 약조두 있다.
계백, 더 큰 뜻을 섬겨 보겠느냐?
en: Gyebek, would you like to serve a higher purpose?

lines: …그 이름이 마음에 드십니까, 제가 마음에 드십니까?
en: …Do you like the name, or do you like me?
…Folks don’t usually ask that.
Yes.

blocks.html: The field returns.
blocks.ko: 벌판이 돌아온다.

en: Your Majesty… I gave my word.

blocks.html: He says it in exactly the same words, the way you set a stone back where it was. Kangrim closes the distance.
blocks.ko: 똑같은 말이다. 돌을 제자리에 도로 놓듯이. 강림이 남은 거리를 좁힌다.

en: Walk, then. The underworld kingdom keeps better hours than Sabi ever did.
lines: 그럼 가시죠. 저승은 사비보다 시간을 잘 킵니다.
네 번은 막고 다섯 번째엔 졌네
한 번 한 약속 꼭 지켰네
en: Gyebek, Gyebek, where did you go?
Out to the field where the yellow winds blow.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Five thousand men stood up in a row:
four times yes, and the fifth time no.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
He counted it all, then he counted his last;
he gave his word, and he held it fast.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
blocks.title: Gyebek of the Five Thousand

blocks.caption: Gyebek, general of Baekje. He gave his word once.
blocks.ko: 백제의 장군 계백. 약속은 한 번 했다.

blocks.html: The Silla clerks count too. Twenty-odd taken alive, two ministers among them. Nobody writes down how many of the five thousand were left to take.
blocks.ko: 신라의 서기들도 센다. 사로잡은 자 스무남은, 그 가운데 좌평 둘. 오천 가운데 사로잡을 사람이 몇이나 남아 있었는지는 아무도 적지 않는다.

blocks.html: Nobody can lead the black horse off the field. It stands over the place where he went down until the Silla grooms come at dusk with ropes, and it takes six of them, and in the night it breaks the line and goes south toward the ferry it was named for. Nobody on either side ever reports seeing it again.
blocks.ko: 아무도 그 검은 말을 들판에서 끌어내지 못한다. 말은 그가 쓰러진 자리를 지키고 서 있다가, 해 질 녘 신라 마부들이 밧줄을 들고 오자 여섯이 달라붙어야 하고, 밤이 되자 줄을 끊고 제 이름이 된 나루 쪽, 남으로 간다. 어느 편에서도 그 말을 다시 보았다는 보고는 없다.

blocks.label: Gumdol Fortress · that night
blocks.ko: 금돌성 · 그날 밤

blocks.html: King Muyeol has spent the battle forty li behind it, at Gumdol, being told things. Tonight he is told the best news a king of Silla has heard in a hundred years. Then he does something with it nobody in the tent expects.
blocks.ko: 무열왕은 싸움 내내 사십 리 뒤 금돌성에서 소식을 들었다. 오늘 밤 그는 신라 임금이 백 년 만에 들어 보는 가장 좋은 소식을 듣는다. 그리고 그 소식으로, 막사 안 누구도 예상하지 못한 일을 한다.

blocks.html: The first chair of the Harmony Council has stood empty since old Geumgang died at New Year. Everyone in the tent has been counting who should have it. Most of them have been counting themselves.
blocks.ko: 화백회의 맨 윗자리는 정월에 늙은 금강이 죽은 뒤로 비어 있다. 막사 안 사람들은 모두 그 자리가 누구 몫인지 세어 왔다. 대부분은 자기 자신을 세어 왔다.

en: The first chair.
Kim Yushin.

blocks.html: The tent goes very quiet. A High Councillor comes from the table: he sits at it for years, waits, outlives better men. Yushin has never sat at it for a single vote. He is Gaya, the bottom rung of the True Bone. Nobody has ever gone from no seat to the first one in a night.
blocks.ko: 막사가 쥐 죽은 듯 조용해진다. 상대등은 그 탁자에서 나온다. 몇 해를 앉아 기다리고, 더 나은 사람들보다 오래 산 끝에. 유신은 그 탁자에 앉아 표 한 번 던져 본 적이 없다. 그는 가야, 진골의 맨 아랫단이다. 의석 하나 없던 사람이 하룻밤 새 맨 윗자리에 오른 적은 한 번도 없다.

lines: 상대등 자리는 언제나 그 탁자에 앉아 본 이에게 갔사옵니다. 저 사람은 의석을 가져 본 적이 없사옵니다.
en: Majesty— with respect.
The first chair has always gone to a man who has sat at the table. He has never held a seat.

lines: 그리고 그 집안이옵니다, 전하. 가야 집안이옵니다.
en: And the house, Majesty. The house is Gaya.

lines: 금관가야는 우리에게 제 임금을 주었소. 그 손자는 오늘 오후 우리에게 백제를 주었고.
여기 누가 내게 이유 하나라도 주겠소?
en: Yes.
Golden Gaya gave us its king. His grandson gave us Baekje this afternoon.
Is anyone here going to give me a reason?

blocks.html: Nobody does. They have watched the Secretariat eat the Council’s seals one by one. They know which way a room votes when the king has already written the minutes.
blocks.ko: 아무도 주지 않는다. 그들은 집사부가 회의의 인장을 하나씩 먹어 치우는 걸 지켜봤다. 임금이 이미 회의록을 써 둔 방이 어느 쪽으로 표를 던지는지 다들 안다.

lines: …전하. 저는 자리 같은 건 원치 않습니다.
en: Chunchu.
…Majesty. I don’t want a chair.

lines: 앉게, 유신. 평생 한 번은 좀 앉아.
en: I know. That’s why it’s yours.
Sit down, Yushin. For once in your life, sit down.

blocks.html: Six sleeves go up. Two of them go up slowly. In the morning the clerks write a Gaya name at the head of the Council for the first time, and spell it very carefully.
blocks.ko: 소매 여섯이 올라간다. 그중 둘은 천천히 올라간다. 이튿날 아침 서기들은 처음으로 가야 사람의 이름을 회의 맨 위에 적는다. 아주 조심스럽게, 한 획도 틀리지 않게.

blocks.html: The pass is open. The river is open. And in Sabi, a runner is climbing the palace steps with one word…!
blocks.ko: 고개가 열렸다. 강이 열렸다. 그리고 사비에서는, 전령 하나가 한 마디를 들고 궁궐 계단을 오른다…!

logline.en: Euija’s first move is to send the West a feast. The oxen come back untouched.
logline.ko: 의자의 첫 수는 서국 진영에 잔칫상을 보내는 것이다. 소들은 손도 대지 않은 채 돌아온다.

images.alt: Poster key art: King Muyeol rides the white heavenly horse through the smoke of fallen Sabi, reining it in at the broken gate
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Smoke-black dusk at the broken gate of Sabi on the Baengma river bluff; Baekje giwa halls burning low in the distance. Worm’s-eye from the ash. INTERACTION: King Muyeol rides bareback on the wingless white heavenly horse Chunma, reining it in hard at the gate; the horse rears half up, forelegs high, and he leans forward along its neck with one hand flat on its shoulder to steady it, his face grim and spent rather than triumphant. Cloud streamers off its hooves curl into the smoke. CHUNMA HAS NO WINGS: a wingless white heavenly horse, bare white back and shoulders, nothing feathered anywhere; it rides the air on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs. Firelight from the burning halls (#D8258C magenta-orange) is the one key on his crown, face and the horse’s white chest; the gate and the sky are ink-black smoke. Ash flakes as painted bokeh. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. Not photoreal, not 3D. No glow aura, no halo, no emissive outline — the accent colour is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — KING MUYEOL — FACE and garments from attached /ch_muyeol.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Now: King Muyeol (stage portrait): royal robes and crown; heavier, tired eyes. Demeanor: Diplomat and strategist: talks with his hands, smiles while calculating, never shouts; half-lidded watchful eyes. #D8258C as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: front-line armored warrior pose; shouting battle face; katana. | CHUNMA (천마, hyukgose's heavenly horse, guardian of Silla) — attached board /obj_chunma.png: WINGLESS white heavenly horse in the Cheonmachong saddle-flap style: long arched neck, streaming white mane and tail, legs flung out in a flying gallop. It has NO WINGS — no feathers, no bird wings, nothing growing from the shoulders. It rides the sky on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs and chest, as on the painted birch-bark flap. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, never a glow outline. Kneels and cries beside the purple egg at Najeong, sees men approach, neighs and rises into the sky. | PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. Yes. I know who counts.

blocks.html: Euija sits down on the top step, in front of everyone, which kings do not do. The court waits for an order. For the first time in twenty years he does not have one ready. So he reaches for the next thing he owns, which is an idea.
blocks.ko: 의자는 모두가 보는 앞에서 맨 윗계단에 주저앉는다. 임금이 해서는 안 되는 일이다. 조정은 명을 기다린다. 스무 해 만에 처음으로 그에게는 준비된 명이 없다. 그래서 그다음으로 가진 것에 손을 뻗는다. 꾀다.

blocks.html: Before noon a second runner comes up the road from the river mouth, muddy to the waist, with what is left of the river-mouth line behind him.
blocks.ko: 정오가 되기 전, 두 번째 전령이 강어귀 길을 따라 올라온다. 허리까지 진흙투성이고, 그 뒤로 강어귀 방어선의 남은 자들이 따라온다.

lines: …바다에서 오래 있었지. 배에서 내린 놈들은 늘 배가 고파.
배부른 놈은 성을 안 태운다. 먹여라. 원하는 건 그다음에 얘기하자.
en: …They’ve been at sea. Men off boats are always hungry.
Nobody burns a city on a full stomach. Feed them. Then we’ll talk about what they want.

blocks.html: So his first move is to send the Western camp a feast: oxen, wine, three cartloads of rice cakes. The court is told this is diplomacy.
blocks.ko: 그래서 그의 첫 수는 서국의 진영에 잔칫상을 보내는 것이다. 소, 술, 떡 세 수레. 조정에는 이것이 외교라고 알린다.

blocks.caption: Two arrows, one capital, and a king who has decided the answer is oxen.
blocks.ko: 화살 둘, 도성 하나, 그리고 답은 소 떼라고 정한 왕.

blocks.html: The oxen come back that afternoon, untouched, with the drovers walking behind them.
blocks.ko: 황소들은 그날 오후, 손도 안 댄 채, 몰이꾼들을 뒤에 달고 되돌아온다.

blocks.label: The Allies
blocks.ko: 동맹

blocks.label: The Red Fowl’s Tent
blocks.ko: 주작의 군막

blocks.html: The Silla army reaches the Western camp two days late. The Red Fowl has the Silla supply officer, Kim Munyung, dragged to his tent gate. They open his collar for the sword.
blocks.ko: 신라군이 약속보다 이틀 늦게 서국의 진영에 닿는다. 주작은 신라의 군량 장교 김문영을 군막 문 앞으로 끌어낸다. 칼 받을 목깃을 풀게 한다.

lines: 열흘. 사비 남쪽. 두 번 말했다.
en: The tenth day. South of Sabi. I said it twice.
Take his head. Then we can start.
zh: 七月十日，泗沘之南。我說了兩遍。
zhLatn: Qīyuè shí rì, Sìbì zhī nán. Wǒ shuō le liǎng biàn.
Zhǎn le. Ránhòu kāishǐ.

blocks.html: Kim Yushin walks into the tent with a battle-axe in his hand.
blocks.ko: 김유신이 손에 큰 도끼를 들고 군막 안으로 걸어 들어온다.

lines: 늦었다는 걸 죄로 삼겠다면, 죄 없이 욕을 받을 수는 없소. 서군과 먼저 결판을 내고, 백제는 그다음에 치겠소.
en: The general did not see the Yellow Mountain Fields.
If you mean to punish us for being late, I will not be shamed for a crime I did not commit. I will fight the West first, and Baekje after.

blocks.hanja: 乃杖鉞軍門 怒髮如植 其腰間寶劍自躍出鞘
blocks.html: Then he stood at the camp gate leaning on his axe; his angry hair stood up like planted stakes, and the precious sword at his waist leapt of itself from its scabbard.
blocks.ko: 이에 도끼를 짚고 군문에 서니, 성난 머리털이 꽂아 세운 듯하고, 허리에 찬 보검이 저절로 칼집에서 뛰쳐나왔다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 5, Silla Annals — King Muyeol, yr. 7 (660), seventh month

blocks.html: The Red Fowl’s second-in-command steps on his commander’s foot.
blocks.ko: 주작의 부장이 제 장군의 발을 슬쩍 밟는다.

blocks.speaker: Dong Baoliang
en: (low) The Silla army is about to turn on us, General.
zhLatn: (Dīshēng) Xīnluó bīng jiāng yǒu biàn yě.

blocks.html: Kim Munyung’s collar is closed again. Nobody in the tent mentions the date for the rest of the war.
blocks.ko: 김문영의 목깃이 다시 여며진다. 그 전쟁이 끝날 때까지 군막 안의 누구도 날짜 이야기를 꺼내지 않는다.

blocks.html: Next morning the allies come at the city together, the West up from their camp in the south, Silla down the road from the east. Baekje puts everything it has left on the plain between them. Euija watches from the wall.
blocks.ko: 이튿날 아침 두 동맹군이 함께 도성으로 온다. 서군은 남쪽 진영에서 올라오고, 신라군은 동쪽 길로 내려온다. 백제는 남은 것을 전부 그 사이 벌판에 내놓는다. 의자는 성벽 위에서 지켜본다.

lines: 저거 봐라. 남은 놈들이 몽땅 한 벌판에 있구먼.
하… 세어 주지 마라. 나두 셀 줄 알어.
en: Look at that. Every man I had left, on one plain.
Ha… Don’t you count them for me. I can count.

blocks.label: The Fall
blocks.ko: 함락

blocks.label: Night Flight
blocks.ko: 야반도주

blocks.html: Euija leaves Sabi at night for Bear Fortress, upriver to the north-east, with fewer men than he expected to have.
blocks.ko: 의자는 밤에 사비를 떠나 강을 거슬러 북동쪽, 웅진성으로 향한다. 데리고 갈 수 있는 사람은 생각보다 적었다.

blocks.html: On the river he sits in the bow and says nothing for a long time. The boatmen will remember it, because nobody had ever seen him do that before.
blocks.ko: 강 위에서 그는 뱃머리에 앉아 오래도록 아무 말이 없다. 사공들은 그걸 기억할 것이다. 그가 그러는 걸 본 사람이 아무도 없었으니까.

lines: 성충이 그랬지. 고개를 막어라. 강어귀를 막어라. 옥에서, 다 떨리는 손으루 적어 보냈어.
이걸 봤으믄 좋아라 했을 겨. 꼴 보기 싫게 굴었겄지.
en: Sunchung said hold the pass. Hold the river mouth. Wrote it out for me from his cell, in a hand that was going.
I put him in that cell. …Ha.
He’d love this. He’d be plumb unbearable.

blocks.label: The City Gate
blocks.ko: 사비 성문

blocks.html: Back in Sabi, the king’s second son, Tae, puts on a crown the next morning and means to fight. His nephews don’t. They go down the wall on a rope with their households, and half the city follows them down it.
blocks.ko: 사비에서는 이튿날 아침 임금의 둘째 아들 태가 스스로 관을 쓰고 싸우겠다고 한다. 조카들은 생각이 다르다. 그들은 식솔을 데리고 밧줄을 타고 성벽을 내려가고, 성의 절반이 그 밧줄을 따라 내려간다.

blocks.html: The eldest is already gone. Yung took the river gate in the night with four men and no mark on his forehead, and a boatman who will remember, years later, that the prince paid in Satek silver and asked which way the current runs at Ungjin. The answer is down. Everything at Ungjin runs down, caves included.
blocks.ko: 맏이는 이미 없다. 융은 밤에 군사 넷과 이마의 표 없이 수구문으로 빠져나갔다. 뱃사공은 세월이 한참 지나서 기억할 것이다. 왕자가 사택 은으로 삯을 치르고 웅진의 물길이 어느 쪽으로 흐르느냐 물었다고. 답은 아래다. 웅진의 모든 것은 아래로 간다. 동굴까지도.

blocks.html: The crown prince comes out of the gate. Chunbok walks a careful pace behind him. Bupmin has the prince knelt in the dirt before his horse, and spits in his face.
blocks.ko: 태자가 성문을 나온다. 천복이 조심스레 한 걸음 뒤에서 따른다. 법민은 태자를 제 말 앞 흙바닥에 꿇리고, 그 얼굴에 침을 뱉는다.

lines: 내 누이. 고타소. 네 아비의 장수가 대야성에서 죽이고 옥 바닥에 묻었다.
열여덟 해를 그걸 안고 살았다. 그 이름을 말할 때는 나를 봐라.
en: Look at me.
My sister. Gotaso. Your father’s general killed her at Daeya and buried her under a prison floor.
Eighteen years I’ve carried that. Look at me when I say her name.

blocks.html: Hyo lies flat on the ground and says nothing. The mark is still on his forehead, ground into the dirt. He wears it to the end, which is more than anyone in his house will do for him.
blocks.ko: 효는 땅에 엎드려 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 표는 아직 이마에 있다, 흙에 문혀서. 그는 끝까지 쓰고 간다. 집안 누구도 그를 위해 해 주지 않을 일을.

blocks.html: The queen mother does not come out. She takes the household up to Busosan, the hill fort above the river, and holds it with women and old men until a soldier opens the gate for the West. The lists take her name, and Hyo’s, and twelve thousand others.
blocks.ko: 대비는 나오지 않는다. 식솔을 데리고 강 위 산성 부소산성으로 올라가 여인들과 노인들로 버티다 군사 하나가 당을 위해 문을 열 때까지다. 명부가 그녀의 이름과 효의 이름, 그리고 만 이천의 이름을 가져간다.

blocks.html: The lists keep the younger brother for a page. Then the page turns, and history loses him the way a river loses a stone. In Chang’an the clerks will one day write “Yung” where the crown prince stood — the eldest holding his brother’s place in the paperwork, the way he never held it on the Rock.
blocks.ko: 명부는 아우를 한 장에 적는다. 그러고 장이 넘어가면, 역사는 그를 강이 돌을 잃듯 잃는다. 장안의 서리들은 언젠가 태자가 섰던 자리에 “융”이라 쓸 것이다 — 맏이가 바위 위에서 한 번도 차지 못한 자리를 서류 위에서 차지하며.

blocks.html: It was Chunbok who opened the gate. He would like that understood as a favour.
blocks.ko: 성문을 연 것은 춘복이다. 그는 그것이 호의로 받아들여지기를 바란다.

lines: 장군들께서도 헤아리시겠지만, 성문은 백성을 위하여, 그리고 전적으로 그 뜻에 따라—
en: As the generals will surely appreciate, the gate was opened for the sake of the people, and in full accordance with—

blocks.label: Falling Flower Rock
blocks.ko: 낙화암

blocks.html: When the gate opens the palace women do not wait to be counted. They go out the back of the palace and up the ridge path to the cliff above the White River, where the rock drops straight into the water, and the soldiers coming up behind them find nobody at the top.
blocks.ko: 성문이 열리자 궁의 여인들은 세어지기를 기다리지 않는다. 궁 뒤로 빠져나가 백마강 위 벼랑까지 능선 길을 오른다. 바위가 물속으로 곧장 떨어지는 곳이다. 뒤따라 올라온 군사들은 꼭대기에서 아무도 찾지 못한다.

blocks.html: The stories that gave Euija three thousand women give them this cliff as well, and three thousand is the number they say went over it, their skirts opening on the way down like petals. Nobody who was there wrote down how many it really was. There was no one left on the cliff to count.
blocks.ko: 의자에게 삼천 궁녀를 붙여 준 이야기들은 이 벼랑도 그들에게 준다. 그 위에서 떨어진 것이 삼천이었다고, 떨어지는 동안 치마가 꽃잎처럼 벌어졌다고 말한다. 그 자리에 있던 누구도 실제로 몇이었는지 적지 않았다. 벼랑 위에는 셀 사람이 남아 있지 않았다.

blocks.html: Two of them go together, holding hands. They are the two who sat in a prince’s garden with a go board and a jar of wine, a lifetime ago. Nobody counts them. Nobody has counted them for years. It had been two, once, and a joke, and a modest number a man was proud of.
blocks.ko: 그중 둘은 손을 잡고 함께 간다. 아주 오래전, 바둑판과 술 단지를 놓고 왕자의 후원에 앉아 있던 그 둘이다. 아무도 세지 않는다. 여러 해 동안 아무도 세지 않았다. 한때는 둘이었고, 우스개였고, 한 사내가 자랑스러워하던 소박한 수효였다.

en: He’ll be reaching for us today, same as yesterday.
He isn’t here today. / …But the body remembers.

blocks.html: The rock is called the Falling Flowers afterwards, Nakhwaam, which is a kind way of saying it, and Baekje’s last invention.
blocks.ko: 뒷날 그 바위는 낙화암, 꽃이 떨어진 바위라 불린다. 부드럽게 이르는 말이고, 백제가 마지막으로 지어낸 것이다.

blocks.label: Ungjin
blocks.ko: 웅진성

blocks.html: Bear Fortress belongs to the king the way a borrowed house belongs to a guest. The Ye family has held it for four generations. Ye Sikjin gives the king his own rooms, and goes up on the wall every morning to count the Western sails on the river.
blocks.ko: 웅진성이 왕의 것인 건 빌린 집이 손님의 것인 것과 같다. 예씨 집안이 네 대째 지켜 온 성이다. 예식진은 왕에게 제 방을 내주고, 아침마다 성벽에 올라 강 위의 서국 돛을 센다.

lines: 식진아! 좋은 놈. 네 할아비가 내 할아비 위해 이 바위를 지켰잖여?
다시 지키는 겨. 주작이 은제까지 진흙탕에 앉아 있겄냐.
en: Sikjin! Good man. Your granddaddy held this rock for my granddaddy, didn’t he?
We’ll hold it again. The Red Fowl can’t sit in the mud forever.
My grandfather held it, Majesty.
…For whoever was king.

blocks.html: The first morning he counts forty sails. The second morning, sixty-two. He writes both numbers on the wall in charcoal, because that is what he does with numbers.
blocks.ko: 첫날 아침 그는 돛 마흔 개를 센다. 이튿날 아침에는 예순둘. 그는 두 숫자를 숯으로 성벽에 적어 둔다. 숫자를 보면 그렇게 하는 사람이다.

lines: 예순둘? 하! 뱃전에 대구 토하는 놈들이 예순두 척이구먼.
식진아, 멀미허는 소루는 밭을 못 갈어. 하하!
술 가져오너라. 좋은 잔으루. 수비대 잔 말구.
en: Sixty-two? Ha! Sixty-two boatloads of men throwing up over the side.
Sikjin, you can’t plough with a seasick ox. Ha!
Fetch wine. The good cups. Not the garrison ones.
The good cups are in Sabi, Majesty.
…I’ll bring the garrison ones.

blocks.html: On the third day a boatman comes up the river with Sabi still on his face. Ye Sikjin hears him out alone, on the wall. Then he takes him to the king, because that is the order things are done in.
blocks.ko: 사흗날, 사비에서 본 것이 아직 얼굴에 남은 사공 하나가 강을 거슬러 올라온다. 예식진은 성벽 위에서 혼자 그 말을 끝까지 듣는다. 그런 다음 그를 왕에게 데려간다. 일은 그 순서로 하는 것이니까.

lines: 태가 왕관을 썼다구? 그놈은 호박에 갓도 못 씌우는 놈이여!
…됐어. 꿇은 아들두 아들이지 뭐. 성 되찾으믄 한 달은 마당에 세워 둘 겨. 하하!
en: Tae put on a crown? That boy couldn’t get a hat on a pumpkin!
And Yung… knelt.
…Fine. A son on his knees is still a son. When I take the city back, he can stand in the yard for a month. Ha!

blocks.html: That night his elder brother comes in by the river gate. Ye Gun is the family’s talker. He has been downriver all day, he says, looking at the weather. It has rained since noon. He comes back dry.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 형이 강 쪽 문으로 들어온다. 예군은 집안에서 말을 맡은 사람이다. 종일 강 아래로 날씨를 보러 갔었다고 한다. 정오부터 비가 왔다. 그는 젖지 않은 채 돌아온다.

lines: 그 장군은 진흙 얘기를 날씨 얘기허듯 허더라. 진흙은 젖은 길일 뿐이랴.
그리구 이 성에 방이 몇 개냐구 묻더구먼. 아우한테 물어봐야 헌다구 했지. 세는 건 너니께.
en: That general talks about mud the way other men talk about weather. Mud is just wet road, if you please.
And he asked how many rooms this fortress has. I said I’d have to ask my brother. You’re the one who counts.
Thirty-nine, brother.
Counting the king’s.
And men?
Depends on the room.

lines: 수비대 술두 마시다 보니 정이 드는구먼, 식진아!
끝나믄 너는 조정으로 올라오는 겨. 진짜 자리루. 앞줄루. 배 세는 짓은 그만이다.
얼굴이 왜 그려? 농담 아니다. 마셔라!
en: Garrison wine! It grows on you, Sikjin!
When this is over, you’re coming to court. A real seat. Front row. No more counting boats.
What’s that face? That wasn’t a joke. Drink up!
You honour me, Majesty.
…Which seat?

lines: 하! 들었냐? 어느 자리냐니! 아무 디나 골라.
en: Ha! Listen to him. Which seat! Take your pick.
I’ve got forty-one of them.

blocks.html: That night he opens the drawer. The list is where he left it. Forty-one names. None of them his. He reads it a third time, being careful with numbers, and puts it back. He does not close the drawer. One day the Western stonecutter will carve his father and grandfather into Baekje’s first rank. Neither of them was ever asked to court. Tombstones are generous that way.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 서랍을 연다. 명단은 넣어 둔 그대로다. 이름 마흔하나. 그의 이름은 없다. 숫자에 꼼꼼한 사람이라, 그는 세 번째로 읽고 도로 넣는다. 서랍은 닫지 않는다. 언젠가 서국 석공 하나가 그의 아버지와 할아버지를 백제의 일품으로 새겨 줄 것이다. 둘 다 조정에 한 번 불려 간 적 없는 사람들이다. 묘비란 그렇게 너그럽다.

blocks.html: On the fifth night he comes into the king’s rooms with his brother and twenty men, and the king understands before anyone speaks.
blocks.ko: 닷새째 밤, 그는 형과 장정 스물을 데리고 왕의 방으로 들어온다. 왕은 누가 입을 열기도 전에 알아차린다.

en: …Which seat. Ha.
The list. You read the list.

lines: 세 번 읽었습니다, 폐하. 숫자는 조심해서 봐야 하니까요.
en: Three times, Majesty. I am careful with numbers.

lines: 사람은 자기가 믿고 싶은 것의 증거는 절대 검사하지 않아.
내가 한 말이여. 열아홉 해 전에. 너 같은 놈들루 꽉 찬 전각에서.
…뭘 보느냐? 밧줄은 좋은 걸루 가져와라. 수비대 것 말구.
en: Nobody inspects the evidence for a thing they already want to believe.
I said that, you know. Nineteen years ago, in a hall full of men like you.
…Well? Bring the good rope, at least. Not the garrison one.

blocks.html: By morning the king is on the river again, bound, going back down it toward the Red Fowl’s tent. The Ye brothers watch the boat from the wall.
blocks.ko: 아침이 되자 임금은 묶인 채 다시 강 위에 있다. 이번에는 강을 따라 내려가, 주작의 군막으로. 예씨 형제가 성벽에서 그 배를 지켜본다.

en: You can stop counting sails now.
…One more.
Going down.

blocks.html: His name was Sikjin, a man of Ungchun in Baekje. His grandfather, Minister Yeda, and his father, Minister Sasun, both held the first rank of that vassal court. … Upright from birth and early marked for righteousness, he read the wind in a foreign land and went toward the sun in Chang’an.
blocks.ko: 공의 휘는 식진이요, 백제 웅천 사람이다. 할아버지 좌평 예다와 아버지 좌평 사선은 모두 번국 관직 정일품이었다. … 일찍이 곧은 법도를 타고나 의로운 절개를 드러내니, 이역에서 바람을 점치고 장안의 해를 향해 나아갔다.
blocks.hanja: 公諱寔進百濟熊川人也 祖佐平譽多父佐平思善竝蕃官正一品 … 夙禀貞規早標義節占風異域就日長安
blocks.source: Epitaph of Ye Sikjin (禰寔進墓誌), Tang, 672

blocks.html: Back in the palace, the winners want their wine poured.
blocks.ko: 궁에서는 이긴 쪽이 술을 따르라 한다.

blocks.label: Victory
blocks.ko: 승전

blocks.label: The Victory Feast
blocks.ko: 승전 잔치

blocks.html: Chunchu finally arrives at the scene. He makes Euija pour his wine, and the Western general’s beside it.
blocks.ko: 마침내 춘추가 당도한다. 그는 의자에게 제 잔에, 그리고 그 옆 서국 장수의 잔에 술을 따르게 한다.

lines: 내가 너를 잡아들이려고 얼마나 고생했는지 아나?
거의 내 인생을 썼다, 이 자식아.
en: So… you are Euija.
The one who started all of this… Buyeo Euija.
Do you know what it cost me to bring you in?
Nearly my whole life, you bastard.

blocks.html: A cup is put into Euija’s hands, and he is made to pour.
blocks.ko: 의자의 손에 잔이 들려지고, 그는 술을 따르도록 강요당한다.

blocks.html: He pours for the Red Fowl first, slowly, with a small host’s bow, and only then turns to the Silla king.
blocks.ko: 그는 먼저 주작의 잔에 따른다. 천천히, 주인이 손님에게 하듯 살짝 고개를 숙이며. 그러고 나서야 신라 임금 쪽으로 돈다.

lines: 제일 멀리서 온 손님부터 따르는 법이지. 그게 예의다.
en: Guests who came furthest are served first. That’s manners.
You live next door. You can wait.
…Do you know what I said to Gesomun, once.
“I do not fear a man who kneels to another man.”

lines: 그 말을 들은 사람이 바로 나였으니까.
en: I know.
I was the man he said it about.
…And so — who is kneeling today?

lines: 나다. 이 잔 하나 받으려고 황제 앞에 무릎을 꿇었고, 다음 잔을 위해서라면 또 꿇을 게다.
무릎 꿇은 사람은 다시 일어난다, 의자. 너는 늘 그 대목을 안 보고 자리를 떴지.
en: I am. I knelt to an emperor for this cup, and I would kneel again for the next one.
A man who kneels gets up afterwards, Euija. You never stayed to watch that part.

lines: 너도 언젠가는 누군가 앞에 꿇을 거다.
en: Chunchu…
One day you will kneel before someone too.
Take this man away.

blocks.html: There is one more prisoner. He has been kept for the end of the feast, the way a host keeps back the dish he cares about.
blocks.ko: 포로가 하나 더 있다. 잔치 끝까지 남겨 둔 자다. 주인이 정말 아끼는 음식을 마지막까지 남겨 두듯이.

blocks.html: Gumil is older. The yellow sleeve is gone. Eighteen years in Baekje have not taught him to stand up straight, and they have not taught him to stop talking.
blocks.ko: 검일은 늙었다. 누런 소매도 없다. 백제에서 보낸 열여덟 해는 그에게 허리 펴는 법도, 입 다무는 법도 가르쳐 주지 않았다.

lines: 저 양반한테 뭐가 들었냐꼬 묻는 거 다 들었다. 해 봐라. 내한테도.
en: Ah~ so the father came after all.
I heard you ask him what it cost. Go on, then. Tell me.
From the start. All of it. Don’t leave any out.
No.

lines: 아니라꼬? 아이고~ 신라 제일가는 말쟁이가, 아니라 카네.
그 성 놈들 다 쓰레기였다 카이. 당신 사위가 내 마누라를 데려갔고, 나머지는 구경만—
en: No? Aigo~ the great talker of Silla, and he says no.
Everyone in that fortress was trash, I tell you. Your son-in-law took my wife, and the rest of them watched—
My daughter was in that fortress.

blocks.html: Gumil opens his mouth, and for once in eighteen years nothing comes out of it.
blocks.ko: 검일은 입을 연다. 그리고 열여덟 해 만에 처음으로, 아무 말도 나오지 않는다.

lines: 너는 나한테서 이야기 한 줄 못 얻는다. 네 이야기는 아무도 하지 않을 게다.
en: You’ll get no story from me. Nobody is going to tell yours.
Take him down to the river.

blocks.html: They put him to death on the riverbank before the wine is finished. Chunchu does not go down to watch. He drinks the cup Euija poured him instead, slowly, the way you finish a thing that took twenty years to pour.
blocks.ko: 술이 다 비기 전에 그들은 강가에서 그를 죽인다. 춘추는 내려가 보지 않는다. 대신 의자가 따라 준 잔을 마신다. 천천히. 따르는 데 스무 해가 걸린 것을 비우듯이.

blocks.label: The Pagoda
blocks.ko: 정림사 탑

blocks.html: A month later the West carve their victory into a stone pagoda. They put it low, where anyone walking round has to read it. It calls the conquest a deliverance. About Baekje’s king it says:
blocks.ko: 한 달 뒤, 당은 돌탑에 제 승리를 새긴다. 탑을 도는 사람이면 누구든 읽을 수밖에 없는 낮은 자리다. 비문은 정복을 구원이라 부른다. 백제의 임금에 대해서는 이렇게 적는다.

blocks.hanja: 外棄直臣 內信妖婦
blocks.html: Abroad he cast off his upright ministers; at home he trusted a bewitching woman.
blocks.ko: 밖으로는 곧은 신하를 버리고, 안으로는 요사한 여인을 믿었다.
blocks.source: Datang ping Baekje guo beiming (大唐平百濟國碑銘), carved on the five-storey stone pagoda of Jeongnimsa, Buyeo (660)

en: Harmonized.

blocks.html: Then the West divide Baekje into five commanderies, with the Western governor over each and Baekje men under them. Nothing in the arrangement is labelled Silla.
blocks.ko: 그러고 나서 당은 백제를 다섯 도독부로 나누고, 저마다 서국의 도독을, 그 아래에 백제 사람들을 앉힌다. 그 배치 어디에도 신라라는 이름표는 없다.

lines: 아버님. 평양 이남하고 백제 땅 전부. 그 말들 앞에서 그래 말했다꼬, 아버님이 그러셨다 아입니꺼.
en: Father. Everything south of Pyongyang and the whole of Baekje. He said it in front of the horses. You told me so yourself.

lines: 천자 말이 곧 문서라꼬도 캤다. 붓을 챙겨 갈 걸 그랬다.
en: I did.
He also said an emperor’s word was the writing. I rather wish I’d brought a brush.

blocks.label: Two Camps
blocks.ko: 두 진영

blocks.html: In the Western lines the Red Fowl’s staff officers are seen pacing out the distance to the Silla camp, which is not a thing allies measure. In the Silla council a man proposes that their soldiers put on Baekje clothes and fall on the West by night.
blocks.ko: 서국의 진에서 주작의 참모들이 신라 진영까지의 거리를 걸음으로 재는 것이 보인다. 동맹끼리 잴 거리는 아니다. 신라의 군의에서 누군가가, 우리 군사에게 백제 옷을 입혀 밤에 당을 치자고 한다.

lines: 그러나 주인이 발을 밟으면 뭅니다. 개도 그쯤은 압니다.
en: A dog fears its master, Majesty.
But step on its foot and it bites. Even a dog knows that much.

blocks.html: Word of the conversation reaches the Red Fowl’s tent, as it was meant to.
blocks.ko: 그 대화는 의도한 대로 주작의 군막에 전해진다.

blocks.html: A month later the Red Fowl sails home with Euija, his sons and twelve thousand captives. He leaves ten thousand men to hold the city. Beside them sits a Silla army that has stopped smiling.
blocks.ko: 한 달 뒤, 주작은 의자와 그 아들들, 포로 만 이천을 싣고 귀국길에 오른다. 성에는 군사 만 명을 남긴다. 그 곁에는 더는 웃어 주지 않는 신라군이 있다.

blocks.html: Across the sea, a confession is waiting for Euija. It is already written, in a lovely hand. It only needs his name…!
blocks.ko: 바다 건너, 의자 앞으로 자백서 한 장이 기다린다. 고운 글씨로 이미 다 써 두었다. 이름 하나만 비어 있다…!

logline.en: In the Western capital, a confession is already written. There’s a space at the bottom for his name.
logline.ko: 서국 도성에는 자백서가 이미 쓰여 있다. 맨 아래에 그의 이름을 쓸 자리가 비어 있다.

images.prompt: 2:1 drama power shot, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop. HIGH ANGLE OVER THE SHOULDER of THE THIRD EMPEROR on the throne dais: sharp dark foreground of his shoulder, black futou cap edge and yellow robe, lit warm by a gilt-bronze lamp-tree beside him. Below and far down the hall at true scale, KING EUIJA kneels alone on the polished dark stone floor, head up, glaring at the throne — one plain undyed WHITE robe, barefoot, long grey-streaked hair LOOSE over his shoulders, no headband, no topknot — two Tang guards with halberds a step behind him. Two lines of officials in dark robes and black caps face inward along the aisle between vermilion columns. The hall doors are open behind Euija: HARD COLD BLUE BACKLIGHT floods in around him, his long shadow stretching up the aisle toward the dais, his white robe and loose hair edged with cold light, the only pale shape in the hall. Incense haze makes the door light visible; candles along the columns reflect in the floor. Colour contrast: warm gold dais vs cold blue doorway. No writing. CANON — KING EUIJA — FACE ONLY from attached /ch_buyeo_euija.png; ignore the portrait's clothing, headgear, jewelry and hair styling — dress exactly as "Now" below (invent a new pose). Now: PRISONER IN THE TANG CAPITAL: broad bearded old king, heavy brows, cynical eyes. One plain undyed WHITE hemp robe and nothing else — no headband, no topknot, no crown, no gold, no crimson, no armor, no belt ornament, barefoot; his long black hair streaked grey hangs LOOSE and unbound past his shoulders; beard unkempt. Demeanor: Licensed wit: drinks, smirks, slumps on the throne, speaks in polished aphorisms. Fatalist. #e08a2e as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: heroic battle pose; smiling innocence. | THE THIRD EMPEROR — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gaozong.png (face only; invent a new pose). #b8935a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | PLACE Chang’an (장안) — attached board /pl_daming_night.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Tang palace of Chang'an, drawn from the Daming Palace (大明宮) site and reconstruction models: Hanyuan Hall's concave ensemble — an eleven-bay hall with a double-eaved hipped roof of dark grey tiles and curled owl-tail ridge ends (chiwei), red columns, white plaster walls, lattice windows, raised on three tiers of rammed-earth terraces faced in ochre-red plaster and edged with white stone balustrades; the Dragon Tail Way ramps folding up the terraces; forward on each side the Xiangluan and Qifeng que-towers (three stepped pavilions on tall battered grey-brick piers) joined to the hall by long roofed corridors; a vast paved square below, entered through the five-doored Danfeng Gate. Wide low Tang proportions, deep eaves on massive bracket sets. Tang palette is VERMILION and WHITE (red columns, white walls); roofs are black-grey tile trimmed with green-glazed ridge and eave tiles (a little yellow and blue tricolour glaze); balustrade posts painted red, blue and green. YELLOW belongs to the emperor's robe; gold is gilt-bronze fittings, lamp-trees and firelight on vermilion. Interiors: dark polished stone floors, rows of vermilion columns, gauze hangings, a raised dais with a painted screen behind the throne. Never the Forbidden City, never all-yellow glazed roofs, never the modern reconstruction or a city skyline. Mood: Staged like a Chinese historical drama (Legend of the Demon Cat, The Longest Day in Chang'an) but lit as full Heewon tenebrism: night or blue hour; ONE dominant hard key per shot — a backlight through open doors or lattice, or one lamp-tree — and 75% of the frame crushed black with no fill; colour contrast — gold-yellow flame highlights against cool blue-green in the few lit shadows; the other flames (lamp-trees, silk lanterns with no writing, braziers) are small points and round bokeh IN the black, never lighting the room evenly; red lantern light through lattice as one pattern on the floor; incense haze only inside the key shaft; polished dark floors reflecting the flames. Staged like a drama, at true human scale: camera at eye or knee height on a dolly or crane; court officials in two lines facing inward along the central aisle with tablets; banquet tables in two long facing rows with dancers in the centre and the emperor on the dais at the head; exteriors are real-scale terraces and corridors, the hall large but never a fantasy fortress. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER canvas, composed like a Romanticist master painting. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is painted with European old-master technique — Renaissance and Baroque oil (Titian, Rembrandt, Tiepolo, Turner): visible broken-colour brushwork, skies scumbled from short loaded dabs, layered glazes in the darks, sfumato edges, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlights — over watercolor wet-in-wet blooms, pigment granulation and faint paper grain; edges of the frame dissolve into paint. LAYOUT is Romanticism (Delacroix, Géricault, Friedrich, Goya, Turner): heroic diagonal or pyramid composition, small figures against a sublime storm sky or vast field, extreme foreshortening (worm’s-eye from the dirt or straight down from above), one break in the clouds or one shaft as the key. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, night-interior cinema): an extreme value range — inky blacks right beside small near-white highlights, almost no middle grey; 70–80% of the frame in deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo and black); ONE hard directional key (a lamp, a single cloud-break, a low sun shaft, firelight) carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock: anamorphic movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain. A CAMERA in a real Korean place — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D archviz, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo. FACE AND GARMENTS from the attached portrait — NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: dutch, crane, worm’s-eye, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key + long shadows — not even daylight wash. ICONIC MINIMAL: ONE architectural device a lens can see; empty negative space; tiny figures or lower-third; the world stays in the shot. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor portrait garments gold. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Not a katana, not a tsuba, not a short jian, not a ball pommel. Real Korean architecture: grey giwa, timber, packed earth. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: movie frame in a real place, not a graphic poster; iconic one-device layout, empty frame, lower-third; high contrast chiaroscuro, not even wash; 2D animated cel-painterly, no photoreal; cinematography: dutch, wide, bokeh, mise-en-scène. Never: halo / bloom / glow aura / emissive skin around figures; graphic split-screen or black-triangle overlay; photoreal live-action or 3D archviz; busy extras crowding an iconic frame; copy-pasted reference as a fashion plate; flat even-daylight postcard wide; katana / tsuba / random sabre length instead of sw_bidam 환두대도.

Tang palace of Chang'an, drawn from the Daming Palace (大明宮) site and reconstruction models: Hanyuan Hall's concave ensemble — an eleven-bay hall with a double-eaved hipped roof of dark grey tiles and curled owl-tail ridge ends (chiwei), red columns, white plaster walls, lattice windows, raised on three tiers of rammed-earth terraces faced in ochre-red plaster and edged with white stone balustrades; the Dragon Tail Way ramps folding up the terraces; forward on each side the Xiangluan and Qifeng que-towers (three stepped pavilions on tall battered grey-brick piers) joined to the hall by long roofed corridors; a vast paved square below, entered through the five-doored Danfeng Gate. Wide low Tang proportions, deep eaves on massive bracket sets. Tang palette is VERMILION and WHITE (red columns, white walls); roofs are black-grey tile trimmed with green-glazed ridge and eave tiles (a little yellow and blue tricolour glaze); balustrade posts painted red, blue and green. YELLOW belongs to the emperor's robe; gold is gilt-bronze fittings, lamp-trees and firelight on vermilion. Interiors: dark polished stone floors, rows of vermilion columns, gauze hangings, a raised dais with a painted screen behind the throne.
