blocks.html: An empire is not finished with a king until he has signed something.
blocks.ko: 제국은 왕에게서 서명 하나를 받아 내기 전까지는, 그 왕과 끝난 게 아니다.

blocks.html: In Chang’an, on the first morning of winter, Euija is brought forth before the Third Emperor.
blocks.ko: 장안, 겨울의 첫 아침. 의자가 세 번째 황제 앞에 끌려 나온다.

blocks.html: First, paperwork. A palace clerk hands the prisoner a confession, already written out in a fair hand. There is a space at the bottom for his name.
blocks.ko: 먼저 서류다. 궁의 서기가 포로에게 자백서를 건넨다. 단정한 글씨로 이미 다 써 놓았다. 맨 아래에 이름 쓸 자리만 비어 있다.

blocks.speaker: Western clerk
en: Aloud, please. Clearly. The scribes are taking it down.
lines: 소리 내어 읽으시오. 또박또박. 사관들이 받아 적고 있소.
zh: 請高聲宣讀，字字清楚。史官在記。
zhLatn: Qǐng gāoshēng xuāndú, zìzì qīngchu. Shǐguān zài jì.

en: ‘I, the criminal Euija, having been liberated by the great West—’
Liberated. Hm. So that’s what that was.
‘—confess with gratitude that without the great West there would be no New Baekje—’
There isn’t one. You burned it.
‘—and resolve to serve the Emperor for ten thousand years.’
Ten thousand? I’m sixty. Ambitious fellow, your clerk.
lines: ‘—대서국이 없었다면 새 백제도 없었음을 감사히 자백하며—’
만세? 내가 예순이다. 야심 한번 크구먼, 너희 서기.

en: It’s a bad story. Nobody’s afraid of anything, there’s no villain, and the hero is a building.
Who wrote this? I’ve done better drunk.
lines: 형편없는 이야기다. 겁나는 것도 없고, 악당도 없고, 주인공이 건물이야.
누가 썼냐? 난 취해서도 이보단 잘 썼다.

blocks.speaker: Western clerk
en: Your name, please. Here.
zhLatn: Qǐng shǔmíng. Zhèlǐ.

blocks.html: He signs in a hand so large the name runs off the edge of the paper, and gives it back. The clerk files it without looking. A confession only needs a name, and has never much minded whose.
blocks.ko: 그는 이름이 종이 끝을 넘어갈 만큼 큼직하게 서명하고 돌려준다. 서기는 보지도 않고 철해 둔다. 자백서에 필요한 건 이름 하나뿐이고, 그게 누구 이름인지는 늘 별로 상관하지 않았다.

blocks.html: Eleventh month, first day. The emperor went up to the Zetian Gate tower to receive the Baekje captives, and released them all, from their king Euija down.
blocks.ko: 11월 초하루 무술일, 황제가 칙천문 누각에 나아가 백제의 포로를 받고, 그 왕 의자 이하를 모두 풀어 주었다.
blocks.hanja: 十一月，戊戌朔，上御則天門樓，受百濟俘，自其王義慈以下皆釋之。
blocks.source: Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 200, Tang Gaozong, Xianqing 5 (660), eleventh month

en: Kim Chunchu…
KIM CHUNCHU!!!

blocks.html: Across the sea, in Surabol, King Muyeol is eating his supper.
blocks.ko: 바다 건너 서라벌에서, 무열왕이 저녁을 들고 있다.

en: Hm?

lines: 삼한의 땅으로 당을 끌어들이는 이 비랄한 만고의 역적아!!
en: Kim Chunchu, you wretch!!
You vile traitor of the ages, who dragged a foreign power onto the soil of Samhan!!
Heaven’s punishment will find you!!

blocks.html: The shouting burns out. What remains is a man who has finally run out of stories to sell — and one last story he cannot afford to keep.
blocks.ko: 고함이 사그라든다. 남은 것은 팔 이야기가 바닥난 사내 — 그리고 더는 쥐고 있을 수 없는 마지막 이야기 하나.

lines: 김춘추 — 네가 끝낸 것을… 끝내지 못하게…!
en: Let someone… avenge me…!
Let someone… raise Baekje again…!
Chunchu — what you finished… may it never stay finished…!

blocks.html: He is shouting at the man who won. Across the sea, a quiet son with lovely handwriting is still waiting to be needed.
blocks.ko: 그는 이긴 사내를 향해 소리치고 있다. 바다 건너에서는, 글씨가 고운 조용한 아들 하나가 아직도 누군가 자기를 필요로 해 주기를 기다리고 있다.

blocks.html: Then the room fills with men only he can see.
blocks.ko: 그때 방이 그에게만 보이는 이들로 찬다.

en: Gods are props. Spirits are lighting.
Heh… so y’all are real after all…
Any last words?

blocks.html: Euija waits. He has always been good at making a room lean in.
blocks.ko: 의자는 기다린다. 그는 언제나 방을 기울게 만드는 데 능했다.

en: No.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads his name three times in the Western capital — Euija. Euija. Euija. — the underworld's receipt before the humiliation finishes.
blocks.ko: 강림은 서국의 도읍에서 그의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 의자. 의자. 의자. — 능욕이 끝나기 전 저승의 영수증처럼.

lines: 사람들은 당신을 해동증자라 불렀소. 당신은 구경꾼들 보라고 사비강 위에 용을 띄웠고. 어느 쪽이었소?
en: Eraha. King.
One question, then we walk.
They called you the Zengzi of the East. You hung a dragon over the Sabi for a crowd. Which were you?

lines: 용은 수백 명이 봤어. 증자가 뭘 허는 건 아무두 못 봤구.
en: …The dragon. Obviously.
Several hundred people saw the dragon. Nobody ever saw a Zengzi do anything.

lines: 당신이 준 이름이 아직 명부에 있소.
en: The boy at the White River.
The name you gave him is still in the ledger.
…A friend.
Put the miracle on the cheap side of the page.

blocks.html: A jar in a hedge, and a prince who ought to be at his own investiture.
blocks.ko: 울타리 밑의 술 단지 하나. 제 책봉식에 가 있어야 할 왕자 하나.

blocks.html: A grey hood at the back of a crowd. A boy going into black water on a rope.
blocks.ko: 구경꾼들 맨 뒤의 회색 두건. 밧줄 하나에 매달려 검은 물로 들어가는 아이.

en: How many times have you gone in?
Nineteen.

blocks.html: A pale deer in the reeds, standing where nobody else is up to see it.
blocks.ko: 갈대숲의 흰 사슴 한 마리. 아무도 깨어 있지 않은 자리에 서 있다.

lines: …그 이름이 마음에 드십니까, 제가 마음에 드십니까?
en: …Do you like the name, or do you like me?

lines: 너였어, 이 바보야. 이름은 그냥 그때 내가 가진 것 중에 젤 좋은 거였구.
en: …You.
It was you, you idiot. The name was just the best thing I had on me.

lines: 그는 나루에서 기다리고 있소. 직접 말해 주시오. 그 사람은 정확히 말해 줘야 알아들으니.
그렇다면 당신은 기록이 인정하는 것보다 부자로 죽는 거요.
en: He is waiting at the ford. Tell him yourself. He will want it said exactly.
Then you die richer than the record will admit.
Come.

lines: 강 위에 용 한 마리 걸어 놓고
성 마흔 개 뺏고 꿈에서 깼네
en: Buyeo Euija, good little son,
laughed like a drum and ruled for fun.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Hung up a dragon over the stream,
took forty forts, and woke from the dream.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Far from home in a cold grey hall:
angry, then empty, then nothing at all.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
blocks.title: Euija, Zengzi of the East

blocks.caption: Buyeo Euija, the last king of Baekje. The Zengzi of the East.
blocks.ko: 백제의 마지막 왕 부여의자. 해동증자.

blocks.html: Euija served his parents with a devotion people talked about, and was kind to his brothers; men of his time called him the Zeng and Min of the East. He reached the capital and died a few days later.
blocks.ko: 의자는 어버이를 효성으로 섬겨 이름이 났고 형제와 우애하니, 당시 사람들이 ‘해동의 증자·민자’라 불렀다. 경사에 이르러 며칠 만에 죽었다.
blocks.hanja: 義慈事親以孝行聞，友于兄弟，時人號「海東曾、閔」。及至京，數日而卒。
blocks.source: Jiu Tangshu (舊唐書) bk. 199A, Eastern Barbarians — Baekje

blocks.html: — Buyeo Euija —
blocks.ko: — 부여의자 —

blocks.html: Sunchung told him. He put Sunchung in a cell. Hungsu told him. He had already exiled Hungsu. Gyebek would have told him, and he had put Gyebek on a boat. A man does not fall because nobody warned him. He falls because he arranged, patiently and over years, to be somewhere the warnings could not reach.
blocks.ko: 성충이 말했다. 그는 성충을 옥에 가두었다. 흥수가 말했다. 그는 이미 흥수를 내쫓은 뒤였다. 계백이라면 말했을 것이다. 그리고 그는 계백을 배에 태워 보냈다. 사람은 아무도 경고하지 않아서 무너지지 않는다. 여러 해에 걸쳐 참을성 있게, 경고가 닿을 수 없는 곳에 제 자리를 마련해 두었기 때문에 무너진다.

blocks.html: The Zengzi of the East. They called him that when he was young, and they meant it. The name was neither flattery nor wrong. He was never a fool. He was a clever man who won, and kept winning, until winning was the only instrument he had left, and then he tried to play a dying country on it.
blocks.ko: 해동증자. 젊은 시절 사람들은 그를 그렇게 불렀고, 진심이었다. 아첨도 아니고 틀린 말도 아니었다. 그는 결코 어리석지 않았다. 그는 이기고 또 이긴 영리한 사람이었고, 마침내 이기는 것 말고는 남은 악기가 없어졌을 때, 죽어 가는 나라를 그것으로 연주하려 했다.

blocks.html: Baekje is gone. Goguryeo still stands. And the man who arranged both can no longer get out of bed…?
blocks.ko: 백제는 사라졌다. 고구려는 아직 서 있다. 그리고 그 둘을 꾸민 사내가, 더는 자리에서 일어나지 못한다…?

logline.en: The man who arranged all of it is fifty-eight, and cannot get out of bed.
logline.ko: 이 모든 것을 꾸민 사내는 쉰여덟이고, 침상에서 일어나지 못한다.

images.at: a monk who knows when not to speak
images.alt: In a temple side hall, Munhee sits upright beside the dying Chunchu, her hand over his.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Interior late night, a quiet temple side hall at the edge of Surabol. Low WORM'S-EYE from the floor at the foot of the sick-mat. ONE device: a single thread of incense smoke rising straight up from a bronze burner on the floor. Munhee, FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, fifty-five, hair dressed with the attached binyeo, sitting very upright beside the mat, one hand resting on the blanket over his hand, eyes on him, dry-eyed and steely. King Muyeol (Chunchu), FACE ONLY from the attached portrait, lying under the blanket, head turned toward her, a faint tired smile; his crown rests on a stand in the shadow. A clay lamp on the floor rakes gold up across her face and the folds; magenta #D8258C as a small specular on his silk collar. Background: a dim gilt Buddha barely readable in the dark. CANON — QUEEN MUNMYUNG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_munmyung.png (face only; invent a new pose). Hair ornament matches attached /bn_munhee.png when the head is visible. Crown: Silla gold crown, as the attached crown: a gold band with three tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. ref_muyeol shows it worn with the king's red robe and gold-scroll collar (ignore its painted backdrop). Demeanor: Yushin's younger sister, Chunchu's wife; quick and warm, the one who bought the dream. #E07FA8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: fantasy tiara instead of her binyeo. | KING MUYEOL — FACE and garments from attached /ch_muyeol.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Slim and elegant; shoulder-length loose black hair parted in the middle; thin moustache and goatee stubble; amused eyes, small knowing smile. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. Crown: Silla gold crown, as the attached crown: a gold band with three tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. ref_muyeol shows it worn with the king's red robe and gold-scroll collar (ignore its painted backdrop). Now: King Muyeol (stage portrait): royal robes and crown; heavier, tired eyes. Demeanor: Diplomat and strategist: talks with his hands, smiles while calculating, never shouts; half-lidded watchful eyes. #D8258C as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: front-line armored warrior pose; shouting battle face; katana. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. | PLACE Surabol (서라벌 (경주)) — attached board /pl_eastern_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Seorabeol palace: Silla giwa halls, packed-earth yards, timber verandas. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). COMMONERS in every Samhan kingdom wear SIMPLE WHITE: plain undyed white or off-white hemp and ramie jackets, wide trousers and skirts, a cloth sash, straw sandals or bare feet, hair in a plain topknot or braid — no dyed silk, no dots, no gold; colour belongs to rank, so a crowd of farmers, porters, servants and townsfolk reads as a field of soft white cloth with the officials' colours standing out of it. Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. Only the people, their faces and dress, the place and the hour change, so the two frames line up like a before-and-after. Ignore the layout picture's faces, clothes and colours. The same shot. King Munmu, Bupmin grown, thirty-five, takes the crown with a soldier's set jaw. The spirit line behind him: King Muyeol (his father Chunchu) nearest, faintly smiling, then Queen Jinduk, then Queen Sunduk and the older kings fading into haze. REFERENCE SHEET. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. Unmistakably Korean face: BLACK eyes (never brown, blue or grey), a small straight Korean nose with a low bridge, smooth oval face. Dress: Magenta-crimson silk po with a charcoal sash, dark layered collar. Silk even on campaign. blocks.html: Chunchu has talked his way out of every room in Samhan. This one has no other door.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 삼한의 모든 방에서 말로 빠져나왔다. 이 방에는 다른 문이 없다.

blocks.label: The Sickroom
blocks.ko: 병석

blocks.html: It is the sixth month of 661. Baekje has fallen, Goguryeo has not, and the man who arranged both is fifty-eight and cannot get out of bed.
blocks.ko: 661년 유월이다. 백제는 무너졌고 고구려는 아직 서 있으며, 그 둘을 모두 꾸민 사내는 쉰여덟에 자리에서 일어나지 못한다.

blocks.html: Yushin comes in the afternoon, still in his riding boots, and stands where a marshal stands, which is too close to the door.
blocks.ko: 유신은 오후에 온다. 아직 승마 장화를 신은 채, 장수가 서는 자리에 선다. 문에 너무 가까운 자리다.

en: The West want us at Pyongyang by winter.
I told them you were rather busy.

lines: 바쁘지요. 죽는 것도 하루 품이 꽉 차는 일이더군요.
형님, 오늘은 쫌 앉으소. 형님이 서 있으믄 방이 성문 같소.
en: Busy. Yes. Dying turns out to be a full day’s work.
Brother, do sit down for once. You make the room look like a gate.
I’ll stand.

lines: …북으로 데려가 주소. 법민이를. 저 애는 성벽에 돌격하고 싶어 할 끼요. 돌격하게 두지 마소.
en: Of course you will.
…Take him north for me. Bupmin. He’ll want to charge the walls. Don’t let him charge the walls.
I won’t.

blocks.html: That is the whole goodbye. They have been saying the rest of it for forty years.
blocks.ko: 작별은 그게 다다. 나머지는 마흔 해 동안 이미 해 왔다.

blocks.html: Munhee (55) sits where she has sat since the spring. Outside the door a monk who knows when not to speak keeps the incense going. Forty years ago she bought a dream off her sister for a silk skirt. This is where the dream comes out: a sickroom, a husband, and a son at the foot of the bed.
blocks.ko: 문희(55)는 봄부터 앉아 있던 그 자리에 앉아 있다. 문밖에서는 말을 아낄 줄 아는 스님 하나가 향을 지킨다. 마흔 해 전, 그녀는 비단 치마 한 벌로 언니의 꿈을 샀다. 그 꿈이 닿은 곳이 여기다. 병실 하나, 남편 하나, 그리고 침상 발치에 선 아들 하나.

en: Munhee. Have I… paid all of it?
Not yet. I’ll pay the rest.
Do you remember the skirt?
It was a very good skirt.
Don’t make me cry in front of the boy.
Best bargain in Silla.

lines: 두 번째지예. 법민아, 문간에 서 있지 말고. 퍼뜩 들어온나.
en: Second best. Bupmin, don’t stand in the door. Come in, quick.

blocks.html: He looks past her, to the boy who is no longer a boy. Bupmin (35) has his mother’s stillness and his father’s hunger, and for a moment the room holds all three of them the way a hill once held a promise.
blocks.ko: 그는 문희 너머로, 더 이상 아이가 아닌 아이를 본다. 법민 (35)에게는 어머니의 고요와 아버지의 허기가 있다. 잠시, 방이 예전 언덕이 약속을 품듯 셋 모두를 품는다.

en: Bupmin.
Father.

lines: 사람들은… 이 전쟁이 오직 니 누이를 위한 줄 알 끼다.
그것도 맞다. 대야는 하루도 이 방을 나간 적이 없데이.
en: People will say… this whole war was only for your sister.
Gotaso.
And they will not be wrong. Daeya never left this room for a single day.

lines: 하지만 그기 내가 갚던 유일한 빚은 아이었다.
언젠가 언덕에서, 네 외숙과 함께, 내가 한 말이 있다. “만인의 왕.”
en: But that was never the only debt.
On a hill once, with your uncle, I said a thing. “A king for all.”
Not a king of Silla. Of everyone.

lines: 그걸 지가 훔쳤다 아입니꺼. 여섯 살 때. 밥상머리에서 그 말만—
en: And I stole it. I was six. I used to say it at dinner—

lines: 너는 그 말을 틀리게 했지. 입 안에서 말이 삐뚤게 앉아 있었다.
내가 먼저 했다. 네가 가져갔고. 아이들은 그렇게 훔친다. 방 안에서 제일 큰 것을 가져가지.
나는 백제까지 길을 텄다. 고구려는 아직 서 있고, 당은 웃고 있을 끼다.
나머지는 — 왕으로서 걸어라. 내 복수로서가 아니라. 네가 여섯 살 때 바라던 나라로서.
en: You said it wrong. The word sat crooked in your mouth.
I said it first. You took it. That is how children steal. They take the largest thing in the room.
I cleared the road as far as Baekje. Goguryeo is still standing, and the West will be smiling.
The rest — walk it as king. Not as my revenge. As the country you wanted when you were six.
…I promise.
Bupmin… I love you.

blocks.html: The escort arrives on schedule.
blocks.ko: 호위가 시간에 맞춰 도착한다.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads the name three times — Muyeol. Muyeol. Muyeol. The room still knows him as Chunchu.
blocks.ko: 강림이 그 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 무열. 무열. 무열. 방 안은 아직 그를 춘추로 안다.

lines: 전에 만난 적이 있소. 대야성에서. 당신은 나를 보지 않았지. 이름 적힌 명단을 보고 있었으니.
en: King Muyeol.
We have met before, at Daeya. You weren’t looking at me. You were looking at a list of names.

lines: 의자가 하늘이 나를 찾아낼 거라 저주했지.
en: Euija swore heaven would find me.
…Is this heaven?

lines: 아니오. 이건 열병이오. 하늘은 왕진을 오지 않소. 오는 건 나요.
질문 하나 하고 갑시다. 고타소를 위해서였소, 아니면 만인의 왕을 위해서였소?
en: No. This is a fever. Heaven does not make house calls. I do.
One question, then we walk. Was it for Gotaso, or for the king for all?
…Yes.
That is not one of the two.

lines: 바둑에서 돌 하나를 한 가지 이유로 놓는 사람은 없소.
두 칸에 다 적으시오. 장부에 칸이 둘은 있을 테니.
en: In go, nobody plays a stone for one reason.
Write it in both columns. Your ledger has two, I assume.

lines: 갑시다. 길이 머니, 가는 내내 말하고 싶을 거요.
en: It does. I will.
Come. The road is long, and you will want to talk the whole way.
Kim Chunchu, bend the knee —
to tyrant, to emperor, never Baekje.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Lost his daughter one burning night,
spent all his clever to make it right.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Baekje’s gone and Goguryeo stands —
half the job in his son’s two hands.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
blocks.title: Chunchu Who Knelt

blocks.caption: Kim Chunchu, King Muyeol of Silla. He knelt to everyone but Baekje.
blocks.ko: 신라 무열왕 김춘추. 백제 말고는 누구에게나 무릎을 꿇었다.

lines: …다들한테 무릎을 꿇은 양반이다. 연개소문한테도, 황제한테도. 문 잡아 줄 사람이믄 누구한테든.
일어나라, 법민아. 인자 니가 왕이다. 왕은 침상 옆에서 무릎 꿇는 거 아이다.
en: …He knelt to everyone. Gesomun. The emperor. Anyone who would hold a door.
Never once to Baekje.
Get up, Bupmin. You’re the king now. Kings don’t kneel by beds.

blocks.html: He died with Baekje gone and Goguryeo still standing. Halfway. The last two names he said were his daughter’s and his son’s. Not the kingdom’s.
blocks.ko: 그는 백제가 사라지고 고구려는 아직 서 있는 채로 죽었다. 절반에서. 그가 마지막으로 부른 두 이름은 딸의 이름과 아들의 이름이었다. 나라의 이름이 아니었다.

blocks.html: Twelve years earlier an emperor had told him that Goguryeo was the one failure of his life, and that Baekje would be Chunchu’s. Only one of them was wrong.
blocks.ko: 십이 년 전, 한 황제가 그에게 고려는 제 인생의 유일한 실패이며 백제는 그대의 실패가 될 것이라 했다. 둘 중 한 사람만 틀렸다.

blocks.html: They give him a name for the dead: Muyeol. His temple name is Tejong, the same name the West gave their Second Emperor. Chang’an will notice.
blocks.ko: 그에게 죽은 자의 이름이 붙는다. 무열. 묘호는 태종이다. 당이 두 번째 황제에게 붙인 바로 그 이름이다. 장안이 그냥 넘어가지 않을 것이다.

blocks.hanja: 姿表英特，聰明多智略。
blocks.html: He was striking in looks and bearing, quick-witted and full of stratagems.
blocks.ko: 자태와 풍채가 영특하고, 총명하여 지략이 많았다.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, accession notice

blocks.html: Bupmin takes the throne. They will call him Munmu.
blocks.ko: 법민이 왕위에 오른다. 사람들은 그를 문무라 부를 것이다.

blocks.html: Silla won the war. So why does the emperor’s new edict call its king a clerk…?
blocks.ko: 전쟁은 신라가 이겼다. 그런데 황제의 새 칙서는 왜 신라 왕을 고을 원님으로 적는가…?

logline.en: The West throw a net over the country. A sixty-year-old in white comes to mend it.
logline.ko: 당은 이 나라에 그물을 던진다. 흰 옷을 입은 예순 노인이 그 그물을 기우러 온다.

images.alt: Ink-painted poster: the Third Emperor, in grey ink wash, points east from a palace terrace as the gold dragon spirals up out of a black ink storm
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; heads and the dragon’s head stay inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Storm dusk on a high terrace of the Daming Palace: balustrades and owl-tail roof ridges as black calligraphic strokes, a sky of splashed black ink. Worm’s-eye from the terrace floor. TWO SUBJECTS: a human-scale emperor AND a huge dragon. INTERACTION: the Third Emperor, young and uncertain, stands at the balustrade with his arm thrown out pointing east; the gold Tang dragon Huanglong (gold ink-brush dragon from the attached board, three claws) spirals up past him into the black storm, its body curling once loosely around his outstretched arm before it uncoils skyward, its head turned east along his pointing hand. One gold break in the storm (#b8935a) catches his face, his arm and the dragon’s coils. TANG RENDER: predominantly DARK and INTIMIDATING Chinese ink painting (shuimohua) on rice paper — heavy black and grey ink washes, wet-on-wet ink bleeding, splashed ink smoke and storm, dry calligraphic brush strokes for roofs, columns, robes and cloud, ink splatters and drips at the frame edges, bare paper only where the edges dissolve; the gold ink-brush dragon is the main colour in the dark, with a few small vermilion and flame accents. Every figure, the Third Emperor included, is ink-painted in the same black-and-grey wash with only a thin wash of dull yellow on his robe; no full-colour figure in the frame. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, big dark masses, one bright break of light, NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp, no calligraphy characters. Not photoreal, not 3D, not a realistic scaled dragon. No glow aura, no halo — the accent is real light. One of each named person. No watermark. CANON — THE THIRD EMPEROR — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gaozong.png (face only; invent a new pose). #b8935a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. | HUANGLONG (황룡, taizong's yellow dragon, guardian of the Tang throne) — attached board /obj_yellow_dragon.png: TANG-DYNASTY dragon painted in gold ink-brush: lean long-necked serpentine body in an S-curve, four lean leonine legs striding, THREE claws on each foot, long open-jawed snout with fangs, two backswept horns, whiskers and mane flung out as dry calligraphic gold brush strokes, whip tail ending in a flame tuft; burnished gold-yellow scales with ochre-umber shading — match the board, not a later Ming/Qing five-claw dragon, never a realistic scaled 3D dragon. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, coiling through black ink cloud and lamp smoke; light catches the scales as real light, never a glow outline. Its stills are predominantly dark and intimidating Chinese ink painting: splashed black ink, smoke, the gold dragon the main colour in the dark; every figure is ink-painted except the Second Emperor, who stays a full-colour webtoon figure. Owned by no one but sits behind whoever holds the dais; it coils over Chang'an and turns its head only for the Son of Heaven. | PLACE Chang’an (장안) — attached board /pl_daming_night.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Tang palace of Chang'an, drawn from the Daming Palace (大明宮) site and reconstruction models: Hanyuan Hall's concave ensemble — an eleven-bay hall with a double-eaved hipped roof of dark grey tiles and curled owl-tail ridge ends (chiwei), red columns, white plaster walls, lattice windows, raised on three tiers of rammed-earth terraces faced in ochre-red plaster and edged with white stone balustrades; the Dragon Tail Way ramps folding up the terraces; forward on each side the Xiangluan and Qifeng que-towers (three stepped pavilions on tall battered grey-brick piers) joined to the hall by long roofed corridors; a vast paved square below, entered through the five-doored Danfeng Gate. Wide low Tang proportions, deep eaves on massive bracket sets. Tang palette is VERMILION and WHITE (red columns, white walls); roofs are black-grey tile trimmed with green-glazed ridge and eave tiles (a little yellow and blue tricolour glaze); balustrade posts painted red, blue and green. YELLOW belongs to the emperor's robe; gold is gilt-bronze fittings, lamp-trees and firelight on vermilion. Interiors: dark polished stone floors, rows of vermilion columns, gauze hangings, a raised dais with a painted screen behind the throne. Never the Forbidden City, never all-yellow glazed roofs, never the modern reconstruction or a city skyline. Mood: TANG RENDER: predominantly DARK and INTIMIDATING Chinese ink painting (shuimohua) — black and grey ink washes, wet-on-wet ink bleeding into rice paper, dry calligraphic brush for roofs, columns, smoke and robes, the vermilion and gold reduced to small accents in a world of ink; officials, guards and other Tang figures are ink figures too. The ONE exception is the Second Emperor himself: he keeps the house webtoon figure render in full colour (yellow robe, black futou, drawn face), a coloured man inside an ink empire. Staged like a Chinese historical drama (Legend of the Demon Cat, The Longest Day in Chang'an) but lit as full Heewon tenebrism: night or blue hour; ONE dominant hard key per shot — a backlight through open doors or lattice, or one lamp-tree — and 75% of the frame crushed black with no fill; colour contrast — gold-yellow flame highlights against cool blue-green in the few lit shadows; the other flames (lamp-trees, silk lanterns with no writing, braziers) are small points and round bokeh IN the black, never lighting the room evenly; red lantern light through lattice as one pattern on the floor; incense haze only inside the key shaft; polished dark floors reflecting the flames. Staged like a drama, at true human scale: camera at eye or knee height on a dolly or crane; court officials in two lines facing inward along the central aisle with tablets; banquet tables in two long facing rows with dancers in the centre and the emperor on the dais at the head; exteriors are real-scale terraces and corridors, the hall large but never a fantasy fortress. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: In Chang’an, the cheapest way to conquer a country is to rename it.
blocks.ko: 장안에서 나라 하나를 정복하는 가장 싼 방법은, 그 나라의 이름을 바꾸는 것이다.

blocks.label: The Spoils
blocks.ko: 전리품

blocks.label: Chang’an
blocks.ko: 장안

blocks.html: The Red Fowl is home with his captives. The emperor asks him a question in front of the whole court, which is how emperors ask questions they already know the answer to.
blocks.ko: 주작이 포로들을 데리고 돌아왔다. 황제는 온 조정 앞에서 그에게 묻는다. 황제들은 답을 이미 아는 질문을 그렇게 묻는다.

lines: 경이 군대를 끌고 거기 있었는데, 어째서 내친김에 신라까지 치지 않았소?
en: You were there with an army. Why didn’t you take Silla while you were at it?
zh: 卿既在彼，何不因而伐新羅？
zhLatn: Qīng jì zài bǐ, hé bù yīn ér fá Xīnluó?

lines: 그 임금은 어질어 백성을 아끼고, 신하들은 충성으로 나라를 섬기며, 아랫사람은 윗사람을 아비와 형처럼 섬깁니다.
작은 나라이나, 꾀로 도모할 수는 없습니다.
en: Their king is kind and loves his people. His ministers serve the country loyally. Below, they serve those above like fathers and elder brothers.
It is a small country, Majesty. But it cannot be schemed against.
zh: 新羅其君仁而愛民，其臣忠以事國，下之人事其上如父兄。
zhLatn: Xīnluó qí jūn rén ér ài mín, qí chén zhōng yǐ shì guó, xià zhī rén shì qí shàng rú fù xiōng.
Suī xiǎo, bù kě móu yě.

lines: 그럼 꾀 말고 글로 하지요. 그 나라 임금을 우리 도독으로 삼으면— 아니. 뺨 때리는 소리 같군요.
en: Can’t be schemed against. Hm.
Then we won’t scheme. We’ll write. Make their king a governor of ours — no. That sounds like a slap.
…Write it anyway.

lines: 절하면서 받아야 하는 뺨 한 대가, 되돌려 칠 수 있는 뺨 두 대보다 값져요.
en: Make it sound like an honour, Majesty.
A slap they have to bow for is worth two they can return.

blocks.label: Gyerim
blocks.ko: 계림

blocks.html: Then an edict arrives for the new king. It makes him Grand Commander of the Gyerim Prefecture. Gyerim is his country’s oldest name, the wood where a rooster crowed over a golden box. In the edict it is one province of the empire. And the king is its governor.
blocks.ko: 이윽고 새 임금 앞으로 칙서가 온다. 그를 계림주 대도독으로 삼는다는 내용이다. 계림은 이 나라의 가장 오래된 이름이다. 닭이 금궤 위에서 울던 숲. 칙서 안에서 그곳은 제국의 한 고을이다. 그리고 임금은 그 고을 원이다.

lines: 주라 카오, 외숙. 아버님의 나라를 주로 만들고, 나를 그 고을 원으로 삼았소.
en: A prefecture, Uncle. They have made my father’s country into a prefecture, and me its clerk.
Then sign as its clerk, Majesty.
And keep a copy.

blocks.html: The court is angrier than the king. Men in the Council hall who have not agreed on anything since the old queen died agree that a prefecture is an insult, and say so loudly, in rooms where no the Western officer is present.
blocks.ko: 조정은 왕보다 더 화가 났다. 옛 여왕이 죽은 뒤로 무엇 하나 합의해 본 적 없는 회의장의 사내들이, 주라니 모욕이라는 데에는 뜻을 모은다. 그리고 서국의 관리가 없는 방에서 큰 소리로 그렇게 말한다.

blocks.html: Only Deto, a smooth councillor who always urges the softer word, keeps his voice down.
blocks.ko: 부드러운 말을 권하는 게 일인 매끄러운 신하, 대토만이 목소리를 낮춘다.

lines: 그쪽 역법 보셨어요? 하루하루가 딱딱 맞아떨어집니다. 우리 책력은 동지가 언제인지도 저 혼자 우기는데.
en: They’re not wrong about everything, you know.
Have you seen their calendar? Every day accounted for. Our almanac can’t even agree with itself about the solstice.

blocks.html: Nobody answers him. A few men remember afterwards that he said it.
blocks.ko: 아무도 대꾸하지 않는다. 몇몇은 뒷날 그가 그 말을 했다는 것을 기억해 낸다.

blocks.label: Restoration
blocks.ko: 부흥

blocks.label: The Black Tortoise
blocks.ko: 현무

blocks.html: Someone has to hold what the West broke. Nobody in Chang’an expected to see Liu Rengui in uniform again. He is sixty. Last year he lost a grain fleet in a storm and was stripped of office. Now he comes east as a commoner in white, to earn it back. In his baggage: the Western calendar, and the list of names nobody may write.
blocks.ko: 당이 부순 것을 누군가는 붙들고 있어야 한다. 장안의 누구도 유인궤가 다시 군복을 입으리라 생각하지 않았다. 그는 예순이다. 지난해 폭풍에 군량선단을 잃고 관직을 빼앗겼다. 이제 그는 흰옷 입은 평민으로 동쪽에 와서 그것을 되찾으려 한다. 짐 속에는 서국의 달력과, 아무도 써서는 안 되는 이름들의 목록이 들어 있다.

blocks.caption: The Black Tortoise. Sixty, disgraced last year, and in an excellent mood.
blocks.ko: 현무. 예순, 작년에 파직당했고, 기분이 아주 좋다.

lines: 하늘이 이 늙은이를 부귀하게 하시려나 보오.
이 나라에 쓸 역서를 보내 주시오. 써서는 안 될 이름 목록도. 동쪽을 쓸어 평정할 거라면, 동쪽도 적어도 지금이 몇 년인지는 알아야지.
en: Heaven means to make an old man rich, it seems.
Send me the calendar for this country, and the list of names one must not write. If we are going to sweep the east clean, the east should at least know what year it is.
zh: 請頒曆及宗廟諱。吾欲掃平東夷，頒大唐正朔於海表。
zhLatn: Tiān jiāng fùguì cǐ wēng ěr.
Qǐng bān lì jí zōngmiào huì. Wú yù sǎopíng dōngyí, bān Dà Táng zhēngshuò yú hǎibiǎo.

blocks.html: Between skirmishes the Black Tortoise does what he actually came for, which is paperwork. He counts the households of Baekje village by village and writes them down as numbers. He mends dykes and bridges. He posts the Western calendar at every crossroads, with the list of names that may not be written, so that the people of Baekje will know which characters to leave out of their letters home.
blocks.ko: 싸움과 싸움 사이에 현무는 정말로 하러 온 일을 한다. 서류다. 백제의 호구를 마을마다 세어 숫자로 적는다. 둑과 다리를 고친다. 갈림길마다 서국의 달력을 붙이고, 써서는 안 되는 이름의 목록도 함께 붙인다. 백제 사람들이 집에 보내는 편지에서 어떤 글자를 빼야 하는지 알도록.

lines: 올해가 몇 년인지 아는 마을은 세금을 제때 내오.
나루에도 하나 붙이시오. 사람은 배를 기다리면서 읽으니까.
en: A village that knows what year it is pays its tax on time.
Put one up at the ferry as well. People read while they wait for the boat.
zh: 渡口也貼一張。人等船時會讀。
zhLatn: Zhī niánsuì zhī cūn, nàshuì bú wù.
Dùkǒu yě tiē yì zhāng. Rén děng chuán shí huì dú.

blocks.label: The Ferry
blocks.ko: 나루

blocks.html: The ferry calendar lasts four days. On the fifth morning it is still on its post, untouched, which is worse. Someone has added a line to the bottom of the list of names one must not write. The charcoal is still soft.
blocks.ko: 나루의 달력은 나흘을 버틴다. 닷새째 아침에도 그것은 기둥에 멀쩡히 붙어 있다. 그게 더 나쁘다. 누군가 써서는 안 되는 이름 목록 맨 아래에 한 줄을 보탰다. 숯이 아직 무르다.

blocks.speaker: Western clerk
en: Shall I scrape it off, General?
Read it to me first.

blocks.speaker: Western clerk
en: “Buyeo Pung.” And under it: “Gwishil Boksin, who sends his regards.”

lines: 왕자 하나, 그리고 쪽지에 제 이름을 적는 사내 하나라.
en: A prince, and a man who signs his notes.
Who is the prince?

blocks.speaker: Western clerk
lines: 의자의 아들입니다, 장군. 조용한 놈이요. 어릴 때 동조정에 보냈답니다.
en: Euija’s son, General. The quiet one. They sent him to the Eastern court as a boy.

lines: 그럼 내가 곧 쓰지 못하게 될 이름을 미리 알려 주는 셈이군.
베껴 두시오. 두 벌. 원본은 그대로 붙여 두고. 내가 읽었다는 걸 그자가 알도록.
en: Then they are telling me which name I will soon be forbidden to write.
Copy it. Twice. And leave the original up. I want him to know I read it.

blocks.label: The Fires
blocks.ko: 불

blocks.html: That night the hills around Sabi light up. One fire, then forty. Boksin has brought the restoration to the West’s front door, and the garrison inside has ten days of rice.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 사비를 둘러싼 산들에 불이 켜진다. 하나, 그리고 마흔. 복신이 부흥군을 서국의 앞문까지 끌고 왔고, 성 안 수비대에게는 열흘 치 쌀이 남았다.

blocks.html: The Black Tortoise has no cavalry to speak of and no reputation left to lose. What he has is a census. He counted those villages a month ago. He knows which of them fed the fires, and which are short of men tonight.
blocks.ko: 현무에게는 내세울 기병도, 더 잃을 명성도 없다. 그에게 있는 것은 호적이다. 한 달 전에 그 마을들을 세었다. 어느 마을이 저 불에 쌀을 댔는지, 오늘 밤 어느 마을에 사내가 모자란지 안다.

lines: 쌀 나르는 길을 막으시오. 정중하게. 수레는 하나하나 다 적고.
en: Not the hills. The villages behind them.
Close the roads they bring the rice on. Politely. Write down every cart.

blocks.html: It takes nine days. On the tenth the fires around Sabi go out one by one, the way they were lit, and the rebels walk back up into the hills to a fortress called Imjon. They are not beaten. They are waiting for somebody.
blocks.ko: 아흐레가 걸린다. 열흘째, 사비를 둘러싼 불들이 켜질 때처럼 하나씩 꺼지고, 부흥군은 임존이라는 성으로 산을 걸어 올라간다. 진 게 아니다. 누군가를 기다리는 것이다.

lines: 다시 올 거요. 먼저 왕을 모셔 와야 하니.
en: He’ll be back. He has to fetch a king first.

blocks.label: The Maps
blocks.ko: 지도

blocks.html: In Chang’an the Third Emperor is told that Baekje is finished and that its king has died in the capital of a broken heart, and he takes out his father’s maps.
blocks.ko: 장안에서 세 번째 황제는 백제가 끝났고 그 왕이 도성에서 상심하여 죽었다는 말을 듣는다. 그리고 아버지의 지도를 꺼낸다.

lines: 아버님은 동쪽에 세 번 가셨다가 기침을 하며 돌아오셨지.
백제는 고구려 등 뒤의 칼이었고, 이제 그 칼을 우리가 쥐었어 — 아니. 이건 아버님이 하실 말 같군. 그래도 적어 두게.
en: Father went east three times and came home coughing.
Baekje was the knife at Goguryeo’s back, and now we’re holding it — no. That sounds like something he would say. Write it down anyway.

lines: 장수 넷이요. 지도 네 귀퉁이에 하나씩. 그래야 아무도 혼자 했다고 우기며 돌아오지 못하죠.
en: Then don’t say it like him. Say it like you.
Four generals. One for each side of the map, so none of them can come home claiming he did it alone.

blocks.html: That is how the Four Beasts are chosen: by a woman who knows how generals talk at banquets.
blocks.ko: 사신(四神)은 그렇게 뽑힌다. 장수들이 잔치에서 무슨 말을 하는지 아는 여자에 의해.

blocks.label: The Four Beasts
blocks.ko: 사신

blocks.html: The Third Emperor launches the Eighth Invasion of Goguryeo — his father’s war, inherited along with everything else.
blocks.ko: 황제가 제8차 고구려 원정을 일으킨다. 다른 모든 것과 함께 물려받은, 아버지의 전쟁이다.

blocks.title: Four Beasts · 사신
blocks.caption: Gaozong’s expeditionary colours: White Tiger, Red Fowl, Blue Dragon, Black Tortoise.
blocks.ko: 고종의 동정 색깔. 백호, 주작, 청룡, 현무.

blocks.html: Samhan never learns their names. It learns their banners, which is the entire purpose of a banner.
blocks.ko: 삼한은 끝내 그들의 이름을 배우지 않는다. 깃발을 배운다. 깃발이란 원래 그러라고 있는 것이다.

blocks.html: The Silla envoy is still in the hall. The emperor turns to him last.
blocks.ko: 신라 사신이 아직 전각에 있다. 황제는 마지막으로 그를 돌아본다.

lines: 백제는 끝났소. 그대 왕의 근심은 내가 덜어 주었소.
이제 고구려요. 돌아가서 왕에게 군사를 이끌고 북으로 오라 전하시오.
이제 우리 달력이 있으니, 날짜도 전하시오.
en: Baekje is done. I have taken your king’s worry off his hands.
Now Goguryeo. Go home and tell him to bring his army north.
He has our calendar now. Tell him the date.

blocks.html: Baekje has no king. Across the sea, an exiled prince is packing his bags…!
blocks.ko: 백제에는 임금이 없다. 바다 건너, 쫓겨난 왕자 하나가 짐을 꾸린다…!

logline.en: Baekje is finished, says everyone except Baekje. Its last prince has lived across the sea for twenty years.
logline.ko: 백제는 끝났다고 다들 말한다. 백제만 빼고. 마지막 왕자는 스무 해째 바다 건너에 살고 있다.

images.at: It is iron, two and a half feet long, with six branches

images.alt: In the hall at Juryu, Gwishil Boksin lowers the black-and-gold Baekje crown onto Pung’s head
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Juryu Fortress: a rough Baekje mountain fortress of piled grey stone on a pine ridge above the western sea, timber gate-house with a plain giwa roof.
