Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: The White Tiger drives his host into the Snake River. They still believe rivers are roads. Yeon Gesomun has been waiting for a man who thinks that. Old men in the north remember another river that ate an army. The Snake is younger. It's hungrier. And it has Yeon's teeth.
blocks.ko: 백호가 군대를 몰아 사수로 들어온다. 그들은 아직 강을 길이라고 믿는다. 연개소문은 그렇게 믿는 자를 기다려 왔다. 북쪽 늙은이들은 군대를 삼킨 강을 하나 더 기억한다. 사수는 그보다 젊다. 더 굶주렸다. 그리고 연의 이빨을 가졌다.

blocks.html: Shallow, slow, and patient with men who think rivers are roads.
blocks.ko: 얕고 느리며, 강을 길로 아는 자에게 참을성이 많다.

blocks.caption: The White Tiger thought the river was a road. Yeon is standing in the middle of it.
blocks.ko: 백호는 강을 길이라 여겼다. 연개소문은 그 한가운데 서 있다.

blocks.label: The Snake
blocks.ko: 사수

blocks.label: The Ford
blocks.ko: 여울

blocks.html: Here is the plan, such as it is. The Tiger is marching west to join the Red Fowl outside Pyongyang, and the Snake is in his way. If he gets there, the city is in a ring.
blocks.ko: 계획이라고 할 만한 건 이렇다. 백호는 평양성 밖의 주작과 합치려고 서쪽으로 행군 중이고, 사수가 그 길을 막고 있다. 그가 거기 닿으면, 도성은 포위된다.

blocks.caption: The White Tiger. The Western general who brought all his sons to war, to show them how it’s done.
blocks.ko: 백호. 싸움을 가르치겠다고 아들들을 모두 데려온 서국의 장군.

blocks.html: Gesomun lets him get halfway. The Snake has gravel at the edges and mud in the middle, and Gesomun knows which is which. His men already hold the west bank, and more of them wait on the east, behind the Tiger, where nobody has looked.
blocks.ko: 개소문은 그를 강 한복판까지 들어오게 둔다. 사수는 가장자리가 자갈이고 가운데가 진흙이다. 개소문은 어디가 어딘지 안다. 그의 군사는 이미 서쪽 둑을 쥐고 있고, 동쪽에도, 백호의 등 뒤 아무도 돌아보지 않은 곳에 더 기다리고 있다.

lines: 데놈은 강을 길로 안다. 걸어 들어오게 두라우.
가운데 말들이 빠지면 — 양쪽 둑에서. 한꺼번에.
en: He thinks it’s a road. Let him walk on it.
When the middle horses sink — both banks. All at once.

blocks.html: The middle horses sink. Both banks open up at once.
blocks.ko: 가운데 말들이 빠진다. 양쪽 둑이 한꺼번에 열린다.

en: Mud. It’s only mud. Keep walking.
…Boys? Boys, on me.

blocks.label: Thirteen Sons
blocks.ko: 열세 아들

blocks.html: The river does not take them in a heap. Yeon counts. Chang’an’s clerks will later write thirteen sons as if a number were a grave. It is a morning. The water is February-cold.
blocks.ko: 강은 그들을 한꺼번에 삼키지 않는다. 연개소문이 센다. 훗날 장안의 서기들은 열세 아들이라고, 숫자가 무덤이라도 되는 듯 적을 것이다. 지금은 아침이고, 물은 이월의 물처럼 차다.

blocks.html: The thirteenth and the twelfth come together at the first bend — brothers who still share a horse’s width. Yeon meets them in the shallows where the current lies. One stroke. Two bodies. The horse walks on a few steps with no one left to tell it to stop.
blocks.ko: 열셋째와 열둘째가 첫 굽이에서 함께 온다 — 아직 말 한 필의 너비를 나누는 형제. 연은 물살이 거짓말하는 여울에서 그들을 맞는다. 한 번. 두 몸. 말은 멈추라는 사람이 없어진 채로 몇 걸음을 더 간다.

en: Thirteen.
Twelve.

blocks.html: The eleventh tries the reeds. Reeds keep a secret until a man breathes too loud. Yeon does not spend a speech on a boy hiding in grass.
blocks.ko: 열한째는 갈대를 고른다. 갈대는 사람이 숨소리를 크게 내기 전까지만 비밀을 지킨다. 연은 풀에 숨은 아이에게 연설을 쓰지 않는다.

en: Eleven.

blocks.html: The tenth and the ninth turn back toward their father. That is the expensive choice. They die reaching for a sleeve that is still too far upriver.
blocks.ko: 열째와 아홉째는 아버지 쪽으로 말머리를 돌린다. 값비싼 선택이다. 둘은 아직 너무 먼 상류의 소매를 향해 손을 뻗다가 죽는다.

en: Ten.
Nine.

blocks.html: The eighth is the archer. He puts three shafts into the rim of Yeon’s shield and the fourth into his horse’s neck. The horse goes down, and Yeon goes into the water with it.
blocks.ko: 여덟째는 궁수다. 그는 연개소문의 방패 테두리에 화살 셋을 박고, 넷째 화살을 말의 목에 꽂는다. 말이 쓰러지고, 연개소문도 함께 물속으로 처박힌다.

blocks.label: Yumla Defied
blocks.ko: 염라를 거스르다

blocks.html: In the worst hour of it — arrows spent, horse down, the Western blade a finger from his throat — the air thins the way Tamla stories promised. The river stops moving. Kangrim and Haewonmek are standing on it, a ledger half-open between them.
blocks.ko: 가장 나쁜 순간 — 화살은 떨어지고, 말은 쓰러지고, 서군의 칼날이 목에서 한 치 앞에 — 탐라의 이야기가 말하던 대로 공기가 엷어진다. 강물이 멈춘다. 강림과 해원맥이 그 위에 서 있다. 둘 사이에 장부가 반쯤 펼쳐져 있다.

en: Yeon Gesomun.
Your page is… persuasive today.
Commander. If you walk away now —
are you choosing Goguryeo, or choosing not to be finished by anyone else’s schedule?
lines: 고구려를 고르는 겁니까, 아니면 남의 일정에 끝나지 않기를 고르는 겁니까?

en: Any last words?
Say them now. The blade is already practicing your name.
lines: 지금 하시게. 칼이 이미 네 이름을 연습 중이니.

en: Kangrim. Haewonmek.
Both.
And neither is your business until I am done.
lines: 그리고 내가 끝날 때까지 네 알 바 아니다.

en: Not today.
I still have bairns to disappoint.

blocks.html: Then he turns his back on them. He takes hold of his own body the way you take a coat off a peg, and puts it back on. The river starts moving again.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 그들에게 등을 돌린다. 못에 걸린 겉옷을 집어 들듯 제 몸을 붙잡아, 도로 걸쳐 입는다. 강물이 다시 흐른다.

blocks.html: He stands up on will alone. The blade misses. He breaks the spearman’s wrist before the man has finished the thrust. Behind him, the two reapers close the ledger with something like respect.
blocks.ko: 그는 오직 의지 하나로 일어선다. 칼날이 빗나간다. 그는 창병이 찌르기를 다 끝내기도 전에 그 손목을 꺾는다. 그 뒤에서 두 저승차사가 존경 비슷한 것을 담아 장부를 덮는다.

en: Hah.
Keep the country a little longer, then.
I hate refiling — and Your Majesty hates wasted parchment.
lines: 그럼 나라 좀 더 붙들고 있어.
서류 다시 넣기 싫거든 — 폐하께서도 헛된 종이를 싫어하시니.

en: Next time we bring a longer chain.
Or a taller boss.

blocks.html: The archer is still nocking his fifth arrow. He does not finish it. Afterward Yeon takes the bow out of the water and breaks it across his knee.
blocks.ko: 궁수는 아직 다섯째 화살을 시위에 메기는 중이다. 끝내 다 메기지 못한다. 연개소문은 나중에 그 활을 물에서 건져 무릎에 대고 부러뜨린다.

en: Eight. The bow ends here.

blocks.html: The seventh almost makes the east bank. Yeon’s throw finds him between the shoulder-blades, and the current carries him the rest of the way.
blocks.ko: 일곱째는 거의 동쪽 둑에 닿는다. 연개소문이 던진 창이 그의 견갑골 사이에 박히고, 나머지 길은 물살이 데려다준다.

blocks.speaker: the seventh
en: Bekju…
Home…
zhLatn: Báizhōu…
Huí jiā…

en: Seven. Home is not that bank.

blocks.html: Three at once in a knot of horses: the sixth, the fifth, the fourth. They shout one father’s name in three pitches.
blocks.ko: 뒤엉킨 말들 사이에서 셋이 한꺼번에. 여섯째, 다섯째, 넷째. 그들은 한 아버지의 이름을 세 가지 목소리로 부른다.

en: Six. Five. Four.
Some days you count in threes.

blocks.html: The third is old enough to bargain. He offers the banner, the southern levy, a road south, if the Supreme Commander will count him as a messenger instead of a son.
blocks.ko: 셋째는 흥정할 나이다. 그는 깃발과 남쪽의 징병과 남으로 가는 길을 내놓는다. 대막리지가 자기를 아들이 아닌 전령으로 세어 준다면.

blocks.speaker: the third
lines: 열셋 가운데 입을 연 자는 저뿐입니다.
en: Let me go as a messenger.
Among the thirteen I am the only one who opened his mouth.
zh: 十三子之中，開口的只有我。
zhLatn: Róng wǒ zuò shǐzhě qù.
Shísān zǐ zhī zhōng, kāikǒu de zhǐyǒu wǒ.

en: You did not come as a messenger.
That is why you are three.

blocks.html: The second is younger. He does not speak. Yeon does not ask him to.
blocks.ko: 둘째는 더 어리다. 그는 말이 없다. 연개소문도 말하라고 하지 않는다.

en: Two.

blocks.html: The first — the eldest — holds the White Tiger banner with both hands so the silk will not touch the water. He lasts longer than the others because he has decided to be a flagpole. Yeon cuts the pole. The cloth goes under. The boy goes with it, still holding on, which is how eldest sons are trained.
blocks.ko: 첫째 — 맏이 — 는 백호의 깃을 두 손으로 잡아, 비단이 물에 닿지 않게 한다. 남들보다 오래 가는 것은 스스로 깃대가 되기로 해서다. 연이 대를 벤다. 천이 가라앉는다. 아이도 함께, 아직 놓고 있지 않은 채로. 맏이를 그렇게 가르친다.

en: One.
Now the tiger.

blocks.label: The White Tiger
blocks.ko: 백호

blocks.html: Then only the tiger is left. He stands where his boys could still see him, if any of them still had eyes. Someone shouts to break east, toward any camp that is not this one.
blocks.ko: 이제 호랑이만 남았다. 그는 아들들이 아직 눈이 있다면 볼 수 있었을 자리에 서 있다. 누군가 동쪽으로 빠지자고, 여기만 아니면 어느 진영이든 가자고 외친다.

blocks.speaker: aide
en: Commander! Toward You Boying’s camp—
Live, and leave the account!
zhLatn: Zǒngguǎn! Wǎng Liú Bóyīng yíng—
Huózhe bǎ zhàng liúxià!

lines: 두 황제의 은혜를 너무 많이 입었다.
이 나라를 멸하지 않고는 돌아가지 않는다.
내가 데려온 남쪽 자제가 이미 다 죽었는데 —
이 몸 하나만 살아서 무엇을 하겠느냐.
en: I have eaten too much favour under two emperors.
I will not go home while this kingdom still stands.
The southern boys I brought are already dead —
what would this one body do, alive?
zhLatn: Shòu liǎng cháo ēnzé yǐ guò.
Bù miè cǐguó, bù guī.
Wǒ suǒ lǜ nán zǐdì yǐ jìn sǐ—
Dú liú cǐ shēn, hé wéi?

blocks.html: He does not run. The arrows make a hedgehog of him. Yeon walks the last three steps through the water and finishes what the shafts began.
blocks.ko: 그는 달아나지 않는다. 화살이 그를 고슴도치로 만든다. 연개소문이 마지막 세 걸음을 물을 헤치고 걸어가, 화살이 시작한 일을 끝낸다.

en: White Tiger.
Titles drown too.

lines: 아직두 정신 못 차렸네, 이 새끼들아?!
en: Still haven’t come to your senses, you bastards?!
I am… none other than… Yeon Gesomun!!

blocks.label: The Old Marshal
blocks.ko: 노장

blocks.label: The Rice Road
blocks.ko: 쌀길

blocks.html: In the second month a train of carts comes north out of Silla and across the Imjin, through snow to the axles. Kim Yushin is sixty-seven, and he has walked half the road beside his white horse so that Hansul can carry a sack of rice instead of him.
blocks.ko: 이월, 바퀴 축까지 차는 눈을 뚫고 신라에서 임진강을 건너 북쪽으로 수레 행렬이 올라온다. 김유신은 예순일곱이고, 한슬이가 자기 대신 쌀 한 섬을 질 수 있도록 길의 절반을 흰 말 곁에서 걸어왔다.

blocks.html: The Western camp outside Pyongyang has been eating its horses. Men sit hugging their knees in the snow and look at the carts as if they might be another rumour.
blocks.ko: 평양 밖 서국의 진영은 제 말을 잡아먹고 있었다. 병사들은 눈 속에 무릎을 끌어안고 앉아, 수레를 또 하나의 헛소문인 양 바라본다.

blocks.html: On Pyongyang’s wall that night, Gulgul counts the West fires twice. They have stopped going down.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 평양성 위에서 걸걸은 서군의 모닥불을 두 번 센다. 더는 줄지 않는다.

en: Somebody’s feeding them.
…Find out who. Then follow him home.
Silla is late.
…Unload it. All of it. Then we go home.
zhLatn: Xīnluó lái chí le.
…Xièxià. Quán xiè. Ránhòu huí jiā.

lines: 말 가슴까지 차는 눈을 뚫고 왔습니다, 장군.
en: We came through snow to the horse’s chest, General.
You may eat it slowly.

blocks.html: The Red Fowl takes the rice, breaks camp within the week, and sails. The road back is Yushin’s problem. Goguryeo’s horsemen follow the empty carts south all the way to the Imjin. At the ford, Yushin turns the white horse round.
blocks.ko: 주작은 쌀을 받고, 그 주 안에 진을 걷고, 배를 탄다. 돌아가는 길은 유신의 몫이다. 고구려 기병이 빈 수레를 남쪽으로 임진강까지 쫓아온다. 나루에서 유신이 흰 말의 머리를 돌린다.

lines: 우리 사는 데를 볼라꼬 여기꺼정 따라왔구마.
en: They followed us all this way to see where we live.
Well, now they know. Water the horses.

blocks.label: The Far West
blocks.ko: 머나먼 서쪽

blocks.html: A thousand miles the other way, the courier finds Xue Rengui. You may remember him: the farmer in the white coat who left his ancestors unburied to answer a muster. He has just ended a war in the far west with three arrows. Now he is given the dead man’s title, White Tiger II. And the bill.
blocks.ko: 반대편으로 천 리 밖에서, 파발이 설인귀를 찾아낸다. 기억하실지 모르겠다. 조상의 무덤을 다 짓지도 못하고 징집에 응했던, 흰 옷의 그 농부. 그는 막 서쪽 끝의 전쟁을 화살 세 대로 끝낸 참이다. 이제 그는 죽은 자의 칭호, 제2대 백호를 받는다. 그리고 그 청구서도.

lines: 죽은 자의 셈은, 산 자가 갚는 법입니다.
en: White Tiger… I will take the name.
The dead man’s account is paid by the living.
zhLatn: Báihǔ… cǐ míng, wǒ lái jiē.
Sǐzhě zhī zhàng, yóu shēngzhě lái cháng.

blocks.html: The fangtian ji goes east again. Men who never learned his birth name learn the white coat and the crescent blade — and begin, quietly, to fear the second tiger more than the first.
blocks.ko: 방천화극이 다시 동쪽으로 간다. 본명을 배우지 못한 자들이 흰옷과 초승달 날을 배우고 — 슬그머니, 첫 번째 호랑이보다 두 번째를 더 두려워하기 시작한다.

blocks.label: Pyongyang
blocks.ko: 평양

blocks.speaker: Goguryeo scout
lines: 새 호랑이는 그 흰옷입네다, 대막리지. 주필산의 그놈이요.
포로들은 이름두 안 대구, 여포랍네다. 여포레 돌아왔다구요.
en: The new tiger is the one in white, Supreme Commander. From Stallion Mountain.
Their prisoners won’t even say his name. They say Lu Bu. Lu Bu come back.

lines: 여포는 성문 누각에서 목 졸려 뒈졌어. 우리한테두 누각은 있다구 전하라우.
en: Lu Bu. Ha!
Lu Bu got strangled on a gate tower. Tell them we’ve got gate towers.

blocks.html: And on an island far to the south, someone is asking: whose side are we on now?
blocks.ko: 그리고 저 남쪽 섬에서, 누군가 묻는다. 이제 우리는 누구 편인가?

logline.en: Two envoys, one fire, and an island king who won’t pick only one side.
logline.ko: 사신 둘, 불 하나, 그리고 한쪽 편만 고르지 않는 섬의 왕.

images.at: The two boats leave on the same tide
images.alt: Tamla’s envoys as tiny orange boats on a vast black sea — the island a far silhouette in mist-white fog

The line: ““Whose side are we on now?” On Tamla, the one who asks is usually holding a fish.” Context: “Whose side are we on now?” On Tamla, the one who asks is usually holding a fish.  This time it is a diver, still wet from the morning, with an octopus in one fist. She asks it in the king’s hall, loudly, because the king’s hall is also where the island dries its nets. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: “Whose side are we on now?” On Tamla, the one who asks is usually holding a fish.
blocks.ko: “이제 우리는 누구 편이야?” 탐라에서 그런 걸 묻는 사람은 대개 손에 생선을 들고 있다.

blocks.caption: An island off the bottom of the map, with two kingdoms’ boats in its harbour.
blocks.ko: 지도 맨 아래의 섬 하나. 포구에는 두 나라의 배.

blocks.html: This time it is a diver, still wet from the morning, with an octopus in one fist. She asks it in the king’s hall, loudly, because the king’s hall is also where the island dries its nets.
blocks.ko: 이번에는 해녀다. 아침 물질에 아직 젖은 채로, 한 손에 문어를 쥐고 있다. 그녀는 왕의 집에서 큰 소리로 묻는다. 왕의 집은 섬사람들이 그물을 말리는 곳이기도 하니까.

blocks.html: Yuri Dora does not answer at once. He never answers anything at once. He has a fire, two cups, and two envoys who will not sit down.
blocks.ko: 유리도라는 바로 대답하지 않는다. 그는 무엇에도 바로 대답하는 법이 없다. 그에게는 불 하나, 잔 두 개, 그리고 앉으려 하지 않는 사신 둘이 있다.

blocks.html: One came down from the last Baekje hill fort. The other came from Silla, with the Western officer behind him like a second shadow.
blocks.ko: 하나는 백제의 마지막 산성에서 내려왔다. 다른 하나는 신라에서 왔는데, 그 뒤에 서국 무관이 두 번째 그림자처럼 붙어 있다.

blocks.label: Two Envoys
blocks.ko: 두 사신

blocks.speaker: Baekje envoy
lines: 칠백 년입니다, 전하. 전하의 선조들께서 백제의 관등을 받으셨습니다.
복신 장군께서 배를 청하십니다. 곡식도. 노를 잡을 수 있는 자라면 누구든.
en: Seven hundred years, my lord. Your fathers carried our ranks.
Boksin asks for boats. Grain. Any man who can hold an oar.

blocks.speaker: Silla envoy
lines: 사수에서 서군이 크게 졌습니다, 전하. 두 번은 지지 않을 겁니다.
저희 임금께서는 전하의 이름을 명부에 올리는 것 말고는 바라시는 게 없습니다.
en: The Snake River went badly for the West, my lord. It will not go badly twice.
My king asks for nothing but your name on a list.

lines: 이 섬에서 제일 비싼 게 이름이주. 몇 개 없거든.
en: Only my name. Did you hear that? Only a name, says he.
Names are the dearest thing on this island. It’s few enough we have.

blocks.speaker: Western officer
lines: 황제의 함대는 어디로 가든 이 섬 앞을 지나갑니다, 전하.
en: The emperor’s fleet sails past this island on its way to everywhere, my lord.
It could stop.

lines: 게민 귤이나 사러 멈추렌 허라. 다들 경 허난.
en: Then it can stop for oranges. Sure, everyone does.

lines: 먼저 멕입서, 왕님. 배고프민 아무것도 못 정허우다.
en: Feed them first, my lord. Sure nobody decides anything hungry.

blocks.html: So they eat. Raw octopus, barley, a bowl of something orange. The Baekje envoy eats like a man who has not seen a full bowl since Sabi. The Silla envoy eats like a man being watched, which he is.
blocks.ko: 그래서 먹는다. 날문어, 보리, 무언가 주황색인 것 한 그릇. 백제 사신은 사비가 무너진 뒤로 가득 찬 그릇을 처음 본 사람처럼 먹는다. 신라 사신은 감시당하는 사람처럼 먹는다. 실제로 감시당하고 있다.

blocks.label: The Turtle
blocks.ko: 거북이

blocks.html: Then the Baekje envoy plays the only card he brought.
blocks.ko: 그러다 백제 사신이 들고 온 단 한 장의 패를 꺼낸다.

blocks.speaker: Baekje envoy
lines: 전하. 백전백승이라 불린 그 장군이 이 섬에서 다섯 해를 살았습니다.
그분은 황산에서 백제를 위해 돌아가셨습니다. 바로 이자들의 군대와 싸우다가.
en: My lord. The general they called Hundred-Victories lived here five years.
He died at the Yellow Mountain, for Baekje. Fighting these men’s army.
Will you bow to the side that killed him?

blocks.html: The hall goes quiet. Even the divers stop chewing. Every one of them remembers the Turtle.
blocks.ko: 집 안이 조용해진다. 해녀들마저 씹던 것을 멈춘다. 거북이를 기억하지 못하는 사람은 하나도 없다.

blocks.html: Yuri Dora turns his cup in his hands for a long time.
blocks.ko: 유리도라는 오래도록 손안에서 잔을 돌린다.

lines: 첫날 밤에 그놈이 나신디 며칠이냐고 묻더라. 인사도 없이. 며칠이냐고.
다섯 해여. 이 불 앞에 혼 번을 안 앉더라.
en: The first night, he asked me how many days. Not hello. How many days.
Five years, and he never once sat down by this fire.

blocks.html: He fills the second cup anyway and sets it by the door, where a man used to stand.
blocks.ko: 그래도 그는 두 번째 잔을 채워, 한 사내가 늘 서 있던 문 옆에 내려놓는다.

blocks.speaker: Baekje envoy
en: Then you owe him—

lines: 떠날 때 딱 혼마디 해 줬주. 사람을 잊지 말렌.
왕을 잊지 말렌 말은 안 했저. 왕은 잘만 기억허더라. 게난 어떵 됐는지 보라.
en: I told him one thing when he left. Do not forget people.
I never said, don’t forget kings. Kings he remembered fine. And look where it got him.

blocks.html: He points his cup at the door. Outside, on the black rock by the eastern shore, a handful of children are drilling in fives, badly, out of step. Nobody taught them. They learned it by standing behind a man who never turned round.
blocks.ko: 그는 잔으로 문밖을 가리킨다. 동쪽 바닷가의 검은 바위 위에서 아이들 몇이 다섯씩 짝을 지어 서툴게, 발도 안 맞춰 훈련하고 있다. 가르친 사람은 없다. 한 번도 뒤돌아보지 않던 사내 뒤에 서서 배운 것이다.

lines: 저것들이 내 사람들이주. 내가 안 잊을 건 저거라.
en: Those are my people. It’s them I’m not forgetting.

blocks.label: Two Boats
blocks.ko: 배 두 척

blocks.html: So the king of Tamla makes his choice the way the island does everything: sideways.
blocks.ko: 그래서 탐라의 왕은 섬이 늘 하던 식으로 결정을 내린다. 옆걸음으로.

lines: 혼 척은 내 이름 들렁 신라로 감저. 명부에 똑바로 적으렌 허라.
혼 척은 이 사람 태왕 그 산성으로 돌아가고. 보리든 귤이든, 해녀들이 내줄 수 있는 건 다 실르라.
en: Get two boats ready.
One goes to Silla with my name for their list. Let them spell it right, so.
The other takes him back up to his hill fort. Barley, oranges, whatever the divers can spare.

blocks.speaker: Silla envoy
lines: 전하— 두 쪽에 다 절하실 수는 없습니다.
en: My lord— you cannot bow to both.

lines: 보라. 나는 섬이여. 편 같은 건 없고, 포구가 있주.
그리고 이야기는 끝을 정해 놓앙 시작허는 게 아니여.
en: Watch me. I’m an island. I don’t have a side. I have a harbour.
And a story isn’t begun with its ending already fixed.
…So whose side is it we’re on?
Ours. Eat your octopus.

blocks.html: The two boats leave on the same tide, one east, one north. From the black rock the children wave at both. Nobody has told them which one to wave at.
blocks.ko: 배 두 척이 같은 물때에 떠난다. 하나는 동쪽으로, 하나는 북쪽으로. 검은 바위 위의 아이들이 두 척 모두에게 손을 흔든다. 어느 쪽에 흔들어야 하는지 아무도 알려 주지 않았으니까.

blocks.html: In the emperor’s city, a clerk writes the visit down. He has never seen the island. It shows.
blocks.ko: 황제의 도성에서 서기 하나가 그 방문을 받아 적는다. 그는 그 섬을 본 적이 없다. 티가 난다.

blocks.html: Early in Longshuo there was a land called Danluo, whose king, Yuri Dora, sent envoys to court. It lies on an island south of Silla's Muju. Its ways are plain and rough: they wear the hides of great pigs, live in leather huts in summer and in pit-houses in winter. … At first it was attached to Baekje. … Later it attached itself to Silla.
blocks.ko: 용삭 초에 담라라는 나라가 있어, 그 왕 유리도라가 사신을 보내 입조하였다. 나라는 신라 무주 남쪽 섬 위에 있으며, 풍속이 소박하고 거칠어 큰 돼지 가죽을 입고, 여름에는 가죽 집에, 겨울에는 움집에 산다. … 처음에는 백제에 붙었다. … 뒤에는 신라에 붙었다.
blocks.hanja: 龍朔初，有儋羅者，其王儒李都羅遣使入朝，國居新羅武州南島上，俗樸陋，衣大豕皮，夏居革屋，冬窟室。…初附百濟。…後附新羅。
blocks.source: Xin Tangshu (新唐書) bk. 220, Eastern Barbarians — Danluo (儋羅, Tamla), Longshuo era (661–663)

blocks.html: Baekje refuses to stay dead. And in Surabol, a great lord feels a fever coming on…!
blocks.ko: 백제는 죽은 채로 있어 주지 않는다. 그리고 서라벌에서는, 한 대귀족이 갑자기 열이 오른다…!

logline.en: Nineteen generals are named for the campaign. Two of them call in sick, and are seen at a gyuku match.
logline.ko: 토벌에 장수 열아홉이 이름을 올린다. 둘은 병을 핑계 대고, 격구장에서 목격된다.

images.at: The Western officer who is sorry for him
images.alt: In a Chang'an palace corridor, Kim Punghun sits on the step with his helmet in his lap; the Western officer's hand rests on his shoulder.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 movie still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Night at the Tang palace in Chang'an (attached board): a long roofed corridor on the red rammed-earth terrace, vermilion columns receding diagonally. Medium close, low three-quarter. A young Silla nobleman serving in the emperor's guard sits on a white stone balustrade step where his legs gave out, his face turned down and away from the lens into shadow, guard's helmet in his lap, one hand over his mouth. A Tang officer in a vermilion robe stands beside him, half out of frame, one hand resting awkwardly on his shoulder. Red lantern spill, cool blue-green shadows, distant lantern bokeh down the corridor, reflective dark stone floor. One hard key from a lantern beside them. Unarmed. CANON — PLACE Chang’an (장안) — attached board /pl_daming_night.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Tang palace of Chang'an, drawn from the Daming Palace (大明宮) site and reconstruction models: Hanyuan Hall's concave ensemble — an eleven-bay hall with a double-eaved hipped roof of dark grey tiles and curled owl-tail ridge ends (chiwei), red columns, white plaster walls, lattice windows, raised on three tiers of rammed-earth terraces faced in ochre-red plaster and edged with white stone balustrades; the Dragon Tail Way ramps folding up the terraces; forward on each side the Xiangluan and Qifeng que-towers (three stepped pavilions on tall battered grey-brick piers) joined to the hall by long roofed corridors; a vast paved square below, entered through the five-doored Danfeng Gate. Wide low Tang proportions, deep eaves on massive bracket sets. Tang palette is VERMILION and WHITE (red columns, white walls); roofs are black-grey tile trimmed with green-glazed ridge and eave tiles (a little yellow and blue tricolour glaze); balustrade posts painted red, blue and green. YELLOW belongs to the emperor's robe; gold is gilt-bronze fittings, lamp-trees and firelight on vermilion. Interiors: dark polished stone floors, rows of vermilion columns, gauze hangings, a raised dais with a painted screen behind the throne. Never the Forbidden City, never all-yellow glazed roofs, never the modern reconstruction or a city skyline. Mood: TANG RENDER: predominantly DARK and INTIMIDATING Chinese ink painting (shuimohua) — black and grey ink washes, wet-on-wet ink bleeding into rice paper, dry calligraphic brush for roofs, columns, smoke and robes, the vermilion and gold reduced to small accents in a world of ink; officials, guards and other Tang figures are ink figures too. The ONE exception is the Second Emperor himself: he keeps the house webtoon figure render in full colour (yellow robe, black futou, drawn face), a coloured man inside an ink empire. Staged like a Chinese historical drama (Legend of the Demon Cat, The Longest Day in Chang'an) but lit as full Heewon tenebrism: night or blue hour; ONE dominant hard key per shot — a backlight through open doors or lattice, or one lamp-tree — and 75% of the frame crushed black with no fill; colour contrast — gold-yellow flame highlights against cool blue-green in the few lit shadows; the other flames (lamp-trees, silk lanterns with no writing, braziers) are small points and round bokeh IN the black, never lighting the room evenly; red lantern light through lattice as one pattern on the floor; incense haze only inside the key shaft; polished dark floors reflecting the flames. Staged like a drama, at true human scale: camera at eye or knee height on a dolly or crane; court officials in two lines facing inward along the central aisle with tablets; banquet tables in two long facing rows with dancers in the centre and the emperor on the dais at the head; exteriors are real-scale terraces and corridors, the hall large but never a fantasy fortress. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. blocks.html: Kim Jinju has a fever. Half of Surabol has watched it play gyuku.
blocks.ko: 김진주가 앓아누웠다. 서라벌의 절반이 그 병이 격구 치는 걸 구경했다.

blocks.label: Nesaji
blocks.ko: 내사지성

blocks.html: Two summers after Sabi, Baekje is supposed to be finished. Baekje has not been informed. Its leftovers hold a hill fort east of the old capital. They collect grain. They hang collaborators. They send boys to watch the Silla roads.
blocks.ko: 사비가 무너지고 두 번째 여름. 백제는 끝났어야 한다. 백제는 그 소식을 듣지 못했다. 남은 자들이 옛 도읍 동쪽의 산성 하나를 차지하고 있다. 곡식을 걷는다. 부역자를 목매단다. 아이들을 보내 신라의 길목을 지켜본다.

blocks.html: Munmu names nineteen generals for it. One of them is Kim Jinju. He is True Bone, from a good family. He led men at the Yellow Mountain. He has a son in the emperor's guard.
blocks.ko: 문무는 이 일에 장군 열아홉을 붙인다. 그중 하나가 김진주다. 좋은 집안의 진골이다. 황산벌에서 군사를 이끌었다. 아들 하나가 황제의 숙위로 가 있다.

blocks.label: Sick Leave
blocks.ko: 병가

blocks.html: Jinju sends word that he is ill. So does his friend Jinhum. Neither of them is ill. They stay home through the whole campaign, eat well, and receive visitors.
blocks.ko: 진주는 병이 났다고 기별을 보낸다. 그의 벗 진흠도 그렇게 한다. 둘 다 아프지 않다. 둘은 원정 내내 집에 머물며 잘 먹고, 손님을 맞는다.

blocks.speaker: Kim Jinju
lines: 산성 하나에 장군이 열아홉이다. 스무 번째는 필요 없다.
게다가 전쟁은 끝났다 아이가. 누군가는 그렇다꼬 말해야제.
en: Nineteen generals for one hill fort. They hardly need a twentieth.
Besides. The war’s over. Somebody ought to say so.

blocks.html: The gyuku field is full that week. Jinju plays well for a sick man. Between rounds, Jinhum leans on the rail beside him.
blocks.ko: 그 주에 격구장은 사람으로 가득하다. 진주는 환자치고 공을 잘 친다. 판과 판 사이, 진흠이 그의 곁 난간에 기댄다.

blocks.speaker: Jinhum
lines: 임금 사람이 관람석에 있데이. 셋째 줄. 공은 한 번도 안 보더라.
en: The king’s man is in the stands. Third row. Hasn’t watched the ball once.

blocks.speaker: Kim Jinju
lines: 세라 캐라. 내 아들이 황제 문을 지키는데.
문무는 장안에 아들 둔 집안은 몬 건드린다. 황제가 너무 아쉽거든.
en: Let him count. My son stands at the emperor’s door.
Munmu won’t touch a house with a boy in Chang’an. He needs the emperor far too much.

blocks.html: It is a good argument. It is the argument every lord in the city would make. Munmu has been king for one year, and nobody knows yet what he is.
blocks.ko: 좋은 논리다. 서라벌의 어느 귀족이라도 똑같이 말했을 논리다. 문무는 왕이 된 지 한 해, 그가 어떤 왕인지 아직 아무도 모른다.

blocks.label: The Moon Palace
blocks.ko: 월성

blocks.html: Nesaji falls without him. Kim Humsun takes it in a fortnight and reports it to the king in two lines, and then, because he is honest and it is his duty, he reports who was missing.
blocks.ko: 내사지성은 그 없이 떨어진다. 김흠순이 보름 만에 성을 빼앗고 왕에게 두 줄로 보고한 뒤, 정직하고 그것이 직분이므로, 누가 빠졌는지도 보고한다.

blocks.html: Before he sends for them, Munmu asks his uncle what he thinks. He has been asking Yushin that since he was nine, on a beach, with a stick of driftwood in his hand.
blocks.ko: 그들을 부르기 전에, 문무는 숙부에게 생각을 묻는다. 아홉 살 때부터, 바닷가에서 유목 막대를 쥐고 묻던 질문이다.

en: Uncle. Jinju and Jinhum. What would you do?

lines: 관등을 거두고 북쪽 성으로 보내십시오, 전하. 조용히.
진주 아들이 황제 문 앞에 서 있심더. 선왕께서는 장안에 묶인 줄은 한 번도 안 끊으셨습니더.
en: Strip their ranks and send them to the northern forts, Majesty. Quietly.
Jinju’s boy stands at the emperor’s door. Your father never cut a rope that was tied to Chang’an.

lines: 아버님은 조심스러운 분이셨소. 그래야 했지. 이십 년을 황제한테 뭘 청하며 사셨으니.
나는 아무한테도 아무것도 안 청하오. 비담이 쓰러졌을 때, 알천 공이 그 집안만은 살려 달라 했지요. 숙부가 뭐라 했는지 기억하시오?
en: My father was a careful man. He had to be. He spent twenty years asking the emperor for things.
I’m not asking anyone for anything. When Bidam fell, Alchun begged you to spare his house. Do you remember what you told him?
Erase Bidam’s house.
The Son line, every one of them.
Treason’s blood must be cut.

lines: 비담은 죽었다. 열흘 동안 차를 따르고, 칼을 맞았다.
그의 대청까지 태우면 — 우리가 지키려던 육촌 중 하나를 스스로 지운다.
en: Yushin…
Bidam is dead. He poured tea for ten days, then took the blade.
If you burn his hall — we erase one of the Six Elders with our own hands.

blocks.html: Yushin leans close — close enough that the officers hear only breath, and Alchun hears the sentence.
blocks.ko: 유신이 몸을 기울인다 — 장교들에게는 숨소리만 들릴 만큼, 알천에게는 문장이 들릴 만큼.

en: Blood is inevitable…

lines: 그건 반역이었심더, 전하. 이건 바보 둘하고 열병이고예.
en: That was a rebellion, Majesty. This is two fools and a fever.
Bupmin-a, listen to me—
Uncle.
I am your king.

blocks.html: Nobody in the hall moves. The secretary’s brush stops above the paper. Long ago, on a beach, this man let a boy hit him with a stick on purpose, so the boy would keep swinging. The boy has kept swinging.
blocks.ko: 전각 안 아무도 움직이지 않는다. 서기의 붓이 종이 위에서 멈춘다. 오래전 바닷가에서 이 사내는 일부러 소년의 막대에 맞아 주었다. 소년이 계속 휘두르라고. 소년은 계속 휘둘렀다.

en: …Yes, Majesty.

blocks.html: He bows lower than he has bowed to anyone since the queen. Then he goes out to give the order himself.
blocks.ko: 그는 여왕 이후 누구에게도 하지 않았던 만큼 깊이 절한다. 그러고는 명령을 직접 내리러 나간다.

lines: 싸움 내내. 둘 다. 격구 칠 만큼은 멀쩡하고.
en: Ill.
The whole campaign. Both of them. And well enough for gyuku.

blocks.speaker: Kim Jinju
lines: 전하, 열이 오르내렸습니다. 사람이 앓는 날을 고를 수는—
en: Majesty, the fever came and went. A man cannot choose his days—

lines: 내 아버님은 이 전쟁에서 하루도 쉬신 적이 없다. 내 누이는 죽을 날을 고르지도 못했다.
en: My father never had a day off from this war. My sister didn’t get to choose hers.
Take them out.

blocks.speaker: Kim Jinju
lines: 전하— 제 아들이… 황제의 숙위에 있습니다.
en: Majesty— my son. He’s in the emperor’s guard.
Someone has to write to him—
I’ll write to him myself.

blocks.html: Jinju and Jinhum are beheaded, and their households with them, down to the cousins. It is the first time Munmu kills his own nobility. After it, nobody in Surabol mistakes the new king for a soft one.
blocks.ko: 진주와 진흠은 목이 베이고, 그 집안도 사촌까지 함께 죽는다. 문무가 제 손으로 귀족을 죽인 첫 번째 일이다. 그 뒤로 서라벌에서 새 임금을 무른 사람으로 보는 이는 없다.

blocks.html: He writes the letter that night. It is short. He does not ask a secretary to do it.
blocks.ko: 그는 그날 밤 편지를 쓴다. 짧은 편지다. 서기에게 맡기지 않는다.

blocks.label: Chang’an
blocks.ko: 장안

blocks.html: Kim Punghun is in Chang’an when the letter comes, in the emperor’s guard, where vassal houses keep their sons. He reads it twice. He hears the rest from the Western officer who is sorry for him, which is worse. He asks for leave to go home for the mourning and is told, kindly, that he has no home to go to.
blocks.ko: 편지가 왔을 때 김풍훈은 장안에 있다. 속국의 집안들이 아들을 맡겨 두는 황제의 숙위다. 그는 편지를 두 번 읽는다. 나머지는 그를 딱하게 여기는 서국 무관에게서 듣는다. 그게 더 아프다. 상을 치르러 돌아가게 해 달라고 청하자, 돌아갈 집이 없지 않느냐는 친절한 대답이 돌아온다.

lines: 황제의 배는 언젠가 동쪽으로 갑니다. 배 한 척쯤은 기다릴 수 있습니다.
en: …Then I will wait.
The emperor’s ships go east sooner or later. I can wait for a ship.

blocks.html: Remember the boy. The emperor’s ships do go east, eventually.
blocks.ko: 이 소년을 기억해 두시라. 황제의 배는 결국 동쪽으로 간다.

blocks.html: Meanwhile at Juryu, the general who crowned Baekje’s king has taken to his bed. He would love a visit…!
blocks.ko: 한편 주류성에서는, 백제 왕에게 관을 씌워 준 장군이 병석에 눕는다. 문병을 몹시 기다리면서…!

logline.en: The general who crowned Baekje’s king is sick in bed and asking for a visit. The king remembers another supper.
logline.ko: 백제 왕에게 관을 씌운 장군이 병석에서 문병을 청한다. 왕은 또 다른 저녁 자리를 기억한다.

A dark hall at Juryu fortress at night: General Boksin kneels on the floor, palms bound together with a leather thong, head thrown back, spitting up at the dais. Over him an executioner raises a ring-pommel sword two-thirds into the frame, the blade high and catching the light. Far back on the dais King Pung sits in shadow, half-turned away, only his hand on the throne arm lit. One brazier at floor level is the key, raking up Boksin’s face and the raised blade; the room is black. No gore. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. images.prompt: CLOSING STILL of the episode: the final scene of this story as it ends (not the next episode). The line: “So the armies split. Most of the generals take the land road. The Black Tortoise takes the water: a hundred and seventy warships, heading for the river mouth. On his deck stands Buyeo Yung.” Context: At Ungjin the allied generals argue about where to begin. One fortress sits where the road crosses the river, and most of the room wants it first. That fort is steep and strong. Rush it and we bleed men. Sit under it and we bleed days. Juryu is the nest. Pull the root, and the branches come down by themselves. So the armies split. Most of the generals take the land road. The Black Tortoise takes the water: a hundred and seventy warships, heading for the river mouth. On his deck stands Buyeo Yung. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — PRINCE YUNG — FACE ONLY from attached /ch_yung.png; ignore the portrait's clothing, headgear, jewelry and hair styling — dress exactly as "Now" below (invent a new pose). Now: In Tang service: same face (high topknot, thin moustache, small chin beard); a Tang officer's round-collared robe (panling) in deep crimson with a black leather belt, black futou cap tied at the back over the topknot, black boots. No Baekje gold scrollwork, no jougwan. He looks like a Tang officer who was born somewhere else. Demeanor: Short and cold, then suddenly too quiet. The son who knelt. #d4b45a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: jougwan in Tang service; Baekje crown. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus.
