LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Nine months. That is how long it lasts.
blocks.ko: 아홉 달. 딱 그만큼 간다.

blocks.label: The Provinces
blocks.ko: 지방 순시

blocks.html: In the spring Namseng rides out to tour the provinces, as a new Supreme Commander should. He leaves his two younger brothers to keep the capital.
blocks.ko: 봄에 남생은 새 대막리지라면 마땅히 그래야 하듯 지방 순시를 떠난다. 도성은 두 아우에게 맡겨 둔다.

blocks.html: Within a month there are men whispering in both directions. To Namgun and Namsan: your brother means to be rid of you when he comes back. To Namseng, at every post station: your brothers do not mean to let you back in.
blocks.ko: 한 달이 못 되어 양쪽으로 귓속말하는 자들이 생긴다. 남건과 남산에게는, 형님이 돌아오면 너희를 치울 생각이라고. 역참마다 남생에게는, 아우들이 형님을 들이지 않을 생각이라고.

lines: …그래도 한 사람 돌려보내라. 조용히. 저녁 자리에서 무슨 말들을 하는지 알고 싶다.
en: Nonsense. They are my brothers.
…Send someone back anyway. Quietly. I want to know what they say at supper.

blocks.html: The whispers travel both ways because they are carried both ways. Seals are cut in the night that look like Gesomun’s and read like him — the old man’s own bluntness, borrowed by a hand that learned it in Surabol. Nobody in Pyongyang asks who profits when brothers read forged mail.
blocks.ko: 속삭임이 양쪽으로 다니는 것은 양쪽으로 나르기 때문이다. 밤에 개소문의 것 같은 인장이 파인다 — 그 어르신의 퉁명함 그대로, 수라벌에서 배운 손이 빌려 쓴. 평양에선 형제가 위조 서찰을 읽을 때 누가 이득을 보는지 아무도 묻지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Supper
blocks.ko: 저녁상

blocks.html: In Pyongyang the two younger brothers eat supper in their father’s hall without their father. Neither of them has done that before. A man from the household stays after the dishes are cleared, and says it plainly: your brother hates having you this close to the seal. He means to clear you out when he gets back. Better to move first.
blocks.ko: 평양에서는 두 아우가 아버지 없는 아버지의 대청에서 저녁을 먹는다. 둘 다 처음 해 보는 일이다. 상을 물린 뒤에도 집안 사람 하나가 남아서 대놓고 말한다. 형님은 아우님들이 인장 곁에 있는 걸 싫어하신다. 돌아오시면 치우실 생각이다. 먼저 움직이시는 게 낫다.

en: Did you hear that? Brother means to clear us out.
I heard. Who says so?
…He does.
And who told him to say it?

lines: 남산아, 꼬치꼬치 따디디 말라. 형은 아바지 밑에서 컸어. 칼두 거기서 배웠구, 사람 치우는 것두 거기서 배웠디.
en: Don’t pick at it, Namsan. Brother grew up under Father. He learned the sword there. And how to clear a man out of the way.

lines: 아바지가 마지막에 뭐랬어. 물고기하구 물처럼 지내라구.
en: What did Father say, at the end? Get along like fish and water.

lines: 기래. 기런데 누가 물고기구 누가 물이네?
en: Right. So which of us is the fish, and which is the water?
…Brother.

blocks.html: Neither of them believes it. That is the first night. By the fourth night they check who is at the door before either of them speaks.
blocks.ko: 둘 다 믿지 않는다. 그게 첫날 밤이다. 나흘째 밤이 되면, 둘은 말을 꺼내기 전에 문 앞에 누가 있는지부터 살핀다.

blocks.label: The Pyongyang Gate
blocks.ko: 평양성 문

blocks.html: The man he sends is caught at the Pyongyang gate within the week. Namgun reads the orders found on him twice, and the second time he reads them as a confession.
blocks.ko: 그가 보낸 자는 한 주 만에 평양 성문에서 붙잡힌다. 남건은 그 몸에서 나온 지시를 두 번 읽고, 두 번째에는 자백으로 읽는다.

lines: 성문 닫으라우! 폐하께 아뢰라, 대막리지레 반역했다구!
en: He sends spies. To his own brothers.
Shut the gates! Tell the king the Supreme Commander has rebelled!

blocks.html: Then, because even a coup likes paperwork, they wake the king. A summons goes out under his seal: the Supreme Commander is to come home at once.
blocks.ko: 그다음엔, 반란도 문서를 좋아하는 법이라, 둘은 왕을 깨운다. 왕의 인장이 찍힌 소환장이 나간다. 대막리지는 즉시 돌아오라.

en: It— it only says come home? Only come home?
Only come home, Majesty.

blocks.html: The summons finds Namseng at a post station. He reads it, and then he reads who carried it: Namgun’s own riders. For ten days he does not come.
blocks.ko: 소환장은 역참에서 남생을 찾아낸다. 그는 그것을 읽고, 그다음엔 그것을 가져온 자들을 읽는다. 남건의 기병들이다. 열흘 동안 그는 오지 않는다.

blocks.html: Namseng’s son is in the capital that spring, with his mother. He is nine years old and wears a little gold ring his grandfather gave him.
blocks.ko: 그해 봄 남생의 아들은 어머니와 함께 도성에 있다. 아홉 살, 할아버지가 준 작은 금가락지를 끼고 있다.

blocks.label: The Shut Gate
blocks.ko: 닫힌 문

blocks.html: He rides back to his own capital and finds the gate shut. His brother comes up onto the wall.
blocks.ko: 그는 제 도성으로 말을 몰아 돌아오고, 성문이 닫혀 있는 것을 본다. 아우가 성벽 위로 올라온다.

en: Open the gate, Namgun.
You are speaking to the Supreme Commander.

lines: 대막리지라! 아우들 저녁상에 첩자를 보내 놓구 그걸 지휘라구 하네?!
en: Supreme Commander! You send spies to your brothers’ supper and call it command!

lines: 너희 안부를 물으라고 사람 하나 보냈다. 너는 그를 목매달았지.
en: I sent a man to ask how you were. You hanged him.

lines: 남건아. 나를 봐라. 요하에서, 매는 누가 맞았냐?
en: Namgun. Look at me. At the Liao, who took the flogging?
…You did.
And why?

lines: 형이 맏이니끼니. 그날부터 하루도 안 빼고 맏이였디.
그리고 형이 내 목 칠 인장을 들구 돌아온다더라.
en: Because you’re the elder. You’ve been the elder every single day since.
And they told me you were coming back with a seal for my head.
And you believed them. Traitor.
Traitor…? Me?

lines: 문 열어라. 안에 내 처가 있다. 내 아들이—
en: Open the gate. My wife is in there. My son—

blocks.html: Namgun does not answer. He looks at Namsan. Namsan looks at the ground.
blocks.ko: 남건은 대답하지 않는다. 그는 남산을 본다. 남산은 땅을 본다.

blocks.html: Something small comes over the wall and lands in the mud at the horse’s feet. A gold ring, a child’s size.
blocks.ko: 무언가 작은 것이 성벽을 넘어와 말발굽 앞 진흙에 떨어진다. 금가락지. 아이 손가락 크기다.

lines: 형한테 가는 편지를 품구 있었어. 수구문으로 빠져나가다가.
en: He was carrying a letter to you. Out through the water gate.
The guards didn’t— I didn’t—

blocks.html: Namseng gets down from his horse and picks the ring out of the mud. He wipes it on his sleeve. He does not look at the wall again.
blocks.ko: 남생은 말에서 내려 진흙 속의 가락지를 집어 든다. 소매에 닦는다. 다시는 성벽을 쳐다보지 않는다.

blocks.html: Outside the gate, his eldest boy Heonseong, the one the uncles did not catch, rides up beside him and says aloud what Namseng has been carrying since the ring came over the wall.
blocks.ko: 성문 밖에서, 숙부들 손에 잡히지 않은 맏아들 헌성이 곁으로 말을 몰아 와, 가락지가 성벽을 넘어온 뒤로 남생이 짊어진 말을 입 밖에 낸다.

blocks.html: “They will kill you by paper, Father. The gate proved it. Go north to Gungnae, and from there, west, before the paper catches up.” Namseng looks at his son for a long time. Then he decides, in one word.
blocks.ko: “서류로 죽일 겁니다, 아버지. 성문이 증명했습니다. 국내성으로 가십시오. 거기서 서쪽으로. 서류가 따라잡기 전에.” 남생이 아들을 오래 본다. 그러고 한 마디로 정한다.

en: West.

blocks.html: That night he rides north to the old capital at Gungnae. From there he sends Heonseong west, fifteen years old, to Chang’an, to ask the Third Emperor for an army.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 그는 북쪽 옛 도읍 국내성으로 간다. 거기서 열다섯 살 헌성을 서쪽 장안으로 보내, 황제에게 군대를 청한다.

blocks.html: In Pyongyang the king’s seal comes out. Bojang does not want Namseng dead — he wants the brothers in one room, which is the one thing no seal in Pyongyang can buy that spring. Namgun’s men hold the seal-hand while it presses. The order says arrest. Everyone in the room hears execution, including the man it is written about, by the time the fast rider reaches him.
blocks.ko: 평양에선 왕의 인장이 나온다. 보장왕은 남생을 죽이고 싶지 않다 — 형제를 한 방에 모으고 싶을 뿐인데, 그 봄 평양의 어떤 인장으로도 살 수 없는 것이 바로 그것이다. 남건의 군사들이 인장 든 손을 잡고 찍는다. 명령은 체포라 적혀 있다. 방 안 모두가 처형으로 듣는다. 빠른 말이 닿을 때쯤엔 그 명령이 쓰인 당사자까지도.

blocks.html: Namgun sits down in the big chair the same morning and takes his brother’s title. Nobody pretends not to notice this time. By the end of the month his army is marching north.
blocks.ko: 그날 아침 남건이 큰 의자에 앉아 형의 관작을 가져간다. 이번에는 아무도 못 본 척하지 않는다. 그달이 다 가기 전에 그의 군대가 북쪽으로 떠난다.

blocks.label: Gungnae · Summer
blocks.ko: 국내성 · 여름

blocks.html: Gungnae was the capital before Pyongyang was. The old kings sleep on the slope behind it, under stone steps the size of houses. Namseng holds it with the riders who came north with him, and the handful of nearby cities that still answer to his name.
blocks.ko: 국내성은 평양보다 먼저 도읍이었다. 옛 임금들이 그 뒤 비탈에, 집채만 한 돌계단 밑에 잠들어 있다. 남생은 함께 북으로 온 기병들과, 아직 그의 이름에 대답하는 인근 몇 개 성으로 그곳을 지킨다.

blocks.html: Namgun’s army camps on the river below and does not attack. Nobody in either camp wants to be the first Yeon to kill a Yeon in daylight. Every week the camp gets a little bigger. Every week there are fewer riders on the wall.
blocks.ko: 남건의 군대는 아래 강가에 진을 치고 치지 않는다. 어느 진영에서도 대낮에 연씨를 죽이는 첫 연씨가 되고 싶은 자는 없다. 주마다 진은 조금씩 커진다. 주마다 성벽 위 기병은 줄어든다.

blocks.html: Some nights he walks up the slope to the Great King’s stone, the tall one that lists every city the Great King ever took. He reads it the way other men pray. He has never noticed before how long the list is.
blocks.ko: 어떤 밤에는 비탈을 올라 대왕의 비석까지 간다. 대왕이 빼앗은 성을 하나하나 새겨 둔 그 키 큰 돌이다. 그는 남들이 기도하듯 그것을 읽는다. 그 목록이 이렇게 길다는 걸 전에는 몰랐다.

blocks.label: Defection of Yeon Namseng
blocks.ko: 연남생의 투항

blocks.html: The answer arrives in midsummer, at the head of an army. The emperor has sent the White Dragon, the Tiele horse-lord who took a Goguryeo spear in the waist at Begam twenty-one years ago and rode out again the same evening.
blocks.ko: 답은 한여름에, 군대를 앞세우고 온다. 황제가 보낸 것은 백룡이다. 스물한 해 전 백암에서 고구려 창을 허리에 맞고도 그날 저녁 다시 말에 오른 철륵의 기마 대장.

lines: 백암에서. 너희 나라 창이 여기 들어왔다.
en: At Begam, one of your country’s spears went in here.
…If you can ride, keep up.

lines: 제 나라는 지금 저를 쫓고 있습니다, 장군.
en: My country, General, is chasing me at the moment.
Then ride faster.

blocks.html: Namseng breaks out of Gungnae with the city registers rolled under his arm. Six cities, a hundred thousand households, and every name on them a tax somebody in Chang’an will now collect.
blocks.ko: 남생은 성의 호적을 둘둘 말아 겨드랑이에 끼고 국내성을 빠져나온다. 여섯 성, 십만 호. 거기 적힌 이름 하나하나가 이제 장안의 누군가가 거둘 세금이다.

blocks.html: Namseng rides west, across the river his father spent a lifetime holding.
blocks.ko: 남생은 서쪽으로 말을 몬다. 아버지가 평생을 걸어 지킨 그 강을 건너서.

blocks.caption: North to the old capital, then west over the Liao. His father spent a lifetime stopping men riding this road the other way.
blocks.ko: 북쪽 옛 도읍으로, 다시 서쪽으로 요하를 건너. 아버지는 평생 이 길을 반대로 달려오는 자들을 막았다.

blocks.html: Two brothers keep the city. Years from now one of them will walk out of it with a white flag and ninety-eight men, and be received with courtesy. The other will bar the gate, trust a monk with the keys, and have to be carried. Neither of them knows yet which is which — though Namsan, looking at the ground, has already begun to guess.
blocks.ko: 두 아우가 성을 지킨다. 세월이 지나면 그중 하나가 백기와 아흔여덟 명을 들고 성을 걸어 나가 예로써 접대받을 것이다. 다른 하나는 문을 걸어잠그고 열쇠를 중에게 맡겼다가 들려 나갈 것이다. 둘 다 아직 누가 누군지 모른다 — 땅을 보는 남산은 이미 짐작하기 시작했을 뿐.

blocks.label: Chang’an
blocks.ko: 장안

en: Goryeo is nothing but swindlers and thieves —
a people beyond hope.

lines: …아버님께서 요하에서 만난 아이 이야기를 하신 적이 있소.
en: …My father spoke of a boy he met at the Liao.
One who would not kneel.
zh: ……先帝說過，在遼水遇見一個孩子。
zhLatn: …Xiāndì shuō guò, zài Liáoshuǐ yùjiàn yí ge háizi.
Bù kěn xiàguì de.

lines: 스무 해 전입니다, 폐하. 선제와 저. 선제께서 요수를 건너오셨을 때.
en: Twenty years ago, Majesty. Your father and I, when he crossed the Liao.
I did not kneel then.

blocks.html: He is thirty-two years old, and his brother has taken his title, his city and his father’s seat, and this is the second time in his life he has been offered a house in Chang’an. Nobody flogs him for the answer this time.
blocks.ko: 그는 서른둘이고, 아우가 그의 관작과 도성과 아버지의 자리를 빼앗았으며, 장안의 집을 제안받은 것은 평생 두 번째다. 이번에는 그 대답 때문에 매를 맞지 않는다.

lines: 페하께선, 혼자는 결코 삼한정벌은 못 하실 겁니다.
en: Your Majesty will never conquer Samhan alone.
Emperor… Your Majesty… ten thousand years…!

blocks.html: Namseng is given the Western title, and a vanguard command against his own country.
blocks.ko: 남생은 서국의 관작과 함께, 제 나라를 치는 선봉의 지휘를 받는다.

blocks.html: The Third Emperor has wanted this war since he was a boy, watching his father come home from it. Now it arrives with a guide.
blocks.ko: 황제는 아버지가 그 전쟁에서 돌아오는 것을 지켜보던 소년 시절부터 이 전쟁을 원했다. 이제 그 전쟁이 길잡이를 데리고 찾아온다.

blocks.html: In the south their uncle Yeon Jungto, who raised two of them, waits to hear which nephew will send for him. Neither does. He takes twelve cities over to Silla, and the family is finished in three directions at once. Silla’s clerks, who love a total, write down seven hundred and sixty-three households and three thousand five hundred and forty-three people.
blocks.ko: 남쪽에서는 그 둘을 키운 숙부 연정토가 어느 조카가 자기를 부르러 올지 기다린다. 아무도 오지 않는다. 그는 열두 성을 들고 신라로 넘어가고, 그 집안은 한꺼번에 세 방향에서 끝난다. 합계를 좋아하는 신라의 서기들은 칠백예순세 호, 삼천오백마흔세 명이라고 적는다.

blocks.html: In the twelfth month the emperor names his marshal for the last war. It is the Blue Dragon, past seventy now, who took Yodong from Goguryeo twenty-one years ago and has been patient ever since. Last time he had to walk around the wall. This time he has a man who knows where the doors are.
blocks.ko: 열두째 달, 황제가 마지막 전쟁의 총사령을 정한다. 청룡이다. 이제 일흔이 넘었고, 스물한 해 전 고구려에게서 요동성을 빼앗은 뒤로 줄곧 참아 온 사람이다. 지난번에는 성벽을 돌아가야 했다. 이번에는 문이 어디 있는지 아는 사람이 있다.

blocks.html: Years later, in the emperor’s country, Namseng’s tombstone will tell the story his way.
blocks.ko: 훗날 황제의 땅에서, 남생의 묘지석은 그 이야기를 그의 방식대로 전할 것이다.

blocks.html: His heart was loyal, but matters went wrong at the centre. He had just gone out to comfort the border folk and tour the wild marches, to survey the old lands of the dawn country and ask for new officers to govern them. Then his two younger brothers, Namsan and Namgun, turned vicious and rebellious in a single morning. Heartless to their own blood, they raised troops and shut him out from within. His little son with the gold ring fell suddenly into the whale's jaws, and left the long table and his parents' arms for ever.
blocks.ko: 공은 속마음으로 정성을 다했으나, 일은 조정 한가운데서 어그러졌다. 공이 막 변방 백성을 어루만지고 거친 들을 순시하러 나가, 동쪽 옛 땅을 살피고 새 관원을 청하려 할 때였다. 두 아우 남산과 남건이 하루아침에 흉악하게 패역하여, 혈육도 아랑곳없이 군사를 일으켜 안에서 막아섰다. 금고리를 찬 어린 아들은 졸지에 고래 아가리에 떨어져, 진수성찬 차린 긴 자리와 부모의 품을 문득 떠났다.
blocks.hanja: 公情思內款，事乖中執。方欲出撫邊甿，外巡荒甸，按嵎夷之舊壤，請羲仲之新官。二弟產建，一朝兇悖，能忍無親，稱兵內拒。金環幼子，忽就鯨鯢，玉膳長筵，俄辭顧復。
blocks.source: Epitaph of Yeon Namseng (泉男生墓誌) — Luoyang, 679; transcription in the Korean Ancient History DB (한국 고대 사료 DB)

blocks.html: Two eldest sons, two rivers. In the south Yung counts his eleven years on a boat to Ungjin; in the north Namseng counts his thirty-two on the road to Chang’an. Each leaves a younger brother holding a burning house — Hyo with the mark, Namgun with the gate. The West will take both houses in. That is what the West are for.
blocks.ko: 두 맏아들, 두 강. 남쪽에선 융이 열한 해를 세며 웅진으로 가는 배에 있고, 북쪽에선 남생이 서른두 해를 세며 장안으로 가는 길에 있다. 각자 불타는 집을 든 아우를 남긴다 — 효는 표를, 남건은 성문을. 당은 두 집을 다 받아들일 것이다. 당이란 그런 데 쓰는 것이다.

blocks.html: Namseng knows the road in. Now he rides it home, with the whole Western army at his back…!
blocks.ko: 남생은 들어가는 길을 안다. 이제 그는 서국의 대군을 등 뒤에 달고, 그 길로 집에 돌아온다…!

logline.en: When the ring closes, the city needs one man nobody can buy. They pick a monk.
logline.ko: 포위가 닫히자, 도성에는 아무도 살 수 없는 사내 하나가 필요하다. 그들은 승려를 고른다.
