blocks.html: Before there are any kingdoms, there is a son in heaven who keeps looking down. He is Hwanung. His father Hannim, the Lord of Heaven, notices, looks down himself at a mountain called Tebek and the people living around it, and decides the world could use his son.
blocks.ko: 나라라는 것이 하나도 없던 때, 하늘에 자꾸 아래를 내려다보는 아들이 있다. 환웅이다. 아버지인 하늘의 임금 한님이 그것을 알아채고, 저도 태백이라는 산과 그 둘레에 사는 사람들을 내려다본 뒤, 세상에 아들이 쓸모 있겠다고 정한다.

blocks.caption: The Lord of Heaven. He has been watching this peninsula since before it had names.
blocks.ko: 하늘의 주인. 이 반도에 이름이 생기기 전부터 내려다보고 있었다.

blocks.title: Old Joseon · 고조선
blocks.caption: Heaven’s mandate made into a capital: Hannim → Hwanung → Dangun → Asadal.
blocks.ko: 하늘의 명을 수도로 만든 계보. 한님 → 환웅 → 단군 → 아사달.

blocks.html: Hannim does not plough — he opens the sky. Three seals go down with his son, so that nobody on the ground can mistake him for a prince playing at exile. Every later king in this chronicle will cut seals of his own, and every one of them is copying these.
blocks.ko: 한님은 갈지 않는다 — 하늘을 연다. 아들과 함께 천부인 셋이 내려간다. 땅의 누구도 그를 유배 놀이 하는 왕자로 착각하지 못하게. 이 편년의 후대 임금들은 저마다 제 인장을 새길 것이고, 그 모두가 이것을 베낀다.

blocks.html: Hwanung lands on a mountain under the sacred birch. He names the ground beneath it the Divine City. Three thousand followers come down with him. Among them are the lords of wind, rain and cloud. Someone has to argue with the weather.
blocks.ko: 환웅은 신단수 아래 산에 내려앉는다. 그 밑의 땅을 신시라 부른다. 무리 삼천이 함께 내려온다. 그 가운데 바람과 비와 구름의 우두머리들이 있다. 누군가는 날씨와 말다툼을 해야 하니까.

blocks.caption: Hwanung. A son of heaven who kept looking down until his father let him go.
blocks.ko: 환웅. 자꾸 아래를 내려다보다가, 끝내 아버지가 보내 준 하늘의 아들.

blocks.html: From there he hands out civilisation in instalments. Laws. Punishments. Lifespans. Illness. Good and evil. Medicine. Three hundred and sixty matters in all. Somebody counted.
blocks.ko: 거기서 그는 훗날 문명이라 불릴 것을 할부로 나눠 준다. 법. 형벌. 수명. 병. 선과 악. 의술. 모두 삼백육십 가지. 누군가 세어 두었다.

blocks.html: There is a short way to tell the rest, the way it is carved on stones. The long way begins, as long ways do, with a bear who wanted something so badly that she outlasted a tiger for it.
blocks.ko: 나머지를 짧게 전하는 방식이 있다. 돌에 새기는 방식이다. 길게 전하는 방식은, 긴 이야기가 늘 그렇듯, 무언가를 너무나 간절히 원한 나머지 호랑이보다 오래 견딘 곰 한 마리에서 시작된다.

blocks.html: A bear and a tiger come to him and ask to be made human. He gives them a bundle of mugwort, twenty cloves of garlic, and one instruction: stay out of the sun for a hundred days.
blocks.ko: 곰과 범이 그를 찾아와 사람이 되게 해 달라 청한다. 그는 쑥 한 줌과 마늘 스무 쪽을 주고 한 가지를 이른다. 백 일 동안 햇빛을 보지 마라.

blocks.label: The Sacred Birch
blocks.ko: 신단수

blocks.html: The bear stays. She comes out a woman on the twenty-first morning, garlic still on her breath, and finds the mountain already staffed — wind, rain, cloud, and not one of them a husband. So she stands under the sacred tree. Not once. Every day, on the path he has to take if he means to reach the hall.
blocks.ko: 곰은 남는다. 스무하루째 아침, 입가에 마늘 냄새가 남은 채로 여자가 되어 나오니, 산은 이미 사람이 가득하다 — 바람, 비, 구름, 그리고 남편이 될 이는 하나도 없다. 그래서 신단수 아래에 선다. 한 번이 아니다. 그가 전각으로 가려면 반드시 지나야 하는 길에, 날마다.
blocks.art: Open on the cave mouth: the tiger’s tracks leading away into the snow, then her first step into daylight.

blocks.caption: Ungnyu. Twenty-one days in a cave, and the tiger left first. A husband should be easy.
blocks.ko: 웅녀. 동굴에서 스무하루, 먼저 나간 건 호랑이였다. 지아비 하나쯤이야.

blocks.html: He means to reach the hall. On the third evening he gets as far as the birch, and the seal in his hand becomes a thing he is holding for no reason he can name.
blocks.ko: 그는 전각에 닿을 작정이다. 사흘째 저녁, 자작나무까지는 온다. 손의 인장은, 왜 들고 있는지 스스로도 말할 수 없는 물건이 된다.

en: You're going to walk past again.
…Not today.
Yesterday you did.
And the day before. I was standing right here.
I saw you.
The garlic reached this far.
Twenty-one days of that, and this is what came out.
…I was going to say don't come closer.

lines: 가지 마. 아니— 가지 마시오. 손이—
en: Too late.
Stay. I mean— don't go. Your hand—
You already have the hand.
…Scared of the rest?
I am.
Because you're looking at me.

lines: 나무는 보고 있을 테니까. 나는… 더.
en: Then come down.
The tree can watch. I want… more.

blocks.html: The kiss is clumsy. Beard, a new mouth, birch bark at her back. She makes a small furious sound and tries again, and the second one lands.
blocks.ko: 입맞춤은 서투르다. 수염, 처음 쓰는 입, 등에 닿는 자작나무 껍질. 그녀가 짧게 성난 소리를 내고 다시 하고, 두 번째는 닿는다.

blocks.html: White silk goes down among the roots. The fur at her throat opens under his mouth. She laughs once, startled at the sound, and pulls him down by the hair.
blocks.ko: 흰 비단이 뿌리 사이에 내려앉는다. 목덜미의 털깃이 그의 입 밑에서 풀린다. 그녀는 한 번 웃는다. 그 소리에 스스로 놀라서. 그리고 머리카락을 잡아 그를 끌어내린다.

blocks.html: By the time the moon clears the snow on the peak, the rust-red sash is somewhere in the moss, and neither of them has gone back up the path.
blocks.ko: 달빛이 봉우리의 눈에 닿을 때쯤, 붉은 띠는 이끼 어딘가에 있고, 둘 다 그 길로 돌아 올라가지 않았다.

en: …You're going already?
I can't.
I don't know where I put the seal.
Under my head.
I took it. …Don't go.
…Thief.
Marry me in the morning.
Right now I'm here.

blocks.label: Asadal
blocks.ko: 아사달

blocks.html: Their son is Dangun. The name on the stone is Wanggum: a king who governs, not one who inherits a bone rank. He founds Asadal where the mountain meets the plain. He rules for fifteen hundred years, and then he becomes the mountain.
blocks.ko: 그 아들이 단군이다. 돌에 새긴 이름은 왕검. 골품을 물려받은 임금이 아니라 다스리는 임금이다. 그는 산과 들이 만나는 곳에 아사달을 세운다. 천오백 년을 다스리고, 산이 된다.

blocks.caption: Dangun. Half heaven, half bear, and all the paperwork of a first king.
blocks.ko: 단군. 반은 하늘, 반은 곰, 그리고 첫 임금의 서류는 전부 그의 몫.

blocks.hanja: 乃授天符印三箇 雄率徒三千 降於太伯山頂神壇樹下 是謂神市 熊女與婚 生子 號曰壇君王儉
blocks.ko: 이에 천부인 셋을 주어 다스리게 하니, 환웅이 무리 삼천을 이끌고 태백산 꼭대기 신단수 아래로 내려와 이를 신시라 하였다. 웅녀와 혼인하여 아들을 낳으니, 이름하여 단군왕검이라 하였다.
blocks.html: He granted three heavenly seals and sent him to govern. Hwanung led a following of three thousand and descended under the sacred altar-tree on the summit of Mount Tebek; this was called the Divine City. He married the bear-woman, and she bore a son named Dangun Wanggum.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 1, Wonder 1 — Old Joseon (Dangun); Ha & Mintz tr., pp. 32–33

blocks.html: Where the mountain meets the plain, and the first crown met both.
blocks.ko: 산이 들을 만나는 곳. 첫 왕관이 둘 다를 만난 곳.

blocks.html: Every later crown in these kingdoms argues, one way or another, back to the woman who used to be a bear. Her son’s city keeps his name long after he has become a mountain.
blocks.ko: 이후 이 왕국들의 왕관은, 어떤 식으로든, 한때 곰이었던 여자에게로 거슬러 올라간다. 아들의 도성은 그가 산이 된 뒤에도 오래 그의 이름을 지닌다.

blocks.label: The Fall of Joseon
blocks.ko: 조선의 멸망

blocks.html: Joseon outlives its founder by a long way. Two thousand years on it is still there, run by other kings now, from a walled city on the Tedong that has kept his name: Wanggum. In the autumn of 109 BC, Han comes to the gate.
blocks.ko: 조선은 시조보다 훨씬 오래 산다. 이천 년이 지나도 여전히 거기 있다. 이제는 다른 임금들이, 그의 이름 왕검을 그대로 지닌 대동강가의 성에서 다스린다. 기원전 109년 가을, 한나라가 그 성문 앞에 온다.

blocks.html: It takes the empire of the West a year to take one fortress, and they do not take it. Wanggum holds through a siege that begins in the autumn and is still going the following autumn.
blocks.ko: 서토의 제국이 성 하나를 얻는 데 한 해가 걸리고, 결국 얻지 못한다. 왕검성은 가을에 시작해 이듬해 가을까지 이어지는 포위를 견딘다.

blocks.html: So they stop attacking the walls and start talking to the men behind them, which is cheaper and has never once failed.
blocks.ko: 그래서 그들은 성벽을 치는 일을 그만두고, 성벽 뒤의 사람들과 이야기하기 시작한다. 더 싸고, 단 한 번도 실패한 적 없는 방법이다.

blocks.label: The King's Wall
blocks.ko: 왕의 성벽

blocks.html: King Ugu has stopped sleeping in the palace. He sleeps on the wall, where he can hear the Han camp coughing, and his son, the prince, has started sleeping somewhere else.
blocks.ko: 우거왕은 궁에서 자지 않은 지 오래다. 한나라 진영의 기침 소리가 들리는 성벽 위에서 잔다. 태자는 언제부턴가 다른 데서 잔다.

lines: 성문만 열면 성 안 사람은 아무도 건드리지 않겠답니다.
en: Father. They’ve sent terms again.
Open the gate, they say, and nobody inside gets hurt.
They said that last autumn.
Who brought it to you?
…Does it matter who?
It matters.
Get off my wall.

blocks.html: One of the ministers who have been doing the talking goes over the wall that week and dies on the road before he reaches the Han tents. Another does not bother with the road. One night at the start of summer he sends men up the wall-stair instead.
blocks.ko: 말을 주고받던 대신 하나가 그 주에 성벽을 넘어가다, 한나라 장막에 닿기도 전에 길에서 죽는다. 또 한 대신은 길로 나서지 않는다. 초여름 어느 밤, 그는 성벽 계단으로 사람들을 올려 보낸다.
blocks.art: Torchlight on the wall-stair, knives, the king turning from the parapet too late.

en: Majesty—!
blocks.speaker: Sung Gi

lines: 사람들 데리고 나가. 살아서… 어디서든, 새로 나라를 세워라.
en: …Sung Gi?
Don’t hold the city. Not for me.
Get the people out. Live… and make a new country. Anywhere.

blocks.html: Sung Gi closes the king’s eyes, goes back up to the parapet, and holds the city anyway.
blocks.ko: 성기는 임금의 눈을 감기고, 다시 성가퀴로 올라가, 그래도 성을 지킨다.

blocks.html: He holds it until the dead minister’s son and the prince go down into the lanes, where people have been eating bark since the spring.
blocks.ko: 죽은 대신의 아들과 태자가 골목으로 내려갈 때까지는 지킨다. 골목 사람들은 봄부터 나무껍질을 먹고 있었다.

lines: 그럼 이제 누구 때문에 굶는 거요? 저 사람?
en: The king is dead.
So who are you starving for now? Him?
blocks.art: Choi pointing up at Seong Gi on the wall.

blocks.html: Before morning Sung Gi is dead too.
blocks.ko: 아침이 오기 전에 성기도 죽는다.

blocks.html: Someone lifts the bar.
blocks.ko: 누군가 빗장을 든다.
blocks.art: Wordless. The gate of Wanggeom swings open from the inside; Han banners wait in the grey light.

en: The wall did not come down.
A door was opened from the inside.

blocks.html: Han takes Wanggum. Some of the people the king told to live go south over the mountains. They settle in six villages around Surabol. Two generations later, they'll go looking for a king. The rest stay, and the empire cuts them into four pieces. The last piece is still collecting taxes four hundred years later.
blocks.ko: 한나라가 왕검성을 차지한다. 임금이 살라고 한 사람들 가운데 일부는 산을 넘어 남쪽으로 간다. 서라벌 둘레 골짜기에 여섯 마을을 이룬다. 두 세대 뒤, 그들은 임금을 찾아 나설 것이다. 나머지는 남아, 제국의 손에 넷으로 쪼개진다. 그 마지막 하나는 사백 년 뒤에도 세금을 걷고 있다.

blocks.html: That is the story Munmu gets, in his mother’s version, with extra garlic. He came for the bear. He keeps thinking about the door.
blocks.ko: 문무가 들은 이야기는 그것이다. 어머니 판본이라, 마늘이 좀 더 들어갔다. 그는 곰 이야기를 들으러 왔다. 그런데 자꾸 문 생각이 난다.

blocks.html: Eight hundred years later, the empire comes back to the same river to do the same thing. This time, Goguryeo has a prince left…!
blocks.ko: 팔백 년 뒤, 제국이 같은 강으로 돌아와 같은 짓을 한다. 이번에는 고구려에 왕족 하나가 남아 있다…!

logline.en: Gum Mojam raises Goguryeo’s flag and finds a royal to stand under it. They disagree about dying, and only one of them sees the morning.
logline.ko: 검모잠이 고구려의 깃발을 세우고 그 아래 세울 왕족을 찾는다. 둘은 죽는 일을 두고 갈라서고, 아침을 맞는 건 하나뿐이다.

images.prompt: CLOSING STILL of the episode: the final scene of this story as it ends (not the next episode). The line: “Ansung bows when the seal comes, very low: a king of Goguryeo in a Silla hall. Far north, on the Tedong, a tent is still standing with nobody in it.” Context: A king of Goguryeo in Silla. The emperor will hate it. Good. Give him a seal. A big one. And end the patent the way the emperor ends his. “Be reverent.” Twice. He’ll hate that most of all. Ansung bows when the seal comes, very low: a king of Goguryeo in a Silla hall. Far north, on the Tedong, a tent is still standing with nobody in it. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — KING MUNMU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_munmu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. | PLACE Pyongyang (평양성) — attached board /pl_pyongyang_city.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Pyongyang: Goguryeo walled city on the Taedong, stone walls and red munru gate pavilions. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). COMMONERS in every Samhan kingdom wear SIMPLE WHITE: plain undyed white or off-white hemp and ramie jackets, wide trousers and skirts, a cloth sash, straw sandals or bare feet, hair in a plain topknot or braid — no dyed silk, no dots, no gold; colour belongs to rank, so a crowd of farmers, porters, servants and townsfolk reads as a field of soft white cloth with the officials' colours standing out of it. Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: The Protectorate
blocks.ko: 안동도호부

blocks.html: Every revival needs two things: a flag and a royal. Gum Mojam has the flag.
blocks.ko: 부흥에는 두 가지가 필요하다. 깃발 하나와 왕족 하나. 검모잠에게는 깃발이 있다.

blocks.html: The empire has done it again on the Tedong. Pyongyang is a Protectorate now, run by the Western clerks who seem surprised that anyone minds. Mojam minds. He kills the clerks, raises Goguryeo’s colours, and goes looking for someone royal to stand under them.
blocks.ko: 제국이 대동강에서 또 같은 짓을 했다. 평양은 이제 도호부다. 누가 싫어하는 걸 보고 놀라는 서국의 서기들이 다스린다. 모잠은 싫다. 서기들을 죽이고, 고구려의 깃발을 올리고, 그 아래 세울 왕족을 찾아 나선다.

blocks.html: He finds one on an island in the western sea, mending a net. His name is Ansung. His father is Yeon Jungto, the uncle who took twelve cities over to Silla. His mother was a king’s daughter. Mojam only needs the second half.
blocks.ko: 그는 서해의 한 섬에서 그물을 깁고 있는 사내를 찾아낸다. 이름은 안승. 아버지는 열두 성을 들고 신라로 넘어간 숙부, 연정토다. 어머니는 왕의 딸이었다. 모잠에게 필요한 건 뒤의 절반뿐이다.

blocks.html: Mojam, a daehyeong of Goguryeo from Surim Fortress, gathered the surviving people, marched from Gungmo Fortress to south of the Pae River, and killed the Tang officials and the monk Bup'an. Heading for Silla, he reached Saya Island in the western sea, found Ansung, son of the Goguryeo minister Yeon Jungto, brought him into the River Palace, and set him up as lord.
blocks.ko: 고구려 수림성 사람 대형 모잠이 남은 백성을 거두어 모아, 궁모성에서 패강 남쪽에 이르러 당의 관인과 승려 법안 등을 죽였다. 신라로 향해 가다가 서해 사야도에 이르러, 고구려 대신 연정토의 아들 안승을 만나 한성 안으로 맞아들이고 임금으로 받들었다.
blocks.hanja: 高句麗水臨城人牟岑大兄，收合殘民，自窮牟城，至浿江南，殺唐官人及僧法安等。向新羅行，至西海史冶島，見高句麗大臣淵淨土之子安勝，迎致漢城中，奉以爲君。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 6, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 10 (670), sixth month

blocks.label: The River Camp
blocks.ko: 강가 진영

blocks.html: By the next spring the revival has a court, a royal, and four thousand households camped along the river. It also has the Western army coming down the north road. The two men argue about it in front of everyone, because a revival has no rooms with doors.
blocks.ko: 이듬해 봄, 부흥군에게는 조정이 있고, 왕족이 있고, 강을 따라 진을 친 사천 호가 있다. 북쪽 길로 내려오는 서군도 있다. 두 사내는 모두가 보는 앞에서 그 일로 다툰다. 부흥군에게는 문 달린 방이 없으니까.

blocks.speaker: Gum Mojam
en: We hold the river. We hold Pyongyang.
If they’re wanting it back, they can climb over us.
lines: 도로 가져가갓다면 우리 시체를 넘어오라 하시오.

blocks.speaker: Ansung
en: They climbed over Pyongyang two years ago. With better walls than ours in the way.
lines: 두 해 전에 데들은 평양도 넘었소. 우리 것보다 나은 성벽을 두고도.

blocks.speaker: Gum Mojam
lines: 평양 땅에는 사백 년 묵은 임금들이 묻혀 계시오. 그분들을 두고 신라 사랑채로 가갓다는 거요?
en: Pyongyang has kings in its soil four hundred years deep. You want to leave them for a Silla guest room?

blocks.speaker: Ansung
lines: 땅속의 임금들은 기다려 주실 거요. 그 위의 사천 호는 못 기다리오.
en: The kings in the soil will keep. The four thousand households above it won’t.

blocks.speaker: Gum Mojam
en: Then go. Take your households.
I’ll hold it with whoever stays.
lines: 기럼 가시오. 그 사천 호 데리고.

blocks.html: He says it loud, to the fires. Around the fires, men stop eating. Ansung looks at them. Nobody stands up. Nobody sits down either. He understands what that means before Mojam does. In the morning they will follow whoever is still alive.
blocks.ko: 그는 그 말을 크게, 모닥불들 쪽으로 한다. 불가의 사내들이 먹던 손을 멈춘다. 안승이 그들을 본다. 일어서는 자도 없고, 다시 앉는 자도 없다. 그게 무슨 뜻인지 그는 모잠보다 먼저 안다. 아침이 되면, 저들은 살아 있는 쪽을 따를 것이다.

blocks.speaker: Ansung
en: …You’re right, General.
Let’s sleep on it.

blocks.html: That night Ansung has him killed in his tent. It is the first Goguryeo blood the revival spills, and it is spilled by Goguryeo.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 안승은 그를 장막 안에서 죽인다. 부흥군이 흘린 첫 고구려 피이고, 그것을 흘린 것도 고구려다.

blocks.html: In the morning the men by the fires do not ask where the general is. They pack.
blocks.ko: 아침에 불가의 사내들은 장군이 어디 있느냐고 묻지 않는다. 짐을 싼다.

blocks.html: Then he takes four thousand households south, to Silla.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 사천 호를 이끌고 남쪽 신라로 간다.

blocks.label: Silla's Guest
blocks.ko: 신라의 손님

blocks.html: Munmu gives him a title, a district, and a name for the thing: Goguryeo, still standing, inside Silla. It is a useful fiction and both sides know exactly how useful.
blocks.ko: 문무왕은 그에게 관작과 고을과 이름 하나를 준다. 신라 안에 여전히 서 있는 고구려. 쓸모 있는 허구이고, 양쪽 다 그것이 얼마나 쓸모 있는지 정확히 안다.

blocks.html: Silla settles him in a town that was somebody else's kingdom ten years ago. Within the year he is called King of Goguryeo. In time he gets a bride, and a seat at Munmu's feasts. Well below the king's.
blocks.ko: 신라는 그를 열 해 전까지 남의 나라 땅이던 고을에 앉힌다. 그해가 가기 전에 그는 고구려왕이라 불린다. 때가 되자 신부도 얻고, 문무의 잔치에 자리도 얻는다. 왕의 자리보다 한참 아래다.

lines: 신라 안에 고구려 왕이라. 황제가 질색하겠군.
en: A king of Goguryeo in Silla. The emperor will hate it.
Good. Give him a seal. A big one.
And end the patent the way the emperor ends his. “Be reverent.”
Twice. He’ll hate that most of all.
lines: 책서 끝은 황제가 쓰는 대로 맺어라. ‘삼가고 삼갈지어다.’
두 번. 그게 제일 싫을 거다.

blocks.html: Ansung bows when the seal comes, very low: a king of Goguryeo in a Silla hall. Far north, on the Tedong, a tent is still standing with nobody in it.
blocks.ko: 인장이 오자 안승은 아주 깊이 절한다. 신라의 전각 안에 선 고구려의 왕. 저 북쪽 대동강가에는, 아무도 없는 장막 하나가 아직 서 있다.

blocks.html: The emperor hears there is a king of Goguryeo in Silla. His general reaches for a brush instead of a sword…!
blocks.ko: 황제가 신라 안에 고구려 왕이 있다는 말을 듣는다. 그의 장수는 칼 대신 붓을 집어 든다…!

logline.en: Xue Rengui would like to win this war by post. The king does not go to bed.
logline.ko: 설인귀는 이 전쟁을 편지로 이기고 싶어 한다. 왕은 잠자리에 들지 않는다.

images.at: Alas! While the two kingdoms stood

In the foreground the scribe's bent back and brush hand over a long paper scroll, out of focus, the writing a soft blur, nothing readable. An ink-stone and spent candle stubs on the desk. Munmu's shadow climbs the receding plaster wall. Key: the desk lamp from below, crimson #C41E3A specular on his silk; the rest umber black. CANON — KING MUNMU — FACE and garments from attached /ch_munmu.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Crown: Silla gold crown, as the attached crown: a gold band with three tree-shaped uprights stepped like the character 出 and two antler uprights at the back, hung with round gold spangles and curved green jade gogok, long gold pendants at the temples. ref_muyeol shows it worn with the king's red robe and gold-scroll collar (ignore its painted backdrop). Demeanor: Cocky, warm, practical; his father's charm with his uncle's spine. #C41E3A as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: katana; Tang dragon robe in place of Silla court dress. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: The First Letter
blocks.ko: 첫 번째 편지

blocks.html: In high summer, the Western monk is rowed ashore under a white flag. He carries a letter from the fleet. The fleet belongs to Xue Rengui, the second White Tiger. He has sat off the coast all summer. If it can be managed, he'd like to win this war by post.
blocks.ko: 한여름, 서국 승려 하나가 흰 깃발을 단 배로 뭍에 오른다. 함대에서 온 편지를 들고서. 함대의 주인은 두 번째 백호, 설인귀다. 그는 여름 내내 해안 밖에 떠 있었다. 될 수만 있다면, 이 전쟁을 편지로 이기고 싶다.

blocks.speaker: Imyun
lines: 대총관께서 문안을 여쭙니다, 전하. 소리 내어 읽어 주십사 하셨습니다.
en: The Commander sends his respects, Majesty. He asks that it be read aloud.
He says it reads better aloud.
zh: 大總管問候大王。請高聲宣讀。
zhLatn: Dà zǒngguǎn wènhòu dàwáng. Qǐng gāoshēng xuāndú.
Tā shuō dú chūlái gèng hǎo.

lines: 신라 왕께, 동방 행군대총관 설인귀가 문안드립니다.
맑은 바람은 도성에서 그대 해안까지 만 리를 불고, 그 사이 바다는 삼천 리입니다. 그 길을 다 건너와 드릴 말씀은 하나뿐입니다.
그대의 아버님은 선제 앞에 무릎을 꿇었고, 일으켜 세워졌습니다. 관복을 받고, 형제를 얻고, 군대를 얻었지요. 그대는 그분의 왕관을 받았고요.
그런데 이제 그대는 황제의 병사들이 피 흘린 땅을 차지하고, 황제의 반역자들을 감싸 주고 있습니다. 그대의 아우는 장안에서, 형님 소식을 물을까 봐 고개를 들지 못합니다.
돌아설 길이 남아 있을 때 돌아서십시오.
이 일 하나만 빼고 모든 일에서, 전하의 종으로 남기를 영광으로 여기며 —
en: To the King of Silla, from Xue Rengui, Commander of the Eastern Fleet, greetings.
A clear wind blows ten thousand li from the capital to your coast, and the sea between is three thousand. I have come all of it to say one thing.
Your father knelt before the Second Emperor and was raised up. He was given robes, and a brother, and an army. You were given his crown.
And now you take the land the emperor’s soldiers bled for, and you shelter his rebels, and your own brother waits in Chang’an, ashamed to be asked about you.
Turn back while there is still a road to turn on.
I have the honour to remain, in all things but this, Your Majesty’s servant —
Xue Rengui.
zh: 新羅王足下：東方行軍大總管薛仁貴致意。
清風萬里，大海三千。仁貴遠來，只為一言。
先王跪於先帝之前，蒙恩而起；賜之冠服，結為兄弟，假以兵馬。王受其冠。
今王據天兵流血之地，庇朝廷之叛臣；令弟在長安，人問及王，羞不能答。
仁貴除此一事之外，萬事皆為大王之僕——
zhLatn: Xīnluó wáng zúxià: Dōngfāng xíngjūn dà zǒngguǎn Xuē Rénguì zhìyì.
Qīngfēng wàn lǐ, dàhǎi sān qiān. Rénguì yuǎn lái, zhǐ wèi yì yán.
Xiānwáng guì yú xiāndì zhī qián, méng ēn ér qǐ; cì zhī guānfú, jié wéi xiōngdì, jiǎ yǐ bīngmǎ. Wáng shòu qí guān.
Jīn wáng jù tiānbīng liúxuè zhī dì, bì cháotíng zhī pànchén; lìngdì zài Cháng’ān, rén wèn jí wáng, xiū bù néng dá.
Jí lù wèi jué, huítóu kě yě.
Rénguì chú cǐ yí shì zhī wài, wànshì jiē wéi dàwáng zhī pú——
Xuē Rénguì.

blocks.html: The copy the archives keep is longer, and has a cicada in it.
blocks.ko: 기록에 남은 판본은 더 길고, 매미가 한 마리 나온다.

blocks.html: It is like a man who goes out with his sling and never sees the dry well at his feet, or reaches for the cicada and never knows the oriole is behind him. That is Your Majesty, not knowing your own measure. … Alas! Once loyal and righteous, now a rebel subject. I grieve that what began in good fortune ends in ill, that what grew from one root ends in different branches. The wind is high and the air is sharp; the leaves fall and the year turns sad. I lean on the mountain and look far off, and it wounds my heart.
blocks.ko: 이는 탄궁을 들고 나서면서 마른 우물의 위험을 보지 못하고, 매미를 잡으려 나아가면서 뒤에서 노리는 꾀꼬리를 알지 못하는 것과 같으니, 이것이 왕께서 스스로를 헤아리지 못하시는 바입니다. … 아아, 예전에는 충의의 신하였는데 이제는 역신이 되셨습니다. 처음은 길하였으나 끝이 흉함이 한스럽고, 뿌리는 같았으나 끝이 갈라짐이 원망스럽습니다. 바람은 높고 기운은 매서우며, 잎이 지니 한 해가 서럽습니다. 산에 기대어 멀리 바라보니 가슴이 아픕니다.
blocks.hanja: 亦由持彈而往，暗於枯井之危，捕蟬而前，不知黄雀之難，此王之不知量也。…嗚呼，昔爲忠義，今乃逆臣，恨始吉而終凶，怨本同而末異。風高氣切，葉落年悲，憑山遠望，有傷懷抱。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 11 (671), seventh month — Xue Rengui's letter, carried by the monk Imyun

blocks.html: The monk is given a bed, a meal, and as long as it takes. The king does not go to bed at all.
blocks.ko: 승려에게는 잠자리와 끼니와, 필요한 만큼의 시간이 주어진다. 왕은 아예 잠자리에 들지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Writing Room
blocks.ko: 글방

blocks.html: By the second night the king’s writing room is full of men with opinions. One of them, an official named Deto, has more than most.
blocks.ko: 이틀째 밤, 왕의 글방은 할 말 있는 사내들로 가득하다. 그중 대토라는 관리는 남들보다 할 말이 많다.

lines: 전하, 여기저기 말 한두 마디 누그러뜨린다고 손해 볼 건 없습니다.
그 편지를 쓴 자가 바로 그 흰옷입니다. 포구에서는 여포가 살아 돌아와 우리 바다에 떠 있다고들 합니다.
저들은 웅진 앞바다에 함대가 있고, 인문 공도 데리고 있습니다. 국경을 잘못 알았다고 하면 안 되겠습니까? 국경이야 다들 잘못 아는 거잖습니까.
en: Majesty, a softer word here and there costs nothing.
The man who wrote it is the one in white. In the ports they say Lu Bu has come back and is sitting off our coast.
They have a fleet off Bear Ford. They have Prince Inmun. Could we not say we were mistaken about the border? Everyone is mistaken about borders.
We were not mistaken.
Write it the way I say it.

blocks.html: There is another reason the room is careful. Nine summers ago, the king killed a great lord and his whole house for calling in sick. The lord's son wasn't in the house. He's in the emperor's guard. Somebody there will have told him by now.
blocks.ko: 방 안이 조심스러운 까닭이 하나 더 있다. 아홉 해 전, 왕은 병을 핑계 댄 대귀족 하나를 집안째 죽였다. 그 아들은 집에 없었다. 황제의 숙위에 있다. 거기 누군가가 벌써 그에게 말해 주었을 것이다.

blocks.label: The Reply
blocks.ko: 답서

lines: 그대의 편지는 승려 편에 왔고, 청한 대로 소리 내어 읽었소. 과연 소리 내어 읽으니 낫더이다. 이 편지도 그럴 것이오.
en: To the Commander of the Eastern Fleet, from the King of Silla.
Your letter came by a monk, and was read aloud as you asked. It does read better aloud. So will this.

blocks.html: He dictates the rest standing up, and does not stop for most of the night.
blocks.ko: 그는 나머지를 선 채로 받아쓰게 하고, 밤새 거의 멈추지 않는다.

lines: 정관 이십이 년에 내 아버님이 장안에 가셨소. 선제께서는 아버님을 돌말들이 늘어선 회랑으로 데려가 말씀하셨지. 평양 이남과 백제 땅은 모두 신라의 것이다, 영원히.
아버님은 내가 스물둘일 때 그 말을 외우게 하셨소. 나는 지금도 외우오. 황제의 서기들도 외우고 있으리라 믿소.
en: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan my father went to Chang’an. The Second Emperor took him into a gallery of stone horses and said: everything south of Pyongyang, and the whole of Baekje, shall be Silla’s, forever.
My father made me learn those words when I was twenty-two. I have them still. I expect the emperor’s clerks have them too.

lines: 그대의 주작이 평양 밖에 앉아 제 말을 잡아먹고 있을 때, 내 외숙은 예순일곱이었소. 가슴까지 차는 눈 속을, 제 흰 말이 자기 대신 쌀을 지도록 그 곁에서 걸어갔소. 그대의 병사들은 수레를 보고 울었소. 그대의 장군은 쌀을 받고 그 주에 배를 타고 돌아갔고.
늦었다 하더이다. 우리는 늘 늦소. 그래도 갔소.
en: When your Red Fowl sat outside Pyongyang eating his horses, my uncle was sixty-seven. He walked beside his own white horse through snow to its chest so the horse could carry rice instead of him. Your soldiers wept when they saw the carts. Your general took the rice and sailed home the same week.
We were late, he said. We are always late. We came anyway.

lines: 그러고 나서 그대들은 백제를 백제 왕자에게 돌려주었소. 서국의 도장을 찍어서, 웅진에. 그러고는 우리를 취리산이라는 산으로 데려가, 죽은 말 위에서 그자의 형제가 되겠다고 맹세하게 했지.
그 말은 내 외숙의 말이었소. 외숙이 손수 끌고 올라갔소. 나는 그 손을 보았소.
en: Then you gave Baekje back to a Baekje prince, with the Western seal, at Bear Ford. Then you took us up a hill called Prosperity Mountain and made us swear to be his brother over a dead horse.
The horse was my uncle’s. He walked it up himself. I watched his hands.

lines: 평양에서는 우리 군사가 먼저 성문을 넘었소. 그러자 그대들의 도호부가 와서 우리 몫을 없음이라 적었지.
그대는 내가 반역자를 감싼다 하오. 나는 그대의 관리들이 세어 볼 생각도 하지 않은 백성을 감싸는 것이오.
en: At Pyongyang our men went through the gate first. Then your Protectorate came and wrote our share down as nothing.
You say I shelter rebels. I shelter the people your officials could not be bothered to count.

blocks.html: Alas! While the two kingdoms stood, we were the hounds that ran at your pointing finger. Now the game is all taken, and it is we who are threatened with the pot. Baekje, the bandits' leavings, is rewarded the way Han once paid off an old enemy; Silla, which died for Han, is cut down the way Han once killed a man for sparing it. Though the sun's light no longer turns our way, the sunflower's heart still faces the sun.
blocks.ko: 아아! 두 나라가 아직 평정되지 않았을 때는 손짓 하나에 사냥개처럼 내달렸는데, 들짐승이 다하자 도리어 삶아 죽이려는 핍박을 받습니다. 적의 찌꺼기인 백제는 도리어 원수에게 내리는 상을 받고, 한나라를 위해 목숨 바친 신라는 벌써 은인에게 내리는 칼을 받습니다. 태양의 빛이 비록 이쪽으로 돌아 비추지 않더라도, 해바라기의 본심은 여전히 해를 향합니다.
blocks.hanja: 嗚呼。兩國未定平，蒙指蹤之驅馳，野獸今盡，反見烹宰之侵逼。賊殘百濟，反蒙雍齒之賞，殉漢新羅，已見丁公之誅。大陽之曜，雖不廻光，葵藿本心，猶懷向日。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 11 (671), seventh month — King Munmu's reply to Xue Rengui

lines: 내 아우는 장안에 있소. 잘 있다고 전해 주시오. 내가 그 이름을 불렀다고도.
그대들이 구하러 왔다던 그 나라의 왕으로 남기를 영광으로 여기며 —
en: My brother is in Chang’an. Tell him I am well. Tell him I said his name.
I have the honour to remain the king of the country you came to save —
Bupmin.

blocks.html: Deto copies it out fair. His hand is very steady. Later that night he writes a second letter, a short one, to a different address, and puts it in his sleeve, and does not send it yet.
blocks.ko: 대토가 그것을 정서한다. 손이 아주 차분하다. 그날 밤 늦게 그는 두 번째 편지를 쓴다. 짧은 편지다. 받는 곳이 다르다. 그는 그것을 소매에 넣고, 아직은 보내지 않는다.

blocks.label: The Second Letter
blocks.ko: 두 번째 편지

lines: 전하의 편지를 받아, 소리 내어 읽었습니다. 오후 한나절이 걸리더군요.
전보다는 적은 일에서, 전하의 종으로 남기를 영광으로 여기며 —
en: Your Majesty’s letter has been received, and read aloud. It took most of an afternoon.
Nowhere in it is the word “sorry.”
I have the honour to remain your servant, in fewer things than before —
Xue.
zh: 大王來書已收，高聲讀畢，費去大半個下午。
仁貴於更少之事上，仍為大王之僕——
zhLatn: Dàwáng láishū yǐ shōu, gāoshēng dú bì, fèi qù dà bàn ge xiàwǔ.
Tōngpiān bú jiàn yí ge “zuì” zì.
Rénguì yú gèng shǎo zhī shì shàng, réng wéi dàwáng zhī pú——
Xuē.

lines: 대총관의 편지를 받았소. 읽는 데 시간이 하나도 안 걸렸소.
en: The Commander’s letter has been received. It took no time at all.
Nowhere in it is the word “rice.”
I have the honour to remain the king —
B.

lines: 그럼 사과는 제가 직접 받으러 가겠습니다.
en: Then I will come and fetch the apology myself.
zh: 那麼，這一聲歉，仁貴親自來取。
zhLatn: Nàme, zhè yì shēng qiàn, Rénguì qīnzì lái qǔ.
——Xuē.

en: Come, then.

blocks.label: Seventy Ships
blocks.ko: 일흔 척

blocks.html: He comes. In the tenth month, off the western coast, a Silla squadron finds seventy Western transports riding low with grain for the garrison at Bear Ford, and takes them: hulls, crews, one Western colonel, and all of the rice.
blocks.ko: 그는 온다. 시월, 서해안 앞바다에서 신라 선단이 웅진 주둔군에게 갈 곡식을 싣고 무겁게 떠가는 서국의 수송선 일흔 척을 찾아내 사로잡는다. 배와 사공과 서국 낭장 하나, 그리고 쌀 전부를.

blocks.html: Winter, the sixth day of the tenth month: we struck more than seventy Tang grain transports and captured the colonel Qianer Dahou and over a hundred soldiers. The drowned were past counting. The geupchan Dangchun's merit was first, and he was raised to sachan.
blocks.ko: 겨울 10월 6일, 당의 조운선 70여 척을 쳐서 낭장 겸이대후와 사졸 백여 명을 사로잡았다. 물에 빠져 죽은 자는 이루 셀 수 없었다. 급찬 당천의 공이 으뜸이어서 사찬의 관등을 주었다.
blocks.hanja: 冬十月六日，撃唐漕船七十餘艘，捉郞將鉗耳大侯、士卒百餘人。其淪沒死者，不可勝數。級飡當千功第一，授位沙飡。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 11 (671), tenth month

en: Send word to the White Tiger that his rice has arrived.
Late. As usual.

blocks.html: the West are coming south. Silla is winning. That is exactly when armies start to chase…!
blocks.ko: 서군이 남쪽으로 내려온다. 신라가 이기고 있다. 군대가 쫓기 시작하는 건, 꼭 그런 때다…!

logline.en: Silla wins the morning, then makes the mistake that costs the year: it chases.
logline.ko: 신라는 아침을 이긴다. 그리고 한 해를 잃는 실수를 한다. 쫓아간 것이다.

Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. images.alt: Munmu signs. The ink is still wet when the first stones of the new walls go in.
images.prompt: CLOSING STILL of the episode: the final scene of this story as it ends (not the next episode). The line: “Munmu signs. The ink is still wet when the first stones of the new walls go in.” Context: The minister thinks it is a joke. It is a room in Surabol, a year before Baekje fell, and a father asking his son a question.  Munmu signs. The ink is still wet when the first stones of the new walls go in. A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — PLACE Stone Gate (석문) — attached board /pl_stone_gate.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. blocks.label: Stone Gate
blocks.ko: 석문

blocks.html: Winning is the most dangerous thing an army can do.
blocks.ko: 군대가 할 수 있는 가장 위험한 일은 이기는 것이다.

blocks.html: Silla and what is left of the Goguryeo revival hit the Western camp under Beksu Fortress together, and cut down several thousand. By noon the West are running back up the road to Pyongyang. Soon after, Silla is running after them.
blocks.ko: 신라와 고구려 부흥군의 남은 이들이 백수성 아래 서군 진영을 함께 들이쳐 수천을 벤다. 한낮이 되자 서군은 평양 쪽 길로 되짚어 달아난다. 얼마 뒤, 신라가 그 뒤를 쫓는다.

blocks.caption: The West come south and turn. Silla gives chase. Watch where the chase ends.
blocks.ko: 서군이 남으로 내려왔다가 돌아선다. 신라가 쫓는다. 그 추격이 어디서 끝나는지 보라.

blocks.html: Among the riders is a lieutenant barely old enough for the rank, with a famous father and a borrowed horse. His name is Wonsul. Like every boy in his father’s yard, he has been taught that a Hwarang does not retreat. Nobody has taught him where a chase ends.
blocks.ko: 말 탄 이들 가운데 그 계급을 달기에도 겨우 될까 말까 한 비장이 있다. 이름난 아버지와 빌린 말. 이름은 원술. 아버지의 연무장 아이들이 다 그렇듯, 화랑은 물러서지 않는다고 배웠다. 추격이 어디서 끝나는지는 아무도 가르쳐 주지 않았다.

blocks.speaker: Wonsul
lines: 타라! 다 타래이, 고개 넘어가기 전에!
en: They’re breaking! Look at them go—
Mount up! Up, the lot of you, before they’re over the hill!

blocks.html: Every banner wants its own three thousand prisoners, so every banner rides off to find them. Nobody watches the Mohe horse leave the road.
blocks.ko: 깃발마다 포로 삼천을 제 몫으로 챙기고 싶어서, 깃발마다 따로 흩어져 찾아 나선다. 말갈 기병이 길을 벗어나는 것은 아무도 보지 않는다.

blocks.speaker: Dannung
en: Lieutenant. The column’s strung out over two li. We’re not in line.
…And where’s their horse got to?
lines: 비장님. 대열이 이 리나 늘어졌심더. 진이 안 섰어요.

blocks.speaker: Wonsul
en: They’re running. You don’t form a line to chase a man who’s running.
lines: 저놈들 달아난다 아이가. 달아나는 놈 쫓는 데 무슨 진이고.

blocks.html: A narrow place that looks like a way out, until it isn’t.
blocks.ko: 빠져나갈 길처럼 보이다가, 아니게 되는 좁은 곳.

blocks.html: At Sukmun the Westerners turn around. Out of the side valleys, north and south of the road, come the Mohe cavalry, into a Silla army that has not yet formed up. It is over in an afternoon.
blocks.ko: 석문에서 서군이 돌아선다. 길 북쪽과 남쪽 옆 골짜기에서 말갈 기병이 쏟아져, 아직 진을 펴지도 못한 신라군을 친다. 한나절 만에 끝난다.

blocks.html: Wonsul sees the general ahead of him go down, and then the next one. He turns his horse toward the Mohe, which is the direction a son of Kim Yushin is supposed to turn.
blocks.ko: 원술은 앞서 가던 장수가 쓰러지는 것을 본다. 그다음 장수도. 그는 말머리를 말갈 쪽으로 돌린다. 김유신의 아들이라면 돌려야 하는 쪽이다.

blocks.speaker: Wonsul
en: Let go.

blocks.html: His aide, Dannung, has the bridle in both fists.
blocks.ko: 그의 보좌 담릉이 두 주먹으로 고삐를 쥐고 있다.

blocks.speaker: Dannung
en: No.
Dying’s not the hard part, Lieutenant. Any fool can manage it in the next ten breaths.
Picking where is hard. This is a ditch. Die here and you’ve bought nothing.
lines: 죽는 건 어려운 기 아입니더, 비장님. 바보도 열 숨 안에 합니다.
죽을 자리를 고르는 기 어렵지요. 여는 도랑입니더. 여서 죽으믄 아무것도 몬 삽니다.

blocks.speaker: Wonsul
en: My father—
Let go, or I’ll have your hand off.
lines: 놔라. 안 놓으믄 손목을 잘라 삔다.

blocks.speaker: Dannung
en: Then cut it. I’ll still be holding.

blocks.html: He doesn’t cut it. Dannung turns the horse himself and runs it back down the road, east, through the dust, with a lieutenant on its back who screams at him the whole way.
blocks.ko: 원술은 자르지 않는다. 담릉이 손수 말머리를 돌려, 등 위에서 내내 소리 지르는 비장을 태운 채 먼지 속을 동쪽으로, 왔던 길을 되짚어 달린다.

blocks.speaker: Wonsul
lines: 담릉, 아버지 이름 걸고 말한다, 말 돌리라!
en: Turn around—
Dannung, I swear on my father, turn this horse around!

blocks.html: Dannung doesn’t answer. Seven Silla generals die in that valley. Wonsul is not one of them.
blocks.ko: 담릉은 대답하지 않는다. 그 골짜기에서 신라 장수 일곱이 죽는다. 원술은 그 일곱에 들지 않는다.

blocks.title: Sukmun, eighth month, 672

units.label: The pursuit
units.sub: strung out, not yet in line

units.label: Seven commanders
units.sub: all seven die in the valley

blocks.note: Seven named commanders died at Seokmun. Silla stopped attacking after it, and spent three years building walls instead.

blocks.label: The Apology
blocks.ko: 사죄문

blocks.html: Silla sends an apology to Chang’an and hands back the prisoners. Then it goes quiet, and starts building.
blocks.ko: 신라는 장안에 사죄사를 보내고 억류한 포로를 돌려보낸다. 그러고는 조용해지고, 성을 쌓기 시작한다.

blocks.html: The draft comes to the king’s table that winter. The court has read it. The court would like a word.
blocks.ko: 그해 겨울, 초안이 왕의 탁자에 오른다. 조정은 이미 읽었다. 조정은 할 말이 있다.

blocks.html: Your servant, guilty unto death, respectfully reports. … All the bamboo of the Southern Mountain would not be enough to write down your servant's crimes, nor all the forests of Baoxie to make his shackles. Flood our ancestral temple, tear your servant limb from limb: in this I await the imperial decision, and accept execution with a willing heart.
blocks.ko: 신 아무개는 죽을죄를 지었기에 삼가 아룁니다. … 남산의 대나무를 다 써도 신의 죄를 적기에 모자라고, 포야의 숲을 다 베어도 신의 형틀을 만들기에 모자랍니다. 종묘사직을 허물어 못으로 만들고 신의 몸을 찢어 죽이시더라도, 모든 일은 칙명의 처분을 따를 것이니 달게 죽음을 받겠습니다.
blocks.hanja: 臣某死罪謹言…南山之竹，不足書臣之罪，褒斜之林，未足作臣之械。瀦池宗社，屠裂臣身，事聽勅裁，甘心受戮。
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 7, Silla Annals — King Munmu, yr. 12 (672), ninth month — memorial of apology to the Tang court

blocks.speaker: True Bone minister
en: Majesty. “Tear your servant limb from limb”? We won the morning.
We are apologizing for the morning?
lines: 전하. ‘신의 몸을 찢으소서’라니요? 아침 싸움은 우리가 이겼습니다.

en: We’re apologizing for the afternoon.
And for the next fortress. And the one after that.

blocks.speaker: True Bone minister
en: …Who wrote this?
My father. Thirteen years ago.
I’m only signing it.

blocks.html: The minister thinks it is a joke. It is a room in Surabol, a year before Baekje fell, and a father asking his son a question.
blocks.ko: 대신은 농담인 줄 안다. 실은 백제가 무너지기 한 해 전, 서라벌의 어느 방이다. 아버지가 아들에게 묻고 있다.

blocks.title: A room in Surabol, a year before Baekje falls

lines: 법민아. 백제 무너지고 나믄 무슨 일이 날 것 같노?
en: Bupmin. What do you suppose happens after Baekje falls?
We move on Goryeo.
And after that.
…Unification.
No. / After that, it is our turn.

blocks.html: He lays it out the way another man would lay out a field. The West will not go home. They will put a governor in Sabi and call it a commandery. They will give you a title with the word province in it and expect you to be flattered. They will keep your brother in Chang’an and call him a guest.
blocks.ko: 그는 다른 사람이 밭을 펼쳐 보이듯 그것을 펼쳐 놓는다. 당은 돌아가지 않는다. 사비에 도독을 앉히고 도독부라 부를 것이다. 너에게 주(州)라는 글자가 들어간 벼슬을 주고 네가 우쭐하기를 바랄 것이다. 네 아우를 장안에 두고 손님이라 부를 것이다.

lines: 그때 절대로 먼저 치지 마라. / 저들이 고려에서 지칠 때까지 기다려라. / 성은 하나씩 되찾고, 되찾을 때마다 사죄 사절을 보내라. / 저들이 원하는 건 땅이 아이고 문서니까.
en: When it comes, never strike first. / Wait until they have exhausted themselves in the north. / Take the fortresses back one at a time, and send an apology after each one. / What they want is not the land. It is the paperwork.
…And the sea?

lines: 바다는 마지막이다. / 저들이 말을 다 잃은 뒤에.
en: The sea is last. / After they have lost the horses.
Father. How do you know all of this?

lines: 이세민한테 배웠다. / 그자가 내한테 할라 카던 걸 고대로 적어 놨거든.
en: Li Shimin taught me. / I wrote down everything he intended to do to me.

blocks.html: Munmu signs. The ink is still wet when the first stones of the new walls go in.
blocks.ko: 문무가 서명한다. 먹이 채 마르기도 전에, 새 성벽의 첫 돌이 놓인다.

blocks.html: Wonsul came home alive. In his father’s house, that is the crime…!
blocks.ko: 원술은 살아서 돌아왔다. 그의 아버지 집에서는, 그것이 죄다…!

logline.en: Wonsul came home alive from Stone Gate. His father asks the king to execute him, and the king answers with something he said at fifteen.
logline.ko: 원술은 석문에서 살아 돌아왔다. 아버지는 왕에게 아들을 죽여 달라 청하고, 왕은 열다섯 살 때 했던 말로 답한다.

images.alt: Wonsul alive after Sukmun — the son his father refuses to see
images.at: The retreat is almost beside the point
