images.alt: Rembrandt’s Prodigal Son, refused: Wonsul kneels at his father’s shut gate offering his sword flat on both palms
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Rembrandt’s Return of the Prodigal Son, with no father in the doorway. Night outside a Silla noble house in Surabol: Wonsul, Yushin’s young son, kneels on the stone step before a shut timber gate with iron bosses, head bowed, in torn grey steel lamellar with blue cloth at the collar, holding his ring-pommel sword out flat on both upturned palms. Behind the gate’s lattice window above him one lamp burns, and the shadow of an old man stands behind the paper, turned away. The lamp rakes down across his bowed head and the offered blade; the street is black rain. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.html: Wonsul gets home a day before the news does. It doesn’t help.
blocks.ko: 원술은 소식보다 하루 먼저 집에 닿는다. 그래 봐야 소용없다.

blocks.html: His father’s gate stays shut. The lamp above it is his mother’s. Lady Jiso is King Muyeol’s daughter, and she keeps it lit every night her men are at war. Tonight it burns, and she does not come down.
blocks.ko: 아버지의 대문은 닫혀 있다. 대문 위 등불은 어머니의 것이다. 무열왕의 딸 지소부인은 집안 사내들이 싸움터에 있는 밤이면 늘 등불을 켜 둔다. 오늘 밤도 불은 타지만, 그녀는 내려오지 않는다.

blocks.label: Father's House
blocks.ko: 아버지의 집

blocks.html: Inside, Yushin is told his son is at the gate. He doesn’t get up.
blocks.ko: 안에서 유신은 아들이 대문에 왔다는 말을 듣는다. 일어나지 않는다.

blocks.speaker: Steward
en: My lord. It’s the young master. He’s hurt, I think. His horse is—
lines: 나리. 작은 도련님이십니더. 다치신 거 같심더. 말이—
왕명을 욕되게 하고 가문의 이름까지 더럽혔으니, 내 아들이 아니다.
en: He shamed the king’s command and the family name with it. He is not my son.

blocks.html: The retreat is almost beside the point. A hundred men ran that afternoon and kept their fathers. But a house that came into Silla by treaty does not get to be ordinary, or it is simply Gaya again.
blocks.ko: 실은 퇴각이 문제의 핵심도 아니다. 그날 오후 백 명이 달아나고도 아버지를 잃지 않았다. 그러나 조약으로 신라에 들어온 집안에게 평범함은 허락되지 않는다. 그러지 못하면 그저 다시 가야일 뿐이다.

lines: 남의 아들은 물러나도 되네. / 내 아들은 안 되고.
en: Another man’s son may retreat. / Mine may not.

blocks.label: The King's Hall
blocks.ko: 어전

blocks.html: Yushin goes to the king and asks, in so many words, for his son to be put to death. It is the most formal request he has made in fifty years of service, and he makes it standing.
blocks.ko: 유신은 왕에게 가서, 말 그대로 아들을 죽여 달라고 청한다. 쉰 해를 섬기며 올린 청 가운데 가장 격식을 갖춘 청이고, 그는 그것을 선 채로 올린다.

lines: 외숙. 그 애는 비장이었습니다. 비장은 따라가는 자리입니다.
석문에서 살아 돌아온 자를 다 죽이면, 다음 싸움에서 질 군사도 안 남습니다.
en: Uncle. He was a lieutenant. Lieutenants follow.
If I execute every man who lived through Sukmun, I won’t have an army left to lose the next one with.
The law is the law, Majesty. A Hwarang does not retreat.
lines: 법은 법입니다, 전하. 화랑은 물러서지 않습니다.

en: On your yard you once asked me which of the five I would break first.
I said retreat. I was fifteen. You didn’t ask my father to kill me.
lines: 외숙의 연무장에서, 다섯 가운데 무엇을 먼저 깨겠느냐고 물으신 적이 있소.
나는 물러섬이라 했소. 열다섯이었지. 외숙은 아버님께 나를 죽이라 청하지 않으셨소.

en: …You were not my son.

blocks.html: The king has no answer to that. The old man knows it. Neither of them looks away first.
blocks.ko: 왕은 그 말에 할 대답이 없다. 노인도 그걸 안다. 둘 중 누구도 먼저 눈을 돌리지 않는다.

lines: 다만 제 집에 다시 들이라고는 하지 마십시오.
en: Then do not execute him, Majesty.
But do not ask me to call him back into my house.
…As you wish, Marshal.

blocks.label: The Hill Farms
blocks.ko: 산골 밭

blocks.html: Wonsul does not go home. He goes into the hill farms east of the capital and works another man’s fields under no name at all, which is the one punishment his father did not think to ask for. He does not write. Twice he comes as far as the road below his father’s gate and turns back at the sight of his mother’s lamp.
blocks.ko: 원술은 집에 가지 않는다. 도성 동쪽 산골 농가로 들어가 이름도 없이 남의 밭을 간다. 아버지가 미처 청하지 못한 단 하나의 벌이다. 그는 편지를 쓰지 않는다. 두 번, 아버지 집 대문 아래 길까지 왔다가 어머니의 등불을 보고 돌아선다.

blocks.speaker: Farmer
en: You hold a hoe like it owes you money.
Soldier, were you?

blocks.speaker: Wonsul
en: No.
…Not a good one.

blocks.html: Yushin is old now. The three sisters in the steam are not. They have kept his ledge warm for fifty years…!
blocks.ko: 유신은 이제 늙었다. 김 속의 세 자매는 아니다. 그들은 쉰 해 동안 그의 바위 자리를 데워 두었다…!

logline.en: Old now, Yushin still finds the cavern. The three in the steam look exactly the age they always looked.
logline.ko: 늙은 유신은 여전히 그 동굴을 찾는다. 김 속의 셋은 늘 그랬듯 그 나이 그대로다.

images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE: Korean webtoon figures with bold tapered ink contours and drawn faces, painted into a watercolor-and-oil world; old-master tenebrist canvas for night and interiors. Movie tenebrism: 75% of the frame in deep painted shadow, one hard practical key raking the subject, crushed blacks, long shadows, three depth planes with bokeh. FULL-BLEED 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop, nothing important at the top or bottom edge. Not photoreal, not a 3D render. No text, no lettering, no watermark. A THREE KINGDOMS ERA BURIAL MOUND, dramatic and tenebrist, not a postcard. Kim Yushin’s tomb: a round Silla earthen mound on a hill among pines, its base ringed with carved stone panels of the twelve zodiac guardians and a low stone railing. Night, one bright star in the east the only light besides a cold moon shaft on the zodiac stones. No people except where stated. Romanticist layout: the tomb on the thirds, half the frame sky, one cloud-break or lamp as the only key, long raking shadow across the grass.

blocks.label: THE LAKE REMEMBERS
blocks.ko: 호수는 기억한다

blocks.html: Old now, between campaigns that are mostly paperwork, Yushin still finds the cavern. The steam is thinner. The three are not. They look the same age they always looked — which is either mercy or mockery, and he has never asked which.
blocks.ko: 이제 늙어, 대부분 문서인 원정 사이에서도 유신은 동굴을 찾는다. 김은 옅어졌다. 셋은 아니다. 늘 그 나이로 보인다 — 자비인지 조롱인지, 그는 끝내 묻지 않았다.

blocks.html: Hyullé’s hand finds the water beside the ledge where he always sits, and stays there. Fifty years of the same ledge.
blocks.ko: 혈레의 손이 그가 늘 앉던 턱 곁의 물을 찾아, 그대로 머문다. 같은 턱을 오십 년.

en: You still undress like a soldier checking for wounds.
Sit. The counsel is shorter these days. So is the war. Slower. Let me look at you.
lines: 앉아요. 요즘은 충고도 짧고, 전쟁도. 천천히 해요. 얼굴 좀 보게요.

en: He’s going to say it.
Watch — three, two —
But Her Majesty is gone.
…I still hear myself saying it.
Ugh… even in the Western Flower Field she gets the title.
What did that mortal have that we don’t?
…Don’t answer. Stay until the steam drops. Before the hill keeps you.
lines: 으엑… 서천꽃밭에서도 그 인간은 직함을 가져.
그 인간한테 우리한테 없는 게 뭐였는데?
…답하지 마. 김이 식을 때까지 있어. 언덕이 널 두기 전에.

en: I didn’t — bring —
…It’s just warmer there.
You always liked it. Come sit. Please.
You used to bring the boy as far as the mouth. He’d wait with the horses and throw pebbles at the steam.
He isn’t at the mouth.
lines: 예전엔 그 아이를 입구까지 데려오셨잖아요. 말 옆에서 기다리며 김에 돌멩이를 던지곤 했죠.

en: I have no son by that name.
Ugh. You did the voice. The Marshal voice. In here.
lines: 으. 그 목소리 냈어. 원수 목소리. 여기서.

en: …He comes as far as the road below your gate. Twice now. The hill feels him stop.
He turns back at the lamp.
lines: …그분이 대문 아래 길까지 와요. 벌써 두 번이요. 멈추는 걸 언덕이 느껴요.

blocks.html: Yushin looks at the water for a long time. It shows him nothing, which in this cave is an answer.
blocks.ko: 유신은 오래도록 물을 들여다본다. 물은 아무것도 보여 주지 않는다. 이 동굴에선 그것도 답이다.

blocks.html: The steam thins. For a breath his father’s mouth is in the water — not the counsel, only the name — and then it is steam again.
blocks.ko: 김이 옅어진다. 한 숨 동안 아버지 입이 물에 있다 — 조언이 아니라 이름만 — 그리고 다시 김이다.

blocks.html: He sits. For once he does not rush the border. Narim talks about a tree that outlived three kings. Golhwa falls asleep against the stone mid-complaint. Hyullé says nothing, and that is the visit he will remember when the biographies start lying.
blocks.ko: 앉는다. 이번만큼은 국경을 재촉하지 않는다. 나림은 임금 셋을 살아낸 나무 이야기를 하고, 골화는 투덜이다 돌에 기대 잠든다. 혈레는 말이 없고 — 열전이 거짓을 쓰기 시작할 때 그가 기억할 방문이 바로 그것이다.

blocks.label: The Deathbed
blocks.ko: 임종

blocks.html: Seventh month, 673. He is seventy-nine. He has fought for sixty of those years and outlived nearly everyone worth outliving.
blocks.ko: 673년 칠월. 그는 일흔아홉이다. 그중 예순 해를 싸웠고, 오래 살 만한 가치가 있는 사람들 거의 전부보다 오래 살았다.

blocks.html: The King comes to the house himself, which kings do not do. Munmu does it anyway — he has known this man his entire life, and for most of it has not been sure whether to call him Marshal or uncle.
blocks.ko: 왕이 몸소 그 집을 찾는다. 왕이라면 하지 않는 일이다. 문무는 그래도 그렇게 한다 — 평생을 알아 온 사람이고, 그 세월 대부분을 이 사람을 대장군이라 불러야 할지 외숙이라 불러야 할지 확신하지 못한 채 지냈다.

blocks.html: The old man's eyes are already somewhere younger.
blocks.ko: 노인의 눈은 이미 더 젊은 날에 가 있다.

en: Yushin…

blocks.html: Nobody has called him by his bare name in forty-one years. The last one was a queen, on her coronation morning.
blocks.ko: 마흔한 해 동안 아무도 그를 이름만으로 부르지 않았다. 마지막으로 그렇게 부른 이는 즉위하던 아침의 여왕이었다.

en: Princess…
…The boy. Is he eating?
He’s farming. Badly. Shall I send for him?
…No.
Good. That he’s eating.

blocks.hanja: 伏願殿下 知成功之不易 念守成之亦難 疏遠小人 親近君子
blocks.ko: 엎드려 원하옵건대 전하께서는 공을 이루기가 쉽지 않고 이룬 것을 지키기도 또한 어려움을 생각하시어, 소인을 멀리하고 군자를 가까이 하소서.
blocks.html: I humbly pray Your Highness know that to succeed is not easy, and to keep what has been won is also hard. Keep petty men far and good men near.
blocks.source: Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 43, Biographies — Kim Yushin (final counsel); Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2, p. 404

blocks.html: Kangrim reads his name three times at the bedside — Yushin. Yushin. Yushin. — before the marshal's last answer.
blocks.ko: 강림은 침상 옆에서 그의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 유신. 유신. 유신. — 대장군의 마지막 대답을 듣기 전에.

en: Marshal.
One hundred and eight draws, one win that ended a friend, sixty years of being useful.
Question: were you becoming Silla — or proving you never needed their blood to outserve them?
lines: 백여덟 무승부, 친구를 끝낸 한 승, 육십 년의 쓸모.
질문: 신라가 되려 한 겁니까 — 아니면 그들 피 없이도 더 섬길 수 있음을 증명한 겁니까?

en: …I wanted in.
Wanting in is not shameful. Pretending I did not is.
lines: 들어가고 싶은 건 부끄러운 게 아이다. 아니라고 꾸미는 게 부끄러운 거지.

en: Clean answer.
His Majesty’s kingdom has room for men who told the truth late.
lines: 폐하의 나라엔 늦게 진실을 말한 사내를 둘 자리가 있네.

blocks.html: When the escort walks out through the courtyard, Munhee is standing by the well. She is sixty-seven. She sees her brother walking beside the stranger. Nobody else in the yard does. Above the roof the eastern star is up, the one that sits among the stars without being one of them.
blocks.ko: 저승 길잡이가 마당을 지나 나갈 때, 문희는 우물가에 서 있다. 예순일곱이다. 낯선 사내 곁에서 걸어가는 오라비를 그녀는 본다. 마서국의 다른 누구도 보지 못한다. 지붕 위로 동쪽 별이 떠 있다. 별들 사이에 있으면서 별은 아닌, 그 별.

en: Brother. Are you a Silla man now?
…I don’t know. Ask them for me.

blocks.html: She lets him go without asking twice. There is nobody left now who calls her little sister.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 두 번 묻지 않고 그를 보낸다. 이제 그녀를 동생이라 불러 줄 사람은 아무도 없다.

lines: 딱 한 번 이긴 날, 그게 끝이었네
동쪽 하늘 저 별이 바로 그 사람
en: Kim Yushin, marshal in blue,
a Gaya boy who made Silla true.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
A hundred and eight draws with his best friend;
he won only once, and that was the end.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Buried like a king but written below —
that star in the east? That’s him, you know.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
blocks.title: Yushin of the Eastern Star

blocks.caption: Kim Yushin, Marshal of Silla. Buried with a king’s honours and a subject’s rank.
blocks.ko: 신라의 대장군 김유신. 왕의 예로 묻히고 신하의 품계로 적혔다.

blocks.html: He is buried at Gumsan with the honours of a king and the rank of a subject. Somebody will close that gap. It takes a hundred and sixty years.
blocks.ko: 그는 금산에 왕의 예로, 신하의 품계로 묻힌다. 누군가는 그 틈을 메울 것이다. 백육십 년이 걸린다.

blocks.html: — Kim Yushin —
blocks.ko: — 김유신 —
blocks.art: Full-page end card. The name and the five italic paragraphs after it (through “…made him a king.”) share one page.

blocks.html: His grandfather bought the family a rank with a kingdom. Everyone honoured the deal, and everyone remembered it. So he made himself the one thing they could not do without, and he was very, very good at it. He loved a queen for forty years and never once said so where it could be heard. They would not let him all the way in while he lived. Once he was safely dead, they made him a king.
blocks.ko: 그의 할아버지는 나라 하나로 집안의 신분을 샀다. 모두가 그 거래를 지켰고, 모두가 그것을 기억했다. 그래서 그는 그들이 없이는 안 되는 단 하나가 되었고, 그것을 아주, 아주 잘해 냈다. 사십 년을 한 여왕을 사랑했으나, 들릴 만한 자리에서는 한 번도 그렇다고 말하지 않았다. 살아 있는 동안에는 끝내 다 들여보내 주지 않았다. 안전하게 죽고 나자, 그들은 그를 왕으로 만들었다.
blocks.art: Full-page end card, continued.

blocks.label: Lady Jiso
blocks.ko: 지소부인

blocks.html: After the funeral Wonsul comes down from the hills at last and asks at the gate for his mother. The lamp is out. Lady Jiso has already cut her hair for the nunnery.
blocks.ko: 장례가 끝나고 원술은 마침내 산에서 내려와 대문에서 어머니를 청한다. 등불은 꺼져 있다. 지소부인은 이미 비구니가 되려고 머리를 잘랐다.

blocks.speaker: Lady Jiso
lines: 여자는 셋을 따른다 했다. 아비, 지아비, 아들.
네 아버지가 너를 아들이라 부르지 않았는데, 내가 어찌 네 어미가 되겠느냐.
en: A woman has three to follow. Her father, her husband, her son.
My husband would not call you son. How am I to be your mother?

blocks.html: She does not come to the gate. The answer is carried out by a servant who cannot look at him. Wonsul stands in the road until dark and then goes back up into the hills. The record says only that he left weeping, and that he never stopped trying to give the afternoon back.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 대문까지 나오지 않는다. 대답은 그를 똑바로 보지 못하는 종이 들고 나온다. 원술은 어두워질 때까지 길에 서 있다가 다시 산으로 올라간다. 기록은 그가 울며 떠났다는 것, 그리고 그 한나절을 되돌리려는 일을 끝내 멈추지 않았다는 것만 적는다.

blocks.html: The king has buried his uncle. He still has one letter to answer, and a path nobody ever showed him…!
blocks.ko: 왕은 외숙을 묻었다. 아직 답할 편지가 하나 남았고, 아무도 보여 주지 않은 길이 하나 남았다…!

logline.en: The day after his uncle’s funeral, Munmu brings one question into the steam. Fifteen generations come to answer it, and the last one only speaks in rhyme.
logline.ko: 외숙의 장례 이튿날, 문무는 질문 하나를 들고 김 속으로 들어간다. 열다섯 대가 답하러 오고, 마지막 한 사람은 운율로만 말한다.

images.alt: The day after the funeral, a letter falls out of a sleeve.
images.prompt: OPENING STILL of the episode: the first image the reader sees, staging its first line. The line: “The day after the funeral, a letter falls out of a sleeve.” Context: The day after the funeral, a letter falls out of a sleeve. It is short. It is addressed to the Western garrison at Bear Ford, and it promises them a door in the wall of Surabol, the way a man at Daeya once promised Baekje a granary. The hand is very steady. The king knows that hand. It copied his letter to Xue Rengui. Majesty. A softer word here and there— A wide or medium establishing frame that hooks. CANON — PLACE Steam Cavern (골화천) — attached board /pl_cave.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Golhwacheon (골화천), the steam cavern hot spring: a dark pond under wet black stone, steam, motes in the element colors; everyone bathes IN the black water like a Korean public bath, bare bathing bodies, nothing on but water; generally dark, magical anime-painterly atmosphere, not a photoreal cave. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #C41E3A. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.

blocks.label: The Second Letter
blocks.ko: 두 번째 편지

blocks.html: The day after the funeral, a letter falls out of a sleeve.
blocks.ko: 장례 이튿날, 소매에서 편지 한 통이 떨어진다.

blocks.html: It is short. It is addressed to the Western garrison at Bear Ford, and it promises them a door in the wall of Surabol, the way a man at Daeya once promised Baekje a granary. The hand is very steady. The king knows that hand. It copied his letter to Xue Rengui.
blocks.ko: 짧은 편지다. 받는 곳은 웅진의 서군 진영이고, 서라벌 성벽의 문 하나를 약속한다. 언젠가 대야성의 한 사내가 백제에 곳간을 약속했듯이. 글씨가 아주 차분하다. 왕은 그 글씨를 안다. 설인귀에게 보낸 그의 답서를 정서한 손이다.

en: Majesty. A softer word here and there—
lines: 전하. 여기저기 말 한두 마디만 누그러뜨리면—

en: You said that in the writing room.
You copied my letter very well, Deto. Copy this one.
lines: 내 편지를 아주 잘 옮겨 적었소, 대토. 이것도 옮겨 적으시오.

blocks.html: It is his own death warrant. Deto copies it out fair, and his hand is still very steady. His wife and children are made slaves. Nobody mentions it at court.
blocks.ko: 그것은 그 자신의 사형 명령이다. 대토는 그것을 정서한다. 손은 여전히 아주 차분하다. 처자는 노비가 된다. 조정에서 그 이야기를 꺼내는 사람은 아무도 없다.

blocks.html: By evening, three councillors have asked him, very politely, for one more apology to the West. A real one this time, with no fortress hidden behind it. The emperor, they remind him, still keeps the king’s younger brother in Chang’an. A house keeps a spare key the same way.
blocks.ko: 저녁이 되자 대신 셋이 아주 공손하게, 서국에 사죄문을 한 번 더 올리자고 청한다. 이번엔 진짜로. 뒤에 성 하나 숨기지 않은 사죄문으로. 황제가 아직 왕의 아우를 장안에 두고 있다는 것도 일깨운다. 집에서 여벌 열쇠를 그렇게 둔다.

blocks.speaker: True Bone minister
en: Majesty. The marshal is buried.
If the West comes back in the spring, who holds the river?
lines: 봄에 서국이 다시 오면, 강은 누가 지킵니까?

en: I heard the question.
Give me one night.

blocks.label: The Steam Cavern
blocks.ko: 김 서린 동굴

blocks.html: That evening Munmu rides alone into the hills east of Surabol. His uncle never showed him the path. He finds it anyway, the way sons find what uncles hid on purpose.
blocks.ko: 그날 저녁 문무는 홀로 서라벌 동쪽 언덕으로 말을 달린다. 외숙은 그 길을 가르쳐 준 적이 없다. 그래도 그는 찾아낸다. 아들들이 외숙이 일부러 숨긴 것을 찾아내듯이.

blocks.html: He strips at the rock lip as if obeying an order nobody ever gave him in writing, and steps into water so black it reflects nothing.
blocks.ko: 그는 종이로 받지 못한 명령을 따르듯 바위 끝에서 옷을 벗고, 아무것도 비추지 않는 검은 물로 들어간다.
blocks.art: The house rule is the same: naked, clean-shaven, and only Kims.

blocks.html: Crimson leaves his shoulders the way a soldier sheds a campaign coat. Steam takes the rest. He does not look up until the water has him.
blocks.ko: 진홍이 어깨에서 내린다. 병사가 군복을 벗듯. 나머진 김이 가져간다. 물이 그를 잡을 때까지 올려다보지 않는다.

blocks.html: For a long time he only stands in the water. He is forty-seven, and a king, and there is nobody left alive who taught him to ride. He lets the steam have his face, so that nobody has to see it. Not even the rock.
blocks.ko: 한참 동안 그는 물속에 서 있기만 한다. 마흔일곱, 왕이다. 말 타는 법을 가르쳐 준 사람은 이제 아무도 살아 있지 않다. 그는 김에 얼굴을 맡긴다. 아무도 보지 않도록. 바위조차.

blocks.html: They smell him before they see him. Uncle’s heat, father’s road-dust, both houses in one walk. He still thinks he is alone. Golhwa’s mouth opens and does not close. Hyullé cannot get a word out. Narim bites her lip and fails at being eldest.
blocks.ko: 보기 전에 냄새로 안다. 외숙의 열, 아버지의 길먼지, 한 걸음 안에 집 둘. 그는 아직 혼자인 줄 안다. 골화의 입이 열리고 다물어지지 않는다. 혈레는 말이 안 나온다. 나림은 입술을 깨물고 언니 노릇에 실패한다.

blocks.html: They know him. The best of both: they said it first when he was twenty-one and came in with a jar, and they say it again now that the uncle is ash. Gaya in the shoulders. Surabol in the mouth. Fire comes off Golhwa’s skin. Water streams from Hyullé’s chin. A leaf turns in the steam around Narim and will not fall.
blocks.ko: 그들은 그를 안다. 양쪽의 최선. 스물하나, 항아리를 들고 왔을 때 처음 그렇게 말했고, 외숙이 재가 된 지금 다시 말한다. 어깨는 가야. 입은 서라벌. 골화의 살에서 불이 난다. 혈레의 턱에서 물이 흐른다. 나림 주위 김 속에서 잎 하나가 돌고, 떨어지지 않는다.

en: …You’re still here.
I brought a jar last time. I didn’t bring anything tonight.
lines: 지난번엔 항아리를 들고 왔었소. 오늘 밤엔 아무것도 안 가져왔소.

en: You brought him. On your shoulders. We can smell it.
Sit. Before you fall—

blocks.html: He looks at her like she is kind. Narim cannot finish the sentence. She is out of breath, and pretends the steam did that. Uncle’s shoulders. Father’s mouth. She is not supposed to want both, tonight of all nights.
blocks.ko: 그가 친절한 사람을 보듯 그녀를 본다. 나림은 문장을 끝내지 못한다. 숨이 가쁘다. 김 탓인 척한다. 외숙의 어깨. 아버지의 입. 둘 다 원하면 안 된다. 하필 오늘 같은 밤에.

en: Hello. I’ll be quiet.
Sit down before you fall in again.
We are the mouths the hill uses. Wisdom, if you stand in the water and ask once. The uncle is gone. The hill is not.
lines: 언덕이 쓰는 입이에요. 지혜요, 물에 서서 한 번만 물으면. 외숙은 갔어요. 언덕은 안 가요.

en: I came because he died.
…And because they want me to write the West a real apology. Do I?
lines: …그리고 서국에 진짜 사죄문을 쓰라 하오. 써야 하오?

blocks.html: Something goes out of the cave. When they speak again the eyes are solid: green, cyan, ember.
blocks.ko: 동굴에서 무언가가 빠져나간다. 다시 말할 때 그들의 눈은 통째로 빛난다. 초록, 청록, 불씨.

en: The west will take your name and call it peace.
Keep a sea in the other hand.
lines: 서쪽이 당신 이름을 가져가고 평화라 부를 거예요.

en: …That isn’t a yes or a no.

blocks.html: The eyes go out. All three go quiet at once, the way birds do before weather. Golhwa is looking past his shoulder at the ledge. Somebody is sitting there who was not sitting there a moment ago.
blocks.ko: 눈빛이 꺼진다. 셋이 한꺼번에 조용해진다. 날씨가 바뀌기 전의 새들처럼. 골화가 그의 어깨 너머 바위 턱을 보고 있다. 방금 전까지 없던 누군가가 거기 앉아 있다.

blocks.label: The Queen on the Ledge
blocks.ko: 바위 턱의 여왕

blocks.html: She is sitting with her feet in the water, the way no queen is supposed to, looking up. There is no sky in here. She is looking anyway. Twenty-six years dead, and she still checks the weather first.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 물에 발을 담그고 앉아 있다. 여왕이라면 하지 않을 자세로. 위를 올려다보며. 여기엔 하늘이 없다. 그래도 본다. 죽은 지 스물여섯 해, 그래도 날씨부터 본다.

en: No stars. I checked.
…Bupmin-ah. You got tall.
Your Majesty—
I was twenty-one. I was already tall.
You were twenty-one and you stood like a boy waiting to be told off.
Now you stand like a king waiting to be told off. That’s progress.
lines: 스물하나에 꾸중 기다리는 아이처럼 서 있었제.
인자는 꾸중 기다리는 임금처럼 서 있네. 많이 늘었다.

blocks.html: He laughs. It comes out wrong, half a sob, and he puts it under the water before anyone can see. She sees. She lets him think she didn’t.
blocks.ko: 그가 웃는다. 웃음이 잘못 나온다. 반은 울음이다. 누가 보기 전에 물속에 묻는다. 그녀는 본다. 못 본 척해 준다.

en: Your mother. Still writing packing lists?
lines: 너그 어매는. 아직도 짐 목록 쓰나?

en: She packed my saddlebags for the funeral. Twice. She put a winter coat in. It’s autumn.
lines: 장례 가는 안장 주머니를 두 번 싸셨습니다. 겨울 두루마기를 넣으셨어요. 가을인데.

en: She’s expecting a long winter. Is she right?
lines: 겨울이 길 줄 아는 기라. 맞나?

en: …She usually is.
And my tower. Does anyone still climb it?
lines: 그라고 내 탑은. 아직 누가 올라가나?

en: The astronomers. Every night.
Looking at the sky, or at the court?
…Mostly the court.
Ha. Good. Then I built it right.
lines: 하. 됐다. 그라믄 제대로 지은 기다.

en: Majesty. They want me to apologise to the West. Properly. On my knees, in a letter, and mean it.
My father would have written it and not meant a word. My uncle would have gone and stood on the river.
I’m not either of them.
lines: 폐하. 서국에 사죄하라 합니다. 제대로. 글로 무릎 꿇고, 진심으로.
아버지라면 써 놓고 한 글자도 진심이 아니셨을 겁니다. 외숙이라면 강에 나가 서 계셨을 거고요.

en: No. You’re worse. You mean things.
Who’s asking you to write it?
lines: 그래. 니는 더 고약하다. 니는 말을 진심으로 하제.

en: The council. The True Bone houses.
How many of them have ever been hungry?
lines: 그 사람들 중에 배곯아 본 사람이 몇이고?

blocks.html: He does not answer. She was always very good at the question that ends the argument.
blocks.ko: 그는 답하지 않는다. 그녀는 언제나 다툼을 끝내는 질문에 능했다.

en: Your father told me what you said on the beach when you were six. About the people with no bones.
“Those most. There’s more of them.” I wrote it down. I was going to use it on the council.
lines: 너그 아부지가 말해 주더라. 여섯 살에 바닷가에서 니가 한 말. 뼈 없는 사람들.
‘그 사람들 제일 먼저. 그 사람들이 더 많으니까.’ 내가 적어 놨다. 화백에 써먹으려고.

en: …Did you?
I died first. Very rude of me.
You have Baekje villages now. Goguryeo men walking south with nothing on their backs. What are they to you, Bupmin? Spoils, or people?
Count them. Give their lords your ranks. Put their sons under your banners. A wall is cheaper when the men behind it are yours.
lines: 인자 백제 마을이 니 끼다. 빈손으로 남쪽에 내려오는 고구려 사내들도. 그 사람들이 니한테 뭐고, 법민아. 전리품이가, 사람이가?
세어라. 그 사람들 귀족한테 우리 관등을 줘라. 아들들은 니 깃발 아래 세우고. 성벽 뒤 사람이 내 사람이면, 성은 싸게 먹힌다.

blocks.html: It is the plainest advice anyone has given him in years. He has heard it before. He said it himself, on a beach, at six.
blocks.ko: 몇 해 만에 들은 가장 솔직한 충고다. 전에도 들은 말이다. 여섯 살에, 바닷가에서, 그가 직접 했다.

blocks.label: The Marshal
blocks.ko: 대장군

blocks.html: The water moves on the far side of the pool, the way it moves when a man who knows the bottom wades in without looking.
blocks.ko: 못 저편에서 물이 움직인다. 바닥을 아는 사내가 내려다보지도 않고 걸어 들어올 때처럼.

blocks.html: He is in the blue robe they buried him in two months ago. The hair is white. The back is straight again. He stops at the edge of the steam like a guest who has arrived early and is not sure he was invited.
blocks.ko: 두 달 전 그를 묻을 때 입힌 푸른 옷이다. 머리는 하얗다. 허리는 다시 곧다. 그는 김의 가장자리에서 멈춘다. 너무 일찍 와서, 초대받았는지 자신 없는 손님처럼.

blocks.html: Hyullé makes a sound nobody in this cave has heard her make in fifty years.
blocks.ko: 혈레가 오십 년 동안 이 동굴에서 아무도 들어 본 적 없는 소리를 낸다.

en: …You came back.
…Hyullé.

blocks.html: Just her name. In fifty years he never wasted a word in here, and he doesn’t now. She sits down in the water as if her knees went. Golhwa turns to the rock wall. Narim tells nobody in particular that the steam is very thick tonight. It isn’t.
blocks.ko: 이름뿐이다. 오십 년 동안 그는 여기서 말 한마디 허투루 쓴 적이 없고, 지금도 그렇다. 혈레가 무릎이 풀린 듯 물속에 주저앉는다. 골화는 바위벽 쪽으로 돌아선다. 나림은 누구에게랄 것도 없이 오늘 밤 김이 아주 짙다고 말한다. 짙지 않다.

en: Your Maj—
We’re dead, Yushin. You can stop.
lines: 우리 죽었다, 유신아. 인자 그만해도 된다.

en: …Princess.
Close enough.

blocks.html: Forty years he loved her and never once said so where it could be heard. He still doesn’t. He only stands a little closer than a subject should, and she lets him.
blocks.ko: 마흔 해를 사랑하고도 남이 들을 수 있는 데서는 한 번도 말하지 않았다. 지금도 하지 않는다. 신하가 서야 할 자리보다 조금 가까이 설 뿐이고, 그녀는 그걸 내버려 둔다.

en: …Oh.
Your nephew just worked something out.
He was always slow on the left side.

blocks.html: Munmu laughs, and this time it comes out right.
blocks.ko: 문무가 웃는다. 이번엔 제대로 나온다.

en: Uncle. At the house, I didn’t—
I had a whole speech. I said your name, and then the physicians—
lines: 드릴 말씀이 한가득이었는데. 이름만 부르고 나니 의원들이—

en: You said my name. That was the whole speech.
…And I don’t have to call you Majesty in here. I asked.
lines: …여서는 전하 소리 안 해도 된다 카더라. 물어봤다.

en: The boy.
His mother wouldn’t open the gate. He went back up the hill.
lines: 어머니가 대문을 안 열어 주셨습니다. 산으로 도로 올라갔어요.

blocks.html: Yushin is quiet for a long time. Then he asks the only question he has ever asked about his son.
blocks.ko: 유신은 오래 말이 없다. 그러다 아들에 대해 그가 늘 묻던 단 하나의 질문을 한다.

en: …Is he eating?
He will be. I’ll see to it.
Good.
Uncle. Do I write the apology?
Write it. Your father wrote six. Paper is cheap. Horses aren’t.
They feed every horse across a sea. You feed boys at home. Make them come to you—
lines: 써라. 너그 아부지는 여섯 장 썼다. 종이는 싸다. 말은 안 싸다.
저들은 말 한 마리 한 마리를 바다 건너 먹인다. 니는 집에서 아이들 먹이고. 오게 해라—

en: We did that at Stone Gate. We won the morning—
And then you chased.
Don’t chase. Hold the river. Make the grass expensive. When it runs out, they go home.
lines: 쫓지 마라. 강을 지켜라. 풀을 비싸게 만들어라. 풀 떨어지믄, 저들은 집에 간다.

en: Your mother asked me something at the well. I told her to ask them.
…You ask them. You’re better at asking than I was.
lines: 너그 어매가 우물가에서 뭘 물었다. 저들한테 물어보라 캤다.

en: Ask who?

blocks.label: The Outlet
blocks.ko: 물 빠지는 곳

blocks.html: On the far side of the pool, where the water slips out through a crack in the rock, an old man is sitting on a stone with his feet in the stream, talking to it. Nobody in the cave saw him arrive. That was always his best trick.
blocks.ko: 못 건너편, 바위틈으로 물이 빠져나가는 곳에 한 노인이 돌 위에 앉아 개울에 발을 담그고 물에 말을 걸고 있다. 그가 언제 왔는지 동굴 안 누구도 보지 못했다. 그게 늘 그의 제일가는 재주였다.

blocks.html: Grey topknot, a little crooked. Plain hemp. Ink on his fingers. Golhwa mutters something about goblins and moves her feet away from his.
blocks.ko: 조금 삐뚤어진 하얀 상투. 수수한 삼베옷. 손가락엔 먹물. 골화가 도깨비가 어쩌고 하고 투덜대더니 그쪽에서 발을 치운다.

en: …Grandfather?

lines: 너, 진달래 밑에 있었지. 등불 띄우던 밤에.
en: Mm.
You were under the azaleas. The night of the lanterns.
You saw me?

lines: 승만 공주가 아무도 그 얘기를 안 해도 되게 한 시진이나 제 치마를 밟고 서 있었어.
en: Everyone saw your heel, Bupmin.
Princess Seungman stood on her own skirt for an hour so nobody would have to mention it.

blocks.html: Beside him, sitting very straight with her hands folded, is a woman with a wax tablet tucked in her sleeve. She has been there the whole time too. They died on the same night, and they have plainly not been apart since.
blocks.ko: 그 곁에 손을 모으고 아주 꼿꼿하게 앉은 여인이 있다. 소매에 밀랍판을 넣은 채로. 그녀도 내내 거기 있었다. 둘은 같은 밤에 죽었고, 그 뒤로 떨어진 적이 없는 게 분명하다.

lines: 저 틈에 대고 한 시진째 얘기 중이다.
돌마다 이름 붙이기 전에 어서 물어봐라.
en: He’s been talking to that crack for an hour.
Ask him your question before he starts naming the stones.

lines: 할아버지. 서국이 저더러 편지로 무릎을 꿇으랍니다.
아버지라면 쓰고 한 마디도 진심은 아니었겠죠. 외숙은 쓰라고 합니다. 종이는 싸다고. 여왕께선 굶주린 사람을 세라고 하시고요.
en: Grandfather. The West wants me on my knees in a letter.
Father would have written it and not meant a word. Uncle says write it, paper is cheap. The queen says count the hungry.
What do you say?

lines: 나는 이렇게 묻지. 누가 너를 세고 있냐?
en: I say, who’s counting you?

lines: 황제요. 국경이며 곳간이며 전부요. 그 일만 하는 관청이 따로 있습니다.
en: The emperor. Every border, every granary. He has a whole office for it.

lines: 그럼 지루한 걸 세게 해 줘라.
충성스러운 조그만 임금. 셈은 못 하고, 맨날 감사 편지나 쓰는.
너를 비웃는 사람은 너를 세지 않아. 난 개울 하나로 사십 년을 그렇게 했다.
en: Then give him something boring to count.
A loyal little king. Bad at sums. Always writing thank-you letters.
A man who is laughing at you isn’t counting you. I did it for forty years with a stream.
And meanwhile?

lines: 석수 품삯은 네 손으로 주고. 무거운 일은 절대 도깨비한테 맡기지 마라.
en: Meanwhile you build the bridge at night.
And pay the masons yourself. Never let a goblin do the heavy part.

lines: 그리고 다 놓으면, 네 아들한테 그게 얼마 들었는지 말해 줘라.
저 양반처럼 그렇게 오래 기다리지 말고.
en: And when it’s built, tell your son what it cost.
Don’t wait as long as he did.

blocks.html: Then the old man turns back to the crack in the rock, says something to it, and laughs at the answer. For the first time in his life, Munmu wishes he could hear what the water says.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 노인이 다시 바위틈으로 돌아앉아 뭐라고 말하더니, 그 대답에 웃는다. 문무는 난생처음, 물이 뭐라고 하는지 들을 수 있었으면 하고 바란다.

blocks.label: The Hands
blocks.ko: 손

blocks.html: Then they do a thing the dead in this water do not do.
blocks.ko: 그때 그들이, 이 물의 죽은 이들이 하지 않는 일을 한다.

blocks.html: You may remember a son in this pool reaching for his father and catching steam. The dead here can’t be held. It turns out they can choose to lean.
blocks.ko: 기억할지 모르겠다. 이 못에서 한 아들이 아버지를 안으려다 김을 안았다. 여기 죽은 이들은 붙잡을 수 없다. 알고 보니, 기댈 수는 있다. 그들이 원하면.

blocks.html: Sunduk sets her hand on his left shoulder. Yushin sets his on the right. They are warm. He feels both weights arrive, a queen’s and a marshal’s, his father’s side and his mother’s, and he does not dare move.
blocks.ko: 선덕이 그의 왼쪽 어깨에 손을 얹는다. 유신이 오른쪽에 얹는다. 따뜻하다. 두 무게가 내려앉는 게 느껴진다. 여왕의 것과 대장군의 것. 아버지 쪽과 어머니 쪽. 그는 감히 움직이지 못한다.

blocks.html: Behind the queen, someone lays a hand on her shoulder. A magenta sleeve. A fox’s mouth, for once with nothing in it.
blocks.ko: 여왕 뒤에서 누군가 그녀의 어깨에 손을 얹는다. 자홍빛 소매. 여우 같은 입. 이번만은 아무 말도 담지 않았다.

en: …Father?

blocks.html: Chunchu talked his way through three empires. Now he puts one finger to his lips, smiles, and tips his head forward: not at me. Ahead. It is the only time in his life, or after it, that he has been brief.
blocks.ko: 춘추는 세 제국을 말로 건너온 사람이다. 지금은 손가락 하나를 입술에 대고, 웃고, 고개를 앞으로 까딱한다. 나 말고. 앞을 봐라. 살아서도 죽어서도, 그가 짧게 말한 건 이때뿐이다.

blocks.html: Behind his father, two more hands: an old man’s with ink on the fingers, and beside it a woman’s, a wax tablet in her other hand. The side branch, back on the trunk, all in a row. The old man winks.
blocks.ko: 아버지 뒤로 손이 둘 더 얹힌다. 손가락에 먹물이 묻은 노인의 손, 그리고 그 곁에 다른 손엔 밀랍판을 든 여인의 손. 곁가지였던 줄이 줄기로 돌아와 나란히 섰다. 노인이 한쪽 눈을 찡긋한다.

blocks.html: Behind Yushin, a hand: a younger man in the night robe he died in. Behind him, a big man with a cone helm under his arm. Behind him, a king in plain clothes, the clothes of the day he handed over his country with the keys still warm.
blocks.ko: 유신 뒤에도 손 하나. 죽던 밤의 잠옷 차림인 젊은 사내. 그 뒤에 고깔 투구를 옆구리에 낀 큰 사내. 그 뒤에 수수한 옷차림의 임금. 열쇠가 식기도 전에 나라를 넘긴 날의 옷이다.

blocks.html: And then it doesn’t stop.
blocks.ko: 그리고 멈추지 않는다.

blocks.html: On the left the hands go back through gold. Crowns with shivering leaves, then older gold, then bronze, then topknots with no crowns at all. Kims, and before the Kims other houses, and before them the first one. Strictly, his line does not run back to that first king. The hands don’t care. The line runs through the country, not the bone.
blocks.ko: 왼쪽으로 손들이 금을 지나 거슬러 간다. 떨리는 금잎 왕관, 더 오래된 금, 청동, 그리고 왕관 없이 상투만 튼 머리들. 김씨, 김씨 전엔 다른 집안들, 그 전엔 맨 처음 한 사람. 엄밀히 따지면 그의 핏줄은 그 첫 임금까지 닿지 않는다. 손들은 상관하지 않는다. 그 줄은 뼈가 아니라 나라를 따라 흐른다.

blocks.html: On the right, nine kings of a kingdom that no longer exists, each with a palm on the next one’s shoulder, iron on their belts and river water in their hems. Fifteen generations. He counts them, because he can’t help it. He has his mother’s habits.
blocks.ko: 오른쪽엔 이제는 없는 나라의 임금 아홉. 저마다 손바닥을 다음 사람 어깨에 얹고, 허리엔 쇠를, 옷자락엔 강물을 달았다. 열다섯 대. 그는 센다. 어쩔 수가 없다. 어머니 버릇이다.

blocks.html: The two lines bend away into the steam like the two banks of one river. At the far end of each, where the steam goes white, a couple stands side by side.
blocks.ko: 두 줄이 한 강의 두 기슭처럼 김 속으로 휘어져 멀어진다. 각 줄의 맨 끝, 김이 하얘지는 곳에, 남녀 한 쌍씩이 나란히 서 있다.

en: …Them.

blocks.html: All that weight comes down the lines, shoulder to shoulder, and lands on his. It should be unbearable. It is lighter than the crown.
blocks.ko: 그 무게가 전부 어깨에서 어깨로 줄을 타고 내려와 그의 어깨에 닿는다. 견딜 수 없어야 마땅하다. 왕관보다 가볍다.

blocks.html: Then the near ones let go, one by one, the way lamps go out down a long hall. His father nods once. The queen squeezes. The marshal doesn’t squeeze; he taps twice, like a man checking a saddle girth. And then there are only four people in the water with him, and every one of them founded something.
blocks.ko: 그러다 가까운 이들부터 하나씩 손을 뗀다. 긴 전각을 따라 등불이 꺼지듯. 아버지가 한 번 고개를 끄덕인다. 여왕이 꼭 쥔다. 대장군은 쥐지 않는다. 뱃대끈을 확인하듯 두 번 톡톡 친다. 이제 물속엔 그와 함께 넷만 남는다. 넷 다 무언가를 세운 사람들이다.

blocks.label: The Founders
blocks.ko: 시조

blocks.html: On his left, a young man too beautiful to be entirely a man, with a farmer’s hands. Beside him, a woman whose lips, the story goes, were a hen’s beak the day she was born, until somebody washed her in a stream.
blocks.ko: 왼쪽엔 사람이라기엔 너무 아름다운 젊은 사내. 손은 농부의 손이다. 곁엔 태어나던 날 입술이 닭 부리였다는 여인. 누가 냇물에 씻겨 주기 전까지는.

blocks.html: On his right, purple silk and a little gold crown. If you have been here before, you have met him; he hums. Beside him, a woman from the far side of the sea, who buried her silk trousers on the beach so the sea god would know she meant to stay.
blocks.ko: 오른쪽엔 보랏빛 비단과 작은 금관. 여기 와 본 적이 있다면 이미 만났다. 흥얼거리는 그 사람이다. 곁엔 바다 건너편에서 온 여인. 바다의 신이 제가 머물 작정임을 알도록 비단 바지를 바닷가에 묻은 사람.

en: Well! There he is. Fifteen of us it took to get to you, cariad, and look at the size of you.
lines: 허! 여기 있네. 그대한테 오는 데 우리가 열다섯이나 걸렸소. 보소, 덩치 좀.

en: You’re— King Suro.
Am I? Who told you that?
Everyone. The six golden eggs on the hill.
Six eggs! And they believed it!
…It was true, mind. Still. They believed it.
lines: 알 여섯 개라! 그걸 다 믿었다 카네!

en: Mine was one egg. Nobody makes a song about one egg.
lines: 나는 알 하나였소. 알 하나로는 노래를 안 지어 주더군.

en: They made one about the horse.
The horse left.
Stand up straight. You are in front of four kings.
Two kings. Two queens.
I said what I said.
Majesties. I’ll be plain. I’m not good at the other kind.
lines: 폐하들. 솔직히 여쭙겠습니다. 다른 식으로는 잘 못 합니다.

en: Plain! Lovely. We’ll soon fix that.
lines: 솔직히라! 좋소. 그건 우리가 금방 고쳐 주께.

en: The West wants me to be their king of Silla. Their governor. My council wants me to say yes. The emperor keeps my brother in his house in case I say no.
lines: 서국은 저더러 저들의 신라왕이 되라 합니다. 저들의 도독이요. 화백은 그러라 하고요. 황제는 제가 싫다 할까 봐 아우를 제 집에 두고 있습니다.

en: What will they call you, if you say yes?
Area Commander of Gyerim. King of Silla, by the emperor’s grace.
And now? What do they call you now?
…The same.
Then they took your name already, and you did not notice.
I crossed a whole sea and kept mine. Two of my sons carry it still. Keep your name. Answer to theirs when it is useful.
lines: 그럼 이미 이름을 가져갔네요. 당신은 몰랐고요.
저는 바다를 통째로 건너고도 제 이름을 지켰습니다. 아들 둘이 아직 그 이름을 씁니다. 이름은 지키세요. 저들 이름엔, 쓸모 있을 때만 대답하고요.

en: So I write the letter and don’t mean it. That’s my father’s way—
lines: 그럼 써 놓고 진심은 아니라는— 그건 아버지 방식인데요—

en: Did I say that?
She didn’t! She never does. A hundred and fifty years married, I got six straight answers off her. Best years of my life.
lines: 안 했소! 절대 안 하요. 백오십 년을 같이 살았는데 바른 대답은 여섯 번 들었소. 내 생에 제일 좋은 시절이었소.

en: Seven.
Now. My turn. Who sings at my mound these days?
lines: 자. 내 차례. 요새 내 무덤에서는 누가 노래하요?

en: …I don’t know. Nobody, I think. Gaya’s gone.
lines: …모르겠습니다. 아무도 안 하는 것 같습니다. 가야는 없어졌으니까요.

en: Gone! Gone where, then?
Into Silla.
Into you, more like. And has Silla sung, at my mound?
lines: 그대 속으로 갔제. 신라는 노래했소, 내 무덤에서?

en: No.
Hm! Not complaining, mind. Dead is very relaxing. Only—
Whose dead are they, now? Mine? Nobody’s?
lines: 흠! 불평하는 기 아이요. 죽으면 참 편하요. 다만—
그 무덤들, 인자 누구네 죽은 이요? 내 끼요? 아무 끼도 아이요?

blocks.html: It is the game he played with the boy’s uncle on this same rock, over a sword. Whose iron? Munmu doesn’t know that. He only knows the question has a floor under it, and he is standing on it.
blocks.ko: 이 바위에서, 칼 하나를 두고, 이 사내의 외숙과 했던 놀이다. 누구네 쇠? 문무는 그걸 모른다. 다만 그 질문 밑에 바닥이 있고, 자기가 그 위에 서 있다는 것만 안다.

en: And Baekje’s mounds? And the ones up north? Your men have made a great many new ones lately.
Whose ancestors are those?
lines: 백제 무덤들은? 북쪽 무덤들은? 요새 그대 군사들이 새 무덤을 많이도 만들었지.

blocks.html: A long silence. The steam drips.
blocks.ko: 긴 침묵. 김이 떨어진다.

en: …Mine.
Faster than I was. It took me sixty years and a wife.
lines: 나보다 빠르오. 나는 예순 해하고 아내 하나가 걸렸소.

en: You’re leaning.
Like a seedling. All of you, one way. West.
…Is that bad?
A seedling that leans to the light isn’t wrong. It just falls over in the first wind.
Roots first. Then lean wherever you like.
lines: 빛 쪽으로 기우는 모종이 틀린 건 아니오. 첫 바람에 넘어질 뿐이지.
뿌리 먼저. 그다음엔 어디로 기울든 마음대로 하시오.

en: He means stand up straight. He always means stand up straight.
lines: 허리 펴라는 소리요. 이 양반은 늘 허리 펴라는 소리요.

en: “One person to cherish, one person to serve.” That’s yours. Everyone in Surabol knows it.
I know who I cherish. Who do I serve? I’m the king. Who does a king serve?
lines: ‘아낄 사람 하나, 섬길 사람 하나.’ 시조의 말씀입니다. 서라벌 사람 다 압니다.
아낄 사람은 압니다. 섬길 사람은 누굽니까? 제가 왕입니다. 왕은 누구를 섬깁니까?

blocks.html: Hyukgose looks at his wife. Suro looks at the ceiling. The queen from the sea looks at Munmu with interest, the way you look at a man about to step on a rake.
blocks.ko: 혁거세가 아내를 본다. 수로는 천장을 본다. 바다에서 온 왕비는 흥미롭다는 듯 문무를 본다. 갈퀴를 밟기 직전인 사람을 보듯이.

en: Hm.
That one’s above my head.
Sounds like a job for someone higher up.
Higher up?
Who could possibly be higher up than Park Hyukgose himself?

blocks.html: Hyukgose smiles. It is a farmer’s smile, the one for a city man who has just asked where rice comes from. He takes his wife’s hand, and the two of them are not there.
blocks.ko: 혁거세가 웃는다. 농부의 웃음이다. 쌀이 어디서 나오느냐고 막 물은 도성 사람에게 짓는 웃음. 그가 아내의 손을 잡고, 둘은 거기 없다.

en: Ooh. Him.
Mind your manners, bach. And don’t ask him anything straight. He hates that.
lines: 예의 차리소. 그라고 그 양반한테는 곧이곧대로 묻지 마소. 그거 질색하요.

en: He will not answer you. Listen anyway.
lines: 대답은 안 하실 겁니다. 그래도 들으세요.

blocks.html: Then they are gone too, and Munmu is alone in the water, and the steam is going thin.
blocks.ko: 그러고는 그들도 사라진다. 문무는 물속에 혼자다. 김이 옅어지고 있다.

blocks.label: The Man on the Water
blocks.ko: 물 위의 사내

blocks.html: The steam goes thin enough to see through, and a man stands on the water as if the lake were a court floor. White robes. Sandalwood-coloured light. A smell of birch bark and, faintly, garlic. A face that has outlived every kingdom on the map. The three go still on the rock. This visitor is not theirs.
blocks.ko: 김이 투명할 만큼 옅어지고, 한 사내가 물 위에 서 있다. 마치 호수가 조정 바닥인 것처럼. 흰 옷. 박달나무 빛. 자작나무 껍질 냄새, 그리고 아주 희미하게, 마늘 냄새. 지도 위 모든 나라보다 오래 살아남은 얼굴. 셋이 바위에서 멈춘다. 이 손님은 그들의 것이 아니다.

en: Six years old and loud on the sand:
“Everyone listens when I rule the land.”
Forty-one years, a crown, and a war.
Who’s doing the listening now? And what for?
lines: ‘내가 임금 되면 다 내 말 들어야 해이.’
마흔한 해, 왕관 하나, 전쟁 하나.
지금 듣는 쪽은 누구고, 무얼 위해서냐?

en: Who are you.
Which court sent you.
No court sent me. I wear no crown.
I came down a mountain, and I’ll go back down— no. Up. One forgets.
lines: 보낸 조정 없고, 쓴 관도 없다.
산에서 내려왔고, 도로 내려— 아니, 올라간다. 깜빡하네.

en: Then, sir, tell me plainly. Do I write the apology?
lines: 그럼 어르신, 솔직히 말씀해 주십시오. 사죄문을 씁니까?

en: Plain is a road for a king to walk.
I am the weather. Weather doesn’t talk.
lines: 나는 날씨다. 날씨는 말을 안 해.

en: You’re talking now.
Then listen faster.
Will I win?
That’s not mine to give, and not yours to keep.
Ask the man with the ledger, the night that you sleep.
lines: 그건 내가 줄 것도, 네가 쥘 것도 아니다.
장부 든 사내한테 물어라. 네가 잠드는 밤에.

en: Sir. With respect. Tonight I’ve had riddles from a king who hums and a queen who counts her answers, and a farmer told me I’m a seedling.
Could you just say it plainly? Once?
lines: 어르신. 외람되지만, 오늘 밤 흥얼거리는 왕한테 수수께끼를 듣고, 대답을 세는 왕비한테 듣고, 농부한테는 모종이란 소리를 들었습니다.
한 번만, 그냥 솔직히 말씀해 주실 수 없습니까?

en: Plain is for kings. I retired.
lines: 곧은 말은 임금 몫이다. 나는 물러났다.

blocks.html: He looks past Munmu at the black water, as if a city were standing in it.
blocks.ko: 그는 문무 너머 검은 물을 본다. 거기 성 하나가 서 있기라도 한 듯이.

en: Walls don’t fall. Doors are opened. You’ve heard.
A city I knew held a year on its stones. Then a man inside said a word.
So build me a house where the poorest one
would bar the door with his own two hands. Then you’re done.
lines: 성은 안 무너진다. 문이 열리지. 들었제.
내가 알던 성은 돌로 한 해를 버텼다. 그러다 안에서 누가 말 한마디 했제.
제 두 손으로 빗장 지르는 집을 지어라. 그럼 끝이제.

blocks.html: Munmu thinks of a steady hand copying out its own death warrant. He thinks of three polite councillors and their spare key.
blocks.ko: 문무는 제 사형 명령을 정서하던 차분한 손을 떠올린다. 공손한 대신 셋과 그들의 여벌 열쇠를 떠올린다.

en: The emperor calls himself the Son of Heaven. If I bow to him, I bow to heaven. That’s what my council says.
lines: 황제는 스스로 천자라 합니다. 그에게 절하면 하늘에 절하는 거라고. 화백이 그럽니다.

en: Heaven had one son that I know of.
He married a bear. Ask your mother how it went.
She tells it with extra garlic.
lines: 하늘 아들은 내가 아는 게 하나뿐이다.
곰한테 장가갔다. 어땠는지는 너그 어매한테 물어봐라.

en: …How do you know how my mother tells it?
I was in the room. I’m in most rooms. They’re mostly boring.
lines: 그 방에 있었다. 웬만한 방엔 다 있다. 대개 지루하다.

en: The farmer said you’d know. Who does a king serve?
lines: 농부 양반이 어르신은 아실 거라 했습니다. 왕은 누구를 섬깁니까?

en: Sacred Bone, True Bone, bone upon bone,
and under them all, the ones who have none.
You said it yourself with sand on your knees.
Serve the most. There are more of these.
lines: 그 밑에 다들, 뼈 없는 이들.
무릎에 모래 묻히고 네가 한 말.
많은 쪽을 섬겨라. 그쪽이 더 많다.

en: That’s— I said that. I was six.
lines: 그건— 제가 한 말입니다. 여섯 살 때.

en: And you were right, and you were six. Now be right at forty-seven.
lines: 맞았고, 여섯 살이었다. 인자 마흔일곱에 맞아 봐라.

en: Your father wanted a king of the bone. Your uncle wanted in.
There is an older word than both. Not Sacred, not True. The one who stayed when heaven came down, and governed.
Wanggum.
lines: 너그 아부지는 뼈의 임금을 원했다. 너그 외숙은 들어가고 싶어 했고.
둘보다 오래된 말이 있다. 성골도 진골도 아닌. 하늘이 내려왔을 때 남아서 다스린 자.

en: My name is Bupmin.
Names are coats. That one was mine first.
It fits you better than it fit me. I was taller.
lines: 이름은 옷이다. 그건 원래 내 거였다.
너한테 더 맞네. 나는 더 컸으니까.

blocks.html: Munmu stands in the water for a long moment with nothing left to ask. Then he does a thing his father never did and his uncle never needed to. He gives up.
blocks.ko: 문무는 더 물을 것도 없이 한참 물속에 서 있다. 그러다 아버지는 한 번도 하지 않았고 외숙은 할 필요가 없었던 일을 한다. 내려놓는다.

en: I don’t understand half of what you’ve said.
…But you know better than I.
Better than you? A little. Better than them? Not at all.
Ask them, Wanggum. Then do as you’re told.
lines: 저들한테 물어라, 왕검아. 그라고 시키는 대로 해라.

en: Them who?

blocks.html: The man in white does not answer. He looks down. So does Munmu.
blocks.ko: 흰옷의 사내는 대답하지 않는다. 그는 아래를 본다. 문무도 본다.

blocks.html: The water has gone still as lacquer. It does not show his face. It shows faces. A Baekje woman in undyed white at a well. A Goguryeo boy walking south with a pot on his back. A Gaya fisherman mending a net. A Silla soldier with no rank, asleep against a wall. Thousands of them. More than there are of anyone else.
blocks.ko: 물이 옻칠처럼 고요해졌다. 그의 얼굴은 비치지 않는다. 얼굴들이 비친다. 우물가의 물들이지 않은 흰옷 차림 백제 여인. 솥을 지고 남쪽으로 걷는 고구려 소년. 그물을 깁는 가야 어부. 벽에 기대 잠든, 품계 없는 신라 병사. 수천. 누구보다도 많다.

blocks.html: When he looks up, the man is gone, and the steam is only steam.
blocks.ko: 고개를 들었을 때 사내는 없고, 김은 그저 김이다.

en: That was the hill. This is me.
Come back anyway. With nothing in your hands, like tonight. We like you better that way.
lines: 그래도 또 와. 오늘처럼 빈손으로. 그게 더 좋아.

blocks.label: Dawn
blocks.ko: 새벽

blocks.html: He comes out at first light with wet hair, wearing the winter coat his mother packed. It is cold enough for it after all.
blocks.ko: 그는 첫새벽에 젖은 머리로 나온다. 어머니가 넣어 준 겨울 두루마기를 입고. 결국 그걸 입을 만큼 춥다.

blocks.html: He doesn’t ride home. He rides south-west, toward a river town that used to be a capital, and he doesn’t tell the escort why until the second day.
blocks.ko: 그는 집으로 가지 않는다. 남서쪽으로, 한때 도읍이던 강가 마을로 말을 달린다. 호위에게는 이틀째가 되어서야 까닭을 말한다.

blocks.label: The Mound
blocks.ko: 무덤

blocks.html: The record says the king sent envoys to the old Gaya capital. He did. He also went.
blocks.ko: 기록에는 왕이 옛 가야 도읍에 사신을 보냈다고 되어 있다. 보냈다. 직접 가기도 했다.

blocks.html: Suro’s mound is a low green hill by the river. The grass is long. The stone table in front of it has a crack, and moss in the crack. Someone has been leaving barley on it anyway, a handful at a time, for a hundred and forty years.
blocks.ko: 수로의 무덤은 강가의 낮고 푸른 언덕이다. 풀이 길게 자랐다. 앞의 돌상에는 금이 갔고, 금 사이에 이끼가 끼었다. 그래도 누군가가 백사십 년 동안 한 줌씩 보리를 올려 왔다.

blocks.html: Munmu kneels. In front of the whole escort, a king of Silla puts his forehead on the grass of a Gaya grave.
blocks.ko: 문무가 무릎을 꿇는다. 호위 전체가 보는 앞에서, 신라의 왕이 가야 무덤의 풀에 이마를 댄다.

blocks.speaker: True Bone minister
en: Majesty— the royal shrine is for the royal line. He was— Gaya was—
lines: 전하— 종묘는 왕실 계보를 위한 곳입니다. 저 사람은— 가야는—

en: He is my ancestor. Fifteen back, on my mother’s side. I counted. It took most of a night.
And the next man on my council who starts a sentence with “Gaya was” can finish it in front of my mother.
lines: 내 조상이오. 어머니 쪽으로 열다섯 대 위. 세어 봤소. 밤을 거의 새웠소.
그리고 다음에 화백에서 누가 ‘가야는’ 하고 말을 꺼내거든, 그 말은 내 어머니 앞에서 끝맺으시오.

blocks.hanja: 朕是伽耶國元君九代孫仇衡王之降于當國也……文明皇后寔生我者 玆故元君於幼冲人 乃爲十五代始祖也 所御國者已曾敗 所葬廟者今尙存 合于宗祧 續乃祀事
blocks.ko: 가야국 시조의 9대손 구형왕이 이 나라에 항복하였고…… 문명황후께서 실로 나를 낳으셨으니, 시조는 이 어린 사람에게 15대 시조가 된다. 다스리던 나라는 이미 무너졌으나 묻힌 사당은 지금도 남아 있으니, 종묘에 합하여 제사를 이어 가게 하라.
blocks.html: King Guhyeong, ninth in descent from the first lord of Gaya, came over to this country… and Queen Munmyeong truly bore me. So the first lord is, to this young man, a founding ancestor fifteen generations back. The kingdom he ruled has long since fallen, but the shrine where he lies still stands. Join it to the royal ancestral temple, and let its rites go on.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 2, Garak-guk gi (駕洛國記) — King Munmu’s edict on the rites of King Suro

blocks.html: He sets aside thirty plots of the best fields beside the mound to pay for the rites, and calls them the king’s fields, so nobody can sell them later without saying out loud whose they were. The record dates all this to the first year of his reign. Records like to make a man decisive early. Most good kings decide early and get round to it late.
blocks.ko: 그는 무덤 곁의 가장 좋은 밭 서른 경을 떼어 제사 비용으로 삼고, 왕위전이라 부른다. 훗날 누가 팔아넘기려 해도 그게 누구 것이었는지 소리 내어 말하지 않고는 못 팔도록. 기록은 이 모든 일을 그가 즉위한 첫해로 적는다. 기록은 사람을 일찍부터 결단력 있게 만들기를 좋아한다. 좋은 임금은 대개 일찍 마음먹고, 늦게야 손을 쓴다.

blocks.html: When the barley is laid, an old woman in undyed white starts to sing. Too low, the way you sing something you were told never to sing in front of Silla men. A few of the escort know the words. Their grandmothers were Gaya.
blocks.ko: 보리를 올리자 물들이지 않은 흰옷의 노파가 노래를 시작한다. 너무 낮게. 신라 사내들 앞에서는 절대 부르지 말라고 배운 노래를 부를 때처럼. 호위 몇이 가사를 안다. 그들의 할머니가 가야 사람이었다.

blocks.speaker: Old woman
en: Turtle, turtle, show your head.
If you won’t show it, we’ll roast you and eat you.

blocks.html: So that is how the rest goes. Somewhere, a king who hums has been wondering for a very long time. Munmu laughs on his knees in front of the True Bone, and does not explain.
blocks.ko: 그 뒤는 그렇게 이어진다. 어딘가에서 흥얼거리는 임금 하나가 아주 오랫동안 궁금해했다. 문무는 진골들 앞에 무릎 꿇은 채 웃고, 설명하지 않는다.

blocks.label: Home
blocks.ko: 집

blocks.html: That winter, the old ranks of Baekje are written into Silla’s, man for man. It is the first time a conquered lord in this country has been handed a rank instead of a chain. The True Bone houses complain at length. Nobody opens a door.
blocks.ko: 그 겨울, 백제의 옛 관등이 사람마다 신라 관등으로 옮겨 적힌다. 이 땅에서 정복당한 귀족이 쇠사슬 대신 관등을 받은 건 처음이다. 진골 집안들은 길게 불평한다. 아무도 문을 열지 않는다.

blocks.html: He writes the West its apology too, in a lovely hand that isn’t Deto’s. He signs it with the name the emperor gave him. He keeps the other one.
blocks.ko: 서국에 보낼 사죄문도 쓴다. 대토의 것이 아닌 고운 글씨로. 황제가 준 이름으로 서명한다. 다른 이름은 간직한다.

blocks.html: Every month a sack of rice goes up into the hills, to a man who farms badly. Nobody tells him who sends it. He knows.
blocks.ko: 달마다 쌀 한 섬이 산으로 올라간다. 농사를 서툴게 짓는 사내에게. 누가 보내는지 아무도 말해 주지 않는다. 그는 안다.

blocks.html: His mother is standing by the well when he comes home. It is where she stands now.
blocks.ko: 그가 집에 돌아오니 어머니가 우물가에 서 있다. 요즘 그녀가 서 있는 자리다.

en: Your hair’s wet.
I was with family.
…Which ones?
All of them.

blocks.html: She waits. She has been waiting at this well since summer.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 기다린다. 여름부터 이 우물가에서 기다려 왔다.

en: Mother. You asked him something here. He told me to ask them for you.
I asked. It’s both. It was always both. They had their hands on each other’s shoulders all the way back.
lines: 어머니. 여기서 외숙께 뭘 물으셨지요. 저들한테 물어 달라 하셨답니다.
물어봤습니다. 둘 다입니다. 처음부터 둘 다였어요. 맨 끝까지, 서로 어깨에 손을 얹고 있었습니다.

blocks.html: Munhee is sixty-seven, and nobody calls her little sister any more. She puts her face in her son’s wet hair and cries like one.
blocks.ko: 문희는 예순일곱이고, 이제 그녀를 동생이라 불러 줄 사람은 없다. 그녀는 아들의 젖은 머리에 얼굴을 묻고, 막내 동생처럼 운다.

blocks.html: Nothing changes that a scribe could write down. He is still forty-seven. The West is still in the north. But for forty-seven years he has been somebody’s son and somebody’s nephew, the boy on the beach with his father’s dream in his mouth. Tonight he goes to bed with nobody’s hand on his shoulder, and he stands up straight anyway.
blocks.ko: 사관이 적을 만한 건 아무것도 바뀌지 않는다. 그는 여전히 마흔일곱이다. 서국은 여전히 북쪽에 있다. 그러나 마흔일곱 해 동안 그는 누군가의 아들이었고 누군가의 조카였다. 아버지의 꿈을 입에 문 바닷가의 아이였다. 오늘 밤 그는 아무의 손도 어깨에 얹히지 않은 채 잠자리에 들고, 그래도 허리를 편다.

blocks.html: The dream was his father’s. The kingdom will be his. Somewhere above the weather, someone who has watched this family since before it had a name is pleased, and says nothing. The rhymes were his grandson’s idea.
blocks.ko: 꿈은 아버지의 것이었다. 나라는 그의 것이 될 것이다. 날씨보다 높은 어딘가에서, 이 집안을 이름이 생기기도 전부터 지켜본 누군가가 흐뭇해하며 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 운율은 그 손자의 생각이었다.

blocks.html: Kim Punghun said he could wait for a ship. The ship is here…!
blocks.ko: 김풍훈은 배를 기다릴 수 있다고 했다. 그 배가 왔다…!

logline.en: Xue Rengui comes back by sea. His guide is a Silla boy whose father the king killed.
logline.ko: 설인귀가 바다로 돌아온다. 길잡이는 왕이 아버지를 죽인 신라 소년이다.

images.alt: Map of the Maeso campaign — the West landing and nine Silla armies converging on the Imjin
images.at: He does not curse them. He checks the ji’s bindings, the
images.prompt: Cinematic historical illustration of maeso map, Three Kingdoms of Samhan / Tang era (675), scene: Maeso Fortress, painterly digital art, dramatic natural light, rich period costume, no modern elements, no text, no watermark, --ar 3:2 --stylize 250

images.at: When the last horse is off, Munhun stands up.
images.alt: Bernini’s David on the dune: Munhun twists up out of the grass, sword drawn, the Western horses standing in the surf behind
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. POSE: Bernini’s David. Low worm’s-eye from the dune grass at dusk on the Cheonseong beach: the Silla general Munhun twists up out of the grass mid-coil, torso wound, jaw set, his ring-pommel sword drawn back over his shoulder ready to swing, grey steel lamellar with blue cloth at the collar, tall cone helm. Behind and below him, small, the empty Tang ships in the shallows and a line of unloaded horses standing in the surf. One last red sun break behind the boats rims his blade with a long glistening streak; the dune and sky are black-violet. Encased in darkness: at least 80% of the frame is near-black umber void, the figures pulled out of it by one hard raking key. Old-master tenebrist canvas (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour oil brushwork, glazed umber-black darks, impasto on the brightest highlight, canvas grain; silk brushed in loaded strokes; only faces and hands keep clean webtoon ink line. The steel glistens: the key runs down every blade as one long white-hot streak with a tiny star-glint on the edge. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. CANON — Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Silla banners: blue silk with a white crescent moon. Attached flag /flag_silla.png. Tang banners: vermilion silk with a yellow sun disc and a dark brush glyph inside it — painted as an illegible brush mark, never readable text. Attached flag /flag_tang.png. SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop.
