FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

blocks.label: The Landing
blocks.ko: 상륙

blocks.html: Xue Rengui comes back by sea in the ninth month. His pilot is Kim Punghun. Munmu killed his father. Now the son is showing the enemy fleet the way into his own coast.
blocks.ko: 설인귀가 아홉째 달에 바다로 돌아온다. 길잡이는 김풍훈이다. 문무가 그의 아버지를 죽였다. 이제 그 아들이 적의 함대에게 제 나라 해안으로 드는 길을 일러 준다.

blocks.caption: Horses by sea, horses by land. Silla has decided this war is about horses.
blocks.ko: 바다로 오는 말, 땅으로 오는 말. 신라는 이 전쟁이 말에 달렸다고 정했다.

blocks.html: He is older now. The white coat is a reputation he can no longer take off. The West’s eastern command sits on his shoulders the way a yoke sits on an ox that still believes in the field. In a poor field at home, his ancestors are still waiting for their graves.
blocks.ko: 그는 이제 늙었다. 흰옷은 벗을 수 없는 이름이다. 서국의 동방 총지휘는, 아직도 밭을 믿는 소의 어깨에 얹힌 멍에처럼 그의 어깨에 있다. 고향의 척박한 밭에서는 조상들이 아직도 무덤을 기다리고 있다.

blocks.html: Punghun stands at the bow beside him. He left Silla a boy, a hostage in the emperor’s guard. He is coming back as a guide.
blocks.ko: 풍훈이 뱃머리에 그와 나란히 선다. 소년으로 신라를 떠나 황제의 숙위에 볼모로 갔던 그가, 이제 길잡이로 돌아온다.

en: You know this coast, Master Kim.

blocks.speaker: Kim Punghun
en: I know my father’s coast.
The king made it mine to sell.
lines: 왕이 그걸 제가 팔 물건으로 만들어 주었지요.

en: I am not buying anything.
I only ask where the sand is firm. For the horses.
lines: 말을 내릴 모래가 단단한 곳을 여쭐 뿐입니다.

blocks.html: Punghun looks at the beach below Chun Fortress for a long time.
blocks.ko: 풍훈은 천성 아래 바닷가를 오래 바라본다.

blocks.speaker: Kim Punghun
en: …There. Firm enough.

lines: 신라… 예전에 우리와 같이 싸웠던 나라.
이제 그 나라가, 나의 마지막 상대인가.
en: Silla… the country that once fought beside us.
And now that country is to be my last opponent.
zh: 新羅……曾與我并肩作戰之國。
而今，那國竟成我最後之對手。
zhLatn: Xīnluó… céng yǔ wǒ bìngjiān zuòzhàn zhī guó.
Ér jīn, nà guó jìng chéng wǒ zuìhòu zhī duìshǒu.

blocks.html: He does not curse them. He checks the ji’s bindings, the same way he once checked plough-rope, and goes ashore.
blocks.ko: 그들을 욕하지 않는다. 언젠가 쟁기 줄을 확인하던 손으로 극의 묶음을 확인하고, 상륙한다.

blocks.html: Above the beach at Chun Fortress, a Silla general named Munhun lies flat in the dune grass and watches the boats come in. He has been told to stop the landing. He has decided to let it happen first.
blocks.ko: 천성 바닷가 위, 신라 장수 문훈이 모래언덕 풀숲에 엎드려 배들이 들어오는 것을 지켜본다. 상륙을 막으라는 명을 받았다. 그는 먼저 상륙하게 두기로 했다.

blocks.html: Beside him lies a ship captain named Siduk, who has commanded boats for twelve years and never once won anything.
blocks.ko: 그 곁에는 시득이라는 선장이 엎드려 있다. 열두 해 배를 몰았고, 한 번도 이겨 본 적이 없다.

en: General, they’re unloading the horses. Horses first.
blocks.speaker: Siduk

en: Good. Let them.
blocks.speaker: Munhun

en: We were told to stop the landing.
blocks.speaker: Siduk

lines: 젖은 모래에 선 말은 못 돈다. 배가 빌 때까지 기다리래이.
en: We shall.
A horse on wet sand can’t turn. Wait till the boats are empty.
blocks.speaker: Munhun
Siduk
en: …Wet sand. I’ll remember that.

blocks.speaker: Siduk
lines: 서국 놈들은 여포가 환생한 기라 캅니더. 우리 애들도 다 들었고요.
en: General. At the bow. The one in white.
The West call him Lu Bu reborn. Our lads have heard it too.

blocks.speaker: Munhun
lines: 그라믄 여포도 남들처럼 발 좀 적시라 캐라.
en: Then Lu Bu can get his feet wet like everybody else.
Lie still.

blocks.html: When the last horse is off, Munhun stands up.
blocks.ko: 마지막 말이 내리자, 문훈이 일어선다.
blocks.art: Silla spearmen pouring over the dune crest; horses rearing in the surf; Western boats backing oars.

en: To the boats.
zhLatn: Huí chuán.

blocks.html: By evening Munhun has fourteen hundred heads, forty Western ships, and a thousand horses standing in the surf with nobody to ride them. The sea road is closed again.
blocks.ko: 저녁이 되자 문훈의 손에는 목 천사백과 서국 배 마흔 척, 그리고 탈 사람 없이 파도 속에 선 말 천 필이 남는다. 바닷길이 다시 닫힌다.

blocks.html: Nobody ever learns whether Punghun knew about the sand. Xue does not ask him. He sends him back to Chang’an on the next empty transport, and neither country writes his name down again.
blocks.ko: 풍훈이 그 모래를 알았는지는 아무도 모른다. 설인귀는 묻지 않는다. 다음 빈 수송선에 그를 실어 장안으로 돌려보내고, 두 나라 어느 쪽도 다시는 그의 이름을 적지 않는다.

blocks.label: Maeso Fortress
blocks.ko: 매소성

blocks.html: So the war moves inland, to a fortress on the Imjin where the road to Surabol begins.
blocks.ko: 그리하여 전쟁은 내륙으로, 임진강가의 한 성으로 옮겨 간다. 서라벌로 가는 길이 시작되는 곳이다.

blocks.html: Good walls. Terrible stables.
blocks.ko: 성벽은 좋다. 마구간이 형편없다.

blocks.title: Maeso Fortress, twenty-ninth day of the ninth month, 675

units.label: Li Jinxing · Mohe and the West
units.sub: a Mohe chief’s son in the West service — the Samguk Sagi says 200,000

blocks.note: 30,380 horses were taken, and weapons to match. Historians read the 200,000 as Silla counting generously; nobody argues about the horses.

blocks.html: The army at Maeso is mostly Mohe, and the Mohe are mostly horse. Thirty thousand of them graze the flats east of the walls. The grass is outside. No fortress on that river was built to stable a herd.
blocks.ko: 매소성의 군대는 대부분 말갈이고, 말갈은 대부분 말이다. 삼만 필이 성벽 동쪽 들판에서 풀을 뜯는다. 풀은 성 밖에 있다. 그 강가의 어떤 성도 그만한 무리를 들이도록 지어지지 않았다.

lines: 말뚝 줄 끊어라. 말부터 데리고 온나.
en: Forget the walls.
Cut the picket lines. Bring me the horses.
blocks.speaker: Silla commander

blocks.html: The worst stretch of the line is under the walls, where the archers can see. A man nobody in the capital has seen for three years asks for it.
blocks.ko: 가장 험한 자리는 성벽 바로 아래, 궁수들 눈에 보이는 곳이다. 세 해 동안 도성에서 아무도 보지 못한 사내 하나가 그 자리를 청한다.

blocks.speaker: Silla commander
en: Name?

blocks.speaker: Wonsul
en: Lieutenant. Of Sukmun.

blocks.html: Before dawn the herd moves all at once, and not toward the fortress.
blocks.ko: 동트기 전, 말 떼가 한꺼번에 움직인다. 성 쪽이 아니다.
blocks.art: Wordless. Knives at the picket ropes in the dark; then the whole herd streaming across the flats toward the Silla lines.

en: The horses! The horses are going!
blocks.speaker: Mohe rider
blocks.art: Mohe riders running after the herd on foot.

blocks.html: Horses are the thing. An army that has lost thirty thousand horses on the Imjin is not riding to Surabol next spring, or the spring after. Li Jinxing knows it by noon. He takes what is left north across the Hantan.
blocks.ko: 중요한 건 말이다. 임진강에서 말 삼만을 잃은 군대는 다음 봄에도, 그다음 봄에도 서라벌로 달려오지 못한다. 이근행은 한낮이 되기 전에 그걸 안다. 남은 것을 이끌고 북쪽으로 한탄강을 건넌다.

blocks.speaker: Silla commander
en: Let them go.
Count the horses first. Then the spears.

blocks.html: Afterwards the king sends for the lieutenant to give him rank. Wonsul comes in still smelling of horses.
blocks.ko: 뒤에 왕이 벼슬을 주려고 그 비장을 부른다. 원술은 아직 말 냄새를 풍기며 들어온다.

en: Your father would have—

blocks.speaker: Wonsul
en: My father would have said I owe one afternoon, Majesty. I haven’t paid it yet.
lines: 아버지라면 제가 한나절을 빚졌다 하셨을 겁니다, 전하. 아직 다 못 갚았습니다.

blocks.label: The Fleet
blocks.ko: 함대

blocks.html: Out at sea off Chun Fortress, Xue hears it from a courier: the army at Maeso has lost its horses.
blocks.ko: 천성 앞바다에서 설인귀는 파발에게서 그 소식을 듣는다. 매소성의 군대가 말을 잃었다.

lines: 농부에게 말을 잃는 일은… 밭을 잃는 일과 같소.
en: …So the horses are gone.
For a farmer, losing horses… is like losing the field.
zh: 對農夫而言，失馬……如失田。
zhLatn: …Mǎ méi le.
Duì nóngfū éryán, shī mǎ… rú shī tián.

blocks.html: He withdraws without spectacle. The chronicle will remember Silla’s thirty thousand horses; it will remember less how quietly the White Tiger II accepted that the east was no longer his to harvest.
blocks.ko: 그는 떠들썩하지 않게 물러난다. 연대기는 신라가 얻은 말 삼만을 기억할 것이고 — 백호 2세가 동쪽을 더 이상 제 수확으로 삼지 않기로 한 그 조용함은, 덜 기억할 것이다.

blocks.label: Surabol
blocks.ko: 서라벌

blocks.html: In Surabol the number arrives a day ahead of the generals.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에는 장수들보다 숫자가 하루 먼저 닿는다.

en: Thirty thousand, three hundred and eighty, Majesty.
blocks.speaker: Messenger

en: …Heads?
Horses, Majesty.
blocks.speaker: Messenger

blocks.html: After they have lost the horses. Munmu is nearly fifty and still, occasionally, checking his father’s work against the day.
blocks.ko: 말을 다 잃은 뒤에. 문무는 쉰을 앞두고 있고, 여전히 이따금 아버지의 셈을 그날그날에 견주어 본다.

blocks.html: The Western history says Maeso was three Western victories, after which Silla begged pardon. It does not mention the horses.
blocks.ko: 서국의 역사서는 매소성이 서국의 세 번 승리였고, 그 뒤 신라가 용서를 빌었다고 적는다. 말 이야기는 없다.

en: Then get me ships.
It’s the sea now.

blocks.html: One last river mouth. One captain who has never won a fight. Three tries to end a war…!
blocks.ko: 마지막 강어귀. 한 번도 이겨 본 적 없는 선장 하나. 전쟁을 끝낼 기회는 세 번…!

logline.en: At the river mouth where the West landed sixteen years ago, a captain who has never won anything loses twice on purpose. Xue Rengui watches his fleet sit down in the mud.
logline.ko: 열여섯 해 전 서군이 상륙했던 강어귀에서, 한 번도 이겨 본 적 없는 선장이 일부러 두 번 진다. 설인귀는 제 함대가 진흙에 주저앉는 것을 지켜본다.

Silhouette suggestion of the attached portrait only; no readable face. Gaozong #b8935a as a single thin cream-gold hem-line along the ribbon. Graphic color-blocking, anime-painterly, monumental.

images.at: The last of it happens at the mouth of the Geum
images.alt: Poster key art: King Munmu gallops the white heavenly horse through the surf at dawn as the last the Western sails leave the river mouth
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE MOVIE POSTER key art, 2:1 letterbox, composed so nothing important touches the top or bottom edge; crowns, antlers, wings and heads stay well inside the central band; no title, no lettering. Dawn at a river mouth opening onto the sea, mudflats and surf, a few tiny Tang sails dissolving on the horizon. Low angle at the waterline. INTERACTION: King Munmu rides the wingless white heavenly horse Chunma at full gallop through the shallow surf, leaning low over its neck, both hands in its mane, crimson robe streaming, shouting with joy; spray explodes off its hooves and curls up into cloud streamers. Horse and king are one diagonal across the frame. CHUNMA HAS NO WINGS: a wingless white heavenly horse, bare white back and shoulders, nothing feathered anywhere; it rides the air on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs. One low crimson sunrise (#C41E3A) behind the clouds catches the spray, his crown and the horse’s white flank; the sea and sky are ink and slate. Spray droplets as painted bokeh. STYLE: HEEWON STYLE, more painterly, with hints of Korean ink painting — Korean webtoon figures (clean ink linework, simplified expressive faces matching the attached portrait, watercolor-washed) inside a hand-painted world of watercolor and oil with traditional sumukhwa ink: splashed-ink storm clouds, bold dry calligraphic brush strokes in manes, fur, feathers, robes and grass, ink bleeding into wet wash, small ink splatters and drips near the frame edges, patches of bare rice paper where the edges dissolve; oil glazes only deepen the darks, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. Movie-poster key art: bold iconic silhouette, the two subjects large and close, one dramatic low angle, one bright break of light behind them, big dark masses, few hues plus one accent, film-poster drama but NO text, NO title, NO credits, NO logo, NO seal stamp. blocks.html: In the second month, the emperor's headquarters quietly leaves Pyongyang. Then it moves further. Then nobody mentions it. Xue still has a fleet, and a fleet doesn't need a headquarters.
blocks.ko: 이월, 황제의 도호부가 슬그머니 평양을 떠난다. 그러고는 더 멀리 간다. 그러고는 아무도 입에 올리지 않는다. 설인귀에게는 아직 함대가 있고, 함대에는 도호부가 필요 없다.

blocks.caption: The protectorate packs for Liaodong. Xue Rengui keeps one fleet and one last idea.
blocks.ko: 도호부는 요동으로 짐을 싼다. 설인귀에게는 함대 하나와 마지막 생각 하나가 남았다.

blocks.label: Final Ford
blocks.ko: 기벌포

blocks.html: The last of it happens at the mouth of the Geum, in the eleventh month. Sixteen years ago the West came in through this same water, onto a mile of grey mud, while Baekje watched from the high ground. Sunchung had begged a different king to hold it. Now Xue Rengui brings the last fleet in from the open sea.
blocks.ko: 마지막은 열한째 달, 금강 어귀에서 벌어진다. 열여섯 해 전 서군이 바로 이 물로 들어와 십 리 잿빛 개펄에 올랐고, 백제는 높은 땅에서 그것을 지켜보았다. 성충이 다른 임금에게 지켜 달라 애원했던 물목이다. 이제 설인귀가 마지막 함대를 끌고 먼바다에서 들어온다.

blocks.speaker: Silla helmsman
lines: 사찬님, 배 우에 망루를 올렸심더. 망루를요.
en: Sachan, they’ve built towers. On the ships. Towers.

blocks.speaker: Siduk
en: Then they’re heavy.

blocks.html: The Silla ships belong to Siduk, the captain who has never won anything. He takes them out on the ebb and loses.
blocks.ko: 신라의 배는 한 번도 이겨 본 적 없는 선장 시득이 맡고 있다. 그는 썰물에 배를 몰고 나가, 진다.

en: Sachan, we’re going out again?
blocks.speaker: Silla helmsman

en: When the tide turns.
blocks.speaker: Siduk

blocks.html: He goes out again and loses again.
blocks.ko: 다시 나가, 또 진다.
blocks.art: Western hulls high and dark over the Silla boats; the Silla line turning back.

en: …And a third time?
blocks.speaker: Silla helmsman

lines: 큰 배는 개펄에서 못 돈다. 끌고 들어온나.
en: Their ships are big.
A big ship can’t turn on the mudflats. Draw them in.
Like a horse on wet sand.
blocks.speaker: Siduk

blocks.label: The Third Sortie
blocks.ko: 세 번째 출격

blocks.html: The third time, Siduk does not try to win. He runs.
blocks.ko: 세 번째에 시득은 이기려 하지 않는다. 달아난다.

blocks.html: He takes eight boats out toward the Western flagship on the last of the flood, close enough to be insulting. Arrows thud into his deck. He lets them. Then he turns, badly, the way a beaten man turns, and makes for the mudflats on the north shore.
blocks.ko: 그는 밀물 끝자락을 타고 배 여덟 척을 서국의 기함 쪽으로 몬다. 모욕이 될 만큼 가까이. 화살이 갑판에 박힌다. 그대로 둔다. 그러고는 진 사람이 돌듯 엉성하게 돌아서, 북쪽 기슭 개펄로 간다.

blocks.speaker: Silla helmsman
en: They’re coming! All of them— Sachan, the big ones are coming!
lines: 옵니더! 다— 사찬님, 큰 놈들이 다 따라옵니더!

blocks.speaker: Siduk
en: Of course they are. They’ve beaten us twice.
Keep running. Look frightened.

blocks.speaker: Silla helmsman
en: I’m not pretending, sir.

blocks.html: The tide turns under them. Siduk’s boats float in a hand’s depth of water. The Western tower-ships need a man’s height. One by one, the great hulls feel the mud take their keels, and stop, and lean.
blocks.ko: 발밑에서 물때가 바뀐다. 시득의 배는 한 뼘 물이면 뜬다. 서국의 누선은 사람 키만큼의 물이 필요하다. 하나씩, 큰 배들의 용골이 진흙에 잡히고, 멈추고, 기운다.

blocks.speaker: Siduk
en: Now. Turn. Everyone, turn!

blocks.html: What follows is twenty-two fights, large and small, in water too shallow for the ships that started them. Silla men cross the mud on planks, on oars, on their own bellies. The tower-ships cannot turn to face them. They can only lean further.
blocks.ko: 그다음은 크고 작은 스물두 번의 싸움이다. 그 싸움을 시작한 배들에게는 너무 얕은 물에서. 신라 군사들은 널빤지로, 노로, 제 배를 깔고 진흙을 건넌다. 누선은 돌아서 맞설 수가 없다. 더 기울 수 있을 뿐이다.

blocks.label: The Flagship
blocks.ko: 기함

blocks.html: On the flagship, Xue Rengui stands at the rail and watches his fleet sit down in the mud like oxen in a flooded field. He is sixty-two. He knows exactly what he is looking at. He grew up looking at it.
blocks.ko: 기함 난간에서 설인귀는 제 함대가 물 찬 논의 소처럼 진흙에 주저앉는 것을 지켜본다. 예순둘이다. 자기가 무엇을 보고 있는지 정확히 안다. 그걸 보며 자랐으니까.

blocks.speaker: Western officer
en: Commander. We can still float the flagship on the night tide. The others—
lines: 대총관. 밤 물때에 기함은 띄울 수 있습니다. 나머지는—

en: The others are a field we planted in the wrong season.
Float what floats. Take the men off the rest. Leave no one in the mud.
lines: 나머지는 철을 잘못 맞춰 심은 밭이오.
뜨는 것만 띄우시오. 나머지 배에서는 사람만 내리시오. 진흙에 아무도 두고 가지 마시오.

blocks.html: He does not curse Silla. He never has. At midnight the flagship lifts off the mud, and he turns her west.
blocks.ko: 그는 신라를 욕하지 않는다. 한 번도 그런 적이 없다. 한밤중에 기함이 진흙에서 떠오르고, 그는 뱃머리를 서쪽으로 돌린다.

en: Ancestors.
I asked you to wait a little longer. It was longer than I said.
I am coming home without the east. I still have Grandfather’s ji.
lines: 조금만 기다려 달라 말씀드렸지요. 말씀드린 것보다 길어졌습니다.
동쪽은 못 가져갑니다. 할아버님 극은 아직 있습니다.

blocks.html: No treaty comes after it, and no envoy. The Western ships simply keep going west, and nobody on them looks back.
blocks.ko: 그 뒤로 조약도 오지 않고 사신도 오지 않는다. 서국의 배들은 그저 계속 서쪽으로 가고, 그 위의 누구도 돌아보지 않는다.

blocks.label: Surabol
blocks.ko: 서라벌

blocks.html: In Surabol the king waits a month for a letter from the west, so that he will at least have something to refuse. None comes.
blocks.ko: 서라벌에서 왕은 서쪽에서 올 편지를 한 달 동안 기다린다. 적어도 거절할 거리라도 있도록. 아무것도 오지 않는다.

en: Have we… won…?

blocks.speaker: Court scribe
en: Nobody has told us we haven’t, Majesty.
lines: 졌다고 알려 온 사람은 아무도 없습니다, 전하.

blocks.html: He laughs, for the first time since the funeral, and goes to tell his mother.
blocks.ko: 그는 장례 뒤 처음으로 웃는다. 그리고 어머니에게 알리러 간다.

blocks.html: The boy who stole a sentence at six is about to be king of all Samhan. His mother would like him to hold still…!
blocks.ko: 여섯 살에 한 문장을 훔친 소년이 이제 삼한 모두의 왕이 된다. 어머니는 그에게 가만히 좀 있으라고 한다…!

logline.en: On the morning he becomes king of all Samhan, Munmu opens the hall to the yard. Five summers later, Kangrim asks him the question.
logline.ko: 삼한 모두의 왕이 되는 아침, 문무는 전각 문을 마당에 연다. 다섯 해 뒤, 강림이 그에게 질문을 던진다.

It has NO WINGS — no feathers, no bird wings, nothing growing from the shoulders. It rides the sky on curling cloud-and-flame streamers trailing from its legs and chest, as on the painted birch-bark flap. Divine render: numinous through scale and atmosphere, never a glow outline. Seorabeol palace: Silla giwa halls, packed-earth yards, timber verandas. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS are a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST room (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt) painted in that same wash-and-glaze: a warm umber-to-black ground, walls, timber, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft with soft sfumato falloff — the webtoon figures are set INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. LIGHT is movie tenebrism: big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. images.prompt: CLOSING STILL of the episode: the final scene of this story as it ends (not the next episode). The line: “The court reads the name Kim Yushin, and an old archivist goes looking. He finds a note in the late emperor’s own hand, from his boyhood: a voice in the sky once told him that one of the Thirty-Three Heavens had been born in the east as a general. Nobody ever learned whose voice it was. Heaven gossips more than it lets on. The complaint is dropped. The tablet still says Tejong.” Context: Munmu’s son answers in writing. Our late king had a great deal of virtue. While he lived he had a good minister, Kim Yushin, and the two of them were of one mind, and they made the three Han one. We thought that was worth a name. We did not know it was already taken. The court reads the name Kim Yushin, and an old archivist goes looking. He finds a note in the late emperor’s own hand, from his boyhood: a voice in the sky once told him that one of the Thirty-Three Heavens had been born in the east as a general. Nobody ever learned whose voice it was. Heaven gossips more than it lets on. The com A quiet, resonant final frame; leave space around the subject. CANON — PLACE Surabol (서라벌 (경주)) — attached board /pl_eastern_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Seorabeol palace: Silla giwa halls, packed-earth yards, timber verandas. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: BOLD, THICK digital-ink linework with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). THE WORLD is WATERCOLOR FIRST, OIL SECOND: skies and ground in granulated wet-in-wet washes and short broken-colour dabs (Turner), dry-brush grass, dust and stone texture, soft bleeding edges, faint paper grain; the accent colour of the scene blooms into the wash near one frame edge and the frame edges dissolve into bare paper; oil only deepens the darks with rich umber-indigo glazes and adds a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight. INTERIORS AND NIGHT SCENES are the webtoon figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER CANVAS — a Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST oil painting (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt): broken-colour brushwork, glazed umber-to-black darks, sfumato falloff, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlight, over faint watercolor blooms and paper grain; walls, timber, stone, drapery and tables pulled out of the darkness by the one lamp, window or shaft. The same oil-on-canvas texture covers EVERYTHING in the frame, the figures’ silk included — mottled plaster, gritty stone, brushed robes — so the webtoon figures sit INTO that painted space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is MINIMAL AND ICONIC, staged like a Romanticist painting (Friedrich, Turner, Delacroix, Géricault): ONE device carries the frame (a ridge diagonal, a road, a waterline, a hall axis, a table ring, a gate) with ONE or TWO subjects placed on the thirds; at least half the frame is quiet negative space (storm sky, empty field, dark floor, bare wall); distant detail stays tiny and dissolving (a line of banners or roofs in haze); no crowds, no clutter, nothing competing with the subject. Heroic diagonal or pyramid, small figures against a sublime sky or vast field, or a bold worm’s-eye / straight-down angle. BLOCKING IS THE RELATIONSHIP: when two people share a frame, the still reads like a history painting with the faces covered — who stands higher and who kneels, the distance or contact between them, whose hand rests on whom, where each one looks (at each other, past each other, the same way), and how their cast shadows meet on the wall or floor; one gesture between them carries the whole bond. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength: 70–85% of the frame sinks into deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo, black), an extreme value range with near-white highlights right beside inky black and almost no middle grey; big dark masses (storm cloud, shadowed slope, umber room, black floor) against ONE bright break — a single cloud-break, low sun shaft, lamp or window — that lands on the subject; inky darks right beside small near-white highlights, few middle greys in the subject; ONE hard directional key carves the subject out of the dark. FORM IS 2.5D — drawn webtoon line on the outside, sculpted painted volume on the inside (the interior benchmark: a bearded emperor in yellow silk standing at a stone relief, under-lit by an oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens, palm on the carved horse, his shadow climbing the wall): the key is a PRACTICAL light IN or just outside the frame, CLOSE to the subject, RAKING ACROSS the surfaces the camera sees from below or from the side — never from behind them. So every silk fold protrudes, built the way an oil painter builds it: the lit side of each fold laid in with one opaque loaded stroke, the turn into shadow a crisp painted edge, the shadow side a thin transparent umber glaze with a little warm floor-light dragged into it, brush direction following the fold; gold thread and the brightest ridges flicked in with impasto; cheekbones, beard, knuckles, armor plates and horse muscle are painted the same way. The subject is large in frame (medium or closer, worm’s-eye or low three-quarter) so the folds resolve, and the light falls off into black across the body — that falloff is the darkness. Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

Mother.

en: Your sister rode out of this room to Daeya.
Hold still. I’m not losing another one to a door.
lines: 니 누이는 이 방에서 대야로 떠났다.
가만있어라. 문 하나에 자식을 또 잃을 생각은 없다.

blocks.html: A letter has come from Chang’an. It is the first in Inmun’s hand in twenty years, and it is very short.
blocks.ko: 장안에서 편지가 왔다. 스무 해 만에 처음 보는 인문의 글씨다. 아주 짧다.

en: Brother.
The emperor made me King of Silla for a season. I got as far as the coast road before he changed his mind. I am told I abdicated. I agreed.
Word came that you said my name. I heard it.
— Inmun
lines: 황제가 한 철 동안 저를 신라 왕으로 삼았습니다. 해안 길까지 갔는데 황제가 마음을 바꾸었지요. 제가 물러났다고들 합니다. 저도 그렇다 했습니다.
형님이 제 이름을 불렀다는 말을 들었습니다. 들었습니다.

en: His handwriting hasn’t improved.

blocks.html: She folds it into his sleeve, next to his arm, where he will feel it all day.
blocks.ko: 그녀는 편지를 접어 아들의 소매 안, 팔에 닿는 자리에 넣어 준다. 하루 내내 느껴지도록.

lines: 아버지가 늘 하시던 말씀 안 있습니꺼. 천 년 가는 나라.
en: Father used to say a thing. A kingdom that lasts a thousand years.
He always did round the numbers up.

blocks.html: Silla lasts nine hundred and ninety-two years. He was, as usual, very slightly optimistic and essentially correct.
blocks.ko: 신라는 구백구십이 년을 간다. 늘 그렇듯 그는 아주 조금 낙관적이었고, 본질적으로는 옳았다.

blocks.label: The Hall
blocks.ko: 정전

blocks.html: The hall is full of bone. True Bone in the front rows, Head-rank Six behind them, and behind them the new men nobody has a rank for yet: Baekje captains who fought for Silla, Goguryeo’s guest king and his officers, a Mohe interpreter. Out in the yard stand the ones with no bone at all. They have come to see what a king for all looks like. Mostly he looks tired.
blocks.ko: 전각은 뼈로 가득하다. 앞줄에 진골, 그 뒤에 육두품, 그 뒤에 아직 관등이 없는 새 사람들. 신라를 위해 싸운 백제 장수들, 고구려의 손님 왕과 그 신하들, 말갈 통역 하나. 마당에는 뼈가 아예 없는 사람들이 서 있다. 모두의 왕이 어떻게 생겼는지 보러 왔다. 대체로 그는 피곤해 보인다.

en: Open the doors.
All of them. The yard too.

blocks.html: The doors open. The yard comes up to the threshold and stops there, the way people stop at a river.
blocks.ko: 문이 열린다. 마당 사람들이 문턱까지 와서 멈춘다. 사람들이 강가에서 멈추듯.

en: Sixteen years of war were paid for with grain borrowed from people who had none.
Every grain debt from the war years is cancelled. Today.
The men of Baekje and Goguryeo who bled under our banners will hold Silla ranks. The same ranks.
lines: 열여섯 해 전쟁은 가진 것 없는 백성에게서 꾼 곡식으로 치렀소.
전쟁 동안 진 곡식 빚은 모두 없던 것으로 하오. 오늘부로.
우리 깃발 아래 피 흘린 백제와 고구려 사람은 신라의 관등을 받소. 같은 관등을.

blocks.speaker: True Bone elder
en: Majesty. The bone ranks are older than the throne. If a Baekje captain sits where—
lines: 전하. 골품은 왕좌보다 오래되었습니다. 백제 장수 따위가 앉는 자리에—

en: When I was six I said everyone would have to listen to me. Even the bone people.
…I meant you, my lord.
lines: 여섯 살 때 내가 그랬소. 모두 내 말을 들어야 한다고. 뼈 있는 사람들도.

blocks.html: Somebody in the yard laughs. Then the whole yard does. The elder sits down. It is the first time that hall has ever heard the yard.
blocks.ko: 마서국의 누군가가 웃는다. 이어 마당 전체가 웃는다. 원로가 자리에 앉는다. 그 전각이 마당 소리를 들은 건 처음이다.

en: I asked my uncle once. Every kingdom, or every person who bleeds for one. He never answered.
Both. Write that down.
lines: 외숙께 여쭌 적이 있소. 나라 전부냐, 나라를 위해 피 흘리는 사람 전부냐. 끝내 대답을 안 해 주셨지.

blocks.label: The Eastern Star
blocks.ko: 동쪽 별

blocks.html: Thirty-four winters ago, three men looked up at one star and wanted the same title. One died a guest in Chang’an, still calling himself a king. One died in his bed, and the king of the dead came to fetch him in person. One left the title in his son’s mouth.
blocks.ko: 서른네 해 전 겨울, 세 사내가 별 하나를 올려다보며 같은 칭호를 원했다. 하나는 장안에서 손님으로 죽었다. 끝까지 스스로를 왕이라 부르며. 하나는 제 침상에서 죽었고, 저승의 왕이 몸소 데리러 왔다. 하나는 그 칭호를 아들의 입에 남겼다.

blocks.html: That night the son climbs the hill above Surabol where two boys once lay on their backs, arguing about the sky.
blocks.ko: 그날 밤 아들은 서라벌 위 언덕에 오른다. 한때 두 소년이 등을 대고 누워 하늘을 두고 다투던 곳이다.

en: Uncle always said it was a planet.

blocks.html: It sits among the stars without being one of them. He looks at it until the cold gets into his knees. Then he walks down to his own house, like anybody.
blocks.ko: 별들 사이에 있으면서 별은 아니다. 그는 추위가 무릎에 스밀 때까지 그것을 올려다본다. 그러고는 여느 사람처럼, 제 집으로 걸어 내려간다.

blocks.label: The Ancestral Temple
blocks.ko: 종묘

blocks.html: In the morning he reports to his father. The tablet stands in the ancestral temple, and beside it hangs the iron oath from Prosperity Mountain, the one he swore over his uncle’s horse.
blocks.ko: 아침에 그는 아버지께 고한다. 위패는 종묘에 서 있고, 그 곁에 취리산의 쇠 맹세문이 걸려 있다. 외숙의 말 위에서 그가 맹세했던 그것이다.

en: Father. I broke it. Every line.
Baekje is ours. Its prince is in Luoyang, with a title and no country.
His sons are growing. I asked. The gods have been lenient with us both.
lines: 백제는 우리 것입니다. 그 왕자는 낙양에서 땅 없는 작위를 받았습니다.
그 아들들은 잘 자란답니다. 알아봤습니다. 신들이 우리 둘 다를 봐주신 모양입니다.

blocks.html: He leaves the oath where it hangs. The kings of Silla will have to walk past it every time they visit their fathers. He wants them to read it.
blocks.ko: 그는 맹세문을 걸린 그대로 둔다. 신라의 왕들은 선왕을 뵈러 올 때마다 그 앞을 지나가야 한다. 그는 그들이 그것을 읽기를 바란다.

blocks.label: The Dragon
blocks.ko: 용

blocks.label: Five Summers Later
blocks.ko: 다섯 해 뒤

blocks.html: The king for all is dying, and he has left instructions his ministers do not like. No mound in the hills beside his fathers. Burn him, and put what is left in the sea the Easterners come across.
blocks.ko: 모두의 임금이 죽어 가고, 그가 남긴 분부를 대신들은 달가워하지 않는다. 선왕들 곁 언덕에 봉분을 쓰지 말라 한다. 태워서, 남은 것을 동국가 건너오는 바다에 두라고.

en: The war is over. Melt the swords. Make ploughs.
Lighten the tax at the markets and the ferries.
And don’t build me a tomb. The people would only have to carry the stones.
lines: 전쟁은 끝났소. 칼을 녹이시오. 보습을 만드시오.
그리고 내 무덤은 짓지 마시오. 그 돌을 날라야 하는 건 백성이오.

blocks.html: Kangrim reads his name three times at the bedside — Bupmin. Bupmin. Bupmin. — the name the boy stole a sentence with, not the one the ledger writes.
blocks.ko: 강림은 침상 곁에서 그의 이름을 세 번 부른다 — 법민. 법민. 법민. — 장부에 적힌 이름이 아니라, 소년이 문장을 훔치던 때의 이름이다.

en: King Munmu.
Sixteen years of war, one hill, one ally shown the door, and a yard you let into the hall.
One question, then we walk. Were you a king of Silla — or a king for all?
lines: 열여섯 해의 전쟁, 언덕 하나, 문밖으로 내보낸 동맹 하나, 그리고 전각에 들인 마당 하나.
하나만 묻고 갑시다. 신라의 왕이었소 — 아니면 모두의 왕이었소?

en: …Ask the ones with no bone.
There are more of them.
The ledger has never asked them anything.
…I suppose I’ll start. Come. The sea is this way.
lines: 장부는 그들에게 무엇 하나 물어본 적이 없소.
언덕 하나, 강 하나, 마지막 나루
바라던 대로 물결 속 용이 됐네
en: Kim Bupmin, the yard-boy king:
sixteen years of war, and everything.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Showed the West the door with his sword —
a hill, a river, and a final ford.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
Burned on the shore and laid in the sea,
a dragon in the tide, as he asked to be.
Eo-heo, eo-heo, off you go
blocks.title: Bupmin, the Dragon in the Sea

blocks.caption: King Munmu of Silla, the King for All. His tomb has tides.
blocks.ko: 신라 문무왕, 만인의 왕. 그의 무덤에는 밀물이 든다.

blocks.hanja: 朕身後願爲護國大龍 崇奉佛法 守護邦家
blocks.ko: 짐이 죽은 뒤에는 호국대룡이 되어, 불법을 받들고 나라를 지키고자 한다.
blocks.html: After I am gone I wish to become a great dragon that guards the country, to uphold the Buddha’s law and protect the realm.
blocks.source: Samguk Yusa (三國遺事) bk. 2, Wonder 2 — King Munmu becomes a dragon; Ha & Mintz tr., p. 95

blocks.html: They burn him on the shore and put his bones under a rock a hundred paces out to sea, which is still there, and is the only royal tomb in the world with tides.
blocks.ko: 사람들은 바닷가에서 그를 화장하고, 뭍에서 백 걸음 나간 바위 아래에 뼈를 모신다. 그 바위는 지금도 그 자리에 있고, 세상에서 밀물과 썰물이 드나드는 유일한 왕릉이다.

blocks.label: The Tablet
blocks.ko: 위패

blocks.html: Eleven years after the tide closes over him, an envoy comes from the Empress’s court with a complaint that is thirty years late. King Muyeol’s tablet in Silla’s ancestral temple says Tejong, and Tejong is the Second Emperor’s temple name, and a vassal may not share a name with the Son of Heaven. Nobody from the Empress’s court mentions the iron oath hanging beside the tablet, broken in every line.
blocks.ko: 밀물이 그를 덮은 지 열한 해 뒤, 여제의 조정에서 사신이 온다. 삼십 년 늦은 항의를 들고. 신라 종묘의 무열왕 위패에 태종이라 적혀 있는데, 태종은 선제의 묘호이고, 번국은 천자와 이름을 나눌 수 없다는 것이다. 위패 곁에 걸린 쇠 맹세문이 한 줄도 남김없이 깨졌다는 이야기는, 여제의 조정 누구도 꺼내지 않는다.

blocks.speaker: Western envoy
lines: 그대들의 선왕이 선제의 묘호를 빌려 쓰고 있소.
en: Your late king has borrowed a name that belongs to the Second Emperor.
Change it.
zhLatn: Ěr xiānwáng qiè yòng xiāndì miàohào.
Sù gǎi zhī.

blocks.html: Munmu’s son answers in writing.
blocks.ko: 문무의 아들이 글로 답한다.

blocks.speaker: Silla reply
lines: 선왕께서는 덕이 자못 높으셨고, 살아 계실 때 김유신이라는 어진 신하를 얻어 한마음으로 다스려 삼한을 하나로 만드셨습니다.
그만하면 이름 하나 값은 된다고 여겼습니다. 이미 임자가 있는 줄은 몰랐습니다.
en: Our late king had a great deal of virtue. While he lived he had a good minister, Kim Yushin, and the two of them were of one mind, and they made the three Han one.
We thought that was worth a name. We did not know it was already taken.

blocks.html: The court reads the name Kim Yushin, and an old archivist goes looking. He finds a note in the late emperor’s own hand, from his boyhood: a voice in the sky once told him that one of the Thirty-Three Heavens had been born in the east as a general. Nobody ever learned whose voice it was. Heaven gossips more than it lets on. The complaint is dropped. The tablet still says Tejong.
blocks.ko: 조정은 김유신이라는 이름을 읽고, 늙은 사관 하나가 서고를 뒤진다. 그는 선제가 어릴 적 손수 적어 둔 쪽지를 찾아낸다. 하늘에서 들린 목소리가, 서른세 하늘 가운데 하나가 동쪽에 장수로 태어났다고 일러 주었다는 것이다. 그 목소리가 누구였는지는 끝내 아무도 알아내지 못했다. 하늘은 보기보다 말이 많다. 항의는 거두어진다. 위패에는 지금도 태종이라 적혀 있다.

blocks.html: But we left someone in the snow. The winter Pyongyang fell, a Mohe father walked north with something in his pack…!
blocks.ko: 그런데 눈 속에 두고 온 사람이 있다. 평양이 떨어진 그 겨울, 말갈 사내 하나가 등짐에 무언가를 지고 북쪽으로 걸었다…!

toneNote: The chronicle exhales — warmth after war, and a new star in the north.
title: Epilogue

logline.en: The winter after Pyongyang falls, an old man carries a piece of a crown through the snow.
logline.ko: 평양이 무너진 그 겨울, 한 노인이 왕관 조각 하나를 품고 눈길을 걷는다.

images.at: the mountains of Manchuria do not care who won
images.alt: A vast Manchurian snowfield under a storm sky, one line of footprints leading two tiny fur-wrapped figures north
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE. Minimal iconic 2:1 exposition still, composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop; nothing important at the top or bottom edge. High wide, almost bird's-eye, over a harsh Manchurian mountain winter in 668: a vast white snowfield sweeping up to black larch forest and granite crags, a blizzard veil dissolving the far ridges into bare paper. ONE device: a single long diagonal line of deep footprints cutting the snowfield from the lower-left corner to the right third, two tiny fur-huddled figures at its head, a father bent under a leather pack and a small boy stepping in his tracks. Storm-dark granulated watercolour sky with one pale cloud-break laying a cold shaft across the two walkers; a dark-red #8b3a3a catch on the father's sash is the only warm note. Long blue shadows, crushed indigo darks in the pines. No buildings, no army. No text. No watermark. CANON — GULGUL — FACE and garments from attached /ch_dae_gulgul.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Mohe-born, lean and weathered; dark skin, hard narrow eyes, thin moustache and a short chin beard as a man. Dress: Goguryeo border warden: grey steel lamellar under a heavy white-grey fur mantle, dark-red sash and wrapped forearms. Now: The flight north: no helm, a fur hood and layered pelts over the lamellar, frost in the beard, a leather pack on his back. Demeanor: Grim and spare. Says little, watches the door, stands one step behind whoever he serves. #8b3a3a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: a Goguryeo court robe; a crown. | DAE JOYOUNG — FACE and garments from attached /ch_dae_joyoung.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: A boy in 668: round face, dark eyes under heavy brows, a soot or frost smudge on one cheek. Dress: Red headband with a black sun-disc, brown fur collar, pale blue padded coat, red sash, tan trousers, wrapped leggings, a walking staff. Demeanor: Restless and stubborn; complains, asks too many questions, then sets his jaw. #c45a4a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: a beard as a boy; a crown before 698. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL world, in a SIMPLE, MINIMAL, ICONIC layout — the benchmark is a lone man in magenta silk walking down a storm-lit grass ridge toward his tied horse with an empty saddle: one diagonal, two subjects, half the frame storm sky, one cloud-break. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, the face and hands keep that clean ink line, but the body and garments are PAINTED, never digitally shaded — broad loaded brushstrokes and dry-brush drag that follow each fold, the shading stepped in three or four painted value planes with soft broken edges, paper-and-canvas grain running right across the silk — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, never a smooth airbrushed gradient, never a 3D render (2.5D, see FORM). Never a garment filled with one flat colour; never a subject backlit into a flat silhouette with only an edge line (if the camera is behind someone, the key still comes from the side and models their back and shoulder); never a wall flat to the lens — walls and floors recede at an angle so cast shadows can climb them. A thin edge of the same real light may graze the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. TEXTURE IS TACTILE RELIEF — the raking key exists to reveal it: thick oil impasto that stands up off the canvas on the lit side of every surface, loaded-brush and palette-knife ridges the eye can almost touch. Cloth: heavy silk in deep ridged folds, raised gold embroidery and brocade threads catching pin-point specular, quilted collars, layered sleeves with real thickness, beads and pins as small sculpted volumes. Buildings and ground just as sculpted: carved, weathered timber grain on pillars and brackets, every giwa roof tile and end-cap a rounded relief with its own shadow, rough-cut stone blocks, cracked lime plaster, lattice in deep relief throwing crisp little shadows, packed earth with grit and footprints. Never a smooth flat wall, never a plain colour-fill robe. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — the lit subject sits in the one pool of light and everything behind it drops three or more steps to near-black (or, reversed, a dark figure against the single bright opening); foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. SHOT VARIETY AND NEGATIVE SPACE: across a set of stills alternate INTIMATE CLOSE-UPS (faces and hands filling the frame, the background a dark blur) with FAR WIDES (the figures small in a lower corner or third, 60% or more of the canvas left as quiet negative space — black hall, night sky, dark water, bare wall — that makes the small lit figures strike). RENAISSANCE CANVAS, CARTOON FIGURES: the world is composed and painted like a Renaissance / Baroque master (Leonardo’s sfumato, Titian’s glazes, Raphael’s pyramids, Caravaggio’s darkness), but every face stays a clean-lined webtoon / anime face — big expressive eyes, simple nose and mouth, smooth cel-like skin with one or two shadow tones — never photographic skin, pores or realistic facial anatomy. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2.5D painterly cinema — drawn webtoon faces, everything else brushed with visible strokes and canvas grain — not photoreal, not live-action, not a smooth digital airbrush or 3D render, not flat cel fill. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.

images.alt: In a snowbound cave, Gulgul bends over his sleeping son by a tiny fire and speaks to the top of his head in Mohe.
images.prompt: HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Close two-shot inside a narrow mountain cave in Manchuria, deep winter night. A fire the size of two cupped hands burns low on the stone floor in the foreground, sharp, with ember bokeh. The boy Dae Joyoung, about twelve, asleep curled against his father under heavy furs, both fists closed around a bundle of red silk with a glint of gold. Dae Gulgul, the attached grown face, weathered, thin moustache and short beard, heavy white-grey fur mantle over grey lamellar, bends his head to the top of the boy's head, eyes half closed, lips moving on a word, the hardest face softened for once. The coals light them from below; the cave mouth behind is a pale blue wall of falling snow. Rough rock walls angled to the lens, their two shadows climbing the stone. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = gulgul, SECOND face = daejoyoung. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. DAE GULGUL — Look: Mohe-born, lean and weathered; dark skin, hard narrow eyes, thin moustache and a short chin beard as a man. Dress: Goguryeo border warden: grey steel lamellar under a heavy white-grey fur mantle, dark-red sash and wrapped forearms. Now: The flight north: no helm, a fur hood and layered pelts over the lamellar, frost in the beard, a leather pack on his back. Colour #8b3a3a. DAE JOYOUNG — Look: A boy in 668: round face, dark eyes under heavy brows, a soot or frost smudge on one cheek. Dress: Red headband with a black sun-disc, brown fur collar, pale blue padded coat, red sash, tan trousers, wrapped leggings, a walking staff. Colour #c45a4a. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.

blocks.html: The winter after Pyongyang falls, the mountains of Manchuria do not care who won. Snow comes to the knee, then to the thigh, and the wind off the ridges finds every seam a coat has. Gulgul walks in front, bent under a leather pack and wrapped in so much fur he looks like something the forest would hunt. His son walks in his tracks, because there are no other tracks.
blocks.ko: 평양이 무너진 그해 겨울, 만주의 산은 누가 이겼는지 관심이 없다. 눈은 무릎까지 차오르다 허벅지까지 차오르고, 능선에서 내려오는 바람은 옷의 솔기마다 기어이 파고든다. 걸걸이 앞서 걷는다. 가죽 등짐에 허리를 굽히고, 털가죽을 하도 껴입어서 숲이 사냥할 짐승처럼 보인다. 아들은 아버지의 발자국을 밟고 걷는다. 다른 발자국은 없으니까.

blocks.caption: The north, after Goguryeo.
blocks.ko: 고구려가 사라진 뒤의 북쪽.

blocks.html: In the pack, under dried millet and a spare pair of boots, wrapped in a strip of red silk, rides a piece of the Goguryeo crown no longer than a finger: one gold branch snapped off when the palace fell, its little leaves still hanging on their wires. Nobody else would carry it north. Behind them is the smoke of someone else’s victory. Ahead is only the cold that Yeon once pulled a Mohe boy out of.
blocks.ko: 등짐 속, 마른 조와 여벌 신발 밑에, 붉은 비단 한 자락에 싸여, 손가락만 한 고구려 왕관 조각이 실려 간다. 궁이 무너질 때 꺾여 나간 금 가지 하나. 작은 잎들이 아직 철사에 매달려 있다. 북쪽으로 그걸 가져가려 한 사람은 아무도 없었다. 뒤에는 남의 승리가 피워 올린 연기. 앞에는 연이 한때 말갈 아이를 끌어낸 그 추위뿐이다.

blocks.caption: Dae Joyoung. A boy with frozen feet, and a piece of a crown in the pack.
blocks.ko: 대조영. 발이 언 아이. 봇짐 속에는 왕관 한 조각이 있다.

en: Father…
Father, my feet… I can’t feel my feet.
Good.
Better than feeling them.
What kind of— Father!
There. Under the rock.
A little more.

blocks.label: The Cave
blocks.ko: 동굴

blocks.html: The cave is a crack in the mountain’s side, deep enough to put the wind behind them. Gulgul strikes the flint four times before the moss takes. The fire is the size of two cupped hands. He sets the pack down beside it, and the boy, thawing, sees a small gold shine through a split seam in the leather, brighter than a fire that size has any right to make it.
blocks.ko: 동굴은 산허리에 난 틈이다. 바람을 등 뒤로 돌릴 만큼은 깊다. 걸걸이 부싯돌을 네 번 치고 나서야 이끼에 불이 붙는다. 불은 두 손을 모은 만큼이다. 그가 등짐을 그 옆에 내려놓는데, 몸이 녹기 시작한 아이의 눈에 가죽 터진 솔기 사이로 작은 금빛이 들어온다. 그만한 불이 낼 수 있는 빛보다 밝다.

lines: 금이에요? 우리 금 있었어요? 그럼 왜 맨날 조죽만—
en: Father. What’s… that?
The shiny thing. That.
Is that gold? We had gold? Then why is it always millet gruel—
Keep your voice down.

blocks.html: Gulgul looks at the cave mouth for a long time, as if the snow might be listening. Then he pulls the red silk free. On his palm lies the gold branch, bent where it was torn, its leaves trembling in the heat off the fire.
blocks.ko: 걸걸은 동굴 입구를 오래 바라본다. 눈이 엿듣기라도 할 것처럼. 그러고는 붉은 비단을 풀어낸다. 손바닥 위에 금 가지가 놓인다. 꺾인 자리가 휘어 있고, 작은 잎들이 불기운에 떨린다.

en: A piece of the crown.
The Goguryeo crown.
…Did you steal it?
I took it.
Nobody else was going to.
But why you?
You’re… Mohe. Everybody says so.
…Yes. I’m Mohe.

blocks.html: Gulgul is not a man who tells stories. He tells this one the way he would report a border skirmish: in order, without adjectives, looking at the fire instead of the boy.
blocks.ko: 걸걸은 이야기를 하는 사람이 아니다. 이 이야기도 변경의 작은 접전을 보고하듯 한다. 순서대로, 꾸밈말 없이, 아이 대신 불을 보면서.

lines: 내가 너보다 어렸을 때다. 마을이 불탔다.
고구려 군사들이 왔다 갔지비. 연 장군의 군사들.
나는 문간에 서 있었다. 지붕도 없는 집 문간에.
en: I was younger than you. Our village burned.
Goguryeo soldiers came through. General Yeon’s men.
I stood in the doorway. A doorway with no roof over it.
…Why?
Don’t know.
It was our house.

blocks.title: A Mohe doorway, thirty-four winters before

blocks.html: A doorway with no house behind it. Snow on the ash. A Mohe boy holds a stick the way he has seen men hold spears. A big man in red-edged armor gets down off a red-bay horse, walks up until the stick touches his chest, laughs, and pulls off his gloves.
blocks.ko: 뒤에 집이 없는 문간. 재 위의 눈. 말갈 아이 하나가 어른들이 창 잡는 걸 본 대로 막대기를 쥐고 서 있다. 붉은 테 갑옷의 덩치 큰 사내가 붉은 밤색 말에서 내려, 막대기 끝이 가슴에 닿을 때까지 걸어오더니, 웃고, 장갑을 벗는다.

en: This is my house.

lines: 이놈 보라우. 다 타 버린 집을 디키구 섰구만.
en: Look at this wee one. Guarding a house that’s already burned.
Good. Get on.

blocks.html: Years later, on the north wall of Pyongyang in a winter worse than this one, the same man stands with the grown boy a step behind him and the river frozen white below. He says the thing he says every winter, to anyone in earshot, as if the cold might forget it otherwise.
blocks.ko: 여러 해 뒤, 이번보다 더 혹독한 겨울, 평양 북쪽 성벽 위에 같은 사내가 서 있다. 다 큰 아이가 한 걸음 뒤에 있고, 아래로는 강이 하얗게 얼어 있다. 사내는 겨울마다, 듣는 사람만 있으면 누구에게나 하는 말을 한다. 추위가 잊어버리기라도 할 것처럼.

en: Cold?
…No, sir.

lines: 기래도 기억해라. 왕은 죽고, 조정은 지치고, 성은 무너져도—
en: Liar. I’m cold too.
Remember it anyway. Kings die, courts get tired, walls come down—
Goguryeo never dies.

blocks.html: The fire has sunk to coals. Gulgul turns the gold over once in his fingers.
blocks.ko: 불이 숯으로 가라앉았다. 걸걸이 손가락으로 금 가지를 한 번 뒤집는다.

lines: 그 말을 몇 번이나 했는지 모른다.
겨울마다. 술 마실 때도, 안 마실 때도. 싸우기 전에도, 싸운 뒤에도.
en: I don’t know how many times he said it.
Every winter. Drunk or sober. Before a fight, after one.

blocks.html: He wraps the silk around the branch again and puts it in the boy’s hands.
blocks.ko: 그는 금 가지를 다시 비단으로 싸서 아이 손에 쥐여 준다.

en: Keep it under the coat.
By the Holy King’s bow — if they see gold, they will remember we were a country.
lines: 성왕의 활에 걸고 — 금을 보면, 우리가 나라였다는 걸 기억할 테니까.

en: Father —
When we stop… what do we call it?
He called it Goguryeo.
Everyone else got tired and said Goryeo.
You — you say it the way he would have wanted.

blocks.html: The boy holds the bundle to the coals. It is warm already, from the pack, from his father’s back. Outside, the snow keeps filling the cave mouth. He presses the cloth once, gold against his palm, and answers the empty north the only way the chronicle will keep.
blocks.ko: 아이는 보따리를 숯불 쪽으로 든다. 이미 따뜻하다. 등짐에서, 아버지의 등에서 옮아온 온기다. 바깥에서는 눈이 계속 동굴 입구를 메운다. 천을 한 번 누른다. 금이 손바닥에 있다. 빈 북쪽을 사가가 기억할 유일한 방식으로 대답한다.

en: Goguryeo never dies…!

blocks.html: He says it twice more, quieter each time, and is asleep before the third is finished, the gold in both fists. Gulgul does not move for a long while. Then he bends to the top of the boy’s head and speaks in the tongue he had in the doorway. He has used it all his life on the border, for orders and for trade. He has never used it for this.
blocks.ko: 아이는 두 번 더, 점점 작게 말하다가 세 번째를 다 맺기도 전에 잠든다. 금은 두 주먹에 쥔 채로. 걸걸은 한참을 꼼짝하지 않는다. 그러다 아이 정수리께로 몸을 굽혀, 그 문간에서 쓰던 말로 말한다. 국경에서 평생 그 말을 썼다. 명령할 때, 흥정할 때. 이런 데 써 본 적은 없다.

en: My boy. Sleep.
Your father’s here.
…Mm? Father, what does that—
Sleep.

blocks.html: The boy sleeps. Gulgul looks round at the crack in the mountain, the snow in its mouth, the fire the size of two hands.
blocks.ko: 아이가 잠든다. 걸걸은 산의 갈라진 틈을, 그 입구를 메우는 눈을, 두 손바닥만 한 불을 둘러본다.

en: This is our house.

blocks.html: The last coal goes out. Cut to black.
blocks.ko: 마지막 숯이 꺼진다. 암전.

blocks.label: Thirty Winters On
blocks.ko: 서른 해 뒤

blocks.html: They walk on. Thirty years later, in 698, the boy will raise a kingdom called Balhae on those three words, and the shard will still be warm.
blocks.ko: 그들은 계속 걷는다. 삼십 년 뒤인 698년, 아이는 그 세 마디 위에 발해라는 나라를 세울 것이다. 그리고 조각은 여전히 따뜻할 것이다.

blocks.html: His capital will be a stamped grid of halls on the Mudanjiang. Lotus tiles. A stone lantern. Nobody there will need telling what the old country was called.
blocks.ko: 그의 도성은 무단강가에 찍힌 궁성의 격자가 될 것이다. 연꽃 와당. 석등 하나. 그곳 사람들에게 옛 나라의 이름을 일러 줄 필요는 없을 것이다.

blocks.html: So this story ends with two kings under one sky, each sure the sky meant him. In the south, a dead king lies under a rock in the sea, listening for the ones with no bone. In the north, a boy with frozen feet carries a piece of a crown. From high enough up, you can’t tell which of them is the King for All. The sky stopped trying a long time ago. It just watches the boy.
blocks.ko: 그래서 이 이야기는 한 하늘 아래 두 임금으로 끝난다. 저마다 하늘이 자기를 두고 한 말이라 믿는다. 남쪽에서는 죽은 임금이 바닷속 바위 아래 누워, 뼈 없는 사람들의 소리에 귀를 기울인다. 북쪽에서는 발이 언 아이가 왕관 한 조각을 품고 간다. 충분히 높이서 보면, 누가 모두의 왕인지 가려낼 수가 없다. 하늘은 오래전에 가려내기를 그만두었다. 그저 아이를 지켜볼 뿐이다.

blocks.html: Dae Joyoung keeps walking north, one hand on the gold under his coat.
blocks.ko: 대조영은 웃옷 안의 금을 한 손으로 누른 채, 계속 북쪽으로 걷는다.

blocks.html: THE END
blocks.ko: 끝
